name: Winter Ember
detailed_description: You are Arthur Artorias – the sole survivor of a massacre that devastated your family’s legacy and tore them out of the history books. Thought to be dead, you emerge from exile 8 years later, the faceless man kindled by the flame and seeking vengeance. Embark on an adventure unravelling a dark tale filled with twisted characters, centered around a militant religion hell bent on keeping control. Key Features: A True Stealth Experience As Arthur, you must stick to the shadows, infiltrate homes and explore hidden passageways; but, be careful not to be spotted! Choose your playstyle: knocking out enemies may keep them quiet for some time, but they will eventually wake up; a quick slice to the throat may be a more permanent solution, but the bloodstain you leave on the carpet might be a dead giveaway! Keep your wits about you, dispose of bodies, peek through keyholes and pickpocket unsuspecting victims. Deep Arrow Crafting System Prepare for your mission by planning your loadout. With over 30 arrows to craft, experimentation is key to your success! Do you craft a smoke arrow to blind your opponent, or do you add on a poison element to create poisonious gas? Use your arrows offensively or defensively: break down weak walls with a blunt arrow to surprise your enemy, or use a rope arrow to reach a higher place and take out your enemies from a distance. Skill Tree Customize your playstyle from 3 distinct skill trees – stealth, combat, and utility. Unlock over 70 unique passive and active skills to choose from and seek vengeance your way. Explore A Dark World Return home to the cold Victorian town of Anargal, on the verge of technological breakthrough. Infiltrate and explore vast environments brimming with treasure and mystery. From rival gangs to unique characters, approach each scenario in a myriad of ways. Take advantage of the environment, find solutions to every problem, and move past any challenge standing in your way.

short_description: Winter Ember is an immersive stealth action game that casts you into the role of Arthur Artorias, the faceless man. Step into the shadows and uncover a mysterious plot that saw your family torn from the history books. On the first night of winter, you unsheath your blade and seek vengeance.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've beaten the game on hardest difficulty, I figured I'd update my review with a little more details even if the "Not recommended" rating hasn't changed. My playthrough took roughly 11 hours, which included completing a large portion of the side quests as well as doing decent amount of exploration/looting.Winter Ember is not a bad game, but it is hampered by lack of polish, some bad design decisions and a gameplay loop that starts to feel repetitive in the latter half of the game.Game opens up with a pair of tutorial missions that at least for me contained some unfortunate bugs where I ended up being stuck inside the geometry and in the process lost 10-15 mins of gameplay each time, as the game does not have quick save or manual save outside of shrines that act as savepoints (and autosave that occurs only at checkpoints) - which needless to say didn't create exactly a positive first impression.After the tutorial missions you arrive at a larger city that acts as the main hub of the game, there are plenty of houses to loot, black market to sell your loot at as well as to purchase crafting components/lockpicks/potions etc, a number of brief  side quests which typically reward you with either skillpoints or money and the main story quests that most of the time leads in to a separate self contained location where the mission takes place.As mentioned above you obtain skillpoints (via side quests, exploration etc.), these can be spent in 3 small skill trees: Combat, Stealth and Utility. Combat tree focuses on making the combat experience smoother with perks like larger parry window, more damage etc. while Stealth focuses on things such as longer detection window, being able to instantly kill opponents with a well timed throwing dagger and utility features easier lockpicking, more money from sold loots and various other little quality of life improvements - all in all, a fairly standard skill tree implementation and in my playthrough I fully focused on the Stealth skill tree which worked well throughout the entire game.Stealth mechanics work reasonably well, but are also held back by the poorly implemented cover mechanic that not only feels clunky due to having to enter cover from a very specific distance of a wall (or object) but also is very selective regarding where you can actually take cover behind. Top down view is slightly too zoomed in at times and sometimes the layered level design causes issues where your vision is obstructed by whatever is above you.Combat is without any doubt the worst aspect of the game, sluggish, poor hit reactions and otherwise simply lacking any sort of fun factor. Fortunately there are numerous ways to break it completely - being decent at parrying allows you to trivialize nearly every enemy type in to a docile punching bags, smoke and sleep arrows can be used to achieve the same, blocking for the most part is also incredibly effective (as you can seemingly block nearly anything, including hits from a mountain of man wielding a 2-handed weapon against your flimsy short sword) and backpedaling while blocking causes enemies to miss their hits almost every time leaving them completely open against yours.What I found unfortunate is that the game starts to feel repetitive in the latter half, as it never really introduces any extra layers to stealth mechanics and instead starts to double down on the combat aspect with things such as scripted enemy ambushes etc.That being said, there is a decent game buried under all the jank, some bad design decisions and the myriad little issues... Just that the pile of issues is simply too large for me to recommend the game in its current state, for those interested in it - I would suggest waiting to see if it receives any patches and what the said patches fix.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you read further, know that Winter Ember is overpriced for what it offers.I love this game, even though I know I shouldn't.I've finished this game twice on Normal, once on Hard, and once on Faceless Man.Winter Ember is a stealth game clearly inspired by Thief and Dishonored, and the sense I get is that it's more a passion project than something refined and precision-made. This game has problems. Most of these problems aren't horrible on their own, but when combined together, they really pile up and become much more noticeable. They also become more apparent on higher difficulties, which is where you most need the game to be reliable and consistent. I think the team that made this was super small, and the team has already communicated they're open to feedback, beginning to make changes / improvements, which I hope we see soon, since while I Love this game, it's rough enough that I wouldn't feel comfortable recommending to the average player who isn't already a massive stealth fan.The atmosphere is incredible, and it was consistently the best part of the game. Lurking through people's houses and stealing stuff while slitting the throats of various guards, zombies and cultists is always such a vibe. If you know, you know. If you don't, there's no other way I can express it to you as a player of stealth games for over two decades. When this game works smoothly, it feels REALLY good, but when it doesn't -- which is often -- it feels horrible. I don't really know where and how to put all these areas that need improvement, but I'll just type them all out here so people are aware; Often, Takedown animations disconnect or "break" leaving Arthur standing still after 'stuttering' toward the guard for a brief moment. Often this happens because the guard turned or angled their back away. On Kills, this is less egregious, because the player can mash, but on Knockouts, this is very noticeable as it's a Held input, so when a disconnect occurs, the player isn't aware until the guard has already walked far enough away. This disincentivizes Non-Lethal play because the game-feel is horrendous on it. This 'disconnect' also happens often during Pickpocketing.The longer the player stays in an Area/District, the lower the framerate becomes. When the player loads into a new district, the framerate is stable and high again. The entire game also seems to run worse over the course of a long play-session.Combat is awful. On some level it's meant to be awful, but on another level it's definitely not. Fighting a single guard should still feel good, even as it's challenging, but it doesn't feel good, and isn't always challenging for the right reasons. There's no satisfying hit-feedback on arrow or sword hits that you land, and even landing parries just feels more like luck than skill. I've heard, and can confirm this feels a little better on controllers, but it would feel better on mouse and keyboard if you could rebind actions to Side/Thumb Mouse Buttons. Guards have no display of Health, neither as an HP Bar over their head, nor in animation and body-language. Typically a game should pick one or the other, but never none. This confuses the player on how effective their tactics are, and disincentivizes Damage Arrows or Poison, as it's unclear when the DoT ends, as well as making it difficult to track which enemies should be prioritized. If this lack of information is intentional, it can be constrained to higher difficulties like Faceless Man. Stronger animations for displaying enemy health states if Health Bars are undesirable are fine too.Aiming the bow often feels unresponsive, requiring the player release and re-click though the aiming should "come out" reliably. There is no feedback on-screen regarding when Arthur is ready to loose an arrow. A shrinking grey circle appearing where the player's aim is, and having an audio 'click' play when he's ready to fire, or some other feedback would've been appreciated.Too many objects in the game have a lock-and-key approach. Switches MUST be hit by Blunt Arrows, when I feel that Normal Damage Arrows should be able to trigger them as well. They're both physical projectiles. Also, it would give Normal Arrows a more valid function than straight damage, since using them for fighting and stealth is moot anyway. If a player can get in Melee range, they should be able to break planks with their Sword. This currently feels illogical and contributes to the "lock-and-key" feeling of the game. It also makes Blunt Arrows essentially premium, one of the most valuable Arrow types in the game, and as such, prevents players from using their Stun effect for stealth/combat. There is NO WAY to prevent slipping on your own ice from Water Arrows, even on the same ice puddle you've ALREADY slipped on. You can somewhat avoid it if you shoot water arrows to the sides of fires you want to put out instead of dead-center, but if the player is Crouching, slipping on your own ice should be preventable, I feel.Rolling/Diving feels inconsistent as a double-tap, especially when needed "on demand," like at the edges of lethal drops, or chasing enemies. Offering an option to have this as a single-press input would've been great, at least on Keyboards, but there's no such luck. The "Jump/Climb" action is only registered when right at the edge/touching an object. As such, players will sometimes mash it to get it to register. It would've felt better to play if we could HOLD Climb to auto-path up barrels/crates as Arthur approaches. There are more things I could say, but I think those are the things players will notice most.I'm Recommending it here for two reasons. One is because I think Winter Ember has a lot of potential and I want to see it get better and succeed. The second is because to the kinds of players who like this kind of game, I think you'll still have fun if you DON'T play it on anything higher than Normal/Medium for your first playthrough and have a lot of patience. On Hard and Faceless Man, while it CAN be fun, most of the time it won't be because the jank, the lack of polish and the bugs will just become so much more noticeable when the game is "stressed" and pushed to its limits, as happens on high difficulties that are very unforgiving. Despite all this, once you understand how it wants you to play, sneaking around, getting stealth kills and exploring the different parts of the city is just a simple kind of fun any stealth fan will be familiar with. I could be wrong, but I believe this is a game made by people who wanted to make something fun and special and that they enjoyed. Even with how messy the final product is, there's too much love and passion you can see all over it, from the generic but lovingly edgy charm of the story that was clearly written by people who adore these kinds of characters and tales, to the beautifully gloomy atmosphere, lighting and creepy vibe of the Greater Heaven cultists. The game also features beautiful animated cinematics that at times feel like something out of the Castlevania Netflix show, and at other times... don't. The quality is hit-and-miss, but generally really fun to watch, a LOT of effort was put into them! If you like this kind of game, and you KNOW it's going to be a janky/buggy experience that you shouldn't play on anything higher than Normal for your first playthrough if you don't want to go insane from moments that weren't even your fault, I think you should buy it just because indie Stealth games that have THIS much potential just... aren't really a thing these days, Wildfire, Intravenous and Mark of the Ninja aside (all of which are better than this, but mostly due to their polish and nothing fundamental).

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be better IF its cover mechanics were smoother. In the present state, you have to be in a specific distance of the object to take cover, and this can and will expose you many times for your enemies. I felt that playing with keyboard and mouse are less responsive than playing with the joystick. I needed to click 3 times with my mouse to attack an enemy after defending.The isometric camera could have less zoom, it would improve the exploration a lot.Other mechanic that is really bad is the stealth assassination. If you push the button to assassinate your target, the character starts walking in the enemy direction, but if he turn turns slightly to any direction, your character stops and do nothing. This probably will reveal your position. You'll need to press the action button a lot to guarantee that you will kill them. The level design sometimes is frustrating, for example, you can climb a box that has twice the heigh of a bench, but you can't climb the bench. The combat is terrible and the audio design of it breaks your immersion.When all of I mentioned above is combined with the manual save game in specific locations, the level of frustration is tremendous! You can lose many minutes or hours of gameplay, and will need to do everything again and again.The game has potential, but in the actual state, is painful to play mainly in the higher difficulties.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really interested in the story. I'm not playing on my main PC. But I'm on my laptop on High settings (1920x1080) and frame rate has been great. I'm enjoying the combat it's fast and there are options in combat. Like normal attack, strong attack, parry, dodge, dodge roll and breaking an enemies stance, which is nice to have in a stealth game if it has to come to that usually I just try to stay hidden. Crafting seems simply yet has multiple steps and the skill tree I haven't really explored yet but has 3 branches Stealth, Combat, Utility with 8 skills in each branch. I just really want to see where the story goes.

_childDocuments_.review: If someone ask, would I recommended this game, I would say "YES" but this game not for everyone. As a fun of stealth games and Taffer, In game industry stealth games wasn't popularly as many AAA titles. I guess only Thief The Dark Project and Thief 2 Metal Age was popular and still not many people playing them, and if you ask somebody for Thief, mostly people know only Thief from 2014 which is really bad and I cant recommended.Well what about Winter Ember?Was waiting for this game since 2020 and I have played two demo versions. And when it released I was happy to buy.I have played 9 hours and still playing, I would like to show pros, cons and my opinion below.Pros +- Story line, really good, isn't boring as mostly AAA game in our era- Stealth theme and design- Sound design and OST- Open world- Side quests, they are really interesting and some of them funny- Arrow crafting, interesting decision by developers- Lockpicking system, one of good system I have seen in games- Looting, same good, strange that's you cant loot from civilians- Optimisation, no fps dropping or any lags- AI, when you knock guard, waking up in short timeCons -- No Alarm? Stealth game without Alarm, unusual thing in stealth game- Civilians, I kill guard or knock him out, civilians doing nothing instead running away.- Combat, could say little bit annoying and buggy.- Stealth attacks, failing for an unknown reason and the guard turning around- Saving system, its really bad one, long gap for next save or checkpoint.- Arrow usability, well some of arrow I don't use at all.- Mini map, is to small- Bug on Saving shrine, I was just stuck and couldn't escape, lucky I trying clicking mouse and escaped.There are a few design decisions I'd make to help things flow better, however:- Save manually- Dollar in Black Market? I guess gold or coins would be better option- Civilians should try wake up downed guard, bring new guards or something.- Difficulty, I playing on Faceless Man and I don't really feel challenge as a Taffer. I guess in this difficult I should try escape guard, not fight. In Black Market make more expensive items to buy.- Arrow, make more points for using them, I have full inventory of arrows and feels like I don't need them- Combat, less fight more stealth, make guard more difficult maybe one hit death or something, so it makes sense for the genre.- If guard dead, disappear bodies when you left in like 10-15 meters and spawn new one guards.Overall I would recommended this game for people who like stealth games. definitely need some patches and hopefully to see some minor changes from my list above. Anyway I have fun and enjoy playing this game.I would like to say Thank you! to "Sky Machine Studios", "Blowfish Studios", "Gamera Game" and everyone who was developed and believed on this project.

_childDocuments_.review: With a lot of reluctance I guess I can give this game a thumbs-up, but for the catastrophic failure they call "you can rebind keys" I should really give it a thumbs-down. You can workaround the issues with keyboards offering hardware-level rebinding (or if you don't have one, you can probably fix this nonsense with AHK), but seriously - what the actual ♥♥♥♥ ? You can find the details in the forum.Anyway, certain technicalities aside, the game is I guess an ok. Reminds me of Seven (though of course Seven is incomparably bigger map-wise, and has the most vertical map I've seen in a game from my recent memory).Story of sorts is passable with decent amount of side "quests" to keep you entertained for a bit longer. I enjoyed my time of assassinating (primarily, with minuscule amount of stealth for quick kills), parrying and stealing everything in the vicinity. Combat is simple - parry, 3-4x hit, back off a bit if enemy not dead, repeat (for the most part, exceptions apply here and there - e.g. dogs, zombies, some "bosses"). If you want to retain semblance of difficulty, avoid certain skills.Other than that there is too much pointless stuff in the game - you could trim most of the skills and arrow combinations/types and barely anyone would notice.Some stuff seemed to not work - e.g. power chest skills seemed to do nothing for me. Or maybe I didn't notice, IDK. Not that they would change anything in practice.I played the game on max difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never felt compelled to write a review before, but I love this game and I definitely don't think it deserves all the negative reviews it has received. With that said, it does have some issues. I personally didn't encounter anything terrible; the most frustrating predicament for me was when Arthur got stuck a few times, requiring me to reload so I lost a little progress. Occasionally I was able to get him to roll out of it,  so I only had to reload like maybe 4 or 5 times in the 24 hours I played. I played the game to its conclusion, but I have not yet played it on a higher difficulty setting and I have heard, but can't confirm, that certain problems are more apparent on Hard or Faceless Man. I know this is a little silly, but I completely loathed the fact that you have so little control over saving the game. I'm a huge fan of quicksaves, and I definitely missed having the ability to create multiple saves at will. I got the impression they were trying to make it feel like you have to react and live with the consequences, but it just made the annoyance of getting stuck or failing a timed objective more irritating for me. I eventually developed a persistent fear that the game would autosave at a point where I was stuck and I'd have to start the game all over from the beginning since there is only the one save to load from. Luckily that never happened, but I feel like I wasted a lot of time running to the nearest save shrine because I was worried about losing progress.  I also wasn't a huge fan of the anime cutscenes, I felt like they didn't quite mesh with the tone of the game.I definitely think the good parts of the game far outweigh the occasional bugs or design choices I didn't like. The artwork is lovely, the game is beautiful and atmospheric. I thoroughly enjoyed exploring everywhere, doing all of the side quests, breaking and entering, sneaking and looting, crafting various arrows, and discovering the special chests. I also liked the skill trees, and the Steam Achievements. I'm a huge fan of the Thief and Dishonored series and this game helped satisfy that itch I have for stealthy rogue games.

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, this is a mess. The story is a somewhat straightforward revenge-plot, and not very well told. The game looks good, but is also so busy visually that it's sometimes easy to miss things, or enemies, before they're thwacking you in the face with a sword. There's a needlessly complex crafting and inventory system. There's a certain degree of jank to... pretty much everything.Despite all this, the stealth-gameplay is decent enough, and the levels are huge. I did finish the game, so I guess I gotta give it a thumbs up. If you're a hardcore stealth fan, there's fun to be had here, but wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I'd say I'd recommend this, though it definitely needs some patching. I personally haven't run into many bugs; I've only gotten stuck in the map geometry once in the tutorial. I enjoy the dark feel of the city, and it's nice to have a proper thief hub map to go through once more. Looting is basic but fun, I always enjoy the dopamine rush of looting a house of valuables to sell later (kind of weird it's in $ though, if it's gold shouldn't it just be Gold or Coins?)The arrow crafting could use a little more of a tutorial, but it isn't that hard to figure out. You essentially have the different arrow heads which give a different effect, the addons to do special things (i.e. ropes for climbing, fire for burning things, etc.) and then I think the shaft type just determines if you're able to put more effects on the arrow. Combat is serviceable, but most taffers will probably try and avoid combat altogether if they can.There are a few design decisions I'd make to help things flow better, however:- Either more autosaves, more save points, or just let us manually save- Combat flow works but it's kind of awkward to do a back and forth, and I've noticed a lot of enemies get one free "last swing" upon death that often ends up hitting me. I think people have gotten used to being able to be a "stealth predator" instead of a fragile thief though, so it makes sense for the genre.- More loot variety; it'd be nice to find even more variety of valuables- Ease up on guard aggressiveness while simply moving about the city. It's okay for them to generally be hostile, but I feel like they get on you really quickly while everyone else gets to just putter around. It doesn't seem like it's particularly late out given the crowds, is it just because I'm armed?tl';dr: The game shows promise and it's cool to have an isometric thief game (Seven is another good one albeit sci-fi). It definitely needs some patching but I think it's got a good future ahead of it if the devs stay communicative and responsive to addressing the community's concerns.EDIT: 4/23 UpdatePlaying more, I feel like the run speed of the human enemies could be slowed down a bit. Mantling and such is already pretty awkward, and you can get hit climbing ladders so there just isn't really a good way to shake pursuit. I'd like to see them slowed down a little, maybe take slightly longer to open doors and such so you can actually juke your pursuit.

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed my time so far with Winter Ember. (13 hrs at the moment) Is the game perfect? No. Is it a fun stealth based game with a descent story? Yes. It can be a bit janky at times, but overall I haven't had many issues during my playtime. I have had only one time were I got stuck in limbo and had to restart, but lost only minimal progress.I'm not going to say that this is a must buy for fans of stealth based games, but I think it definitely deserves to be played if you are thinking about it.The story is descent and is played out in cut scenes that are well done. The voice overs are good. Nothing made me want to mute them.Besides the main story there are of course many side quests to do. Most are enjoyable and have branching stories that keep them from being repetitive for the most part. There are plenty of buildings, houses, and other places to sneak into and help yourself to the goodies you find. Which include blueprints for the different arrows recipes. Without those you can't make certain upgrades. Some have guards or enemies, but many do not. Finding the way into these places is the trick. This brings in the bow and the different arrows you craft to get access to different areas as well as secret passages. Of course you can use the bow in combat also. Which brings us to the weakest part of the game in my opinion. Weapons are few and include the bow, daggers and a sword. The sword is your main weapon. Which you can parry incoming attacks (quite easily) stunning the enemy. Making them easy to dispatch. Once killed they stay dead were they lie the rest of the game. If you sneak up and knock them out they will be awake if you comeback to that area at a later time. Taking a non lethal approach definitely raises the difficulty. It all works, but it lacks in creativity. I'm playing on normal difficulty for this review. The bug issues that have been mentioned by many others, I have been lucky to not have experienced. I definitely feel the game is worth playing. Just don't come in expecting a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Needs more polish to be worth $25.  It's just that I would have liked to see this game kept in the oven for just a smidgen longer. I will gladly re-purchase this game if a lot of the jankiness gets buffed out, but at half the cost of a AAA game, it's not quite there yet.Looks great and the game mechanics are there with a high potential of being a wonderful Thief-like game, but the feel of it and actually controlling everything feels really janky and jarring/disorienting. Not being able to zoom in and have the camera angled to be more forward is a huge bane - very easy to miss enemies in a long corridor, you have to be close enough to put them in view but also be able to detect you (and enemies detect you very quickly). Cover is wonky and excessively "sticky" (cannot move away from cover to disengage from it, you have to press the hotkey to unstick yourself from it), and is missing in places where it would have been immensely helpful (or at least intuitive as you won't get caught in lower difficulties as an enemy passes by you) like behind barrels and boxes, or to peek around a select few corners.It's very, very,  stupid that chest-high containers, tables, and many other props cannot be climbed on top of nor vaulted over, which you'll see in overabundance. It's really aggravating.I was too lazy to look in the options menu, but the default aim sensitivity is absolutely ridiculous; had to use my alternate mouse DPI setting (250 CPI) just to aim at a very small target. Again, there's  a setting to change this, but I am too lazy to go look. Something to note is that when I first pressed RMB to aim, I was defaulted to looking as low as possible to try to hit a brazier, it wasn't intuitive that you had to change the elevation of your aim alignment until I gave the wooden barrel in front of me a free acupuncture treatment. Just a tiny little nitpick about intuitiveness that I wanted to bring up.Blowing out a light and relighting a flame source should be on two different hotkeys. I should not have to worry about taking out a light source in a panic and accidentally switching it back on because I double-tapped the Interact button by mistake.Combat may as well not exist, no less forced onto the player in the tutorial when it's implemented in this state.The compass is very unhelpful with ink splotches to indicate pathways + obstacles, and with bad symbolage to where it's not immediately apparent of what is being indicated (a black triangle could be anything, ).Crafting was confusing at first, but after doing it once or twice, any decent player should know how to work with it.In summary:Wait for a sale or wait for improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd normally wait until I was a bit further into the game before reviewing, but at time of posting the reviews are overly negatively skewed, for what is an enjoyable stealth & loot game.Very enjoyable stealth game so far, some nice reminders of Thief. Bleed mechanic can be cool at times (can leave a path for guards to follow akin to footsteps in the snow on MGS), although can also happen a bit frequently at others.Graphics are pretty good, world is nicely designed. Some of the tutorial bits although generally fine could be fleshed out a bit more.Combat is a bit clunky. Some minor bugs that can be a little annoying, such as stealth attacks failing for an unknown reason and the guard turning around, and "jumping" with the roll for platforming is tricky to do - although this seems to be just for secrets so far. There is a crash related to moving items around in your inventory, which is annoying, but organising it isn't essential, and I have found one quest I don't seem to be able to finish, possibly because I explored the area before picking up the quest. I've also gotten stuck once in approx 4 hours. So the game could certainly use a patch, but still relatively polished.
_childDocuments_.name: Winter Ember

_childDocuments_.review: That's a good game, excellent visual and level design, with satisfying stealthy game play. The music is very similar to Dishonored's, which is a big plus in my book.The game gives you freedom and treats you like an adult, no objective markers or quest arrows or similar fluff. In the tutorial level, one of your objectives will be to get to a rooftop. On my first play through I found 3 different ways to do that, and I'm sure there's more.After the tutorial level (where most reviewers quit), the game becomes an open-world stealth game, with free roaming around its world, where it encourages you to play it in your own way, always offering you multiple ways to tackle a certain problem.Most negative reviews are infantile or related to its translation. I get that this game might not be for everyone (no game is, really), but for stealth lovers, it's a treat.At the time of review, I played it around 10 hours, most of it offline. I also run it on Linux (Proton), the game works flawlessly, albeit the cinematic videos don't work yet.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a real stealth fan, then you will understand the beauty of this game. And Initially, I advise you to start the game at the maximum level of difficulty, this is how the price of an error will be correct.Stealth - Everything you know about stealth is here. Also added a few features. Plus, you have a very large arsenal of different arrows for different situations, which allows you to be very flexible in your approach to solving problems. The progression system is amazing. You are the perfect killer and thief, and you choose the style of play. A lot of mechanics are taken from the Thief game, but here it's even a plus.AI - Enemies are very attentive, but you still have time to hide, even on faceless difficulty. Enemies have a large patrol radius, which is not typical for such games. If you are an experienced stealth killer, then you should not have any problems.Sound- The soundtrack after 6 hours of play is excellent, does not bother and keeps in focus.Story - So far interesting, but I think this can only be said towards the end of the game.Final, if you are a fan of stealth - then the game is for you, you will be happy to get this experience and this challenge, must play. If you don't really like to hide and go through the whole game unnoticed, then I think you need to choose another game.

_childDocuments_.review: Upfront, only played 4 hours of it before this review, take that for what you will.  I couldn't really be bothered to play more.  The game has some interesting ideas, but just poor execution.  The mechanics aren't well polished (rolling in mid air, weird lag in striking with your sword, get good at parrying and the game is a joke from then on out barring severely being outnumbered). The isometric view doesn't really lend itself to stealth and seems to actually hamper it. The cover system seems unreliable and inconsistent about what you can take cover behind.  There is a lack of depth to the skill tree.  Far too often peeking through doors and windows doesn't matter because it will look clear yet when you enter there is a guard standing right there, whom you should have seen when you peeked. The game feels repetitive very quickly into the play through.  This isn't Thief or Splinter Cell, although it desperately wants to be the former.    I can't recommend this game as janky and shallow as it is.  Also the longer you play the less it seems to be about stealth and the more about combat.  You can fairly easily win all combat with a single parry, and the stealth mechanics are weak and unreliable enough that its better to go that route which is at odds with what a stealth game should be. There is a lack of precision in all of it (guards freaking out at random or repeatedly over the same provocation, not staying stuck in cover when leaning out, cover not preventing a guard from spotting you often...) it all makes for a frustrating instead of satisfying stealth game, and not because its hard, but because its poorly made with bad mechanics.  This just isn't a good game imo.  If I wasn't beyond the 2 hour cap, I'd get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: The look and feel of this game was very nice...but...it kind of stops there....unfortunately the tutorial is severely lacking especially in terms of the crafting system. Honestly, if they could simplify the crafting system or, in the very least spell out how to craft something (arrows in particular, which apparently you have to craft 3 different sections to make one), then this game may be good.  At this stage in the game though....I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: So what's Winter Ember?-It's a stealth, action RPG where you control a single character named Arthur on his quest for revenge. Basically you'll be traversing through large maps collecting loot, fighting enemies, and completing main and side quests. Stealth gameplay includes sneaking around, locking picking, backstabbing, pick-pocketing, hiding bodies. The action portion consist of melee sword/dagger fighting, launching crafted arrows, blocking, parrying, dodging and rolling around. Exploration of these giant maps are recommended for gaining money and finding precious skill tokens.Is Winter Ember worth playing?-Personally, I think it's fair for the price it's launching at. There's a good effort here in terms of story telling, the starting animation is well done and voice acting for the main character is decent. -Gameplay takes some getting used to. Some might call it clunky. Bow and arrow doesn't have traditional twin stick controls, instead you whip the camera around like a maniac but at last you can aim up or down to solve puzzles-The dagger melee fighting is kinda rough but at the same time it's very overpowered if you just roll around and kite the AI-The stealth is good, there's fog of war, enemy patrols, and even foot steps to take caution of, but it doesn't really feel like you NEED to hide much, just bumrush and steam roll them. At least on normal this is the case.-The performance is not great on the highest settings, I was running at a GPU capacity of well over 80-90%. To give you reference running Elden Ring for me gets only up to 60%~-There are bugs for sure. Had times where I soft locked myself jumping on crates and falling in between the geometry with no way out except to reload my latest save. Also had an instance of NPCs being completely dead but still able to talk. Odd stuff.Final Verdict-It's not bad, and for the price it's fair. Expect bugs and the odd gameplay choice but overall if you're on the fence read a couple of more reviews and watch more videos because this is definitely one of those 50-50 hard to recommend or not. Another one of those example where I wish Steam had a Mixed recommend instead of a black and white Yes or No.Check out my full gameplay review video for Winter Ember. It feels so good to sneak around , cover, peek and then take out an enemy by killing them or knocking them down- the game gives you choices here and there. _childDocuments_.review: I almost feel compelled to write this review. Winter Ember deserves without a doubt, better than a 'mixed' review status. Don't let these negative 'under 4 hours of game-play' reviews put you off this hidden gem of a game.The 'Mixed' status this game boats, appears to come down to a mixture of a poor launch and bugs. If I had to guess, the developers have definitely put in the time & effort to rectify most of the complaints. I've only had one bug, that was rolling over a piano and getting stuck in an area of a room I wasn't supposed to be in. Mostly my own fault for not noticing a hidden button and trying to brute force my way past (lol), & nothing a quick load last save couldn't fix.The world itself is beautifully crafted, the ambience & atmosphere is top notch. Levels range from mixture of hub-like open worlds, to more linear and structured missions. The economy of loot vs. equipment feels solid, feeling over equipped at the start but feeling the pinch as you progress to the later stages of the game. Side quests are interesting and amply rewarded, most of the time with skill points (best not to ignore them!).As for criticism... The game at least so far, doesn't offer the strongest story & characters. If your priority is a compelling narrative this game probably isn't for you. Character's don't particularly leave an impact. I wish light and darkness played a more obvious role in effecting decision making (water arrows are probably my least used arrows). On the topic of arrows, the arrow crafting system is a clever mechanic, and it's grown on me as I've played, however it does lack a certain degree of intuitiveness which can be hard to grasp at first. Oh, and while the skill tree is mostly solid, hiding extra hot-bar slots in the skill tree just feels cheap and lazy. Often just resulting in the tedium of having to pause the game, go through your backpack and re-equip the arrow variant you want.Sure this game has a few rough edges here and there, but that's the part and parcel of small indie teams. For such a small team to put out a game like this, deserves applauding. While unlikely, I can't help but hope to see a more evolved sequel come out at some point. Hopefully the mixed reviews haven't put the developers off. There's the foundations of something special here...

_childDocuments_.review:
You are Arthur Artorias – the sole survivor of a massacre that devastated your family’s legacy and tore them out of the history books. Thought to be dead, you emerge from exile 8 years later, the faceless man kindled by the flame and seeking vengeance.  Embark on an adventure unravelling a dark tale filled with twisted characters, centered around a militant religion hell bent on keeping control.  
Key Features:
A True Stealth Experience
As Arthur, you must stick to the shadows, infiltrate homes and explore hidden passageways; but, be careful not to be spotted! Choose your playstyle: knocking out enemies may keep them quiet for some time, but they will eventually wake up; a quick slice to the throat may be a more permanent solution, but the bloodstain you leave on the carpet might be a dead giveaway! Keep your wits about you, dispose of bodies, peek through keyholes and pickpocket unsuspecting victims. 
Deep Arrow Crafting System
Prepare for your mission by planning your loadout. With over 30 arrows to craft, experimentation is key to your success! Do you craft a smoke arrow to blind your opponent, or do you add on a poison element to create poisonious gas? Use your arrows offensively or defensively: break down weak walls with a blunt arrow to surprise your enemy, or use a rope arrow to reach a higher place and take out your enemies from a distance.
Skill Tree
Customize your playstyle from 3 distinct skill trees – stealth, combat, and utility. Unlock over 70 unique passive and active skills to choose from and seek vengeance your way. 
Explore A Dark World
Return home to the cold Victorian town of Anargal, on the verge of technological breakthrough. Infiltrate and explore vast environments brimming with treasure and mystery. From rival gangs to unique characters, approach each scenario in a myriad of ways. Take advantage of the environment, find solutions to every problem, and move past any challenge standing in your way.

detailed_description: More from us About the Game While out fighting for the glory of your kingdom, you and your fellow soldiers are whisked away to Terragaya, a mystical land on the fringes of the afterlife. Your task is to locate the Guardian and move on to the next world. The hitch? You and your compatriots never actually died. Battle your way to the heart of the mystery: Outwit cunning enemies, solve nefarious puzzles, upgrade your character and explore every corner of a dazzling, intricate 16-bit world. Souldiers is a handcrafted retro epic for the ages. Featuring: Gripping melee combat: Slash, parry and dodge your way through an ever-evolving roster of enemies, upgrading your skills and equipment to find a combat style that’s perfect for you. An interconnected world: Discover a sprawling handcrafted landscape filled with treasures, tough-as-nails bosses and secret pathways. 16-bit sensation: Terragaya comes to life with vibrant world-class pixel art packed to the brim with details. Smart moves: Solve environmental puzzles and leap from place to place using an ever-expanding moveset.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a case study of what can happen when you release a game too early and don't do proper play testing if any at all.At a distant glance, the game is visually beautiful, has nice music, and sports a giant map with dozens of hours of content.  A true rarity in the metroidvania genre to see a game offering this many hours.  Even the first dungeon, which the player starts in, fits the theme of the game having massive dungeons that can take upwards for 3-5 hours each.Once you leave this first dungeon, the cracks start to slowly show, at which point you will have already played too many hours to get a refund.  I understand there are a lot of mixed reviews for this game and it can be confusing trying to understand why there is such a disconnect between players.  The first main issue stems from the class system being wildly imbalanced to the point where picking the wrong class can be a ruinous terrible experience, and the game expects you to make this choice based on limited to no real information.  Once you pick a class, you are hard locked into it for the rest of the game, and this explains why people who picked the melee class are more likely to review the game better than those like me who picked the mage.  The mage, who the game tried to tell me is low on HP but has the highest damage according to a graph, has laughably terrible damage and low HP.This is not a difficulty issue, this is a balance issue.  Do not listen to anyone invoking "souls-like" as a case for what this game is about because it has nothing in common with souls games anywhere in any way except the word "soul" is in the title, which has more to do with the story and nothing to do with another game franchise.There's a talent tree for each class, but you can't read any of the talents until you are high enough to use them.  A complete blunder in game design to expect the player to come up with a build using a finite number of skill points without letting them see the skills so they can plan.  In my 40 hours, I never saw a way to respec my points either, which compounds the sheer stupidity of this design.At level 1, my mages basic attack does 3-4 damage.  At level 40, with 60 points into attack, my mages basic attack does 8-9 damage.  Let that sink in a minute.  While my damage is increasing only a few points for the entirety of the game, the monster HP is completely out of control.  Dungeon 5 had me fighting monsters with 450 HP each, and they are all over the place.  Meanwhile scout players having their melee attacks do 4 times this amount, while also having double the HP.  My MP regen is so slow that I could raise a family before the bar fills up again, and even at higher levels after getting the regen talent it still feels painful.  It's easy to see what player experience varies here.The basic and obvious issue is that you can only conclude there was minimal play testing done, especially with the non-melee classes.  These issues are everywhere and would have easily been picked up on if someone who taken the time to play the game before releasing it.  Instead you have a game that is not only riddled by terrible game balance, but a stunning amount of bugs.  When I say bugs, I mean game-breaking, game-ruining, file-corrupting, end-of-your-playthrough-because-you -are-hardlocked type of bugs.  The second half of the game is littered with ways for your playthrough to come to an unexpected end by no fault of your own, and we aren't even talking about the lesser bugs where I opened a box and lost a heart container piece forever because the game decided I couldn't have it.This combined with the balance issues make for a long and frustrating experience.  Combine this with the fact that for some reason the devs decided that rationing save points just for the sake of difficulty, a terrible "check point" system which locks the player into bad situations with low HP, and the fact that when you die everything you did since your last save never happened.   No map coverage, no items kept, no levels gained, nothing.  In later dungeons, the game expects you to go through 20+ minute stretches without a save, fighting monsters which have laughably inflated HP, only to die in 2 hits and lose everything.  Let's also not forget the infamous second dungeon which locks you inside until you can kill the final boss 5 hours later preventing you from being able to upgrade anything in the mean time.  Luckily the rest of the game's dungeons don't do this, but they become mired by damage sponge enemies at every turn.Healing potions must be purchased for 100 gold each, heal a laughably low amount of HP, even after being "upgraded" by doing a terrible collection quest, they barely do anything.  The gameplay is a muddled mess as well.  Between input lag and the game outright eating your inputs, and the ledge grabbing.  That ledge grab mechanic is enraging.  Your character will snap to any ledge in the game, grab it, and hang there waiting to get hit.  Why is a platform 1 foot off the ground a ledge grab if you can jump higher than it?  Because in mid fight you will grab it, get hit while hanging there, die, and lose 20 mins of progress because the last save was so far back you will be in elementary school when you reload. Hit boxes on enemies and boss attacks also seem to be wildly larger than their visual as well in some cases, combined with their trial-and-error attack patterns make them a slog. Don't forget to throw in some unskippable cut-scenes into the mix, the game's final boss being the worst offender.Most of the rewards for exploring are a complete joke as well.  Upgrading your weapon costs a baffling amount of material and money, especially in the higher tiers, and the gains are a joke.  On the mage, it makes virtually no difference at all.  Combat gets more annoying by the the fact the dodge cooldown is upwards of 5 seconds, and monsters are flailing and spamming attacks like they are cocaine.  Mage shield breaks in 1 hit, so forget blocking, and monsters can aggro and hit you from 3 screen lengths away at times, well before you know they are even there.  Half of the chests in the game, the wood ones, contain literally nothing of value, ever.  The red ones which contain more important items, most of them are worthless as well, or you need to find so many of them to make a difference in any way that it kills any interest to finding them.  Even the gear is trash as 95% of the items you find from monsters and boxes have useless passives which bonuses so small you would be hard-pressed to even notice them.This is also a PC game that has no mouse support.  The UI is a muddled mess that has menus within menus then all use different buttons to navigate for what I can only guess is to try to be console friendly since the controller has a finite amount of buttons.  Consumables are broken into 5 different tabs because the devs think we need a different tabs for potions and vials.  The exp curve also makes no sense, as some levels costs a higher amount of exp if it unlocks a talent box, then dips down to a lower exp weirdly for the level beyond.Patches will come, and maybe some of this stuff will be fixed or will already be fixed depending on when you are reading this.  The fact remains that despite the games visuals and size, this is a muddled mess that could have easily been preventable with the absolute bare minimum of play testing, and another month or so of polish.  The result is you paying money for what feels like a half-baked beta to be their Q&A tester while you hope not to hit a game-stopping bug, or pick the right class.  The game deserves every negative review you see for it's state at launch, and it has nothing to do with difficulty, it has to do with a stunning lack of Q&A testing and balance issues that make the game into a dumpster fire depending on what class you picked.

_childDocuments_.review: In this game you choose one of the three heroes to go on an adventure through alien planet. Its a 2D metroidvania with all main features of the genre - non-linear exploration, platforming, secrets, collectibles, quests and side-quests, combat and so on.I've played this game for about 40+ hours, did a 100% run on medium difficulty, meaning getting all collectibles/side-quests/etc, and at the moment of writing my review i do not recommend this game for vast majority of players. Why? Because every good thing this game has (and it has plenty of good things for sure) is outweighted by numerous bad things.The pros and cons:+ The WORLD is truly vast and nicely drawn. Locations are huge and have distinct features in different zones, lots of secret rooms, hidden collectibles, different puzzles. There are A LOT of different types of enemies with unique moves/attacks patterns, many challenging bosses.- This beautiful world HATES you and wants you to die, horribly. The game features 3 levels of difficulty (easy, normal, hard), but even if you pick the easiest one every enemy is tearing you apart in a matter of seconds. You HAVE to get VERY good at dodging, blocking, using terrain and memorizing all movesets from all enemies if you want to actually play this game. From the very beginning the enemies start as VERY challenging, gradually moving to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HARD, then to seriously unfair and then finish as downright obnoxious. Seriously, I passionately HATE with all my heart the weaponized doggies, foxes, rats, ravens, toads and all other enemies this game throws at you. They are fast, have bloated HP pools, and hit like a ton of bricks ON TOP of some questionable “special abilities”: teleporting from any point of the map straight to player? Check. Dodging half your attacks and becoming untargetable while ALSO dealing damage? Check. Homing missiles that ENDLESSLY spawn in certain area and go through terrain? SURE, WHY NOT. The list goes on, but you got the main idea.Normally it wouldn’t be such a problem, but your hero is fragile as glass, has pathetic HP pool that gets depleted in 2 (3 in the endgame) monsters combo attacks and you hit like wet noodle – even with FULL damage and defence upgrades (I had every upgrade from the previous zones before entering the new ones).And here comes the MOST INTERESTING part – when you die, you lose ALL your progress – the XP, quests done, items collected, map explored, etc. This leads to a numerous chains of gruesome deaths over and over again until you “get gud” at the game. I’ve played many “soulslike” games, ALL the good metroidvanias ever released on PC and console (starting from first castlevanias and metroids to hollow knight and ori of the modern days) and I have to admit – the difficulty level of this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ INSANE. Its harder than dark souls, harder than elden ring and harder than even those grindy console games of the 90-s era. You have been warned.+ Game has great variety of secondary weapons and main weapons upgrades- Most of them are useless and cannot be realistically used on a regular basis, because the required ammunition is scarce commodity – it either drops from some of the toughest enemies OR can be bought at shops (which are all rather far away from each other). + Puzzles are clever and require you to actually use your head. Gamedevs really love their puzzles AND various platforming tricks to solve them.- The game wants you to be VERY good at platforming, but fails to provide the necessary conditions. For example, the devs want you to use the “triple jump” combo (double jump, then wall jump, dash into the same wall and wall jump again) VERY often, but when your hero actually touches the walls to make the final jump the game...doesnt even register it and he slides to the ground like a meat sack, daring you to try again and again.I’m not joking now, I’ve spent 2 ENTIRE HOURS (!!!) to make a certain jump in a sewers area because the hero kept ****ing slipping on the wall instead of jumping. And this is only one episode, there were many others.- Game is riddled with bugs, some of which are game breaking. Seriously, ive beaten the final boss, seen the credits and then….black screen, nothing. Didn’t get any achievements for killin it, finishing a game as a certain class, nothing. Did the devs actually TEST the game they’ve made? Seems not very likely, as the bugs thread in steam discussions is overflowing with reports.TL;DRA beautiful and colorful metroidvania game plagued by questionable design choices and serious balance issues. I haven’t sweared so much in my entire life as when I was playing this. Prepare to die edition, you have been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying this: as soon as the developers truly fix the game, I will be happy to change this review to a positive one. Please read the entirety, because "Yes" or "No" is not always the best. First and foremost, this game is beautiful and very nostalgic for me from the days of Super Nintendo. It has a ton of content, a relatively decent story and the "usual" fantasy type of stuff like swords, spells, dragons and so on. All in all, they have nailed the theme and presentation. However this only adds to the frustration of many of the issues I will describe, because in the end - we know this game has so much potential and aside everything it has its fun. What was really wrong with this game was a swath of bugs (some of which still have not been fixed as of the major 1.1.1 patch, like black screen after beating final boss) - and also several questionable design choices. The patch spoken above at the time of this writing fixed some of the bugs, but in terms of gameplay addressed very little of the actual problem and, in my opinion, created new ones in the opposite direction. That is, by applying a blanket nerf to enemy HP and damage, AND boosting player damage (and several other player-benefiting things) - the game, even on the hardest difficulty, is a total joke for anyone with a desire for challenge. Especially considering the gritty, grindy challenge it was before. I will not lie and say this game frustrated the hell out of me many times. The initial version was not fair, not at all easy and required some grinding. But that's what made this game special and what made the hardest difficulty the hardest difficulty. The real problem(s) with the game are things like:1. Poor wall jumping mechanics, where the arc once you jump is too parabolic and you don't have a sense of power from your jumps, leading to a lot of missed jumps. Expectations from games like HollowKnight make it even worse, because compared to the controls and movement in that game, this one is horrendous. 2. Ledge-grabbing mechanics, which put your hero in a "ledge grab" position prior to jumping onto the platform if you touch the corner of it. This has some interesting applications, but in practice it is a total annoyance and requires getting used to with the controller because of the high sensitivity. Automatically jumping on a platform after a ledgegrab is many times a fatal decision, while trying to chase flying enemies and getting hung up (no pun intended) on ledges by accident is an equal frustration. 3. MASSIVE list of collectible subweapons, with 90% of them literally being totally useless because of low damage and a poor animation. In this last patch (1.1.1) they "cured" that by giving the player cheaper subweapon usage, but this doesn't solve the problem. The subweapons are mostly trash because of how they work. Instead of giving us more, which was a decent start, they should have redesigned the subweapon system. I would rather have high boss HP and better subweapons that actually allow for various builds then for an easy boss that now doesn't even require subweapons at all, let alone regular enemies. Before regular enemies were so tanky that you needed subweapons. Now it is even more meaningless of a system. 4. Not being able to skip cutscenes. This is self-explanatory and a major annoyance in several places, especially the last boss which has several that you have to go through. 5. New Game+ is meaningless. I tried it (before the patch) and it was easy, even on hard mode. The enemies had more health and traps did more damage, but it was a joke - and you can't level beyond the max level (50), which means all you are doing is just running the content again to re-get your items and upgrades. This point along with the subweapons point are 2 things the devs could address to give this game literally hundreds of more hours of gameplay per person. 6. Unrewarding chests. In general the rewards in this game are few and far between. Subweapons suck, like I mentioned, and outside a bounty system where you clear a hero type enemy in an area once you've beaten that area, there is very little reward. In this last patch (1.1.1), they gave the player more gold from kills, but this was never the problem. The problem was doing a gauntlet that was absolutely ridiculous, or a quest, only to get a crappy weapon or something that is just not at all useful. More on this on the final point below. 7. Healing. Health and healing received a major buff in this last patch (1.1.1), but to the point where this game is now ridiculous in the other direction. The wizard has a vampiric AoE type skill that now fills the whole screen and, with all the new healing buffs, basically means he can stand there and just attack enemies. Literally destroyed the gameplay, especially since there are no cooldowns for spells. Potions were a large gripe for many people playing this game, but I think the real problem was all of these mechanics which, on hard mode, lead to many frustrating situations because healing was sparse in the game. Potions were expensive and didn't heal that much, so the signature of this game was resource management, However now this has been totally washed away. Flying enemies floating off so you can never get them was fixed, which is good, and checkpoints were added in more places. Off-screen damage from projectiles has been fixed seems like in post places, and subweapon cost has been reduced so you can use more. Players receive more gold. ALL OF THESE CHANGES I JUST LISTED are more than enough to cancel the healing problems the game had without the need to nerf it into the ground like you did. 8. Skills. Skills are cool for the most part but suffer the general pattern of poor design choice, which I can only ascribe to a team that has very little experience designing metroidvanias. That's OK, we have to start somewhere, but the devs need to listen to the players. As Scout your skills get interrupted which is totally stupid. Now with all these vanilla nerfs it doesn't matter, but in the past melee was brutal to play in this game despite having more HP. In either case, skills also do "normal" type damage, which makes them mostly useless against bosses who require the opposing element to really do damage. This is another stupid design choice. Lastly, in situations like the wizard, you cannot use more than 1 spell at a time. This is yet a 3rd area that, if really worked on, could give massive replayability to the game by having different builds possible. 9. Item design. Last but definitely not least. The "unrewarding" aspect I mentioned above is really because items in this game are largely poorly designed. According to the game's beastiary, most monsters drop something. Yet the drop rate is horrendous. In over 150 hours of play, I only got a handful of items from the entire beastiary. Supposedly this changed in this new patch (1.1.1), but I've yet to really see. On top of that, the actual items themselves have very little to offer. There are probably a handful items in the game that are desirable, but outside of that most items have paltry bonuses and items in the game are nothing exciting or life changing when you get one, which they should be. It is yet a 4th area for development that could add replayability. CONCLUSION: If this game actually addressed the real issues, it would become a total classic. Awkward movement mechanics can be addressed to give the game tighter controls and balance out an inherent "ledge grab" mechanic that is baked into the game. Addressing poor item design, poor subweapon design, poor skill tree and skill design and a meaningless New Game+ will give the game massive replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: The general consensus is basically correct, the game is a visual masterpiece with great music but mediocre SFX. The difficulty is quite high but that isn't a good reason to give a negative review.  The controls and QoL issues with saving are the the biggest issues that need fixes ASAP, followed by some balancing.Here are some of the issues that people are complaining about regarding controls:There are no coyote frames when making jumps. This is an extremely basic thing to have in a platforming game, and absolutely essential if you have instant disappearing platforms, which this game has.Inputs can be "eaten" (ie. ignored) rather than "buffered" in many circumstances that are surprising to the player. It's a problem because it feels unfair and in a hard game that means some folks will review your game negatively. There is no grace distance or frames for directional input on wall jumps, which means you have to be sure you are continuing to hold towards the wall while you are against the wall BEFORE you hit jump. It feels unintuitive and clunky because you want to change the direction you are holding the instant you jump so you don't lose any speed.This last one is just a personal preference but the ledge hang has burned me many times by triggering when unexpected. Because you cannot attack while ledge hanging why not make the attack button instantly take you off the ledge and start an air attack? Anything would be better than suddenly eating your attack inputs and doing nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: Souldiers is a game with an amazing art style, interesting gameplay elements, and a massive world filled with numerous different dungeons and puzzles that should please fans of difficult Metroidvanias. Yet, it is plagued by so many glaring and unacceptable flaws that I can't in good conscience give it a positive review.Perhaps the most frustrating aspect of this game is how the save system works. Most Soulslikes do it like this: you lose a form of currency (e.g. Souls, Geo, Runes, etc.) and are sent back to the last save point.In Souldiers, you have the equivalent of Bonfires. However, you also have a checkpoint system, which makes a temporary save that you'll go back to should you die. You often get a checkpoint whenever you unlock a door/shortcut or defeat a boss. There are numerous problems with checkpoints:1) You respawn at a checkpoint with the same amount of health you had when you activated it. Activated it with 9/100 HP? Too bad.2) Despite this, most enemies RESPAWN when you revert to a checkpoint.3) Quitting the game or going to the main menu removes your checkpoints; you are forced back to the last time you MANUALLY saved.4) There is no way to load back to a checkpoint (and killing your own character is dependent on Bomb ammo), forcing you to quit to the main menu in the event of a softlock.Additionally, unlike other Soulslikes, when you die in this game, you are sent back to the nearest save or checkpoint and lose ALL progress made from said save or checkpoint. This means everything from solved puzzles to unlocked chests to gained EXP to opened shortcuts to unlocked skills. This can result in hours where you've made absolutely zero progress.This makes for an extremely infuriating experience (especially if you're playing on the hardest difficulty), because you'll frequently have to redo entire sections and resolve every single puzzle all over again, with some attempts taking around 15 minutes each.By itself, this system isn't the worst: older games usually feature this type of system, after all. It is combined with everything else that it turns from a difficult game to a cancerous ordeal.You have perma ice physics.Instead of consuming stamina, the dodge roll has a long cooldown. This makes gameplay feel unnatural, since most other 2D Metroidvanias have it on a short, fluid cooldown and have air dashes refresh upon landing on the ground. Stamina is used for blocking, which promptly gets depleted upon being hit twice, forcing you to wait minutes before you can do it again.Instead of letting you favourite items and skills, the devs decided to dump EVERY item and skill into your hotbar. You are forced to either a) spend half the fight scrolling through your entire item bar in one direction to get what you what or b) open the menu mid-fight every time you want to use an item.The devs clearly felt that Estus Flasks were beneath them, so instead of having your health potion refill every time you rest at a save point, you have to spend hours farming for money to buy potions instead. This becomes less of a problem late game, but in the early game where the enemies are poorer than a child working in a Nike sweatshop, and where you die in two hits, the game truly manages to achieve the perfect union of brainless grinding and masochistic running-into-a-wall.The parry skill feels extremely inconsistent and doesn't even interrupt enemies.Your i-frames and hitboxes are shorter and smaller than they seem. Enemy i-frames and hitboxes are way longer and larger than they seem. Also, your i-frames don't seem to kick in immediately, which can cause you to be immediately destroyed by multiple hits in a row, sometimes from different enemies.You lose horizontal momentum after a double jump. ???You cannot double jump after wall climbing. ?????????You can't use items if you have any input whatsoever on your joystick/D-Pad/WASD. ??????????????????????????? (This is more annoying than it seems, as it means you have to come to a complete stop to use hotkey items.)Flying enemies constantly zoom away from you, which makes fights against them EXTREMELY frustrating.Some enemies are absolutely unrelenting, making the only way to fight them to be hitting them once, running away, hitting them once, running away, and repeating that 42 times for high-health enemies.The game is obsessed with wasting your time. There are numerous "puzzles" where the "puzzle" is to wait 10 seconds for an electric wall to come down, get to the next safe zone in the 1 second the wall is down, then wait another 10 seconds. And you do this at least 10 times in a row for one room. This number is not an exaggeration.Pushing giant crates/boulders onto buttons is an exercise in agony, since you move them agonisingly slowly. There is no good reason why it should be this slow, unless the devs decided that frustrating and pointless realism should take precedence over fun.There are also drones you have to escort very slowly to their destinations. You can't speed them up in any way, and if you leave the area around them, they'll just zip back to their original positions, forcing you to have to redo it all over again.Many enemies have attacks where you're doing nothing but waiting. You can't even hit them. This is okay in brief bursts, like with  in Hollow Knight, but some bosses in this game spend 60% of their time invulnerable. The attacks aren't even hard; they're just tedious.The third dungeon is a combination of everything bad in both the combat and waiting sections. I have not wanted to completely uninstall a game out of rage ever, and this game got me very close to that point. All this waiting, combined with the fact that you have to redo the "waiting mechanics" all over again should you die, makes this game feel less like a Soulslike Metroidvania and more like a torture experience that is designed to strip you of all autonomy until you lose your mind.The bugs in this game are really annoying. Softlocks are common, and you can be afflicted by a status condition during cutscenes.The worst one I've experienced is how you can be cucked out of completing the game after finishing the ending and watching the credits. I've beaten the very final part of the game 4 times now, each time being met with a black screen. I'm missing two achievements because of this.If you're a masochist and enjoy hardcore Metroidvanias, hours of waiting around for stuff to happen, and dying to random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, including being softlocked and losing all your progress, this could be the game for you.Playing Hollow Knight and completing 10 captchas every 5 minutes (with each mistake forcing you to start all over again) would be a more pleasurable experience.Many of the horrible design choices are still there; the enemies just have a lot less HP and deal way less damage. What I, and most other reviewers, asked for was a challenging but fair game. Instead, they changed their tedious and broken game into an easy and broken game. EDIT: Hey, they finally fixed it in another patch. 7th time's the charm, I guess.The only good thing that's come from this is the absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ going on in the Steam Discussions. It's a complete war zone in there, and I love it. 10/10 more fun to read than the actual game is to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often write reviews for games, but the negative reviews on this one confuse me. Complaints about too many mechanics/too many weapon options? How exactly does this detract from the game? Dungeons that are too long? I never had a dungeon take longer than 2-4 hours total, including backtracking for missed items later on. Combat that is tedious? The game consistently gives new main weapon mechanics and secondary weapons to experiment with, and nothing I used during my archer run felt like it was useless. Most of these negative reviews sound like people who wanted less of a game, which simply boggles my mind.I love the metroidvania genre, and to me this was a shining example of it. Each and every environment was fresh and unique with new mechanics, interesting enemies and wonderfully crafted bosses. Unlike many metroidvanias, this one did a great job creating and telling a story around the player, including the other characters throughout it, and making the side quests and dialogue feel meaningful. I highly recommend Souldiers to anyone looking for a good metroidvania with interesting characters and, in my opinion, incredible and thoughtful map design. Don't let the negative reviews scare you away - I genuinely enjoyed every second of this game!

_childDocuments_.review: The initial mixed review kept me away from this title.I finally tried it a few days ago and I was blown away.It's a masterpiece, hands down one of the best Metroidvania I ever played, and I am 42, I played the first Metroid and the first Castlevania on NES back in 1987, and I kept playing most of the games in the genre since.I wouldn't put this Souldiers at the same level as SotN, Hollow Knight or Ori, but it follows closely.So far (I am at around 60%) I encountered no bug, not a single crash, just some minor clipping usually immediately after saving.The game is amazing, grafically is goergeous, animations are adorable, the maps looks great, vibrant and full of details. The gameplay is super solid, at level 2 the diffculty is farily easy for a veteran of the genre, while at level 3 the challange is fair. The controls are responsive, the platforming very well done, not trivial, not frustraing.When you die you know it's because you f**ked up, not because of anything unfair.It's a bloody shame it got such a low rating, it defintely deserve better and I wish devs will do a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Have not finished the game due to a game-breaking bug that has been reported by another user since fing July see below Therefore until it is fixed, I will leave a thumbs down.
