_childDocuments_.review: It's an absolutely beautiful game, but the combat leans back and forth between mildly enjoyable to unadulterated frustration.This is one of the best looking pixel art games to ever be released, without a doubt.  The UI is polished down to every button (although equipping accessories is a bit obtuse).  The environments are vibrant and memorable.  I have absolutely zero complaints about anything visual in the game at all, I'm blown away by some of the artwork here.The only reason I'm giving this a negative review is that the difficulty spikes WILDLY out of control at random points in the game to the point where it's just exhausting to play.Most enemies are either flying or crawling on the walls, and completely outside of your range if you select the melee class, and you have a very limited supply of ranged sub-weapons, so you are forced to jump up and try to hit them.  The problem is that while jumping you are almost entirely defenseless, so if the enemy decides to attack when you jump, you are going to take a hit and there is nothing you can do about it.  So you usually end up waiting until they attack and then using the window afterwards to hit them once or twice and then go back to waiting.  This is fine for some encounters, but in the very common case that there are TWO flying enemies on screen at once, you spend the next 5 minutes fighting them or just give up and take a hit to put an end to the misery.Then the ground based enemies have their own problems.  You can block them reliably, but they often break your guard with a single attack, so you have to wait 30 seconds for your stamina to regenerate.  That's fine though, you also have a dodge roll, but your dodge roll has a cooldown.  Aaaaand now you've lost 3/4 of your health because the enemy just attacked too many times and you simply did not have enough ways to avoid that damage.You're also just going to take a lot of damage as a result of the ledge snapping.  Jumping anywhere near a ledge means your character is going to grasp onto it for all that is holy.  This happens most often when you are trying to avoid an enemy attack.The other thing, I mentioned the pyramid earlier.  I've been inside this pyramid for about 5 hours now, and I wanted to leave after the first hour.  The areas are WAY too big and WAY too elaborate and you have to fight enemies all throughout them.  If I didn't have the small mercy of quick traveling to other save points in the same zone, I would be rioting for my money back.I flip flopped between writing a negative or a positive review for a while, because there's so much quality in the visuals and I actually enjoyed the first area.  What finally tipped me over the edge into negative though was a boss that was designed entirely around memorizing mazes in between deaths.  I rage quit 3 times before I finally got it and I don't feel triumphant or relieved, I just feel robbed of my time.  I understood the mechanics, I'm not underleveled, I'm competent at video games generally, I just hadn't seen the maze before so I had to continuously die in order to learn it before I could progress.If you want something with difficult gameplay, this is technically that, but the difficulty is so cynically implemented that I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful looking metroidvania, that really falls apart in the combat and movement sections.Movement is often quite limited and clunky, but it does have the usual metroidvania abilities - dash, wall jump, etc. Your character is painfully slow, until you get one of those abilities, which helps you move about 15% faster. The decision to not re-enable double jump after wall jumping also limits whatever platforming options you have.Combat has A LOT of variety, regarding secondary weapons, but you probably won't get to utilize them, due to the limited amount of times you can use them. And it's not like ammo shards regen after resting at a dragon statue, no no no, you need to either buy them for dirt cheap from the shop or find them in chests/enemies.Speaking of chests, it's like a 50/50 split if you're gonna get something useful from a wooden chest (coins, area items) or something completely useless (potions that you don't use or aforementioned ammo shards). The big boy red chests are less of a gamble, but you can still get ass warts from them (secondary weapons you're never going to use).The world is beautifully constructed and animated, there's virtually never a place where it feels empty (by metroidvania standards). However, the dungeons are a bit too large. They all have their separate unique gimmicks and that's fine, but boy is it tiring trying to re-visit those areas to get all of the chests, bugs and crystals.On the topic of those green flying ♥♥♥♥♥, I wish the map marked them (as it does with every other collectible on the map), because doing 100% exploration without a third party map is impossible. You can absolutely find them, but it's going to take hours upon hours of wall hugging, jumping down random cliffs, straining your eyes to see the littlest crumb of differing texture on a wall (which would indicate it's bombable, very nice). This is like a joint point on map clearing, but it does blow at times. I have no clue how people even found some of those secrets, they're sometimes hidden at absolute random locations, with no indicators that something is there to be blown up or passed through.If you're going to 100% this game, the game requires you to complete it 4 separate times (for the 3 classes available and 1 NG+ mode). Complete insult of anyone's time. Speaking of that, everytime you collect a health crystal (forgot what they're called in-game, it doesn't matter), the game plays the collection animation (ala Legend of Zelda) and then plays a separate animation of the crystal going into the collection slot. Waste of time, every time. Also all of the cutscenes are unskippable. At least you could skip the credits.The game gets the general idea of metroidvanias, but really falls apart trying to execute everything. I'd still recommend playing it, but do beware ofthe scare of being lost in the humongous dungeons.

_childDocuments_.review: Striking graphics, decent music, and, after listening to criticism (both here and on traditional media), satisfying game play. Some negative reviews are now here specifically lamenting the changes, but I just spent nearly 50 minutes looking at the profiles of people complaining that the game-balance patch is a bad thing, and not a single public one had achievements past the first dungeon boss before the patch. Some people are just invested in a certain self-image I guess. If you want a challenge, you can always self-impose arbitrary rules like no upgrades or potion purchases.Genuine criticisms I feel is that the heavy attack with the melee character is mostly worthless. Would be nice to see a combo system, or a switchable skill instead of a longer, slightly more damaging sword swing compared to the quick melee attack. Same with having two buttons for both shield and parry - could have just had parry be a perfectly timed shield block and free up another button for an additional mechanic. Also heals are not restored on bonfire like in Souls or bankable like Bloodborne. Instead you have to purchase a limited amount for a sizeable chunk of money (in the early game, money becomes trivial about 40% of the way into the game). Personally I like Hollow Knight's risk/reward system balancing healing, spells and melee attacking, but that is just my preference, so take this as something to be aware of and not a blanket criticism. Finally the secondary weapons. There's too many. I will literally never try most of them, and I prefer just using the standard attack. To be sure, this isn't a negative against the game, but something I hope the developers take onboard for their next game, because I really hope there is a next game,TL;DR - decent metroidvania with gorgeous pixal art and responsive devs. Some parts are more polished than others (that first dungeon is gold), but for a debut game it is remarkable. Buy it if you're waiting for Silksong and need to scratch the itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, but I just can't with some of the poor design that drags it down. While I am being critical of several aspects it's not a singular thing alone that drags it down, it's the culmination of multiple things. The game is just frustrating in design, it's not even as challenging as some people are making it out to be. The checkpointing is generous enough and redoing lost progression isn't a new concept but an old one that used to be the standard.(Class used: Max Leveled Scout)The short version is that the game is designed to be played by the person who designed it and gives the impression they did not have alot of testing to work out clunky features.There is plenty of good in the game but its not outweighing the frustration from playing it.Movement at best feels clunky. Ledge grabbing only occurs on very specific spots so it's easy to jump through the ledge when it looks like you should of grabbed it. Wall jumping is also very inconsistent and often feels like there is input lag when doing it. The "sprint" you get late game is tied to the dodge button and seems to require you to "dodge" before it activates which is a bit awkward. Double jumping is pretty consistent and feels fine although there is some very awkward jumping puzzles that don't feel natural or obvious at first.Combat is a real mixed bag. The Bosses are overall fun with the exception of the final boss phase which is some of the longest most drawn out tedium I've ever experienced, You get maybe 1 or 2 attacks in per cycle that requires jumping to hit and this thing is a massive health sponge.,Normal enemies lack the same detail of telegraphed attacks in some cases and oddly enough are the harder part of the game. Seems odd that the Boss should be the challenge but normal enemies provide more headaches. Often you will fight some enemies that teleport and immediately attack before they lose their iframes. This is a bit harsh at times. Then there's the flying enemies, which always hover or fly away out of reach until you move around or jank the position to force them lower. They are not hard, but they are tedious and extremely annoying and very plentiful throughout the game. Flying Enemies in this game = Pure frustration, not actual challenge. Its like playing keep away when you were a kid, the kid in the middle doesn't enjoy that ♥♥♥♥.There's also an endless amount of times you get hit with status effects that generally will kill you, while it is challenging it would be more forgiving that these applied only on attacks you can read opposed to every hit from an enemy type. Paralyse for example gets spammed on you alot in the 3rd dungeon and it just makes it drawn out as you wait for it expire so you can actually get back to traversal.The dodge is reliable if you time it right, but it has a cooldown so when fighting groups of enemies you are better off not using it and rely more on avoidance with jumps since it leaves you open if you dodge some while others where not attacking (and thus they attack you after you dodge)Blocking feels utterly useless. Maybe 1-2 blocks if you are able to block at all (some go through block) and then you are staggered and basically dead. Avoiding attacks is always the better option. This design around the block makes it feel like a trap that punishes you. While there is perfect block with a reduced stamina cost it doesn't outweigh the risk of using it over avoiding attacks.Countering is much in the same boat, its flashy and neat when you pull one off, but it isn't worth the risk in the end and feels out of place considering the limited applications it has.Attacking in general is simple and works, but the skills feel clunky and hard to find moments to use properly. Any hit cancels a skill use and they all have a wide up. Additionally they do not use the elemental orb you have equipped so in some cases it's actually a damage loss to use them.There is also a massive amount of subweapons, and honestly it feels like too much. It's odd to complain about having this much variety but I would prefer if I could choose 3 to equip so I can tab through only those three opposed to every single one.  They are limited in use but some are quite useful in clearing rooms although it seems they do reduced damage to bosses.Upgrades come in the form of weapon and armor, while the weapon ones are small in amount they do become noticeable if you are lacking them later. Armor however only upgrades your Stamina, which if you are not blocking it's pretty useless and feels bad. Late game I can block early game enemies for a long time, but late game enemies feels the same as when I started so the upgrade only exists so you can keep using it, you never feel stronger or safer with it.Art and visual design is fantastic, truly the selling point of the game, whereas the level design can be very confusing to navigate at times. It would also help if the player could add markers to the map to flag points of interest for later when they lack certain abilities. While the game does mark certain things for you it doesn't mark everything (Like the glowing bugs you seen but missed) so backtracking becomes a memory game of what you still had to grab.Several Gauntlet style fights exist, but they are more endurance based then actually challenging, many just go on for far too long and you are sitting there waiting to see when it ends, they could use better pacing or end sooner, some are broken up into several rooms which are far more enjoyable.The puzzles can be a bit confusing and some cases the timings felt off (5 drone room for example with the water cannons not being in sync with the moving parts) but nothing felt undoable, just unpolished. The sidequests also fall into this category as well, with a racing challenge where you are more fighting the controls then anything.Audio can be a bit weird, namely in the city there's a really loud part in the town square that doesn't seem to have the same levels of adjustment you do in the settings, its a bit annoying when you have to pass through there. The rest of the audio is pretty spot on though and the game has a solid OST (Dungeon 3 in particular is fantastic).Menu's are also a bit clunky to use but easy to overlook as it doesn't impact the gameplay outside mild annoyances.Then there's bugs, and I mean a whole lot them. My game for example softlocks after beating the final boss since my main quest progression bugged in the Final Dungeon since I did something out of order that I wasn't aware was out of order. Testing should have caught this kinda thing but it feels like they didn't try and find what was broken only test it knowing what works, assuming it was tested at all.As a whole the game does nail the Metroidvania aspect but the design feels severely unpolished in some areas which can sour the experience. With some bug fixes and a bit more polish it would help alot I would gladly recommend this to people that like the genre. The balance could use a pass too, but not for difficulty but more to get rid of the tedious nature of flyers.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't in good heart recommend this game at this stage.I wanted to, but I can't.The game in itself is ok, it is a good throwback to all the exploring, secret passages/chests, and whatnot, but In more than one instance I had the game glitching on me which was rather annoying.1. In several instances I couldn't open the pause menu/inventory while in the city. I could open the map and shops, but not my pause/inventory/status menu. If I would go to a dungeon or something, It would work normally.2. Glitching through wall in Sewers slime maze.3. During a colosseum run: Paused the game and got a prompt due to miss clicking while unpausing the game at the same time. The prompt stayed over the unpaused game and I couldn't get rid of it. When pausing again, still couldn't get rid of it and even worse, couldn't check/cancel/confirm anything else, essentially locking the game.There are just too many subweapons and only a handful are really useful or will get your preference, and a few others are really just for puzzle solving.The problem with this is that all of them are always available on your "quick access" and you have to cycle through all of them or pause the game and navigate menus to get the right one.Same about items, though to a lesser degree as there are fewer items.It would be good if you could select/attach/sort what gets put into quick-access.Even better if you could do a few "quick-access loadouts".All dungeons are massive, which is good and bad for a variety of purposes. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Too many minor inconveniences on the core mechanics to a point the game feels like attacking you by not doing what you're trying to tell it to do. Otherwise, it's mid at best. Decent music though.Platforming sequence design is ok but the awkward ledge hang controls (climbing up a platform from a ledge and jumping up from a ledge to reach another ledge is 2 different inputs for some reason) makes a LOT of the platforming puzzles a lot more frustrating than it should be. Timing on some puzzles are weird. lava flood chase sequence is just a trial and error and you're forced to waste 10 seconds on cutsecenes every single time. Elemental change controls are on awkward 60 degrees angles on the right stick instead of the more accessible 45 degree angles. Changing on the fly is VERY unreliable. _childDocuments_.review: I missed the whole launch-bugs-balance-omg! drama, he-he. Judging just from my experience after 35 hours in game.TL;DR: This is one is in the top-tier of Metroidvanias I have played (and I played a lot, trust me)So, what makes it great? I don't know where to begin. All the whine in negative reviews comes from basic misunderstanding of core game mechanics (IMHO). I was about to advocate for the game and answer to some criticism points from reviews, but nah.Level Design: Beautiful. The maps are huge and there's a ton to explore. The game makes you want to look in every corner to get your potions, materials, upgrades or gear. I was expecting the water level. I was expecting it to be the most annoying. But surprise-surprise - it's fun and great. Not even the Swamp level made me frustrated. All good. Puzzles are well crafted and fun to solve. Art: No comments. 10/10Sound: Pretty good. Varies from "oh that's nice" to "How much is the OST for this one, you say?"Controls & Combat: Jumps are perfect. Combat is fun and every punch you land is satisfying. Overall movement & skill using is pretty great. Tho this game has two flaws and I hope the devs will come up with better solution. First one - switching potions/sub-weapons. It's just not working. You have to cycle through whole roster of your belongings in mid-battle to select the needed. Could we have like "Equip 3-4-5 of your favorites and stash the rest?". Cycling through 20+ sub weapons fighting a boss is a pain. Yes, this can be dealt with a pause, but come-on. This makes you lose the momentum of a battle. And the second thing: wall-jumps (and overall combining them with regular/double-jumps & dashing). It just doesn't work so well. Yes, you can overcome the controller and achieve what you need, though for many players this would be a negative experience. That Scorpion Necklace++ from THAT chest is a great illustration of what I'm talking about :DClass & Skill system: Loved it. You have three classes. You pick one - there you go. Yes, the skills are hidden before you reach a certain level to unlock them, but that's the charm. You just expect them to be good and they surprise you (or not). Warrior is the class to start the game with, then, when you get all the core mechanics and how things work - give yourself some challenge with Scout and Caster. Gameplay differs drastically.Enemies: Oooh. Enemies are plenty and some of them. Well, you'll just hate them. But then you will learn the patterns and the attacks and voila! - it's so much fun. I can't but praise the Bosses of the game (no, not the Dark%Weapon% guys, though they are pretty great too). Quite creative and really fun to fight. Quests & hidden things: Boy... There are bounties, "find me an item", race the Pegasus (no, seriously, are you sadists?) and couple more. Pretty fun and varying. Loved them. Difficulty is just right, btw. (Except, I think, Coliseum is a bit too long with the slimes part).Difficulty: At some points - your arse will burst in flames. But it gives you a good clean fun of that retro feel, when games didn't hand walk you through. Suffered quite a number of times and loved every minute of it :DSo, what do we have? A brilliant game that makes you want to explore and uncover each corner of the world you are put in. Challenging at times, yet quite rewarding if you understand how the things work. Quite diverse in design of everything from enemies to weapons to puzzles to playstyle. Absolute gem and a must-buy for ya'll metroidvania lovers. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This is great game with gorgeous pixel graphics. It has flaws or some issues that may hinder you somewhat but it's still a decent game. This is going to be a big post. It's a metroidvania. It has three classes with skill system. That alone makes this a game of interest for many people. I have rarely seen pixel graphics of this quality in a game. That's how much I am happy with how nice it looks. You can take any screenshot of game and tell me that it's a artwork from an artist on a social media and I would believe it. And the fact that the artstyle was solid from beginning to the end made me happy.You have a base in a city where you can upgrade, buy, sell etc. This is standard. But they did more. They have added a notice board with sidequests or basically bounty to beat unique monster. This is something you see in a rpg game but it worked extremely well in a metroidvania with big maps or area. Even npc's have sidequest. It even has beastiary with drop for monsters.Then let's talk about abilites. You have the standard dash, wall jump, sprint. This is normal. But Souldiers did it more. As you keep playing, you unlock 6 elements eventually. Monsters have elemental weakness. So there is an actual incentive to change elements while fighting. What's more is that these elements also have feature related to ablities and platforming. There is also a great attention to detail with the element usage which are always joy to notice. For example, you use water element from glacial orb on fruit, the fruit will get bigger and provide you more healing. If you use fire element, the grass will caught fire in the environment and spread. You also can't use fire element under water, using electric element will damage you etc. So the elements added a lot more abilities to use.The map size is also good but at the same time, it may feel overwhelming for some. This is not a bad thing. I love big maps to explore in metroidvania game. But even for me, I felt sometimes overwhelmed late game. This is again not a bad thing. Performance wise, I am also really happy. I had no crash at all. Only faced one bug with a dark screen. That's it. There were slight lag when saving but this never caused an issue.There are issues with changing elements during gameplay. It doesn't matter how carefully I choose, I can't consistently change elements. Luckily this game allow you to go menu to change elements. This simple thing basically ensured me to finish a certain platforming section and even certain bosses which required to use a specific element as required.The story is also decent and it also sets up for a sequel. But after finishing the game, you also realize that certain things which happen in the game is never addressed by the game as to why it happens. As I said, they hint at a sequel but the sequel won't happen in this world but in the original world that the player character arrived from. So there are things which are unanswered.Then you have consumable and other secondary weapons you can use. But here is the weird thing. Every consumable or secondary weapon you unlock, gets automatically equipped. Meaning if you wish to a variety of item, you have to scroll through all of them to find them. It should have been like equip like 3 items + 3 secondary weapons, that's it. There is no reason to scroll past 10+ secondary weapon to find the one you want to use.Now remember when I said that I like big maps and also like the request board or bounty quest? Well that created a unique problem. Since the map is so huge and the map keeps getting bigger with new area unlocked, I had no idea where the unique monster spawned in that map. And monster doesn't spawn till you accept the quest. So it's not possible to get lucky while exploring the area first time and beat the monster before accepting the sidequest. I gave up on half the quests to look for monster and googled it to know the monster location.The platforming is good. But there are some specific platforming section that just doesn't seem to work properly. Lastly, extremely disappointing final boss fight. Honestly some people might quit on the game just cause of this boss alone.All in all, I still recommend this game. It still has some of the flaws mentioned by other reviews. But at the same time, I do think this game is now at a quality where it deserves more recognition and praise.

_childDocuments_.review: Writing a review while some issues I have with this game are fresh on my mind.First off: this game is a blast. I would recommend it any day. The dungeons are fun (if a bit long). The combat is fun. The sorcerer class (only class I've played) is fun. The story is good. The characters are fun.There are some issues:1. The scrolling potion thing. It is incredibly frustrating to scroll through it to find the right potion to pop while a boss is trying to rip my head off with 5000 projectiles. A dedicated button for the healing potion or something other than the scrolling inventory thing would have been nice. I have died to boss fights multiple times because I accidentally scrolled past the healing potion and then focused too much on not skipping it the next time that I got hit again and died.2. The thing to choose your element is super inconsistent. It is a 50/50 shot that I get the element I have the marker over. The fire one likes to choose neutral instead. The water one likes to choose wind instead (the issue is by far the worst here). Super frustrating to have to take time to just try selecting the element over and over and over and over again until it finally gives it to you.3. The sprint on lava ability is also crazy inconsistent. It is maybe a 40/60 shot that it will work. Lots of the time, I'll do the dash, keep holding dash, even dash along the ground a bit, but get hit by the lava and teleported anyways.(Speaking of sprint, it would have improved the gameplay a lot if we had got sprint sooner. Maybe upgrade sprint to include the lava-walking ability in the Fire Temple while giving basic sprint early-on. I raced the flying-horse dude multiple times wondering what in the world I was doing wrong before I even considered that the sprint ability existed.)4. Wall-jumping is not consistent. There are times where I'm on a wall and spamming the jump button only to have my character just ignore it and keep sliding down the wall.Want a portion of the game where all these issues combine into one crazy-not-fun experience? The rising lava part in the Fire Temple. I died a couple times because it just wouldn't give me the water element when I needed to hit the bubble. I died at least once because the sprint on lava ability just simply didn't work. I eventually got it, but good lord that was infuriating.As far as boss fights, I think there are two bad ones so far:1. Babylon in the Pyramid. If you weren't close enough already by pure chance when he did his laser, that attack was unavoidable. Unavoidable attacks are never EVER fun. The ability he did where you had to stand between two lightning bolts was frustrating as he would change directions so quickly you didn't have time to react.2. Razor guy in the Fire Temple. The attack where he produced all the smoke was immensely cheap. You just had to wait it out while invisible attacks soared at you. You can't dodge invisible attacks. The indicator that he was in a spot was inaccurate. That fight almost made me alt+f4. That fight needs a major overhaul. It is cheap and not at all fun.Lastly, and I never thought I'd say this about a metroidvania, but the dungeons felt a bit too long. They got a bit repetitive and were a slog before the ending finally came. The dungeons themselves are good, don't get me wrong there, but they suffer from "Too much of a good thing is a bad thing." Oh, and it also made finding the bounties inside the dungeons a major pain in the rear. Maybe some more of a hint than "It's in the ultra-huge dungeon somewhere!" would help.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked up this game cause it looks great and a lot of comments talk about its challenging nature. Playing it so far, I think the biggest problem is having to override the simpler instincts you learn from other metroidvania games. Your strength in this game seems to be divided among multiple abilities that each have cooldowns - forcing you to learn how to use them in sequence in order to do any real damage. If you just spam the attack button, you'll hit like a wet noodle and enemy health bars will seem endless. Instead, you need to chain dash-special-heavy-jump-grenade combos while spamming light attack where applicable. Its the same with your defensive powers - you've got dashing, jumping, and a shield, but they've got cooldowns which prevent you from relying on only one of them. You've got to respond to the enemies' chain attacks with a dodge-block-jump combo of your own. There's definitely a learning curve here, but as long you get the hang of using all of the game's mechanics, the difficulty becomes much more manageable. -----Okay...second impression after beating the game. Of the three mechanics of primary element, secondary weapon, and equipped potion, only the primary element gets a quick wheel. Secondary Weapon and Potion you have to flip through in list form and there are just too many secondary weapons and potion types in the game to do it like that. So many times during a boss fight where I'll find myself fumbling through my potion wheel. I'd like to use the crit chance potion here for bonus damage, but now I've missed the window and will have to wait the next round...oops took some damage, now I'll need to flip through to the healing potion. Other than that, solid game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm playing as Archer on normal difficulty and having a lot of fun, but I do have some caveats.Pros: - Combat is fun. It forces you to be deliberate with your abilities. Dodge cooldown prevents i-frame spam and requires you to pay attention to enemy movesets. I like these features.  - Movement options feel good (so far have  and ) - You unlock weapon orbs that change your weapon elemental damage type. These allow you to open up new map areas. In addition, you can hot-swap them in combat to hit the weak spots of different enemies. Reminds me a bit of CrossCode in that way. - Boss fights are very fun and feel fair (I have fought 5 bosses so far). Checkpoints right at each boss is very nice and lets you learn patterns without the frustration of a run-back. Beating bosses feels very earned here. - Huge dungeons. I've been in the pyramid for nearly 4 hours. This could be a con for some people. - Very nice pixel art style. Reminiscent of older games like Sword of Mana.Cons: - This game is very punishing. You can go very long times without a save point and death means completely lost progress since your last save. You can die in 3-5 hits from a lot of enemies, and you are reliant on environmental drops and non-refilling potions for health regeneration. IMO, the devs would do good to add either more save points or at least some checkpoints at the mid portion of some long stretches. I have gone over 30 minutes without finding a save point. Dying feels very, very, very bad when exploring.  - My damage felt completely anemic in the first dungeon since the arrow cooldown is so long and the boomerang is slow with terrible range. I'm well into the pyramid now and its starting to feel better since I have more arrows and my boomerang hits 2x faster.  The melee guy seemed less finnicky to use. Not sure about the mage. - Inconsistency of shard drops and requirement of gold for upgrades and HP potions prevents me from using shard weapons. - The platforming is not great. Jumping and movement functions well enough, but some hazards can be a bit janky. Platforming sections mixed with enemies can sometimes be more frustrating than challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never took the time to write a review before, but this thing made me do it.This game is a hit and miss in so many instances it's not even funny.Gameplay is clunky when compared to the likes of Blasphemous, wall jumping is one of the worst I've experienced, ledge grab is more of a nuisance than any help, holding jump to go higher combined with the imprecise double jump can be a chore, changing items (which are plenty and useless) mid-combat is painful to the point where you'll find yourself changing items through the pause menu or selling useless support potions to make it easier to find that healing or critical boost potions in a boss fight.Combine all that with annoying flying enemies (which make up for 70 to 80% of the enemies you'll find) that are always out of your reach, putting status on you at the worst possible times in dungeons that overextend more than necessary with an overwhelming re-use of mechanics that will make you sigh and go "yep, I knew it." and get tired of so much repetition in the same section. Especially when they decide to put all of the gameplay mechanics in the same room, making you wall-jump, double-jump, air-dash, ledge-grab in the span of seconds, not to mention during some boss fights...Your dodge-roll is on a longer than it needs be cooldown while enemies roll left and right several times in a row to try and stab you in the back. It's not fun when the gameplay is clunky. It's frustrating.Plot-wise it's an OK story but some characters and their lines are so childish, they made my eyes roll twice and almost fall-off (Euder and Galath, I'm looking at you.) I get it the game has that "chibi" looks, but you can still tell a compelling story with adult characters acting as adults. Play Albert Odyssey (Sega Saturn) and take notes.If you are thinking on spending money on this, wait for a sale and do your sanity a favor and play it on normal or easy. Don't do it like me and play it on hard mode, you'll thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After putting 60 hours into the game and finishing it to 100%, my original thoughts are mostly the same. Incredible souls-like metroidvania with a huge amount of content for the genre. The developers put out a balancing update when I was nearing the end of the game in response to the criticisms of the game being too punishing, which made the game a lot easier (and less punishing) on the normal difficulty, which could be seen as a positive or negative depending on the player. Hard mode and new game+ still exists for people that want an experience more akin to the developers' original vision, but the balancing changes make it more accessible to players that enjoy metroidvanias but not punishingly difficult combat. I did encounter some bugs but these were patched out very quickly after the devs knew about them. Definitely pick this up if you like metroidvanias, souls-likes, amazing pixel art and an intriguing, expansive world to get lost in.Let me preface this by saying i'm a huge metroidvania fan and have been for a while, and have recently started getting into souls-like games due to elden ring, so I'm by no means a veteran.I've put 20 hours into the game so far, and it's telling me I'm at 40% completion, and I intend to complete the game and probably go towards 100%.Short: Absolutely stunning blend of modern metroidvania and souls-like combat, with a gorgeous pixel art style, but can be extremely challenging and punishing (I've only played on the regular 'soldier' difficulty as a caster so I can't comment on the harder or easier difficulty and as other classes yet). If you like metroidvania games and souls-like combat, this game is an absolute must-buy.- Visuals are amazing, animations are smooth and beautiful, pixel art style is second to none- Level design is very well done, especially the first spider dungeon. While the second dungeon (pyramid) did go on for hours, I felt like it never overstayed its welcome and ended just before I got tired of being there.- Combat is solid and crunchy, as souls-like combat should be, although it does take a little bit of getting used to. *can only comment on the caster class at this point*- Enemy attacks are telegraphed, while leaving room for trial and error to find the best way of taking down an enemy if the player desires.- Boss fights, unlike some souls-like games, cannot be cheesed, and enemy attack patterns must be learned and attacks need to be consistenly avoided in order to win. This added to the challenge, which I see as a pro since I sometimes find myself cheesing boss fights in souls games if the mechanics allow it, but there is simply no way to do this with most fights, so you need to adapt and learn patterns to progress.- Consumables are scarce but not punishingly so; I never found myself without enough gold to buy potions if I needed to (although I would recommend saving those valkyrie feathers for when you absolutely need them).- 20 hours in and I'm not half way through, so plenty of content, definitely one of the longest metroidvania games I've played.- 3 different classes to choose at the start of the game for replayability.- Characters and story are actually very well done, I don't play these type of games for the story, but I was pleasantly surprised.- I can't comment on console or switch versions, but the steam version on my rig runs perfectly, I've not encountered any bugs in 20 hours and the load times are quick, while not instant (between 2 and 10 seconds depending on the area, I have the game on an NVMe SSD). I appreciate many people are complaining about this, but I can only speak from my experience that the game has run really smoothly.- Unlike most souls-like games, money is not dropped upon death for you to retrieve, your save point is simply re-loaded, so you return to the save with all your money intact, but lose any items you've gained since that save. This wasn't really a problem for me, it makes the game both more challenging due to no item saving but also less challenging since you can repeat boss fights as many times as you want with no risk to your money if you lose, which led me to experimenting with quicker ways to burst down bosses than I usually would in a souls-like.- Movement takes some getting used to and, for a 2D platform game, felt very strange to me at first, with the change in momentum when you change direction. I did quickly get used to it though, and honestly it made the movement and combat feel more methodical like a typical souls-like which added to its uniqueness as a metroidvania for me.- Upgrade system isn't a game changer, and some of them are more like minor helpers rather than true upgrades.I will be updating this when I complete the game, but I wanted other people to hear my positive experience of the game so far since it's so new and there are mixed reviews. I won't be surprised if this game becomes one of my favourites I've played this year, I really am enjoying it that much after 20 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Answer:Insanely beautiful world with lots of tiny details and adorable extra animations, the team went the extra mile in that regard.  It's got well built platforming and a huge amount of content- it a few parts do drag a little.More detail:The jumping and platforming is top notch.  It gives you challenges that feel like you've overcome and learned to master the different movement methods, but none of them overstay their welcome, forcing you to get overly technical- an example of a difficult late game jump is a collectible that's way too high to reach even with normal doublejump and wall jump- so you need to get a 4th jump in by using air-dash to launch yourself back to the wall and walljump again, suddenly making it easy to get.  This level of difficulty makes you feel like you're mastering it, without making it too finnicky and troublesome like some extremely precise platformers.Its biggest faults are that some segments are slightly too long, the minimap really needed a zoom out option, and it's frustrating that you lock in to one of the game's three classes early on without having any idea what sort of skills you'll eventually unlock or playstyles they may have opened up.I personally went mage and parts of it are a bit frustrating early, but I settled into using the dodge-technique that lets you blast enemies where you dodged away from, and it feels really good to smack them with it- but the other magics are still viable too.But the little parts of the game that are beautiful and enjoyable to look at are just one of the best parts of this.  My friend was watching me play and pointed out the leafcutter ants on one of the trees, or the way your character always pulls out a map to look at where you're at- which only gets more cute when you've got the transformation to go through narrow passages, and you still pull out the map.  There are so many little things that it is just beautiful.It apparently had some difficulty issues early on, but patches smoothed that out, while still letting you take the hardest difficulty to keep it as originally released.Simply put, Amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Souldiers looks and sounds wonderful, but it's held back by mountain of bad game design. I had intended to write a more thorough explanation until I realized it's not worth my time. Cliff notes:1) Bad controls. Forced to use the thumbstick to move, no deadzones on said thumbstick, no efficient way switch sub-weapons, failing to grab walls, menus are a mix of thumbstick and dpad to navigate, bad activated skills. 2) Levels/Enemies. Poor spacing on checkpoints, frustrating enemy design, needlessly large and convoluted levels, tedious boss encounters, badly balanced numbers, lousy consumables. 3) Cutscenes. Unskippable cutscenes, dialogue boxes you can't button through, not a word worth reading in the whole game, cutscenes that replay when you die due to the checkpoint system. Maybe this studio's gameplay team to can live up to their aesthetic counterparts in their next title, but this one is a hard pass. Many of the problems here are too deeply rooted to be fixed by patches.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun, engrossing game. A lot of reviewers complained about the massive levels, but they didn't feel too large to me. That might have been a problem if the gameplay wasn't fun, but combat is engaging (sometimes tough but never unfair), the controls are mostly tight and it's overall a blast. The visuals are excellent, filled with little touches that really make the environments stand out. Neat things like how your fire element doesn't work underwater and the lighting element actually makes water damaging to the player and enemies... great attention to detail.The game is not perfect of course. I do agree that the game gives you too many tools, but not simply because they exist. It's having access to all of them, having to cycle through them all the time that's bothersome, especially the subweapons. There should have perhaps been a dedicated button for healing potions and the ability to equip a few tools on other dedicated slots, Dark Souls style.The map is fine but it could have used some improvements, like enabling marking locations and scrolling around the map on the fast travel screen. I would have also liked to be able to customize the player character. It seems like the game is filled with interesting characters but your soldier isn't one of them.Outside of that, I see no issue with the game. It's massive but not bloated, enjoyable to explore and return to the environments with new abilities and it's kept me engaged for the nearly thirty hours I've played it as of this writing. Pretty sure I'm going to finish it and probably play through a second time with a different class.I recommend it at full price, even though I got it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, from start to finish, through my multiple playthroughs, I have always had so much fun. _childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of negativity on this games review corner, so I'd like to clear some things up. It seems to me that a lot of these review are coming from people possibly coming to this as their first Metroidvania, or from rouguelikes, which I would argue is the reason for the negative reviews. This is a souls-like Metroidvania that demands a large amount of skill to play. I'll get to why I describe it as such below.  This game is very difficult. It has very tight and rewarding fights and rewards the player for exploration and combat. Their are little to no i-frames, punishment is intended, and similar to souls games, decisions in combat matter. Platforming is refreshing and exciting and entices the player to explore the world around them. Backtracking when you unlock more gear is worthwhile as it gives the players at higher difficulties the tools they need to play, and players at lower difficulties more room for error. While the balancing at times may seem unfair or extremely unbalanced, the difficulty when chosen at the beginning of the game is realistic. It's unfair of me to not knock on some clear issues the game does have. Some bugs do exist that affect console and switch players. The blocking/counter/stamina system in game currently feels useless, if not unusable against a majority of enemies, wall jumping is frustrating if not too challenging for some, and there are clearly some enemies that outperform or are over-tuned compared to others. To say this game is the hardest Metroidvania I've played would be an understatement. To say it is unrewarding, sluggish, unbalanced, or overall unpleasant would be a lie. Players that pick this up as their first metroidvania are challenging themselves. I would recommend something more along the line of Rogue Legacy 1/2 or Bloodstained if their interested in the genre, and want something less challenging. This is a very solid game that forces the player to weigh risk vs reward and focus to survive. On a very separate note, the design for this game is unquestionably amazing. Beautiful soundtracks that transition with the environment the player encounters, gorgeous lighting and effects for the characters and the world surrounding them, and a great story that does a good job of transitioning you from one adventure to the next in a very unique world.I cannot speak for Switch or console players, as it sounds to me like they are experiencing lag or other game issues. I can say that in my 30+ hours of the game, I do intend to beat it, and get as close to 100% that I can.Currently I would give this a 4/5.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend this game, even though the presentation and style (metroidvania) convinced me to buy it very quickly :- quite a few bugs (no sound, no side quest completion recognition, no achievements unlocking)- bad level design : dungeons are big but there are almost no skip, so traversal becomes tedious ; and the basic sequence for most of the time = a chest out of reach at the beginning of a platform sequence, you need to fall at the end of the sequence to get it, and then do it all again. The saving system where you have to interact twice to actually save otherwise it's just a temporary checkpoint is also very frustrating, just look at the number of messages mentionning this...- badly tuned combat : you get killed in 3-4 hits by everyone, but they have no clear tell ; you can get stunlocked very easily ; the parry system feels inconsistent - levelling up : you can only unlock a specific skill every other level, meaning you won't have an evolving gameplayit's really a shame because you can see this game has a lot of potential, but I feel they went overboard with the old school difficulty and weird saving system. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game but man is it unfair. Not hard. Not challenging, just unfair. Whats worse is its not just a balance issues. Its not just enemies hit too hard. From a core design that game has many unfun mechanics. Platforming mechanics that ask for pixel perfect jumps. Enemies that attack faster than your dodge roll recharges making it a liability rather than a tool. Enemies that fly and actually move out of your range when you jump to attack them. Enemies that at times break expectations like asking you to jump over them to avoid an attack, then immediately turn around and hit you. Also you get sub-weapons. However enemies rarely drop the resource for this. It also doesn't recharge on save like everything else. Then your sub weapons can be used to reveal secrets, discouraging you from ever using them. Then there is the issue of checkpoints not actually being saves, so unless you specifically hit save game at a dragonsword you can't quit or you lose all progress. Often it can be 30-45 minutes between swords. Also when you die *everything* is reset. So what will happen is often you will die to bad platforming then have to do the last 20 minutes over. People say this game can be saved, and maybe it can, but it will require massive changes to not only stat numbers, but enemy attack patterns, platforming puzzles and overall world placement. Have subweapon recharge on saves. There is a lot to fix here to make this game less unfair. Check back in a year and see if the game is better.

_childDocuments_.review: * I completed this game on the Steam Deck, so my actual play time is about 40 hours. I almost passed this game up based on it having mixed reviews, and I'm glad I didn't. Most of the negative reviews seem more based on the players lack of ability than the game play itself. Overall I would say a 3.5-4/5 if I had to assign a number.If you are a fan of challenging platformers/metroidvanias, this game is pretty fantastic. For its price, you are getting a pretty decently long game. It's very reminiscent of games like Mega Man where you have to be pretty accurate. I will admit there were a few challenges that this precision became a bit aggravating, but that's half the reason to play. First, the good:This game is long! I didn't grind a lot, and it took roughly 35 hours on my first play through. I think that's quite a bit of game for the price. The combat is challenging enough that you have to actually pay attention to what you are doing. It is centered around picking up elemental orbs, to which the enemies are either weak, neutral or healed by it. For the most part, you can run all the way through without using them, but they effect the game enough to be very useful. The orbs augment your attacks so that they are also needed to solve puzzles. All of the boss fights were fun and challenging as well, but none were so bad that you would have to die repeatedly to learn. The artwork and style is pretty great too. I really enjoyed most of the characters, everything is pretty flashy and crisp. There are a ton of secrets to find, and none of them are too hard to figure out. The Meh:Again, this game is big. Some of the areas ended up getting a bit tedious. Namely, the Pyramid level, which is a dual layer type of map, where you have to use "back passages" to navigate a lot of the tunnels. Most of the other areas are pretty large as well, so by the time its time to move to the next zone, you are ready for the change of scenery. Most of the secrets and power-ups don't carry a lot of weight. They don't feel particularly necessary to hunt down and find other than for the sake of map completion. The story line is borderline bad. Its not too bad, but the "big mystery" is sort of shallow/doesn't make a lot of sense when its all revealed. The skills and sub-weapons, although cool, also don't really carry a lot of weight. There is a huge selection of them, but most of them I never used more than once, just to see what they did. The Bad:A few of the challenges/timed events can be especially unforgiving. They aren't bad by design, they just leave very little wiggle room for any mistakes. I only put this in the bad section because they are a bit of a leap in difficulty from the normal demands of the game. The only other thing that really stood out to me was that there were quite a few spelling and grammar mistakes. Its not a big deal, just kind of messes with the immersion of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was put off from the "mixed scored" in Souldiers store page until I realised that most of the negative reviews come from an old version of the game that wasn't properly balanced, an issue that's resolved now on version 1.1.6. My first playthrough was on Soldier difficulty with the caster class. of Souldiers is carefully crafted with beautiful backdrops and a great attention to details that help make it feel alive.  is fantastic, each dungeon has it's own different and recognizable art style that helps them feels unique. Inside each one of them there are plenty of secret rooms, collectibles and a great amount of puzzles and platforming sections. These last ones really require you to use every mobility upgrade you got through out the game leading to hard yet fun parkour sections.  are also varied in their style and are in line with the dungeon aesthetics they are in. The bosses are fun to fight, with some exceptions of course, while still retaining a challenge, they are also feast for the eyes thanks to the great attention to details that the sprites have. are mostly solid even though they can feel a little wonky in some platforming sections. The mechanic that I really enjoyed and that brings the combat to a more active state is the different weakness and resistances of each enemies, swaping between orbs in the midst of a battle to get the upper hand is extremly satisfying and also rewarding thanks to the increased damage.. Some dungeons can feel too long, for example the second one, or also too difficult to navigate. Some bosses can be extremly difficult out of nowhere or have irritating attack paterns, when at little health some may decide to give you very small attack windows that are hard to exploit.The bugs that I run mostly into where crashes out of nowhere, varying from 10 minutes into playing to never crashing once in a day, and ones that relate to achievements, for example beating a main boss never rewarded me with an achievement. These bugs can be minor depending on your point of view, one that isn't though is the loss of save data. This bug seem to happen specifically on a save point in the second dungeon but can apparently also happen at random, even tough i'm not sure on this last one. This is where the game save data is located: "C:\Users\”your_user_name”\AppData\LocalLow\RetroForgeGames\Souldiers", I copied the entire folder and put it somewhere safe. (This next bug seems to be fixed but I'm not sure) I think this game is a hidden gem with great sprite work, satisfying combat, puzzles and platfroming sections that was unfortunatelly forgotten due to the bad difficulty in the launch days. I higly recommend this game even at full price, it took me 40h to beat it 100%, so I'm sure anyone will get their moneys worth.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't unplayable. It's just got too many bugs as of right now. Some of them are amusing, like when the camera pans a little too far in one direction to reveal the seams of the game world. Others are annoying, such as when you can no longer interact with anything in the world, including save points, or falling out of world. Even worse is when a cutscene bugs out and locks you out of a room. If you're unlucky like I was, this will make the solution to a puzzle impossible to discover without the help of a walkthrough. Game doesn't seem to be fairly well optimized either, as it make my PC chug every single time I save the game and load times are strangely long sometimes. Game has surprisingly high specs recommended for what it is. I have an easier time running Monster Hunter Rise than this game.That's basically the only reason I'm giving it a bad review. I can tell a great deal of love and care went into this game, and it seems like they really wanted to make sure to put everything they could think of into this game. Combat and platofrming is good. Exploration is fun, if a bit slow. Each area is quite large and full of dozens of treasure chests and many secrets. Some folks don't like that. I actually love that because I love this genre of game. It's just too bad it isn't optimized or polished as well as it should be by this point. My playthrough of this game is done. I can't stomach another bad bug that forces me to reset the 30 minutes to 2 hours worth of progress I made. I'm tired of being paranoid and running back to a save point every time I take a step forward. I'm tired of bugs that screw up the progression of the game. Maybe I'll come back to this game in a year or two, but that'll only happen if I see some patches come out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an excellent metroidvania. It has great combat, enemy variety, character development, and exploration. The character development in particular is outstanding. There are numerous amulets you can find throughout the game that upgrade your stats and give you special passive abilities. Things like being able to see the enemy's healthbar or seeing what element they are weak to. Speaking of elements, as you play the game, you will come across different elemental orbs. These orbs will imbue your attacks with the element and you can switch them on the fly. I had a great time using the different elements to deal the most damage to my enemies. The orbs also give defensive benefits. There are numerous bosses throughout the game and they are very fun and satisfying to fight as well. The boss fights actually remind me of megaman in the way they play out. You will need to memorize the attack patterns and dodge the attacks and find openings to attack. The boss fights are more formulaic than other metroidvania type games and the best way I can describe it is like a megaman boss fight.In conclusion, Souldiers is an excellent game worthy of your time and I'd recommend it for any side-scroller RPG fan.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun fantasy metroidvania with multiple classes and a pretty large world for this style of game. You swap between element orbs which change the flavor of your attacks and grant you different mobility powers in an intuitive and satisfying way. The locations are interesting and look great and the bosses are memorable and challenging. I really enjoyed this one... all the way up until the final boss. The final boss is a back-to-back fight where each fight has 2 phases, and you have to execute perfect double jumps to land a single hit, against a health pool that is far too large, all while dodging multiple hazards (in some cases, the hazards are simply not dodgeable, forcing you to eat the damage and waste your limited pool of potions.) It is simply poorly executed and a huge blemish on this otherwise very fun entry into the genre. Despite that, I still recommend it for the other 95% of the game, just prepare to be far more frustrated than challenged when you get to the final boss.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential it's such a shame they do so many things poorly.The game has pretty good visualsThe story isn't very interesting but I'm fine with that.Where should I begin1. Buttons and doors- In this game you push a button on the left side of the map, which opens a door on the right side of the map. Through that door is another button which opens another door on the opposite side of the map. Rinse and repeat that process and you have the core gameplay of Souldiers. It gets so bad that at one point there is a cutscene with an npc just to open a few doors. 2. Elements are rock, paper, scissors damage enhancers/reducers that do little else to improve combat. They also provide a few platforming mechanics. 3. The loot system gives items that are mostly useless. There are very few useful accessories.4. Bounty missions are given after clearing the area with no directions or waypoint to the fight room. This forces you to explore large areas a second time.5. Puzzles are not challenging or memorable and feel like a formality.6. This game gives you and abundance of mostly useless sub weapons that you have to cycle through to get to the useful ones or use the menu to swap weapons.7. Lack of multiple save slots for the same play through. This isn't objective necessary but it would be nice QoL upgrade. Until you beat the game and have to overwrite all your progress just ot test out a new game + which is even easier in the beginning.8.Conclusion:Buy this game if you want a mindless indie metroidvania. The core gameplay felt like a chore that you have to complete to get to a challenging boss fight. Until they removed the challenge in the boss fights by overtuning survivability. Now the entire game is grindy mess without a rewarding loot system. Otherwise, save your time and your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not really sure what the majority of gripes are concerning because it seems polished with cutesy graphics, really good music, lighthearted surface story with darker underlying concepts, fun enough game-play, etc.  I only share a couple of complaints...  The leveling system is pretty dumb as others have said.  The abilities you gain through leveling are seldom if ever useful compared to the moves your characters start with. Most don't even do anything to bosses.  You get 1 HP per level and 1 stat point, of which you need 3 to unlock new abilities. Understanding that, you'd think your character would be leveling up left and right, but they do not happen very often.  There's no perceived increase in power level or defensive capabilities due to killing bad guys, and the item stats are pretty irrelevant too.  Some have added effects like being able to see the enemy health and elemental weaknesses which is a big creature comfort though.  Equipment upgrades feel almost pointless.  Overall, maybe they could just ditch the leveling system cuz it feels tacked on and unnecessary.  The monsters are trivial too due to the fact that you're roughly as powerful at the beginning of the game as you'll be at the end.  It would feel unfair for them to deal or take more damage, which does bring up the next problem - difficulty levels.  That is all increasing the difficulty does - increases how much damage they deal and can take.  It turns fighting into a chore so I think this game is best experienced on the lower two difficulty settings.  Normally I have a sadistic relationship with metroidvania games that demand near perfection, but this is just not a game that plays well under those circumstances.  It's just not fun unless you're dispensing casual, swift death upon the world's baddies.  Speaking of, some of the enemies have techs like teleporting, unblockable moves, status ailments, etc. It does keep things somewhat fresh which is easy to appreciate because this game seems long with upgrade-gated progress.  Each area has its own gimmick that cooperates nicely with the upgrades you'll find there.  Backtracking is easy due to the fast-travel system, but again you'll find the beginning enemies are not much diminished when you come back later.  This may be jarring to veterans of the genre who expect your character's strength to increase meaningfully in these kinds of games.  The boss fights can be fun but are seldom challenging.  About 1/2 can be beaten 1st try with no knowledge of what's going on.  Some will like this and others won't.  The bosses look super cool and explode nicely when you beat them.  I've only experienced two glitches that I was not able to reproduce.  I didn't see any glaring typos, regional translation errors, or crashes either.  In this day and age, releasing a COMPLETED GAME is enough of an accomplishment all by itself to warrant applause.  It shouldn't be and may be the biggest complaint I have with gaming now, but it is what it is.  This game is not only finished at the time of release, but it's beautiful to watch, play, and listen to.  I can tell there's love there.  It's certainly not perfect, but this is a small dev with an ambitious project.  Those really are my only two gripes.  Otherwise, I couldn't imagine Retro Forge pulling it off much better than they did.  I really like this game and appreciate their contribution.UPDATE:  So I have gotten a little farther in the game now and have gained an increased appreciation for some things while losing faith in others.  The ding above about leveling being unimportant is still somewhat true, but later you gain some quite useful upgrades.  You also start gaining slightly more stats than just 1 HP per level. Still though, at least as a fighter, none of the special moves that use mana are useful.  Some are actually a straight up nuisance and can get you killed.  Maybe the devs could push an update that allows them to be turned off so they're not triggered accidentally.  You do get some nice passive bonuses eventually allowing you to do things like equip an additional relic and decrease the exorbitant ammo costs of some items.  So you do get stronger through leveling, but it's not much, and it's not evident at all when you're playing. Also the story is picking up now, and it's genuinely very good!  I am glad I stuck with it.  Too bad I won't be playing the game further, and I'm outside of my refund window.... cuz holy glitches!  On the deprecating side of the coin, around the 9 hour mark for me, I reached a section of the game where I collected an item.  That item stayed stuck above my character's head, rendering him invincible.  Seeing no real detriment to this, I decided to wait it out till the next savepoint and reload, but I was then trapped in a room where I was forced to kill enemies to progress and several spawned inside of the walls, trapped.  This softlocked the game as I could not kill the enemies.  I reloaded, losing 1/2 hour or so of progress.  Then after killing the next boss and progressing, another softlock.  I think the boss was supposed to die in a certain spot.  According to YT playthrough videos, this was due to a cutscene that follows, but my character was stuck, clipped through the floor on the killing blow.  I had to force-close the game b/c the freeze was during a cutscene. Another reset and more non-impacting graphical glitches later I did succeed in beating the boss and exiting the level, but I think my save is broken now.  Things do not behave properly overall and the fluidity of the game is gone.  I'm losing patience trying to figure out how to reinstall the game without losing progress, and verifying game install files did nothing yadda yadda.  Eventually I did reinstall it and complete the game.  The farther I got, the more of a glitchy, typo-ridden mess it became.  I still love it, but dang, I HATE the vine-climbing mechanic where you get 1 air-jump sometimes and 2 the next with no rhyme or reason for it.  Whoever did that... shame on you.  In games like this, glitches can really mess with your head.  it's all about exploration and you don't always know when something isn't working because you're not doing it right or if something in the level broke.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential, but I could not recommend it to anyone in it's current state.  There are some really annoying design choices, as well as some poor controls that really end up making this game a waste of time.  For bad design choices, hands down the worst offender is that there is no auto save, nor is there any way to recover exp or items if you die.  You are sent back to your last save state whenever you.  That is, except for the times that the devs decide to throw in an arbitrary checkpoint without getting healed back to full for whatever reason.  There have been quite a few times that I have found myself stuck on some checkpoint deep in a dungeon with 5 hp and no easy way to get back to a save.  Some retro gaming features are best left in the past as it adds nothing of challenge or value to the game.  It makes the player frustrated, and shows the game to be tedious.As for controls and combat, it's just not good.  Let's take counterattack.  While it's easy enough to counter an enemy attack, the game refuses to recognize the follow-up input for a counterattack strike for massive damage, and most times you are just stuck doing a standard attack instead.  The same goes for any combat skills, even simple ones like just mashing the X button to do 1000 stabs doesn't work most of the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing on Master Difficulty, liking it. The maps are well thought out and the layered design makes it way bigger than expected for a Metroid game. 14 hours in and I can see myself returning to certain spots just to completed the remaining sections of the maps as well as sidequests.Controls are not that intuitive but can be customized and does well with a bit of practice. Having to keep track of Stamina > Mana > Ammo > HP > Element is pretty fun if you enjoy souls like combat.Shortcuts for items and etc could probably be done better instead of cycling through things every single time.Not being able to swap class/weapons between dungeons and missions is quite a miss and could maybe allow new players to enjoy trial and error more even at higher levels.Story and Art is pretty amazing, even for combat which gets hectic sometimes since it's mostly about timing your dodges, parry and distance guaging.Balancing is honestly alright ever since the new mode has been introduced. _childDocuments_.review: I wish this game would just end, so that I can be done with it... Almost there...Its fun, but its annoying as hell.Off screen attacks from enemies.Flying enemies that hover just out of screen range and attack from that height.As many others have said, saving system is confusing as hell at first, with checkpoints not actually saving real progress.Weapon range is incredibly annoying, especially at first.I've attacked enemies point blank and had attacks go through them, no hit marker.I do not find money to be an issue at all, as others have mentionedA ton of variety in sub weapons, but you are only going to use 1 or 2.Inaccurate, inconsistent hitboxes.The metroidvania aspect is kid of meh. I can now go back to areas I couldn't, but the items it gives me, I have no care in the world for. How much mana do I need? Mana attacks don't even do elemental damage, so therefore, no weakness bonus. Can't rapid fire charged shots, so what is the point?How many potions, tonics, sub weapon ammo do I need? That's all I have been getting from going back. You do not need nearly as much as they give you.In super metroid, weapons made much more sense. Specific ammo and requiring different weapons to open things. Not just 1 ammo type and 100 different weapons that use it. I barely even use the sub weapons still.Level scaling feels off. Starting is the most difficult part of the game, low health, low damage, archer has pathetic range. Then 15 hours or some into the game, it feels insanely OP. Bosses are getting dropped without even much thought anymore.There are parts that are difficult, but only due to the length of them. Run path and die, run path, get further, die. Repeat until you get to the end. Seems to be a theme for this game. Outlast this fight that just keeps going and going and going and going. Filled with so much fluff to extend it. Fight 100 slimes, ok. Great! Now its hard, now its not for 2 more minutes, then make it hard again, repeat. There are parts in the game that give you no indication of what is going on with the UI. Parts where you cannot use the map for some reason. Cant pause the game for some reason. Cant use a teleporter for some reason. Cant unmorph for some reason. _childDocuments_.review: My time with the game has been enjoyable and I already feel like I've gotten my money's worth, a challenging metroidvania that has a megaman feel, beautiful art, and a decent soundtrack.TLDR: A bit rough around the edges but it's still an enjoyable experience overall!I went with mage on normal difficulty, after reading a bunch of negative reviews I wanted to see it's problems for myself (and I love the aesthetic most.) While the first dungeon was fairly rough with it's lower basic attack damage and health pool once I hit the second dungeon my damage was good enough to start two-shotting most enemies with magic/strong attacks. (I can still do so in the third as well.) Things got a lot easier once I stopped being so stingy with my mana and sub-weapons. The lower health is noticeable but once I learn how an enemy works they don't hit me very often, the difficulty feels spot on for what I chose.Movement feels great, my only complaint is ledge grabbing- you really do stick to any ledge you move near and it WILL get you hit when you're trying to dodge a group of enemies. Had no problem with wall jumping. Switching between elements is instant, if you remember what direction each element is you can fight multiple enemies with different weaknesses and exploit both or swap into an enemies' element just before getting hit to reduce the damage you take, very fun.A couple of enemies do feel more annoying than hard, some turning invulnerable in the middle of getting hit and then instantly attacking with nearly no time to react feels more unfair than challenging. Some of the bigger enemies have attacks that come out VERY fast, a lot of the time I'd be baiting out attacks rather than reacting to them, which I guess isn't necessarily bad but I definitely find reacting to attacks more fun. After reading reviews about it I expected the pyramid to be brutal and unforgiving but honestly, it wasn't bad. There were plenty of save statues and while you can't leave there's so many jars that drop money I could buy potions to max at every shop and still made a sizable profit, the amount of gold that drops in there is ridiculous. It IS pretty long though and I found myself lost on where to go next multiple times but all in all enjoyed it, the bosses were fun fights.My biggest complaint would be some traps having no sound, most traps/enemies have sounds to alert you they're near but some are completely silent, the only tell being a small shake before they go off; it's pretty easy to miss and makes reacting to them harder than it needs to be. Also, skills don't use your element for damage so you can't exploit enemy weaknesses with them, making them useless on enemies resistant to neutral damage and sub-par otherwise.. at least with the mage I've yet to find a time to use them that feels rewarding.I've run into some bugs as well, a few cutscenes have gotten "stuck" where I can move my character but the camera is focused on where the cutscene happened. I fixed it both times by walking to a nearby loading zone using the map to navigate myself so I didn't lose progress, but it is a little worrisome it happened twice.. had a moment where I took damage from spikes while being mid-air and nowhere near them, and a spot in dungeon 3 where the sound was glitching out but it fixed itself after a while. The option to skip cutscenes would be a welcome addition.With a few updates to iron things out and fix bugs this game could be one I play through multiple times!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like crack... once you go into it... you cant stop, time seems to cease to be... you forget reality, and the time as you crawl slowly through the trecherous terrain, Being a Scout (swordsman), a Archer, or a Mage... every step could be your last unless you kill a enemy for a bouncing green blob...The save is very easy to do, just go to the Banner, activate it, go to save, and use that... and your saved....I do not understand the issues people have with the game, its very well done, I hope in the future, other classes can be unleashed, maybe some cosmetic adjustments (Like letting the character be a different gender, let their hair loose from the helmet, that kind of thing).The story is simple, and you are not some sort of epic hero, just a plain soldier in a army who got pulled by Valkyries, are you dead? are you trapped? are you in a nightmare? who knows...This game is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's art and music is great and this game would've been an instant classic if it weren't for some of the game/level design decisions. The biggest and most annoying/constant issue is the fact that critical hits and elemental weakness hits cause a screen freeze on impact that can eat some of your inputs - getting used to playing through this is really annoying.      The game's difficulty, aside from the final boss segment, really isn't too hard if you have experience with 2D side-scrollers but the main difficulty comes from the level design. Areas can be really tedious to get through with the way they're laid out (Sunken Laboratory) and some of the methods to progress are really cryptic. (Floating Module/Fire Temple)     I beat this game on Master mode as Caster, which, for most of the game, is a weak combination of the other two classes [Scout (swordsman) and Archer] that's extremely dependent on the Reflection skill. (A stationary afterimage that you can detonate) This is a cooldown-heavy class that only really shines late in the game when you can utilize your elemental orbs more effectively.This is a really solid metroidvania that gets more fun as you progress but has some serious blemishes. 8/10
