_childDocuments_.review: Most of my object-level thoughts have already been articulated by other reviews, good and bad, so this is mostly high level.  I really wanted to like this game going in, and go-figure, I did, but before the recent balance patch, I had to concede that it was a niche and frustrating experience.  Other reviews (and the devs) have called it "unfair"; some reviews, interestingly, have called these criticisms "whiny"; and of course I don't think either is really it.  As with many games in this space, it, for me, amounted to confused expectations regarding the genre.  The game presents itself as a JRPG-inspired metroidvania (or even a souls-like, though I don't think that characterization fits at all), but the previous difficulty made the game much more of a precision-platformer than either of those things.  This was less the case in general dungeon crawling/exploration (where enemies were tanky, but there was still a combat-vibe to the action) than in the boss fights, where they had a bazillion health and a series of attacks that were all very difficult (and different!) to dodge, such that the dynamic was that attacking/combat was a formality, and it was really about executing the pixel-perfect platforming necessary to dodge every one of their attacks perfectly over an extended (and sloggy) period.  I'm sure this was someone's ideal game, but it's not at all how I would have designed it.The player damage buffs have gone a *long* way toward making this game sane to play as a metroidvania.  There are a number of complaints iterated in other reviews that I think are legitimate (bugs, unclear use of your bazillion ammo-based weapons), but the game is now in a state where I am both enjoying it a lot and would actually recommend it to other people.  I'm curious as to how the devs will respond to the remaining feedback here, but they have now passed the point where I feel the game is solidly worthwhile and very definitely meaty enough to be worth the price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm reviewing this game because it deserves far better than the mixed rating it currently has.This is a difficult game, and if you're not prepared for that, you will be disappointed.  This accounts for most of the negativity I have seen, but this is not a flaw with the game; it's a clear design decision, and a welcome one for me.  If you enjoy old school platformers like Castlevania and Megaman, and can handle a challenge, you will like this.The issue with the game not auto saving is a fair one to point out, though the game does very clearly explain this when you start it up.The Good:The graphics and animations are excellent, the gameplay is tight, responsive and fun, the music is great, and there is a surprising amount of content for the price point (I am 11 hours in, and nowhere near the end.. and you get 3 fully fleshed out characters to choose from)The Bad:Some (but not all) sound effects are poor, and the sound mixing seems inconsistent (like there is some limiter on the whole mix, which is based on volume.. the more stuff is playing the quieter everything is).  I have encountered one soft lock bug that happened when beating a boss, which is obviously irritating.  The writing is a mixed bag of pretty good, to pretty bad.

Even Sekiro was more forgiving in that regard and i beat Sekiro. also there's gotta be a better way to execute the the thousand stabs right? i can't tap the x button that fast with my right thumb. maybe pressing and holding x would've been a better way to execute that special. _childDocuments_.review: There's some good stuff in this game, but it's like they needed more play-testers to evaluate the balance.  There are some enemies that are straight up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  There are flying enemies that hover out of reach of your attacks (except for certain items that are hard to aim and come in a limited supply), so you have to wait until they dive-bomb you, dodge out of the way (but not too far out of the way!), get an attack in (maybe two if you're lucky), and then wait for them to come down again.  These aren't enemies you can skip, because they'll follow you.Progression is slow, and weird.  I got an amulet in the first dungeon (within the first hour of play) that gave me a nice boost to some stats.  Five hours and over half a dozen new amulets later, and it's still the best amulet I've got.  You level up in this game, but level gains give you marginal improvements (one extra hit point, one extra point of damage/stamina).  This means if you're struggling in an area, you can't simply grind through enemies to level up and make it easier on yourself, because you'll only be 1% stronger.There are items scattered around that, after collecting four of, grant you an extra ten hit points.  I found them pretty easily in the first dungeon, but haven't found any since.  Granted, maybe I'm just missing them, but it seems like they've been forgotten about to some extent after the first dungeon.Save points are inconsistent.  Save points are like bonfires in Dark Souls - you need them to heal.  Sometimes they're pointlessly close together, others they're way too far apart.  With the somewhat unforgiving difficulty (USUALLY it's fair, but not always), these gaps between save points feels cruel.There's some other weird stuff in the game that shows a lack of polish.  You can slide down ladders by pushing down + a on the gamepad, but if you push it once, then release, you can't slide down the same ladder again.  In the first major town, walking past a specific section triggers a sound effect of "town noises" (people murmuring), but it's always triggered after running past this one specific point and the volume is way louder than everything else.  Rather than make you feel like you're in a living, breathing town, it feels like you're playing a game developed by an amateur team.That's not to say there aren't good things.  The artwork is beautiful.  There is some challenging combat that demands patience.  Jumping around trying to find all the treasure chests can be fun.  Unfortunately, I think the game needs some polish.  I'll probably keep playing, but if I could get a refund for the game right now I'd probably take it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to start by stating that this game is one of those “mixed reviews” that deserve it. I started enjoying this game, but it grinded me so hard in so many aspects that I ended up just wanting it to end, and it refuses to end. When I started playing this game, I wanted to eventually play three times with the three classes in it. As I’m writing this review, I’m at the , which is not even close to the end yet (I googled) and I don’t think I’ll finish this game, but if I do find the willpower to do it, I’ll edit it later.I have seen a few other reviews mentioning this, and I will have to reinforce it. Often, the game has “too much” of something, and you’ll see me repeat this during some sections of this review. This game bloats itself so hard and when you think it has done enough, it will bloat even more.There are three classes, so your mileage may vary. I have played with the Mage for my main playthrough, but I have a few hours in the other classes. Combat in general is enjoyable for the most part, but the game is very punitive. Everything does a lot of damage, but you can manage to learn enemies patterns and move on. You get access to a few improvements and new skills along the way, some of them are very situational, some of them I ended up using a lot. I feel like a couple high level talents are very nice and should’ve been made available earlier. The game gives you access to elements as you play, and it wants you to explore vulnerabilities. The way you switch them is by using the right analog and I feel this was somewhat inspired by Wonder/Monster Boy. It is fine, but it brings me to something I disliked very much: Visual effects for elemental/critical damage. The visuals are . When you deal bonus damage based on element affinity, there is a very distinct visual and sound effect, including screen shaking, kind of like a fighting game, which goes in front of the enemy, often making their visibility diminish a LOT. I have taken damage far too often because I literally can’t see what the enemy is telegraphing and avoid properly. I ended up doing damage slower to some enemies until I memorized their patterns, which kind of sucks. Doing critical damage is even worse, the effects are way more obnoxious. The game also has secondary weapons, and there are  of them. I ended up using very few, next to nothing, and 90% of them I didn’t even test.This is what killed me. The game is a Metroidvania, but it focuses on isolated dungeons for the most part, and it feels like each dungeon was designed by a completely different person. For example, the first dungeon was the only one that I enjoyed without any complaint. Felt nice exploring it, didn’t feel too long, it was somewhat balanced for a new player with few skills. After that, it was frustration after frustration. I won’t delve into each dungeon problem as I think that would be too spoilish, but I can tell you what many other reviewers are saying and my main gripe with them: They are . They are HUGE with unintuitive paths and feel bloated just for the sake of it, not to mention that they all have unique gimmicks that, in my opinion, are flawed to some extent. They’re not difficult, they’re just tedious. Another thing I’d like to bring is side quests. A lot of them are “wanted” quests that require you to kill a certain elite mob or miniboss. However, the side quests for them are only offered after you beat the area they are in, forcing you to revisit, again, a giant huge freaking map. There are no hints  where the mobs are, so good luck finding them out. The worst part is that the rewards are not even worth it, it’s only money, amulets or secondary weapons, that for the most part, you are drowning in it already.This is the only thing that I enjoyed, really. The game is charming and pretty. It feels like a confort modern 2D game. The lore itself is alright I guess, there are nice characters, I just had a bad time with everything else that I ended up not caring for the most part. Main “bad guys” don’t seem to have nothing in common and each dungeon feels like they have their own thing, which again, makes me think each part of the game was designed by a different person that had no communication at all with the rest of the teamThis game lacks a minimap and minimap pins, with such a huge map, this is just bad. Fast travel window doesn’t let you freely move the map to look around, and looking at the map requires your character to actually pick his map in his pocket. It’s cute, but gets old fast, since you have no minimap and you have to look at it often.I wanted to like this game really bad. But I ended up not liking it as much as I wanted, but I would say, give it a try if you like a challenging metroidvania. Buy it on sale and keep track of the 2h refund window. If you don’t like it by the first two hours, just drop it, it doesn’t get any better.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a moment where I wish there was a mid-level recommendation on Steam. I'll say I'm giving it a positive here because I think the people that made it had really great intentions, and there's some really interesting stuff here, but it's a LONG feeling game. I got to nearly 90% completion in my 22 hour time as an archer, and I would recommend avoiding 100%-ing, instead going for a 60-70% target. And use the maps made by Demajen - don't be a hero in this case.The art is consistently good looking. The music is fitting and never got exhausting. The combat and mechanics aren't deep, but I enjoyed it until close to the end. And there are some neat Metroidvania ideas here - there's very clearly a love of Metroidvanias on display all through this game that tells me this team wanted to hit the mark.The issue is just the length of everything. There's about 6 dungeons, and most of them took 2 hours to complete. It was the second dungeon that I realized I'd been working through it for two hours and for no real reason did it need to be designed so sprawling and multi-legged. And then it happened again, almost worse, in the third dungeon. And then again in the 4th and the 5th. The final dungeon is probably the shortest, but I was also trying to speed through. They all have this structure of having to find one too many keys to unlock a door - if the amount had been halved and the design shrunk a bit, I honestly think this could have been a solid B+, A- Metroidvania. It's just so padded that it makes it very exhausting.Also, way too hard to know how hard a boss is going to hit and too frustratingly easy to get stun-locked into more damage.Definitely get it in a sale or bundle and definitely don't try to grind through it - take your time and come back to it in chunks if needed. And if, by the end of the sand dungeon, you feel exhausted, let it collect dust in your library and be free.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely beautiful art style with stellar music. If you're an old Legend of Mana (Or most Mana games), then you'll appreciate this style.The game itself is fun, with a pretty interesting story.Now, while there are 3 difficulty choices to choose from, I really feel like the 'normal' difficulty is a bit too hard. The game is usually forgiving when you die, but it can definitely wear on your quickly. There's a few bosses I've gone through so far, and one specifically has really bad hit ranges that will irritate the ♥♥♥♥ out of you.However, nearly every boss follows attack patterns. So as you keep dying to them, you learn their patterns and there's always a way to get around it. If you've played games like Hollow Knight, then you should feel at home with this playstyle.The game can be considered a 'souls-like' if you're talking about the checkpoint system. When you die, you respawn back at the last 'dragon sword' you rested at. And when you save your game at a dragon sword, it gives you all your mana, stamina (So far only used for blocking), and health back. And this is strange, but only SOME enemies come back when you rest. It really doesn't follow a pattern on what enemies come back to life.With that said, the game is very enjoyable and cute, but can definitely try your patience. You start to feel like maybe you should be grinding levels, but you're where you're supposed to be when you're supposed to be there. The game is just naturally difficult. So if you're looking for a more casual 'Mana-series' feel, maybe play on the easier difficulty. You CAN change difficulty at any time, with only the risk of losing access to some achievements.There are 'side quests,' or I should call them side objectives. There's a 'bounty board' system, where you accept a bounty to go hunt a dangerous enemy somewhere in the world, and will get quite a good payout from it.In terms of progression, there's a ton. You can upgrade your tools (Things like bombs or throwing knives), your weapons, your protection (Offhanded shield for scout, arcane bubble for mage, etc), health, stamina, mana, and you get levels with a full-fledged class tree depending on the class you chose. And a lot of these progressions seem to differ depending on the class you chose.Lastly, there are effectively 3 classes to choose from in the beginning, and they all play differently. I've watched someone play the Knight-type class (Sword and board) a ton, and I personally play the mage.-The knight (called Scout) class is obviously melee, with an emphasis on personal defense.-The Mage class has homing projectiles, which makes it easier to hit enemies above or below you, and can cheese some enemies outright. However, it seems like your range gets shorter if the enemy is horizontal to you. There's especially one boss fight where your range as a mage is exactly that of the boss's hit range, and it becomes frustrating trying to balance the difference.-The Archer. While I haven't seen this one played much, nor played it myself, it definitely seems like this one might be the best to choose at the start. The classes may scale differently, but this one seems to have the best horizontal range, which is going to be 95% of your fights.That should give you a good idea of the type of game this is. I personally love it, and think that if the art style is attractive to you, you should definitely give it a try. The music is just amazing.

The patch solved issues that were present with bugs, not just a quality of life community update, so not downloading to the most recent version would leave some of those issues in. Again the game is wonderful and I would highly recommend it both before and after the patch.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I had real fun with this game, it was interesting and I enjoyed testing out the three playstyles (Scout, Archer, Caster) before I locked in my choice (Caster) to play the entire game with. The enemies were interesting, the graphics were good ol' retro, and the platforming was a bit floaty but still enjoyable.Then I reached midway through the first dungeon, and that's when the cracks first started to form. The game difficulty (at Scout) was never truly hard, but there were plenty of issues that started popping up that just started to create a gestalt of inconveniences which made it hard that had nothing to do with skill.-Bloated level designs. The dungeons always wear out their welcome well before they're done. You could easily cut out 1/3 to 1/2 of each area and nothing of value would be lost.-Pointless upgrades. The skill trees for the classes seem superfluous at best, especially since the actually useful skills aren't available till you hit levels 15-20. Before then, they're just sort of there, and you have no way of planning a basic build because it's all hidden.-Instant 'death' areas. I've always hated these parts of platformers, and Souldiers ranks up with the worst of them. The Fire Temple is so much more frustrating then it needs to be with all the times you'll die because you stepped somewhere you shouldn't, not helped along by enemies that will block your way or rebound you into lava because of bad timing.-Enemy hordes. Unlike other metroidvanias, you HAVE to kill enemies because they will chase you far beyond what their expected haunts should be. It doesn't help when a dozen can appear on screen at once because of poor level design/spawn points (once again, Fire Temple, I'm looking at you).-Weak sub-weapons. I actually liked the idea of sub-weapons like from Castlevania (bombs, spears, poison knives, etc), but the ones in this game not only are more or less worthless for combat, dealing a fraction of what your basic or specialty attacks could do, but the way they're upgraded is... frustrating, to put it lightly. Just not worth it.All in all, I tried really hard to enjoy Souldiers, but even with the endgame in sight, I simply stopped caring because it felt more like a slog than a way to relax. I'm not mad, Souldiers, just deeply disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this is a pretty long MV, and I don't personally think that's a problem because I do like density, and it really does extrapolate on some really interesting concepts and incorporates ones I've never seen in other offerings of this genre. The game is really toothy when it comes to the combat mechanics. I mean it feels really damn good, and it's an area where these folks really delivered - the combat encourages you to actualize some degree of mastery or at least familiarity with the skill and spell behavior to employ it in combat situations because the combat is very snappy. Like nearly fighter game levels of emphasis on this front. However, there's an eventual point with the power scaling that you will begin to overwhelm the enemies with your raw stats. So my opinion on that is, that needs balancing because some spells are overwhelmingly powerful if used optimally but I'm not sure how to do that with the presented paradigm of power growth here. Enemies power is static so what it lends itself to is that some enemies might as well be not there at a certain point. If this is their first rodeo with an MV, like this hits on all the important notes - but yes it does have shortcomings. I didn't expect the world, and obviously I didn't get it, but honestly I was pleasantly surprised with what I got.It's really hard to offer a encapsulating opinion of Souldiers other than the very generic and binary 'Play it" or "Stay away." At the time of writing this I have around 160 hours played, so it is a good game. I am the opinion of if you're into that 32bit SNES type of side scrolling, parallax using, artistic adventure with a fairly safe yet decent story and great combat and very lengthy dungeons, yeah - this is both fun and a lot of value for it's price. But it's sort of one of those games that I would submit that when it was over, I was left wishing there was more.. even after acquiring all the side quest items and that's really hard to articulate why without spoiling things - but I did bother to play through all three classes and unlock quite a bit of content. I wish the Dev hours they were slotted to porting this were instead sunk at least a little bit more into some extrapolation of the game because they have a pretty decent foundation with this IP and it deserves more. I honestly look forward to them capturing this world and making a successor of some kind. There's a lot of room here for that.I'm conflicted with Souldiers when discussing the overall 'finish' of the game if you will, but I would say it's absolutely worth the price tag and if you're looking for something different while you're waiting for new installations like Altered Alma or Silksong, and have completed Blasphemous 2, you could do a lot worse. It's fun, it's a little janky at times, this strikes me as a development studio of maybe 10 to 15 people, and it's in this old gamer's opinion a pretty damn good first shot at a MV.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not gonna go into huge detail cause this is an old game and there's a ton of reviews here and on other platforms, but I actually really enjoyed this game after bouncing off of it a few times.I think it suffers from something that a lot of metroidvania games kinda suffer from and then further exacerbates it with the class choice - the game doesn't really start to feel fluid until well into the game (mostly due to how big the first two dungeons are, so you spend a lot of time at a very basic level of mobility). When you add the fact that you may not jive with your class and your class's spells and skills, it creates a lot of ways for the game to sort of make you not want to play. I think a lot of this could've maybe been fixed with an opening section (potentially still in Zarga prior to being sent to Terragaya) where you get to play each class with a few of the mobility options and special spells unlocked so that you can really get a feel for how the game is going to progress before being locked into a class choice. That said, I did a run on the "normal" difficulty of the Scout just to give the game an honest shot on a very straightforward character and ended up getting through the whole game and really enjoying myself (especially after unlocking the air dash). There's a lot of interesting puzzles and cleverly hidden secret rooms, and some of the movement that the game clearly expects you to do is very different than most metroidvanias while still doing a pretty good job of showing you how to use your movement in low risk scenarios. I actually ended up having so much fun that I did another (100%) run on the third difficulty with a Caster.Also, while the story wasn't amazing (some of the writing kinda made me think that English is not these devs first language), it was a fun little twist on the idea of Valhalla and Ragnarok that didn't take itself overly seriously. The art is really nice and it gave the side characters a lot of personality, and I enjoyed that each dungeon has you working with different NPCs (both humans and other beings on Terragaya that you run into) in a way that generally made sense. As far as combat, that was definitely the thing I struggled the most with - some of the fights were really fun and interesting (and felt different on different classes) but some of the fights (Dark Razor and Agginox most noticeably to me) were just the unfortunate dual combo of not very fun and not very forgiving. The "true" final boss also felt kinda strange on my first run as Scout, but when I got there as Caster I realized that two of the three available classes are ranged and both phases felt a lot easier on Caster so I imagine it's just a scenario where Scout felt a little less favorable (but Scout also absolutely demolishes some of the early bosses that Caster struggled a bit more with so it at least felt kind of fair).Overall, if you already really enjoy Metroidvanias and aren't afraid to spend some time learning a new game, I felt like this game was really interesting and worth my time. I'm actually probably going to get all the achievements (I'm pretty close after my two runs anyway), and while it took a few tries to really get into it I really enjoyed it once I got going. Highly advise if you're going to give it a shot to play until you get to the third dungeon if you enjoy the combat, because while the platforming and movement is a little flat early on, the air dash in the third dungeon opens up some interesting puzzles and movement and makes traversal quite a bit faster so it starts to pick up around there.

_childDocuments_.review: Patch Update: Folks! They did it! I have now experienced the updated version with all three classes, and it is a resounding SUCCESS. I am completely satisfied with all of the adjustments, and they make for me what is an objectively superior game. The tweaks to the defensive mechanics in particular really make the game click. You can dash, jump, and parry, but you still have to do so with care because a premature dodge will result in a world of pain. But now, unlike before, it actually feels fair, and your suffering more a result of your own mistakes rather than the game just being arbitrarily hamstrung.I put extra time into Archer and Caster, both of which I thought were atrocious at first. They now both feel much better, especially the Archer. Still can't get the "Skirmish" to trigger, but it functions as another form of dodge in a pinch, so it honestly works just fine as is. They increased the damage on the boomerang dramatically, actually making it a practical consideration in fights. The whole class has a groove to it now that I was really enjoying.The Caster too feels better to me, though I think that comes more from enemies not being such sponges anymore. The Caster feels like its basic rhythm is similar to how it was pre-patch, but with the slight tweaks to other areas, it fits much better. Oh, and the fact it starts with the same health as Scout is sublime. Best change by far.Souldiers devs, a personal note to you: You should be proud. Taking that kind of negative feedback on the chin could not have been easy. But not only did you roll with the punches, you turned them into energy that fueled a remarkable fix. Let it never be said that I won't admit when I was wrong. You all have done great work here. Now I feel the game is where it was always meant to be.TL;DR - The patch is everything you could have wanted. Now is the time to experience this great game!

_childDocuments_.review: - Beaten the game in full on Normal difficulty on Caster, working on getting 100% collectables before proceeding to Game+ Mode- Played Archer to about 40~%, Scout to 10% on Normal difficulty.- Planning to Platinum the game at some point.- Really enjoys the Fromsoftware series, having played Bloodborne, Dark Souls II/III and Elden Ring.- Plays FFXIV and really enjoys the endgame content, from extreme / savage / ultimate fights. - 1st Metroidvania game in a very, very long time.I think my context is important, because it does affect how I perceive and approach challenging content. I don't consider myself a -super- hardcore thrill seeker, but I do enjoy challenging myself in my own personal way! I find progressing through a tough boss bit by bit really rewarding for example- it's thrilling and satisfying knowing I'm learning and inching towards a goal. I also tend to resist calling things "cheap" or "unfair", and think more about how I can change or adapt to overcome the odds because when you do it's feels really great to have succeeded against them!But with that out of the way, here's what I have to say about Souldiers:Souldiers from the get go is a gorgeous game, full of beautiful pixel art. From the expressive, lovely character sprites, to the awe-inspiring vistas- there is an immense amount of passion and dedication put into the visuals. It really speaks volumes that the art being really good is practically unanimous across the board despite its currently mixed reviews. Very little argument there.The music evokes a really nostalgic, really fantastical SNES era feel. Every area has a very specific mood set, from the triumphant, adventurer swell of Tempes Plains after emerging from the Spider Lair, to the cooler, chiller mood of Hafin Sewers or the serenity and ancientness of Fyr Forest. Overall a great memorable soundtrack.As a pair, they really complement each other really well. It's great.Gameplay wise, it's an interesting challenge. You really need to take advantage of all the tools available to you, as well as your classes' inherent strengths to succeed well which I love.Every enemy has a different rhythm you can learn and take advantage of, and I think Souldiers is always trying to make you approach them in different ways every encounter. You can never be too comfortable with one approach or strategy all the time, and I found that quite engaging.Exploration wise, I loved the tension of a long gauntlet / stretch of a dungeon, not knowing when the next save point was coming when I was running low on resources- the triumph and reward I felt when I survived on my last legs upon discovering a new save point. During my 1st play through in particular I really appreciated the genuine deep dungeon thrill of these segments.I can't stress how dense some of the areas are as well. There is a lot to discover and explore to keep you busy, wondering where every nook and cranny are, every piece of treasure. Realising every new ability gives you a reason to revisit the old areas to find new possibilities. There's so much to discover in this beautifully vast world.The variety the classes offered was also really interesting! Having finished the game as Caster then going to try out Archer and Scout, I liked how each class made me approach the game differently. What were simple situations on Caster were very different when I played on Scout because of it's limited close range- or even Archer because of how arrows are shot statically VS Caster's homing light attacks to reach certain enemies. Learning to master these three classes over time, slowly unlocking different abilities and seeing how they evolve over the course of my playthrough was so fun.Overall, Souldiers was a rich gameplay experience for me.I do really enjoy this game, but I am aware of its objective flaws.There are definitely a handful of bugs here and there that have caused varying amounts of gameplay disruption that should 100% be ironed out. Things like: - Some cutscenes locking up the game or halting progress forcing a quit. - Proceeding through some parts of the game in a way you aren't supposed to and causing some errors in achievements or locking up at the credits.- Some items not working as intended, such as the accessory that detects nearby treasure.- A lot of console optimisation problems, particularly load times and lag in some graphically intense areas and controls.- Some saves getting locked up. Having played this on Steam, I feel like I ended up avoiding a lot of the more egregious problems like long load times and laggy controls, but I did end up experiencing some of these (thankfully nothing that completely broke my saves).It's so unfortunate. Obviously these problems produce hugely negative feedback- which is totally understandable but it's really such a shame considering the actual core game itself has been said to be really full of potential and promise- even from the negative reviews.The devs are doing their best to come out with a patch this June 23rd to alleviate some of these issues, and it shows again their passion and dedication to this game they've made. I almost wished they had stuck to a Steam only release first, then taken some extra time to release to other consoles later but... perhaps this is an unfortunate lesson learned for the future.There's probably more I could have written on, but this might be getting a bit lengthy as is.I want to see more from these developers! I want them to continue making games as gorgeous as this, and as engaging. Their first step wasn't perfect and there's still a lot of work to be done, but I think they still gave us something wonderful at it's core.I for one, love this charming little game they've made, and I hope despite some of it's technical flaws you give the world of Terragaya a visit and let yourself get immersed into this journey full of wonder, challenge and adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings for this one. Although I am more leaning to the "I recommend this game" side of things.So first and foremost, the game is great. If you like metroidvania games that involves alot of back-and-forth, revisiting like Hollow Knight, Aeterna Noctis or the older ones like Megaman ZX, Castlevania Symphony or Metroid. Then this game is for you.Actually I really like the game, from puzzles, presentation and combat difficulty. Furthermore for its price, the game is pretty huge too which is a good thing.It falls short on the quality of life stuff. For example, as a mage, you tend to rely on alot on spells but mana is a big problem. When you're out of combat, you tend to have to stop and catch up with your mana bar a bit (even if you got the regen + mana capacity upgrade) before you get into the next action. The monsters do drop mana points but its far too few. Sure there are mana potions but you tend to save them for the bosses and recklessly using them costs gold which you have to grind eitherway.Another one is no minimap option. So I have to always press select/map button from time to time just to keep track where I am and where I want to go and also potential not missing on secrets and doors (because certain doors do look like the background so you will miss it unless you happen to open the map at that moment or always trying to press the interact button here or there.Lastly some polishing improvements are still needed, even despite the balancing patch and bug fixes, I have experience a couple of bugs where I got stuck on a puzzle because I did it incorrectly and I had to restart the game for it to go back to its initial placements. For example in the spider lair square block puzzle (the one where the room is below Dark lance's area), as I drop the square block on the empty weight, changing the weight's position. I fell down and I cant go back up, because the weight is now in a place where I cant reach it to go back up. So I had to restart the game and redid the part which was kinda of a bummer since I waste a couple of minutes figuring out where I went wrong.Regardless of these issues mention the game is still great and the devs are listening to the issues raised anyways so yeah definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am loving this game!  The pixel art is amazing, the music is varied and unique, and it's challenging.  I'm writing this review as a response to the update that the devs posted today (6/8/22) regarding the game being unfair and trying to balance the difficulty to a point that they are saying that there will be a "new version" of the game.  PLEASE DO NOT NERF THIS GAME.  I think that I'm about halfway or more through the story and it's been a blast.  I don't want this game to turn into a walk through the park.  I'll admit that having zero I-frames after getting hit can cause you to die from two or three enemies hitting you at the same time but that's only happened once or twice in my 50-60 hours of playing the game. I've been way more frustrated with the final areas of Elden Ring where you can die in a single hit from the bosses and even some standard enemies.  I'll also admit that getting paralyzed or confused can be extremely annoying in areas with lots of environmental hazards, but that's always just been a reminder that I need to stop trying to rush through and be more methodical. Which brings to mind that it would be really nice to equip and unequip the secondary weapons.  The list gets pretty long and it takes a long time to scroll through to the one that you want to use which is not helpful when you're in a pinch.  My only other complaint was with a certain boss in certain dessert area that involved hitting crystals in a really specific timing that caused me to attempt it around ten times or more to figure out the pattern but you re-spawn immediately at the boss battle, so multiple attempts are never that much of an issue.I am so happy that this game exists and I really enjoy that I don't feel like I'm just crushing through every single enemy that I encounter.  I'm really afraid that it will be balanced to a point where every enemy dies in one or two hits which would make all of the charge attack mechanics meaningless.  I also hope that an infinite use dodge roll is not implemented.  I trust the devs to fix issues and improve the game, but it worries me when they talk about re-balancing it.  The game was released this way because that was the devs vision of how the game was meant to be.  I just hope that it doesn't go too far.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished a playthrough on Normal (Soldier) with the Archer class and felt inclined to write my personal spoilerfree review.All in all, I was really impressed with the movement options that made battles and exploration dynamic and fun. Although you unlock these as you progress through the game, this gives you ample time to get used to the new mechanics and how it evolves the way you've been playing so far. Besides the movement, your huge arsenal of weapon arts and sub weapons also increase, although it could end up becoming confusing. The battle difficulty was also very pleasant as I was rarely in real danger which was made doubled true with the many save points and checkpoints. Maybe it was due to the Archer class but the crit vials made me kill many bosses without really seeing their full attack roster. The animations and sprites were gorgeous to look at. The music fit the occasions and I was never annoyed.I've been playing with keyboard so I had buttons to switch sub weapons, elementals, usables and also a dedicated button to execute weapon arts. With the huge selection of sub weapons that all fulfill a certain use case, I had to select specific ones that would cover my weakness as a ranged character. But this doesn't solve the fact that I need to cycle through 20 sub weapons to use the 4~5 sub weapons that i needed. My primary playstyle during boss fights was to stall time in order to switch to appropriate sub weapons or element. Once unlocked, the sub weapon will stay (stain) your inventory forever.In concern to money, I never had any problems. I finished the game with more than $100000 and never actually found a use for the money. To be honest, I also sold any healing items because it made switching between the crit vial and the status recovery potion a real chore. I was so sure that I would get into financial problems sooner or later but the weapon and subweapon upgrades were very very cheap and the numerous bounty rewards were plentiful. I also kind of hoped for an achievement for having a lot of money but it never appeared so I am sure there isnt one.I encountered some very uncanny transitions in the sections after the third dungeon. Characters would randomly teleport before/after cutscenes, plot is moving at lightning speed, graphical bugs would happen. It's like this section wasn't playtested.The races with Euder could be attempted rather early into the game and the players are baited to think that they could win with skill but it's clearly gatekept by having all movement upgrades. I just wished it would give a notice for the players to attempt it at a later time.The maps didn't give enough indications for missing chests which is a real bummer because the hidden walls are not explicitly marked even after having played through the game.The game plot felt like the devs thought of a cool premise for their metroidvania game but forgot to think of a good conclusion to their plot so they added it literally right infront of the final boss door. I don't mind too much but it take away the game experience.The map sizes of dungeons didn't match the overall game progress. The shortest one was definitely the last dungeon before the final boss. The longest one? The second dungeon in the desert. It was unnecessarily long with two separate but connecting maps with many doors connecting them. Especially for backtracking and treasure hunting it proved to be a real chore. I don't recommend doing that dungeon in several sittings as it basically requires the players to remember the pathways and which doors connect to what.Some later platforming sections were not tested enough. Especially the dungeon before the last dungeon had incredibly tight platforming requirements that i began to suspect it had to be solved in another way. Also the character movement options were tested to muscle memory by the developers so newer players would never think about using the mid-air dash to execute a second walljump for additional height. It is easy to get stuck in certain platforming sections that requires players to perform these high-level movement tricks, especially beginners to platforming in general.Although my points had some bad things, I enjoyed my time with the game. I am now playing the game on Hard (Warrior) difficulty with a different class to see how balanced the game is in concern to other classes. I bought the game on sale and so should you. I didn't encounter any game breaking bugs, just graphical bugs where textures didn't load it properly or when a button was disabled for no reason. The developers seem to push some updates lately and they are keen to make it right for both the casual audience and also hardcore fans who want challenge and honor.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wasted potential. It has okay ideas. If they came together, it would be a pretty good Metroidvania that could be recommended if you were a fan of the genre. Instead, what you get is a game that reuses it's assets to pad it's length for no reason other than to be as long as possible. The first major dungeon is a Pyramid. Most of my playtime on my account is in this pyramid. It's a massive map, that reuses the exact same ideas for hours. Every time you think you are finished, it just keeps going. The amount of trash mobs and bosses you have to fight is enough to want to make your character rest in that tomb forever. And your reward for finally getitng out of the pyramid after the massive 5 hour slog is another boring boss fight. Reading this reviews, it seems every major area is like this, so I'm calling it quits. If enemies had 1/4th the health, and everything was 1/4th the length, this could have been a good game, but instead, I can only recommend if you are looking to play this to scratch a metroidvania itch, go play something else and don't waste your time. (Because this game absolutely loves wasting your time.)

_childDocuments_.review: I just played half way through the second major dungeon. The game definitely demands that you learn how to juggle dodging and blocking (playing as warrior) and it definitely feels like the bosses were designed without the dodge cooldown in place, but I still haven't hit this mythical difficulty wall.People who are complaining aren't using every tool at their disposal. If you are near death, you can turn the game into super meat boy and just gun it to the next checkpoint. If a tanky enemy is giving you trouble, you can chuck bombs at it until it goes down. it costs like 30 gold to refill bombs at the shop, and There's shops like every 10 feet. If you really need full potions for a hard section, you can just buy them. If you die before a checkpoint, you get all your potions back.I think the difficulty is comparable to Hollow knight. I'm getting push back, but not in a way that detracts from the experience, so far

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to like this game. For a large part, I did, but often just baffling design blunders completely ruin the experience. First off, the game is unarguably gorgeous, the art design is off the charts. Some of the backgrounds are best in class, and the character designs are great as well. The music is fun and really hearkens back to earlier days of gaming in a way that's nostalgic but also fresh. Very good. But as soon as you get into combat you'll notice it feels a little bit off, I can't quite put my finger on it but it's just not snappy the way good side scrolling metroidvania-ish/whatever games are. All the right pieces are there, dodging, blocking, parrying, etc, but it never comes together in a way that makes combat feel smooth and effortless like in other games. There's several secondary weapons but they all felt mostly useless, except for the bombs to blow up secret walls. They either did piddling damage or required too much ammo, which wasn't easy to find.Maybe this is just a personal preference thing but the levels are HUGE, way too huge imo. I don't mind complex dungeons but this was a little excessive.In any case, there's enough here to like if you can get past the bad stuff. Unfortunately, I couldn't.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty good, but not great by any means. The art and music are beautiful, the story is interesting, and the levels are large, interesting, and full of fun platforming. As the game progresses, though, it relies more and more on the worst boss fights I've seen in a while. I will add the caveat that I know many people love boss fights in games, but they are the worst part of all of video games to me. I see this fun world that I am platforming and fighting through, and then all of the sudden you are locked in a tiny room, with none of the scenery or music, and you have to just engage in these long boring fights (often several times) before you can get back to actually playing the game or experiencing the story. It's the worst. There should really be a feature in games where you can just turn that off. For the first few levels these are pretty spaced out and balanced, some of them are even fun (there's a scorpion I rather like). Then I got to the floating city. Midway through the puzzle/keys section of the game, you have a fight. The second half of the puzzle is very quick, followed by another fight, followed by a long cut scene that forces you to go to a new area, which leads you to not just one, but TWO boss fights back to back, neither of which I enjoyed. Which leads to ANOTHER long cinematic that takes you to another place, and it seems like the game will finally restart. However in my case, what happened was the game crashed. No worries, I thought, surely there was a save of some kind after all that nonsense. Nope. When I reloaded, it was back before the really obnoxious double-boss. So, anyway, I'm done with this game now. But I got several hours of enjoyment out of it, and enjoyed what the game could have been, and the story, and the jumping and bouncing off walls and whatnot. For those who really like all the boss fights, this would be dope. I just have too many other demands on my time, and too few gaming hours, to waste any more of them on the same loop.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended.  6/10.  I think its a shame this game has mixed reviews because I think its quite a bit better than that rating suggests.  They were ambitious when making this game with all the ideas and scale of the map.  Some of the boss fights were a great experience as well.  This game takes ideas from a lot of games and executes on most of them pretty well.  The reason for the score is probably the same as most peoples...this game overstays its welcome.  It could probably be cut in half in terms of zone sizes and be a better game for it.  You always feel like you're on the brink of getting completely lost and turned around and yet I was able to keep pushing forwards with almost no frustration. The combat is only  a game with this much combat this is another thing keeping the experience down.  I ultimately dropped difficulty to easy and really enjoyed just having a chill time going through the game.   To think there are two other classes to try if I ever feel the urge.  Good game.  At times a very good game.  Ideally played on easy while listening to podcasts and the like.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the unfair reviews and average currently being set to "mixed", the game is a piece of art and not many other metroidvania-like games can even compare. So, for the huge fans of the genre, go for it and try it for yourself (while supporting indie devs).However, the game can be unnecessarily frustrating at times, some of it was addressed by the major update, but still, wall jumping sometimes requires too much to get to the right spot, (I think some places might actually have bugs that stops you from naturally jumping on them), subweapons are useless most of the time, the dungeons were a bit too big and confusing (the real challenge was to understand the correct path, no any puzzle mechanic or fighting a tough enemy), quest rewards didn't really worth doing for any other reason besides the story, etc...Overall, its an awesome game if you focus on everything else that is has to offer! I'm sure the devs will make an even better job next time with what they learned from this one. Keep it up!

_childDocuments_.review: Really big metroidvania that really needed an editor to cut content.  It's also too heavy on the platforming for me.Level design is confusing, and exploration is not very rewarding.  I had to look up where to go next in half of the dungeons, and most chests just contain junk.  Even if it's a new weapon or accessory, it's probably junk.  The only 2 things worth finding are health and damage upgrades, and those are pretty rare.Cutscenes are unskippable and placed right after checkpoints.  I'm putting the game down after trying a required 3 minute platforming section and failing a bunch of times, where failure puts you back right before the 10 second cutscene.The platforming feels bad; the wall jump feels finicky and the air dash is on a timer instead of refreshing when you hit the ground.  The sprint button is tied to the roll button, when it really should have been a dedicated button.Every metroidvania has backtracking, but in this one you'll often be expected to backtrack a bit within every room.  Flip a switch to swap which door is open for a puzzle? you're going to have to flip is back when the puzzle is solved so you can leave.  They could have easily had the solution open all of the doors and saved everyone some time.Combat was okay to sometimes fun.  Bosses are pretty swingy, in that some are trivial and some are really hard, but you can probably just chug potions through their damage, not learn anything about the fight, and move on.  Enemy placement during platforming sections was pretty annoying, sometimes requiring you to wait things out or kill the enemy and start over.

_childDocuments_.review: Would absolutely recommend the game, artstyle, gamefeel and setting are great, progress can feel a bit slow when it comes to levelling early game, it's very much a metroidvania so exploration is key to character improvement. This is a lesson I had to learn.Expect some frustration with progress loss as it can be some time between save statues and checkpoints, also don't forget that you have to manually save at statues as this doesn't happen automatically on first activationThe game definitely could definitely do with a patch or two but I still recommend getting this if it looks like your kind of game

_childDocuments_.review: The game can have a steep learning curve depending on what class you select at the start, but it's an excellent Metroidvania. The RPG elements are delightful, the animations are well done, and the story is interesting. Combat is well managed, though there are times that the dash/dodge cooldown gets in the way, but that's not a huge problem. Controls are tight and responsive, discovering secret areas is as enjoyable in any metroidvania, and the game is charmingly adorable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if the game had a massive shift in difficulty or what but I've been playing on the warrior difficulty as the mage and have been having a great time. _childDocuments_.review: I have over 20 hours into this game and about halfway through.  Unlike some of the more unluckier folks I didn't encounter my first softlock until the 3rd "dungeon" and it was only a few minutes after a recent save so I lost minimal progress.That being said.  Prepare to be frustrated if you play as any class other than the Scout.  The other two simply do not have the damage to make things anything better than a slog.  Even as a Scout, you will quickly discover that your dodge timer is always too long to matter in clutch circumstances and nothing short of memorizing attack patterns will allow you to survive.Right around dungeon 4 you will then start encountering enemies that get super armor during their attacks...even with an advantageous element, you will plink away at them for days before they go down unless you wait for them to finish their unblockable move.  No, not bosses...regular rank-and-file enemies.And that perhaps is the most frustrating part of this game.  The waiting.  Can't skip cutscenes even it you've seen them before but died before the next save point.  Waiting for platforms, traps to finish, enemies to stop rushing around the screen.  I can understand a little punishment if you try going in all "Leeroy Jenkins", but the sometimes you just get ambushed from out of nowhere and get insta-gibbed.While the pixel art is beautiful and the music is actually quite good, I really cannot recommend this game even on sale until the Developers fix the softlocks and do something about the other classes.  Like others have said, this game was clearly not thoroughly tested before release.  Wait to purchase until the ENTIRE game is playable.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm trying to keep this short and informative, even though I could spend hours writing about this game. Souldiers is an 2D metroidvania with challenging combat and a lot to discover. Hell, I'm on my second play through and I didn't get everything on my first even with 100% map. Now would I recommend it?  Why are there so many negative reviews? Well I'll try to explain. When the game released it was brutally hard at points, at least on some characters. Also, it had some bugs (And some players say that it still does, but I only encountered one that made it impossible to complete one side quest). I just started my second play through few days ago on "middle" difficulty, and been breezing through the game. When the game launched I also started on that difficulty, and quickly turned it to easy. Now that's partly because of the patches that balanced the game, and also partly because I understand the game better.  First time I played as archer and pretty much only used dodge, now I play as mage and use both. Just using one or another will make your game insanely difficult, although it's still possible to beat it. Sure you might die a million times but I did it. But it's not designed to played that way.Overall I'd say the game is pretty much perfect. It has awesome music and graphics, the gameplay is tight, the challenge is there but if you feel like it, you can always drop the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: Very surprised to see so many negative reviews. This is a genuinely solid game, and I can easily recommend it to fans of metroidvanias or hack-and-slash action games.The devs have built a living world. It's beautiful to look at, the controls feel good (although they may feel a little quirky at first), the music is good, and the exploring the world feels good. I felt comfortable recommending this game after the first 30 minutes.I look at the negative reviews, and it seems like players are complaining about the game being difficult. That's a personal problem, and maybe easy mode would suit you better. Every metroidvania shouldn't be as easy as SotN. Some bugs are to be expected for brand new games from indie devs.But there are some things I'd like to see improved. Menus are oddly difficult to navigate. Saving is slow, and load times on entering a new area feel excessive for a 2D game. Getting into the game takes too long, because you have to mash through so many screens and animations. Unskippable cutscenes in 2022? And forcing you to quit to title instead of quitting the game, so I have to Alt + F4 every time. Indie devs, please respect your player's time and implement basic QoL.None of those things stop me from recommending the game enthusiastically.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game jam-packed potential unfortunately let down with horrendous controls is the gist of it.I have not fully completed the game yet but with more than half way through I sadly do not think I will continue. Which is a shame considering the game could have been a insta classic in the likes of hollow knight, dead cells etc. The pros come down to:+ Great visuals, I think most people who bought or got interested in this game was first drawn to the amazing job from the art department on this game as it is one of the most stunning pixel art games I've seen to date.+ Combat, I actually like the combat. A lot of other people seem to not like this aspect but I generally like it. Now I have not played on the infamous patch which a lot of other reviewers are referring to but what I can say now is that I personally enjoy the difficulty level of the game and I am playing on the hardest difficulty and have yet met a boss which has taken more than 3 tries (Except the scorpion second encounter). +- Level design, this is both a con and a pro. At some points it is amazing and really well fleshed out and makes you naturally come back to familiar places just to proceed a different route and you never feel like it is a chore to come back from which you started. At other points it's is horrendous, I am looking at you pyramid. The save points can be extremely far apart at later parts of the game. I learnt the hard way that as soon as you see a shop you stock up, no matter what. Sometimes it feels like you just turned the corner and there is a save spot and other times it can take up to 30 mins to find one, couple this with trap puzzles and the "save system" which does not work like every other souls-like which makes you respawn at the last rested place. No instead you get back to where your last save was. This has confused me so many times as I die and then lose 20 mins of progress just to have no idea where I am anymore or how I got there. I think a solution would just be to adapt the souls-like respawn system and also do a whole overhaul on these dragon sword locations (Bonfires).Cons:- Controls, by far the biggest gripe I have with this game is the movement controls. They are at best clunky and at worst mimicing "rage games". I don't understand why there is a point to make SO MANY JUMPS pixel perfect. We are talking things that look like it should hit but then "nope" and you fall down and lose 1 min of time just to try again at that pixel perfect jump just to lose another 1 min because you didn't hit it at the exact angle it needs to. And don't get me started on the wall jumping mechanic. You would think that games in these genres at least should take one thing as inspiration from the likes of hollow knight and that should be controls. I feel like hollow knights controls are very tight and that is a fundamental thing about that game which makes it a classic. For Souldiers unfortunately it is by far the worst part of the game for me. Everything that is manual is extremely unforgiving and frustrating while everything automated feels like it tries to "help" you in the worst times ever just to ♥♥♥♥ with you. I think the developers really should have playtested this a lot more and release it to the community for them to come with feedback before putting it up for sale like this.- Story, not much to really say here as it is not that much to write home about but honestly I think most people aren't playing this game for the story.- World, games that claim themselves to be "souls-like" just like souldiers does has to hit some check marks I feel like to actually call themselves that. Respawn mechanic? Check. Dodge and roll/Block/Parry combat? Check. Open world with several paths you can take? Eh not so much. The game really dropped that ball on this one. You are basically force fed a path to go and I really tried to go to other places before going to the dreaded pyramid but nope the game does not allow you. And this is straight after being in the tutorial area which you already get forced to be within. The game seems to have some kind of mechanic in which the ramp up the enemies in the old places you already been at after a point in the game so I really don't get why they are forcing one path in the game and not instead letting people explore and just have this mechanic of making the enemies harder in the areas you not been in so they scale with you no matter where you start going after the tutorial. Welp that is all for now. I think I will give the game another try later but for now I am really done with the clunky controls and have to set down the controller before I break it after missing another pixel perfect jump.

_childDocuments_.review: Souldiers is a very well done Metroidvania with absolutely stellar presentation and engaging gameplay. Playing on Master mode was just the right amount of difficulty and resulted in a well-balanced experience throughout the whole 40 hours playtime for a single class. Caster in particular was very fun and dashing around creating exploding afterimages never got dull.While not without its flaws, I also don't believe the Mixed reception to be merited. It features incredibly large levels and, while I loved trawling through these vast maps, spending hours in a single location listening to the same music might wear you down. The subweapon system is also underutilized and as a result, undermines much of the rewards for exploration. This system is also further let down by how you switch subweapons and items, needing to scroll individually through each one, which really breaks the pace of combat in those moments. It is, regardless, a very competent game and one which I wholeheartedly recommend if you enjoy these kinds of games.

_childDocuments_.review: But unironically. Souldiers is a stunning looking metroidvania that could've been cut in half and it would've done great.Let me get this out of the way first -- Come ON, man, those dungeons are ridiculously bloated with so many indecisive paths and 'secrets' that are mostly some random coins and potions I ended up not even using. It was such a frustrating experience but I stubbornly continued just because the artwork is wonderful and the gameplay loop is actually cool, but very, very repetitive with the exception of the wall-jumping upgrade; that thing straight up sucks.How many times I caught myself realizing I spent 4~5h still in the SAME DUNGEON. Listen, I love playable content that keeps on giving but this is sincerely lazy; a multitude of gorgeous, but copy-pasted scenarios with a few changes here and there. The game drags on and on and on! So much of Souldiers could've been done in so little time; this game should've been a 12~15 hour game and I'd honestly look past most of the rest of the bullcrap that I will talk about now.The story is ok, your character is just some dude with main character plot armour plus everything feels like an acid trip after a while so it doesn't matter-- it's all over the place. The characters are really charming and the sprites for both allies and enemies are amazing but that's about where the 'fun ends' because the game doesn't want you to have any.Let me explain-- Souldiers starts really charming, it gives you time to get used to your character's moveset and such; I chose the archer and I liked it, did not look back even with the somewhat clunky ammo system we have for arrows, but it's alright, we can still throw the bow as a boomerang to deal damage. The first dungeon is the Spider Lair and it's really simple and straight-forward for the most part but boi... at the end of the dungeon I thought aloud "if the first dungeon is this long... imagine the rest." and not only imagine I did, I also experienced it.There's a ton of exploration but like I mentioned before, the secrets are hit or miss; sometimes you get a nice secondary weapon and other times... coins. Coins are used to upgrade your items and weapons together with a few different ores we also get on chests, which is fine but wow, the game disrespects your time so much with how terribly paced the dungeons are. I would've prefer to grind enemies to get these rocks, not having to get inside dungeons with terribly placed checkpoints, which mind you, IT'S THE ONLY WAY YOU CAN SAVE THE GODDANG GAME. Yep, I did a fcuky wucky, needed to restart my game and guess what? I lost 2h~ of exploration because I didn't want to save since it respawns enemies. It's my fault but still, what a lame mechanic.Now, the "Floating Whatever" (I forgot the name) was the dungeon that almost made me give up because it is that frustrating. Not only there are some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ZIPPY ZAPPY RATS that TELEPORT ON YOU and can PARALYZE you, there's also some very annoying birbs summoned by an invisible 'birbmancer' that go through terrain just to kamikaze you to inflict paralysis; yep, they're 'those' kinds of enemies that die in one hit but if they hit you, it's just infuriating if you're far away from a save state or out of paralyze heal or whatever -- my point is that the game does almost everything in its power to anger the player, at least it annoyed me to no end. It felt these obstacles were only testing my patience and not giving me a challenge or that thirst for progress; they were just being a nuisance for the sake of being one. Ok, I get it, Souldiers is one of those harder games but hard doesn't mean stupidly annoying-- you think the toxic dart dudes in Blighttown are bad? Check out the poison, frozen, paralyze status and such in this game, some even stop you in motion to take damage and/or have to redo an entire platforming setting because 'get wrecked mid jump loser lmao'.In short, the game is beautiful but terrible to look past its awful decisionmaking which sucks because the artwork is pure eye candy... what isn't is the game design; not everything has to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ maze within a maze within a maze in a metroidvania, guys. Seriously that pyramid is terrible.I find it funny the achievement for finishing the game on its hardest difficulty is called "The Impossible". Even the cheeky devs know the game is a slog to go through. I'm a bit disappointed I will not 100% finish this one, it is simply not worth my time... man, to think even ELEX 2 was worth my time, holy shid.Anyway, best avoid it if you value your time. I wish I did but alas, we live and we learn... who am I kidding, I'll probably play something worse than this eventually. lmao

_childDocuments_.review: ---What I played: 37 Hours finishing the main story all on Master Difficulty (Highest) Using the Soldier Class. Explored the majority of the areas while looking for secrets.---A video compiling all the mechanics and features I found interesting while playing the game:---+Metroidvania with 3 Classes to choose from Soldier/Archer/Mage+Life Upgrades/Multiple Weapons/Leveling up stats/Movement and Combat Upgrades as you progress to access more areas etc, classic Metroidvania game design+Combat and movement animations are very smooth and satisfying to do+Can Parry and gain additional Combat Techniques by leveling up+Also has a skill tree+Bosses and enemies are fun to fight, learning their patterns.+Interesting Elemental Mechanic where you can use a radial menu to change you elements on the fly. This is used for combat and puzzles and the more elements you unlock the more varied the combat and puzzles become.+Very rewarding exploration with a lot of treasures to find+Backtracking doesn't feel tedious because you will always gain a new treasure to help you in the form of upgrades like health/weapons/materials/accessories+Enemies drop loot as well in the form of money/weapons/accessories that are useful.+Decent amount of accessories to try out and you can swap them mid fight, they also have different effects, such as resistances, healing buffs, money gain, or damage increases etc+You can fast travel immediately without needing to unlock it+The map shows treasures and other interactables when you discover them so you can keep track of what you missed+A lot of checkpoints available so you won't lose much progress if you die, and boss fights let you retry the fight right away so you don't need to go back from a save point+Amazing Pixel Art Style with ton of tiny details throughout the game +Music and sound effects are also very good----Some glitches that made me have to reload the game-Some QOL stuff such as not being able to scroll down quickly in the menu---+/-The game could be very easy on lower difficulties. On Master it can be hard at the start but eventually becomes easier the more upgrades you get. ---Overall a very fun and rewarding game. Great for Metroidvania fans and also has SNES classic game nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a lot more recognition. I understand it began with a rough launch with serious bugs and some not-so-fun more frustrating-than-fair mechanics. BUT, to their credit, the developers went back and addressed the complaints, and as it is in its CURRENT STATE, Souldiers is a fantastic game.The developers should get a lot of credit for creating a massive world absolutely filled with beautifully crafted environments and tons of memorable well-animated characters and creatures, plus a great musical score to boot.  The artwork really draws you in and creates an immersive experience that you just want to keep exploring.  The huge areas are also designed with an impressive and well thought-out complexity.  There are countless secrets to discover, and plenty of varied puzzles to keep things interesting--but not so many as to break-up the flow of exploration and combat.  There's a great balance achieved and the world is one I just never got tired of adventuring through.The gameplay is fluid and controls quite well.  You get to pick between 3 different characters which can suit different play styles and offers an extra layer of replayability if you're so inclined--I played as a Scout and it offers satisfying melee, but when you add skills, secondary weapons, perks, and the prominent mechanic of switching elemental attacks--which are constantly important both in combat (affecting offense, defense, and status effects depending on opponent) and ability gating (elemental attacks have extra effects to help you traverse areas) you really get a well-rounded and engaging experience.If you are a fan of big beautiful Metroidvanias that give you a ton of quality content, fun engaging gameplay, and a large, smartly designed world to explore, don't sleep on Souldiers!

_childDocuments_.review: Souldiers is one of the best games in recent memory. There's something about Souldiers that I've never experienced in another game before: the level design. Areas are 2-4 hours long and each one has a different level design philosophy for the most part. The first dungeon has standard metroidvania design (Get powerup, find wall, break wall, proceed). The second dungeon has a Zelda-like design (get keys to unlock doors), while the third has a Mega-Man style approach (linear gauntlet of enemies and puzzles). It is amazing to me how each level feels like part of a different game. The combat, enemy design, boss variety, etc is amazing as well.  While I would under normal circumstance give this game a 9.5/10, it deserves a 9/10 due to some bugs (infinitely active hitboxes, save time stutters, etc). This game is worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Review edit after sinking another 27 hours into the game, and after the major update.tl;dr: I still do not recommend the game. The major update didn't solve the core issues that the game has (which I will not list again, as the devs just blatantly skipped over them), they just put a band-aid over this crack and called it a day.The major update just rescaled hp, damage dealt and damage taken throughout the whole game and all difficulties, without addressing why those issues were talked about by reviewers. Some of the game breaking bugs were fixed so that's a good point for the devs.Despite these changes the game still feels not interesting to play. It still feels like doing a chore rather than going through a challenge, and everytime I complete a major milestone I don't feel rewarded. I tried pointing out some of my concerns in a post in the discussion section but was ignored, wasn't expecting much to begin with, but completely ignored makes me feel like they don't even care about the game themselves. I'm currently at the fire temple, I've got more than 24k gold to spend after completing probably 4 side quests and constantly refelling everything at the store at each save point; some sections are still poorly designed, and story wise the game doesn't tell you that much, unless you collect stuff that is completely optional, and nobody in the game tells you what those things are and what purpose they serve. I will not continue my playthrough for the aforementioned reasons, but should anyone of you be interested in the game just buy it at a discounted price. That would be allOriginal review:I was really excited to play this game after trying out the demo.The game felt challenging but seemed like had a nice take on the metroidvania experience, cool art and a not-so-bad (at least while playing the demo) gameplay experience. Honestly felt sad when I saw that the release date was going to be delayed, but it was just a week so whatever, right?God I wish those were like 6 weeks. The game feels extremely unfinished and unpolished; the art is still good now that I'm well over 5 hours into the game, but the gameplay is just... bad. I have yet to realize how the game wants me to approach fights, wether or not I should man up and tank a couple hits, turtle all the way to the end or I don't know. Mobs deal WAY too much damage (they can even crit) and have WAY too much health at the early stages of the game. My save file states that I'm at 22% of the game completion, and I'm afraid it's gonna stay there: it is not fun to play or satisfying to overcome.Spoiler-ish so read at your own risk (playing at the soldier difficulty):I am currently at the pyramid thingy, and I kid you not it took me 30 full minutes to beat the scorpion. Issues aren't really within the gameplay, how the boss deals damage or how much damage it deals... you have to do the "intro" to the boss fight  you somehow lose to it. At least the minotaur and the arachnid were just "you die? cool try again".The pyramid is also where my playthrough stops, as it's honestly not fun to go through. I genuinely cannot understand how the game wants me to engage in certain fights. I tried different ways to overcome either bosses or mobs, but none seems to be the correct way: blocking is completely out of the question, as it breaks in one or to hits, and takes a ♥♥♥♥ load of time before it's up again; dodging is somehow fine, combined with the jumps seemed to be the "safest" way to not get hit, while doing little to no damage. I wanted to upgrade my staff before journeying to the desert, but I lacked the money to do so. The orbs and the weakness mechanic is cool, but playing with a controller feels like it's to clanky, therefore not being a good experience to switch between elements (at the time of writing I am at 3 orbs, counting the standard one too). I should also mention that currently remapping keys and actions is bugged, and some buttons are shown inverted, even if when pressed perform the correct action.The platforming part of the game also feels bad, as there is little to no movements that helps you journey between each screen, and this further translates into bad gameplay, as there are less ways to move around and play the game, effectively.I don't intend on lowering the difficulty to make things easier, I enjoy challenges and I enjoy testing myself in tough environments to eventually overcome them and get a feeling of reward. Sadly Souldiers doesn't yield anything whatsoever, just frustration after completing tasks that should not be as challenging.Genuinely upset that I cannot refund the game, now at 8 hours into the game. As for right now, stay away from it, or buy it at a discounted price, definitely not worth its full price.
