_childDocuments_.review: Souldiers is a metroidvania with soulslike elements, as you probably guessed from the name.  Soulslike in the "tough but fair" sense.  The main hook of the game is that you are one of three normal soldier types and the game will play very differently based on that initial choice.  I like that you aren't some prophesied hero, you are just a soldier.  The second gameplay gimmick that sets this game apart from similar ones is a set of elements that you acquire through the game.  You can freely change your core element for your attacks on the fly.  Each element does a different thing, and all of the enemies are weak or resistant to certain elements.Back when this game was released it was a bit overtuned.  I didn't play the game at that time so I can only really speak to what I see now in 2024.  It looks like they put in some difficulty options and dialed things down a bit.  Naturally that sparked outrage, because we are on the internet.  As it is now the combat and bosses feel fair to me.  I played the game as an archer.The bosses are pretty good, and where the soulslike part comes through well.  The bosses have a yellow or red color flash before they make certain attacks that indicates if you should jump over or dodge.  You can do the bosses without taking a hit if you put enough effort into learning their movesets.  No I didn't do that, but I like that you can.  The element match game portion of all the combat was fun to me as an extra layer of complexity.  Unfortunately, seeing those element vulnerabilities is locked behind a modifier on certain amulets.  I feel like that should have just been baseline as it adds to the game.  You don't have to match elements, but it adds a little damage if you do.Four of the biomes are really big.  There is a ton to explore in each of them, and lots of backtracking to do.  The "soulslike" portion also extends into the parkour of the game.  There's a lot of times where you'll have to do some interesting maneuvers to progress, like "fall through a floor, dash forward, double jump up, wall jump back".  It had me wondering a lot of the time if I was going the right way, and I was.  I wasn't that into these aspects, but some people are excited by everything in this paragraph.Overall I had fun with it.  Finished it in about 20 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I can't speak for archer or mage as I've only completed this game on normal and master mode as a soldier.This has easily become one of my more favorite metroidvanias. I initially glossed over it because it didn't stand out well to me but once i saw the news of this game getting review bombed due to how hard it was, it caught my interest. I feel bad for the developers because they received so many bad reviews, and a good number of them are people complaining about janky controls. The controls are perfect, and honestly I think it's just people being bad at the game.few things to note:A lot of ledges are placed for perfectly timed out jumps, ie a full height jump followed by a double jump. Funnily enough I've seen a number of youtube videos of people constantly having trouble with this concept cos they're so quick to double jump all the time.There are many instances of having to do trick movements with the controls that are going to frustrate people. ex: jump > dash > jump under an obstacle to get up to higher platforms, double jump > jump off wall and dash back > triple jump to get to certain ledges.While optional, the race with the marathon bandana requires some near perfect precision. It honestly took me a good hour the first time in normal mode but I cleared it first try on my attempt in Master mode due to getting the obstacle course down so well. This may frustrate casual completionists to insanity especially since the reward is pretty decent in certain fights, while definitely not needed.There is a mandatory "run for your life" segment. The first time doing this on normal mode I felt it was a bit too precise for the average gamer to get through reasonably without being frustrated, second time around I did it no problem with plenty of time to spare. There is a lot in there that can happen and cause you to fall back in progress though. It's one of two things I really feel is kind of rough in this game.No joke, there is a roughly 25 minute long gauntlet of enemies. This is optional. The first time around I did die near the end and having to sit through another 20 minutes + of that was painful. I did it in Master mode as well but this time I used the fire staff and it made life a lot easier. I just feel like a checkpoint needs to be put in there at some point for normal mode, but again it is optional and the reward at that point is pretty useless.Master mode definitely is not much harder than normal mode. There are people complaining it is far too easy for being the hardest difficulty, but I felt it was difficult enough to truly enjoy the full mechanics of every boss battle and it made the game much more fun playing it a second time around. I didn't have to "master" each boss fight to get through them but I had to redo them enough times to get a pretty strong grasp on each situation.For bugs:One that I was able to replicate is the desert goes pitch black if you walk from the 3rd save sword to the 2nd save sword after you progress far enough to the game, around the time of the 3rd major dungeon. It's a bit jarring but otherwise insignificant once you go into the cave and back out.Another frustrating issue is the menu button not working if you do some quick button presses after using a save point or certain other areas. I haven't been able to replicate it but it happens often enough where the menu button wont work at all so I can't change amulets conveniently until I get back to a save point where it will then work again.Anyways I'm hoping there's a sequel, I legitimately love this game and can't wait for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.  Several hours into me playing this I surfed over to steam and was absolutely flabbergasted to see the dismal reviews. I would highly recommend this game to anybody looking for a (challenging) experience that involves a bit of a learning curve.+Strong visual and audio presentation+Combat 'feels' good+Areas are large with lots of secrets+Diverse play style among the 3 classes+Game does not go easy on you-Some funky hit detection with ledge grabbing/wall jumps-Handful of glitches.  I only had two minor ones, but have seen several others mentioned-Consumable items are largely not that great until late game-2 very annoying side quests...Lastly (assuming I didn't miss something) it would have been nice at end-game to find something that revealed hidden locations and/or missing treasure chests and byguls on the maps. _childDocuments_.review: Souldiers ended up being a really solid metroidvania, and I wanted to wait until i beat at least one campaign before writing a review, as I thought id have been unfair to play 4 hours, and then give my thoughts as if I've played the entire game. Especially since the team for the game is seemingly very small, and I wanted to see if the game had any extra content after completing the main game. The game for the most part is VERY fun, but needs a good ironing out, which was promised to us by the 23rd in a patch (which I'm planning on revising the review after said patch). Fixing bugs, balancing gameplay, and improving on what they've already made. So what is the game like *now* without the patch? [TLDR: whats coming next is mostly for the DEVS to take a gander at, if you want t know my final thoughts then go to the very bottom][HOW THE FIRST PLAYTHROUGH FELT]I started my first blind playthrough as an Archer, on warrior mode, This playthrough took the 48 hours I have in this game upon writing the review. I chose warrior mode because I like challenges and the game promised to be challenging, so I cranked up the difficulty as high as I could. Any game with difficulty choices should be fair on any difficulty, just harder. Warrior mode is for the most part was very fair. Being prepared for fights always led a victory after some attempts, much like games like Hollow Knight or Salt and Sanctuary, having healing and curing items usually nets you a win, but some bosses/enemies did have some iffy mechanics tied to them. Normally panning down to intangibility during attacks you could easily hit them in. Some bosses annoyed me, but I never would say I couldn't beat a boss. The only thing that truly annoyed me was that some key bosses were immune or highly resistant to skills. Meaning I had stocked up on certain potions for no reason, and checkpoint placement was rather poor. In the second, and third dungeon, there were long stretches of areas which were checkpointless, and you'd die with a passage unlocked or key item collected. Having to do it all over again. Not game ruining since my choice of difficulty meant I asked for a hard time, but It did end up being a lengthier time then it had to be. A notable moment of no checkpoints being a terrible idea was the boss battle before the DC dungeon (trying to stay spoiler free, the Devs will know what the DC is). I beat the boss only to wander into the next dungeon, and die instantly. Where I had to fight them AGAIN. This happened twice, as the game failed to load the previous area where I was planning to save, restarting the game to have to fight them one more time. Some kind of save or checkpoint after that boss is really all that's needed, as the boss itself is fine, really fun as archer actually.Overall the first playthrough was really good, I liked the gameplay the bosses are fun after you get a hang of their patters, and I'll be completing the other 2 campaigns. [COMBAT]Very good combat feel. Its fast, fluid, and fun. (the wall jump could use some work though). Archer specifically is a pretty difficult class to get the hang of, due to their main attack always being on a recharge which you have to manage very well, but they're a strong class once you get into the feel of it. the Scout from the demo (which I played a good while) and Archer from the full release do feel completely different from one another though, so I didn't get a samey feel from playing with them bothThe only problem i had with archer was that their counter mechanic, "Skirmish" felt useless. Taking from the stamina bar told me that countering with the Skirmish dodge was my main way of defense, but it has what feels like 0 I-frames on the roll, and definitely not the attack. So what ended up happening was that I would eitherA. Dodge successfully and get hit anyway due to being in the counter animationB. Dodge into the attack trying to roll past the boss and get hit anyway.With the dodge being that janky, I never bothered to try using it, only blocking the occasional melee attack when it was too hard for me to dodge it fully, or I had no choice I can guess making it like that was to keep players from simply spamming the dodge, but changing the stamina consumption around or making it so it takes more and more stamina with each successive dodge could fix this.The other two halves of combat is the accessories and elemental orbs. You put them on, you can get specific boosts, like a boost to your elemental damage/defense by orbs (and some accessories), and from accessories, a boost to money gain, seeing an opponents health/weakness, an additional elemental boost, or unique stuff like % health healed on kills, crit chance, evade chance, or resistances to debuffs. They also give stat buffs to ATK, Stamina, and Mana boosts. The only thing I wish would be added to accessories are some more unique buffs, for things such as bosses. The most you can get as a unique buff is an elemental boost, or debuff resist, as the ring that heals on kill doesn't heal you when you attack a boss. Some new accessories that help you with bosses would be welcomed, like a ring that does heal you when dealing damage, but at the cost of say an increase to stamina/mana usage, or the heal being tied to a % chance, an accessory that will always revive you once, but with a random and non-curable debuff signified by a colored flash, so you have to wait out the debuff like normal, or, for players looking for a huge payoff for skillful play, stuff that increases damage significantly, but you take 2x damage. These are things that could be added later on, if the game decides to add additional content, but this is mostly suggestions for things to add to expand on things already present.[EXPLORATION]Dungeons and other areas of this game are HUGE. Hence the 48 hours it took for me to beat the game once. Large maps are fun in the fact there's a lot to explore and look out for, and there's a big chunk of backtracking you'll have to do to finish the entire game collectible wise. My only thing about backtracking is the map. I got lost multiple times starting out because the map shows things like locked gates, but gets rid of them when you unlock the gate, meaning if you die and either forget where you went or turn off the game for a break, going back without remembering where you left off can be a nightmare. Simple fix; add the ability to add markers to the map. It helps everyone, hurts no one. For players that know what they're doing on their third playthrough, they can mark secret rooms or hidden chests for later, and for new players, mark where the heck to go next. When everywhere on the map starts looking the same.[OVERALL, SHOULD YOU BUY?] by the thumbs up on my review, yes i think the purchase is worth it, the game is a nice length, with 3 different campaigns to try out, and after beating the game, it does feature NG+, so you can keep playing even after you beat all 3 campaigns. They even seemingly set themselves up to expand on the game, as there are 3 other entirely unique Soldiers that are unavailable to play, the Slayer, Rider, and Ironclad. A perfect setup for more DLC like new optional areas, characters, and hopefully a Boss Rush/select mode. The game is overall a blast, and with the patch currently coming up, It'll be better than it is now, without all the little bugs strung here and there.

Sometimes you go up a level and don't gain one of the above stats.4- There is only one, that's right, one piece of equipment, which is the ring and only from level 18 (Caster) and level 20 Soldier and Archer can equip the second.5- The sub weapons are not very efficient, with the exception of 2 of the 3 variants of the bombs.6- The Soldier and the Archer have telentos to increase the critical chance can increase 3 times, the Caster does not, instead he gets a buff to increase his damage of all his skills, but it is buggy and does not increase the damage .7- Throughout the game you get Orbs, each one has an element. Fire, Earth, Electric, Water and Wind and has its base form. When you choose an orb, fire for example increases your fire damage and defense and each element is more effective over the other example Earth deals more damage in Electric. However, enemies like you also do not deal only elemental damage and there is nothing to decrease base damage, because in Souldiers there is no base defense, I make a point of being very specific here. For example: you started the game with the Soldier but it could be anyone, you are at level 1 the spider hits you causing 10 base damage, some time passes you reach the level cap which is 50 gave all the upgrades to your shield and go face the spider it will do the same 10 damage... that doesn't make any sense... For God's sake fix it!8- throughout the game you get rings that increase the damage of the elements, for example: the ring of fire increases the fire damage by x% and the defense against fire attacks by x% and throughout the game you get rings with their respective elements, now comes the problem. you are in a room you have 5 enemies, each one with their respective element, you already have the 2 fire rings equipped so by logic you will defeat the enemy that is weak against fire, you defeat him and soon after you will face the enemy is weak against water, so you change your fire orb to ice, but you also remember that you also have 2 rings that increase water damage and defense so you have to pause the game, remove the fire rings and equip the ice ones... Seriously you use the name 'Soul'diers so please! make a setup so that when we change orb we automatically change our rings! there is only one equipment in the whole game that you can change so please! do it!9- Only less than half of the enemies in the game drop items and the drop chance is almost zero! there is no luck status in the game and much less has a ring to increase drop hate10- In ''Soul''diers you can play with 3 characters Soldier, Archer and Caster each has its bug. Soldier parry works when the game wants, Archer doesn't defend, you hold the defense button and nothing happens, you fear full damage and Caster is the one left over he is the one with the least hp he attacks in two ways when you get to a very small distance I'm going to be very specific here, when you get to a very small distance the basic attacks are guided, but extremely weak, the caster's greatest damage is the staff attack but it takes 4 seconds to fully recharge and the range is less than the Archer's arrows and the icing on the cake! good luck landing the staff attack in midair! when you do it it takes 1 second to launch and in that period you can't hit the enemy because you don't stay still in the air, the Archer for example can shoot 4 arrows in a row in the air and stays in the same place, well at least the Caster defends...11-In 'Soul'diers you have a roll, well you can only use it every 3 seconds, when the roll ends the character has a slight brake, some enemies you can pass through them, others you can't, some projectiles you can turn with the roll, others don't... Welcome to the world of 'Soul'diers! _childDocuments_.review: Souldiers is... alright.The visuals are beautiful, but at the same time... mostly not very... distinct? The pixel art is incredibly good but it's used to draw... caves... forests... a desert... a pyramid... there's one or two environments that are kind of cool but I think a general struggle of this game is that it lacks personality - the characters are all a bit generic, the story is a confused mess that has a completely non-ending,  the world is very fantasy to a fault, and your protagonist is just. Not a character. A completely emotionless killing machine. And the characters you do get to interact with are far and few between and usually complete their brief story arcs in a single dungeon's worth.In terms of map design I think it's actually generally really good, very sprawling dungeons stitched together by fairly reasonable connective tissue, though interactions between different zones is fairly minimal with the overarching map being mostly a flat line with a few areas jutting out above or below it. The platforming is not amazing - you carry momentum similar to La-Mulana, meaning it tends to feel a bit stiff, but the game generally is designed well around that and rarely did a platforming section feel unfun or unfair, plus the variety of mechanics at play allowed for a decent amount of different challenges.Combat is... well, i can only speak to scout, but it's... okay? I feel some elements are done really poorly - between enemies having very, VERY short windup animations for attacks and the parry window being so small, it becomes functionally useless, and the shield, even fully upgraded, breaks too fast to ever be too useful, leading to movement and dodge-rolling as the only viable options for dodging attacks. The worst mechanic, though, is switching between elemental orbs - it's set up in a good, smart way, but they did NOT account for joystick kickback at all, leading to hundreds upon hundreds of instances where I go to select an element and get the polar opposite of what I wanted instead. The exclusion of a failsafe for this is baffling and it wrecks the combat whenever elemental switching becomes mandatory (the final boss in particular is MISERABLE for this very reason). In general I also found most subweapons useless since they're all tied to the same very limited ammo count, and the majority of them deal neutral damage instead of elemental damage - the ones that do also don't tend to be that great, but it's hard to be encouraged to experiment with them when there are so, so many (too many) and so little ammo. The skills the scout gains as the game goes on are also all completely useless for the aforementioned reason of dealing neutral damage only - I used the uppercut and air spiral on rare occasions but the rest I barely if ever felt a need to pull off.Enemy designs themselves are mostly fine, boss designs range from "kind of cool" to "why did you do this". Most egregious are any bosses who have long periods of invulnerability while they do a long, tedious attack - I don't know why we're still doing this in the year 2022. It's boring. it drags out fights without giving players a chance to do anything. It's not fun. There were definitely fights I did have fun with, and some I didn't, though I'd say it leaned more towards the former overall and like... combat at its base mostly feels good aside from my aforementioned problems, so generally it's -fun- to fight. A few overlong arena rooms really test that patience, though.The game's size is very respectable, although I'd say in some cases... too large. Dungeons are MASSIVE and often boil down to repeating a lot of the same ideas over a huge amount of space, and the game has a nasty habit of hiding stuff behind invisible walls with little to no indication of a secret - even collecting the maps doesn't reveal everything and to my knowledge there's no item or upgrade that shows what's missing on maps, so I ended up just using a guide to clean up everything since... it wouldn't be fun otherwise, between how huge areas are and how annoyingly hidden secrets tend to be. If you like MASSIVE, exploration-dense maps though then, yeah, you'll get a kick out of it even with those caveats.I think that's the thing, at its core Souldiers is a good game, but it has waaaaay too many key missteps to be a great game, and its lack of personality in both presentation and gameplay leads me to suspect this game is going to fade from memory much quicker than other similarly large metroidvanias of its ilk like Hollow Knight or Aeterna Noctis. And I definitely wasn't incentivized to push through it the same way those aforementioned games kept me HOOKED - i slowly grinded my way through this one over the span of like, three weeks -  but I can't say I didn't overall enjoy my time with it either, just that the rough corners keep me from truly loving it.You do absoutely get bang for your buck here, though, like... three whole classes mixed with a pretty massive world? Maybe I'll come back and play as a ranger sometime in the future, who knows.

_childDocuments_.review: Off the top: THIS GAME IS GREAT SINCE THE JUNE 23RD UPDATE!!! I did not recommend this game previously, but the devs have really done an amazing job fixing all the issues that I had with the game in addition to improving many additional things. This game is a true gem now and I hope that it will not be tainted by the rather rough original version of the game. If you dropped the game like I did, then I would highly recommend giving it another shot now. You will not be disappointed! I won't attempt to mention all of the changes but here's a few changes to highlight:- All classes were buffed in some way. The Archer and Wizard classes in particular are MUCH stronger now. They do more damage and more durable in addition to more intricate buffs- The flying enemies' behavior has been adjusted to remain much closer to the player for a less frustrating experience- Bosses and enemies do less damage across the board. Additionally, their health pools are smaller- Health orbs, coins, and other resources drop more frequently- There are a few quality of life changes such as marking important doors and items on the map, Pros:- Gorgeous graphics- The platforming is well done (although nothing special)- Combat is fun and fair with enemies having telegraphed attacks, good placement, etc.- Environments are diverse and appealing - The music is good and fits the specific themes respectively.The Cons- Although you can learn abilities through leveling up and earning skill points, it takes some time to gain new abilities due to a rather slow leveling system and needing 3+ skill points to learn a single skill in most cases.- With all the changes, the game can now feel rather easy (especially important due to the game being labeled as a Soulsborne). I would highly recommend playing on the Warrior difficulty if you want more of a challenge. And even then, Warrior difficulty is easier than the Vanilla Normal difficulty. Overall, I would highly recommend this game to anyone who likes 2D games in general. If you like Metroidvanias, Action games, or simply like Pixel-Art games, then do not pass this up!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, levels, and the beginnings of good gameplay are all there, but it sadly falls short from actually being fun. There are tons of baffling design decisions in the game. Upgrading gear takes both a ton of gold as well as secondary currency from exploring, but the gold requirements are much higher than you might actually get from progressing through the game. Additionally, healing items only come from rare one-time chest drops or from spending gold at shops. Fast traveling doesn't auto-save (Why?). Flying enemies take ages to kill because they idle outside of attack range between their own attacks. The game checkpoints at boss fights, but only after the fight starts, so if you die and want to go shop beforehand you have to exit the game and manually reload your last save. You hit like a wet noodle. Character movement is slow and not very smooth. Game will checkpoint after events happen in the world, but if you reach a checkpoint with 2 health and there's no save points for miles, you either have to make it to a save point without getting hit or exit the game, reload, and do it all again. Every other hard metroidvania and soulslike game retains progress between death, it's incredibly stupid that this one doesn't.Overall a pretty big disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame people are giving this so many bad reviews I really don't understand it. Fans of the genera are not helping themselves. "mixed" at the time of writing this does not reflect my experience at all and seems really unfair.If you're thinking about buying this know it's a high-quality, polished (no bugs for me so far), and well made game, and I wouldn't necessarily trust the "mixed" review. I play a lot of metroidvanias and this is one is right up there. The art, the music, the combat, the level-design, all great and keeps you on your toes and rethinking your strategies. It's definitely not a mindless game you just run through, mashing one button, and that is a good thing. You have a parry, a roll on a timer, a shield with endurance, and a variety of abilities to keep things interesting. I'm playing through on hard mode or "Warrior", so it can be a little frustrating at times but you can switch difficulties whenever you want, so I can't really understand the complaints from most people. It's true it can be a bit punishing at times, so if you really can't tolerate frustration try easy or medium difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I may update this review after progressing more.  I've only progressed to the Sand level with one character, and beaten the first area with all 3 classes.  I leave the game open without playing a lot, so my playtime on steam isn't accurate.This game has far more going for it than against it, but the bad parts are hard to overlook.  You will probably enjoy this game if you like the action/exploring aspect of metroidvanias more than the RPG aspects.  The game tries very hard to provide a slower pacing for character advancement, and this can become tiresome if you don't find the puzzles and exploration to be exciting for their own sake.  There seems to only be a few options to modify your character's numerical advantages (attack damage, defenses, health, etc.).  I think a lot of games go way too far in min-maxing those sorts of values, but this one might be underplaying that aspect a bit too much.  I really enjoyed the focus on level and enemy design.  Puzzles and gimmicks are prevalent to add excitement to the pacing of level progression beyond simply fighting enemies.  The enemies themselves often seem like combat puzzles by offering attacks and movement that becomes increasingly complex to deal with.  Unfortunately both of these concepts work against the game because...Difficulty and controls are a real problem here.  There are limits on your character's capabilities in terms of movement and defense that don't quite mesh with the number of enemies and dangerous environments that you're expected to face.  Your movement capabilities are particularly limited early in the game, and the impact on combat is quite heavy.  While these challenges aren't completely insurmountable, you're going to die a few times from unintentional interactions, experimenting with enemy attacks, and just not handling situations "correctly".  When you die, you go back to your last save point, and ALL of your progress is lost.  None of your pickups, XP earned, or impacts on the environment are saved.  This means you have to completely retrace your steps all over again, and it becomes extremely annoying to repeat the same fights and level navigation over and over again for particularly hard sections until the "puzzles" of enemies and hazards become routine rather than engaging.  Any excitement from exploration and secret-finding is gone as you simply have to do it again after already discovering it the first time.  This might appeal to perfectionists that enjoy going through challenges until the player achieves complete mastery over them, but I think the way it's implemented here is going to turn a lot of people off (myself included).Quick side-note: The three classes don't seem super balanced.  The bow class seems particularly hit by problems with controls and limits to their kit.  Manually aiming the bow at enemies at diagonal levels is PAINFUL, and you automatically miss attacks at a certain range that doesn't feel very good.  However, class capabilities really change with advancement, and they may just be a slow starter.  Mage and Soldier have advantages and drawbacks depending on the enemies they fight (mostly if it flies or not), but they seem to be a better option.  The nice thing about this is that these classes definitely have different playstyles that can add some replayability to the game if you fall in love enough to play multiple times.Ultimately, I'd say this game really depends on how okay you are with retracing your steps.  Personally, I *hate* that part.  However, I'm still going to recommend this game because the levels and enemies are creative and challenging enough to keep me engaged, and I'll just take a break for a bit if I hit a section that requires a lot of retries without progression.  There's a very well designed metroidvania here, but you just need to embrace or get over this aspect of the game to enjoy it.  Decide for yourself, and watch some videos if you're uncertain.  I offer kudos to the devs for what they were able to accomplish even with the mixed reactions and hope they can improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, not dividing this up into sections because I'm bad a writing. For starters, the graphics are amazing, that's something it's got going for it, graphics are amazing. But the starting area ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SUCKS! For all of my playtime, I have been in this ONE DUNGEON, and I don't know how to get out! And that's another thing I don't like about it, I was expecting this to be a bit more open world-ish, but it isn't. I feel like the start would've been better if there was a level select screen or something. Now, me expecting it to be open world was a mistake, because it doesn't list it in its tags. Yes, I know that you have to actually aim when playing a ranged class, but the aiming feels a bit to tight since you can only aim in 8 directions and not in between, In my opinion, you should only have to aim in their general direction, so it slightly homes into them, not requiring the perfect aim that you need right now. Plus, you have to be moving *towards* your target, which SUCKS for close combat. Scout was just okay. Although, multiple times I tried to parry those goblins' bombs, and it didn't work a single time. I don't know if it's intentional or I just suck, but if it is intentional, that's stupid. Let me parry all projectiles. But the main reason I don't like this game is because of the long ass time it takes to get past the FIRST DUNGEON. That's it.EDIT: I completely forgot to state something. Feels nothing like a metroidvania. In my opinion, a metroidvania deals with getting a powerup then backtracking to areas you already explored to discover more. This does not do that at all. Also, level design kinda sucks.EDIT 2: Back after a while, I think the concept of this is really really good. Horrible execution. I like the concept of the exploring a new world, and the fact that you're just one of the soldiers sent to patrol. This would TOTALLY do better if it was a sort of open world top down thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend the game as it stands.Lets mention some good things before the flaws. - The art-style and animations are all very nice so far, I love pixel art and this game does it very well. - The Score fits nicely with the environs and the effects are nice (Music dampens when you enter a dark area for example to give a better feeling of claustrophobia)For context on the criticism following, I'm playing on normal difficulty with the mage character and am currently walled at the forest area with the minotaur from the opening cutscene (that'll come up later). I realize I am probably only still at the beginning of the game but like with the big daddy example of ff14, who wants to sit through a slog of a beginning before it finally becomes fun?Now on to the meats and potatoes of the this:1. Probably my biggest gripe so far is the loss of progression when you die. You lose everything you got up until when you last saved when you die. Map progression, money, exp, items, all gone and I kinda have a feeling that the devs knew this because at certain points in the spider cave you would get a random autosave before a particular area. Not that that particular inclusion resolves this, There was one particular area in the spider caves with a platforming puzzle with quite a few enemies around that was a challenge, I died quite a few times (one in particular is a point later on) and the distance from the nearest rest point back to where I was trying to make progress was just long enough to be frustrating (one of the large spider enemies and a slow elevator away) and the fact that every time I died meaning I wasn't gaining any exp progression from the enemies piled on top of that. I do not want to draw comparisons to other games but dark souls does this much better2. The mage class doesn't feel like it 'fits' (Again I can't speak for warrior or archer) for a couple reasons: - The ending lag on mages basic attack animations is longer than you would think meaning you can not dodge out of the end of a combo when a boss/enemy telegraphs an attack and you stand there and just eat it. I understand that the description for mage was 'wait for your timings' but it feels very bad when your game sense says that you can deal damage and then dodge but you end up not able to do any actions because the mage needs to finish his flourish with the wand before moving. - Mage's defensive options. Mage dodge is nice but feels like bosses attacks are far too frequent and the cooldown on it too long so most time you end up dodging into another attack and his guard gauge is fairly small so you enter a catch 22 situation in some circumstances (Which I will get to later).  - For a mage type character he does not have a lot of range and it seems inconsistent when you can or can't fire the magic bolts from the normal attack. This extends to the mage blast ability which is pitifully short and in some cases, means you have to run towards an enemy to deal in any way significant damage. - All in all mage just feels too slow for the pace of the enemies you encounter.3. Very cheap hazards that you can't react to, there are hard to see buttons on the ground that are sometimes hid by destructible objects when stood on fire arrows at you and stalactites and enemies that fall on you from offscreen. Sure the damage isn't that much but its basically unavoidable on your first entry to an area with these. Referring to the difficult platforming area from before where is reasonable to be low health at the end of, there is one of said arrow trap buttons hidden, I died after clearing the difficult section to a cheap trap. If I wanted to feel such anger and frustration at cheap hits like that, I'd go play cat mario or I wanna be the guy.4. Bosses feel very rough, I've only encountered 3 so far but I have had different issues for each: - Spear knight didn't have set attack patterns and 3 attacks, which is fine don't get me wrong, he is the first boss after all. From what I gathered after he performs an attack he then rolls a dice to see what his next attack is. One of the attacks he has is he throws 4 spears at you in relative quick fashion that can be easily dodged by timing jumps, The issue that arises from this is that he can choose to use it again.... and again... and again, he has no openings (for mage atleast because ending lag on attacks means you will eat a spear if you try) to attack him while he does this which just drags out the fight. - Spider queen. I quite enjoyed her fight, from what I saw it was a very fitting last boss of an area... and then she got to half health, climbed on the wall aaaaand she broke. She just sat on the wall doing nothing while I plinked her to death. - Minotaur. Hoo boy this where most of my complaints about mage arose from. So the minotaur, from what I've seen, his main game plan is to walk at you and do this large swipe. Occassionally he will throw his axes head at you boomerang style which you are supposed to use the opportunity to dodge through him and swap sides or spin his axe around himself. As a mage, you do not want to stand beside him because, your a mage, you are squish and you want to hit him with magic bolts from range, your max range puts you just inside the edge of his large swipe and with the end lag of mage attacks if you are attacking when he telegraphs the large swipe, your options are block or dodge, no running last minute. You can't dodge towards him because he is guaranteed to repeat the swipe attack and you can't walk through him so you take a hit, if you dodge away from him, he walks towards you until you are cornered and then you're out of luck because then he just repeats the large swipe which leads you to dodging through him and brings you to the situation where your dodge is on cooldown and he qets a free hit and you have to block, I'm not sure how it is for the other classes but mages block bar is tiny and takes ages to recover so you are guaranteed to end up in a situation when you are cornered with no block and your blink on cooldown so he gets guaranteed hits on you and with a mage standing at ~40 hp at that point, you die in 4 hits.quickfire small issues:  - Controller support. Why can't I use the d-pad to navigate menus? This just seems obvious - Ledge grabbing feels like you magnetize to it on occasions when you just want to fall past or you have a pair of broken arms and can't grab on despite rubbing your face along the ledge (Looking at you, totem poles in spider cave) - The shops, why does the game explicitly tell you that the shops boxes, which are the only thing available to you until I assume you get to the hub city, are more expensive? It discourages buying items and stockpiling money until you make it to the hub city making the experience more difficult, especially when healing items aren't replenished on reaching a rest point and healing is the most expensive buy in the shop.In summary, I feel there is a lot that can be improved upon but I can see this is a good game, I'll continue playing this, bashing my head against it to see what else is on offer and will update this later given what I find.EDIT: Beat the minotaur because his ai decided to non stop throw the axe instead of anything else then died repeatedly to the wolf-taur type enemies because I was punished for using my dodge to escape an attack only to eat a heavier attack, because they recover real fast, that STUNS you and you have literally no recourse but to eat another attack and die. Giving this one a break.

_childDocuments_.review: Dont be fooled by the current mixed reviews, this game is a masterpiece. _childDocuments_.review: A wonderful blend of top tier pixel art, retro-inspired music and seriously gritty combat makes Souldiers an enjoyable, though sometimes prickly, experience. _childDocuments_.review: Originally gave this game a thumbs down and I really didn't want to. Played through more of the game though and still think it's too beautiful not to love and the music and general style and polish is fantastic despite it's pit falls. What this game has going for it is the tight controls, the beautiful visuals and top notch pixel art and the classic SNES RPG style music. The music reminds me of Chrono Trigger and Legends of Mana. The aesthetics of the game was also very reminiscent to Legends of Mana. The backgrounds are all so lovely to look at and backtracking through them never felt like a chore as they are always a treat to see all the beautiful nooks and crannies of the art. The problem I had and the criticism I still have is the platforming is obnoxious and out of place in a JRPG style game. It REALLY stops your nostalgia high and happiness playing the game. I played it on Normal mode, and you can play it on easier mode if you want and I tried it. But the easy mode doesn't fox the core issue that made it aggravating in the first place, the platforming. The enemies were never really the huge issue with the game, just the platforming. And that can't be fixed in easy mode. I found myself doing a platforming section over and over and couldn't help but thinking how utterly boring it is and how simply unappealing it is not to progress in the game whilst also being bored at a part that wasn't fun, wasn't interesting or engaging. Completely ruining the momentum, the feeling of progress and unlocking new things. Just some stupid platforming you had to do over and over again, a complete halt of entertainment and fun. I would say this is it's biggest weakness. I would hope future titles by these fantastic developers will have less aggravating horribly boring unenjoyable platforming and more of the actual game to play. EDIT: I changed to a downvote. The platforming in this game is atrocious. It ruined the game for me. Got to fire level. I've since quite the game. I don't recommend this game until there is a way to TUNE DOWN the platforming. They have an easier mode but it does nothing to change the horrible platforming. What a shame. I didn't want to give this a downvote. If only I could get a refund from this horrible disappointment. I won't ever pick this back up again.

_childDocuments_.review: Not going to lie, it is an interesting game and I just beat a Minotaur boss (I have just started). The cave area was very draining but at the same time it held a grasp on me to finish it. So let me keep it simple after playing for 4 hours that felt like 8. Pros - the world itself is interesting, the enemies are somewhat creative, and the game refuses to hold your hand by constantly telling you what to do...it simply wants you to explore and learn. The bosses I faced so far are fun and let me think a little along with the puzzles and equipment.Cons - I played on the easiest difficulty and it still seems challenging as in enemies hit a bit too hard (so balance issues), the cost of items seem outrageous since you don't have a good source of income, and it is really draining (dark areas still make you take risk due to how much light is around)Conclusion - this game will be taxing on your soul, so I will put it this way. Love Hollow Knight and want this game to be exactly like it? then probably wait till its on sale or skip it. Love Flynn: Son of Crimson and want this game to be exactly like it? then try it out. Mainly walk in knowing this game will demand a lot from you but is its own game. I'll try to finish this by the end of the month (work life and being old lol) but i do recommend if you need a challenge.UPDATE (AFTER 12+ HRS IN)Easy mode is not very easy at all, leveling up seems to be ultra crucial (enemies/mini bosses/ bosses from the Spider Cave don't compare to the horrors in the Pyramid I stg). I do love the puzzles but it is somewhat repetitive. So once again new pros and cons.Pros: You can definitely see the game devs love their work.Enemies aren't mere copies of the previous enemies you faced so farSometimes the level is too interesting to the point you lose track of timeThe allies aren't merely standing around during combat and serve a purpose to assistPuzzles are unique and fast travel spots are not scarceBosses I must admit, regardless of difficulty, I love the design of the bosses I have seen so far Cons:I should've noticed before but the jumps required to advance are like too precise, like wayyy too precise for the player to always have to do (wall jumping is a chore to get used to)Leveling up feels like it takes forever, along with making enough moneyFlying enemies in this game are so accurate with moving back and will stay out of reach for some time (along with certain ones having a guard and can still attack while guarding wth)Along that line some enemies attack too fast, barely a split second cue, and have butchered me (on the easiest difficulty mind you with a full health bar)Conclusion - this game went from "you should buy" to "i wish it was on sale". Still having a decent amount of fun but I'm playing on easy (why are enemies wrecking me constantly). I plan on playing the hardest difficulty next month. HOWEVER...the balance issues, the constant grinding, and minimal reward makes you feel exhausted like your actually the souldier yourself taking the hits of life (in that way the devs succeeded).I'll end up putting a play-through on YT & keep pushing with one more edit after a few days. Good luck to any souldier out there, hopefully devs at least fix the balancing. And if I may add one more thing, defeating bosses feel amazing (at least for now).---FINAL UPDATE (WAYYY OVER 24 HRS)-------I'm simply going to say at this particular moment I'm not frustrated or annoyed anymore. Souldiers is its own game and I believe the devs are actually caring and working on fixing the issues...That being said, the tech area is insanity (almost like the pyramid but worst outside of the freedom to leave when you want). The hovering/flying enemies, enemies that can teleport, constant status hits, and hunt you down as if they have no limitations (Blink i believe is the creatures name aka little rat thing) is crazy. All this can be forgiven if it wasn't for the insane mini boss, Dark Claw. He moves so quick, you can't think or play like your still learning (in a bad way) . He can cause bleed damage AND has an ally droid who causes paralyzing status.  None of this matters to me if there were actually a sensible pattern. Every mini boss/boss all had a pattern that you could work with and understand when to hit without getting hit. My scount is going swing for swing with him.But I am happy to say that I will be waiting on the update and leave my scount on pause because Dark Claw is crazy. Mind you I'm on the easiest difficulty the game offers. I still love the game because I can tell the devs went full on into it, its just the balance of too much and too many.Wish you luck if you pick this up, cant wait for the update, still a beautiful game. Hoping for DLC and possible new classes.

_childDocuments_.review: My main summary of this game is "it's a shame".When the game started the art style and to some extent music reminded of my early teens playing Final Fantasy 3 on the SNES. I was captivated straight away, this had the looks and the story, I was hoping it was going to be amazing.After a few hours of play time as an archer though, I'm left disappointed on the whole, mostly by the control scheme and character mechanics. The character controls feel jarring and delayed, every movement seems to want to make the character stop dead instead of flowing nice. Grab a ledge, stop dead as a new input is required. Jump or dodge to the side and a certain amount of lag grips your feeling and moving around feels like an actual effort. As if the game is fighting back at every turn when you just want the player to move around. I tried to excuse it and say I just needed to get used to it, but I didn't. It annoyed me. A lot.The game starts off fine but then feels slow to play physically and initial progression is also quite slow. After a couple of hours I got bored and just didn't want to explore because it was too much of a chore moving around.Unsure if it's just a class thing as well but the archer class feels poorly designed. You can shoot straight in front of you, but there is no "hold a button to free aim" option, meaning if you want to shoot at angles you either have to be moving or jumping.This isn't ideal as it means to shoot anything slightly above or below you, say stood on the edge of a ledge, you either have to drop down to be eye level with it, meaning you get a shot off and it hits you because of the delayed input on the character movement. If you are a bit more adventurous you can jump up and down on the ledge and angle the analogue stick diagonally down hoping that when you aim at the enemy it is both aligned with the shot and you don't fall off the edge of the ledge and open yourself up to a hit. You'll miss a lot as the enemy just wanders around randomly and you're stuck aiming at 45 degrees.At this point given how annoying it is to actually shoot at an enemy (the fundamental mechanic of the game after movement) I'd rather the archer just aims AT an enemy without me having to tell him to when you're in range. Much like Dead Cells does when it recognises an enemy is in rage and nods to the fact there is no free aim.Even Super Metroid in 1994 had a moderate amount of free aim with the collar buttons (45 degrees up an down) and for a character that predominantly works at range, the archer can't actually hit anything at range without being dead in front of it for the most part. If that isn't bad enough you're limited to shooting an entire 3 arrows before having to "recharge" with a skill that launches your bow out in front of you meaning you CANT shoot until it's both recharged and the bow has come back, is just bloody pointless. You spend more time standing around waiting or risking taking a hit because spinning the bow out in front of you has limited range and takes 5 odd seconds to complete. They've put a class in the game that is meant to work well at range and then removed most of the ammo and ability to actually aim. Why? Who play tested this and went "ah yes, this is frustrating, jarring and completely not fun, keep it"A lot of people have said great ideas and art style but poor execution and I can only agree.The first level upgrade came fairly early on but the next one requires 3 additional levels on top of that and after a few hours of play I still hadn't got there.I'm just going to put this down and either replay something else, hollow knight, or another metroidvania and just shelve this one. A real shame, if it actually controlled well and some thought was put into making the mechanics enjoyable and useful it could have been great. But it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: So I should point out this is not a bad game, but the mixed reviews you see on it are not baseless. I am so mixed on this game because it's a solid game dragged down by one core mechanic you can't really fix with patches. It did feel good to beat the game, but I never want to play it ever again.I only beat it because I liked the demo, bought the game on release, and I'm the gamer that goes out of his way to BEAT video games. And deep down, I really wanted this to be a hidden gem that gets overlooked but the further I played through it, the more soul-draining it got and the more I wanted the game to just end.The Good:- The game runs very smoothly. I did encounter a couple bugs but the game otherwise runs smooth as butter.- The art style is INCREDIBLE. It reminds me a lot of SNK arcade games like Metal Slug and I just love all the character designs, environments, and enemies.- The Orb system is pretty cleaver as each element has a different effect and the ways they are used to navigate the map are pretty well-thought out (mostly).The Neutral:- Combat is good and there is good variety but I found that I didn't really need to do any of the spells/abilities I got because the most effective system I found for bosses was drink a Crit Up vial and spam light attack while dodging. Even for higher difficulties, i don't see why you would use the spells I got, at least when I was playing the Scout (melee fighter).- The Secondary Weapon system is mixed. I found I rarely used them in boss fights or regular fights as they suffer from the problem of a few being really good and the rest being worthless.- Bosses are fairly good but there are times in which they do feel unfair but the challenge comes from learning their patterns and coming into the arena PREPARED. There were one or two fights that just outright SUCKED for me but it's not too bad if you keep up with upgrades and side quests.The Bad:- The level design of the dungeon is the biggest problem in that they are WAY TOO LONG. This is the biggest problem I have with the game in that it is not fun to travel across the levels of the game. And that's saying something considering I replayed Elden Ring for the forth time BEFORE this game, and that has a MASSIVE map.- You are in control of way too many spells, items, and attacks for the amount of buttons you have and the pace of the game. For example, I would lose a boss fight more than once because I had to stop moving so I could hit DOWN on the D-Pad so I could scroll through my items to get to my health potion and then hit UP on the D-Pad to drink it. And by the time I did that, the boss would do another move that would hit me before I could dodge. And as stated earlier, you are going to forget you have abilities or be frustrated when getting a new subweapon because it's not gonna be as good as the most basic attack combos.In conclusion, its a really solid game dragged down by soul-draining levels that go on and ON. And it's a shame cause this game could have been a hit, but Hollow Knight or Dead Cells this game ain't. But if my reasons do not discourage you then I'd recommend picking this up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: After putting 50h in the game and completing my first run at 100% on hard, I'm sad to see so many negative review as even if the game has issues, it is still a very good game.First as many other review already explained, the game is hard, can be frustating and its mechanics are particular BUT it is fair. Indeed you can't spam the roll or the block but you lust alternate them to avoid being it and again, the game is fair, all enemies and bosses have precise pattern which can be all dodged if you know what to do.- You take too much damage and you don't have the time to learn what needs to be done.- The game use chekpoints mecanics. if you diej, you return to previous checkpoint with your progression lost. Some checkpoint are truly too far apart and you can lose up to 15min.To avoid these, I suggest to start the game in easy mode as you will take less damage and enemy will have less HP so you will die less often and will be able to learn the mechanics of the game with less frustration.A lot of the review told that only scout class is viable, and al the other are unplayable.For the sake of testing, I played 3hours with the archer class (in normal) before making this review and I was able to go prteety far for this little time. I don't find it that hard, a little harder than the scout but if you use all your arensal it is clearly manageable. It is probably the same with mage class. ( I will update this review if mage class is indeed too hard).Now that I have addressed what was the major issue most player have with this game, I will make a short list of good point and bad points with Souldiers- Excellent pixel art- Nice soundtrack - Most bosses are really good- A lot of exploration and some secret to find. ( It reminded me of the old metroidvania games)- Once you master the mechanics, the game is very rewarding.- Quite a few bug present. Some of them really annoying- The menuing is clunky and you have too many items. It pake using some item a chore and it can kill you the time you select them- Input lag sometimes- The game drop frames when a save is in progress- Can be frustrating in some placeDespite the issues the game is still really good and it will be a shame to miss it. Moreover, devs are working on fixing a lot of the bugs. If you can, give it a try ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I intentionally chose the Warrior difficulty on Mage class because I feel that its a good playstyle for myself. I did have some trouble on some of the bosses and content (not anything that took me more than 10 minutes though), but I thought that was because I chose the hardest difficulty and I guess it did deliver. A lot of the comments here are quite frustrated with some of the difficulty aspects so, why not just play on easy mode? As for the complaints on the melee class, you dont have to fight every flying enemy. Thats why the melee class is designed as a tank, so you can absorb more hits and be punished less. I could make the same argument saying that the mage class is terrible at fighting grounded melee enemies as well, but thats not the case.One thing that I do agree with however is the spacing of checkpoints and the cost of items. Health potions should not be an exorbitant 100 gold just for 20 points of healing, especially seeing as gold is an essential item to progressing the level of your equipment and sub-weapons, which gets expensive quickly.I also did think that the pacing was rather slow at the start of the game, but it did get better for me as I unlocked some of the new passive abilities. The pacing should be much better in my opinion, especially if you plan to play the game on all 3 classes. This should include quality of life features, cutscene skipping and modified numbers (shop prices, enemy stats, etc.). I really do see the passion put into this game and I hope that the rest of the game onwards will deliver what the first few hours did not.

_childDocuments_.review: 76.5 hours in, at the last boss and I am just fed up with the cheap and/or inconsistent mechanics that I have encountered in much of this game. A lot of the platforming mechanics are very inconsistent and janky. For example, the speed run mechanic when you're on top of lava doesn't work at times creating a lot of frustration. Another example is the double jump mechanic coupled with the dash because sometimes it just does not work when the buttons are pressed. To say that the bosses are bullet sponges would be a severe understatement. This is even an issue with some of the normal enemies even when using amulets that show the elements that are their weaknesses and I have the proper element equipped. I have also been hit by projectiles from bosses and normal enemies that were nowhere near my character in-game.There are plenty of other Metroid-vania games that are put together well and function correctly. Avoid this one unless you enjoy mechanically inconsistent games with bullet sponge bosses that have attack patterns you have seen in a thousand other games in this genre. At this point, even though I am at the literal final boss I have uninstalled the game and have no plans on attempting to beat it. It's just not worth the frustration. Lastly, I played this on the new Steam deck, not a PC so there is no excuse for it to not work properly so I can only assume these flaws are within the game's design itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I played post patch on the hardest difficulty as mage (100%) and thought the game was kind of too easy ngl. There's *really* any non-linear exploration as the zones have to be completed in a set order and are gated by event triggers. Sure, you can backtrack to get some minor upgrades, but it really didn't feel worth it. Most of the chests are filled with garbage, usually about as much loot from a single mob or two. Consumables are kind of busted, and once you start hitting the mid game you'll have enough money to just restock all of them at every save. Just chug flasks can you'll win most fights, especially with the mage's clone ability that does a ton of damage. If you run out of mana, just get most of it back with a potion and keep spamming your strongest attacks.Sub-weapons were kind of meh, except for a small handful. Outside of getting some fast damage on some early bosses or abusing the fire scepter late game, they just didn't seem to do much damage, even maxed out. It felt like enough of the enemies that were tough enough to use them resisted the neutral damage type that it was hardly worth using. I was somewhat tempted to play ng+, but when I realized I was locked into the same class I beat the game with, and that the vast majority of the dialogues and cutscenes were going to be unskippable, I passed on it. A decent amount of the conversation is even "background text" where you can't even spam to get through it faster! With that combined with the triggers that prevent you from doing zones out of order (getting the upgrade and going straight to the next dungeon for example), essentially meaning no sequence breaking, I didn't really see the appeal of playing a second time.Art was great, music was okay, but the story was kind of just kind of whatever.  I really didn't feel like I got anything meaningful from the story.  It didn't seem like anything meaningful was at stake. I never got attached to any of the characters (the closest *might* have been Melian, but not really), and there was nothing that seemed to really threaten them either.I had fun playing the game, but I honestly still can't recommend it. It's too rough around the edges. Play it if you need something to help burn 25-40 hours, but don't expect much from it.

_childDocuments_.review: *Important Note* This review is based of of not having finished the game. I’m about 40+ hours in and I’m also grinding more than I probably should because there are some serious boss-walls in this game.So it seems like “soulslike” is a genre that is becoming increasingly popular. One can probably also call it masochism as well and there is definitely a market for that. Fromsoft has taken the crown for themselves, but other titles have released that stick to the “die a lot to learn how to beat something” method of gameplay. Enter Souldiers from Retro Forge. It’s also a challenging experience. Is it worth the hair loss though? Let’s break it down together.Side note: I was about 30 hours in when my wife pointed out to me that it was called Souldiers and not Soldiers. Which seemed about right as my soul did die a little bit at a time playing this game.One thing you notice right off the bat is that they went for the 16 bit aesthetic and they did it very well. They take you back to the Super Nintendo era with some awesome talent. It’s a very gorgeous game and it shows in the attention that is paid to details in a lot of places. The animations of the characters while you’re talking to them. The lighting is great! The smoothness of the movements (which is nice, because they could have gotten away with not having as many frames in the animations too). It’s also the little touches like kneeling down to put out a campfire as a person leaves the area. (Great paralaxing as well.) Once again, it’s the attention to detail that really impresses.Moving on, you’re not the main hero here. You’re not even a general or some soldier of great renown. It looked like the game was going to start off somewhere in that area, but then doesn’t. You’ll still interact with a number of the NPC’s that I swear I was going to play as, but they are there as a narrative pushing device. (I kind of wish I had Brigard’s giant sword though.) Oh, and you’re apparently dead, but only technically dead. So there’s that. You all “died” and are now working with some Valkyries… for some grand purpose? Maybe? The story is still developing at the point I’m at in the game. Sorry…When you get to, you’ll pick between the caster, scout and archer. The classes are very different in terms of gameplay. The scout is the tankier of the three (as one would expect with a shield and heavy armor) and he also hits like a truck. In that sense, he’s also the easiest class to pick up and play. Swing, swing harder, block and dodge. The caster comes off as easier with baddie seeking magic missiles, but there’s a catch as well. You must be close to a baddie to be able to cast these spells and you don’t have as much HP. You do have a few extra moves like a powerful blast of pain and you can leave a copy when you dodge and then explode it. It’s pretty sweet. (It’s also the class I continued playing on after trying all three.) Lastly is the archer, who I originally thought would be the easiest to play. However, you need to be close here as well and you have only three arrows that go on cooldown after loosing them. The arrows have a damage drop-off so if you’re too far away your arrows do no damage. If you run out of arrows, you could either wait for the cooldown or get in closer and throw your bow which decreases the weight. You also don’t have as much HP as the scout so this is risky. You do get some sweet dodges (if you can time them correctly) and retaliate with a blast of arrows. I’m personally horrible at the timing. It also seems that you can’t do it from every enemy attack, just most. Soooo… either it’s trial and error or I’m missing a tell. (I’m also horrible at the scout parry too, but I’ll get it eventually.)I tend to find myself running back and forth to save points to get my health back and not lose the progress I’ve made. It’s pretty frustrating to plow through a few tough opponents and then level up only to die on the next baddie (who isn’t a boss) and have your progress reset back to the last save or checkpoint. There are plenty of enemies that I have struggled against and got better at fighting eventually. However, there are times the game will fill a room with multiple tough baddies that don’t respect my boundaries. Every enemy has a pattern and you will (hopefully) learn them in time. Still, knowing the patterns when there are multiple baddies throwing attacks at you feels fruitless at times. That’s where the main skill you need comes in: patience. Without patience, Souldiers will eat you alive. The more I step back and take my time, I do a bit better until I start bunny hopping and casting magic willy-nilly. It’s’ not the best tactic, but sometimes it feels good and the timing is easier than the dodge.The challenge is real here. There are a good amount of tough opponents in the first few areas. You might be thinking that it’s fine. Then they lock you into a room with a new enemy type and you’ll keep respawning there until you win. Enemies that you’ve gotten used to suddenly get more difficult when you’re locked into a room with four or more of them. Then they introduce rooms with a whole lot of **** flying around and you’ve got to dodge it or get impaled or poisoned… or poisoned and impaled together. Take your time. Also, remember to use potions. This isn’t Resident Evil and you can easily buy more health potions. Goodness knows I’m guilty of saving a potion for “when I really need it” only to die a few seconds later.As you progress you’ll level up and gain points to put into your skill tree that will unlock different abilities to add to your repertoire or allow you to wear more than one necklace. This is also why I’ve grinded so much. However, as I’ve done a bit of grinding, I’ve come to the realization that leveling up is useful in two aspects. First is the points you get for your skill tree (as I mentioned already) and then as a full health potion. Nothing is better than leveling up after a tough fight and getting all your health/stam/mana back. Dying right after that is the rough part. I tend to try and find time to go back and save my progress. Doing so also (unfortunately and good for exp fortunately) respawns a lot of enemies so you’ll have to fight your way back to where you were… which could have you taking too much damage and running back to the save point again etc. etc. On the plus side, saving also respawns all of the breakable stuff so there’s that. (Need to get that second tier achievement for breaking thousands of more things! My inner Link beckons!)Final Score: Tasty!Unlike some “killing you” platformers, I do plan on continuing to play Souldiers after this review goes up. Most in the genre will give me to much frustration and when I can be done with them I am. While there is a lot of dying in this game for me and I have no idea how much farther I have to go, I still want to beat this game. It is difficult, but I’ve overcome so many different obstacles that I want to finish this up. I may even try the archer out again and work on my timing a bit more with both he and the scout. It’s tough and I’ve face-palmed more times than I care to mention after having leveled up and thought “I’ll just clear this next area” only to die and lose that progress. That’s just a testament to how much fun I’m having here. (This may have been different if I wasn’t so prone to hugging the save point as often as I am.) The game runs so stinking smooth and if not for my terrible reaction speed most of the time, I’d probably even look cool playing it. This game is an easy sell for people who really enjoy platformers with some soulslike seasoning sprinkled on top.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like leaving negative reviews because in most cases, faults of a game don't overshadow the positives.Not in this case.I'm not going to cover everything that I find wrong with the game, so if you're wondering whenever to buy it, do yourself a solid and at least skim over mostly upvoted negative reviews. You'll know what's wrong with the game beforehand.1. Visuals and audio are definitely this game's strengths, The game's presentation is gorgeous, and that's coming from a person who's sick and tired of "m-m-muh pixelart!" indie games. Controls are fine for the most part (with the exception of no support for mouse, in a PC game).2. Difficulty is a bit tricky to judge objectively, but after all of the "nerfs into oblivion" that happened with the only patch that came out very soon after the game's release (AFAIK), it seems okay. Not frustratingly difficult, but also not braindead easy to a point where you just press the attack button repeatedly and beat the game.3. Combat. Keep in mind that I played as Scout, the melee focused class. That said, combat is, as others already pointed out, rather shallow. You meet a new enemy, you get hit, you learn their pattern, you deal with them. That's about it. Secondary weapons are often a meme not really worth using in most cases.Dodgeroll is on a somewhat long cool down and for some reason, if you dodge out of enemy's attack range (which is most often melee) you'll have to run back to the enemy to hit them. Interesting design decision. If an enemy has a multi-hit attack, it might happen that you dodge the initial strike, then proceed to get stunlocked by the remaining attacks. Cool stuff.Blocking is very precise and does nothing else than just preventing damage. There's apparently a skill that gives you an opening if you block properly, but since the skill points are limited and you don't know what's coming before you level up, you might as well not risk speccing into something if there are more interesting options in the future. Which, again, you have no idea about until it's "too late". Also, you cannot cancel your attacks by blocking in the right time.Enemies will interrupt your attacks (including secondary weapon use, which consumes ammo anyway without releasing a projectile), but you can't interrupt their attacks (at least not from the start).4. The Metroidvania element of the game, which in this case is mostly just backtracking to open chests that you couldn't previously get to and will award you with currency, consumables or crafting materials. Maybe an equippable item if you're lucky. Genre's staple branching paths, shortcuts to other areas etc., are very few.5. The game doesn't shy away from classic era memorable design ideas like off-screen projectiles or surprise enemy attacks that you don't have enough time to react.6. Puzzle/platforming elements are a hit and miss. One thing to note is that, contrary to what some developers might think, waiting isn't a game mechanic, nor a challenge. You're just waiting.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally give a game about 8 hours to see if I really click with it or not. On paper, Souldiers looks great. In play, the combat feels tedious, and the exploration feels one-dimensional. The devs clearly have a passion for this, as evidenced by the effort put forth in the art and creative direction. Unfortunately, their lack of experience in creating balanced combat shows. I feel like their two options were "souls-like" or "SoTN" and they flail about in the middle. The difficulty seems uninspired. More health on enemies, less health for you, etc. All that does is make things more monotonous. I'm also not a fan of being committed to movement using the analog stick. This is a pixel art game, and would have worked wonders with a d-pad. If you're a stickler for audio, the constant footstep sound will be grating. Footsteps in a game should be very low, almost non-existant sounds especially for a main character. Large enemies and bosses should have big sounding footsteps. After an hour I had a headache. The enemies are uninspired. Slimes, bats, kobolds, etc. The art style leans towards 'cute' rather than functional. Most chests are money. When the platforming is difficult for the sake of being difficult, you start ignoring chests. I dunno. I think the idea was good, and would have been a nice game if another studio made it. I don't recommend.
