_childDocuments_.review: On the surface, the game's good. If you look at a specific area, it'll seem overall fine. But when you dig deeper you find out the game's great potential was just so poorly executed.For reference, I played Archer on the highest difficulty.Platforming: you can only ledge grab if you jump right on it, jump too far and you'll go right through the platform or slide on the wall. If you dash into a ledge, you phase through and can't grab it. Also jump height is tied to how long you press, so you might fail to clear a big step with a double jump + wall jump when a big double jump is enough.Combat: Archer gameplay is very mediocre for half the game. Limited arrows you need to replenish with close combat, fast damage falloff basically forcing you in melee range, first skills require holding a button (either waste an arrow and/or hard to platform while charging) for little upside... trap's useless. And even the "good" ones can't use your current element... many key enemies are resistant to regular damage, making those skills so bad. Having the final skill be the auto-aiming arrow when you're stuck shooting in only 8 directions is ironic.Enemies: there's good variety, I'll give you that. But cheap tactics are so overused. Flying enemies which are so annoying to hit. Ambushes from a hidden spot behind a wall. Enemies that teleport onto you. Invisible enemies.  Stuns you need to spam buttons to escape from. Auto-aiming projectiles that go as fast as you (btw when you shoot, you can't move). And of course, raw high damage with multi-hit combos that can empty your health on the spot.Bosses: Overall pretty cool, a shame that high difficulty only seems to make them damage sponges that can tri-shot you.Inventory: Prime example of what not to do - stack every equipment and consumables on the same screen and have both the Dpad and analog stick navigate in different ways that mess with each other. Also shoutout to the invisibility potion, which is useless. Also, you cannot select what goes in your "quick-select" list, you have to go through every single item even if useless or too valuable to waste. Subweapons are neat, but most are meh (especially for the cost) and half don't tell you their damage type clearly, besides bombs you might use a handful... you don't need to scroll through dozens of them to swap item.Side-quests / map exploration: Putting both together because they have the same main issue - clarity. No way you're supposed to figure out where X or Y is without a guide, there's no indication to help find most secrets, you have to blindly bonk into walls. Some quests gave me hint for the wrong area entirely.Pacing: Areas are HUGE. You can go 20 minutes without finding a checkpoint, if not more. And the sections you go through aren't easy either, but you gotta clear 3, 4, 5 of them to get the next checkpoint... or go back to the old one to heal. Got hit by a BS ambush? Welp, too bad, try again. There are "checkpoints" but they're pretty useless, you mostly respawn at the last save point anyway. Oh, and if you're fighting a boss and there's a pre-fight dialogue or tutorial? Yep, you're getting it all back every time. Got stuck in a gauntlet room by accident? Hope you are prepared, cause your options are to beat it with the heal you have (retrying this over and over), or reset to last save. The last side-quest in particular is a looooooong gauntlet where you start with a bunch of single slimes spawns, and end with enemies that can easily take you down.QOL: Some features are locked behind specific accessories. Things like seeing enemy health, enemy weakness, magnet pulling coins etc. Some are missing entirely, like the ability to warp back to last checkpoint (given how long you can go between two...), or the ability to store excess items you find in the wild - or at least buy them later, it is frustrating to find a valkyrie feather and lose it forever because you already have one (because they're so rare you better die and retry than waste it).Last, but definitely not least - Bugs: I have encountered so many bugs in my playthrough, it's impressive. Multiple times I've hit a spike in the sewers, and I would continuously get hit by it again - recoil included - until I got far away or died. There were areas clearly designed to use the water power, but I couldn't use it there. In the last dungeon, I explored half of it until I noticed my map wasn't drawing and only had the spawn and my current position. And bugs include achievements. I have cleared my save 100% yet I am missing 14 achievements, including 12 for boss kills and one each for beating the game and unlocking all skills. Most likely because those achievements are for clears on non-easy difficulty but they only check for "soldier" or "warrior" difficulty, not "master"...So overall, the game is... okay. Some bits are neat, but a lot of frustration incoming. I'd call this wasted potential, I hope they learn from their mistakes if they do a sequel. I kept pushing because I was already too deep in to give up, but you can probably find something better to play; this game will make you feel you're wasting your time.

There's a lot of different items and a lot of different enemy types and creative attack patterns. And the economy is actually balanced. I never feel like I'm drowning in money, like most games. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good for the price. Whatever bugs it had on release have been reduced (never had crashes, had 2 breaks that were solved by fast traveling or reloading). The complaints about control are not valid - it's not as fluid as Hollow Knight, but it is still reactive enough to allow fluid platforming and fighting simultaneously. Some of the balance issues with skills are problematic, but only for the first few levels. As you gain mana, this issue tends to go away but early on it's a struggle to keep your mana up. Dungeons are huge, so you have a trade off of a lot of content with a lot of map management. Having said that, if you're playing metroidvania games, discovery and quality of life stuff like minimaps really shouldn't bother you enough that you can't overlook these issues. It's actually somewhat fun to find a spot you missed on a map - it's ironic that people playing games with intentional mystery like Tunic will likely complain about an easy to follow mini map in a game like this because it isn't explicitly intentional.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, what a crazy game. Up until now bigger has been better when it comes to metroidvanias. However, this game breaks the trend. Despite being the second biggest metroidvania I have ever played, there are a lof of positive and negative things about this game with one standout positive aspect that makes it a must play for people in certain regions.THE BAD:- Probably the worst thing about the game is the combat. How the developers expected you to dynamically change your element orb while in the middle of combat is beyond me. The devs also thought massive shantae style dungeons filled with dark souls style combat is a good idea. Luckily the dark souls aspect was toned down in later updates but they still cause a lot of unnecessary frustration- There are quite a lot of bugs in the game although the more serious ones have been patched out. Still, I did need to restart the game twice from two gamebreaking bugs- The game has been abandoned by the devs following negative feedback despite their regular patches and the fact that they put all their eggs in their basket and that basket broke.- A few enemy encounters are extremely frustrating and unfair- The plot is about as good as the plot of the mummy. Not surprising since this game is the Metroidvania equivalent of that movie.- The game is linear and progression is story gated. It is debateable whether this is a metroidvania or a zeldalike.THE GOOD:- Graphics are great- sound effects are good- music is good- world is big- great secrets- great level up upgrade tree- However, the best thing about this is the PRICING. The baseline price is 20 dollars and the exchange rates are adjusted to the old rates from before 2022. _childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, however after a few hours of gameplay on Master mode, I'm feeling this game is too rough around the edges and lacks the polish and care that could have potentially made this a stellar classic.On paper, everything is here to make this a great of the metroidvania genre. However, the reality is that the end product feels incoherent and rather disjointed in design and could have most definitely benefited from going early-access to gain early adapter feedback.I would have preferred a single difficulty that was specially curated to be both difficult and fair. Like literally, why are 4 difficulties available? This game is trying so hard to have souls-like difficulty, which it does achieve to some degree but it just seems to have been cobbled together without being fully play-tested.It's tough to say where things really went wrong for this game, but I feel like the underlying issue is that Retro Forge made a critical strategical error in their decision to work with a publisher for their game. There were most definitely outside forces that strong-armed them into making decisions regarding accessibility and difficulty, and more importantly the pressure of meeting project deadlines on time. The knee-jerk reaction from the publisher to make the game easier for a wider audience (which isn't a bad thing inherently) has corrupted the soul of this game, and it is now twisted and warped into something it was never meant to be.The difficulty dilemma could have easily been solved by adding in a souls-like character creator style system, where at the outset of the game, the character has the option to come pre-equipped with specific weapons / armor / trinkets which significantly reduce difficulty (items that can be found in game during later stages but a player starts with to make it more accessible). So, a player starts the game on one difficulty and then selects a predefined "loadout" so to speak.But all of this is neither here nor there, and it's all ancient history at this point since the game is dead and no longer receiving any further updates. I feel like the issue at it's core is that at some point the developer's vision for the game got lost, which is unfortunate because the pixel art is charming and leagues above what currently exists on the market. But as we all know, graphics and art style cannot carry a game to success, and there just feels like a severe lack of polish around the gameplay which is just sad at the end of the day.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews until I've completed the game, but I feel this one deserves it, specially given the many negative reviews regarding difficulty and gameplay.I'm roughly 2 hours into the game and I already love it. This game has so much charm! The soundtrack reminds me a lot of Yoko Shimomura's work on the Mana series, specially Legend of Mana. The pixel art is also very reminiscent of Mana in terms of aesthetics and details, but it also reminds me a bit of the Tales series.The game is a Metroidvania, but many people are comparing it to the "Souls-like" genre because of its difficulty (and probably its clever pun); it simply has nothing of that. . Yes, the difficulty, even on Soldier (Normal) is very unforgiving, but the game gives the option to swap between difficulty settings at any given time, so don't feel ashamed to play on Easy; there is nothing wrong with that. And considering the game has very generous automatic check-points, it's not that hard.I have some small nitpicks so far (such as being unable to navigate the menu with the directional pad when using a controller), but nothing that hinders the experience. Would also be nice if there was a small visual indicator of the timer for the dodge cooldown, aside from just the character flashing.I'll leave a better detailed review after I complete this game, but combat feels really responsive. Simple and easy to grasp. Kudos to the developers. You can really see this was a title made with love and care.________________________________________ I've finished the game and played with all the classes, as well played again after the big patch on June 23rd that tweaked a bunch of things. My final thoughts: Souldiers still is a fantastic game. It does a lot of stuff right, but has a few hiccups that prevents it from being truly remarkable.✅ Gorgeous pixel art and animations. Characters look great. Enemies look great. Environments look great. They call it a "16-bit" retro game but the quality of the pixel art is definitely on par with 32-bit.✅ Amazing soundtrack. Incredibly catchy. I had the chance to actually ask the composer himself, Will Savino, about it, and he said that Chrono Trigger, Donkey Kong Country, Final Fantasy VI, Tales of Symphonia and Golden Sun were among his inspirations to compose for Souldiers.✅ Combat is tight and responsive. You can cancel almost any animation on the ground with the block button, and as you unlock new abilities, you get more mobility and better crowd control.✅ The three classes are very distinct, each having its own strengths and weaknesses, as well a diverse talent tree.✅ The Scout is the standard melee class. He actually hits the hardest among the three characters, at the expense of requiring to go close combat. His gameplay is snappy, very straightforward and feels great to control, dishing out damage while blocking and parrying enemy attacks.✅ The Archer is the long range class, able to snipe enemies from safe distances, but able to hold on his own in close combat thanks to his ability to throw his bow like a boomerang. In many ways he plays a bit like Samus in her classic 2D titles as he can aim his bow upwards, downwards and diagonally. The arrows actually run out but refill over time. I didn't enjoy this class very much, but it's quite powerful and mobile.✅ The Caster is a high-risk high-reward class that uses a bunch of magic attacks to pelt enemies from afar, but can also engage in close combat to decimate its foes. The Caster has the weakest basic attack of the three, but his attacks will launch guided bolts that will hit enemies from mid-distance, making it the safest class in the game as he can cheese a lot of enemies. It's the class I personally most enjoyed to play with; it starts the weakest but becomes a powerhouse in the late-game.✅ Lots of stuff to discover, secrets to unlock and materials to level up weapons and armor.✅ The story is actually pretty interesting and filled with lively characters. It ends on a cliffhanger and also has plenty of unanswered questions; I assume they either have a DLC in mind or even a sequel.❌ This game has A LOT of flying enemies, which often makes the Scout suffer a bit. While they fixed the AI of said enemies to make them not fly away from characters so much, it still is a bit obnoxious.❌ Sub-weapons are, unfortunately, practically useless, specially against bosses. There is a massive bunch of them, but they're very situational; not to mention that rather than recharging automatically, you have to collect shards to refill them, which drop  from enemies or can be found in small treasure chests. It is best, for the most part, to save your sub-weapons in case you find a breakable obstacle to destroy with the bombs. A real shame and wasted opportunity.❌ Even after the patch there are still some weird performance issues, such as occasional stutters out of nowhere, minor graphical glitches and even the dreaded ending black screen (which devs said they will fix on June 27th -  they did).❌ Revisiting previous areas after getting new power ups to hunt for collectibles can be very tiring, especially in maze dungeons (like The Pyramid). This game really needed a map marker that has become staple in a lot of Metroidvanias.❌ The major dungeons are very, VERY big, to the point they kinda overstay their welcome. I would've preferred a larger variety of smaller dungeons, personally, especially since the puzzles are quite creative.❌ Sometimes particles are so intense they clutter the screen. The screen flashes also are a bit distracting and there is no way to turn them off.❌ The game has a New Game Plus, but other than pumping up the difficulty there is little to no reason to play it again. Would be nice if there were new content or new abilities to acquire on it.❌ The June 23rd patch may have made the game a bit  easy, though this is easily remedied by just playing in the highest difficulty. I wonder if the devs plan on adding a "Very Hard" difficulty in the future to please the more hardcore gamers.___________________________________________________________Overall, this game is great. I had a lot of fun playing it, and with all classes being so distinct, the replay value is great.This game BEGS for a co-op mode, though. They could add a Survival Co-op akin to the colosseum fight and could really be something fun that would keep the playerbase alive for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: In some ways a pretty good game with some fun aspects.  Sort of metroidvnia like, but mostly straightforward rather than exploring.  You do need abilities to get around, but you don't really need to backtrack much to find new things.  Most areas you can do better than 80% on first visit.  You only go back if you really want every thing for completion sake. I recommend against it though because a few difficulty ramp ups against enemies and several rather annoying side quests just really distract from the quality.  Multiple bosses and some enemies feature attacks that are basically undodgeable and unblockable, mostly because they happen before you can tell where the enemy is.  If you sit around holding the block button waiting for an enemy to attack, you will block the attack, but then you aren't trying to fight the enemy, you are just waiting for them to hit you. Enemies that travel into your space then attack before you notice they are attacking, bosses that do the same, and some quest and platforming quirks are enough annoying parts of the game to have me say that the game is meant only for someone that only plays games like this to perfect them.  This game is only meant for other people if they play on easy and don't want to 100% it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly a mixed leaning towards the negative review.Really polished visually but extremly flawed in the gameplay and technical side.First of all having to make a game defining choice that you have to stick with for the next 15+ hours of gameplay as the very first choice you have to do just makes literally no sense and your gameplay experience can be extremly conditioned by this without basically any warning, pick the wrong class and essentially you're just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ buddy, have fun restarting the whole game from the start and losing those 15 hours of progress, same thing goes if you wanna 100% the game.Secondly the controls for this game are just absolutly terrible and I cannot believe these got a pass, unless you play using a claw grip the button mapping for this game (which you cannot change) is extremly unconfortable and later in the game requires finger and hand combinations that are physically impossible unless you play with a specific unconfortable grip. This combined with the fact that this game cannot make up its ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mind on if it wants to be an exploration game or a precision fight and platforming game lead to needless frustration when you either let go of a button combination for a single frame leading you to take damage that instantly teleports you backwards to the beginning of the whole platforming sequence or you miss your whole combo on a boss because the game registered your analog input at 44° instead of 45° making you attack the wall like a total idiot and waste all of your stamina leaving you open to free damage while dealing none back.Thirdly, this game is just way too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ long, metroidvanias for the most part aren't really that long when you look back at them, if you know where to go you can beat them in a couple hours sometimes even under an hour, in this game every single area feels like a full game, every area is way too big, now it's arguable if this is a good or a bad thing, but, for me, when you're so in an area for so long exploring every single corner of it and all you get as rewards are basically useless currency that you just stockpile like crazy and have literally no use for, potions that you can't use or 1/4th of an hp upgrade, you really just feel like the game is wasting your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time when you get to the 4th/5th zone thats basically just this all over again, same thing goes for most of the sidequests, you'd think for the amount of effort and time that they ask of you that they would at least give you something useful but most of them just give you useless garbage like more coins or gear that you probably already have better versions of.Lastly I don't know wtf the other reviews are on about they must have not played enough of this game but yes it is still buggy, now it's not unplayably buggy as I assume it was on release, but even today it is still buggy you will see random enemies stuck in walls or floating stuck in midair, you will sometimes hit enemies and deal no damage, your attacks can sometimes register hits on enemies twice with a single attack, the camera can forget waypoints and sometimes it just teleports to random points in the map when its supposed to be showing you something important, now again most of these aren't gamebreaking, except for the broken enemy spawns when you get locked in an arena that only opens when you kill every enemy, but mixed with all the other problems when one of these bugs forces you to restart the game and you remember how long ago your last save was it gets really hard to resist the urge to just say "♥♥♥♥ it" and just quit the game completely.

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving a review early to let people know I recommend this.  I'll return later to edit this after I complete the game.EDIT: I'm 8 hours in.  I still recommend this game, but it has caveats.  There are strange difficulty spikes, and not all of the classes seem to have the same love applied to them.  If you have a love for SNES Metroidvanias, you will find a lot of fun here, it's just mired in a few baffling design choices.I don't tend to spoil sections of the game, but I am making an exception.  The second dungeon locks you in when you enter it.  This is at a point in the game when you can upgrade your weapons, armor, and items, but only in the main city.  This dungeon is both long and difficult, and it's feasible that a player has done minimal upgrades, which leads to a scenario that could be incredibly frustrating.   This is one scenario of several that may make you scratch your head in confusion over what was happening in the mind of the designer at this time.I cannot in good faith give this a thumbs-down.  It's too beautiful and has too many great ideas to be in my negative category.  However, it only barely gets the thumbs-up.  Do your research and see if you are willing to look beyond the aspects that may trip you up.  Alternatively, you can wait and see if the game improves.  As of this posting, the updates for the game are signaling some big changes, but it's still unclear just how big those changes will be. _childDocuments_.review: It’s a recommendation with caveats. The game offers a broad spectrum of enemy variety, beautiful pixel art, a large world to explore with diverse biomes, and a decent story. The pixel art especially stands out. However, there are several missing quality-of-life features that I would expect in games released after 2015.For example, you cannot zoom into the map or set your own markers, which has significant consequences. I often forgot which route I was planning to take after checking my map, or which paths were inaccessible due to missing abilities. Additionally, the bounty system only specifies the biome where the target is located, without indicating the exact position within the biome, which feels like a waste of time.The game has a checkpoint and save system, but they are not the same. If you explore a map, travel to a town, talk to people, or visit other biomes and then close the game, you lose all progress. The only autosave I encountered was after defeating bosses. While I understand this design choice ties into the game’s lore, it feels disrespectful to the player's time.Spoiler Alert: The last power-up you acquire is the ability to sprint. I found this frustrating, as I had already spent so much time walking everywhere, searching for hidden secrets. Receiving the sprint ability near the end of the game, when it was least needed, felt like a wasted opportunity. It would have been much better if this ability was unlocked early on. The maps are fairly large, and walking everywhere quickly becomes tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish i had not. Wow, great game. This was a meaty adventure leaving me wanting for the sequel.  Feels great. Responsive, fluid, multiple specials(magic and stamina based), and a Element Weakness/Resistance system with Debuffs. Your character levels up as you get kills and will get points to learn new moves and buffs. Most enemy attacks are well telegraphed and never seemed unfair, you have a dodge, block and jump to deal with them.   I chose Warrior. The difficulty felt perfect, not too easy not too hard, nothing ever felt unfair or too random. The hardest parts are the boss battles (as it should be) but once I stopped smashing the attack button every second and learned the attack patterns i dealt with them pretty quick. Also several types of healing and buff items to make it easier which you can buy and upgrade.  Yes this is a meaty game, but felt finished and not padded out. Good level cohesion, themes, and lots of secrets to find. By the end i felt like I had my fill and was done. I did not play NG+ much but it is there and you retain some... stuff. I played as a swordsman, you will need to also play new save files as a mage and archer to get all achievements.  Interesting enough, i was curious to see how it ended. There was some things i would have liked touched on a bit more . The best part is the ending and it really leaves off on a cliff hanger. I do hope they make that sequel!  Hidden gem, one of the best metroidvanias iv played since Hollow Knight. Now to go back to waiting for Silksong...

_childDocuments_.review: this game stops being fun pretty quick and it really doesn't get better. the art is beautiful and the music is good, but the game itself is just not fun.first off, the dungeons are huge and the layouts are great, and normally this would be a good thing but there is very little to make it worth the effort of exploring because the vast majority of the chests contain a few coins or an item you're already carrying at max capacity. the exploration is also very frustrating due to the developers love for destructible walls that look mostly like normal walls and walk-through walls that look EXACTLY like normal walls, so I hope you like rubbing your face against literally every wall in the game looking for that next secret passage. the quests are also quite terrible, they tell you the general area you should be in but don't give any hint what room you're looking for, so you will end up wandering aimlessly in massive dungeons you never managed to complete blindly looking for the quest target. I did a couple of them this way, but after an hour or so you'll want to just look at a walkthrough. on paper this game looks like exactly what I'd want, but the execution lacks basic considerations for the player and the longer you play the more annoying the game becomes. this game would have benefited a huge amount by taking a less-is-more approach and polishing the best parts of the game instead of dragging out the mediocre parts for so long. this is a 15 hour game that wanted to be a 40 hour game and it becomes a slog very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, fun game, especially if you're a Metroidvania fan.I love the mega dungeons and the different class / skill system. Played on the Warrior difficulty the first time, caster class and it was great. Not a single fight was auto-pilot (well I don't count slime fights lol) which I appreciate very much. A single mistake can throw you off and punish you immensely and EVERY single thing in the game is fair, meaning you have nothing to blame but yourself if you die - big plus.Secrets are done very well, had a lot of fun figuring them out, and there are A LOT. Nothing beats the feeling of "ohhhh I got this new upgrade and I know 10 places where I can now access, hopefully there's Ragnarite there :P"Brilliant orb interactions with the environment, for example setting the grass/bushes on fire which yield extra HP, loved it the first time and the 100th time I did it. There are so many things, I don't want to spoil too much.As for the negative side, I have 2 issues with the game.1) The secondary weapons / consumables / bombs / orb - switching system. Should've had a more convenient way to use bombs and secondary weapons without switching through it for ages. Bombs (all types) are used way more, at least for me, so they could've been separated from the secondary weapons since they're the only ones used for exploration (they can share the shard system, I don't mind that). You can always pause and select an item, but it kills the pace of the game, at least for me. Orb switching as well. Should've added a wheel system for it since it's not PC only (just implement it on the right analog stick) and for the PC there could've been hotkey implementation for each orb. These QoL changes would be huge. I find myself in fights focusing more on switching orbs, weapons and consumables than on the actual fights (which are all challenging - huge plus). Instead of enjoying the fights more I'm just annoyed that I misclicked one too many times on the item switch and oops the potion is now 8 clicks away again... Or having 2 secondary weapons in the rotation so far away from each other... It gets bothersome really quick.2) SOME side quests. Once again, love the mega dungeons, but the "Find this one unique enemy in this massive dungeon that you already completed and without any hints or location marks" are annoying. Easiest fix is to just have it marked precisely on the map where to go, that's it. These enemies are very challenging, no complaints there, just this QoL would've made it so much better.Also that side quest that requires you to collect 20 items from defeated enemies. Again, explain which enemies we need to defeat ESPECIALLY if they don't have 100% drop rate. Or give them a 100% drop rate and players will figure it out easy.These 2 issues that I mentioned are really REALLY minor. You can always look on the internet for side quest info, not a big problem. The game is great, hard recommend if you're a Metroidvania fan looking for huge dungeons/zones.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great example of a fun and original metroidvania with its own style. that I highly recommend. worth $20, but even better if you can get it on saleFor the Pros:The combat is tight, with split second movement and positioning being key and there is content galore. So far, the story has a lot more promise and charm than your average indie metroidvania. There is a leveling system in addition to new abilities gained (which help in both traversal AND combat via an element system) and a weapon/armor upgrade system that encourages you to sniff out every nook and cranny for chests containing materials. My biggest surprise is the sheer amount of sub-weapons you can find in optional chests that all have different uses and each one can be upgraded 3 times for more power. you get to choose from one of 3 classes at the start of the game that all play very differently as well. there is a decent bit of challenge to the game, especially with the boss fights, but nothing a metroidvania fan can't solve in more than 5 tries, plus the checkpoint system makes it easier to respawn close to major points in the map instead of that one save point you were at 20 mins ago. For the cons:I saw in reviews before I installed it that the dungeons you go into run too long. I initially blew it off thinking that they had never played a long metroidvania before. I do understand what they mean now though. I am at a little over 10 hours in and I have only just gotten through my second dungeon and visited town once to upgrade my gear (headed back now). THAT SAID! The dungeons are long, but the level design is great and in both dungeons I went into, I came out with multiple new abilities both for combat and traversal, having fought several major and minor bosses. once you get out of a dungeon, you REALLY feel like you have progressed!My other gripe is that there is no way of testing a class before you start and you are stick with that class for the entire game, so if you want to try out a new class, you will need to use one of the other save slots to start a new character and play around with them before really committing. This is necessary because each class plays so differently. That said, the variety is very much welcome.my only other gripe is a minor one but messes with me constantly. once you get the wall jump and double jump, you can't use the second jump off of a wall jump, so if you need some extra height while jumping between walls, you need to get your second jump off right before you grip the wall. again, very minor gripe, but I had 2 major bosses in the 2nd dungeon that required a lot of platforming/wall sliding and it kept messing me up

_childDocuments_.review: Greatness alongside flubs. Mixed reviews are unfortunate but understandable. Souldiers is leagues ahead of most competitors when it comes to sound/music, art, and in some aspects even level design.Pixel art: more impressive than most I've seen in years. Reminds me of the best artists back in super nintendo and playstation1 days. In many ways it really compares to the greats working on the old Final Fantasy games, and other jrpgs like breath of fire. Whoever handled the art must be inspired by that age of gaming. Music as well. While it may not be Nobuo level, it's much more than background noise. The art and music add so much to the game because they're not the least bit amateur. These people (creators of the art/music) are obviously very talented and kind of carry the game.Combat is good. It does nothing innovative, but has all its fundamentals done well and feels great. The only complaint I'll make is that the item system is TERRIBLE. It works like dark souls except you can't remove items/weapons from the list, so you're fumbling around trying to scroll through way too many items and screwing everything up because of it. You also cannot see a preview of the next item. Based on the game wanting you to use certain potions at certain short windows, I am amazed at how bad this is. You can switch items in the menus/pause screen, but this is an unncessary pain especially since the menus are kind of trash. Other than this rant, combat is engaging and well done most of the time.Why mixed reviews? Mostly it's the insanely long dungeons. They're probably 2-4 hours most of the time. For most people it's really a slog and damages otherwise good map design, good battle, etc. They really overstay their welcome, and start feeling like work. Not to mention having to listen to the great music for hours will definitely lessen their impact eventually and possibly get annoying. Not because the songs aren't awesome, but because that is way too long to listen to 1 song. What I will say is if the dungeons were shorter, much of what's going on them is quality. They are simply too fatigueing in the long run.The overly long dungeons also screw up the pacing. The dialogue and character built into the game are good, but you hardly get any relief since most of the game is spent in dungeons. The dialogue just like the rest brings me back to more traditional jrpg storytelling. It's charming and has character. But you get only a snippet as you're stuck backtracking around dungeons for so long.I like this, for sure, and was very close to loving it. It's so close to giving that snes/ps1 vibe.

_childDocuments_.review: Souldiers is a solid metroidvania. Given the expanse of the game and some wonderful art it is in some regards surprising that it is not more popular. I would argue "soulslike combat" is a bit of a stretch, but there are certainly some difficult fights, particularly early on.That being said, Souldiers does come with its share of flaws. From small things like spelling/grammar to awkwardness like having thirty sub weapons to cycle through. Only once did the game actually break and that was an enemy not spawning correctly in the coliseum forcing a restart.So, if it is at its base a good game, not succeeding at being more enthralling must come from little bits all over the place. Perhaps the theme of 'generic fantasy' is a difficult hook to pull off well. Maybe a lack of characterisation? There are characters in the game to make the story, none of them are offensive, but they don't manage to stand out particularly well either. The aforementioned excess of subweapons and other similar gameplay beats like having to pick one of three classes at the start? Maybe. It can certainly be improved upon, perhaps allow the freedom to switch between the main classes, and refine the extra weapons.There are many ways that Souldiers can be worked upon. There's plenty of set up in the story for a sequel. I still enjoyed that a lot of the time I was actually reminded of the Megaman Zero games, and overall I still enjoyed playing a decent Metroidvania.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review the game works perfectly, looks stunning and is an easy recommendation for all players out there looking for a tough and lengthy metroidvania. Extra recommendation for players with a completionist itch, since the game is transparent about your completion percentage in each area. Just one warning: the dungeons can be very long.I reached 100% completion as a Mage just shy of 50 hours, on the 2nd hardest difficulty out of 4. There are other 2 classes which play quite differently, but you cannot change class in the same playthrough.---The All-time Steam review score for this game is due to it being release in a rough state but it has been patched to hell and back both regarding bugs and gameplay tuning. In my whole playthrough I experienced zero bugs, loading times were fast and the gameplay felt solid and balanced.Nowadays, a lot of those reviews are unfairly outdated and the Recent Steam review score is much more relevant and informative. Since this is a very easy recommendation, I am going to spend a few words concerning a couple of points that I think require additional attention.ART AND ANIMATION: The pixel art in this game is outstanding, but I was not expecting the animation to be so phenomenal! Especially at the beginning of the game, I was in disbelief in front of the high-quality animations that almost every character, foreground and background elements have. Everything moves with plenty of frames and from that point of view it is incredible to think that this is made by an indie dev studio. The screenshots cannot do this justice because you must see the pixel art in motion. It's a 10/10. Similarly to Death's Gambit, the developers have developed animations for all attacks and people often find this kind of combat clunky because you cannot cancel all animations immediately. I think this is a design choice and in short you as a player need to move in a deliberate way.DUNGEONS: One common criticism to the dungeons of this game is that they drag on forever. It is undeniable that dungeons are very long, however the quality is pretty high and more than half of them are compelling. I thought that I was subtly guided towards the next tortuous path about 80% of the time, while the remaining 20% I was opening the map and could quickly identify unexplored paths. Frankly this is how dungeon crawling should be, instead of railroading players all the time or mislabelling long corridors as dungeons. I came to the conclusion that either this criticism was justified on release, or that the real issue lies in the fact that the dungeons are all very long despite the fact that in the first dungeon you have way less combat and traversal abilities to spice up the gameplay than in the later dungeons. You do not reach the major hub before completing the first dungeon, which is highly unusual. I agree that the first few dungeons could have been trimmed a bit, but I think we all think the same way about certain areas in any other game. In any case, because of this, some of the latter dungeons are a highlight of the whole game.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: A lavish and sprawling platformer, most similar to PS-era and similar generation portable fare.  There is an amazing amount of detail in animation and sound design, such that still pictures simply do not do it justice, and the soundtrack punches well above its weight.  The negative reviews had kept me from it for some time and I regret that they had.I'm playing on the highest difficulty and it feels like where it's supposed to be, relative to the games of the era - bosses are a little tanky and regular mobs need some attention to get by, and you can freely change the difficulty (though I'm seeing it through thus far).  I honestly prefer this to any of the Wonder Boy remakes, and that's saying something.  Just know that the first two areas do give a bad impression in the sense that you do have to get through a BIG area to finally get to the anticipated town, and not long after you become trapped in another BIG area until you finish it.  Still, once you hit your stride it's just fun to play, gorgeous to look at, and varied enough in enemy arrangements and behaviors (and there are a LOT of unique enemies, considering) that it holds your focus.  Fast travel is well implemented and while saving resets enemies (a la Dark Souls) there are more frequent auto-checkpoints that at least prevent losing too much progress if you die.Oh, and there's a New Game+ and a total of three classes to play through as, so you're definitely getting your money's worth in terms of game-per-dollar.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: This game ticks all the boxes a great game needs. Good enemy variety, stunning visual appeal, large and interesting level layouts, solid controls, replay-ability (3 character classes), adjustable difficulty to suit a range of players. It's all here. Overall you cannot go wrong trying this one if you are into the genre.Additionally, The game world here is very large for a metroidvania (dare I say too large), so expect to sink an above average amount of time into this one to finish a play through. Moreover, some enemies have specific item drops (Not required though) and the drop rates are very low which will add a lot of additional time if you decide to hunt for them.I had some technical troubles with controller detection when using a dualshock 4 on bluetooth wireless. Using the steam controller assist got it to work but you'll have xbox360 visual button cues in-game.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: It's overall a really good game. Read at first that it was too difficult, but after updates it seems very easy to play with some moments of difficulty. The main positive is that it is a true souls-like metroidvania: a truly large map with memorable locations and enemies, combined with some hard but rewarding dungeons. The negatives are two: some dungeons take too long to complete and have large areas where, after hours of exploration, you get new objects that add little to your arsenal. I kept most of the weapons I got at the first 1/3 of the game, to be honest. Second, the lore is a bit disperse and uninteresting at times. Fun to play, with some important flaws. Recommendable at large.

_childDocuments_.review: The production quality of Souldiers in exceptional. It's equal parts challenging and beautiful. And IF you're a hardcore gamer you'll love it.That said; this review is more for the CASUAL gamer on the easiest difficulty. Someone who may not want to spend dozens of hours perfecting mechanics or enemy patterns but rather just explore the gorgeous world of Terragaya and interact with awesomely designed NPCs like the cute and charming Sirfiel, or the funny and quirky Euder.  The easiest difficulty lives up to its name and combat is not difficult at all. You can completely face-tank bosses and win if you wish to. The levels/areas are beautiful and expansive, which to those who enjoy exploration, should be a treat. But sadly it can be more frustrating than fun; with the feeling being one of 'Jeez, get me outta this place already'. Why is that though? For me it was two things: 1. Enemies. In most metroidvanias with backtracking and traversing the same areas multiple times, enemies are mostly fodder - easy to kill or run away from so they don't get in the way of your purpose for revisiting previous areas. Enemies in Souldiers are no pushovers. They attack relentlessly or continue to chase you (and even teleport to you) way beyond what you'd expect. They won't kill you on easy mode but rather just become an annoyance that you have to stop and deal with every two seconds. 2. Precision platforming. While most of the platforming in Souldiers is fairly straight forward and simple, there are times it will throw some precise maneuvering your way. For a casual player, the only thing worse than precision platforming is precision platforming on a TIMER. It's used sparingly but when it does it can be frustrating to attempt a platforming section numerous times only to run out of time or be knocked all the way back down by cheap projectile placement. I don't want to get gud, I want to get back to Sirfiel. I highly recommend Souldiers for players who like a challenge. I think that's who it was made for and perhaps not for casual players. And for casual players, it'll depend on your tolerance or how easily you become frustrated.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write video game reviews, but this one deserves one because it is clearly rated below average. It gets a perfect 5/5 from me. Let's start with the rpg/metroidvania hybrid: well-structured, it allows you to play with three very different types of characters, all of whom are well-balanced.Also, four difficulties are more than enough in my opinion.The game is difficult and requires you to use a lot of resources, but it always introduces them slowly and allows you to choose which ones to use. The graphics are excellent (though I found a couple of levels uninspired, but that's just my opinion) and there are numerous animations, some of which are unique or extremely specific, which will astound those with a sense for such things. This game was created with passion and devotion, and it shows. The details are minute, sometimes overwhelming: fruits that grow when hit by water attacks, grass that burns when hit by fire attacks, unique animations when using certain things in slime form, and so on.The dialogues and npcs are numerous, pleasant, and more than adequately written for the game genre. Despite the fact that the protagonist is our avatar and is mute, some scenes are emotionally charged.It does, of course, have flaws (some musics that are a bit too hypnotic. the inability to store some important items that, if already in your inventory, are lost because the chest no longer contains them, forcing you to reload the game and leave such chests closed to store the items, ecc.).Overall, however, this is a must-play title for anyone who craves a bit of a challenge and a metroidvania with rpg elements and a lot of good ideas and care.Last note to the programmers: screw you for the pyramid level. I hated every f***ing second I spent in that infamous maze. I got lost at least fifty blasted times in that hellhole. Now I hate egypt. excellent work on everything else (joking)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal!The extreme negative reception this game has gotten is a genuine enigma to me. It ticks all the right boxes and scratches all the itches. It is pretty vast. It took me about 10 hours to really feel like I had penetrated the surface of what it has to offer. It has expertly crafted pixel art, catchy OST which captures the essence of the classics which inspired it, super addictive gameplay and wonderful progression system that doesn't take too many "innovative" risks as seen in many other titles attempting to stand out from the crowd. As far as metroidvanias are concerned, Souldiers pretty much has it all. It's not a flawless game, however. There is some level design, particularly in some of the dungeons, which I found pretty boring and sometimes grueling (a particularly caustic combination) and it has clunky potion and sub weapon systems. But these flaws are entirely overshadowed by what the game does well, and that's everything else. I can see how these flaws would be unacceptable to some people, and that's fair. Many people complained about game breaking bugs. I have not encountered any, but if others have, then their review is certainly warranted. Others also gripe about how the latest version of the game is too easy... I never played the earlier version, but I'm the kind of gamer that appreciates all the "grind and punishment" a tough RPG can throw at you. Souldiers' Master difficulty completely satiates my sado masochistic gaming desires. In short, the game's overall negative reception is nothing short of madness. For fans of the genre, Souldiers is not a game you can afford to sleep on, or disregard due to this enigma.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: Souldier's got top notch pixel art graphics and it might be some of the finest ever. The artists even include plenty of artistic flourishes with environmental story telling. I was particularly impressed by the desert area in this regard. That area really tells a story, music and sound effects are equally high class.It's a complete package with excellent stage design, controls and story, but...When it released, it started off real rough with *insanely* high "Dark Souls of Metroidvania" difficulty. To the point where it was pure bullcrap and this left an indelible mark on the Steam User Score. I still finished it pre-nerf before it was re-balanced by the developers. Now it's much better and I will do another proper playthrough in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best metroidvanias ever made. _childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'd like to point out that i enjoyed this game.I really like plattformers and esepcially those with open world &/or hack'n slay elements.But the things this game hits off right, are quickly put to the side, as it's problems become apparent and annoying.First and foremost, the dungeons of this game. There are quite a few - and they are super confusing to navigate. You are super unsure where to go, how to reach it and when you should return to places. Add to the fact, that new items (weapons) are obtained at a pace, where you tend to forget they even have a purpose other than combat.In addition to that, the game outright requires you complicated and precise inputs, not only for combat, but for navigating the world as well. The times you need complicated movement are numbered, but they are fairly difficult, regardless.More than once i found myself running back to the beginning of a dungeon, just so i could view the entire thing from the beginning again, thinking i missed something important that i couldn't see on the map.Combat - outside of the mandatory bossfights - is fairly mundane. At no point in time i ever had the need nor the intention to grind level ups, as they are quickly capped at each area. This means you'd grind untold hours in order to get the same EXP of the following areas.TL;DR:Interesting concept, cool design, but unfortunatly a (very) flawed execution.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game but I cannot.  I played this game after the patch fix and it still has fundamental issues that are troublesome.   I used the ranger/archer class, I lost interest in the game after Dungeon 3, completed all but 1 side quest (a 3 part fetch quest with abysmal rewards), and defeated the final boss on Soldier difficulty (hard).I've always felt in metroidvania games, you are rewarded for exploring and backtracking.  Your rewards for exploring are abysmal.  You will find a hidden chest, open it, and get either a consumable, upgrade material, secondary weapon, amulets, or money/health globes/mana cubes/secondary weapon charges.The consumables are the most irksome - if your inventory is full the item will fall to the ground and disappear once you save or leave the location.  Doesn't sound too bad until you realize you can purchase all but the rarest consumables from vending machines at each save point.  The reward is that you can save 100 gold unless you already have the item then you lost 100 gold?  Bizarre.  This also includes the one per Dungeon revive option.  Didn't use your revive?  Too bad, watch it wilt away to nothingness.  So while exploring, you're hoping that you'll increase your power through upgrade materials.Upgrade materials fall into 3 categories: primary weapon, defense, and secondary weapon.  Primary and Defense have the same upgrade path/costs.  This means you will need X of Primary/Defense materials and Y Gold to purchase the upgrade.  The quantities increase significantly with each upgrade level.  I personally couldn't be bothered to find all of the materials (the only real gate keeper of upgrades) because the upgrades felt minuscule.  For the bow, the damage increase by +3 each level and I honestly don't even know if I saw a flat +3 damage on my attacks based on my tier.  If it does work that way, the archer does horrendous damage even with changing amulets and orb affinities to maximize weaknesses.  Upgrading the defense increase stamina by... a bit?  Stamina felt like it didn't exist as a Ranger/Archer as blocking one to two attacks would typically deplete the whole stamina bar leaving me guard broken.  Stamina as a whole felt like an underutilized mechanic (Ranger/Archer has an ability that can "dash" away from an attack and retaliate - the only good ability you learn).For secondary weapons, they fall into an easier leveling bracket: 1 x material + 50 gold, 2 x material + 100 gold, and 3 x material + 150 gold.  This material is seemingly sparse in the beginning but by the end you'll be able to easily level the majority of the secondary weapons to max.  Not that this matters.  There are a total of 3 useful secondary weapons, 2 of them are for exploring purposes and (this is a "spoiler") the only good offense one is Dark Axe.  The rest are fun to use once in a blue moon when you're bored but provide no benefit.  During bosses, Dark Axe is the most applicable for damage and you should primarily be focusing on your characters attacks versus the rest of the useless secondary weapon arsenal as your primary attacks can be augmented with amulets.Amulets are also found in chests and provide a myriad of bonuses.  These are about the best rewards you can get from chests from my experience.  Each dungeon drops amulets that are specifically designed to increase your defense of that Dungeon's primary element and increase your offense of that Dungeon's primary elemental weakness.  Enemies may also drop amulets.  If you do the side quests of hunting specialized enemies, you may also receive an amulet.  By the end of the game, I had so many amulets I didn't know what to do with as they slowly become obsolete.  My bag was full of amulets and it is a nightmare scrolling through the inventory system.  You can't wrap to the bottom by scrolling up and there is no "jump to next page" option.  You will tirelessly scroll all the way to the bottom as each amulet becomes a higher value and after 10 hours of this you'll be fatigued, at 20 hours you'll start to not enjoy this butchered inventory system.The final reward for exploring are generic chests with gold, health globes, mana cubes, and secondary weapon charges.  I was drowning in gold by the end, I could carelessly walk through a zone and spam heal and repurchase my used consumables with ease.  Health globes are nice to keep you afloat but also doubles back on negating the drops of consumables.  Mana cubes are a joke - use spells on generic enemies only, all spells were useless on bosses.  The element orb you've selected does not apply to the spell and the cast times typically left me getting hit.  The final Archer spell is a constant barrage of arrows.  Cool, except you stand still through the whole cast and can get hit out of it easily.  Hopefully the Mage class benefited from mana more than my Archer as I'm sure the Scout class was equally underwhelmed.  As an aside, I had more mana than I had stamina which was an absolute slap to the face.Exploring is also not a joke in this game.  This game is massive.  I thought I would love this but it reached a point of absurdity when I realized how large Dungeon 5 was and remembered Dungeon 1 and 2's size.  There's a point where too much is too much and it definitely felt that way after Dungeon 3.  This is also felt with backtracking as when you gain a new ability, you will access a new area but potentially be blocked by needing another ability later on.  It would be most efficient to wait until post Dungeon 5 to go back tracking which doesn't feel great.  There are also mechanical issues with exploration.Donkey Barrels are in the game and shooting at the wrong one would make the barrels disappear and you'll most likely fall into a trap and take some damage because you chose the wrong 50:50.  Minor but annoying.  Ledges are a nightmare.  You'll latch on to a ledge mid combat and get hit because you didn't believe you were going to grab it.  The game also has implemented that if you are not pushing towards the direction of the wall, you won't grab the rock climbing ledge but if you're on that style of ledge and push up on your analog stick, you'll automatically jump.  This feels unnecessary as this game is very much a platformer.  You don't need a "quick" jump option, we've been trained to jump at specific times.I loved Dungeon 3 but Dungeon 3 was also the most problematic for me.  There is an arena section where birds come out of the ceiling that you need to full clear.  Luckily, I had the habit of restoring all of my resources at each vending machine because I was soft locked in this arena 6 times.  The birds would spawn too far into the terrain and would keep sliding through the impassible terrain until they were outside of the arena.  These enemies typically obey wall boundaries so when they were outside of the arena you could not progress.  I mentioned restoring all of my resources earlier as I had to suicide myself 5 times until I was able to kill these enemies stuck in the terrain before they were outside of the arena.  Awful.And another gripe is the checkpoint for the last boss.  Do the first phase well or you will have diminished resources for the final phase.  It will checkpoint you as soon as you hit the second phase and store what resources you have used.  Granted, you'll learn that fight very well if you don't save your resources like I did.

BUT at parts of the game there are some masochistic platforming at times. also a few times game mechanics were not properly explained. wall grabs were a bit iffy too. besides questionable game design choices on platforming and sub weapons that lack power even if fully upgraded, i found the artstyle and story Quite enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Game looks good, but has difficulty problems. These problems don't come from the combat, but from the platforming itself, so the difficulty mode won't fix this. The Pyramid level feels out of place, being a more difficult area compared to the airship level coming after it. The second scorpion fight with the earth crystal and platforming is aggravating, expect to start over alot here. Platforming challenges that throw you back  upon hitting lava, especially one where you are a slime and jumping with fans pointing in certain directions. Crabs are immune to damage, except when sometimes they throw their claw out, then it is a 50/50. various times I would run across the lava and then fall in for no reason, this happened alot when running from ground to lava. I am glad I didn't play this when the game was first released, having to manage the platforming BS with enemies that hit twice as hard on normal difficulty compared to today's hard mode. The bosses came down to "deal damage before they kill you" except they became invincible and super aggressive and incredibly fast. The block and dodge are very unreliable in these cases. The dark razor fight when he has 75% of his area covered in a dust cloud. Here you can't leave the safe zone or you take damage (but the area is very small) and the boss is invisible. You have to block his attacks, but like I stated earlier, I ran out of stamina between his attacks and could not block anymore, so I had to dodge, but that threw me right into the dust and I took damage. With enemies and bosses that move quickly, the player feels unresponsive when you want to dodge or block to prevent damage.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm starting this review off with the following note: I am neither new to rogue-lites/rogue-likes, platformers nor metroidvanias. My experience with these type of games shape my review, please keep that in mind. Also, I have so far completed one play-through and am 80 hours into the game. Short summary of all my lengthy points at the end of this wall of text.Souldiers is one of the best indie platformers I have played in recent years. People experienced with these types of games will quickly recognize the various sources of inspiration. Souldiers imo makes all the best aspects of the genre work for itself.Souldiers is visually pleasing with character and background art as well as an awesome soundtrack that all has a lot of love for detail. It does not re-invent the wheel with its setting or the general plot of the game but it does a very solid job with a world that takes you captive quickly if you allow yourself to.Souldiers is hard. I have started out with the hardest difficulty and as the archer class. Some game passages - especially various platforming passages and mini-puzzles can send you into despair and may take you many attempts or require an online guide or video for you to figure out. Game mechanics, damage values, FOV and other factors have been overhauled with the first big patch and are now truly fair in my opinion but still by no means easy on the higher difficulties. But it is a worth a try because the game most of the time feels rewarding if you complete a difficult passage, beat a boss or get a hard to find item.As for the story, as previously mentioned it is superficially nothing to write home about yet the world, its creatures and characters and the plot still are very enjoyable and can rope you into this world in a way that just makes you want more of this adventure. I enjoyed it very much and I hope we can expect more games in this fashion from this developer in the future. To summarize:Souldiers is:- difficult but fair- loveable, detailed pixel art- great and very fitting soundtrack with very nice variety - fun and interesting game mechanics (3 completely differenct character classes with different skill progression system, gear upgrade system, level-up system, great variety of usable loot and secondary weapons to customize your playstyle and character values)- somewhat generic but very fun story that makes you want to learn more of this world and its inhabitantsall in all: - if the difficulty and some of the platforming and puzzling passages don't ruin this for you and you got the grit to bite through them, this game is one of the absolute best platformer/metroid-vania games in recent years and a MUST PLAY.

_childDocuments_.review: I stated playing this game before the first patch released and finished after it came out. Initially the game had a lot of balancing issues. Enemies did a lot of damage and had a lot of hp, and most of your gear was not useful enough to aid in this. It didn't help that the checkpoint system was very unforgiving, and everything, including health potions and ammo for your side weapons, cost a lot of gold. A lot of people compared this game to the Souls games, but as a fan of FromSoft games I couldn't disagree more. This game had a lot of balancing issues and I'm glad it received an update. Although I do agree that the devs overcorrected a bit, and now the game feels a bit too easy. But they're close to getting it right and I praise their efforts.All that aside, the game is great. The combat system is fun and engaging, its not just spam attack to win. The level design is great, with fun and interesting puzzles. And the story engaged me more than I though it would. Over all this is a standout metroidvania and I absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: Souldiers makes me think of a mix of Legend of Zelda 2 and Castlevania(which is an awesome combination to me). I see a lot of people are mixed about the difficulty, but whether its super hare or super easy to someone it doesn't mean you should give the game a negative review over just that the game should be reviewed in multiple categories not just one. That being said the difficulty is just fine to me and that the visuals/animations are amazing as well as the varied locations you will be visiting all look amazing. The music is pretty good, nothing that makes me pause just to listen to it, but not the less the music is not bad. The story is quite good it isn't super deep, but its very interesting paced well and the characters you meet along your journey are all pretty entertaining/interesting to me (plus I love their designs). Last but certainly not least the game-play is good its simple at first, but the further in you get the the more you have make use of the mechanics you learn along the way (aka the Zelda/Castlevania formula). Combat while not too hard definitely keeps you on your toes so as to not be super reckless. So all in all I definitely recommend this game, don't let the mixed reviews deter you as most of the negative reviews are just the product of a silly difficulty controversy that plague many games today and I rather not see a game with such love and care put into it be hurt because of said controversy.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no two ways about it, Souldiers is a beautiful game. Detail is lovingly crafted throughout all of the games main areas making exploration incredibly easy on the eyes. That is where anything easy about this game ends, and it turns into a murder machine hell bent on making you hate yourself. Should you decide to buy this, and I think it's worth it, be thankful that they patched this game. There were some glaring mistakes and balance issues that made this game frustratingly awful to play, but they've since come around and made a more balanced experience that most gamers should be able to enjoy (as playing on easy no longer feels brutally difficult). While I wouldn't say it will have the staying power of other high profile metroidvanias, it's a grand adventure worthy of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, gorgeous pixel graphics, very lengthy and previously really challenging. I only played the game with the scout so far, but the developers obviously put a lot of heart and effort into this. The new balancing patch improved the lower difficulties, but may have made things too easy for the hardest one. I'd suggest to restore Warrior difficulty to before, or offer an alternative classic mode to play the game. That way everyone, hard-core and casual gamers alike, can be happy. Balancing issues aside, I'm very happy with my purchase. Only other criticism is the abrupt ending - I very much hope for a sequel down the road!

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amazing game, the art is gorgeus, the music is fantastic and I recommend it very strongly! The game can be quite unforgiving at some points, but it's never impossible, you'll die a lot, but it's always a learning process that make for great challenges and great boss fights. The game also has some really clever usage of it's platform mechanics in some parts that are really fun to traverse and very satisfying when you discover the intended way to take on a platform.One thing I couldn't like though is that sometimes I'd come from a large platforming section and the game goes "oh those monsters you hate? theres's 3 of each in this room, also we're blocking the exits, good luck!", and even after barely surviving I discover that there's still another long platforming section before the next saving point, I used then to find myself being stuck doing these sections all over again after dying in the middle, things like that sometimes comes more like annoying than fun, still, this comes as an opinion of a casual player, so maybe I'm just bad at the game haha.The character skill tree was not the most impressive thing, as the most interesting powers are unlocked early on, and the rest are mostly passive upgrades of the previous abilities (I was playing as a caster), there are also some really interesting habilities you unlock by defeating certain bosses, but most of the time I found myself only using the basic skill set, that is enough that takes to beat most monsters.Aside from the parts that made me annoyed, I still think the game is really fun with a great atmosphere and satisfying combat, so I recommend it with all my heart despite it's flaws. I'd still caution that game IS very hard, so you have to keep that in mind of you plan on buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Souldiers

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to all fans of the Metroidvania genre. The pixel art is beautiful, the soundtrack is enthralling and the gameplay is quite addictive. Following the major patch (V1.1.1), a lot of difficulty issues people were talking about have been nerfed. The game still requires good reflexes and forward-thinking, but it isn't as unforgiving as it was at launch anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Dont be fooled by the cute anime characters, old school graphics, and side scrolling platform. This is more like someone injected some dark souls into a metroidvania. The map is expansive and full of secrets. The enemies and bosses are challenging, and frequently require some grinding and upgrades before you can hope to take them on. equipment makes movement in the game very similar to hollow knight, but the similarities end there, with a much more complicated elemental based combat system that has you flipping back and forth between elements just to attack different creatures in a mob. I think even experienced platformer players will find this game a welcome challenge, with plenty to explore, lots of upgrades, and 3 different fighting styles to play through. Its got a lot going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game. Lovely pixel art, great combat, nice soundtrack, everything was made with love.It's good to see some ranged characters in a metroidvania once in a while. Also, all the RPG elements (equipment, upgrades, level, skill points), alongside the 3 classes, adds lots of replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I have to say - I've read some of the negative reviews, and decided to go out on a limb and purchase this anyway.I am still in the first dungeon, but almost two hours in and I have to admit I am having a blast. This is scratching a very deep itch I didn't know I had.In reading the reviews, I've decided NOT to risk a "normal" difficulty playthrough and I am playing on easy. It still presents a bit of a challenge but you aren't punished too hard. First boss was a "warm up" for me, second boss (with the spear) almost totally wrecked me, but wasn't that bad once I got his patterns down and abused roll->jumpIf you are on the fence about this game and are afraid of the reviews, do what I did: Buy it, start on easy mode, and set a timer for 1.5 hours. If you dont like it, refund it. But if you're like me....you'll probably be having a blast!EDIT:I have put some serious time into this game, and this COULD HAVE BEEN a hidden gem on Steam.The game is plagued by clunky platforming/level design/controls to the point that several aspects of it are increasingly frustrating to the point of being outright playable.Day one bugs that should have been caught by the Dev's Q&A team and/or immediately addressed, are still outstanding.I want to love this game, and a part of me does, but I am changing my Yes to a No. The Developer has had time to address the GLARING flaws of this game, and they have addressed some, but not enough.If you are a diehard metroidvania action platformer fan, this game may scratch your itch, but go into it knowing you're going to have issues with the platforming and controls.Oh, and don't listen to the whiners who complain about how this game got nerfed. If it's too easy for you, play on the hardest difficulty. The balance changes that were made had to happen in order for others who play on easier difficulties to be able to actually progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo months ago when it was available and completely fell in love with the game's art and design. I was really looking forward to the full release but having finally played the final product, I have to say I'm a bit disapoointed in what I got.There has got to be a better way for players to switch between the types of bombs and potions they currently have selected. You need to go through several selections before you land on the bomb/potion you want and if you use controller like me, you probably have to resort to the D-Pad to do that, which means having to take seconds out of movement to pick the right one. Right now potion selection is uni-directional, so if you miss the potion you wanted because you were too distracted by an enemy/enemies, you'll have to go through them again. It feels like I'm an illiterate trying to read 3 books at once. Bombs can be toggled going left or right but because of the huge selection you'll end up gathering, it takes 3 days and 3 nights to pick the one you want in that moment. I wish there was a UI similar to when you change the element you pick. This has probably got to be the worse mechanic in the game to be honest. Most games with this mechanic allow for a few seconds of grace when you tilt in the other direction so the player has time to make the jump, but not here. Here you're a budget spiderman who manufactured his webslingers from those sticky hand toys. Before you jump to the other you have to keep the stick titled towards the wall you're currently on, then jump and THEN you can finally tilt towards the other side. It was already bad enough that you need this mechanic to traverse trap ridden areas and timed events, but then there are bosses that require you to use it too or die. It's very clunky, not smooth at all and needs to be worked on.All the characters are sexually oriented towards ledges and it doesn't matter if you're attacking or being attacked, they will elope with that ledge. Again, a grace period when attacking as the ledge comes into contact would be nice or just add a button that triggers it.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating my review after the major rebalancing patch. TLDR: The game was amazing and still is. The negative reviews here are nitpicking what is to my mind a top-5 modern Metroidvania. Personally, I didn't feel the difficulty was too high per se, though I 100% appreciate their adding checkpoints and optimizing restart/reload times, as these were cause for frustration. That said, there is a hard difficulty option which remains quite tough, so you can get that steep challenge if you want it. They might consider adding an extra hard down the road that eliminates life gain on restart and further ups enemy health and damage, but doesn't feel necessary to me. Combat is still much more involved than 99% of Metroidvanias, closer to a Hollow Knight or souls-like. The good: - Boss and mob design feels purposeful, designed to test each of the three classes in different ways. Enemy AI/pathing is good enough that each enemy feels like a meaningful challenge, however small. Nothing feels slapped together. - This is reinforced by the hand-drawn art and level design (hooray for no procedural generation). Everything is purposeful and tells a story. - Combat feels responsive and is dynamic, with different battles/boss phases calling on different strats. Way too many indie metroidvanias boil down to spamming a fast melee attack — combat is much more interesting here. - Fast travel. Yay. - Checkpointing. This was under mixed but fixed in the patch. Plenty of checkpoints.The mixed- The edge grabbing works great when trying to clear long gaps, but is incredibly frustrating when you inadvertently prompt a ledge grab (usually when jumping/dropping vertically to avoid an attack or trap). Basically the "hit box" is too big and not context-aware/there's no great user override. - When you die, you lose all items acquired between checkpoints. This means repeating tough, out-of-the-way platforming sections in some cases. This has become much less of an issue post patch.- Optimization. This is not a graphics-intensive game, but load times can be very long and the game stutters occasionally on my high-end gaming laptop. While some issues persist, the game is already much better optimized post patch.
