_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review as someone who actually really didn't enjoy Mutaizone (the previous game by this same developer) and I think they have really addressed some major design issues with that game in Saltsea Chronicles, really delivering on the strong writing and ideas that were already present in Mutaizone.I really disliked my time with Mutaizone because while the writing was strong, it was also very SLOW. Not very much happens in Mutaizone, and you get this slow plot dripped out over very long walks across an island. I'm generally a fan of media that allows itself to linger in spaces, but Mutaizone really pushed that even for me. The garden planting minigame also always felt very shallow and simple.Saltsea Chronicles, on the other hand, is fast and pacy. Things are HAPPENING, you're moving around often and plot is unfolding. You move around the various islands in a very fast way, and it's very quick to get the little drips and drops of writing. The writing is just as strong as Mutaizone, but is aided by the fact that you are actually doing something! Having a purpose gives all of the writing weight, even the things that don't directly move the plot forward matter more because there is a plot to be moved. I cried many times over the course of this game. That isn't to say the writing isn't variable, at its weakest it's reproducing very well-trodden queer romance tropes, and at its strongest it's plumbing the nuance of art, grief, and reparations. My biggest issue is that a game of Spoils (a trick-taking card minigame) takes three hands. It takes too long to play and disrupts the pace of the game too much. Even though I liked it I found myself avoiding it to not disrupt the game flow.In concluision, I highly recommend, especially if you didn't like Mutaizone, as weird as that might sound.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Well. Dunno. This is one of the games i would like to give a neutral rating.The story is catching, the worldbuilding great, the places you visit diverse, the (playable) characters deep and believable. There are some interesting twists and i also believe that choices here matter more than usual and you could get a lot from a replay (except for the main plot i think). This could have been a wonderful continuation of the great Mutazione (which i wan't to recommend, if you have not played it yet).But then there is the gameplay.Since all you actually do from beginning to the end is clicking though and reading dialogs.  The A or B answers you give don't really tell you what your character will actually say.  Let alone that you have to guess which of both your current characters is actually answering. There are no puzzles to solve or exploration to do. All is done for you, even the walking.I liked the minimalistic art style. Sadly i think it lacks in sound design and music. The game is far too quiet for my taste, what kept me at some distance (speaking about immersion).In summary this is a good visual novel (that you still read) with some decision making, but don't expect any game in it (besides an optional cards mini game).
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If you are considering trying Saltsea, because you loved Mutazione ... hang on for a second. In my opinion - and only my opinion - this title leans even harder on its writing (so much of it) than Mutazione, and the quality of that writing is significantly worse. There are too many characters, too many branching story possibilities, too much endgame exposition dump, not enough uniqueness, and too much general preciousness to make multiple playthroughs of Saltsea worth the trouble. The art is simplistic and rendered at the Where's Waldo-meter level. It is also frequently re-used. The world building is even more hippie-dippy and ignorant of actual human nature than Mutazione, without Mutazione's more fully realized scenario. It's almost hilarious in its earnest communalism. The main characters suffer from the same issue as Tacoma - too many psychosexual traits and themes crammed into too small of a group. Everyone is Special.Still, this title is ambitious. The branching story definitely shows its seams (especially when it comes time to select an onshore party), but it feels far less cookie cutter than something like Fallout: New Vegas or The Outer Worlds. Making something like this even appear to have consequential decisions with so many branching choices is pretty impressive, even if the content isn't consistently amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of Mutazione, the devs previous game, and played it at launch on Apple Arcade. I have been looking forward to their follow up and Saltsea Chronicles does not disappoint if you are into well written narrative tales.Like Mutazione, Saltsea Chronicles is narrative first (even more so than the former game, this is more akin to a pure visual novel) that features excellent writing, characters, a wonderfully unique art style and aesthetic and a great digestible chapter structure. As said, this is all about the story but the story is told via multiple well realised characters. There is a deep lore to this world but it is told via character interaction and observation and has a wonderful show/don't tell approach. There are branching choices in the sense of who will join you and where you will go that are unique to you. There is a card game included as well which I normally don't like but it is wonderfully simple and varies on location (as well as being entirely optional). My only minor critique which doesn't change my recommendation is spoiler related so.. . As a side note, there are characters and locations that I believe are hidden between choices, as well as character development. This is not a bad thing and gives the game more re-playability. This shows the depth of the writing but I personally feel that my choices were honest and probably won't play with different choices because I did what I felt was right to me as a player. Again, nothing to do with the game but I liked who I met and travelled with so will leave those memories intact!All in all, a great game if you like narrative tales told well with excellent world building and characterisations. In total I played for about 10 hours (my Steam Deck didn't register an hour or so of play when i was offline) and was excellent value.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of excellence, intentionality, and care. This game is better than most of today's prestige television. The indie team built a world as vibrant as any narrative AAA game, but it feels like they made it just for you. Instead of playing as one character, you play as an entire crew, and you choose where they go and how they approach the places they visit. Every location and character is meticulously written and animated, and the variety of people and places is jawdropping. The emotions I felt playing the game were so strong that the crew felt like a family. I want to see everything the world has to offer, and I probably will because of the game's novel save system that allows you to revisit choices you made. I cannot recommend this game enough. It will see you in a way no game has before.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgous looking game with a truly interesting fantasy/sci-fi setting that you really get to delve deep into. The story can veer a bit close to a soap opera at times, but swerves back to bigger and headier topics just as easily. I can imagine the fact that you can't retrace your steps can be frustrating (like, if someone complains stores are low, why not swing by that big trading hub again?), but it does serve to tell a concise story. Gotta mention Spoils, the card game based on  Bridge and similar team-based trick taking games. I love how well it plays and how well the island-based variants are developed. Some of the best variants tie into the theme of the island. I also love the 'hoarding' rule that completely flips the score if one team scores too many points. It ties in perfectly with the broader theme of the Saltsea, but also works well to add another layer of strategy to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Despite how much I love Mutazione, I didn't like Saltsea at all. Almost everything what I loved about previous game unfortunately didn't cross to the new one. Such as: great music, interesting and unusual gameplay, deep characters (the last one is arguable, I know).When I play a game, I expect to, you know, play at least something over than just reading. I can read... books duh. Or just don't tag your game as an adventure genre. Modern so-called adventure games just pisses me off. (We should name those genres like text quest or something idk, and it is not even text quest, because you are actually just reading, and all your choices doesn't do anything at all!)Characters delved into the side of liberal diversity, which isn't bad, if only they were believable and deep, which they are not, they look like empty pop capitalistic liberal agitation. I was exhaust by their social struggles at some point and didn't have sympathy to anyone. So to my opinion characters of Mutazione were dramatically better written.Zero soundtrack! What a pain. I listened to Mutazione soundtrack so many times.The artstyle is still kinda cute and the idea and the setting are nice, but overall it felt cheesy and incomplete. I'll give a try the next game of the studio though.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A robust conversation-based game allowing for some player agency in where the crew travels and how they resolve conflicts. Solid replayability, since many locations and characters can't be accessed in one playthrough. The illustrations are gorgeous, with a fun, interactive quality, and the characters and story are compelling and well fleshed-out. If you like the look of this game, or you enjoyed Mutazione, I hope you'll give this one a try - it really deserves more love!
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I already played the demo back in June and was already curious about how the final product would turn out. And wow, I didn't get disappointed. Saltsea Chronicles offers rich worldbuilding and a colorful cast of characters, all with their own struggles and secrets (and, well, a baby). The presentation is stellar - from the quirky characters to the breathtaking locations and the soundtrack. The game contains branching paths in a couple of chapters. These will lead to different islands, which are equally self-contained episodes but also connect back to the greater narrative. The writing takes you through highs and lows, from murder mystery plots and spooky stories to a post-apocalyptic religion, whose relics all stem from the present-day world. However, the apocalypse was not really an end to everything, but rather humanity's starting point for something new. Many conflicts and struggles of today's society have been washed over by the sea as people came together and reconnected with the world and each other. Saltsea Chronicles is a consoling story full of hope - a game about the things that unite us, even though we are all different and unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the game for the first time, and I know I will be replaying it many more times. The story is beautiful, heartbreaking at times, and very well-written. It's hard to create a game with one overarching narrative that also gives the player the feeling that their choices really matter, and this game achieves that. I enjoyed the pacing of each chapter. It would be very easy for someone to play this game in short intervals, if they wanted or needed to, without losing track of the overall story. I really enjoyed getting to know each character that joins the adventure. I loved seeing them all change, and grow, as they experienced new things. The issues system was very cool, and helpful. It made it easier to tell what choices would affect others, and also added depth to the characters and their interactions. It was also very satisfying to resolve issues! I really can't wait to replay the game, make some new choices, and get to know more about our lovely band of misfit adventurers :) i appreciate the accessibility features that were included. Subtitle size, font choices (a dyslexic-friendly font is available!), dark mode, and button remapping (for mouse/keyboard as well as controller) are all ones that I remember off the top of my head. I also appreciate the change in tutorial for the in-game card game (Spoils) from the tutorial in the demo. It was very helpful to be able to play practice rounds instead of just having the written rules and explanation. I also appreciate being able to speed up or slow down the pace of the game while playing it (Spoils). Overall, I absolutely love this game. I am a huge fan of their prior game, Mutazione, and have been looking forward to Saltsea Chronicles for a while! They absolutely did not disappoint. 10/10 will definitely be recommending to people!As a personal note - as an autistic person, seeing Iris stim and show other autistic traits was wonderful. I absolutely love them and it was very affirming to finally see someone like myself represented on screen - stims and all <3
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Got this because Mutazione was a great game, have to say this is just as good as Mutazione so hats off to Die Gute Fabrik, relaxing chill game...well it is unless you want to 100% it then it turns into a enormous beast that will have you shoving the blanket you rapped yourself in to relax right up your own cake hole.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I played mutazione, an earlier game of this developer's, a couple years back, and enjoyed it. aspects of the gameplay somewhat often slowed the experience down, but unmistakeable in the game was an abundance of creativity and heart. so when I saw that Die Gute Fabrik had released another bright, intriguing game with an even more intriguing cast of characters, I decided to lead gut first and check it out, with minimal pre-researchand I am so delighted I did! I loved this experienceto start, the art design is exceptional. lush. unrelentingly creative. the world and its characters are so gorgeously realized. and not just in the classic ways, like with its stunning color palettes, but also in how it interprets every locale, building, character.the character designs in particular are my favorite, in part because though they can seem abstract in style, they do a better and more meaningful job capturing the beauty and breadth of human visual diversity than every other game, movie, tv show, comic that stacks itself with template mannequin models. zo's nose, kittick's body, stew's eyes, amrita's face—I see these wonderful features in the world around me, but rarely reflected in mediaand this embrace of variety and diversity reflects in the game's themes and narrative. it's a story about community, and finding healing and growth and hope in connection. the crew as the main character is quite fun, and tending to their relationships via the choices you make at each island really drives home the importance of acting as a communityand mechanically, I commend how the game makes it so accessible to explore and tinker with save states and make new choices. the format encourages exploration in a way far improved from mutazione, and every chance taken to learn about the world of saltsea and its players felt so rewardingI have some potential notes on some final act storytelling choices that I'm still chewing on. nothing capsizing. but I do find myself wondering if they were delivered as well as they needed to be, or if that gnawing is just part of the experience. all in all, an absolute superb end-of-year surprise from what has now become one of my favorite developers. a sequel isn't necessary for the completeness of the experience, but boy howdy would I not be mad at one. I'll remain dreamsailing until then
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: - Multiple protagonists was challenging at first but quickly became second nature.  - Central mystery propels the story along with a nice sense of urgency- Every part of the game well considered and not a word is wasted.- The mini game is a welcome addition and I'm looking forward to seeing how that evolves.- A nice sense of agency from knowing that choices have consequencesLooking forward to unravelling this mystery and savouring the adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished chapter 2 of Saltsea Chronicles. I can say easily and already that this game is something beautiful. The characters are wonderful and deep, the progression mechanics are great, and there's obviously a lot of room for replayability.In addition, I also want to call special note to the humanity portrayed in this game. Saltsea has done a great job so far portraying a world brimming with different characters, showing complex relationships (including people with trauma, hurt, or complex motivations), and telling a beautiful, hopeful story about what the future can look like. It does this without belittling its players or creating a wholly utopian world -- it's relatable, personable, and very human. I really like how community-oriented Saltsea is: you don't play as one character, but instead as the whole crew of a ship, which emphasizes relationships and shared goals and troubles. There are many games that do similar things poorly, but it's very well done in Saltsea.This is a more personal element to my review, but I want to make special note of Iris. I love games of all kinds (extremely hard bullet hell roguelikes, card games, puzzle games, indie walking sims, etc), but despite having hundreds of games in my library, I've never seen another character like them. Iris seems straightforwardly nonbinary (they use they/them pronouns at the least) and also straightforwardly anxious, but the devs seem to have thrown in pretty clear hints that they may be autistic or neurodivergent. I'm not sure if this is confirmed -- that may not even be a meaningful category in the game's world. Still, as an anxious nonbinary autistic person, I saw them and immediately saw myself for one of the first times. Seeing a character in a game who I can so literally connect with for the first time has been a really meaningful experience -- I'm serious when I say I'm crying when I write this review. It's a really cool and fantastic detail to include. (Side note -- even if you aren't autistic or nonbinary or anxious, I think there's SO much to relate to for so many people in the characters in this game, especially historically underrepresented people. There's an older woman, two sapphic women, and a lot of really well-written people of color. People are funny and sweet and sometimes irritable and always feel real.)Thank you to the dev team for this game! I can't wait to explore the rest of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game definitely scratches a specific itch -- but it also really left me hanging. I love the relaxing gameplay of just getting to explore, the beautiful art style, and the fact that you get to really play as the crew as a whole and not just one character. The world is full of fun (but not overwhelming) lore and it's just really fun to play. It feels like a much more relaxing "I was a Teenage Exocolonist" -- there's no combat, you're never really having to manage rations or anything, you're just playing through your story.That being said, in its current version, the ending felt more like the ending of a first arc instead of the ending of the game. I actually asked out loud, "is that it?" as if the devs were around to hear -- my playthrough left me with three major cliffhangers (the fate of one person, the fate of the crew, the the fate of the world) and just a "the end....?" So I'm hoping there's a big update planned at the very least, because I definitely felt underwhelmed at the end (and underwhelmed enough where I don't really want to play through other variations of the game unless I KNOW there's real endings).
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played a few hours so far, as despite the developers assurance that I shouldn't regret my choices, I just had to repeat the first island for a second time to see how different choices would influence the storyline. The graphics are beautiful - the game has such a unique, expressive style that invites the eye - each location and character is a pleasure to look at. There are small vignettes which provide an insight into the world of Saltsea Chronicles that are drawn in such an evocative and gorgeous 60s/70s style and are so transporting. The writing so far has been pretty gripping. The characters are well-rendered, and I found myself immediately captured by their plight and driven to shepherd them as best as I can for the best outcome (hence repeating the first island!). I'm already falling in love with Molpe (and little Ade), Iris, Murl, Stew and even Maja despite the very little screen time she has had.So far my closest comparison for this game, despite their entirely different settings and art style is Pentiment (which I adored). I know that I'm going to love this game and would recommend it to all who enjoy richly written prose, diverse and intriguing characterisation, and have a love of adventure in video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game with a great deal of passion and care put into it. I was shocked after playing to come back and see how little attention it has gotten. A shame, I love truly creative projects like this. Great writing and worldbuilding and artwork. Gorgeous and unique locations. Delving through each setting made this world feel so lived-in, with history and nuance behind each location. I was immersed.Loved the forking decision paths and replayable chapters, which lets you change your mind and experience the totality this game has to offer. Really impressed, as much as I was with Mutazione which I loved.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, unlike Mutazione, Saltsea Chronicles is essentially a visual novel. A good walking simulator -- and Mutazione might be one of the best ever -- needs to have some exploration, some simple activities for the player and some stuff happening around the player. SC has almost none of that, we just move from one static dialog window to another.If you don't mind visual novels, SC is a very good one. The writers keep their absurd agenda of SC being, in their words, "anti-capitalist" (and, I would add, anti-science) in the subtext and just let the players enjoy the dreamy story.There are some beautiful pieces of lore, some interesting plot points (and some questionable ones, like ), but what is supposed to be the climax isn't very convincing, we're just told that doing X wouldn't be a good thing, it would be a very very bad thing. Also, the whole game ends on a "To be continued, maybe" (I'm paraphrasing). I'm not a big fan of that.Whether or not inviting people to leave reviews for SC before finishing the game is related to the ending, I think it's a rather questionable move, I wouldn't consider such reviews very reliable.I have mixed feelings about the game's art, the backgrounds can be very beautiful and evocative, but why does every single character look like a clown?There's one rather annoying issue where most of the time one click at the end of a dialog does nothing, I have to click again to close the window, but several times a single click closed the window before the last text line was fully displayed. Besides, it's a bit too easy to accidentally click on one of the dialog choices. It's a visual novel, please get your dialog UI right. Also, I thought at first that the game didn't have mouse support, because I have to click a mouse button first to be able to move the mouse cursor.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game unsure of the concept. I was a big fan of Mutazione, and trusted that I would like whatever else the developer put out, and I was absolutely not disappointed. Saltsea Chronicles is a beautifully crafted world with engaging writing & characters. If you enjoyed Mutazione, you'll love Saltsea.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I am very charmed so far by this narrative adventure game. I love the crew of the ship, and I like the dynamic of choosing who works together on expeditions, to further their relationships. I am intrigued by the world and the mystery of our missing crewmate. There are a lot of choices to be made but it's not high pressure at all: feels kind of breezy and dreamlike, and it seems like you can just play how it feels best for you and not worry too much about optimizing choices. The art is just stunning.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've only just gotten through what could be considered the "intro" to the game, but I'm already captivated by the world and its characters. I played Mutazione and was absolutely enthralled, and this game seems to even have improved upon the style that one had. I think this might be an incredible experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: If this game was a text adventure without any art I would still heartily recommend it. A beautiful and overwhelmingly rich script. I can’t even imagine how many choices and words and avenues there are to explore and experience. I also really dig the episodic nature, that gives smaller sessions a feeling of completeness.However, this game is also a total aesthetic treat! Beautiful & strange places lovingly animated and gorgeous music. If you care about indie games and moving stories this is a no brainer must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Having only played the demo and the first half hour of the main game, my impressions are overwhelmingly positive- a warm and intimate adventure- stunning artwork that I enjoy greatly, although it may be overwhelming to some- economical writing, suitable for the medium- open-ended storytelling that steps away from binary and often inconsistent or obtuse morality systems- the game tutorializes gently, with a thoughtful UI that is effective at explaining itself and a suite of accessibility options for both dialogue and play
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Cute lil crabs...and CATS! and island full of them!...what else is there to say? :DI went through 2 playthroughs and still more to explore. Great storytelling (D&D from GOT should take note), art is wonderful, I love the characters esp. Molpe who stays true to themselves. The card game is very fun. Sad to see what happened to DGF but hopefully some day there will be some resolve there and we will get to see a bit more of the characters. This game made life more bearable for me in a troubled time. Big love and many thanks to the devs, artists, and writers. 10/10 will play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played 7 hours of this game so far, but it feels like I know it more intimately than most of my Steam library. It took a bit of time to get into it but every single aspect of Saltsea Chronicles is heartwarmingly magical. The crew, as individuals and as a group are a gateway to the game's world and its emotional centerpoint at the same time. The music, evolving seamlessly as each conversation and interaction unfolds feels amazing. Congrats to the team for creating something this touching and memorable. Once I finish my run, I hope to one day play this game again with friends, but for now it lives in my brain rent-free surrounded by a lot of affection.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Really interesting story. I love that it was mysterious to the end. I started a replay to see if I can get a better result. Loved the art of the boat and different villages. I like the card game and I find I will open up the game to just play a quick round of cards from the beginning menu.  My only complaints are: Why can't I play more than one round of cards within the story at different locations? 2. I wish each location had it's own music theme. I got so "spoiled" [see what I did there] with the amazing music in Mutazione.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This was an instant pre-order game for me, as Mutazione has been my favourite game for literal years. Saltsea Chronicles has cemented Die Gute Fabrik as a forever-love developer for me. The graphic style of art is beautiful and the soundtrack added the perfect atmosphere. The story was immersive and all-consuming. I love that we got to know the characters more and more as we progressed, and as a result I grew incredibly fond of them. I also enjoyed the mini card game that acted as a reprieve from some of the intensity of the story. I have only played through once so far, but there definitely seems to be replayability - I have things still to collect and there were other choices I could have made.This is the perfect game to while away the time with and relax. Definitely for those who prefer story-heavy games as making choices is pretty much it. Perfect for me. The soundtrack is also wonderful to listen to outside of the game - love!
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, a story about found family/misfit crews that never takes for granted how difficult found family can be. Every character drawn and written with so much love. A really unusual but kinda brilliant ending.Also, if you like Creatures, this is a game with some incredible Creatures. 10/10 would critter again
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game ! I was really happy to se it out, since Mutazione is in ma favorite. I must admit I wasn't really convinced by the demo, as it threw us in the middle of nowhere, but I'm glad I bought the game ! I just finished the first chapter and it is excellent. As usual, the art goes well with the story and the color palet of the first island is beautiful ! I love all the small details and the world-building and I will for sure replay it and take other characters with me to see their interaction with the locals, the art and everything
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Queer and POC representation in one of the most charming art styles I've seen in a game. I'm nowhere close to finishing it but was sucked in from the first few scenes. If you like games where choices matter, point and click mechanics, and examining friendship and the interpersonal dynamics of game characters, this charming game is for you :)
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I adored Mutazione, and Die Gute Fabrik deliver once again. The world of Saltsea Chronicles is so alive with wonderful people. And I mean people in the broadest sense: these are very human people, with their own backstories, their own intrigues, their own characters. I don't think anyone writes about people like Die Gute Fabrik does, and yet, this game is even more about community than just people. The art is phenomenal, the soundtrack is one of my faves from this year, and this game is going very high on my GOTY list. Thank you, Die Gute Fabrik, for creating another marvel. Please let us dive even deeper into this world if possible.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I was never going to not like this game after I saw the beautiful artstyle, but after playing for only a little bit I can already say that more than just the art is beautiful. So is the animation, the music, the story, the themes, the presentation, this game really is yet another example of what makes the medium so unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Mutazione so I was excited to play the creators' next game. I've just finished my first playthrough. It's similar to Mutazione in art style and characterisation/story-telling but otherwise that's it.This game is a complicated mystery, told from the points of view of a crew. You play various characters either individually or in pairs, fixing their issues along the way, or perhaps not! If I hadn't known before hand that there'd be multiple possible endings, I'd have guessed from the way my first playthrough ended! I'm going to have to go back now and try other things... without letting my knowledge of what happens distract me too much.Utterly enthralling and the interactions between characters is beautifully done.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a while since I've left a Steam review, but tonight, I discovered that Die Gute Fabrik has just released another game.  I am such a fan of Mutazione that this was pretty much an insta-buy, I didn't watch the trailer or read any reviews or anything, I just clicked the buy button and was happy.Anyway, this game has some serious art.  It's so good!  I'm not really making much progress in the story because I am too busy just looking at all the things.  It's a sort of point-and-clicky type of game, and very text-heavy.  I'm maybe two hours in, and it feels very much like an Inkle-inspired mystery with a nautical flair.  I'm already falling in love with the characters.  I'm reeled in by the flavor text and little animation touches, and I am only just scratching the surface, but I can't wait to continue my journey.  If you've landed on this store page, this game is probably for you.  With all the inflation these days, $25 or whatever is practically the price of a morning coffee.  Just buy the game.  One of the best surprises of 2023 for me so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Just started playing and I'm loving the chill, inclusive vibe, the colourful setting, and the interesting characters. I particularly like the way the text is subtly animated in places to add emotional tone. I'm looking forward to exploring the islands and getting to know the crew at a leisurely pace.Edit: Continuing my first play through and already looking forward to my next one, where I’ll be aiming for different choices of islands and different teams onland. I realise you can branch out like this on one play through but it feels more honest and respectful of the story I’m creating now to save those choices for another.Still loving the chill vibe and the characters (including npcs) are all such good yet flawed people (apart, so far, from one person) which is fleshed out through believable dialogue. A gentle, moving hymn to diversity, acceptance and kindness.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: A narrative game wrapped in charming visuals and striking colors! Highly recommended if you're into ensemble cast stories (has strong sitcom energy with multiple plotlines, but without the filler). The game is very good at giving you small choices with reverberating impact throughout the crews' relationships.Sometimes I don't always understand the intention behind each choice, but I always enjoy how the story plays itself out. It was my night time ritual to play one chapter of the game, make silly choices, enjoy the art, and get hit in the heart with some heavy dialogue. At some point in the game, I just couldn't put my steam deck down -- I ended up staying up pretty late just to get to the end of the game.I think this game is criminally underrated!!! It has so many strong moments, so many beautifully crafted characters with very grounded personalities. I need more people to play this game (and more of a community around it) so I can go online and read about all the potential outcomes I had missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: ✅ post apocalyptic climate change setting✅ non-binary they/them main character✅ ambiguously polyamorous queer relationship ✅ generic corporate Memphis art style❌ good writing or compelling characters❌ interesting and compelling music and sounds that complement the storyI bought this game because I loved Mutazione. This game is a very poor follow up. I feel like they took every faddish progressive meme and shoehorned it into some poor excuse for a video game. It lacks the deep and interesting characters prominent in Mutazione. I was also expecting some amazing music and sounds but the game seems remarkably quiet.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Saltsea Chronicles is a great narrative game, each chapter a bite-sized story in its own right, building up to a moving ending. Every land had its own identity, with a central theme and lots of little details to make it come to life, building up to a world that you want to help flourish. Every member of the crew has their own goals and worries, clashing and reconciling as they pursue their common goal. The way you traverse is also very stream-lined - the game is text heavy, and everything else is in service of that, with easy (and controller-friendly) navigation, clear menus and goals that let you focus on the core narrative experience of reading and making choices, and music and graphics which add to the ambiance of the game but don't take centre stage. (I haven't tried the card game yet, so I can't speak to how it fits in)I also enjoyed exploring the game's possibility space. You can have your own personal playthrough (~5hr long) of Saltsea, and walk away satisfied with how you decided to handle matters. But if you're ready to dive back in, there are new lands to discover, potentially with different characters, and different ways to solve (or not solve) dilemmas. I always enjoy games that feel more dedicated to the journey than just its conclusion, and Saltsea is a journey worth undertaking.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Yes yes yes I love this game! I loved Mutazione too from this dev, so I was excited for more cool stories in this pretty art style, and this has so much more to be interactive with PLUS a fun little card game!? The story and the characters are incredibly good and the structure with chapter selects is so interesting, I just can't wait to see what else this game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: My review is entirely subjective. This game is so different, I don't think there's a good or bad value to it. It is just personally not for me. The beginning is an overwhelming amount of phrases and slang that I couldn't understand, the art style was not to my tastes. I just don't think this product was for me. That said, it looks to be extremely creative and different, so if you're not put off by trying to decipher what each character means with their world's slang, you're not bothered by very fast moving exposition, and the fact that you're not following any set character, this might be for you instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the story and the writing. There's also a lot of beautiful art in this game. The character designs are great, and the landscapes for each location are very beautiful and evocatively drawn. Overall it's a solid game for fans of visual novel style games and point and click adventure type games. My one drawback in my personal experience for this game is that there are so many things to interact with and click on, and so many conversations to read through that it can sometimes become really overwhelming. I try not to play the game in too long of sessions because otherwise my eyes will just start to get tired of reading and I might find myself just spamming clicks to get through everything. This also comes from the fact though that I like be very thorough in games like this and see everything though, so it might just be a me thing. Overall a solid game, and I could see many people finding this appealing, especially when it comes to the dynamics of your crew and the key decision making that progresses everyone's stories and resolves key conflicts.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game is somewhat different from what I usually play. I played this after playing Mutazione so my hopes were pretty high. Gotta say, I wasn't disappointed in the least bit.You play as the lively crew of De Kelpie exploring a world where the seas have submerged almost all habitable land due to humanity's crimes against nature pre-Flood (Saltsea's version of apocalypse). Captain Maja has disappeared so it's up to you to sleuth your way around the archipelago to figure out what happened and where she can be found. The world of Saltsea has its fair share of spirit and science - scientists on Youlouca, story-tellers on Sky-Eye, dreamsailors everywhere, mutated flora and fauna (njars, ventfeeders, pinroot, nightberries); and like our modern world, you have those who stand firm on either school of thought.As the crew traverses the seas chasing down a mysterious ship with indigo sails, you learn the nature of the land with the help of Peeble von Dray who occasionally pops up in dialogue (and is apparently, EVERYWHERE - I'm not sure if we get to meet him. This game needs a replay) as well as keep stickers of every little thing you stumble upon in your travels. The stickers rage from rudder oil to food stalls to feisty little crabs. (Stickers are love, stickers are life. All games should have stickers as collectibles!)Every decision counts. Mend your crew's relationship, chart their character growth, or not. Decide whether to pursue science or spirit, fact or fiction, compassion or judgment. It's all up to you. Watch tensions build and unravel between the crew members and the world. Heck, the game offers so much replayability value it'd be a shame to not try different routes each time and see what you uncover. Also, did I mention the very, very pleasant art style? It scratched the same itch in my mind that games like I Am Dead and TOEM did. My rating? 9.3/10Love and lost is inevitable on the horizon. You cannot gain some without losing some, even though sometimes two losses come first before the gains do. Now back to achievement and sticker hunting I go.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: Stories are such a powerful force, they can divide us or connect us. In this developers work we find that duality represented as well. In  the mc Kai is forced to learn the social codes and navigate the societal intricasies of an insular island society. The focus there is on nature, on showing the strength of society and the resilience of individuals. On the island, as in small towns, everyone knows each other and everyone meddles. There is gossip, there is misunderstanding and some reluctance to accept the new. The newcomer Kai must learn to integrate her goals with the islanders. The relationship she has with her grandpa is touching, and what remains with me of the game is the wonder of exploration (finding the swimming hole) and the gradual unfolding of that story around the central nexus of their world tree. There is the same sort of mythology of strange world inhabited by creatures we do not fully understand, people open up slowly. And they begin to tell Kai the story of their life. The way the community comes together in the end is nothing shy of amazing.I found that  built on this base expertly, there is the same sort of adventure style exploration of the world with thought bubbles. Which kind of remind me Disco Elysiums thought cabinet system. And they build upon it with the dialogue system, you pick one of two options and the story unfolds around it. Sometimes you can pick what looks like the wrong option, and that is no less interesting. The choice of companions also matters greatly in how the narrative evolves, with the amount of choices made you could almost call it a kind of emergent narrative. This also greatly enhances replayability. What i really like here is the emphasis on the story. The crew of the De Kelpie start out as mutual strangers (kind of) and they have to find their way into the world as well as a path forward. The event that determines their course is of course the departure of their captain Maya. There is a sort of reluctance to accept this at first, visible mostly with Molpe of course, and confusion. But as they learn more about events they begin to see their voyage as a quest.The ambigous nature of the story means that you can lay your own emphasis on words and interpret meaning as you wish. The characters are wonderfully written, there is the stodgy historian Murl, who learns to feel for others again. The adventurous and motherly Stew, who forms the nexus of the crew. The decisive single mother Molpe who has to deal with her loss. The introverted and nonbinary Iris who is kind of autistic but tries so hard to make her own way. And of course all the stragglers you pick up along the way, i will avoid spoilers around those but i have a suspicion that the destination you choose matters in this as well. In any case, you find that the crew slowly learn to rely upon each other and begin to regard themselves as family. As they begin to understand the past they can move forward to uncharted waters. What is so beautiful here is the way they make the De Kelpie a home. They learn to find solace and belonging in each other, as they confide and support each other. Collectively they mourn and find meaning. As they mark passage and cross borders they also deal with heartbreak and loss. This makes the characters so real and multifaceted.Sometimes the Fates weave cruel twists and turns into their plaids. So too must people learn to deal with things they cannot understand. The choice for empathy is usually the right one as demonstrated in this game. Patience, kindness and understanding go a long way to healing rifts and clearing up misunderstandings. And with friends we feel like we can handle the whole world. So ultimately the story we tell ourselves becomes the story we tell others. But the author always remains at leisure to edit, it is a work in progress. And its messy, like some of the choices in this game. Sometimes there is silence, there are arguments, there is awkwardness. Sometimes things cant be resolved anymore. Like Neshko has to learn to live with his past. Or Murl who has to find a way to move on. So there is also a kind of finality that we have to reckon with. But who knows what lies around the bend, where will we moor next? So sail on brave seamen, take refuge in the wise words of Peeble von Dray.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: By going beyond the constraints of the Hero's Journey the game unleashes a rich world where the player is able to feel agency, togetherness and being part in something important. Omitting numerical metrics and replacing them by emotional ties and personal experiences it really feels like going on an adventure, together.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of those where I wish we had something in between a thumbs up and a thumbs down. But I guess that what the written review is for.If I could give stars, it would be 3.5/5, so a decent game, but I have some issues with it personally. Will try to keep my review as spoiler-free as possible.The Pros:- Clearly made with love. Playing this game, you can feel the care that went into it, and I like that.- Characters you can care about, character relationships that make sense.- Casual queerness.- A fun mini game (even though I don't even like card games).- Very relaxing to play. I was looking for games that only require me to click and read, no reflexes or fights. This game is perfect for that.- Excellent soundtrack.- Interesting places to discover.- Deep and fascinating background lore.- I do like the concept of replaying from the beginning or ending of a chapter that you've already played. Excellent concept! No need to replay the whole thing from the beginning, when you're just curious about a single decision.The Cons:- Even though you get a lot of choices (who do you take to an island with you, dialogue options), it feels like none of that has any actual impact. I even went back to a specific chapter to take a different landing party and change the course of events, but aside from some (adorable, tbf) character interactions, exactly the same thing happened. Very frustrating.- I read in other reviews that there is apparently only one ending, which makes the lack of actual impact of my choices even worse. I was planning on replaying, until I learned about this. What's the point of a choice driven game (as that's really all we do! Make choices!) if there is only a single ending? I'd be happy if there were even just two ...- Speaking of the ending, I found it incredibly anticlimactic and at the same time a cliffhanger. As if it was actually the end of act 2, but act 3 never came. I fully expected there to be more and then ... it's over. I wanted there to be more! There was so much unresolved, so much undiscovered!My review boils down to "Good game, but I wish we had an actual choice, instead of just an illusion of choice". I'm currently not inclined to replay this game, but I'll be watching its page to see if there will be updates. More endings? A continuation of the story? More impactful choices? All things I'd love to see, and that would make this game a favourite of mine. But it's simply not quite there yet.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: What a charming, character-focused adventure game! Delightful art, and the ensemble cast are compelling.And then the story takes all of that character-driven investment and uses it to hurt you in the best, worst, way.This whole experience is like sitting at a table comprised of soft queers playing Apocalypse World or Dream Askew, imagining life after the worst has happened, and embracing the pain of being alive, of being human. Hearty recommend.EDIT: I've nominated Saltsea Chronicles for most Outstanding Story-Rich game of this year and it's absolutely a winner in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review: I have only just started playing this game but I'm honestly so engrossed already. I'll continue to update as I go. Chapter 1: I have to say, this is just as refreshing, calming and inspiring as Multizone. This studio has continued to outdo itself. I'm fascinated by the very practical anti-capitalist mechanics in this charming well illustrated story-driven game. Even the in game interface is part of the story, positioned as Mural's log and personal journal, each important thing you come across, a new sticker for his and your collection. If they come out with a sticker pack I'm so preordering it. The mini games are even well designed. I've never felt prompted to screen shot the rules of a in game card game before but Trick just seems much too fun to not bully my friends into playing it during our next game night. God and the world building, the bird island is so richly built, I've clicked on every bit of dialogue, every conversation,  I mean come on just fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

_childDocuments_.review:
Saltsea Chronicles is a new story-driven adventure game from the award-winning indie studio Die Gute Fabrik (Mutazione, Sportsfriends).

Captain Maja's misfit crew must heist their impounded ship and mount a rescue. Guide the crew across islands of a post-flood world known as 'Saltsea'. Explore strange and wonderful communities, uncover a deep conspiracy, choose where to go and which crew members to investigate with, and chart a journey through twists and turns, difficulties and delights.

As well as investigating the mystery of your captain's disappearance, you will uncover secrets, create and resolve tensions between the crew, and add to your number as you meet others who ask to join you.

Each chapter, you pick which island to visit and who to send on the expedition. Your choices will unlock different content, develop relationships, and give you a chance to resolve (and create) tensions within the crew.
_childDocuments_.name: Saltsea Chronicles

name: Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World
detailed_description: OTHER 'WONDER BOY' TITLES BY OUR FRIENDS About the Game The adventures of Asha and Pepelogoo begin! Asha, the warrior protagonist of the game, is involved in a serious incident that will affect the survival of her world. Our green-haired heroine doesn’t have to save the world all alone, and sets off on an adventure with her cute flying friend, the blue Pepelogoo. Asha and the Pepelogoo have to work together to become the heroes the world needs them to be. The road ahead is long - but will they be able to save their world? ■A side-scrolling action game that is light, fun and easy to play. The action is fast and challenging, but the game has been refined, making it easier to try again. ■Call it, grab it, throw it, move it - her blue buddy, Pepelogoo! Join forces with your partner to overcome puzzles and powerful enemies. ■Various action levels High mountains, volcanoes, ice worlds, even the sky! Let's explore the various areas with Pepelogoo. ■Explore the vastness of the world! The vast world is full of unknown and often surprising encounters, events, and discoveries. Even if you've cleared a stage before, you might discover something new if you revisit it! ■Power up Asha and you'll be ready for the difficulties! By acquiring items and equipment, you can strengthen your attack and defense capabilities. Get ready to face powerful enemies. A full remake of 'Monster World IV,' the action RPG masterpiece released in the 90's, by the original development team! We hope you will enjoy the remastered 'Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World' with new visuals and sound adjustments. ■Staying true to the series legacy For Wonder Boy - Asha in Monster World, the original staff from the former Westone Bit Entertainment studio gathered together to create a game that stays true to the spirit of the original titles. The team is led, and directed, by the creator of the Wonder Boy series, Ryuichi Nishizawa and supported by Shinichi Sakamoto (sound), Maki Ōzora (character design) and Takanori Kurihara (creative management). You can't get more Wonder Boy than that!The adventures of Asha and Pepeloglu begin! Asha, the warrior protagonist of the game, is involved in a serious incident that will affect the survival of her world. Our green-haired heroine doesn’t have to save the world all alone, and sets off on an adventure with her cute flying friend, the blue Pepelogoo. Asha and the Pepelogoo have to work together to become the heroes the world needs them to be. The road ahead is long - will they be able to save their world? ■A side-scrolling action game that is light and easy to play. The action is fast and challenging, but the game is tuned for easy retrying, making it easy to try again. ■Call it, grab it, throw it, move it, her blue buddy Pepeloglu. _childDocuments_.review: This is a remake of Monster World IV. But not in the same way Dragon's Trap was a remake. They actually remade all the gameplay and everything from scratch, instead of just making new art and putting it on the original game. There are bigger differences. You can save anywhere, which eliminates practically any possible frustration you'd experience. Graphics are fine, if fairly bland. I found it all palatable enough. The controls are solid, even if Asha can still only attack once at a time, which feels awkward and limited in this day and age. But the level design mostly holds up despite some of the levels feeling barren. There are few resolution options, but setting it to fullscreen should make it fit your native resolution, so that's not that big of a deal. The framerate is uncapped by default, and the game plays very well at 120 FPS. However, in Ice Pyramid 1, the spell doors won't work if you're playing the game at a framerate above 60. I guess no devs noticed that one. Still, it's an enjoyable game, even if it is basic and won't take all that long to beat. It's cute and colorful and I liked exploring the levels while collecting coins and life drops. Plus the whole "collect money to buy new upgrades all the time" loop always hooked me in these sorts of games. Good times, great oldies.

_childDocuments_.review: My short video review for Asha in Monster World features here: Written Review:For gamers who grew up in the 1980s, I imagine SEGA’s Wonder Boy series will hold special memories. I remember playing the first game in the arcades, although it later released on the Master System console.  The original game was a side-scrolling platformer where you moved from left to right collecting fruit to replenish an ever-depleting time counter. Things slowed down somewhat for the sequels, with ‘Wonder Boy III: The Dragon’s Trap’ a series high, and an early example of what would become the metroidvania genre.  Released exclusively in Japan in the ‘90s for the SEGA Genesis/Megadrive, the fourth game in the series finally gets a proper release for western players in the form of a HD remake. It came out last month on consoles, and gets a PC release via Steam this week. ‘Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World’ has similarities to its predecessors, and could, perhaps, be seen as a mix of all of them. Rather than play as the titular ‘Wonder Boy’, you play as Asha – a girl on a quest to free four spirits confined by evil forces.   Compared to modern platformers, combat is pretty simple – and doesn’t change much as the game progresses. You have a sword slash, which can be charged for a special attack, and a shield to defend yourself. It's certainly not as varied as ‘The Dragon’s Trap’ or the recent ‘Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom’ game – but it’s satisfying, nonetheless.  Perhaps the most unique aspect of the gameplay is the introduction of a companion, a blue creature called a Pepelogoo, who allows you to glide, double jump and solve a number of interesting puzzles.   The new art style for the remake features a striking colour palette, which, along with the simple character designs and new cutscenes, makes it feel like playing a cartoon. The game utilises a 2.5D perspective where you are able to move from the foreground to the background in certain areas. This may be a divisive move for fans of the original, but I rather liked it.  Music and sound effects are on point through a fully remastered soundtrack. Anyone familiar with the original games will recognise the noise made when enemies drop coins. It’s a lovely, and very welcome, nostalgic touch.  ‘Asha in Monster World’ is a lovingly crafted remake. It remains faithful to the original, even down to the little bottom jiggles Asha makes as you open a treasure chest. If you enjoy platform games, or are a fan of the series, this one is well worth a look.

_childDocuments_.review: Was excited when this was announced because I really enjoyed the previous Wonder Boy remake and the Monster Boy spiritual successor. Unfortunately, this game is not like those games at all. I played this entire game hoping for it to get good, but it never did. There are no cool transformations, no unique movement abilities, nothing that actually makes the game fun. Worst of all, this game is beatable in about 3-4 hours which is much shorter than the previous Wonder Boy remake, and a fraction of the length of Monster Boy.In my opinion, this game is functionally no different from something you would find on the Gameboy. The combat is extremely simplistic and not engaging, and the level design is uninspired and consists mainly running from right to left or vice versa for long stretches, occasionally taking out enemies. The sound design is repetitive and grating on the ears after a while. Music is not particularly good and most tracks are on a very short loop. The sound effects are repetitive and loud, causing a lot of annoyance after a while. There is no progression in the game aside from buying stronger weapons and armor. The only "ability" you get is the ability to use your pet to jump long distances and double jump. Don't get used to it though because you lose access to your pet in the last act of the game. This will prevent you from backtracking to older levels if you missed any collectables, so be aware. My advice is to collect what you can, but don't go back for the rest. The time and effort aren't worth the reward. It's extremely unlikely that you will be able to get 100% on your first playthrough anyway so don't bother.One thing that isn't a huge deal but really annoyed me are the controls. This game has "Japanese controls" which means if you are playing on a Dualshock, X is cancel and O is confirm, or if you are using an Xbox controller, A is cancel and B is confirm. There is no way to change this in-game, so you would have to fix it with a 3rd party program. This doesn't affect the actual gameplay, but I can't tell you how many times I pressed start to open the menu, and immediately closed it again because I pressed X to try to select an item instead of O.If you wanted graphics options, sorry but there aren't any. I kind of get it because the game is obviously very easy to run, but not even basic stuff like anti-aliasing or Vsync is there. To make matters worse, the game only supports 1080p and 4K while in fullscreen mode, but not 1440p. There may be some workaround for this, but judging by the complete lack of other options I wouldn't count on it. Beware if you have a 1440p display.As you can probably tell, I didn't like this game. It's not god awful, but it feels extremely rudimentary. If you absolutely must have it, wait for a heavy discount. Remember, the game is only 3-4 hours long and has basically no replay value. This was supposed to be a remake of a 16-bit game, but it feels like an 8-bit game with fancy graphics. Your money will be much better spent on the Wonder Boy 3 remake or Monster Boy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a terrible game, but definitely the weakest in the series. The controls are kinda clunky, long animations for things you do a lot of, and having to call Pepelogoo over (which isn't even explained) every time you want to double-jump is just annoying and unnecessary. The "puzzles" so far have amounted to little more than "which direction do I need to face when I throw the blue thing?" (also not actually explained) But my biggest beef with this game so far is no monster transformations. Yes, I knew that going into the game, and I was really hoping the rest would be good enough to make up for it. But it really isn't. The characters all feel really hollow and boring, and the environments are generic and empty.Frankly, the only Real monster involved in this game is whoever decided that the jump button should also be the cancel button.

_childDocuments_.review: Good effort, but not the best game choice for creating a very faithful remake. As far as efforts to revitalize this game go, the developers did a fantastic job of enhancing the original game's atmosphere, particularly the 2.5D areas, which make for some interesting platforming. The original and faithful remake soundtracks have some really good entries, most if not all of which share a melody/motif (which is unfortunately a double-edged sword). Sometimes, the music doesn't entirely fit with the scenario, and other times it feels like you are listening to the same track throughout most of the game (compare this to The Dragon's Trap, which could have easily suffered a similar or worse fate if not for efforts to mitigate that). I was a little annoyed that the animation for opening chests is kind of long like in the original game, as you come across many chests and it gets old quickly (it matches the character's attitude, but we get enough cheeriness as is). The main problem lies in the gameplay of the original game. It often does not hold up, and that unfortunately shines through in this remake. The game has few levels, but pads time within each level: There is a tutorial level, four tedious and mostly boring main levels, some decent intermittent action in the town, and the final level. The level design generally feels very simplistic and maze-like, and often has boring puzzles that seem to just pad for time, due to weird physics quirks (I'm talking to you, ice floors). The worst culprit of this is the ice pyramid, which has three separate segments (with slight differences), all with the same task of exploring extremely long halls to find five statues. A dumb quirk about ice pyramid 1: when approaching a door with the directional pad pass codes, you cannot back out of pass code entry if you accidentally pressed on the door without knowing the code, which is frustrating if you take damage from the tricky-to-avoid traps. Funny enough, I got the first pass code correct by accident on the first try. Ice pyramid is the worst. Combat and progression are especially hit and miss, as enemies are usually either mindless or tedious to fight through. Bosses are kind of cool but some are just cheap or too easy. The idea of bouncing off enemies while taking no damage is an annoying mechanic that gets you boxed in during some boss fights (the ice wizard boss feels especially dated as a 'last one to lose all health' challenge). Also, there seems to be a miss-translation at the beginning that says "You can hurt some enemies just by touching them", when they probably actually meant that YOU can get hurt by enemies if you bump into them (the fire enemy immediately follows, and does not take damage when you walk into it). While the downward sword thrust can give you some interesting quick movement, it is usually very wonky with the slow sword swing rate given to the player. Weapon prices seem well-staggered, until you realize the purpose of a certain item,  and learn that saving money is nearly a complete waste of time. This just doesn't feel balanced. The premise of level difficulty variation in this game is interesting: Your blue pepelogoo comes into play for the earth medallion stage, and you fumble around to learn its abilities, but as it grows, your movement with it becomes more hindered and needs to be timed better, then you lose it all together, putting your basic platforming to the test once again. Elixers are thrown at you left and right at the beginning so you are almost guaranteed to find out how the pepelogoo can apply elixer to you if you die (Zelda fairy style). This can get annoying quickly though, because what if you want to keep your elixers? (you don't necessarily know ahead of time that a boss is in the next area, so you might not be able to set up a convenient save, and reload it to keep elixers for later). Silly enough, this pepelogoo progression setup works against players if they are hoping to backtrack to collect all life drops, because you cannot access pepelogoo-requiring areas towards the end of your first playthrough (). This is a big no-no, and one cannot confuse this with replayability. I am surprised the remake developers didn't alter this, [spolier] and yet added 2.5D elements [/spoiler]. I nearly had all life drops, except for some sun medallion ones (the pyramid levels sucked so much that I didn't even want to try for 100%, ). Let's discuss some remake changes that the developers included to try to improve the gameplay, rather than aesthetic. First and foremost, now you can collect any item at any time, rather than being restricted to one of a certain pickup. This is a good quality of life touch, no questions asked. The new save system aims to alleviate the game's original difficulty, as it gives you many slots and you can save/load at any point outside of boss fights, rather than saving at the wizard guy like in the original. However, there is no parallel auto-save slot, and this becomes a problem for reasons discussed above: What if you don't want a pepelogoo to use an elixer, but you didn't save in the room leading up to the boss (the boss door transition is generally not apparent)? It's tedious to load the previous save, but it is also devastating to waste all the elixers collected in early game on an arguably easy segment you are learning because the pepelogoo feels like it. Either the save system should be revised or the revival should be optional, bringing you back to the boss door transition if you choose no. In addition, being able to save anywhere ruins the flow of the game, because a new player constantly has to internally debate whether or not to save to avoid cheap deaths (which there are quite a few of before you have lots of health). The weird thing is that this game requires a controller, and I am not sure why, given the other quality of life improvements made. When you compare this remake and its original to The Dragon's Trap and its original, the kind of light fantasy story telling with minimal depth is mutual between them. This is nothing to complain about, but most would probably agree that The Dragon's Trap is still infinitely better than this in terms of gameplay. I cannot speak to the other games in the series, but I may try them. I was kind of disappointed with this game, given the unique enjoyment I got from The Dragon's Trap remake (faithful to the solid core gameplay, super good visuals with retro options, and awesome soundtrack decisions). There are also cool elements that had a lot of potential in this game, and I was especially curious because this remake seemed to be trying to present itself as more modern with its new visuals in 2021. The thing is that the visuals are good, and so I am glad that there was at least something nice to take from this. Cheers to the developers for finding creative ways of enhancing a game that has questionable core elements. While the game didn't sit perfectly well with me (and other players with similar thoughts), the hard work is not unnoticed.

_childDocuments_.review: Lately I've been playing the entire series in order, starting with the arcade ones, then the 16-bit era ones, then to all the Steam ones in series order.I  played the original MW4, fan translated, in 2013 already, and remembered loving it. So I went out of my way to play it again BEFORE getting around to this remake.Look, uh, as much as I appreciate the little QOL changes this version has over the original... You can tell at a lot of points that it really lacked either time, budget, or both in a lot of aspects.Gonna start with a quick little description first though., already, is a lot more linear of a game compared to the prior games in the series, going from the interconnected Metroidvania-ish maps of  and  to what essentially amounts to a hub area and a bunch of linear "dungeon" areas.No magic system either, since that one was replaced by the Pepelogoo system (a little birdcat pet of sorts that follows you around and can be used to perform several types of actions, including mobility-based ones like doublejumps and gliding).Same thing goes for armor; instead of reducing the damage you take, it ADDS to your maximum heart count, and you always take one point of damage from any hit.On top of that, you go around the game gathering "life drops" that can extend an entire SEPARATE set of blue hearts to give you even more health, rewarding exploration (because even though the game is linear overall, there's still a bunch of spots to explore throughout the stages to find more of these).So you can already tell the game is a lot more streamlined in a lot of senses.That's not really a bad thing in itself.The main issue is that you CANNOT go back to older areas after beating them, as they become locked out once beaten.This is one of the things the remake PARTIALLY fixes; you can still revisit older areas for a while, until ONE point in the game after most of them are cleared where they all lock out at once.Granted, this isn't necessarily a bad thing for everyone, but if you're going in wanting to 100% the game, it means there's a lot of things you NEED to know beforehand, as a lot of collectibles quickly become permanently missable unless you start the entire game over.Those details aside, the remake does add a couple extra improvements on top of everything else.For starters, movement is slightly faster as-is compared to the original, and sprinting just requires a single analog stick movement as opposed to double tapping a direction every time you leave the ground or do anything else so you can re-start the sprint.The "magical hit" system was completely reworked too; shared from the original, each weapon you can get has a certain assigned "level" of those, which pretty much acted as your critical hits, doubling your damage output. Some weapons have them, some don't, and their damage is fixed at double the base damage rate (except for one sword that had something crazy like 8x crits).In the original game, magical hits are ; that is, every FIFTH hit you threw out would be a critical. Which was workable enough once you figured out the pattern, but made it slightly annoying having to whiff attacks on purpose to buffer that critical hit for actual use.The remake, instead, gives you a magical METER that charges up from hitting enemies, and lets you unleash that critical hit whenever you choose to with a dedicated input for it, which is a much better way of handling it.Despite the rough visuals of the game, the controls never really FEEL as stiff as you'd think from looking at footage of it, which was honestly surprising....Speaking of the visuals though, uh... Yeah.As gorgeous as the 2D art and 2D background elements in this remake look, everything else is 3D, since the remake is 2.5D overall, which is kind of unfortunate because almost every 3D aspect of this element feels cheaply made, almost mobile-like in the worst cases. Character animations especially, they're ridiculously stiff and weird.Most of the areas look decently faithful to the original, but also a few like the pyramid area had their looks COMPLETELY changed; in that example, going from a more interesting dark purple/black stone color scheme to a more generic cartoony blue ice block architecture, which just looks... blander?The cutscenes also have a lot of weird camera angles and details that feel like they were added to TRY and counteract the overall cheapness and make them more "cinematic" but a lot of these scenes also end up losing the subtle impact a lot of the original game's had....Oh yeah the game's fully voice acted in japanese now, but that doesn't really add anything to it, especially knowing that part of the budget could have gone literally ANYWHERE else and it would've helped a lot more.All of that stuff said, the music's actually pretty good. The original soundtrack was already really solid, with a lot of really interesting tracks with neat experimentation like odd time signatures, which helps keep them interesting despite a lot of them sharing the game's main leitmotif.The remake (as you'd expect) rearranges all the original tracks into new versions and I never really disliked any of them, they're alright.Even then if you don't like them you can just use a  cheatcode to unlock an option to use the original music instead, which is a nice plus. This remake DOES admittedly feel kind of cheaply made (which is weird coming after Dragon's Trap and Monster Boy which are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful), but it's decent enough to at least be worth it on sale. Has a couple QOL improvements over the original too, which I genuinely appreciate.Just... be aware that if you played the original already you might be disappointed at a good few of the changes present here.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World is a remake of the 16-bit Japan/Mega Drive only release. Unfortunately, I never got to play the original back in the day so this is my first experience with the game.I absolutely loved 2018's Monster Boy game and for those hoping for something of that quality might be a little disappointed. This is a straight remake of a Mega Drive game and isn't a long or fleshed out game like Monster Boy. It does have similar visuals, music and gameplay but that's about where it ends.Asha is a pretty simple game overall but that also makes it charming and relaxing. It's pretty much a straight forward action platformer with minor equipment upgrades. While it's no Monster Boy, I had a fun time with the game and the voice acting (Japanese only) gave it extra charm and likability.So while I can't say it's an all time classic, if you enjoy games like Monster Boy or the Shante series, I think you'll enjoy Asha.

_childDocuments_.review: Asha in Monster World is a very well-done remake of the original Monster World 4, with a few slight differences in layout here and there.  The original version was quite challenging, so it was a delightful surprise to see an easy mode that allows saving any time and any place.Although the description says that a controller is required to play the game, it has been discovered that there actually are keyboard controls built into the game -- though the mapping can't be changed.  Have a look at the third reply in this thread for details:Also, don't believe the system requirement of Windows 10.  It works wonderfully for me in Windows 7 (64-bit, of course).Otherwise, my only beef about the game is the poor proofreading in dialogue in places -- but at least it's still readable.  The game is fun, with great graphics and catchy music.  I highly recommend it. :)

_childDocuments_.review: AiMW is first than anything a remake of a 1994 game, the differences and upgrades are nothing out of this world (more save slots, faster screen transitions, two soundtracks etc) but they do make for a smoother experienceJudging the game as a purely retro game though, it really stands out as one with excellent controls, a short but satisfying plot full of humorous moments and a bit of seriousness and the closure of the Wonder Boy sagaI'm very biased but I think AiMW deserves a 9/10, very old fashioned but an example of a low budget miracle
