_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game?Hell yes I do!But it's a game for those that are really into platformers and an old-school approach to puzzles and problem-solving. This game is basically a side-scrolling Legend of Zelda complete with simple hack'n'slash-action, maze-like dungeons, platforming shennanigans and puzzles.First thing you notice when you start up the game is the vibrant and cheerful aesthetics. The game looks like a cartoon and only a few cursors in the menus and pixelated monsters in the loading screens tell us about the game's retro-past. This game is despite it pleasant looks a remake of the old Sega Genesis-game Monster World 4. I don't know much about the difference between this version and the old version, so you will have to look elsewhere if that sort of thing is important to you.The second thing you notice is THE MUSIC! Just like the graphics it is very cheerful and vibrant in that way that it makes an impact on you immediately. I love it. The only downfall with it is that just like all old school-songs they start looping pretty quickly. For the most part that is okay if the game have several songs it can switch between for different areas and you don't stay too long in one area (unfortunately, this happens a few times in the game).The third thing you will notice are the controls - they are pretty standard for a retro game. You run, jump and slash. That's it. Simplicity at it's best. Running happens via double-tap though, which isn't my favorite - but it never broke the game. But holding down a button (preferably one of the top ones) is the optimal for platforming games, I think.You also have an inventory which I love. Giving simplistic games like Megaman, Castlevania, Mario etc an inventory is a very easy way to add a small layer of extra depth. For Asha in Monsterworld, the inventory is mostly used to store different key items, restorative items and swords & shields - and that's good enough for this game!Besides being a simple action-platformer with Zelda-dungeons this game is also part Metroidvania. The game is very linear, but you have a hub-town that you can explore a bit to find different secrets and side-quests and some of them are only available when you unlock new ways to move. The dungeons themselves also have LITTLE bi of this, with the Life Drops being an collectible item that you have to search for. I didn't find them all - but supposedly something magical happens when you do!The most interesting things about Asha in Monster-world are some of the puzzles - especially those inside the Ice Pyramid. I don't want to spoil it, but you end doing it old-school, real old-school, like "having paper and pen ready"-old-school. It was really refreshing to see. There is a story in Asha in Monster World, but I never cared much for it - but to my liking they actually kept it super-basic so I didn't need to care about any twists or convuluted relationships to enjoy my Zelda-ish platforming romp. When I finished Asha in Monster World the game recognized I was a of the "gamer-tribe" since I actually chose to play the game on the original difficulty which I thought was neat. There were however save slots and quicksaves that made it much easier, but I tried to not use them too much. The game doesn't allow you to "micro-save" though, since whenever you save and load that game, you start at a check point and not exactly where you saved the game - which is fair!Anyway, if you like retro-games, check this one out!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played and beat the original 1994 16-bit Sega Genesis/Mega Drive version a while back, I was NOT disappointed by this 2021 remake. It is truly an impressive update of the classic game and while certain aspects are different, overall, it plays the same. I really appreciated the quality-of-life improvements (e.g. being able to carry up to NINE life potions at once instead of one) and the Japanese voice acting (with English subtitles included). I cannot understand the negative reviews that it received. Granted, it is not perfect (there ARE times where the game feels much easier than the original), but it is still just as fun and addicting. Truth be told, it is also my second favorite in the Wonder Boy/Monster World franchise ("Wonder Boy: The Dragon's Trap" is still #1 to me) and I had fun reliving Asha's epic quest all over again. If you are a fan of the series, it is definitely worth checking out!

_childDocuments_.review: While is game is barely seven hours long (save-scumming nonwithstanding), if you were a Wonderboy fan, you won't want to miss this one.At first I considered this game was aimed at very young children considering the game's simplicity (the game discards Metroidvania elements in favor of strict dungeon crawling), but it's entertaining enough, also the difficulty ramps up in the second half. The music doesn't start great, but it grows in you, and Asha is just too damn endearing, which is an achievement in itself for a mostly mute protagonist.It's not fabulous as Monsterboy and the Cursed Kingdom was, but it's still good, and it's Wonderboy. If anything, give it a chance on next sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World, by developers G Choice and Monkey Craft, is a remake of the 1994 game, Monster World IV, and is playable on the Nintendo Switch and Steam. However, this game adds a lot to the original game, and I would consider it an old-fashioned, yet charming game that is accessible to everyone. At the beginning of the game, you are playing as Asha, an adventurer and warrior, trying to prove yourself in the vast world of Monster World. After Asha clears the first dungeon, the “Tower of Silence” the princess of Rapadanga City begs you for your help. She wants to clear the four elemental dungeons and save the world from darkness!Combat System: The combat system is relatively simple, with Asha being able to attack, jump, shield, and be able to use several items in her inventory. However, during the game you get a companion, which allows you to do extra moves such as double jump and even glide. I can see the combat system reminding me of an early Legend of Zelda game, and other games coming out of the late 80’s/90’s. With the extra mobility offered by the companion, it becomes more complicated than an 80’s game, but still relatively traditional compared to modern gaming. Fun and Exciting 2-D platformer with an extra addition: Asha can travel some areas with some aspects of 3-D. I felt that it added to the complexity of areas, as I had to consider moving forward/backwards alongside the more traditional 4 directions used in 2-D platformers. There are more ways to hide secret bonuses and hearts with this addition as well, adding a sense of mysteriousness and curiosity that could only be offered with this. Graphics are nothing special but are improved from the original game. The art style is cartoony and fun to look at, not serious or dark at all. The characters, including the enemy monsters, are comedic and are funny to look at, which will appeal to many, especially younger audiences. My Experience: I had a lot of fun playing Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World. As a seasoned platformer gamer, I did not find it too hard to beat the areas at all. Some bosses might take a few tries to learn what their attacks do, but once you find an opening it is relatively easy to beat. However, I think that some of the puzzles are challenging and might cause some confusion. A guide might be necessary to not get stuck on puzzles. Although I was not around in the 80s/90s when the original series came out, I still have some nostalgia for some of the tried-and-true gameplay that defined much of the video games of the 80’s. I believe that this game is accessible to all ages and experience levels. The straightforward, yet tried and true story, its lovable and cute characters, and the old-fashioned gameplay all add to its nostalgic charm. If you enjoy a platformer who enjoys the Mario or LoZ series and do not mind the dated battle system or graphics, Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World is definitely for you, and I would recommend this game. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovingly crafted remake of a classic game that went ignored in the west. The art and music are top notch but, unfortunately, this game is too loyal to its aged design. It will just throw you into dozens of senseless, identical rooms asking you to make the same 3 jumps and fight the same 3 enemies over and over and over and call that a dungeon. I simply cannot accept a game that has so little meat to it.That said, there is an audience for this. For anyone who grew up with this series, for anyone whose heart has been touched by any aspect of the rich history of this franchise, the passion that went into this project will shine through. A game like this, one so loyal and respectful to ancient gaming history, cannot exist without that history and without the shared love and passion between game developers and audience. I could never give that a thumbs down and I hope that this game finds those gamers.But for those who crave a more modern design, I recommend going for Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom, also on Steam, instead. (I would even recommend Wonder Boy and the Dragon's Trap, which is an equally loyal remake of an even older game than Asha in Monster World, but Dragon's Trap is a tighter package that plays far smoother.)

_childDocuments_.review: I have no experience with the original or the series but I have played similar games. The game has what you'd want from a remake/remaster in that there is voiced dialogue, the graphics are crisp and the frustrations of playing a 2d platformer from the snes/genesis era are still present. You can make it easier on yourself by playing on easy and you can save at any time you want, as emulators have spoiled retro gamers. From the bit I played, easy mode is supposed to make recovery items more plentiful but I mostly noticed that you start with more health. The game has a mix of 2d combat but none of the monsters are particularly -hard- if you are patient and can spot patterns. However, if you play casually or carelessly, trying to speed through a level, you -will- start to take damage fast. The game has an element of non renewable resources in that monsters do not respawn unless you leave the level and come back through the magic lamp. You use coins to either recover hearts from vending machines or upgrade your equipment and misusing your coins will take you behind the equipment curve fast. Monsters either drop coins or hearts and you need to pick those ups before they fade away which can put you in dangerous situations. Fortunately, after the first *real* dungeon, you can redo dungeons and have all monsters respawn. The game has missables in the form of health drinks and heart fragments (like in zelda). However, since you can redo stages other than chapter 1, you don't need to stress too much since the game will tell you how many heart fragments you missed and you can go back and get them. One thing the game doesn't make clear is that the magic lamp allows you to leave a dungeon and go back to town to buy equipment or after picking up what you missed the first time. Getting all the way to the end of a dungeon you already cleared rewards you with a treasure chest with money. You're welcomed. A game for people who like retro/platformers.If you like Japanese games like this one, check out my curator page specialized in them.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Monster World IV on the Mega Drive is one of my personal favorite games of all time. While I wouldn't exactly say this version is "better" than the original release, it is a fantastic recreation and follows the original game's design to a T. The new 3D polygon graphics are bright and colorful, and Asha's expressive animations will put a big smile on your face while you play. The new arranged music is also wonderful. Very pleasant to listen to and accurate to the original songs from the Mega Drive version. As for the gameplay itself, everything controls as it should. If you enjoyed the original game as much as I did, I think you will have a lot of fun playing with this new version. If you haven't played this game before and you enjoy metroidvania-esque action platformers, this game is fantastic and has some of the most satisfying progression of any game in this style. I don't want to spoil anything in particular so all I can say is: play it!

_childDocuments_.review: I remember back in 94, I read about a cool looking game called wonder boy 4: Asha in Monster world. It had a Claymation cover, cool looking cutscenes, and was Japan exclusive. I really wanted to play it, however importing for the genesis was harder and more expensive than for the SNES back then, so my dream went unfulfilled. (Standard games already cost around 100 where I lived at the time, so imagine import games) Now, almost 30 years later, I got to play the remake.The Game is Bright and vibrant, with the ability to listen to the remixed and original OST. Just input Up, Down, Up, Down, Left, Left, Right, Right. and pick classic soundtrack from the menu. Filthy casual that I am, I choose to play on easy mode. To the best of my knowledge this makes combat easier, but not the platforming. Not that MW4 is difficult, if you die due to a misstep, being flattened, electrocuted, or fried, you lose a heart and get to start at the last firm platform you stood on beforehand. You can also save almost everywhere from the menu. Even so, I managed to have a few “murder the TV with my controller” moments because I just kept narrowly missing a jump. Turns out 20 years of turn based RPGs have withered my once mighty Platforming muscle into a flaccid little jelly doughnut.Anyway, if you are looking for a short but sweet retro platformer, I can recommend Asha in Monster World. Doubly so at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World

_childDocuments_.review:
An icon in adventure gaming history is back!

Wonder Boy: Asha in Monster World becomes a real Wonder Boy adventure that stays true to its roots as the latest part of the legendary and successful series, that dates back to 1986. 

Asha is tasked to free the four spirits being confined by evil forces whose origin she discovers throughout her journey. Luckily, she does not have to face this adventure alone, as early on she finds her new companion, a special blue Pepelogoo.

The players can experience the adventures of the dynamic duo like never before thanks to cell-shaded 3D graphics and 2D gameplay as well as enhanced visuals and refined play content. Especially in the event scenes the performance is deepened and the world view is reproduced vividly and colorfully. Plus, for the first time in the series, it comes with a character voice by the popular and talented Japanese voice actress Ai Fairouz.

name: No More Heroes
detailed_description: The name's Travis Touchdown. Buckle up, 'cause this is how my story began. It all started the night I was out drinking with some smokin' hot chick at the bar. Before I knew it, I was ranked #11 in the UAA (that's United Assassins Association)--with ten suckers standing in the way of me being #1. I've got my trusty beam katana in one hand to take care of the small fries, and the other one ready to hold my girl once I take my place as the best assassin the world's ever seen. It's a long way to the top, but this all-American otaku won't stop until he's #1, baby! The classic slice-and-dice, nonstop action of No More Heroes has been given the HD makeover it rightfully deserves! Get ready to cut down legions of foes and square off against a cast of rival professional killers just oozing personality as you slash a path to victory. But it's not all hack-and-slash insanity! When you're not fighting for your life, you'll do part-time jobs to buy new merch, undergo training to power up for the next ranking battle, and take your tricked-out motorbike for a spin through the streets of Santa Destroy. Features Burn rubber through the coastal city of Santa Destroy on Travis' motorbike, the Schpeltiger! Unlock a devastating arsenal of pro-wrestling moves—from Power Bombs to Brain Busters. Unleash the powerful Dark Side to mow down the competition and show 'em who's boss! Master a unique combat system that's easy as pie to pick up, but deeper than a deep-dish pizza.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, Steam Deck users, I have good news and bad news. The good news is that despite a ton of PC users reporting constant crashing and this game showing up as "unsupported," so you'd figure the game would be unplayable... Set compatibility to force the game to run on "Experimental" and you should get zero crashes. That's right. I just played from beginning to end without a single crash. Now, I didn't test out some of the reported crash triggers... (eg apparently a common crash trigger is trying to speed up through the ranking updates after each boss fight? I don't know. I played it safe & just let the animation go through.) But that's right. No crashes. Not one. The bad news? Well, JFC, it's No More Heroes and it's Travis Touchdown. Depending on your point of view there is no bad news or it's all bad news, right?I first played this game long ago on the Wii. I couldn't believe how perfect this game was. On most games, once I beat it, I'm done. Oh, there's a "NewGame+" option where you can play at a higher difficulty? Pfff. I beat the game. I'm done. NMH is one I played through several times, just because it's that much fun.Let me be clear: if you're looking for something deep, something thoughtful, something that requires a fine art of gameplay.. go play something else. If you're looking for a button-mashing killfest where you slice people in half/cut off 5 heads at once, blood spraying everywhere in fountains, weird perverts, semi-fake badassery, ultra-meta "break the fourth wall" nonsense, ADD-level distractions and a story-line that is about as thick as chicken broth... Well, this might be the one for you.Now, a lot of that sounds like a "bad thing," but let me tell you, it's not. This game is all about being... or trying to be.... the biggest, toughest assassin ever. To that end, killing is a game, and one to be taken to the next level. As Travis, you won't have ninety-two weapons to choose from, special weapons like grenades, and all that nonsense. You've got your beam katana and some wrestling moves. That's it. And even your beam katana doesn't start off as a flawless weapon.. you've got to charge it from time to time. You've entered an 'assassin ranking list,' where you have to kill your way to the #1 position by killing each of the other assassins in turn. Of course, each of those assassins has a plethora of bodyguards you've got to slice your way through first, so... have fun. 'Be careful?' pffff. Run in and go nuts. Get creative with your killing. It will be satisfying.Along the way, you've got to experience all Santa Destroy (where Travis lives) for all the money you can get. You'll need to earn plenty to pay the fight fee for each next level assassin.. and buy cool T-shirts and jackets (and more), buy videos, upgrade your katana, train with your sensei, and more. You'll have to start with menial physical labor jobs like picking up trash and wiping down graffiti, but do well and you'll be referred for some more 'shady' jobs, such as killing a hundred people before the timer runs out and things of that nature.There are tons of little side quests such as finding balls hidden around the city so you can get an old drunk to beat you up, digging up buried treasure, and other stuff.And, of course, this game will NEVER let you forget that you're playing a video game. Ever. Don't even try for immersion. It won't happen.The game is silly and makes you laugh. It's brutal and makes you say "YESSSS!" It's fast-paced so you lose track of time. It's simple. It's bloody. It's... Travis Touchdown.Yes, I remember spending who knows how many hours on the Wii hacking my way through the levels.. I loved the game so much I ended up buying one of those blue light-up controllers just so I could experience the game in a cooler way. I just loved the nonstop nonsense. Couldn't get enough.When I saw it was on Steam, I was so excited.. but then so sad when I saw all the reports of constant crashing. But again... I can't speak for PC, but it ran FLAWLESSLY on the Steam Deck when set to run on Experimental. I was so thrilled I bought NMH 2 and 3 (I had already beat Travis Strikes Again on SD) and will get to playing those... uh... as soon as I play through this title a few more times.Is it worth full price? Should you wait for a sale? For twenty bucks, I'd say this game is not only worth full price, it's worth double full price (to me at least). Yes, it's a little dated... and unlike GTA V, you won't have tons of cars and groups of people walking around the city.. it's a bit old school. But you know, somehow the developers still made such a cool world that it still feels great to me. Still feels like home. Santa Destroy.I wouldn't recommend this game to people who don't like mindless violence... but I'd recommend it to literally anyone else in the world.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally made this review just to say this:XBOX ONE DOES WORK STOP LYING TO ME I'M LITERALLY PLAYING THE GAME WITH AN XBONE CONTROLLERBut I'll add onto it and say that NO, it's NOT Dolphin repackaged. If you stopped believing random strangers saying bulls**t and actually looked at the files yourself, you will see files from the Switch port of the game (like music and videos) which in fact AREN'T in the original Wii version. So no, it's not Dolphin, it's a port of the Switch port. Now, onto the actual game review.No More Heroes is an amazing game. I beat it myself multiple times on the Wii and it's one of my all-time favorite games. How is the port like, then?I understand all the frustrations with the issues and bugs of the game, and I do think that they should fix it soon, but despite all that, I'd still recommend picking this version up. Yes, currently it has issues (like I said before), but I beat this game myself with only one ​gameplay-related issue to speak of, and that was the baseball minigame being quite broken, but otherwise, it's a perfectly fine way to enjoy the game, and it was mostly smooth sailing for me. I'd say wait for the patches to get released, but if you really want to play it now, there's no problem with that.Controls are smooth, the hack-and-slash portion of the gameplay is fun, the soundtrack is bliss for my ears, and the story is great. If you're curious for a more in-depth look at this Suda51 classic, I recommend GhenryPerez's YouTube video about this game from his Deadly Individualism series.edit:where are the patches

_childDocuments_.review: This PC port is actually awful and the team has claimed they were going to fix it for over a year now. I'll change my review if the patch actually comes out and stops me from hitting crashes on loading screens when I start ANY SIDE ASSASSINATION JOB or leave Thunder Ryu Building.It's been a very long time since I've played a PC port that crashes this often and as unpredictably. I've had less trouble with "infamously bad" PC ports because at least those work on a good day.The awful Dynasty Warriors PC ports at least have a workaround to keep the game from crashing, this one doesn't. You just have to deal with the crashing. I tried compatibility mode, no dice.EDIT: GUESS WHAT, turns out this game's exe is a 32-Bit non-LAA binary, which means the game's crashes? All out of memory errors, if you use the generic 4GB LAA patch it's more stable.EDIT EDIT: Wow, not a single crash for a 4 hour play session today, looks like my fix worked. If XSEED cared they could compile a 64-bit binary and solve the problem, their minimum specs are already in the range of 64-bit PCs, not like any 32-bit machine could run this game.EDIT EDIT EDIT: After a year, XSEED made an update saying "We're still working on it". To be clear, most of XSEED's other ports aren't this rough, their Falcom localizations are all pretty good, Rune Factory 4's port was fine outside of generally not being up-scaled well, which is an issue that the Switch version also had. Most of their other Steam releases are pretty no-frills but functional. I do not know what's happening here.

_childDocuments_.review: 🔵To fix resolution problem change the "high DPI settings" of the game executable:- Find the game executable nmh.exe on your system (manage > browse local files).- Right-click the executable, then select Properties.- Switch to the Compatibility tab and click on Change high DPI settings, under "Settings".- On the new window, under "High DPI scaling override", activate the checkbox: [✓].- Select Application from the dropdown menu and confirm with OK.- Click Apply, then OK on the Properties window.- Launch the game.Tested on: OnexPlayer Mini Pro 6800U

This version also doesn't use motion controls at all from what I can tell, which is a more complicated point. The game's controls were essentially rethought from how things worked on the Wii. This aspect is fine.This port is a small but essential patch away from being the definitive way to play No More Heroes. I don't expect us to get it at this point. If you've never played this before, got it for free and are willing to have the game flat-out lie to you about which buttons to press, please play this stylish action classic. Just don't support this inexcusably sloppy effort by paying for it.

Little did I know, both this game and its sequel would eventually come to PC, so of course I just had to pick it up. Everything I loved about the game is still here and I honestly enjoyed playing with the Xbox One controller over the Switch Pro controller.The story follows , a stereotypical otaku, who runs out of money to buy his video games and wrestling videos all thanks to him winning a bid on a katana in an internet auction. Shortly after this incident, he is introduced to  at the local bar who gives  an offer to take out assassins with a shady background in exchange for the funds he is now in desperate need of. He accepts and goes out to take down the assassins, and in the process earns himself the rank of 11 by the . Now, aspiring assassins are out for him, so he sets out to secure himself number one in the .While the story itself is fairly generic, there is one thing that makes the story special and that is the characters. We have  who is sort of a closet otaku with quite the otaku-based room, yet he tries to act like a cool guy. He has a very likable persona that I fell in love with. I really like his attitude and that he is able to keep up even though he is clumsy, he quickly became one of my favorite characters in the game. The bosses are also interesting where you get an idea of who the character is and their personalities, it's what makes them special in their own ways. One of my favorites is , a master gunslinger and corrupt vice detective that also has a talent for singing. There are other bosses but I don’t want to spoil the story too much as the characters are what make it special. truly shines in the gameplay department, mainly in combat. You have a low attack and high attack, so depending on how your enemies are blocking, you will have to mix up your moves. When you are done depleting the health of an enemy, you can initiate a finishing move where you will have to move the right joystick in that direction. When you kill the enemy, there is a slot machine mechanic that will give you a random special ability that you can use on the next enemy helping to keep things fresh.You can also learn new wrestling moves and special abilities to help deal increased damage to enemies and bosses such as having the ability to run or the ability to extend dark side mode.There are also a number of collectibles for you to find throughout the landscape and levels. So it’s best to go out into the city of  to find as many collectibles as you can.I did run into two issues with the controls. First, I used an Xbox One controller and there were times where my button commands never worked. When you knock enemies down to the ground you can do a finishing move by pressing the Y button, but the game would fail to register my button presses. There is also no police or justice system built into the game so even if you run over pedestrians with your motorcycle, nothing happens.Lastly, I should note is that some of the achievements are bugged and will not unlock or register. Lastly,  missions are very difficult because if you get hit once, it’s game over and you will have to redo the mission. You will need money to do the ranked fights so it’s best to do them to get enough for them and the upgrades which are very useful.The only issue I had with all these side activities was the fact that you can’t retry the missions when you complete or fail them. _childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed a lot of my time playing No More Heroes, I cannot in good faith give this game a good review due to just how shoddy of a port the game is, and that is due to it being a barebones port of the Switch version over to PC.  There has been a lot of debate on whether or not this game is being emulated via Dolphin, but the game will straight-up admit to you how it's a no-effort port from the Switch version when it shows a graphic for Joy-con controllers later on in the game, while also being referred to as such in the credits.That being said, I don't blame people for even getting that far, because the game has other problems PC-port wise that make the fun get sapped out of it.  Thankfully, I have an XBOX controller, but not everyone does.  The game is controller only, but only Xinput controllers are allowed.  Dualshocks, Steam Controllers, and Switch Pro Controllers, all require meddling in order to even be usable.  The game often has audio clipping with its sound effects, and framerates will often drop when encountering large groups of enemies.  Physics for certain minigames are broken, as well as counters for achievements, making 100%ing the game nigh impossible.I would still highly recommend that people play No More Heroes in some shape or form, just not buy purchasing this game (and likely its sequel, Desperate Struggle) on Steam.  Emulation using Dolphin, so I've heard, is a better alternative to experiencing this fun romp with an otaku loser through Santa Destroy.  You won't regret playing No More Heroes, but you might if you choose this way to play it.

Travis while being a blood thirsty, misogynistic, psychopath, is also surprisingly relatable in the sense that he's also just an ordinary dude trying to meet ends needs, as horrific and brutal as his methods may be. He also while not necessarilly becoming a hero, does grow and learn throughout the game that human life is precious, and that it's wrong for him to glorify death as he kills. While I do recommend you play No More Heroes, I do not recommend the PC version (or the Switch version as it has issues and is actually directly responsible for some of the issues in the PC version.) I recommend that you play the original wii version with an actual wii remote. It's by far the best way to experience the game. I especially recommend you play this game if you are in the 17-21 age demographic as it may actually help you grow as a person and change how you view a lot of things. I know it did for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The first No More Heroes is a strange game with a lot of charm. Combat has a lot of button mashing and lacks depth, but it's wrapped up in this dark, blood-splattered aesthetic that makes it compelling on a moment-to-moment basis. Enemies erupt into mesmerizing fountains of blood, paired with shrieks of unimaginable pain. There's something unsettling about how unglamorized the game's depiction of murder is. However, the combat isn't really what makes No More Heroes so special; Suda 51's unique directorial approach is what really sets the title apart. Cutscenes have this unhinged, captivating energy that can draw you into a character's raw charisma. You barely interact with the game's bosses, but they're made incredibly memorable with the precious screen time they receive. But perhaps the most memorable aspect of No More Heroes is how it depicts the typical carnage of an action titles as merely a break from Travis' boring everyday life. The title pokes fun at the idea of games as escapism by making the player engage in the exact sort of repetitive day-jobs that they're attempting to get away from. Games such as No More Heroes attract players who are looking for mindless, bloody carnage to distract them from the mundanity of their everyday life; the fact that the game lampshades this primal desire for senseless killing fascinates me. No More Heroes doesn't necessarily shame us for engaging in blood-soaked power fantasies, but it does ask us to be a bit more honest about the shallow reasons we often play games for.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally had a positive review but after some more time I'm not a fan. For 2 reasons: 1. The port 2. The game itself.1. The port is bare bones and glitchy. There's one graphical setting for AA and nothing else. The LOD is pretty terrible, the game will run at your native res only, runs like garbage on lower end systems when I tried this on my laptop (this is a Wii game, it should run on a toaster), and while it's 60fps locked there's a decent amount of micro stuttering even if you use a decent rig (I have a GTX 1080 home rig).2. The game is charming, from a writing, acting, and presentation perspective. I like Suda 51 and I like the game on a writing level a lot, but I wish he made his games better mechanically. Because the gameplay is so clunky and repetitive. It feels like a game made 10 years before it released. The boss fights are pretty great but everything around it is a slog imo. Combat is fun when you first play but then most levels leading up to bosses feel like endless empty rooms of repeating enemies.I've heard playing on hard makes the game more fun but I found the combat to just be stiff and janky; the camera doesn't adjust to you well so you're being attacked by enemies off screen and you'll miss enemies by being off to their side by a bit. The wrestling moves are cool but except for bosses feel pointless as they can't kill enemies and can leave you open to attack when trying to execute them.The open world is barren and driving your bike is janky and not fun, yet they space everything out so far from each other, and entering and leaving a place is full of loading screens and transitions. But all these things are required for progression as they lock off new bosses behind grinding for money. I just got so frustrated trying to get to the next boss I gave up.I think Suda's natural charm and nostalgia by adults who had a Wii growing up plays a big part in the game's popularity. But I had this similar issue with Lollipop Chainsaw. I loved the presentation and characters but eventually got frustrated with the gameplay.If you want to try it maybe you'll like it, get it on sale for $15. Any more than that I wouldn't waste your time and just emulate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul. No more heroes is, in every sense of the word, soulful. I use soulful as a descriptor because the game is very much flourishing in originality and creative drive, spear headed almost entirely by Suda. Suda clearly just did whatever he wanted stylistically and this is the games strongest aspect. usually, a raw creative vision being made into a game can have the opposite effect, a developer can get too caught up in their vision sacrificing the quality of the game and user enjoyment. however, no more heroes wears its uniqueness proudly while also still being made rather well, and being quite inviting. The game doesn't take itself seriously at all but it will still captivate with its raw style, especially its character design, music and writing.No more heroes' gameplay wise is fairly shallow, but the combat system is rather fun to control. The issue with the combat is the over abundance of having a room be populated by worthless, weak enemies you can just blaze through. the game isnt particularly challenging (safe for one of the end bosses), but it still managed to keep me engaged. Other action games do combat better, but no more heroes gives you something those other action games dont, its style and writing, and thats something not to overlook.(I didnt have any problems with crashing or controller support in my time playing, so my experience was unhampered)

_childDocuments_.review: No More Heroes is an incredibly jank game that is still a 10/10 experience. This is a game with a LOT of issues, that both embraces and moves past them to deliver an outstanding narrative and world, being weird as hell without sacrificing the player's experience.Just to get it out of the way: combat is repetitive and can be completely brute forced (for the most part), grinding for money can get extremely tedious, the overworld is weirdly empty, and there's some technical issues like enemy dialogue and sound effects being extremely loud relative to the music. There's also a pretty severe imbalance in the missions, with the longest being right at the start and no real variety in what you're doing in those missions showing up until the last two. Regular enemies are mostly a joke outside of those that have beam sabers or machine guns, yet sometimes there's encounters that can be a real pain in the ass with the group make up. Some of the free fight and money making side missions feel nearly impossible, and again there's a severe imbalance in the reward money you get that makes the early game require repeating missions (and those early missions are the least enjoyable). And yet, none of that matters. This game is all about the characters, the world of Santa Destroy, and the assassins themselves are the real meat of the experience. Get through the tedium of picking up coconuts and filling up cars, and you're rewarded with some of the best written individuals you'll find in any video game. Driving around the empty Santa Destroy is honestly something I came to enjoy by the end of it, providing a nice breather in between the sometimes 15+ minute boss fights and sensory overload blood sprays and screams. If you go into this and you hate it because of how tedious it can be, that's totally understandable. Don't go into it expecting Devil May Cry level intricate combat, this is a button masher that occasionally requires some strategy, with boss fights being the only time you really get to make use of anything but basic "block, hit, block, hit" tactics. This is a very, very weird game that's all about the story, and despite how goofy it looks at first glance, actually has quite a bit to say about humanity's fascination with violence and real emotions with familial trauma and betrayal.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start out by saying that No More Heroes is in my TOP 3 favorite games. I have loved it ever since I played it on the Wii. I've beaten it countless times, and have always had a good time doing it. This is the game that introduced me to the creations of Suda51, and I've enjoyed every game that he's had a hand in (that I've played, of course).No More Heroes is a game about Travis Touchdown. His entire goal in the game is to get laid, and all he has to do is climb the assassin leaderboard to reach the #1 spot. That's it, that's the story. It's absurd, it's hilarious, and it gets so bizarre that it often doesn't make a lot of sense.The game isn't perfect, but it has charm. Combat feels good, the characters are likeable, and the story is one wild ride. Although, the voice acting is a mixed bag, there's quite a bit of bloat to pad out the playtime, and the moneymaking endeavors can get repetitive.This game is worth a playthrough - it's short, it's sweet, and it's all around a good time. I managed to 100% it in around 20 hours, and I was taking my time with it.Some final thoughts:- Yes, you can pet the cat. Her name is Jeane.- Travis uses multiple toilets in the game, but he never wipes.- It's good to be back in Santa Destroy.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not exactly the biggest Suda fan, but since we got the third one coming out later this month and these two just dropped on PC, I figured I give them both a look.You've probably noticed the mixed reviews. This is not because the game itself is bad – which I’ll discuss in a bit – but rather because the PC port is incredibly lazy. The game completely lacks keyboard and mouse support, does not have any rebindable controls, is hard locked to 60 fps, and the only graphical settings are a fullscreen toggle and anti-aliasing option.It gets worse when you realize that it is an online-only game – as in, it literally cannot launch if you are offline. I have no idea why they made this a requirement given that this is a port of a singleplayer game from the Wii, but that’s the reality. That and apparently some of the achievements are bugged and the game does crash a bit for some users – I myself ran into a total of one crash.That said, it’s not entirely bad. For one, the game does run at higher resolutions (whatever your monitor is set at) and it looks far better than the 480p that we had on the Wii. That and the 60 fps is at least constant. I never had any dips there and no issues with stuttering, freezing, etc. Xbox controller support is also there and they did a decent job adapting these controls from the Switch release. I didn’t have any issues and didn’t feel the need to rebind any controls.Now as for the game itself – not bad. A bit repetitive and definitely dated overall, but still a good time. The combat is fast, responsive, and satisfying. It lacks in depth, but it does offer up a fair challenge in spite of that.What the game lacks in depth it makes up for with its incredibly creative boss fights. Sometimes they will just be a standard fight, but sometimes you’re on a bike, or dodging missiles, or shutting down a massive laser.The bosses are all over the place and really highlight Suda’s writing style. It’s one of those stories where you don’t really know where it’s going or really what is going on, but it’s just such an interesting mess that you can’t help but be sucked in by it. There’s crazy plot twists, an entire roster of oddball characters, and a touch of crude humor too.The standard gameplay is more hit-or-miss. Cutting down enemies is fun, but not when the game has you do that 100 or so times in a single area. And the simplistic level design offers very little exploration, so there’s really no getting away from the endless wave after wave of enemies.A bit of a toss-up here. On one hand, No More Heroes is fun enough and I’m glad to have finally played it – but on the other, the PC port is not great. There’s “lazy, but runs well” and then there’s “can’t launch the game offline, can’t unlock all the achievements, and occasionally crashes” kinda bad. So on that front, it is completely understandable if you outright skip it. That said, I still had a good time playing through the game and would recommend it on that aspect – it just comes with a huge warning label.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

I find the trade off to not be worth it unless you only get a few pieces  of clothing.There are different Beam Katana's that you can get throughout the game, some hitting harder but slow and others faster but weaker.Travis's movement and gameplay is a lot smoother in Desperate Struggle, though I wish he could do aerial movement and attacks. He is unfortunately glued to the ground for the most part in battle.There's an overworld you can "explore" on your motorcycle, which plays even more jank than Travis himself. You'll find practically nothing except collectibles for upgrades like the balls and small amounts of pocket change spread throughout the map as most of the city is copy and pasted buildings with some non-interactable npcs walking around to try to give the overworld life but end up making you question why even have an overworld in the first place.I recommend getting this game on discount personally unless you're a big hack-n-slash fan and want something new to play.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my absolute favorite games of all time. Decided to replay it after many years to see how it holds up and before I knew it I had done 2 playthroughs and are already starting my third. The world and ambiance of NMH1 is just so fascinating, creepy, unsettling, bizarre and weird. It blends elements of horror and dark comedy with it's beautiful cell shaded art style and gory visuals to consistently grab your attention throughout the game. The story albeit simple drops hints of something deeper, peaking your interest in the world and it's characters all the more. You play as Travis Touchdown a loser otaku trying to make ends meet by doing assassin jobs. One day while drinking away his pain he meets Silvia Christel who offers him to join the United Assassins Association with the promise that if he becomes the number 1 ranked assassin, she will offer herself to him. Travis being the gullible idiot that he is joins the association, climbing the ranks from the eleventh spot. Each boss battle is unique and memorable from battling a guy cosplaying as a super hero to an old lady pulling a shopping cart, all with their own deadly twists. SUDA 51 brings a master class in character design.The combat is simple yet has enough depth to not get boring, slicing enemies in half with your beam katana never gets old, the constant stream of blood and gore everywhere, the insane powerups and stylish visuals brings it all together so well.The music is really really good. Eerie piano notes, catchy synths and chill bass tracks bring the world alive, Masafumi Takada did an amazing job.As much as I love this game I do recognize it's not for everyone, the gameplay loop consists of working part time jobs (mini games) in order to collect funds for the next ranked battle, you can also grind assassination trial missions where you kill a certain number of enemies in a short amount of time or try to kill several waves of enemies without getting hit. The last 3 or so ranked battles require quite a lot of money, it's not too bad in my opinion but I can see that turning people off. The pacing overall sets you up to get familiarized with a pattern only for it to get thrown out the window which really helps keep the game from getting stale or too repetitive though. The controls for Travis' bike are rough, constantly crashing into things and struggling to line up your path correctly, it's overall clunky and feels janky. The hit detection/collision can be bad too, the Shinobu boss battle comes to mind as there are several wooden beams throughout and you constantly run into an invisible space around those beams causing you to get stuck. Overall, it's not a perfect game by any means but it's charm, style and personality set it apart from anything else. It's a unique and one of a kind game that forever holds a place in my heart. Great characters, great atmosphere, fun combat and stylish visuals. Can't recommend this game enough, it's a must play from me.Side note: This is a port of the Switch version which is a port of the Wii version. The port ran fine for me, it crashed once but I did find many of the button prompts to be incorrect or not changed at all from the Switch version. Ie. the Glastonbury mini game showing joy-cons for the button prompt display. In my opinion the PS3 version of this game remains the definitive version to play.

Where do I begin?:Loved the story, well-paced and well-written. Absolutely LOVED the characters, from Travis to Jeane. The gameplay is legalized crack, like it's genuinely AMAZING! If you like character action games and or hack n' slashes like Devil May Cry or Metal Gear Rising, PLEASE at least try this game. Soundtrack and voice-acting are AMAZING and really make this game's iconic characters and vibe even MORE iconic. Without saying too much because I want you guys who haven't played the game to try it out for yourselves. It's AWESOME. Keep in mind that this port and No More Heroes 2's port have issues (i.e. crashing, bugs, etc.) I recommend looking at community guides and forums if you're having issues with the game. I actually made a guide to (potentially) help remedy the crashes for the game. Keep in mind too that these are ports that are capped at 60 FPS and are just straight Nintendo Switch ports that were put on PC. If you're okay with that...wait for a sale maybe (or if you REAAAALLLY) want the games now, go ahead and pick them up, they're good introductory games to hack n' slashes and SUDA51 games alike.[Edit 02/07/2022: Replayed the game through Bitter mode and hey...it was fun. That Henry fight's a lot longer, but the rest of everything else was basically a NG+ Run. Game's pretty easy once you're all maxed out, but it's fun as hell too! Still lovin' it!][New Edit 05/13/2024: The patches released as of today DO indeed fix some of the issues, not everything, but it's big step in the right direction and I can wholeheartedly recommend these ports to people getting into the series now.]

_childDocuments_.review: First of all let me state that this game is fun as hell, like seriously it's so fun while doing missions like "Kill 100 clones in 3 minutes" assasination job. The bossfights aren't very difficult since you get overpowered by the time you reach the final hours of the game, and sometimes they can get pretty fun too! The part time jobs aren't that bad either, some of them are very fun actually like lawn mowing or motorcycle stunts. The story of the game is pretty basic, straightfoward and even predictable, the whole plot is just the main character wanting to bang the woman that gives him jobs to assasinate other assasins so he can move up the ranks and eventually become number one and bang her. Of course i won't spoil what happens when he reaches number one but you can pretty much predict it after i just explained the plot of the game. The graphics are very good looking on PC, I truly had high hopes for this PC port and my wishes were fulfilled! I know all the job has been already "done" on the Nintendo Switch and that this is practically just a port of the Switch version with no major enhacements, while that is true I'm kind of disappointed that the people who made this port didn't add keyboard and mouse support and I know, I know "Why would anyone need to play a hack 'n slash game on keyboard and mouse?" but i just feel really bad for these people that are strictly PC gamers and wanted to check these series out but they realised they could not because it didn't have mouse and keyboard support. Many great titles I got into I discovered them on Steam and normally played them with keyboard and mouse and started falling in love with them and I even bought a brand new PS4 just to play some titles that were not ported to PC yet. I'm not sure that if the same was on Switch or PS3 but in the opening cutscene of the game the main character (Travis) says "And for you there holding the controller..." which made me believe that the whole opening was re voiced because the original snippet from the original Nintendo Wii version is different and it sounds like this: "And for you there holding the Wii remote..." As i said I'm not sure if this was adopted from previous ports like the PS3 port which was completely remastered from scratch or the Switch port so I need to check that. My point here is that this is some wild dedication if they revoiced an entire cutscene with the exact same voice actor the same tone of voice just for one word to change from "Wii remote" to "Controller" just wow so amazing for a game with a small number of fans back then. Suda you did a great job on this one please make No More Heroes III. an even bigger success that this already is! All in all completely amazing game 10/10 no questions asked except,  there are just a few bugs i have to report but one already got fixed by a patch that happened a week from now while im writing this review. My problem there was that there was no Dualshock 4 support which is something common, but atleast you fixed it unlike some other devs so cheers to that! And the other bug that was bothering me and for some reason only me is every time i played the game in fullscreen the game would just run at like a really low and laggy framerate so i had to use a tuner to lock and tune up my fps, but thats just a me problem apparently so yeah! All in all good port, good game, good music, memorable characters, good voice acting, hot women (side note: pls fix the glasses disappearing from travis when you enter garderobe k thx bye).

_childDocuments_.review: Holy sh*t, what a ride. I've wanted to play this game since I saw it on the shelves in a game-stop in the late 00's, but money was limited at the time and frankly I hated the Wii as a kid... and now. Well, here it is on PC and I had to give it a chance. Originally the main thing that drew me to this game was the title and cover art of the box, they oozed style and that permeates throughout the entire game. I found my self not having fun until about the 4th boss battle, then things started to click (though I still believe the Shinobu fight is the hardest in the game, like what the hell). From there it was a wild ride, fun all the way out. To go more in-depth in the game, It's separated into two sections, and open-world with mini-games and the actual missions which all lead to the true meat of the game: The boss fights. I won't lie, the open-world is not a selling point, in fact, it's a grind at best. Yet, somehow some of the odd activities will lead to you strangely having fun, I don't know, it ended up kinda charming. As for performance, this is a bare-bones port. You can choose anti-aliasing, fullscreen, and that's about it. I had about four crashes in my 14.5 hours, twice losing pretty significant progress including having to repeat one of the least interesting boss fights. Annoying as hell, but if you connect with the game, their worth suffering through. Now, story isn't the strong suit of the game, it's the one-on-one sword play with the bosses, but at times the story hits harder than it has any right to, when it really doesn't take itself seriously 90% of the time. Now, if you don't care about relatively minor spoilers, here's a final excerpt from my time playing the game to try to sell you on giving it a shot:*SPOILERS*You ever find yourself in a toxic waste dump trying to catch poisonous scorpions so you can earn enough money to fix your Master's Laser Katana after he died in a tragic giant future cannon accident after he picked a fight with an old lady who turned out to be the 3rd ranked assassin in America, who you're there to kill so you can bang a French girl, but then one of the scorpions stings you so you have to race back to your boss so he can give you an antivenom shot in the ass, but you don't make in time so you have to start over? ...Y'all should play No More Heroes.

_childDocuments_.review: NO MORE HEROES is a third person action brawling hack and slash by GRASSHOPPER MANUFACTURE and SUDA51.This game is loads of fun. The base gameplay loop is simple. Hack and slash your way to number 1. To do so, you'll take on oddjobs (minigames) to make enough  scratch to participate in the next ranked fight, then, you go to a location, genocide mook goons, then fight a boss.This game marks Suda51's breakout in the west. While THE SILVER CASE, and FLOWER, SUN, and RAIN were cerebral noir thrillers, and mystery's, NO MORE HEROES is a punk action game and it doesn't pull any punches. You have High and Low slashes, and enemies can block high and low. You break low guards with high slashes and vice versa. The main combat is silky smooth and still to this day is satisfying as hell.Inbetween your ranked fights, you need more money for the next entry fee. To get this dough, you can take on "free fight missions" (kill all enemies in a time limit without taking one hit), or, get a job like the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ neet you are and pump cars full of gas, deliver coconuts, mow lawns, pick up trash, remove graffiti, or pick uo scorpions. All of the jobs are mini games, and even the most "boring" ones are engaging, and you can infinitely replay them for all the money you could ever want.NO MORE HEROES is a satire of open world games. A lot of people hated this games open world when this game came out because there was "nothing to do", but that's the point. its mocking games like GTA and Jak II with big open areas with nothing much than point a to b affairs. The Boss Fights are the star of the game. Shinobu, Rank 8, is the good ole Suda51 "filter" fight. Rank 10 and 9 can be beaten easy, but Shinobu locks you in to basically an 8 - 15 min boss fight because if you get greedy, she'll insta-kill you, and every fight after her has 1 or 2 insta-kill moves. If you can beat Shinobu, you can beat this game.The games story is a parody of hyperviolent games, and it works for what it is. Travis is an absolutely loath full otaku Anti-Hero who doesn't seem to have much going for him, but as you work through the game you start to sympathize with and understand his position. All of the boss characters are distinct and diverse, in both backstory and fights, and the game never wants to let up at all.This is a port of the Switch version. It runs alright, but I will say this, as well for 2. Run the game in Win 7 compat. There's a well known crash after the ranking system in this game that will crash you if you've played for a long session at the rank up screen. Running in win 7 compat seems to fix this error and I haven't had an issue with it since. The baseball assassin mini game is broken on pc, because it uses motion controls to determine how hard you hit the ball. Those problems aside, NO MORE HEROES is well worth your time, and one of the action hack and slash greats. Absolute must buy.<UPDATE MAY 15th 2024>An update came out for NMH that removed most Switch port elements, and the game NOW has glyph support for keyboard and mouse, AND xbox game pads and playstation. They have committed a bunch of bug fixes, and, also added a feature where, if you hold the turbo button after a bike crash, it speeds up the animation.I tested the classic good ole "if you skip the ranking animation the game crashes" bug, and, I'm happy to say, it's fixed! The game may not require to be ran on Windows 7 compatibility now, but I've kept it on regardless. Either way, the game is far more stabler now.

_childDocuments_.review: MOE~So, I've known about this game for years and didn't have the chance to play it until now. Take this as the opinion of the game itself and not how it holds up as a port, although I'll mention I didn't have any major issues like crashes or game breaking glitches, just some frame drops.So, No More Heroes, the game about a weirdo loser becoming an assassin to make use of his new light saber he bought on eBay. The gameplay is pretty fun, the boss fights are the main highlight of the game with all of them being colorful, interesting characters that play well of our hero's personality. Some combo moves with certain combinations of high and low stance attacks would have been cool, but no such luck. The combat is still fun, especially with how over the top it can be. Always love a good suplex after all.Presentation is pretty good, the overall style holds up rather well, and character designs are memorable as well. Music can be pretty top-tier. Voice acting is great.The only things I didn't really like about the game was grinding for money in between the ranking fights to get all the upgrades as well as just pay to enter the level. Also those free fight one-hit-KO missions could be really frustrating. Overall, the game is pretty solid, but has a few noticeable cracks here and there. I'd give it like an 8/10, definitely worth a try, even just to see how weird it can be.

_childDocuments_.review: The core game here is still the Wii cult classic, which is fantastic. However, I cannot wholeheartedly recommend this port of the game until (or rather IF) the developers patch out its frankly numerous issues. Attack animations are broken, achievements are broken, the sound is too loud, the config launcher is barebones and most of its settings appear to have no effect on the actual game, the game is locked to 1080p resolution with no option to lower or raise it, until very recently most controller types weren't supported despite the game REQUIRING a controller to play due to the lack of keyboard and mouse controls, the baseball segments are broken, and most damningly of all, this single-player game with no online features whatsoever requires an internet connection for the game to run, despite the store page saying otherwise. In the event that this port is fixed, I'll amend my review to reflect the changes made. Until then, avoid it.EDIT: It has been almost two years since this port launched, and apart from one series-wide forum post announcing new patches for all of the No More Heroes games, the "fine" people at Xseed have been radio silent about when or even if these abysmal ports will ever be fixed. Even joining their official Discord to ask the developers directly gets you no straight answer. I'm begging you, please buy literally any other version of these games, because it's becomeing more and more apparent that Xseed doesn't care to fix their incompetent work.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely fantastic, it's truly entertaining, as a game should be. Originally the reviews left me skeptical, so allow me to address the issues through my personal experience.Bugs, crashes, game being old, etc.: I've only had ONE game breaking bug that required a restart, no crashes, and the unstable nature is greatly overstated from my experience.The need to earn money to participate in boss fights: This one I'm a little harsh on, because I flat out think it's a stupid complaint. It reeks of a short attention span and incapability to understand responsibility. Yes, you do have to do some jobs to afford the next boss, but they are WAY simpler than some reviews would lead you to believe. Finishing a boss fight gives you money, and the more missions you do, the more you unlock which give you more money. On average I literally have to do like three missions for the next fight, it isn't that bad. If you can't handle a little bit of work and a little repetitiveness then you should be less worried about video game jobs and more about how you'll hold a real one.Vehicle controls and Open world: The vehicle controls really ain't that bad at all if you're playing on controller, I can't speak for keyboard since I haven't tried it. The "Open world' truly does not matter in the slightest, exploration and discoveries are NOT gonna happen here, this is just some generic american city that you'll primarily just be crossing for shops, mission objectives, and maybe even collectibles. If you actually care about an open world aspect, you will be immeasurably disappointed.Too repetitive: This is somewhat true if you're not all that big of a fan of the game. Me personally, I think the game is hilarious and interesting, and I care about the writing, characters, and boss fights enough to not mind the repetitive nature, since I look forward to the next character I'll meet, and how their unique fight will unfold.My main conclusion is, if you think you'll care about no more heroes, or if you want an extremely unique game to look into, you'll enjoy yourself. If you're looking for a quick bit of hack and slash fun, just go play Devil May Cry, it's combat is more stimulating anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally released for the Wii back in 2007, No More Heroes is like a cross between Kill Bill and the graphic novel Scott Pilgrim. The main character, Travis Touchdown, must climb an assassin's ranking system to become the number one ranked assassin. To lengthen the game, each boss is hidden by an in-game paywall where you must do side jobs to pay the fee to fight the next assassin. While this would be tiring and repetitive at first, some jobs are much more straightforward than others. While the game was originally released on the Wii, this version of No More Heroes seems to be more of a port of the 2019 remastered version of the game released for the Switch. The Wii version's open-world area had a terrible frame rate, which this version seems to fix. Aside from the motorcycle controls being rubbish, the game controls very well as Travis has both a heavy and light attack. Travis cannot constantly attack, as his bootleg lightsaber needs to be recharged by wiggling the right control stick.Overall, this is a lot better of a game than the original Wii version.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this a Negative Rating because there's no neutral one and this port and game really doesn't need more smoke blown up it's rear.The port itself is very poorly made, i was actually shocked givin that xseeds last port i played was Daemon X Machina which was fantastic, with lots of options, key rebindings and stellar mouse and keyboard controls. This one however and i assume by extension No More Hereos 2 (Have not tried that port as of yet) are the complete opposite. So many issues that someone must have just glanced over and ignored for them to not be noticed and fixed. From textures disappearing to the instructions giving you wrong button inputs (There is even a switch controller being shown for the controls of one of the minigamey sections) to not coming up with the simple idea to include a bit of quality of life stuff or atleast make some things less jank. This is as barebones of a port as you can get as if it was copypasted straight from the switch. And with that i'd like to move on to the game itself.Unlike a lot of people i have no nostalgia for this game as i have never played it before, which in turn after now having finished it and gotten the true ending really makes me wonder why the game is getting this overabundance of praise. This game has a lot of issues which led to me ultimately coming out of this experience with very much "Meh" -feeling torwards this game. Let me give you a list of examples, some of which could've and should've been fixed from Original Game seeing as this is a port of a second rerelease of this game but have been left in for no reason other then lazyness, and some of which are just ingrained into the game:-The Motorcycle controls, no one and i mean no one can tell me they honestly think these are good. It's stiff and delayed and the game feels like complete jank when you happen to run into a car or crash and happen to get travis land inside the bikes model, in which case you can even get stuck in it. And the game later expects you to drive this monstrosity through a lazily designed obstacle course to get to one of your rank fights, which btw ends with a quick time event which if not done correctly kills you and resets you back to the beginning of the level. (That gave me Bayonetta 1 Cutscene Death Flashbacks)-The Overworld, it is no secret that suda didn't want the overworld in the game to begin with which is why the second game doesn't have one. But nonetheless it's here and it's big, empty and a waste of everyone's time. Not helping this is the fact that inorder to proceed through the game you to farm money, which you do by doing sidemissions which with the exception of "Don't get hit" Missions have to be accepted from the jobcenter, then be drivin to manually, and then you'll have to drive back to the job center to accept another one, and you'll do this loop over and over if you want to get the most of the game. Sure you could just do the "Don't get hit missions" inbetween when you come across them to make up for it but these feed into my next issue...-The absolute lack of quality of life improvements, when you do a sidemission, you get told on the top right what the mission is about and if necessary what special controls you'll have to use. Sounds good at first, but this quickly becomes an annoyance when you try to do the "Don't get hit" missions. When you get hit and you will, you will get booted out of the mission. There's no Retry option or anything of the sorts, which means you'll get a loading screen, go back to overworld, accept the mission again, get another loading screen, mash through mission instruction and ignite your beamsaber only to try the mission again. And as you keep failing this time builds up. There's no reason for the instruction to pop up again after first time, there's also no reason for there to not just be a retry button to cut loading times AND the unnecessary instructions. This honestly made me ignore "Don't get hit" missions after a while because I'd rather go drive to a mission i know i can complete, then to be mashing and waiting just to get another shot at a mission in which it is very easy to mess up because enemies have longer melee range then travis, can attack faster then travis and there's also ranged enemies with guns which will 100% hit you and make you hate your life if you even slightly mess up your attack timing which feeds into yet another issue and probably the one i will get the most flag about...-The combat system, i will say it right away, is bare bones and really not good. Now before you grab the pitchforks hear me out. There is no dedicated block button instead you block by locking onto an enemy and not pressing attack , i don't even mind that it only blocks in one direction if it werent for the fact that you can't decide who you're gonna lock on to. Instead travis will lock on to whatever enemy is closest which can result in you getting turned around and that in turn if there are more enemies around, will leave you open to getting hit. The Energy meter which at first seems like a neat idea also comes off as annoying in a lot of situations, especially when you're being ganged up on while out of juice in which case eat ♥♥♥♥ and die. And tho these can be played around by kiting and being precautious they're not even my biggest gripe with the combat. No, no no, cause that would be bossfights. A good portion of the bosses in this game don't give a flip about engaging with half the combat options. Most of them can't get hit unless they've performed an attack and are in downtime state, with them even blocking charged attacks (are these a joke to you?) and later on (unless my game was just being buggy) they even ignore perfect dodge counters and the final boss is even punishing you for trying to do grabs. So the further you get the less options to attack you get and the more the game becomes a slog of you baiting out enemy attacks so you can get hits in during recovery animations, which gets worse because the bosses become more healthspongy and get annoying moves that you're unable to punish and will have to wait them out and hope they do a different move afterwards, oh and the Boss AI selects these moves at random so it's very much possible that they'll spam these. It's funny that the secret true ending boss of all things mostly does away with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and let's you fight him proper and to no surprise is the boss i enjoyed the most.So overall what are my thoughts? The game is just okay. it has a lot of tedium, some of which could have been smoothed out with this port or the previous rereleases. And as someone who plays both fast paced action games like DMC or Bayonneta and punishing/difficult games like Dark Souls or Nioh, No More Heroes is unable to hit the right rythm in either direction. (Here's hoping the second game improved on this). Really when people speak so fondly of this game i can't help but feel that they only think about the writing and completely drown out the bad parts. (the Gundam topdown shoot'em'up section sucks and you know it)TL:DR the game is a 6 out of 10. It's okay but i wouldn't grab it at full price if you're new to the series and are trying to get into it, especially since the port is very lazy. And if you're a fan of the series you won't care eitherway since you allready bought it and gave it a positive review just because "IT'S NO MORE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ HEROES!!!!!!!1!111!" /jk

_childDocuments_.review: BLUEBERRY CHEESE BROWNIEAlright, so Grasshopper Manufacture's NMH series is crass and extremely stupid, but very fun. The combat on controller is kind of awkward but not terrible (that being said, it's clear from the get-go that it was designed with motion controls in mind, and I think the QTEs using the right stick makes this glaringly obvious -- they cause fatigue relatively quickly and are somewhat worse than button prompt QTEs).The game has not aged particularly well, but you're probably aware of its age going in, assuming you're a longtime Suda51 fan. The game has v-sync forced on without any way to disable it (as far as I'm aware of), at least one song has been removed due to a lapse in licensing (this was the issue with the old PS3 version of this game), the audio distorts often, at least during the first boss fight, and there's no way to change the resolution of the textures in-game, resulting in some pretty blurry and artifact-filled jpegs that are occasionally stretched due to the new aspect ratio.I don't know if the issues here will be fixed, considering Grasshopper Manufacture is a relatively small studio with a finite source of money, and the company that did the port were likely contracted out for a quick release before the new No More Heroes game comes out.Be cautious if you're considering purchasing. I'll update the review if people are able to figure out how to fiddle with the PC settings and fix some of the aforementioned problems.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to judge the GAME and the PORT separately and split the review into 2 sections.[[THE GAME]]The game is pretty good and the story top notch. It oozes style and the humor breaks the 4th wall on occasion. The combat is clever and translates to the controller better than I expected. There are tons of mini games for making $$ and they mostly range between fun time wasters and boring busy work. There are also assassination side missions which are pretty fun and challenging, although sometimes they are a bit too difficult requiring you to not get hit. That goal would be okay if the game had a good dodge and parry system but those aspects are pretty half baked in this game. However the open world part is just as bland as it was back on the Wii. The driving is super stiff as well. The meat and potatoes of this game is in the story and style.Score: 7/10[[THE PORT]]This port however has some serious issues. Incorrect button prompts, the players motorcycle despawns sometimes after entering a store, frequent freezing (infinite loading screens) when leaving certain buildings, and left over graphics from the Switch version even showing JoyCons on the screen in one part of the game. The most important one I want to point out is the frequent freezing on loading screens requiring you to quit the game from task manager. After causing me to lose progress while grinding for money several times I just decided to use cheat engine and give myself the money in order to see the story through to the end with less frustration. People shouldn't have to cheat or suffer through a repeated loss of progress in order to reach the end of a game.Score: 4/10
