_childDocuments_.review: + excellent writing and voice acting+ every character has charm and wit+ some of gaming's best bosses+ really upbeat and frenetic soundtrack- side quests only serve to pad length- open world is awful to navigate, contains nothing of note- abysmal PC port, lots of issuesI'd beaten No More Heroes a few times by now and I always get a newfound appreciation for it each time. Its characters, in particular Travis, are a mishmash pastiche of action movie stars, otaku culture, and American popular media. Every character is written well and acted well, even if you can tell the game is a little bit lower budget. It's cool to revisit as I get older as I understand the references or understand context a bit more.As a postmodernist punk fantasy, it pushes the envelope for art in gaming: Suda51 really is an auteur and I'd consider No More Heroes the best example of his games that illustrates it. I haven't been a huge fan of some of his other works but No More Heroes always appealed to me and it's understandable why Travis has graced multiple titles when Suda51 typically is a "one and done" guy.The gameplay is bloody and crass, it's so over the top that it's lovely in a macabre way. Beauty in ugliness, you know? It may be simpler than most character action games, but it's effective. You've only a high and low attack, combos are basically just chaining inputs together, and you can opportunistically land wrestling moves if a prompt procs. There's not much to it but it's still engaging because it's fast and frenetic like a character action game should be.Bosses are the real standouts and are the real reason to play the game. Their musical tracks have themes related to their character or fights, and their pre- and post-fight cutscenes are wacky but also often poignant. Bosses are mechanically distinct and can be very lengthy by boss standards. One caveat, though, is they can be very challenging, especially if you don't grasp dodging and sidestepping early on. There's some crucial skills you'll need for later bosses that may not be explicitly explained but you grasp with practice and experimentation.But everything besides the bosses and the stages leading up to them are... pretty bad to put it nicely. The open world is devoid of things to do or interesting things to see, and what you do outside of the main story is busywork for the sake of busywork. To continue with the story, you need to periodically have a certain amount of money amassed and you gain money by doing menial jobs like cutting grass or collecting coconuts. It's boring and blatant padding for game length. Some combat objectives are to be found here but they felt more like checklist ticking than anything meaningful.Maybe it's sacrilege to say but if you can find an efficient way to farm money (or use cheats to get infinite money), you can skip all of that entirely and focus just on the story. Otherwise, you end up spending stretches of 30-60min every time you're back in the overworld just to afford the next boss. It's boring and uninteresting, but worth it to trudge through to get to the meat of the game, though.The PC port is a mess. No graphic settings besides antialiasing and a toggle for fullscreen, I frequently encountered missing input glyphs in tutorial screens and was greeted with a Switch controller to describe a layout for a minigame, even. Sometimes effects are broken, like lasers shooting out of the air instead of a boss' eyes, or missing textures and glitchy shadows. As well, achievements are broken because many of them don't track, or reset counters. There's also some crashes: you roll the dice on load screens and on ranking update screens, unfortunately. The issues are small but plentiful, they concatenate into frustration that makes me wonder why no one playtested this. Despite the issues, I still think No More Heroes is one of those timeless games because of its music, bosses, writing, and humor. It's something you can replay every few years and have a blast, provided you can ignore the monotony accompanying the story. It's definitely a must-play, just maybe not on a PC. Good game, but awful port. Awful awful awful port. Consider my recommendation assuming a best case scenario where you don't experience crashes or gamebreaking issues, because the underlying game is really quite good.With max TDP at 5w, it can keep 60fps throughout. I noticed very minor dips to 50s when traversing the open world but never in a mission and never in combat. Controls well on Deck. There are no ways to have some kind of motion control input for use with the Deck's gyro but it's a "nice to have" and not a requirement.No support. There's no option to choose resolution and the default pillarboxes to 16:9.The requirements are not steep, it would be hard to find a PC incapable of hitting high framerates, but there's only a barebones selection of PC-related options. Antialiasing is really the only graphics option, not even v-sync is here. If your monitor is above 60hz, you might encounter tearing. I did despite having global g-sync on. You may need to look for mods or cap your monitor's refreshrate to get a smooth experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Cat petting simulator I've ever played. The pros: -Great hack n' slash game. -Excellent story. -Great voice acting. -Gorgeous graphics (if that's what you're into). -Extremely gorey (in a good way.) The gore is all over-the-top and not a horror-porn kind. I think even the queasiest of stomachs could handle this. The cons:-The whole game is basically 10 boss fights with some tedious mini-games in between. Very simple. -The bike handles like it's made of legos. You'll fall over a lot. There's this weird problem where you'll have to back away from the bike to activate the hotkey again if you messed it up the first time. -Weird bug: my audio settings reset after every time I use a save spot. -Based off my 20 minutes of searching, it's currently impossible to 100%. One of the achievements is bugged.I played the game on Wii when I was 15 or so and it was a great walk down memory lane. Mostly. A lot of the mini games are incredibly frustrating. Half of them are basically just "walk around and collect stuff. Then you get paid." Those are fine and mostly mindless. The other half is "kill as many people as much as possible. You only have 1hp. You get X,000 dollars for each kill." Frustratingly the instructions imply that you'll get paid even if you only kill 1. That's a lie. It's all or none. Even more frustrating, quite often the invincibility frames of your moves magically and randomly lose their invincibility and an enemy's attack will slide through and force you to restart. Oh, and there's no restart button. Every time you die, you get kicked out to the open world and have to go back in. That's two loading screens, the same instructions you've seen a few dozen times, and another mini-cut scene of Travis pulling out his beam saber. If you've upgraded your sword all the way, it's even more aggravating because that sword has horribly long animations where you're completely vulnerable. Eventually you'll "get gud" and start to read the enemies better, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is a irritating process. My controller took some structural damage towards the end of this game because the deeper into the game you go, the more you have to play these mini games to collect more money. It really was a nostalgic experience. Just like I haven't played this game in 13 years, I also haven't broken a controller in about that long. It was made in 2007 and some of the mechanics really show. But I still love it. May you find your proper path.

_childDocuments_.review: No More Heroes is an action-combat hack-and-slash set is a pseudo-futuristic America where life is cheap, and hitmen kill each other in a brutal game of dominance. The game is redolent of other action-combat titles, such as DMC, and brought to us from the colourful and crazed imagination of Suda51. As a beat-em-up style game, NMH is fairly basic, though that is partly due to this being a port from the Nintendo Wii. For fans of combat style-em-ups, NMH will probably feel a little too shallow, but is quite friendly to those newer to this type of genre. However, even those who find the gameplay wanting, may still enjoy it's colourful characters and bizarre story.You play as newly minted Hitman: Travis Touchdown. While some will find Travis to be somewhat obnoxious, it is part of what makes him compelling. Travis is something of a dorky loser, spurred on by his own desires, and kept alive only due to his odd talent for combat. He is the sort of person who lives out of a dingey motel, but also drops absurd amounts of cash on collectables. He is a witless Otaku, who, despite everything, is at least true to his own desires unconstrained by normal considerations of society.While many may, perhaps rightly, see Travis as an absurd psychopathic human being, he is also interesting for those same reasons. Travis exists on the opposite end of the typical brooding, cool, assassin archetype so often found in games. He opposes the notion of killing requiring an overly complicated philosophy behind it, and that life is better when one is unreservedly honest about their desires. This belief, and others, are explored as Travis combats 10 ranked assassins in his nonsensical journey to be the United Assassins Association's top hitman.To reach the top, Travis needs to find each Ranked Assassin and defeat them to take their rank for himself, a task that almost invariably requires him to slay his opponent. Each Ranked Assassin has their own mission, exploring a new combat area populated by thugs, goons, and sundry lesser killers who will need to be slaughtered. To do this, Travis uses a Beam Sword, able to slice enemies into humorous pieces.Combat is comprised of High and Low attacks both with the Beam Sword and with martial arts. Your sword damages health, while martial arts will stun them, allowing wrestling moves. Once an enemy is low enough, an you enter a sort of zen 'killing blow' mechanic. You can mix up your combat by dodging or clash against an enemy in a quick time events. Lastly the Beam Sword can be charged for devastating wide swings, or for powerful leaping attacks.While the above may seem to be somewhat complex, it actually boils down to four buttons and some minor dodging and lock-on mechanics. It is rather easy, at least in most ranked missions. Enemies are not bright, and some simple movement is typically all that is needed to position them in front of you in order to quickly attack multiple enemies at once. This makes a lot of the mission combat straight forward and it can become boring. Bosses, on the other hand, can be more compelling, as their unique moves can be learned and defended against. As the game's focus is on the 10 Ranked assassins as Bosses, this is much appreciated.Part of the trouble with the game's simple combat is that No More Heroes was originally for the Wii, and is tailor made to use the motion controls to the fullest. As such, playing on PC with a gamepad removes a great deal of complexity. Where on the Wii, Travis's blade was supposed to mimic the player, having them need to quickly move to attack enemies blind sports, this quickly becomes button mashing on  the controller. Similarly, the side quest mini games are also far more compelling when you consider they were designed to use the full novelty of motion controls. With this in mind, I can see how creative No More Heroes really is/was, even if my own experience has been diluted by the nature of porting it to PC. All that said, what may draw people most to NMH, is it's bizarre story telling.[BEWARE, Here there be Spoilers.]Travis's journey begins with a drunken night where he meets the beautiful and enigmatic Sylvia, who tricks Travis into the life of a hitman, even plying him with the idea sex. But becoming a ranked assassin, Travis is now a target. Too late for regrets, Travis decides to enjoy the ride and revel in his new found passion for being a killer.Each mission has him pitted against one of 10 deadly, and strange, assassins, whose own philosophies and motivations clash against Travis'. Each one carves away part of our superficial understanding of Travis, showing who he really is.10. Death Metal, is a older assassin. As the first boss, he has everything Travis thinks he wants materially. However, he cautions Travis that the paradise around them is hollow.9. Dr. Peace, is a corrupt Detective who sings his lament over the pain of his estrangement with his daughter. Dr. Peace is again, a warning over what can be lost in pursuit of wealth and power. Strangely enough, on death, Travis returns the microphone to his hand, and not his gun.8. Shinobu, a teenage swordswoman seeking to avenge her father, but willing to slay anyone to do so. While Travis does not accuse her for killing witnesses, he notes that they could not have posed much resistance, showing us how Travis enjoys killing as a matter skill and sport.7. Destroyman, is a villain dressed in a gaudy superhero costume. While at a glance you might think his egotistical personality is a mirror for Travis, their fight shows that Travis is an honest fighter, valuing true victory without cowardice.6. Holly Summers, is a beautiful and intelligent woman, seeking understanding in life and death. She reveals that Travis cannot bring himself to slay a woman, and causes him to reflect on his nature as a killer.5. Letz Shake, is killed before he has the chance to fight. Travis becomes upset that he was robbed on the battle, despite getting the rank.4. Harvey Volodarskii is a performer.  At a stretch, both he and Travis see death as entertainment, but where Harvey sees it has a gaudy show.3. Speed Buster is an old woman able to kill incredibly powerful opponents using her massive energy cannon. She slays Travis' mentor, Thunder Ryu, before the fight begins, throwing Travis into a vengeful rage.2. Bad Girl is just as crass as Travis, but the majority of her kills are from bound individuals sent to her on a conveyor belt and treats the whole affair as a job with no greater meaning or joy. This contrasts with Travis's need to challenge, and the reverence he has for the fight.1. Jeane, is the true final boss, and Travis' half sister. She is the true reason he became an assassin, Sylvia having actually promised to bring Travis to his parents murderer. With bare motivations, he accepts Jeane had her reasons for murdering his (and her) parents. However, she also killed his innocent mother, traumatised him, plunged him into ruin, and ultimately destroyed his life.In a strange, dark way, after killing Jeane, Travis achieves a sort of enlightenment. He is a bloodthirsty killer, but not a mindless one. He admits that even though his father deserved his death, he could still avenge the life taken from him, and better man he could have been.This introspection, which has been built through each boss fight, is truly interesting. While the story can be nonsensical and the world absurd, NMH rewards those who free themselves to revel in it. While the port has it's issues, and some of the fun is lost without motion controls, it is still fun and unique. Those who favor deep technical fighters, may be disappointed, but those who enjoy bombastic action and humor will be entertained. You may feel I have been overly kind in my intellectual analysis, and that may be fair. As Travis says himself: "[It's not good thing] Seeking meaning in everything... especially killing."

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10 (newcomer to series)This is strictly for the games sake. The game runs well, no real issues except for the rank 5 fight or something you have to wait for score screen to play out completely or else it crashes.Tedious as all get out. You have ranked missions which are basically the true story missions. You end up having to complete side jobs and assassination missions too in between. These really bog down gameplay experience. With the city so bland and looks like ancient graphics, you get very tired having to motorcycle around and around, when it could've been a menu system or a phone menu thing. Fighting is weird. EVERY kill must be done by an timed animation thingy where you either need to swipe up on joystick or left/right. Those quick time things really slow things down. Every. Single. Enemy. Makes me almost want to "not" call this game a hack 'n slash, its a quick time event action game? Travis also moves pretty slow too, no sprinting, only 2 speeds; stopped and "running".Audio is atrocious.... So poorly mixed. Enemies death yell almost breaks my speakers while the music is quiet AF.Boss fights are a cool experience at first for the first couple of rank missions, but then rank 6 is a brutal awakening on how cheap every enemy boss is. Every boss has different mechanics that are kind of fun to figure out, but when I got to the rank 2 mission, it really took a turn for the worst. Always waiting for your opening, which is usual in games, but here its like the bosses are way cheaper, and kind of lazily done.(?)I grinded out 498,000 for a newer sword so I could more efficiently kill the rank 2 boss... Still seems to take her health at the same-ish rate. From my google searches, this is a notorious boss for her super slim margins for openings; and even then its always just 2 hits from my sword, then wait for the next opening. Its harder to imagine I'm sure, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I am so tired of waiting for a attack opening. She constantly is in a state of involunerability, aka cannot do any damage UNTIL she attacks. This may sound like a usual boss mechanic, but here it's so brutal and slim that I start to not have the patience or care to try and validate the gameplay. It just sucks, does not feel fun. The off beat story is refreshing to be sure, but paired with archaic gameplay mechanics (grinding $$$; also for example, there is no lootable gear, no clothing drops, no dropped weapons, EVERYTHING needs to be bought. And money is such a grind in this game, the enemies drop such little cash in comparison its almost funny but actually sad.Wish the gameplay was as good as the off beat story. The story here really is what's going to keep you wanting to play. What happens to Travis when he climbs the ranks completely? Its fun to want to find out, but I also don't want to get as mad as I've gotten at the slowness of everything together.TLDRStory is pretty good/alright and refreshing; combat could be improved to make it a real hack 'n slash because flow stops too much for quick time events every enemy; too much filler: side-missions & assassination-missions = grind for money. Just let me get to ranked missions, they're the real fun.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could some up "No More Heroes" in a few words it's: comical story, but awfully repetitious.I was first introduced to the game as a teenager and it truly feels as though it's catered to that audience -- and, don't get me wrong, that can be a good thing. But revisiting it nearly 10 years later, I cannot suggest the first "No More Heroes" in good faith to the average "adult" player.It has a ton of comic and retro-inspired flavor to it; however, it is not enough to carry the immense amount of filler shoved into the game. It feels as though you are watching an anime with more filler than there is actual plot. I would say 80% of the game is spent doing fetch quest while the other 20% is fighting bosses who can oftentimes feel repetitive and uninspired.Not only that, you can often hear some of the awkward voice lines up to five times within seconds of one another.Despite my gripes with the game, I am a person that loves the manga/comic art-style enough to play the second installment -- though I hope a lot of my criticisms are fixed next go round.

_childDocuments_.review: Suda51's games are pretty much acid dreams given life, and I've gotten used to that. But I can't recommend this game because of the horrible job that was done by the team that put this on Steam and Switch.I experienced crashes just about hourly while playing this game. Usually whenever the loading icon came up when I was about to save or complete a cutscene. This required me to beat a couple of the ranked bosses twice. Infuriating point number one.The controls are garbage. The tutorial tries to explain all the things you can do, but there's so much to remember. And several bosses have instant kill attacks that are difficult to avoid if you are in the wrong place at the wrong time, or have reflexes over a millisecond to react. The final rank is especially infuriating, because there is a bike race sequence that ends in jumping a bridge, and the game offers no guidance on how to survive it. You basically have to either keep trying (And when you fail, do the WHOLE thing over again) until you get right, or look up an FAQ. Infuriating point number two.And lastly, the game just isn't that fun for most of the final third of ranked battles. You've seen everything there is to see, half of the assassination jobs are impossible to get Gold on, and the side jobs are tedious and take all of one playthrough each to get the most out of them. Just an absolutely un-fun slog until you fight the two near-impossible final bosses.I liked the presentation of the game, the off the wall story and the humorous and weird moments. But honestly, save yourself some money and just watch a playthrough on YouTube if you're that curious. The developer stated two years ago that they're trying to make the game better, and as near as I can tell they haven't done anything to accomplish that.A rancid port made by a rancid porting team. _childDocuments_.review: The game has been updated as of May 2024 and can be 100% completed. No More Heroes is a fun hack and slash game that has a very simple premise: You are rank 11th assassin in the world, and you must reach number 1 by killing all the other assassins. The game feels like what if Kevin Smith took a Tarrantino plot and fused it with Star Wars to make a game. It has a dorky plot, silly over the top characters and wacky gameplay - everything you want from a game by Goichi Suda and his Grasshopper Manufacture team.It is a port of an old Wii game, so it feels a bit stiff to control at times, the open world section is barren and you can get caught on scenery or other vehicles, but the combat on the other hand is immensely fun; A fine mix of swordplay and wrestling. You engage groups of enemies, where you must use a series of high and low attack combos to defeat them. You can stun foes and use wrestling grapple moves to subdue or finish them quickly, or you can rely on dodges and parries to deliver decisive blows.There is an upgrades system in the game, Travis can go to the Gym to get stronger, collect balls and see a retired master to learn new combos and moves. There are collectable cards and balls to find. Hidden money, and mini games  in the form of side jobs and assassinations to do, and finally, street brawls. If you want to get all of the upgrades for Travis and his swords, you will have to complete most of them (Or unlock Assassination mission 18 and grind - which is advised for ease.)The game can be beat in under 15 hours on the easy or normal difficulty, and under 12 on the hardest difficulty IF you have all of the upgrades. I racked up more hours as I was a bit stuck on four boss encounters but once I mastered dodges and parries, the game got easier. I recommend Mild (normal) difficulty, then Bitter (Hard) next as you can get 100% completion that way, and 100% achievements. The game was littered with issues and bugs, achievements not popping, unwinnable baseball minigames due to the lack of motion controls, however most of the bugs have been fixed. The biggest problem is that the game comes across as grindy at times, but with perseverence it is doable.The game has a goofy plot and is very self aware. It never once takes itself seriously, and that makes it a gem in my eyes. You should play it.

_childDocuments_.review: No More Heroes, developed by Grasshopper Manufacture and directed by Suda51, is a stylish and eccentric action-adventure game that breaks the mold with its unique blend of over-the-top combat, irreverent humor, and a captivating storyline. With its distinctive visual style, addictive gameplay, and memorable characters, No More Heroes stands as a true gem in the realm of video game eccentricity.One of the standout features of No More Heroes is its unapologetically eccentric style and tone. Players assume the role of Travis Touchdown, an unlikely anti-hero armed with a beam katana, as he sets out on a quest to become the world's number one assassin. The game's unique blend of hack-and-slash combat, open-world exploration, and outrageous boss battles creates a thrilling and unpredictable gameplay experience. From battling bizarre assassins to engaging in quirky side activities, every moment in No More Heroes is filled with unexpected surprises, irreverent humor, and an unabashed love for the medium of video games.Visually, No More Heroes presents a striking visual style that combines cel-shaded graphics, vibrant colors, and comic book-inspired cutscenes. The game's art direction pays homage to various pop culture references and manga aesthetics, creating a visually captivating and dynamic world. The character designs are imaginative and memorable, each boasting their own distinct personality and style. The visual flair, accompanied by energetic animations and stylish finishing moves, makes every encounter in the game a visual spectacle that keeps players engaged and entertained.The gameplay in No More Heroes is addictive and satisfying, with fast-paced combat that centers around Travis' unique beam katana. Players can perform a variety of combo attacks, counters, and special finishing moves, all with a single goal: to emerge victorious in epic boss battles and climb the assassin rankings. The game's intuitive control scheme and responsive combat mechanics ensure that every swing of the beam katana feels impactful and exhilarating. Additionally, the inclusion of various mini-games and side activities adds depth and variety to the gameplay experience, providing a welcome break from the main storyline while maintaining the game's quirky and playful atmosphere.No More Heroes also shines in its storytelling and character development. The game's narrative is a mix of self-aware humor, cultural references, and unexpected twists, creating a captivating and engaging storyline. The characters, from the enigmatic Travis Touchdown to the eccentric assassins he faces, are vibrant and memorable, with their own backstories and motivations that unfold as the game progresses. The dialogue is witty, irreverent, and filled with pop culture references, delivering a unique and self-aware narrative that sets No More Heroes apart from traditional action games.In conclusion, No More Heroes is an unapologetically quirky and thrilling action-adventure game that embraces its eccentricity with open arms. Its unique visual style, addictive gameplay mechanics, and memorable characters make it a standout title that captivates players from start to finish. Whether you're drawn to its irreverent humor, stylish combat, or simply seeking a gaming experience that breaks the mold, No More Heroes delivers on all fronts. Prepare to immerse yourself in a world of assassins, pop culture references, and offbeat charm as you embark on a wild and unforgettable journey with Travis Touchdown.

_childDocuments_.review: I, personally, really liked this game. I cannot recommend it. I loved this game on the Wii. It was a blast - I had never played anything quite like it. This Steam version is same game - hack n' slash, part-time jobs, assassination gigs, 'open world exploration', fashion game, escapist fantasy, meta commentary, etc.  It's the same graphics, albeit sharper than they were back in the day. While for some reasons that can be bad, it is generally an improvement. Load times are better. I see comments around that speak of crashes in this Steam version. I played through the whole game without crashing, though I took note of the advice of others, specifically not pressing anything until prompted to do so on the ranking up screen. Did that help? I like to think so. I recall getting much greater satisfaction whipping the Wii remote around compared to simply using a controller. That heightened visceral sense that came with physically blasting enemies to bloody mist with your beam katana is diminished. There are definitely times where using a controller is a better experience, however. For instance, I found the bike is much easier to deftly maneuver and numerous minigames are improved with the change in controls as well. But that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ audio buzzing out of the Wii Remote whenever Sylvia calls you or your beam katana powers to life - Those touches *are* missed. There are typos in the captions here and there. You may not notice them. I don't recall if there were captions in the original, let alone typos, but their existence in this port is a point against it. Not being able to get all the achievements blows: This cannot be understated. The game has a nice slew of achievements, but for reasons unknown there has not been patched to fix this issue. The other bugs, glitches, and lack of polish I encountered (such as your sunglasses not appearing when looking in the mirror and the controller depicted in-game as being a Switch controller) were unfortunate enough to be of detriment to the experience. Also, parts of the game have not necessarily aged super well (meaning gameplay or mechanics or whatever), though that is not explicitly the fault of the port. That being said, most of the things that are wrong are because this port was done shoddily. All that in mind, I still really enjoyed playing this. I think there's some content not included in the original Wii version. Maybe it's from the PS3 version they did? Perhaps the Switch port? It is possible I am wrong about this. Anyway, more pertinently, the game in general is still just fun. It's an unpolished gem with charm and attitude. While this port improves some things and screws up in many other ways (RIP Heavenly Star while I'm thinking about it), the game is ultimately worth playing.Please fix the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: (Only reason I'm not recommending the game is because this game uses online-online DRM, which is a complete disgrace to this great game. DRM is a cancerous tumor and it's such a shame this game has it.)  No More Heroes is a quirky, unique hack 'n' slash game. It's also one of my favorites in the genre and one of my favorite video games of all time. This and Killer 7 are definitely Suda 51's best games. I think it's a really good game, but it has its owns flaws since no game is perfect. Here are the pros and cons. Pros:- Good high-octane gameplay and action- Sick artstyle- Motion controls are not mandatory in this port compared to the original Wii version- Fine story with unforgettable and likable characters like Travis Touchdown- Good voice acting- Memorable, fun boss fights (Dr. Peace, Death Metal, Shinobu, and Badgirl to name a few)- The game and story sometimes changes things up and subverts your expectations to prevent it from becoming very predictable (Letz Shake and Dark Star)- Lots of customization when it comes to Travis' clothes.- Side missions and jobs that even though they were criticized for being mundane, they do help break the monotony of the campaign- PC port that is much better than No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle- Really good and arguably great soundtrack (No More Heroes, Pleather for Breakfast, Heat in your Hand, Cashmere Cannonball, and Steel Python to name a few)- Decent replayability- True ending that's pretty awesome- Based on the frankly great Nintendo Switch remasterCons:- Game requires an internet connection to play it, a Wii game from the late 2000s requires an internet connection - PC port is bare bones- Game can be a bit grindy and repetitive at times- Does not include an option to replay certain ranked assassin missions; you have to re-complete the game to replay those story missions.- Henry on Bitter difficulty- Open world feels underwhelming, but not as empty as a modern Ubisoft game- PC port doesn't even change out the button layouts used in the Switch version, which this version is based off of, in the shoot-em-up mini game that you play later on, but it does display X-input buttons throughout the game. - I could be wrong, but I believe this game has online-only drm, which is ridiculous since it's a single player game- Even though Travis's motorbike is very useful in traveling the open world, its collision detection is quite annoying- Collectible items like trading cards and the Lovikov Balls can be pretty annoying to search for.- Some of the side missions are quite a nightmare   In a nutshell, even though the game has some problems, I still find it enjoyable and I think it's one of my favorite games of all time. $20 is not too bad for a game like this, but I recommend buying it on sale like I did. Although No More Heroes 2 & 3 improved on some things like the gameplay and mechanics, but I still think the original No More Heroes is the best one in the series. It's quite unique and memorable, and it also has a unique charm. Also, "MOE~"

_childDocuments_.review: Alright before getting into this review I have in the past played the original wii version multiple times and the switch port which is the basis for the current PC port of the gameNo more heroes is a cheesy raunchy fun hack n slash coming from the mid of SUDA51 (Killer 7, The Silver case) and in that style really shows as it's flowing with the charm and flair that only SUDA can bring out in the game. You are an broke otaku assassin who one night in a bar gets mixed up with some hot lady and you end up in a wacky rankings fight system taking down the one's who stand in your way to reach the top. Every single one oozing with their own flair and character from the schoolgirl shinobu to the cocky prick destroyman to even bad girl which I won't spoil later parts of the game for you. In order to enter in these rank fights you have to do side jobs/missions from multiple places in order to scrape out that pocket change for a chance to climb the ranks. Those side jobs can rank from anything to lawn mowing, finding lost kittens, and even scorpion collecting.While I'd like to say this is a perfect conversion of the switch remaster sadly it's not as the game crashed on me 5 times during my play through. One time while I was trying to save the game locked up on a white screen. Random crash while trying to enter a free fight mission. 3 crashes during the ranking screen after the holly summers fight which that crash happened every single time I tried to rush to the save screen so I couldn't skip any of those rank screens after destroyman. I also couldn't earn almost half of the achievements due to miscounting and the fact the last one is locked behind getting all the bugged one's. Also some parts of the game will display switch controls like the glastonbury mini game before the rank 4 fight and in the credits it says nothing about anybody who ported the PC version over and doesn't even mention this port at all. It just has the same exact credits as the switch port had.I'd honestly say yes this was a lazy port of a great game that should've had a bit more work put into it and maybe a little more testing so those crashes wouldn't happen making me lose an hour of lovikov ball searching after rank 9. Still it's a great game overall and yes I'd say go in being ready to save often if you play through this version of the game. 6/10 because I'd give it a 10 if it wasn't a buggy mess at times

After winning a beam katana in an internet auction, he runs out of money to buy video games and wrestling videos. After meeting with Sylvia Christel, he accepts a job to kill Helter Skelter, also known as "the Drifter," which earns him rank 11 by the United Assassins Association, a governing body of assassins. Realizing that he has the opportunity to make it to the top, he sets out to secure himself the coveted position of number one assassin in the UAA.So what are you waiting for? _childDocuments_.review: I finally got around to playing No More Heroes, I've been waiting and hoping for them to port it to Steam so I could finally play it for the first time, and I gotta say it's pretty great.It isn't exactly what I was expecting, I was told it's similar to games like Devil May Cry or Bayonetta but it feels very very different than both of those. No More Heroes is a hack and slash game just like those games but it's less focused on doing combos and more on using the right stance to hit the enemy and instantly killing them. Every enemy can block either high or low and you have to figure out which way they're going and then wail on them from there. Since NMH was a Wii game originally you have to move the right stick to slice enemies before finishing them and I found it to be pretty addicting and fun. The combat overall is pretty fantastic, it's fast paced and satisfying although it would be nice to be able to change targets on the fly like later third person action games do.On top of the combat being unique compared to other hack and slash games, No More Heroes is also an open world game in between missions. Essentially in this game you need to earn money by doing jobs, digging up hidden money around town, or doing assassination missions in order to pay for the next main mission. I really dig the gameplay loop of this game and trying to get gold ranks on every mission is lots of fun too.Another thing I really enjoy about NMH is that it doesn't take itself very seriously, the protagonist Travis Touchdown is really funny and loves to break the fourth wall, he's pretty much the Deadpool of videogames in my opinion. There's tons of references to pop culture and video games, especially Star Wars as Travis is obsessed with it. I think this game definitely lived up to my expectations however this port didn't, not that it's unplayable or anything but it crashes every 7-8 loading screens and that can be really annoying because if you don't save, you will be set back to an old checkpoint and have to do all the missions you just did once more. This port also has sound bugs, mainly when there's tons of enemies on screen the audio starts to clip and it hurts to listen to. Other than that, there's no real graphics or control options to change and that's really lame for a 2021 release. No More Heroes is a fantastic game overall, and even though this port has issues I still think it's worth getting especially if you love hack and slash games or are looking for something unique and different.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, but poor port. No native Joy-con/wii mote support(considering that steam currently supports these). No unlocked framerates(capped at 60fps) with no seemingly easy way to modify like a simple ini file tweak. Additional Anti-aliasing options are actually worse than the base FXAA. Not sure if it's due to playing in 4k(with MXAA) but characters have a weird puppet like effect where dark lines are showing at their articulating points like the mouth and joints(super distracting). Don't recall this being an issue in the switch port, but the Y camera axis stays inverted(down is up/up is down) regardless of changing the settings. X axis is changeable though. Some neglect of button prompts(in particular a minigame literally shows joycons from the switch port). Audio clips frequently. reducing the SFX to 50% helps a good amount, but this only mitigates the issue. Clipping still happens, but not as often. Overall this game needs a reasonable amount of work to be considered passible.It is playable otherwise though and if you don't have an option to play on the switch(or even the wii to be honest), then this is the next best option, but I would wait until they hopefully fix some of these other Major issues first.
_childDocuments_.name: No More Heroes

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend but there are some big BUTS in the middle which you should take into account. Frankly I love this game, it's one of my favorite (if not my favorite) game on the Wii, beated both NMH1 and 2 a few times when they were out on Nintendo's little motion controlled box. It's something about how the whole idea was executed, you being Travis Touchdown a loser otaku that bought a lightsab... I mean ... bean katana in an online auction, ends up getting roped into a competition between the assassins in Santa Destroy by a hot blonde babe, who Travis wishes to bone. It's silly, stupid, but oh so glorious and full of character.Gameplay is simple, during missions you'll mostly walk around and kill the thugs that stand between you and the boss, you have high and low sword strikes and punches and kicks to break their guard, stun them to pull off wrestling moves, lower their health until you can land the finishing blow with stylized fountains of blood. Wash, rinse, repeat until you get to the boss. The bosses are pretty memorable on their own right, the banter between them and Travis are always interesting. Once done, before heading towards the next level, you're set loose in Santa Destroy where you can buy and upgrade your bean katanas, workout, learn new moves, buy new clothes, all which you'll pay by doing humiliating jobs which will lead into some assassination gigs on the side.The entire setting is charming and funny, with a visual design that is still distinctive enough that you can overlook the fact that this is a Wii game.Now for all those big BUTS I mentioned in the beginning.This is one of (if not) the most barebones port I've played. At the moment of writing this, the options you'll get are VERY limited, no resolution options, no other control schemes outside of controllers and it's not a very well optimized port, while it hasn't crashed, it's not running very smooth, while my PC is old but it can run more visually advanced games than NMH.So, tl;dr: Love this game, still think it's awesome, but the port itself is REALLY basic.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a classic from the 7th gen (hard to believe those can be called classic now). And this version appears to be an almost direct port of the Xbox 360 version. It's playable in HD with minimal customization options, the only one I found being anti-aliasing.As such, the game comes with all the good and all the bad of the original. Which is to say, lots of good and a fairly mild amount of bad. The visuals and character movement are loaded with jank that firmly cements this game as one of those oddballs from the late Naughties, and a Wii oddball at that. Furthermore, there are a couple issues that (I believe) are exclusive to this version. First, the characters have what appears to be vertex warping on their faces; tiny gaps in the polygons that resemble cracks in the skin. Second, the audio mixing is abysmal. No matter how low I set the volume, without outright muting it, the death screams are still incredibly intense, and the sword clashing from the first boss fight peaked the audio constantly.Other than that? It's No More Heroes. One of the best experiments on the Wii, and one of Robin Atkin Downes's most memorable performances. The game has hilariously corny dialogue and an undeniably lovable sense of self-aware humor. While I personally prefer the second game, that's also available and seems to more or less be the same in terms of porting struggles. Or should I say Desperate Struggles..? No..? I'll get me coat...

_childDocuments_.review: So, as a person who's played three different versions of this game (Wii, Switch, PC) I can pretty confidently say that this is a slightly-sloppy port. All of the comments regarding M+KB support are completely valid . Haven't had any issues with audio clipping or texture popping like people seem to be complaining a lot about, although I have noticed a strange issue with the audio settings resetting each time I'd save the game. To fix this, all you have to do is go to the config menu on boot-up and change the audio settings to whatever you'd feel most comfortable with for the duration of the game. Feel around a little (the default 100% was a little too loud for me) and figure out what works best.Another issue I noticed were certain button prompt instructions that have been left mislabeled, likely from the Switch port. I played using an XBOX Series X controller, and during the lead-up to the second boss fight of the game, you're forced into a mini-game where you have to bat at balls pitched towards you with the beam katana. The instructions say "Press B or ... Button" when in actuality, you're meant to press X, the standard low-swing button.That being said, other than a few minor issues, this game isn't an unplayable port like a fair few Steam review exaggerators seem to be making it out to be! It's virtually the same port as the Switch version, still perfectly playable, and if you haven't played the game yet, I'd definitely recommend giving this game a look. Suda51's eclectic taste is on full display, with the main plotline of the game being a mixture of Branded to Kill from Seijun Suzuki, Star Wars, and Paris, Texas. The mundanity of the open-world sandbox (as bare-bones as it is) is contrasted heavily against Travis Touchdown's veritable rogue's gallery of psychopaths. The writing is pretty excellent and a prime example of auteur game design. 9/10, just wish the port was a little better.

_childDocuments_.review: A good ol' classic. There's some jank, but it's good jank. No More Heroes is a game with some twisted themes that in the end you shouldn't take too seriously. Stick around for Suda's ride and there's a great arcade 3d hack n slash. Doing attacks, specials, suplexes and finishers feel great to pull off, especially with a lovable idiot like Travis Touchdown. This game came out on the gamecube a while back, don't expect the snappiest game controls wise especially if you're coming off something like Devil May Cry 5. It's still a smart combat system with fun bosses that you can't just mash through. As for the port itself it runs well, but not the best. Some of the sound effects can blare with static a bit and there's a couple other odds and ends. At the end of the day It's a solid unique game with a sense of humor that you won't find elsewhere. People are reporting controller problems, but I've loaded up steam configs for my DS4 controller, no DS4 Windows running and it's fine. For those of you trying to play this type of game with a keyboard, get real.

name: No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle
detailed_description: Travis Touchdown here. It's been three years since I clawed my way to #1 in the United Assassins Association. I thought it'd be fine to take it easy for a while after that, but it looks like I rested on my laurels a little too long. I found myself sliding down the ranks all the way to #51, and to make things worse, some other assassin—Skelter Helter—comes out and starts nagging my head off about me killing his brother or something. So yeah, a real pain in the you-know-what. Fueled by a thirst for vengeance (and a bit of good old-fashioned greed), I whipped out my beam katana once more and plunged headfirst into one helluva desperate struggle. Experience the frenetic hack-and-slash gameplay of the sequel to No More Heroes in glorious HD! With more characters to play as and even more foes to stand in your way, there's never a dull moment in the world of No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle . Featuring three playable characters, the ability to dual-wield beam katanas, and even bigger baddies to battle, this sexy sequel is a wild ride with more to love than ever before. Kick back, grab a slice, and get ready to dive into a mind-melting drama the likes of which you've never seen! Features Dual-wield beam katanas as Travis Touchdown to dial the hack-and-slash insanity up to 11! More baddies than ever before to go toe-to-toe with! Jump through combat as the agile Shinobu or leave foes in the dust as Travis' brother, Henry. Experience a blast from the past by playing 8-bit minigames to earn money and power up!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun sequel to the original Sudaverse game by Grasshopper Manufacture, but pretty bad port by Engine Software in its current state. Bugs that never have been seen in original Wii release, broken achievements, lots of crashes.After the initial prologue and ranking 51st I had lots of crashes, slowdowns in retro mini-games, and just couldn't even progress in game until the next save.What I did so I could finish the game from start to finish:1. Set screen refresh rate to 60Hz in windows settings2. Disable fullscreen in game settings3. Force vsync off in your Nvidia/AMD driver4. Compatibility mode > Windows 7 + High DPI scalingNavigate to game folder, right click on nmh2.exe, then properties, left click on the Compatibility tab, check box in Compatibility mode, from the options give to you by the drop down menu, choose "Windows 7". Also, click on Change High DPI Settings and in a small window click on "Override high DPI scaling behavior. Scaling performed by" then check Application. Apply and run the game as usual.With this I managed to beat the game with only one freeze on loading screen, around twelve hours with no issues. Do not alt+tab while playing, it can cause freeze on loading. Audio SFX and BGM can overlap each other, make sure to put BGM at max and set SFV volume somewhere around 3-4 bars lower than max.Sometimes items from Airport 51 such as Travis classic jacket and first beam katana in Naomi's lab may requare multiple purchases to register and save it in your inventory. Tested by myself, and yeah, eventually you'll get 'em all, just make sure to buy them over and over again.Hope it helps someone too.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not exactly the biggest Suda fan, but since we got the third one coming out later this month and these two just dropped on PC, I figured I give them both a look.You've probably noticed the mixed reviews. This is not because the game itself is bad – which I’ll discuss in a bit – but rather because the PC port is incredibly lazy. The game completely lacks keyboard and mouse support, does not have any rebindable controls, is hard locked to 60 fps, and the only graphical settings are a fullscreen toggle and anti-aliasing option.It gets worse when you realize that it is an online-only game – as in, it literally cannot launch if you are offline. I have no idea why they made this a requirement given that this is a port of a singleplayer game from the Wii, but that’s the reality. That and apparently some of the achievements are bugged and the game does crash a bit for some users – I myself ran into a total of one crash.That said, it’s not entirely bad. For one, the game does run at higher resolutions (whatever your monitor is set at) and it looks far better than the 480p that we had on the Wii. That and the 60 fps is at least constant. I never had any dips there and no issues with stuttering, freezing, etc. Xbox controller support is also there and they did a decent job adapting these controls from the Switch release. I didn’t have any issues and didn’t feel the need to rebind any controls.Now as for the game itself – not bad. A bit repetitive (more so than in the first game) and definitely dated overall, but still a good time. The combat is fast, responsive, and satisfying. It lacks in depth, but it does offer up a fair challenge in spite of that (excluding the awful final boss).What the game lacks in depth it makes up for with its incredibly creative boss fights. Sometimes they will just be a standard fight, but sometimes you’re in a mech, or dodging dragons made of lightning, or taking down a sniper maid.The bosses are all over the place and really highlight Suda’s writing style. It’s one of those stories where you don’t really know where it’s going or really what is going on, but it’s just such an interesting mess that you can’t help but be sucked in by it. There’s crazy plot twists, an entire roster of oddball characters, and a touch of crude humor too.The standard gameplay is more hit-or-miss. Cutting down enemies is fun, but not when the game has you do that 100 or so times in a single area. The sequel does this way more often than in the first game too. And the simplistic level design offers very little exploration, so there’s really no getting away from the endless wave after wave of enemies.I actually prefer the sequel's approach to the gameplay loop over the original. Instead of “kill boss, grind for money to kill next boss, repeat” like the first game, the second altogether removes the money fee for main missions. It also removes the awful open-world aspect of the first game. I can see why some like It – but to me, it felt like an unnecessary inclusion that just made it harder to get where I wanted to go.The game camera unfortunately takes a nosedive in the second game. In the first, it was already a little bit tricky, but it straight-up just does not want to cooperate a lot of the time in the second. Whether that be because it’s far too close or the lock-on working a little too well – it’s a bit of a pain.A bit of a toss-up here. On one hand, No More Heroes 2 is fun enough and I’m glad to have finally played it – but on the other, the PC port is not great. There’s “lazy, but runs well” and then there’s “can’t launch the game offline, can’t unlock all the achievements, and occasionally crashes” kinda bad. So on that front, it is completely understandable if you outright skip it. That said, I still had a good time playing through the game and would recommend it on that aspect – it just comes with a huge warning label.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the No More Heroes franchise, but I'll start off by saying that this is a flawed port. It's not bad, but there are many present issues. The game can freeze, crash, and some of the achievements are broken. It's unfortunate, because issues aside, this game is still pretty darn good.The story follows the events of the first game, with Travis Touchdown returning to Santa Destroy. Travis will encounter some old faces, and his protégé, Shinobu, is even playable for a bit.No More Heroes 2 improves on some of the mechanics of the first game, but also does quite a few things worse. The combat is still pretty good, there's no longer ranking fees for continuing through the story, the graphics look better than the first game, the story is still quite outlandish, and fast travel makes for a delightful option. Improvements aside - the side missions aren't quite as fun as they could be, I would have liked to have the option to free roam around Santa Destroy, the final boss is pretty lame, and the other bosses are well-designed, but seem much simpler to fight.The game is still worth a solid playthrough. It's short, but it still is quite an enjoyable experience. I'll definitely return to 100% the game if they fix the achievements.Some final thoughts:- You can now interact with your cat, Jeane, to try and get her into shape.- Travis still doesn't wipe after using the toilet.- You can now dual wield beam katanas. Awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Aaaaand that's the next game all done! What an experience this game was. Let's begin with the review:Soooo...once again, I'm glad I gave these games a chance and I'm glad that I bought both of these instead of just one, definitely got a more fuller experience with them. So, where do I stand on this game?While I don't think this game is  better than the first game, The assassins in this game don't feel like real people at times and more or less just feel like 'oh, just another bad guy for Travis to fight to get to the top, I guess.' It's kind of jarring going from a game that had characters with some levels of depth to them and you could almost feel their struggles up until they died to a sequel where only a few of the assassins actually feel like they're properly fleshed, and one of those few is just a character from the first game brought back from the dead that Travis himself doesn't even get to face, with that character being 'New Destroyman', instead Shinobu fights him (or rather them since there's two now and it's kind of an annoying fight, ngl.) The story is....worse than the first game and while it has it's good moments in it as well like Henry fighting an anime mecha girl, Shinobu making her moves on Travis which is uhhh...kind of funny and kind of weird at the same time considering the fans who probably DID ship them got slapped in the face and those who didn't were probably just thinking 'Yeah, that seems about right', and Travis and Sylvia having more banter (which was some of my favorite moments in the first game and this one since we got to see the two interact more here and form a sort of...screwed up bond), overall, the story is just...okay, not as good as the first game's but not god-awful either...Jasper is a really crappy character, though, ngl, he's comic-book as heck and he really only just made Travis get out of retirement because of him killing Greg/Bishop...who barely mattered before in the games asides from him fetching your bike on NMH1 and running the shop in both games. It's just kind of sad we didn't get a better story considering how amazingly improved everything else was.The gameplay feels smoother, all more Soul-Caliber-like, feels faster with it's combos (both with your sword AND your punches and kicks), almost giving a Devil May Cry kinda of speedy style to your attacks, the first game's combat was pretty good and while I'd say it's still good, it has aged a little bit, NMH2's combat feels really good in the sense of it feeling more polished and ironed-out. This game even lets you play as Shinobu and FREAKING HENRY! How can you NOT like that?! I dunno, something about this game's combat rubs me in a really good way that I can't help but get that same high as I did in the first game going through it for the first time. It's CRAAAAACK!Oh...and you still have Jeane...but you can play with her and make unfat now! 😃Man, for a Wii game, this must've looked INSANE back then to play compared to all of the other stuff you'd see on the console. It's got that signature SUDA style with the usage of shadows, unique camera angle, and direction of the cutscenes. It's all really solid stuff, especially with the more brighter usage of color compared to the first game, which I didn't mind since that game was at heart very grungy and dark. I would say that NMH2 just communicates a better amount of personality in the way the characters moves, look, and how the world is presented. A lot has changed in Santa Destroy in just a few years and while that did cause the exploration of the overworld feature to get removed, the world is still shown full in its new malls, business buildings, and beaches. It's all really nice...though I can still say that the textures on everything were just kind of upscaled, but ehhh...at least it isn't as bad as RE4 Ultimate HD's level of 'HD textures.'While this part of a game wouldn't be so important in most  NMH2 it means EVERYTHING. I LOOOOOOOVE this game's more diverse soundtrack. The first game's soundtrack was great, don't get me wrong, the guy who did Danganronpa 1-V3's soundtracks [Masafumi Takada] composed it after all, it more or less just felt like the same batle theme was just being repeated over and over again with different instruments and tones. In NMH2, EVERY part of the game has it's own music and it all simply SLAPS, the boss themes, the normal battle themes, even the 8-Bit minigame music is great! That just goes to show good of a composer was.....wait a minute...Jun ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and...AKIRA YAMAOKA COMPOSED THIS?! Well, there's your answer, guy did the soundtracks for Silent Hill, which already on it's own was GOATED, no wonder the music is so diverse and out there...what else can I say?Overall, No More Heroes 2: Desperate Struggle is the kind of sequel a game should strive to be, fix everything that was wonky about the first game and make it better (except for the story, which took a bit of a hit like I said before.) I'd overall ABSOLUTELY recommend this game (obviously, play the first one first) if you enjoyed NMH1, you'll get a kick out of this one and be just as blown away as I was when it came to how good a lot of this game is. Absolutely give it a chance when you can....except, wait for it to go on sale...just read the note below...HOWEVER! There some kinds to keep in mind: Keep in mind that this port, JUST LIKE No More Hero 1's PC port, has some issues (i.e. crashing, bugs, etc.) I recommend looking at community guides and forums if you're having issues with the game. Someone actually made a good guide to (potentially) help remedy the crashes for the game done by YAR Oracool, so take a look at his guide. Keep in mind too that these are ports that are capped at 60 FPS and are just straight Nintendo Switch ports that were put on PC. If you're okay with that...wait for a sale maybe (or if you REAAAALLLY want the games now, go ahead and pick them up, they're good introductory games to hack n' slashes and SUDA51 games alike.) I'd say just be cautious about them and don't just run them out the book and use the Windows 7 Compatibility mode trick that YAR and I made guides for both NMH1 & 2. However, keep in mind you may still crash here and there (which happened to me twice towards the end of the game and once during my whole playthrough), ...NMH3 better come to PC with a good port, seriously, there's NO excuse for these games to have lazy, mediocre ports like this and NMH3 was made in Unreal Engine 4 for crying out loud, it should have a PERFECT PC port.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the hardest review for any video game I've had to write. I don't know how I feel about No More Heroes 2. It would genuinely be easier to give a play-by-play of this game because it's an emotional rollercoaster in the worst way. And yet, also the best way.No More Heroes 2 feels like a team strapped for budget tried to make a game that would be more epic and grand than the first game, and their design document was literally everyone at the office doodling assassin concepts and ideas for specific moments that they thought would be cool without really thinking about how they would flow in a video game.The problem is, sometimes it works. The first 3 or so hours are kinetic, crazy, over the top and silly and it feels like they're going to absolutely deliver on making something that will top NMH1. The combat is vastly superior, the jokes land more often, the soundtrack is fantastic, the mini-games are fun, it makes a wonderful first impression and I was in the mindset that everyone who thought this game was disappointing were just lame-os in those first few hours.The other side of the problem is, sometimes, it really, really, really, REALLY doesn't. I feel like if they shaved off at least 4-5 hours off the runtime, the game would be so much better off. There is literally a segment in the last few stages where you spent probably almost literally 10+ minutes in a glorified box of an arena killing the same few enemies over and over and over again, in a game where the enemy variety isn't that big to begin with.Yeah, sure, there are diversions and wacky gimmicky bits like in the first, but they're FAR more spaced out and don't amount to much for the most part. The points of interest in this one come more from the various assassin characters and the story. And... what a story it is.To keep things short, it's kind of a mess. I've heard people say that "Suda was deliberately trying to make a bad story because unnecessary sequel blah blah", but honestly, it kind of feels like the exact opposite. I think it tries TOO hard to do too much at once. It's at its strongest when it focuses on Travis and Sylvie and their relationship with themselves and the violence that permeates their lives. It seems like that's the main arc overall, and I think it does that well... when it focuses on it. Which it doesn't, for like 60% of it.You can say the first game had an issue with having the violence both be fun and stylish but also trying to have weight and consequences, but the first game definitely strikes a better balance than it does here for most of it. But honestly, I personally don't care about that. I care about the fact that it seems like they tried to cram in as much ♥♥♥♥ as they could within the plot to make it more wild without really thinking. I think the best example of this is that .While I won't say the bosses in the first game are amazingly life-changingly great or anything, this game's bosses are incredibly hit and miss, which I think furthers my point on them just doing whatever to make the game seem more grand than the first. Some of the designs are cool, some of them have neat personalities, but when they're pitifully easy and/or obnoxiously busted, it drags them down significantly in terms of me actually wanting to give a ♥♥♥♥ about them. You don't even learn the names of half of them until you kill them! The Million Gunman fanbase is dying. RT if you're a true Millionaire.And I think that's my overall opinion of No More Heroes 2. It's a rollercoaster, but a rollercoaster shaped like a square wave. It's either really entertaining and wacky, or it's just so grating and monotonous it makes you want to shove a beam katana up your rectal cavity. For the average person who just wants a good arcadey beat 'em up, look elsewhere. For people who want an unusual one-of-a-kind experience and can tolerate "old mid-budget game jank", play the first one instead (or play the dev's previous work killer7, even if that's a completely different game). For people who really want to experience a massive improvement over the first game, skip it. I'd really only recommend it for those who really want to play through the whole series and want to see how it progresses, but even then, don't be surprised if your patience wears thin and you shut it off early.

_childDocuments_.review: As my third Suda51 game, No More Heroes 2 is nothing more of a miracle happening. The fast this game even exists just shows the impact the first game had. This game improves on the original in many ways. This game is a unbelievably amazing soundtrack, less money grinding, more playable characters, no dumbass unnecessary open world, more weapon variety, and less padding. On the contrary though, the game's combat is slower paced, the jobs give you way less money and are more frustrating than fun, leveling up your strength and stamina is lackluster, and the build up to bosses is way worse than the first.So am I not recommending this game because of the downsides? No. This game's fantastic just like the first game. Both games are absolutely worth your time playing. So.... why not recommend this game? Well, much like the first game, this port is pretty bad. This game has no proper in game graphic options, it's capped at 60 FPS, the textures are lazily upscaled so there is tons of artifacting, horrendous pop-in, and no Steam Input. Yup. We're still making games on PC in 2021 with no mouse and keyboard support. And much like the first game, it'd be fine if they had Steam Input so that every controller would natively work, but NOPE. Only Xinput. Only Xbox controllers. No Switch, no DualSense, no DualShock 4, no keyboard, nothing. Again, I absolutely recommend you play this game, but please don't buy this version of the game till it's fixed or has more mods to fix it for us. Just stick to the Wii or Switch version. TL;DR - Fantastic Game. Lack Luster Port just like the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: "no more heroes 2 is the worst in the series" really? this one is so much of an improvement compared to the first. you dont have the godawful santa destroy open world segment anymore (thank god), you dont have to drive back and forth just to grind out the same revenge mission in hopes of acquiring enough cash to progress to the next level. the combat isnt monotone any longer and theres more variety and freedom fit to ones playstyle. the bosses actually fight like bosses compared to the joke, parody, meta-narrative of the first. . .the combat has been elevated on such a high level, dark stepping has been completely altered to actually make it more skill-based move to pull off. you can carry multiple sabers with you this time around and even switch between them during combat. you can parry, juggle, wallsplat, stagger and so on, it definitely plays more like a traditional beat em up and can be called an actual "action" game than the first installment which is nothing more than an glorified console experiment. oh, i also really like the neat detail of travis having his sabers dangle from his belt as you acquire them, its a nice touch. the boss fights in this are so much fun, and i love the no BS approach of just putting you straight to the fight without having some foreplay prior. they've put so much effort into the bosses this time around that they even made an entire boss rush mode to playthrough, it could also work as a "training mode" if you are ever planning a challenge run on bitter difficulty, which as the name suggests, will definitely leave a bitter taste. its going to test your patience for sure.on a side note, should i really not be surprised that suda51 wasnt head director for this? his cult of personality is definitely more toxic than that of kojimas! im pretty sure these auteurs dont want to come off that way or intend the slightest hint of narcissism, its always emitted by the fanbase instead. i think praising suda51 as some kind of experimental genius in interactive media is laughable. what is experimental exactly? something thats slightly different than your usual thing? id love to see these bugmen try to sit through a stan brakhage film heh.honestly though, suda51 definitely delivers when hes more laidback. killer7 is an all-time favorite game of mine and now no more heroes 2 coming in close second. both of which were supervised by others! i even think this game does a way better job in its presentation than the first. it definitely left an impact for sure. and the "paris, texas" intersections are very much appreciated :)

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, Steam Deck players, once again, if you set compatibility to Proton Experimental, you're set up for a full playthrough with no issues.So, I liked certain parts of this game and didn't like certain parts. It's obviously a continuation of No More Heroes, so if you haven't played that one, I highly recommend playing it. You can of course start with this one... the characters in this game even state that some video game players may not care about continuity... but still.For the uninitiated (if you haven't played NMH), this is a game featuring Travis Touchdown (and his cast of unsavory friends), who is the most lethal assassin in the USA. The first game saw a desperate struggle for Travis to climb the "assassin ranking" list to the #1 spot, killing each assassin in the rank above him... and this one is somewhat similar, although you start in place... I think it was 52 rather than 10, although that doesn't matter much (more on that later). The NMH franchise features a very weird, meta, and sometimes completely random stuff. The themes run the gamut - extreme, excessive, gratuitous violence... skeevy pervishness... anime that sometimes becomes uncomfortably close to loli.. Japanese themes... lots of cursing, lots of cheesy catch-phrases ("you're a joke!"), weird meta moments where the characters discuss you playing the game, and sometimes things happening that are kinda beyond explanation.The cast of characters in this game are just as entertaining as the first - bizarre, over the top, excessively eager to kill, and even a few call-backs (such as a return of Destroyman!) (wait... how is that possible!? you'll just have to play). The story is fast and fun. You'll never have a bored moment.So how does it rank vs NMH? Do I prefer NMH or NMH2?To be honest, I liked the first better. As fun and engaging as NMH2 was, NMH still wins the prize in my book. I have done some reading online and have found that plenty of folks prefer NMH2, but many still hold that NMH wins the title.So what's different?Well, first of all, the "ranking" system means very little in a game where you can be in 50th place and then randomly jump to 25th. When I saw that I was in 51st place, I was overjoyed that I'd get to meet 50 more insane NMH whack-jobs. But, it kinda jumps around. I get it, it's a video game joke, but you really lose that sense of 'climbing up the ranks' when you just shoot up by leaps and bounds. AGAIN - Still very fun, just kinda eh.Second, no more open world, and no more K-Entertainment. You don't drive your bike around Santa Destroy anymore... you've got a list of places to go, and you choose your place. That really cuts down on the immersion. And no more K-Entertainment!? In NMH, everyone knows you play the side-jobs exactly one time to open up the K-E fights, because no one likes the side jobs and K-E is where it's at to earn money. But no, the primary way to earn money now IS the side jobs, and also kinda the ranking fights.Third, let's discuss money and side jobs. Money? What do you need money for? Oh, you'll need it to unlock new beam katanas and train and Ryan's Gym (Ryan is fabulous, by the way), but other than that, you don't "need" money anymore like you did in NMH. So you only really "need" to play the side jobs enough to train and get new katanas. There's nothing else you do - no fight fees, nothing like that anymore. As a NMH fan I still love buying new clothes for Travis and going out in cool or wacky outfits, but... the struggle for money is gone. And the side jobs? Instead of being just part of the normal game, you now play these super cheesy old-school-graphics (like, original Mario level) mini games. And it's not just the side jobs, either... it's training at Ryan's gym, everything. (I HATE the strength training game at Ryan's gym). If I had to do side jobs, I'd much rather just be normal Travis than 8-bit Travis, lol.The game has also lost the in-your-face feel of NMH. NMH's sounds were jarring and loud, leading to a sense of true brutality. The voice-acting was over the top - we ALL remember the "BAAAAAA!!!" scream. The voice acting in fights is a little less severe now.But, there's a lot that's good. The graphics are really cool in this game - like really pretty cool. The story is very engaging. The bosses are mostly super fun - although a little unbalanced (some of the earlier bosses are easier than some of the later bosses, etc). It's also really cool that you get to play as other characters, such as Shinobu and Henry - although Shinobu's jump mechanics are painful at best. Oh, and a painstaking amount of physics animations are put into boobs now. I guess the skeevy pervy side of the game is coming out.Overall, I find this to be a great game. Although I don't like it as much as NMH, it is still a very fun play and I enjoyed myself thoroughly, as I do with all games involving Travis Touchdown. I would recommend anyone who hasn't played the original play that one first, and to anyone coming from that game, I say, go for it, and if you're not sure, wait for a sale.Is it worth full price? In my opinion yes. Even with the drawbacks I had a lot of fun.So overall, yes, definitely recommend - especially if you're a fan of Travis.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is okay, but damn is this port BAD. I cannot believe that the game, after the few years it's been out, has only been patched a handful of times, and STILL has it's major issues that plagued it at launch. If you've read previous reviews, then you probably already know, but to summarise, I'll list the few major ones here.Frame drops, limited graphical settings, constant crashing, broken achievements, low quality cutscenes, settings not saving after quitting to the TITLE SCREEN, shops displaying items you've already bought, only for you to buy them again and realise it's not an upgrade, it's just a bug, and you've wasted 20 minutes money grinding, and over a mill of your money on literally NOTHING, and no proper controller support nor keyboard and mouse support. Don't get me wrong, this game isn't perfect, even without these issues, but I had more frustrations with the issues listed that I did the actual GAME part of the game. This game is a step-up from the previous, but then it takes another 3 steps back. It's got better character animations, more exciting combat, and the story has a bigger focus.. But they drop the ball so hard in most other areas. I personally find the combat in this game more enjoyable than the first, but I'm not going to say it's better. It feels way more button mashy compared to the previous, with faster attacks, but much slower enemies, making it easier to just button mash past an entire mob of enemies without much thought. The story, although much grander, and even a little more chaotic and fun, is unfortunately shallow, with not many twist and turns as before. Although it can be more funny, it's a little more in your face than the previous game, with even MORE fan service to boot as well, especially with a returning character, which not gonna lie, made me a little uncomfortable. I also found a lot of the assassin fights more forgettable, with only a handful that I remember being just marginally better, or far worse than previous bosses in the series. The other side of the game, being the mini games, was fun and also infuriating. Some of the games are super fun, like the first 2, while some, make me feel like they were intentionally designed to be extremely frustrating, like the Coconut and Trash mini games. My God the coconut mini game, I've played old school NES and SNES platformers more forgiving than this one mini game. Grinding money WAS frustrating, although you won't have to do it much, unless you plan on fully upgrading your stats and buying some clothes to customise Travis, if so, I recommend playing the "Tile in Style" mini game, as it's easy to do, and you'll get 10K per completion if you can do it within 30 or so seconds. If you find that too difficult, you can give the "Getting Trash" mini game I mentioned earlier a go, although it is frustrating to start, you'll probably eventually get used to the controls and timing, earning over 50K if you can do it without losing a single life and with a minute or so left of time. It's a shame, because I went in blind with this series, not expecting it to blow me away, but for it to be really fun and somewhat engaging, but this sequel has soured my hopes of my playthroughs for the next games. I really enjoyed the first No More Heroes, it was so unique, and simple on the surface, but had a little bit of depth and nuance if you dipped your toes in further. But this sequel just turned it up to 11 and took away half the things I enjoyed about the first, it feels like it's more "Style over substance" if you will. More characters and fights, more flashy moves, more humour, more sex appeal.... But less of that uniqueness that pulled me into the first. Most of the other reviews and opinions online suggest to play this game using other means, so I'd recommend buying this game to support the devs, then play it somewhere else. PS. The Switch version is NO better than the PC version. You know what to do then...?
