They literately elevated the game itself.There are 3 really big problems with this game:Level design. Oh its bad. In fact its absolutely horrifically awful. It can be maddening finding out where to go next and is by far the biggest problem with the game.Weapon variety. _childDocuments_.review: Port and remaster of an old Apogee FPS, I think their last before Duke Nukem 3D. Doesn't take itself seriously for one second, and the design was clearly guided by whatever the developers felt was fun on any given day during its development, not necessarily an overarching idea of what would have made a tighter, better balanced game. It's completely antithetical to modern shooter design and there's nothing quite like it, so it's a must play in my opinion. It'll probably be an acquired taste if you've never played it before, though.It adds a ton of quality of life improvements like mouse aim, high resolutions and butter smooth frame rate, as high as your monitor will go. I would have been happy with that alone, but they also added a full new four episode map set. The maps aren't throwaway crap either: they're high quality levels often on par with or better than the original Dark War levels.Also included are the shareware episode and the thoroughly evil Extreme ROTT expansion levels. If you you are an achievement completionist you'll be happy to know that you don't have to finish Extreme ROTT to get all achievements; it's enough that you finish one level at any skill.The game is also bundled with a GZDoom based fan-game-turned-official that I haven't spent much time playing.I haven't used the built-in editor, but as of writing this the workshop activity is promising; a lot of people are making new levels or importing old ones. Some people have already uploaded full episodes worth of levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive did a superb job at getting the annoyances out of the way, so the game can be judged fairly on its own merits. Whether that's a good thing or not determines how much of a ROTT fanatic you are.This is a game by Tom Hall. This game will, by extension, beat you into the ground with a cartoon-sized fist. If you get mad at video games easily, this is not the game for you. However, you cannot blame the game anymore for getting owned. :^)Pros: Mouse control is solid, movement is solid, gameplay is as accurate as it's gonna get at this point. Probably over 200 levels in here?? I didn't count, but it's a LOT. Wallrunning physics issues are largely fixed, so Extreme ROTT isn't as painful as before. Cons: You will see monks and enforcers in your nightmares for a few weeks. Having to physically maintain ammo by picking up and dropping weapons is still a lame gameplay mechanic, but only one level requires that you do, so, you know, don't miss.I have not played Comm-Bat on the release version yet, but that's going to change soon. :^)

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I am not sure if I should recommend this or not. For me this would be a neutral review if Steam would allow it. Can't really relate to the 96% positive reviews. As the reviews are all so positive I gotta be the negative Nancy. The remaster is mostly pretty good, but I don't think the og Rise of the Triad is a great game. I assume most positive reviews are from dudes who played the og game and are huge fans (for some reason) or are just fans of Nightdive Studios (which is relatable though, huge respect to you guys, please continue remastering the classic (or not so classic) old school shooters from the 90s and early 2k's.Personally I never played the og RotT before, but I did play the remake from 2013.-Flaws of the remaster: It's actually lagging quite regularily, always 3 times in a row, it's so weird and feels random, besides that framerate is consistent over 100. A game with those graphics shouldn't have any framerate issues though. There is no stat screen until you finish a level which kinda sucks.-Now regarding the og RotT: Yes, the game tried to be a bit different than the other 90s shooters, however different doesn't mean better. In fact I think this is probably one of the worst 90s shooters. So what is different: You have only 3 "different" bullet shooting weapons, a pistol, the same pistol akimbo and the mp40. All of them have infinite ammo and the next one is always better than the previous. Once you got the mp40 which should like always be in the very first level of each campaign, you will only use that weapon for like 95% of the time. This makes combat often very boring, especially since most enemies just feel pretty much the same as some hit scanning dudes. (Except later on you also encounter an unkillable enemy sometimes which is even worse.) You just stand in a corner so as few as possible enemies can see and shoot you while you hold the left mouse button spraying your mp40. If this feels braindead, that's because it is. Now the only fun part of the combat: There are other weapons, all projectile based and some sort of rocket launchers. I gotte admit those are usually very fun to use but also quite similar to each other. But another annoying part is you can only hold one rocket launcher at a time and you can't even recharge ammo for any kind of rocket launcher, you always have to pick up a new one. Levels where you get a lot of rocket launchers are fine combat wise, but when you don't get a lot, it gets really boring.Let's quicky talk about power ups: There are actually two kind of power ups which only gives you big downsides which is just stupid. Especially since most of the time you can just stand still when no enemies are around and wait till the negative effect vanishes. Then sometimes you can find a random power up. Well, the strategy is pretty much to quick save before collecting it. And then when you do get a negative one, you reload and repeat till you get dog or god mode. Pretty dumb.Level design is another big problem, at least in the old campaigns the level design is often so bad, often way too confusing and maze-like. Yes, 90s shooters were often maze-like but even worse in RotT you often have to find some switch or barely visible pressure plate or even push walls to be able to proceed. And even if you did find the switch or the pressure plate you then often have no clue, what door/wall or whatever opened/changed. So I would rather play through the whole Wolfenstein 3D for the third time which is all maze like than to replay RotT again. Especially the secret levels in RotT are so bad. Also the huge amount of traps can be annoying. I get it: as the combat basically lacks any challenge, devs thought to add traps to make it not that easy overall. But they overused the traps and they don't really make it harder, just more annoying.Before starting a campaign you choose between one of five characters to pick, each having different stats, mostly varying in movement speed and maximum health points. First I think this is out of place in an old school fps and second most of the characters have such a high movement speed that they are kinda unplayable for me. Another dumb part related to that is some areas/secrets can only be accessed with some of the faster characters...The platforming (yes, a game running on the Wolfenstein 3D Engine has platforming) is mid at best, can definitly be annoying at times. Collecting extra lifes is completly pointless as the game has quicksaves. Don't get me wrong, without quicksaves this game would be unplayable, just the addition of extra lifes is unnecessary.What's the good stuff: The best part by far is the soundtrack which is so great. Combat can be fun when you do find enough rocket launchers. The content in the remaster is huge: You have the shareware The Hunt Begins campaign, the "regular" og Dark War campaign, the way too long and way too hard Extreme RotT campaign (as far as I heared even fans of RotT mostly don't like it) and the new The Hunt Continues campaign. I played through each campaign except for Extreme RotT where I only played the first level, played through maybe half of the secret levels and didn't even got all other secrets which took me overall about 20 hours. If you play through everything and wanna 100% everything you can easily take double or triple the time. On the other hand after 20 hours I had more than enough from this game.At least the new campaign is mostly really good, by far the best campaign from the game.Oh and it also contains the Doom TC Return of the Triad which I didn't even started as well as editor which I haven't used either.So I'd probably only recommend this to big fans of the original or other huge fans of old school fps if you don`t mind the problems that I see with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: edit: originally posted on november 21st 2023 and rewritten on february 5th 2024great game, great art style, wildly confusing and endearing gameplay. you'll never find another one quite like it. truly the height of the old apogee games. it was apparently the result of a troubled development, but Tom Hall's sensibilities shine through brightly. it's a great time!dual pistols, an mp40, and various rocket weapons are your arsenal. the bullet weapons have infinite ammo, but the rocket weapons only have a few shots before they are permanently spent and must be replaced. in my playthrough i found myself using the mp40 at all times, except in situations where i needed to make some guys explode.each level is like a puzzle box. only one solution but a long, long journey to get there. luckily this remaster has an improved automap which will help you figure out most levels without hassle. i enjoyed every second of it, even when the levels were confusing and obtuse.ultimately i was driven to get all of the achievements, complete the shareware episodes, the registered episodes, and the new episodes that came with the remaster. i got a decent way into Extreme ROTT, but those levels were just too extreme for me, even on the easiest difficulty.i haven't been this immediately hooked on a game in years, honestly. there's also some fantastic workshop levels available, like Operation Fyrewall parts 1 and 2. if you love arcade-y first person shooters from the 90s, this is the remaster for you. the game was sadly overlooked in its time, but this remaster is truly the best way to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great remaster of a painfully mediocre and dated game with some of if not the worst weapon balancing and level design I've experienced in a Boomer-Shooter.Usually I would happily recommend a game ported by Nightdive to anyone, but I had such a bad time trying to navigate the endless mazes in RoTT.  Getting lost over and over in the samey looking corridors trying to find the same 2-3 keys in every level that I wouldn't recommend it to anyone.I never expected to play a game with more obtuse level design than Turok 2 but RoTT is somehow much worse.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. Not only that, this is also a great port. Great job to the team that made this happen.Before I start, I just want to get one negative out of the way. For some reason, the MIDI tracks stutter and pop. The other music settings don't, but these do. I got that fixed though via a website, but it should still be looked into.This is really the only nitpick I have, and everything else is great. The controls are smooth, the music (modified) sounds great as always, and everything is here. For a port, I was surprised to see a whole countless bunch of content. I was stunned to find a whole other GAME packaged here, with it basically being a DOOM mod but with a ROTT skin.For those who want to play this game, I want to tell you to TURN FREELOOK OFF AND TURN THE "Y" MOUSE SENSITIVITY OFF. Freelook BREAKS the illusion that this game sets, and honestly, this game pulls it off outstandingly. In some parts, I was surprised that this was even a fork of the Wolfenstein 3D engine (I think).This game is great and the port does an outstanding job at capturing the old experience while adding new content. I HIGHLY recommend you play this game.

Charge a grunt and take em' out with an explosive weapon to know what I'm talking about!  And for those interested in good old-fashion fun pvp shenanigans in your multiplayer... _childDocuments_.review: "EAT LEAD!"You know I expected some QOL patch and HD stuff and that's it, but no. Apogee, New Blood and Nightdive went far and beyond with this port. _childDocuments_.review: A ludicrously oldschool FPS, an actual boomer shooter for one thing. I was actually a kid when this game came out, but it sort of passed under the radar when I was experiencing Ultimate Doom, Doom 2, and Duke Nukem 3D for the first time.Rise of the Triad is sort of like if you took Wolfenstein 3D then added some more advanced things such as transparent textures, floors, ceilings, and moving platforms. After that, in the boomer shooter pot, you mix in some Ultimate Doom for good measure... then you just GO WILD and add spices! Traps, so many traps, and other assorted stage hazards, or objects like hundreds of floating platforms, in some of the most eccentric, arcade-style levels I've seen in a retro game. The levels are fun, but do suffer from some esoteric moments where you'll get stuck and have to look around a level for awhile to find what you need to find. This is, of course, a classic affair of finding keys to open the right doors, or finding the right button to open the right objects. There are even hidden floor plates to step on to open things, and there are tons of secret walls to wall-hump till your heart's content! The level design isn't exactly the best and is quite primitive, but it's also way more wacky than its peers back in the day.There used to be "extra lives", but they are basically useless. I don't know if it's the difficulty level, Medium, that I'm playing on. But as you collect Ankhs, the main collectible, you can get extra lives. But I don't see an extra life counter anywhere currently. In fact, when you die you just start the level all over again and have only your pistol, score intact. You can quick save and quick load, or do saved games, making the pistol start after death sort of pointless. It would've been neat to have limited quick saves as a challenge mode TIED to extra lives, where you'll start the whole episode all over again if you run out. It's possible that this mode already exists, and it's one of the hard or harder modes. The game is very oldschool from a bygone era, and quite arcade-like as a result. I do enjoy scoring points in these games... but it doesn't look like there's a high score system or leaderboard? I'd like the game to save my high scores and best times!One of the more interesting aspects of the game is the limited weapon loadout. You can hold four weapons only. Pistol, dual pistols, MP40, and a launcher. The small arms have infinite ammo once you pick them up, but launchers have limited ammo tied to the weapon itself, and you can't pick up more ammo until you find another launcher or replace your currently held low ammo launcher with another one. The launchers are honestly really fun, and kind of nuts for the time. The Fire Wall is my favorite, basically shooting a bomb that will explode and unleash a huge wall of flames that quickly moves forward, searing enemies into goofy charred skeletons! The Split Missile kind of sucks, but satisfying if you can hit two enemies at once with the two missiles that fire out in a DNA helix pattern. There's also a classic Bazooka to keep things "grounded". The launchers are the star of this game, and offer some variety despite the limited enemy types.The other star of this game, however, is the crazy "powerups" and "powerdowns" you'll find. Want to turn into a dog? Yes! Wanna be God and smite hordes of enemies? Yes! Wanna trip on mushrooms? Very yes! These are all really fun, and either help you, such as Flight, or hinder you, such as tripping balls on mushrooms.The story is nothing at all but 90s as hell, basically. You're a member of an ELITE 'MURICA TEAM, your job: DEFEAT THE TRIAD AND THEIR BASICALLY NAZI-ESQUE SOLDIERS! Explosions, gibs, freedom! Heck yeah, brother! The story and the way it is told is very much of its time, simple and to the point like Doom and Doom 2.The music is actually really awesome, and it's funny because I was wondering where YouTuber Civvie got his ending card song from, and it's actually from this game after beating a level and it's the result screen. We have some delightful and remastered MIDIs that truly make me feel nostalgic. I feel like I'm playing Doom again for some reason, but it's a bizarre amalgamation of Wolfenstein 3D and Doom with tons of stage hazards or bounce pads and platforms.Rise of the Triad is probably one of the more wackier shooters from many years ago. I'm glad I get to experience it again after sort of just not wanting to bother with the version in the Apogee Throwback Pack, which still uses DOS Box and isn't a very good version of the game unless you really like how painful it was to play PC games back in the day. Thanks, Nightdive, for giving this game a good remaster and better controls!

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible remaster! Not only do you get the definitive way to play this cult classic 90s FPS with widescreen support, you get a level editor, lost content restored in the game, a brand new episode, access to the expansions and shareware episode, and a jukebox that allows you to play any music track in the game AND Andrew Hulshult's remake soundtrack! And that's just all that I could think of off the top of my head!Another incredible remaster from Nightdive, with the help of Apogee and New Blood Interactive, which may be one of the biggest crossovers in the retro FPS community this year! And they still had the time to do the equally incredible Quake 2 remaster around the exact same time!The game itself is an 8/10. The remaster gets a 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: ROTT is a masterpiece of game design, it's a genuinely fun, well-thought out and incredibly humorous experience that's unlike most FPS games not just from the era, but in the entire genre - with Doom, Quake, Half Life and Halo, fps games went down the way of envoirmental storytelling, combat situations, epic adventures, ROTT is the opposite, its levels are wacky and trippy, abstract, it's much more like Mario in the sense that it embraces the genre's wackyness and unapolagetically designs its levels using all the tools it has to deliver an incredibly fast and dynamic experience.I personally love it, it might be an acquired taste given the dated graphics and weird mechanics, but for those that are into it, there's a LOT to get into. My favorite campaigns are The Hunt Begins and Extreme ROTT (although so far i've only been playing it on easy), because they have the best levels, and the best part is that I still think there's room for more - The Hunt Continues proves that much like Doom, ROTT is ripe for new fresh content, tailor made for the creative people that can work past its limitations when creating a fun, mindblowingly fun level to play in.I'm a fan. I hope others are as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, this is Nightdive's (with help from New Blood & Apogee) best remaster next to the 2 Quake games. The amount of customization with how you want the game to look, sound, & play is an awesome feature & the game itself is extremely fun & I love that it doesn't take itself seriously, you can tell the original developers must have had a lot of fun making it. Also impressive how well it plays & looks considering it was made using the original Wolfenstein 3D engine which was pretty dated when compared to ID Tech 1 (Doom 1&2, Heretic, & Hexen) engine at the time.All the campaigns were great (Extreme Rott is questionable lol) but the base campaign, Dark War was my favorite. Also the level editor & workshop support is another awesome addition. I need to learn how to use the level editor but the stuff people have come up with on the workshop that I've played were great!10/10 Highly Recommended if you're into the retro/boomer shooter genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest (if not the greatest) game(s) of all time got a really amazing overhaul including new content. This was something to really look forward to.Other than this being undoubtedly the best version of the game ever released, and the new content that was added being beyond incredible (which like Extreme ROTT takes a new unconventional approach to existing game elements and applies them in a new way (which was partially also made possible by upgrading to nightdive's KEX engine), just without the high difficulty) it does have a few downsides.For me the major downside was the Return of the Triad expansion, frankly I didn't care for it, since basically everything that is wrong with it is already covered by the official map editor guide. (the maps are symmetrical and too huge for their own good which makes you get lost all the time, and you just get god mode all the time by collecting points, overall making it quite a snooze fest. The maps for the most part also don't feel like actual ROTT maps, but instead as maps of a different game with ROTT skins over them) Other than that the doom map overlay (given it was made using the Doom engine and not the ROTT engine) also doesn't help since it doesn't display switches and keys like the ROTT map overlay does. So there is nothing indicating where you're supposed to go; no pathing, no enemies that spawn in such a way to leave a trail showing where to go, and checking the map doesn't help since it displays nothing that is of help in determining which direction you should go.But despite of that it does have a few nice touches, the first boss on Return of the Triad is something I think would have worked well with the game, the problem is just the poor execution, but the concept was great. They added a new enemy, which is a death fire monk which uses (and drops) a dark staff. And some of the mechanics of the enemies have changed, mostly for the worst, but I did like how the enforcer now actually throws grenades in an arch, rather than them moving in a straight line like a missile.Even though the main game has a brand new campaign and new levels, it unfortunately doesn't have any new enemies, not even any new bosses (other than Big John from ROTT 2013 in a secret level) but it makes up for this lack of new enemies, by reusing old content in a brand new way (the fight against NME on The Hunt Continues is absolutely brilliant, as is the reuse of the ballistikraft as static objects on some levels) and also releasing the previously unreleased alternate skins, which does make it feel as if you are fighting new enemies.It also doesn't have any new weapons, not even weapons that were added on ROTT 2013. Furthermore on the new campaign I couldn't find a place in which gun turret 2 was used (which to me is not a big deal, but it is an example of something they didn't play around with) and I also couldn't find a place where they used the gas and the gasmask (which is something I do find unfortunate as I do really like this mechanic and item).But with all that said the new The Hunt Continues campaign was absolutely incredible, and how absolutely good it was cannot be overstated. One should not get the impression that the lack of new enemies, new bosses and new weapons and the lack of using a few mechanics from the Dark War campaign doesn't make it an absolute masterpiece.TL;DR:It is an absolute must have for ROTT, and boomer shooter, fans in general. And my hope is this will inspire Apogee (perhaps in collaboration with others like the new campaign) to create a sequel to the original ROTT, which mostly stays true (gameplay and aesthetics wise) to the original, while borrowing some elements from ROTT 2013, yet at the same time add lots of brand new content that they didn't add here.This game is absolutely LUDICROUS!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Before describing games and campaigns included in this release, I have to say that this current port is a masterclass of ports. Four campaigns (one of them is brand new one) + level editor and custom campaign with Steam Workshop support, multiple settings, including UI settings, 3 sets of soundtracks, alternate SFX sound, restored alternative enemies, that were cut in the original game, every level has designer's name written down. And they nerfed Monks, with option to undo it! It's absurd amount of love and care to a – let's admit it – mediocre shooter.RotT is an interesting beast. It's hard to grade this game. One one hand, its revolutionary for its time because of the high variations, 3D elements and dynamic lighting. Oh, and one of the first games that allows you to dual wield pistols. But on the other, it's stuck in the past: Wolfenstein 3D engine, thus only 90 degrees walls; most of the locations are blending together; combat certainly feels like Wolfenstein 3D (not always, but mostly); low variety in enemies (5 out of 10 common enemies feels the same in their behavior and moves) unnecessary life and point system since game allows you to save. And all of this came out after Doom 2. Game still have certain appeal. Variety of explosion weapons, powerups and powerdown, ability to fly, gimmick to rocketjump before Quake (which is necessary for good ending in original campaign), it helps to differentiate this game from others.The Hunt Begins is a short campaign with 11 levels, which was shareware version, showcasing environments, basic gameplay, some enemies, pover-ups. Nothing to say about it, it can become a little boring before final level, which introduce Triad Enforcer. Best enemy in the game, constant threat and annoyance. Most of the enemies you can stunlock in hurt animation so they cannot do a thing, but not this lad. And they throw 5 or 6 of them right at the fake end of the final level.Dark War is the main original game, with 30+ levels. Pretty decent for the most part, some levels are interesting, some traps and enemy placement is engaging, but this package is a little uneven. One level will take you 10 to 15 minutes, short, tightly designed and sometimes even beautiful, but another level will be tediously long, confusing to navigate with very detailed map, sometimes enemy placement is way too ♥♥♥♥-ish and some secrets are almost impossible to find without humping every wall. I was growing tired by the end of the campaign. Highlights: little gimmicks like heating food with explosives to recover more HP, bosses, especially the NME (i have no idea how people back in 1995 – with little to no experience in shooters – dealt with him), platforming and gimmicky sections like The Room level.Extreme RotT, at least in this port, is more interesting. Yeah, most levels are gimmicks, but because of it, levels are shorter and more focused than original ones. Well, i didn't play it on max difficulty because I still have some love for myself, only on Normal, and that made experience way more tolerable. Because this is a cruel campaign. Most of the traps in Dark War designed to caught you off-guard and give you some room to deal with ambush. Traps and even normal encounters in Extreme RotT designed to kill you. This is very unique, a lot of staff you see here feels like user created levels that found out about certain tricks and gimmicks in level editor. But no, this is pretty much equivalent to commercial release of Kaizo Mario World, and Tom Hall and Joe Siegler are laughing at your misery. And funny I mentioned Mario, game sometimes has a certain feel of 3D platforming before 3D, in a good and in a very bad way. I still had more fun with this than with Dark Wars, levels are never overstaying their welcome, they are mostly short, I think this format suits RotT better. But Lord help you to go through levels blindly or without cheats. The Hunt continues is a brand new campaign from New Blood stuff. Good, if a little bit long, levels, most of them wrap around itself pretty nicely, fine traps and enemy placement. Showcasing some new stuff like new lighting settings and effects. Very good addition.I'd say i gave this game too much time (30 hours to complete every campaign), but I do not regret it. Maybe it's better to appreciate this game through videos, since game can drag on in some places. Watch Civvie 11 or something idk. Oh, and listen to the soundtrack from Lee Jackson (and a few from Bobby Prince), this is 10/10 soundtrack. And Andrew Hulshult's 2013 RotT soundtrack is a banger, also included in this port. Maybe not the best game, but pretty interesting experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Old-school fun. Ludicrous gibs. The level designs can get a little cumbersome, in part because it uses the Wolfenstein 3D map format, so each level is a large single floor, but they definitely designed it to get the most out of the format. I dig their style and how they ramp up the difficulty. Good times, and props to Night Dive/New Blood for giving another classic game a fresh coat of paint.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Buy this if you are a RotT fan, but YMMV if you've never played it before.A phenomenal, above-and-beyond remaster of game that I've tried and tried to enjoy but just cannot. If you are a RotT fan, you're going to love the Ludicrous Edition. For everyone else, here are the cons:-Unpleasant platforming-Hit-scanning, bullet-sponge enemies-Tons of traps-Levels that all blend together.-More a challenge of patience than skillI played it back when it first came out, and while it was graphically impressive at the time, I still don't get why people love this game. Heretic and Blood were more for me. I highly recommend this to RotT fans, as there was a lot of care put into this remaster, but I wouldn't say that it's a must-play for those who want to play the FPS classics. For me, there just isn't enough variety in both the levels and the enemies, but the soundtrack is great. Forgive me Civvie.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I was eleven years old when the original Rise of the Triad was released.  Being the son of largely-inattentive parents, I played all the classic first-person shooters: Wolfenstein 3D, Doom, Quake, Heretic.  Each of these games tapped into some of my worst childhood fears, namely the dark and nasty dogs (Quake did both!), so they never resonated with me as much.  But I played the crap out of the ROTT demo and I loved it, particularly all the wild weapons, the exploding bodies (patiently awaiting a Carmageddon remaster), and all the hidden spots and walls.  To this day ROTT remains my favorite of that second generation of first-person shooters.  Of course, I never got to play the full game (because no one's going to buy an eleven year old kid a first-person shooting game, that's be crazy) and thanks to the the incompatibilities of modern software it took until this remaster for me to have the opportunity.I'm anxiously awaiting Kill the Triad!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, Rise of the Triad has always been an excellent game. Flawed, but still entertaining. The soundtrack is perhaps one of the best, thanks to Lee Jackson and Bobby Prince.Nightdive has done it again. A fabulous remaster that not only puts the Shareware episode and the two official releases in a single package, but also adds a new episode.  There are also new additions like restoring cut enemies, new HUD options, QoL like reducing the Monk's health, or allowing you to play the original soundtrack or 2013 soundtrack.This is a must for anyone who played the original ROTT. Or anyone who is interested in old FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: A long, boring festival of mazes and hidden switches that open who knows what. A plus for a few solutions that were original for their time and a good remaster in itself (Nightdive, as always, did their job well - the source material was simply weak). I completed all the campaigns (including the Return mod - by the way, also very weak), and at the very end I completed (almost) the entire Extreme. Unfortunately, due to a game bug (switches not working), I wasn't able to see the final boss! Almost 40 hours of gameplay and i can't to finished! What a shame. 3.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Another great Night Dive remaster, but this is them polishing kind of a turd here compared to the other boomer shooters they’ve remastered such as Blood, Doom 64, or Powerslave. Rise of the Triad originally was supposed to be a Wolf 3D sequel before Tom Hall left id and man does it show; this game feels more archaic than Doom and it came out two years later. Rise of the Triad examples most of the flaws people levy at classic boomer shooters, its obtuse key hunting  in samey labyrinthine corridors; if the in-game map wasn’t such a massive QoL that highlighted pressure plates and what areas open up I probably would have dropped this game. The game doesn’t haven’t much of a consistent aesthetic, it’s very slapdash and amateurish, and so is its game design in general. Feels like they just threw everything at a wall to see what stuck and it doesn’t really work super great. Your arsenal is absolutely anemic, I mainly used the infinite ammo MP40, because most other weapons are pickups with limited ammo so you really just want to save them for the bullet sponge enemies like the Enforcers. The powerups are mostly useless trolls aside from God and Dog mode and are best ignored aside from those two. There’s also a live system that just feels tacked on because you’re better off just quicksaving because dying just sends you to pistol start at the beginning of the level.The soundtrack is indeed quite a banger though.I did have enough fun with it and I don’t regret getting this game at all, especially because as I said, Night Dive did great work, but I had my fill after beating the shareware campaign and Dark War. I’d only recommend this if you already a fan of this game or if you’re a boomer shooter fan who’s already played the better games of the era.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is what remasters should strive to be, keep the original with all of the new engine features, quality of life improvements, etc. Then also add every official content that existed for the game. Then you add new content on top of it by ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ new blood. Then add official mapping support with workshop support.I'm sorry but this is the best remaster that's ever released in the history of everything so far and it's for rise of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ triad.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Rise of the Triad is up there with Duke as the best early-mid 90s FPS. Tom Hall is one of my biggest inspirations and this game's personality totally lines up with his craziness. I love this game, even if the level design is a bit simple.I have more fun with ROTT than I do Doom. ROTT is just so crazy and wild.The only gripe I had was multiplayer was a bit naff on launch, but I hear it's been fixed with the 1.1 update. Will have to give it a try.I'm excited to see what else Nightdive can remaster, this one was (aside the initial multiplayer issues) perfect in every way, and one of the few games where I went achievement hunting. I normally don't give a hoot about achievements.Also you nerfed the monks' health, so Episode 4 is actually fun to play now!!Thank you Apogee, Nightdive and New Blood for bringing back one of the GOATs. This is the proper treatment ROTT needed.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: *Played on DeckNew Blood does it again but ludicrous. Remaking/Remastering one of my favorite childhood FPS games with all the love and care you'd hope to see. They don't just remake the game, they improved it with all these tiny little things that will forever make you look at every other game (EVERY OTHER GAME) and go 'huh. Why didn't they do that?'. _childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo for a quite while and grew up with the original (have played many times over the years). Many of the features are a welcome addition for this release. The original game was far from perfect. On the one hand (for its time) there's some cool features or ideas relatively unique to the game. Mechanics like unlimited bullet ammo (which you will use a lot) and missile weapons with limited ammo and the ability to hold only one missile weapon at a time (trading them when found) for example. The game has a decent amount of charm and has very game-y mechanics (collectible ankhs acting as Mario Coins, bounce pads aka springs). I do feel that the limited gun mechanics (as fun and interesting as the unique missile weapons are) and some of the spongey enemies (particularly later enemies although this port does tweak that somewhat apparently) do bring the game down a bit, coupled with the limits of the engine (levels have different height levels like Doom, but are restricted and consist of blocks like Wolfenstein). Nevertheless it's a great port and still a fun nostalgic experience that deserves some love. Just (especially for those who experience motion sickness) beware when 'under the influence' of the Mushroom Power-Down in this port. The original DOS version had your sight and movement affected with flashing colours, but in this port there are added distorted effects that do not appear to be able to be disabled, and can be quite uncomfortable and disorientating to stare at! While it's a cool effect it's likely to cause at least some people potential issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loving it.My focus has been mostly on the Level Editor, which is a really cool addition to the game.The editor has a bit of a learning curve in the beginning, but becomes clearer over time. If you're having trouble working with it, I'd suggest loading up the levels from the game itself and studying how they function.The game itself also plays really nicely. The performance is great and the amount of content you get for the price is definitely worth it in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Important note: Runs on Steam Deck just fine. No proton changing or patching needed. I just clicked and started playing.I was never a big ROTT player. I played it a bit and owned it way back in the day, but it didn't hook me like Doom, Wolfenstein, Catacombs, and others. I guess it was just a little to goofy feeling for the time, or the aiming up and down with the keyboard.But wow does this play so much better now. The updated controls feel just right. This is 100% run and gun if that is what you are looking for. And there is no reason to get the Dark War version on Steam now, unless you are hurting that much for cash. But my advice would be to mow a couple extra lawns over getting Dark War.However, a very big warning: this is still as old school as it gets. If your experiences with shooters all start with "C", end with "y", and have "all of dut" in the middle...you probably won't dig this as much as those of us that grew up in the time this first came out. Its not nostalgia...its just a different kind of shooter than what you get these days.So if you are looking to turn off the big puzzle solving and jumping part of your brain, to reallocate those resources to the run and drop bodies everywhere part...well then: welcome to ROTT.

_childDocuments_.review: This is Blake, and while you guys might have the wrong impression of me for being misdiagnosed (don't mean to be personal but it's true) I love you guys for bringing this game back with such a bad ass source port, and for once i can create levels which is surprisingly fun for a tile editor , simple but also not, and requires alot of patience I thank you guys so much, Scott might have the wrong impression of me due to this misdiagnosis that induced mental illness on meds i never needed to be on and we bumped heads at a point after being really cool, but at least Tom hall grew to like me, thank you guys for making my childhood so damn awesome YES, buy it, and if you want even better graphics look into a simple tool called reshade, can add ambient occlusion all kinds of ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: Is this an arena multiplayer shooter? Absolutely!!.... a very unique and uncommon experience among the grandfather classics of the uprising local Deathmatch over IPX (Coaxial NIC), serial null-modem; or dial-up gaming of the yesteryear.Rise of the Triad is in a category by itself with how EXTREMELY fast paced it is compared to Doom / Doom 2 of the early 1990s.The pros and cons of this release (on a multiplayer standard) rely on how many players are connected to the host. While the host has an advantage over the clients with a zero ping, clients have some delay and a sync on respawn after death (in due time i'm sure will receive an update for smoother gameplay).Crossplay will be an even more chaotic experience as console players will join the ranks of the fast paced action that Rise of the Triad brought to the table.Overall, the game is a blast from the past.... lag or not.I haven't lost track of time in awhile, but when I downloaded Ludicrous Edition it was 2am when I finished multiplayer sessions.... and I thought it was 10pm. That being said! It's worth the purchase and enjoy the game. :)

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT buy this for multiplayer!At least not now.  I suppose there's a chance they will fix and improve it, but this kind of thing seems to rarely happen.And IF that happened, it's very unlikely multiplayer people will come back to the game and populate it.TECHNICALLY it "works" ....I was able to join a few games and play,but you go rubberbanding all over the place frequently, and die from actions you don't see until after your dead. _childDocuments_.review: It's like if you took Wolfenstein 3D, Super Mario, and a Salvador Dali painting and put them in a blender.One of my favorite games as a child - thanks mom and dad! - and now with full controller support.Can't wait to play this on my Steam Deck and relive my PTSD nightmares all over again.10/10 Retro FPS
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Very badly aged game.The remaster is mostly fine, except for the glitchy map that still to this day has not been fixed yet.The engine pulls off impressive things from a technical standpoint for its time. But the levels just do not hold up in quality and fun. Especially the "Extreme Rise of the Triad" expansion being the worst offender.Most enemies are hitscan, the levels are all grid-based like in Wolf3D, but adds another layer of complexity with verticality, which often makes levels even more confusing. Many levels are filled with switches that do not inform the player what they did, leaving you to wander around the level over and over to find the one thing it opened.Many levels also come with a ton of obnoxious traps and obstacle courses.Now I don't mind the occasional platforming and traps to avoid as a pause between combat, but many levels are simply too filled with this obnoxious crap, making the whole experience just a tedious mess that you mostly just want to skip.The main combat is pretty fun, although a bit lazy since the game gives you infinite ammo for the MP40. The rocket launchers are mostly cool, but unusable because of the cramped spaced everywhere. The Excalibat is a useless piece of crap that I do not understand how anyone put through testing. So in the end you'll just be spamming the MP40, which will become annoying when dealing with tanky enforcers and monks, that all will take a long time to take down, making the combat really boring in some areas.Generally speaking just a massive dissapointment, and only played through all levels for the sake of this game being pretty historical. But in the end a game I will never ever replay again. Just not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Bonkers 90's shooter, kept alive by some dedicated folks at New Blood. This game really leaves an impression despite it's shortcomings compared to it's contemporaries. The Ludicrous Edition is definitely the way to go if you wanna give it a shot nowadays as it has some nice QOL improvements as well as having all the ROTT you could possibly want in one place.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: While this is a great treatment for this game by Nightdive, the game sucks and the price is too damn high.Boring, maze-like, and overall irritating gameplay plague this version just like the original. The multiplayer is screwed with awful netcode that still hasn't been updated to be actually playable. I get that this is a cult classic cherished by many, but I really cannot recommend this game unless you have some nostalgia for it. Just listen to the soundtrack, it's really the only thing worth your time from this game.

Runs like a dream on Steam Deck at basically no power drain for tons of hours of boom shoot on the go. _childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I love my boomer shooters. It's nice to see a not-so-known FPS receive the remaster treatment (well to be fair, the 2013 remake was pretty badass too). This is basically a cross between wolfenstein 3d and doom. Point is, anything ROTT will always have my money. Pure 90s shooter nostalgia with a badass soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: If you're coming into this after something like Doom, you'll be a bit disappointed in this game's simplicity. This is a really fun game though, it just suffers from the unfortunate fate of being released a month after Doom 2.The level design can be a bit obtuse and labyrinthine at times, but the action is very fun! The guns and rocket launchers are all super satisfying to use, and because most enemies are hitscan you have to make good use of cover. This game has a really silly sense of humor that sets it apart from most FPS games of the time, and it also does a decent job of implementing verticality into the level design using floating platforms and the like. Rise of The Triad Ludicrous Edition consists of the original 3 episodes made by Apogee, plus a new episode made by Nightdive, this totals up to around 40 levels, PLUS you have a level editor with Steam Workshop support! Edit: Also the soundtrack is AWESOME!Honestly I really only have 2 complaints:1. That price truly is "Ludicrous." Wait for a sale. (Like right now, Summer sale, woo!) I got this in a Humble Bundle a little while back so it was effectively like $2 for me.2. Vertical mouse movement makes the game look a little off. Edit: I figured out what it is, whatever they did for the perspective change when looking up and down isn't correct. If you look at a straight wall you'll see that the sides of the wall look perfectly parallel no matter how you look at it, causing this weird slightly warped environment. You get used to it, just looks weird. If you can't get past this, they include "Return of The Triad," which I believe is a port using the GZDoom engine instead of KEX which shouldn't have this issue. (edit 2: I was wrong, it is an entirely new fan-made sequel using the GZDoom engine, still though that one doesn't have the weird rendering issue.)
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: ROTT never really had a super good source port like Doom or Duke3D got, so this is a very, VERY welcome product.It's not perfect, but it's better than anything else by a country mile. I also like that they included the cut alternative guards and a brand new episode.As for things to improve on, I'd like to see a true 3d render instead of Y-shearing, and it would've been nice to have some kind of upscaling on the sprites.Overall though, very very satisfied.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Rise of the Triad is a bit of an oddball game - originally intended as a sequel to Wolfenstein (and built on a vastly expanded version of its engine), Id Software abruptly dropped support for the project, apparently not wanting to draw attention away from their upcoming Doom.  However, Apogee continued work on it while removing any direct ties to its predecessor, and the end result is something totally unique.  While Wolf3D at least had a semblance of grounded storyteling and realism despite its primitive tech and fantastical elements, RotT goes all out in becoming strange and surreal.  With rocket-propelled floating platforms, huge sections of level walls sliding around, bizarre level layouts full of traps and switch puzzles and all manner of outlandish weapons and powerups like the "Drunk Missiles", "Dog Mode" and the "Excalibat" (an enchanted bat which fires flaming baseballs), it definitely isn't wanting for weirdness.  2023's Ludicrous Edition is definitely the one to check out these days though, with a more modernized control scheme, much of its cut content restored, a map editor and numerous new levels to check out.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The original 2 campaigns are a complete mixed bag of quality, more often than not the levels are designed so so so so SO poorly. Complete mazes with no sense to where the exit is. Also the fact that the pistol is even in this game is weird tbhHavent really played the new campaign yet so maybe its better enough to justify it, just most of the content in this game is not worth it.TBH jumping around as a dog is the most fun part, should've been the whole game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The only Rise of the Triad I've ever played (or started playing) was the 2013 remake. I've never played much of it because it felt like a mindless mix of elements that don't really fit together, with labyrinth-like levels that made no sense whatsoever.Little did I know, the 2013 remake is indeed true to the original in this regard. Even this original game has the same, mindless labyrinth levels, the same blend of things that feel like they were slapped together just to have them.I'm getting absolutely no enjoyment out of this and I don't understand how anyone could. This feels like a game that I would have made when I was 14 years old, had I had the ability to make games then. Tall walls here, random items there, enemies everywhere but no context or sense to be found.The only reason I'm not refunding this game is because I like Nightdive and they did a good job with the remaster - it works exactly as advertised. They're not responsible for the content of the original game.This game was a bit of a blind spot for me and now I wish it had stayed that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Rise of the Triad is what happens when Wolfenstein 3D snorts a full mile of crack, orders every expensive drink at the party bar and goes absolutely nuts on the dance floor while projectile vomiting everywhere.It is a product of 90's gaming that specifically only that era of gaming could deliver, and it's worth every last minute.Sure, it's a bit of an acquired taste and most of the game's mechanics and humour probably won't land well for you, but I had an incredibly fun time with just the "The Hunt Begins" episode alone.Give it a shot if you're a fan of the older DOOM or Wolfenstein games. Or if you just want something weird, wacky and wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I've been hearing about this one particular FPS for a while now, and how much people loved it and still loves it. So obviously I had to jump at the chance to play it after Nightdive made it's due remaster.Honestly, I find it mid. Always looked average to me and I do find it amazingly average now.Sure, it is somewhat of a sequel to the grandaddy of FPSs Wolfenstein. You can tell the influence. IT IS pretty much an spiritual sequel because it's is a very arcadey game.And you could go "ok, it's an old DOS FPS what were you expecting" but this game came out in '95 bro. Doom had already came out 2 years prior, and we were one year away from Duke 3D. Hell, even System Shock had come out in '94!Level design is "mazey" as you would expect but specifically in the Extreme ROTT espiso, it feels like one of those insane mods for old games, you know, those in which nothing makes sense and are as insufferably hard as they can be. I mean, Jesus man, I had to turn on the cheats by the end because I was just fed up with amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the nonsensical levels were putting me through. I did choose hard difficulty so I guess the joke is on me.Movement is iffy, there's little enemy variety, little weapon variety, it's whole difficulty is based on how much it can throw you off with hazards and shooting can sometimes be unresponsive. Now I don't know if this has always been the case, or if it due to the Nightdive version of the game, but it does have a sense of humor. I give it that.This is a game for nostalgics and hardcore retro FPS enthusiasts. Other than that, I find it to be above average to be honest. I mean, it is fun in it's own way, like Wolfenstein, but even at this time there were far more interesting FPSs coming out.3/5
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best way to experience this absolutely deranged and insane fever dream of a game, where almost every mechanic has a weird and unique twist that keeps things interesting and add a lot of charm and personality to the game.Shoutout to Lee Jackson for cooking some of the best tracks of all time for this game's soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you've enjoyed this game before or are new to oldschool FPS, this full-fat port is a must-buy.My only issue is that for some reason, I can't find the "Return of the Triad" extra package anywhere. Edit: It's in its own folder inside the game files, and is not integrated into the game proper nor Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't for everyone. It wasn't when it was new and it certainly isn't now, but if you like Wolfenstein 3D and those other early IDtech games you will like this. This is the best version of the game to ever exist. Period. It has everything ever released, in widescreen, running perfectly on modern hardware WITH multiple improvements. Do you want the Monks to have half HP? One click in the menu. Do you want the annoying as hell low health sound turned off? One click in the menu. Do you want to see what percentage your health is at instead of the green bars? One click in the menu. New alternate sound effects? One click in the menu. Speaking of sounds, all of the music from Bobby Prince and Lee Jackson is here in multiple formats including the entire re-records that Andrew Hulshult did for ROTT 2013. Also, you can switch between them at will, on a song by song basis, in the menu. Not to mention an all new episode that has so many great creators on it, it would be worth the price alone, but that's not even the end of it. Bring back the alternate characters from the credits? One menu click and it's a percentage slider so they show up sometimes, half the time or only new character models. If you haven't bought this by now, why are you still reading this? You either know you want it by now or you don't.

_childDocuments_.review: Rise of the Triad: LE: DOPEFISH LIVES!One thing that's always been on my mind, especially as the patron hipster of boom shoots has been "what game inspired this one". It's a genre that has some pretty clear influences for sure, with every week someone deciding to cover another retro game for funsies. But I'm more so talking about the energy. The manic indie dev vibe that looks at various design ideas and goes "yknow what'd be cool?". And that's when I remembered ROTT's remaster was finally going to be a thing.And it all came together.Rise of the Triad is the precursor game to every boomer shooter solely because it's built on "y'know what'd be cool". No other game has had that vibe to the same extent as ROTT. There's not a single chunk of this game's design that is not done because Tom Hall and the D.I.P.S thought it'd be cool. Completely silly ideas done because they were handed a basically functional Wolfenstein 3D engine and Tom had all of the silly ideas from DOOM still in his brain. Beyond the chunk of DOOM bible he's lifted, although adding 5 playable characters for no other reason than you  is certainly a "that'd be neat" idea. The idea of taking Wolfenstein and forcing it to be in quasi-3D with the floating G.A.D's, the various off-kilter weapons where half of them were basically just bugs they decided to make into weapons. The enemy variety that is just the entire Apogee office digitized into the game, because that'd be cool. Or the various power ups that still remain some of the best and funniest I've seen. Nothing on this planet will bring me as much glee as "dog mode" not only being a thing but being a terrifyingly powerful thing. The fact Nightdive and New Blood added a suite of goofy Doom Guy like sprites to it is just icing on an incredibly disjointed cake. Yeah this game's stupid. It's an incredibly clunky not-3D FPS game that will give you vertigo if you look up or down long enough. To say nothing of the fact you will accidentally kill yourself trying to shoot rockets up at enemies. And it's all wrapped in a layer of such sincere creativity and stupidity that it's stood the test of time. That combination has kept the meme of this game surviving long past the point of 3D Realms eclipsing this game in complexity. Through Duke Nukem Forever, the 2013 reboot and Scott Miller's move to bring back the height of gaming excitement. A dumb back-of-the-catalog game that waited almost 20 years for a remaster is worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the game that just doesn't care. It's violent, it's an FPS, it's from the mid-90s, it has blood, it has guts, it's obviously a Doom/Wolfenstein clone. We kids knew it from the beginning, when this little 90s gem was a mere cheap shareware on the shelf. Doom clones were abound, but this one just didn't care. It gets to the point rather nicely, complete with missile launchers and meat grinder levels. It doesn't even bother with demons, just occult Nazi themes and a hearty dose of ultra-violence. There's just infinite bullet ammo and Nazi-look alike enemies. This game added added eyeballs and ludicrous gibs to the blood and guts department of video gaming. Then there's the fact that, in this game, you literally have your almost-a-Nazi enemies begging for mercy just before playing dead, only to suddenly rise back up and go at you again. If you got far enough on the shareware, or had a friend who had all the episodes, then you had the ol' endless "Here! Catch!" The trampoline effect was cool until Duke Nukem and Quake arrived, but in this game you can take mushrooms and play a tall moaning god....for better or worse! ;-)The dual pistols were an old obsession of mine when I was about 14-15 years old. It wasn't until the complete Rise of the Triad edition was released on IBM compatible 3 1/2 disks that I played the other missions beyond the shareware version. There are so many hilariously ludicrous features to this game. Sometimes after a particularly brutal take-down there will be a voice taunting you, almost moaning in a ghostly manner...."you.....suuuucckkk!"..... In this game you can't even exit properly without some tongue-in-cheek reference to violence and death. 'tis so cool to be playing this lil' ultra-violent, vulgar, rebellious, an' impertinent lil' twerp once again! One last note however, I never imagined myself playing this game with a full-mouse-view feature. This game was released before I started using a mouse-keyboard combo and held it's own for a long time in my world. It just feels so weird using a mouse with this game and some of the appeal is lost in time....

_childDocuments_.review: Its Rise of the Triad, mostly as you remember it, but with enough QoL improvements, and new content, to make it worth the asking price. Stuff that was cut from the original release, like more guard types, including female counterparts have been added back in. You have a choice in how you want the game to sound as well, with OPL-emulated Adlib-style music, General Midi or the soundtrack from the 2013 remake of the original game.

_childDocuments_.review: The greatest Doom clone ever made. Sure it's got more in common with Wolfenstein 3D, including its engine, but that's what we called them back in the day, bucko. It was made by a bunch of people from Apogee who did Wolfenstein 3D. It was almost Wolfenstein 3D 2, but it turned out to be too bad@$$ to be part of any series. This game is totally awesome, just buy it. What's it about? Who cares? The plot is about some cult that tries to take over the world or something, and you stop them by shooting lots of guns into lots of people and robots and fat, undead monks. It was made back before games tried to have stories, so it's all about having fun and shooting people constantly. Watch the opening slideshow if you want to know the plot, and know that I think less of you for doing so.They also realized that looking for bullets for your basic guns wasn't any fun, so everything apart from heavy weapons has infinite ammo. Get a machine gun as soon as you can, and just never stop shooting. Occasionally you might meet an enemy you need to shoot with a bazooka to kill, like a robot or a guy with a big honkin' machine gun, and then you do that instead. There's also a few really annoying bosses, and one of them even has special needs which is very cool. When they go down, you'll get a false feeling of catharsis that you should be getting from actually achieving things in your life, but your brain won't notice the difference. Neat!You can choose your character sort of like a fighting game, and it changes your speed, accuracy, and hit points. How many other FPS games do that? Probably none worth talking about. There are power-ups that give you Jesus powers, dog powers, or let you fly, as well as power-downs that make you disoriented or bouncy. You can get flame or bullet-resistant armor too. There's a ton of levels from the original, and a whole new episode in this version, so you should really be playing it right now rather than reading all these nerd words like some lame-o.Speaking of lame-o's, how have I gone this long without mentioning the tunes? I don't know, there's something wrong with me, I'm talking to someone about it. The soundtrack of ROTT is famously awesome, and sort of sounds like if the music from a bunch of different classic retro games got bashed together in an explosion of auditory perfection. The only real difference is that most of the music of which ROTT's soundtrack is redolent was written by Japanese people, and those tracks have either weird names written in moonrunes, or really bland descriptive English names, and ROTT's songs were written by Lee Jackson, who wrote a bunch of other Apogee music that is also really good, but not quite this good. And instead of being named weird made-up words, they have slick English names like 'Havana Smooth' or 'Going Down the Fast Way'. In fact, you wouldn't be wasting your time by foregoing the game and just listening to the soundtrack, which many people who aren't as gamer as I am choose to do.But if you're gamer, if you have the hardcores, just go ahead and play it right now. See what happens.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't the biggest fan of this game back in the day. What with me already being used to the cartoon realism of Build games, the abstract, monotonous environments seemed lackluster by comparison. Looking back now, it's easier to appreciate it for what it was: a unique game with some crazy-ass weapons and creative level design. Its humor and over-the-top violence are pretty typical of that era of gaming. It was a time when developers didn't take themselves too seriously and the overall lower budget required to make a video game meant that, as a gamer, you were thrown a curveball every so often. Rise of the Triad was one of those curveballs, being an FPS that stuck closer to the Wolfenstein 3D formula than Doom and its 'clones' , and expanded upon said formula enough to make the game feel like a totally different experience - an experience that is still hard to compare to any other title from that era.What also stands out about this release in particular is that it's a blueprint for everything a remaster should be. Nightdive already have a good reputation for salvaging these ancient games and preserving them for generations to come, but ROTT: Ludicrous Edition is probably their best work yet. It features all of the content associated with ROTT (except for that 2013 reboot of course) and countless gameplay options you can use to tweak the experience. ROTT is still not my favorite title from that era by a long shot, but it's a fun game to play when you do a few levels at a time. We should count ourselves lucky if Nightdive decide to give any other classic games the Ludicrous treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: ROTT was not my cup of tea as a kid. I didn't get it's design philosophy. The extra content, modifications, soundtracks, etc. just show an absolute appreciation for the original game.Highly recommend this if you like games that are a little wackadoo, A LOT classic gaming-style and ultimately completely, utterly, ridiculous......especially this edition!The ONLY caveat is, mapmaking is it right now for modding. I think the hope is that can expand and folks can add more content beyond just levels eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: Another remarkable remaster from Nightdive, but I really want to commend NewBlood for their contributions as well. NewBlood focused on restoring the cut enemies, putting together the new episode and working on QoL features like the extra HUD, which really elevates this remaster as an ultimate edition.The new episode is great if you're into ROTT's brand of level design and uses some more advanced features as well as taking advantage of the verticality that's possible with the jump pads and platforms of the game in very natural ways. Engine side, this game got put in KEX really well, everything in this feels right, from the rendering to the movement, some of the signature but lovable jank is still there. I don't love ROTT nearly as much as other people do but asides from a near complete overhaul like the Quake II remaster, which I feel like would just mess up the personality of this game, there's nothing more I could ask from this.It's true that nobody loves ROTT more than NewBlood and Nightdive and I'm really glad they're the ones who got their hands on this after it got taken away from 3DR, if you're a fan you can't miss this release.

_childDocuments_.review: OLD REVIEW: "by all means, great remaster, probably one of the best even. just that the game itself sucks"that review was bad. it wasnt even a hour of playtime, and I only got to the third level of The Hunt Begins. so, after some thinking, I decided I'd pick up this game again, and to actually play it. and I ended up liking it, too.in short, this remaster is pretty damn good, even if the game it remasters has some bad aspects.I do and have always greatly appreciated the content they put into this remaster. they put as much content as they possibly could. balancing, alternative weapon sounds (since apparently people didn't like the original ones?), a brand new episode, a level editor, workshop, and more. probably one of the best remaster in terms of new content, right under Quake 2's. it's also great how now we have an actually good way to play ROTT on modern systems, too (trust me, rottexpr is not that good).as for the game itself, that's a different story. it's fun, yes, but also has it's flaws. the maps are confusing and nearly maze-like, even having stuff like moving walls and trapped floors that are hard to find, the floating platforms are pretty annoying and Extreme ROTT is a sinful curse that makes Final Doom's TNT Evilution look like the greatest game ever. however, the game does has its upsides. weapons are fun to use, there is a good variety of enemies (especially with the new alternate enemies), and quite a few levels are ones that I really enjoy. and of course, I cant make a review of this game without mentioning the soundtrack. definitely a must-listen.

_childDocuments_.review: Rise Of The Triad is a game I have known existed for almost my entire life - an old physical Apogee shareware catalogue, sadly long gone, registered its name in my head from a young age, and it was mentioned here and there in various places by various people as I was growing up. Somehow, until this remaster, I had managed to unintentionally avoid playing it, despite playing and loving many of its contemporaries, a lot of which it was compared to (often unfavourably). All of this in mind, I knew I wanted to finally play it, but I was also prepared to run through it and call it a day whenever I got bored of it, consigning it to the status it seems to have been given popularly - a historical curio.Playing through in the order in the menu - shareware into the full Dark War campaign followed by Extreme ROTT, I found myself liking it, and wanting to play a bit more every now and then, but it didn't grab my full attention. It was at about 30 hours in, partway into the Extreme ROTT expansion, something clicked. Deep in the sea of surreal moving walls, spinning blades, pyrotechnics and overenthusiastic jump pads that make up ROTT's arsenal of environmental death traps, I came to understand that ROTT is not a game that exists to make sense.ROTT is a messy game, built on a messy engine that was already a couple of years out of date by the time it released, using messy conventions that barely made sense at the time, and yet somehow it not only doesn't feel limited by it, it *thrives* in it. It's silly, it knows it's silly, and it knows that you know it's silly. It doesn't try to make itself look or feel realistic, even by the standards of the time. It gives you a bunch of silly weapons and powerups, a big pile of enemies, some weird platforming challenges, and points you in the general direction of more things for you to blow up.The shareware and original campaigns show their age, but are quite fun. The new campaign, built by various Nightdive and New Blood devs, serves to even more strongly highlights the game's stronger aspects, with more imaginative levels and layouts, more generous availability of the best weapons (i.e. anything explosive), and bigger piles of enemies to expend them towards, and the remaster itself is well made (including Andrew Hulshult's soundtrack from the 2013 reboot was a particularly nice touch).But for me, the most surprising part of this package is Extreme ROTT. It has... let's say a poor reputation, and by the standards of the shooter ROTT otherwise is, it's not an unfounded one. A lot of the levels are poorly decorated, often quite simple in terms of layout, and in a lot of cases, *very* difficult. But if you can look past that, Extreme ROTT is full of some extremely creative ideas and uses of existing objects. In some levels, it almost plays more like a puzzle game. In others, it plays more like a platformer. In a few, it plays like nothing else I've ever seen, a chaotic maelstrom of blood, explosions, moving walls with strange faces on them, trap elevators that teleport you into a huge open space full of enemies, thirty enemies shouting "HERE, CATCH" simultaneously, robots that look they were made from used cans of food with wheels on them, and the giant illuminated face of Scott Miller watching it all unfold.I couldn't stop playing. Not because the gameplay was exceptional, it was merely solid. Not because the graphics were all that interesting, it's mostly greys, browns and reds. I couldn't stop playing because, despite knowing that I had seen all the objects before, even having come to understand their behaviour fairly well, I had *no* idea what would be thrown at me next. The level design constantly showed me the same building blocks that all the levels I'd played before had used, but in a way I hadn't seen them used before, or even considered that they could be used.In short, this game won't be for everyone. Although it gets a lot right, there are plenty of questionable design decisions, some fairly strong limitations, and the "looking up and down by stretching" technique (also employed by other games of a similar age) will make some people feel sick. But for me, it made exactly the right impression, in the right order - first it endeared itself to me with its sense of fun, then it reinvented itself repeatedly, first with its unusual expansion, and then with the remaster's new levels, drawing me further and further into a game that I hadn't expected would be capable of it, just to see what it would come up with next. This may indeed be a historical curio, but it is one that is well worth studying.EDIT: Oh, I almost forgot - if all of this wasn't enough, the remaster has a very capable built-in level editor and Steam Workshop support, and there's already a bunch of properly solid user levels for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another game from my childhood whose Shareware version I played for countless hours, remastered and re-released to work flawlessly on modern PCs and draw in a bunch of new fans. What's not to like?The game itself takes a little effort to wrap your head around. Where normal FPS games of its time had a number of weapons that just scaled upward in power (Wolfenstein 3D) or were best used in particular situations (Doom, Blood, Duke Nukem 3D, etc), weapons in Rise of the Triad fall into two categories: bullet weapons, and missile weapons.Bullet weapons have infinite ammo, and scale up in usefulness; once you get the MP40 machine gun, you'll never need to use either of the others. On the other hand, the player can only hold one missile weapon at a time, they each have limited ammo with no pickups for additional ammunition, and they're all fairly different in how they work. Maybe one fires a heat-seeking shot. Another launches a pair of them that split when you let go of the fire button. Yet another will hit the ground and turn into a rapidly-expanding wall of fire to instantly take out anyone in its path.I'm going to re-write this review someday; right now it's just something I slapped together for the 2023 Steam Choice Awards.

If you're into the old-school shooters and don't mind a challenge, this is an easy buy.Also, EAT LEAD!
