Though somewhat obtuse and weird, it's always nice to appreciate the old ideas in the modern era.With the amazing job that Night Dive made here, we not only have an amazing port with all the modern necessities (such as high resolution support), the QoL improvements (such as the reduced monk's life), all the levels released in the time AND a brand-new episode hand-made by the Night Dive devs!If you like retro-shooters, you can't pass this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Very quirky and over-the-top old school FPS that feels closer in spirit to something out of the Sega Genesis than any of its contemporary shooters. While the gameplay is solid with some nice ideas, the ludicrous amount of levels means it can get repetitive (the new levels are much better in this regard). However, the absurdist tone and AMAZING soundtrack won me over completely. I love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Rise of the Triad was very much overlooked in its day and was held fondly in the hearts of those few who played it. I played it back in the day and carried a lot of nostalgia for it, despite never revisiting it. Until now, that is. Rise of the Triad Ludicrous Edition takes an underrated gem and makes it as good as it can possibly be.This is the equivalent of showing your wife your favourite Star Trek episodes. She isn't necessarily going to fall in love with Star Trek, but you can rest assured that she's seen the best it has to offer. This is the best, and indeed the most, that Rise of the Triad has to offer. Love it or hate it. I love it. I hope you love it too.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Back in the 90s, any FPS game released was important, since we didn't have many of them. Rise of the Triad (ROTT) came in during a period that we had very few alternatives: Wolfenstein 3D, ShadowCaster, DOOM, and some lesser known variants of the latter.ROTT is quite repetitive and its formula was a bit outdated already, but I loved it nonetheless. This remaster revitalised it for me, and now I love it even more. They've included the prelude, the main levels, the official expansion, and a brand-new episode with levels carefully designed like the original ones. Oh, you can also play competitive multiplayer that requires zero setup, although you will have a hard time finding someone to play with.Make no mistake: this game was already old when it came out. ROTT's repetitive action is not for everybody, but if you like firing the same weapon over and over, kill packs of armed soldiers (and crazy monks), and explore labyrinths with lots of secrets, then this game is definitely for you. Don't be shy in using the explosive guns, by the way — they are exactly for mowing down large groups of foes, and saving them for a better moment never pays off.This is yet another great work by Nightdive Studios. Do Keep 'em coming! I am having a great time reliving these timeless classics in such good shape.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic work by the team, as a fan for years living off the WinROTT port (and the Apogee Throwback Pack before that) this is such a loving and diligent effort to recreate everything that made the game great, and pack in everything that a fan would hope for; if Desktop Themes were still a thing I wouldn't have put it past them to make their own ROTT version just to put one more little extra in, screensavers and all. If you're not a fan of the game and it looks a little primitive I'd still encourage you give it a go; there's a simplicity to the main loop that I always like to return to occasionally for a mindless hour or two, and combined with Lee Jackson's still unmatched OST and all the original personality of the game (FULLY intact, that's for sure) it's still a very fun, very entertaining package. Also Andrew Hulshult's remixed soundtrack from the 2013 reboot is also amazing as you'd expect from the guy, and you can freely switch between the two which I've been doing often.The new episode is also amazing, props to all of the level editors for making a completely new set of levels that feel right at home with the rest of the experience;  that NME fight really messed with me, but then the NME always does.Now to continue working my way through Extreme ROTT, which out of respect to the Tom Hall and Joe Siegler I decided to do  writing a glowing review; love Nightdive, love the DIP, now maybe we can see ROTT 2013 get a proper tune up!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game. I am happy this glorious game got some sort of enhanced version, even if the graphics aren't totally reworked, the fact this game runs better than the OG Dos game is good enough for me. I've already unlocked all achievements, I can't wait to delve into the map editor, so many possibilities for new episodes. I haven't played online yet, so can't say much about that. I just like the fact I can FINALLY play this game w/ my Xbox Series X/S controller. playing with mouse and keyboard was a chore in the GOG og version.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This includes everything!  Shareware back in the day contained the first episode or first few levels of the full featured release.  RotT was the exception where the shareware version, "The Hunt Begins", contained its own set of levels that came *before* Dark War rather than being included in Dark War.  The Ludicrous Edition contains ALL of this content, in its proper order, and re-done to work on modern systems with bug fixes and while keeping it VERY true to the original and adding the Andrew Hulshult soundtrack as a selectable option for the original game or you could listen to the original OPL MIDI!  Everything is here and it's RotT as we remember it with an added episode, "The Hunt Continues".  This release couldn't have been better!  I wouldn't mind if they added optional video filters like HQ2x or XBRz for those of us who like to use them, but not having them wasn't a deal-breaker, either.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The team at the short lived Developers Of Incredible Power have really sent out a signal to FPS fans.  We are just now seeing the light from that large explosion.  I recommend you crank your speakers and play the demo instead of reading any further (it's free).You know the backstory already, now play the game!  If you don't and enjoy the game, pick up the excellent book "Masters Of Doom" which explains a bit what the developers were trying to accomplish here given the time and technology.  Running with Scissors shill Civvie11 also has many great videos covering the different episodes in the game.New Blood (and Night Dive) clearly wanted to play homage to a game that meant a lot to them.  They stepped up to be the latest curators of this weird, confusing, exhilarating and cathartic video game.  By including a new map editor, they hopefully ensure its posterity with crezzy user created content.Hopefully this stuffed turkey of a release revitalizes interest so others can appreciate the scrappy punk attitude that is all over the game.  If you feel any negativity toward Rise Of The Triad: LE, that's OK.  It's just a video game.PROTIP: If the game is not enjoyable, please explore the jukebox.  There is a lot of history in those songs and they're a great PC throwback.  With different versions to choose from, you can tinker and see which suits your style as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I will be honest, I play only a little bit of the original DOS version years ago, I mostly remember reaching Scott´s Magical head and got shock after finding it for the first time, that and getting scare of Dorian´s instant spikes and thinking he will telefrag the player.Still even without too much nostalgia, I knew about this game and after buying the Ludicrous Edition, I think I   can summary as: It is the same game, BUT Nightdive throw everything on it including the kitchen sink while modernize it at the same time.For the game, The soundtrack is still really good while giving the option to hear the Original,MIDI and 2013 versions. Visuals of the game are the same from the DOS game with modern improvements, making it the only port/version you need of ROTT. Gameplay wise, it is a DOS First Person Shooter, it plays as good as it was on 1994 or even better.Recommended for fans of FPS games or curious people that want to play a great game for once.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Rise of the Triad is simple compared to its contemporaries, but it uses every design and trick its capable of to create a plethora of unique maps. There's many many secret doors, dark humour, great music, heated porridge, multiple playable characters, useless power ups, monks, and lots of customization. Nostalgia or an interest in retro FPS is definitely a boon to liking this great remastered edition.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite 90's shooters. Along with Doom, Doom 2, Duke Nukem 3D, Shadow Warrior, Wolfenstein 3D and Eradicator - Rise of the triad has been a game that I've come back to many, many times over the years.It's an old school shooter, but with more tricks & traps than most. On the surface, the engine it runs in is pretty limited, but the map designs can be fiendishly complex and very fun to explore.The floating platforms, bounce pads, moving walls and myriads of traps do a lot to make this game play in a very unique way. The best maps in the multiple available campaigns are the ones that really make good use of what ROTT can do that it's contemporaries couldn't do.The new campaign made by the developers of this port is a very good exploration of exactly what makes ROTT unique. I also find the original shareware and full version campaigns very worth playing. Extreme ROTT is more for those who want pain. And then there's bunches of user made content (hopefully much more in the future), as the game has a very good level/campaign editor and workshop integration.As far as other new features in this remake goes, I'm not listing them here. But it's an all-round success. The resolution bump and character mug shots in particular are great additions. My only gripe is that the MIDI music sounds nothing like on original hardware. I wish they'd add different MIDI standards, especially something equivalent to 90's Soundblaster 16  and AWE 32 cards.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: ROTT: Ludicrous Edition is the definitive was to play the 1990s cult classic. It's fun with some frustrating hiccups here and there yet very fun at the same time. They're power ups where you become God and throw projectiles that vaporize bad guys and where you turn into a cute dog and are invulnerable while in both of those power ups. They're also power downs one where you go high on shrooms while dizzy and enemies and objects to interact with flash colors as well as one that where you uncontrollably bounce around the map Flubber style. Enemies come in a semi-diverse shapes and sizes from wannabe Nazis, robots that can only die from explosives zombie from original Quake style, and monk-like superior cultists that can drain your health if you're too close to them, and others that will fling fireballs at you imp from Doom style except the Deathfire Monks fireballs do more damage than the imps from any Doom game that I can think of. Also one of the wannabe Nazi type enemies in the Triad Enforcer who is like Doom 2's Heavy Weapon Chaingunner with the amount of hit points of a Baron of Hell and will also toss grenades at you the same way Blood's cultists would toss dynamite bundles at Caleb during harder difficulties! They're also death traps and deadly obstacle courses that will make the 1997 Build Engine version of Shadow Warrior blush! Ludicrous Edition has five different campaigns being the original shareware port The Hunt Begins, the main source port Dark War, the frustratingly cheap as hell Extreme Rise of the Triad, the brand new The Hunt Continues which is a combination of the three mentioned campaigns, and in a separate add-on with the fan made Return of the Triad in this single package which I'll need to try Return of the Triad at some point next time I boot up this game! I may or may not try some multiplayer mode also when I make the time to do so. Yet again a great pick for fans of the 1990s cult classic from back in the day yet a lot of newcomers may find it frustrating but ROTT: Ludicrous Edition can be played however you like to play and I enjoy this WAY better than the subpar remake from a decade prior to this remastered version of the original!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Nightdive returns once again to prove their dominance in the field of remastering classic games, this time joined by New Blood, the team behind every good game you've ever played in the past 6 years or so and the developers of the (janky but full of heart) 2013 reboot of ROTT. There's nothing really to say, this is the best possible way to play this overshadowed gem of 90's ludicrous gibitude. 4K DOG MODE
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is ROTT!!!  This is hands down, an amazing remaster.  Nightdive, New Blood, and Apogee understand what we want.  Take the old beloved game, update it to perfection, change as little as possible, while fixing anything that "sucked".  These guys obviously love the material and it shows.  Not only do they thank the fans, they say "but wait, there's more" and list things they are going to add.  If you like Boomer Shooters, if you like retro games, if you like Doom, Wolfenstein, GET THIS NOW.  for $15, this is a steal!  They even added features and music from the 2013 game in the right spots.  The soundtrack is bumpin!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: It's very faithful to the original, while bringing along a lot of modern fixes. This is currently far and away the best way to experience this game. Honestly- it was a cult classic around release in the early-mid 90s. Many of my friends were on the Doom kick by the time I found this one. I'm glad it's getting love today.Multiplayer is great.The artwork is fun.The music is amazing.The gameplay is fun and definitely different. It can be very puzzle/platformer based at times. Tons of tricks and traps- definitely a change of pace vs some of the games that came out around that time.It's worth the cost of admission. Runs like a champ. Devs are responsive and laid out a roadmap with some killer features that I really hope come out.Easy to recommend if you're a lover of classic shooters. I don't leave a ton of reviews, but this one is definitely warranted.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Old man, here. Played ROTT way back in 90s.  What the game lacked in "modern" 3D graphics like DOOM, it made up for in doing it's own thing and being blood-soaked fun for the whole family.  Levels are labyrinthine at times but still visually interesting and complex given the limitations of the souped up Wolf 3D engine they were working with.The OG MIDI soundtrack is one of the best ever made in a time before a lot of shooters went with moody ambient style soundtracks (not that those are bad necessarily).  The Folks at Apogee definitely were developers of incredible power!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic remaster of a game of its era.  If you liked the original game when it was new, then this is absolutely the BEST way to relive it.  I haven't gotten a chance to test multiplayer yet but the single player is spot on.  If you haven't played the original, then just know that this came out BEFORE Doom did, so keep that in mind when it comes to the game engine.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Good challenge type FPS, the rules of the world are clearly defined, enemies are more like obstacles while you work out what wall moved and which new path has opened, its brimming with secrets.plays great on a controller, if you turn off freelook you don't really need a KBM for this game, you can control your speed much better with the sticks and you'll need that to navigate around some traps.Thanks for this nightdive, at 11 years old this was my first FPS game and it got me on the path to pcgaming, I also get to play the game properly because i only used cheats as a kid.You did a great job nightdive!* Try to play it without quick saving
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic re-release of an absolute cult classic of a game.  All of the features added are just great ideas that don't detract from the original experience (Though all additions can be toggled off for absolute purists), while simultaneously adding to the overall experience.  The addition of new HUDs complete with the doomguy-ish faces give the game just a touch more character.  The addition of alternate versions of enemies is a wonderful restoration of a scrapped feature that adds a subtle change to a game that I'm very familiar with.  I also especially like the addition of the option for alternate sounds to replace the original, somewhat anemic sounds for the bullet weapons and other various noises in the game.All in all, this was obviously a VERY loving remake for a game that is already much beloved by a large portion of the boomshoot fanbase.  Tom Hall's baby is very well taken care of.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: If you're the target audience for this (someone who played ROTT back in the day and wants to play it again with modern convenience), I can't recommend this enough. It's everything you would ever want from an official modern port, including upscaled resolution, mouse look, various HUD options, and multiple soundtrack options. They clearly wanted to make the definitive version of the game and it shows.Only criticism I have is that the online multiplayer kind of sucks ass. Maybe it's better in a LAN situation, but the internet-driven online multiplayer is extremely choppy and laggy and feels very half-baked.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played this edition for very long, but I have played quite a bit of RoTT through the ROTTEXPR source port. Finally, this fun ass game is actually playable and enjoyable through an official channel. And yes, this is a fun ass game, one of the greatest (in my opinion) shooters from the 90s. It had more character than Doom, was more fun than Quake, and more ludicrous than Duke Nukem.Just...buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Finally after many years of getting postphoned an acceptable sourceport for Rise of the Triad has gone gold.Its all one could hope for and then some, but right now it comes with a few caveats:1. Sound Volume problems.Music, enemy, weapon and trap sounds constantly change volume. Example: Opening a door while activated traps around you are going off will make enemie wake up sounds make almost unhearable.When no weapon is fired the music gets louder without a reason only to turn down as soon as weapons are fired. Its kind of distracting and the devs are already aware of the problem.2.Occasional Sound stutters when "midi" music is selected. 3. No highscore table.The original game had local highscore tables. Considering that rott is an arcady game with a life system and collectibles awarding points, thats a disappointing ommision and a baffling oversight.4. Maps have been changed.The original had some almost unsolvable map riddles. (The pushable stone pillar on the "Ride Em Cowboys" map comes to mind.) This sourceport went above and beyond and changed those dead ends and hard to grasp puzzles to make them easier.Part of a sourceports duty is it to preserve the original game while still making it accessible on modern machines. So i hate that quite a bit as it changes the original experience considerably. 5. Netcode seems to be pretty awful.A small wonder that the game even supports all the multiplayer modes. Still, right now playing Comm-Bat games is a subpar experience with lag spike even on low ping matches.6. Shroom Mode Eco effects are missing7.Remote Ridicule sounds are missingDespite all of that the game gets a recommendation. The devs put a lot of work into it and went the extra mile to make it as close to the originally intended experience as it could be.There is even a full fledged map/campaign editor and a completely NEW campaign with its own story and "cinematics".After a few patches this may very well be the best oldschool shooter remake to date.Thanks Nightdive, you guys are awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a classic for a reason. It has a pace of play that's very rare these days and level design that stands out even after all these years. The graphics definitely benefit from being viewed through nostalgia's rose coloured glasses but the original midi soundtrack still kicks ass.Movement is excellent, as fast as the gameplay is you're always in perfect control without the inertia and momentum that modern games use to give a feeling of weight which makes zooming around levels blasting bad guys and searching for secrets feel effortless, your character reacts as fast as you think. It all comes together to form a game that is just good plain fun and still very much worth playing today.Nightdive and New Blood have done a great job of updating the game while staying true to the original, integrating their work in a way that lets you choose what parts of the game you'd like to experience as they were originally and which parts you'd like experience in an updated form. Even the updated stuff like the new HUD options also integrate so well you'd never know they weren't part of the game originally while making the game current enough for a modern audience. One of the few examples of an update to a classic game done right.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: The DEFINITIVE way to experience Rise of the Triad. Loaded to the gills with features and extra content. If you've ever been curious about ROTT this is the place to go. The amount of love and attention paid by the devs really shows their love for this flawed(but still extremely fun) cult classic FPS. If you consider yourself a fan of boomer shooters you have no excuse to give this a go. I'll bury you in a lunchbox if you don't.
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: A classic returns! Runs amazing has the full suite of customization options, and excellent controller support if difficulty using a keyboard has ever made you hesitant to play this classic then there's nothing stopping you now! Also there have been some balance adjustments that have made the later levels and Extreme ROTT much more enjoyable. I've been waiting for this for a long time and it was absolutely worth it, one of my favorite oldschool shooters is back and better than ever!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I loved as a poor kid that had the shareware version of ROTT back in the 90's, now in 4K! I still remember the "buy this game!" screen at the end advertising Dog Mode in ROTT95 (RIP Loki!). Game is just as good as I remember it, but now I can see the baddies much further away, which makes plinking them off with the MP40 much easier. I'm so happy this game had enough support to get picked up, and the devs responsible for this remaster did a fantastic job. Day-of-release is usually spotty in multiplayer, so there was some map clipping and lag here and there. Nothing that a patch can't fix as we get some play under our belts.Strongly recommend picking this bad boy up!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Dave Oshry & Stephen Kick have done it again!This is a remaster/re-release/collection of "Rise of the Triad" one of the OG so called "boomer shooters" that was left in the dirt for some reason. The game is full packed of absurdity and the whole thing feels like some sort of bad trip to play, but it's fantastic in general.You only have a couple of weapons, mainly two pistols, an mp40 which gives you a headache after using it for a while, and a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocket launchers that can take you out in one hit if you're not careful.This superb edition includes, widescreen resolutions, high fps options, a new and extra juicy episode, and all the previously released ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ content!This is the big one, the motherload, come and get some!
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: It shows that the ROTT Ludicrous edition is the work of passionate developers who must love the Rise of the Triad. Attention to detail in this remaster is amazing! That's the best treatment this classic could ever get. Apogee, Nightdive, and New Blood never disappoint!If you are a fan, grab it immediately, ROTT can't get any better than this ultimate version. If not, check out the demo to see what you're missing out and buy it after 😉
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: Ludicrous Gibs!It's great to be back and the inclusion of Return of the Triad and a new level editor is the icing on the cakeThe choice of several soundtracks is also a nice touchI did have to cap the FPS at 60 or it runs at crazy speed - even walking and I was going into trapsBut highly recommended - it's like it's 1994 all over again and in this case, that's a good thing
_childDocuments_.name: Rise of the Triad: Ludicrous Edition

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most addictive shooters i ever played. The gunplay feels great and the pase of the game is awesome.Lots of secrets, lots of enemies, fat monks and great level bosses.10/10 so happy i can play it again without dosbox or crappy ports.I subtracted one point because not all original multiplayer modes are in (ie tag and a few more)But overall, if you liked it in the past you will enjoy it now. I you never played it, give it a try.Edit: I added a point because they mentioned new gamemodes will be available soon(tm)

_childDocuments_.review: The HUNT Returns... AGAIN! Play the original Cult Classic '90s FPS remastered in 4K Ultrawide with UNLIMITED frame rates, restored content, NEW episodes, a level editor, cross-platform multiplayer, additional music, new options and MORE. Make 'em EAT LEAD or they'll bury you in a lunchbox!

name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective
detailed_description: Join our Discord About the Game From the award-winning studio behind Homo Machina (2018) and Californium (2016), Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is another one-of-a-kind revolutionary puzzle. Fun, engaging, and beautiful, Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective lets you explore the visually stunning universe created by IC4DESIGN Playing as detective Pierre, you must find your way and solve puzzles to retrieve the magical stone stolen by the nefarious Mr. X. On your way to getting the Maze Stone back, you will meet adorable and hilarious characters, travelling literal works of art, and interact with a world that was previously only available on paper! Storyline A terrible crime has been committed at the Opera City Museum! Mr. X, Pierre's sworn enemy, has stolen and fled with the Maze Stone, a magical artefact that turns everything around it into a labyrinth. Under the call of the Opera City Museum, Pierre must undertake a new adventure that will lead him from the museum, to the city streets, to a castle in the sky, a haunted mansion and much more! There is no time to lose, lest the whole world turns into a maze! Game Features Enter colorful worlds teeming with life and intricate details based on the best-selling children’s book series Pierre the Maze Detective by IC4DESIGN More than 100 hidden objects and unique trophies to find, engaging puzzles and minigames to stimulate your brain Over 500 interactions possible with the characters, items, and background Original soundtrack Each scene is based on a double-page illustration from the original work All levels are tied together by an overarching narration that will fill the detectives within us with purpose Available in Chinese (simplified and traditional), English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Spanish and Russian Introduction of Darjeeling Darjeeling is a multimedia studio based in Paris, France. Its founders, Marc Lustigman and Noam Roubah, established the studio in 2009, focusing on documentary production, animation for television, and video games. The studio first became recognized through the 2016 video game Californium . Its other notable milestones include Homo Machina in 2018, which won the Best Mobile Game award at Game Connection America and the Ping Awards. Introduction of IC4DESIGN Studio (creator of Pierre the Maze Detective ) IC4DESIGN, creator of the Pierre the Maze Detective franchise, is an illustration studio based in Hiroshima (Japan) which was established by Hirofumi Kamigaki in March 1998. Thanks to their unique style, associating intricate worlds and scenes to colorful visuals, they have won many awards such as Bronze for Cannes Lion 2017 and D&AD 2017 wood pencil.

short_description: Adapted from the bestselling children’s book series Pierre The Maze Detective, play as Pierre in this adventure/puzzle game and recover the stolen Maze Stone. Journey through breathtakingly hand-drawn illustrations, meet eccentric characters, and solve puzzles to save Opera City!

_childDocuments_.review: I dislike Hidden Objects games, and I despise mazes for being the cheapest form of puzzles.That's why I'm currently erecting a statue to honour the people who took these two ingredients and concocted a great game out of them.Talent and effort combined into extremely attractive level design, full of little things and movements and interactions. Always something to look at, and the beauty of it all, of course.Each maze has a theme, with some variation in the use of space and sometimes in mechanics.Not to forget the music, terrific as well.Impeccable gamepad interface.Unchallenging - it's a maze at the core, plus it's generous on visual hints - yet highly entertaining.It's a bliss for all ages.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Mr. X has stolen the rare and valuable maze stone from the city museum and fled with it. The artefact has magical powers and can mysteriously transform everything around it into a labyrinth.Pierre, and his friend Carmen, has been hired to track down Mr. X, his arch enemy and nemesis, and bring the stone back to safety before the whole world turns into a maze. Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is adapted from the bestselling children’s book series and based on “The Search for the Stolen Maze Stone”. It is a path finder game where you have to direct Pierre through a devious maze full of surprises, in pursuit of the evil Mr. X. It is just so much fun. It constantly entertains and surprises, and I was chuckling continually throughout the whole game.The developers have created a very well-balanced game and a faithful representation of the books, with scenes and mazes brought to life and transferred to screen straight from the publications.Opera City, where the game is set, is incredibly vibrant with so many interesting things happening wherever you look. I just wanted to investigate everything, and if you do you will be rewarded. I thought the humor was very reminiscent of The Lego games. Not one joke fell flat, and I couldn’t wait to interact with people and objects just to see what would happen. The hand drawn art looks incredible with its colorful environments and lively characters performing all manner of shenanigans. The sound effects and music inject further atmosphere into the game with its jaunty tunes, crowd reaction noises and special effect sounds. The cut scenes after every maze are so entertaining and outrageous, with an overzealous narrator hamming it up beautifully. It is just wonderful, and keeps that high intensity fun moving by linking the story and the mazes together. It never feels like you are just trying to escape a maze, rather you are on a continual hunt through ten environments within the city. The mazes are well designed and can be quite challenging if you want to bag all of the collectibles.If you enjoy hidden object games and achievement hunting, this game will be a perfect fit. Missed achievements can be mopped up after the game with a level select which keeps your progress.I think it is an exaggeration to describe this as a puzzle game. There are very light puzzle elements but they are quite scarce and rather repetitive. Don’t buy the game if you are after a challenging puzzle experience. The mazes are cleverly designed with so many nice touches scattered throughout. Finding Mr X on each maze isn’t difficult but it’s not easy either, especially if you want to gather all the objects.Labyrinth City is a pathfinder and object locator game with some very light puzzle elements. There is no specific detective work involved. This is not a detective game. There are also hardly any puzzles. This is not a puzzle game either. It is wholly a comical maze game.You direct Pierre through a maze of ladders, paths, platforms and buildings on the hunt for various characters who will ultimately direct you to the thief’s whereabouts.There are lots of collectibles to find in each maze including four chests, three stars and four pages of Mr. X’s notebook. There is also a special prize awarded for finding and completing a mini game or puzzle. Chests and stars are concealed throughout the maze, usually in bizarre spots, and the pages can be hidden almost anywhere, including inside objects or delivered by the mailman, if you can find him.The mini games and puzzles are very easy to complete. The challenge is in finding them. They are certainly not designed to test your mental attributes but are usually very amusing to participate in.Whilst chasing his illusive arch enemy, Pierre will travel through ten hand drawn mazes full of bustling scenes of everyday life containing different characters and objects.A lot of these characters and objects can be interacted with, resulting in hilarious outcomes. There are a ton of Easter eggs and references to popular culture.Some of these characters will aid you on your quest. For example, finding a wizard will magically reveal a directional arrow to help you navigate, and other objects may divulge useful information also.There are usually four of five characters to find in each maze before you catch up with Mr. X. After finding each character, the maze may change slightly, blocking certain paths but opening others. Certain characters will block your path on purpose and force you into taking detours, whilst other times these same characters will let you pass in one direction but not the other.Occasionally, there are timed puzzles where you press buttons or switches to open up an entrance and have to find a path through before the time lapses and the opening closes.Pierre can enter some buildings and passageways which might relocate him in some unexpected places, usually the location of stars or chests. At the end of each maze, when you catch up to Mr. X, a cut scene is initiated which takes you into the next maze.There are forty-one achievements to obtain and they are all meaningful and very enjoyable to chase. The game should take around nine or ten hours to complete to one hundred percent.I loved the colourful hand drawn artwork. It looks amazing, and characters are surprisingly well animated and drawn for their size. The backgrounds and the mazes look attractive and the characters within them are always high spirited. Cut scenes are bursting with energy and drama. They’re so much fun to watch.The music is so addictively charming and upbeat. It doesn’t over burden gameplay. It just plays merrily along in the background whilst you tap your foot. The special effects noises are superb and add an extra dimension to proceedings, and the voice acting in the cut scenes is delightfully tongue in cheek and exaggerated.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderfully creative game. Feels like a spiritual successor to 'Where's Wally'/(Where's Waldo) book series with how intricate and vivid the details of each of the levels are. Turns out this game is based on its own book series by Hiro Kamigaki and I'm sad to discover that only one of the books is currently available within my local library services. I personally found the 'maze' aspect of  to be very simplified and a little bit linear. Sometimes the paths were deceptive but on the whole not very difficult at all but the creators have done an excellent job of making you want to explore every nook and cranny of the maps for they are filled to the brim with interactable objects, easter eggs, secrets and collectables. There's only a couple of things that I didn't like about the game: firstly - the voice acting in the cutscenes; secondly - controls were a bit wonky sometimes especially with keyboard. Both of these are fairly negligible though. Still worth grabbing if you want a 'sit back and relax' experience. I also want to mention that I loved the soundtrack, it was fun and added to the adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I guess I didn't watch enough gameplay videos before buying but I also forgot that steam reviewers are liars and make non-sensical comparisonsThe game is not like "where's waldo" except maybe in the art style. I was under the impression that this was like a more interactive version of "where's waldo" where you can click and interactive with lots of things on a large hand drawn scene. Sounded awesome in my mind.but it's not like Where's Waldo. It's a 2d walking sim. You directly control a character that you move around on a linear path. You cannot stray from the predetermined path. It's completely on rails, though sometimes you can go left or right (and usually one of the two options leads to a dead end so you have to go back the other way eventually). Then periodically an icon will popup on your screen indicating that you can interact with something nearby. You cannot interact with anything that doesn't have an icon, and you cannot turn the icon popups off in order to explore the area on your own. There is basically no exploration factor whatsoever because of how guided you are in this game, which is why this game is nothing like "where's waldo"There's some light puzzling but nothing innovative and there's some kind of story but I couldn't play enough to find out if it's good because the gameplay was boring. I can't imagine doing this for multiple hours till it's finished. As for the "maze" part. I didn't really get any feeling that I was walking through a maze. It's not like there's that many directions to go and since we're on a linear path on fairly small maps, it's not hard to deduce your way to the end by just going in any direction until you hit a dead end or find the exit. Also some paths won't even open up until you've triggered some event, so you are kind of forced into traversing the "maze" in a certain way no matter what. Failure is not really possible.The art is great, but I can't recommend this as a video game.If this dev makes a digital "where's waldo" game with this art, I'd buy it in a heart beat.

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this game - every map of the Labyrinth City is unique, cute, colorful, and rich.This is not a typical hidden object game, you are not expected to find anything hidden. Labyrinth City has lots of replay values as there are many to see and to click, you tend to miss something in the first walkthrough.I also love the quotes, made the game even better. For this price, I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s difficult to describe  simply because it’s a masterpiece and games like that should be experienced personally rather than read about. Each scene from  is a rich and colourful world in itself, vibrant and full of energy, a children’s book gorgeously made alive by the talented developers and graphic designers of .At its core,  is a collection of 10 levels, each of them representing a maze. You take the role of the detective Pierre and together with your sidekick Carmen, you chase after Mister X who stole an important artifact that can create these mazes of people, and who uses it in an attempt to slow you down and escape from your grasp. The corridors and paths exist among crowds of people but the arrangement seems so natural, that you’d find yourself often wondering if you can pass through a group of characters or not. The game thus turns into an exploration adventure, in which you try to reach every corner possible. To keep things entertaining, there are dialogues with various characters, sometimes puzzles, and a lot of interactive objects. Pretty much like in Where’s Waldo games, almost everything is alive and reacts to your clicks, and it’s pure joy to trigger all these responses.Since ’s gameplay relies heavily on exploration, collectibles are a must. Each level has 10-11 collectibles of different types. These are usually laid out on the not-so-obvious paths, but most often easily visible from afar (though not as easily reachable). Aside from this, there are several recurring characters that you’ll have to find, and many many Easter eggs. Achievements are rewarded not only for finding all collectibles or special people / completing all levels, but also for interacting with some specific objects in the game world.The levels are split into 5-7 stages each and there are NPCs that guide you on the right path, either by showing you the correct direction to go, or giving you the next objective - reaching a specific area / NPC. There is no map available though, no top-view and no hints, so you’ll have to base yourself on your sense of direction and on remembering where you already went. The levels often have multiple floors and the mazes are not placed only horizontally, but also vertically. Reaching a top level can also mean taking a longer path by going in some other area first. Thus there’s a strong escher-esque component to the level design, with contorted paths, stairs, or even access ways hidden behind buildings.Each of these levels is truly a work of art, not only in how the paths are designed, but also in how elaborately they are conceived. There are likely hundreds of individual characters per level, each of them having unique animations, positions, clothing and other details. They all move independently of each other, have different personalities etc. It’s a miniature world laid down at your feet, waiting for you to discover all its secrets.Because of the sheer amount of meticulous work put into creating such an intricate universe, I strongly feel that  is totally worth the price. Mazes can get frustrating sometimes, but not in  - it’s a very fun and relaxed game but also versatile: you can enjoy it alone as well as with your family / children. Feel free to also check out the illustrated children’s book that the game is based on, Hiro Kamigaki’s “Pierre the Maze Detective: The Search for the Stolen Maze Stone”.

I never can understand why developers want to add timed stuff to games such as this one;  up until that point, a perfectly relaxing and charming puzzle game. Still I heartily recommend it , it was a lot of fun and I am sure that there are many players who enjoy a certain amount of pressure in their game play. I am hoping that, in future builds they allow Pierre to take an alternate route, if one so desires....

Probably not... maybe my perfectionism is the problem, but introducing punishing elements into a simple search game? No, thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: ------------------: Requires Glorious Eggrolls Proton-6.5-GE-2. Details on ProtonDB website------------------Darjeeling’s Labyrinth City is a maze puzzle game based on Hiro Kamigaki’s work . It is a colorful and greatly stylized beautiful moving artwork with moderately challenging mazes, imaginative world building, creative level design, whimsical soundtrack as well as quirky and charming characters.Though it will primarily appeal to a niche audience, Labyrinth City have enough here to be a great fun for the family as well as being adequately suitable for adults. If you’re a fan of Pierre the Maze Detective, this is probably a must buy. If you’re a puzzle player, this is worth your consideration. Recommended. ----------------------------------------First and foremost, the . I think fans of the book will have no complaints with how the graphics turned out as it seems pretty faithful to the source material. Complete with detailed moving artwork, the world of Pierre the Maze Detective feels alive and breathing with 9 distinct settings from the modern to the medieval. It is vibrant and wonderfully absurd; beckoning you to explore it and there is much to explore and discover. The voice-acting (in English) is also very good and the  by Xavier Thiry perfectly captures the mood and tone of the game. The team plays around with the sound design and sound stage, having the music quiet and aloud depending on where you are on the map. ----------------------------------------The , for example, the Haunted Manor has a shifting maze mechanic while the Black Market has a timed mechanic. Unfortunately, you can only do so much with a puzzle game but what Darjeeling came up with is satisfactory. The Polar Bear mini game is a nice addition albeit, it is very very mini game. The collectibles are also well hidden and are fun to search for.The story too while being overtly simple and perhaps too generic, suffices to move the story forward and keep you engage. However, for me the star of the show are the charming and quirky characters that you’ll encounter along the way. Gmlf the Wizard, Coco the Adventurer, even the main villain Mr. X are all memorable. ----------------------------------------As I stated earlier, this is a , it will not appeal to everyone. Admittedly, Labyrinth City is  (), with your playtime consists of running all over the map finding the next clue, the next collectible or the end goal. Some stages are very large and very long (i.e. the Medieval Village) that requires you to run all over and . Thankfully, this is the only Extra Large and most of the others are adequately sized. The , it will take quite getting use to especially when you want to enter/exit a pathway, (the game can be played with a joypad/controller). Overall though, if you’re going to make a walking simulator, this is one excellent way to do it. And if you’re going to play a walking simulator, this is probably the game to play.----------------------------------------If you want something wholesome for yourself or for you kids, I highly recommend .

_childDocuments_.review: Who doesn't wish their maze books to be interactive? Well, this video game will make your dream come true: it is an adaptation of a children's book of mazes called Pierre the Maze Detective: The Search for the Stolen Maze Stone.There are 10 levels, each one consists of a giant maze which is beautifully illustrated and full of interactables (à la Hidden Folks, which, by the way, is also a great family-friendly hidden object game). For each level, your goal, naturally, is to navigate through mazes. Your optional objective, however, is to find all the collectibles and to talk to various NPCs, some are recurrent while others are just passers-by.The game is relaxing and enjoyable to play since:None of the mazes is difficult due to the fact that there are signposts everywhere guiding you to the right track, and that most dead ends are immediately recognisable;On those more length and winding paths leading to a dead end, most frequently an intractable (usually a collectible) awaits, awarding your effort.The mazes have tons of visual details (and Easter eggs) to admire, which gives you a visceral urge of curiosity to thoroughly explore them.The soundtrack is outstanding and always fits nicely to the scenes.Missing collectibles is no big deal, since you can reload a finished chapter and play it again. Once you know the drill, getting through a maze only takes several minutes.My only regret is that the dialogues in mazes are not voiced. Being an indie studio, they probably did not have the wherewithal for a full voice-over, but they could at least do it for the NPC who sings a few verses about the story in every level.One final remark is that the game used to have many bugged achievements. The devs have probably fixed them, since I have 100% completed the game without a hitch. I suppose completionists should not worry too much when they see other reviews mentioning this issue.In short, I highly recommend Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective to casual gamers and those who love mazes or hidden object games. Just one little caveat: this is a slow-paced and immersive game that needs you to take your time to savour instead of rushing through. If you are looking for varied gameplay or challenges, you should be warned that there is none here.I really hope the devs would consider sequels that adapt other titles of the book series of Pierre the Maze Detective!

_childDocuments_.review: With this game, you seem to be returning to a carefree childhood, when the sun was shining brighter and surprises were more unexpected and joyful. Exciting adventures in pursuit of the elusive bully Mister X sweep before your eyes like an extravaganza of colors, and the fearlessness of the main characters - detective Pierre and his companion Carmen helps them break through any obstacles. The plot for the whole family is naive in the right sense, creating the atmosphere of a wonderful adventure fairy tale in which you open the main role. The illustrations are simply amazing, everything in the game is so alive that you literally want to touch it, each location is filled with some prohibitive amount of details. And this is what makes the passage of the labyrinths so exciting, because even when you stray from the route, you can always stumble upon some kind of surprise, unexpected companion or hidden treasure, the level of detail here is crazy. Locations are presented for a wide variety of tastes; here is Dracula's castle, an oriental bazaar, a museum, and much more. For those who like to explore, this game is like the Holy Grail, it constantly surprises you without resorting to speculative methods. The humor is very kind and positive; it is fun to interact with all the characters (even when this bully sailor does not allow you to go up the stairs, which you REALLY need to cross!). An incredibly kind thing that causes pure delight, now I want new games from this series to appear and faster.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the main point I'd like to hammer home with this review is not so much that the game was bad in and of itself, but rather you should ease your expectations with this game.I expected this game to be similar to "Where's my Wally" where the objective was to look for a well-hidden character or series of characters within an overcrowded landscape filled with characters and to a degree I did get that experience. However, this game felt less like I'm searching for a specific character within this amazing world and instead following a waymarker to their destination. It feels hollow to play and it's a bit of a shame that this was what I felt because everything else in this game is absolutely amazing. The beautiful hand-drawn worlds this game boasts is absolutely phenomenal, down to every minute detail, you could tell that the artists put in everything they can to show off a wonderful world. The music was good too! It's not the best soundtrack, but it's so fun to just listen to while going around the world. All in all, I think this game really just wasn't I expected and I urge everyone to truly see others get to play this before purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand that the charm of the design of this game is alluring, but the gameplay is dreadful.  From poorly behaved isometric navigation to calling random wandering a maze game, I just think this exercise in tedium had a lot of potential and disappointing execution.  Achievement hunters will find aspects of the experience maddening.  Casual and hardcore gamers alike will find many choices in the *gameplay* to be onerous.  Again, the design is lovely, but this is meant to be a game with challenges, not irritating ways to waste your time.  I think some developers conflate wasting your time with adding time to gameplay value.  Spending all day chasing down collectibles with dubious guidance or explanation of why I'm doing it is not engagement.OCD parts of me will likely make me try again and again, but I wrote this review to spare those of you who cannot walk away from a frustrating experience once it has begun.  For everyone else, YMMV.

_childDocuments_.review: caught my attention because its art reminded me of the  (also known as  in North America) series of puzzle books that I grew up reading. Little did I know at the time that the game was based on , the first puzzle book of a series by Hiro Kamigaki and his illustration team at IC4DESIGN.Franco-Belgian bandes dessinées and ligne claire art style were obvious influences on the aesthetics of . The original hand drawn art was faithfully recreated for  by developers, Darjeeling. This is fantastic given how beautifully and intricately drawn the mazes were. In fact, I later learned that the mazes for this game were pretty much lifted straight from the pages of . It appears that  tries to replicate the maze-solving experience that the book offers. It’s a shame that at least a couple of mazes from the book were left out, likely due to resource constraints and/or keeping them exclusive to the print medium. In spite of their omission,  is still a substantial game and very enjoyable. It took me about 8 hours to solve the 10 mazes, plus additional 2 hours or so to locate missed collectables and to hunt down remaining achievements.The mazes are detailed, grand, and amazing (pun intended) to behold. They get more sophisticated as the game progresses, with the final maze clearly inspired by M.C. Escher’s . To make the locales more vibrant, Darjeeling added animations to people and creatures that populate the mazes, along with objects you can interact with. To further differentiate itself from its printed counterpart, the game also has moving obstacles and timed puzzles.The game doesn’t punish you for straying from the intended path. In fact, you’re encouraged to explore the many nooks and crannies. As rewards for your curiosity, you’ll come across interesting characters, treasures, notes, pop and geek culture references, as well as complementary puzzles. I wish I can jump into the game and explore the wondrous locations from first person perspective. is wholesome and simply joyful. Because there is only one solution to each maze, this game sadly has little replayability, especially if you’ve also found all collectables. However, I can see myself returning to it at some point should I want something relaxing to play. With at least two other books to inspire them or draw materials from, let’s hope Darjeeling will make a sequel because I just can’t get enough of .

_childDocuments_.review: Labyrinth City is absolutely charming, a children's book come to life, and just as fun to play. The look might create the impression that it's just for children -- it's not. It's for the child-like, including gamers wanting a refreshing change of pace. The animations are tip-top and often made us laugh out loud. It's joy on the screen and highly recommended. My only request of the developers: I want to let my wife and others I know play from the beginning with everything in place. Please either allow for individual save profiles or include an "Erase Progress" option so that new players can play fresh from the beginning and be able to find all the stars, notebook pages, and treasure chests where they are at the start. As it is, any of those already collected by a player stay permanently collected. Thanks for such a wonderful game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the digitalization of the book 'Pierre the Maze Detective: The Search for the Stolen Maze Stone' of IC4DESIGN team spearheaded by Hirofumi Kamigaki in 2015. The visuals are stunning, they are not cheaply done. You often see visual distinctions between static and moving parts in these type of games because of the lowres source image not properly redone, but that is not the case in this game. every art looks crispy and not a single one of it stands out. And the way it structured is also amazing, every stage is a prime example of clever usage of space, filled with details and references and at the same time it really do feel like a maze. In one sentence, an absolutely phenomenal work that deserves more attention. it's a shame this rework project seemingly ended as a one time only work because there are two more books in the same series now in 2024.They just sold 3 more books and and whenever they arrive they will reside in a spot besides my old Walter Wick and Where's Waldo books. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just... Awesome.I'm only on the 4th level, taking my time, but I had to stop and write this review. It's visuals are charming, the voice acting and animation is on point, and the music and sound effects are beautiful.My one major reservation going in was the possibility of getting eyestrain (thinking it was some kind of "Where's Wally/Waldo" type find-the-hidden-object game), but its mechanics avert this and it's all just so wonderfully done. _childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Such a charming game! Basically you just walk everywhere you can to master the labyrinths. But the graphic detail is amazing and there are many spots you can interact for small animations. I had a relaxing time and let myself get lost in all those details. Easy game, it can also be played by/with little children as the storytelling suggests. All in all if you like mazes and those detail books this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I used to love the Where's Wally books and always wanted to explore and interact with those dense scenes filled with interesting characters and oddities. Now with this game I finally can, based on a book series that clearly takes inspiration from the aforementioned series. I loved soaking in the incredible art and endless creativity on offer.The game is simple - find your ways to various points on the maze like maps while interacting with people and objects, and finding the way to various collectables. There's also the odd minigame here and there. Gameplay is limited, but just enough to be engaging.I'll give a special mention to the soundtrack which is incredible, and changes (sometimes subtly) depending on where you venture on the map. You're enjoying a chill background tune, then drums fade in as you approach the marching band and then you're greeted with a full jazz number complete with horns and cymbals.As an interactive game, this is decent enough. As an audiovisual experience it's phenomenal.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Labyrinth City is an unexpected gem of an adventure/maze/hidden object (technically, I think?) game. The settings are nice to look at, the characters are charming, there are hidden Easter eggs throughout the game, the music is enjoyable, and the length of the game (~5 hours to complete, and another ~1.5 hours to get the achievements I missed along the way) feels appropriate for the price. If I had to describe the game in one word it would be "fun". The only real negatives are the storyline basically exists to get you to go from point A to point B without the game straight up telling you, "Go from point A to point B" and the isometric view can sometimes feel a bit finicky (there were a handful of times where I thought I was stuck when I wasn't because there was an area that didn't look like I could pass through but then it turned out the angle was a little off and I actually could). I think this is a solid pick if you want to feel some nostalgia for the books you might have enjoyed as a kid, or you're generally a fan of this genre of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming and beautifully designed/drawn. The mazes themselves are well crafted, not challenging per say, but enough "difficulty" that the simplicity of the type of puzzle you're playing, does not detract in any way from the experience. Thematically each level, and even parts of levels, feel distinctive and unique from one another.  The world of Labyrinth City feels genuinely lived in and has so much character, you can't help but smiling the entire time. The comedy is for the most part age appropriate, but I could imagine if I played this as a child there would be a good chunk of jokes that I would have missed; but I don't think that would have had any deterrence from the experience, as there are so many things going on, on screen, at any given moment, that I would have been giggling constantly. In fact, I was just giggling constantly as an adult.It does what it sets out to do perfectly. Can't wait to play Labyrinth City 2! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this game filled a need I did not know I had. I didn't know this Pierre dude existed, I didn't know about the books, I didn't know about hidden objects/mazes. Now I need more, please devs! Do the other books too!You basically go around these huuuuuuuge, intricate and colorful levels, each with hundreds upon hundreds of paths and characters and things to interact with. The main goal is to find a few main characters in each leveI, but the fun is all in exploring every single path trying to find as many details, collectibles and achievements as possible. I love that there arrows that point you towards the main objective, since I could use them to figure which path was NOT the right one to advance the level. The soundtrack is also awesome, making it a real pleasure to just leisurely go through the mazes taking your time and taking in the scenario.A thing that I would have appreciated as a bonus content, is full sized images of the whole mazes, since we never get a full shot of them even while playing them.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★★★★☆☆ 8/10 Past a certain point, the whole maze thing and the story feels meaningless and prolonged “just because”, but the beautiful artwork and unique cheerful mood are enough to keep you in the game. Which also means for certain people, those aren’t enough to stick till the end. That explains the 24.5% clear ratio at the time of this review.+) Beautiful and mesmerizing artwork.+) Uniquely cheerful mood.+) Background music is very apt with the game.+) One can definitely feel how the studio focused on blending these 3 elements in the game. +) No bugs and no crashes, as all games should. Something AAA games should care more about these days. -) Controller dependable. You can still navigate with keyboard and mouse since it’s only maze but you will definitely want to use a controller instead. I almost unpacked mine. -) This one mini-puzzle (Not mini-games) contradicts two elements in the game, which are listening to npcs, and seeing what happens when you interact with certain objects. -) Should there be a sequel, will I play again? NO. The way they prolonged the campaign, how they handled the gameplay progress was an insult to their own masterpiece level artwork and music.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Okay hands down best game of this type I've ever played.The movie/TV show/historical/general life references were amazing. The artwork is beyond amazing. The story line is actually interesting and definitely makes you want to get all the achievements. The puzzles themselves were difficult enough to not become frustrating but also not too easy and boring. Please please please make more of these cause I'd buy the ♥♥♥♥ outta them ♥ 100% deserved those awards too
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Mazes in games are ; nobody likes them. In first person, they require tedious mapping. In third person with doors/teleporters/etc., ditto. In third person without such... why not just buy a book of mazes?Where's Waldo/Wally-like games, while not universally reviled, are difficult to pull off - you need to have features beyond just what a book would have.But together, these make for a magical experience. Every maze is full of life and surprises - like a Living Books or Humongous Entertainment game. And the actual main gameplay being extremely easy (thanks to plentiful purple arrows) actually works well, because it's not the point - the point is to mentally keep track of the topography of the maze as you desperately scour every last part of it for optional secrets.And as for the style and aesthetics of the game, it's incredibly charming. It captures important elements of French comics - it's filled with simple humor, yet at the same time oozes personality from every pore. The whole thing is an absolute delight.An aside about the voice acting: it's cheesy as heck, but that actually works in this game's favor. It evokes a sense of childlike wonder, like it's a book being read to you by an older sister who does all the voices. "'Zut alors!' shouts Carmen. Mr. X simply throws back his head and laughs. 'Ha ha ha haaaaa!'"
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I quickly realized that this was probably based on a series of picture books with maze puzzles for small children. Google confirmed that my suspicion was correct. How I managed to figure this out was for two reasons:1. The presentation is decidedly appropriate for all ages.2. It truly is illustrations of mazes that you walk around in.Despite the graphics being charming I cannot recommend it. For anyone old enough to be looking for a challenge this does not deliver. The books have a recommended age rating of 3-6 which feels appropriate for this digital adaptation as well. For anyone in the aforementioned age bracket I suspect the original books will be a more rewarding experience. As is, you never get any big overview over the mazes, it is always zoomed in. That has two effects: 1. You never get a nice overview to admire the full illustrations. 2. As a player you have no ability to plan out a route. That felt restrictive, and turned the challenge into a trial-and-error affair.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a full review and some gameplay here:  This game was very interesting for me. While, truthfully, I don't know that I've heard much of Pierre the Maze Detective before this, it does seem to be based on a rather delightful book. It's kind of like an interactive Where's Waldo, except all the Waldos are unique original characters. This goes beyond your mere hidden object game--this is art. The way so many things are illustrated, animated, and interactive really offers a lot of  entertainment. I recommend playing it that way too. You can complete the mazes quickly, but there are lots of achievements that tell the story. The humor is witty and wholesome, and the game is such a wonderful experience. Plenty to see here and the price is correct for the amount of content. Very family friendly too without being simple. It is good.

_childDocuments_.review: A charming puzzle game with the most delightful artwork. The soundtrack is pleasant without being distracting, there are lots of hidden cultural references and plenty of achievements for trophy hunters. The puzzles aren't super challenging to get to the end of the level, but finding all the extras takes a bit more thought.
