_childDocuments_.review: From the screenshots, it’s easy to think that Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is a Where’s Wally\Waldo?-type of game, like Hidden Folks. That’s what I thought at first too. But while wonderfully detailed screens, full of charming characters and fun interactions, are indeed present, the game plays quite differently. This is, as the name would suggest, a maze game, where you must figure out how to get from one point to the next. And it’s quite fun, even though it has some frustrating elements to it.This game is, from what I could gather, a mostly accurate adaptation of the first book in the series of Pierre the Maze Detective adventures. Books that I’ve not encountered before, but after playing this game, I’m genuinely interested in getting them. The story is relatively simplistic, with a classic masked villain, and while it exists solely to get Pierre into more and more wild and exciting adventures, there are lots of fun charismatic characters to encounter along the way. In this regard, it’s kinda like Professor Layton titles, except the story doesn’t even attempt to take itself too seriously and focuses on just being fun and evoking the feeling of adventure.How does it play, though? Well, the levels are gigantic detailed screens and the architecture, the position of some props and characters on the screen, make up for the “walls” of the “maze” that you must navigate. You rarely get depth of movement on a stretches of the “maze”, instead just being able to go in a straight line. Kinda reminiscent of something like killer7, or if Hitman/Lara Croft GO games didn’t have dots to move between. On practice, this is far from ideal, as any controls you decide to use feel slightly awkward. Sometimes a path isn’t really a path, sometimes you need to move in an unintuitive way, sometimes the interaction prompts don’t appear until you’re in some very specific spot. It’s never extremely frustrating, but at the same time does feel like having some sort of guidelines or the already mentioned dots and moving automatically between those could’ve felt better. But then again, exploring some less obvious paths and finding secrets would’ve been less fun this way, I suppose.It’s also a bit of a shame, that the game doesn’t really have any of those Hidden Folks-like interactions – you can’t just click anywhere on screen and get a reaction and there are no elements tied to that either. Everything is done by proximity, which is perfectly acceptable for a game emulating tracing mazes with a pencil, but I can only wonder how much additional fun depth could’ve been added to the game otherwise. Oh and it’s also worth noting that at the time of me playing the game, I’ve encountered a few annoying bugs. But with the developers so quickly pushing patches, by the time you read this, they might all be fixed.Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is a very simple, but also a very charming title that I enjoyed thoroughly. It has beautiful adventure inspiring soundtrack, wonderful visuals, fun simple gameplay, lots of optional exploration and it doesn’t last too long to start getting boring. Definitely check it out if you get the chance. And I’m definitely going to see if I can find the books in the meantime.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up, I absolutely LOVED solving mazes, and this game fits that niche perfectly. Gameplay-wise, it almost feels like a combination of "Professor Layton and the Unwound Future", "Scribblenauts", "The Witness" and a Wimmelbilder piece. I absolutely LOVE this game's art style, and each environment in the game is absolutely FULL of life (the animation alone must have taken collective years), and there's so much stuff to interact with. The controls are a bit awkward, but they work pretty well.All I can say is that even if you get lost, you'll have so much fun doing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: For this game being about Labyrinths the levels are quite linear with few side paths that mostly contain optional collectibles. Your character is rather small and disappears behind object with no transparency effect to keep track of your character, worse is when you go through a door and are teleported it becomes hard at times to find where you ended up.The Games controls can be iffy in places the character sometimes walks on a very specific small path with intersections/ladders and sometimes won't move a simple up/down/left/right you need to move diagonal for it to register you want to go that direction. I like the areas more where you can more freely move they are finicky with controls.There are some mini games you can encounter but listing what the controls are for it would help greatly.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely casual game. In this game, you'll make your way through a maze by moving from one quest NPC to another. And it's a piece of cake to find an exit and Mr. X, but you'll have to use a few braincells to find a way to the collectables. There're mini-games on each level, and they're as easy as falling off a log too. The art is bright, colourful and charming. And it definitely looks like illustrations from children's books. I never had the original book myself, but I felt like I was looking at the book while playing the game. The music is pretty decent too. It gets you in an adventurous mood. There're a lot of things to interact with, NPCs to talk to, and references to discover—a ton of references to the culture. On the other hand, the story... well, it exists. The story serves only one point—to make you move from start to end, from one map to another. That's all. I can describe the whole plot in two words—pursue Mr. X. Yes, it's that simplistic. I like when games have interesting stories, I can endure much for a captivating plot. And this game took me like six hours to complete. If I weren't into its relaxing gameplay and atmosphere, I would never finish it. Anyway, the game is excellent. It's a fine addition to the collection of kind of hidden object adventure games. A calming experience to spend a few evenings and relax. But this one bugged "Unmazed" achievement is getting on my nerves.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: One word can describe this game: Charming.There is so much to take in with these extremely busy, intricate and detailed scenes.  So many sounds, noises and music it transports me back to my youth reading Highlights magazines in waiting rooms.  I am a big fan of this art style which helps to keep me enjoying  playing it.  There are various details I dont understand such as what the sheets of paper i collect are for but it hasn't hampered my progress.  I hope they make another one after this.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Pierre the Maze Detective is a series of children’s books created by Japanese artist Hirofumi Kamigaki and illustrated by IC4Design. Double spread books that paint elaborate sceneries where kids and adults try to help the titular Pierre through a number of twisting mazes. If you’re familiar with Where’s Waldo or Wally and the Professor Layton series, the Pierre books are similar in art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the where's waldo-type of illustrations, with a ton of people doing silly things, this is a fantastic game. I've only cleared the first maze, but it put a huge smile on my face from start to finish. The illustrations are already so detailed and fun, but I'm genuinely amazed by how well integrated all the animation is! Chaotic in the best way, I love it. Definitely taking the longest route in any maze.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, generally speaking.  Fun and cute, and not just intended for children, what with a great number of interactions and encounters with amusing characters and a Ripley's Believe It or Not collection of oddities.  I would compare it to the circus as an activity.  I did have a problem about four-fifths of the way through, where the way forward was literally blocked, and there was no way forward, so it was impossible to complete the game.  Trying to play the same level again led to the same situation.  It was in effect impossible to play the level after this occurred and get things right.  Would starting the game over from the beginning allow one to complete it?  Hard to know, since the replay value would probably not be great enough to follow through.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Well first off the artwork in this game is absolutely beautiful, whoever designed this really has an artistic eye, and an eye for detail, everything is bright and colorful. There are so many themes and even humorous things that happen in the levels, and every level has is its own masterpiece that same art piece is never displayed more than once, its always something new and exciting, and I was always wondering what would be next, not to mention that this game also held my attention for 8 hours straight, never once did I feel bored. Around every corner was always something new, very well done, I greatly admire your creativity.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is a cute, simple stylized game about working your way through crowded areas to find Mr. X, who is causing mischief. The main draw of this game is it's beautiful animation and graphics. It's quite impressive how huge these areas are. This definitely takes artistic inspiration from books like Where's Waldo, Amazing Cross Sections or even the Mormon equivalent books I read as a kid (yes, those exist, and they are pretty good).This is a very simple game and isn't really a maze until later games. It's very strange and quirky, but I'd say it's a great product, especially if you get it in a bundle.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. Lovely visuals, good music, simple and fun game-play. The mazes are not difficult but interesting nonetheless. Though I do think the game is slightly overpriced for the length. Maybe more levels in free DLCs later? In any case, a good and fun game. What I did  not like was the narration in between levels marking the transition from one level to another. It was annoying. I know that the game is primarily for a younger age group and they might enjoy it but still, maybe some thing else would have been nice. Rather than the lady voicing Pierre and Mr.X, maybe each could have different voice actors. No offence to her. She put the effort but I found it tiring. Also, even though the 'Flea Market' level was a fun maze, the colonial/imperialist/orientalist hangover is strong there. I realize that the game takes influences from Indiana Jones, Tintin etc. but I think we can make some efforts to move on from that. I do not know if we did need a level themed around an 'Oriental' underground market-place filled with tired tropes of corrupt and shady Middle-Eastern and Asian merchants, snake-charmers and smugglers. No amount of cuteness makes it fun or engaging. Please, developers, if you could give this some thought for your next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I can definitely say that it is the best hidden object game I have played in my life. Apart from the hidden objects in the game, the details and of course the art are beautiful. The story is also very good and enjoyable, almost like a cartoon. As the name of the game suggests, its map resembles a maze. I enjoyed navigating the map and exploring the details around. The length of the game is also quite satisfactory, but I hope there will be more. I think there should be a continuation of such a beautiful, detailed and high quality game. I definitely recommend it to detective and hidden object game lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightful little puzzle game with really beautiful mazes and fun easter eggs. There are collectibles in every level and I found myself wanting to veer off the path to the end to explore. Very relaxing game. Cute. Fun. Recommend it. NOTE: My kid left my computer on with the game open, so my time estimate is probably about 48 hours wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful adventure game that takes players on a journey through a maze of hidden treasures and secrets. As the main character, you must explore the environment and interact with objects to uncover hidden items and progress through the game. One of the standout features is its charming hand-drawn art style, complete with enjoyable animations that bring the world to life. The addition of pop culture game references was a pleasant surprise, adding an extra layer of fun to the overall experience. The music in the game is perfectly suited to the environment, and the voice acting during the comic book-style cutscenes was well-executed, adding depth to the story. While the game may cater more to the casual gamer who seeks simple and fun gameplay, there is plenty of content to keep players entertained for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game and it was a childhood daydream made reality. It strikes a happy medium in that it can engage both children and adults. There are a lot of pop culture, and references to other video games that would go over the head of a child but caught by the adult player. The game invites the player to explore by encouraging them to interact with their surroundings, yielding a fun cinematic or collectible. The levels provide enough material, that if a collectible is missed, it is still fun to go through the level again, without it becoming tedious. The only criticism I have is that the game could have used some difficulty levels, as it would provide another avenue to replay the game. As the game is, after going through a level two or three times, it does lose the magic. If someone is looking for a chill game to play for a day, I would highly recommend this. It delivers a great experience
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: This game is especially good to play for  and / or with kids!  The game itself is just a maze you have to find your way through to find Mr. X. On the way you can find some collectibles and unlock achievements by clicking people and items.  Also there are a few mini games to play during your journey.   You can not really go wrong,  but you might get lost a little, or miss a turn to find a collectible. At first I thought Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective  would be too childish to finish. The story really is,  but just walking passed so many different scenes was very relaxing.   Finding all collectibles turned out to be harder as expected.   However personally I did not consider restarting the chapters to find everything and get a 100% achievement rating.  One play through was good enough for me.    Recommended for the art style , level design and atmosphere.   It is just a cute game.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. Its everything you could possibly want in a casual game. The level design is great, the mazes aren't annoyingly hard and they don't feel like a chore to get through. You can go out of your way to collect items, they aren't vital to game play though. It gives you something else to do while also being able to experience the whole level. You can go back and replay the level if you missed anything. I'm not sure how long it is but it's well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE this game. It's in the same cartoon style as Where's Waldo, so lots to look at. You get your objective and find your way to it through a maze,  while simultaneously looking out for chests/stars/etc. It's not timed and there are short cut scenes between each level with an option to skip. A simple, no stakes, puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: It's like a Where's Waldo book come to life, there's always so much going on in the background and lots of little things to interact with. Very charming ^^My only gripe is that it doesn't have cloud save, so my quest for 100% completion can only be done on my, uh.. less than stellar laptop.Everything else is great tho, the narration and humor bring me such joy.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why I originally thought this was a point-and-click where's waldo kind of game. It does have the same feel as Where's Waldo but involves a lot of walking around labyrinths.The artwork is very cute and the achievements give you that extra challenge of finding all the things, which is really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game about wandering and discovering inside a maze world. Like the Waldo books in my childhood, this takes that and makes it reality. While the story is simple, everything makes up for that. The level designs are amazing and unique to one another. Now the graphics are simply beautiful. They really look like hand drawn pages from Waldo and the animations really bring this game to life! I am blown away. the graphics and animations are a masterpiece! Then add in the collectibles to find in each level really make this a great game. Do not forget the fun easter eggs to pop culture! Highly recommended to everyone!
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: A super relaxing and absorbing game. I bought this as part of a bundle, and it wasn't something I'd normally even look twice at. It seemed too kiddish. But they really managed to make mazes fun for grown ups too. Lots of things to collect, and tons of little easter eggs. I couldn't stop until I'd finished the whole thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable spin on "wheres waldo" type game. Running around and talking to various characters, looking at the nice details in the scenery are all good. One thing that I liked was the continuity. Characters from one area show up in other parts. The main story is super basic, but that's how it is with these types of games. The detail is what matters and the detail is very high effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing and interactive game. My advice is to take your time going around the different areas and you will definitely find surprises hidden round the corner.There are some bugs in the game so if you are a achievement hunter or completionist, I suggest waiting till all the bugs have been fixed before playing. However, it's definitely a game worth replaying again.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It reminds me so much of this game I had when I was a kid called Puzzle Castle. Labyrinth City has a little bit of everything with mazes, minigames, collectibles, and hilarious dialogue from characters along the way. It's also a winner because it was involved enough to keep a 20-something like me engaged, but not so difficult that a child would be unable to successfully play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played through the first level. But as soon as I saw a trailer for this game I saw the beauty of Where's Wally and the joy of Wimmel Bilder. I'm sure I'll love every minute of this game, never has a game brought me such a big smile and the wonder of my childhood through every moment of play.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: My 5-year-old kid loved it. Took us 15 hours to finish. Very lovely art, lots to explore. The maze is very packed. You pass some spots 4 times, but on different levels. Time critical tasks exist only in the last levels. Its a relaxing game. 30% of the jokes could only be understood by adults. The game is super easy for adults. Don't expect too much. I would buy the sequel on an instant.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: A game in the form of Where's Wally, where hidden things in hyper-detailed pictures tell a story. Overall, a nice change from the usual game format, but something feels lost in the focused nature of the way the puzzle unravels itself as players unveil the hidden secrets. If anything, the puzzles feel too railroaded. Visually appealing and unique nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective is such a charming casual game. It's quite obvious that the game takes its influence from the popular "Where's Waldo"series of books. However; there's not a lot of similarities beyond the graphics here.. but I found it to be a good progression from a particular book style to an interactive video game. Labyrinth City keeps your eyes peeled and is a great way to relax for a few hours. It adds puzzles and extraordinary detail to the environment (maze) you're walking through without tearing your brain apart trying to figure stuff out. There's a relaxing quality to the game... almost therapeutic. There's so many things happening if you just observe.Essentially the story line sets you in tracking down "Mister X". There's a lovely hand drawn style to the entire game that reminds you of the "Where's Waldo" books but adds charm to a normally stagnant book page by allowing Pierre to walk around and explore. "Explore" is a misleading term here because there is a sort of narrative that has to be followed to complete the game.You never really see the entire maze while you are playing. While you do get a glimpse of the entire maze at the start.. you quickly zoom in to your Pierre and have to remember where you've been... and what you did.As the game progresses through several mazes, you're given several tasks for each maze map. The tasks usually have to do with finding a certain character or item in the game besides Mister X. Finding the characters can be a bit of a forced narrative because some mazes will block access to areas you need once you passed a certain point. As the maze changes, you lose your ability to "explore". So the story feels a bit forced to "move on" to your task at hand. There are Steam Achievements. If you've missed any achievements along the way, chances are you will have to start the maze again because now the area is blocked off.There's hidden games within the game itself. Find the Polar bear on every map to unlock achievements and games separate from the tasks at hand. Normally relatively easy simple games but a nice diversion.GREAT game to relax and enjoy without the bullet hell or slaying. "Challenging" is not a word that comes to mind... I would use "Casual". There is a fixed story.. so once completed, players will find replaying the game easier and easier. After you find an item or character once... you now know where they are.. or how to get there... which kind of makes the game ripe for speed runs. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: The electronic adaptation of the famous comic book retains the complete plot line in the comic book, and the game has a series of playable decisions such as collecting, searching, dialogue, and tribute to the easter eggs in the form of video games.To1. The plot line and world view are normal, suitable for children and adults aged 4-12. (Players of adolescent age are skipped here, in view of the dark humor and the guidance of negative energy hints in the game. Teenagers do not have enough experience to judge right from wrong.)2. Beautiful children's comic style, the interaction of multiple characters and objects is perfect. Appropriate guidance allows the player's enthusiasm to be greatly increased without reducing the fun of the game.3. Perfect collection system. And there is a specific display position in the main menu, which reasonably improves the player's coupling to the in-game item collection system, and gives the player a sense of accomplishment in the game.4. Trust things and make aspirations. This is an important game feature in line with adult players. The character dialogue in the game process reflects the author's dissatisfaction with the current social phenomena, but the degree of criticism is just right, will not mislead children's correct thinking, and at the same time resonate with the psychology of adult players.5. Tribute to the classics (EE). _childDocuments_.review: This game was amazing, its like playing this game brought me back to my childhood where i would read I SPY or Where's Waldo? books and experiencing the magic reading them. _childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: A super-fun romp through a beautiful hand-drawn maze, but with a few minor issues. First, the English translation is low quality: several obvious mistakes, though nothing that hinders your play. Second, the controls are occasionally frustrating: you want to go one way but instead go another. And lastly, the majority of the dead ends feature some kind of item you need to get for completion, so it's not so much a "maze" as it is a "dungeon". In a maze, your objective is to get from the start to the finish in the shortest route possible, but in this game, you have to explore every passage to every dead end in order to get all items and achievements, making it more of a map exploration game. Still, a fun game for sure!
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Nice cute game, mainly intended for younger players although it does have a lot of humorous pop cultural references. Great level design, somewhat reminiscent of Where's Waldo and with a big influence of French culture. Music is sweet, too! Would be nice for the lead dev to make it available to download ;-).
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: It took a quick moment to figure out the controls for this game BUT once that was overcome it was loads of fun to play this with my kids. All the beautiful details, character interactions and just finding all sorts of things held my 6 and 9 y/o's attentions so well!Definitely looking forward to playing this several more times to come with my kiddos!
_childDocuments_.name: Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective

_childDocuments_.review: Explore the maze, solve simple puzzles and find hidden items/achievements. It's a relaxing game and pretty easy but there is some challenge. It took me about 6 hours to complete though I'm missing a few achievements so expect a little longer than that if you want to 100% it.

_childDocuments_.review: Vibrant environments, lovely interactive animation, and the dynamic soundtrack tied it all together nicely. I hope they make more of these!

name: Into the Pit
detailed_description: As members of a family of lore-hunting mystics, you and your cousin Luridia separately wander the land following rumors of occult power. After discovering a demonic pit in a nearby village, Luridia’s once prolific letters grow silent. Something has gone terribly wrong. Now it is up to you to journey to the desolate hamlet under dark eldritch skies. What did Luridia discover? And what great power has this village unearthed? Key Features: FIGHT WITH CHAOTIC MAGIC - experiment with various spells and powers to become an unstoppable magical force SHIFTING TREACHEROUS DUNGEONS - high-octane energy and short-paced levels will keep you on your toes. You’ll never know what horror lies beyond the next corner. GROW YOUR POWERS - rescue villagers to open shops for permanent upgrades to prolong your runs and maximize your potential CHOOSE YOUR CHALLENGE - mix keys and runes gathered on your journeys to generate and combine different dungeon encounters.

short_description: A fast-paced retro-FPS roguelite! As a member of a family of lore-hunting mystics you are summoned to a cursed village, drawn by rumors of a demonic portal. Dark magics have overwhelmed the village, It's up to you to rescue the survivors, grow your powers, and journey forth INTO THE PIT.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of roguelikes, this game gave me more mixed feelings than anything. =The good=-Visual style is really nice-Movement and physics feels good and is satisfying-Damage feedback is great=The bad=-After 3 hours, I have seen literally everything in the game. Every layout, every enemy and every weapon and powerup-"Fight with chaotic magic" is a flat out lie. This game does not show you anything you have not seen before. You have a selection of weapons at the beginning of each run which can be summed up as: a shotgun, a sniper, a 3burst midrange, a midrange auto-shotgun and a rocket launcher. If you are looking for interesting magic combinations or actual spells, this is NOT IT-The lore is non-existent. The game sets itself up in an interesting way but falls on it's face 30 minutes in. You have to rescue 48 villagers throughout the game, and they have 4 or 5 different scripted dialogue which repeats over and over. Rest of the village is just different shops saying the same thing every time you interact with them-Shops are pointless. They let you buy permanent upgrades but the ones you begin with are kind of the best-in-slot in every way, so there is no real reason to bother with them after you have upgraded the ones you like. This renders the currency system completely useless about 2 hours in-Loading screens after every chamber disrupts the flow-No build variety. Every run feels the same especially once you figure out which weapons you enjoy the most-Enhancements are so boring I can't even begin. +20% dmg has never been an interesting concept. 8 out of 10 powerups are just there to bloat the overall list of things and are utter useless therefore you end up picking the same things without even thinking-Boss fights are all the same, and it wasn't interesting for the first time either. Bullet sponge, brain dead enemies that you can kite infinitely with no effort.-Difficulty is a joke. I have literally not died ONCE while playing this game and I don't believe that is a normal thing. None of the enemies pose a challenge even when they pop up in your face or the game tries to overwhelm you, they are so dumb and easy to outplay no matter what gear you have. And the powerups just make it even more of a faceroll - bad design-At around a third of the game (which I have stopped at), you have actually discovered everything there is in the game, but it still blatantly wants you to grind out the rest without giving any incentive as to why.I can not recommend this game for roguelike fans, and even for players newer to the genre there are just so many other (and better) options out there. The 15€ price tag baffles me for the amount of content put into this game and I wish I could refund it.=TL;DR=Looks good, plays good, horrible design decisions, doesn't respect your time, serious lack of content and variety. Not worth the price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: I do like the game but mostly because I'm a big fan of fps with rogue lite elements.Maybe I expected too much, it's far from being a ♥♥♥♥ game but it could have been so much more.Unfortunately it gets repetitive and boring way too fast, pretty much the cardinal sin for a rogue lite...Most of the levels look exactly the same, always the same environments with the exact same colors palette every playthrough.We do get new biomes after saving villagers and it does increase variety but we have to grind levels to unlock more of them.The level design is mediocre, all levels are short and uninspired with cheap patterns of ennemies spawns.Not even two hours in and I had already seen repeats in the levels layouts, talk about replayability...Into the Pit graphics are also hit or miss, at first I liked the visual style of the game but sadly I ended up kinda disliking it.There's so much chromatic aberration, it's full of saturated colors and annoying on screen effects, it's pretty close to be headache inducing !Gameplay wise it's very limited, not enough different powers or modifiers to use, no double jump, dash or cool abilities, the only upgrades are the classic crit chances, fire rate and the likes.Somehow I find the controls a bit floaty, moving the character forward or backward is faster than strafe left and right, there is also not enough air control.No real depth during fights, just spam left and right clicks until health bars are depleted, it does not feel really satisfying to play.During levels it's always the same objectives, collect motes, kill ennemies and destroy keystones, so damn boring.Repeat this three, four or five times until the final boss and your playthrough is over, not much variety right here...Not impressed so far, I might as well go back to play Ziggurat or Roboquest, way better indie fps rogue lite.Honestly if you played the demo well you've seen about 40% of what the game have to offer, so it's not surprising they removed the demo lol.I'm being very negative with this review but the game is not entirely garbage, it's fun for 2-3 hours then after that mark you start to realize all the game's problems.If you love fps games mixed with rogue lite elements give it a go, you may enjoy it but lower your expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the demo, you basically played the whole game.Great aesthetic, but ultimately boring gameplay with very little player choice as far as builds go. Every environment looks good, but plays out the same way. All boss fights are nearly the same (get giant guy to 50% health, they shield and spawn a wave of enemies, kill all enemies to continue to fight boss).Maybe get it on deep, deep discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo, bought the game as soon as it launched, and played a half-dozen or so runs. It's... hard to recommend.On the plus side, the demo is very honest about what you're getting in the game; the game is exactly what's in the demo. The problem is that the game is ONLY what's in the demo. It's not a long game; I estimate it would take the average player no longer than 6 hours to beat the final dungeon, and much less time to see all of the game's content. The game also looks really nice (to me, at least) and the moment-to-moment gameplay is a blast.There's remarkably little replayability for a roguelite. The different dungeons have more or less the same layout pools, with perhaps a couple of unique ones per dungeon. There's a decent variety in enemies, but hardly enough to carry you through the 4 or 5 runs you might see them in. And the bosses are disappointing. Whatever they do, circle-strafing and firing continuously usually deals with them quite handily.The lack of variety in your personal armament is the primary issue. The player gets about 8 options of bullet-shooter (basically just tweaks on clip size, spread, range, and presumably damage) and one option for a bomb. That's the entirety of the offensive arsenal. It's a shame; it doesn't take much effort to think up some more exciting weapon options. Why not a tesla-style spell that chains to multiple enemies if one is hit? Why not a spell that fires a long stream of projectiles that deals more damage the longer you fire continuously? Why not a spell that has a minimum range? An AoE spell that hits everything near you for massive damage? Why not spells that have negative effects to yourself, like one that pushes you backwards or slows you down when you fire? Why not have a flamethrower spell that blocks part of the screen, making it riskier to use since you won't be able to see incoming projectiles? Or a spell that deals damage in proportion to the enemy's remaining health (i.e. high damage to enemies with lots of health, but almost no damage to low-health enemies)? More weapons that represent tradeoffs and different styles, that actually change how you move and shoot, would greatly improve the game.The upgrades you can get aren't too exciting. A few conditional damage modifiers (more damage at high health! More damage at low health! More damage against afflicted enemies! More damage on crits! More damage when afflicted yourself!) and a few status ailments (poison, bleed, weakness, slow, and 'curse' - i.e. damage when they attack). Compared to some other roguelites, there's not much to see. Nothing that changes movement up, no risk vs. reward upgrade paths (aside from objectively bad decisions like "deal damage when enemies damage you" or "more damage at low health"), nothing that can change how your weapons fire or what you actually try to do. Here's some more upgrades that they could put in, just off the top of my head: deal more damage in proportion to the number of enemies nearby; your bullets ricochet; your bullets knock back enemies (and make enemies take damage from environmental hazards!); begin stages with a damage shield, negating the first attack you take; increase damage for a spell massively, but every subsequent shot in a stage gets progressively less damaging until it's just a peashooter; increase all stats of a weapon, but misses deal damage to you. There's so many more things they could have done, and instead, we just have a serviceable, but boring set of upgrades.The runes that you set up before runs are similarly boring. It's just generic, "drop more of or start with this type of resource," "get more of this type of upgrade," or heal during the stages. The healing runes dominate all others in terms of usefulness and make the game absolutely trivial. They could have made these more interesting as well, amping up the risk vs. reward factor: all upgrades are higher level, but you no longer get a choice of stages; no healing is possible at all, but you deal increased damage; ALL afflictions (to you and enemies) last longer/are more severe; double the amount of enemies/make all enemies elite but guarantee bonus motes for each stage completed. As it stands, you can pick a core set of runes and just dominate everything from about the second dungeon on.It's cheap. It's fun. It's a decent game for what it is. But it could have been so much more. I don't know if they're planning on expanding the available options to the player in DLC or FLC or what. If they do, and I remember, I'll check back in and see if this review needs to be updated. I hope so, because the core here is so good. But I'm afraid I can't recommend it as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: In a game where mobility is important, it is unforgivable that you get hung up on wall details. Not like a hazard or something, but just doodads attached to the wall to make things look visually interesting. 90% of the damage I take in the game is from getting hung up on the walls after jumping out of the way of something.It's neat that the enemies glow so they stand out from the background, but as you play longer everything starts to glow. Your hands glow. The doodads in the background glow. The stuff you pick up glows. The keystones you interact with glow. When everything glows so it stands out better, nothing stands out anymore.I can count on one hand how many times I walked up to an interactive object and pressed E and had it respond the first time. This game is unimaginably simple, so when the simplest things don't work, they stand out hard.None of the 'weapon' options are interesting, none of the builds do anything fun, and the upgrades are uninspired. The pool of room layouts is so shallow that you'll get repeats on the same floor. The enemies don't do anything interesting.Nothing about this game is interesting. No risks were taken, everything is a recycled idea or direct copy of something better. You'd be better off digging a big hole in the back yard and tossing your hard earned money directly Into the Pit.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: Downloaded the demo for Into The Pit, along with many others, during a Steam Next Fest. Unlike most demos I played Into the Pit's until I ran out of content, due to the "Demo-gorgan" impeding further progress. Bought this on release for like 20$ and had a blast 100%'ing it. Into the Pit is a fun, fast-paced twitch shooter with randomised offensive and defensive power-ups, as well as randomised dungeons and enemy types. It's the kind of game you can play for 15-30 mins or longer if you want. The game really shines when external currencies (required for keystones to dungeons, support runes and upgrading support runes) cease to matter and you can focus on the in-dungeon currencies that increase the drop quality of power-ups or let you re-roll your choices. That's sort of when the game was the most fun.All in all, fun game, immensely enjoyed my time with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: Dang. Game visuals and concept had a lot of potential. After reading other reviews I find it surprising that no one has mentioned the odd amount of colliders on every bit of terrain. I get stuck on each tiny speck jutting from the walls. I noticed the colliders first when I fell into a poison pond and couldn't get out because of a brick sticking out. That almost killed me. Ultimately, the enemies never killed me, but I softlocked in the fungus biome floor where I was stuck for good. I also agree that the magic attacks are bland. There could have been a summon spell or a charm spell or anything you can think of, but it's really just 4 range-specific shooties that get more numbers to them as you progress. The bomb spell damages the player so if you design your build to kill the enemy fast and one of these better-door-than-window colliders pops up you just nuke yourself. TLDR; Needs more content in most/all of its aspects, buggy movement near objects will randomly end a run.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: I'm afraid I have to agree with the other negative reviews here: It's fun for a couple hours max, and then it's just grindy and boring.On the whole the game is easy, and at first exciting visually and with respect to the gameplay. After a few rounds rescuing villagers you start to notice that there are only 5 or so flavor texts and the village never changes. Continuing after that you realize that the levels are all just about the same, enemy attacks are all the same with minorly different effects, and the bosses are all just about the same. It's just too much of the same. When there are 45 total villagers to rescue and the flavor text doesn't even have audio, there's simply no excuse for not varying it a little more than this. In the end I think it seems lazy.With respect to player power scaling and upgrades - the effects are really quite minor. There's no satisfying juice with  things like exploding attacks or even consequentially different effects. The choices are very limited and they don't compound nearly as much as the loading screen tips imply. I came into this expecting even a hint of the roguelite in-run growth of others like Risk of Rain, Caveblazers, or Hades, but it is lacking.On the whole the game seems lacking and sort of empty. There are some really good bones here, but unless there is quite a lot more development on the game content, I wouldn't recommend it even at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't realize that I play FPSs for the architecture until I tried this game and realized how much bad level design hurts my enjoyment. The levels are boring, all the same, "randomly" generated (but I've seen the same levels several times, so I think that's a lie, it's more like "lazily" generated). They attempt to make up for the boring design with a heaping helping of retro visual post processing VFX, but it just ends up looking like pixelated mush. The only really GOOD part: you almost always have the option to run around with the equivalent of a rocket launcher as your primary weapon, and you have unlimited ammo for all your weapons, so I actually use it unlike in most FPSs. Too bad it's kind of weak, making the other guns that can't hurt you a better option most of the time, even if they are less fun. In the end this game isn't bad, it's just MEH in every way. With so many games released every week on steam there are far better games to play (for instance, instead of this play: DUSK, AMID Evil, Prodeus, etc etc).
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: No variety. After the first hour or less i pretty much saw everything there was to see with the repetitious layout and gameplay mechanics bringing the boredom quickly. Got boring and tedious in no time which is unfortunate considering the graphical style and what there was of the world design was interesting but it was the same thing over and over with nothing else as if ninety percent of the game had not been added yet. _childDocuments_.review: The stunning retro game looks and the roguelite aspect drew me into this game.Unfortunately the game mechanics are very unimaginative. _childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: This game suffers from a lack of novelty. By the four hour mark you'll have seen everything it has to offer and the story isn't interesting enough to push you forward. I only rescued 24 villagers, so there may be some drastic gameplay change up that I didn't see, but I doubt it. It's easy for your avatar to get stuck on walls, though not in a run-ending sort of way, just one that makes it a pain to jump around.
_childDocuments_.name: Into the Pit

_childDocuments_.review: This game is decent at first. I am obsessed with retro style FPS games, especially any that even remotely resemble Heretic/Hexen, which is why I bought this. You can jump in and have a good time in the short term. But long term, it gets repetitive very quickly. The game description really doesn't do justice to what you actually DO, and what that is is basically single "runs" where you pick a magical load-out of left and right hand powers, then try to delve as many levels down into The Pit as you can, using different runes to control which dimension you're delving down into. At certain progression intervals, you can upgrade the powers you picked in the initial load-out, but this is temporary. If you quit or die, you are returned to town and have to start back at the very beginning of "the pit" at level 1, losing all of your upgrades in the process. There's really almost no real progression, this game is basically a magic themed version of Tower of Guns. Now you might be thinking, "There are plenty of wildly popular games today deploying this exact same format", and this is true. I thought long and hard about that, why does this game kinda suck where lots of other games just like it are extremely fun and addicting? And I found that for me it comes down to the rewards and upgrades. In other games where you KNOW you're eventually going to die and return to the beginning(and thus you're just really competing to see how far you can make it) there are usually rewards and/or upgrades that are permanent; things you get to keep even when you return to the beginning that keep you coming back for more over and over again. A good example of this is Vampire Survivors, where each run has the potential to unlock new characters, unlock new powers via collected gold, unlocks new Arcanas, etc. . This game tries to do this and utterly fails in making it feel worthwhile or exciting. In this game, you sometimes collect Gold and Fire emblems, which let you craft new support runes or forge new Ritual runes at 2 shops in the Town. The problem is, these mechanics are tied to how many Villagers you have "found" down in the pit. Once you've found enough people in the pit, a new shop opens up, which lets you get more upgrades, or a shop you've already unlocked starts offering new upgrades. Unfortunately though, towns folk are sparse and it can take dozens of forays into the pit just to find 2 or 3 towns people. You find so few townsfolk during your "runs" down into the pit, and it takes so many "found" people to unlock new upgrades and Shops that your Runs feel pointless and arbitrary. Why go on ANOTHER run into the pit? If you're lucky you might find MAYBE 1 towns person before you die and are shuttled back to the beginning, with no new powers or anything to make the next run feel more interesting. Vampire Survivors, and other games like it, keep things interesting by creating an upgrade curve where there are a ton of things to unlock in the beginning, and only as you progress much further do these available upgrades start to thin out. In this game, the upgrade process is slow right from the beginning. It takes way too many of the SAME runs down into the pit to unlock anything new, and that pretty much kills any long term fun to be had with this game. In the end, this game was a lot of missed opportunities. If they had made the town a Hub world, and made each dimension of the pit its own fully built level where you unlock new powers and abilities as you progress, this game would have instantly been 100 times better and more playable. In any case, unless you pick it up for a DEEP discount, I wouldn't spend your hard earned money on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Into the Pit is another roguelike, dungeon shooter, but with its own unique style. If you enjoy games like Ziggurat, Immortal Redneck, Tower of Guns, Mother Gunship, etc, you will enjoy this new adaptation of the genre as well.  As you can see the visuals is very old school with some neon colors splashed into it. The atmosphere is pretty dark in the town and throughout the dungeon.  is where I think this game stands out from others. In order to enter the dungeon, you have to put runes into this sigil that gives you buffs or changes the game up (for example there is one that doubles damage dealt to you, but you gain double the nodes.) In order to get to new dungeons, you have to craft its perspective rune to unlock it. In these dungeons, there are 4 arenas per floor. Each arena has 2 different choices that you can pick from. These choices let you choose which node you collect in them. Nodes are the type of currency/resources in the game. You use nodes to buy/craft more runes. There are also nodes that you can only use per floor that affect luck, let you reroll buffs, and revive yourself. You fight with spells that you put in each hand. You only have 1 spell per hand and they range from a shotgun-type spell, to a sniper-like spell and it allows you to play different styles. After you complete an arena, you have a 3 choices to upgrade yourself. You can add bleed damage to one hand, make one hand weaken enemies when hit, increase your health or speed, etc. There are many different combos to choose from which allows each run to be different. have a nice variety to them. Some fly, there are stationary turrets, ones that explode when killed, ones that spawn little enemies when killed, etc. The first boss seemed a little to easy, but maybe the later bosses will prove to be more difficult. At first the enemies may seem a little underwhelming, but it doesn't take much to kill you. I'm enjoying this game so far and what it offers. I will continue playing and can't wait to see what the developers add later on.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game. It starts promising, but fizzle out without even taking up from the ground.The whole game is just a bare skeleton.There is no content. Developers blatantly baited and switched everyone who tried pre-release demo. There is nothing new beyong the demo. You literaly could see everything what game could offer during the demo itself. Steam Store description is misleading at its best and false at it worst.But you dont have various spells and powers. You chose one attack for LMB, one attack for RMB at the start of your run and thats it. You don't have anything else. No spells, abilities, not even dash.The gameplay never evolves or even changes from the start.More over, game actively discourage you from choosing different attacks because of its clumsy and wierd firing mechanics. To attack efficiently you need to tap your mouse button with certain rithm. If you hold it, then attack whould not recharge and become much slower, drastically reducing your DPS. With two different attacks you will have two different rithms making keeping consistent DPS an absolute nightmare.Different attacks also greatly vary in usefulness and power, making half of them useless. There is no point to choose anything but Nebula unless you want to deliberatly handicap yourself.There is also no need to experiment with various perks and powers because how those powers work.Status effects does not stack. All attacks will apply same bleed or poison, so there is no choosing between types of attack for a specific build.Bleed and poison are very weak and do negligible amount of damage, even at their max level.Enemies are generaly pretty squishy and whould die from couple of shots even BEFORE FIRST TICK of bleed or poison. It can contribute against the bosses or rare tanky enemies, but 95% of the run those effects are completle negligible.The weakness effect are completly useless. This is rougle-lite. The enemy what can hit you is usually the one who you didn't see first or walked in to accidentally.If you see the enemy, its easy to avoid its attacks. If you don't see the enemy you can't apply Weakness status to it.The Curse status effect deal damage to the enemy when they attack you. For melee enemies its never, for ranged enemies it's the same problem with bleed and poison.The only remotely usefull status effect is frost, what slows down enemy movement speed. It can be usefull agains rare tanky monsters.Besides those what i described, there is no other notable perks. All other abilities are boring increases to DPS like damage, crit%, crit damage etc.Increases to projectile range are indistinguible to naked eye and rarely usefull because most levels consist of cramped corridors.There is stationary turrets-type monsters, but they either unvulnerable at long range or hide in the ground untill you come close. A lot of enemies also like to spawn from thin air after you enter their range.Increases to rate of fire also totally meaningless because of wierd firing mechanics that i described before.There is no perks what change how weapons work in any way. Just by looking at that system of perks any player can imagine wealth of possibilities. And the game shamelesly hints at it, just to leave players dissapointed.The levels here certanly short. But they are repetitive. Amount of layouts are small and you will grow familiar with all of them even before you unlock all of your shops in town. Even more, different zones here use the same layouts as all previous levels. The only thing what changes is enemies and walls. So no matter what dungeon Key you use, there will be the same levels, just with differently themed skin.The game graphics style also making it hard to differentiate between them.Thats a blatant lie. Meta-progression in this game is laughable.You never unlock new weapons, perks or powers. The only thing what you unlock is runes with starting bonuses like additional resouses at the start of the run, better chance for specific perks or resistance to poison/bleed.And the most hillarious part? I unlocked EVERYTHING what game has to offer with resouses gathered during the demo.Yes, i unlocked everything just by experimenting with availible demo content for three hours. Im not joking.You have three types of persistent resourses in that game. Gold, Insight and Fire.With gold you buy runes, with Insight you upgrade them and with Fire you unlock keys to dungeons. After that those resouses useless and can be skipped.There is no challenge. This game is too easy, even with rune that double received damage and earned resources. I spent 9 hours to finish the compaing and unlock all achievments. And i'm mediocre at roguelikes. All bosses require same strategy - strafe and shoot. The final boss was a joke.This game feels like first Early Access version of Ziggurat 2. Only with less content and worse game mechanics.It lacks most basic things that makes game from its genre appealing to its audience.You will see everything what game has to offer in the first dungeon. And whats left after that is the same grind without progress, changes or even deviation.It can be a great game if devs keep working on it, but in its current state you'll be better with original Ziggurat. It's ten time more content for the same price.And without eye-gouging art-style.

_childDocuments_.review: Played to death on Xbox Game Pass before it left, just HAD to re-buy it here. I feel like boomer shooter/roguelite enjoyers have really slept on this gem.  It's clean and simple running and shooting in bite-sized levels against a set of enemies whose variety you influence through a selection of unlocks to reconfigure the dungeon.There's a decent variety of spell types, boosts, and combos that keep each run interesting as you work on your build synergies, and the meta-progression is targeted and meaningful, always offering you a reasonable degree of control over what type of power you want to pursue.  I also personally dig the over-saturated, over-bloomed visual effect, but some might want to tone that down a little.  There's a real beauty to its gradual addition of complexity, while keeping the underlying basics of room-clear-get-power simple. Best of all, it's not over-long. You aren't signing up for a second job with this one, butting your head up against 'git gud' skill checks that you can't overpower.  It's achievable, which is something a lot of rogue-lites don't do - wasting your time with 'failed run' build combos that screw you from the start. I've seen a lot of new rogue-lite shooters trying with middling success to do what Into the Pit has already done better and earlier. More folks should take lessons from Into the Pit.

_childDocuments_.review: A little disappointed with this game. I played the demo during Steam Nextfest and had lots of fun with it. Bought the full game when it came out only to find out I played the whole game in the demo. The only thing you didn't get to do in the demo was unlock more keys or runes and you couldn't upgrade your runes. There are also only like 10 different chamber variations and all the different keys do is just change the skin of the dungeon. Pretty much the same thing with the enemies too. The skin changes but they are all more or less the same. The bosses are pretty disappointing too. Each boss fight is just a boss in the middle of the room that barely moves, or doesn't move at all, get them down to half health, they go invincible, adds spawn, kill the adds, finish the boss. As long as your just strafing in the circle, you'll never get hit.I'm hoping in the future they add more chambers and add a little more variation in enemies and bosses. So for now i can't really recommend the game as after you've played an hour you've pretty much done everything. It's unfortunate because this game felt like it had a lot of potential. Wait for a sale if you want to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Into the Pit emerges as a compelling FPS roguelike, blending fast-paced shooting with procedurally generated challenges. Despite delivering a thrilling experience, the game stumbles in terms of content and narrative depth. Levels can feel repetitive, and the story remains underdeveloped, leaving players craving a more immersive backdrop for their demonic encounters. While Into the Pit might not justify its full price tag due to its current limitations, a substantial sale could make it a worthwhile addition to the library for those intrigued by its promising concept.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-The visual aesthetic of this game is both respectful homage to the game's influences and still something uniquely its own. The pixelated graphics add a layer of surreality to the fast-paced gameplay, all while keeping the file size down! -The soundtrack is banging, a la Doom-lite. -Challenging, reward gameplay, especially with bosses. Cons: -It is really hard to run-n-gun in this game, which is odd considering the clear Doom influences. HP is just too vital a resource so trepidatiousness seems necessary for survival. Maybe if excess Motes of Blood healed you for even the slightest bit instead of just being useless and deleted upon pickup? -Certainly has its bugs. I got flung three map heights upward because of a weird interaction of landing on an enemy's head and a jump pad at the same time, as an example. -Some of the upgrades feel nigh useless compared with other, clearer choices presented, and you do tire of the same ~7 weapons after repeated runs. Granted, this encourages mastery of the weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: I had such high hopes for this one. I love Roguelikes. I love FPSs. I love Roguelike FPSs.This game? Bad. Barebones, and lackluster combat. Not enough variety, gets old REALLY fast. Like, within 2 hours. That's not a good sign. This game might be good a year or so from now if they add in more content, more variety with spells/skills. Maybe add passive items, or a skill tree? Classes? You might have seen the other reviews talking about the "unique" weapons. It's the same crap you've already seen, with nothing new to offer. And not even alot of it, either.Not even to mention how awful the terrain is. Within the first 30 minutes, I got stuck in between a wall and a doodad, and had to quit the game and lose my run.I will say, there was ONE idea I liked. The keystone system. But that's not enough to save this game.TL;DR: It's bad. Do not buy this unfinished crap. Go play Ziggurat II, that game is what this game WANTS to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Yikes, feel kind of burned by this game. It's alright honestly, but you can play the demo and get the majority of what the games has to offer -- although I don't know if the demo is around anymore. This game is 5 levels each time with very little variation. You can vary the environment and enemies, but the environmental variation is minor and the enemies stop varying beyond the first 3 environments. The enemies after those first 3 keys seem different, but I couldn't tell you how, they're just more of the same with minor changes. The real killer is that weapons and abilities don't change over the course of the game as far as I can tell. In fact very little variety is ever unlocked, the game just kind of goes limp whenever it seems to threaten to become something more interesting or engaging. Like I can't imagine playing this much more than 2 hours because it's just the same thing, over and over, no meaningful changes. The one shopkeeper I haven't unlocked is the merchant and I've been trying -- but getting eighteen villagers is just such a slog. I thought the support runes would be more interesting than "% increase to find X runes," or rather more interesting than just dull numerical adjustments like that, but they're all boring. I've been playing with the "take 200% damage rune" that also doubles the currencies you find and I think that might be the most interesting modifier in the game, if not the only interesting one in the game. There's a lot of promise here, but I can't bring myself to play anymore. There's not even difficulty options really, it's just all so straight forward and so uninspiring.

_childDocuments_.review: I mean it's really NOT the worst game you'll ever play. Into The Pit is quite decent, but it's the repetitive aspect of it that makes it to be lazy and repetitive. As a roguelike, it's quite straightforward: The story is that you're an outlander who arrives at a village in quite the precarious situation; the villagers have gone missing and it's now up to you to go into the pit and save them. The rune master crafts keys for you that take you to other realms of the pit, which are really just palette swaps of the first dungeon ever. Let's talk about the pit; it's got 5 floors total. The fifth floor is always a lazy boss that's got two phases (for all of my 5 pit runs, it was a golem that's got a different color each time... I'm guessing there are no other bosses lol). You start off by choosing a style of gun for each of your hands (left and mouse buttons), I recommend you go with gattling cannons, not the bomb slow ones as they are fast and get the job done. In a floor, you have to activate 4 pillars to be able to proceed to the next, you do that by going into a challenge. Each pillar has got two challenges you can choose from... And, hear me on this, EACH CHALLENGE IS THE SAME: you collect motes (upgrade materials you can use back in the village) and have to destroy some keystones... that's the ENTIRE game! Doing the same bullcrap over and over and over and over again until you no longer feel like doing it. Well, after you do that, the pillar activates and you get to pick up an upgrade for your weaponry! You lose everything once the run is over... and that's the roguelike part I guess.This game gets a  at best... For what it's worth, the animations are quite smooth and being able to go around gunning down hordes of demonic beings with magic that sparks out of your hands is, I gotta say, quite satisfactory... but the lazy level design as well as a lack of any incentive to actually play the game (no storyline, no nothing... just your character thrusted into the dungeon and that's all) makes it quite lackluster.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game dearly despite its shortcomings. The demo sucked me in and I purchased the game on day one (very unusual for me). However, after reading the (thoughtful) negative reviews, I can't help but agree. It's quite repetitive, there isn't much in the way of playstyle choices, the enemies are simple, the powers aren't that exciting, and it's too easy.In spite of that, I actually enjoyed this game quite a bit. This game became a nice nightly ritual  for unwinding. After a certain threshold in figuring this game out, I could guarantee that I'd complete a dungeon everynight without a death. Procedural death labyrinths have always been too difficult for me to really enjoy, so this was a nice way of playing one in a positive mood.The first 2/3 of my progress, I kept exclaiming to myself "I love this game so much!" I prefer magic over guns and this has been my one of my favourite implementations in an FPS. It's so satisfying. This plus the gorgeous visuals (lighting, environment art, shaders) automatically made me fall in love. It doesn't hurt that the music fits the mood perfectly, especially combined with the juicy sound design.It was a joy to learn the system, from combining runes to choosing which motes to go for in the current run. It's a very well-put together game, but could have benefited from more variety or a smaller dose. Very happy with this and highly recommend it as long as you know what to expect.

_childDocuments_.review: Somewhere between an acid trip and an eldritch nightmare, this game was a great ride. It's pretty short, and there's no voiced dialogue, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. There was enough lore and story through dialogue and notes to keep me interested. The main meat and bones of this game are its fast-paced, small-scale levels, packed with nasties. You've got plenty of spells and upgrades for your arsenal, and I soon found myself getting into the swing of things with an enjoyable build. Great for when you just wanna shoot some ♥♥♥♥ without a massive time commitment. Good stuff!

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty great, tl;dr if it you like FPS and roguelites it's worth the money.Good- Movement feels good- Weapon variety is solid - sniper, rocket launcher, shotgun, smg, etc but in magic hand form- Combat in general is satisfying- Upgrades come pretty thick and fast in a run- Runs themselves are pretty speedy, easy to dip in and out of- Graphics are stylish, you can turn the crunch off if it's too muchNeutral- Areas can get a bit samey within the same biome, I don't find it an issue but some might- Upgrades are fairly simplistic, may not be satisfying for people looking for serious depth- Basic gameplay is the same all the way through - kill enemies > get motes > destroy keystones to finish a room, I find it fun but may get boring for people wanting variety- No looping, I just like looping when I get a good run going in a rogueliteBad- Bosses are pretty much all the same - big enemy, one or two ranged attacks, one aoe area denial attack. At 50% they go immune, summon waves of enemies, kill them and then kill the boss. No real variation.- Motes can sometimes be hard to see against the backdrops, wasting some time trying to hunt them down- There's some odd collision issues with some parts of the map, can occasionally get stuck - lucky 'exit to title' resets you back to before the room you were in - I believe the dev is aware there are some issues and is looking to try and fix

_childDocuments_.review: Good fun mixed with procedural generation and meta progression.Into The Pit asks you to select some Runes (think passive perks, which you can unlock and upgrade) and jump straight into Hell. Once there, you are tasked with charging a central teleporter (think level exit) by going into 4 different rooms. In each room, you are to destroy up to (so far) 4 Keystones. Finding them is simple, just look up at the sky for a glowing light. Getting to them, however, can be tricky. Enemies smack you, shoot you, poison you. Some rooms have traps and enemies. You have a left hand attack and a right hand attack that you select at the start of a floor. I personally go with a machine gun like spread on my left hand (left click), and a longer, more powerful shot on my right hand (right click). You can combine two, if two of the same kind appear during selection. In this dungeons you are recuing villagers. Remember how you have to clear 4 rooms to charge the exit to the level? Each room is a selection of 2 doors. The doors have the reward on them in symbols AND in text. If you are ever unsure of what a reward type is, or what your powers are for that matters, you can press I to go to your inventory and mouse over the information to learn what it does. Overall, the game is very fun. I played old school FPS games when I was a kid a long, long time ago. I'm not so much into them now, to be honest. But this game is a great spin on great ideas. You don't search for keys or back track, you just navigate fun levels and pew pew well designed enemies. Fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Into The Pit Steam Review #129 By HyPo Jeanuary von MesserschmittRating : 4/10When it comes to roguelike FPS games you expect a fun experience. This game failed to deliver in being fun. This is barely a roguelike. The level layouts are the same after an hour or two of playtime and they never change, not once. You only use one weapon with 4 or 5 different layouts. Enemy designs come off as basic and generic, Worth pointing out that enemy path finding is broken. Flying enemies walk up and down stairs for example instead of flying towards you. Levels are way too small and i would end up being stuck on the walls sometimes taking damage. The general gameplay loop is terrible for a roguelike if i am being dead honest. So you have runes that lead you to a new dungeon and you combine these runes to unlock new areas. So 15 dungeons and 45 villagers to rescue, the problem becomes when you end up fighting each boss expect the final one 5+ times. And you once you know what each logo means you can easily choose the area that take up the least amount of time to complete a depth. At depth 5 you fight a boss and bosses in this game are a joke. Usually they are very lame and it's the same for almost expect the last boss. So get the boss to half health, fight enemies that come out and then kill the boss. It's very easy and boring. Worth pointing out you can't hear enemies if you don't turn off the music and still you will have a hard time hearing enemies coming towards you, so you might be shooting at an enemy and you look around and the enemy is 2 or 3 meters away from you and you almost take damage. The enemies do have sound cues but you can barely hear them most of time, in the heat of battle. Combat is fun but too easy, you use different shooting layouts like fan or cannon for enemies which would be alright if there where more then 5 choices as previously mentioned. Ending was underwhelming as they i think teased a sequel and the game just ends with no conclusion to the story. Oh yeah this game has a story but it's very forgettable and they don't do anything to make the story stand out besides the gameplay loop.  This in a way feels more like a proof of concept demo to me but it has zero new ideas.  You fight the same enemies, play through same level layouts with the same few shooting layouts for a few hours, 100% completion took me 12.3 hours but a normal playthrough should take at 5 to 8 hours. There is no reason to go for the 100% unless you are an achievement hunter. So time to wrap the review up. What we have here in the package is the repetitive gameplay loop, samey level layouts,non existent story. It's ticks the box for me about being a terrible and underwhelming boomer shooter. Potential is there but they wasted it like a drunk sailor. And the optimization on integrated graphics was garbage,should have been better.A 4/10 seems like a good rating overall but if you don't like FPS games or roguelikes this will be nothing special. For those that like these types of games ,you will find a shallow and boring experience that you wish ,was better made since shooting feels good,story needs some work and the rest needs to be scrapped and made better. The rating might be high for some considering what i said, but it feels just right in the overall ,counting in everything department.

_childDocuments_.review: "Into the Pit" is a retro shooter, basically a ripoff of Heretic/Hexen, but with more limited gameplay concept and the developers didn't bother doing any content, it's all procgen.  Which is the chief reason this fails hard... they want $15 USD for a retro game without any content, and that must be a joke or something.  On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.The game features low-polygon "retro" assets with 2D retro pixel "art" textures on them, making this look like a barely functional 3D game from the early 1990s.  This very poor quality visual style is a method that lazy devs often use to disguise their lack of talent/interest in doing the graphics properly and trying to disguise it under the name of "art", or "We made it look bad on purpose", which really isn't something gamers should have to put up with. I know this is a definitely deliberate decision to make a boomer shooter, but it doesn't work well, especially because of the ugly and inauthentic blur filter over the game.  It looks bad as a result of their decisions, worse, it doesn't authentically recreate the 1990's vibe the developer is hoping people will accept instead of doing their job properly, and that's just another reason to avoid it.The game features no proper level design or game/story flow/plot, as they opted to try to use samey repetitive procgen algorithms as a substitute for adding such content to the game, to avoid doing the important job of level/map design.  As a result, the game doesn't actually have any content worth mentioning, just endless, boring, repetitive, soulless algorithmically generated sameyness.  Developers must learn that procedural generation is not an acceptable substitute for content.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game."Into the Pit" didn't appeal much to the people who own a copy of the game, either.  It has achievements, and they show us a very clear picture that the game didn't really capture any interest from gamers.  The most commonly and easily attained achievement is for collecting 100 "Motes of Wealth", trivial to get, but less than 21 percent of players bothered to get that far before uninstalling the game.  Hardly a success story, gamers just weren't all that interested in the game.The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?"Into the Pit" has the cash grab price of $15 USD, for which you could easily get any number of older AAA games.  Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, this is impossible to recommend.  For comparison, the $15 asking price for this game could get you games like "Doom Eternal", "Prey" or "Final Fantasy XIV Online".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.
