_childDocuments_.review: I imagined this to be a fun rogue-lite magician boomer shooter.Combine spells to create a new one, level up, collect loot/resources and gain random buffs etc.But it turned out to be not that.Spells are all pretty samey especially in their visual style (you basically ever shood shard-like projectiles in different colors with an occasional orb spread inbetween), not you shooting lightning out of your hands, not you flamethrowing, placing magma on the floor, swirling enemies away with windforce, no poison cloud or throwing rocks in their face.You simply get the equivalents of sniper/assault rifle, SMG and Shotgun shot out of your hands.Boring.Its also all arena based and they repeat pretty fast, some arenas are even pretty bothersome.Its all timepressured too, no real looting or gathering either, meta progression is boring, because the spells you get are boring.You can have some hours of fun, but its insane how much potential was wasted here.Especially in a time where loot-extractor shooters and the action-rogue-like are two of the more popular design ideas floating around, this could have been a great singleplayer variant of Brotato mixed with Zero Sievert.Instead its a generic arena shooter with repeating contents.I say get Crab Champions instead. _childDocuments_.review: Fun little roguelite shooter, its nothing groundbreaking, but the core gameplay is pretty addicting. Into The Pit instantly draws attention with its unique and colorful retro visuals, but its the gameplay that kept me playing for almost 8 hours straight.Your weapons are spells which you choose at the start of each run, one spell for each hand. There is a wide variety of spells to choose from, but unfortunately your "weapons" always look the same, its just hands with different colors. Using them however is pretty satisfying. You can shred your enemies with barrage of magic missiles, blow them up with bomb spell or take them out from long distance using concentrated magic shot, just to name a few spells at your disposal.Enemy variety is pretty good, you face different monsters depending on the location you chose at the start of the run. I didn't find combat that challenging, as its easy to keep your distance thanks to your high mobility and speed. Still, it was satisfying to blow all manner of monsters into the bloody chunks.I think what makes Into The Pit so addicting is its core gameplay loop of 1-3 minutes of combat, short downtime to choose rewards, decide which room to do next, more combat, rinse repeat. Sound boring, but it actually works quite well, thanks to the variety of locations and constant stream of new perks keeping things fresh.Each run consists of 4 floors, each with 4 different mini dungeons to clear, which grant new perks upon completion. After clearing all 4 floors you face the boss of the dungeon. These bosses were pretty generic and rather easy, but it was a decent way to finish each run. Every time you start a run you need to select runes you'll take with you (health boost, resistance to poison, more gold, etc.) and dungeon variant that will determine the location's layout and enemy variety. Its interesting how you can mix these variants with each other, as it makes locations look like they got warped and twisted with each other.Between runs you visit the village where you can upgrade your runes, buy new ones and buy keys to new locations. It a bog standard progression, nothing to write home about. Another unremarkable aspect of this game is its music and sounds. Music is pretty bad and gets repetitive fast, while sound effects often sound weak and make some of your powerful spells sound like you just hit a ghoul with a wet sock. I recommend using your own music, it really enchances the power fantasy.Overall I think Into The Pit is worth a buy, its fun, simple roguelike with interesting visuals and solid gameplay loop. Its not especially challenging or deep, but its easy to look at and offers fluid gameplay with some satisfying mechanics. I'm quite interested in what these developers try next, as there is a lot of potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 2/3 Recommend. I shall explain why after describing the core of Into The Pit. It is a first-person shooter were you play a sorceror descending into a fiendish Pit to rescue villagers and find out what happened to those who descended before you. To some degree, the maps are randomized. Each level of a descent - or a run - is comprised of 4 chambers. Complete the 4 chambers, descend to the next level, or return with your gains in resources to the village. Then upgrade the village for persistent boons. Merchants, keymakers, etc. offer you help commensurate with the number of villagers you have saved to date. The game very much is in the spirit of Heretic. Your "magic" consists of projectile spells tagged for the duration of your run to each hand. Every completion of a chamber allows you to apply an upgrade to your abilities. : Into The Pit's demo is fun and promises great things in an extended 1.0 full game. Unfortunately, if you play the demo, you've pretty much appreciated everything Into The Pit is going to offer you. In the full version, no new spell types, no persistent boosts to abilities, and the few upgrades to your run modifiers are pretty straightforward, as well as quickly obtained. The vast quantities of persistent resources you accumulate serve no purpose... you max out whatever you can in short order, with nothing further to look forward to. The most disappointing village aspect has to be the unlocking of the "Merchant". Aha, you think - now I can purchase persistent equipment and/or spells and/or spell upgrades for further spelunking. But el-POOF-o, no such thing is to be found... instead this "Merchant" is simply a resource convertor. Resources for which you long ago ran out of uses for. Too bad: all sorts of potential here to deepen enjoyment, including equipment, potions & scrolls, spells & spell modifiers/boosts, levels comprised of more than 4 chambers, additional chamber objectives, villager consequence, etc. . Into The Pit is pretty good, and it *could* be interesting to see what the developer does next. Ziggurat 2 is the better & more rewarding experience. Love fps action games with rpg depth and long-term replayability. Into The Pit is a 2/3 entry though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to pretty much mirror other negative reviews I've read. In short, the game looks pretty and has some potential but seriously lacks depth and staying power. I wanted to like this game because it looks cool and, in theory, could be fun, but in the face of reality I just can't.This is probably my biggest complaint, which others have said - I very rapidly saw everything there was to see and had nothing new or interesting to try. Unlike other roguelike/lites I've played, I felt that my choices had no impact on how I played in any given run. The list of "weapon" choices is short and none of the upgrades meaningfully changed their behavior - they're the same no matter which "weapon" you choose and are all pretty much just different forms of "do more damage". Poison and Bleed felt like the worst offenders, doing too little damage too slowly, and with some mobs inexplicably immune to them. I was never getting a list of upgrades and going "Yeah, I want that!" - it was more like, "Ugh alright I guess I'll take that". None of the upgrades I saw can be used to build on each other, to something greater and more interesting than the vanilla you started with. There was no potential for interaction, creating interesting combos, or new abilities and play styles.Some smaller notes:- Terrain collision physics or code or whatever is, frankly, inexcusable. The number of times I got stuck on little terrain artifacts, doodads, and the like and nearly (or did) die is really aggravating. In particular, falling into hazard rivers was pretty much a death sentence, since you get stuck on the corner as you fall, take tons of damage while you're stuck, and cannot move or jump to get out.- Rescuing villagers felt bloated and grindy rather than rewarding - unlocking anything required an obnoxious number of villagers rescued and I didn't care long enough to actually do it.- The graphics did not look as smooth and refined actually playing the game as they do in screenshots and footage. There were times I felt more like I was playing the original Quake than a game that came out in 2021.- I felt there were a lot of really cheap monster spawns, popping up directly in your face once you enter an area, or from around a corner in a tiny nook.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and love fast paced games, that get harder, then you should at the very least check out the demo. I just unlocked a new area with mushrooms and was immediately screaming out with glee about how awesome they were. Lots of amazing things in this game too, from awesome sensitivity options (thanks for a really fast max speed - perfect!), to very awesome UI design choices. In fact let me stop and say, the menu/UI choices, are so clever and easy to understand, that your brain will literally make simple connections for you and then your psyche will eventually be like, "Yo I see what the dev did there, clever!" a few seconds later.I started with the demo back on October 6th, I was like ruh-oh, when i thought it was gunna be a reading game with text boxes and missions. To my delight it was nothing like that, at all. Then an hour in I was in love with SIMPLE but EFFECTIVE FPS gaming again. Clever design choices all around too. One thing I would 100% recommend doing, if you're like me and play on a max brightness screen, go into the graphics settings and turn off every box. To me the game looks even more amazing then. Fun fact, 3 hours ago I was stripping down getting ready for bed, then a dude on Discord was like hey man, you could review it now eh!? Jump forward a few hours and I now want to stay up and play it more and more, as just discovering new areas and enemies, I'm excited. Can't wait to come back and play this tomorrow. To the dev, amazing job man, amazing! To everyone else, give the demo a shot. I did, and as someone who tries new games and adds them to my wishlist often, but doesn't buy 99% of them at launch, I'm honestly so glad I just had 'that feeling' and trusted myself and bought Into The Pit when Steam sent me the email saying it was released (kinda shows you how much the demo is worth playing eh ;-) ) It's 100% my cuppa tea and would recommend it to everyone. Just don't go in expecting Fortknuckle or Call of Terribad and you'll likely be pleasantly surprised :-D

_childDocuments_.review: Neat GameI love the art-style, and the modelling on the town is fantastic. Dungeon tilesets are well made, but due to the procedural generation of the levels, they can't be quite as detailed as the ritual room in town, which is unfortunate.This game lets you get pretty Godlike fairly easily, so it is fun for that.If the enemies had a little bit more strategy to how they attacked you, or how you have to approach them, it could make the combat a lot more engaging. (maybe they do later, but the enemies in the first dungeon, and the Obsidian Docks kind of seem to just run at you or stand around and shoot)The audio is fine for the most part, but the spells lack any sense of impact or power. All the ones I've used so far have very "pewy" sounds. Some extra crunch on the spell audio would be awesome. Enemies have nice crunchy death sounds though, which makes them satisfying to mow through, and mow through you will! As I mentioned earlier, this game makes you feel very powerful. When you're at your best you'll be flying through the levels, destroying enemies just as fast as you can see them. If you're not careful they can take you out fairly quick, so keep moving! (I have only played using the Calamity Rune, which doubles incoming damage in exchange for bonus rewards)As it stands, Into the Pit is a fun experience, and I'll definitely play more of it, but I see the potential for true greatness just beneath the surface. As far as I can see the game is in full release, so I don't expect major changes, but for the asking price of $15, you'll get your money's worth out of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is super fun and interesting enough to keep you going for a few hours.  The soundtrack and overall sound design do a great job of building tension.  The graphics and palette choices just work, for such a colorful game its feels dark, adding to the overall immersion.  The FPS mechanics are tight, but the choice for a "walk" key is puzzling; we'd have been better serve to dash mechanic like in DOOM.  Some people complain about doo-dads on the walls but at least it adds some difficulty in a game that needs it.Its a package of aesthetics and fun that draws you in, at least initially.  But the game doesn't have a lot of staying power.  After about an hour you've seen all the game has to offer.  The game play reminds me of Doom 2016's monster arenas, and there's not that much variety for a game that's procedural, and its a stretch IMO to compare this to any kind of rogue like.This is a good base for a game, but for what it has its not worth it.  Its a good base for a game but its not enough.  It feels more like a tech demo or an art project.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could like it as much as I did in the first 30 - 60 minutes of playing it - but sadly that's not possible with all the flaws that you spot in your first 2 - 3 hours of gameplay.The first 2 - 3 runs are quite enjoyable, but after that you've seen most the game has to offer, the visual style is something different and nice, gameplay feels good and (for the most part) smooth, bad design decisions killed the replayability, lacks content for the current price tag (15€), if you can get it for ~2-3€ give it a try.- It has a pretty interesting and unique visual style- Movement feels pretty good for a "fast" roguelike (except for a common "bug", more further down)- Your choice of weapons/spells is okay-ish, but after a few runs you mostly stick with your trusted combos, since there's no real benefit in using different combinations of spells, since they don't interact in any way.You can break them easily down into: Assault rifle, Sniper, 3-burst rifle, shotgun, mid-range shotgun and a rocket launcher.- There isn't much content to explore, after visiting all of the 6 main dungeons only once (takes ~2-3h) I've literally seen every single possible upgrade, monster, boss, room / floor layout, weapon and meta-progress-upgrade.- The choice of upgrades you are presented with is way too basic and boring - "wow, 15% flat dmg boost, never seen that one before", same goes for everything else, mostly flat bonuses to either crit %, crit dmg, movement speed, dmg while below / above % hp and so on...- Boss battles are a joke, they may have different designs and 1 or 2 different abilities, but the whole fight boils down to: jump around them in a circle while clicking LMB and RMB and wait for their HP to slowly make their way down to 0- For a game that seems to be pretty focused on (fast) movement it still features a few unpleasant bugs in that regard, especially the following: > Some walls got some nice decor on them, the downside to it is that you can get caught in it and have to wait to either slowly glide to the floor, or die to enemies that just keep attacking you.> After clearing a floor you have to wait quite a few seconds before picking up your upgrade, otherwise the game sorta softlocks you in the "Choose your upgrade"-screen and you have to force-close the game and restart it (which also makes you miss out on said upgrade)- The only point I kept from my original review is that the game is  - in my 4h of playtime ( + a few hours in the Demo) I've literally never died once, even taking a rune that doubles my damage taken.- After clearing around 6 Dungeons there isn't much to do anymore - I've literally bought everything possible, upgraded everything as far as possible and am only missing the last villagers, which would require you to grind for at least a bit, without any other reason than to get to your 45 / 45 villagers.- The price just doesn't match the amount of content you receive, 15€ for a game that provides around 2-5h of fun just doesn't feel right to me.

Across eight episodes, you’ll forge friendships and create rivals, all in the name of developing the best dodgeball team. _childDocuments_.review: 100% achievement No. Yes (~19 achievements). No. is a sports RPG game about dodgeball with fantasy elements. You'll play in a team of 1 to 3 players, fighting against up to 6 enemies. It offers both story and versus mode, but since there isn't much to cover in the versus mode, this review will focus on the story, single-player mode instead.- A lot of playable characters with different stats and mechanics- Scalable difficulty through the options menu- Child-friendly- Various minigames to improve your dodgeball skills- Fights can be repetitive sometimes- Inactive characters are not controlled by AI- Difficulty in switching charactersIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The combination between 3D backgrounds and 2D characters blends very well in the game. They both give a cute look, presenting the visuals with simple-looking 3D backgrounds and cartoonish 2D characters. The interface is also in sync with this style, giving you the same look while still showing everything that you need on a single screen without overloading you with too much information.The story lacks depth, but it's enough to keep you going. That doesn't mean that it is lacking in dialogues though. A lot of nonsensical, trivial dialogues are presented by the main cast to move the story forward. Each character also has a different personality, giving a unique view of their attempt at each struggle that they are facing. Their carefree, outgoing personality will surely give smiles on your face.As someone who does not know anything about dodgeball,  does a good job of explaining the rules. I'm not sure whether the game has the whole rule embedded in the game, but the gameplay is simple enough: you have to grab a ball, whether by catching a thrown ball or picking it up from the ground, and throw it to the enemy until they run out of HP while dodging their attacks that comes your way. Additional rules will be added as you play the game, adding more challenges to it.The gameplay forces you to focus on one character. Although you'll start playing solo, more players will be added to the screen, allowing you to play with up to three players on the court. However, switching characters can be annoying due to the unnecessary extra button that you need to press. I ended up playing as , the main character, most of the time and only switched to another player whenever he needs healing.The lack of AI on your side makes the game more complicated than it should be. You'll often play in a party of three, with you having to control all characters at the same time. Moving in any direction will also move all players at once, although some actions like charging your ultimate move bar and unleashing it can only be done by the active player on the front. However, all players on the enemy side don't work the same way - they all can move separately from the other, allowing them to unleash attacks from all sides. This makes it hard to dodge their attacks, especially if you only focus on controlling the active player.All characters have different stats and abilities. More characters will join your group as you progress, allowing you to create a party of three from 6 players. Each character can be played differently from the rest, whether it's their ultimate move, mechanics, or even movement. However, the game hardly gives you a chance to try out other characters, and as someone who usually sticks to the first few characters that are given to you, the latter three characters that I got were buried in the roster. Sure, there might be one occasion where you are stripped off some characters, but that doesn't change much since I ended up focusing more on the main character instead.Combat can be repetitive at times. The game seems to have inspiration for  in battles with it having enemies waiting on the premises to challenge you for a battle. However, the optional battles can be tedious due to their number and level. You only need to dish out the same strategy over and over to beat them, allowing you to get some money and exp. Although you don't need to do these battles, you might risk being low-leveled in a certain area, and since the game has a fixed number of enemies before you reach a certain point in the game, you are forced to fight them all to make sure you are not underleveled.The game can turn into a bullet hell sometimes. Some matches can have more than 5 balls in the court, giving more havoc to the field. It's up to you whether you want to unleash all balls to the enemy side or keep them all but one not to get overwhelmed with all the dodging, but keeping the ball for a long time will make you lose its handle, allowing the enemy to grab it. Moreover, the ultimate move can be troublesome sometimes, especially since you need to dodge a barrage of balls that are thrown at you or risk getting a lot of damage.Both allies and enemies have different throwing patterns, whether it's a straight one, a curved one, or others. Some throwing patterns are also hard to catch, and the difference in the throwing speeds between some characters can throw off your tempo if you want to catch everything. It helps to keep you focused in the game, especially after doing all those optional, repetitive battles.I finished the game in 14.2h. The game can be challenging at times, but it allows a quick button to replay the match if things go south. If you found it to be too difficult or too easy, you can also change the damage taken and/or damage dealt modifier through the options. Personally, I found the difficulty to be alright. Most fights are easy to beat while some might give you trouble, forcing you to retry the match several times before you can beat them.The game is a mix between , , and dodgeball. As someone who has been looking for another sports RPG game since the  in the , this game does a good job of sating my thirst. It has the same core feature as that game, namely a story mode and the openly explorable areas. Sadly, the game doesn't seem to support a co-op story mode despite offering up to three players on the field at the same time.As a sports game, the game does a good job to make it unique and memorable. The core gameplay and additional fantasy elements blend well together while still giving you various mechanics to keep you engaged. It was satisfying to see new throwing styles and/or ultimate moves that are thrown at you, or even the whole chaos that happens due to having a lot of active balls at the same time. Still, I wish it doesn't end this soon though - I surely will miss playing this game and definitely would recommend playing it if you like to play sports games with superpowers.

_childDocuments_.review: The very first thing that just pops from this game is the artstyle. Absolutely colorful and vibrant environment, and the character designs look inspired by modern cartoons just from the simple shapes. Not too saturated that it hurts to see, so it's just a right amount of balance, especially giving all the characters a little more contrast making them really stand out off and on matches.If you played other sports rpgs like Golf Story or even the Mario sport rpgs made from Camelot, you'll definitely see the resemblance. Main story, side quests into matches, fetch quests etc, traditional stuff.All the characters are just so goofy that you can not not hate them. Just like the game is trying to look, it pulls off a charming and cute vibe that everyone follows suit. Lines may be cheesy but nobody is trying to pull off a super serious tone, so everybody acts kinda silly and it's alright.The mechanics for playing dodgeball are actually pretty fun, and sometimes intense. Probably the only gripe i have right now is fixing the detection of when you can catch or counter a ball. The animation that plays when you attempt to catch does not align well of when you can  catch. I miss being early more times than being late and it just seems that the ball has to be point blank range and would help if the game was just a tiny bit more more lenient than eating another attack of what you thought would connect, just didn't happened because of the game mechanics. One suggestion would be that if you were early in catching or countering, you would be knocked back or become dizzy, just enough for the other player to have another opportunity and then the opposing player would have to react much faster. Other than that, the gameplay is pretty spot on, nothing too complex, but also not too simple where it just seems you can just mash the throw button. I love that you can strategize for matches, as i thought there wouldn't be much to add but i was wrong. Equipment with different powerups, different team members, various abilities, ultimate finishers, playing the offensive and defensive in certain match ups, plan ahead with current HP, charging the ball, and even countering the ball. It's in-depth enough that it's not just mindless throwing and you really have to be engaged or you'll just be pummeled hard. It doesn't favor reckless or tactical playstyles, just know that you do have to defend just as good to be surviving.I can't get enough the artstyle, as if the game is an adaptation from a recent CN show, very cartoony and very good. If you like the charming, goofy, and zany characters, vibrant artstyle, or loving chucking dodgeballs, you'll really love this.

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball RPG.  This concept pleases my inner child, and Pocket Trap delivered. This game is stylish, endearing, and smashes your face with exhilarating gameplay.Dodgeball Academia's super electrifying visual style is distinct and colorful, with 2D animation that explodes with personality and reminds me of cartoons from the '90s and early 2000s.Otto is such a likeable and vibrant character. He's always eager to play some dodgeball and show what he's capable of, but first and foremost, he's there to have fun and make friends, and he never lets go of that fire in his heart. He also has this very iconic look that I really like. He'd make a great shounen anime protagonist.The rest of the main cast is also really cool and memorable, thanks to creative designs, charming dialogue, and grounded storytelling keeping it real.The main tunes are super catchy and will rock your socks off. They're vibrant and exciting like a sunny day. The soundtrack fits perfectly with this game's summerlike atmosphere, and I love it. It just feels nice to spend time in this comfy little world overflowing with good vibes.Easy to learn, hard to master. Just how I like it.The controls are immediately intuitive; it's a game about dodging and throwing balls. But there's more to it than that. The more you play, the more you'll uncover the underlying depth. Improving at the game is very rewarding, because each second of gameplay matters; there's never a dull moment. is a really fun mechanic, because it rewards you for not hogging all the balls and keeps the game going. There's also a hot potato mechanic. The game is actually really well thought-out, it has an excellent flow. The RPG progression on top of all that results in a very engrossing experience where you can customize each character to your liking.Just a small thing, but I like how each character has food preferences, and even allergies. It's a nice touch that makes the characters feel more real. I also like In terms of scale and concept, this game is most comparable to , which is really the only other sports RPG that comes to mind. If you enjoyed that game, I think you'll find this one to your liking as well, and vice versa.In terms of mood, this is a very uplifting game that makes me feel reinvigorated and happy. I think the soundtrack has a lot to do with that. The first Splatoon had a similar refreshing effect on me. It almost feels like watching Pokémon as a kid. I don't know how else to describe it, but it's a warm nostalgic sensation.In terms of style, an RPG with 2D sprites in a colorful 3D environment always reminds me of Paper Mario, so that's always a good thing. One of the later characters even has an ultimate that is taken straight from Mario RPGs, it's really fun.I almost forgot to mention this very important thing: I played the entire game in French and it was delightful. A lot of love clearly went into the translation, as there are many clever jokes, wordplays or simply funny lines that were made specifically for each language. That kind of genuine effort to make a good game doesn't go unnoticed by me.Speaking of language, there's a really neat function in this game called "bilingual mode", which allows you to instantly change the game's language at any time simply by pressing a button. If you do it during dialogue, you'll be able to see that dialogue in another language at the bottom of the screen.When I first saw this game, I could immediately tell it was a passion project made with love. There hasn't  a Dodgeball RPG before; this game is wholly unique and full of soul. I'm very grateful for it. Here's hoping it won't take 16 years before we get another sports RPG this good...In short, video games are awesome and so are you.

_childDocuments_.review: Beaten the game and everything completed. Here are my pros and cons.Pros>Charming and beautiful game with an easy to follow humor filled story. Animation also looks so good that it's highly comparable to a saturday morning cartoon.>Lovable characters each with his/her own personality and unique playstyle.>Simple to understand rpg mechanics. It's not trying to be overly complicated or pretentious.>Fun, addicting, combat has variety in the form of elemental dodgeballs, court hazards, dynamic rules, and even the enemies has his or her own playstyle to keep you guessing and forces you to adapt to the situation.>Challenging without it also being too frustratingly difficult. Although you do face some difficulty spikes and get your butt handed to you by cheap enemies, but they're also too far between to worry about. >Lots of cool items and equipments to collect. There are variety of equipments to cater to everyone's playstyles.>Game has a built in difficulty slider which makes the game really accessible to everyone and gives you the ability to customize the game's difficulty to your likings.Cons>Too short.>Game world is too small, so there isn't really that much to explore in this game. It also makes the game too linear since there isn't really much to go anywhere else but the objective.>Game's settings is still a bit lacking like being able to reassign button controls.>Combat is similar to a game called super dodgeball on neogeo/arcade back in the 90s which means you don't have any help of an ai and you're forced to control all three players simultaneously. This would have been fine and balance overall if the same rules also applies to the enemies which it doesn't. While your party is locked to moving simultaneously each enemy can move and do things individually. For me this was a pretty unfair and a weird combat mechanics decision by the devs imo. >No online pvp but would have been nice if it did have one.All in all It's still a well crafted game and I freaking love playing every minute of it. It shows the hardwork and care that the devs poured into their game. I hope there is a sequel or another game from the same developers in the future. This is a 9/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia® is a light game fun for the whole family.Programming, graphics and story line is fun, engaging, and light without any bad language or chaotic references.This game I played for four(4) hours with my six year old son, and we had some quality father and son time laughing and playing innocent dodgeball.If you want a laugh, have a bit of a challenge, and enjoy some innocent light competition while being bashed in the beak, then this is right up your pie hole!The controls will get kind of difficult and we hope they allow remapping because the layout is unorthodox and difficult for the little ones. Definite help from adults as things progress, but still the light heart of the game, is fun for all ages.Just one thing... don't get caught key smashing, because once things get going... you will have a hard time.My six year old played with me doing basic throwing and such until chapter 2. Then was very hard for him and started taking some of the fun away. So we stopped.. and did it for real. Put lumps on my head quicker than I could run them!Get it today and have a good time with your family! Not demanding on any pc setup!
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic is super fun, but game itself feels half-baked. Combat never gets much more skillful than the reflex test of catching/dodging balls - your characters have slightly different moves and there are ostensibly different rulesets, but they all play largely the same. Matches are made more difficult by making them less legible, crowding the small arena with extra balls and characters with unclear hitboxes. There's not much beyond the matches - outside of combat, you're mostly just walking back and forth across campus to battle for a mission and then turn it back in to the quest-giver. Past the core gameplay, there are a number of smaller complaints; clumsy menus, the balls you use for opening chests disappearing when you load a game, and mechanics that might be bugs or might be intentional but entirely unexplained. It's a short game, which makes the flaws a little more tolerable, but it's really hard to recommend at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me feel and wanting to be young again.Dodgeball Academia is what it sounds and more. You play as a student named Otto who's goal is to become the very best through hard work and friendship. Sounds cheesy, but the dialogue is so well written, you can catch many clever references. And even though the character's personalities is somehwat cliche, I loved them! "GO CRUSH THEM, MINA!"The graphics are an excellent blend of 2D characters in a 3D environment. Gameplay is incredibly smooth and it will remind you of Pokemon a lot even though it's very different. It's dodgeball themed  and if anyone loves dodgeball, this is by far the best of its kind.In simple terms you run around throwing and dodging balls. Of course there's more. You control your character and the potential additional 2 members of your team which they do not move on their own with exception if they are on the knockout zones. If you are good with them, you can control them efficiently as they will catch balls the same way you do, pick them up and automatically pass them to you, or pass to your teammate, doing that will switch your main character in control.When you start doing the campaign, you might think it's pretty easy and repetitive , but thorought the campaign, you'll see how the tables start turning on you. This game has a disguise of being luck based but it actually involves a lot of skill. Being able to predict, time your strikes and catching just right, dodging at the right moments, etc...The campaign length is about 15-20hrs long, so this will definitely take you a few days to finish it.I had to legitimately cheat my way through several battles, because it was this much HARD! Oh and those "Balltimate moves", this was some Undertale level of dodging required. I'd definitely had to cheat more if I wouldn't have leveled up through completing all of the side missions. The soundtrack by the way is rocktastic!Oh and even though there's no multiplayer, you can play versus mode with a friend through Steam's Remote play together feature. So if you have plans to play this against a friend, then the game is definitely worth its full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: As an action game, it's not great.  If you were missing "Super Dodgeball" on the NES (as I do)... look elsewhere.You don't have much space to maneuver, hit boxes are unpredictable, the AI behaves in a really unsatisfying way (it kind of just decides to get hit or not, irrelevant of whether you make a "good throw"), timing catches is super important and super bland, and animations/stuns take too long and feel frustrating.  They needed to work on the core action game here and make it tight and fast, then add gimmicks.  Instead, it feels like the action was constrained by "art/design" vision, and then they tried to rescue the resulting terrible action game with a pile of gimmicks.If you do asymmetrical fights: players should be fast and agile, but weak; while AI opponents should be slower and more predictable, but stronger.  That tends towards satisfying gameplay where you are consistently outplaying the game in order to make progress.  This game is often getting that backwards (your opponent is more agile and is "playing better" than you... and you just rely on them sometimes eating a shot for no reason) and ending up with aggressively crappy encounters.As an RPG, it's very low effort.  Writers seem to have got directions like "You know, just do some sport-anime (and or comedy RPG) nerd tropes", and the writers and artists just kind of phoned that in.  If you were looking for "Super Mario RPG" type stuff here, you're also in for disappointment.Little stuff: Somehow they messed up the button tempo of speeding through dialog, so as you tap you're either going "pretty slow" or "missing stuff".  I wish these games would just have an option like "Don't animate dialog text".  (I apologize if that exists and I missed it... to be honest I started just "full skipping" the dialog here and don't feel like I'm missing much).  Dialog in general feels like all setup and no punchline.  Like they did all the "goofy character" archetypes, but forgot to have them do or say anything actually entertaining.  I dutifully sat through the first few days of dialog, and I don't remember a single fun story moment.Playing it feels choppy and slow.  Lots of area transitions/loads when I feel like there could be none given simple-asset art style.  Rolling around the map you are always bumping into some tiny edge, changing what should be satisfying speed into frustrating tedium.  Why can't you roll up hills?  Was that going to be game breaking?  Realism?  The post fight screens don't take long to go through in an absolute sense... but they're also absolutely uninteresting so it'd be nice if you could push through the faster.  Speaking of time, did the players really need persistent health in areas where they can just run back to hospital between fights?  Just feels like wasting player time.Why isn't there mini-maps for some indoor areas?  Why aren't "navigatable areas" more clear on the mini-map?  While the overall look of the game is polished, playing it feels very raw and slow.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: While the game takes a while to get going with a lot of tutorials, it gets a lot better as more mechanics are unlocked. While it seems like just a simple dodgeball game there are a decent amount of mechanics to mix things up. Character specific abilities, charging moves, charge throws and elemental attributes. This makes it more than just simple dodgeball. There's a neat world to wander around in, some quests and busy work and a bit of a story to keep things moving along. Art style is colorful and appealing. About 5 hours in and the plot is opening up. It borrows some ideas from Pokemon for sure, including fighting for badges and the tournament system. Very fun and good in short bursts, and the game has a cool sense of humor. A note to devs: Please add AI to the versus mode, it's rather lacking in features atm for solo players. Also you get stuck in versus mode atm and need to Alt+F4 to exit as there's no UI option to exit that mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most charming and innovative JRPGs I've seen in a while. Everything in it just oozes polish and charm. The character designs are AMAZING (I love Ballooney!), the effects, the music, it just feels like a great saturday morning cartoon that just happens to be playable. And the gameplay is satisfying too - light RPG elements with smooth and responsive controls for a super cool dodgeball combat system.If any part of this (the visuals, the characters, the dodgeball school concept) interests you, just do yourself a favor and buy this game.(+style points for the Yu Yu Hakusho references!)
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm really loving it.Funny, lots of charm and beautiful art direction;I'm a fan of RPGs, and Action RPGs even more so, but it's not rare to see their gameplay become too simple and boring. Dodgeball, on the other hand, is proving to be a great way to keep battles interesting. Plus, I'm still early into the game but I already got a taste of what the difficulty curve has in store and I'm looking forward to play this one to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: The main character, like your usual protagonist is optimistic, empathic and ambitious. Paired with enjoyable and savage characters on their humorous dialogues. This game dont take itself seriously.Giving off a vibes of a tv cartoon mixed with rpg and sports. Has a colorful environment which is just balanced and not too much for the eyes.Gameplay itself is fast paced, absolutely fun hitting and releasing incredible powers to your opponents.An incredibly fun sports-rpg game with humorous dialogues set in a school for dodgeball and each students have unique abilities. What's there to miss?
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: This game is basically one of those sports movies you see, a protagonist must overcome numerous factors to become the champion of dodgeball, and while it may seem dumb, it works incredibly well. This game is straight-up amazing, it's a semi-short game (It took me 16 hours to 100% complete it), but it's got adorable visuals, funny writing, and amazing combat. Just playing this game makes me want to play dodgeball. To anybody reading this, I really recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: I recommended, but it's a HEAVILY mixed recommended.A vibrant, upbeat and colourful presentation.  Gives a combination of Cartoon Network and Cliche Shonen Anime vibes, specifically, OK K.O.! Let's Be Heroes, which I certainly don't mind.  Love that colour scheme.Very varied cast of characters, of all shades, shapes and such (oh species too how about that), but don't get your hopes up thinking your favourite may be playable.Humour can be hit or miss, as mentioned up top, has a rather cliche and corny plot to it, it is very un-serious with it's plot so if you want a funny little game then it certainly gets the job done, definitely drags since it's not serious and is surely an RPG to it's core, gotta get your moneys worth in slight variations of the same fight.Matches most of the time are pretty high action whether you try to avoid getting it, stall for that special, or even psyche out the opponent.  CPU's are at least quite varied both in technique and colour scheme.  However the game play is EXTREMELY repetitive (1% Pokemon inspired, some may understand this), with plenty of attempts to have different courts, status ailments and dodge ball types to keep it a little interesting with some maybe relying on half focus half luck that you aren't beaten into a corner or met with the very often dog piles that overpower the catch mechanics most of the time.  Pray you aren't stuck with dodge or counter when you REALLY don't want it.Versatile options to make the match go in your favour, but some mechanics work better than others, some not all that well.The battles can be a little cluttered since you may need to command a group of three that try to move glued together most of the game, which can often betray the whole idea of dodging with 2 big targets stuck to you.Music is upbeat, powerful and has that Shonen college rock n' roll vibe to it for sure, very fitting.  Eventually you run out of tracks to hear in actual fights regardless of how important the match is, some extra would've been nice.Probably way more fun with a friend (No online sadly, local play only, strange), you'll have to work to get all the characters available first, but if you want to give it a shot, maybe just wish list it and wait for a big discount or if you have nothing left to play, good for 3-4 on and off days of not doing anything else.Shonen
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: A combination of action and RPG mechanics during dodgeball matches. The game takes place at a school for fledgling dodgeball players. Good art style and entertaining writing with fun basic gameplay. Although the more random RPG/Pokemon style battles you run into tend to offer little to no challenge and rarely do anything interesting, they start to become more tedious. Some well done difficulty options where you can make yourself or your opponent do anywhere from 1 to 400% damage if you wanted to make things easier, more difficult, or just have longer or shorter matches can improve those battles though.Gives you little options in the way of multiplayer or co-op. Multiplayer is only going to be local or with invited friends and characters need to be unlocked by going through the single player game, poor character selection in multiplayer where you are just cycling through them to set them on court rather than being able to see what their stats, abilities, and passives for the level you set everyone to are. Not even an option for one team to be computer controlled so you can just set up the court, dodgeballs, and players of your choice.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly creative and fun game that's largely self-aware and feels great to play.The RPG sports genre is one of those highly underappreciated styles of games that lay down a great framework for telling a story. With a cast of colourful and whimsically written characters, it's a recipe for success. The lovingly crafted aesthetic that combines 2D and 3D graphics only helps accentuate all the other great things it's already doing. Even the little touches of how the text behaves really allows characters voices to shine through despite a lack of voice acting.The gameplay itself is snappy, intuitive, responsive, and simple enough that it just makes for a fun experience. There's a simplistic depth about controlling 3 characters at once, especially given that each character possesses different stats, abilities, and playstyles.I don't know, it's just a great time. A seriously great time.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of classic dodgeball games such as:All-Star Slammin' D-BallSuper Robot Taisen Battle DodgeBallSuper Dodgeball BrawlersI wanted to play a modern arcade dodgeball game but couldn't find any until I came across this game.I liked the artstyle, the music and the most important part "the gameplay". The artstyle is really unique and reminds me of the cartoon network artstyle. The music is amazing and the beats suits the game style. The gameplay is surprisingly good for a dodgeball game. There are different characters with different play styles, all the way from regular throws to the special move, some characters can't jump but can dodge which vary them from other characters.When I first started the game, I jumped straightly to versus mode, there was nothing but one character, and I thought the game was not that good after all. However, I unlocked everything after completing the story mode and versus mode became a banger.The story mode is good and have good writing. It took me around 10 hours to complete the story mode. It gets repetitive after a while.My only complains about this game is the repetitiveness at the end of the game and the versus mode UI. Other than that, good game, highly recomended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can best be summed up in: The devs had a lot of heart and made a really stylised unique game with terrible controls and horrid gameplay.Now the long story. I will try to go as indepth with this as i can for both people that are interested in this as well as the developers themselves, if they were ever to see this review, which i doubt but, hey, maybe they do. This is a Dodge-ball RPG. And it works how you think it does...except it doesn't....ever.  To begin with, this game doesn't have Team Vs Team fight. it's always only 1 vs (Insert arbitrary enemy number here) yes you often will take several team members into a fight BUT they don't do anything until you switch to them (they can theoreticaly catch balls thrown at them but there is a reason why in practice this just cannot happen, i will get into it in a second) so, you don't actualy have team fights...which is really dissapointing in a game about dodgeballs, especialy as this game as some absolutely amazing AI, that understands and can use many a dirty tactic depending on the enemy type, so not seeing your own guys muck in really hurts the feeling of playing dodgeball. This also introduces the problem of threat. You as the player can only ever threaten with a single ball, no matter how many you hold, the enemy however can threaten you with however many it wants. This is kind of a problem due to a charge ability called focus. This ability let's you charge for a short time to obtain a buff, this however requires a ball to be in the enemy field. Now since ALL AI players can throw a ball at you independently (plus they will try to interupt your focus or a charged throw since...again, the AI is actualy somewhat good) you cannot focus UNLESS you hold all the balls and throw one at them to set a Focus up, the same counts for charged throws. Of course, the AI can  Focus and charge their throws however they want as soon as they have more than 1 ball since you at most be able to interupt only 1 at any given time. This is also the reason why your team members cannot catch a ball. If you press the button to catch a ball (or counter as some characters do) ALL of your active team members will do so, but since you will often get shot at from different angles at different intervalls...yeah you see why it's practically impossible?Now unto controlls, they are bad! Now to start with, i use a controller here, because that's the type of game that should be good with one. I never used a keyboard to play this game...anyway, now the big BIIIIIIG problem with the controlls is that you cannot buffer in a command. Now, as i have already stated, the AI is mercilless and smart, and the moment they pick up a ball they will throw it and since you cannot buffer a throw, YOU CANNOT DO THAT UNLESS YOU HAVE FRAME PERFECT INPUTS! Seriously Pocket trap, i am genuinely asking you, is there a reason for there being no way to buffer any kind of command? This slows down anything you want to do of course and forces you to mash buttons in frantic situations, and as you can imagine, being slowed down by this PLUS being 1 vs many PLUS the thread problem leads to often very VERY bad matches and since the game tries to scale accordingly to your members stats and your own skills, this can lead to many a situation where the KO of a member is genuinly quickly felt as something brought by a cheating AI.That the AI feels cheaty in such situations is also not helped by the fact that you never see any stats of them. You do see their Lvl but that is incredibly missleading and also....kinda useless. it's very easy to see on your own members that the stats can vary wieldly among them regardless of Lvl. This get's worsend by the fact that sometimes stats feel meaningless, as an enemy which a higher level can very quickly be rendered mute if he has a bad moveset, on the other hand, a low lvl enemy with a rather nasty moveset or tricks can KO all of your team rather quickly.To extend on this, the game has a massive Phobia of providing you with any information. There are so many games with useless glossaries and codexes and what not, and funilly enough, THIS of all games really needs one. You would be surprised at the amount of variation the devs managed to cram into here. This starts at the health items. Your team members have preferences and sometimes allergies to certain food items, this impacts the effect massively. Going from double healing to litteraly being unable to use the item to heal certain characters. Now the only way to know that is by hovering over the item and then seeing which members of your team like it, the items are BTW grouped, the only way to know which item is part of what group is to try and feed it to someone with an allergy, example, feeding a piece of chocolate to Suneko will tell you that "Suneko should not eat Milkproducts." This then continious over to the different balls, there are elemental balls, balls which move slightly on their own, balls that get you stuck on the ground, having a wiki for these in game would be such a help as for instance the gumball that makes you stick and the basic dogeball, look really similar. Of course a wiki for enemies would also be helpfull, especialy due to their ultimate abilities, since they tend to spam them. There are also different rules for the battles, it would be really nice to have an indicator to know which rules would be applied to the next battle.All of this saddly leads to the odds being stacked against you massively in even engamenets. Now this is not to say, the game is overwhelmingly hard, i'd say it tries to be a nice challange. The problem is more that, since these issues almost synergize against you the way they do, you don't wantt to play on even ground and instead try as much to cheese the enemy as best possible, which destroys many of the foundations of how the game works or wants you to play it. And that is very sad and the reason for me not recommending it.I congratulate you if you have read this far. Now i want to again state. This is a really unique game with a ton of charme and smart dialog. The AI is incrediebly good if you ever get the chance to engage it on even footing and they make sure that you'll get more variety than you ever thought possible with a Dodgeball-RPG, if you don't mind the points i have raised, or you think that the way you approach games  avoids these then feel free to try it out, because the devs do deserve some money for their work here. If these points do matter, i'd hold off to a sale or don't buy it, and to the devs, i hope we get to see a second installment maybe at some point, will all the improvements and bells and whistles that this game idea and title deserves!

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia sounds a lot like Golf Story (for the Nintendo Switch) on paper. Since the PC lacks a game similar to that one this might seem like a good alternative. So let’s see how it holds up.Dodgeball Academia has a story about your character trying to get into a dodgeball academy. There are a few twists and turns along the way but nothing to write home about. It’s a decent story that functions as a way to keep you playing dodgeball matches. I won’t judge it for what it is, or isn’t, but yeah, the story just isn’t great.The RPG mechanics are to be considered ‘light RPG’. Winning matches (and you will play a lot) will earn you money, items and experience and when you reach a certain level you will automatically get new skills. And every time you level up your stats also increase a little. Each of your party members has a specific special skill that can be used when the correct meter has filled up. Most of these are kind of useless but a few of them can turn the tide.Some of the items can permanently increase specific stats and food (healing items) has to be given depending on one’s taste. There are characters that like or love items that others do not.Each of the (sub)quest given has you play dodgeball. Later on during the game the matches get some new rules and mechanics.After completing each quest you’ll have to return to the quest giver if you want to actually complete it.During the game you’ll move from the schoolyard to the forest and parking lot so there aren’t many diverse areas. There are some canisters and trash cans located in these areas that be opened up by throwing balls into them that lay around the areas. These will either reward you with healing items or equipment to make your character(s) stronger.There were a few instances where the AI seemed to have the upper hand, meaning the matches were a little overpowered unless you used a very specific technique/strategy the game already had in mind.I did not appreciate having teammates unlock so slowly and I also didn’t like the game for introducing new match rules and mechanics so late in the game. You’ll be playing a lot of matches and I got already bored before reaching the part where you get to play with and against fire and ice balls, for example. Disclaimer: I didn’t finish the game, I made it until the beginning of chapter 6 I think.As far as the graphics are concerned: everything looks nice and colorful, with a good mix of 2D and 3D objects. You can tell some shortcuts were taken, especially when it comes to the animation and the aformentioned lack of environments, but other than that there are no complaints.There is zero voice acting and the music to me wasn’t all that interesting, but then again, what sort of music do you put together with a game about dodgeball?I’ve been told the game has eight chapters in total, with each one taking about an hour to complete. I’ve only played 5 chapters so far and doubt I will return but the amount of gameplay you get for this price is excellent.Dodgeball Academia is no Golf Story, that’s for sure. It does try some new things and sometimes succeeds, but the lack of diversity fairly early on soured the experience for me. Together with some other issues I would not recommend this game, unless you’re aching for a sports RPG in which case this game would indeed do the trick.Now I may have sounded a little overly negative this review, but I can assure you that’s not the case. I try to keep an open mind for every game that I play and I try to judge a game on its own strengths, but in this case the inspiration for the game was clear from the start and it unfortunately had a tad too much ‘too little too late’. I enjoyed it until shortly before the part where I decided to quit. Just a little FYI in case you were wondering if I was in a bad mood or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: A game that you should not dodge! Dodgeball Academia is a solid little game that follows Otto as he attends a school for dodgeball where students are granted special dodgeball powers and attend dodgeball lessons as well as competing with one another in a tournament. The game breaks up into eight days with the days playing out as their own individual episodes where some issue occurs and the characters need to resolve it. As you progress you play tournament matches, explore the school and its grounds, level up and gather numerous interchangeable team members. First and foremost the game is an RPG. It plays like a mix of Pokemon in regards to team management, RPG elements and overworld with the dodgeball battles feeling akin to that of the Mario RPG series with timed inputs and special moves and such. Both of these work well within the game with the controls feeling generally satisfying across the board. Each of the characters play differently in regards to their charges, throws and special moves. Some characters catch balls whereas others counter. This allows you to figure out how you prefer to play and what works for your three player team. In terms of story, as stated earlier each day is an episode with these generally lasting an hour each. Each day feels unique and stands out overall with some days introducing new areas of the school to explore. The writing is generally cheesy but is fun overall. with tonnes of dodgepall puns and wordplay. Most of the characters are engaging though rather one note overall. One striking thing about the game that is impossible to miss is the style. Everything just pops. All of the characters are charming and identifiable. All of the animations and effects are all polished and solid. The visual detail that went into this game is amazing. Additionally the sfx bolster the visuals perfectly for every ball thrown, for every effect that triggers and for every action made. It's solid across the board. The soundtrack, whilst repetitive, is quite energetic and engaging with all of the tracks fitting the areas and themes well. It's definitely something that sticks out the second you boot up the game.  One of the main gripes the game has is that overall it is repetitive in nature as you generally go from area to area battling folks and progressing the story or side quests and whilst that is true overall there is a decent variety of content overall. As you progress different effects, balls and characters are brought into the mix which mix up parts of the battles as well as arena hazards such as dodging cars in the middle of battles. You can also mix up your play style and team if you want to engage with combat in different ways. One flaw for me personally is that whilst there are a variety of areas, I would have liked to have explored the same areas a little less and instead had more varied areas as you do typically explore the same areas numerous times throughout the different episodes. Overall the game is great. Aside from being a tad repetitive the gameplay is fun, the character and world is charming and everything is well polished. A solid game through and through!

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the Super Dodgeball RPG that so few of us knew we wanted, but that we definitely needed.This was a really charming and fun game. The character and world design are excellent, with all of the characters really expressing their personality at a glace. The world can be best described as "sports anime on steroids" - we've somehow managed to craft a world that revolves *entirely* around the sport of dodgeball. It's extremely silly, but really fun if you can let yourself get wrapped up in it instead of repulsed by it.The gameplay loop is basically "get quest; fight everyone on your way to the next waypoint" It's not complicated, but the matches are fast and fun and offer a surprising amount of variety. It drips elements one at a time so you can learn them without getting overwhelmed, but gets everything into play pretty fast. Each character has their own throw, charge throw, "balltimate move", 'evasive' move (roll or jump), defensive move (catch or counter), stats, level up perks, and two equipment slots to further customize them. Three of your players play at a time, so you can build an actual synergistic team out of them. Genuinely, this gives you a huge amount of potential variety between your opponents and allies alike. There are also special AIs from enemies that add a little more variety still, such as the twins who will pass the balls several times, weave across the field, and eventually do a jumping pincer attack. It's a nice touch that adds some extra personality and excitement to the combat.I have some small gripes. The sprites are very lively, fun, and charming, but we could have used a few more of them for different emotions in the dialogues - it's a little odd to have Otto keep his usual protagonist-gremlin smile when he's in the middle of having a bad time, or Balloony smiling sweetly and tapping his fingers shyly when he's scared out of his gourd (his default state). There are locked chests all over the map - eventually you get a character who can unlock them for you, but it's not telegraphed that they can do this that I noticed. I honestly didn't know until I was sweeping up after the story and touched one again for a clue, only to have my friend pop up and just unlock it for me. When an opponent gets knocked out, they will  move behind your line and thrown dodged shots at your back - this is fine, but when they move to the sidelines the game immediately cancels all action, resets to neutral, and gives them advantage. This still isn't an issue on its own, but it's frustrating when your ultimate move gets almost completely cancelled because the first thing it hits is the opponent with 1 HP left. It would at least be nice if you could tell which opponents will become backliners and which will just get KO'd so you could plan your big attacks better.In spite of these minor complaints, Dodgeball Academia is a really fun game with incredible charm and surprisingly robust gameplay. I can recommend it to most folks, as long as they're someone who can indulge in a little over-the-top silliness.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is a victim of way too many cooks. Each individual cook has made something great. There are a lot of systems that just don't play well into each other. Enemies that you face seem to have their own unique strategy that you can learn to play around and beat. This makes it feel more strategic. You can also individually target each enemy so you can focus on one that is more problematic. BUT then they throw in generic battles and group fights where it devolves into more same-y combat. Being able to read the unique portion of each character also drops when there's 3 enemies and they throw dodgeballs at the same time with different "counter" timings and it messes everything up. oh and the targeting system is tacked on with all of the AI swapping places and moving everywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Super Dodgeball on the NES, so I had to give this game a try.  Happy to say, I loved it.  It's not strictly dodgeball matches, as the older game was.  Dodgeball Academia is a sort of rpg/adventure light game, with dodgeball matches serving as the battles.   While matches in SDB could drag on, DA matches are fast and entertaining.  Charge throws, catches, counters, and specials keep things interesting without being overwhelming to learn.  Your teammates' skills are different enough that it's interesting to play them each, even if it's not strictly necessary to do so.   And the story was fun enough to keep me motivated.   Loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would really rather put this as a sideways "meh" review and that hurts. It's a solid game that is seriously let down by some just absurdly crappy design choices that make no sense at all.Your "sprint" has you curl up like a ball and roll, but you have no real directional control so you just slam into things. It's a minor annoyance, but it builds up.The really bad call though, the most wretched of all bad calls I've seen in a good long while - your teammates are quite literally useless. The entire enemy team can move around independent of one another, they can all pick up and throw balls at each other...your team does LITERALLY nothing but stand behind you getting hit and passing balls to you. They don't move on their own, they don't throw any balls for attacks. They do nothing.It's effectively a bullet hell, but you're on a SMALL area and are a GIANT target. It's just the dumbest thing ever.All that said though, the story and visuals are top tier. I've laughed out loud multiple times and want to keep slogging through the TERRIBLE combat to see more of it.It's a dodgeball game, devs. Have you ever PLAYED dodgeball? Clearly you haven't There are no formations and everybody can throw.

_childDocuments_.review: 10h 1/10 With accessibility difficulty options, 7+ without 1 Yes, You can find one  or  No Yes, the one for getting all the equipment, for more info check out the review below No No No No No No, you can play with only 5% damage and doing 400% damage and unlock all the achievements NoDodgeball Academia is a fun RPG/ sport type of game. The game is clearly an RPG, but the battles are in the form of a dodgeball mini-game. You play as Otto who takes fate into his own hands and decides to sneak into the biggest dodgeball school. He is the new kid in school, gets bullied, and doesn't know the relationships between people but will figure them out during the course of the game. The most important thing is playing in the upcoming dodgeball championship and the steaks of winning that tournament get higher during the game. The game has 8 episodes, aka 8 days you will play through. Each day has its own main quest, side quests, and duels to get through. You'll be allowed in more areas around the school in later days, which will be led by the main quests of each day, which has multiple stages. That Dodgeball Academia feels mostly like an RPG comes because you earn experience and equipment, but also because it took inspiration from the sounds in a pokemon game. Like when a dual starts or when you heal your team. I do like the music and sound design, but the art style is my favorite part of this game. The achievements in Dodgeball Academia are for the most part very straightforward but can be so difficult if you don't use the accessibility difficulty options. I don't know how anybody can beat the challenges the teachers will give you with an S ranking without using those options. The are also achievements for getting a character to level 50, but that is quite easy. If you do all the quests during each day (which you should do) and do as many duals as possible, you will already be around level 45 or higher. There is a shop underground where you can buy a drink to level up, so you don't have to grind those last levels. After finishing a day, it becomes available through a new game to start on that day, so if you missed out on some achievements, it is easy to go back to a specific day, but there is one achievement for which this doesn't work. The achievements for getting all the equipment will not work through chapter selection, so that is the only missable achievement. And to probably make things a bit harder, there are guides that say that your last equipment must come from a chest to make sure the game calculates if you have all the equipment and that it doesn't work with rewards you get from battles. I'm not sure if that is the case because my last one ended up being from a chest because there are some sneaky hidden chests. If you want to make sure you have everything on each day, . I hadn't found that list while playing but I made sure I did every side quest each day, did every duel, and also bought as many from the shop as possible each day. The duels and sidequests are visible on the map, which is very helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really solid game and it's pretty amazing how good the execution is. _childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia is a game set in a world that revolves around - you guessed it, dodgeballs. The game features a single-player story mode wherein you will join Otto and train to become the ultimate dodgeball champion. Then there’s a versus mode, where you can sit back and play locally with your friends (or by yourself, no judging). This RPG game is giving me a lot of classic Pokémon vibes, from the transition music, the menu UI, some gameplay mechanics and more. And I am here for all of it!Since there isn’t that much to go on about the versus mode, this review will specifically focus on the single-player story mode.You will play as Otto, a transfer student in the academy, who aspires to be the best dodgeball player out there. The story unfolds like it’s some sort of a Saturday morning cartoon. Its cartoonish art style and the same time, combining a 2.5D world and 2D sprite sets this game apart distinctively. The story progresses somewhat linearly, having a main quest each day and a few optional quests in between. Its main quest dubbed as an ‘episode’ really makes this game feel like you’re watching a cartoon series.The gameplay of dodgeball is very simple. Two teams are matched and the first team that gets wiped out, loses. If you are familiar with the game, then you had a nice childhood. But if not, don’t fret because the game did a nice job of introducing the rules to you. Your team may compose from one to three members, while the enemy team will range from one to six. You control one character or switch up to another on the fly during the matches.Throughout the story mode, you will come across unique characters that will contribute to your story progression. With each character having different characteristics, they also come with different set of abilities; from counters, whether to dodge or jump, and balltimates (ultimate moves). As you progress through the story, you will be unlocking characters that will join your team. You can freely customize your party in the main menu.There are two types of obtainable items in the game; (1) consumables that can heal/revive your party members or give a permanent stat boost, (2) equipment that will give you additional boosts in your stats if your characters have them equipped. Each character can only equip up to two items, so plan strategically. While for the consumables, it is worth taking note that each character also has preference. Meaning to say, some consumables will have a better effect to those who loves or likes the food as opposed to dislikes and allergic to it. Aside from using consumable items, you may also get your team healed up in an infirmary.The core gameplay of dodgeball can get repetitive quite fast if you’re burning through this game quickly. Since all the main quests and optional quests will revert to you playing dodgeball. I highly suggest that play this game in short bursts to avoid the feeling of it becoming a chore. The game is fairly short, ranging from 10 to 15 hours of playtime to finish the story mode. So, there is no point of rushing this one, just take your time and let the game come to you.With the positive notes out of the way, now it’s time to tackle some negative ones. First off, your other team members are pretty much useless. All their movements and actions will depend on the character that you’re using. It’s crazy seeing your enemy moving so independently and contributing to win the match. Your teammates will shadow you, mimicking your movements. It’s already hard enough to dodge volley of balls thrown at you, imagine having to that while minding your teammates position. And they are not contributing at all. I often feel like my other team members are only there just so I have a backup life just in case my character’s health depletes to zero.Next is that rolling ball mode (sprinting). Since by default, your moving animation is already running, going from point A to point B can be hassle especially if it’s on the other side of the campus. Thus, they are introducing this rolling ball to somewhat kind of sprint. On paper, this shouldn’t be something negative, right? Wrong. Going into a roll feels like you don’t have any real directional control. You will bang keep banging into something and this will eventually annoy the hell out of you.Overall, I do recommend this game to anyone who has an itch for a sports RPG. Its visuals and soundtrack make this game really stand out. Story-wise, it’s not that heavy and that’s fine for me. The core gameplay of dodgeball is solid especially with how they’ve added a cartoonish twist to it. The ability effects are amazing and satisfying to execute. And besides, there isn’t that many dodgeball games out there. So, grab a copy and start playing!

_childDocuments_.review: I was right there. In the thick of the action. Bandages all over. My body shattered on the floor. The sounds of balls surrounding me getting closer. Closer. I didn't know if I could avoid the next onslaught. I breathed. A very rapid breath. As this was all the time I had. Closer. I could hear them again. Footsteps switching sides. Laughter. Some gasps. Closer. I was terrified. "I must", I thought. Fighting. I clung to my knees and forced my legs to bend towards me. Closer. I put my only good arm down. Pushing myself. Slowly, I got up. I slipped down one or twice but. Almost there. I got up. Closer. I ran. Well whatever run I had left in me. Like a obese dog, I had to walk slanted, at a 45 degree angle. It hurt. Closer. I could hear the balls. They targeted me once again. I began to sprint. Barely. My inevitable pain was gathering momentum. I reached for the door. Closer. CLOSER! I CAN FEEL IT! CLOSER! CLOS... *SLAM* I did it! I had escaped!So anyway, I left the brothel and played this game. It was quite good.+rep cool guy easy fair trade

_childDocuments_.review: I liked . And it’s a shame this is the best we can do on PC. I really wanted to like it, too!I think RPGs about anything other than fighting are dope. This is an RPG about something other than fighting. This is a great-looking and great-sounding game. A lot of care has been put into the game's appearance, and it paid off. All the relevant story characters have a cool unique design and playstyle that really pops. But the game itself? What a mess.I couldn’t get through this one. It was just too tiresome. Any second not interacting or dodgeballing with a character (rather than generic NPC) is a second of my life I’ll never get back. Slumped in my chair mashing attack. Most fights, at least up to the middle of chapter 4—where I finally threw in the towel—are trivial and extremely boring. You finish the fight and sit through the results screen. You knock out a guy and the game interrupts the match to yell ‘OUT’ at you. Let me play! Let me fight the guy that only does lob shots! Let me participate in the tournament—isn’t that the whole point!?And look. The worst, most unforgivable sin this game does is not even how boring it is. It’s not even how you spend most of your time rolling back and forth in the school. It’s something emblematic of how this game thinks: it’s the fact that your teammates aren’t controlled by the AI. Instead, you just move them like a blob, sort of doing all the moves at once. No multiplayer, either. It’s just not fun.
