_childDocuments_.review: Y’know, normally when I am scrolling through Steam or other store fronts, I am willing to see new stuff and try what is on the market, if you get my drift, however, Dodgeball Academia flew completely past my radar, and I never noticed that this was released like in 2021. I only just learned about this game a couple of months ago on SwitchUp's YouTube channel. If you can, please go check out their work, they have very interesting videos that I think will be worth your time. So, now that I have finished the game, I want to give my thoughts and perspectives. Also, prepare yourselves because I am going to be singing a lot of praises despite some flaws I have encountered. Well, with that said, let's talk about DA, shall we?Presentation	If I am going to be honest with you, the art style in this game kind of reminds me of Paper Mario in a way. What I mean is that you have the characters as 2D sprites in a 3D world and the dodgeballs that Otto, the game’s main protagonist picks up help differentiate themselves from the environment so that the player can pick them up easily. Speaking of which, I really loved the character designs for this game, especially one of Otto’s friends and roommate, Balloony. Can’t believe I’m saying this, but don’t you think he looks cute? Not only do the designs look amazing but I really appreciated the fact that the writers gave them their own separate personalities as well. Next up, the music. Personally, I found the music to be quite charming. Now yes, the soundtrack does get repetitive, especially when you participate in dodgeball fights, but I didn’t find myself too bored or tired at all. Before I end this segment, I want to take a moment to appreciate how the game’s world feels like you are moving around a campus. The places you can go to like the forest, academic building, library, etc. have really interesting designs. Now I will admit, there were some aspects of the presentation I noticed. For example, during the robot mascot invasion when you go inside the academic building, the lighting inside remains as it was during the first 7 episodes. I also wished for more unique designs for the students around campus as well. Heck, one of the students you fight against even breaks the 4th by asking if they are just a carbon copy of everyone else. However, those small hiccups weren’t too bad for me. By the way, doesn’t the theme of this world remind anyone of The Amazing World of Gumball? Sorry, I’m just spitballing here.Presentation: 9/10Gameplay Surprisingly, I found the gameplay unique. So, does anyone remember the Nintendo and SQUARE ENIX collab. game, “Mario Sports Mix?” Well, just imagine if there was a Paper Mario game retaining the same RPG mechanics as seen in 64 and Thousand-Year Door but adding in a sports theme on top of to make it unique from the other Paper Mario games. That was the kind of vibe I was getting while playing this game except that you are only playing in dodgeball matches. However, not only will you be playing in dodgeball matches in the “Versus” Mode, but you can also experience this game’s campaign in the “Story” Mode. We’ll talk about the story later, but I want to focus on the gameplay first. Now I mentioned that you can experience this game’s campaign and if I am being honest, I felt like this game’s world struck a good balance between open world and traversal mechanics. If you ever want to get to your location faster, you can utilize Otto’s roll move by spamming the east button. I don’t want to spoil the game, but this roll will be important in the later episodes. If you have already played this game, you’ll probably understand what I am talking about. However, not only will you be moving around campus and interacting with students, but you will also encounter bins and chests that contain items that can only be opened if you hit them with dodgeballs scattered in the world. However, for the chests, you will need to recruit Shoy on your team as he is the only one with claws to pick the lock. My goodness, I was just overall pleased with how the devs managed to make the world fun for me to explore all around.If exploration is not your thing then don’t worry because it’s time for me to talk about the dodgeball battles. Now much like any other dodgeball game, the main thing you will be doing is knocking out your opponent with a dodgeball, right? Well, yes and no. I mentioned Paper Mario once in the first paragraph of the “Gameplay” section and how it would be interesting if the series had a sports theme while having RPG mechanics. Well, as you fight opponents in the story, you will be leveling up and gaining new power-ups that will strengthen your charge and special attacks. For example, Otto can do a dodgeball Hadouken that will burn opponents, Mina can shoot multiple bolts of lightning depending on however many balls she has, and Balloony can create a puddle of water that will heal your teammates. Speaking of teammates, I am a little bit mixed on this mechanic. The reason I said that is because, as far as I know, the only place where I could think to turn off the tag mode was in the versus mode. If someone else managed to turn it off in the story, I will love you for the rest of my life. By the way, while you fight PvP in versus, you will at times have to fight more than 3 opponents and most of the time the KOs will stand on the sidelines and throw balls at you, and your teammate gets hit or KO’d, they are out for the rest of the match. That is why I was mixed about the tag mode I mentioned earlier. Oh, and I played most of the game with 100% DMG taken or dealt but I was terrified about the later bosses. I know I am a coward, but I am bad at dodging, countering, and catching the balls in this game. So, I changed the damage dealt by 0%. Now, I had to go back into the game because the only characters I unlocked were the ones you encounter in the story mode. I even had to check in the Steam discussions to see if the rest would be unlocked. Sadly, I couldn’t find anything. I know it’s not that big a deal, but I would have loved to experience the rest of the cast’s move sets. I also went into the versus mode and you will probably need a second player to play with because the CPU players would just stand there and take the hits. Again, it’s not too big a deal but I would have loved to take the CPU head on. Overall, the gameplay, while not perfect, still managed to keep me invested.Gameplay: 8/10Performance	Sorry to keep this segment short but I am running low on character space, so I’ll try to keep this segment as short as possible. The performance managed to remain stable throughout the majority of my playthrough on the Deck. I can’t say much on PC, but so far, I think the performance was great.Performance: 10/10Story	Now, originally I was going to leave out the story, but as I kept going, I started to feel invested. In my personal opinion, I found the cast to be likable and relatable. I won’t lie, most lines got a laugh out of me. Now it’s not perfect and I’d say my only complaint is probably the pacing. For example, while going to the scary woods, you are stopped by two characters who want to fight just because. While that is a minor hiccup, that doesn't change the fact that the story in this game is charming.Story: 9/10Final Verdict	As you can imagine, I really like this game. Now, it’s not perfect and has some flaws, but I still really enjoyed this game and am always willing to try out new stuff from indies. Currently, the devs’ next game is still in development, and I can’t wait to try it out when it’s released. So, thank you for your time and have a nice week.Verdict: 36/40

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game.It's like it a jrpg with the theme/vibe of pokemon. But instead of turn-based combat, its dodgeball matches.Sounds great, looks great, characters/world is fun, and most importantly, the gameplay is fun. It did get a little repetitive and too easy at the end for me. But that is partly my fault for grinding away at one side quest for too long, so I was over-levelled.Would strongly recommend. I hope a sequel comes out so I can play the inter-school tournament.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun games, I do recommend, but just so the criticisms get out there I'm leaving a few bad notes :- Healing items are almost entirely useless, since you can't use them in combat and outside combat you can nearly always go to the infirmary and get fully healed back up for free (only exception seems to be the very end of the game).- This game design is BEGGING for coop but there is none ; the only multiplayer mode is outside story mode, and is 1v1.Now the really really good points :- It's a solid RPG, and the combat mechanics are really fun. It can get complex if you want it to be, despite appearances the variety of the characters' playstyles mean you can get creative when working at higher difficulties. You can tune difficulty at will by changing the damage dealt and taken in the options.- Visuals, music, and writing are so fun and full of personality, especially the original Portuguese version. It's a really particular artstyle and sense of humor that gets you right in the zone.- There's a "language learning mode" which allows you to toggle between the main set language and a secondary language in a non-intrusive way. It's insane I haven't seen this in more games for how simple and useful it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia is a flawed, repetitive game that managed to make me smile throughout the entire 15 hours I spent with it. For every thing you can criticize, there are two more things that just feel magical with how full of love and character they are. Definitely recommend to anyone that sees the screenshots and thinks it looks cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: It overstayed its welcome a bit for me, but all in all I had a great deal of fun. The first 10 hours especially were a blast.The second half of the game dragged on a bit because almost no new mechanics were introduced, but the plot just went on and on. I guess this is partly my completeionist ass' fault, as I had to literally do anything the game had to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must.Before anything else, I have to say that's IMPOSSIBLE to describe what kind of game it is without going on a frenetic comparison with things like Super Dodge Ball Advance, Golden Sun, Megaman Battle Network and a few more.It’s unique to the core, with a great gameplay curve, a simple yet fun and funny plot. All while having a wonderful cartoon aesthetic that makes you feel like you’re part of a Saturday morning cartoon.It’s definitely a labor of love, and sincerely what any indie game should strive for, an experience in itself not (streamer bait) meets (streamer bait 2).
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam Deck.Controls well on SD. The graphics were nice, humor was solid for the most part. A good length for this type of game, not too long. Ends before you get tired of it. Only issue I had was entering buildings. I don’t know if I was doing something wrong, but the doors to buildings or rooms would not open. I would have to repeatedly walk up to them to get them to open, either a bug/issue or I’m dumb and didn’t know how to trigger them.Either way, this gets a recommendation from me. Preferably on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun RPG focused around dodgeball for game play. It starts off rather slow but after the first hour or so it picks up. The conversations with NPCs were pretty fun and had a lot of cheesy jokes that got a chuckle out of me. The aesthetic style and music were also top notch.The game play focuses around fantasy with dodge ball. You get ultimate moves and there are different kinds of dodge balls that can shock, freeze, burn, etc opponents. It's never overly difficult but the game play is still fun. I finished the story in probably 12 hours while doing all the side content as well. It took about 20 minutes to wrap up the remaining achievements if you're into that kind of thing.The game is surprisingly really fun. I enjoy these fun RPGs that don't take themselves seriously and this is a solid one.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- The art-style was nice; 2D sprites on a semi 3D background might not be to everyones taste but it works for me.- Soundtrack was pleasant although very repetitive; I think they could have added some breaks in the music and some background ambiance instead.- Charming wacky characters and fun dialog- Story was fine, it kept the game ticking over at least.- Controls with a x-box controller were fine.- I guess the basic gameplay was fine but be prepared for 99% of it being dodgeball matches and I do have some gripes. Cons- I think it could have used a bit more varied game-play and less dodgeball matches. Ok yes they overtime introduce some new mechanics in the form of balls with special attributes/effects and encounters with new player abilities but yeah I think I've played enough dodgeball matches now for my entire lifetime.- Pretty big difficulty spikes in the last chapter. - Some of the matches are only difficult because once you get hit you are typically stun locked and can't avoid or catch another ball. In alot of the games its very easy to get hit once and then die from several more impacts that you can't do anything about as your just perpetually stunned. So effectively one hit your done.- Players can equip 2 trinkets in order to boost some stats or slightly mod the character in some way but I felt 2 trinkets was just not enough to facilitate any kind of stragety.- New characters joining the team start at lower level then existing characters. Doesn't give much incentive to any other characters outside the starting 3.- Weird placement of trinckets; like some powerfull items would just be lying in a bin and then less powerful ones you have to buy in a shop.Overall despite the cons I still enjoyed it,
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: A goofy little dodgeball rpg with fun animation and character design, an enjoyable plot that takes itself not too seriously, fun dialog with its own endearing sense of humor, a soundtrack that goes surprisingly hard, and gameplay and length (~10h) that doesn't overstay its welcome. I enjoyed every hour I spent with it, definitely worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia is a silly game... Oh, but I don't mean that in a bad way!DA is lighthearted. funny, charming and has a lot going on on it's mechanics. The game jests about being a Manga Anime, and in fact that is what if feels, cheesiness included!It's a good game with good gameplay, good dialogues, great characters and a lot of charisma. A good time indeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia emerged as a serendipitous discovery in my gaming repertoire, having initially acquired it as part of a Humble Bundle. Prior to this, I had no inkling of its existence, yet post-engagement, I find myself ensnared by its allure.The game greets you with a delightful narrative that holds its own charm. However, the true quintessence of Dodgeball Academia lies in its innovative game mechanics that ceaselessly captivate your attention. It ushers in a sense of continual novelty through an expansive array of abilities, diverse play styles, and escalating challenges that ensure the gameplay remains enthralling.However, every rose has its thorn; the health system, in my early experience, appears to be an unwelcome pause in an otherwise rhythmic gameplay. It momentarily hampers the pace to regain them outside combat where I see it's not necessary, although with a mere two-hour immersion, I remain hopeful that its role might unfold as a contributory aspect to the game mechanics rather than a mere vexation.Certainly, Dodgeball Academia warrants a recommendation for those on the prowl for a game that seamlessly intertwines an engaging narrative with inventive gameplay. The journey through its athletic academia is not just a game of dodgeball, but a course in gaming satisfaction.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Along with some other psychological schemas, this is mostly an exposition of the effects in being raised by a narcissistic parent not so subtly presented in a game.Both the protagonist and the antagonist have parents who see them as extensions of their own will.The protagonist results to surviving through rebellion and deception.While the antagonist is dominated by the programming that they are supposed to be superior.Since its a game, its written so that in the end, almost all major characters learn core life lessons, and overcome the developmental personality disorders and deeply ingrained behavioral conditioning due to past trauma (or at minimum embrace the truth of brokenness and the need for healing) in just a few days, and with very little friction or effort.If only it worked that way in life as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: If you bought this game looking for a HIGH ADRENALINE super fast paced game... Wrong game!! Check out Lethal League instead, that game is the BEST out there in terms of digital adrenaline. That said, while Dodgeball Academia is a game that is much slower and less speedy, it has its own charm. The whole thing has a weird Pokemon vibe complete with the main hero stealing Ash's cap, and running around a community battling others. (yes also by throwing balls out) And yes it still has some adrenaline fun going, but definitely not the same level as Lethal League. (once you play the other, you will understand)I would highly recommend this game if you are looking for a nice slow paced story with its retro feel and the characters... that's what I'm in this for - the characters are excellent! You can tell the developers tried their best to focus on character development. Quite a number of the jokes are cringy, but it's all good in the long run. I find myself coming back to this game again and again, just to be part of this cute little world with sidequests and interesting rivalry build-ups. They even had some pretty interesting ideas like bringing back that nostalgia of Sonic games where you can mash a button to spin the dude and go faster and faster. And it fits the theme! A dodgeball game - a character rolling like a ball to go places!The main downside is: YOU CAN'T REMAP YOUR CONTROLS!!! The Keyboard default makes the game more challenging than the final boss.The only other downside to this game are the girls. Most of them FEEL and LOOK like they have balls (and I don't mean those balls they use on the court). I had no idea one of the professors was a FEMALE until almost 2 hours into the story... If you like Pokemon, and balls, and girls that are gender challenged, this game is superb for you! I know it is for me!!
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Although tacky and shallow in parts it provides a satisfyingly colourful experience.The game is almost immediately identical to stock, children-oriented cartoon shows where a generic excitable protagonist sets out on a journey filled with conflict, humour and drama in order to accomplish some grand goal. Many of the characters fall into extremely typical archetypes or are defined by a shallowly exaggerated aesthetic. The music is so overly energetic all the time as to be outright obnoxious. The game is just discouragingly generic and feels void of a soul, like stuffy adults trying to emulate vibrant silliness in hopes of making their content appealing to children.In spite of this a tolerable quantity of characters are reasonably interesting despite their shallow design, there's a fair amount of good humour; and a decently endearing if not typical degree of existential depth to the story by its end. The character graphics are quite pristine and well animated, making each character visually distinctive at least. But there are many copy pasted characters who serve as extras to fill up the student base of the school, which is unfortunate. It would of been more interesting if the school was exclusively populated with distinct characters that players could interact with, rather than a bunch of forgettable clones. Similarly there's almost zero dialogue for examining anything in the environment, which could have been used to give the game more substance as well. As mentioned the story has solidly endearing and humourous elements; but there's also a significant amount of asinine plot points where things happen which just don't make practical sense.The dodgeball gameplay is reasonably compelling but definitely has issues. Stunlocking being a major problem that becomes more and more prevalent in the later game. It's also quite obnoxious when enemies instantly counter an attack and launch it back into the player before their initial throwing animation has even concluded. There aren't many mechanics that take advantage of the fact that players often have passive teammates following them around throughout the match, those characters kind of just hang back and do nothing unless you swap to them. The whole system is also clogged with some disruptive interruptions like the game briefly stopping when a character is sent behind enemy lines, or how all the characters in a match specifically move into certain positions before performing their victory and defeat animations at the end.By far the most infuriating part of it all is the Underground Tournament. In which the developers decided that in a game with no invulnerability frames, attacks that lock the player in place and brazen stunlocking; players must fight five enemies simultaneously to win the final bracket of that side quest. So basically the whole side quest is just a gauntlet of random chance as to whether the player gets chained for six or more hits in a row while surrounded by enemies all attacking in sequence. it took me two and half hours to finish and I'd like to give this game a thumbs down just for that but I won't.Some other points of annoyance are the Defense Challenge side quest in which players must counter oncoming attacks which sometimes come at the player in multiples simultaneously so that it's impossible to counter them all. Or the fact that the game doesn't tell players when they've unlocked the lockpicking feature, which comes from .Although I would not say this game accomplishes anything especially unique aside from compressing a generic animated show-for-children storyline down into a single experience, it remains satisfying and entertaining. There's a decent amount of substance for the price and it offers a fair array of enjoyable moments, wrapped in a delightfully vibrant artstyle.Just don't do the Underground Tournament until you're literally max level, if at all.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Easy, reliable controlsJust enough gear and lootJust enough explorationWholesome story and characterizationCustomizable difficultyCrisp, clean graphicsGreat soundtrackRelatively short, no fluff, respectful of my timeConsPoor traversal, needs fast travel or faster run speed in the overworldAI plays by different rulesRelatively short, wish there was more!ReviewI had fun with this one. I completed the story, but did not "100%" all acheivements. The mechanics are easy to grasp and it's fun to level up your team over the course of the game. There are very light RPG mechanics that are additive. The story is wholesome, positive and moves at a brisk pace. The characters are likeable!The short play time is either a pro or con depending on how you feel about game length. For me, the short run-time actually allowed me to beat the game. The real issue is overworld traversal. The world isn't huge, but there is no quick way to navigate the overworld. The run animation is too slow, while the roll lacks precision and is just clunky. Thankfully, there aren't too many fetch quests so overworld traversal was a minor (but persistent) pain point.This one is easy to recommend if you just want an easy-breezy, fun game to beat in a few sittings.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I'm putting my thoughts together on a list of games I've come to love that more people should play and this is at the very top.If you like POKEMON, if you like quick sports games, if you enjoy wonderful hand-drawn aesthetics, humorous dialogue, skill check mania, and are just into a FUN game this is No.1 for all of those things combined.It's an incredible game and seeing only 250 reviews has me shocked. Play Dodgeball Academia.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that I think this is a rather under-appreciated title. It's colorful, fun, and entertaining all the way through. The story starts off a bit weak, but the characters get more interesting after a couple chapters in. The gameplay is probably the most impressive part of the game, with a lot of potential depth. The basic concept of dodging, catching, and throwing balls is fun, but learning to combo your various teammates' abilities can make for some interesting team compositions. The devs did a pretty good job of adding a lot of variation between the game's playable characters, with most of them having completely different playstyles. Additionally, the game's difficulty curve remains mostly consistent throughout its runtime, with new small challenges slowly added to each battle as you progress through the game ensuring that you're constantly on your toes and staying focused. Overall, it's a pretty well-balanced game with some really fun gameplay and entertaining writing. This title is worth getting if you're into a more light-hearted action game experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Off the top, I highly recommend this game. I had an absurd amount of fun playing it. The art style is bright and bubbly with unique character designs. The game mechanics are simple to learn and get more depth as you progress. Don't take that to mean this is a git gud system. Each character is limited to 2 power ups. While they are welcome bonuses in no way do even late stage accessories break the game.There are also numerous accessibility options. You don't have to be a great gamer to get to the end of this heart warming coming of age story. I could go on. Simply put I had a good weekend with this game. It's absolutely rock solid and a welcome addition to any collection.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: This is a true indie gem.The 2D art is phenomenal, the whole concept is excellent and I love all the *winks* to old school Pokemon (Before it became absolute ♥♥♥♥ with Sword and Shield).It's basically a RPG about dodgeball with powers, pretty bonkers. 11 hours to 100%, game has accessibility options to tweak the damage you deal and take (up to 0%) so really anyone can play it.Only gripes are that sometimes the targeting in fight kinda sucks, especially against like 4 or 5 enemies, you control only one character at a time and the constant need to back to the "pokemon center" to heal.I can't wait for the next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, unique little indie game that I thoroughly enjoyed and recommend for anyone. Combat is easy to learn with just the right amount of gameplay elements to keep you on your toes. Lots of accessibility options so you can fine tune the difficulty and a few other things. Replayable and even has a versus mode to keep you engaged after you beat the game. Look forward to more titles from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly charming, funny and cute. The combat system has more depth than I was expecting and it really is a fully fleshed out RPG about dodgeball, like Golf Story was to golf. 3v3 combat can get really messy when there is such a small field and so much going on though, it's hard to do battles perfectly because there is just too much to keep track of. Highly recommend for all JRPG and anime fans. The only major complaint I have is running back to the medical building to heal after every fight is very tedious; especially considering you're auto healed for the first part of the game. I don't know why they couldn't just keep that turned on or at least give you the option of turning it on. There is no reason to not heal after every fight as its free to do it, so it's just a giant time waster.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun Dodgeball RPG.I used to play a lot of Super Dodge Ball Advance back in the day and this game sort of give the nostalgia of playing that game.The fun 2D Dodgeball style game combined with RPG elements really give a nice twist to the game.The interesting dodgeball powers each character has makes the game enjoyable throughout.Its a short game which would possibly take somewhere between 10-15 hours to complete depending on how you play the game.Would recommend to people who enjoy playing dodgeball games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia is an addictive sports-based RPG akin to the Mario Tennis GBC game and Golf Story. I was very fond of the art style which reminded me heavily of The Amazing World of Gumball cartoon. The statistic system was very streamlined and easy to understand, and the many different types of equipment were interesting enough and beneficial enough for me to actually seek them all out as opposed to just using whatever I had.Some may say that the game is quite short at around 10-15 hours. I did at times feel that the game was being padded due to the lack of unique areas to explore. You would quite often spend a chapter running back and forth between locations you had visited previously several times before. This was especially apparent during the last chapter, where you fight the same enemies you had already defeated in the first half of the game, and visit every area of the school again in order to collect key items to progress. While I don't think the game should have been shorter, it definitely started to outstay its welcome due to the constant padding.Overall though, Dodgeball Academia is a very polished, well written and - most importantly - fun game that is well worth a purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful little game.This relatively short Dodgeball rpg only took me around 10-11 hours to beat, but I thoroughly enjoyed my time the whole way.Visuals: The game's budget shows, but the team clearly knew where to put their efforts.  While the backgrounds can best be described as "passable 3-D unity project," the spritework for each and every character in the game oozes personality.  You literally can tell what kind of person most of these characters are without a single word of dialogue, just by paying attention to their designs and animation.  My highest praise for those in charge of character sprites.Story: This is a self-aware, scenery-chewing, EXTRA CHEESY, sports manga.  The plot is completely and utterly ridiculous, and the game knows this.  It never takes itself too seriously, but puts just enough conflict and meaningful character goals in there to keep your attention.  If this game were longer, a number of the characters may have come off as stale, but for the length of time you know them, it's a good ride.Gameplay: It's... it's dodgeball.  The gameplay is dodgeball.  It is wrapped up in rpg mechanics, but it is an action game as well.  You pick up dodgeballs on your side of the field and throw them at opponents to reduce their health, and you must in turn dodge or catch balls thrown at you to avoid taking damage.  Throughout the game, you will gain new characters, able to participate in a 3 man team for each match.  Each character has their own traits and skills when it comes to how they play (such as hitting thrown balls back instead of catching them).  You also level up, gaining new skills and abilities.  A minor nitpick is that all the abilities gained are passive, augmenting a character's base functions, rather than gaining any truly new actions.  Oh... and every character has their own crazy anime powers from touching a super-powered dodge-ball.  Did I mention this game is ridiculous?Overall, if you enjoy a cheesy anime story, and you're down for a unique battle system with a unique premise, this game is well worth the price of entry.  As stated above, doing everything in the game for me took about 11 hours, but I had fun throughout that entire time.  I also fully expect to return to this crazy dodge-ball-centric world at a future date when I need a pick-me-up.  Seriously, give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: I would have to say this game is in my top ten. The art style brought back so much nostalgia from shows such as: The Amazing World Of Gumball, Adventure time and Steven Universe. The light and upbeat music go so well with the art style, as well as the more intense music when in a battle. The game is also very reminiscent of Pokemon as you swap out members in your party who each have different abilities and powers, use various items to buff and heal your team as well as equip-able items. The combat in the game is very different from most others as it is a dodgeball game after all. It was done very well, keeping you engaged while also providing a challenge. I only with the story was longer or that there was a dlc.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: I fully completed the game, 100%, and here are my thoughts (NO SPOILERS). For starters, the ART STYLE is amazing and has this Saturday morning cartoon vibe to it that's always appealing to look at. Regarding GAME PLAY, it is equally just as fun and controls incredibly well! This game takes the concept of dodge ball and really makes it its own thing. The STORY was good overall, nothing incredibly mind blowing but still really entertaining! There's no post game stuff (besides getting the achievements missed) but it honestly had a very satisfying ending. Overall, I HIGHLY recommend this game and hoping for a future sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite games of the last few years, indie or otherwise. Somewhere between Mario Tennis/Golf, Pokemon, Persona, Stardew Valley, and Zelda, this sports RPG has it all. The dodgeball combat is fun and can get quite hard, and there are a number of different viable playstyles. The story is also great, and I just love the positive and friendly outlook that this game has. Also, this game truly captures the low stakes feel of a schoolyard. For example, $100 is A LOT of money.If you love sports RPGs, or if you like JRPGs and just want to try one with dodgeball combat, give Dodgeball Academia a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: I reaally loved dodgeball academia, the writing is really fun and the gameplay is really rich, fun and responsive. The whole game looks really good and is super polished. It reallly give this saturday morning cartoon mood and it's wholesome. I would have loved chapter to be a bit shorter (they are between 1 and 2 hours) because I often get carried away past bedtime t go through the end of the chapter :DI hope you'll enjoy this game as much as I did.Hats off to the dev team, you did an impressive job !
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Dodgeball Academia is a new take on a RPG Games, where the world seems very much like a "Pokemon World" but the battles are real time and around dodgeball.First of all let me start with that the game isn't perfect. At same places seems unoptimized, there is an area called  where I had 30FPS without reason, there are bugs that they have to fix, either with items either with world interactions, but overall I really liked it. It was a fun 2 days playthrough searchin each area, talking to everyone and play each fight, doing all the side quests etc.I have some thoughts about how this game could be better but I will leave the developers to find that out. If a Dodgeball Academia comes out the next year or so, I will give it a try too.

_childDocuments_.review: What an utter blast of a game! Definitely did not expect to enjoy it as much as i did. There are definitely a lot of indirect references in the game. One obvious one is Pokemon! You have a healing center in the game which has a similar vibe as a healing center in all pokemon games.Whoever thought a dodgeball game could be this enjoyable!!10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Loving it so far!  A great mash up of real time and turn based combat in a vibrant world to explore with quirky characters, side quest. Easy to pick up, practice to master. Love how varying all the opponents are. This game was definitely made with love and is worth every penny. Only downside for me it only goes up to 1080P, but very minor complaint in regards to the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute dodgeball RPG that reminds me of other sports RPG games (Mario Tennis, Mario Gold, Golf Story, etc). It seems to be on the short side (Currently on episode 4 out of 8) but I have no regrets buying full price. The plot is engaging, the gameplay is fun (and keyboard friendly), and the graphics are aesthetically pleasing. I highly recommend! 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: Charming look and dialogue. Unique characters, fun dodgeball gameplay with good rpg elements.I also see good speedrun potential with this game, especially with just how the moving feels, you can roll, choosing to crash into things (like doors or npcs that start dialogue in range) or jump (stop crashing but keep momentum) or jump throw, which is just a straight momentum cancel.
_childDocuments_.name: Dodgeball Academia

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where dodgeball is life, you join Otto at the academy and train to become the ultimate dodgeball champion. Across eight episodes, you’ll forge friendships and create rivals, all in the name of developing the best dodgeball team. Level up Otto and develop a dynamic team across a vast and customizable party progression system. All the while, explore the vast Dodgeball Academia and uncover the long hidden truths that reside within the very walls you live, learn, and dominate in.

About the Game “As the last summer day fades, all is illuminated.” With gorgeous translucent designs by Mel Kishida, as well as a story that depicts the youth of lifelike girls, based on a theme of human identity and bonding, a new title in the BLUE REFLECTION series is here! Story Under a piercing blue sky, surrounded by crystal clear water, the sun scorched Ao Hoshizaki's skin. Gazing at the summer scenery, it seemed as if the girl was left behind in a world that she had wandered into. At a school adrift in the distance, there lived three girls who had lost their memories. The only thing they could remember was their names. Ao, shrouded in confusion, begins to lead a strange communal life with the girls as they seek clues about a way to return to their original world. One day, in this world where the school was surrounded by nothing but water, a path that led to new scenery suddenly appeared. At the end of the path was a mysterious location, where familiar things existed inexplicably. In order to grasp the situation, the girls decided to venture forward, but as soon as they took their first steps, they encountered a monster they had never seen before. But just when they thought things had become hopeless, the girls obtain a mysterious power. In a world that seemed to be trapped in summer, young girls have lost their memories. If the girls solve the mystery, what will they obtain? Features ■Make your very own school with “School Development”! The girls are the only ones at the school surrounded by water. You can freely build useful facilities the girls come up with, such as a “Takoyaki Stand” or “Pool”. By building the facilities that your favorite girls like, or simply the ones you are interested in, you can enjoy building a school to your liking. ■The command-style battles are even faster with “Exhilarating Real Time Battles”! The real-time battles from the previous game have been greatly improved with this title's exhilarating real time battles, allowing players to increase the tempo of battles based on the amount of time elapsed and the skills they use. By unleashing skills one after another to chain together combos and aim for maximum damage, battles will excite players with their sheer speed and power! ■Communicate with the girls in a wide variety of ways! By listening to the girls' requests, going on dates with them, and more, players can communicate with the girls at the school in a variety of ways. By strengthening your bonds with the girls, they will develop, and new items can be obtained. ■Explore beautiful, mysterious worlds! In this game, you explore Heartscapes, locations that embody the heart and mind of each character. At them, you can enjoy travelling to a mysterious world where the voice and memories of the character are revisited. Note: Costumes can be used after unlocking Change Outfit. Note: For details about content, please visit the official site. Note: The game is also included in the set products 'BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light Digital Deluxe Edition' and 'BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light Ultimate Edition'. Be careful to avoid making a redundant purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: "Game is hella expensive but I still find it worth every penny for it is undoubtedly the most wholesome, most relaxing RPG experience I've ever had.The yuri vibe in this one is quite strong. With or without intimate content, possibly the best yuri themed RPG to have ever hit the shelves, a.k.a. my dream game. If you are a yuri fan, I think every minute of this game is to be savored. I'm sure post-game depression is going to hit hard with this one."-my review at 16 hours of playtime--------------------------------------------------------------------------Now that I've finished the game once, and post-game depression does hit hard, I feel the urge to elaborate on my old review..First off, actually my favorite game currently. One of the best game experience I've had in a while.===About the game===This game is basically a school setting fantasy anime with a twist, the twist being you are in it as the protagonist. If you've watched any of those such as Guilty Crown or Angel Beats, it's going to feel very familiar. The game does a terrific job at establishing the atmosphere of "living a carefree life as a high school student on a summer vacation". The story itself is a bit cliché, but is still interesting and enhanced by the whole concept of being in an empty school in an unpopulated alternate world. This concept alone makes the game feel very relaxing to play, there's no rush to do anything, you can explore the world and socialize with your friends to your heart's content.The game feels a lot like Nier: Automata, not only because of some of the later maps, but the general atmosphere of being in an isolated world too. Just felt like pointing that out because I love that game as well.===Gameplay===A pleasant mix of JRPG combat, base building, and dating-sim...? (kind of). Combat is easy to follow and pretty cool. As a JRPG combat system, it's neither too slow and bland nor too complicated, with its fair share of uniqueness. Character customization with the talent and fragment system is a nice touch, reminiscent of the classic Final Fantasy 7 and 8, and is undeniably fun.Base building - its existence alone in this game is pretty great, especially considering the game's setting, albeit a bit held back by the lack of ability to customize or actually interact with them. Pseudo-dating-sim - Just awesome. It's basically the game's means of character development, but you get to experience it more personally. The dating events are all wholesome and cute, and makes you come to love the characters so you can better enjoy the whole experience.===Characters===The entire cast of characters are lovable, some of them relatable, and all of them simply amazing. The voice-acting is spot on - exactly what you would expect from watching a good anime. They each have their own distinct personality, and learning their backstories and interacting with them are a total joy. Character development is done very well, so as the story goes on, you grow to love every one of the characters, making it easy to fully immerse yourself in the setting.===Visuals & Music===Vast world with photo-realisitc textures like in Forza Horizon 5? No.Beautiful world that makes exploration absolutely enjoyable? Yes.Everything in this game is pleasing to look at. Everywhere I go I feel is worthy of a screenshot, and there are places that are clearly designated photo spots. Combining the gorgeous scenery with a lovable crew, the photo mode is really a great tool to spend some time playing around with. Actually feels like a vacation trip, and gives off a nostalgic feel.Music - unique, catchy, and overall great. Sets the mood perfectly throughout the game and never gets old.===Yuri content===Even though there's no intimate interactions between characters or anything of the sorts except holding hands I guess, there is certainly a mild yuri vibe in the air throughout the game that I'm sure yuri fans can appreciate. My statement from old review still stands, I think it's the best yuri themed RPG out there.===Conclusion===All aspects are done decently, leaving not much to complain about. It's a fairly standard modern JRPG, with a brilliant setting and extra immersion.In addition, there's always this mood of nostalgia throughout the whole game, the feeling of being young, full of energy, and surrounded by wonderful friends. It makes the game feel very special, at least for me.For all of the above, I consider this absurdly priced game to be very much worth it, and I can't wait for a third game in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a strange game to review.  It's a decent jrpg with interesting characters, a story full of twists and turns, and a fun ATB battle system.  It's fairly standard, but it does it well enough to recommend.  THAT'S what is weird about it, though.  The original Blue Reflection was UNIQUE.  It was full of interesting design choices and systems that made it a hidden gem (though admittedly a janky one).  But in this game, rather than polishing and fixing those unique systems, they just kind of...removed them.       -No more distributing stats to meet skill requirements; just generic skill points to buy whatever you want.     -No more leveling by helping and hanging out with characters; just fight enemies for exp.       -No conflicted protagonist going through their own personal journey; just a self-insert, blank-slate protagonist.Compared to the weirdness of the first game, this one feels kind of bland.  It's a fine game overall, but I can't help feeling kind of disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: As a Steam Curator and JRPGs entusiast, Blue Reflection: Second Light is exactly what a player would expect and hope from a better version of its predecessor.Everything presented in its first instalment is either reimagined or evolved in this sequel. From its characters that unfolds better to the actual gameplay, which ends up being richer. Blue Reflection: Second Light strikes in with a story that works as a soft reboot to ensure new players and as a continuation of what was narrated in the first game and anime altogether, to please those who have already experienced the franchise in the past. The "magical girl" legacy that this franchise is keeping to its heart is still going strong and faithful, even if the world and the thematic are changing from the first game. Second Light succeds in finding a way to retain what actually means to be a "magical girl" while pushing to give something more, that was never presented before, without resulting excessive superfluous.If there's one thing that seems to be annoying, is that the fast-paced style of the combat, while still resulting frenetic and fun, doesn't make justice to the animation overall, as the player doesn't have the time to look and appreciate what's happening on the screen because keeping the pace of the battle is a core part of the gameplay. For this reason, I hope Gust is going to implement a "Pause Animation Option" to ensure a pause when the girls attack during a battle. With such options, attacks would be divided from animation that a player can appreciate while the fight would still end up being frenetic and fast. I already hope for a 3rd game for main consoles and PC![If you find my reviews interesting, follow me as a Steam Curator, I go by KureinInSight]

_childDocuments_.review: The first Blue Reflection was a deeply flawed but very beautiful experience; while I would never say it was a good game as such, it did evoke a lot of feeling in me and I really appreciated what they were going for, even if it did feel like an amateur's first JRPG project in many respects.Enter Second Light: a much improved sequel, with a great deal more confidence from the team producing it. Many of the problems from the first game were addressed, but unfortunately I would argue some still remain!So, let's talk disadvantages immediately; in order to fully understand the characters in Second Light, you must watch the Blue Reflection Ray anime first. As the anime goes, I'd say it's similar to the first game: a good experience with some touching moments, but very flawed. It's also not a short watch; you could skip it, but you would lose context around certain plot aspects which are otherwise only vaguely hinted at.Secondly, the battle system - it is dynamic, fast, and fun - but it is not challenging. There is a massive amount of customisation present in the game, but you don't have to fully engage with it, and the game is easy regardless. The camera zooms in whenever one of your characters is attacking, and since it's not turn-based, it means you can't actually see what the enemy is up to half of the time - you just see your characters' HPs dropping! There's a lot of different status effects cast on you by enemies but you never really have to interact with them, and the crafting system is surprisingly robust - but again, you never really have to use it.In the first game, the normal encounters were the weakest part of the experience while the five major bosses were the peak of it. In this game, there's only really one proper major boss, maybe two - the rest feel like sub-bosses, and tend to have the same music. There's no adrenaline-soaked massive epic bosses here until the very finale!Compared to the first Blue Reflection, I'd say the music as a whole is considerably weaker, though it still has its good tracks; it's a much longer game, yet doesn't really vary its tracks much, which only highlights how unexciting some of them are. For example, I really wish the home base had different music for varying times of day and weathers!There are many more "bonding events" now but they're somewhat poorly paced - the game will typically throw a massive amount of them at you at once, such that you'll spend an hour or two solely doing bonding events, and then have none for ages - while they're fun and give you good insight into the characters, it can be overwhelming - and there's one point in the story in particular where there's a great sense of urgency, completely disrupted by the game suddenly throwing a new slew of sidequests and bonding events at you, where all of the characters act like nothing is happening.Now, while the above are disappointments, let's talk about what the game does well: character. All of the characters are fun, have depths, and have great interactions. Much like the first, there are some strong emotional moments and if you're a fan of the Blue Reflection series as a whole (including anime), you're going to really enjoy your time here. The setting of the "endless summer" is both beautiful and nostalgic, evoking memories of youth and happiness, and it really has an extremely cozy atmosphere which will have you smiling throughout.So, to summarise: is this game a masterpiece? No. It's still rough around the edges in some places, but is overall a massive improvement from the first Blue Reflection - I would say the first Blue Reflection is a flawed game but a good experience, while this one is a good game with a great experience!
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: Long time ago, I had a discussion with community, ‘If one day, you get ONE ticket to a game world, you are granted to travel there and live there forever, but you won’t be able to come back, which game will you choose to go?’ The answers were vary. To me, the answer is: the world of Blue a Reflection, there isn’t another. As a long time fan of Blue Reflection, I am not going to praise 2nd Light sky high like I did to the first game, instead, I want to use this review to help the franchise at very least has the possibilities to improve even further for the future titles, since the 2nd game is different from the first one, we have the opportunity to see a larger scale of the world setting of the game; a bigger cast than the first one too. Before I get myself started, I’d like to state: 2nd Light has changed many things comparing to the first game, and improved A LOT regarding to combat system, general gameplay. There isn’t any doubt that Gust put tons of ideas and thought into making 2nd Light a better game, and did a great job to deliver the final product to meet fans’ expectations.This is where we begin to see the true potential of 2nd Light, though the game seems lacks of the depth of the developments of these ideas. Starting with combat strategy & bosses fights.I love every single character in the game, the art, costumes, personalities, interacted conversations, everyone is different and unique. And that’s exactly why I felt like the combat needs more work in order to let everyone standing in the front equally. What does this mean? Alright, I will give specific examples here. We have 6 reflectors instead of 3 in 2nd Light who can participate in battle, while having one support slot to choose one more reflector who will be supporting members in battle instead of fighting directly, only switching in if the tide of the combat changes. 3 place for 3 reflectors, huh? Classic. However, Ao’s combat efficiency is somehow bond with Kokoro, because her ability is doing high critical damage when enemies are under debuff status ailments and Kokoro has tons of abilities that inflecting negative ailments while doing damage. Which made them a duo, either one of them alone in battle isn’t going to achieve the max potential and efficiency they’re capable of, despite you can still do that as you like. Meanwhile Ao chan is the protagonist of the game, and the ONLY character in 2nd Light who has Combo Guard which is a skill that prevent combo reset from bosses’ special attacks. Which means, Ao is a must in boss fight, because long combo count= high damage, especially for higher difficulties. So logically, Kokoro would tag along, then only leaves one last placeholder for a reflector, in the other word, 1 out of 4 to choose. The problem here is, Shiho chan is so OP in the game, she’s like the Goddess of War, who can do massive damage alone while providing healing and curing status ailment which made her almost pointless to be replaced by others. Other 3 reflectors either is healing focus character(Rena chan) or damage types( Hinako & Hiori chan) who will rely on consumable items to heal or equip healing amour fragment for healing on boss fights which again, doesn’t seems necessary while Shiho chan gets both problem solved solely.Don’t get me wrong, I am not saying Shiho can’t be OP, she is a formidable reflector in battle and very heartwarming character in the story. She is my favorite girl and I love her from the bottom of my heart. I’m not complaining the difficulty is low on my first play-through either, I know Gust can easily make a game very difficult if they wanted to. What I am talking about here is: the variety of situations of boss fights 2nd Light lacks of WITHOUT increasing the difficulty. You know, even you can oneshot enemies, there are still many ways about how you oneshot them. The combination of Shiho, Ao and Kokoro(SAK) had done 95% of the situation in battle which got me rarely using the other reflectors in general. Because during the long game progress, I have more than enough opportunities to test which combination is the most effective against foes, SAK was the star-champion all the time.Now, let’s imagine a different situation the game doesn’t have, what if there is an elite demon/ boss who has a massive chunk of health, it start attacking your party with low damage, the longer you battle it, its attack becomes more and more devastating, eventually, if you couldn’t kill it in time, it will oneshot your teammate that you won’t be able to revive them in time. Well obviously, my SAK is all-in offensive type, and will be no good in a situation like this, this is Rena chan comes to play. Rena has very high defense value and healing ability, by equipping all kinds of defensive fragments and the fragment that taunt enemies to attack her, she will be a sentinel role which likely would be crucial to a fight like this. If we had these type of enemies, Rena will no longer be sitting on the supporting seat only, doing healing and curing status ailments most of the times. Isn’t this a better respect for her after all? Boss’s 2nd phase?Though there is a boss that you need to beat it several times during the story, but instead of beating it over and over with the same team members, why not separate 6 reflectors who participate in battle into 2 teams, using the support girls who doesn’t join in battle directly as a support per fight? The idea may not be original, but I found it’s actually suit 2nd Light the best, since everyone levels up equally whether they join the battle or not, and there are more than enough fragments to equip, making every reflector in a ready-to-fight statement. If there are bossses kinda forcing you to form 2 different teams to fight at the same time, I dunno, in a different phase or stage maybe, and everyone gets chance to participate in battle, while putting gamers’ understanding of each reflector’s strength and weakness to test, isn’t it one stone with two birds? For example, Hinako chan may not have combo guard to stop bosses from breaking the combo chain, but her special ability adds combo count instantly and support other teammates to gain temporary ability to do so. Couldn’t she be the leading role of the 2nd team seems to me? She seems fine to fight a boss with 2 other reflectors along, while team one -Ao is busy with the other boss?I haven’t studied deeply enough about how Hiori can do her maximize efficiency in battle on my first finished walkthrough, definitely gonna research more about her on my returning 2nd run. Still, it will be much appreciated if we ever get another awesome BF game some time, there are situations she’s a must in combat just like I listed above for others rather than players are desperately creating an opportunity to use her because we love everything about her dearly too. Last thing in this section, I’d advise one thing, the support slot is a great idea, though using purely support girls might be a even better way for reasons (a)every character is making contributions to the fight by doing so, not just in cutscene stories, it means a lot to the world of BF; (b)because of the existence of support fragments, I found there isn’t any point to switch a character in the middle of the fights, rather than fully prepared 3 set reflectors from the start. Reflector who has equip half of her fragment slots with support fragments won’t be that helpful and efficient in battle comparing the status she’s powered by fully equipped battle fragments, it’s better just let the support role being a full supporter all the time helps a lot which is a waste to let a battle participator doing so, don’t you think?Deja vu of Ryza ?Ao chan is a likable character, there’s nothing wrong about being a tomboy, there isn’t any problem to use a tomboy as protagonist in the game. But don’t you feel like Blue Reflection 2nd Light is a bit too Deja vu of Ryza?  Please see the comments below to finish

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Character interactions - An enjoyable and varied cast of characters that you will get attached to over the course of the story.Visuals & Music- The Heartscapes (dungeons) each have an interesting aesthetic and accompanying music that keeps you interested in what the next one will look and sound like.The bad: Combat system - Reminiscent of Xenosaga from back in the day, where enemies and players operate on an action timeline and you need to try and stop their attacks while getting yours in. What I didn't like was the Combo system and the drive system. Essentially, your characters will grow in power as the fight progresses but to me it felt like needlessly dragging the fight out and makes actions taken early in the fight feel less meaningful because well... they are.Crafting system - Will routinely ask you to gather items but often times will not tell you where they are and/or it involves grinding enemies for drops.Stealth missions - Sneak past spastic enemies while using objects for cover that may or may not actually obfuscate you.Story - If you didn't play the first game and watch the Anime, prepare for much of the exposition to fly over your head.Difficulty - The game's difficulty isn't very balanced. Early on it's a struggle, but about 25% of the way into the game you will basically begin to streamroll most encounters if you get a pre-emptive strike. Even bosses usually arent that dangerous - mostly just HP sponges.The ugly: Localisation - Typos aside, other bizarre narrative changes have taken place like trying to portray these clearly high school girls wearing seifuku as being in college. Even non Japanese speakers will probably pick up on some of the spoken dialogue not matching the English text as some words are fairly common in anime. This narrative change is especially jarring if you are familiar with characters from the previous entries and is borderline gaslighting.Yuri themes - If you're coming in expecting lots of yuri content, there isn't a whole lot of substance outside of one established couple involving two of your party members. The 'dates' the player character goes on could have easily been called 'hang outs' and would probably be more accurate as to how they play out. There is handholding later in the game, but as soon as you reach your 'date' location, the interaction is played straight 95% of the time. Occasionally you can flirt which is played for comedic effect and goes nowhere and there is no ultimate payoff at the end of the game. I believe this is referred to as 'yuri bait'.Fanservice - Unfortunately what the game is probably most infamously known for is the character designer saying some controversial stuff in terms of reducing fanservice. If you have played the first title, you will definitely feel that, but someone new coming into the series will probably not notice. For me personally, if that's truly what the developers wanted to do and weren't being coerced by outside pressure, I don't really care one way or the other. Having said that, the lengths they have gone to in order to ensure no 'naughty' upskirt pictures could be taken is both comical and a bit pathetic. In the end, I enjoyed it for what it was, but several things left a sour taste in my mouth that it tarnished the overall experience enough that I don't think I would have paid the exceedingly high asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: The first JRPG game that I really completed ever, so I absolutely recommend you to play this game. Let me get into detail about it.This game is just like a normal JRPG turn-based game, in which we have a character walk in the field and enter the combat mode when hitting the enemy. For the combat system, what makes this game's combat system different from normal JRPGs (or the ones I used to play) is the Real-Time turn-based, ether, and gear. It's cool and fun to play; even after 30 hours of gameplay, I still do not find it boring, which is one of the main reasons why I stop playing other JRPGs.As for the characters, Cute Anime Girl + School Student + All-Girl = The best. I don't have anything much to tell.Story and Plot: I find this game has quite an interesting story and plot, not amazing but not that boring. At least I managed to read almost every line in the game till the end, and this is from me who normally would skip all the plot in games. Some character arcs are better than others, some a little too normal and stereotypical.UI and Graphics: THIS GAME HAS THE BEST UI EVER! I really love how the UI looks, clean, easy to read, looks cool, absolutely perfect. For the graphics, just standard, not bad, runs smoothly, but in some scenes, I still find it quite strange.Design: I love map design and enemy design in this game. For the map design, every map has its meaning, every structure can refer to the scenario for each character, and that is wonderful. I enjoy walking around the map just to chill and find some minor details that hide in it (especially in the school map).Sound: Opening and Ending songs are ok. BGM is enjoyable, can listen to it for a whole journey without feeling irritated.Other Systems: Side quests and the dating system are cool. This game really put a lot of work into it, resulting in a ton of side quests for each character to do and discover, including dating in each scenario too. I also love it (although I didn't finish all of it). School development and crafting are also great additions to the game, making combat more fun and less repetitive, really a plus to a game for those who love big numbers and stats calculating like me.Overall, I would rate this game in each category as follows:Combat: 9/10Character: 10/10Story: 7.5/10Graphics and UI: 7/10Design: 8.5/10Sound: 7/10Other: 9/10If you are looking for a good JRPG game and this game is on discount, it's a must deal. If it's not, then it's really up to you. I would still cheer to buy it at full price though.

_childDocuments_.review: A massive improvement over the original. Would I recommend playing the original before jumping into the sequel? I would say yes simply because of returning characters and it gives you more insight into the universe of Blue Reflection despite all of it's faults.Second Light improves on everything the first did including a better port, Gust seem to be getting better at porting to PC while other KT properties are either hit or miss (Warriors Orochi 4 had a good port while Fatal Frame V and Ninja Gaiden collection had rather lazy ports). As for the new additions there is a faster more in depth combat system similar to what Atelier Ryza has. There is more playable characters (BR1 was limited to 3). They also added the two leads from the anime as playable characters, which I haven't finished. The level design has been vastly improved while also giving you more ways to trek across each area. Seriously, the level design in the first wasn't great. There is also live banter while exploring dungeons which give the characters more personality and makes the game more lively. Ao has the ability to date other girls which the first game kinda let you do. Another improvement and one I'm glad about is the overhaul of the progression systems. In BR1, Hinako and the girls didn't level up in a traditional manner instead they gain skill points from interacting with other characters in the game meaning the only thing combat rewarded you with was items. In the second game they scrapped that and added in a traditional leveling system through combat but also retained some of the original elements. Instead of gaining a single stat point from interacting with characters you get TP points that also level up the relationship you have with each character. The points you get from here can go into one of four trees. These can give a character a slight stat increase or an ability. Mel Kishida's art is as beautiful as it has ever been with high quality character portraits and designs, seriously his character design's in Blue Reflection and the Atelier Arland games are really good. The music still has that laid back feeling it had in the original. The story is also improved from the first because there is a mystery of the girls finding out about their pasts and about the world they currently inhabit. All in all Blue Reflection Second Light improves upon what the original did and it's really like Mel and the guys at Gust really listened to the criticism's the first game got and decided to create an overall better package than their previous outing.The game is peak "cute girls doing cute things". As for my favorite girls it looks like a tie between Ao, Kokoro and of course Hinako, the protagonist from the original who returns in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: My JRPG GOTYStory feels realistic, you get to peek inside the minds of high school girls that felt human, instead of over-sexualized & idealized template waifu typical of anime these days. For those thinking it's another 'schoolgirls save the world' story, then you probably didn't get the point of this game and should stick to Sword Art Online or something like it.Art is 10/10, Kishida Mel is the all time GOAT, and Gust did a fantastic work translating his art into 3D. The dungeons are vibrant and well designed, UI design is beautiful and crisp just like the last game. It's Tecmo Koei/Gust we are talking about, their graphics department is amazing.Gameplay has improved a lot this time, in all aspects. Crafting is actually useful and important in the game just like the Atelier series. Battle system is exciting, as it's real-time like FFXIII. You operate 3 characters and 1 support simultaneously which has always kept me busy (if you are lame then you can keep them on auto). There's no weapons and gears, so no need to bother about constantly upgrading your kit, just spend the APs and equip new fragments once each chapter, which is a refreshing change for an otherwise dungeon crawling JRPG.If you like girl-girl interactions and slice of life JRPGs, then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I finally completed the whole game and feel ready to make a review. If you at all care, sit tight and read the whole thing. If you're buying finger is itching to pick up the game, do it, but it's by no means perfect.Coming from the first game, the improvement in quality is substantial. Levels are way more compelling to explore, not to mention the sheer number of levels to explore is way higher than the first game.The old combat system, really to my disappointment, has been replaced with a new combat system. This new system is good, but I was hoping they would explore the "tug-of-war" (on the timeline that is) combat from the first game. The new system is still good though, but I have a few problems with it.Just like in the last game, if you tend to be someone who is a bit of a completionist (at least as far as exploration and doing side quests) you will quickly find yourself out leveling the game. This also becomes even more annoying of a problem since the Hard difficulty mode is locked at the start of the game, which I don't think is doing any one any favors, just seems like an archaic game design philosophy. Back on topic though with the combat, since you will quickly outlevel it, a number of problems crop up: 1) You are never required to engage with any of the in depth systems. Why would you care to engage with them if "press A to win" is all you need to know? 2) Combat becomes a real tedious chore, and waiting for your "ether gauge" to fill up just so you can 1-shot the enemies really becomes a trial of patience.On the note of never being asked to engage with the deeper systems: Holy hell do I hate the new "one-on-one" battle mode that are suppose to be an important part of boss battles (but you'll out level the bosses and quickly make one-on-one another trial of your patience). The timing is so awkward and the feedback is so negligible as to when the proper time is to dodge, and even more annoyingly it sucks that getting hit just 1 time breaks your combo. If they're going to have sloppy dodge mechanics, then it really shouldn't be so punishing to fail a dodge. Otherwise, they need to tighten up their controls a lot...or, imo, stop adding unnecessary complexity to the game. I think the game doesn't benefit from the addition of one-on-one.On the note of bloat, I guess Koei must have required the game to be a certain length. Let me tell you, the amount of levels in this game really would make it a solid 40 hour game, add on the school life stuff and you got 50 hours...and yet they still pad the game. Often you will be (unnecessarily) booted out of a level you just entered for (weak) story reasons, just to make you reenter and redo everything you had already completed in the level. Before unlocking the final level, you are required to trek back through EVERY. SINGLE. LEVEL. To do a boss "rush" (hesitate to call it a rush, because that implies it's fast). The game really didn't need the extra padding.As for the story...Blue Reflections is at it's best when it's dealing with interpersonal drama between characters...and it is at it's absolute worse when it's dealing with post-apocolyptic, sci-fi, anime nonsense. I won't spoil it...but...y'all remember the twist in Star Ocean 3?...At the very least, despite my hatred towards this really dumb plot idea (really, so, so dumb), it resolved in a satisfying way. At more than a few points in the game I vocally shouted how dumb the concept is, and nearly just wanted to quit playing. What a trite idea.Blue Reflection has always been about dealing with emotional trauma, and likewise in that space is mental illness. I was hoping to get some sort of satisfying melodrama once the schizophrenic girl was introduced, but leave it to the culture that likes to dig their head in the sand about mental illness to hardly give a real (and satisfying) conclusion to her arc (also, that playing coy at the very end of "what is this feeling" nonsense for raising her affection level...oof, felt like I wasted my time there.)Couple last thoughts before wrapping up my review:The school crafting system is fun at first, but Rust, this is not. Because "dates" and stats are also tied to building you construct, by the end of the game it becomes tedious switching out building in storage to check if there is a date available, then switching back to maximize your battle output.Fragments (read: equipment) also become a disaster by the end of the game. Sure they provide a function to sort all your fragments, but by the end and hundreds of fragments, it is a nightmare to try to sort through all the fragments to build useful synergies. I ultimately gave up, and still curb-stomped the final boss thanks to overleveling.Overall, here's the tldr:Combat is great with a lot of depth, but you'll quickly outlevel the need to explore the depth.The music is friggin great.The drama and emotions are higher than ever and really dealt with well.Anything that isn't dealing with emotions or interpersonal drama is stupid (including their tepid attempt to explore mental illness)The level design is superb, a massively huge step up from the first game, making exploration fun.One-on-one combat is the worst.The music. Equipment system needs work. Too many fragments by the end game.Music is super good.School development system is...interesting, but becomes a chore by the end of the game because dates and stat buffs are tied to the buildings you construct.Music is super good. [edit: snipped]Good game, do recommend.small edit:album's available on Amazon. I'm dumb. Go buy it. Music's good.
