_childDocuments_.review: The story of Blue Reflection Second Light is what impressed me the most. Considering that it's a Gust game and they're famous for doing slice of life of cute girls doing cute things, they managed to do a heavily emotional story this time. I think they were able to create a very heart touching story with very deep meaning and emotion.It's a serious story about evil gods trying to reset the world and delete humanity. You play with a group of magical girls trying to survive and reconstruct the world by overcoming difficult and depressing moments of their lives with the power of emotions. The pacing of the game was really good in my opinion, at each chapter a new character is introduced and as you go through each dungeon, the game slowly reveals the character's past, important moments of their lives, and a bit of the greater story about the existence of world itself.If you're coming looking for yuri content, you might get a bit disappointed because it's not the focus of the game. There are a few references in the game and the hangouts, but I'd say it's more about the characters being good friends. Even though there's no significant yuri content, you'll be impressed by how good and deep the story is.Illustrations are made by Mel Kishida, he's very known for his art for the Atelier Arland series. The character designs are great and the transformations are also really cool and completely different from his previous works. The magical girl outfits have a darker tone this time around rather than being all cute and colorful dresses.This Mahou Shoujo theme is still unexplored territory in gaming, and it's great to see it being implemented so well here by the designers.I think the most impressive aspect about this game's visuals are the dungeon designs. The dungeons are very creative, mysterious and beautiful at the same time, representing each character's distorted view of the emotions within their hearts. Gust really did a great job with the dungeon designs and it's a completely different take from the fantasy and colorful worlds that they make for the Atelier series.The combat in this game is very simple and easy. It plays almost the same as Atelier Ryza but the time stops when you are selecting the skills; it's a hybrid ATB and turn based combat.The main idea of the combat is to upgrade each turn in order to accumulate more points to unleash more attacks or more powerful ones. When the girls reach a certain upgrade level, they can transform into a magical girl receiving buffs and more powerful moves.The one-on-one boss battles are pretty much the same as Atelier Ryza with the real time ATB cooldown system.Dungeon exploration is pretty much the same of a standard JRPG that we all know very well, so there isn't much to talk about it.At school, you can receive quests from the characters, hangout with them and construct new facilities that are going to give new status boosts and new character events. Crafting items and developing the school is an important aspect of the game because by developing new facilities you unlock new events, and by watching the character events, you receive points to level up the character's status.The game took me about 40 hours to complete without rushing anything. I tried to complete side quests and watch as much events as possible.Music in this game is excellent. Composed by the legendary Hayato Asano.The first game's soundtrack was an absolute masterpiece and probably one of the best video game soundtracks ever made, but unfortunately it didn't get enough recognition due to the game itself not being very successful.The soundtrack in Second Light is more laid back compared to the first game. It's really good and fits the theme of the game perfectly, but I think Asano held back a little bit this time.I personally prefer the first game's soundtrack, especially the battle themes, but Second Light is still incredibly good overall.The port is the typical Koei Tecmo thing. The game itself is very polished, doesn't crash and I did not encounter any bugs or glitches, but the performance is not good.I was able to run this game at 1080p standard quality at variable frame rates that goes between 30 and 60fps on a GTX 1050 Ti. It's impossible to keep this game locked at 60fps even at lowest settings and resolution due to poor optimization. A more powerful hardware would probably be able to brute force more frames.The port is better than what KT used to deliver in the past, but it still need to improve a lot. Blue Reflection Second Light PC Port is not really on par of what they delivered with Atelier Ryza and Samurai Warriors 5.Blue Reflection Second Light really impressed me. It improves a lot in every single aspect from the previous game and has a very deep, heart touching and emotional story.No wonder why this very niche game managed to get overwhelmingly positive status on Steam. It is really good and I hope they make a third game soon. There's still a lot of room for improvement for the next game, especially in combat and graphics, but I think they already have the most important aspects that a good game needs right.If you're looking for an unique JRPG with a good story, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game despite it being overly simplistic and repetitive. There was a specific charm to it like the half decent battle system and the beautiful animations to go along with the plethora of skills at your disposal. The story was nice enough and although it could've benefited from having less characters and more growth among them all, it was still enjoyable.This sequel expands on a lot of the first game's systems and concepts, but despite that, it pains me to say that this is an utter disappointment to me. Here's why:So you play as a new protagonist named Ai who is trapped in a high school with a bunch of other girls who have amnesia. Ai is the only one who can remember her life before getting trapped in the school and slowly but surely, you could venture out into what's called the Heartscape to help the girls recover their lost memories of their previous lives.I like the premise, I really do, but the execution just didn't feel strong enough to keep me around. There was something about the beginning that was quickly disappointing. Maybe it's just how they're so skippy and peppy despite their situation and instead of letting you see what it's like for Ai to get transported to this other dimension, the story starts where she's three days in and already feeling at home with the girls.I think the story would've been way better if they all just had a ton of confusion about their situation and then slowly to grow to trust each other rather than being so instantly chummy as they were considering their situation.The battle system looks flashy and entertaining, but you barely get to really enjoy it because every character has so few skills and regular battles are over before you know them. I got a headache hearing the music shift so dramatically between the dungeon, battle, and victory, and hearing the same voicelines over and over again.Speaking of repetitiveness, when you craft items at a school it triggers a cutscene ALL THE TIME and it's just so unnecessary. I would've understood if you crafted something for the first time it should be a celebration, but no every tiny little thing you craft needs a cutscene which you can thankfully skip, but I kinda just wish it stayed in the menu and let the inventory number go up.Then of course there's an onslaught of boring ass sidequests that feel like absolute busy work. Feel like they threw them in to pad the time out and while you can get pretty cool rewards and equipment from them, it doesn't matter because combat is too damn easy. Or sometimes too damn hard in the case of mini boss enemies roaming the map. BOSS battles feel like it takes advantage of the actual strategy involved and it's too bad that middle ground of difficulty wasn't used for regular battles and save the mini boss difficulty for actual ones.So much wasted potential in this game. Another thing that really kills this game is that you can't take a few steps without triggering a stupid pointless cutscenes. Like c'mon, I really miss when video games REWARDED us with cutscenes rather than shove them in our faces every chance they can get. When the cutscene just has the characters making a generic sound or saying a generic phrase rather than what's actually written in the dialogue box, you just know the conversation wasn't worth recording a real dialogue for, and honestly should've just been cut from the game. Every dialogue scene like this should've just been scrapped because it adds nothing to the game other than a huge waste of time when you just wanna continue the dungeon and kill ♥♥♥♥.The music is still nice in this and while I'm not much a stickler for Japanese voice acting, I think the girl who did Yukio's voice did a great job. Something about her inflections were charming. (Hope I got the name right it's been a while since I've played this game). But yeah decent music, just not as memorable as the original game.I really wanted to like this game because I liked the first one so much. In fact, I bought this when I was only halfway through the first game because AT THE TIME I felt like I was really gonna get into this series and that the second game, considering its improvements, would hook me just the same. But it didn't. I've spent weeks apart between sessions because I get overwhelmed by how tedious everything is in this game. From the crafting, the pointless dialogue where the characters just have to stop mid exploration to talk about nothing, and of course the onslaught of sidequests thrown your way. I know you can skip them but having a list of too many unfinished things really trigger my OCD and hurts it badly.Couple that with my ADHD and my attention span for this game just gets ruined because as much as I'd love to have the patience to put up with the constant interruptions, KNOWING I can just skip them, I feel like I'm pressing buttons more for skipping crap than actually enjoying the game.If they focused more on engaging combat and pad the time out with THAT instead of sidequesting and sim dating crap, maybe I'd have stuck around. But no...we can't have nice things all the time.

_childDocuments_.review: In our review of Blue Reflection: Second Light we will provide no spoilers. We will only provide a brief synopsis of the first half hour of the game’s plot and characters. Overall, Blue Reflection: Second Light is a very lighthearted game, just like the original Blue Reflection. The developers have really learned from the missteps of the original Blue Reflection, and have made many improvements to the gameplay to make this title more fun and approachable.The cutscenes in the game are all voiced in Japanese, which Gust have been doing since the release of Atelier Firis and Lydie. All of the main story cutscenes are voiced, but the optional character event cutscenes and optional request cutscenes are unvoiced which is reasonable.All scenes will have English subtitles. The translation in this game was handled very well. The lines of dialogue flowed very naturally and there was no awkwardness in the translation. All of the cutscenes, both voiced and unvoiced, have a convenient auto-advance dialog option, so you can sit back and read as you progress through cutscenes.I really enjoyed the work from the Japanese voice actors/seiyuus because you can really hear the passion they put into this project. My favorite in this title was Rena’s voice actor, Maki Kawase, who, without spoiling, did a very good job of voicing several impactful scenes.In the beginning of this game we’re introduced to a new set of characters: Ao, Rena, Kokoro, and Yuki. Ao is the protagonist and is the controllable character. The girls have only met each other 3 days ago in a school and they’re getting along quite well. For some reason, the school has no other students or teachers.To put it briefly, our cast of girls find themselves in a strange world. The exit of their school has been destroyed and is surrounded by an ocean of blue, and they refer to the area as the Oasis. From Oasis, they are able to enter different worlds as well, which have a surreal combination of real-life and fantasy elements. These explorable areas seem to reflect the memories and emotions of our cast of characters as well. Our cast of girls need to survive by gathering resources from these worlds. They continue to explore farther in hopes of finding a way to escape from this mysterious world.Ao remembers that she got an app called FreeSpace (parody of Myspace) when all these problems started happening. She talks to someone or something called ReSource, who teachers her and the other girls how to fight demons and survive in this strange world.As you progress, you will recruit many more characters and you’ll also learn about each character’s backstories which you’ll confront and solve. Although the premise I’ve explained is simple, the plot is full of many twists and there is definitely seriousness to the plot during the main story.In addition to the main plot, there is a lot of side content. If you’ve played Gust’s other games such as Atelier Ryza, you’ll know that their JRPGs are full of optional events involving the cast of characters, and this title is no exception. This game has a lot of lighthearted fun with the cast of young adults with great dialogue and banter. Talking to characters level up the T. Level, or Talent Level, which unlocks Talent Points you can use to get more Talent Skills. These Talent Skills can include permanent passive bonuses to characters as well as improving how well they can create items.Your friends will also have optional requests for you to do. These include collecting items in dungeons, defeating a number of a certain type of enemy, or even sneaking through previously explored dungeons to find an item they lost. As you progress through the storyline you’ll unlock more types of buildings, some of which get pretty funny such as a Comiket market (indie comic stand), a giant teddy bear to hug, and even beds you can sleep on and watch the stars. You only start the game with a few spots you’re able to build in, but as you progress you can demolish useless areas to make room for many new structures.By making more buildings, you’ll be able to hang out with friends who are interested in that kind of activity. By using more materials, you can upgrade these properties to make their passive effects even stronger. When you’re out in the levels, you collect blue and gold orbs as collectibles. Collecting materials in this game is similar to modern Atelier games, but if you’re not familiar with that series, you collect items for item creation. The items you can create can include consumable items or new buildings for the school. There’s a new stealth mode added to the game, where you can crouch and see the enemy detection range as a glowing red colour on the map, but you cannot dash while doing so. It’s mandatory to sneak in one of the earlier game segments, but from there on it’s only used in optional requests afterwards.The item creation mechanics in this game are not as detailed as in the Atelier franchise. Rather, in this game it’s just basic crafting of items. You can have properties on the items you synthesize, but your materials don’t have quality or traits so to speak. The combat in this game is turn-based, but the turns are not discrete. Rather, you, your teammates, and your enemies are on a continuous timeline. You choose when to have you and your teammates have their turns, so if you want to wait to do a more powerful skill, you can do so.You also have a combo meter, and as you perform more skills you actually build up a damage multiplier. Enemies and bosses will telegraph “powerful attacks” as well, but you can use certain skills that allow your combo meter to remain unbroken from your enemies’ attacks.While in battle you will control three characters of your choice. You’ll always control your main character you select, and you’ll also control your two partner characters using the left and right triggers. You can set the battle to Auto to have your two partner characters do actions automatically. Still, the game was easy to the point where I still set my partner characters to Auto even on the bosses. Like Atelier games, you can craft items to buff your characters or even debuff enemies in battle, and you’ll be thankful to know that even bosses aren’t immune to all ailments all the time like in most other JRPGs. You can also knockdown enemies with repeated use of skills. Each time you defeat enemies and bosses you will level up your characters, which will let you permanently gain stats like any other JRPG. You can level up to a maximum level of 50. The soundtrack of this game is really great. It matches the tone and atmosphere of this game quite well. Many somber scenes will have a sad piano playing. It took me 50 hours to complete the game with all sidequests and all optional character events. It may be possible to beat the game in perhaps 20 hours if you’re rushing through it and not pursuing optional content, but this game is a lengthy JRPG no matter how you approach it.The optional events are intertwined with the main plot. Say you’ve finished a dungeon and are returning to the school. You’ll probably get approached by a character who wants to talk to you. The game also offers a New Game Plus mode, where you’ll carry over Fragments and also carry over half of your team’s Talent Levels, as well as all your Database entries so you won’t have trouble finding where everything is again. It offers an extra layer of replayability to the game.In the end, Blue Reflection: Second Light was a very fun JRPG to play through. It has a great mix of content, from funny optional content to a serious overarching storyline. The character designs are beautiful and the enemies look cryptic. I always felt that the original Blue Reflection video game was rushed, but this game has a lot of improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Some random thoughts:The game improves on the weaknesses of the prequel. Namely: More fluid and complex animations, less fan service, better textures and a whole bunch more yuri.The story is okay. There's some mystery and suspense going on, the girls are in dire straits but making the best out of it. However do not expect the mystery part to be resolved by logic. As instead deliverance comes from the power of friendship and lots of wishing.The surreal atmosphere and environments are what define Blue Reflection, its world is simply beatiful. And if you are a fan of the magical girl / yuri genre this game is definitely recommendable.A lot of time is spent on the backstories of the characters. It's mostly cutesy and expectable stuff you would find in your typical magical girl show. Some bittersweet moments hint at more complex themes but overall I think the writers could have delved deeper.The combat system is flashy, rather fast paced and has some depth. However ability descriptions are vague to the point of leaving you guessing. Mathing anything out requires extensive research because numbers barely exposed to the player.Apart from simply leveling your characters this game also allows for improving your characters through visual novel style romances. There are a ton of rather short and sweet sequences that contain choices for the player to make.The other possibility of improving character is by crafting facilities that can be placed around school grounds. Both systems are rather time-intensive and some crafting will be required to progress the story.The soundtrack builds upon the previous game and features very uplifting tunes, emotional pieces and intense dubstep tracks that all hit the mark. Loved it.All in all, a very heartwarming, emotional and pleasant ride. Would love to see more!

_childDocuments_.review: Schoolgirl waifus!! bring me more of them, Koei Tecmo, I always have room :-DI played the first game 2 years ago and really enjoyed it. I think I get why Gust made us to play all the game again in order to feel the same loop as Ao, and finally being able to break the loop, but playing it again with almost exactly the same content and get just 30 extra seconds, was a bit too much :sigh: ... Well, at least we got a happy true ending. I think I'm okay with that.

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Reflection Second Light.You can call it a miracle that we got a sequel.Due to being a huge fan of the first game, I had almost unfulfillable expectations. Will they manage to create a soundtrack which can rival the first game's? Will the boss fights be as a epic as before? And will the story be as emotional as before?Those were quesitons I asked myself since the anouncement.Well, some expectations were overly exceeded while others were not.Let me elaborate.Right from the first second after starting the game, I knew that they surpassed themselves in this matter.This game's main theme is not only super emotional, it also carries the soul of it's predecessor (The whole OST does).I stayed at the main menu for at least 5 minutes until I finally started the game. This theme is just too beautiful.Each Heartscape has it's own soundtrack. These tracks not only fit the aesthetics of the levels perfectly, they also manage it to convey the emotions and struggles of the respective characters. They will arouse some really complex emotions in you. I can't praise this OST enough.But is this OST better than in the first game? That is a question which can't really be answered. Those two OSTs go in two different directions. BR 1's direction is way more action oriented, while BR2 is way more emotional and deep.Well... This is one of the few letdowns. The battles aren't bad and even quite fun. But compared to BR1 they lost their uniqueness. And most importantly the boss battles are a joke (presentation wise) Coming from the first game, you expect these huge, giant monsters and epic OST accompanying them. But here you only get generic monsters which are  slightly bigger than the average ones... WHY? Boss fights were one of BR1's main unique selling points...Aesthetically, this game is just amazing. Given the premise, the heartscapes are all surreally desgined which allows some really beautiful levels. (Turn off Depth of Field in the graphics options!!!) Each Heartscape is unique in it's own way design wiseThe bonds which the characters form over the time are just wonderful.Also, the characters themselves are way more deep than in the first game. They are growing on your heart very fast, so that you can enjoy seeing them ovcercome all these hurdles they have to face. The whole cast is very likeable (yes, every single one).This deserves a special mention. I have rarely seen such a smooth introduction into the story.The mood which the soundtrack and the design of the first heartscape creates is hard to describe. It is magical.This game is more easy than being hard. But not too easy though. It feels just right, or at the very least a wee bit too easy (On normal)- When you move your thumbstick just a little bit forward, it can happen that Ao moves forward without moving her legs (reproducable but doesn't happen too often)- Long hair has some clipping issues (Especially Yuki's) and stuff like ribbons start to vibrate in cutscenes. Very annyoing, since BR1 didn't have such problems.They are a bit cluncky and a lot of people seem to hate them. But I think these sections were okay-ishEither I haven't found it (unlikely), or it really isn't included this time. BR1 had an "extra section" after clearing the game where you could listen to the soundtrack or look at some artwork. BR2 has none of these.Also unlike BR2,  BR1 had a small mini game  (nothing to special, but was still a nice idea).:The hidden Island DLC is a cash grab. 8€ for low effort (40min of gameplay, no new soundtrack, lackluster boss rush mode)It really feels like just cut out from the base game.Ryza DLC. This one on the other hand is worth the money. You get several new soundtracks, some new craftable items, a new Heartscape with a small new mechanic and some challenging bosses.Sadly both DLCs aren't voiced. Such a waste...It took me roughly 65h to clear the game and 74h including both DLCs. This is twice as long as BR1 took me.In short, excluding the boss fights, BR2 is a big improvement over BR1 in basically all aspects.Especially the atmosphere and characters interaction.PS: Gust being Gust, they included their famous "Barrel" (たる) running gag here as well :)

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Reflection Second Light is a worthy sequel and an overall improvement from the first game. While it is more refined and experience than the original game, it doesn't outclass it on every aspect, especially in the ones the first game was at it's best.I finished the game and only missed the locations achievements and the maxed out the T-Levels achievements, except for Ao's. I watched the True Ending on YouTube.A little summary:+ Excellent art direction.+ Decent graphics.+ Interesting story.+ Very good soundtrack.+ Lots of characters.+ Very well done character development.+ Good amount of voice acted cut-scenes and events.+ No grinding required.+ Collecting materials is not as tiresome.+ Shiho, best girl.+ Ao is a gigachad.- The soundtrack is nowhere near as good as the first game's.- Boss battles are underwhelming.- Same problem with character levelling balance.- Game is extremely easy on normal difficulty.- Battle system is not classic wait turn-based anymore.- Almost impossible to finish everything in one run.- New Game + is kind of meaningless.From all these aspects I mentioned the one that got me the most was the overly simplistic boss battles and the lack of dedicated music tracks for them. The game also suffers from having a not very high amount of enemy variety, like the first game.The battle system has also been modified to be more action-oriented. While it wasn't as action-oriented as Ryza 2's (in which the turn based system was removed in it's entirety) it definitely, in my opinion, made the game stray away from it's roots. I would have rather had the original wait turn-based battle system. This is just a minor complaint though.My biggest disappointment with the game has to be the soundtrack. While they nailed the locations music tracks, the boss battles and the music that goes with them are just completely underwhelming. I'm not saying it's terrible, Second Light does it way better than many other JRPGs, but the first game set such a high bar that it feels this sequel didn't even try to reach it. They even reused some tracks from the first game like some sort of filler, cutting them quickly with new ones during some scenes. It honestly felt like there were some complications and they just did what they could and not the best they could in the music department.There are few real boss battles in the game and lots of sub-bosses, but even the last boss fight feels underwhelming. Probably it is because of the combination of the soundtrack not being on par with the original one and some artistic decisions, but boss battle don't have the magic that made the original game so special.Other than these, the game has way better graphics and is arguably a more refined experience than the first one in every other aspect. I enjoyed it very much and while the things that I enjoyed the most from the first game are no longer there or are not as good, I think this second entry, as a complete package, is a better and more solid game than the original.If you enjoyed Blue Reflection (2017) you will enjoy this second entry in the franchise for sure. Hopefully there is a third game.

_childDocuments_.review: As a crossover of the franchise as a whole, it's probably fine. If you were like me and wanted a direct sequel to the first game, it's sorely lacking. The whole BR franchise seems to be about swapping and replacing, rather than improving and expanding. BR's combat system is replaced with the Atelier system. Main character is replaced with someone new, although Hinako does make an appearance at least. The entire supporting cast is replaced. The story's genre is completely different, aesthetic nods to its starting point aside. If all you want is yuri, that's still here, even moreso than before. Though Blue Reflection Sun even swaps that out.*minor-ish spoilers*The old magical girl with a regular high school life is completely gone. There is no high school, no society, no humanity, just an empty building after the apocalypse. Potentially interesting in its own right, but a massive genre shift from the first title. There's still some characters working through issues, but honestly, it doesn't feel as meaningful or believable to have them mulling over their personality problems when the fact that every other human is dead dwarfs anything else they could be worried about. Some of the characters' stories are more connected to this fact than others, but the point is that we're no longer in the territory of dealing with relatable coming of age personal struggles. Being socially awkward isn't very important when there's no one left in the world to talk to. Anyway, Blue Reflection's setting was mundane reality with a magical layer beyond it, whereas Second Light is purely magical. Story aside, the main advantage of this game over the first, to me, is having more environments to explore. Although this isn't so much expanding the setting as it is just having a series of levels to move through, filled with monsters and cutscene triggers. There are no NPCs beyond your party. The environments can have this ethereal, haunting quality at times, thanks to the dream-like setting, but once that started to wear off, they felt more and more like a set of linear dungeons. Also, imo, the overall animation quality seems to be lower than the first title, as well as some other issues with the graphics that feel like downgrades. I assume part of this is the price of larger environments, and probably more generalized animation sets or something. But worth mentioning. For a direct sequel, a continuation of the episodic story, an expansion of the character's neighborhood and circle of friends, more of the Common to explore, and tweaking the combat system all would've been great. Second Light isn't any of that. It's a completely different game. More expansive, but worse in some ways. I'll still recommend it, because none of that necessarily makes it bad. And players that come directly to this one probably won't notice any of this. Since it isn't a direct sequel, that's a valid strategy. Though in my opinion, the first game is the best representation of what the franchise should be, before it became this frankenstein creature, on its way to its ultimate fate as a mobile gacha title stripped of most of its identity.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't get to experience the first entry and just jumped into Second Light nearly blindfolded, without any sort of expectations whatsoever, but the enjoyment I had from playing the demo on PS4 around the time of initial release. While you can clearly tell it's not a high-budget production (although sold at a pricey, let's be honest), it turned out to be a well-rounded RPG in terms of what it can offer with its narrative and mechanics.If for some reason you can't afford playing the first entry, well, you absolutely don't need to. While there are multiple references to the first game which may indeed refine your appreciation of the lore, the storytelling of Second Light flows quite naturally, and you likely won't feel dramatically lost or hindered since enough story elements from the prior game should be provided to back you up.Now, this is accounting for the fact that you can put up with the cheesy, overly cute tone of the game. Because for the most part it's about cute anime girls doing cute things by the means of your typical "power of friendship" trope, and if that is enough to turn you off, I definitely wouldn't recommend to even try. Still, this shouldn't be a criterion that overshadows what I really did find valuable in the narrative — dialogues are rather well-written, at least enough for me to empathize with the girls and the whole dire situation they're in, being trapped all by themselves in a deserted school in the middle of an endless sea, having lost their memories and striving for survival, which in turn will lead the way to somewhat unexpected character developments and, without delving into spoilers, an overarching plot that's actually quite daunting.As for the gameplay, I can hardly not draw parallels with Persona since this Blue Reflection is roughly structured as a "lite version" of it, most notably because of its socializing/dating/sidequesting (aka powering up your team) and dungeon/exploration phases responding to each other, albeit not as extensively developed as in Persona. What shines the most to me is definitely the combat, although you won’t immediately see the full extent of it as you would need to reach the 10 or 15-hour mark to have more girls join the party, more Talents and other perks unlocked. That said, it's a very interesting and thought out take to time-based turns that allows for some degree of strategy and  time management, while also incorporating pretty interesting mechanics such as One-on-One battles, supports and character swapping, and you'll gradually build a foundation for some dynamic and fast-paced battles as you progress through the story.Crafting is also a nice addition to this game, as you might expect from the setting (being stranded on an island). Using materials you’ve gathered during exploration, not only can you craft items for battle and unlocking areas, you can also build facilities for the school that actually serve a practical purpose beyond aesthetics, as they trigger permanent buffs for combat, especially when specific facilities are combined. The thing I’m more nuanced about though is that the whole crafting system is maybe a tad too elaborate in comparison to what you can actually leverage out of it. In fact, aside from facilities and items you will be crafting as part of sidequests and level ups, it just isn’t worth figuring out the intricacies of the crafting system on a deeper level, as you most likely will rarely need to craft any item that’s either useful or indispensable for battles.And that makes the perfect opportunity to address the main downside: this game is  too easy, at least on Normal difficulty, which is the only difficulty you can access on first playthrough anyway. The only notable “challenge” was the final boss, and even that was a bit underwhelming. Never did I witness the Game Over screen even once in my entire run of nearly 60 hours, and I wasn’t particularly looking to max out the girls either. To put things more into context, I ended up completing my run while having 100 to 200 Talent Points unspent for each and every team member, which represents quite a lot of level progress/skills to be unlocked. The game just seems to be very unbalanced difficulty-wise, and I think that has mainly to do with the generosity of the effects you’re granted upon building facilities and through leveling up your party via Talents, maybe coupled with the drawbacks of a somewhat rich yet permissive battle system in which you’ll usually have enough time as well as options to anticipate your enemies’ moves (hinted on the UI) and react accordingly.On a more positive note, I absolutely cannot overlook the amount of dedication put into the art direction, especially when considering what ambitions could such a niche game possibly have. Well yes, this game might not be a technical prowess, but it certainly can deliver some gorgeous sceneries nonetheless (special mention to Kirara's Heartscape), as well as enjoyable soundtracks that fit well the ethereal atmosphere of the setting.There’s much more I wish to elaborate on but I think that's enough verbose, so I’ll just wrap this up here. But yeah, this was a very pleasant surprise overall. Decently good story , solid mechanics, good amount of content and a bunch of original ideas poured into that game. Only real downside to me is the lack of challenge, and maybe more options to enhance the school makeover thing would have been appreciated. Anyways, I hope to see more from this series and Gust in general. I did my entire playthrough on the Deck and it was playable. Not quite optimized but definitely not unplayable. The only thing I would highly suggest is to install the Atelier fix available on GitHub to gain a noticeable amount of fps, though you will still see drastic dips to lower 20s in some particular areas and weirdly enough during nighttime at school. Otherwise it oscillates between 40-60 fps most of the time. If you’re playing docked, be sure to lower the resolution to 720p and enable FSR. I also kept the default Proton layer so maybe you can tinker with that as well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the first game and enjoyed it I would definitely consider buying this game. If you haven't I do think that this game (the second) is the one you should buy if you are interested in only playing one game from the franchise (and are interested in magical girl light yuri JRPGs). If you want to play both the first one is cheaper, quicker, a lot easier to 100%, and directly linked to the second one.If you are a completionist, want serious yuri development, or care about challenging combat I would probably recommend another game unless you are really invested in the concept.As someone who has played the first game I found this game to have a far superior early/mid game story, although the ending wasn't as good as the first one (but still interesting.) The early/mid game (7 chapters which are basically character introductions) mechanics are also a lot more engaging with each character actually feeling relevant to the story as opposed to just "tools" to become stronger. Story-wise it does kinda suck that the first 7 chapters are character introductions but at the same time the entire game is pretty much built around meeting girls, going on dates with them, and learning more about them through their missions/events. I did enjoy it but it is very much a slow burn for 70% of the game (similar to the first game.) The yuri moments are nice but in the end it doesn't really go anywhere that far if you were expecting actual romantic relationships.Fights are flashier, but the combat is admittedly pretty boring due to how, apart from a handful of enemies, combat just isn't that challenging. The combat really suffers from an issue where every fight you start off weak and become stronger while building up your combo/transforming, making a lot of trash mob fights feel more tedious than they should be. The crafting synthesis function (create materials using other materials) being locked behind a DLC is kind of stupid, and the game having so many DLC is also kind of stupid. If you don't plan to buy any outfits/extra stuff then I would recommend only getting the crafting DLC due to how immensely useful it is but it's a shame it's locked behind a paywall so buyers beware.From a completionist's standpoint the first game is a lot better to 100% as this game has a lot of missables and goals that aren't always attainable in one playthrough. This game requires NG+ to max all character talent levels (individual achievements for each character) and the true ending is only available by completing NG+ (though it is only 10-20 seconds worth of extra content if you care about that.) There are a lot of  collectibles (locations) that are unobtainable after you finish the chapter they were introduced in, meaning that if you miss a location from the first unlockable area you need to go into NG+ to properly unlock it. Frankly, there are many things in the game that feel like they are just there to extend your playtime without offering any tangible replay value, so I wouldn't recommend this game if you care about getting all achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely niche JRPG with a lot of heart.Second Light is very much anime. It draws a lot from magical girl shows, iiyashikei and a bit of Moe culture. It you are into all of this, and jrpgs, it is amazing.Atmosphere is king here. The game does a lot to sell the idea of these girls hanging out and having a good time, despite being in a very absurd setting. The soundtrack is incredible,  their highlight being peaceful ambient tracks well tied together by strong leitmotifs. Graphics are serviceable, and although the character models are very pretty the enemy designs, lighting and textures are a bit dull. Each dungeon reflects a character thoughts, and they have some really good concepts. Bridges leading to nowhere for a character who thinks she's wasted all her chances and perfect sculptures for an ex ballerina who suffers heavy pressure from being an overachiever are some that come to mind. Unfortunately, actual dungeon traversal is uninteresting. The game will have you walking around, fight some enemies, press a button, read some dialogue and repeat.The battle system is ok, nothing fancy from a jrpg perspective. The highlight is the transformation mechanic, with which you can have one of the girls change costumes and power up massively. Its a lot of fun seeing their transformation sequences. Character designs are brilliant and imaginative, and they really come to life in their attack animations.The writing can be nonsense, especially when dealing with the overall plot, but that is unimportant. The game shines in the interactions between the girls, which are heartfelt and sincere. You end up caring a lot for them, learning their worries and their stories. The last dungeon is a bit of a slog as the writing loses itself in the world's plot, as is usual for gust games. The translation could be a bit better, sometimes the Japanese leaks through the prose. But it's a wonder we even got this game translated, and it's not pervasive, so it didn't bother me that much.Overall, an amazing feels-good game, for a very specific audience. If you are into jrpgs, iiyashikei anime and cute girls, give this a try. And while you are at it check gusts other titles, they are pretty much the only dev working in this genre, and they are pretty dang good at it.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is a difficult recommendation for a variety of reasons.  I think I am a poor fit for it -- its very outside my usual genre of 'pretentious artsy, hyper-depressive RPGs'.  I also hesitate to point people to the steam page because the store here has a bunch of advertising for DLC that, for lack of a better term, ogles and objectifies the characters.But I'm writing this review because I wound up very taken with this game and enjoyed it a lot despite its flaws.The pacing is weird, the gameplay is effortlessly easy and makes one wonder why they would add half the mechanics they did when you can roll through the game without breaking a sweat, and I didn't even realize "ether flows" were a mechanic until I looked through the Steam achievements.But this game oozes charm.  A charm I didn't properly recognize for a dozen plus hours, until I found myself looking forward to playing, spending time with the characters more, and by the end of it, feeling like I was genuinely saying goodbye to friends.That might sound silly, especially since many of these characters are anime and specifically Magical Girl genre archetypes, but those archetypes land, and are given a lot more nuance than I expected, and frequently without playing up terrible melodrama.  Everyone has their problems and secrets, but by in large, these secrets are pretty mundane and tightly linked to the central themes of the game.All in all, I really enjoyed my time with this game.  I'd want to give it a number review like "7/10", but that feels misleading.  The real meat of this game transcends my problems with it, and while I might describe it as a kind of video game comfort food, it was the kind of comfort food I really needed.Also Ao best girl.  Y'all can choke on my correct opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good.The main story is certainly where the game shines. Despite not playing any previous games in the series, or watching the anime, I was still able to follow what was going on. However, I probably would have had a better appreciation for some of the major reveals if I did. It was enjoyable, and had a few good twists.The combat system is actually really good. The problem is that I didn't really begin to see its potential until the end of the game when bosses are much stronger. I really wish some of the earlier enemies and bosses would have been more challenging so that I could experience the combat system at its best more often. The Date mechanic is interesting. Dates give you an opportunity to deep-dive into the characters' personalities, pasts, and feelings. This allows the player to become more engaged with the characters and the world, and the emotional weight of some moments will  be deeper to players who go on more dates. Most dates present interesting character development. However, there are some that are unnecessarily long and  boring. Although many are inconsequential (from a story perspective), dates (and side quests in  general) are quintessential because some stat boosts and abilities can only be obtained by using the points and items earned from them.All in all, I do recommend this game, but I suggest buying it when it goes on sale. It is a solid game that I had fun playing.

System was kind of active turn based actions on combat and that was very playable but how damage scales with number of actions performed and sometimes a character gets to 1 vs 1 on a boss fight were not to my taste. Atelier series is better. Buy this game from a sale and check provided game material if that is for You first.
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended, but not a full price. Thoughts below in no particular order:- A huge improvement over the first game, but still fundamentally flawed. The game structure and story is much more focused, but the scope still felt too vast for what the developer's budget could handle. - Minimal enemy diversity. Same enemies and movesets over and over with slight reskins. Even the DLC content reused the same enemies.- Poor game balance. The combat system is limited, but interesting. However, the game is far too easy to even begin to require any amount of strategic thought or planning. Hard mode is locked behind NG+.- I enjoyed the customization with fragments, crafting, and school facilities. But in the end, every character was shoehorned into a specific build with little room for diversity.- The characters and social aspect of the game carried it in my opinion. The amount and frequency of dates / bond events could be a little much at times, but overall they were interesting and entertaining.- Pacing of the story was all over the place. Started out good, but it was a mess by the end.- The stealth missions were absolutely disgusting. Who thought this was a good idea?Story Spoilers Below:I realize I listed a lot of negatives, but I made it to the end which is very rare for JRPGs I play nowadays. If the game is on sale, and you like cute girl slice of life then it should be a no brainer to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: The game has the Atelier vibe but is different as well.Its a decent game to play just to relax and enjoy the story.The excessive amount of dating that u cant skip if you care about the "game experience" can drain the gameplay.The crafting as well as the looting and overall character control on field really felt like atelier, althoits not an atelier game so the actual crafting part is a lot loose than the actual atelier games.The combat tbh looked less cool than the first game which is surprising actually..But overall the game was fun to play, but theres so many dating u have to do to get "skill points" I dont see myself doing ng+.Still the game was worth doing 100% completion for me, and that speaks the volume, since I am not anachievement hunter.But Id still say Atelier games are x5 more fun lol. Buy on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who uh, generally doesn't play magical girl games or anime:Art&music: The world design is gorgeous, set in dreamscapes, we see everything from twisted home settings to abstract geometry landscapes, all of which conveys its mood splendidly. Oftentimes areas will have a theme but then a twist that highlights it visually; for example a natural landscape dotted with giant rainbow crystals. These highlights do a great job at making the areas memorable. Sometimes these areas seem to represent themes in the story, but other times they seem kind of just there (like why is there a landscape of naught but ash between two natural landscapes, with no story beats)?Animation work is great; the characters all have bjillions of animations, oftentimes made just for specific one off events. Characters are really expression and genuine looking. Enemy animations are less expression and straightforward but good quality. Really great work.I suppose given the genre I'm obliged to discuss the girl designs.  Outside of magical girl outfits, there isn't much to make characters stand out. Different hair styles, eye colors, and heights, and a couple of them have different outfits. Actually it seemed strange to me that most of the girls wore the same outfit because they didn't go to the same school and only know each other in pairs (I know her but no one else) before hand. School outfits are unique to the school. The outfits are customizeable, but everyone gets the same options. We get a 'tiny' girl and a 'tall' girl but no weight diversity. With magical girl activate super powers outfits, they are all very very cool. A large portion of my critical thinking here went to which outfit/personality combination appealed to me most. I had never played the original but someone without knowing it, I chose the main character of the first game as my favorite for this game, because of her elegant and clear design. Outfits have strong motifs, with excellent highlights, much like the zone design. In a couple of them, the highlights were a little garish (the girl with the giant chains hanging off her most notably), but there really aren't any misses.  Unsure where to mention this but one girl uses two swords in cutscenes but only has one in combat-she also reuses some of her animations. I think there might be some unfinished work in that realm. Also, bonus points for actually letting me pick which characters to play with, as opposed to forcing me to use the main girl; that, combined with the designs, gave me a strong sense of getting to pick out my story. Some girls can't fight, for reasons poorly explained in logic if at all, but I suspect the real reason is because their animation and abilities weren't done yet. Developer went through the effort of giving characters normal clothes customization but I would have liked to see some combat outfit customization too.Music isn't my specialty, but I did notice several earworms. The combat riff is addictive and really vibes.mechanics: very cool combat system-I like it. Very systems driven and it has a lot of depth and strategy. I found myself theory crafting it quite a bit, and it made fights quite enjoyable. It did a really good job of making fights feel heart-thumpingly fast-paced while actually being decision driven. I would love to see it again in future installments. The only thing I didn't like was the one-on-one system, which only happened during boss fights, and it made boss fights too easy. Otherwise, there are lots of abilities and customization to combat and I always felt like I was in control.There are what? Maybe 20 different enemies before they start getting reskinned. Most of them are great, with unique mechanics you can strategize around; except for 'knock-down' enemies. Harder than bosses them. They will chain stun you to death. Bosses too are great, minus the mentioned one-on-one system. I was a little disappointed to see bosses are also reskinned at some point. "Equipment" in the game is gated behind going on side-quest 'dates' with other girls. Not only that, but girls level up and learn moves based on how many dates you've gone on with them. So you go on a date, you receive a random piece of gear and the girl levels up. I found it to be a really uncomfortable system, because it meant that all the systems were tied to me liking a character. I'm not a completionist; I didn't want to learn all the bits and pieces of every single character, just the ones I thought or hoped might be interesting. So I ended up with less equipment than I otherwise would have. The equipment is also random in that I will have no idea what I get out of an exchange. Several characters even have abilities that benefit everyone, even outside of being in your party, and the main girl's level is dictated by getting to know EVERYONE. Basically, it's a system that punishes players for not getting to know every girl.Story: As is I feel traditional with this genre, the overall plot gets increasingly abstract as it goes. I don't know if I'd call it bad per se, more like difficult to feel strongly connected to. Where it CAN be really good is in the individual character narratives. These stories have some great moments, some really, teary eyed, eye-sparkle emoji, want to hug the girls close moments. However, these moments are limited to about 50% of the cast. The other 50% of the cast are sooo forgettable, so much so that I started to mix them up (especially as apparently every character at some point decides to love cooking and start identifying as 'the cooking girl'). I started referring to these characters as the I-know-her girls. These girls only significance to the overall narrative is that they know a girl who IS important to the narrative--which is important because the plot centers around exploring memories. This is a case of the story being dragged down by the characters unfortunately. Considering the game also is missing a couple of missing animations (and swords), as mentioned above, and because many of the girls are just prototypes of other girls, I think this game could have easily 'collapsed' its girls into fewer, more meaningful relationships.It takes a good forty hours or more to beat, if that's important to you.Overall: It's good. I liked and enjoyed my play through. It's not like a perfect game or anything, but for the tier of gaming spheres this exists in, the developers seem really passionate and hard working. Mostly I'm excited for another installment, with better balance across the design. So you should buy this game so they make enough to let me see that.

_childDocuments_.review: I've really been enjoying blue reflection second light.I loved the first game but you could feel the first game was made with a small budget. The second game just plays better and fixes a lot of issues like the limited amount of maps, enemies, overabundance of useless skills in the first game.My two big complaints are that you spend the entire game grinding out warm/cool sand and the game gets too easy past the halfway point. This is fixed with the hard difficulty but you don't have acces to that on your first playthrough.The ending is satisfying and the music is once again absolutely amazing, I really recommend blue reflection second light it's really fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a flawless PC port of a great game. If you've enjoyed the previous game and the anime, then another emotional journey awaits you. Here, you will be building memories with both new and old friends. Even if you have no prior experience with the series, the game provides you with enough backstory to ensure that you don't miss out on the most heartfelt moments.Production values have been vastly improved this time. Character movement has enough weight that we don't feel like we are just floating around. The visuals are consistent, and at times breathtakingly beautiful. Mise-en-scène resembling contemporary art films from the first game is still present here. Both party members and NPCs move around the school and do various activities on their own such as watering plants or eating takoyaki. It's quite endearing at times just watching what they do.Bonding events are plentiful and a lot more interesting. As a matter of fact, I haven't come across any bonding event that feels trivial enough to skip - even though the temptation can be high as the main plot gets intriguing. One might say that there are simply "too many" of them, which can get exhausting. Also worth noting is that there are a lot less incongruous fan service scenes this time.Unfortunately, the game is not without elements that can compromise enjoyment. First and foremost - the stealth missions. I know they are optional, but the completionist in me tells me otherwise, and so does the character who has lost her phone and needs my help sneaking past densely packed enemy hordes to retrieve it. Enemy movement appears to be completely random, and the camera often prevents us from being able to see whether it's safe to move forward or not. This, combined with exhaustion from monotonous battles and a few uninteresting maps, makes the game fall short from being my favorite Gust produced game.Regardless of some annoyances, the game is, after all, an amazing experience with its excellent story and lovable characters.
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:The musics and arts are as great as the first game and the combat system is more flexible than the first game. The story plot is pretty interesting and still looking forward to see all characters' story line Cons:Without controller the game will glitch every two seconds, plug in a controller can fix the issue as the game manual mentioned. This can make the game experience very bad even though is still playable (for people who can bear the issue).Overall:The first game is good especially the ost and arts, didn't expect a second game of the series coming out which surprise me when I first saw the announcement. I will recommend this game since I have a controller to plug in to solve the lagging issue, I wouldn't recommend to people who don't own a controller because of the glitching issue.
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: Summer holiday JRPG that delivers well on core values and exceeds the sum of its parts - outstanding writing and characterisation, decent map design, complex ATB-like combat system and detailed crafting/building system (but with q of life feats making them really approachable).A key feature is that you can progress either by battling, or by developing relationships with the varied and engaging characters.Anime streak is running strong in this one, with a slice of life + light yuri experience combined with an over-the-top fantasy plot. An engaging, modern soundtrack and good voice acting for icing.Not sure this can be recommended for lower end gaming PCs. Visually: art but not without technical blemishes, and cloth + hair physics come across as a little broken (even mid/upper rigs).Game systems are well integrated (they support each other) my only gripe being I'd play happier if they went easier on the signposting (or just let me turn off some of it)There is enough content to justify a 2nd run unless you doggedly grind and unlock every upgrade at every chapter on first play (in which case you're spoiling the RPG/combat experience cause it will be too easy).Isekai/yuri/slice of life/magical girl fans will be delighted; likewise: have a good time if an all-girls cast is not off-putting, and you JRPGs but usually feel they are too grindy.Striving for objectivity, I'd say Second Light has evolved, and here is now a better game. Still, I recommend Blue Reflection (first game) as the ultimate magical girl experience; can understand newcomers may skip the first issue, but they'll definitely be missing out.
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, adorable, fun and engaging. A must try for anime fans. The game and characters are just too kawaii to even ignore ;)  Beside from the improved graphics and enriched in-game activities, some of the best OST from the previous title was carried over in addition to new tracks. The slow story development of the previous title has also been improved through more concise cut scenes, humorous interactions and interesting characters. Battles mechanics and battle animations are also more fascinating. Overall, Atelier Ryza vibes (battle & crafting) + Blue Reflection world (story & design).
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: Combat is a lot of fun, visuals are great, characters are likeable, plot is basically what persona would be as a CGDCT anime (so far, haven't finished the game yet). It very much does not hold your hand from time to time (or at least it's very bad at telling you what you're supposed to do/build to progress the story, and where you can find certain materials), I've got more or less stuck a few times and in one of them I ended up away from the game for a few months.It's important to point out that there's a massive performance problem - and there used to be a bug where the game would stutter without a gamepad connected but it seems they have fixed it - but I still find it very much playable even at 40~50 fps when it dips on certain scenarios for no apparent reason
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: This sequel is nothing to scoff at. Gust has taken some great strides this time around! The original game had some serious pacing issues by gating you with padding and any menial sidequests with not much pay off other than earning enough points to unlock the next main story quest. BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light quickly found its footing. There are still hunting quests, stealth missions, etc BUT this time you are rewarded for your time helping your friends by getting talent points and levels, new scenes and more chances to take your friends out on dates. It's not your typical JRPG. The pacing here will be a bit different due to BLUE REFLECTION's focus on intimate character interactions. In this game, in order to unlock new talents, its important to spend time and bond with your friends. By building relationships, your party grows stronger. This game is very cutscene heavy, but please stick with it. The character interactions are great and are the big highlight of the magical girl genre.Gameplay: 8/10The questing can be a bit mindnumbing, but the rewards and the battle system keep it interesting and fun. I am close to 20 hours in and I am still enjoying tweaking with my character builds and trying different teams. You will eventually unlock fragments which grant you skills and bonuses that you can equip to each character. Do not neglect these as they are extremely useful. They can be earned by going on dates with friends.Graphics 8/10This is not a graphically intensive game, but they have really stylized it and made it their own so it still looks gorgeous. Their use of colors and effects for transformations are flashy and fun. I really don't mind the repetitiveness of the transformation animations since its a key aspect of any magical girl show :DStory 8/10The story is definitely not for everyone, but I personally found it engaging. I found myself getting very excited when a new zone opened up so I could learn more about each character. This is an extremely character driven narrative and the interactions between Ao and her friends are the highlight of this adventure. I am not giving a summary because it can get spoilery quick, but if you really enjoy deep, personal narratives with slice of life aspects, give this a shot!Music 9/10The battle music is fast paced and fun. Each zone's music is heavily stylized to the theme and I really loved all the different effects that they used. It may not be for everyone, but I always feel like Gust nails their OSTs.Overall 8/10 I am so far really loving BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light. If you are on the edge of the water, just dive right in. I think Ao and her friends will make it worth your while!
_childDocuments_.name: BLUE REFLECTION: Second Light

_childDocuments_.review: Blue Reflection: Second Light follows the adventures of three students – Ao Hoshizaki, Kokoro Utsubo, and Yuki Kinjou – who find themselves transported to a mysterious floating academy, searching for clues to find their way back home, with only their names as memories. One day, a path leading to a new land appears, but when the three protagonists set off to unravel the mystery, they’re met by a series of deadly monsters. By battling the fiendish creatures, they unlock unknown powers that only seem to deepen the cryptic nature of their surroundings. Throughout the adventure, the three friends cooperate and struggle to make their everyday-life as rich and as fun as possible. While spending every day trapped in this unknown world, the characters’ true feelings and personalities will be revealed, and as their bonds grow deeper, they will acquire new strengths and abilities.

name: The Solitaire Conspiracy
detailed_description: High Stakes, Highly Powered Protego, the world’s leading spy agency, has been destroyed. Only one person can wield C.A.R.D.S to take control of Protego’s scattered spy crews and save the world. You. Guided by Protego’s only remaining analyst, Jim Ratio (Greg Miller), you must master the unique powers of each crew in a game of tactical Solitaire like none you’ve ever played before. Guide your crews home in a tale of intrigue where nobody can be trusted. Keep your cool in a world of AI spies and cyber-enhanced operators. Once you’ve taken back control of Protego, play infinitely via Skirmish, or test your skills against the clock in Countdown, a survival mode that will test your grasp of the game’s surprising tactical depths. For a new challenge every day take part in the Daily Hotspot leaderboards! Key Features: Five modes and counting makes this the biggest Bithell Short yet! Campaign tells a tightly packed story and introduces the game’s mechanics. For an added challenge, take on Campaign Plus instead, with its turn limits and locked tables requiring optimal tactics. The popular Countdown mode tests your endurance with wave after wave of unique decks. Skirmish gives you an infinite playground to enjoy unlocked crews. And, finally, the Daily Hotspot tosses crews into a new bite-size challenge every day. Beautiful original character artwork and atmospheric design put you at the heart of your own cyberpunk conspiracy. No heightened game of Solitaire would be complete without full FMV cutscenes, featuring Greg Miller and Inel Tomlinson in an original story from the team behind Thomas Was Alone, Volume, Subsurface Circular and John Wick Hex . FREE UPDATE The Return of The Merry adds new cards, new music, and new FMV cutscenes featuring Samantha Béart (North Star Rising, The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy - BBC Radio). The soundtrack for your adventures is provided by Jon Everist ( Battletech, Shadowrun: Hong Kong, Shadowrun: Dragonfall ). The game has received several updates since launch with more planned in 2021. FAQs Is this a solitaire game? Yes-ish. The Solitaire Conspiracy is inspired by a variant of solitaire called Streets and Alleys, but with some small adjustments and the big addition of suit based powers. Campaign, Campaign Plus, Daily Hotspots and Skirmish (choose your own suits and powers) are take-at-your-own-pace experiences that fit into your schedule. Countdown mode is a place to test your skills with nuanced powers against a ticking clock. This game is endlessly replayable. Are there microtransactions? Nope. We know we made a card game, and we know that there’s a risk you might think this game will charge you for unlocks, speed bonuses or aesthetics. We won’t. We may come up with a cool DLC at some point, and if so, will probably charge in the traditional way, but we won’t be charging you for double XP or a particularly shiny new colour theme. Is this Bithell Short an entry in the “Circular” series? No. While our previous Bithell Shorts ( Subsurface Circular and Quarantine Circular ) have been twists on the text adventure, The Solitaire Conspiracy is a new take on solitaire. We love storytelling and world-building, so it absolutely contains a full narrative experience, which we’re telling via full-motion video (FMV) and in-game lore. We decided to use the Bithell Short name to signal something digestible and original. Thanks for continuing to support these odd experiments between our larger projects. If this game is ‘short’, what’s to stop me getting a refund when I’m done? The Solitaire Conspiracy is our third Bithell Short (and with continued support from the player base our biggest). Our previous two games, Subsurface Circular and Quarantine Circular , both have a return rate of less than 2%. Steam players have shown us that they understand the work that goes into games, and are up for paying for ones that entertain them. Thank you (again). Do I need to have played other Bithell Shorts games to enjoy this one? Not at all. The Solitaire Conspiracy is an entirely different game from Subsurface Circular and Quarantine Circular . It tells its own self-contained story set in a world of spies and intrigue. Of course, our games are all set in a shared universe, so expect some mentions of old friends.

short_description: We need your help, Spymaster. Join a world of near-future spies and take on a supervillain in this supercharged take on classic Solitaire. Precision engineered for replayable espionage action.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game! A big shout out to the Bithell Games group. This game really takes the classic solitaire game and turns it on its head. Wonderful artwork, acting and soundtrack. Also I love the graphics and use of color/gradients in this game! This game is challenging and as you level up it gets considerably tougher but that is a good thing. It makes you think strategically so it's not as mindless as most solitaire games where you can buy your way out of a tough situation by simply buying power ups and jokers. You actually need to think in this game. There is also a story to this game that progresses as you do. I am still only in the first stage but it continues on as you hit certain level ranges. So very happily surprised at how good and fun this game is and whole heartily give it a positive review! Going to watch the team for future games and look forward to what else they may do. ❤️
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Total eye candy of a solitaire game, with pretty great music and FMV cutscenes to entertain you now and then. Probably one of the most unique and entertaining ways I've ever played solitaire. Note that this game does not use the more popular versions of solitaire like golf or klondike, so this may be a new way of playing to you. Just like many other virtual solitaire games, this one also features triggered special abilities that can heavily change the outcome of your plays. In this game you need to play very strategically with your special abilities, so be prepared to think carefully about your moves and not just fly through cards.There is a short storyline campaign in which you act in the interests of a spy organization set in a cyberpunk world. You are given the chance to pick your 'quests' from a selection of offerings with slightly different challenge levels and rewards. The story campaign actually acts as a slow tutorial, teaching you all the various tactics the game employs so that you have a solid start in the open modes such as Skirmish and timed challenges, which are pure solitaire games. There are leaderboards and achievements tied to your skill in the other game modes.Definitely worth a try if you've already played other solitaire games before and would appreciate a completely fresh take on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played Beleaguered Castle solitaire or Streets and Alleys. I mostly play the more traditional Klondike, tri peaks, spider and free cell. If this game is anything to go by then I won’t be looking to play BC or SaA in the future.  Throughout the fifteen levels and estimated thirty-five missions, I never got stuck or had to reattempt a level. It wasn’t very challenging. I wouldn’t say it was easy either but if you have any sort of solitaire experience it will only be a matter of time before you solve the level. There doesn’t appear to be much scope for making wrong moves. The idea of having a story-based solitaire game is not a new one but the presentation of the story is certainly unique. There is an impressive voice acted full motion video that narrates between each level culminating in an interesting plot cliffhanger. This was the most compelling part of the game yet it felt too brief and ultimately felt like a gimmick rather than a serious spy thriller story. To gain levels you’ll need to complete missions earning experience points. You will get a choice of missions each gaining various XP depending on their difficulty. Later, you can earn even more XP by choosing campaign plus mode which limits the number of moves. I tried this mode and it is actually difficult to complete in the allotted moves, so if you do find the normal campaign mode too easy you can always switch to this. The missions are irrelevant however. At first, I read the briefings setting up the missions and found them quite interesting, but I soon realized that they had no bearing on the story whatsoever and the GUI for the solitaire was always the same. There wasn’t even a background image relating to the mission. The playing arena is soaked in neon and it looks quite colourful but it gets repetitive after a while. The only difference in gameplay is the type and number of different crews you bring into the arena. The more crews, the harder the game is to complete. Each crew means another set of cards to order from ace to king. There are eight crews in total all with a unique set of abilities. On paper it sounds mouthwatering but in reality, it doesn’t add much to gameplay. Some of the crew’s abilities are a little confusing and most of the abilities seem to hinder you rather than help. The best abilities are given to you at the end of the campaign.I never quite felt like I was in control using the ability cards. You don’t have a choice whether you want to use them or not. Most of the time you’ll have to move these cards which activates their power, so there isn’t much tactical gameplay. You move the card and deal with the consequences!  There are a couple of other modes to play called Skirmish and Countdown. Skirmish is suitable for practicing with your crews but felt boring. Countdown is a timed mode where you have to complete as many waves as possible before the time ends. This mode was a bit more exciting with friends and global leaderboards. Most solitaire games have some feeble story associated with them usually mystical and very brief. The Solitaire Conspiracy tries hard to beat the usual fluff by introducing a voiced spy thriller FMV between levels. The story isn’t going to win any awards and is quite brief but I liked the idea and the game deserves credit for producing a polished and professional attempt. I believe that there may be more games in the series as the story ended on a cliffhanger.  There are up to four “Target” piles where you place cards Ace to King on. The number of target piles depends on how many crews you are playing with. Four crews equal four piles of cards. The number and names of the crews are at the top of the screen.You can only move one card at a time and not a pile of cards like some solitaire games. The jacks, queens and kings are special cards and when activated will perform special abilities. Examples of abilities are exploding the stacks and sending the cards randomly scattered to other stacks; ordering cards from high to low or low to high; sending cards immediately to the target pile and shuffling the stack randomly. The idea of the game is to fill each target piles with cards from ace to King.The FMV sections look particularly nice and the solitaire arena is neon soaked and extremely colourful. It’s a shame there wasn’t more variety in the card sections of the game. Some different backgrounds might have been nice.There is a dramatic tune playing throughout the game which is nicely arranged. The voice acting is professional in the FMV sections.Curator Info:

_childDocuments_.review: I respect this game more than I like it. The developer took the most mundane game in human history and did something interesting with it. That's worth praising. Also, I'm a sucker for good presentation and UI, so the game gets bonus points for that.Once I realized that there was no failure state, however, I also realized that the story elements were going to be mostly (really, almost entirely) disconnected from the game play. After that, you're left with a good, but not great implementation of a game you've probably played tens of thousands of times, and a story that's not interesting enough to stand on its own. I'm sorry to say that, because I wanted to like the game, and I want to encourage indie developers to make games like this. Straight-forward mechanics and excellent presentation are something I've been missing in games lately. I'm glad I bought this game, for that reason, even if I didn't actually care that much for it.
