_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy's story puts you in the shoes of the new recruit for a nebulously defined secret agency that works towards stopping conspiracies that would shake the world order. Or does it? An extremely tropey, predictable, uninteresting, so-so acted spy story ensues. This is a spy story told through a solitaire game that has some elements reminiscent of both Patience and Freecell. There are one to four suits that have to be ordered Ace to King on the foundations and the whole deck starts randomly dealt out in eight cascades. Face cards have an special ability that depends on the suit and that is triggered on playing the card on another cascade. The abilities must be activated by placing its Ace on the foundations and each face card can trigger its ability only once (exceptions apply). Every solitaire dealing represents a mission attempted by the crew (suits) in play. Missions grant experience points (extra points for solving a preset dealing in less than a known number of turns or a random one in an unknown number of turns). Exp points work toward leveling up the character's "credentials"; every bit of the main story is played on leveling up. There are six suits unlocked through the main campaign and two more available through side quests. ALL the actual gameplay consists on playing solitaire dealings. There's usually a selection of three available "main" missions that determine the flavor and the crews available, which has an impact on the difficulty through the number of suits in play and the specific abilities of those suits. The abilities order stacks or grab cards according to different criteria, grant free placements on the foundations or offer ways to reactivate spent abilities. Strictly speaking, all the abilities can be used for strategic benefit; in reality, some are powerful positive abilities, some others are hindrances and a few are in between. It might be some card dealings cannot be solved but if they exist they are extremely rare. The solitaire game is not very fun and feels a bit like a chore, particularly with a full (four) crew set.The dialog bits of the story start nice enough but get progressively worse. The story barely makes any sense. Besides their lore, there's some intent of characterizing the crews through the self-contained narrative bits of the stories they take part in; there's some implication that they are, so to say, independent agents with their own agendas and failings -- this is tangentially mentioned in the main story but mostly left unexplored. Mission bits are dissociated from the main story, except for sharing an antagonist. Absolutely no philosophical, ethical or intellectual questions are posed; rule of cool prevails.Besides the classical randomized mission and its preset dealing variant, both already mentioned, there is a time attack solitaire mode, a daily challenge and a free mode where the player can freely choose the crews involved. No new twists are introduced. Finishing the story allows the player to keep playing the same missions that were used for the main story to advance; the missions start to repeat themselves during the main story, but this is particularly noticeable after the ending. The fact that those missions are still available after the ending kind of makes sense, but the story bits should probably be adapted to after-the-end world status quo.The story occurs in a near-future hypermodern only-moderately-cyberpunk setting; the interface strongly reflects this. Main campaign and sidequest progress both unlock different palettes for the interface; there's an absurd number of them, with a lot of them extremely similar. You are encouraged to keep your current one only until you have unlocked the next one. The character roster of the crews and the actual live actors cover a very wide spectrum of identities, as long as they are cool. The OST is the child of Jon Everist, of Shadowrun and BattleTech fame, but the composition for this game feels quite generic.The achievements are mostly tied to the main story. Five of them require exploring the extra modes. Only one of them is remotely difficult.I appreciate what they were trying to do, and the result is quite slick insofar usability and looking pretty are concerned, but all in all The Solitaire Conspiracy makes for a poor solitaire and a poor conspiracy.Verdict: D

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting mix of Solitaire, narrative, and FMV.You are The Spymaster, you must stop an evil villan by playing a card game using crews that you unlock access to as you level up. Each crew has their own powers, some helpful, some quite unhelpful at times- sometimes downright negative to your strategy. Strategy is key- you have to plan your moves and use of crew members well, to complete the table in as few moves as possible.There are 2 modes- one very casual, with no turn limits, and one with turn limits that can be somewhat frustrating if RNG deals you a crappy table layout. You can choose between them at the start of each table, the more difficult one giving higher XP toward leveling up.There are what I would call "minigames" on some maps- Skirmishes, which let you choose your crews from those you have already unlocked it seems- no XP for these, just practice and 2 achievements tied to the minigame. At the time of this review I have not tried the Countdown minigame- so I can't really say how it works or if it's enjoyable. I may update this review after I try it, I may not.There are also Recruitment games on some maps, where you play to try to free or recruit a new group. No XP for those either, but it seems to be tied to the campaign narrative that you must complete. Each of these games gives a % toward completion toward recruitment.The game is visually very nice, if a bit busy with the color schemes at times. As you advance, you will unlock new color schemes to use on your tables.The music is suitably "urgent", giving a feeling that you are on an important mission that could go very wrong.The FMV is very well done, as is the voice acting. The dialogue and narrative are a bit beyond cheesy, though. Think "bad hacker/IT/Programmer humor memes" type of jokes and references. But even though a few of the jokes have made me raise an eyebrow at times, some have made me chuckle- and it is a break from tension before you move on to the next level map.If you are looking for difficult classic solitaire, this isn't it. Go get the Zachtronics Solitaire Collection for that.If you're looking for something with a story, some silliness, strategy and using you brain needed in varying degrees (based on mode or minigame)- it's good. Not great, but good. Suitable for short sessions, all dialogue is captioned so it is doable for Deaf/HoH gamers, though the captions and dialogue can move quickly with no way to replay it if you missed something, and the text is small with no option to scale it that I could find.The game runs flawlessly on Windows 10 22H2 Pro/ i9 11900K/ 3080 RTX Ti/ 32 GB DDR4, and it also runs flawlessly on my older desktop on Windows 10 22H2/ i9 9900K/ 2070 RTX Super/ 16 GB DDR4. I have not tried it on Linux with Proton yet, so I can't say how well it plays on any Linux distro. ProtonDB shows it as Gold (with tweaks) and the video playback issues reported 2-3 years ago seem to be fixed, though it is noted that the small text is an issue on Steam Deck.I did get the game at 50% off, and have no problems with paying that amount. I won't know if it's worth full price until I complete the full game and have it 100%'d, but I suspect I would not have too many issues with paying full price for the game due to its uniqueness amongst Solitaire/Card games.(quick edits for typos and formatting error corrections)

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy did two things I thought were impossible: first, it made me play a game of Solitaire; and second, it made me enjoy it. The third Bithell Games short (after Subsurface Circular and Subsurface Quarantine) is a sci-fi thriller where players must take over a spy agency called Protego and wield it against a global threat—and they do this by playing rounds of Solitaire, of course.The premise is simple enough and a quick tutorial will bring those unfamiliar with Solitaire up to speed. You’re given a spread of shuffled cards and need to sort them in a central pile from Ace to King; on the rest of the board, you can place cards on top of other cards if they’re of a smaller value. That’s it. Well, it would be, but The Solitaire Conspiracy adds its own twist to the classic: each card suit represents a different group of agents with a unique set of abilities that you use by playing their picture cards (Jack, Queen, and King). Drive Team Six will fast-track the next card of the suit you place them on, the Mantis Group will explode a pile of cards, scattering them randomly among the other piles on the board, and so on.Leveling up unlocks new interface themes and spy crews. As you play through the campaign and level up, you’ll unlock these agencies (8 in total), each with their own backgrounds, visuals, and characters. The abilities they bring to the table add a layer of complexity absent from regular Solitaire, as depending on how you play an agent you might either ruin your strategy or consolidate it—with the exception of a couple of agencies, most abilities are double-edged swords that can hurt you just as much as they can help you. Even those that seem completely negative, such as shuffling a pile from highest rank to lowest, can be used in positive ways if you give it some thought.They’re also the main source of variety in the game, as the missions themselves are always the same; in fact, if there’s one thing I wish the game had done, it’s more mission variety. Timers, conditions, handicaps would all make perfect sense in the setting, but are sadly left untouched (with the exception of the Countdown mode, where you race against the clock to complete as many rounds as possible).All of this is conveyed through fantastic visuals and UI. In a way it reminded me of Zachtronics puzzle games, where mostly static gameplay is serviced by a ridiculously polished interface and beautifully rendered backgrounds/character portraits. If you asked me to make a sci-fi spy game about playing Solitaire, this is what I’d aim for as an ideal. The story itself is told by a series of short FMV cutscenes centered mostly on Protego’s analyst and your handler, Jim Ratio (Greg Miller of Kinda Funny). FMV scenes always feel like a blast from the past, but in The Solitaire Conspiracy’s case they fit in with the game’s mood and humor well enough.The campaign will take you around three hours to complete, if not less: it mostly involves playing enough of the game’s missions to get you to level fifteen. Other than the FMV cutscenes, you can get glimpses of Solitaire’s sordid affairs, your agents, and the world in general through the short mission descriptions. Once beaten, there’s little reason to do so again—there are no choices to make, and if you just want to play the game’s version of Solitaire, you can do so in the Skirmish and Countdown modes.The Solitaire Conspiracy delivers exactly what it promises: a short game centered on playing Solitaire. It does this with plenty of flair and aplomb, from its stylish visuals, inspired soundtrack (from Jon Everist, of Battletech and Shadowrun fame) and high-stakes story, this isn’t exactly the Solitaire you recall your mum playing in the 90s.

_childDocuments_.review: Bithell strikes again!So listen, it's Solitaire with cool abilities tied to the face cards (J, Q, K). Simple as that. If that doesn't interest you, fine. The music is faaaar better than anything I expected. And the man of the hour, Greg Miller, is hilarious and honestly pretty damn good. Mike Bithell did an intelligent job of wrapping the character of Jim Ratio around Greg. Sure, if you have trouble looking past a face/voice of a popular media personality, then it's just Greg playing the story with you. But 2 hours in, I'm loving it. Greg is perfect for the role of a witty *guy-in-the-chair*.Very excited to finish the story, and considering how addicting solitaire can be, that very well could be today.Summary: BUY IT, especially if you dig solitaire, vibrant art styles, and Greg Miller.

_childDocuments_.review: i knew the game will be boring to me, good enough for few spreads per session only, nothing to spend hours with, so i didn't buy at the regular price & i was right. sure, the design is absolutely flashy, acting is good, music fits, though all that fancy spy drama is really lost on me, same with the strategic part which is too complicated for my taste, but that's really just me, if someone likes complex strategic planning, the game surely delivers & leans therefore towards a puzzle game. the solitaire itself is pretty simple, start with Asses & build up to King, so a variation of Freecell or Klondike & theresuch. i suppose the spreads are all solvable, but the difficulty comes from the different modern gimmicks like changing the sequence of cards when one card is placed on another or removing of the already placed Asses & following cards back into the mix. all in all a good game though breathtaking only on the design side, not gameplaywise. but i think people who usually like complex puzzle games to ponder about might be positively surprised with this solitaire game.  i've got it now at a discount of 1,99€ & don't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason for a negative review here is if you are not familiar with Solitaire. Yes, guys, it is played with cards. Any talk of lack of content should also be dismissed. Once you reach higher levels in the admittedly short campaign, you unlock different ways to play the game, including timed runs and competing for high scores against other players on the net. No hand is the same. If you don't like your hand, just restart the hand and the game will draw you a new, completely random one, just like playing with a deck of cards. The only fixed runs are the ones with turn limits, which are optional. I am planning to tackle those once I finish the campaign and hopefully have learned enough to beat them. The strategy involving the powers of the face cards of the various factions is complex and rewarding, the presentation is top notch - stable and slick - and the live acting is fun and doesn't take itself too seriously. This is hands down (pun intended) the most fun I have ever had playing Solitaire, and a must-buy for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice take on the Solitaire game. You play with crews and the crews represent a suit (Ace, numbers, Jack, Queen and King). When you place the Ace, the suit becomes active and the J, Q and K cards get charged. Play a charged card and it gives the crews power. Matches have up to 4 crews active and the mixing of the powers leads you to solving the Solitaire "puzzle".The rules are slightly different from the real Solitaire, but you still have to clear the board in neat piles of suits. It plays fairly quick and is ideal for when you don't have much time.There is a campaign that is a few hours long. It currently also has a mini side campaign to gain an extra suit for skirmishes and from whwat I've read in the roadmap later this year another mini campaign with a new suit will be released. So the devs are still working on the game, which is nice. When the campaign is over, you still have the option to keep playing missions, which basically are skirmish matches. You also have the option to actually play skirmish, where you can select the suits to play with. Lastly there is a countdown mode, which basically is a bunch of timed skirmishes where placing cards on the piles adds time.All in all it's a neat little game with a few game modes that are nicely put together. As said, the various crews and crew powers give a nice variation. It can be played in a few hours to completion of the campaign and is ideal for short time moments. I recommend this game if you like card games and just want a simpler nice inbetweener.Also a note for the achievement hunters, you can 100% it as you go. The only achievements out of the way are the ones tied to the Countdown and Skirmish, but those are fairly easy to get as well. I'm not an achievement hunter, but I got them all through just playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who avidly played Microsoft Solitare's daily challenges for several years, I found this game to be a really fun challenge!As other reviews have already said THIS IS A SOLITAIRE GAME AS THE TITLE SAYS! There is a storyline going on here, and it's interesting enough as a sideline. But cool and fun as I personally thought the story and setting were, it really is not the main focus of the game, let that be said.However, I don't feel you need to be experienced to play this game. It's fairly easy to get the hang of it with practice. On the other hand, if you are experienced and want a challenge, I'd suggest you play the missions with move limits, makes for a more satisfying experience.I don't agree with some of the other reviews here that say either that the ability cards are "cheating" or "not as useful as they should be". I feel that all the ability cards must be used strategically to be effective. It's just a different way to play solitaire, a different game mechanic. Everyone has their preferences of how they want to play. Some people like the original klondike, some people like freecell. Others will love playing solitaire, whatever form it comes in. Sound like you? You'll probably love this game!Other notes:- Graphics are great!- Music is suspenseful (I'm sure some will love it, while others will find it irritating after a while)- This game is exactly what the developers state on the store page. It is short. It is solitaire. If you didn't read the page well... why are you down here reading my review already?Conclusion: I really like this game, both as a solitaire player and a fan of the other Bithell games. I can see myself playing it a lot more when I just want to pass some time. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm rooting for Mike Bithell.I loved Thomas Was Alone, I enjoyed the first half of Volume and I quite liked Subsurface Circular. All Bithell Games take place within a shared narrative, and it's very compelling to look for how the events of earlier games influence the context of later ones. After two "dialogue simulator" games, Solitaire Conspiracy seems to be an attempt to return to more gameplay-focused, uh, gameplay. Unfortunately, that gameplay is pretty lacking. Most of the reviews so far can be summed up as, "Buy this game if you like Solitaire!" I would revise that to, "Buy this game if you  Solitaire." It's adequate, and the powers are neat, but so situational I often found myself using them only half the time.The reward structure is so strange. In the main campaign, you earn bonus points for beating a level within a certain number of turns - but you aren't told what that number is, and there's no indication of whether it changes based on whether RNG gives you a tricky hand. (I encountered quite a few Aces stuck behind Kings.) Once you beat the game you unlock Countdown mode, which throws out the turn-based rewards in favor of a time-based reward system. Countdown is  hard, by the way. I don't know what kind of Speed Chess savants are getting to the top of the leaderboard or whether it's just hackers, but less than half of the people who beat Wave 5 manage to get to Wave 10, and you need to get to Wave 15 to 100% the game.The art is great, the flavor text is mostly good, the FMV acting is... fine? I saw the first twist coming even before the anagram, and the ending wasn't much of a shock. Greg Miller puts in a good effort, but most of the videos consist of him congratulating you for levelling up while the story is running in place, so there's not much for him to work with. Even the mission descriptions are often underwhelming. Between footraces, fistfights and general faffing about, quite a few of them seem to amount of the good guys getting into a measuring contest with the bad guys. Some are so bizarre (breaking fugitives out of prison in the hopes that they'll volunteer nondescript intel afterward?!) that I legitimately thought some of them might have been planted by the bad guys to dupe the good guys into doing their bidding. Unfortunately, nothing that interesting was going on.There are so many events alluded to that sound more interesting than the card game you're playing. I wanted to read that manifesto! I wanted to see that space station break-in! But no; different flavor text, same game. It brings me no joy to say that I sometimes wished I was looking through a digital artbook or even a graphic novel rather than just moving cards around. Asking players to imagine that rearranging these cards represents the management and maneuvering of agents in the field strains credulity to its breaking point - and that's coming from someone who was 100% bought in to the idea of a small red rectangle being the liberator of artificial intelligence!Ultimately, the entire experience left me unenthused, which is a shame. Mike Bithell is completely capable of making videogames that really impress me. Unfortunately, this one didn't.Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: rarely give reviews. but this has been my main game since it came out. the mechanics each suit brings give so much strategy to think about. combine that with other playstyles like countdown where you need to quickly make those decisions or now with campaign+ think long and hard as each turn counts when you have limited moves.love the visuals on this game. but more importantly, this game allows me to play in short spans of time. you don't need a huge commitment of time to play a round or 2. given that i now have a kid and a wife to take care of, my time is limited and i appreciate the joy this game gives me in 15 minutes or even less. Thank you so much Mike Bithell and the team for making games that are full of value, and that is not a time sink. I truly appreciate this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Bithell? More like Bit heaven! Mike Bithell and his team have a genius where they can take something familiar and well worn (platformer, text adventure, stealth, er... John Wick?) and infuse it with so much character, intelligence, story and warmth that it's the kind of art that changes you when you experience it. Their treatment of solitaire may not kick you squarely in the feels like Thomas was Alone or the Circular games BUT it is a great game and has a great twist where the picture cards are characters with powers that alter the game. The short story is great and keeps you hooked until the end (I'll say no more to keep this spoiler free) and then there are the modes you unlock play playing the campaign - this is what you'll be playing tomorrow and after that. Countdown is a cool endless mode with a global leaderboard which is both exciting and addictive with that "just one more turn" quality to it. Skirmish mode lets you experiment with the different spy teams - analogous to the suits (clubs, hearts etc) except there are much more than four to choose from, each with their own unique abilities!Finally the visuals on this game are incredible. You almost certainly have not played a card game as gorgeous as this - the videos on the steam store don't do it justice. Your eyeballs need to see this running in HD+, 144Hz, dripping with neon in the palette of your choice.This game is fantastic value, is eminently replayable, fits around your schedule for long or short sessions and the card abilities keep it fresh, giving you gameplay you just won't get anywhere else. I love it.Update: A daily challenge was introduced so now you can compete with players around the world to use the least moves to solve a non-random daily game. This is a great addition which compels you to replay the game just to beat that person who used one less move than you! It really makes you think about the teams, even ones you don't like, and how they can work together for maximum efficiency. There's no time limit other than the daily reset and it is pretty satisfying to use your skills to indirectly compete with other humans. Refining your game so you leap up ten or twenty places on the leaderboard is incredibly satisfying, more so than completing the campaign, and it keeps me coming back every day.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game but I can’t. There is a great foundation here to build upon however.The Solitaire Conspiracy is a fabulously made game with a great premise. Why don’t I recommend it? Beyond just Solitaire and a slick interface, there’s not much else there.I don’t usually post reviews but since more work was announced to be made on the game I thought I’d provide my 2¢ in the unlikely event a developer reads this.I’ll try to keep it brief:

_childDocuments_.review: There's enough praise already of the execution of this beautiful little game, so I can be honest and say that it just doesn't work, as a game.The problem is that in the actual game, there's just no wrong move. There's no situation that you can create that is even remotely unfixable. You can just click around almost randomly, or loosely in the right "direction", and simply win. It's not even "too simple", it's just not even a puzzle at all, not in any way. You can't even make your life harder - except by accidentally using an "agent", an addition to the normal card rules that is mostly useless and makes one want to avoid using them as much as possible. (Narratively, it might have a cute interpretation, but it's just doesn't work as a game design.)As a big fan of patience games, the thrill of them comes from the complicated situations and combinations one has to execute. Here, this thrill is competely lost, because it's just not worth it to think about the game. Just idly clicking your way around works, and this is very disappointing. Even when I tried to somehow make my life more complicated, to demand some thinking from myself, by trying to solve each level with as little moves as possible, the game is structured in such a way that it was a completely unrewarding and annoying attempt. The feedback it gives is related to the clock-time of solving, rather than the count of moves, so again a brute-force approach is just clearly and disappointingly the best.So instead of puzzles, you get basically clicking chores to execute to proceed with the plot. I don't know. Buy it if you're curious (as a person interested in game design, I've definitely got some stuff to think about from this), but don't expect anything like an interesting challenge or an interesting patience game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I don't spend a lot of time with Solitaire games, but they do fill a niche, and I have a few.   Most of them are quick, and for the single deck games tend to be the most interesting and tight.  They don't tend to bog down like a lot of the two deck solitaire games do. But none are as interesting as this game. It is definitely a solitaire card game, but in a class of its own.  I love the back story, the graphics, and the ingenious use of the face cards to create characters with special abilities.  It is a great thinking game that rewards you for efficient strategy.  And you can if you wish, play the game a little on the lighter side if playing against the limited number of moves option.  In fact, I liked the game more, as I played it further along. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Super terrific game. Mike Bithell knows how to make the most out of very simple elements; really fun characterful writing, great little story snippets of text and tons of incredibly dramatic VFX make this deceptively simple package incredibly impactful. I don't think I even like Solitaire but this uses that classic game as the jumping off point for a really effective puzzle game.. Absolutely worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This game seems somewhat interesting BUT,If you do not have a LARGE screen you will be very disappointed in the design choices of this game.During gameplay the cards are stacked in a line vertically in the center of the screen leaving huge chunks of space on either side of the screen. What this does is makes everything in the game SMALLER including all the text of the game. This text is so small on the screen that you have to move closer to read it.It's hard to understand how this game got past QC with such a crippling design style.They did not utilize the screen area properly and the game is lame as it is unless you have a large screen within a few feet.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played for about 3 1/2 hours but already beat the story mode and have all achievements. I never "lost" a game or got into an unwinnable situation but I'm assuming it is possible. Having said that, I know it sounds like a short amount of time but I'd liken it to a movie. Would I pay $12 bucks to see a good movie in a theater? Yep. Would I pay $12 bucks to play a good 3+ hour video game (paid $9.59 since it was on sale)? Also like that you can reset all of your progress if you'd like to unlock everything again.10/10 Another fun and enjoyable game from Bithell Games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: A visually and aurally pleasing version of streets and alleys where face cards have powers (some good, some more tricky to get benefit from).The story is fun enough, but the real meat is countdown mode, where you race against the clock. It's hard as hell. World record is around 38 minutes as I write this. Think you can do better?Edit: Bithell has decided to expand the game, so far adding a puzzle mode to the campaign (deals are fixed, and you have a limited number of turns to complete). Looks like the game will continue to grow, so watch the news as it evolves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The Countdown mode is far more fun than it has any right to be. It fits that perfect little niche where I want to do something active that's quick and satisfying, much like Rocket League, but it's about quick thinking rather than fast reflexes. It's hard to describe the panic when I realize multiple Aces are stuck under Kings, and how satisfying it is when I can quickly go through the contortions required to fish them out.It's easier than it seems to be, even with 4 crews, when you don't have a time limit. And that's okay, sometimes a relaxing puzzle is nice, and you can set up hellish situations to practice for Countdown. Humanity+ is simultaneously the coolest and most infuriating power I could ever dream of in this sort of game.There's always ways to get better, to get faster. Recognizing where the cards are is only half the battle, but it is a HELL of a battle with the timer ticking down and the damnable pressure of that music.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Its Solitaire but not as we know it. Each suit is a different team with different powers and you use these to play solitaire and get all the cards in order. Has a story mode that introduces the teams and gets you in the flow.The cards look great, the powers are a neat twist and the music is perfect to sit back and play some solitaire
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I've had a blast with the game so far. I was initially somewhat intimidated by some of the mechanics but I was also pleasantly surprised by their deceptive simplicity. I love the artwork and the soundtrack. The FMV parts added a good story wrapper to the whole thing and I enjoyed it even more after a particular twist. The gameplay is basic card sorting with a few situational interactions with Jacks Queens and Kings. Most of the interactions are limited in usefulness and can be detrimental. _childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: So far this game has proven to be quite fun, I'm not even that big on card games, I just saw the concept and found it interesting.If you enjoy something as simple as solitaire, why not spice it up? The story behind this game and the multiple abilities you have at your disposal make it much more interesting to be playing solitaire. I'm up to the point where four decks are involved and it is definitely a challenge I enjoy. If you're looking at this game and thinking that it's too expensive, you're very wrong, a lot of work was put into this game for sure. If you can afford it, I recommend picking it up.(UPDATE: Just completed my first four deck game and it felt super satisfying.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is all about the presentation. The gameplay? Not so much. It is a Solitaire game, but definitely not the kind you'll either play casually for a long time or play for hours and hours.Don't get me wrong, I liked the game, but it was way too easy, I never once thought I was done and I could only restart, like usual solitaire.What makes the gameplay of it different is the power of each crew, which can honestly be ignored. Most of them felt detrimental or just luck-based, so I made sure to avoid triggering it, making levels longer than they should have been. That's defintely not a good thing when that's your unique mechanic. Each crew represent cards 1 to 13 of a suite, which is nice, but for some reasons I had trouble differentiating most cards from other suites... yikes. You can only play with 1 to 4 crews out of the group of 8, which greatly limits the possible difficulty of the game, and I personally would have loved a way to have more 4, but the the interface doesn't really have space for it, sadly. The game would also need to be "rebalanced" for it to happen, but still, I can dream.About the rest of the game? It's gorgeous. FMV cutscenes, but they're kinda long and make it lose their charm after 2 or 3, since they're a bit frequent. The story is a nice touch, but not really engrossing enough to follow it through, I skipped most of it. Especially since it made it seems like an hard mission that only the elite can win, when it's then a super easy solitaire game. It might be solitaire, with a story, but there's really little content here. I got bored way before finishing the story, and that'S before two hours of gameplay. Ultimately, I really don't feel like recommending this game. Sure, it's fun, but just for a short time. There's better solitaire games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really stylish take on Solitaire. It's got gorgeous art and great music. I didn't think that the story (which is presented via FMV every time you level up), was anything special, and I found myself skipping them more often than not. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Updated to include my thoughts on Campaign Plus and Daily Challenges. Also, there's a TL;DR at the bottom if, like me, you hate reading.Let me just get this out of the way quickly: this is the best version of Solitaire I've ever played. The amount of strategy that is taken out of such simple mechanics is frankly incredible, and I have to commend Bithell Games for creating such a finely-tuned game. As the description probably told you (at least, I hope you read it), each crew (representing a suit) has a unique power. What's so interesting about it is that they all have their pros and cons. For example, an early crew you unlock is Blood Legacy: their ability is to sort any stack they're placed on, with highest numbers on the top and lowest on the bottom. Now initially, this seems terrible: all it does is put all the valuable low-number cards where you can't reach them. However, they do bring the J, Q and K cards to the top, which are the only ones that can use crew abilities, meaning that if used right, they can actually be incredibly useful.It's little stuff like that that makes it such an enjoyable game, since each crew has moments like this, even if it doesn't seem like it at first. Now, here's the part where I have to complain about some things. First of all, the story is pretty weak. It's fun, certainly: the campy performances and interesting scenarios were enough to lead me through its short campaign, but it's pretty disappointing to see a simplistic story like this from Bithell Games of all people. However, I imagine that the gameplay was more of the focus here than the story, and I can respect that, especially since that gameplay is so good. The game really shines in Countdown mode, where you try to survive as long as possible, and each ability used and card placed in a suit earns you extra time. Trying to figure out the optimal moves under a limited time is really rewarding and compliments the game's sleek presentation, where info is clearly accessible. Additionally, I have yet to run into an unwinnable game, which is a common problem for me with Solitaire. The focus here is less on whether you  win, but how  you can win, and I really like that.I was a little apprehensive at first to write a review, since I wasn't quite sure whether this game would have enough replayability to keep me coming back. Countdown is super fun, but runs of that have taken me roughly 10-20 minutes each (and that's only after a few runs: I imagine I could get even further, and the highest ranking on the leaderboard reaches almost two straight hours of solitaire), meaning that it's not the most pick up and play experience. After leaving this for a while, I haven't played it much, but that's less because of a lack of enjoyment and more that there were other games I just preferred to play. I like standard Solitaire because it's something relaxing to focus on and the Skirmish mode, which is just a freeplay mode, lacks any kind of stats or win counter that give it that consistent sense of progress. The standard campaign doesn't really give much challenge or replayability (you can't really lose), but Campaign Plus helps a lot by enforcing a turn counter, forcing you to actually use the game's mechanics properly, and Daily Challenges provide that focus on efficiency with more replayability. My problem with the Daily Challenges is that, like Skirmish, it lacks any stats, so all that optimising a challenge appears to do is give you temporary bragging rights. However, I'd keep an eye out for updates: the additions made so far have all been great and there's plenty more to come, so my problems could be fixed in future.TL;DR: overall, the game's slick presentation, fun dynamic soundtrack and great core gameplay mean it's probably a good sell if you like puzzle games and/or solitaire, and it's definitely worth a buy on sale. If you like the calm progress of standard Solitaire, Skirmish and the standard campaign are your best bet and provide a decent (but not especially challenging) time killer. If you want to optimise the hell out of this game's systems, Daily Challenges and Campaign Plus have a lot more meat on their bones and are a great bit of fun. However, if you're looking for a fast-paced, arcade-like puzzle game, I can highly recommend this game for Countdown because of how tense and enjoyable that mode is, with all the other modes just being a cherry on top.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun variant on classic software solitaire. Giving it a campaign and flavour is fun, but the true meat of the game and understanding its mechanics is in countdown mode. I hope it updates with new modes eventually, and maybe some modding would be nice too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Great little solitaire game with a twist (or several). I loved the cinematic soundtrack, especially as it adds more instruments and speeds up when you're about to complete a stage.I didn't understand much of the overall plot. I'm assuming it's linked to previous games by Mr. Bithell, which I haven't played (yet), except for his really fine TRON game. Anyway.I had a good laugh at how cringe the entire FMV acting was. The actors were supposed to be talking with us, but you can see from their eye movement (except for Ratio) that they're reading from a script. I'm also not sure whether they're proper actors or just friends of the creator. Ratio was especially campy after level 7. Ouch.The sidequests don't make any sense, especially as the British one concludes after the main campaign (and acknowledges it), but the other one concluded even later for me, but the script implies it's set before the end of the game.Also, probably a bug: the game keeps asking you to replay the same missions after you're done, even missions you just did, but it never offered me to play missions I skipped earlier (or at least, I think I skipped them). Doesn't matter much, I don't know if I'll replay this a lot. I like the idea of power-ups, but overall, I'll be back to Microsoft Solitaire Collection for clean, simple daily gameplay. _childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: It's Solitaire, but it has a pretty nice coat of paint, some neat FMV cutscenes and cool character art on the face cards. The UI is definitely the game's strongest aspect.I wish the "missions" in story mode had more variety like timers, card shuffling, or any sort of outside force you can tangibly feel like you're working against. That, and the story just isn't very engaging, especially towards the end. You're just watching it happen and aren't given much choice in anything.Skirmish is just practice mode, and I'm glad it's here for people who just want to play Solitaire and use the decks that they like the most, but there's not a whole lot else going on with it.The Countdown mode is by far the most fun, working against a timer with increasingly difficult waves is legitimately engaging and I can see myself spending the most time in this mode.Overall, I enjoyed it and it was definitely worth a movie matinee price of about $10, but don't expect to get much longevity or "wow" factor out of it. I was expecting this team to push its mechanical strength a little more, but I wasn't overly disappointed. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This Solitaire does not weigh you down with tons of currencies, leveling mechanics, or fluffed-up table layouts. It will not waste your time with equipment, skills, or Building A Castle. Despite the over-the-top Spy Thriller presentation, this is a relatively pure game to play. I highly recommend it. I wrote much more about it for my blog, Turn of a Friendly Card:
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend because I stan solitaire and designers trying to do interesting things with the solitaire format. Do I think it's decent? Yeah. is it a fun variant of solitaire? My head says yes but my heart says no. Is the story good? Nah.Regarding the solitaire, it's a variant of Beleaguered Castle with more lenient packing rules and the face cards have special abilities. If you play Beleaguered Castle you'll understand how those changes make it work out so that each deal will play out. But that's the problem. It's always solvable, it's just a matter of how quickly. The solution in Solitaire Conspiracy is a challenge mode where you have a move count maximum on a set deal. This turns it back into a tough puzzle game like most classic solitaire variants with the benefit that you know the deal must play out.The variations of the powers and the thematic relation to the story is done well, I just don't care for the plot. Given what it's trying to accomplish it's doing it well. But I don't crave another round of the Solitaire Conspiracy solitaire format like I do with other variants. I think it's because a lot of the card powers induce randomness which runs counter to what you're trying to do when playing solitaire. In these cases they're "powers" but they're more like landmines. This actually makes sense if you pay attention to the plot, but it's an odd design choice because as a player you then avoid them. So some team combinations (especially in "normal" mode) feel like you're just playing a super easy version of Beleaguered Castle with some annoying cards.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, and keeps me coming back, desperately trying to get to the top of the leaderboard in Countdown mode has been a little obsession (and as of 1/11/20 I'm there!!!).It's such a simple concept of making Solitaire and giving the face cards special powers but it works so well, especially when it comes to certain powers which can either be helpful or detrimental depending on how you use them.The single player story is short but fun nonetheless, Greg Miller being fantastic as the lead.Another great addition to the Bithell games library
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this solidly for 2 hours now, the time kinda flies as you just...do...1...more....round. Me and my partner have been sat glued to the computer, trying to figure out how to get an Ace buried behind a King. I've never played solitaire before so I didn't know what to expect, and at the beginning I thought it was straightforward, but once the fun spy powers kick in it really turns into a brain twister. Drive Team will save your life, Blood Legacy are frankly a liability to the mission.Anyway, it's a super fun casual game, wrapped up in some really slick presentation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Great Solitaire game with an engaging gameplay loop. Sadly the story mode is the weakest part of the game, but can serve as a tutorial for the other modes. Although the FMV performances were fantastic, I did not care for the static text mission introductions at all (Thank you SKIP button). The game shines in COUNTDOWN and SKIRMISH. I spent the last hour trying to get into TOP 100 in Countdown and that is were the game sucks you into its "one more round" loop. Cyberpunk-y soundtrack and user interface keep you on the edge of the seat. Big kudos to the development team, I am looking forward to future updates!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: A disappointment for me. The solitaire aspects are interesting but there is no challenge to the game. Also, and these are very personal issue, but the design choices made me feel physically ill. The motion as you move the mouse gave me motion sickness (not something that I routinely get) and you cannot access the settings to change this anywhere other than the main menu. In addition, the card colour scheme was garish and caused me headaches - even on low blue light settings on my monitor.A real shame as I think there's something potentially there, but it needs some work on depth of gameplay and QOL options.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I was skeptical that Solitaire could be made into an interesting game that would hold my interest, but I'm delighted to have been proven wrong. I'm impressed with the amount of story they've managed to bake into the mechanics, and how slick the mechanics are.The campaign's story is a fun, campy hacker/spy thriller; very silly, and very enjoyable. The real star of the show, though, are the different factions (i.e. suits of a deck). The powers of the face cards for each faction are all potent, but can and will screw you over; which feels very much like you're managing a fragile alliance where everyone is out to do things their way. On top of that, each faction's backstory ties in to the power: where flashier factions have bombastic, obvious uses, and the more subtle factions have powers that look like pure downsides until you spend some time puzzling them out.Short and sweet, the campaign took me about 2.5h to complete, and I had a lot of fun with it. As far as replayability goes, the time trials and skirmishes are fun, and I have a feeling I'll be going back to it occasionally out of fondness.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great solitaire-style card game that incorporates special abilities by activating unique factions. The game plays as expected, but the special abilities add a lot of tactical challenge and requires thought on how to proceed. The campaign is short, but there are other challenges and skirmishes that extends replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to enjoy games that involve a deck of playing cards, and Bithell's "Subsurface Circular" is one of my favorites, so I was curious to see the developer's take on the card game genre.The first thing you'll notice is the undeniably slick presentation, like many Bithell titles. The game has many gorgeous unlockable color schemes, and I rotated between one that reminded me of the modern gold Deus Ex aesthetic, and the blue interface from the Orwell series of games. The interface was intuitive, while still setting cyberpunk tone that the game aims for.I suppose that in some ways the gameplay could remind a player of espionage work. You'll constantly be thinking a few steps ahead, and determining how you can best use the teams at your disposal. However, the story itself felt tremendously silly, sort of "throw away."The biggest knock against the game (for me) was that I only liked perhaps three of the nine (w/ DLC) teams: Drive Team Six, Omega Coda, and the Alpha Division. I was lukewarm about the Mantis Group, The Merry, and Incognito Unlimited, but when forced to use the other three (Humanity+, Blood Legacy, & Scorpio), I felt that I was succeeding despite my teams rather than because of them. For some of these teams, I'd go out of my way to ensure that their abilities  activate or affect the board in any meaningful way (putting a Blood Legacy face card on a stack with only one numbered card, etc.).I actually felt like siding with the character that the game clearly designates as the villain, simply because the team that the "good guy" was on (Scorpio, I believe) was such a pain to use on missions.I enjoyed my time with the Solitaire Conspiracy - I actually played the entirety of the game in one sitting. However, for the game to because a staple in my casual game library, I'd like to feel more like I'm actually  the teams that I'm sending on a mission, rather than trying to ensure that they don't sabotage my efforts.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little twist on spider solitaire! Definitely worth a try. The campaign story is interesting. I figured out how it was going to play out about halfway through. The acting is completely over-the-top. I think that's intentional (to poke some fun at the whole spy genre), and I love it even more as a result.The campaign is not overly challenging and you probably won't fail missions often but it is completely entertaining. The timed mode is where the real challenge lays. Graphics and music are top-notch - way better than I would expect for a game that is a fun take on solitaire.9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a bunch of solitaire games on Steam, and while I can't say The Solitaire Conspiracy is the most anything - not the most challenging, not the most creative, not the most innovative - it's so well put-together as a package that I absolutely have to recommend it, and with a roadmap for even more content coming, it's going to keep getting better.The core of the game is simple; four suits scattered across a board. Move cards on the top of any given pile onto another one of higher value to reach what you need, try to build the suits in the centre from ace to king. You can see every card's location from the very start, and consequently you won't ever have to actually bank on RNG to save you. Every face card (jack, queen, king) has a special single-use ability determined by its suit, which you can use to get yourself out of a sticky situation. That's it, that's the game. From the first level to the last, regardless of difficulty, the basic rules of playing TSC will stay the same.And yet, it remains compelling for hours.Though some of the cards' abilities bring some RNG to the equation, it's minimal and the player can manipulate it to their advantage. Being able to see every card from the get-go leaves you creating plans and strategies, adapting them, and seeing the level change from an indicipherable mess to something you've brought under your control, while the soundtrack changes on the fly as you progress. There's a distinct feeling of 'coolness' to playing The Solitaire Conspiracy. I've always felt like I was the reason for all my victories, never like I was at the mercy of RNG like so many other solitaire variants on Steam. And of course, the slightly cheesy FMV cutscenes always felt like a great little reward.I've spent 6.4 hours so far on the campaign, some dabbling in the challenging survival mode, and the first DLC campaign to recruit a new suit, The Merry. With more DLC coming, I feel like I'll happily keep coming back as the game evolves, and for €10, I can heartily recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I am interested in seeing known games being enriched with new gameplay elements so this was a fun experience. Having cards with powers was a nice addition and executed in a fun way.I did not expect a video told story which made me grin occasionally.In the end however it is its own game and not solitaire. Maybe a game with story and achievements simply feels completed once everything is done.After around three hours of having fun I think I might come back to this game at a later time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The developer of this game has somehow made Solitaire interesting with a story about espionage, and some really cool UI colours. I've been playing Solitaire for 5 hours, haven't done that since the Windows 95 era. Good job developer looking forward to your projects in the future. Maybe make Rummy into a game with an alien invasion as the story lol.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Solitaire but with a slick coat of graphics and style.  Not too hard to finish the story and get all the achievements.  A little short and seems like they could have maybe done more with the player choosing the teams he/she uses rather than what seemed like them randomly assigned for each mission.  But had fun playing it without thinking too hard.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy (Tactical Table Based Espionage) is a very aesthetic and atmospheric short game. From the stylized FMV sequences in the campaign to the beautiful art and collection of colored UI themes, everything in this game reinforces the visual appeal and mood, especially with the brilliant soundtrack (Available on ).Gameplay wise this is solitaire but with a twist, J/Q/K are power cards that are activated once an Ace is placed on the deck. There are 8 powers in total, with 4 being the maximum amount on the deck at one time. It mixes it up quite well with some powers being highly situational and possibly setting back your progress, while others are highly useful in any situation.Story is serviceable, I really appreciate the way it's presented with mission briefings and FMV sequences, a very peculiar approach to narrative and world building. Feels very fresh and inventive.There are 4* modes: Campaign (Story), Countdown (Time-based endless mode) and Skirmish (Free play). (*They've just announced today they'll be adding a 4th mode: a harder Campaign+).At the time of writing this review I've completed the game once, tried out Countdown and Skirmish modes and have gotten all of the achievements which weren't that difficult to get. You'll most probably complete this game in under 4 hours but you might want to come back once in a while to just zen out and play some solitaire.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: is a solitaire card game with a short story told through FMV component. The game uses plenty of flashy colours and and good acting to make a solitaire game fun.You will make use of a group of spies that you unlock as you progress through the campaign and level up. You will be playing games of solitaire in order to regain  your crew and save the world.The game has an interactive tutorial and it's easy to get started. There are 3 game modes, you have to play the campaign to unlock some of the features. The Skirmish and Countdown modes have leaderboards as well.The campaign is split into levels that you play, in between these you will have FMV to watch to reveal the story. You can skip the FMV but this part is really well done. Overall the story is not too long, so it's worth watching through.You will choose from among 3 games at the beginning of each scene, each uses different crews and give you various Xp that are needed for leveling up.Your cards are dealt in the middle and you need to build up the 4 suits from Ace to King. When you place cards you will activate face cards to do various things. You can check ahead of time on what will happen. So it's a little different from your standard plain solitaire game.The graphics are beautiful, the colours make the game look really high tech.The music and sounds go really well with the game. The FMV is well acted with spoken dialogue. can be fully played with a mouse.€9.99/$11.99 might seem a bit steep for a short solitaire game. I am at level 11 of the campaign and there are only a few more levels. Luckily there are 2 other game modes that you can enjoy.If you enjoy solitaire games, definitely check out  I like what they did with a simple solitaire game. Sometimes you need to use strategy and think further ahead.It's short, so if you are worried about the price, it's reasonable to wait for a sale as well.Score: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Recently got this game and I am in love with it so far. I am an avid solitaire fan, and have never experienced solitaire in this way. The mechanics with the court cards are really interesting and helps move along the classic game play elements of patience card games. Graphics are outstanding along with the sound design. A nice story is woven into the game, and helps deliver incremental rewards as you play. This game uses the solitaires games beleagured castle and streets and alleys as the foundation of the game. Despite your familiarity with the previously mentioned solitaire games, you owe it your self to try the solitaire conspiracy. You won't regret it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Overall aesthetic is really polished and the color scheme options are slick.I was kind of hoping for, at it's core, a replayable deep solitaire experience. I was hoping maybe it would have repackaged standard solitaire variants (tri-peaks, spider, standard, etc), but instead they applied their own variants to a solitaire-lite experience. The problem is those variants don't add any meaningful changes and essentially make things way too easy, each 'crew' or suit comes with it's own special abilities. Part of the lure of certain types of solitaire is that not all decks are solvable and there's weight to certain decisions. This game lacks that. I beat it in 3 hours... prolly would have completed it sooner, but was also chatting with friends and watching youtube.The Story? The Skip button is your best friend. It's obvious, predictable. Felt rushed. Ultimately, doesnt really make much sense. Talk about ludonarrative dissonance. You'd be better off just spending your money on Shenzhen Solitaire or sticking to MS Solitaire.

_childDocuments_.review: I wouldn't recommend this game for friends of solitaire. Not much classic left in this one. _childDocuments_.review: I haven't gotten very far in this game, as I've only played 2 rounds of solitaire and I think I'm still solidly in the tutorial section. _childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy is a Solitaire game. There is a story (2-3 hours long) with FMV cutscenes. The Story is okayish, nothing really brilliant tbh but definitely more engaging than most other story's in indie games. I don't need to explain how Solitaire works. Even if you don't know, the game has a short tutorial. You also learn about new mechanics. Each Set of Cards has special agents (J,Q,K - Cards are your Agents). If you put them on a stack, they will activate their ability (for example: crashing the stack, sorting the stack by numbers and a lot more). This spices things up a bit. The best thing about this game is the Countdown-Mode. You start out with 90 or 100 seconds left and one set of cards. For every card played you get + 3 seconds. If you finish a set, the next wave starts. It's a pretty fun endless mode. You get points based on how many waves you survived. There is a world ranking and you can compare your points to your friends. There also is a skirmish mode for anyone interested. All in all, this feels like a high quality game. The aesthetics is nice, the translation is very good and the acting doesn't look that cheap. It's a bit short, but you can squeeze out many more hours of fun (especially if this is your second screen game). I would recommend to get it on sale (20% or more). If you're really addicted to solitaire it's well worth 10€/USD.

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy has the most intense music I have ever heard while playing a card game.  It seems a bit out of place, but I suppose the music is supposed to add dramatic tension or something, which is admittedly a tricky job, considering I'm just clicking some cards around.  The visual side of things is better, it's a good looking game, although I had to turn off the screen wobble, as it was a bit disorienting, and I nearly fell off of my balcony because of it.  More concerning, my house does not have a balcony.  Conspiracy indeed.There is a neat story unveiled as you play, and serves as an aperitif between rounds, despite me not knowing what that word means.  I would go so far as to say that the story kept me motivated enough to actually finish the game, as the solitaire itself felt a bit flat.  Well, cards are like that I suppose.The thing is, as you unlock different suits of cards, they introduce new powers.  Royal cards have abilities that can move or shuffle things around in various ways, but considering that the King, Queen, and Jack are the highest cards, and I always wanted them at the lowest spots, I wound up just ignoring their abilities as far as any kind of strategy, and just playing a regular round of solitaire.  Which is fine too.  I like solitaire.  It's a good thing to play when you have cats that think the only place in the house to sleep is on your arm.In conclusionato, if you want some solitaire, well, here some is.  It's not on the level of some of the Grey Alien solitaire games, but also better than most of the other solitaires you'll find on Steam.  Might want to turn the music down a notch though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Русская "нечитайка": очень стильная и атмосферная игра с предсказуемым и оправдывающим "прокачку" сюжетом. Проблема в том, что это пасьянс с очень простыми правилами и единственным сложным моментом в игре будет выживание до 15 волны режима с ограничением по времени. Фанатам пасьянсов брать, но лучше по скидке.Solitaire Conspiracy is very debatable game. I'll recommend it only to fans of solitaires who enjoy learning new things no matter how short or easy they can be. And of course long fans of devs could buy this game without waiting too. However, I won't recommend it for other people and in current state it's better to wait for sales.Game is surely stylish and atmospheric and it's best part of product. Music is pretty much repetetive, but it's not annoying and only helps to build pressure, especially in time limited mission. Art of characters is great and you can see big diversity in their design, meaning you'll probably remember who is who very soon. (if you are paying attention to their names and images at all) Artists were working hard on this one......that's why gameplay is problem. Many negative reviews state right, that's pretty simple solitaire. One suit levels are bad joke, two suit levels are unfunny jokes, only three and four suits levels can make some challenge, but with skills of agents they are still solved easily with little thinking on player part. Only challenges game can propose to you are timed mode (but it's not really hard to get to 15 wave for achievement) and custom game in which you can set four suits with most awkward powers.But before that you need to finish story mode. Plot of it is quite predictable and cliched, but still enjoyable thanks to actors and music score. At least it justifies locking some features of game behind level up system, however, I was really sad, because in the end To make game more harder during latter missions I set "home rule" for myself to put lesser number cards only on bigger number cards of same suit (of course, excluding active agents cards) and it made game much harder, especially with kings on top positions of rows, but still solvable in most cases. I also tried to play with "slowpoke" alternative to time limited system, limiting my turns instead in same add-few-if-card-landed mechanics but for turns. Also, I wish there were some other "random" handicaps tying to setting of game, like "rogue agents" or "wild cards" whose abilities weren't activating or even working in bad way to confuse player or "precise" mode which asked player to finish suits stacks in specific order. And of course, while 8 teams are quite enough, I wished there were few more content. While 4 suit games are still kinda challenging, maybe it would be cool idea to allow player to play with more suits at once.And of course, after reading about good sales and wish of developers to add more into this game I hope they will add things same or similar to ones I mentioned and add more replayability into this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, creative take on solitaire.  Just what I was looking for in a sea of disappointing "AAA" games.  The visuals are surprisingly good, along with a fitting soundtrack and dynamic UI.  The game's narrator adds a quirky but fun aspect to missions.  The game itself is fairly straight-forward, though the concept is not one I've seen before in solitaire.  As of writing, I'm only level 4, so I have a feeling things will get quite a bit more complex at level 15 and over.  I'm looking forward to it.  I recommend if you're looking for a quick but strategic and gorgeous game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty medicore, since there is no inbetween i will go with downvote sinnce thats where i incline mostly. Solitaire is fun so i thought to myself that if they were to add some cool twist to it can be fun, but they twitch they added didnt do it for me. Anyway first thing first, they story is basicly non-existant. To be frank you cant call it a story, its mainly some discription and some FMVs that add a spy setting to the game. So other the establishing the setting the story was pretty boring and i couldnt wait for the FMVs to end so i can move on. In my opinion the removal of the FMVs would even make the game better, since much of the solitaire script repeats pretty much the crew description os basicly stuff you already saw and the acting was mediocre, from solitaire's endless blabing(with the exagerated performance of the character) that i couldnt wait to end and diamonds eyes that went left and right when he was reading the script ( i just couldnt avert my eyes from it), but i also didnt want to skip just so i can give the game a fair chance.Gameplay wise they changed the solitaire formula a bit by adding crews, changing the layout and removing some mechanics. _childDocuments_.review: If you look at the description and think that this game looks goofy and disjointed, then you are below the truth.the FMVs are cringe, the cartoony political-fiction story assumes that you're a child, the genderfluid main actor is unpleasant. The videos don't bring anything to the game and you'll quickly want to skip all the long text descriptions before each level.The interface is ugly with hard to read fonts. IDK what's wrong with the devs because every casual game dev knows that this type of futuristic look doesn't work with the casual audience, and it's particularly ugly here.The art style on the character portraits looks so generic and out of context that it's slightly into the uncanny valley category.The music would be great for an action game, but it's very annoying here.As for the game, well, it's a very tedious variation on solitaire, played with tiny unreadable cards, and the figure cards having annoying properties that you can confortably avoid for most of the play. There's no auto play so you have to drag each card in the suit one by one, even when the game is basically won. Each game is very long and the meta game wants you to reach level 15 for some reason, which looks like a lot of hours of bad game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I have always had a soft spot for Solitaire games and I am not sure why but that is why The Solitaire Conspiracy really caught my attention. It is a spy themed story driven solitaire game that has a ton of polish with a unique spin on the Solitaire formula. I never expected a solitaire game to be this good.The main campaign this game has to offer starts off with a FMV cutscene of Greg Miller apologizing for kidnapping you and saying he needs your help. He claims he is part of a spy organization that’s sole purpose is to save innocent lives and some evil figure known as Solitaire has crippled the spy network and is causing mayhem all over the world.And so the game will give you a little bio of what each mission you are currently doing consists of so it could be hijacking a plane that Solitaire is using to transport goods, or stopping a bomb from going off. And the gameplay is pretty much solitaire as you would expect but with a twist. So you need to get each crew into the center starting from Ace all the way up to King but every face card for each crew has a special power that you activate once you get their corresponding ace on the board.Each crew is different and unique and have their strengths and weaknesses and so each mission in the story will have you playing as different combinations of these crews.And every time you complete a mission you will get some experience and most times when you level up you unlock new crews, or ui color changes, and are given another FMV cutscene that helps move along the narrative. And the story is slightly predictable but that doesn’t mean it isn’t interesting. You are mainly playing the game because you like Solitaire, I would hope that would be obvious, but just having that motivation to keep on playing just to get a little bit more of the story told is very nice.There are also two extra modes you can play to give more replayability after you beat the campaign.I have not experienced a story driven solitaire game like this that has the level of polish and charm that this game has. It may be a shorter experience if you are just playing the campaign but for the $12 it costs I would say it is totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy is a game developed by Bithell Games, the creators of games like Thomas Was Alone and Subsurface Circular. It's a - to nobody's surprise - Solitaire game. The twist is that is has a fairly high-quality production FMV aspect to it. You're a Spymaster recruited to undo the damage done by a criminal mastermind called Solitaire. At your disposal is an ever-growing team of agents, represented by the faces of suits. You complete espionage-themed missions by playing matches of a peculiar variant of Solitaire, which earns you XP. Enough XP levels you up and every time you level up you're treated to a new FMV segment involving one or two actors.There's an attempt at blending a dystopian espionage story with Solitaire-based gameplay but it mostly falls flat. The only connecting factor between the two are the faces of each suit, but since none of these faces every make an appearance in the FMV elements - and aren't even mentioned by name - these two aspects of the game feel disconnected from one another.As for the gameplay itself, it's essentially a light version of Solitaire, but in which placing an Ace 'powers' the faces of its corresponding suit, and playing a face card then has an effect on gameplay. It might make cards of a certain number surface to the top, shuffle a stack or order a stack from lowest to highest (or vice versa), etc.There are a lot of different suits to unlock and play around with, but the most useful ones aren't unlocked until the very end. (There's also a bonus Robin Hood-themed suit that can be unlocked though a side-quest of sorts that seems to tie in with a previous game by the same developers, though I haven't played that at the time of writing.)If you're not done with the game after finishing the campaign (meaning you've reached level 15) there's a difficult time trial mode, a daily challenge and more. Personally I had my fill after completing the campaign in about 5 hours.If you like 'Solitaire with a twist' games or FMV games with acceptable acting, give this a try. Just don't expect too much from either aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: This spy thriller starts off strongly with an incredibly well defined ambiance and presentation, a great soundtrack and promising narrative setup, one of the few games to make good use of FMV, well written and played, smoothly animated and entirely bug-free.However, its gameplay demands a bit of perseverance before it really converges. Some faction powers are not very intuitive on their own, with randomized effects that make it difficult to plan an exact strategy, or an outright negative impact that inadvertently makes their avoidance a primary objective. I had a hard time developing a valid approach around many of them early on, until more factions later became available and their combined powers began to make complete sense.Once enough complementary factions are at play, particular alliances feel like a stroke of design genius, and the game becomes fully enjoyable from then on. I simply wish there were more of those and less of the randomness and negative effects, especially early on.Campaign missions regularly pop on the world map. Though some opportunities disappear seemingly randomly, creating some level of FOMO, they eventually return if missed or failed. Each mission features a refined synopsis worthy of an espionage series that serves up a great mental image, accompanied by light contextual visuals. These scenarios are mostly about ambiance; in truth they only alter which factions will be at play.Face cards are spy field agents, dormant until enabled by placing their corresponding suit's Ace on the center target. Powered agents trigger their effects when moved to another pile. Each agent has a unique bio and appearance, but all agents from a singular faction deliver the same benefits. Sort and build all suits up to King to complete the mission.Every match plays nearly identically, except for number of suits in play, and their associated powers and teams. There is a single type of board arrangement throughout the entire game. The spy thriller was a perfect setup to organize stacks variably and instill some gameplay variation — a sorely missed opportunity.A few other modes unlocked after some time will also show up on the world map. Countdown against the clock is optional in separate non-campaign mode, along with a single daily challenge leaderboard, and a skirmish mode that lets the player create a custom game with any teams of their choice. These become the main points of interest once the campaign is done, but without the supporting narrative and limited options I did not feel compelled to keep playing. Campaign Plus also introduces turn limits for a more challenging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Solitaire: the Motion Picture, directed by Bithell Games;  coming soon to a theatre near you.Might be hard to see how a classic single-player game can be made exciting, but Bithell Games played their cards right and succeeded several times over. This game might still be Solitaire at its core (i.e. still using the core rules of arranging randomized stacks of cards into orderly suits), but  excels with its cinematic atmosphere.A stunning combination of intense music (by  of Shadowrun fame), sleek UI design, and gorgeous character artwork help immerse you into the role of spymaster in a turbulent futuristic world, and that feeling is hammered in during the Campaign mode where a thrilling tale of conspiracy is told mainly through FMV videos. even adds its own twist to this classic game by having the cards' suits represent specialized spy crews, each with having a unique effect when playing any of a crew's cards that are ranked Jack or higher. And you'll be putting those effects to good use with 5 varied game modes to explore.This game also had a few free updates, with special mention for those in 2020 December and 2021 June, as each brought a new spy crew (adding up to a total of  spy crews and suit effects) and a new story told through even more FMV scenes. With everything laid out, in terms of both price level and amount of entertainment,  is a fine pick to draw out of the deck. What's more, if you have a non-gaming friend who likes spies and solitaire, this could make an excellent surprise gift.
