_childDocuments_.review: - Not a lot to talk about visually given that it's just a card game with some FMVs separating the rounds. I did like the character portraits and some of the art on the face cards, though- The soundtrack is pretty generic, and all that I really recalled about it was a predilection for brass instruments- The FMV performances were interesting since all the actors are content creators, many of whom were at some point associated with Rooster Teeth. I won't say that it broke my immersion (how immersed can you truly be in solitaire?), but it's difficult to put on a serious face while taking mission orders from Greg Miller when all I've watched him do is video review Oreo cookies. I'm also more used to seeing Alanah Pierce try to convince a man from Tennessee that Deadly Premonition is good, not asking me to save her spy mentor- You're just some dude that Greg Miller kidnaps because you're apparently some god of 1-player card games. In this universe, I guess that translates to being good at orchestrating teams of operatives aiming to waylay the global domination plans of the game's antagonist, Solitaire- You'll travel the globe to exotic locales to... play a card game on an unthemed background. Could they not at least put a picture from the real world location or something?- Honestly, the vibes are all over the place. I can't tell whether the game is trying to be serious or not, and I'm not sure the devs knew either. It comes off feeling inconsistent and confused- So, it's a game focused on a single card game, but there's lots of flavors of solitaire. Surely they mix it up here with stuff like Klondike, Golf, Yukon, or Pyramid right? Nope. There's only one variety with 8 stacks of face-up cards. You don't even have to worry about alternating suits or colors- The game does inject a little variety by giving you factions to work with ahead of each mission. The face cards from each faction have special abilities that may be purely beneficial, purely problematic, or a double-edged sword that can be useful if used correctly- These powers mainly come into play if you're attempting to beat each level in a defined number of moves. Finishing a mission in fewer moves than that limit will net you experience points- Leveling up doesn't confer any benefit other than unlocking more factions for use in other game modes, which include a survival mode, "countdown" (same as the regular game, but the move limit is actually enforced), and an infinite mode- Your main task in the campaign is to reach level 15. Given that the reward for playing optimally is additional experience, the de facto upshot of good performance is that you play the game less. No new skills, card art, backgrounds, or side missions. You just get to play less Solitaire Conspiracy - I beat the campaign, but I'm not so enamored with card games (or, in reality, the single solitaire variation present here) that I had any desire to go back and try the additional game modes. Not much replay value here in my estimation- I'm not sure what I was really expecting going into this, but the biggest disappointment is that the game barely evolves as you beat it. Unlocking new factions just didn't offer enough variety- It ran well, but that's unsurprising. All it has to do is render cards, a map, and some video. No issues on the Steam Deck- . I guess I just thought there'd be a bit more variety as far as gameplay is concerned. There's so many varieties of solitaire, and it's not like you have to pay anyone to add them to a game. It's not a complete waste, but I just don't know who this game is for or who I'd recommend it to

_childDocuments_.review: I agree with the other reviews that have criticized the story line, FMV, and quality of acting.  The story line is standard spy genre motifs, but the connection to the game of Solitaire and playing cards is unclear.  The videos were hammy, cheesy, and awkward.  I didn't find any of them to be endearing in even a quirky way.  However, I enjoyed the gameplay.  I thought the various spy teams created variety to the playing style with their unique card powers.  Additionally, the game has replay value beyond the story mode.  For these reasons, I am willing to give a positive review.  I watched all the videos, but I was strongly inclined to skip them (and you wouldn't miss anything if you do).

_childDocuments_.review: Much in the same way as you'd end up playing Solitaire on the school PCs when you were bored, The Solitaire Conspiracy is perfect for your downtime, and is best enjoyed over lunchtimes at work or the wee hours of the night. A simple premise with its aesthetic appeal boosted through the roof with gorgeous art, sound, and UI, TSC provides a novel twist on a classic that somehow paves the way for spy flavour, with some pretty neat acting performances to carry it along. At times, the random nature of the first draw can work either for you or against you, and it would have been nice to feel these scaled more predictably with difficulty. That being said, you can very much fine tune the difficulty to some degree using the limited turn modes.Short but sweet, well worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game worth the price. Plays around with Solitaire mechanics by making most special powers more negative than positive, but this only leads to you having to play creatively or carefully. Just because it's usually negatively doesn't mean you can't use them to great positive effect. Need that power of a different suit? Stack the highest card to the top and get that power available. Guys steal the card you need and push it to the bottom? No problem I only have one card in that stack anyways so you just made it easily available to me.It's also extremely pleasurable to rearrange and stack cards to form perfect piles of a suit ranging from lowest to highest, going back and forth and finding out where you have to place the cards what piles to dig up to get cards placed correctly so you can stack consecutively from high to low, wonderful feeling.I enjoyed it greatly trying to use the powers as little as possible. The only time I ever reset a mission was once, because I picked the wrong suit to use the power of (because they can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ identical looking in colour, the symbols alone aren't that easy to glance).Simply put, a great chill game of solitaire that allows for a lot of different playstyles and variety if you want it to.Story-wise I have no idea what tone they are going for, is it supposed to be cheesy B-movie, or is it trying to be taken seriously? I literally can't tell because it's delivering both at the same time but it's also failing at both. But who cares, everything can be skipped anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: Solitaire with powers.Unlike the most well-known version of Solitaire, all the cards are face-up at the start. The goal is still to order every suit from A-K in the targets, using the eight stacks on the sides to stage and rearrange cards. Instead of the traditional card suits, these suits are themed as spy crews with their own color & icon. Each suit has a unique power that will activate when you move a face card onto a stack. These powers might help, might hinder, or might be all in how you use them (for example, a power the sorts all the cards with the highest on top seems disadvantageous, but it could give you access to a powerful face card currently buried in that stack). As you play through the campaign, you unlock additional crews. Individual missions provide specific combinations of crews, and so you need to learn to effectively use (or effectively avoid) the powers provided. The campaign missions can be played in a casual mode or in a higher-stakes mode. In the casual mode, you can take as many turns as you need, or restart the round with a new shuffle. In the higher-stakes version, the card layout is curated & you must win within a certain number of turns.Eventually, you unlock a few specialty modes: a quickplay mode where you can use 1-4 crews of your choosing, a daily seed where you try to finish in as few moves as possible, and a speed mode where you play wave after wave until time runs out, gaining seconds on the timer for each card finalized.Two of the crews were apparently added as an update after the game was originally released, but the missions to unlock them are parceled out in a way that you basically have to finish the entire campaign before they will be available to you. These quest chains add a few new characters in cutscenes, which made the lack of such treatment for the game's original crews very apparent.The lore cutscenes are skippable if you prefer to focus on the gameplay. Some of the cutscenes strongly imply that you have important decisions to make, but the story is linear and you do not make any choices. The active story isn't really anything to write home about, but it provides some flavor to differentiate it from any number of faceless card games out there.I finished the campaign in two dedicated-but-comfortable sittings, and the game didn't wear out its welcome.After completing the campaign, a few of the late-game missions became replayable from the map, but otherwise you cannot choose to replay specific campaign missions over again unless you completely reset your progress.I would have liked the option to select and replay any already-beaten mission at any time, especially to attempt the "Plus" hard-mode version if I didn't do it the first time around (if not with achievements, then at least with in-game tracking). There is a sort of puzzle quality to playing a curated table with specific crews and a turn limit, and it feels like a bit of a disservice to say that if you don't choose that mode the first time around, you have to wipe your progress and replay the campaign to access it again.I also would've liked a single-button quickplay with four random crews. Admittedly, it doesn't take a lot of time and effort to manually navigate to Skirmish mode and press the "Shuffle" button a few times (depending on whether it offers me three crews or four) and then click to confirm, but random play seems to be where any replay value would come from after the campaign, and it would be nice to streamline it. A numbered seed mode would also be cool, but the number of possible card layouts multiplied by the number of permutations of the various crews would make the seeds very long and difficult to input.The visual & sound design are great. The music is engaging and tense without being distracting, and neon gives a slick look. You can unlock over 20 color palettes to customize the game, and it even remembers your choice at the title screen when you launch the game for your next session.Submerge / 10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far. The game took me a few matches for strategizing to click. Once I realized how to visualize gameplay in the same way I would in the board game Rummikub all bets were off. You'll enjoy Solitaire Conspiracy if you like playing games  that require thinking tactically 5 moves ahead to manipulate cards so you can clear the board effectively. This is especially true if you play with the optional limited moves setting which grants extra experience points to progress the story.It's immensely fun to watch the story unravel in this mystery, puzzle game where your loadout of abilities change with the "crews" (the suits cards have; diamonds, hearts, etc) that are run with each scenario.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid game, from well thought in-game mechanics, to enjoyable acting we see for the story.But the part that had the most value for me "Countdown" mode, I would never expect a solitaire game to excite me that much, I had the same thrill of a trying to find the last puzzle pieces of an important pattern in a 3000 piece puzzle board.And also shout out to nice ideological themes played out, I really felt the game was giving me something to think in the form of philosophical arguments between class separation and equality. And I really appreciate it. And I also appreciated the game ending with a possibility of a third way. Quite refreshing.

_childDocuments_.review: When it comes to card games, I never was particularly interested in solitaire, definitely preferring poker, hearts or spades. But this clever twist on the genre is worth your time. Solitaire Conspiracy shakes things up with special powers. Cards like aces or kings have their own abilities, depending on deck. Powers like reshuffling a stack or digging up some buried cards on top. Besides that, there’s a storyline -  making You a “spymaster” figure, decks being your different spy crews and every game a field mission. Little abstract concept, but FMV cutscenes help sell that idea… and it works! Visually, it’s eye candy. Great neon, cyberpunk aesthetic. And there’s that small things like music dynamically changing when you’re close to completing a level. Yes, you are just stacking cards… but hell, such details highlight that experience. Campaign should take you around 7-8h. You can take a relaxed approach or choose to limit your turns, to make things bit difficult.  There’s also survival-wave mode, if you’re actually good at solitaire and want a challenge.For me, Solitaire Conspiracy is a great casual game, a fantastic interpretation of a classic card game.  I would never thought I will sink 7 hours into solitaire. Honestly, I’m still surprised. Good work, Bithell Games. Bloody good work.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy is a very fun, very well made puzzle game. The story is a fairly straightforward spy adventure, featuring solid writing and some enjoyable FMV performances by notable industry personalities like Alanah Pearce and Greg Miller. Its most outstanding quality is the presentation: an excellent UI featuring digitized effects and glass-smooth animations that really suit the vibe.The gameplay is pretty simple -- Solitaire with a twist, would you believe it? You have eight piles of cards with up to four suits matching whatever spy, tech, and wetworks teams have been brought on the mission. You organize the piles into four stacks in the center of the board, from low to high. Placing the Ace card of each suit in its respective pile enables the special powers of that suit's spy team, which can then be activated by moving the King, Queen, and Jack to new piles. Some of the powers are so useful they tend to trivialize the challenge, like the team that can organize any pile from lowest to highest card value in one move. However, some powers, like the team that "kidnaps" the next required card from a suit and puts it on the bottom of a pile, require skill to manage. I appreciated that some of the crummier powers made me actively avoid playing the face cards of that suit, turning the game into a sort of mixture of Solitaire and Minesweeper.I completed the game in about six and a half hours. Whether you will take more or less time to finish will depend on how many of the missions you play, and how good you are at simple card reorganization puzzles. It wasn't particularly difficult, but I like that they give you the option to play each mission with no limitations or with a restriction on the number of turns, and I dug that the variable experience granted by each mission means you can tailor the length of the game to some extent.tl;dr: Thumbs up. Recommended for players who like card games, spy stuff, and/or FMV.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Live action acting is great and the story is fun. Game play-wise it isn't the solitaire you know, but instead it takes the central concepts from that game and twists them around a bit, making it easier in some areas and a lot tougher in others. Music is intense and mostly really great. What helps this stand out is the different abilities of each crew/suit; for the most part they're not completely helpful or harmful, but rather it's all in how you use them.Definitely what I looked for in a puzzle game: unique and intriguing throughout, with tons of polish, while maintaining a fun balance between challenging and casual. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: One of those recommendations where I wish I could say yes and no to this game.  Solitaire Conspiracy tries to make a card game look new and innovative with FMV and a unique nuance on the gametype.  However, the FMVs get old and boring, and the storyline is way too predictable.  I get it though it was only meant to try and entertain between card games.The card game itself is unique in the sense that different suits of cards have different reactions when you play face cards.  Some will shuffle the deck and place the card at the bottom, another will place the next card in the suit you drop you card on in its home, and others will explode the home stack of the suit that you place it on.  While this brings a unique way of playing solitaire, it also brings a lot of confusion with so many different ways of playing the game.  If you play the standard game, knowing how these work really does not matter as the levels are simple enough to beat without caring how card interactions work.  However, if you play on advanced, which is a choice you have with each level you start, that is when the game requires good strategy and tactical gameplay versus a click fest.  A part of me wishes that the entire game was forced in advanced mode to truly challenge the player.The graphics are great for a card game, far beyond what most offer, the sound was great even though a card game does not require much for sounds, and the innovative idea, while not brought together into the best product, stands out from other solitaire games.  Due to this innovation, that is why I still recommend this game, and if you want a challenge, make sure to choose to play the levels in advanced mode where you are limited in the number of turns you have to accomplish your goal.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This game is solitaire with powers. It was a pretty quick win. I don't know why my playtime is 11 hours. It was much faster than that.Plot is done in FMV movies done like you're having a video call with someone. Basically you work for a spy organization trying to take down a Bond-esque villain called Solitaire, and each face card in the suite can be activated for a special power once you have placed the ace in the run. Its... a pretty generic storyline, but the FMV sequences were nice. I don't see that in games too often nowadays.Other than that, its solitaire. If you like solitaire give it a shot.There was one difficult achievement that was basically a time trial challenge mode where you got +3 seconds for every card you played, and when you finished all of your runs, more cards are added. Thankfully its never 4 suite runs during this mode, only 3 suite runs, but still very challenging to basically complete 15 games of solitaire back to back very quickly before time runs out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy is a surprisingly fun little card game. It's basically the same Solitaire that we all know and love, but pumped up with FMV cutscenes and exciting music and a few cards that have special powers. The storyline is the main reason why I bought the game - it's a super hammy over-the-top spy yarn that unfortunately does not have a very good payoff. There is no climax, you just keep on playing till you get to level 15 and then the story abruptly ends without any resolution. After that you can keep playing, but without the storyline it's just pretty Solitaire.And, well, that's still worth the money. There are only one or two levels that are fiendishly difficult (assuming you play with limited rounds - if you play unlimited rounds it's trivial). There is a pleasant sense of accomplishment when you figure out how to best use a new special card that at first appears more like a hindrance. Compulsive, but fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad but not brilliant.  Neat little solitaire game with a fun little connecting thread and occasional cinematics,   Keeps a person occupied for a few hours and you can doodle around with it for longer if you want to.  If you're vaguely interested and it's on sale I'd say give it a shot.  Possibly a little overpriced at full cost, but if you're a solitaire fan and the theme grabs you there's a pretty decent argument that it's not.  Use your judgement.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I think the gameplay was fine, probably. It must have been or else I wouldn't have 7 hours in this game (even if a lot of that was AFK). But a few months after playing the game all I remember about it is the obnoxious storyline. It keeps coming back to mind every time I consider which card games to buy going forward. I'm not opposed to a narrative-based card game, or else I wouldn't have bought this to begin with, but if your game is narrative-based, you should probably have a decent narrative. Buy it if you like grating intrusions on your card games that involve terrible FMV actors and stupid writing. If you want a good story-based Solitaire game play Shadowhand.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: As a solitaire game, it's not at all interesting. You are mainly trying to sort cards, which represent agents, and the suits are supposed to represent different the different secret organizations to which those agents belong. The face cards of each suit all share a special power thematically related to that suit. For example, the extraction specialists can help you pull the card you need from the bottom of a big, messy stack. Handy at times, but I found I wasn't using them all that often, even when I was doing the "plus" challenges where you have a limited number of turns. So even with that extra layer of choice, it's still just a lot of tedious sorting.(Also, I did not notice an "auto" command to finish up all the obvious plays at the end after you've untangled all the stacks. This game sorely needs something like that.)As a spy story, it's just a random collection of tropes forcibly smashed together in a nonsense arrangement that doesn't advance a plot so much as give you something to read between "missions." They try to hand-wave the weirdness of it all by saying it's an "abstract interface," but sorry, no, I'm not feeling it.I do feel slightly bad giving it a negative review, though, because the acting in the cutscenes is actually decent. The problem is that what they are acting out is totally silly and pointless, and the game beneath is just dull -- so dull, in fact, that the color palettes you receive as level-up rewards are the most interesting part of the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: What a super fun take on Solitaire! I was able to beat the campaign of this game in about 5.5 hours, but there is tons of content to where that is not a huge deal. _childDocuments_.review: A well-made little solitaire game. I finished it in a bit less than 8 hours. The story was finely crafted around the game concept, but there wasn't much continuity between individual missions. (which, by the way, I would have liked to be able to select individually and directly once the game is finished, so I could do the ones I missed)The challenge level is just right: barely enough turns to finish each puzzle without it getting frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: So here's the thing. The gameplay is fun, it's a good solitaire game. _childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy is a new twist on solitaire play by weaving a tale of espionage with the different suites playing the role of different spy teams (and some missions may need 4 teams), each team with its own capabilities, while still doing the original game: clearing the board of all cards. With pretty slick visuals, some randomness to add replayability, timed modes and survival mods for leaderboard challenges, and more, and you have an interesting game. You have been contacted by someone who claims he works for the good guys, and you are his last hope... You are on a list of potential recruits, and due to an attack, the agency had been cut off from its teams of agents, and you, as the temporary spymaster, need to reestablish the network by plowing your way through various missions and confront the person responsible for this mess, someone only known as Solitaire. The actual game consists of you choosing missions from a global map. You start with easy missions, only 1 or 2 teams, but as you continue, you will need to handle 3 or 4 team missions (full 4 suites of cards). The objective is pretty simple: you have the center 4 piles, those are for Aces to start the stack. Then the cards are randomly dealt into 8 stacks to either side of the center 4, face up, but you can only play the "top" card. The objective is to move all the cards into the center stacks from Ace to King for all suites in play. You can move the top card to another stack if they are SMALLER than that stack's top card. They don't have to be consecutive. So far, simple. The fun part starts when you got the Ace in the middle stack, as this activates the special ability of that team (suite), and every team is different. Some will shuffle that entire stack and randomly move cards elsewhere. Some will sort the stack a certain way. However, only the hole cards (J, Q, K) have the special abilities. So use them wisely, and in combination with other team's powers. As you win battles and earn XP, you will also level up, and your objective is to hit level 15, and have a final confrontation with Solitaire. Along the way, you will do a lot of solitaire, and perhaps, even play a few "recruitment missions" where you unlock additional teams with their unique capabilities. The between level briefing is done via video monolog of your "handler", and some special missions have its own video monolog as well. All in all, production value is good, and the game itself is quite challenging. Overall, an interesting variation on Solitaire card game with a good narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought in on discount and I am happy I did.It fun if you like solitaire, but I was expecting to be able to play different solitaire games as I had seen there was a selection menu in the images but that is just choosing the teams.Fun experience, it is a bit weird when the characters of the story are talking to you while reading the script that is on there other monitor tho.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very enjoyable game, especially for people who like solitaire. Presentation is very strong. The graphics and UI design are top notch, and the music is perfect. I really enjoy how it increases in intensity when you get close to completing each stage. The story is interesting and while there are some weak points in the back end, it finishes very strong. All in all, a good time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Mike Bithell really doesn't know how to make a bad game, and this game continues that trend. It's a fun twist on Solitaire, actually a lot easier than Solitaire but the puzzles are fun and the powers on the cards makes what would be totally straightforward rather unique. The story is fine enough, it is kind of neat to see popular games media people popping up as characters. All in all, not a bad way to spend a couple nights.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a neat game, the timeless concept paired with wacky obstacles and tricks make this stand out among a lot of other card games I've played so far. I'm also a big fan of the art and the stylistic choices with the colors as well ;0 thank you for putting the option for me to change themes when I get a new one and giving me the option to nix it if I don't feel like it lol

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this, but ultimately, it's not that good. The solitaire game itself is not great compared to other, more familiar types. The campaign is pretty short and there's not much reason to continue playing afterwards. Although the world of the game was interesting, the story was not. I suppose the acting was decent for being intentionally hammy.I encountered a bug with the mouse cursor which the developers apparently know about but haven't been able to fix. Check the Steam forum for more info. Even though this was a mostly 2D game with fairly straightforward graphics, it consumed resources on my computer like there was no tomorrow. Definitely needs to be optimized.Overall, I just didn't find it fun, which is a shame because there were some interesting ideas here that ultimately didn't work out.

_childDocuments_.review: A ton of fun, although I do find the campaign+ missions to be a bit obnoxious once Humanity+ cards are involved, I just...do not enjoy the gameplay design of when they are involved, those cards are such a headache. That and, Campaign+ missions are the same puzzle over and over again. While regular campaign is randomized. Oh well, + mode is just for extra XP anyways! Absolutely recommend this game, it's solitaire, but freshened up, at a great price!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I can't gush enough about this game. I bought it thinking at least it will be pretty which it certainly is with it's elegantly sophisticated interface that has a cyberpunky vibe and the well-written cinematics really help give the game purpose. Loved the simple colour themes you unlock as you get further into the game for quality of life value along with a couple interface cosmetics in the options. They don't try to be too clever since they do the trick of suspending your belief and wanting to join them on their larger than life vision of what a normally mundane game of Solitaire could be my fluffing your eagerness for progression with slick crew mechanics that turn a repetitive game into something approaching spycraft zen. I would've bought this game full price for sure but I was a bit confused with the ending since I thought I would have a choice of how the plot ended but I guess they decided on something more open-ended for interpretation? Otherwise definitely have this when you need a quick filler game to chill with when you have your beverage of choice. Kudos to the game design team and hope they introduce more teams or cosmetics.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played any of the other games by bithell studios, do yourself a favor. Each entry is a unique micro-experience that are as memorable as they are breezy. Solitaire Conspiracy starts as a very basic solitaire like game, that quickly ramps up in complexity and opportunities for the player to feel clever. You are your own driver to figure out new ways to squeeze a little more efficiency by playing the right combination of cards. Highly recommend for anyone looking for a unique little indie gem.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game and pretty much what I needed lately - something that I can play when I have only a few minutes available. The gameplay is addictive (in a non-exploitative sense :P ), the sound and visuals are also on point, somehow selling very well the fantasy of being in control of a spy network.If I had to pick criticism for the game, it would be that the abilities of a few of the suits involve randomness, which doesn't fit that well with a puzzle-like solitaire type of a game, but seen in another way, this just adds to the challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Preface***I got this on sale with a deal for Ancient Enemy, the campaign is short but sweet and it clocks in at a leisurely 5.5 hours.It's fun, the story is fairly corny but, you gotta give it to the actors as it was enjoyable. The best part is that the game does not outstay its welcome.Two gripes~1) While the decks are amazing, some of the colors meld together and make it rather difficult for me to distinguish. I caught myself hunting excessively just because I could not see the card I was looking for as it looked too much like another suit.2) *PERSONAL GRIPE* Was not a fan of the Wave system. The game is built around being tactical and this system punished you for being tactical in favor of just madly throwing cards around as fast as possible.Great time!

The design is brilliantly simple, but keeps adding new flair and fun features. I just started university for game design, and I have always loved PlayWatchListen, which inspired me to achieve my dreams. _childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I usually love Bithell Shorts, and I love unusual genres mixes (think Yoku's Island and things of the likes), and I even love solitaire games. I was therefore expecting this game to be right up my alley, but it did not do it for me. The UI is often confusing, which I found surprising for something as simple as a Solitaire game. The cutscenes become boring after a while, which is a bummer considering it's one of the main selling points of the game. The game itself is not super engaging; you don't need to plan ahead and there's no way to be blocked as far as I know, so it makes for a very unchallenging game. And finally, the special abilities don't add much to the game and can mostly be ignored, which is disappointing considering that would be another thing that could have set this game apart from other solitaire games.The game is super juicy and polished, I'll give it that. However, it's sadly a game with a lot of style but no substance.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: In some ways this game is great, it's got a fresh take on solitaire. Loved the adventure aspect of it.But this game gets boring fast and has no replay value for me. Reached level 15 and there's nothing left to do but the daily grinds.  Not even going to bother trying for the remaining achievements. Too frustrating trying to get the last few and not fun in the least bit.This game desperately needs a real classic solitaire game option. As it is I wouldn't recommend this game unless it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals and sounds are very nice ! The acting is ok. The "story" is cringe and honestly I wouldn't even have bothered. This game is a Solitaire x Yu-Gi-Oh kind of game with decks having abilities. Just sticking to that was badass enough. But eventually the "campaign" is very short, and just like the Windows version, solitaire is getting boring fast, even with such interesting concept.They could have implement some roguelike based mechanics like random rules when you launch a game (can't move card twice in a row from same pile, etc whatever you can think of). Dunno if that is possible but at least it'd add some replay value.The game lacks a loadout system for custom decks. I mean being able to choose exactly the number of KQJ effects however you want (like 1 alpha, 2 merries, 2 atlantis, 1 incognito etc), with different effects within same team. That would be dope for speedruns, trying to make the most optimized deck !Finally a salty note I'm sure players can refer to : when I play challenge mode on a mission, I fail. But when I play the same mission on standard, I win within challenge objective lol, fml.Good attempt to change a classic tho !

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to leave a bad review of a Bithell game, but I'm doing it.  It is what it is.Before I go on, though,  I'd like to encourage you to buy any or all of Bithell's other releases.  They are all excellent.  Maybe you too will fall in love with their shared setting enough to feel, as I did, that this game is worth taking a risk on.  Maybe you will have a better experience than I have.  I hope you do.First and foremost, if you don't like solitaire, you're not going to enjoy this game.  The game is honest; it is right there on the box art: SOLITAIRE.  There's no false advertising here.  It's a solitaire game.  I don't enjoy solitaire, and I resisted buying the game for a long time because of it, but after finishing and enjoying everything else Bithell has made, I decided that it was worth the risk, and at the end of the day I'm happy to have given Bithell some more of my money.  No harm, no foul, I knew what I was getting into.But the game is not enjoyable.  It is a paste-thick grind.  I'd go so far as to say that I'm quite resentful of Bithell for making me play this thing to get at the last bits of their worldbuilding that I was missing out on.  I’m disappointed because I’ve been led to expect so much better.I'm taking into account the fact that I'm not a solitaire fan as I write this, but it is always going to color my perceptions to a large degree.  The game is attractive, the controls are good, the choice of processed video for the storytelling is unusual but not too jarring, the acting is... fine... but the game itself is a repetitive puzzler and the story is just weird.I can't figure out whether Bithell wanted to make a campy spy game and lacked the budget for more than a simple puzzler, or if they wanted to make a solitaire game and slapped together a campy spy story to give it some depth.  What they definitely did not do is take a look at their shared universe and think, "This next bit is an espionage epic, how are we going to tell it?"  The plot is goofy in its simplicity, and carries none of the moral or ethical weight of Bithell's other offerings.As far as the solitaire itself is concerned, the face cards of each suit have a special ability, and the game fiction positions these as being beneficial, but very few of them are, and by the time you reach the latter half of the game the narrative has stopped pretending they are useful at all.  Many are out-and-out obstacles, for the most part, but this doesn't make sense in the context of the fiction, so it is never explained.At one point the villain tries to slow you down by limiting the number of suits you can play with, but this makes the game exponentially easier, with no drawback that I could see.  It feels almost like the suit powers were a gameplay element that was originally supposed to be very different, but wasn’t executed upon, and the script still reflects an earlier version of the concept.The goal of the game is to reach "Level 15" -- no smoke and mirrors here, just grind that XP and level up.  Every level requires a few games of solitaire.  They are themed as spy missions but the theming is essentially irrelevant.  Some of the missions have an interesting story blurb, but the most interesting ones leave you with an open-ended mystery.You can gain fractional bonus XP for being efficient, or for playing with a turn limit, but I frankly didn't have the fortitude to worry about it and it doesn't seem to matter much to the math.  Some new levels unlock new suits of cards (games are played with one to four suits each), but as I note above, this is more of a punishment than a reward.The net result is a bad solitaire game.  I want to sugarcoat it, but I just don't know how.  I admit that I am a poor judge of what a solitaire player is looking for, but even my best educated guess would not look anything like this game.Sorry, Bithell, better luck next time.  Now I need to go make sure I have left positive reviews for all of your other games, to offset this gross karma.

_childDocuments_.review: The dialogue in the video parts is terrible, and I stopped paying attention to the mission descriptions after the first couple. Other than that and how quickly it's possible to get to Level 15, I like this a lot. The visuals are slick, and it adds an excellent twist to the basic Solitaire game.The goal is, of course, to arrange each suit from smallest (ace) to largest (king). In each game, the suits each represent a spy crew. When you uncover and place the ace for a suit, you power up that suit's Jack, Queen, and King so that, the next time they're placed on top of another card, their special power automatically activates. This can be a good thing or a bad thing, depending on how you've managed to plan things. For example, one crew has the power to take every card in the stack their placed upon and spread them on top of all the other stacks - this could cover up cards you'd hoped to use next, or uncover a card you need that was previously buried. My least favorite crews were Humanity+, Scorpio, and Blood Legacy, but there were times I managed to use even their powers to my advantage.Each mission has two options/difficulty settings - I only ever did the hardest one, which puts limits on the total number of turns you can take. When you're all done with the main story, there are still some things you can do. I haven't dug into that aspect much, but it looks like there's a daily game where you compete against other players to see who can complete it in the fewest number of turns; a timed game (I haven't done this yet); "choose 1-4 crews" games; and a series of "recruitment" games that adds the Merry to your roster of crews in the end.I'm not sure yet how much I'll be playing this now that I've finished the main game. While I wish that had taken a few more hours to complete, I don't regret getting this. Figuring out how and when to use the various crews was a lot of fun, and the gorgeous artwork, huge variety of color scheme choices (which gradually unlock, the same as the crews), and good soundtrack definitely didn't hurt.Oh, one thing I should add: when I first started the game the way the camera would move slightly when I moved my mouse bugged me a lot. Thankfully, this effect can be turned off.

_childDocuments_.review: Mike Bithell makes some of the most inventive and interesting indie shorts I play across all of my time with video games, and he delivers yet another wildly diverse entry into his catalog with The Solitaire Conspiracy. Here, you solve government conspiracy missions by ordering cards in randomized decks from Ace to King. It has basic card game ideas and properties, but certain cards switch up the playstyle when certain moves and strategies can be employed. The gameplay is extremely fun and addicting, and the rogue-like Countdown mode I can see becoming an essential to speedrunners and high-score chasers. Overall, I will say I was disappointed by the story. As a person who was totally captured by Bithell's two previous "Circular" games, this story felt completely flat for me, and the FMV of Greg Miller made me want to skip the cutscenes sometimes and just get back to the cards. Overall, well worth it if you'd like a card-based puzzle game, or you really enjoy playing Solitaire and would love a twist.

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy is a fun game. As with most Bithell Games there is a central narrative, which is both well written and acted to take you through the campaign. Highly recommended for both a fun, new way to play solitaire and to spend a tense five minutes with.

_childDocuments_.review: The game this most reminded me of is Monaco: What's Yours is Mine. In a similar vein, this game features stylized espionage, but with solitaire. You start off as a mysterious yet highly knowledgeable person who is chosen to take emergency command of a spy agency. Solitaire represents your command system.The good:* The graphics are amazing and polished. It has to easily be one of the best looking digital card games I've seen.* The game nails the vibe with an excellent soundtrack, cool missions and nice art. The flavor text is very well written and tickled my imagination.* The gameplay is fun and can get pretty tough. The incentive to take fewer moves rewards doing better while not punishing people for doing worse.* Hey, an FMV game!The meh:* The story is very linear, and while I expected it to be the perfect game for the main character to be able to make choices about their alliances, and encounter moral dilemmas, it's ultimately a straight path. Lacks replayability for that reason, which could have prolonged its length.* Similarly, you don't get to talk/interact with any of the agent characters or hear their dialog. Leaves most to your imagination.Overall: 8/10I thought it was a short and sweet game, though I can fully understand if people don't want to get it based on its really short length, even for the rather low price. What is there is very polished and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the writing in Mike Bithell's games (I strongly recommend his earlier games  and ), so this game was an instant buy for me.The writing is fine; however, the campaign ends abruptly, right as the story is getting good. In the game's defense, there is a lot more content in the works. I'm definitely looking forward to it.Visually, the game is simply gorgeous - I love the neon aesthetic, and the character art is beautifully drawn. The FMV segments are a bit overwrought in some places... but that's practically a staple of FMV games at this point.Mechanically, the game is based on a very simple variant of solitaire -- one where a card need only be of lower value than the card it is placed on, rather than a directly  lower value. It also needn't match the suit. Furthermore, this game's special gimmick is that the face cards (Jack, Queen, and King) of each suit have a special effect when they are moved to a pile, as long as they have been 'activated' (i.e. their suit's Ace has been moved to the centre column), and those effects allow the player to bypass the classic solitaire mechanics (e.g. by sorting piles, exploding piles, immediately moving the next needed card of a suit to the centre column, and so on). Those effects are cool, and they allow for interesting strategic gameplay, but they can significantly negate the basic challenges of the solitaire game. As a result, the default difficulty mode - just 'Campaign' - is far too easy.Fortunately, the devs knew this and were quick to add 'Campaign Plus' mode shortly after launch. 'Campaign Plus' makes the levels fixed (not randomly dealt) and imposes a turn limit, changing the game from merely a series of random solitaire levels into a set of much more interesting and challenging puzzles. For players who want to compete on scores, the game has a daily challenge ('Skirmish' mode) with a leaderboard.For players who like their solitaire to be competitive  frantic, there is the 'Countdown' mode, which spawns endless waves and imposes a time limit; each card successfully moved to the centre column adds a small amount of time to the countdown. This mode rewards quick thinking and familiarity with the various special card abilities, and it is easily my favourite mode.Overall, this game is a bold departure from the developer's previous games, but still reflects their keen eye for sleek aesthetics and intriguing, suspenseful storytelling. It's not a cerebral masterpiece like the  games, but it definitely provides a thrilling and immersive experience for its roughly 3-hour play time, and a reasonably interesting and eye-pleasing diversion for anyone who continues to play the daily challenge and/or endless modes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solitaire variant with special powers in the face cards. It's very well designed, and each level is usually in the range of "fairly easy" to "making me think but not needing multiple attempts", though obviously this is going to vary person-by-person. Campaign plus (fixed puzzles) are really well made to be more challenging, which adds more replayability. I'd say if you really enjoy solitaire and variants its worth full price since you'll be coming back to it. Otherwise I'm more of an eh, maybe catch it on sale if you're interested.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The most dramatic game of Solitaire you will ever play.At the core it is the usual card sorting, with the addition that the face cards have various special effects depending on the suit. But while you slowly bring the cards in order and place them on the goal positions, increasingly dramatic music plays that feels like an action packed spy thriller is happening, instead of a calm card game.Between the games of solitaire, a bearded nerd explains to you how your actions in the card game actually correspond to you coordinating spies and mercenaries in various high stakes missions. These cutscenes also contain the plot of the game which is of course a story about spies and conspiracies and which has a surprisingly satisfying ending.The game is very pretty, especially the artwork on the face cards.It's not a very long game, but I enjoyed every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who vaguely knew the rules of solitaire but didn't see the appeal this game is great.It's a much friendlier empowering variant that is satisfying to play, there's no rummaging through unknown cards and it swiftly onboards you with ramping complexity starting off with reduced suits and powerful special powered face cards that gradually ramp in ability complexity and comboes as you learn to handle more suits.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game. It takes the classic game Solitaire and tweaks it just enough to keep the core game there, but with an extra layer of strategy. The "story" is a little hokey, but I enjoyed it, and found myself enjoying watching every cutscene, curious to see what would come next. The real bread and butter is the gameplay, so once I finished the story (just under 4 hours) there is still plenty to do with daily challenges and a skirmish mode, which I have not tried yet. On top of the fun gameplay, I love the art, and really like the ability to change themes quickly and easily. I like how the themes are pretty varied as well. It's basically just a color scheme, but with the neon accents and color palettes used, it does change the overall feel for me. Recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent gameplay paired with beautiful artwork and a dynamic score. The writing is entertaining, and T.J. Miller has the perfect amount of camp to propel the story. The Story+ mode also adds depth and makes returning to the game rewarding. There is one instance of a difficult "tutorial" explanation, and I wish the devs could offer more challenging levels. Otherwise, this is a quality solitaire re-imagination. Would recommend if you like Solitaire but wish the cards could help and/or betray you.(Play, Watch, Listen brought me here)
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Mike Bithell and his cohorts are consistently great at taking interesting concepts, making short games out of them, and polishing them to a AAA-level shine. The Solitaire Conspiracy is no exception - it has great, pithy spy-fi writing, some fun FMV cutscenes, clever "power-up" mechanics, gorgeous visuals (with unlockable alternate color schemes!), and an excellently moody soundtrack. Plus, what sets this apart from the past Bithell shorts is you can play this one pretty much forever.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend if you're a fan of Solitaire or want to get into that world.The production values on the interface, experience and story mode videos are stellar.The story mode is entertaining and the videos do not overstay their welcome.The game has gotten a Campaign+ mode since release, which makes each level a set puzzle that you have to solve in a given amount of steps. More features are planned that I'm looking forward to, like freelance agencies and the daily challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed the cheesy FMV story/acting as well as the slick visual effects. The game itself isn't exactly what I'd call challenging, but solving each round is still rather satisfying in the way that Solitaire card-sorting games tend to be, and the special abilities associated with the face cards of each team were enough to keep me engaged. Content updates do seem to be forthcoming, so I'm looking forward to seeing what else they put in.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're very much in the market for a new relaxing solitaire experience, this should satisfy well enough. But if you're looking for something fresh and engaging, you're likely to be disappointed.Definitely don't buy for the story. It seems to be cliche on purpose, but it's not clear why it needs to exist at all. It just kind of putters about with obvious twists before confidently striding off to nowhere.The acting really grated on me as well. Greg Miller starts off well enough, a bit quirky with only an occasional sour note here and there. But about halfway in he takes a nose-dive with some one-note grunting that's likely the result of bad direction. I hate to knock an earnest attempt, but it had me grimacing and eyeing the skip button.The solitaire itself occasionally offers a moment to make you feel clever by saving yourself a handful of moves. But it's all a formality as it's impossible to fail. There are challenge modes available that might tickle you if you get a kick out of perfectly optimal play or topping the leaderboards, but I didn't find the mechanics compelling enough to sink that kind of effort into.It's a respectable experiment, but the result is underwhelming. I don't regret my purchase because I like to see new ideas and support the kinds of people who put them forward. But if you're on the fence, you might as well skip it. It's not going to win you overe.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Don't normally leave reviews, but this game kinda stands out. I have never played any version of solitaire before this game. Saw Mike on a podcast and thought I would give it a whirl.Fun game with right amount of challenge and critical thinkingRight amount of story, with genuine interest in completing it.Overall for $10 its a great little experience!EDIT: Beat it :) can't want for the Bithell Solitaire Extended UniverseEDIT2: Endless modes are fun
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The Solitaire Conspiracy brings to the table a fresh way to play the classic card game, Solitaire. Each deck has a different power/abilities, helping/making it harder for you to complete the game and the type of deck you place a card on doesn't matter until you're trying to stack the total deck. This was actually a pretty fun game, way too easy, but had a lot of fun with it. It's a shame that it was so short, I was hoping that it would last a little longer while progressing through the missions, but enjoyed myself nonetheless. The story line was actually pretty entertaining for a card game too, I did not expect to enjoy the characters as much as I eventually did.  - < 3 hours   - Well, apart from the Main Campaign, there are two other modes you can play;   - A custom Solitaire game where you can pick how many decks/what deck powers are available for one individual game.    - A timed game mode where it will continuously get harder as you advance. You get time bonuses for each card you put down, so being speedy is the trick to winning this game. I enjoyed playing Countdown much more than Skirmish. I found while Skirmish was great and being able to train myself at some of the decks I was unfamiliar with, it was very repetitive and often just as easy as the Main Campaign. Countdown felt like I was being pushed to do better, one day i'll make it to round 15!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Positive:A very solid and enjoyable experience, the smooth visuals and music really complement the game experience and story. It actually reminded me a lot of playing a combo deck in Magic The Gathering which I love. When the voice acting is kept at a pace and intense it really adds to the tension. Neutral:I'm not sure if some of the agents are way better than others or if they just suite the way I play card games.Negative:Some of the voice acting felt rigid and unnatural in it's delivery, with a slow purposeful pace, was not a fan. As stated in positives, this isn't all of the time, but I'd be lying if I didn't mention it.Update: The Merry is exactly want I want from an update, fun new crew, I thought the fmv actor was the best so far and the new track is pretty nice as well.Overall I'd heartily recommend, I'd first play through the campaign and then use it as a  daily activity to get the brain going, sort of like a mental warm up activity.

_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, quick game putting an interesting spin on Solitaire.I've managed to finish the campaign twice (both original mode and campaign plus) in about 7 1/2 hours.The original campaign is a good introduction, but gets to be fairly simple once you've remembered how to play Solitaire and understand the new powers of the different spy crews.The campaign plus mode provides a challenge. It reminds me of the puzzles in Thronebreaker: The Witcher Tales, but less strict about what cards to play and when. In the new, set card layouts there are definitely some moves you HAVE to do, but there is still flexibility in solving the puzzles.Skirmish is fun to play a quick game and I can see myself coming back to it when I feel in the mood for Solitaire. I think I'd like the option to play a game without the spy crews powers as well. I know they're a great part of the game, but it could be nice to just take advantage of the fancy assets and aesthetics for a normal game of Solitaire.I'm looking forward to what Mike Bithell and his team does with the game over time! I've still got some more time with it now anyways while I try to get to round 15 in the Countdown mode. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Never thought I would play solitaire for extended periods of time in my life and yet here we are. The only reason I even purchased/stuck with the game till its conclusion is because of the promise of a story and because I like Greg. The story is lacklustre but Greg's performance is certainly campy and fun. Only recommended for fans of Greg and those who need a game to play in short bursts.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting variant of solitaire. Each suit has their own abilities, you build up each ability by matching cards with their corresponding suits. _childDocuments_.review: I really like the presentation for this game. The dynamic soundtrack is well implemented and fun, fully matching the spy theme. The acting was good. I am familiar with Greg Miller's work, and it made it a little difficult to not see "Greg Miller plays a super spy" rather than "There's a super spy." But your mileage on that will vary.But other than that, there's not really much here. The story is rather lackluster, and I saw the plot beats coming from a mile away. The gameplay itself is alright, but to my knowledge it is impossible to lose. The game is adding a hard mode, where the player has to try to beat the game in X moves to progress. Some of that will come down to luck, because sometimes you'll just get a lucky deal, and other times all your aces are buried. The game also has a time trial mode, which I don't have much interest in because I don't play solitare to be fast, I play to be efficient.Some people really enjoy the gameplay, but if you are finding it tedious due to the lack of any real required skill, and minimal rewards for playing well, don't keep playing to get to the end of the story. It doesn't get any better.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: It's practically a cliche at this point, but this is another one of those games that really needs a sideways thumb option.Let me start by saying the UI is slick (if sometimes hard to read), the presentation is fun and there is very obviously some real love put in this game (especially in the cutscenes). I did not encounter any bugs.Unfortunately, the actual solitaire sucks. I'm not sure what variant this is, but it's miles from classic Klondike. All cards are placed face-up at the start into 8 stacks. There only as many sets of cards as the number of "teams" (basically suits) the mission has, so the vast majority of missions are 3 or less. You can only move one card at a time (never a stack, whether ordered or not) and face cards get "charged" with their abilities as you place cards. "Charged" face cards can be played on top of anything. What results is a version of solitaire so comically exploitable I'm not sure it's even POSSIBLE to have a hand you can't win.The abilities each "team" has can be somewhat interesting, but I found all but the last 3 or so counterproductive (though a couple of them are actually negative by design). You cannot choose when to use an ability and when not to. Once a face card is "charged" placing it anywhere but an empty stack activates the ability. Basically, the closest thing to challenge this game musters is occasionally forcing you to shoot yourself in the foot.It's pretty short, too. I completed the campaign and a couple skirmishes just for the achievements in under 3.5 hours. They just introduced a new game plus mode, but I really don't see the point. At $12 the price isn't completely out of line for what you're getting, but it doesn't feel like much of a value either. I was tempted to refund it at a couple points, but stuck with it to see how the story would end. It ends on a cliffhanger that is genuinely intriguing, so maybe they'll implement some DLC or something to continue it. Hopefully free. I have a hard time seeing a reason to pump more money into such mediocre gameplay.TL;DR - Interesting cutscenes and concepts meet mediocre gameplay that never gets better. Thankfully short.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply amazing. First off, gameplay is fun and addicting. A great twist on Solitaire/Free Cell and enjoyable to play even when I just wanna sit back and chill. _childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I fully did not expect to enjoy a solitaire game this much. When launching Solitaire Conspiracy for the first time, I figured I'd play for 10 - 15 minutes and come back to it when installing other games. Almost 2 hours after that first boot up, I found myself playing solitaire in a fashion I'd never before imagined - mindfully. I'd never put much thought into playing other versions of solitaire, but The Solitaire Conspiracy's agencies and abilities had me carefully planning my moves and actually using simple strategy rather than mindlessly clicking away. It's not overly complex, but I find that to be a beautiful strength rather than a critical flaw. I adore the UI and overall art direction. The music invokes memories of great spy films that I enjoy so much. Greg Miller's acting is superb. Overall, a welcome surprise and an inspiring experience. Kudos to Mike Bithell and his talented teammates for giving us a stellar game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: It didn't occur to me that you could make a story line around a traditional card game and it was a clever plot. Definitely was entertaining that the mechanics of Solitaire was explained as a method of strategic planning involving spies. It had a very Mission impossible vibe to it. The Royal suit ability system added a good depth and I didn't ever feel too stuck which was good for the pace of game play but not challenging enough; I completed the main game in a single sitting and restarted only a couple levels throughout. - Really good graphics (easy on eyes and attractive)- Loved the cast of characters, illustrations and back stories- Game play was really fun and made for continuous repetitive play. Sticks in my mind after I completed the game.- Very well written Mission objectives of each level (I read them in Mike Bithells' voice), added depth- I liked Inel Tomlinson's take on his character- Loved the C&C Red Alert style FMV! - Preferred if Greg Miller was more relaxed in his role, it felt a little zoom meeting one dimensional- More sound effects when selecting a card- More highs and lows of the music. Felt a little panicky from the start of every level- Selecting missions didn't affect levelling/difficulty outcome so much (would love a nuanced point/penalty system or even disabling moves)- Bonus Mission points weren't clear how they were awarded. I didn't even know they were in the game until I got them in one level - Some of the Royal suit abilities didn't feel beneficial to use, not sure if it was intentional or I wasn't being strategic the way the game wanted me to play (could be used as a future plot line maybe?)Overall, the aspects that I thought needed a bit of tweaking didn't overshadow my enjoyment of the game at all, they were nitpicky things I thought about if the game were to be further expanded upon. I'm keen to start playing the other game modes and would recommend this title if you are a casual player of Solitaire and like a more modern game design instead of the typical green board and old school card look. It's been years since I bought a new release game and am glad I did. 7.5 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit for introduction of Campain+ : What happens when you polish gold? I can now even more highly recommend this gameWonderful game! Mechanical and artistic polish are both incredibly high. Others might complain that the campaign is too short or that the amount of overall gameplay (including future play using the "free play" modes) isn't enough for the price being charged, I disagree. At its base, it's an upgrade version of solitaire, but with new mechanics that are built so cleverly that I'd want to support the dev team in the interest of seeing what they'd make in the future (be it updates or completely new games). But then add in the artistic polish to further deliver the overall concept, help draw in players new to the solitaire variant, and the fact that this theme's execution is nailed perfectly? Absolutely fantastic.Lastly, speaking as a fan of indie games, I think this is a wonderful Short. The base idea is explored, taken in some delightful new directions, but also doesn't feel like things were pushed too far or otherwise "overstaying its welcome". Bravo!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: 4+ hours of a delightful take on solitaire with a short story to motivate you forward, great soundtrack and eye-candy UI.Bought on a whim, I spent about 4.5 hours playing the classic card game of solitaire (but not so classic as you will see) in ways that I could never have imagined would spark joy (wink MK fans!).: sure it's solitaire, but the face cards of each suit have very cool and special powers. And unlike standard cards, there are more than 4 suits (8 or 9 factions, each faction have their unique power and suit). The campaign requires you to reach level 15. You take on various missions (from a choice of three - with higher difficulty / XP reward depending on your choice). Each time you reach a level you are "rewarded" (more on that latter) with an FMV sequence and new UI colours. New factions are slowly introduced, and there are a few twists along the way which I will not reveal. The campaign will last you anywhere between ca. 4 to 5 hours depending on how well you play (you get bonus XP for completing in fewer turns) and the difficulty level you pick at each mission.: a friggin awesome soundtrack which gets you heart pounding and goes crescendo as you near completion of each mission. Seriously, the soundtrack just puts you in the mood and is stellar.: near flawless, with a cool neon vibe and (optional, but totally worth it) change of colours at each level.Now as to the structure / narrative / FMV. The vibe here is that of a spy / espionage / hacking thriller. And it really makes a difference in terms of motivation... but I have to say the FMV sequences are a bit cringy, though I suspect this will largely depend on personal taste. Some may really dig it. No matter, it was still enjoyable and the game would not be the same without it.I had not played solitaire in more than 20 years. I do not particularly love nor hate solitaire... yet I had a blast here. So if you are neutral about solitaire (or love it) there is a good chance you will enjoy The Solitaire Conspiracy. Once the campaign is over you can play a couple of other game modes but I'm personally not that interested in them... but I suspect if you really like solitaire you will totally enjoy those.Apparently the game is doing well (deservedly so) and the devs are planning new content.Bravo team Bithell!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game with great audio and visual presentation. Has several layers you can engage with. You can play just for the solitaire. It's a pretty simple variant with an interesting crew powerups twist. There's also a nice video/text "spy story" behind it and then you can read all the crew and character bios for even more immersion.There are 3 modes - main Campaign, Skirmish (quick single game) and Countdown (a time limit variant).The campaign took me about 3h. It's shorter if you skip the story aspects.Technically game had a pretty smooth release. The few small bugs that were found got patched pretty much immediately (great dev support!). It looks and runs great. Buttery smooth animations and transitions, even on a pretty niche 32:9 120Hz monitor.If you're a solitaire fan and looking for something fresh and modern in that genre it's a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: You've probably been there at some point; You've been bored, looked through the computer just for  to kill the time, right? And what's that? Is that solitaire? Yeah, why not play a round or two of it? And we all know, it turns into several rounds of it. Well, here we are. Solitaire Conspiracy. You're playing solitaire with a twist. Each type of card - what would've been hearts, clubs, diamonds, and spades - have special abilities. They can take the next card you need and put it at the bottom of the stack... or on the top. Or could "blow up" the stack and place the cards in a random stacks over the "board".All this while playing out a spy movie plot. Jim Ratio (played by Greg Miller from Kinda Funny Games Podcast and formerly IGN) is training you and helping you defeat the evil mastermind Solitaire and every mission (every round) has a different narrative that ties into the overall storyline. That's the basic gist of it all. And it being just solitaire, it really does work for a few hours. At least it did for me. The time just flies by, you just  finish that round and get the next cutscene... but it turns into five more. It's kinda addictive. Bravo Mike Bithell and company!
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This is a POLISHED Solitaire experience. The story mode provides a nice narrative that reminds me of the FMV games of the 90s (Command & Conquer or Crusader No Remorse). So a bit cheesy but on theme. The story acts as a tutorial that introduces you to new suits that provide different face card abilities. When you're done the story you can learn more in skirmish mode or hit the real fun in Countdown. Having a time limited competitive Solitaire experience with a leader board is good fun for people driven by competition. I found the story and skirmish relaxing fun and I really felt the pressure in Countdown.I prefer shorter games these days. The 4.6 hours I've put into this felt like good value for the money to me. I have two achievements left to get for Wave 10 and Wave 15 in Countdown and I'm not sure I'm good enough to get either.
_childDocuments_.name: The Solitaire Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game that's pretty much exactly what it sets out to be: a cheesy spy adventure as played through a game of solitaire.
