_childDocuments_.review: A [Good] simplistic puzzle game. Simplistic in both puzzles and flow, but simple does not mean interesting, it's engaging and has a decent chapter boundaries, it would be more interesting if there were more plants available at the same time, to figure which is which.The game does boil down to a exploration in few rooms, figure which clue is for which flower, grow the flower, continue to next set of flowers.But the target audience is definitely more for developing minds which would i highly recommend for, as it's a basic cute logistic puzzles about flowers, it's a tad too easy for adults.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.  I only wish there were more puzzles.  And I don't think there really needs to be more rooms or mechanics, either.  I think you could make a whole host of puzzles by combining the existing elements.  Have plants that need certain amounts of sugar added to the soil and a certain pH level.  Except, say, every unit of sugar decreases the pH by a bit.  Or expand the pH puzzles by attracting other pollinators to grow the other varieties.  Or sing to the plant while you play it morse code messages.  Wind speed and soil temperature, but the soil's heat affects the airflow.  Use a flower to feed the smoker to grow another flower.  There are so many plant settings and info set up to camouflage the real answers, but creating other puzzles that make use of the same information could expand this game significantly.  That's my wishlist, anyway.All that said, the story told in the backgrounds and is beautiful and bittersweet, the atmosphere is relaxing, and growing magic plants is always entertaining.  There is so much promise on display, and I eagerly await further titles from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: THE PERFECT CASUAL PUZZLE STORY. I don't have a single complaint about this experience. I was so immersed the entire time, I forgot that this was a game. The atmosphere, music, colors and art style are all impeccable. I was really able to connect with the character and her story, which made it all the more charming and intriguing. The puzzles were the perfect level of challenging. It made me use my brain but not to the point that would normally frustrate me. I would love more games like this! Worth the money I spent and I recommend this game 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Botany Manor is such a relaxing and beautiful game. I love the slow pace, love the sightseeing around the house, and loved even more that the puzzle mechanics were not so hard to solve, it was even more pleasant and satisfying considering that the beauty of this game lies in the story - rather than its difficulty. I see many comments saying it is not worth its price; I would say otherwise considering the quality of the narrative and originality behind every chapter. It might be short but I have found very boring some cheaper and longer games. Such a breath of fresh air to the 'escape room' game trend, and perfect for nature lovers :)
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and immersive game with a lovely soundtrack. This was very cozy to play and I enjoyed the puzzles, though I wish there was an easier way to reference clues than sprinting back around to search for them. I do think that the price I paid (£25) was a little steep, but I did have a lot of fun playing this and will be keeping an eye out for similar vibed puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but thought-provoking and pretty puzzle game. Highlights of the game are definitely the scenes where you solve the plant puzzles -- the game plays an animation of the plant blossoming, several of which are really beautiful. The atmosphere is also really nice to just hang out in; a couple times I found myself sitting down on a bench to just soak in my surroundings.There are some rough edges here. It's obviously on the shorter side; I finished my playthrough in ~3 hours, and I wish there were more. I also found myself missing a clue a couple times, and had to search every inch for what I'd missed, which broke my immersion temporarily. And navigating around the manor was a little harder than I'd have liked; the game gives you a map, which I didn't find particularly helpful. I found myself wandering around once or twice, trying to figure out where to go.Still, definitely worth your money and time! I'm excited to see what they put out next.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: One of, if not my favourite cosy game yet. The map is gorgeous and fun to explore, the puzzles are diverse (although sometimes a little farfetched) and i liked how you unlock different parts of the story and map as you go. I do think the game is pricey, didn't have to be longer but definitely cheaper for its length. It was also annoying that you couldn't view previously found clues from the book, if you played the game in multiple sitting or found something early, you had to go all the way back to the clue to remember small important details. overall hoping for a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Roughly three hours of gameplay inside, I wish there were more. Once you get the hang of how to solve a puzzle it becomes pretty easy as long as you're always paying attention to surroundings. That being said, there's no shortage of charm in this game, I was delighted to just sit in chairs and take in the settings once in a while and all the lore that can be found in letters, books, and newspaper clippings tells a compelling story of the players life as a woman who is content with her plants. I enjoyed myself, but perhaps I should have waited for a sale considering it is roughly three hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game! I love the creative plants and figuring out the puzzles. The art was well done and exploring the house was pretty fun. I liked all the small little details and things you could see to figure out some of the lore. Over all just a nice peaceful time. I would definitely recommend this if you are looking for a relatively short and cute puzzle game!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable game, perfect puzzle solving cozy game. The music is fantastic, whenever the gate bell would go off and the music would swell, I'd feel like running around a park or a meadow in a pretty dress like I was a character on Bridgerton or something. lol Loved the puzzles and all the little details. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I don't recommend this is because of the price. DO NOT BUY FULL PRICE!!!Other than that, cute & cozy & easy.Cute cozy relaxing game that really does not require much brain power but it's pleasant enough to pass the time.I finished it in one sitting (about a few hours?). But I agree with other...do NOT buy this at full price. For the replay-ability and content of the game, it is a steep price. The puzzles lack sustenance and are too simple to charge $25!!  I kind of regret paying the high price of this when it first came out. Wait for a 50% off sale or more.PS -  Strange Horticulture has more to offer at less than half the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Game was neat. Puzzles were at a easy/medium level if you play a lot of puzzle games. For the price, it was not really worth it. I was able to beat the game in 7 hours, and that is getting up every 20 minutes because the kids needed something or the dog needed to go out. great concept and relaxing. Hope there will be an update or more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful game with smart but soothing puzzles. No guessing required, all clues are given. It is a bit short for the length of gameplay, but worth it to have a gorgeous atmosphere to take time in.As of today, achievements are broken; I gladly will eventually replay this after they are fixed, and will enjoy revisiting each plant puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: [h]The Good[/h3]Relaxing and peaceful. I really enjoyed the research-based puzzle mechanic where you figure out how to proceed by finding and reviewing documents, drawings, and other artifacts.The storyline is simple and hopeful, if a bit bittersweet, and the area gating was pretty unobtrusive. The puzzles are pretty straightforward--it's more research than logical deduction--but overall that suited the chill vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A short, relaxing point-and-click game in which you play an elderly female botanist in the late 1800s. While you cultivate plants, you learn a bit about how disrespected female scientists were in this time period and the struggles they faced to be taken seriously. The accessibility options are pretty good, with motion-sickness options and the ability to read found objects via a text overlay. However, the player cannot change any of the controls, which did make it a little uncomfortable for me playing as a lefty. I usually reassign certain functions to a different button so I can keep my right hand on the right side of the keyboard while using the mouse with my left. Being able to reassign controls is an accessibility issue and a quality of life issue that I am always disappointed to see excluded in games.Although I loved this game, I agree with other reviewers in that the price-point seems a little high for what you get. If you can get this on sale, I definitely recommend it. The one bit of game-play feedback I have is that plant clues should be readable in the game's journal, so the player doesn't have to waste time running all over the mansion because they forgot the pH balance required to grow red hydrangeas.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: In Botany Manor we play as plant scientist and manor owner Arabella Greene. Her mission is to write her own Herbarium about rare or forgotten plants. To achieve this, we use clues and her scientific research to help grow those plants around the manor. I loved the game, it felt very cozy. The mansion and gardens are bright and beuatiful, a delight to look at. The puzzles for growing the plants were easy at first, but gained complexity throughout the game. While exploring the house, we also learn more about Arabella - her passions, her career and her love for plants. All in all, I would highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a moderate puzzle game, slow pace and beautiful environment. The only thing I was a little sad about was the short play time, I would have liked to stay in Botany Manor a little while longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun and the puzzles are good. It's quite relaxing and there is a bit of a story to it that fits the time period.But I'm a little on the fence. I got 4.2 hours of playtime out of this game, but for a 24.99 euro game, I think the price is rather steep and I'd recommend waiting for a discount.One small personal issue is that I was constantly running around trying to find previously found hints. The game tells you the general area of where it can be found, but some areas are rather large, and I wasted a lot of time frustrated that I couldn't find things anymore. I would have liked it if I could have checked the hints directly from my book. But that's probably personal preference.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED the game! The puzzles were great, the plants have such neat designs, the world building was amazing! Only complaint I have seems to be the same that others have voiced, I just wish there was more. If I'm remembering correctly, there were under 15 plants that you're able to discover. It would be really cool if more plants were added. Maybe adding a basement level or something similar?
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A unique puzzle game that felt satisfying and not frustrating to solve. Unfortunately, I agree with the majority of reviewers: it's way too short. I want to support the developers but I feel like there could have been more content added for the price point. I got this game on sale for $22.49 and was able to 100% complete it in less than 3 hours without looking up solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this -  a good level of challenge with the puzzles and prettier than expected. Relatively lighthearted, with just enough back story woven in. I was enjoying the scenery, reckon you can easily get through everything in 4 to 5 hours. But why rush, when you can sit by a pond and listen to birds?This game was bought for me as a gift.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 stars. The game has a great atmosphere and the sound design is satisfying. Each puzzle is unique and fun. You can find more about the character you play as by exploring, which is a puzzle in it's self as well. Only thing I would add is a map in your inventory for players, that way if you take a break from the game they know where they are. The game is only 2 to 3 hours long, but it was worth the wait. Not a 5/5 because of the price, However,, everything else is close to perfection in my book. Hopefully there will be either a free dlc or a 5 dollar dlc.  if you are fan of puzzles and flowers, this game is heavily recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves puzzles and is a huge sap for aesthetically pleasing games, this ticked those boxes. It's definitely a scavenger game mixed with logic-deduced actions, so it gives you a bit of a tactile feel. Be warned there is quite a bit of running back and forth. If you're like me, you can blow through the entire game in less than 4 hours, even while going back to finish up the achievements. Like many of the other reviews, I share the same opinion that this game seems to be a bit overpriced for the amount of content you receive. I'm hoping a DLC can be made in the future to make up for the lack of replayability. Overall, its a decent puzzle game with an interesting story that nevertheless leaves much to be desired.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: "Botany Manor" is a charming blend of puzzle-solving and botanical exploration. The game's vivid art style and the variety of unique flowers create an immersive, picturesque world. Puzzles are cleverly integrated and offer just the right level of challenge to keep you engaged without frustration. Alongside the enjoyable gameplay, the story unfolds beautifully, combining botanical lore with heartwarming tales. Perfect for those who appreciate a thoughtful, aesthetically pleasing gaming experience. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful - as in, full of delight; the delights of steamy water, full winds, and warm sunlight washing through spacious rooms. This puzzler is generous, genuinely relaxing, and quite an achievement for such a small team. It's clever in a way that isn't antagonistic. I had simply a delightful time with the few hours I spent with it, like a midday lunch in a luxurious garden.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: So, at first I wasn't a fan of the hint system; filling in a slot with 'Note X' or 'Orchard Booklet' was very unhelpful as far as it pertained to giving me an actual hint. It's sort of grown on me a bit though in that I'm starting to take physical notes on things I think could be the actual hints. (In addition to accepting that having a nice walk through a garden to double check a hint is meant to be relaxing). That having been said, when you have multiple hint sources to plug into multiple plant pages, it can get a bit overwhelming with how vague they are.I'm still enjoying the process of growing these plants though. Figuring out what to do is engaging and relaxing, (for the most part. See: Hints), and it feels good when they bloom. It's a nice relaxing puzzle game with a lovely style.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful experience. The graphics and detailed environment were really well done. Music and ambience were lovely. Some puzzles got me thinking but not too hard where I was fed up and reaching for a guide. Any fans of flowers and/or puzzle type games are bound to love this. Sad that the game only took be about four hours to complete, would have loved to have more plants to grow. So I could suggest picking it up on sale if you can.I did have some small frame rate issues in the formal garden but not to where the game was unplayable. Only a small complaint and not something that would deter me from recommending this came.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely peaceful puzzle game about growing unusual plants. The puzzles are not terribly challenging but are really satisfying to solve, and the musical trill/animations of the plants sprouting was always a nice reward. I agree with other reviewers that being able to quickly reference the clues you find would be a nice quality of life feature, and the game is relatively short - I think it's worth the price but some people might want to get it on sale. I really hope there is some additional content at some point for it as I'd absolutely play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and fun game! Tho it doesn't take long to complete, I had a lot of fun solving the puzzles and enjoyed the style of the game a lot. Normally, I'm not much a story game person myself but the little story behind all of this here touched my heart. Don't want to spoil it but it is kinda sad. I do hope to get a sequel to this! Also worth noting that I did not experience any sort of bugs whatsoever, so that was really nice :)
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and cozy puzzle game that involves plants. Who wouldn't love it? While exploring this adorable manor, you get to learn about the story behind the owner and learn a little bit about plants. Even though the plants in the game are fake, some of the aspects on how to help them grow are actual ways to help real plants. Overall, I enjoyed the game and wish there was more.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This was a truly beautiful, cozy, short puzzle game. Lovely art style and music. Great atmosphere and scenary. Nice but not too hard puzzles. Interesting story that also shows how women had to struggle being recognized their for (scientific) work in that time. Technically this run flawlessly using Linux. Total recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very sweet, relaxing game. I felt like most of the puzzles were comfortably easy to solve, and intuitive. Only once or twice did I have to think about it for a bit. I'll definitely go back and finish the rest of the achievements I missed the first time through (I'm at 28/36 upon completing the game).
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely stunning, beautiful, and inviting! I absolutely love the entire 'world' of the game -- the location, the time period, the environment as a whole -- and all the many detailed pieces that you can interact with! I love the characters (and that I get to imagine them however I wish) and all the puzzles. A magical and peaceful experience that I absolutely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Short but beautiful. It's a hefty price for a puzzle game. I can't say if its worth how expensive it is but considering how rare a well crafted puzzle game is and how often stuff like this comes around, you can consider this a rare purchase making the price seem more accurate at least. I enjoyed it, and felt it was worth it on a personal level. No promises here though.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great cozy game, The only beef i have with it is when i save and come back, I can't remember the clues so i have to track them down in game. It would be helpful to have the full clues added to the journal in some way so they are easier to keep track of. i definitely enjoyed the game otherwise! 8/10 from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! I was so pleasantly surprised by this gem. The puzzles are challenging but not impossible. They require critical thinking and paying attention to your surroundings and the clues. This is not a game where you can breeze through the reading and still be able to fake it. You need to pay attention, which I normally struggle with but thankfully the "wordy" parts are actually quite short. A+ in my opinion!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Short and lovely. I enjoyed myself the entire time. I thought the backstory I got about Arabella was quite lovely and I found the puzzles to be easier than I thought they'd be - which is good because I hate bashing my head against my keyboard. I really think anyone who's a fan of cozy games would find this enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet... maybe a little too short for the asking price. It took me only slightly more than three hours to 100% it. 5-10 minutes of that time went into one optional achievement that was kinda tedious, and another 5 into looking for something for another. If you don't care for those, you should be able to finish the story in less than 3 hours. So if the asking price for an afternoon worth of game is too high for you, wait for a sale.Anyway, the graphics are lovely (if you can stand the The Witness like art style), the music is fine and doesn't overstay its welcome. There were some instances where the activation/use prompt was kinda fiddly and I had to reposition myself to get it working, but that happened one a couple of times.The puzzles are on the easy side if you're able to take notes and capable of deductive reasoning. I would've preferred if the hints in the book would display the relevant information, at least after they are assigned correctly the the fitting plant, as this would've saved me from taking notes / screenshots. Without that be prepared for some backtracking to look up a certain value needed. I can't say too much about the performance as my system is overpowered for what this game is asking for, but it ran perfectly fine and never noticeably dropped below the 165fps I've set it too. It also runs perfectly well on a 21:9 display. (7800X3D, 4090, 64GB, at 3440*1440)
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little puzzle game with a cozy style and unique setting.Yes, it's short but it is good quality. You can really tell how much care and work went into the development. I always prefer a game that is short and sweet over one that wastes my time with needless bloat.My biggest critique is that there should be a way to review clues from the journal so you don't have to keep track of where each clue was found just to see it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Not a very difficult puzzle game, but still quite enjoyable! Beautiful environments, a "just enough" story, and enough variety in the puzzles to keep it interesting.I had some pretty bad stuttering issues though. I wish it had run silky smooth so I could enjoy the environments better. Also a bit pricey considering the amount of hours I got out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Positively splendid game! I played with two biologists who loved both the charming puzzles of speculative biology, and the narrative of Lady Arabella Greene's struggles being a woman scientist in the 19th century.  The game world is beautiful, and made me wish I could move to a countryside manor and cultivate the gardens all day. Really looking forward to Laure De Mey's next projects, and hoping we can learn more about Lady Greene in the future :)
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so wonderful, I had so much fun finding all the clues and getting to watch my plants grow. Quite genuinely the only downside is that I wanted more plants to grow. A detail in the very ending post-credits scene makes me hopeful (?) that there will be a continuation at some point, whether an update or a sequel game? Either way, I'd love for there to be more plants to discover and clues to sniff out. Some of the details they put into this are just amazing. Not to mention I'm so envious of the manor itself you "live" in in-game. If I don't live somewhere similar in twenty years what's the point. Needless to say, I'm trying to get the rest of my friends to play and experience the joy of growing their own little garden. I loved this an awful lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that a game I play manages to bring me to tears. The story may not be heart wrenching, but it paints a beautiful story using wonderful game mechanics and fun puzzles. I'd 100% suggest getting this if you enjoy putting together hints to solve puzzles, or even just find the premise interesting- it's a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet cosy puzzle game. It's nice just to wander around, though towards the end I started getting lost a little. It would be nice if the clues were readable in your book once you've collected them rather than having to go find them again. Otherwise though, a lovely colourful little game with fairly gentle puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game and found it very charming. It's a short, cosy game that lasts 2-4 hours, depending on how you solve the puzzles and put together the clues.It has a little, underlying story which his heart-felt and honest of how women back then were threated in pursue of education and becoming an expert in their fields. The ending was very cute and fitting. I recommend this came to anyone who wants to relax and have a few nice, good executed puzzles to solve without wracking your brain for hours to no end.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning. Although it's a relatively short game, the environment and feeling that you get from it is so worth it.Positives:- Stunning scenery- Beautiful birdsong and music- Fun puzzles that won't melt your brain!- A lovely story that gradually unfolds as you go through the chapters- Wonderful artwork and flowers- Just an overall calming, beautiful experienceI think literally the only downside I can think of is it would be good to have a 'hint' button to help if you get stuck. But really the puzzles are so well explained through the clues that I don't think most people would need this.I would very much recommend this game. Absolutely worth the buy!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely cozy puzzle game. Entering this beautiful world while curling up in a blanket with my tea and puppy made for some great and much needed relaxing escapism. I only wish the game were longer or perhaps had holiday theme event updates in the future. The design aesthetic reminded me of the game The Witness (2016) but I enjoyed Botany Manor far more because of the underlying story.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This game was extremely cozy, and just the perfect amount of challenging for me to feel engaged, but not out of my depth. As a puzzle game, it doesn't have replay-ability, but the four hours I spent on it tonight (100% complete + achievements) were very peaceful, engaging, and overall enjoyable. I would highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 While I agree with most people that the game is rather short, it does what it does phenomenally. It's got great puzzles, with a really cute art style and some very simple narrative lore and world building that is easy to immerse yourself in. I'm not at all surprised to say that I did cry a tiny bit at the ending, because there's nothing that gets to me more than women who are laughed out of their fields finding vindication and power in continuing to be excellent in their jobs. I really hope the devs go on to give us some DLC, or perhaps some spiritual successor to this really fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game! Very cute and the puzzles were at times challenging, but not stressful. There were fun and interesting story elements as well as items that were clues. Easy to navigate and play. Only negative I would say is the price for such a short game and with lower tier graphics quality. That being said, for me, it's fun, cozy, and probably something I will pick up again and replay.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, i loved how the game looked visually, the puzzles were really fun to do, it took me 3 hours to complete the game so i think the price is a little expensive for such short game play. If you take away the cost of the game i would highly recommend itAlso none of the achievements worked for me, i'm not sure if this is a steam issue or a developer issue
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A wholesome game, with just enough of puzzling to tickle a tired brain in the right folds. The artstyle is simple, yet it pops with vibrant colours that is still pleasing to the eye. It's perfect for the casual gamer who don't enjoy the chaos of action games, and a nice change of pace for the ones who needs to relax yet keep the fidgeting at bay.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: It is currenly around 0 degrees Celcius here and occasionally snowing even though it is late April, and I am longing a lot for spring and summer. So this was a game with great timing - a lovely non-stressful little puzzle game about pottering around in a huge British manor, making rare (supernatural) plants bloom by finding out the exact conditions they require. This is very gamified stuff with plants requiring exact music notes played for them and similar causing them to grow to full size and bloom in seconds and usually opening up a new part of the manor while at it. So you won't learn anything about real botany or gardening here of course, but still very entertaining and beautiful.No dialogue, some light plot, and has a mix of the combine clues mechanic from Obra Dinn or Case of the Golden Idol, with the careful observation of environments of something like The Witness and many other adventure games. Peronally i would ignore the "short, no-replayability" complaints of some reviews, there are so so many endless addictive live-service games available for these people at the very cheap price of having all their free time and life sucked away. This is well worth the full price in my opinion, buy it so more games like this are made.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy this game and I thought the story was fun to read along to as you read the letter. The puzzles are fun and not too hard, everything was figure-out-able once you found all the clues. I wish there were some more flowers to find and maybe a few harder puzzles towards the end of the book that maybe needed a bunch of clues to figure out.I have to agree with a lot of the other reviews though that, for the amount of game play you get out of this game, the price is a bit high. Compared to other similar puzzle games, like chants of sennar, I was expecting something closer to 10 hours game play over the 3 I got. It is still a fun little game but I would get it when it is one sale if you can. It would be nice if they added some more flowers in the future but with how the game ended I think that is unlikely.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: its a puzzle game in which you need to figure out how to grow fictional plants. the horizontal movement and performance in general isnt the most fluid.  you can grow plants as much as you have pots for it. but you cannot place them anywhere ( not on the ground ). the walking through the map is a bit clunky and can take a while when youre further into the game.I wouldnt say its worth the full price, but definately a nice game to pick up during sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute adventure game! It is quite simple and short, so don't expect too much challenge if you are a puzzle aficionado, but if you are a newcomer to puzzle/adventure games, or are just looking for a little escapade in a flowery XIXth century house, this is the perfect game!The graphics and music are delightful, the interface is simple to use, the story is charming (there are tidbits of narration in every room) and I loved the ending.The only thing I see that could be improved is a way to see the content of the clues directly from the journal (it does tell you the name of the clue and where it is but not what's inside). You have to backtrack a bit if you don't recall what's inside, but the manor isn't very large anyway.Congratulations to the whole studio !
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: I was lucky enough to be sent a game key by the team and played this on stream. It was an incredibly refreshing break from some of the content I had locked myself into and my community and I adored it to bits! Though we did have some feedback.To start, the game is BEAUTIFUL! The puzzles are challenging and dear god the amount of times I'd discover a new part of Arabella's home and just wish I was that rich lmao. I don't know what it would take to implement this game into VR, but I think the beautiful design is definitely worth that effort. Can you imagine growing the Fool's Emerald and experiencing that animation in VR? My god. There are two puzzles that stand out above the rest. The wind tower and the library door. Despite my best efforts on stream and my community trying to figure out those puzzles with me, we did sadly have to break immersion and look it up after exhausting all of our ideas to solve the puzzles. I hope that for at least the library puzzle, they go back and add annotations from Arabella or something of the sort to make it a bit more obvious what you're searching for in the books. The answers are italicized, but with so many varying fonts and styles, it's easy to miss the significance when you're desensitized to all the varying extravagant fonts. Other than that, the puzzles are the perfect amount of fun and challenging! The music was delightful and I wish there had been more of it throughout the entirety of the game. This may be more of a streamer issue than a standard player issue, but I'd have to play my own music to accompany the long stretches of silence and music would only play juuuuust long enough that I had to pause my own music to experience it, only for the game music to fade away almost immediately after. Overall, I give this beautiful gem of a game a 9/10! It's a lovely experience from start to finish with a fun and exciting blend of fantasy and reality. Fun puzzles, beautiful world, and a story that genuinely got me a bit emotional at the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: is a charming game for any aspiring horticulturist. If you like puzzles, plants, and old Victorian mansions, then there is no better game for you! Follow Annabella Greene as she returns to her manor, documenting the strange flora that grows in her family home in hopes of publishing it and being accepted into the then male-dominated botanist society. There are several beautiful things about the game, the first being the manor itself. I thoroughly enjoyed exploring the old house, and seeing how expansive it was! The lore tidbits here and there about Annabella's life really add to the world, handwritten notes from friends and family that make the story feel whole. And the puzzles were very fun to explore! The game is a good length, 12 flowers taking about 4 hours in total, and a pleasing experience all throughout. My only criticism would be that I found some of the puzzles to be overly simple. The first few were straightforward in a way that I didn't find enjoyable, mostly staying for the art and the atmosphere. My tune quickly changed when faced against the Priest Hole, which took me an embarrassing amount of time to complete. Chapters 3 and 4 were the highlight of the game, and I so wish there were more Forgotten Flora to unearth. I recommend this game as a short and sweet story for any puzzle fans, and especially for plant lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Botany Manor - A Tranquil Horticultural Mystery"Botany Manor" offered a delightful experience immersed in botanical puzzles and historical intrigue. Here's my unique take, influenced by fellow players' insights: Despite its brevity, exploring Botany Manor was a tranquil journey filled with engaging puzzles and charming narratives. Reminiscent of "Strange Horticulture," the absence of horror elements allowed for a more serene gameplay experience. The puzzles, while not overly challenging, provided a satisfying blend of deduction and exploration. Every clue served a purpose, leading to a cohesive and enjoyable gameplay flow. However, a convenient feature to review collected clues in one place would enhance the overall experience. The game's aesthetics, from its beautiful graphics to the cozy English manor setting, created an immersive environment. Coupled with soothing music and authentic sound effects, it fostered a sense of tranquility throughout the experience. Lady Arabella's tale, woven through letters and snippets found within the manor, evoked a range of emotions and added depth to the gameplay. While simple, the storyline contributed to the overall charm of the game. Some players noted the absence of a map indicator, which could enhance navigation within the expansive manor. Additionally, while the game's price may seem steep for its duration, the quality of the experience and the emotional investment in Lady Arabella's story make it a worthwhile journey. "Botany Manor" offers a cozy and relaxed gaming experience, perfect for fans of mystery and gardening alike. While its brevity may leave players longing for more, its tranquil atmosphere, engaging puzzles, and captivating storytelling make it a memorable journey through the halls of a historic English estate.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved Botany Manor, and with taking it semi slowly I was able to get to the end in just under 6 hours. _childDocuments_.review: A delightful little puzzle romp. Very linear, but enchanting. The audio cues are evocative and keep you in a cozy puzzle mindset. Nothing overly difficult, and able to be beat rather quickly, but with lots of little details to add to this story experience. IMO great for STEM teens (especially young women!) as we remember that women have fought for their place at the table. Uses scientific facts and natural processes to encourage fantastical flowers to bloom, without trying to confuse you, or lead you astray. Highly recommend! I'd definitely be hoping for some DLC so I could revisit this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy, laid-back puzzle experience with flowers is just what I needed. The solution to making each flower bloom by spotting clues in the context of papers, books, posters, paintings, and real life settings is really engaging and I enjoy that each flower has such a unique set of requirements! I also enjoyed that those same clues tell a story about Arabella and her passion for botany, as well as the barriers to pursuing botany she encountered in a male-dominated field (at the time).My main critiques are minor. When putting clues in the Herbarium, I would like to be able to review the text of the clues IN the book. A few times I had to scrabble around hunting down a clue I'd already found because I forgot what it said, which was a tad inefficient. Aside from that, I do think the misogyny conveyed in some of the letters and passages was a BIT too on the nose and blatant. It felt a little too "elbowing you in the side, didja get it?" in nature - could have been a little more show, less tell. But those are VERY minor gripes. Overall I think this is a pleasant puzzle experience and I thoroughly enjoyed myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: Cosy game with no timed elements, really well-balanced puzzles that require some thought (but ALWAYS make logical sense), and actually achievable achievements that don't resort to cheap goals like "press X five hundred times". The rush of endorphins when you figure out the conditions a plant needs to grow is massively addictive.There's a very light story (revealed through completely optional 'flavour' text) which highlights the struggles women faced to be taken seriously in academia in the 19th century, but for the most part it's just exploring a gorgeous Victorian mansion and figuring out how to grow extremely varied and unique plants. Best game I've played all year, and can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Botany Manor

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a game like this for years, a game where I play as a main character, discover their story through clues, discover new plants and solve puzzles. I can take my time while admiring my surroundings and the penny drops or the light bulb goes off.The art style, environment design/sound design and puzzle design are some of the best I've experienced in a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a sweet, short puzzle game on the light to medium side of difficulty depending on if you're just aiming to complete the story or if you're going for 100% achievements. The narrative or plot is mostly up for you to discover on your own by thoroughly exploring and reading various letters and finding souvenirs, mementos, art, etc. You will do a decent amount of running around and retracing steps (you're speedy, however) and I recommend keeping a scrap of paper to take notes or, even better, take screenshots of things you see for use in later puzzles. My stats say I spent almost 4 hours playing but I had to restart the game from the beginning a couple of times due to achievements not being triggered for some reason (steam issue, not game issue). I also stopped several times and left the game running so all told I beat the game in approx 2.5 hours. Is it a little pricey at $22 for 2-3 hours of actual game play? Maybe? Not really. I tend to compare the cost to what I would spend at a movie being entertained for a couple of hours and I feel good about spending my money on this. It was clever and hard enough to make me scratch my head a couple times without making me feel frustrated at any point.

_childDocuments_.review: I have had this game on my wishlist for what felt like forever (in the best way possible), I was really hooked from the beginning and I'm so so happy it's out! _childDocuments_.review: If you're someone who wants to breeze through games without reading, this isn't the game for you. At just over four hours to complete the game and all achievements, I will admit the gameplay felt short for the price; however, this game was clearly a labor of love. _childDocuments_.review:
Botany Manor is an exploration-puzzle game where you play as a retired botanist called Arabella Greene.

Explore a complete historical English manor and its grounds. There are many rooms and gardens to discover, all set inside a beautiful countryside surrounding.

detailed_description: Huge cast with over 70 girls! Add the main heroines, angels, and all the students/faculty at the academy together, and you get a huge cast of over 70 characters! In addition to the students and faculty, you may even cross paths with some ladies who are pretty rare sightings! Let those Pheromone Shots fly to stop the hoards from girls trying to confess their love to you, and you just might be in for a happy ending with your one true love! Aim for the ecstasy shot! Every girl has a weak spot where Pheromone Shots are extra effective! You know you found it when you see things like 「ハッ」 and 「キュン」 appear! Steady your aim and land a shot there, and that'll trigger an Ecstacy Shot, which gives a girl euphoria in just one shot! Enjoy the satisfaction of Doki Doki Mode! Once you meet certain conditions, you can really concentrate and marvel at (shoot) a girl from a bunch of different angles in Doki Doki Mode! Fill that girl's Doki Doki Gauge within the time limit, and not only will you give her euphoria, but you'll also be rewarded for your...efforts! An absolute wealth of panty design! True aesthetics in those hidden areas is what Gal*Gun is all about! A grand total of 423 types of panties are waiting to be discovered! There may even be more to come?! Fall in love with the girl of your dreams in Story Mode, show off your sharpshooting skills in Score Attack Mode, live out your fantasy of a multi-person Doki Doki Mode with Doki Doki Carnival, and a whole lot more! Fully voiced dialogue! Every single one of the 70+ girls in the game is fully voiced by a wonderful group of voice actresses! Enjoy every minute of this amazing cast's performance! Brand new CGs have been added for each heroine's introduction, and in a bunch of instances throughout the story as well! Complete Gallery Mode! The game is very cute and dialogues are very funny. However that is all.While GG Double Peace makes sure that you can hit girl's sensitive spots at any give moment, in this game you will find them often blocked and unreachable.In GG Double Peace during shooting sequences you can pick up student's books, look for ghosts or shoot happy blobs or do tasks for girls. This game doesnt have any of that.Geting True ending in this game requires you to micromanage your stats to precise values, which either requires lot of preparation, looking up what stats girls changes during doki doki mode and then chose them during action sequences and doki doki s*it out of them. Or you can set your stats correctly during intro questions and then don't do any doki doki mode for rest of the game .... both options are less then ideal. As a reward for getting true end you will get little bonus cinematic that is same for every girl, but otherwise the route is exactly same ..... that was very dissapointing.This is remaster of PS3 game but I was expecting they would also remaster the graphics but it is dissapointingly bad for game released in 2021.Only thing GG Returns does better then GG Double Peace is engine. GGR actually  have graphic options, it lets you set resolution and stuff and it didn't crash at all for me.Despite all the complains, this game is still fun to play and this would be positive review if they didn't ask 50€ for it.If this game was like 15€ I would be happy with it but 50€ for PS3 game that is vastly inferior to it's sequel that is much cheaper is pure ripoff.If you didn't play any Gal*Gun game then I can recommend Gal*Gun Double Peace, it is masterpiece of comedy and very fun on-rails shooter.If you played GGDP and want to try this then only buy it in sale, it is not worth it's asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's a fun, charming game that made me smile and laugh quite a few times, just like the other games in the series. In my opinion, it really shows why these kinds of games do have a place in the industry, and why so many of us are upset with what some console platform holders are doing to them.The release of this game was a bit more hyped for many fans of this niche sub-genre than many other games. In a world where cartoon characters wearing bikinis are forced to be censored, but photo-realistic characters can raw dog it with impunity, Inti Creates and PQube's refusal to release this game in a more (details on what "more" means later) censored state had many of us cheering them on. I personally purchased the game twice to support them; once as the Limited Edition Switch version for the physical copy, and again on here digitally. Was the final product worth that show of support? Let's find out.If you've never played any of the other games in this series, Gal*Gun is an on-rails shooter. Think House of the Dead, but instead of zombies and biological freaks of nature, you're fending off hordes of love-struck schoolgirls (and teachers) in the pursuit of your one true love. The games heavily pride themselves in their gratuitous helpings of fanservice. Just as with the other games in the series, this is a surprisingly solid arcade style on-rails shooter, if a bit on the easy side. Being a remaster of the first game in the series, what you're getting will be closer to Gal*Gun Double Peace than 2. The GGDP style of Doki Doki mode is back, for better or worse, and the clothes-vac of 2 is nowhere to be found. The game is significantly more strict about nailing Ecstasy Shots, shots on the girl's weak points, which are one-shot kills indicated with colored Japanese text that appears when the reticle hovers over parts of their body. In previous games, so long as you actually shot them in the general area (head/chest/waist/legs), you would get credit for the shot no matter what. In this game, you MUST hit them in their weak area specifically, if a limb or something gets in the way of your shot, it will not count, and unlike the other games, you lose your chance for the extra points awarded from an ecstasy shot. This doesn't really make the story mode any harder in most cases, but it does make going for high scores more challenging as it demands more precision.Between each of the rail-shooter stages you're presented with mini games involving one of the four girls you chose as your love interest for the playthrough. These involve unique gameplay mechanics and are much different than the standard rail sections, some being shooting gallery-esque challenges such as shooting down iron balls being launched at you as part of a "training" regimen, or shooting off parts of a cage your girl is being kidnapped in suspended from a flying helicopter. Some are actually very creative as well. Like one where you have to hold a ladder while one of the girls looks for books in the library by keeping the reticle in a highlighted zone. While doing this, you also have to help her find books by firing at flashing books on the shelf, but as you do so you're grip on the ladder will slip, resulting in her falling if you neglect it for too long, so it's a balancing act between hitting as many books as you can, as quickly as you can, and maintaining your grip on the ladder. Another one has you helping your chosen girl come up with lyrics to a song, which involves you having to quickly fill in the blanks in the phrases as she sings by picking the right words out of three options in music notes that bounce around the screen. They're all pretty cute, and the creative ones really made me wonder why they decided to ditch these unique little diversions for the more run of the mill stuff we're given in later games in the series. These mini games really made each of the girls feel more unique than the love interests in future games, and it's a shame they never kept this going. Finally, there's Doki Doki Carnival. The mode, which plays more like a separate campaign, obviously is all about Doki Doki Mode. It's similar to how Doki Doki worked in GGDP in that you're wooing multiple girls, but this mode stands apart from the fact that rather than GGDPs maximum of three girls at once, you now will be juggling up to 7 of them. If you're not a fan of Doki Doki Mode, it's doubtful you'll find much to like here unless you're interested in the plot; this mode is a direct continuation of the main story.Now, a game like this basically requires a discussion on the fanservice. And...it's here, for sure. But it isn't exactly as gratuitous as it is in later games in the series. Let me explain why. See, this game was originally an XBox 360 exclusive (though eventually it did make its way on PS3). Back in 2011 (and still today since they wanted the game to be further censored for an XBOne release) Microsoft wasn't too keen on the fanservice in the game, so to get the game released on the platform, they had to tone it down. You'll notice that there is a bit less fanservice outside camera manipulation in Doki Doki Mode and certain mini games than there is in other games, and while all the DLC outfits (except one that couldn't be included due to licensing) are included in this version, they too are not as risque as those in GGDP and GG2. This isn't them censoring the game, (in fact it's actually less censored as apparently the original 2011 version had to modify the camera angles in Doki Doki so you couldn't look up skirts) it's how the game originally was made. There's still plenty of fanservice to be had, but don't expect to be removing clothes like GG2.The biggest point of contention for GGR is in the graphics. Now, yes, the models and textures aren't as polished as those in GGDP and especially GG2, but do remember that this is a remaster; what you're getting is the original spruced up a bit. In that regard, it does a fine enough job. The focus was clearly on the character models as the environments are significantly less detailed. That does make sense though as the highlight of the game is fanservice and the girls, and again, this was originally a game from 2011 with a likely small budget; compromises were made. However, the sticking points a few people will have are in the frame rate and resolution options. The frame rate comes in two flavors; persistent 30FPS, or 60FPS. However, it's important to note that the 60FPS only applies to Doki Doki and rail segments. Dialogue, mini games, and boss battles are still in 30FPS. While the lower framerate is somewhat noticeable in the mini games and bosses, they're quite a bit slower paced than the rail sections so it doesn't really effect gameplay much. The resolution options however, are going to potentially be a bigger issue for some people. While the game does offer up to 4K, anything above 1080, if I have this correctly (I do not use a 4K display), will actually just stretch or scale 1080 up to your chosen resolution. This isn't anything new in the series as evidently every port of every game in the series did this, but I can understand why people are upset that a game in 2021 is still doing this. Again, I don't have a 4K display to see what the game actually looks like with higher resolutions, so I don't know how badly this hurts the visuals.Overall, to answer my question from the first paragraph, yeah, I think it was worth what I spent to support the devs. It's a fun, charming game that made me smile and laugh quite a few times, just like the other games in the series. In my opinion, it really shows why these kinds of games do have a place in the industry, and why so many of us are upset with what platform holders are doing to them.

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly, I knew nothing about this series coming into it, but there have been four games made for it thus far. Gal*Gun Returns (GGR) is a remake of the first game, which previously had never made it to the USA, coming from Japan. My interest in GGR stemmed partially from its asking price, as $50 is typically reserved for AAA releases. Does what GGR have to offer warrant such a price? I don't think so. In this case, GGR blends its visual novel (VN) elements with an on-rails shooter, giving the game more gameplay and action than many VNs. Instead of shooting at aliens or terrorists though, the protagonist fires at his high school peers, in a way that's thankfully not as horrific as that first sounds. What makes all the difference is his projectile consists of pheromones, which is used to quell the frantic desire of his female classmates. Although its content and focus would be bizarre for most parts of the world, this emphasis is very fitting for Japan, and almost seems normal by that standard.There are three modes of play, and the first is Story Mode, where the protagonist pursues four love interests, trying to confess his interest in her while dealing with mobs of boy-crazy females. Score Attack only lets you play the Story Mode routes you've already completed, progressing through each on-rail shooter section of that route without any story segments, except for the final trial to win over the gal. Doki Doki Carnival is centered around Doki Mode, where you specifically target a girl by zooming in on her and firing on her weak spots. It's a very specific mechanic of the game, and doesn't seem like a worthwhile feature to develop a mode around.There are two main ways to control GGR, using either a controller or keyboard and mouse. For an on-rails shooter, I decided to use the keyboard and mouse, as I found the cursor hard to control comfortably using a controller. For the most part, the mouse is used for aiming and firing at girls, and occasional obstructions, although it does change in various circumstances. The protagonist of GGR is Tenzou, a Japanese high schooler who's never had a girlfriend before. Things look promising for him though, as love is in the air, and cupid has an arrow just for him. Unfortunately, this cupid botches the whole affair, blasting him with a volley of arrows, which makes him a love magnet. There wouldn't be much to complain about if the effects didn't wear off in 24 hours, and the repercussions wouldn't make all women despise him on sight, dooming him to a loveless future.His only hope is to develop a relationship by the end of the day, as a girl who loves him won't fall out of love. Ignoring the strange gameplay, this plays out like an anime storyline, and isn't a bad VN premise. However, the actual writing is pretty horrendous, straining even stereotypical shotgun romance stories.Although the 3D models used in GGR look alright from a technical perspective, it comes across looking like a generic school anime. Since there isn't a distinct style to the art, the round, smooth character models don't stand out. Plus, when I carefully look at their expressions, it makes me think of the LEGO games, as they're not any better than that. A school environment is also rather sterile and bland to base a game around.Much like with the visuals, the music comes across as fairly generic. It does a serviceable job as it seems suitable for the school setting, and there's appropriate songs for the shifting moods. For instance, a slower, sappy track for the ending sequence, and quirky music during the comical moments. I don't think any of it is bad, but it won't stick with you for long. The voice acting from the females might linger for a while, but I don't know that it'd necessarily do so in a good way. It's something I'd turn down for my own purposes, though I don't intend to play the game further.🌟 There's not a ton of on-rail shooters available on Steam, and this does somewhat satisfy that style of gameplay. However, as that's not the most prominent focus of GGR, this alone wouldn't be a sufficient reason to get it.🌟 The ranks have humorous titles.❌ On-rail shooters tend to be very repetitive by design, as the layout is quite rigid: the path taken, how fast the screen scrolls, and where enemies spawn. Incorporating VN mechanics with it, and not making each route unique, worsens this downside further. ❌ Even if you were interested in GGR for its ulterior purposes, I'd think the scenarios presented would make it feel uncomfortable. For instance, crawling underneath cafeteria tables.❌ I didn't notice much difference in difficulty between newbie and seasoned.🔍 You don't have limited ammo or get penalized for missing shots, usually. However, rapid-firing at all times might not be the best approach. Well-aimed shots will matter more at times, such as the relationship-building events in Story Mode.🔍 There are nuances to the mechanics that the game never outlines in normal gameplay, so it's a good idea to check out the manual.When it comes to the perverse aspect of GGR, I think my tolerance for it is higher in contrast to other games because such things are more prolific in Japanese media. That's not to say it isn't a gimmick to appeal to the lowest common denominator, but seeing as how stuff like this shows up in several anime series, it's not surprising to see it in a game. However, I can't say that how things are presented don't come off as creepy. The idea of intentionally scoping out high school girls to peek when their skirts flip up is already sad and desperate enough, but adding over the top voice acting with it makes that much worse. It'd be fair to ask why I took any interest in GGR if that wasn't appealing to me, and it was to see if the gameplay stood up despite this aspect, as well as thinking it'd catch some attention on my YouTube channel.Even if you were interested in GGR, there's no justification for its asking price. Having played through three of the five Story Mode routes, and trying the other modes, I was already getting bored with the repetitiveness of how the game plays, and that was only after ten hours. There are factors that could increase the game's life-span, but only if you care about unlocking everything through repeatedly playing the same modes multiple times. For its asking price, I expect a lot more out of a game. I don't think suggestive content makes up for that difference, so I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to write this review from my personal perspective of a Gal*Gun addict who has 100% completed not only this game, but all of the others available here on Steam (Double Peace, 2, and VR), and pre-ordered the special edition without even thinking about it. Specifically, I will be comparing to Double Peace, for two reasons - first, both this game and Double Peace are true rail shooters, with very similar forced camera movement gameplay, whereas 2 and VR are stationary wave shooters where you have some control over the camera and when you proceed down the track. Perhaps more importantly though, the other reason is that I think Double Peace, as a sequel to the original console release of Gal*Gun (which came out 10 years ago, and of which this game is a remaster), is a more interesting and robust game. So if you haven't already played Double Peace, I suggest you start with it. Don't get me wrong, Gal*Gun Returns is a great game on its own, and I definitely recommend it even to a new player, but Double Peace has more features and is currently cheaper, or essentially the same price for the Deluxe Edition add-on for all the costumes (which is totally worth the extra cost, BTW). So I'm going to assume you've played Double Peace, and base the rest of the review on how Returns differs.As would be expected from a remaster of the first game in the series, Returns is a much more stripped-down (pun only partially intended), pure rail shooter. The gameplay itself is definitely harder - the camera moves faster, there are a lot of "bonus" women who are extremely difficult to hit, the ecstasy shot hitboxes are smaller (and, unfortunately, also less consistent and sometimes slightly misplaced), and you only get one chance to get an ecstasy shot - whereas in Double Peace you can score a non-ecstasy hit on a woman and still get an ecstasy with a subsequent shot, in this game your first hit has to be the ecstasy shot to earn one. Hit her anywhere else, and you lose your chance for the one-hit takedown. This is particularly important with the bonus scoring mechanics found in Score Attack mode. So in terms of pure rail shooter mechanical play, Returns is the better game.But most of the extra features Double Peace adds to that gameplay are missing. There's no shop for purchasing power-ups or stat adjusters, no invisible items to be found by zooming in, no add-on missions or hidden objects to find (aside from the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Kuroda sisters), no Mr. Happiness to boost your score, no Kurona in the story nor her little demons in the gameplay, no knockdown or kissing attempts, no path choices (or at least, not obvious ones - there is at least one stage with an alternate path, needed for one of the aforementioned sneaky sisters), no stage select options within routes. About the only thing this game has that's better is multiple costumes without buying a deluxe edition, and that all the women have unique swimsuits in this game, rather than the generic bikinis for all women that Double Peace's DLC gets you.Well, there is also Doki-Doki Carnival mode, which is a unique game mode found only in the original and Returns, but that's not actually a good thing. I've never really enjoyed doing Doki-Doki, so a game mode that is ONLY that, with no rail shooting at all, is not really a bonus to me. Story-wise, I do prefer Returns. There are four heroines to pursue, and you can pick any of them on your first playthrough (unlike Double Peace which forces you to clear the two main heroine routes before letting you explore others) and I liked three of them (Kaoruko, on the other hand, can go jump off another , without me to save her that time). You can also get the random girlfriend endings at any time, simply by letting a woman get the last hit on you, instead of needing to go through all the efforts of clearing all other routes first. So you're far less railroaded here in terms of who you go after.So while I do say Double Peace is the better game, it is also very close, and both games are definitely worth playing. So I fully recommend both, and keep going back to both for replays, depending on what I'm in the mood for. Great games in a great series. Enjoy!....Also, Saori Fujino best waifu. Had to be said.

_childDocuments_.review: It took ten years, but the original Gal*Gun is now available to fans worldwide. It comes in the form of a remaster and, as someone that plays a ton of these more questionable titles, I had to give it a look.So I’m just gonna be blunt and not sugarcoat things here: I did not enjoy my time with Gal*Gun Returns and it was honestly a struggle to play through. For those that don’t know what the game is, it’s an on-rails shooter kinda similar to House of the Dead. You’re moved around automatically and all you have to do is aim your cursor at girls and left click – that’s it, that’s the extent of the gameplay here. Sure, there are a few extras like weak spots, doki doki mode, and some other mini-games, but the core is some of the most basic fps gameplay you can get.There’s no moving your camera, no abilities outside of your basic left click to shoot, and even when you do get mini-games, they just repeat the same basic “move your cursor and shoot” gameplay, but with a different skin slapped on it. Granted, it is nice to have at least something interrupting the otherwise monotonous gameplay, but there’s no real depth here – not in the core gameplay, not in the mini-games, and not really anywhere in the game at all. Just constant left-clicking of the same two enemy types (which are only different by way of their HP pool) and on the same blocky levels. Even the first House of the Dead game – released all the way back in 1996 – had at least some variety there.It’s not even a difficult game either. I breezed through it on the hardest difficulty and don’t think I ever dropped below 50% HP. Granted, this is in part due to the game being originally designed for controller (and thus, harder to aim), so if you’re taking it on with a mouse and keyboard, don’t expect much of a challenge.As you can imagine, the gameplay I just described grows repetitive FAST, like just 20 minutes fast. In fact, by that point, you’ve already seen most of what the game has to offer – it’s just a matter of repeating that until the end. And it won’t even take that long either, with each route taking about an hour and half to beat and there being four routes for a total of about six hours. Big thing to note with the different routes though is that you’re pretty much playing the same game, but with slightly altered locations and a different character story.The story element is there, but don’t be expecting too much from it. It’s told through some very basic visual novel segments that add just the bare minimum backstory to each character. I mean, this isn’t the type of game you’re playing for the story anyways so I can’t say I expected much there.As for why you would play this game, many would point to the fanservice aspect, but even that is kinda limited here. Unlike Gal*Gun 2, there’s no stripping of the characters and the most you’ll get are some upskirts and a few questionable camera angles. I honestly don’t care for this element, but if you’re the type to base a purchasing decision off of it, well this one might not be the best choice.Normally, in a remaster, you would expect better graphics, additional content, and other technical improvements, but Gal*Gun Returns hardly does that. For one, the fps is capped at 60 and it isn’t even a constant cap. There are several elements still capped to 30, including all the dialogue scenes, the menus, and even gameplay segments like boss fights. It’s really only the core gameplay that is 60.On the resolution front, the game may say it offers support for 1440p and 4k, but those resolutions are just upscaled from 1080p. This is immediately noticeable with the character models because there’s no anti-aliasing and all of the jagged lines are blown up for you to see. In fact, there’s no graphical settings outside of resolution, fps, display mode, and screen brightness, it’s as bare as PC ports come.I will give the port some credit though, the controls were much better than what we had with Gal*Gun 2. I had no issues playing through with mouse and keyboard and the only thing missing there was the ability to navigate menus with the mouse.Gal*Gun Returns is a flawed remaster of a bad game. From its tedious gameplay to its extreme lack of depth, there’s honestly not much to like here – even if you’re interested in just the fanservice aspect. The “remaster” portion of the game is just an outright disappointment, with no proper high-res support and a framerate that constantly jumps between a 60 fps cap and a 30 fps cap. For carrying such a premium price, we should expect better.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: So far (3 hours) so good!So this game is a remaster of the original Gal Gun game which didn't make it into the west back in the day, a game i didn't get to play so i can't do a direct comparison to that game so i will review this based on "being the 1st" entry in the series.First of, this game is pretty fun, there are several stories (or routes) to complete as with the other Gal*Gun titles and the gameplay is a lot more full on, what do i mean "full on?". The game has a lot of rail shooter moments - it feels there is even more game play than before and the visual novel style scenes aren't too long or short making them enjoyable enough to make a story from without it dragging too much either. The shooter moments feature a 4th weak spot unlike other games, this ups the difficulty to take them down which is fun but sadly this weak spot is the knee and below making it hard/ impossible up close to hit. I do enjoy the shooter moments a lot though, the teachers feature buffed hp and tank more shots which is a interesting mechanic. The game has lots of mini games in it which are mostly simple but fun enough to add some extra  content, one thing i missed from GG2 was the mini-games so seeing so many of them here is pretty great.The gallery has a huge amount of items to find, not seen into what these are but with so many to unlock it looks like it could be more extras to unlock. All the original games DLC is included, it's pretty much just costumes but adds more to the fun. I have found thus far the game is pretty fun, it runs smoothly and it's enjoyable, some quality of life features are missing from later games but this is standard as this is the 1st game  in the series so don't expect some of them. I also have enjoyed seeing how the girls have evolved over time, small things but it is fun. The graphics are nice enough, they aren't quite as sleak as Gal*Gun2's graphics but they still look pretty well polished. Also some extra Quality of Life features are present, for me the adding a star icon to a girl you have Doki Doki'd and got their profile is pretty nice, running double peace was tough collecting profiles as there wasn't always ways to know who you was missing without learning them first.I look forward to what the modding communities will produce in time ;)So far, very good game and enjoyable. I will confirm and update the review when fully finished playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This could be considered the first game of the series as this is a re-release to the west and to the PC platform with some improvements, but this doesn't mean that is bad or looks way to old, as it stands pretty good for today's standard and it doesn't require a powerful PC to play.Overall the gameplay could get repetitive because the on-rail shooters doesn't come with a lot of variety to it, but for me the "boss fights" and doki doki carnival helps to give a bit of fresh air but its not very often and its understandable that some people complain for how repetitive is, but personally I enjoyed it very much and is way better than the typical zombie shooter or war kinda theme.The story is decent, but doesn't stand out of how original or immersive it is, but it gives a big plus for the game. The graphics as previously mentioned are not super-detailed or almost realistic, but stands up in a very good way.Compared to the previous games, it does lack certain aspects of Double Peace or Gal*Gun 2, and I think the 3 of them are very good games and I don't have a favorite, but it really is more recommendable to go with either of them first, because the basis of them are way more solid than this one, but if you're up to it, go with this one as an entry to the series.The only aspect that wasn't the best, is the frame lock, to 60fps in gameplay and doki doki mode and 30fps to bosses and dialogues. It would've been awesome if it had 100+ frame unlock, but the difference isn't really that big and doesn't affect gameplay that much, so it won't change that much any aspect of it.Great game overall, no complains at least from me, and big respect to INTI and PQube to refuse to censor it even more for the Xbox release and cancelling it right away, you guys are the best! Hope to see more games like this in the future.

Truth be told, I have fond memories of the opening song, as one of the very first times I made love to a real woman was during a non-so-well-thought-out playthrough. Those were carefree days of lazyness and lack of responsibility. Lovable moments of total void, filled with the simple joys of life. Time went by slowly, youth was in full bloom. What a great time to be alive and experience this little gem. I often joke about loving relationships and how those affect the mind more than the human heart. Because the heart can lie better than the mind can. The heart has no limits, knows no bounds, and sometimes it even defies its own previous statements to give itself more time basking in that sweet pleasure that is a healthy - or not - relationship. The mind however, has constant constraints, either imposed by society or by ourselves. Mistakes are inevitable when dealing with a loving relationship, no matter if opposite sex is involved or not, we are not prepared to enter adulthood until the door leading there shuts before us and hits us in the head. _childDocuments_.review: Gal*Gun is just lighthearted fun.Mechanically, as an on-rails shooter, it's entertaining enough with the kind of depth you would expect -- standard 'enemies' with different weak points, varied patterns that reward both reaction time and accuracy, and a Story Mode that's neither too short nor too long.  There are a lot of fairly obtuse achievements to get and modes to play, which should give the game some longevity.Oh, right, and your 'shooting' of 'enemies' is making schoolgirls faint from ecstasy before they can confess to you.The game probably gets a lot of flak for that, especially the "Doki Doki Mode", a minigame (and screen-clear bomb) the player can trigger that features zooming in on a girl, who reacts as being stared at or touched by the shots used in that mode.  If is kind of sketchy; this isn't the kind of game you want someone glancing at you playing without any sort of introduction and it certainly does exist for a degree of fanservice.But, despite that, the game really feels just... goofy.  It doesn't take itself seriously, and while offense is always going to be personal, for my mileage that really defuses any that might have been given.  It's bright, it's colorful, the easy mode is easy enough for a Level 1 Shooting Game Idiot like me to just sit down and play and even feel like I'm doing well with.  It's the kind of game where, if I've had a bad day, I could just turn my brain off a little and make my day a little better by smiling at the pretty colors as the pretty anime girls vanish into flowers.  And that has a very real value.  A guilty pleasure?  Perhaps, but pleasant all the same.

detailed_description: Steam Deck Compatibility Valve’s testing indicates this title is Verified on Steam Deck. This game is fully functional on Steam Deck, and works great with the built-in controls and display. About the Game Plunge into the depths of STASIS: BONE TOTEM, the latest installment in the STASIS anthology. A new story, new characters, and a new underwater environment to explore. Follow Mac and Charlie, a husband and wife duo, who make their living scouring the ocean for salvage. But, when they stumble upon an abandoned oil rig in the Pacific Ocean, they uncover a horrific secret that Cayne Corporation will do anything to keep hidden. As you embark on your adventure playing Mac, Charlie, and their trusty Super-Toy, Moses, you'll encounter an immersive narrative filled with spine-tingling horror and unexpected twists. Combining the thrilling storytelling of STASIS and a tense underwater setting, STASIS: BONE TOTEM offers a personal story that will test the limits of family resilience. Navigate through a massive underwater base, complete intricate puzzles, and solve an ancient secret concealed at the bottom of the ocean. BONE TOTEM features the same isometric, point-and-click gameplay that made STASIS a classic fan favorite, but with a new cast and a unique setting that will leave you gasping for breath. With stunning visuals, a music score by Mark Morgan, a screenplay written by a Hollywood ace, voice acting by veteran actors, and a gripping storyline that will keep you on the edge of your seat - STASIS: BONE TOTEM is a must-play game for horror and sci-fi adventure fans. So what are you waiting for? Dive into the unknown and uncover the BONE TOTEM beneath the waves.
