_childDocuments_.review: a fantastic adventure game. I loved the first stasis and this is a continuation of form in that universe. It's well crafted, with good characters, good sound and art design. The story itself is also great, there's enough twists and turns to keep you entertained and everything keeps moving at a good pace, till the end where it accelerates rapidly to the conclusion. Both the art and writing are great (though some of the descriptions are a bit excessive, it's nice to have them, it feels like an old-school point-and-click)There's a neat difference between the characters you can jump through, sometimes you have to use the ability of a different character to solve a puzzle (only one can combine items, another can break things apart) which is a neat addition, since you get an incentive to read item descriptions across characters (each one has something different written about - i believe - every item in the game, there's a lot of writing in this!! in a good way!)Some puzzles are a little tough (though with some of them it was me being obtuse) - however there are hints that can pop up, as well as an official guide, both on steam (less good but gives you tips) and a nicely illustrated PDF one from their website. so if you get stuck and just want to continue the story you still can.I believe there's some AI-generated art in the faces of NPCs in PDA logs but they aren't a deal-breaker. Buy this, buy Stasis, play them both, PLEASE, you're doing yourself a service.

_childDocuments_.review: was completely invested during my play through. the story is fantastic along with the voice acting being very well done, it never brought me out of the game. i loved reading through any PDA i came across and many did not disappoint, every character had their own small story and had details that arent discussed in the main stories. i loved seeing something i read about, pointing at something and saying OH GOD that's the thing i heard about! the game has a some quality of life mechanics that smooth over some of the problems with the genre, one right click shows all of the interactions so there will be 0 pixel hunting, i got through only needing to look up a guide once. bone totem has now become one of my favorite adventure games of all time, highly recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished playing Bone Totem, and WOW!Extremely impressive, especially for an indie game. I thought they did not make games like this anymore. Nowadays almost every new survival horror AAA title has this 'junk food' vibe about it - cliché, vapid, forgettable, tons of unnecessary copy-pasted enemy mobs. This game is definitely different.To start off, various underwater environments are a work of art, unique, detailed, and believable. The somewhat simplistic isometric style just adds to it, making the game feel a little bit retro. The lighting and water effects really translated the atmosphere of the game: dark, gritty, unfriendly depths of the ocean, hiding ancient secrets. It was enhanced by superb sound design as well.The setup itself is pretty unusual, as the story takes place deep underwater, which really emphasizes the 'survival' element. Everything in the surroundings is a threat to the main characters, and sometimes they just barely manage to escape death, in order to go even deeper and uncover the true purpose of their visit to the facility. The game does a great job of keeping it mysterious for quite a while, and there is always something happening story-wise, so you never feel bored. There are a few nice plot twists as well. The story is rich and is building itself up in the form of numerous PDA's scattered around the locations containing journal entries of various characters inhabiting Cayne Universe. The puzzles are interesting and not too obvious, complex enough to make you think, but not to the point of being annoying. Each one of the main characters has a distinct personality and feels like a real person (yes, even the robot bear Moses). You will have to constantly switch between all three in order to progress, as they all possess different skills that you will need. Don't worry though, there will be no unnecessary backtracking to retrieve the items from each other, as this is solved through their shared inventory.I would describe this game as a hydropunk Event Horizon, with a sprinkle of Sanitarium, in all the best ways possible.If you care about deep storytelling, sci-fi world-building and relatable characters, instead of braindead monster shooting, you will not be disappointed.I cannot wait what THE BROTHERHOOD comes up with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is a great point and click adventure game. The story and art direction are phenomenal, and Mark Morgan really did a great job with the soundtrack (that credit alone was a big part of why I decided to buy this game).Problem-solvers, rejoice! The puzzles can be tough. The shared inventory system between the characters you control (and them moving independently from one another) can add a pretty thick layer of complexity to finding solutions. Screenshots are your friend. If you find it too frustrating to solve this game without help, let yourself use a walkthrough. It's worth experiencing Stasis: Bone Totem's tale all the way through regardless of how you choose to do it.I'm glad this game popped up on my Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a fan of Stasis, so when I saw there was a sequel I jumped right on it. This game inverts its forerunner, going from the vacuum of space to the intense pressure of the deep sea. The player controls three characters as they explore an increasingly macabre set of environments. Two of the characters have special interactions with the items, and all three have different descriptions of them which can aid in solving puzzles. I thought the puzzles in general were fine, but I didn't hesitate to look at a guide if I felt like something was going to be a pain. Since items can only be picked up and used in specific nodes in each room, it's easy to see if you've overlooked an item or what the current obstacles are. I like the corpo-horror world that the developers created across their games, and that's present here as well. My biggest complain is probably that the story elements across the environment, items, narrative and logs don't always line up in a coherent way. It's not bad enough to detract from the experience unless you were trying to get invested. A strong recommendation for people looking for a horror adventure game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is a masterpiece of sci-fi horror.The core plot of Bone Totem involves a trio of adventures, Mack, Charlie and robotic bear Moses arriving at a seemingly abandoned floating facility only to uncover a dark secret lurking below with true horror to experience. The characters and their interactions are the driving force here because the story and voice acting behind it are simply astounding. I don't want to spoil too much but this is one of the best stories I have ever experienced in a game, it's that good. The gameplay loop here surrounds traditional point and click adventures, you must utilise the three characters and their unique skills to explore the nightmare environment with most puzzles being logical but somewhat challenging. The game takes place with a isometric viewpoint showing the gorgeously disturbing environments with animated 3D cut-scenes in between (which are amazing). Visually the environments are gorgeous, the cut scenes while creepy are fantastic and the voice acting and audio in general just oozes quality and amazing production value for an indie title. The game is breathtaking. While there maybe isn't too much repeatability here the main game is chunky clocking in 8-12 hours, amazing value for the price. Stasis Bone Totem is a masterpiece of sci fi body horror the likes of which are so rare to see. Great puzzles, an amazing cast and literally some of the strongest storytelling I have ever seen make this a masterpiece work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first Stasis and was happy to find out that the second entry is an improvement pretty much in every aspect.First of all I just love the environment design and the atmosphere generally. It has this terrifying but beautiful Giger-esque art style that just resonates with me.I also found the story to be more intriguing and suspenseful this time. Usually I am not big fan of reading text logs in games but this is one of the exceptions as the writing is strong enough and it has that puzzle aspect of trying to understand and piece together whatever happened here in this underwater hellhole. It does lose some steam at the end as some of the dialogue drags on and you cannot move between areas when people are talking which slows things too much for my liking. On the gameplay side I think it found this nice balance between puzzles being challenging but understandable that make sense in the context of the world. I was little worried as you can control three characters that this could turn out the be just an item hunt and trying everything everywhere but this was luckily never a problem for me as interactable sections are marked as blue and visual detail that cannot be interacted are marked as green which makes clear what is an puzzle and what is not.And yes Moses, you're a very smart bear.

_childDocuments_.review: STASIS: BONE TOTEM is a really interesting point-and-click game set in the futuristic, post-apocalyptic setting of the CAYNE universe. It's incredibly atmospheric, well-written, and features beautifully intricate sets, arts and environments that will have you glued to the screen until the end, if you appreciate what it offers as much as I did anyway.What really sets this game apart from a couple other contemporary games of its genre is that it's really refined a lot of frustrating aspects about the genre. There are very clear indicators for what you can interact with, and what you can simply investigate to read flavour, the latter for which you merely need to hover your cursor over. Furthermore, any and all puzzles within all acts always wrap up by the end of it, meaning that with the exception of a handful of items, 90% or so of items are found and used within the same chapter, meaning you you won't get too bogged down by having to lug around several items for several chapters and won't ever know what it'll be used for.For the most part, puzzles are pretty sane and sensible, as always there's a few handful of puzzles I got stuck on where the logic was perhaps a bit too much of a leap, and because of its futuristic setting and sci-fi elements, some key parts seem cryptic in its function because, well, you're not an inhabitant of the world so you weren't really aware what you were looking at. There were a few puzzles that I didn't like, and I generally dislike anything to do with numbers, but the game has a generous hint system and if you truly get stuck, there are walkthroughs out there.But it's not the puzzles that should draw you in, rather, the setting and incredible lore that's jam-packed into this experience. Without delving into the actual plot, the game has phenomenal build-up over the course of the story, with several key elements that seem bizarre but then somehow make sense within the pseudo-science of the universe. The game is confident in its own narrative to the point where it boldly presents plots in your face that you won't even understand the ramifications of from just this game alone, and there are very big narrative strands to other games within its universe, but these aren't necessary to understand the actual plot of the game.The characters took a bit to grow on me, but there's a goofy charm to their interactions, and I think that's important because they talk a lot, as one would expect from this sort of game. The only complaint I have is that at points the dialogue was a bit too much, and a good 20% of the dialogue consists of various grunts noises as characters are shimmying, crawling or otherwise traversing, and this alone wouldn't be so bad if it didn't stop you from interacting with puzzles while the dialogue box is open. But again, this is nitpicky to the max, and these things can be skipped.Of note, if it wasn't apparent in the game's aesthetic, this game is gruesome and gore-y. I'm usually not a fan of this sort of thing, but it's done rather tastefully here and is used pretty sparingly, and it tries to use it only in moments when it wants you to feel unsettled. There are a few key puzzles that very made me a bit uncomfortable, though I can't help but think this was done on purpose and it helps you stay immersed in the game. And immersion is something the game truly excels at.There's really not much else about the game I can say without spoiling anything, I can safely state that it was really, really good and ranks probably among the top 10 best point-and-click games I've played to date. The game is well worth the price tag, but I myself grabbed it when it was on sale. Highly recommended to veteran or newcomer alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. _childDocuments_.review: Stasis Bone Totem is perfect for horror atmosphere enthusiasts, similar to Dead Space or The Callisto Protocol. While it remains a point-and-click game, the emotions it evokes are comparable. Unfortunately, some significant drawbacks make the game a bit frustrating, but it's still worth considering.- Exceptional and atmospheric environmental design- Intriguing storyline- Creepy and unsettling audio- Challenging puzzles- Well-characterized characters and outstanding voice acting- High-quality cutscenes- Innovative inventory system and unique character features- Excellent environmental awareness: the game highlights all the elements you can interact withMost issues come from a poor user experience:- Navigating quickly requires constant mouse clicks, contrary to the conventional double-click method in similar genre games for setting waypoints.- Too much reading: hyper extensive and irrelevant documents are common, there are simply too much of them to read, contributing only marginally to the plot, slowing the gameplay and breaking the atmosphere.- Some puzzles can only be solved after specific actions by other characters, without clear indication or prevention; this led me to spend a couple of hours trying to solve them, without having the right knowledge or tools to do that. I didn't want to solve it with the game help  so I had to rely on a walkthrough.- Joystick support is erratic and imprecise; certain key presses may not register the input consistently.- As with all point-and-click games, some item combinations with puzzles are entirely absurd, necessitating random trial and error.Personal observations:- The item exchange system in the inventory seems somewhat unrealistic; how one can rationally and posibbly pass an item to a companion who is in entirely different and distant location?- One character is intended to be a teddy bear, but its face looks anything but bear-like. Considering the price, mechanics, and the gameplay time, Stasis Bone Totem is definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:I don’t know how to put this into words. I’ve never written a Steam review before, but this game absolutely blew my mind, so I had to say something. Moses was the first stroke of brilliance that got me hooked. The contrast between his innocence and the dire circumstances the characters find themselves in, with Charlie’s words of encouragement for him whenever he shows fear and Mac’s initial distrust, really breathe life into this world, much more than the larger elements of the plot. There next unique character, Faran, really cemented it for me. I can’t say much without spoiling it for everyone though, so you’ll have to find out for yourself. I also wouldn’t call this a horror game. It won’t give you nightmares the way watching a movie like Hereditary will. Yes, it’s gory and violent, and there’s an engaging Lovecraft like plot to uncover, but it’s really the dynamic between the main characters, their conflicts, how they support each and how they evolve that make this game stand out. This is why I love adventure games.Cons:If I were to point out any negatives it would be the mechanism the characters use to exchange items. The game does provide an explanation, and I understand how it makes the gameplay mechanics more fluid, letting you focus on the story and puzzle solving instead of an alternative mindless running back and forth, but it did break my immersion just a tiny bit.Another one is the rather overt manner they present the morals of the corporation behind the main plot. I understand they’re trying to present an oppressive cyberpunk like future where corporations control every aspect of a person’s life, but I think it could have been handled in a more subtle manner so as to make them seem more human, and less cartoonishly evil. I think you can make the impact of flawed morals more impactful when corporate types at least look like they’re trying to do the right thing, and are more reserved and diplomatic in their interactions with employees. I’m a little taken out of the experience when I see executive types using the words “indentured servitude” and straight up admitting to sending people’s families to hard labour camps to pay their debts in a casual email.Summary:Regardless, this game makes up for its flaws in so many other ways that I mostly forgot about them. The rest of the story delves into so much more that is so well crafted, I couldn’t stop playing until I finished it, and I wasn’t disappointed. I was deeply moved, all the way to the end.

_childDocuments_.review: What is Statis Bone Totem? It is an adventure, horror/science fiction game where you control your characters from above (isometric view like in cRPGs). Gameplay consists of listening to dialogues, solving riddles and exploring enigmatic base deeper and deeper to unravel its dark secret.I must say I was very surprised (in a positive way) with this game. For starters I do not like games filled with puzzles and riddles so I was quite sceptic. Static Bone token game-play is like 30% walking 40% solving riddles and 30% listening. There is no combat or sneaking in the game. You cannot control what your characters say and are unable to make any choices. However the story got me really hooked on and it right up my alley. The story is very interesting. Enigmatic with lots of unknowns that are being revealed while you play. There are twists of the story and images where your jaw drops and you are left speechless or surprised with how things turned out. The setting and the lore are suprisingly good and well written. There are lots of diaries to read and trivia about the world (which is a vision of future on the earth in a hundred years or so) The riddles themselves are a mixed bag. I personally dislike the HUD idea (shared storage idea where characters being apart can teleport items between each other without hassle) but I get this game could not work without it so I can turn my blind eye. Some riddles are intuitive, some puzzles are well thought overs but some do not make much sense and without online help you would be stuck quite a few times. I only used only help when I got stuck and I really limited it to absolute minimum. Sadly I do not have time to sit in front of my Steam Deck thinking what to do next and walking circles helplessly with the characters. Especially that riddles and puzzles where part of the game which I for the most part did not enjoy that much.The game is a strong 7.5/10 for me. It is like a good sci fi horror film. But it could have been so much better. If they added guns, turned based combat (not too much maybe occasionally later in the game) and enemies to the game it would be super cool. Plus if you would be given more to say in the plot and what your characters say ( with possibly different endings) it would be awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game. If you liked the previous Brotherhood's games, this is their best game so far, The voice acting of the characters feels so real, the story telling and the conversations are so interesting to hear. The hint system is an excellent idea, avoiding people to get stuck (I had so many issues on Beautiful desolation because I was forgetting some items), and in Bone totem you don't have to worry about this because all the clickable items are marked up. Concerning the sound, it goes so well with the ambience, and as I told before, the voice acting from all the characters is so nice, it really feels like a movie. (But I have to say that a I liked most the voice and the aspect of the bear in the demo)The puzzles are ok, most of them can be easily completed just following a little bit of logic, or must of the time there's hints in the same or surrounding rooms. Concerning the graphics/art, I think it the worst part, no because of the art itself, but because the game is too dark, even with the brightness at maximun, I feel like I'm missing a lot of cool art. An any case, this an amazing game, and if you like point and click games, and adult ambiance, there's nothing to wait for, buy it! Thank you brotherhood games.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Entertaining indie horror point and click with a heavy focus on story. The story itself was for me interesting and while many things seem like they are going in a very obvious direction from the start it still managed to add futher to what is going on deep below the see to keep whats happening interesting. The story and graphics feature heavy use of gore so beware if you cant deal with that stuif.The voice acting in the game is pretty good considering its a smaler indie title and even had some characters which I would honestly say were pretty great. Although sometimes I would have prefered a bit less "breathing noise" from simulated close mics that was not really such a big deal.Regarding the gameplay its mostly straightfoward since you can highlight all interactble objects .... until it isnt. As with any Point and click there is the issue of getting stuck sometimes and in this game it is most often the case because you missed something which in most cases is hidden with an object you have ineracted with before and considered to be finished. Most of my time getting stuck was when I was required to go back to a previous "thing" that had changed in the meantime without any good indication. These moments can be frustrating but I personaly resorted to the steam walktrhough after a certain amount of time so that I could continue the story and not get further frustrated.The PDA entries in the game are a bit of a mixed bag too there is interesting info in there but it is burried between a lot of entries that are just not very interesting. After the first couple ones I mostly scanned them only to see if there is anything interesting although I think they got better again towards the latter 1/3 of the game.Overall I bought this game because I saw Mandalores review of the previous title in which he teased this game and I would recommend the game to anybody who likes a good sci/fi horror story and can deal with some hiccups in the puzzle design or has no problem to use a guide in the few instances it comes up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent.  The graphics are greatly improved over the first one, while maintaining the visual style.  Much more detailed models, animations, everything.  The gameplay has also received some changes that make completing the game more possible, and the developer actually outright includes a walk through (which I had to consult a few times when I misunderstood a clue or needed to walk into a specific spot to trigger dialogue to progress).  There are a myriad of ways this game encourages and indirectly helps you complete the game.  There are 3 different controllable characters, which all have different notes about the various inventory items you can use throughout the game, hinting at their potential uses.  There is a button you can press to show interactive objects, which are the only places where you are required to use items.  There is a hint button, where the characters can then make a comment on the puzzle they would realistically know to further nudge the player in the right direction.  All of this makes this game much more fun to puzzle out then the previous one, where you had to do some pixel hunting to find all the items.I will say however, it does rely a bit too much (imo) on simply having the answers to a puzzle located in a somewhat obscure spot that only a different character can access.  Meaning, it is less puzzling and logic, and simply needing to be extra thorough when searching areas.  I got stuck because there is a clue given when looking at a certain computer screen when important dialogue is playing (meaning I'm looking at the character portrais), and when you revisit it, it appears blank... unless you wait about 5 seconds, and it resets when you back exit the screen.  That was a cruel trick!The logic overall makes sense as well, though as mentioned before, there were some places where I didn't completely understand the clue.  Having completed the game, I say give it 10-15 minutes if you ever feel stuck before consulting the walkthrough.  Sometimes the puzzles are deceptively simple!The writing in this game is also wonderful.  The dialogue feels extremely natural between all the characters, and I very much enjoyed every single one of them.  The descriptions of the disgusting and visceral scenes help further create a dark, disturbing atmosphere that at the same time doesn't abandon an emotional core.  I actually teared up at a couple sections of this game, which I have to say I wasn't expecting at all considering the sheer amount of disgusting scenes!The voice acting is much improved over the first game as well, which had varying quality depending on the character.  Here, everyone gives a great performance suitable to the material, which only further improves the emotional storytelling.  The music is also effective at contributing to the atmosphere, although I will say I cannot rightly recall any "setpiece" tracks which isn't to say the music isn't good, just that it blends into the background more than the last game, which had some tracks clash a bit with the scene, but you surely remembered!Overall, I recommend this game to people who enjoy adventure games, enjoyed Stasis, love horror stories, or are a bit of a gorehound!  The games are mostly separated as well, so you can safely play this one first as well, as long as you don't mind the jump back in fidelity.

_childDocuments_.review: From my full review: I’m mainly a console gamer these days, but there are a few studios and games that make me dust off and fire up ol’ reliable the moment they become available.The original Stasis was clearly a love letter to a childhood filled with sci-fi, horror, and sci-fi horror—with an all-new setting and story set in space that had its dimly lit corridors filled with the echoes of the games, books, and movies that inspired it. It was dark and tense, violent, and had all the traits of point-and-click adventures that I miss from the old days of PC gaming. While the old-school feel was charming, it could also feel a little clunky and dated.About halfway into Stasis Bone Totem, I’m happy to report that a move to full 3D graphics, improved cinematics, and some much-needed updates to interface and game design have gone a long way.Stasis Bone Totem is an isometric sci-fi horror point-and-click adventure that tells a personal tale of salvagers, a husband named Mac and his wife Charlie, who come across what looks like an oil rig, only to discover that they are trapped. Together with Moses, a ridiculously creepy toy bear retrofitted with some advanced functions, and a small gizmo that lets them share items via a pocket dimension, they unravel an ancient and sinister mystery—while also struggling with the pain of having lost their daughter.Stasis Bone Totem is about exploring an underwater lab and the environments it’s connected to, as well as reading and solving puzzles to progress through the story.The three characters spend most of their time split, with you needing to jump between them GTA V style. As mentioned before, they share items. However, Mac can use his strength to bend and break things, while Charlie can repair or combine items.The bear’s job is to be creepy (it can also hack certain devices and do most normal things).Creepy-ass creepy bear.This makes for an interesting system where you are constantly trying to figure out what might work with what or where—and I also liked that each character’s descriptions of items are different based on their outlook or knowledge. Stasis Bone Totem is chock full of puzzle scenarios that need to be solved, and make no mistake… some can get quite tough. Just like in the ’90s, you might find yourself backtracking or clicking on all the items as you scratch your head to figure out what to do and where.The thinking needed to solve some of the puzzles was enough to make me wonder if the solutions were obtuse, even with the in-game hints that sometimes present themselves, or if I was just being brain-dead. But we now live in a connected world, which means the answer is always a quick Google away. However, if you, like me, really want to try to take them on without help, prepare to get stuck a bunch.Get something wrong or take a wrong step, and you’re sometimes treated to a death cinematic. I say “treated” because they’re awesome to watch and make failure a part of the fun and even count as achievements.The incredible art and sound design alone could do a lot of heavy lifting, but the incredibly detailed writing isn’t afraid to challenge your intellect. It elevates the experience to one that isn’t afraid to take the necessary risks to deliver something special and feels like it’s willing to perch itself on the same level as a solid sci-fi novel.There’s no cheese-ball video game writing going on here.On that same note, some of the really great story beats and discoveries of what took place are delivered via messages and logs from personal PDAs. While it’s old school in its nature, it can become quite tiresome to read through a whole bunch of messages, but that’s also the nature of adventure and indie games, so it’s not a major complaint.Considering the age of my hardware, I was pleasantly surprised that the game was able to look as good as it did while running at 1440p with all the bells and whistles turned on, with loading as well as hot swapping between characters taking only a few moments even without an SSD.Conclusion:I’ve really enjoyed the time I’ve had with Stasis Bone Totem. So far, it’s almost everything I wanted from a sequel – despite it not being directly linked to the original.It’s familiar in some ways while feeling completely fresh in others, with visual and gameplay upgrades that give you a great reason to jump back into its world and unravel its mysteries.If you’re looking for a deep isometric sci-fi horror adventure to get stuck into, my experience with Stasis Bone Totem so far says you’ve come to the right place.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique and captivating horror/puzzle game with a surprisingly moving and emotional story at its core. You can tell it was made by a small team, but whatever the game lacks in polish and production value it more than makes up for with its heart and characters (especially Moses). The puzzle solutions can be a bit obtuse, requiring a fair amount of troubleshooting and guesswork, but the relatively linear nature of the game's progression means you'll always have a clear set of options in front of you. The developer is even kind enough to provide a full guide/walkthrough for those times when you get truly stuck. If I was judging on an out of 10 scale, I'd give it a solid 8/10 for sure, especially for its low asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is insanely good. The developers "THE BROTHERHOOD" have created their own universe with STASIS, CAYNE and now STATIS: BONE TOTEM which are connected, but still independent point & click adventure games with psychological and body horror. But no cheap death or survival sections, thank you very much.While I liked their other game (BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION), I found it quite convoluted and hard to complete without a guide -- not so for BONE TOTEM. The three playable characters have unique abilities, interactions and are mostly separated from each other, so it does not become a needle-in-a-haystack affair of matching the correct character to the environment puzzle. There is almost always a somewhat clear path to follow. And if not, switching characters and going in a different direction normally leads to progress.I have just entered chapter 4 and feel like I am getting close to the end, but damn, what a ride it has been so far. The quality of the first three chapters and the downward spiral of horrific insanity that transpires is excellently presented and the generally charming characters, beautiful graphics, fantastic voice acting and dark atmosphere keep me glued to the screen. If only I did not have to work and sleep. ^^More of this quality, please. And, THE BROTHERHOOD, kudos.---Edit after finishing the game: The quality held up for the 4th and 5th chapters. This was amazing. Not going to spoil anything about the story, but it speaks to the quality of the writing and the voice actors that the relationships between all of the characters felt real and worthwhile, with the most emotional impact for me being between a toy bear and .

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem, is a deep sea point and click adventure, and just about one of the finest damn pieces of horror fiction I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing.This is a game that should not be spoiled, at all possible costs, so I'll leave my praises in bullet point format.-No jump scares-The plot winds downwards endlessly, with each act offering new and deeper takes on the core mysteries of the story-Oppressive writing that never seemed to repeat itself even once in a given 10-16 hour playthrough-Well written, and even charming protagonists with well paced, meaningful arcs-Absolutely phenomenal voice acting-A unique visual style that harkens back to the days of pre-rendered titles from the 90's, but with a modern coat of paint-A lovecraftian take on horror. Unspeakable madness, ritualistic murder, occult worship, and fleshy horrors await. -The game manages to be a tale about so many things without ever seeming over simplistic or pandering. Expect discussions on capitalism, religion, artificial intelligence, and more. These things can easily be a turn-off in many modern media products, but every one of them was executed so sharply that the story never turned into the same boring lecture that so many other products seem to devolve into.The game is not without its frustrations, but the pure level of craft in this title completely outshone all of it. This game is easily an immediate recommend, and will doubtlessly be on my list for best games of the year. Please don't sleep on this one!

_childDocuments_.review: Bone Totem offers an atmospheric, immersive horror experience that truly stands out in the point-and-click genre. Its top-notch voice acting, coupled with a hauntingly terrific music score, sets the stage for a dark, creepy environment that really gets under your skin. This is the world of Cayne - a world where you can almost taste the fear and experience the grisly end of the unfortunate souls trapped in the MULE.The game's storytelling is remarkable. It draws you in, pulling you deeper into the unsettling narrative with each click. It is not just the plot that is compelling, but the way the characters are brought to life that gives Bone Totem its unique edge. Each dialogue, each interaction, is so masterfully crafted that you cannot help but be invested in their fates.Every moment in Bone Totem is climactic, making for an undersea adventure that is equal parts thrilling and horrifying. Each step you take reveals something new, something dreadful, and yet, something absolutely captivating. It is a great addition to the Stasisverse, but it is not for the faint of heart. If you appreciate a good horror game and are a fan of the point-and-click genre, Bone Totem is an absolute must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a testament to how well Stasis: Bone Totem's story is presented that I became emotionally attached to an artificially sentient toy, 'super bear.' The game is a dark, twisted, atmospheric adventure that isn't afraid to get under your skin. As far as these types of games are concerned, I don't usually play them too often, with The Walking Dead being the one I've played most prominently. Nevertheless, after reading some reviews, I was intrigued by this macabre story about a doomed research station at the bottom of the Pacific Ocean. It is very much an adventure game, but you would be right to assume that it's also a horror game. Because it is, and it's an experience that beckons you to keep pushing just a little further to see its terrifying story unfold.Three playable protagonists are mainly involved in this story: Charlie, Mac, and their super toy Moses, a very smart and brave bear. As a result of past traumas, Charlie and Mac have grown apart from one another, putting an emotional and financial burden on both of them. When they discover an abandoned but very large research facility isolated in the ocean, their fortunes begin to turn. Despite what the pair are unaware of, this place harbors an ancient, chthonic evil that can be described as anything but good. The trio is trapped, however, after a series of horrifying events occur. This forces them to venture deeper into the facility and uncover an ancient secret to find any hope of salvation.It's a harrowing tale as you learn more and become engrossed in the experience as the tension slowly ramps up. The story evokes sheer dread as you realize how much of a nightmarish hell these characters find themselves in. I was engaged with the story throughout my time playing, and while the pacing can drag a bit in the middle sections of the game, I was always interested to see the next shocking turn. I would have played the game just for Moses alone (Charlie and Mac are great, too), but again, it is a testament to how good the writing is when weaving real character-driven drama along with your classic 'evil corporate scientists play god' trope. Even that is used effectively here as the Cayne Corporation (which is a part of a larger narrative universe the Stasis games take place in) uses religious dogma to ensnare its devotees to what is supposed to be a divine cause that is nothing more than a front for a harsh, downright evil corporation to enslave people by amassing them in untold amounts of debt for various medical procedures and other financial aid people may need. It's a twisted amalgamation of unregulated corporate greed and religious postulation. Funnily enough, this isn't even the coolest or darkest aspect of Stasis: Bone Totem's narrative. The deeper you dig, the more terrible, vile secrets that aren't for the faint of heart or easily squeamish.Bone Totem also has some pretty neat gameplay features, primarily the QSD system, which allows for real-time item swapping between the three playable characters, as the trio are very rarely together in the same place at once. Also highly praised is the pinging system that hasn't been used in other adventure titles. You can press right-click and highlight items within the environment that you can interact with (puzzle and key items) or show you the various detailed descriptions of the environment. This allows you to read and take in the environmental story-telling at your own pace and better find and understand what items you'll need to progress. It cuts down on much of the downsides of the adventure game genre in that you spend a decent amount of time clicking everything, wondering where to go and what to do to progress the story. However, a couple of puzzles here will inevitably force you to think hard and long on what to do or look up a guide. It's not a cakewalk in the puzzles department, though they aren't too obtuse or frustrating. It works well and ultimately remains engaging throughout the experience.The story is told in real-time, simultaneously as the group progresses throughout their journey. Voice acting does much of the heavy lifting here when conveying the story. However, it delivers in spades as these characters suffer through their internal pain and traumas. Each brings that aspect of the character out so convincingly. There is a fair amount of text to read here and numerous PDAs, terminals, and environmental descriptions of the areas around you. Each line of text describes the world around you in an expressively gruesome, obscene fashion. While I didn't read them all, the majority I read added even more context and understanding to what was happening. These logs painted a picture of a fate more terrible than death for these characters.You should check out Stasis: Bone Totem, especially if the game is on sale. The highly engaging game will keep you on the edge of your seat for hours as you slowly uncover the horrifying truth below. There are other games set in this universe that I want to check out now. However, as it stands, my time in the Stasis universe was fun. Remember to be a brave bear, and you'll be fine. Probably.I highly recommend it.

Whatever misgivings you may have, this game pays it back in spades.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather yay than nah, mainly due to the horrific and repulsive atmosphere, nice pre-rendered graphics stemming from old-school isometric games like Planescape: Torment and variety of non-cliche puzzles. Rough at the corners, but acceptable for an indie team, which is extremely talented with high attention to details.Things I'd like to see improved in the next game (I hope there will be):* UI - tracing lines to both interactive and observation active points are way annoying and must go. And so are all the glowing effects in UI - inventory, objects, etc. Especially tedious was the object interaction, as even the simplest act of swapping objects in slots is not supported.* Animations - with amazing backgrounds, the walking animation stands out poorly. * Story is good but lore is cumbersome. Xenomorph easter egg is nice but also WTF, alongside some of the designs resembling Giger's. I think that authors couldn't agree on one and decided to mix all in one basket. I hope next game stays more focused and keeps to the unique style.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Buy this game, if you like point and click adventures. Buy this game if you like surreal horror.Top class art, top class sound design/atmosphere. (Use headphones!)This is gonna be long, but I really want to express how good this game is, while the experience is still fresh. There aren't many games that have such richly detailed environments. Much like Stasis, each area is unique. Each series of rooms is its own encapsulated story, with its own cast of characters and role in the overarching plot. Graphics wise, it is on par with Disco Elysium, or a notch above. The writers/designers managed to pack so many horror vignettes into one game, it truly blows my mind. It is like a collage of perfect horror short-stories that all mesh together, each more horrible than the last. Every time you enter a new screen, you are met with some new kind of unimaginably spectacular disaster. And I mean, really, think of the most horrible scenario you can imagine and add a lot of MSG. Your eyes dart around the scene, trying to piece together "what the hell happened here?". This process of examining a series of rooms and reading through the various log entries (and now also image galleries on computer terminals) is quite addictive. Each piece of information rides the edge of giving you just enough to captivate your attention, but withholding enough to keep you wondering what else you will find. Every room will have some things that you can take a closer look at, which will be viewed from 1st person perspective. This switching between 1st and 3d person perspective really adds to the immersion. There was a little of that in the previous games, but Bone Totem is full of detailed perspectives. I can not stress enough how detailed the art is. Everything is infused with character and meaningful details. You just have to look. The whole "derelict research station" trope is well worn, but Bone Totem delivers one of the best takes on it that I've experienced so far. This is the kind of game that makes you feel like the story could not have been told in any other way. It would be cool as a movie, I guess. But nothing beats the immersion of reading through journals next to the corpse of someone who met yet another fantastically gruesome death, while hearing the characters talk to each other as they try to cope with the situation.  Each room is littered with "tooltip style" text pop ups that embellish the visuals. And these are absurdly well written. They offer such vivid descriptions that draw you even more into the game. The environments are also very dark and your characters flashlight follows your mousecursor. Which means that, as you read a text popup, the area it describes is simultaneously illuminated. There is all kinds of body horror, psychological horror and existential horror blended together in this game.The creatures are very "Cronenberg-ian", and the environments remind me of Zdzisław Beksiński rather than Geiger. You are wading through the remains of people who died in absolute desperation. Anything you can think of, really. Starvation turned to cannibalism. Mutiny, torture, murder, betrayal. And you get to inspect, and revel in the detail of the ways in which everyone lost their battles, or their will to live. You get to learn what insane hope they hung onto and how they eventually accepted death or how they died in a hopeless attempt to escape. The whole "dystopian super corporation" trope is also well worn, but again, I find that the many references to Cayne's treatment of employees is on a next-level of extreme cynicism. It's often so horrible that it makes you laugh. Just one example, there is a women who literally throws herself into an incinerator so that her body could be damaged above the required 86% tissue damage for an insurance-covered organ transplant.You see every aspect of reality go through stages of spectacular and fantastical decay. From human bodies, to catastrophic infrastructural damage, as well as the systemic breakdown and corruption of corporate hierarchies. Since the characters are all encapsulated in their own compartment or division of Cayne enterprises, you get to see the situation from their particular point of view. Each of them trying to piece together what is happening with the information they have. Which means that all the aforementioned is examined from these many different angles. The insanity of the situations you encounter becomes gradually more extreme. I'm not going to spoil anything here, but it's amazing just how wild it all becomes. There are layers in the physical locations of the game, as well as there are layers in the history of the places you are exploring. And the deeper you go, the more you become able to understand how they are all connected. You can review all of the journals you find in your pda, which I found myself doing often. The characters all make references to various events, or to each other. So then you go back to read their journal with a better understanding of what they went through. Which often means that you grasp the horror of their predicament to a fuller extent. Even at the very last 30 minutes of the game, you are still treated to horrific revelations. If you look closely, you will find many connections to Stasis. A character that is mentioned in many of Stasis' journals can be found in this game. Gameplay wise:The puzzles are devoid of moon logic, and there is a good balance/ratio between inventory items and interactable objects. The puzzles are fun to interact with, which is important imo. Clues are strewn around and obfuscated in ways that feel organic. (As opposed to arbitrary) I would rate the difficulty as medium to easy. The puzzles serve as a vehicle to immerse you into the environment/atmosphereWhen I saw that there would be multiple characters, I was a bit worried that it would be clunky. As I usually don't like having to deal with inventory, or having to navigate the same space with multiple characters. But what they did in this game is really brilliant, which is to give each character their own path/environment to explore. This gives you a great sense of scale, without forcing you to travel too much. Instead of walking between 9 screens with one character, you walk between a set of 3 between each of the 3 characters. It's a great way to give you a lot to explore without feeling bogged down waiting for the characters to move around. I really like the inventory sharing, and it was implemented in a satisfying way. That part could have easily been clunky but they made it seamless and fun to use. I play A LOT of point and click games, and Bone Totem manages to improve on every mechanical aspect of the genre. The ping mechanic with the connecting lines is a brilliant innovation. There's something about those lines that takes a processing load of your brain. It's not something I would have ever thought about, but it is somehow better than mere object highlighting. The "puzzle screen" system is also very good. You never have to waste time wondering what you are supposed to interact with. There is a clear division between crucial and peripheral data. This system allows you to become more immersed in the game. Since your mind is less occupied with having to sort through what matters to progression or not.Widescreen is fully supported, and looks great. The game runs at over 100fps on a gtx 1650ti

_childDocuments_.review: Why can't movies and shows today be written this well?  Why do I care so much about an ugly teddy bear!?  Charlie-Mac!  Anyways, great game.  I enjoy the point-and-click adventure games and this one with its Lovecraftian-vibe is right up my alley so I gave it a shot.  I expected an interesting point-and-click horror game with interesting themes and setting but was not expecting to be so engrossed in this game, nor was I expecting to genuinely care about the characters as I did.  Would love to see these writers adapt their stories for a show or movie.  We need good stories with characters that truly feel human and yet strive on as a family through whatever horror life throws their way.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: STASIS: BONE TOTEM is a GotY 2023 contender in my book. A big step compared to the first game of the series. Basically bug-free at release and without any BS. Simply a masterpiece. An interesting setting, extremely detailed and beautiful environments, great atmosphere and challenging puzzles that never feel tedious. This Point-and-Click-Adventure has it all and gives me strong Planescape: Torment vibes for some reason.While the story can be a bit overwhelming at times, it's still an interesting mix of concepts.What this game lacks compared to the first game is the feeling of solitude, the three main characters and their sidekicks are real blabbermouths at times. This would be my only nitpick, some of the dialogue is a bit cringe, especially considering the situation in which the protagonists find themselves.Moses is brave and strong.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with great writing. I easily put it in my top for favorite horror games. Reminiscent of Soma, but much darker. The game has a dark story to tell and relies on that storytelling rather than jump scares and chasing you through narrow corridors. Point-and-click puzzle game play requires thinking, but never felt unfair. Definitely recommend to anyone who's a fan of horror and doesn't mind the point-and-click style.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I went into STASIS: BONE TOTEM totally blind, and I came out with a newfound appreciation for point&click games. I'm a big fan of reading, but this was a genre I had never really touched before. The great descriptive writing paired with the awesome environments really made me feel like I was playing through a sci-fi novel. I found the universe and lore super interesting, and I'm really excited to see what comes next for the STASIS world!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Very good story. The graphics, the voice acting, the story are all fantastic. I was never really frightened while playing the game is definitely unsettling. The narrative of the game was so compelling I couldn't stop playing.  My only complaint is that some of the puzzles are extremely weird and unintuitive. _childDocuments_.review: Not without its flaws, but a great entry in a niche fandom. _childDocuments_.review: Not bad, not bad at all.- The game is a bit too dark (visually)- Dialogue and voice acting are considerably above average for an indie game- The character portraits in the emails are... quite interesting. They look like something from the works of Wes Anderson or French directors. Don't get me wrong, they're cool, but somehow not quite fitting to the game's overall visual style.- Remember Kubrick/Spielberg's "A.I."? _childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: STASIS: BONE TOTEM is a very well executed point-and-click game. The game is very atmospheric; It has a decent visual aesthetic, solid musical score, good world building, and great writing. All of these elements gel very cohesively and produce a pretty unforgettable game. Bone Totem's story is fairly interesting and relies heavily on the game's world building, which is a fairly unique blend of themes and visual style. It may have been served better with a bit more of subtle exposition on some of the more esoteric elements of the world. Interesting themes and styles are explored throughout the game, with significant focus on belief, faith, and corporatism among other classic cyberpunk themes.It runs into some common pitfalls in the point-and-click genre, namely some obtuse puzzles and interactions. There's an excellent guide available to help spur progression, which I found necessary on occasion. Over the course of the game, the visuals range from really great to unpolished. There are certainly instances where the seams of the visual presentation are visible, which is slightly disappointing in comparison with the polished and well-executed visuals otherwise. As a complete experience, I would highly recommend STASIS: BONE TOTEM to fans of the point-and-click genre and those who are interested in its setting. Its unforgettable, if a bit uneven in certain respects.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

If you are into Point and click games, and not afraid of horrors, this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite enjoyed this game. I recommend for any horror fans that enjoy point and click puzzle games. Especially those that like body horror and science fiction with a dash of lovecraft.It's filled with dark secrets and twists, and a lot of the puzzles were fun and quite engaging. However the guide was necessary at times in the second half of the game, some of the puzzles were just illogical and not as well thought out as the earlier ones. Music was good, helps with the ambience and really enjoyed reading the logs to it. The bear won't stop laughing and humming away at the most inappropriate times though. Odd.Story was well paced and I really like the wider narrative. it had me very curious to try the other games, wanting to learn more! I'd love to read a book or see a film set in this universe.There were some good moments in the script between the characters. However there was too much dialogue overall with the actors also taking their time reading lines. They often repeated themselves too which grew tiresome. I just had to start skipping dialogue toward the end as soon as I read the text, which was a shame as the voice actors did a great job.The cut scenes were okay, but far too many tight angles trying to hide the bad animations. However there is some great environment dressing in places that the cut scenes capture very well, setting the tone. Would not have been the same horror experience without them.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, nice atmosphere , with constant feeling that something will happen. _childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Totally solid sci-fi horror point & click adventure. The voice acting, story, and writing are top notch and really carry the experience. I liked swapping between the three characters and inventory management was nice and snappy with an excellent magic pockets feature. Controller controls were kinda pretty clunky.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Have played all the brotherhood games and i have to say this latest one maybe is best one from them yet and the competition was first stasis game.I felt like puzzles etc were pretty good and not too hard but not too easy either. I think all the things were quite logical to solve so this game did not have too big of a issue of trying every single item on everything like some games do that you just cant even imagine why that works there. in this game you could pretty much logically thing of what could go where. I do highly recommend this to people who love point and click games, there are not too many of them out there and this one is really one of the best ones. Depends do you like the very dark theme of the game but for me that was a big bonus as i love it because not too many games have this dark theme in them. _childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is a fairly lengthy horror game set in the very depths of the Pacific Ocean. You play as 3 characters, each one with their own set of skills and viewpoints as they go on a mission to explore what appears to be an abandoned oil rig. Of course, they soon realize the situation is far more complex than it seemed. Visually, Bone Totem is nothing short of astounding. The environments (and cutscenes) are hugely detailed, beautiful yet oddly terrifying at the same time. In addition to the visuals, the developers also did a great job making me feel invested in the narrative and main cast with Moses being one of the game's highlights. Huge shout-out to all the voice actors who worked on this game as well. So yeah, I very much enjoyed Bone Totem from start to finish, so I can only hope more people get to experience it as we need more games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute treat of an adventure game in a market that has seen less and less of them over time.The puzzles are for the most part intuitive and make sense but with the three characters and multitude of things you can check use items on and subsequently forget what you need, the hint guide included is quite comprehensive, maybe too much so, spoiling a reveal when i was struggling to keep up with said 3 people perspective.The story is wonderful and deserving of your time!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This was fun! Fulfilled my craving for a horror point and click. Like the rest of the Stasis games, this is a gore fest full of nightmarish visuals, body horror, and a bleak atmosphere. The descriptions for each item in the environment are deliciously over the top and aim for maximum gross factor, while also helping to visualize things that would probably have been hard to animate (sometimes your imagination can create a more horrific image than a graphic visual ever could). That might also be why they decided to make this game so dimly lit/dark, which is a criticism I've seen in reviews but it didn't bother me too much. I thoroughly enjoyed the voice acting and the characters - especially the fan favorite, Moses. He really is the best bear <3
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played in many years. I love point-and-click adventures, and STASIS is, in a way, a new version of the point-and-click form I have encountered so far, reminiscent of the legendary game "SANITARIUM". The storyline is excellent, as are the dialogues, the intuitive interface, the sound design, and the voice acting. God... I have nothing to complain about. Moreover, I haven't felt this close to characters since "The Longest Journey".And now a word to the game developers: I am currently going through a very difficult period, both mentally and physically. Thanks to Waam and your work, it has been easier for me to get through the worst of it. You cannot realize how much you have done for me. But two points you will understand:1. You have created this game, and I thank you very much because it has helped me during the worst time of my life.2. You added Polish to the game. If you hadn't done that, I wouldn't be writing these words right now, and all these great moments would not have happened.Thank you very much.I recommend the game to absolutely everyone. 10/10!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the game and will give you a short pros/cons list:+ Atmonsphere/Music+ Very well designed riddles/no moon-logic + Length+ Story is pretty good and well written- Some Audio Issues (Volume)- Characters don`t talk about invironmental details (text only)- Camera-Zoom feels a little weird sometimesRating:8/10
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good point and click adventure with an amazing visual experience.  Great atmosphere and story with excellent puzzles that occasionally get a bit goofy.My only complaint is not having an in game note system.  It's 2024.  I shouldn't need to get pen and paper to write critical notes to solve puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: As to avoid any spoilers Ill keep my review short. I've never had a game's story hook me as fast as this one did. Within the first 20 minutes of the game I knew I wasnt going to be able to put it down for a hot minute, and i ended up finishing it within 2 days. STASIS: BONE TOTEM has very quickly and easily became one of my favorite Sci-Fi horror stories ive ever had the pleasure of experiencing. If you are a fan of anything horror, I guarantee you will enjoy this game thoroughly. 100% accuracy prediction. I am Numen.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Statis: Bone Totem is a well crafted, dark and disturbing underwater horror story. No unnecessary jumpscares, just the crushing feeling of claustrophobia, darkness and loneliness. The ocean is dark and full of terrors, and they are well on display here, alongside heaps of gore, mixed with stories of flawed humans and corporate greed and complete disregard for human life.All of the speaking characters are well written, distinct and interesting. They interact well and they all have their own reasons to push forward through the dark horror. Even the dead crew members and scientists have their own dark stories to share.The art design is excellent, although the dim lights and top down view made me overlook most of the details. One thing I did not like is that, while I can't see much, the environment is filled with written descriptions. I do not like these descriptions. They are full of purple prose that detracts from the atmosphere and annoy me. I would have liked shorter descriptions or no descriptions, and more lighting.The puzzles were mostly not difficult and logical, and the hints are most welcome. I used a walkthrough in some sections, but that's just my lack of patience.I enjoyed this game and would strongly recommend it. No obvious flaws, just a good horror story.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this short, because I don't want to spoil anything.Absolutely loved this game. I'm a sucker for bio tech and weird sci fi horror settings and this certainly scratched that itch. The writing and voice acting is pretty universally great and the music sets the tone perfectly. The cutscenes are a little jank but the game is low budget and they aren't a common occurrence. This game's sound design and environments are really detailed and varied as well.Also, I'm very picky with my Point N Click games. A lot of them get a little silly/dumb with their puzzle solutions. I feel like this game did a very good job avoiding that trapping (for the most part). If you like old school story based RPGs, point and click games, or just really good sci fi horror, pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good way to spend your time and your money. In my mind, that's all you need for a thumbs-up...**However**If you came here direct from MandaloreGaming's review or some other YouTuber, let me warn you that they fixed this game's biggest flaw in their own presentations: PACING. The story will try to tell you that crises are happening, then make you perform extremely long-winded puzzle-chains to resolve that crisis. There are also bizarre item pickups and combinations that slow down action scenes, and the option to proceed through "chapters" in any character order means that someone coughing and wheezing in one conversation will jump back to casual banter in the next. "Immersion" in the horror of the situation will likely not happen.Normally, this isn't a problem for point-and-clicks, but this being a horror adventure puts the spotlight on tight pacing and appropriate reactions from the characters. After all, this is not the first time I've had to confront nightmarish flesh-things in a corporate-project-gone-wrong and I'm sure it's not yours either, so the VAs' stellar work in conveying the "fresh" horror of this setting is working very hard to counter the slowdowns caused by moonlogic puzzles.I feel like I should point out one very bad puzzle: A number is required by an atmosphere machine in parts-per-million (ppm) and the answer is given in percentage (%) in a different clue. That's just...wrong. Appalling. Especially for a sci-fi setting.But, I don't think these issues deserves a non-recommend. If you like point-and-clicks, this is definitely for you.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely a must-play for anyone who likes point-and-click adventure/puzzle games. The writing is stellar, the voice acting is spot-on, and the puzzles are, for the most part, extremely satisfying. There were one or two occasions where I found myself grinding my teeth in frustration, as the game loves giving out red herring solutions, but otherwise I had an absolute blast, and I certainly have no qualms recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is one of the best games I have ever played, no question about it. Utterly excellent all the way through, in all areas. There is very little I can say now, as I sit here, misty eyed, is that it hit me. I mean it really, really hit me. This is a game I think everyone should play.While you won't need to play the other games--Stasis, Cayne, and Beautiful Desolation--to understand or enjoy this, I think you should, because The Brotherhood deserves sales so they can make more games.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Another absolutely stunning release by The Brotherhood adding to their already fantastic lineup of Stasis, Cayne, and Beautiful Desolation. Seriously, if you haven't played any of these games yet, you are truly missing out. Bone Totem is a slow build story-focused game that builds on the dread and anticipation until it reaches a fever pitch and once it hits it ramps up SO HARD. I finished the game in two nights after sacrificing sleep for work the next day because I just did not want to let go. The atmosphere and world building is genuinely incredible (if incredibly depressing at times!). Do yourself a favor and spend the money on these developers. The overwhelmingly positive reviews do not lie and the devs 100% deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and I do in many respects, but basic quality-of-life stuff makes it so I can't recommend this.The good?The voice acting, writing, mood, setting, all great. I wanted to learn and know more about what was going on.The bad is that this started with a save issue. I was using a PS5 controller and DS4Windows to map it because I hate Xbox controllers. But during the course of the game, the pause menu would cease to function and autosave similarly wouldn't work.I lost five hours of playtime, but the team was nice enough to get me a save file. Unfortunately, my trouble didn't end there, as the issue recurred.I restarted my computer and tried with just an xbox controller. It worked, for a time, but eventually the same issue would happen and the pause menu would cease to function alongside autosave.Halfway through chapter 3, I just said F it and stopped. Perhaps I'll watch a playthrough.But this is basic, quality-of-life stuff. I've never had problems like this with any other game that I can recall, certainly not something like this that is otherwise high quality.While I haven't finished the game, some other thoughts:1. The puzzles are sometimes convoluted and frequently it became a matter of me having to take photos of my screen with my phone to remember this combo or that diagram to input it later. That's not particularly fun either. That aside, I found myself simply trying everything with everything else at many points, and when the right combination worked, I usually wasn't saying "Ah ha," but more, "I guess that makes sense?"2. The video cutscenes are well-animated for an indie studio, but there were audio synchronization issues with them that I also had to look past.3. While I like the use of a web to see the active objects and viewable objects, in many respects there's just too much text on items around the screen. It does add character to the world, but it makes the gameplay sluggish and less dynamic. I don't mind absorbing myself in something, but having ten different things in a room attached to a paragraph of text was visually exhausting.4. So much of the game is mired in the tedium of switching items between characters and locations and the flow just isn't there. It's clunky and obtuse and it doesn't engage the right levers.I probably would have overall looked past most of these if not for the technical problems I was experiencing. If this had been said to have no controller support from the beginning, perhaps I'd be more understanding, but I have to go with what the game was presented as working with.I backed this game in Nov 2020, so I'm pretty disappointed in this result. I do commend the team on their work in creating an interesting setting, location, and aesthetic, but the clunky gameplay and game-breaking bugs kept me from having a go of it.I really do appreciate the developers trying their best to help me navigate the technical issues with it, and I do look forward to seeing what they create in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The horror element comes from the visual design and atmosphere, includes body horror. There no jump scares, the character may die during certain events.The puzzles difficulty ranges from easy to hard, as some of them are based on finding solutions in the environment. The inventory system is uncommon, you may have to transfer items from one character to another (done instantly) to progress or solve puzzles, which also adds to the difficulty sometimes. In case you get stuck there are hints or official manual in the Steam Guides section. Most of the puzzles can be figured out by yourself even if you aren't a puzzle person.The visuals are great design vise. The graphics and animations are good for a puzzle game but don't expect it to be cinematic. The main characters do have dialogues and the voice acting is good, sometimes really good, but lots of the story of the previous events is learned from reading the PDAs and notes. The plot and its development is interesting to learn.The game has improved in every aspect compared to the previous titles of the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the story, voice acting, production values and the general vibe of the game. However it is one of the weakest if not one of the worst adventure games I ever played. The puzzle design is outdated and remind me of old 90-s adventure games with their moon logic. I don't think any human being will be able to complete it without the guide. We have the classic bingo - endless backtracking, lack of hints where you need them, pixel hunting, some action zones are straight up not highlighted (hi decontamination zone valve), similar items straight don't work when they should thematically be usable, etc. etc. This make me as a player to be completely alienated and detached from the story. And when the game tries to create a sense of pressure and urgency I laugh cause I know i'm gonna spend next 3 hours brute forcing through my inventory.Nobody playtested the game. If this one is so bad, I can't even imaging how bad was the original Stasis.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually have tens of hours in this game on Steam Deck. Don't know why it doesn't update the hours.The game is very good looking and has some really fun and quality cutscenes. It is a little too dark, but maybe that's just the steam deck. I never played on my desktop.The story is really interesting. The characters are okay, and mostly just a vehicle to the lore. They don't really have arcs or anything.My main problem is that the puzzles are inconsistent and I've had to look for answers more than usual. I try very hard to never look up an answer to a puzzle game because that is the game. If I'm looking up answers, then I might as well just watch a let's play. I'm also good at puzzles, so I feel like my criticism is well-earned.One solution required me to visit a station, but you have to interact with the station and then after a couple of seconds some numbers start to pop up. I did not linger long enough to see the information pop up because nothing else in the game starts displaying information seconds after interacting with it. Also, I was already many hours in and had done an exhausting amount of backtracking over and over throughout the game. I had checked many other interactable stations. You walk slowly, too, which definitely makes the frequent backtracking much less tolerable.One puzzle requires you to perform an action over and over that does nothing until many button presses. It is not obvious that persistence will be rewarded. Also, no other puzzle I encountered utilizes this type of persistence solution.The last puzzle I encountered before walking away from the game, you had to match three items. I did my best to figure out the puzzle with clues in the room, but couldn't figure out the solution. I finally looked up a let's play from a very popular YouTuber. He tried my solutions. In the end, he randomly cycled the last item two extra times when his solution didn't work. The two extra cycles led to the correct solution. I tried to reverse engineer this solution that he stumbled upon, but could not see how this answer was communicated.Other than that, some of the dialogue was annoying. The male, Mac, kept telling his wife, Charlie, that he's got a bad feeling and they should go back. Charlie insists on continuing, and Mac says okay but if he gets anymore creeped out he's calling it and that's final. That was part way through chapter 1. Things obviously get much much much much much worse. AKA, worried feelings way more than justified. But they continue!The Bear character is really good and kind of unsettling.I really appreciate the effort they put in to making this game. That being said, the puzzle elements (my favorite) were less than satisfying. I put a lot of hours into trying to complete all the puzzles they threw at me, but it was frequently a grind and unfun.I haven't played in days, and do not think I will return to finish it. I believe I am very near the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved STASIS and CAYNE so I was expecting this one to be as good, especially since the reviews are overwhelmingly positive. Sorry, but no. STASIS: BONE TOTEM is an overwhelmingly tedious game. It's too dark and too long. There's no brightness setting so you're unfortunately 90 % blind navigating through the environments. I got constantly confused trying to find my way back and forth. Yes, I could have changed the settings on my screen but I didn't want to have to that every time I was gonna play the game. Maybe I'm lazy, but brightness settings in games are usually standard.As I mentioned, this game is too long. Even though the story was good, I lost interest in it after some hours. Controlling three characters didn't work in this game, it made the experience confusing. Swapping between them and swapping items in their inventories all the time to see who could use them on what and keeping track of each ones task eventually just made everything into a boring and annoying chore. I have to admit I'm pretty bad at solving puzzles, especially in point and click games, but the irritating multiple character thing made me turn to a walkthrough a lot. The puzzle solutions were often confusing too since it was hard knowing which documents were relevant and which were just random "decoration". But as I said, I'm not super smart when it comes to puzzle solving so maybe my negative experience of them here is because of my brain. Or maybe the logic in these kind of games is always far fetched and ridiculous. I didn't like the characters at all. Mediocre voice acting and they were all irritating and uninteresting with zero personalities. While everyone seems to love Moses I really HATED him. Not does Moses only have a very irritating English accent and an annoyingly slow and calm monotone voice, he speaks of himself in third person and is supposed to say "funny and cute" things like  everytime he makes progress or  when Mac curses. Moses appearance is also very weird and depressing. He looks like a retarded cave man, not a (smart) bear which he's supposed to be. I can't really describe what's so depressing about his looks, but you Swedes who read this and remember  will get an idea.I also wished there was some kind of a quest log to hint what each character are supposed to do if you get stuck and have no idea how to progress. Or if you simply don't remember when you haven't played for several days. STASIS: BONE TOTEM is an overrated game that doesn't deserve its current rating. Only buy on sale and if you can endure many hours of increasing boredom.  I asked many times. Play the previous games instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Mind numbingly awful dialog which gets progressively worst as you advance through the game. Seriously, Tommy Wiseau writes better than this.
