_childDocuments_.review: I really expected to like this game a lot, but ultimately I did find this pretty disappointing. While I enjoyed playing about 75% of the game, it was the story and the setting that kept me pushing forwards and both of these aspects severely fell off by the end of the game. I think there was a lot of promise:  sci-fi intrigue, biotech body horror, an interesting setting of an oil rig, good voice acting and interesting characters (especially Moses), However, the intrigue ultimately fell flat as most of the threads were resolved in predictable or anti-climatic ways and the sci-fi element faded and was essentially replaced by cheesy ancient aliens / lost tribe stuff (I do not consider this a spoiler as you find one within 20 minutes of starting the game, but I didn't realise they would be so important or straight-forward).The plot also petered out, to the extent that  and lots is left unexplained or hand-waved away. For example, in the main menu of the game, before you even start, you see a sacrificed corpse in that is present on the oil rig. This you also find within ten minutes of gameplay. It is never explained. The game also lacks much of a proper ending.The plot also conflicts with gameplay due the extreme number of written logs. You can spend 5 minutes reading one of these, but the characters in the plot never absorb the information. This leads to some frustrating points where you have been reading about some amazing secret for the last three hours but your characters still act surprised when you stumble across it. I guess the devs felt like they had to write the game for those players who didn't read the logs - and maybe that is the best solution for text logs like this, but in that case why include them? It would have been a much cleaner experience if the log information was cut down and implemented into gameplay or even just delivered as audio logs so that the characters and players had no choice but to listen.I think the horror is also lacking, probably because just too straight-forward. People are being killed and tortured and infected with horrible diseases - yes, it's not my idea of a Friday night, but it's so direct and uncompromising in ideas and presentation that it just seems very plain and uninteresting. I would have expected that in this horrible sci-fi world there would at least be some horror that was specific to this vision of the future. Signalis is a good example of a game that extracted a lot of horror and emotion from its premise, and it's even set in a biotech/retro-futuristic setting as well. Unlike Signalis, Stasis: Bone Totem didn't really show me much horror that derived from the world in which it was set.Same goes for many of the plot beats. I really felt that towards the end, things were almost getting exploitative. I got the impression that bleak things were occurring simply because the writers wanted maintain their chosen tone, rather than provide emotional payoff or preserve narrative flow.Anyway, if you really like point-and-click adventure games and you don't mind a cheesy story so much, you may enjoy this. The puzzles are generally good and there isn't too much "adventure game logic". Personally I will look out for whatever comes next from The Brotherhood but I will be more sceptical when listening to recommendations.PS: Also, although the devs claim to have removed a lot of the AI art, I think some of it is still there (for example, in the bone clock at the start of the last chapter). It kind of bothers me because it just looks out of place. I don't really have any ethical qualms with AI art in particular, but from their statements I got the impression that all of it had been removed, so if I'm correct then this is a little dishonest.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: There need to be more games like this. It's not perfect, but its one of the best horror games you'll play this year. 9/10What do I like:(1) The writing is great(2) The art direction is even better. (3) Having multiple, switchable protags offers a surprising amount of freshness to the point and click game-play. Nearly every puzzle requires contribution from every character, and it makes for some really fun puzzles. What do I not like:(1) There were a couple of bad puzzles (two in my opinion). One math puzzle in the late games has two objectively correct solutions, but the game only accepts one of them. It was annoying. (2) The game is over now, and I'll have to wait a while to play the next game from these devs. If you are at all a fan of Lovecraftian horror or aqua horror, this game is a must.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game really punches above it's weight showing that budget means nothing compared to having a solid idea and vision on how to execute it.Obviously, as a point and click the story/characters/narrative will make or break the experience and I'm glad to say Bone Totem delivers a surprisingly nice story within the scope it setup for itself. The game takes the smart approach of having a more complex setting/mystery that can slowly reveal while sticking to a small trio of main characters that allows it to keep the emotional side of the narrative more focused. The presentation (in particular the voice acting) is also very impressive and really allowed the story to hit the emotional moments it needed to especially towards the end.Something that I wasn't expecting going into this game was how clever its point and click puzzle design would be. Well maybe not the design of the actual puzzles themselves (those were rather standard but still decent for the genre) but instead the system the game uses to interact with said puzzles. Bone Totem makes the smart design choice to allow the trio of playable characters with different abilities to be able to exchange items and communicate when in different places. This makes it possible to have very rewarding domino effect puzzles while keeping the character interactions still going strong which makes the player care more about the characters. Although in some stretches of the game the pacing suffers a bit with some puzzles requiring a bit too much moving parts to advance forward without feeling like it was dragging (important to say that this was rare).I really enjoyed this 15 hour experience much more than what I was expecting to. I recommend it to anyone that is a fan of story driven games and finds the premise/synopsis of it intriguing.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: There is a reason why less than a quarter of people who have the achievement for finishing the game have the achievement for not skipping dialogue.During dialogue you can perform no actions, nor can you move to a new area.  The dialogue is boring and excessive, and just plain agonizing towards the end.  I spent the last half of the game mashing the skip dialogue button constantly like it was a QTE and just hoping to get through the senseless yammering before it blocked me from performing actions or moving to the next zone.There also needs to be a better way to traverse long distances, because the movement speed is awful.  Lots of backtracking and moving between zones and it was just painful.Story was good for the first half, but the ridiculous amount of dialogue and action lock made me hate playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Impressive quality production that captivates all the way. The game sticks to core values of point-and-click adventures with straight forward mechanics. You focus on what matters, the gripping story and puzzles, no pixel hunting. The shared inventory is easy to use and makes every character feel contributing. The three paths you follow in the game have tons of locations so there is always something new to riddle, read or look at. The pre-rendered backgrounds, animation and UI ooze with classic detail. Cinematography has some of the most memorable scenes in a long time. I have been craving for these beautiful short cutscenes that highlight your ingame progress (including hidden deaths). Voice acting is spot on and a surprising number of volume sliders allow you to customize your soundscape. Music is not overused, just manages to carry the mood perfectly.Since this gem is not an action game, take your time to explore the locations, enjoy the horror setting and dive into the lore. "You do not know what the story really is, until the ending."My Charlie-Mac-Moses
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I backed the game because it was the most logical thing to do. THE BROTHERHOOD delivers every time. I absolutely loved the first STASIS, even with the somewhat less intuitive puzzles but the setting was mind blowing. I also loved Beautiful Desolation and both games brought me a lot of empathy for the protagonists. STASIS: BONE TOTEM does a lot of things different, starting from the 3D Engine mixed with prerendered Backgrounds, adding 2 more protagonists and changing the gameplay here and there. Solid writing as always and i wasn't expecting to like Moses that much. It is absolutely not necessary to play the first one, this is a completely unrelated game even though it has some references while exploring and reading.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked how this one turned out. Unlike the previous Stasis games which were more about exploring how horrifying the larger game world is, this one utilizes the extreme backdrop of the game's setting to focus more on various personal struggles. I don't want to say too much, but I find it all comes together neatly in the end. Lots of food for thought.Really one of those games that's on your must-play list. If it clicks for you, you'll have a hard time putting it down.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Given the overwhelmingly positive reviews, I was really looking forward to this. But I had to return it after 2 hours because the point-and-click controls were so unpleasant. Getting a character to run to an object and interact with it requires multiple precise clicks. There were multiple times when two objects were arranged on the screen such that one was nearly impossible to select due to the strange way mouse pointer proximity is handled.Even old adventure games like The Longest Journey don't have these problems. I'm not sure why this game does.The puzzles were also quite unintuitive and featured what I would call "bad adventure game moon logic". The game includes a pdf with a full walk through, but that feels to me like a cop out.Despite the puzzle issues, which I think are probably unfixable, I would be interested in trying again if there is an update that improves the input handling.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Nice Story and decent execution, the atmosphere was nice too, though if you played the original Stasis let me tell you that this game isnt on the same level.What holds it back is the fact you have to play 3 characters which makes the gameplay somewhat slow and disjointed and the clichee "Mommy" Storyline wasnt exactly my favorite. Also the puzzles were a little far fetched and often resorted to "try everything on everything"Other than that, great game with a nice story, decent atmosphere, good soundtrack and Voice Acting.Greatly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is a $5 title.Bone Totem is a point-and-click adventure game that has tedious, frustrating, and contrived puzzles.  At least one solution is found only by reading walls-of-expository-text provided through a bad "journal entry" trope.The plot is linear, level design is unenjoyably awkward, and sprites are janky.  Similar games for the C64 and NES published in the early 1990s were better than Bone Totem.Artwork and production values are otherwise good.  The story had potential as a movie or novel, but it fails to land when the game mechanics are distracting.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a wonderful gem and I urge everyone to play it. Starting from its immersing story to the wonderful memorable characters, Stasis: Bone Totem is a sequel to a currently established point and click scifi-adventure which you would never forget. It's also very much award winning.  The story has so much to give here, because it has interesting sci-fi elements and the characters make much of the story. There is of course elements of horror with aliens, ancient civilizations and other creatures that you don't find in casual games. The story is definitely very well written, you can tell the devs gave their absolute best in crafting it. You follow a husband-wife duo who are pirates and scavenges in the mechanical sea and you get a contract to go to a place but accidentally stumbles upon this abandoned mysterious underwater base with no survivors you think. Vague hints give out what happened to the inhabitants there who is a part of a large cooperation. I will be honest you can play the game twice and never understand the story because its very complex. It has a lot of emotions, lot of pain, lot of suffering and survival urges.  I got very attached to the characters especially the robotic bear and his biggest strength - Faran. Yes he is my absolute favorite character in the whole wide world. The state he was in when he was found and his profound support for the team is so inspiring. He had nothing left but he helped who can be helped. The husband and wife they have very good characterization and development, they don't get alone but they love each other and they loved their family. Their robotic bear was their family too and the friend of their daughter who is a part of a more bigger plan. There is even an ancient creatures who will take part in the story which I did not get about. You also find out a lot about side characters in the story through the PDA's they have left all over the base. There are mad scientists and mad doctors and also mad engineers.  It's a sci-fi game so I deeply do understand that it has a lot of interesting items where you need to pay a lot of attention to. I liked the fact that each character has different abilities. The husband can break items, the wife can combine them. There are also three characters where you can choose at will and you are a team, this game would have made it to the top more if its multiplayer but that would need more development. There are some tough puzzles which makes you ponder for a while and grab that hint. They are definitely innovative. You can also use items on characters and see what they will tell you. Definitely a ground breaking breakthrough in the history of point and click adventures. Also the conversation cut-scenes are a bit long but they are skippable. I think the concept art for this game is so well done, you can just see the hard work. The cut scenes are overboard and beautiful for this type of a game. The music is okay, it gives out the atmosphere.  The achievements are not hard except that one where you need a lot of endurance. I wanted to get everything in 2 playthroughs, so I had two different walkthroughs, one on phone and one on desktop. There is one where you must play the whole game in one sitting without loading. Not recommended and I don't appreciate this achievement, people need rest from gaming and the ergonomics. It can harm the laptop if you are using one. The other achievements are okay. I liked the fact that instead of saving them, killing them and viewing different deaths would unlock achievements. The gameplay is around 21 hours for me without a guide and took me six hours to get the rest of the achievements. I saw in a thread that it requires 12 hours for a single playthrough but that depends on you.  It's an amazing adventure filled with its own original content and grappling sci-fi story which is memorable for days. Would definitely play another game from the devs, because of their dedicated work for the series.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: My kid plays shooters, I play adventure games. As an old-time gamer, I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Fantastic production all round.  Having played the first Stasis game, I had certain expectations. I was not disappointed. I was pleasantly surprised by the improved graphics, design and mechanics of the game. In the first Stasis you were commanding a poor desperate character. In this game you instead play many characters with shared inventories. It's a recipe for disaster, but the designers of the game balance the user interface and gameplay complexity with great insight. I get easily discouraged by complex game mechanics, so I was relieved to find that the gameplay is intuitive and helps you dive quickly into the story without distractions.The puzzles are the driving force of the game. Most are intuitive. You need to have patience and to read the environment in order to solve them using and combining items from your characters inventories. You'll be fine.As regards the story, the writers of these games touch on things such as love, loss as well as defiance and courage in the face of utter hopelessness and horror. It looks like they have a story to tell and they pick the adventure game medium to convey it. As such the game has substance and narrative prowess. Its bleakness reminded me of Dan Simmon's Hyperion novel.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastically haunting modern adventure game. The story here is so engrossing, especially when coupled with top tier voice acting and writing. The gameplay is simple, but does its job of engaging the player with the world, and isn't frustrating like many games of this genre can be. The art is deliciously Gigeresque, more so the further you get. One thing I didn't love was the environment descriptions. They tend to be written too dramatically and were more a chore to read than anything. I stopped checking them except in the most standout rooms. Gotta thank Mandalore for leading me to this game and I look forward to what the brothers make next.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is a very solid horror puzzle experience with some incredible sci-fi concepts and deeply emotional character writing. While the story often only offers glimpses into the wider world, I found them to be fascinating. It's not often that cyber-punk, biological-horror, body-horror, and Lovecraftian-horror are so artfully mixed into a coherent setting. The character dynamics often felt raw and pained in ways rarely seen in gaming stories. My one major complaint is that the pacing often felt a little off and the fascinating concepts in the endgame felt somewhat under-baked compared to those in the early game.To be specific:  All in all, Statis: Bone Totem is a very good time with great atmosphere and character-writing, the occasional underbaked concept, and a runtime that doesn't outstay its welcome. Highly recommended for anyone with a taste for story-rich horror and/or puzzle games. And finally, I'm now extremely excited for any future releases set in this wild, fascinating world.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the first Stasis game, I admittedly went into this sequel perhaps with a little scepticism and doubt gnawing in the back of my mind. As much as I loved Stasis 1 would it turn out to have been a flash in the pan? Was the atmosphere of nightmarish despair, brutality and creeping horror set by the first game a never to be repeated experience?I’ve never been so happy to say that no, the exact opposite is true. The incredible world building of Stasis 1 has been taken to a new level in Bone Totem. The setting, establishment of the in-game universe, the tone and the atmosphere in my mind solidify themselves as a worthy peer to stand amongst the great and notable works of sci-fi horror that the creators of Bone Totem so clearly love. The entire game is a love letter to the dark and macabre, and although it oozes reference to and reverence of the genre of sci fi horror, it never feels like a hollow facsimile but rather a deserving torch bearer of all that I love about the genre.  The biggest compliment I can give this game is that with every tenuous, agonising grasping step deeper and deeper into the fetid black hell of the depths beneath the waves I grew sadder because I knew I was one step closer to the end of this experience. A masterful addition to the “Stasisverse”, breathtaking story imagery and world building, a work of passion and love. For the love of Cayne please let there be another instalment, I need to experience more of this universe!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: The game is absolutely great, very good intricated and detailed story with a big scope, fun puzzles that will rarely get you stuck mainly because of some missed clue or item. Very good graphics with a lot of descriptions, good writing overall and lots of lore.  Beautiful CGI cutscenes.Due to the nature of game progression backtracking is very limited so it's always very fast to go look for something you may have missed in a previous room. I found many descriptions to be (intentionally?) misplaced, like sometimes the UI will offer a description of some object or room element but it is targeted on something else, like a description of a chair targeted on a nearby wall and so on, confusing at times with no evident reason to be so but with negligible effects on gameplay. Pretty long game (20+ hours in my case, trying to take most of the setting in). Last but not least, amazing Dev! I had an issue playing it on another device with Linux (not listed as supported OS yet), and asked for help on the steam forums, and the Dev himself answered me on the fly to come check back in 24h for a linux-beta that may fix my issue; checked in the next day and the Dev actually solved the issue that fast, I just finished playing it now on a linux OS with no issues whatsoever. In short Great game from a great Dev, don't miss it if you're into the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I *loved* this game.I was already hyped for the game ever since it was announced. i played the previous titles in the "Cayne-verse" and they were really good. This game is another descent into abyssal depths (literally), but it adds another layer to the proceedings, thanks to the characters. You control not just one, but three main characters, two of which have special skills, which makes the puzzles a bit more intricate.But in addition to the mechanical aspect, I also started to care deeply about them (Moses <3), which really surprised me. I attribute this not only to the stellar writing but also to the superb voice acting. The previous titles had strong main characters, but if i remember correctly, they didn't get a lot of chances to interact with other people, which puts a limit on just how much you can actually get to know their thoughts and emotions. Another thing I liked were the PDA logs. Normally, I don't *love* reading in games, but the way it was done here contributed immensely to the world building. They didn't feel fake, they seemed like personal diary entries of people that knew each other and you learn about their relationships, if you want to. Like a puzzle, you can figure out what happened. Or you can just skip it, of course. Obviously, this game has some technical limitations, due to the fact that the developers are a truly miniscule team. The perspective does put some distance between you and what's going on - but for me, personally, that was more of an advantage. What you cannot see can actually be more terrifying than what you can. And there are cinematic sequences in crucial moments, so you get to see the characters up close and personal. Which is not to say that the game is not visually interesting. There are really amazing pieces of scenery and the animations are really well done. The sound design also contributes to the atmosphere of dread and horror.Anyway, what The Brotherhood pulled off here, is nothing short of a miracle. Not just in the sense of "for an indie dev". This is just a truly great game. Period.It's an improvement over the previous titles, why holding on to their strengths. I wish this game a ton of success, if only for the egotistical motive that I'd like to see more from this dev team.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I played through this game in an utterly intense couple of sessions. I can't recommend it highly enough. Everything about this gripped me like the finest of horror and science fiction movies. Several scenes shocked and stunned me at a visceral level, and at least a few scenes near the end brought genuine tears to my eyes. I don't want to talk too much about the plot for fear of spoilers, but it deals with themes of loss, grief and mortality like few other games I've played. The three central characters are played to perfection by excellent actors - as are further supporting characters, who I will not be forgetting any time soon. Aside from some minor quibbles on a graphical level with the final area in the game, everything here looks amazing. The isometric perspective snakes and coils around a diverse and impressive range of maritime architecture, and the highly detailed short CG cut-scenes deserve full praise for capturing emotion so well. The inventory system, which shares items between characters in different areas, took some mental adjustment. It is neatly woven into the narrative and puzzle structure however, and a late game scene utilises it to great effect.The influence of Disco Elysium can be felt in some of the writing and presentation, and there are many nods to classic horror adventure games such as Sanitarium as well. Fans of both will find plenty to enjoy here.

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is a horror point-and-click adventure game from The Brotherhood. It is set in the same universe as their previous games, Stasis and Cayne, but stands alone in its narrative. The game starts with our protagonists' ship bobbing violently inside a raging storm. Within the darkness, a shape beckons—an oil rig that seems to be abandoned, with "DEEPSEA 15" written on the decaying metal hull. This is the stage where the horror to come will unfold.Right after the fantastic opening cinematic, we take control of our first protagonist, Mac. The game promptly teaches us how to point and click to direct where Mac is going, as well as how to interact with his surroundings. The ping helps highlight interactable objects and entrances/exits of each screen.As Mac exits the ship, he is met with an unrelenting storm pelting away endlessly on the deck, and the oil rig stands silently, waiting to be boarded. Getting inside the rig's interior is Mac's first objective, but he can't do it alone. The game then shifts to other protagonists, Charlie and Moses. Mac can use his brute strength to snap objects in two, Charlie can jury-rig machinery with her expertise, and Moses, as a sentient teddy bear powered by advanced AI, can hack into computers. Using each character's abilities is key to delving deeper into Deepsea 15. Thankfully, all the items and clues they gather can conveniently be shared with each other using their Quantum Storage Device, which acts as a pocket dimension of shared inventory, no matter how far apart the protagonists are.Puzzles come in a few different forms, but essentially, Bone Totem is a point-and-click adventure game where you need to use the right object in your inventory on something in the game's screen. Occasionally, you have to solve logic puzzles, like figuring out a password to a safe by cracking a code. The puzzles never veer into moon logic territory, but they can be quite tough, so you need to be thorough. The three protagonists keep the pace fresh because if you feel stuck with one character, it's effortless to switch characters and explore other areas to gather more jigsaw pieces. Sometimes, failing to properly solve these puzzles results in a failure state that leads to tragic deaths of our characters, but the game autosaves before death scenes trigger, so failure is never punished.A beautifully morbid part of Bone Totem, as with the other entries in this world, are the suicide scenes. These are bonus, fully animated CGI cutscenes where we can watch our avatars disemboweled, burned, crushed, and die in gruesome ways. Unlike regular death scenes, these aren't failure states. The CGI videos only trigger by using a specific combination of items in the right place and time. They are very easy to miss, and it's up to the players to seek them out. They've become the unique flavor of the series because they allow me to act on the intrusive thoughts I occasionally have, and I absolutely love them.Like the gameplay, Bone Totem's plot is something the players have to piece together. As our heroes descend further, they uncover remains—remains of people who once walked the metallic halls of Deepsea 15, remains of their thoughts transcribed into digital logs. Each piece falls slowly into place on the board, as our protagonists learn of the actions made by people before them and how the past cascaded into consequences that our trio must deal with.Carrying the passive method of storytelling from PDA logs, our characters actively relive the current events before them. They are expertly written and voice-acted, vividly delivering their various states of emotion. Even though the game is littered with violence and despair, there are still warm moments and funny jokes that legitimize their bonds from their past, carried into the present. After all, these characters have nothing but each other and a little ironic jest to dampen the lunacy around them.The plot of Bone Totem definitely reaches a huge and satisfying crescendo, and I savored the afterglow of the exploding emotions I experienced while playing this game. On a more objective note, the satisfaction of this journey directly scales with how involved the players are. I spent a good chunk of time analyzing every log and constructing my own timeline of events. I realize not every player is willing to be this involved, and they might be left confused about the broader plotline that took place before the game began.Based on their track records, I feel it is safe to say that the Bischoff Brothers are virtuosos of video game setpieces. The pre-rendered isometric view doesn't detract from the godly amount of detail in the game's world. Scattered appliances in living spaces abandoned by their owners, wild floral growth bursting out of airlocked containment experimental labs—each screen in the game tells a little story of its own for players willing to spare the time to absorb all the details.The beautiful backgrounds aren't where the developers' skills peak. Their true mastery shines through in the portrayal of body horror and the aftermath of great carnage. The images presented are hauntingly horrifying. They challenge the limits of how much human flesh and bones can be twisted and stretched without being unnecessarily edgy. Bone Totem doesn't shy away from depicting the cruelest violence and the deepest despair, presenting them as an important part of this world. This is where the horror stems from. Unlike survival horror, the characters are almost never in real danger; the feeling of dread is carried by two pillars: Bone Totem's storytelling and visual design.If visuals and storytelling are the pillars of the game, then the audio design is the arch connecting these pillars, creating a support that forms the basis of the game's entire structure. The audio is crafted with the same care and attention as the rest of the game. As you go deeper into the facility, the distant echo of heavy metal creaking heavily reminds you that these rust-speckled metal walls are the only thing standing between you and thousands of tons of water pressure.The music provides a proper ambiance that enhances the uneasiness. As previously mentioned, the characters' emotions are beautifully portrayed through superb voice work. Kudos to the team for finding and directing such talented individuals with limited resources.Stasis: Bone Totem is a dreadful game. It made me experience many swirling emotions while playing, and that's certainly high praise for a linear horror game with no survival elements. In my opinion, the game is a masterpiece, and I will die crucified on that hill. If you hate puzzles, I would still recommend you to try this game and use a guide because the sum of the game is much greater than each of its parts.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Bone Totem is a shining example of what indie game development should be: a labor of love and a true testament to the passion for the craft. The narrative is compelling and layered, characters are amazing and visuals pay homage to the era where PC gaming was at it's peak. The writing is superb on par with heavy hitting sci-fi movies, weaving a tale that is both engaging and emotionally resonant (Moses really resonated with me.). In a world where so many games are created with profit as the primary motive, Stasis: Bone Totem stands out as a beacon of what can be achieved when developers prioritize passion over profit. The Brotherhood has created something truly special and I wish Chris & Nic Bischoff the best, never stop creating guys. One of my new sci-fi favorites for sure. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very much a hidden gem. Great mixture of sci-fi and cosmic horror with lots of great puzzles strewn throughout. The world building is one of the strong suits as well, throughout the game you learn more about the world, 'Cayne', the bio technology and such. It makes you very curious to learn more about how things came to be and what the future holds for this world.Definitely worth a try for the price! Hope to see more games like this from them in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: So I'll say this: I wouldn't normally recommend games that I had to find myself 'forcing' myself to finish. However, I found a lot of things super impressive in this game. The idea behind it is great and interesting, but the execution was just not what it could have been to make a full formed product.It looks great, visually impressive, even so much of the dark and gore like stuff littered around the levels are tastefully done. (Even if some of the images could be subject to copyright... I saw the facehugger and chest burster guys. Alien's might have a few words to say). Gameplay is simple for point and click, but somehow feels convoluted at times. Even with hints littered around, some puzzles didn't make since. While others were so obvious that I put together the solution item together well before I could use it.The main thing that bother me was how slow everything moved. Dialogue, traversal, cutscenes. All set to a snails pace it feels. When a character is injured, the over acting pain turns into a slow text crawl while listening to heavy static and forced dialogue. Not to mention that the ability to interact with anything gets taken away when a random line from the other characters is triggered. And sometimes you never know when they will trigger multiple times just by moving a small bit into a new room. I found myself skipping conversations towards the last 20-30 minutes of the game because I would know exactly what to do but the game kept repeating the thing that I needed to do. And  that ties into the one character I wanted to love, found myself connecting with, just for them to turn around and crush it by having Moses repeat the same lines over and over. I get it, child's toy, but it's a child's toy with what I assume is a super computer in it. I don't need it repeated so much, especially  when in a section where one of the 'hurt' characters talks to him super slow. I was just kinda burned out on the game by that point.Again the game has gems to it. It's beautiful, it's got a style and does it well, simple mechanics (well could be tweaked to make moving to an object or thru a room faster), but the one thing that killed it for me was the dialogue. I'm sure that sucks to say when the voice actors did such a damn good job (most the time). It was a chore to finish at the end but I recommend any one to try it for themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this one a positive review even though I'm really not into the point and click genre. It falls into a few of the pitfalls associated with the genre, particularly stretching its playtime and a few obscure puzzle solutions. However, the writing is fairly solid, the story was intriguing enough to keep me going, and the atmosphere is spot on in most cases. The asking price feels about right for what I got and I feel like I came out a little ahead getting it on sale. Definitely a good pick up if you're into this type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I am usually not a person who pre-order games or buy them on release. I’ve only done it with Metro Exodus and Stray and both games were amazing from day 1. In the case of Stasis Bone Totem I was even more confident in the developers so I made a decision to back the game! I am glad that I did, because after over 10 hours of gameplay (I am not finished with it yet), I must say that Stasis Bone Totem is extremely fun to play, very polished and most importantly, highly atmospheric. If you like modern point and click games and games like Bioshock, Dead Space, Alien Isolation, you will love this game.Another reason why I am so excited to play it is because I am somewhere in the game! I haven’t found myself yet, but hopefully I will soon so we can talk about me a bit more in this review 🙂I think we have an adept for game awards here. If Disco Elysium could do it, I don’t see why Stasis Bone Totem couldn’t!Give it a try. For a very reasonable price you will get an amazing indie game which is actually working well on release.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis Bone Totem is a disappointment. It's pretty, has great sound and decent voice acting.Characters will constantly talk, even if the voice acting is good it detracts from the atmosphere here.Puzzles are classic point and click puzzles, meaning I could not solve them without a guide, good on the devs for including one in the game folder.You switch between three characters, two of which have unique abilities to use on every item/item combination. Even when the game puts time pressure on one character none is felt. You have to get items for her while playing as the other characters, taking ages to do so. I suppose these take place simultaneously but this reasoning does not help in the moment.I just don't really like where the story went, that it really drags its feet. I didn't like one of the player characters, nor the few NPCs you encounter and talk to.

_childDocuments_.review: Another amazing game from Stasis makers. Fantastic art, smart puzzles (no silly adventure game logic here), excellent writing and strong characters. It's a rare game that can entice feelings of anxiety, pride, disgust, hope, sadness and joy in an emotional 10h rollercoaster. Highly recommended to all adventure game fans!

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent adventure game. The puzzle logic starts to go awry near the end, but the plot delivers and the presentation is top notch!It isn't an horror game. It's a dark and gory family drama in a sci-fi setting, though. Don't buy it expecting an Isometric Dead Space. It isn't that type of game.But everything the game promises, it executes with excellence. Another slam dunk for the Brotherhood!

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Yes, as long as you enjoy sci-fi point and click adventures. For me, this is the best pnc adventure of the year.Just interested in point and click advenures? Find all on Steam here: You play Charlie and her husband Mac, a highly indebited couple operating a salvage ship. They work together like every couple, Charlie can repair or combine items, Mac can break or crush them. The couple is soon joined by an annoying teddy bear with hacking skills. The story starts when they find an abandoned oil rig, or at least something looking like that, somewhere in the ocean, of course during the night and during a rainy storm. They board the rig and begin to search it for stuff to loot. It looks to have been abandoned quite hastily, with equipment lying around everywhere. Was this really an oil rig? Reinforced steel doors? Lots of damaged infrastructure, and of course you soon encounter mutilated bodies.... what has happened here? It would be time to go home... but you need the money! Even when it goes down deep, into an underwater facility where an experiment seems to have failed terribly...You do not press a hotspot key to magically show you all available hotspots, but you have a computer (a quantum storage device, QSD) on your shoulder which pings the environment and shows you hotspots to examine or interact. Green hotspots just give you something to read, while the blue hotspots show you places where you actually have to do something. Works quite good once you understood how it functions. Your QSD also allows your characters to communicate with each other, and it allows you to transfer items between them over a distance. You will do this a lot. It makes sense to give all items to the character you are currently controlling. The gameplay is more or less the usual point and click adventure stuff - exploring the sourroundings, reading descriptions, using items on each other and on hotspots, solving puzzles. What makes the game great is the slick user interface and especially the atmosphere. The graphics are fantastic - dark, detailled and well animated. An eerie soundtrack supports the feeling of danger and suspense. The descriptions are well written, also not too long but also not too short. Messages on PDAs that lie around help you understand what happened, you can also find collectables lying in remote places. You can die, even quite violently, but the game allows you to continue before your fatal mistake. Saving is possible any time if you need a break. Enjoy fully voiced characters, ultrawidescreen is supported, playing with controller also works fine. I found no bugs, only sometimes I was shown controlller buttons to press while playing with the mouse. All in all, I haven't enjoyed exploring an abandoned station so much since... Stationfall (Infocom, 1987). This game gives me the same vibes, and also reminds me of Ridley Scott's Alien or John Carpenter's The Thing. The game takes place in the Stasis universe (Stasis, Cayne), but you do not need to have played the older games to enjoy this one.Very well presented horror sci-fi point and click adventure. Explore an abandoned oil rig in the middle of the ocean during a dark, stormy night. Of course the rig is not what it seems to be - something terrible has happened here and might still be around.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: The horror, the (gorgeous, atmospheric) horror...Went in the jaded hero of a hundred daytime-tv narratives, nodding my head and making 'jerk-off' motions at the wrist at what I thought were just so many classic tropes. Then, like the man caught in quicksand, I only realized too late what the writers and voice-actors had accomplished-- got me! Got me Jonesing to figure out wtf is going on and what is coming down the pipe. Even got me to tear up.As far as the story: you'll enjoy this more if you, like me, are into the 'well-everybody's-dead-but-boy-they-kept-articulate-diaries' story-telling style of Bram Stoker's 'Dracula.' The world-building is kept at the periphery but keeps entering the story in interesting ways. There's your Weyland-Yutani-style megacorp, 'Cayne' (which has it's own church!?! and has built digital heaven!?!) vs an organization called Yellow Leaf. (Digging into the nature of this relationship has got me wanting to play the other 'Stasis' games.) There are several stories which begin as what might be throwaway sketches only to muscle their way into our heroes' lives. As far as the game play: I don't usually play point-and-click-- or even puzzle games in general-- so if you're an officianado feel free to disregard. My move was to try to brute-force a lot of the puzzles and I was occasionally rewarded but more frequently stalled out. Then I would take a breath, look around, try a different character for a while, wander, find a clue in the environment, and the light bulb would go off. Quite satisfying in many cases. Psychotically frustrating in others. I am pleased to state that I was only forced to utilize the (free, easy-to-access) cheat guide once... or maybe twice. The devs say use it if you need to to get the whole story and I would agree with that.As far as the horror, the horror: yeah, good ♥♥♥♥. Hell, the bear friend had an uncanny-valley thing that unsettled me for a while (but finally I couldn't help myself and I became fond of the bear). A lot of gnarly body horror and bio-tech nastiness and bloated corpses and things of the deep. There's some psychological horror which our man Faran bears up (ha ha) heroically under. There's cannabalism and indentured servitude and subcutaneous crawler buddies. All lovingly brought to life.Which I think is why I'm writing this review when I don't usually write video game reviews: the love and craftsmanship of the devs is so evident in this one. Stasis: Bone Totem is fun to play and kept me very entertained for 20 hours. But it's also has got that je ne sais quoi that keeps you thinking about it after you're done. I think they call that, 'art,' baby!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that absolutely loved the original Stasis game, I was surprised and excited when the sequel was announced. I'm happy to say the sequel not only lived up to the original, but surpassed it in many aspects for me. The irony is that I'm someone that hates games with a lot of puzzles, and this game is 90 percent puzzles.. But the atmosphere and story are just so good, that even someone who hates puzzles will likely love this game.  Pros:- Excellent well crafted narrative. - Likable characters that are easy to get attached too.- Exceptional voice acting.- Atmospheric and immersive world. - Top notch sound. - Great performance (I played on the ROG Ally, and it was perfect).- Great support for controllers, a rarity for these type of games.Cons:- Some puzzles are really nonsensical. - Zooming not supported for controllers (at the time of this review).- I don't like how the descriptions of things automatically appears on screen with controller, because after a certain amount of time my brain started automatically ignoring the descriptions. I would rather have the option to walk up to the eye icon, and select X to read the description.. But I could be the only one that feels that way.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was not a fan of the new game-mechanics and characters Stasis 2 ... erm Bone Totem introduced. The way you played multiple characters and had to share different items to solve puzzles was too convoluted... or so I thought.But after a hour or so, it clicked and the game did suck me in like a disturbing vortex of bodily horror, otherworldly halucinations and creepy, really creepy enviroments and storytelling!Imagine "the Thing" and "System Shock" meets "Alien" with rivers of blood and its own thrilling story! Its soooo well written!Everything from the dialogue to the describtions of your surroundings or items, to the texts and photos you find on PDAs or computers screams high quality and effort!It builds a scary but hypnotizing world only a very few games can. And tbh there is no other game in this genre that introduces the horror- and exploration-element in such a powerful atmospheric story-telling like this one and still manages to surprise you with new elements and twists!Some puzzles are a littlebit too complicated and feel a littlebit out of place, but thats just me again.(I did use a Guide when I could not progress despite trying it multiple ways or was too tired after work).If you are not afraid to read and treat this game like a perfect artpiece, made out of fantastic artwork, animations, cutscenes, voiceacting then do yourself a favor and experience it!I still haven't finished the game and I guess I'm relatively far in the story by now, but I can already praise this outstanding piece of art!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part the puzzles are okay, although there are some really poor ones, but the story is very derivative and totally falls to bits towards the end. It's also about as scary as a trip to the dentist and the mountain of PDAs your given to read equates in interest levels to the stack of old periodicals you can browse through while sitting in the waiting room.But the absolute worst thing, and the reason I couldn't finish it is because almost every single step you take triggers character conversations that prevent you from actually playing the game and this only gets more jarring and annoyingly common as you progress. Your mercilessly battered with pointless exposition chatter, being told the same thing over and over and over again in a slightly different flavour until you begin to deeply resent the characters for speaking. I read somewhere that there is an actual achievement for not skipping any dialogue and I really can't say I'm even slightly surprised, as it requires immense levels of stamina and Godlike patience to pull it off. At chapter three I thought I could push through it but by chapter Four, I realised I was actually counting the number of steps I had taken before more BLAH BLAH BLAH WAFFLE WAFFLE WAFFLE!, and I hadn't got higher than four steps yet. I just couldn't take it anymore so started mashing the skip dialogue key, then realised this meant I didn't care anymore so just quit.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful point and click that twitsts into new shapes the familliar bones and guts of Alien, Dead Space, the thing, event horizon. The game is well written, each character are strong and likable.This would be a strong recommendation, unfortunately, the presence of a LOT of AI-generated Art gets in the way. Every now and then, the game will have "lore element" scattered, little items that you can look at, and your eyes will glaze over them, because they were quite clearly  computer generated AI mess with no ryhme nor reason, not supposed to convey any information but just the general vibe of a scientific journal, with the marginalia filled with nonsensical diagrams for things not related to anything they were doing in DS15.A shame as this got in the way of my enjoyment.

_childDocuments_.review: Was initially put off by the gratuitous displays of gore, but as I got deeper into the game and hearing about their other titles I figured they aren't completely senseless, just dissonance within the established setting. Something newcomers should realize going in is that Bioengineering in the world of Stasis is just remarkably loose and unbound by ethics, even by corporate dystopian standards, people in the game are just appropriately desensitized to a certain level of body horror.One of my gripes is how much you're struggling to view the maps in poor lighting. It fits the atmosphere but does not contribute well to map playability, and you're forced to rely on the ping system which detracts a bit from the immersion. They do put a lot of work inserting observables that describe the environments at great detail, though as someone who reads every text I come across it gets a bit excessive at times and slows down the story beats. They often contain surprisingly flowery language that I'm not sure really fits a horror title, but then again I don't really read horror novels to really know what to expect.Difficulty for an adventure point and click is reasonable for someone who've played a bit of them. I have gotten stuck, but most of the time the hint dialogue is sufficient for me to beat the game without a walkthrough.The cast of characters are the true highlight of the game. I enjoyed the story arcs of the 3 playable protagonists and the entire cast had superb delivery in their voice acting. While its no SOMA in the realm of existential horror and philosophy there is a strong undercurrent of the tenacity of the human spirit in the face of trauma, something I enjoy and resonate with.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the experience of the game, but I felt there was a lot that kept me from enjoying the actual playing of Stasis Bone Totem. The story, characters, setting and worldbuilding, all of this works wonders and lends to a really intense experience that drew genuine gasps of shock from me. I felt rattled, and that was something a game hasn't managed to do for me in ages. definitely there are scenes and conversations that will stay with me and have let their mark.For the most part this is a vast improvement from Stasis, it is worth your time.One the gameplay, though, there's a lot that didn't work for me. I don't hate point n click or puzzle games, and I enjoy them from time to time, but I found myself drained quickly by this one. There's a good amount of haziness about things, uncertainty and moon logic both make their appearances here. Near the start of the game a character makes a comment about doing something, and I assumed this was a death flag for a gruesome death. Turns out it was the right way to go, and later the opposite was true. Besides this, my other complaint is the logs. They feel very formulaic and take a lot away from the feeling of humanity in the game. There's more wordlbuilding, but it feels like the world is inhabited my generic sci-fi characters. That is, interesting world, mundane characters. Each log is fairly summed up as "Gee, dystopia blows" -> "How could they do this to me?" -> "Ah, the horrors!". Again, I enjoyed the experience of this game. These complaints may seem petty and counter to that, but I enjoyed parts of the game so much that the parts I didn't enjoy felt all the more painful. I really wish this had been a book, that I could pour over the descriptions and dialogues again and again and generate the imagery in my head.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: It's really hard to be scared in a horror game when you're too frustrated over the obtuse puzzles with solutions that only make sense in the devs' heads. As a player, how are you suppose to know that embalming fluid is to be combined with a lighter to make a flame thrower? You're just suppose to know, OK?! Some of the puzzles are logical and well made, but a lot require such leaps in logic that I'm surprised made it into the game. The golden rule in making a good horror game is that good horror games are about player immersion first and foremost. This game is constantly taking you out of the immersion by reminding you that it's just a video game with it's lousy and gamey puzzles. How are you supposed to be immersed in a horror experience when you are busy being frustrated and alt-tabbing for solutions?

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like it. First Stasis was really good, and I was hoping that next one will be similar but better. But they had to introduce some big changes in game play. Now you are in control not one character but two. And this breaks immersion for me. I can't tune in when I need to switch between two characters in two different locations.I just can't, in case of horror games I need a single character. Then it get worse, you can teleport items between the characters. There is no logic in that, it just happens. If you want to check what items you can interact with, you need to "ping" first, ant by ping I mean to shoot eye gouging bright blue and green lasers across whole screen. And you need to do it quite often, because highlighted items don't stay like that for very long. Graphic in game is too sharp and because of that textures on characters are noisy. GUI somehow stands up from game graphics too, it feels off. But what convince my to return the game was first puzzle, I just couldn't figure it out at all. And I finished first Stasis with joy.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Bone Totem did not disappoint!  It continues the Stasis series' commitment to being the darkest, most unsettling, and horrific point & click adventure games possible.  This was a very intense game for me to play.I was really impressed by the structure of Bone Totem.  The gameplay is split between three characters, each on their own part of the adventure.  Despite being in different areas, they aren't on  adventures and are working together to make progress.  This game design is ingenious.  I assume it has probably been done before in some other adventure game, but Bone Totem is the first I've seen it.  All three characters are always in contact with each other and can freely exchange items.Moving items between all the characters' inventory is an outstanding new mechanic that is elegantly justified in the STASIS canon.  It's an extension of the Quantum Storage Device that was introduced in the very first game, STASIS.  Two of the characters can act upon inventory items: one can combine two items and the other can separate an item into multiple items.The third character is very, very strange and utterly,  bizarre.  But over the course of the story I grew to really like him.I enjoyed the large amount of dialogues and conversations in Bone Totem, which are the main way the story is told.  The voice acting is emotional and each actor has an interesting voice.  I've got to say, though: the woman, Charlie, could be hard to listen to with all the breathing and sucking sounds in her very raw performance.  It reminded me of the main character in Days Gone, but thankfully without all the wet mouth noises he made.I took a lot of notes about Bone Totem and there's so much more I could say about what I though and felt about it.  But nobody cares about all that.  Just have your own experience with it.  I'm glad The Brotherhood is keeping high-quality 2D adventure gaming alive.  Their non-STASIS game, BEAUTIFUL DESOLATION, is already in my library for me to play in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry.  That's not a fear thing, they snuck in a really strong emotional arc underneath the horror writing.I'll start out with arguably the worst aspect first: mechanically, it's pretty good, though for me it comes short of being fantastic.  The puzzles generally felt like they made sense...after the fact.  It does a good job of avoiding the moon logic you sometimes get from adventure games, the answer is at least something that makes sense with the resources available.  I can't recall ever feeling like there was a much more straightforward solution the characters should have been able to do.  That fact doesn't always do you any good while you're in the middle of trying to solve one however.  There's a ping system that mostly addresses the problem of pixel-hunting, though there's the occasional screen where you might not realize there's something to pick up, so you forget to check it.  There are also sometimes places where what you need from a screen isn't a item but a number written somewhere, and the ping system cannot help you there, since it really only finds interactibles.The biggest issue with puzzles, for me at least, was that it was often unclear exactly what puzzle I was supposed to be solving.  Sometimes everything came together, sometimes not.  Part of the way the game builds puzzles, is throwing several obstacles at you but you'll only find what you need for one of them in the moment, and then part of the challenge is figuring out which puzzle you can solve.  Particularly when mixed with the possibility that some items or solutions are things you might not find at first glance, it's possible to be stuck by way of not knowing which puzzle is the one you need to solve in the moment, or if there's an item you need to find that you missed on first pass.  I'll note it's not possible permanently miss an item, from what I could see the way the game is structured it won't let you pass points of no return without everything you need, but it is possible to get stuck in the sense of having no idea which puzzle means current progress or if you need to find info, an item or a combination you haven't chanced or happened upon yet.If nothing else the devs posted a guide that's as story-free as possible, so if some bit of gameplay is getting in the way of you enjoying the story it's simple enough to track down a way forward.I do want to give them credit for the Quantum Storage Device, returning from the previous game and now with increased function with the ability to pass items between characters.  It's a novel way to approach point-and-click inventory, and they do some interesting things with it.The visuals I generally liked.  Every so often you can see something that's rough around the edges, where the movement is a little bit stiff or something's a little disjointed.  As often as not though it adds to the uncanny feel of everything, and in general I thought it worked well.  It gives a sense of efficiency, in a way, taking full advantage of the fact that it's an adventure game to make static backgrounds and interaction screens go a long way.The visuals are hauntingly beautiful.  I don't really have a lot to say about them, I just like the design and atmosphere.  A good mix of lived-in or reasonable, with intrusions of horror or decay, with the balance between them shifting as the story demands.I should perhaps note, if you're looking to be scared in a conventional way, the game probably won't get your heart rate up and nothing ever really jumps at you.  So if that's what you're looking for from horror, you'll probably be disappointed.  It's definitely a horror game, but the horror is more how awful what you're seeing is, and the implications of it, and what it means for characters to be stuck in the situations they're in.  Many of the visuals and scenes a absolutely grisly, there's just nothing that jumps out or makes a loud noise.  I love the atmosphere of the whole thing.The writing is what really got me.  The dialogue is tight, everything fit the characters, nothing got annoying, everything feeling really distinct to the character speaking.  The voice acting I found universally good.  The only real complaints I have are nitpicks: sometimes the subtitles will come out more slowly than the characters speaking, particularly for short lines; and sometimes you can move through a room while dialogue is playing, but you'll be unable to move rooms while dialogue is playing.  This can conflict with the sense of urgency otherwise in the scene.I don't know how much I could talk about the story itself, or rather how much I'd want to.  It's paced phenomenally, starting in an ordinary if tense situation, and then gradually building up the horrific elements, to really develop that sense that your characters are way out of their depth, but don't have a choice but to press on anyways.  At the same time, they're almost secretly building up an emotional arc underneath it, not quite hiding it but leaving it out of focus enough that when it came back to the fore in the climax I wasn't quite expecting it, and it hit me extra hard.If you really don't like adventure games, I don't think this will be the one to win you over.  If you want to be scared, feel your heart pounding in your chest in anticipation, that's not really what this is going for either.  But, if you're looking for something with a great atmosphere or story, I can't recommend this enough.  It's a game that will stick with me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of THE BROTHERHOOD for a long time ever since the first STASIS came out, I was captivated by the atmosphere, the story and the grotesque horrific scenery. Bone Totem has been a project I've been long waiting to play and now here it is. So what do I think so far? I'm currently in the middle of chapter II and while this game seem familiar to the previous titles, it really sells the story and characters well and the graphics along with U.I. has been improved a lot.I really like the deep sea exploration setting, it kind of reminds me of SOMA, but that would be an unfair comparison.All in all, This is a title I'll do my best to finish, despite the daunting puzzles, but that's pretty much a skill issue of mine.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful, thrilling and dark adventure this was! I've played every single The Brotherhood game and this one did not disappoint either. The devs have improved their craft a lot since the first STASIS game from 2015. I liked the characters, the fact that you have three protagonists each with their abilities and how you can switch around items with ease. The story felt multilayered that had its own unexpected twists and turns (although I did kinda predict a couple of them, being familiar with their previous games). Gory and bloody deaths that felt like fun secrets you had to unlock instead of something annoying and frustrating you had to deal with by saving a lot. The environments, animations, 3D models and cinematics were all great. Definitely one of the best adventure games of 2023!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is a spine-tingling masterpiece that delivers an unforgettable journey into the realms of horror and mystery. From the moment you step foot into its eerie world, you're engulfed by an atmosphere dripping with tension and dread. The game's haunting visuals, coupled with its immersive sound design, plunge you into a nightmarish adventure where every shadow hides a sinister secret.But it's not just the atmosphere that shines in Stasis: Bone Totem – its storytelling is equally compelling. As you unravel the dark mysteries surrounding the ancient totems and the sinister forces at play, you'll find yourself drawn deeper into a web of intrigue and terror. The narrative twists and turns keep you on the edge of your seat, eager to uncover the truth lurking in the darkness.Yet, what truly sets Stasis: Bone Totem apart is its gameplay. The clever puzzles and spine-chilling encounters keep you engaged and challenged throughout your journey, while the intuitive controls ensure that every moment feels fluid and immersive.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's grim, atmospheric game with somewhat lackluster puzzles and a rather weak story.Pro:Neutral:Con:It's great to see The Brotherhood growing, and their games are always a neat diversion from classical point&click pattern. And while I'm looking forward their next installment, I wish Stasis: Bone Totem was less focused on delivering horror and a bit more on conveying a believable story and maybe a smarter ending (as Beautiful Desolation did). The  beared so much potential for some nice plot-twists, but it was just dropped in favor of some more blood and torture and monsters and saving the world.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, a masterclass in how to craft a point and click game. Loved the story, loved the lore, the sci fi elements were all very well put together and some genuinely horrifying moments. Music and visuals were great, length was the perfect amount before feeling burned out. The only real criticism I can think of is some of the solutions to certain puzzles were far too vague, and can take a while to figure out when the solution can be related to any of the 3 characters locations. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games I wish there was a neutral rating for. Every person who specifically looks for Lovecraftian horror knows that feeling of dread, hopelessness and the unknown that made his books so unique. Not many games have been able to capture those feelings. This is where this games shines the most. You will find out things that make you reflect of what it would be like if something like this would happen as we speak, in regions we have not yet explored. The story as a whole is pretty good and keeps you hooked for what happens next.The gameplay, however, is definitely not my cup of tea. I had to google 50% of the game or I would have never have guessed on what to do, especially when combining/ripping off stuff. Like a syringe filled with some necrotic goop and a lighter makes a flamethrower so you can burn a huge tower of torsos, arms and legs out of the way. There are multiple such cases where I was really lost on what to do, eventually it grew so frustrating that I just gave up and basically cheesed the rest of the puzzles.If not for the story, needless to say I would have stopped playing long before. Maybe these types of games are not my cup of tea and I haven't played that many of them. It kept me hooked nonetheless until the end so I hover more towards recommend, especially if you like Lovecraft. Also, RIP Moses. You were a very smart, strong and courageous bear.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my favorite brand of horror. It is tragic, malicious, and unnerving. I really loved the story and the experience as a whole, even if it absolutely broke my heart at times. Voice acting is great and the mechanics work smoothly with only very minor hiccups here and there.Overall, I'd give the game an 8/10 overall. Definitely recommend to fans of bears, puzzles, isometric gameplay, and good horror.The following are the only 2 major complaints I had with the game:1. While most progression is pretty intuitive, despite requiring some thought, there were occasional progression moments where I felt incredibly frustrated and felt like I was spending way too much time going back and forth between characters to figure out what the hell I was supposed to do next. I almost never use guides, but there were a couple times when I almost felt like it was needed. A great, spoiler-free example is when a character refused to do something, but then after an event decided they would after all. At no point did the game even hint that the character had changed their mind. I am a very smart bear, but having your characters just retry everything over and over again after every bit of progression is not a super intuitive or fun way for a game to be experienced.2. Sometimes I felt that the dialogue mechanic was purposely annoying. While dialogue is active, you can move, but you can't interact with anything or move screens. This wouldn't be a huge issue if there wasn't CONSTANT dialogue every 5 seconds. The game gives you the option to skip dialogue (semi-slowly), but when characters are supposedly in a rush and you have to manually skip like 10 lines of dialogue or just wait for them to finish before you can move to the next area that you supposedly NEED to RUSH to, it breaks immersion and enjoyment a bit. An especially annoying version of this mechanic is a section where 2 holograms argue with each other every time you get near them. This always results in at least 4 things of dialogue that you have to skip or listen to before you can do anything else. As this game requires you to go back and forth a lot, and this was an area I crossed at least 6 times, that especially was an annoying design choice.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a loooong time since I played a point and click adventure game that grabbed me as hard as this did. A dollop of John Carpenter, a dash of Ridley Scott, a pinch of HR Geiger, bake with cyber punk and you get Stasis Bone Totem. On the surface as you go in, you feel like you already have a good idea of whats going on, the usual 'Corporate Greed, dug too deep, ignored human safety to experiment with unknown alien thing and a hapless team stumbles across it, ignoring all the signs of something nightmarish' etc etc. But as it goes on it becomes a fair bit clearer that there's more to the story than that. The voice acting is stellar, and what a relief because few things can kill a game like this as fast as bad VA performance/direction, but the primary characters are fantastic. Initially, some of the dialogue can feel stilted, particularly from Moses, (A very smart, strong and brave bear) but over time as you come to understand him, it becomes endearing. The character's relationships also grow in response to the events as they occur in a way that feels organic. Faran in particular is a fantastically written character and his interactions with Moses didn't tug so much as wrench at my heartstrings as the game neared the end. Graphics are some of the best I've seen from an adventure game, and the sound design is solid, if a little bland. Mostly ambient tracks, the occasional spooky sound or song (Twinkle Twinkle little star being whistled etc.) As for the meat of the game, the puzzles, I'm glad to say they were just a scant few times I had to resort to looking up the solution (using a bear trap to open a door never crossed my mind). Aside from a rather onerous waiting puzzle, the majority of the puzzles follow enough of a line of logic that you can usually figure it out for yourself. If you're really stuck, eventually a hint option will pop up while you're looking at a puzzle.The game has some interesting mechanics going for it; you control all three protagonists, Mac, Charlie and Moses independently of one another, with a Quantum Storage Device that allows them to share items between the three of them regardless of where they are. Additionally, Charlie can repair or combine objects using Engineering know how, and Mac can break stuff good. The story is fed to you slowly, and blessedly, without too much of the characters loudly reiterating what they just discovered to spell it out to the player. Additionally, there is a mechanic where by right clicking, the game highlights observation points with descriptions, and interactive objects which is a god send in a game with so much environmental detail that a pixel hunt would be a nightmare plus, it works on the puzzles themselves, so no pixel hunting there either. Overall, Stasis Bone Totem is a fantastic game, certainly the best adventure game I've played in years. Well worth the 20$ asking price and your time.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. The story and atmosphere were brilliant. The puzzles were fun to figure out and made me feel smart that i only had to peak at the guide a couple of times. What impressed me the most was the quality of writing and the character development. I really felt for the characters by the end of it. This is easily the best Stasis game in the series!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is a phenomenal adventure-puzzle game. I only have to tell you to make sure you find "locomotion" in audio settings and set it to zero. It plays a 24/7 corny "spooky sounds" halloween loop in the background that doesn't even really make sense in the game world. Outside of that, the ambiance and sound design otherwise is great. Honestly, one of the best produced puzzle-adventure games I've ever played. From a game mechanics stand point, giving players a highlight option and doing away with "hidden object" shenanigans is something I hope the entire genre takes note of - hard puzzles are great, searching every pixel on a screen - not so fun!-Excellent puzzle designs-Excellent visual design-Excellent writing-Excellent cinematics-No hidden object BS9.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually play puzzle games but the setting has peaked my interest enough to try, and the game truly deserves all the high praise it currently gets. Even though I'm not much of a puzzle enthusiast the puzzles in this game, for the most part, are logical and the in-game hint system does help. The true "meat" of the game is the setting, the characters and the story. The characters have interesting personalities, amazing voice actors and great character/redemption arcs. Story and the setting are exceptional and keep you engaged until the end with its mysteries and twists. An amazing experience that I truly recommend, a brave and strong game.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally, this kinda game ain't my thing - but I am so happy I took the time to play it! Story was good, acting was good, it was free of most of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I remember from playing old adventure games, and the artwork was phenomenal.If you are on the fence, grab this thing on sale and enjoy it for a weekend. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely a breath of fresh air in gaming, no matter how ironic that sounds for a claustrophobic horror game set under the ocean.Heavily inspired by the old-school sci-fi horror media but with a fresh intriguing story and lore, really lovable cast of characters with great chemistry between them and fantastic voice acting in general. The puzzles can be challenging but are never unfair with ridiculous point'n'click logic.I wholeheartedly recommend.Moses is a very smart bear! 🖤
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Bone Totem is amazing!I really liked how well constructed "Stasis (2015)" was for a Point & Click game, then I played Cayne and then Beautiful Desolation, and had high hopes for Bone Totem, after all the praise online.But this exceeded my expectations and I personally would call it the best game in the Point & Click genre!Bone Totem has beautifully crafted environment, claustrophobic atmosphere and superb voice acting.Direct upgrade to Stasis. Playing is a pleasure, though a bit confusing on the beginning, but once you familiarise yourself with the controls, you will be positively overwhelmed!The mystery is highly intriguing and playing 3 protagonists at the same time is just genius!When stuck on one, it is best to switch to the others and progress there, maybe even find an item that will help solve the puzzle that you were stuck on. Really refreshing!The reason why I call Bone Totem one of the very best in the genre, is because all puzzles and solutions are logical and are not plagued by the insane moon logic that has taken over the genre (to artificially prolong the game).Our time and intelligence is respected.Awesome game!P.S. Moses is the bravest and bestest of bears!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely captivating game! The story is the best of 2023 imho. Cryptic. Shocking. The art, the gore, the voice acting, the music, the interface, everything is perfect. But the devs created the puzzles so perfectly, they equally challenging and easy at the same time. I loved the first stasis game, and I absolutely adore this one.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that feels good enough to give the adventure game genre a revival.Shockingly good writing and voice acting, like this is blowing pretty much any game released this year (and maybe this decade) out of the water. Moses is quite possibly the best character I have encountered in any video game.
