_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game.. I'm overwhelmed with feelings and I can't remember the last time I felt like this, nor have I played anything likely to this.The atmosphere and the gameplay are great, it's tense but not frustrating. Some puzzles gave me some challenge, but overall they were creative some not in design but in the gore or art department.The gameplay was well crafted, yet I would say that what kept me going was the story and the charakters.Most the time I loose intrest in games with multiple protagonist, because of the backtracking to transfer items, the boring interactions or wathever bad mechanics plague such games, but in this one the multiple protagonists intertwined with the fascinating story reacting to everything there's here or discussiong their previous life making them feel real people is what kept me going. Moses was my favourite but Mac, and Charlie are relatable too.I think I will buy this game for some of my friends for christmas, the game is worth full price. The devs deserve full payment.

Now that  Bone Totem is even better then both of the précis games. The atmosphere is spot on, feels kind of like alien and the thing in some places. Creepy atmosphere the entire playthrough . _childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I guess this one deserve a thumb up even if it's not without flaws.The story was compelling and I really enjoyed unveiling all the weird ♥♥♥♥ going on as you progress deeper and deeper. The voice acting is good, most of the dialogues are fairly well written and our three main protagonists have very distinct personalities which make them authentic and endearing.Regarding the Gameplay, the game mechanics are rather standard. You pick up items, and you use them to solve puzzles. You can dismantle or combine them, which can create other items, nothing hyper fancy but it's alright.There is a system that highlights point of interest around you, that's cool because it prevents the struggle of some Point and Click games where you're stuck because you didn't find the 2 pixels trigger for an important interaction. This will not happen in Bone Totem, the game doesn't hide anything from you... and that also might be a shortcoming. Why explore if all the important elements are already displayed on the screen? I had this "Walking simulator" vibe from time to time when the game felt more like following tracks rather than really being involved regarding the decision-making.Maybe what this game lacks is a bit more novelty in the Point and Click genre. Multiple paths, multiple solutions, multiple endings, choices with consequences... branching and player agency basically. I felt often disconnected from the stakes because I had no control over nothing, and I think like a few mechanics to make us more involved as a Player could have been a great plus.Regardless, it's a good experience that shines more for its artistic quality than for its gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Performs very well on the Steam Deck, getting about 4 hours of playtime on one full charge.I don't like the cycling through the points of interest when playing with a controller. I think Disco Elysium did that better, where you can manually move towards the point of interest with the right thumbstick, instead of random cycle with R2 until you get what you want to see.Also, I spent the first half hour trying to understand the controls, as there is no Tutorial at the beginning, which was a bit frustrating.Otherwise, ignoring the things whom I would be happy to see for the next game (and I WANT another one!!!):An amazing Game. Brutal and Dark Art-Style. Great story too.I think I am a fan of the Brotherhood devs now, because I just had to buy the first Stasis too after Bone Totem. I did not play many Point and Click adventures so far, because most of them are not the horror gore type, which is just a great ambient to experience some kind of "fear".After Bone Totem, I went for CAYNE and could see how the Controls and Quality of Life improved. I hope they keep that up with their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: STASIS: BONE TOTEM is a point-and-click adventure that brilliantly revives the spirit of the classic games in this genre. It's a journey filled with mystery, horror, and mechanical puzzles that will keep you engaged from start to finish.I agree, the game is Very Positive.The game's high-definition pre-rendered visuals are a standout feature, reminiscent of the classic point-and-click games from yesteryears. You follow the story of a married couple, Mac and Charlie, and their AI Super-Toy™ Bear Moses, as they explore an abandoned ocean oil refinery. The narrative takes a thrilling turn as they descend deeper into the ocean floor. Saying more would spoil the mystery.The gameplay involves controlling the three characters simultaneously, each in different areas, helping each other to unlock mechanical puzzles and progress through the story. The puzzles are satisfying to solve, and the game even includes a walkthrough for those particularly tricky moments.I would say that this game is ‘Chill’. There are no enemies to fight and no timed events – even if it looks like it, it is not. The characters can die, but you only witness them ones as part of some failed puzzle attempts or deliberately doing something you are advised not to do. (Find them and get achievements!)STASIS: BONE TOTEM is a compelling game that excellently blends the charm of classic point-and-click adventures with modern development. It is sure to captivate and entertain long-time fans of the genre and newcomers.

The visuals in Stasis Bonetotem were beautifully crafted. The attention to detail in the game world was apparent, from the eerie, atmospheric settings to the intricate character designs. It added an immersive quality to the experience, making me feel like I was truly a part of the game's world.While Stasis Bonetotem might not have been a game I'd normally pick up, it managed to win me over with its compelling story and impressive graphics. If you're like me and typically shy away from this type of game, I'd still recommend giving it a shot. You might just find yourself pleasantly surprised, just as I was.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the first game, enjoyed the sequel even more. Really appreciate the tremendous attention to detail the developer puts into the assets and world-building. Great story and characters with rock-solid voice acting (which could be a bit uneven in the first game). Puzzles are very well designed and polished, satisfying most veterans of the genre.One distinguishing feature I appreciate most about these games is that they don't ascribe to the 'less is more' school of horror. Often horror movies/books/games attempt to build tension through various means during most of the story (which may be pretty mundane), leading up to actual 'horrifying' parts at irregular intervals. I definitely appreciate that technique, but that's not what Stasis does; it sets the macabre dial to 11 fairly early on and keeps it there. In lesser games this tack would make the experience cheesy and boring pretty quickly, but not in Stasis, as the creepiness is just so varied and so well presented that the nightmare in the next room will always make you feel something, usually something unpleasant.Major nitpicky complaint is that the plot tried to 'raise the stakes' a bit too much for my liking at the end and filled in too many blanks. Would have preferred if the last 1/4 of the game or so were chopped off with a less grandiose and predictable resolution to the situation the characters found themselves in. Not a huge deal as it's still a great story, just think it could have been better.

_childDocuments_.review: Clocking over 15+ hours, I've finished the game and I can say that I'm quite pleased for what I've got for such a friendly price. I used to write reviews for gaming magazines in the good and old era, and while it has been a LONG while (and my english is rather rusted), let's see if I can get those gears moving, shall we?- The setting is the highest point of Stasis Bone Totem, very few games properly explore or mix sci-fi and the horrors lurking in the depths of the sea and this game nails it perfectly. The backgrounds and visuals are gorgeous, every room you enter is carefully handcrafted and will oftenly have a lot of elements described in omnious detail to fully immerse you in. Great sound and ambience design!- The prequels were incredibly gory and nauseating games that could be too hard to stomach, yet an argument could be made about it being too gratuitious for pure shock value. This sequel still got a TON of blood, body horror with rather invasive funguses and eldritch ruins for those who enjoy it that, but done so in a much more disciplined and thoughful manner for better effect, so it isn't simply trying to make you feel sick for every step you take.- Adventure, point & click, puzzle games oftenly get a lot of pixel hunting and interactibles that you might miss unless you are hovering your mouse over everything, Bone Totem solves this with a ping system that highlights all the important interactibles as blue circles, while everything else, the "extras" like descriptions of the rooms and their elements as green circles. Go blue if you want to progress. Go green if you want to read.- Most of the puzzles are quite intuitive and the characters tend to talk a lot with each other so you can have a good idea of what you are supposed to do. Puzzle games require a lot of abstraction and thinking outside of the boss from part of the player, but Bone Totem never does so in a crazy or nonsensical manner, most puzzles are quite grounded in average rationality, so you don't need to go out of your way to find a solution that might be incredibly dumb or convoluted.- Smooth interactions and navegation with an easy to understand UI and gameplay. One character breaks, opens and bends items with his strenght. Other uses her smarts and technological knowledge to merge two into one. The third character can hack into computers, machines and interfaces. The prequel games were oftenly clunky in many aspects, like puzzles and items that you would try to interact or use, but the game wouldn't register your actions properly so you would be stuck for a long while wondering what you had done wrong. Fortunately, this never happens in Bone Totem and the game was a bug-free experience (at least, in my case)- Horror games tend to be quite lonely experiences, presenting main characters that are chattermouths with a tendency to talk out loud to overcompensate for the lack of dialogue or presence of characters,  --- and this can grate your nerves REAL fast. If you want an example of how bad this can get in a modern game, Amnesia Rebirth was an unsufferable experience with one of the worst characters that I ever had the displeasure to listen to, because she had a grating, cyclical monologue and thus, never learned when to Well, I'm glad to say that unlike other horror games, Bone Totem got a lot of different characters with some quite good voice acting. They've got their own issues, past, traumas to be exposed, bones to be picked, talked and ranted with each other, so you have an actual story and personal developments going on instead of long ass monologues and filler lines.- In the 90's, games of this genre were strictly straighforward and linear. You had puzzles to solve, things to look at, and only one solution, only one path to be found and followed, so failure meant that getting stuck for hours and hours in one place while growing increasingly frustrated until you either gave up or went out like a madman using every single item in your possession on everything... and unfortunately, Bone Totem is one of those.In the last decade, games like Disco Elysium have evolved and moved forward by adapting some RPG elements in the gameplay. By multiple ways to progress and different outcomings for your actions, there's a a ton of extra tidbits to be discovered in new playthoughs. Bone Totem is still like the old games. It is a very fun experience, but once you have played it once, you've seen all of it and your next playthough will be a breeze with nothing new to be found...... and if DO you get stuck, well, be ready to use your items everywhere, switch characters, backtrack to check everything again or just look for the solution in a youtube video.- The solution for many puzzles can oftenly found written and draw somewhere and won't require any logical thinking at all, you only need enough brainpower to take a screenshot or snap a pic with your phone.- Some may say that playing the prequels is not necessary for understanding the story, but not doing so will leave you clueless about a lot of the crazy technologies present in the game and who's a certain character/religious figure that is CONSTANTLY mentioned (and said religion is not really detailed either). Hell, I've played the two other games and I still fell there's way too much of the setting that is never explained properly or doesn't make sense at all since apparently there's a HUGE timeskip between the events of the previous games and Bone Totem. Not even the quantum storage devices are introduced or explained, so a lot of players may end up just thinking that it's a gameplay thing that allows characters to swap items.All of this could had been solved with supplementary information scattered in notes, papers and PDAs, but while you learn a lot about the gruesome fates of many of the NPCs, in the end I felt like Bone Totem was really bad at introducing or explaining its setting. I would had gladly sat down to read some extra lore after having finished the game, but there was none to be found.- ... speaking of that. The only "extras" to be found are apparently some VHS tapes and other 20 collectibles that... you can't even watch? I've found a sole tape in my entire playthrough and I don't even know HOW I got it --- it simply showed up in my PDA from nowhere, so I dunno how I was supposed to find the others or if there's anything worth in collecting all of them.- While the art and visuals are gorgeous, I've oftenly had issues trying to understand what I was looking at in the screen... at certain point, I was exploring the depths of the ocean and I could even grasp where I could WALK without using the ping feature. I wished I could zoom further in some of he objects or simply shine/adjust a better light in some places that were way too dark to be fully appreciated.- The meat of the story is fully exposed by half of the game, after that there's not big reveal, just a cast of characters trying to get out of a rather awful situation... with a certain... weird spiritual-like figure... being introduced by chapter 4 to guide our heroes and serve as a plot device... and well... yeah, I'll leave at that so you can check it for yourself.Stasis Bone Totem was a remarkable horror experience, worth of every cent, created by promising developers that are leagues ahead of many other indies and game devs in an era chock full of repetitive, half-baked horror games that are barely different from each other. While my own age, the lack of time and a short budget keeps me from playing or testing more game, I'll be sure to keep an eye on whatever the developers got in store for the future. Maybe I'll try out Beatiful Desolation next, who knows!

The characters and how they interacted was great, brought to life by excellent voice acting. Puzzles made sense and required you to be observant and logical. _childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis Bone Totem is very well worth your time if you enjoy a good mystery and have an iron stomach.The game is in every measurable way an improvement over the original Stasis. The visuals are fantastic and there's so many interesting and wonderfully rendered environments. The pacing is excellent and kept me and my friend (we played through the game together, I streamed it for him) hooked all the way through. There was never a moment where there wasn't some interesting mystery to think and talk about. The writing is much improved over Stasis as well, with all voiced characters genuinely engaging and memorable. The people you read about in the PDAs also feel much more believable and human compared to the large amount of goofily cruel ones in Stasis. The puzzles also felt good, no moon logic here but also not too braindead. Requires thinking and exploration, but no galaxy brain.They really knocked it out of the park with this game, and I am very much looking forward to Stasis 3.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This may be my favorite game I've played this year, and it is a *crime* that it isn't more widely known. The gameplay takes some getting used to, and the visuals aren't great, but the sheer amount of innovation in terms of characterization and tone-building are absolutely worth the jank. I very nearly stopped playing on three separate occasions because I loved the characters so much I did not want to see them getting hurt, which, you know, horror game. Kind of inevitable :P My only real criticism: the devs should have done more research in terms of the cultures that appear throughout the game, especially the non-western ones. As someone who's a bit of a history bug, I can tell they've based their depictions on other depictions in media, rather than looking into actual scholarly literature on the subject, which would normally not be an issue, but in this case unfortunately lead to the recreation of some, uh... not great stereotypes and misconceptions about certain cultures, stereotypes and misconceptions that still cause real, actual, physical harm to this day. I know the devs didn't do this on purpose, and I'm sure they tried to handle the various cultures well and in good faith--but everyone has blind spots, including me. Regardless, this game is a fantastic work of art which has provided genuine inspiration and insight for me creatively, and I am hugely excited to play other games by this publisher. Y'all should be proud of yourselves. You did good. :D
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the good. The story, environments and atmosphere are fantastic. It's some great sci-fi horror material that doesn't rely on jump scares to terrify you.Now let's talk about the bad. The puzzles are horrendous. Half of them do not make any sense, they're not intuitive, and even after getting the solution you can't even manage to reverse-engineer them. To quote a few streamers that I saw play the game: "these puzzles are dogsh*t".It's still a positive review overall, but I'd suggest to the devs to improve their puzzle design if they ever release a sequel of some sort.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game and story, only thing is that the plot is hard to follow sometimes. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely devastating and very likely the grimmest game all year.Stasis and Cayne were bleak and depressing adventure games. Stasis: Bone Totem succeeds in being not only extremely bleak and depressing, but also horrific, disturbingly gross and sad.There is no joy here, once it gets going. Things start out bad, and they will keep getting worse. The deeper you go, the worse it only gets. Every chapter, every location, every description, every personal log, every scene of environmental storytelling, each a poisonous piece in a morbid puzzle that is this relentless journey. It expands and elaborates a lot on the world building and lore of this messed up universe, and while it is fascinating and engaging, I cannot stress how much of a bummer of a trip this is in the best and worst ways.This is not a spooky and slightly fun kind of adventure, it is BLEAK and it WILL choke you.I can't wait to see what these brothers do next.tl;dr would cry for this brave and strong bear again8/10
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I hadn't played a point-and-click adventure game in a decade before picking up this one, so I can't really gauge it against other games in the genre. Nevertheless, SBT is a nightmarish descent in the abyss of rampant capitalism, all-powerful corporate madness, and gory hellscapes. The gameplay is improved over other classics of the genre, since the game points out interactable bits in every scene, sparing you the maddening pixel hunts of other titles. The solutions to the puzzles is not some weird moon logic (most of the time anyways), and the game provides some hints when it detects you're stuck on a puzzle screen. The only times I really got stuck it was because of something I missed in some other screen, or because I forgot about Mac's ability to break down items. While there is no shame in looking at the walkthrough (included with the game) I only had to look at it once , which I believe is the only occurrence of a piece of a puzzle that you cannot go back and look at multiple times. The story is fascinating and well-written, and helps you get attached to the main characters (my Moses <3 ). It has a few interesting plot twists and a bittersweet ending. The scenes are very detailed and realistic, even if some are definitely ugly and clearly show what is pre-rendered and what isn't . I am not an expert, but it seems to me like some assets were made with AI (the PDA character portraits). I have no problem with that, but it seems like someone in the community was disappointed with it. The dialogue between the main characters is always excellently voice acted and there are thousands of entries and logs to read and immerse yourself in the setting. Most of the written text is worldbuilding, but some text entries foreshadow some of the plot twists (which I loved). Finished it in about 12 hours with occasional looks at the walkthrough. We are brave. And strong. <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game was quite something. It most definitely is worth the 10€ that I got it for when it was on sale.I'm surprised how good the voice acting was. The characters were interesting and each had a distinct personality. It made me actually feel something towards them which not too many video games or movies are capable of. The story was interesting. Pausing the game to do daily chores always left me curious to see what was through the next door or hallway. The plot twists and revelations were the opposite of boring and predictable. I was not a fan of the amount of gore but I understand that it probably was necessary to make the game have that certain type of feel and atmosphere.Some small gripes: The graphics are a bit too dark in my opinion. It felt some of the renderings are quite low resolution as well. Sometimes it was hard to make a distinction on what is happening on the background. The puzzles were okay, nothing great. At times they were more of an annoyance than a fun minigame to solve and I would just brute force things like trying items on a problem one-by-one. Some solutions seemed to have ambiguous logic to them. Of course it could be I was just too dumb to solve them all in the intended way.Overall though, a great experience! I definitely recommend it if one enjoys a story that slowly unravels to reveal horrifying and macabre truths.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great reviews, so maybe something with it just didn't click for me. I didn't enjoy it though. The puzzles were dull. The dialog was painfully simple, and there was so so much of it. At least half of the 3rd character's lines oscillate between "I do not like xxx" or "I am brave and strong". So much meaningless dialog from annoying characters. So much time waiting for characters to say the same thing they said on the last screen.The atmosphere and world building is pretty powerful. It didn't do much for me, but it was pretty intense. It feels dark and twisted like the warhammer 40k universe. If that's what you like, you'd probably love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: HOLY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ - ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!! WHAT A GAME!!! Cons: you WILL need a walkthrough to get through some of the more challenging parts of this game, I won't lie to you there. Some of the puzzles are obscure and sometimes the traversal can be confusing, but that's where the cons end.Pros: LITERALLY EVERYTHING ELSE!The atmosphere and vibe: flawless.The art direction and interfaces: superb.The sound design: amazing.The worldbuilding and immersion: exceptional.The lore and storyteling: incredible.This game is on a whole other level than most modern games. Dark, creeping, ambient, intriguing, and unnerving as it beckons you deeper into a twisting narrative that will genuinely have you on the edge of your seat. It's a work of both art and passion, and that passion shines through every single aspect of this game.VERY RARELY have I come across a game that makes me genuinely feel something. I could easily liken the narrative quality to that of the Bioshock franchise, specifically the Burial at Sea DLC, if you know, you know. This game feels like actually going on an epic adventure, encountering trials, having truly unique, memorable experiences, and walking away actually changed for the better for having gone through it.I could go on. but if you're on the fence, just play this game. 111/10 - would HIGHLY recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is worth playing by just about any point-and-click adventure fan, but especially those who like when horror permeates every facet. It is visually appealing, both in its 2D isometric form and with the 3D cinematics that occasionally feature cool deaths. Puzzles are challenging, logical and satisfying, with multiple steps and a good indication of what is required. With the three controllable characters remaining cut off from one another, the game injects variety thanks to its shared inventory system. And since it offers around 10-12 hours of solid puzzle solving, the game will not leave players empty handed.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Great story, voice acting, and dialogue.- Gorgeous environments and general design/art.- Puzzles are rarely annoying, some quite fun.- Just unique in general.- Moses.Cons:- You often can't do things during dialogue moments. This becomes particularly annoying later in the game when the formula becomes 'Walk into room, wait for long dialogue to finish, click on object, wait for long dialogue to finish, etc'. - Some cutscenes look fine, others are quite janky.- No actual risk of death or loss. Some may consider this a pro.Neutral but Perplexing:- The cover shows Charlie being attacked by tentacles, but no tentacled beasts ever appear as threats. Summary:Great story driven point-and-click game. Despite a few annoyances and not being a fan of the genre in general, I really enjoyed my time with Stasis: Bone Totem. Interesting visuals and characters that will stick with you. Highly recommended to anyone with an interest in sci-fi horror.

_childDocuments_.review: The further along you get in any of these old style adventure games the more you start just randomly combining items or using items on anything. I must have used the scrubber critter on everything at one point or another... do I fix the lock with the scrubber? Can the scrubber blow a hole in the door? Can it fix a pipe??? Pay off my debt??? Then when you finally do use its like "".I think this could have been solved really easily by just using things as you get them... and they're not terrible with most of the items but man, there's just a few items that you will be stuck with trying them on everything before you can progress. That aside, what a sick atmosphere and art direction with a cute little video gamey mechanic with the object teleportation (its like the turned DOS2's biggest flaw into a mechanic). The characters feel fairly fleshed out with pretty great voice acting (the cutest bear as well!) and what a fun and horrific ride! I know there's probably a million comparisons to old adventure games to be made but weirdly the game ended up reminding me of Chahi's Heart of Darkness for PS1 of all things...I would recommend the game wholeheartedly but then there's the AI art stuff... I only know about it from reading about it here and Mandalore Gaming's video. Apparently its all been taken out of the game according to the devs, which is better but still isn't great they even thought to do that. I know its a two dev team but I would rather they straight up stole images than use AI, its such a scummy way to cover up the fact that you are stealing just in a round about way. From what I understand they didn't even use it for like major assets just character portraits and images, aren't there royalty free images you can just download for that ♥♥♥♥?So they say they've taken that stuff out which is good however, there's a straight up Xenomorph in one of the images on one of the computers in game (). At the time I thought, "" now I'm more in the camp of "" I don't like saying that because for all I know it was just a cute reference but this is the kind of thing that happens when you let AI poison a work like this. I can't say with 100% certainty that that is just a cute reference image (especially because of the legal ramifications). With that said I enjoyed my time with the game, it felt very old school in a fun way its just that I don't think I can recommend it with what I've just said sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend buying and playing this game.It had a good story and a good pace to it, the interface was good with the item swapping mechanic between the 3 playable characters working well.Many PDAs to read.I did find some of the puzzle design frustrating at times, I solved a few of them without really understanding why it was the correct answer, they could have done a better job of breadcrumbing the solutions or just providing necessary information.Overall though it was great.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Tons of promise in the first few hours that is absolutely not delivered upon.Let's talk puzzles first - this game definitely falls into the "nonsense" trap of point and click adventure games. Piles of items with very obscure and unintuitive interactions that you have to work out - I did not feel like a clever player learning about the world around me, but instead like someone just stumbling around trying everything that even vaguely made sense. It's a common issue in adventure games, and it's the same here.What about story? I *loved* the bleak, capitalist-eldritch horror vibes at the start of the game. For a long time, that is really what carries the whole experience. But for the latter half it turns to an entirely different vibe which I won't spoil, that felt extremely silly and undermined the tone terribly.Then there are some very irritating points of friction. The hint system is rubbish - often providing no useful direction, and it only shows you it once! So if you forget what was said or accidentally skip it, good luck!And there were multiple occasions where ways forward were hidden until you walked into a certain region, which was very frustrating.So overall the characters were great, the presentation was good, but the game was frustrating otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I have entered the Nexus and will not be able to complete this games.  Great story, cut scenes, characters, voice acting and for these I will give a positive review.But the puzzles killed it for me.  At times it turned my brain in a Bavarian pretzel and gave me a migraine.  Way too many puzzles and if you don't examine every nook and cranny you may lose that vital clue to turn the next page of the story.Characters were interesting.  With Mac, who looked like one of the cast from Duck Dynasty and had a penchant for smashing things.  He is dominated by Charlie, his wife, who has the skill of MacGyver, to combine two things, like magic, and make something new.  Last but not least there is Moses, a precocious teddy bear robot, who looks like he would be at home at Five Nights at Freddy's or Chuckie Cheese.All good stuff.  I in the end uninstalled it after 20 some hours.  I think this game needs more than just puzzles.  Maybe, it needs some lite turn based combat or even a stealth sequence.

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem stands alone as an excellent point-and-click puzzle horror game, not requiring knowledge of the previous games' lore but enhanced by it. The previous Stasis was maybe just a little too graphic and bleak to recommend to everyone you met, but S:BT has a wider appeal - it's not quite so relentless in its outlook, the story is richer, the puzzles not too insanely hard, but more importantly, the characters absolutely soar. Well-written, but truly elevated by excellent voice acting.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: A good and interesting adventure game, perhaps a bit short (around 18 hours with help) but it has a compelling and good story and quite a few scary things happening. It's set in the future, but at the same time it is somehow in the "past" and the game is very good to get you to search for more as you play through it.There's also a lot to read if you love that and information and logs from the people from old times in paper form and more recent in digital form from sources such as computers etc.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible, dark, emotional story. This game has really thought out world, with retro-futuristic tech and where life is quite brutal. What sets apart this game from other point and click games, is that it is fully voice acted, and voice acting is god tier. All characters are complex, full of personalities and not single one is boring or annoying. I was emotionally invested in this story because it is my kind of dark horror story with really interesting world building and technology. Puzzles are logical, medium level complex which is great for this game. I would recommend to read all PDA logs and documents and don't rush, it will be worth it. Idea of controlling three characters with technology that lets them share items that are crucial for each others progression while on the different parts of the ocean, really helped with avoiding backtracking and covering so many locations. After this game, I will be playing definitively other games in Stasis universe. You should not miss this game if you are a fan of sci-fi horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Well, this was a ride of ups and downs, but in the end the ups clearly outweight the downs. The most important bit to me, the story, was very symptomatic of said rollercoaster: it had very cliche moments and eye-rolling sequences but also genuinely good writing. In the end, the story and the characters are pretty well-written and despite my better judgement I did care about their fate. There's some parts I didn't fully understand and I'm not entirely sure if that's just me not paying enough attention or not, but it all was wonderfully weird.Graphicswise, the game does look good. Which isn't important to me, but it helps. It has a very cool graphics direction; but the biggest question this game asks of you is: are you OK with body horror and grotesque imagery? Because it does have that. In spades.I really enjoyed the gameplay. It wasn't a full-fledged point&click, but (almost) all of the puzzles make sense and you very rarely grind to a halt and try the good ol' randomly combine stuff in your inventory trick.All in all a pretty good game that I'm probably being harsher on than I should; probably because there were few but significant moments where I was greatly annoyed by how characters acted/the story unfolded. But if you're a fan of adventure/point&clicks and can stomach body horror, this is very much a game for you. Also, thankfully there are no jumpscares.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent little gem of a game. Some of the puzzles are way too hard though and the devs recommended I read the hints book, which is actually a pretty nice art book to boot. A pity to have to effectively cheat to progress but there we are. I'd still be stuck at the very start of the game if I hadn't.The story is certainly original, I haven't seen anything quite like it before, except maybe SOMA on some levels and the Amnesia games were a clear inspiration, but otherwise Bone Totem is original. Visually the body horror is both horrific and delicious. There are some astonishingly gross scenes, with one particular making feel sick.A more effective in-game hint system and some sort of log book to keep track of clues, particularly the visual ones, would have made the experience that much better and negated a lot of back-tracking and taking photos on my iPad. Some scenes were visually confusing with no signposting as to what exactly I was looking at. Better descriptions would have helped here.Recommended for point and click, adventure and horror fans alike. Just don't feel bad about reading the hint book when you get stuck, which you will. A lot.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that's dripping in atmosphere and in that sense, very well worth a play. The puzzles however, can be anything from clever to just frustrating. I think what would have helped is the addition of some kind of log of events or clue items or something.Managing multiple environments with multiple characters that have to juggle items back and forth makes it difficult to keep track of everything. It's not terrible by any means; for the most part I got through just fine with a walkthrough only needed for a few parts.But it definitely killed the tension and pacing that was building up while trying to find the solution to a puzzle.Otherwise it's a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time playing a point and click adventure game. Never really got the appeal for this type of games before playing this game. I had seen a review Stasis (The first one) and just fell in love with the world building the game did. Bone totem does not disappoint at all and I actually believe it to be a very worthy successor of Stasis.That said I played this game in a single sitting so not sure how would one play this with multiple breaks as the story sort of requires you to remember a lot of information in your head (Not really necessary that one would do this except for a completionist run) before the juicy reveal. I guess reading the PDA again can help one to catch up again, but I just can't picture myself doing that.It's awesome, 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Very good point and click adventure game with no pixel hunting! Upfront warning: extreme body horror. Seriously, the body horror just gets weirder and grosser. However, It adds to to setting and atmosphere very well.Excellent voice acting and cutscenes. Story is great, though a lot is through text logs. Puzzles are pretty good overall. Most are intuitive, though some are fiddly because you zoom out of puzzles when you switch characters. Again, cannot overstate how much body horror there is in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: very good point and click. the theme of the horror reminds me a bit of The Expanse books but under the sea. The three controllable characters worked well as they are generally segregated and the environments were very well done throughout the game.i did struggle with some puzzles and often mostly around 'who should i use now to progress' or 'i forgot to see if i could use an ability on this item' as you pass found or modified items between the characters, but it was tolerable. Towards the end though i started to get a little tired and followed a guide to finish up.The VA is good, but it does require you to skip or listen before you can perform another action, and I started skipping at the end as the dialog quantity increased significantly with more lines being single words or sighs. Some VA optimisation was needed there.Worked well on steam deck which I played the entire game on, but this meant the environmental art was less visible so I would advise a full sized monitor.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool horror adventure game with a surprisingly well-done story. Follow a desperate, mourning family of three to the depths a of lovecraft-infused sci-fi horror undersea hellscape. What crazy creepy ♥♥♥♥ lurks beneath the waves? It couldn't be worse than whatever it is they're already going through!The characters are well-developed and unique, surviving in an equally fleshed out vision of an impressively bleak future. The story is particularly touching, and while the plot occasionally drifts out of focus, everything really comes together. I loved the slow, layer-by-layer reveal of the mystery and thickening of the plot.The gameplay only actively conflicts with the storytelling in moments of high urgency. One character could have moments left on their oxygen meter, while you jump to a different character and meander around at your own pace. A lot of games have this issue and it's a tough one to crack without railroading the player, so at those moments it's best to lean in.Gameplay-wise, the hint system and highlight-able interaction points help even a point-and-click adventure noob like myself get a good experience. No bashing your head against the wall hunting for pixels - unless you're into that.It's gruesome, it's gory, it's family trauma story. Play it!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I wish you could hear my eyes roll, is how bad and cringe this game is. Even worse than the first one. I'm not sure why I even bought it in the first place.The story is boring, uninteresting and just dumb. No huge secret, nothing interesting about it. And what's worse, how the story is told. There's too much stuff to read. I got bored after reading a few logs and just stopped reading them. They could've added like audio or video logs with few interesting messages to find out what happened and what where the people that lived there. But no. Just text, text, text and more text with names and actions that make no sense. It's like starting to read a book in the middle of it and trying to make sense of it.Every object in the world you look at is just bunch of text. The characters you play as, can't inspect them or say anything about them. This made the world boring, uninteresting to look at. Just a bunch of icons clogging up the screen for no reason. However instead, in almost every room the characters interrupt your movement and actions by trying to say some generic things. The characters you play as are just plain boring. Their backstory is also generic garbage.The voice acting is the worst I've seen in years. I can't listen to it. The voices are annoying to listen to. It's just heavy breathing followed my a pause and more heavy breathing. And they talk only for the sake of talking. Nothing important. Just filler words and long pauses. Nobody talks like that in real life. And every few minutes you're interrupted with more and more talking and heavy breathing. And the robotic voices are ridiculous. Sounds like sound FX I made back in the 90s.No point in making characters with unique abilities while they can simply pass items to one another in seconds where ever they are, how deep underwater they are and how apart they are with magical sci-fi materializing things (teleporting?) out of thin air. It's just stupid. And when they stand next to each other, they talk like they are speaking on the radio, not like they're next to each other.The puzzles didn't make any sense to me. So cryptic that I lost interest. Once I though I did a puzzle just by closely listening to sound, but it didn't work. Turns out I had to use an item and then repeat the same stuff. Only then in worked. The items you find, the things you interact with make no sense. Most of them at least. I had to use a walkthrough. And even with the whole walkthrough on my side monitor, I was really confused where to go and what to do. Had to read it 4x times and had to still run back and forth clicking on every single thing.The movies are zoomed in. Almost all the of the time I can't understand what's going on. It's like those selfies where a person is just a face with minimal background. And all cutscenes are like that. I have no sense of where they are, what's happening to them, where are they going, where are they falling etc. It's just dumb.At some point in game, they give each character some flashbacks, but those too are worthless time wasters, because they don't give any valuable information what so ever. They don't make characters more interesting or story more interesting.Graphical settings are bad. At least the default ones. I had to use accessibility options. Made me feel like a disabled person. I mean they could've made it graphically stunning, but no. Not even visuals are good.I remember the first game was a horror game. This one is not. It's just a bad point & click game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: The other positive reviews already tell you enough about why this is an excellent game. One thing that I would like to add is that the environment and the general setting of the game combines such an odd combination of elements and yet it blends incredibly well. It combines historical elements with sci-fi with deep sea with grief with religion and it just works.Just an amazing, tenseful horror game, actual characters to feel sorry for and some well-thought out puzzles for smart bears.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: solid game! it's not without the typical point & click caveats, but anyone should expect that going in (and if you cannot stand the occasional convoluted logic, this genre simply isn't for you). pacing feels stretched at times (i cannot BELIEVE i've only spent 12 hours playing this, feels like waaaay more), voice acting can be slow and a bit cheesy. but it's very atmospheric and the environments are really beautifully made, and discovering the story was quite enjoyable. definitely a recommend if you like this type of thing. i will say though, damn this game is bleak. like overtly bleak. just some real sad, dreary stuff

_childDocuments_.review: Rather new to the point and click stuff but its very well made and only has a few annoying puzzles. Really interesting world design and story which supports a triage of genres which reminds me of OG fallout 1. Shame after beating it it all feels so linear. I wish there was more outcomes to puzzles but I enjoyed this non the less.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game does a fantastic job of creating a dark and foreboding atmosphere while also creating fully fleshed characters that you can't help but care about. I thought the writing in this game was incredible, to the point that the ending actually brought me to tears. I was not expecting a point-and-click horror game to tell such a compelling and touching story. I loved how it felt to piece together the mystery of bone totem through its environments, puzzles, and written logs you find throughout the game. I highly recommend this game, especially if you like rich narrative games with dark horror elements.

_childDocuments_.review: almost beaten it, so i can't comment on the ending yet. incredible game so far, the puzzles actually make sense for the most part which is all i ask for in a point and click really. Very dark and a good sequel to the first stasis. good characters, good story, good price point, good everything, really. buy it if you like horror stuff. very epic and poggers

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible, especially for the list price.I took a break from Starfield to try this out and it kept me so on edge and waiting to find out what's next that I'm finding it difficult to return to playing the newest Bethesda monstrosity.Story is great, characters are great, setting is great, voice acting is great, puzzles are decent and doesn't have any real examples I can think of true adventure game moon logic; almost everything just sort of clicked based on what I had collected.Don't listen to the people saying that the puzzles are too hard, either. I don't think they pay enough attention because 98% of all the puzzles I was able to quickly solve by just thinking for a second about what I had in my shared inventory. I played 100% of this game stoned and only had trouble on like, 3 puzzles that required me to hit the BUILT-IN HINT BUTTON. One of those 3, I literally had figured out what I was missing and got high and forgot, so that was 100% on me.Edit just so I can explicitly state that I LOVE MOSES

_childDocuments_.review: I am a brave bear, now. Very cool, and tbh I think the first game I have found the need to review.Puzzles are some times killer, had some issues with interaction with super ultra wide screem where I needed to go to low res for it to work.But 10/10, loved it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely made with love and care. But love and care doesn’t always create good art. The entire game relies heavily on the story, and the writing isn’t particularly good. The prose is pretentious and waxes on about science and religion, when it is clear the creators know very little about the subject matter. The premise is sound, the over all plot is interesting, and some of the characterization (the bear) really shines. But it ultimately fall short of similar work in other mediums.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game that's dripping with an atmosphere of creeping dread. If you enjoyed the original STASIS game, you will certainly enjoy this one too - the new system of managing multiple characters in different locations to solve puzzles is a great step up from the original STASIS (which had a single main character).What stood out particularly to me is the excellent voice acting; all the characters really grew on me throughout the story, better than even many RPGs and visual novels do.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game in uncanny. Cut scene animations, facial animations - the entire scenery gives me the creeps. As it should, the driving force of this game series has always been the atmosphere. A lot has been improved in this game, whilst the previous one felt like it lacked in puzzle elements, often having to endure puzzle elements that didn't make sense, this one was pulled off much better. I recommend playing it, one of the better modern point and click adventures. Animation might look like jank sometimes, but it gives it charm.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good. I don't usually go for point-and-click style games that are centered around solving puzzles, but I was hooked for the full 12hrs it took me to finish it. I finished it over a weekend and it was a great experience. The story is so intriguing and the world building is some of the best I've seen in a while. If you are a fan of sci-fi horror then this is a must play.I have not played any games by this developer before but I will definitely be checking them out now.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the best games of its genre. It has a well written story in a well written lore. The story always makes you wonder what's going to happen next. I have never read all the notes in a game before. This game made me want to do it, and I did. Also the game is very successful to make you love or get interested in the characters.It has clever puzzles that doesn't overwhelm you much. But I have to admit I had to look for solutions several times not to waste time.The art is awesome. The visual quality is perfect for this kind of game. I know that they used AI to generate some images and I fully support that. I think it is a good example of how AI can make it easier for developers to make games.I will definitely play their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: A very good sci-fi point 'n' click adventure in an isometric view style. Nice graphics and a spooky atmosphere. I've found it quite funny sometimes too (Mac's dialogue). Recommended. Important Note: I couldn't run the game past the very first loading screens unless I had it installed on the same drive as Steam. Perhaps this will help someone stuck in this way.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, creepy horror game. Took me awhile to get used to the interface, but it became pretty natural after playing for awhile. The ability to click a button and have it highlight all interactable objects was a life-saver. A couple of puzzles caused me to look things up-- one I apparently hadn't actually tried the combination that I needed but I was convinced that I had. And another I was trying to make sense of the settings on a device but it was one of those where there was only one correct setting and you had to find and read the document with the settings written in it. The story is touching and even funny in a few places, but definitely don't expect an unambiguously happy ending. It's not that sort of setting. Took about 23 hours to play through. And be sure to watch the credits through to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely loved this game.I've now played Cayne and Stasis 1, an will be playing Beautiful Desolation next. I can definitely see the hard work you guys have put into all these games an I am grateful to get to experience them.The puzzles were very well thought out and gave a nice sense of achievement. Even adding the deaths as achievements was nice whilst making me feel more like "I'm going to murder this character THEN solve the puzzle" which in no way was a bad thing. The story, I thoroughly enjoyed too, I read every PDF/Diary an found myself eager to find more, without spoiling I also found the story quite emotional at times an I liked that. I didn't realise there were multiple endings too until reading the achievements after my first playthrough, Which added some nice replayability.The voice acting was so spot on, the raw emotion and the chemistry you could feel between characters was really something a lot of games are missing these days.And the artwork, was amazingly done, I mean the entire game was a masterpiece, but the addition of terminals with research files containing concept art was a nice touch, while needed for clues to puzzles at times.I will continue to buy and enjoy the games you guys are producing, 100% accuracy prediction.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is unique when it comes to point and click games. The inventory system especially, where you can just trade items between all the characters and see how it interacts with their environment. The story as well was engaging and while some puzzles can be very frustrating, the hint system that's in the game doesn't ruin the experience and actually helps you along. Would recommend to any point and click fan or anyone in the mood for an overall creepy game in general.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing horror Point-n-click game. The story, game play, puzzles, music, sound, atmosphere, writing, voice acting... everything is surprisingly good. You can ping the points you can interact so the game play is very satisfying. All puzzles are challenging and meaningful. If you watch or read things around you carefully, you must solve every puzzles. Plus, there is no jump scare at all. ; )After finishing the game, I'm really excited to think how the next game from THE BROTHERHOOD could be.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, this a point and click with puzzles with a good level of complexity that will keep you entertained throughout the whole game.Good story that borrows from a lot of classics terror movies like The Thing, Aliens and others less famous movies. Beware, the story is mostly given to you through records and descriptions of the environment and sometimes it can get a bit text heavy but you can feel how all comes to life thanks to the descriptions of the non-interactables in the rooms and the recollections of the dead.Nice twist over previous games to turn deaths into collectibles, it's nice not to have to save every minute to avoid progress loss.I don't know if Bone Totem is the ending chapter of Stasis but I would love to know more about Stasis universe.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Hey hey people! No, wait, wrong Youtuber. Anyway, Finished with a help of guide and sure as hell there I am not doing another playthrough, there is zero replay value. The idea of controlling multiple characters with shared equipment is nice, until you get stuck in 3 different places at once, not knowing how to progress.There is no pixel hunting, all interaction places are marked, if you want that. The items can be used only in valid places, so there is no risk of soft-lock. They also disappear after last possible use (or, what I didn't expect, get "replaced" with another item, that you have to pick up). That reduces clutter significantly, I am not even sure if there was a moment in game when items could fill a single character's inventory slots.So there is really limited number of combination of stuff you can do, yet I still guessed wrong. It just felt frustrating. Oh well, maybe that is just my inexperience with the genre. But what really killed the game for me were the late game locations and items. I mean, there is only so much my suspension of disbelief can handle. Some weird ass body-horror? Fine for me and staple of horror genre. Probably centuries old yet well  preserved items? Here is where I draw the line. The whole "And somehow they survived ? I might as well watch modern "documentary" TV. I don't really get it - they can do the graphics, characters and game engine are all fine but the story (or at least the setting) just falls apart. P.S. And I would love to listen to audiologs, while I move through the locations, not to read journals, watched by some creepy faces. System Shock did it right in 1999, so can you.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, very good story, puzzle solving will be on the hard side, you'll need a guide handy when your completely stuck, developers have one posted which was nice. the Macabre Giger styled art draws you into the world, and you begin to feel for the characters throughout their ordeal.one of the best strat/puzzle/iso rpgs ive played.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis Bone Totem, where do I start? This game has more bones than a skeleton convention and more totems than a woodcarver's workshop! The gameplay? It's like being a kid again, playing 'the floor is lava', but this time the floor is actually a terrifying alien landscape and the lava is... well, still lava, but scarier!The graphics? They're so good, I've started seeing bone totems in my sleep. My dreams have never been more... architecturally interesting.The sound design? I've heard less creepy noises in a haunted house. But hey, who needs sleep when you've got bone totems to collect, right?And let's not forget about our furry friend, Moses, the teddy bear[^1^][1]. This isn't your average cuddly toy, oh no. Moses is a bear with a mission, helping you navigate the rig and hack the security systems[^1^][1]. He's the bear-y best companion you could ask for in this bone-chilling adventure!In conclusion, Stasis Bone Totem is a game that will keep you on the edge of your seat, mostly because you're too scared to sit back in case a bone totem sneaks up on you. Or a teddy bear starts talking. 10/10, would recommend if you enjoy adrenaline, bone totems, and questioning your sanity!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good point and click game, big fan of the art style.Puzzles were good.Only downside was the tons of dialog (though you can skip but you'll miss the story) that basically put me to sleep because it locks you out of trying to do puzzles/move between rooms while you listen to it, that in the second half or so of the game is like every single room over and over where you're just standing around doing nothing.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about half way through the game and can tell you this is one of the greatest point-n-click adventure games ever made. The highlights of this game are certainly the characters and their interactions with one another. If you don't end up falling in love with Moses - a smart bear, a very smart bear - you're just not human. The puzzles are pretty good and I wouldn't say that any of them are too obtuse that you couldn't figure them out with a little bit of thinking. The story is pretty good, though it borrows heavily off the Alien franchise. The visuals are astounding and compounded by some gorgeous cutscenes (I'm honestly surprised they made the cutscenes with such high fidelity as they did with the price they are asking for).Definitely an amazing game and worth the 20 dollar purchase, which I think, is a pretty big steal for what you are getting in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: It's an entertaining game that's quite fair to the price point. Some challenging puzzles with classic "adventure game" logic and the writing is straight up cheesy, on your nose and repetitive sometimes. I don't know how many times the line "I do not like this" was used to underline that a scene was creepy, but it felt really overused by the end. Prepare for a lot of text in the PDAs, some of it you have to sift through to solve puzzles in the first half the game. Then it becomes pure setting.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.Incredible art, atmospheric music, horrific story that constantly has you guessing, and pretty brain twisting puzzles.My only issue I think was with the item combining and breaking systems.Some of the things you need to do with items can be really... out there, in that they don't seem like they would go together and the only way you would find out is if you're just mashing combinations of items (which is kind of slow/sticky in the UI). There were quite a few points I had to use a guide in the later 1/3 because I was staring at my items and at dead ends on all 3 characters and had zero clue what I needed to combine and use.The lore was really really excellent and interesting, and the story was quite heart wrenching by the end. I was fully invested in pretty much every character and they all very nice personal arcs and progression.One other thing to look out for is sometimes you have to backtrack to something you thought you were done with either because something new appears, or when you last interacted with it, the icon for another interaction didn't appear. I don't know if this is due to animations taking too long, or if it's genuinely that you had to wait, but either way there were at least 4 points where I had to go to something I was sure had nothing left to do on it, and it suddenly had a interaction.Besides these few bizarre instances of insane logic, the game is very good at letting you know what you can interact with and I would wager most people could get through a huge chunk of this game without a walkthrough while feeling rewarded from some cool puzzles. That said, if you get stuck, feel free to just use a walkthrough only to find out where to go next and then put it away. This is what I did and it worked well enough that I didn't feel discouraged or like I ruined the game.I'm not a big point and click kind of guy, but this is a must if you think it looks even mildly interesting.Evokes big SOMA vibes being at the bottom of the sea.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the characters, atmosphere, and puzzles. Truly feels like a point-and-click adventure done right.I've been following the game ever since the initial demo release, and the final game is absolutely worth the wait. _childDocuments_.review: A horror point-and-click adventure in the STASIS series (STASIS, Cayne).  The graphics looks good, though it is mostly hidden in the darkness, given the mostly underwater/indoor setting. The voice acting is excellent and very engaging toward the end. The music is purely ambient, setting up the mood.  Gameplay mechanic is, I presume, intentional callback to Martian Gothic: Unification. There are 3 protagonists in separate locations with shared inventory and some special problem solving abilities. Otherwise it is a classic point-and-click adventure. Puzzles are logical, sometimes they rely on help from other characters or cannot be solved until other character progresses in their story and gets new items. This could potentially lead to getting stuck unless you are aware of this. There is a system of hints in the game and a full official walkthrough is available.  The story is interesting, it starts with exploration of a corporate black facility and descends from cyber-punk to Lovecraftian horror. The world building follows from previous titles in STASIS series, showing even bleaker and stranger world (God was disproven, people pray to CEO, ...). The descriptions of items and scenery tend to be too flowery for my taste, however dialogs are excellent and realistic given the situation. The main characters are a couple who lost their child and their leftover AI toy. This leads to a lot of emotional moments through the story. There are usual logs of corporate scientists and employees with varying degrees of excentricity. And the trademark of the series: milking some horrible abomination for a resource needed to progress.  I enjoyed the game. It was an emotional ride, despite few moments I got stuck for a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended: 7/10Bone Totem delivers an excellent horror, disgusting and sad atmosphere. The dialogue and the vocal performances of the three playable characters (as well as the two NPCs that join later) are what makes this game memorable. I finished the game in ca. 12 hours.The game mainly contains two types of puzzles: environmental puzzles that require observing clues scattered around, and inventory puzzles that require moving objects between the protagonists and splitting and combining them. Some of the environmental puzzles are challenging (in the good sense) and are mostly well designed. The inventory puzzles are the opposite since they quickly become a repetitive chore leading to the player trying all possible object combinations. Overall, the puzzles are good and I managed to solve them without any external hints/help. However, some puzzles are annoying not because they are complex but because they negatively interfere with the pace of the game or are just illogical. So, there is plenty of room for future improvement here.The visuals are good but they are just too dark. This makes navigating many areas virtually impossible without using the ping/hotspot feature. Some areas are so dark that the details of the environment cannot be understood at all, limiting the visual storytelling. So, in many cases the player is just clicking the hotspots in an otherwise dark screen, which breaks the immersion. My major negative comment are the final acts, which account for maybe 1/3 of the game. The first 2/3 of the game are very well-knit together and follow and complement the story arc of Stasis and Cayne. However, in the last chapters it seems like the protagonists are suddenly teleported to new game that looks like a kind-of Indiana Jones inspired gore movie. The issue is that most of the narrative that was experienced before and the whole story arc of Stasis and Cayne story are now simply ignored. Worse, the new narrative and unnecessary "explanations" introduced at this stage add a number of plot holes to the story. This makes the story of the original Stasis to be more consistent than the story told in Bone Totem. Yes, Bone Totem has a more complex narrative than Stasis, but the developers deviated way too far and lost the plot in the final act.All in all, this is a very good point-and-click adventure game despite some of the annoying puzzles and the rather disappointing final chapters that are somewhat disconnected from the rest of the game. Will certainly be watching what The Brothers will produce next. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, engaging point and click puzzle game. I found the story engaging and felt for the characters, each one has their own arc full of emotion and learning. I disliked a few characters when I first met them but really did end up loving each one in their own way. Highly recommended, there's a guide on the community page if you need help through some of the more esoteric puzzles or are kinda dumb like me.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Very atmospheric and creepy environments and art, with fantastic voice acting and solid writing to back it up. The music is a star as well. Basically all elements of the game are executed superbly.There is a small amount of the classic point and click thing where you're mashing everything into everything because you're  bit stuck, but I'd say that's minimal.Most interactions are very logical and require only a little lateral thinking. Switching between characters and unlocking items for use with the others is a genius way of handling it IMO. Add variety and a bit of a prompt to think "Right is this going to be useful for where my other characters are stuck?" Top marks

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to sci-fi horror fans, or the folks who enjoyed the VHS golden era of Alien and The Thing.  Point and click is back, much like the days of Myst.  Read on:Buy it because the developers made this with passion.  Buy it because it's scary, and because it defies its point-and-click constraints, a game both nostalgic yet innovative.  Buy it because it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bargain!  But, above all, buy it because it's a good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game made by people who love games, and because these people deserve the chance to let lightning strike as many times as they can manage.  I personally hope to see more in the future.  Very rarely will you get bang for your buck, quite like this.  Kudos.  Bravo.

_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow. I'm not really the audience for Point & Click Adventures but this game hits different. Great story, great characters, good voice acting and amazing visuals. The only thing I really wasn't a fan of were some parts of the puzzles which were a bit illogical/unclear to me (could just be me not being used to the genre). Other than that a great game!Moses indeed is a very smart bear now
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, really gruesome and creepy (read: VERY gory) I like that there aren't jumpscares bc it's point-&-click, but I still get that nice meaty horror story.  Play this if: you love horror, even the really grotesque stuff, but timed puzzles and games where you have to run away make you fumble and panic. Thalassophobia and body horror TWs. I am absolutely obsessed with ocean/submarine horror, so this is perfect.  Also, don't be afraid to use the walkthrough (helpfully provided by the devs themselves!) bc story is more important than "being the best" at everything (also some of the logic is really impenetrable).
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game a neutral review but last third of the game absolutely ruined it for me. Basically, it starts really strong as really fresh sci-fi adventure and devolves into cheap tedious cheesy melodrama in the end. Basically first third of the game is amazing, second third is okay and last third is a terrible boring whiny slog.  Other comments praise voice acting and it is good in first in first half of the game but towards the end it degrades into sobbing, crying with poor recording quality. Dialogues are too long, the authors reiterate simple points over and over again -- as I said, this game becomes cheap melodrama really fast. The same happens to puzzles. In the beginning they are well designed with adequate amount of challenge and toward the end they become classic convoluted adventure puzzles based on obscure logic. That being said, this game has very cool characters like Moses and some others that I wouldn't want to spoil. I also should note that most of the logs are really well written. If you are a fan of adventure games and good world building and are okay with over the top drama (tears, prayers and family above all), this might be a game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big hecking coward, and yet I come back for Stasis. This game is fantastic, love the character interactions & the extra layers of thought that having multiple locations active all at once provide.There's been a couple of puzzles that have stumped me hard, their solutions leaning a little too far towards the old point-and-click adventure game style of "try everything on everything". I am also not the smartest egg, so that fault could easily be on me.Overall still absolutely loved this game, would recommend giving it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Even after coming to this game moderately spoiled by the Mandaloregaming review i still had an amazing immersive experience. It is one of the best pieces of scifi horror i have ever seen or played. People familiar with the Dead Space series, movies like Alien, the Thing, the Abyss and also Lovecraft in general will feel quite familiar with the themes in this game. Yet Bone Totem also puts its own unique (and horrifying) spin on things, and explores some interesting new ideas in the process.All of this is done with great execution. The characters are interesting and likeable, the graphics & sound  are very detailed and immersive and the gameplay strikes a good balance between difficulty and QoL. The devs even provided a handy guide for those who cant be bothered with puzzling.An absolute recommendation from me!
