_childDocuments_.review: In brief, an isometric point-and-click adventure game with strong horror and cyberpunk elements.  You play as three characters that have discovered the abandoned wreck of the DEEPSEA 15 facility and are there to determine what happened and claim it as salvage.  Of course, things are never that simple, are they?  It is connected to both the first STASIS game and the free to play Cayne game, but is not a direct sequel to either.  You do not need to have played either in order to understand Bone Totem.Bone Totem features the ability to scan the environment, right-click by default, and will show you all things that you can interact with or mouse over for flavor text - there is no pixel hunting.  Additionally, all puzzles take place on their own separate screens, and the game has hints and information about the puzzles spread liberally throughout various screens.  Taking notes (or screenshots) is highly recommended.  Pretty much all puzzles can be solved quite quickly indeed, if you paid attention while exploring and made notes so you can reference charts or other data later on.  If you are stuck on a puzzle, a button will appear in the top-right corner of the screen that you can click on to have the character give you a hint.  And if that fails, the developer also includes a full walkthrough (with gorgeous art, if you get the supporters' pack DLC!) in the install folder (it's also hosted as a Steam guide, too.)  As always, games like these are best solved on your own, but if you're stuck and it's preventing you from enjoying the game, there's certainly no harm in using a guide to move on.  Play it at your own pace, and in the way you like best.Bone Totem features a strong narrative, with excellent voice acting for all principal characters.  You can expect to get 10-12 hours out of the game, and there is some (very) limited replayability for collectibles and deaths (finding ways to die are essentially puzzles unto themselves, and there's an achievement for getting each one), if you didn't use a guide to get them all on the first run through.Definitely one of the best games I've played this year.  Very highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing take on Point n Click adventure games. Memorable characters, engaging puzzles and a metric ton of world building make this an easy recommend. Stasis: Bone Totem is easily the most memorable game I played in 2023; somehow both nostalgic and innovative. Pick this up if you enjoy a good story and can handle a bit of gore. P.S. Huge thanks to the devs for continuing to work on the Mac version which had no official release at the time of this review. It was great and I only encountered 3-4 very minor issues across the entire playthrough!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: - Great environmental art- Great character models during cinematics- A compelling narrative that keeps you wondering 'What the hell am I getting into?" the further you get into it- A persistently uncomfortable setting, which is great for the genre- Solid to great voice acting depending on the section- A pseudo-linear game design that leaves you with other things to work on in case you get stuck, instead of just brick walling- Thoughtful game mechanics that help you not waste time, like shared inventory spaces and highlighting the key interactables you need to use to progress- The narrative arc of one of the playable characters is genuinely emotional by the end of the game- and it's not the ones you would expect.- Diverse range of puzzle design, most of which is pretty solid and able to be figured out with logic- A solid amount of length for the price (my playthrough took about 12 hours)- Some of the art design makes it hard to tell what you're looking at. One puzzle in particular,- There is an overwhelming amount of descriptive text about the environment, most of which basically says the same thing. By the end of the game, I had stopped reading the environmental descriptions because they usually had no bearing on the narrative or the puzzles I was working on, just a lot of flavor text.- The end of the game creates a situation in which time is of the essence; at the same time, the game also decides all of the characters will start talking 4x more than they have been the rest of the game. When people are talking unfortunately, you can't actually interact with the important objects that you need to, so the game tries to create a sense of urgency, and then immediately destroys it for the rest of the game.- Even though the character models look great in cinematics, they animate terribly- which is probably why the camera is usually stuffed into the characters' faces during cutscenes so you can't really see anything.- The game is dark, like in a problematic way. A certain amount of it can definitely be used for tone, but some sections of the game you can't even figure out where you can walk to advance because of how dark the screen is and objects being in the way.- Some tropey ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that pops up too much in scifi already, including everyone's least favorite, flashbacks to 'before things were bad' where you can only walk slowly and click on things. It at least plays into the plot in this game by the end of it, but so rarely do I find sequences like these add anything to either the narrative or the gameplay.Overall, this game is great. It's ambitious, it has diverse puzzle design, it has a memorable story arc and setting, and its non-human characters are interesting and memorable. There's a few hiccups of the adventure game genre, where its hard to tell what the game wants from you, but I think I only got unreasonably stuck 2-3 throughout the whole experience. Overall, if you like horror and you like puzzles: pick it up and you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is bleak and depressing. An incredibly dark exploration of humanities hubris and the lengths it'll go for the sake of exploration, a game that is built around the ideas of loneliness with Hope at the center. What could be considered a rudimentary point and click adventure, this game wins us over by having fantastic characters and incredibly thought provoking plot mixed with some of the most distributed visuals I've seen in a long time, this is not a jump scare game, far from it, but this game will leave you sleepless as you not only try to digest the disgusting visuals but it will also leave you pondering it's many mysteries.I do think fans of point and click may find it a bit too story heavy with the trio of main characters constantly talking back and forth but I absolutely love it and I really loved all the characters, moses may be one of my favourite characters in a game in a long time but the less said about the story the better, it's grim, very bizarre and a little lovecraftian.Do yourself a favour and just play it, if you can handle really disturbing games with stories that require some patience and a lot of reading then you will play one the years best games. Now go play, you are smart and brave.

It's just an amazing work, I believe that the concept artwork was done more than brilliantly.In terms of gameplay, the game is pretty standard, but it doesn't make it boring. _childDocuments_.review: If you played any of their games, you know you are in for a treat!The first game I played by Brotherhood Games was Cayne and after that STASIS.This is a whole new game in those genres. And it is one heck of a game!If you love point-and-click adventures with a little horror than this game is definitely up your ally.The atmosphere is dark and gloomy, the story-line eventful and suspenful, and the switching of/between the three characters ... it just works. I love it. The game is just "weird" enough to get me hooked. I now desperately want to know what is going to happen!As we speak (at point of writing)  I'm in Chapter 2; everyone is safe and accounted for (yay!) but we are scattered accross the rig (awww), but I'm sure we will make it through - hopefully in one piece haha.So far, the puzzles were not hard, and the story has been eventful (and I died once - which took me by surprise because it totally blindside me). And after dying, I did not have to start the whole chapter again, the game just continued like I had never died! How awesome is that! I love the amount of "gore" and bodies, much like it was in STASIS and Cayne. And I love the close ups you get of some of them. Nicely done. After seeing some of them I really wonder what the deal is with the flowers, and I am wondering if it has to do with STASIS. So the game play is easy, point and click. Gameplay is also really responsive. Right clicking lets you see what and were you can interact with people of stuff.All voices are spoken, which I really enjoy. And as with Cayne and STASIS PDA are scattered through out providing backgrounds to various characters.If I had to nitpick at something it was the manner in how the voices were in the first minutes of the game. It was a bit slow and I doubted for a moment if I could get used to it, But it did and now I don't want it any other way. And how adorable is Moses....! He is the " bestest " and the smartest bear :)Can't wait to play more, but after 3 hours non-stop playing I need to eat!

_childDocuments_.review: One minor spoiler hidden regarding the setting.Excellent voice acting, atmosphere, and body horror, especially in the first 2/3 of the game. AI children's toy bear companion operating a sentry gun (he is a very smart bear now). For a point and click adventure, the devs have tried their best to ease the solving of puzzles (e.g. right-clicking shows you all the interactable zones on the screen); I checked a guide 3-4 times in total, two of which were because I walked past/missed something from earlier. The dystopian elements are really something: the initial environment is an oil rig operated by the Cayne Corporation, effectively a more-evil Amazon  (probably my favourite part of the entire setting). The artwork is all rendered in 2D, with isometric environments reminiscent of 90s RPGs/adventure games, which means they are highly detailed and lovely/horrific to look at (depending on what is onscreen lel), same for the close-up shots during interactive segments.Janky pre-rendered cutscenes with the 'Hunt Down the Freeman' wobbliness to the characters, and the camera just has no idea where to look during these moments. A good portion of the story is a bit of a hodge podge of multiple scifi tropes and is fairly predictable, although I still think the buildup was interesting. Minor spelling/language issues that sometimes detracts from the description/log being read, although that's forgivable as the development team are not English. Music can be a bit repetitive due to reuse/looping of tracks, which is a shame because they got Mark Morgan (of Fallout 1 and 2) to do it. play it if you like point-and-clicks and/or dark body horror scifi adventure. I'll be trying out the first game in the series after this, which seems to amp up the body horror and dystopia even more. Cheers to Mandalore for drawing this to my attention.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10This is a good point & click adventure  - Minimal moon logic  - Most puzzles are not annoying  - Many different types of puzzles  - Many different types of environments to explore (everywhere's dark and damp though) This game has a decent story  - Very interesting lore - and there's a lot of it  - Immersing at the beginning  - Main story is a bit too humane but still interesting  - Predictable ending but multiple storylines to follow This game has excellent horror  - The lore is creepier the more you think about it  - Multiple different horror genres explored  - Does minimal punch pulling  - Has many parts where I went "WTF?!" which doesn't happen that often  - The "corpse hole" almost made me not finish my breakfast Some annoyances though  - Has great amounts of repetition in the dialogues (I'm looking especially at you, Moses...)  - The music (especially twinkle twinkle little star) gets annoying after a while  - Starts to drag in the latter part (end of chapter 4)

_childDocuments_.review: I admit, I don't care about point & click adventure games in general. I wouldn't play Bone Totem if it wasn't so good. I also admit that I would never complete the game without online guides. The environments are well done, it's interesting and genuinely scary, even though there is no real fear of dying (there are deaths, but they're pretty obvious and avoidable). Voice acting and graphics are good too. The game is very brutal. There have been numerous situations that makes me nauseous. Sometimes it even goes over the top. So it's not for everyone.The game reminds me a lot about SOMA. Futuristic horror game underwater. I'm sure I would like Bone Totem even more as FPS game (like SOMA), but as said, it's great even the way it is.You find out most of the story from logs left by dead crewmembers, same as System Shock. This is one game where I wish they had journal with list of characters with details, because I keep forgetting who is who of the many characters being mentioned in logs. Fortunately you can review the logs at least, just that there's no description of characters, not even pictures (there is a picture when you first find the log). Another thing I wish they had is dates in log messages, because it would help figuring out in what order the events happened. By the way, there's a lot of plot twists. It feels like Deus Ex (the original), where they crammed every possible conspiracy theory in one game.Good:+ Scary and atmospheric+ Voice acting+ CutscenesBad:- Need better journal.- Need option to always run by default

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who never plays point-and-click adventures, I can confidently say this game kicks ass for the story alone. Get it if it at all interests you!Above all else, the story is super good. Very interesting & dynamic characters stuck in a unique (and gross) predicament. The concept for Moses, alone, is a fantastic idea that they've utilized perfectly. The game, predictably, has tons of realistic body horror, but also uses this to pose lots of moral questions, with themes of religion, capitalism, and post-humanism. It does have a few issues with pacing, in my opinion, but certainly not a deal breaker.Graphics & sound design are phenomenal throughout. Voice acting especially deserves commendation. The scenes never felt like you were railroaded onto certain paths - you really felt able to interact with the environment. It could get a bit confusing at times on where you can walk to, but the "ping" feature is fantastic in helping you out. Only two complaints are that the cutscenes are pretty jank, and it's very clear that some assets were created with AI tooling.And of course, the puzzles are great! I had to cheat a few times since they can get quite tricky. Felt a bit random / unfair at times, but I'm also pretty terrible at point-and-clicks, so take that with a grain of salt!

_childDocuments_.review: The first Stasis was decent, but Beautiful Desolation was incredibly boring to play and despite that, I decided to still give the devs a chance with  Bone Totem. It's a classic top-down point-and-click adventure game that focuses a lot on the narrative and its horrors while having a very good amount of puzzles to solve. It's not a scary game, at all, and at times I really disliked it, however, as I reached the end, it slightly grew on me enough to recommend. 👍 +Nicely crafted atmosphere+Sound effects👎-Annoying voice acting most of the times-Gameplay drags a bit mid-gameI haven't played Cayne and outside of Stasis which I barely remembered, the lore was somewhat very unknown to me. The game starts to hit you with a lot of things that make absolutely no sense and it gets extremely aggravating around mid-game, so much that you'd think you missed out a lot of story bits or you have to know the lore about Cayne. However, that is far from the truth, it's just the way they decided to expose the story, that feels overwhelmingly ambiguous. It's a horror story, but what made it annoying for me is that the horror parts were actually normal things in the universe of Stasis and the characters act normal around it, like a huge brain being the central system for the base and whatnot or how instead of God, they praise Cayne. This creates confusion as to what exactly makes the game a horror experience when the unknown parts of the game are less horrific than what the characters perceive as normal. It annoyed me to no end, but as you reach the end, it starts to sorta make sense, but at that point I just wanted everything to be done.It's clearly a story for the hardcore fans of the developer's games, and not so much for the rest. The game also has a very annoying habit of giving you PDAs to read which are 10 pages long. Imagine a horror within a horror. Once you get past that, it has generic tropes such as big corporations doing experiments and anti-corporation saboteurs and finding some ancient civilization. Heard that before? Yeah, every horror fan has, a million times. Also, I really hated Moses. Story rating: 7/10It's a classic point-and-click adventure game. Not much can be said about it. It doesn't reinvent the wheel, it doesn't push the genre forward, and at times it uses the exact same annoying tropes you never want to see in a puzzle game. The only "unique" part of it is that you play as 3 characters and you have to switch between them to progress through the story. These characters can swap the items between them magically and each character has a unique "ability" to complicate things, such as dismantling certain objects or combing them to create something new. In theory, it sounds creative, but at the end of the day it's just a classic game split in parts between characters, since in games similar to its genre, you can combine or dismantle stuff with one character. In Bone Totem's case this creates annoying padding because you have to swap a lot of items between characters and most of the times since it's very unintuitive what you have to do, you have to test each character's ability with the item. It's all done in high quality, the gameplay I mean, there are no cut corners, and it doesn't feel bad to play, but its ideas and mechanics just don't click well with me, just like they didn't in Beautiful Desolation, even though I'm a huge fan of the genre. Gameplay rating: 7/10I hated Moses and its voice acting. Really dragged the experience down for me. The rest of the cast was ok at best, but nothing really good about it either.The atmospheric music and sound effects are all good though, but nothing worth talking about. Audio rating: 6.5/10Visually the game looks really good. It has some nice-looking background locations and some very high-quality cinematics for such a game. The level design is pretty decent as well, there are a lot of places to visit, maybe a bit too many, but overall well done. There were no bugs and no performance issues with the game, so, overall, a very polished game.Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 8/10It's certainly a massive improvement over Beautiful Desolation and I do recommend it with the caveat that, it's not a game you get scared, its story tropes may be extremely predictable and the gameplay might annoy you.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal. I won't deny that it's not perfect, there were a couple parts that made me say... yeah I don't know about that. But they were few and far between. _childDocuments_.review: Rarely has a game touched me the way the way Bone Totem did.  This is a real gem!  Great pacing, excellent story, good visuals, superb voice acting, wonderful musical score, and evocative cut scenes - it has it all.  The puzzles integrate well with the story, and while a few were difficult to solve without resorting to hints most were logical, internally consistent, and could be worked out with in-game information and a little patience.  The evolving relationship between Mac, Charlie and Moses, creates an emotional depth that few games achieve.  I truly came to care for these protagonists and was propelled forward by a desire to see their story through to the end.  And what an ending…I sat in silence as the credits rolled reflecting on the experience.  This is the mark of an outstanding game, and I cannot wait to see what ‘The Brotherhood’ will do next!  **And speaking of the credits, one piece of ‘non-spoiler’ advice – BE SURE TO FOLLOW THE CREDITS THROUGH TO THE VERY END!**

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, emotionally gripping story and adventure in with incredible presentation for being such a small developer.It's extremely approachable as far as point-and-click puzzle/adventure goes, which is great; the puzzles aren't so hard or obtuse that they drag down the pace of the storytelling. The Ping system helps you find and highlight what elements are set dressing vs. important interactables, and the puzzles are constructed in such a way that the information you need to solve them is never very far away.Playthrough took me 8.5 hrs as someone that hasn't played a point-and-click since Myst; not super long, but 100% worth the price tag, and more importantly, the game feels just about perfectly paced with zero filler.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterpiece and one of the best games I have ever played, not just in point-and-click genre.The game is a big step up from the previous Stasis title in basically everything: - very detailed, beautifully rendered environments, portraits, objects and cutscenes - Very memorable, loved all of them, especially This is also(imo) what differs most from the previous title - You control multiple protagonists, and you can share items in their possession among them as you see fit. This is also important to progress, because each got different abilities and all must work together. - Very intriguing with many plot twists, kept me on my toes the whole time. I really did not see what will happen next. I even teared up a bit. Well written!  - From submarines and bloody laboratories to ancient temples, this game got it all - composed by Mark Morgan, it speaks for itself - you will see some pretty disturbing/disgusting/horrifying stuff in the game, but the game also got a great sense of humor too. - sometimes I really had to use my brain cells. But nothing impossibly hard - I was pleasantly surprised how long the game is. Finished it in 16 hours - Well polished, didn´t encounter any bugs during my playthrough.To sum it up, this is a GOTY for me and will stay in my memory for a long time. Feels like an AAA title and only for 15 Euros?? Support the devs and grab the game!

_childDocuments_.review: It is a great game and an absolute steal at $20. But I will take this opportunity to voice some complaints.Whenever the characters talk, you're prohibited from interacting with objects. All you can do is either stand in place, or walk around. This has been INFURIATING at the point where I'm at. A character is deep underwater. The diving suit loudly announces that it's taken damage, and only 20% power is remaining. Wow! We need to hurry, right?! Yeah, no. You will be required to wait around for the characters to finish chatting about 20 TIMES while dealing with this emergency. You get conversations in which they are VERY CASUALLY chatting as though they aren't concerned, only for the suit to interject "10% POWER REMAINING" and then still nobody cares. It creates this gargantuan tonal clash where the game clearly wants you to take things slowly and soak in the atmosphere, meanwhile one of your characters is trapped at the bottom of the sea with a damaged and failing diving suit and barely any time to fix it.This introduces my next complaint, namely that the characters have to react to EVERY SINGLE THING THAT THEY EVER SEE. It really started to wear me down when I realized what was happening. You walk into a room, your characters go "OH WOW OH MY GOSH OH THE HORROR LOOK AT THAT", and only when they're done do you get to proceed. And it can happen back to back, over and over again. Walk into a room, REACTIONS, walk into the next room, REACTIONS. I'm writing this review because I just experienced what may be the worst example of this by far.I walk through an underwater hall. A system announces "DANGER HIGH ELECTRIC FLUCTUATIONS AHEAD". Oh dear. I walk a bit forward and find a giant swarm of fish monsters generating electricity blocking the way. I mouse over it and read that it is indeed a giant swarm of fish monsters generating electricity blocking the way. That makes 3 warnings for the same problem. I decide not to go near and instead look for a solution. I then find the solution. As I'm going to administer the solution, I step a bit closer to the swarm and I now have to stand in place as my characters go: "OH MY GOOOOSH LOOK AT THAT IT'S A GIANT SWARM OF FISH MONSTERS GENERATING ELECTRICITY BLOCKING THE WAAAAYYYYY!!!! OH MY GOOOOSH! THAT'S SO DANGEROUS!!!""WAIT, DID YOU JUST SAY THAT THERE'S A GIANT SWARM OF FISH MONSTERS GENERATING ELECTRICITY BLOCKING THE WAY???? NO WAY!!!!""THAT'S A PROBLEM! YOU HAVE A PROBLEM THERE! YOU NEED TO GO FIND A SOLUTION FOR THAT PROBLEM!!! LET ME TELL YOU A THING OR TWO ABOUT HOW YOU MIGHT SOLVE THAT PROBLEM!"This was especially annoying because obtaining the solution to this problem required me to solve a puzzle that seemingly leaves out an important bit of information and requires you to just guess. I couldn't for the life of me figure out why you would start a certain sequence at A1, but the game is VERY concerned that I might not be able to figure out that the swarm of electrical fish monsters is dangerous. This is also right after a part where you get warned about something ONCE and then you die if you get too close to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I support all games from the Brotherhood. They are awesome. It's a very hard work they do, and I still think these are highly creative. I played with my partner, that's the way I play adventure-like games nowadays, and wow, what a journey. We played several days straight at the end of the game. It is a very very long game (compared to other similar games). I really wonder how they manage to do the games, with so many environments. It's insane, and I really think these guys are superhuman. Congrats for the work!.Here are the improvements I've seen from previous games:- Environments can be understood much better than in previous games. More contrast.- The light can be moved around the character and it depends on where you point at with your mouse. That's is very very cool.- The script was much much better. All scenes had something in them. Fewer objects, challenging enough puzzles...  no backtracking, and not having to move between 15 scenes to reach something and back again, which killed Beautiful Desolation for my partner :-(Now some criticism from a follower and supporter for future games:- The amount of text to read killed us. I know you didn't have to read them... but better you do, sometimes it had clues, but sometimes it was part of the lore, the story...  There were times when we saw a PDA and thought: Oh no, another one??... let's go somewhere else, for God's sake!... Nevertheless... we read all of it, but at the end of the game it was insane, the tension was broken by so many things to read... it was very very cool (and unsettling), but it ended up being too much... for the first time in my life I wish I've had less and all of it read by someone (I don't care if it's a dirty voice AI.....)- I'd rather do a short hire for a professional animator to give all the animations the realism they need. This is a problem I see with all their games. The movements are stiff and characters look like androids... sliding feet, mechanical movements... Doing everything means not everything will be awesome. Animation is by far the worst part.- This is a very common problem with TB games: Environments are 3d and then Photoshopped. Some of the scenes lack contrast, in many of them you have no idea where you are... But I must say It was much worse with Beautiful Desolation. I bought the DLC and the full scenes fully illuminated were SUPERB. I wish I could see better...- Integration of the 3d characters into the 2D/photoshopped backgrounds is a little weird. The 3d characters have a lot of aliasing, I guess models are way too detailed for the size in screen...  I suggest applying a little postprocess (blur? antialiasing?) to the moving characters.Overall... a VERY GOOD GAME. I loved it. It gave me chills, I was sad, I was scared, It had extremely tense moments. The dubbing was superb... it was a very good experience. Please, less text, animation checkup, and keep up the good work,   ;D    We don't need that many environments...but it's up to you. hehe.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is gorgeous and smacks of passion, but I just can't overcome the clinical feeling that comes from actually playing it.STASIS: BONE TOTEM is, fundamentally, a puzzle game. It does involve adventuring, dialogue, and worldbuilding, but even when these are at their strongest they are background noise compared to the focus on puzzles. Sadly, those three sidelined aspects are really the game's hidden strength; the puzzles are often unclear, and overcoming that vagueness becomes incredibly irritating over time.The game's puzzles are almost entirely of two types - memory checks, and inventory logic. You're either remembering a code shown earlier, or you're working out which items to combine and use in which place.This game isn't the worst I've played when it comes to puzzle logic (probably in the top third of vageueness), but it certainly feels the worst with how items work. You're flooded with items and can trade them between multiple characters, who are all in separate areas with separate things to interact with. Some items can be modified - broken, bent, changed - and some can be combined together.So think of it this way: if you get stuck in a logic puzzle in most puzzle games, your best bet is to just try every item you have on what you can interact with. In this game, you would need to send items back and forth between characters to check every item that can be crushed, every item that can be combined, and check every interactable object. As chapters go on these objects also become more spread out within zones, requiring running between each point - especially slow in underwater areas.So with all this, when the logic behind a puzzle is too nebulous, it feels BAD. Brute forcing it is an absolute chore with items, and it can make discovering the right answer incredibly frustrating as these stack up over the course of several chapters.I knew by around halfway through Chapter 1 that the puzzles were going to annoy more than entertain, but I was engrossed by the world and the steadily unfolding tension. The descent underwater, the painstakingly slow unveilings of some evil forces; it hooks you and makes you take it at pace.The real horror is that by Chapter 3, I realised the "painstaking" had become "painful", and the "slow burn" was just plain "slow". There are so many questions playing through Chapter 1, but by Chapter 4 there's not just a lack of answers - there's a lack of new questions. Just the same questions over and over again, as you see more of the same stuff with no development or reveals to match those of Chapter 1.I'm at an impasse. I want to see if the story picks up, if the puzzles become cleaner, if questions are answered. I even tried using a walkthrough for a bit, just to see more story, but found that half an hour of guided gameplay yielded nearly nothing in story, so that time felt even more empty than just brute forcing. If I force myself to complete the game, and the story goes nowhere, I'll hate the game and it won't even be its fault - because it was just a puzzle simulator with scattered story all along. So I'm judging it from where I am right now, at 5 hours played. STASIS: BONE TOTEM is a beautiful labour of love held back by sidelining its story for inventory management. If the puzzles were more diverse and didn't rely on an inherently frustrating mechanic, that'd carry it. If the puzzles were less frequent and the story had a greater focus, that'd carry it. In the end neither mark lands, and the most memorable part of this vibrant game is the drudgery of shifting items around in bags.

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem is right up my alley, and I rarely see a game like this - a dense narrative title without combat, that is also overflowing with personality, sense of place, and emotion. It is optimistic and positive, despite the absolute nightmare world that is both the world above and below the sea. It is full of hope, despite taking place in an endless abyss of despair. It is serious, without being stifling. It is one of the goriest pieces of fiction I have ever seen in my life, yet is not gratuitous and does not revel in it. The force that oversees humanity is one of the most inhumane corporations I have ever seen in any fiction that has superseded traditional religion as both a place of work and worship - yet does not heavy-handedly execute such an oppressive organization, instead leaving much more to the imagination and only revealing tidbits. Tidbits that are absolutely stunning and horrifying, but you get the idea you're only seeing the tip of the iceberg. As it should be.This game, to me, is about the triumph of spirit in the face of incalculable horror, and it does this masterfully. There are minor technical issues, as well as visual effects I can see straining against the budget of the game's development, but the strength of the characters and the narrative are so strong it relegates these to being trivial annoyances that can be easily overlooked to me. To me, this is a really important experience that I will never forget, and will most likely permanently ingrain itself into my creative language.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually almost at a loss for words in trying to describe how much I loved this game.It's not perfect, but the emotional arcs of all three main characters had me going through so many different emotions through the course of the game that I feel winded having beaten it. Without spoiling the narrative, I wasn't expecting this game to resonate so strongly with me as a person with deep existential curiosity as well as a person with powerful empathy.I also have to acknowledge that it feels like nobody else is making games like this anymore. People make adventure games sure but not this specific blend of surreal horror and existential dread. It makes me want to reach back and finally play Sanitarium and other games I'd put off for years.If you can handle some truly disturbing events and environments in the media you enjoy, I highly recommend playing this game as soon as possible.Also Moses is the best bear. The smartest bear. The bravest bear.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t want this to be an excessively scathing review, what The Brotherhood devs did here is an amazing work of love and I encourage them to pursue their vision as much as they can and at the best of their capabilities. Contrary to many horror games, those made of poor and cheap ideas thrown around for shock value to create the bare minimum Outlast-clone, Stasis Bone Totem is far more than competently made, with a clear image behind, engaging concepts, strong writing and intriguing puzzles, and the sum of each part is a chore to play.For example, it’s a given apparently that point-and-click adventure games must have some sections with a sprawling, intertwined map where multiple interactions must be followed simultaneously to progress, at the risk of having maybe too much backtracking, unintuitive inventory puzzles and some areas that are visually less interesting than others. That is the entirety of this game.There are so, so, so many screens to traverse that at one point I dreaded finding new places rather than feeling curious at what might expect me. In no small part because there are clear limits in what the map design could achieve with texture and effects alone, and so much of the impact was conveyed through written descriptions, of gore, flora, environments, decors and so on, and they are fine, evocative even, but there is just too much of them.I don't think a horror game necessarily loses its spark when the danger and mystery behind it are solved, but there is a moment when the balance between subtext and text is broken in favour of the latter and, at that point, you start to think the game is actively wasting your time. Each time I found a new room and scanned it with the ping, ten new green points with no interactions but text would pop up and I shivered at the idea of having to find and read each of them. That’s not even mentioning what I felt whenever a new PDA showed up. The cardinal sin, however, is having entire areas devoid of anything but items to pick up or just descriptions; if a room is only there to make the player walk more from one puzzle to the other instead of offering anything worthwhile but text, that room should not be there in the first place.Same goes for the dialogues between the characters, there are only amazing voice performances in the game, and the players will absolutely take note of that because the characters never ever shut up. Every minute, interesting thing in the game necessitates for them to actively react and describe, talk between each other about what’s clearly there in front of them and it’s excruciating. It’s fine in terms of showing their interactions, the family dynamics and how they feel in key moments, but again it’s just too much text, just let me find something disturbing and react to it before any of these berks have something to say about it.Between the end of chapter 2 and the halfway point of chapter 3 I was detached from anything that was happening in the story. There had been some interesting twists, but I had to run around empty maps so much, between so much text and hearing so much of the same reactions and dialogue from the cast, that it made some of my favourite tropes (the underwater horror, being trapped in a sci-fi confinement, violent murder mysteries and the moral implications of what capitalism and religion do to people) felt cheap and overwritten.Sometimes it felt like the developers knew this too, because there were many terminals and documents scattered around with barely any text or commentary but simply pictures of experiments and unknown lifeforms or old drawings of alien schematics, and they were just so much more effective precisely because there was no explanation or reaction. Stasis Bone Totem is kind of worth the effort though, I kept going ‘til the end because this is the type of video game that *needs* to be made. Just last year we had Signalis and Iron Lung, among many others I certainly have not even heard of, and they did nail the feeling of being trapped, haunted, oppressed, helpless but having to move forward, and they clearly conveyed all these emotions through gameplay and very little with straightforward narration, because in such hostile and terrifying situations the mind can fill in the blanks immensely well. A lot of work was put into SBT, amazing and effective work, just too much work for the kind of experience, I think, it was going for
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I absolute loved this game. If you enjoy horror with a focus on atmosphere and story, I can't recommend it enough.The actual gameplay is point-and-click adventure game style with plenty of puzzles to solve.  Nothing too surprising or complex there, although just like some of the older classic point-and-click adventures, solving the puzzles can take some leaps in logic or just trial and error at times.Where this game truly excels, is in the atmosphere and story.  Wow.  Just wow.  In case you did not know, this is the third game in the Stasis series, with the previous games being Stasis, and STASIS and CAYNE.  While they take place in the same universe, you don't need to play the first two to enjoy this one, as it's a standalone story in the same universe.  This is a gritty, cyberpunk world where the Cayne Corporation rules all, religion is dead, and individuals have only the rights given by Cayne depending on their usefulness to the corporation.  As a warning, this game focuses a lot on body horror.  I'm a weirdo who's a big fan of a game that can make me feel viscerally uncomfortable, and Stasis: Bone Totem does that extraordinarily well many times throughout the experience.  The voice acting and narrative are also incredible, with compelling characters and a really interesting story (even if it requires some suspension of disbelief in parts).  I found myself unable to put it down because I wanted to see what horrific twists would come next.I play a lot of horror games, and this one hits all the marks for what I'm looking for in an experience.  You should absolutely give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: A real hidden gem of 2023. Its an horrific point & click with a huge work done on atmosphere and writing. Story wise, I loved the whole story with some beautyfully written characters and a general plot better than most AAA nowadays. SOMA ambiance everywhere but with it's own touch and topics.Gameplay wise, the puzzles are perfectly balanced (not too easy not too difficult) and are very satisfying to solve and progress through.If you love good stories, point & click and horror this is a must play of 2023 !

_childDocuments_.review: Hungarian:Szerintem bátran kijelenthető, hogy még a felsorolt hibái ellenére is a Stasis: Bone Totem 2023 egyik legkiemelkedőbb point-and-click kalandjátéka lett. A fokozatosan adagolt feszültségének, a teljesen korrekt sztori- és karakterépítésének, a környezet grafikai részletességének és az átvezetők minőségének köszönhetően az összkép nagyszerű elegyet alkot. Véleményem szerint a folytatás szinte minden téren képes volt szintet lépni az előző részhez képest, ezért a Cayne univerzum rajongói valószínűleg ezt a részt is élvezni fogják. A cselekmény lezárása lehet, hogy pár embernek csalódást okoz majd, azonban manapság annyira híján vagyunk a jó sztoriknak a játékokban, hogy emiatt a Stasis még így is pozitívan kiemelkedik a mezőnyből.A teljes ismertetőt  találjátok.English:I think it's safe to say that, even with all of the above mentioned flaws, Stasis: Bone Totem is one of the most outstanding point-and-click adventure games of 2023. Thanks to its gradually ratcheted tension, its great storytelling and character building, the graphical detail of the environment and the quality of the in-game movies, makes the overall picture a great mix. In my opinion, the sequel was able to improve on the previous installment in almost every way, so fans of the Cayne universe will probably enjoy this installment as well. The conclusion of the storyline may disappoint some people, but we are so short of good stories in games these days that it still makes Stasis stand out positively from the pack.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, but definitely NO. First of all, the amount of violence and cruelty - something like this is just sick to me, forcing me to ask what is wrong with the authors of this production. It is possible to tell any story in an alternative way, without getting excited about liters of blood. Secondly, many puzzles require taking screenshots, which completely contradicts the idea of adventure games. This is not a "where is Wally" game. What's worse, if you skip an item that you need to remember, it's a killing experience later on to find that picture/drawing/place from the flood of information from PDAs and computer screens. The effect is to take pictures of anything that even minimally looks suspicious (fortunately Windows has a built-in screenshot program, otherwise I would have uninstalled the game after an hour). And what, this is supposed to be satisfying according to the authors? Third, some of the puzzles are completely not making any sense right, on a "because so" basis - logic cries somewhere in the ruins. Fortunately, not all of them, but what does that change? And that's it. Pluses for the graphical refinement, here you can see that someone put a lot of talent and work. The sound design, on the other hand, is misery: there is no music, but to counterbalance the excellent voice actors. Technically OK, no problems, so the code is refined. The price is low, so maybe someone will like this production, but I advise against it.BTW: Oh, and I suggest that the authors brush up on their elementary school mathematics, because there is one math puzzle that can be solved in two ways (giving the same result): one works, the other does not.As an aside: the captain of a 1982 Soviet nuclear submarine believing in God? Alterative reality? Well. No. The creators of this pathetic production have the same knowledge of history as of mathematics. This level of stupidity simply insults intelligence.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Bone Totem was.... okay.  I wish there was a "sure, I suppose" option beyond the 'yes' and 'no' steam allows.Pros: Interesting multi-character system I haven't seen in decades, good visual design, reasonably interesting puzzles.  I enjoyed how different characters provide different item descriptions, which can offer puzzle clues.  It was interesting to see the "roshomon effect" of different characters' journals describing the same events.Cons: The narrative is too busy, with several layered arcs that don't really have any reason to be stacked on top of each other.  The game also has a disjointed flow from the start to finish with several segments feeling thematically out of place with the larger picture.  Some of the puzzles have solutions that aren't well telegraphed, and some puzzles have solutions that are VERY well telegraphed but the solution they strongly hint at isn't well connected to available actions/inventory.There is one "puzzle" in the final third of the game which requires using an item on a character in the general field screen.  This was very infuriating because at no point prior in the game was this a communicated input method, and the game very deliberately ONLY lets you use items on environmental features in zoomed screens prior to this point, so the player isn't primed for this to be a possible solution.Overall, it's not a bad game and I don't regret playing it, but it feels too clumsy for a developer which has previously put out competent graphic adventure horror titles.

_childDocuments_.review: A horror game that brings the fun world of point and click puzzles and translates it into a freaky horror game that is both interesting and off putting. Biggest plus is that the game knows when to build suspense and when to release it, there have been no cheep jump scares that you cant tell are coming (usually the horror is when you die), but the game chooses to scare you by showing showing something freaky like body horror or something dead. I have been enjoying this game so far, I wouldnt have checked it out cause I cant deal with horror well and dont really like point and clicks , except that I saw it on fanatical and it was a game with overwhelming reviews so I picked it up and played it. Definitely a game you should pick up its been amazing
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: What a journey. I had this game on my wishlist since it released and I was kind of wary. A small team, the games that released up to this point seemed to be my kind of thing but their (Steam) reviews were okay, so I hesitated.I couldn't be more wrong. This game is an absolutely masterpiece. In the first 3-4 hours I was hooked but didn't really understand the reviews. But after compleating it after some 15 hours I'm absolutely amazed. It's the perfekt mix of an obscure back story, gameplay and the kind of eery feeling that just wants to make you finish the game. After those first hours I couldn't get away from it, I wanted to know everything. Normally I'm no person who reads every single file or diary, but in this case? Every diary you read will have some kind of relevance while you finish the game. The only thing I didn't like and that is a really small thing, is how some puzzles seemed kind of random if you didn't understand what you had to do in the first place.I'm in love with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: really fun point and click game with an amazing story and art style. occasionally there are puzzles with completely idiotic solutions, but i experience no shame in looking up the answers when i get stuck so it doesn't bother me too much.there are some rumors that some background image assets were ai generated, but they don't stand out and clearly fit the art style
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Originally followed this game because I stumbled on it from seeing art on Twitter. Then motivated to buy from MandaloreGaming's review. Phenomenal game. Highly recommend. I have to give it 4 stars though on principle. A large plot important section in the ending 4th of the game uses primarily Generative Art as assets. I understand this is a small team and the appeal of generating assets is high. But I really hope the devs don't rely too heavily on it in the future. A tiny poster on a wall is one thing, but an entire section of a level and a puzzle utilizing Generative art rather then intentional illustration or 3D modeling is disappointing. Its very noticeable and took me out of the experience because it just reads as gibberish. "Biological Mayan skull Glyphs, Body horror, HR Giger" is all that passed through my head during this section. It does nothing to generate intrigue for me in the setting or clue me into the world you've built. Its disappointing and I can only imagine came from time and budget restraints. Which is why this is still a recommend. I recognize this wasn't a choice made out of laziness or lack of skill. The rest of the game is beautifully rendered with intentional artwork that speaks to the vast world and setting the devs have put together here. I hope my purchase of this game and the supporters pack enables the next game to be free of large amounts of generative art. Keep up the good work :)
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first real experience with a game from THE BROTHERHOOD, and I have to say that I enjoyed my time.The story is kinda wild and I had trouble predicting it, which I like.The puzzles generally made sense, which is not typical for this genre. With very few exceptions, the only reason I had trouble with any puzzles was because I hadn't tried a combination or forgot about the unique abilities each of the characters has.I felt like I was playing an adventure game from the late 90s/2000s and I love this game for that.20 bucks is worth it, ultimately. If it's on sale and you enjoy adventure games like this, with a dark sort of tale, then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great horror adventure game with surprisingly good characters, a story with fun twists and turns.The only faults I can find is some adventure-game-logic which can make it frustrating at certain parts.Its simple: You like horror? You'll love thisYou like adventure games? You'll like this a lot.Game length is ~13 hours, and you'll be hooked within 30 minutes.Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Played this right after the original STASIS. While this game improved a bunch of things STASIS was lacking, it also made a few things worse. Overall, still high quality story with great aesthetic, sound- and music-design, voice acting and pace. The things I would like the developers to bring back in the next installment of this fascinatingly terrifying series (or any other Point and Click adventure they will produce):  It helped me immensely in the original STASIS to put together a timeline and get a lot more involved and immersed into the whole unfolding of and disovering the backstory. After a while, I couldn't keep track anymore and forgot who was already mentioned and who was connected to whom. The original made this much easier to understand. It reduced my interest in Logs a bunch and I felt overwhelmed.  While I got used to this after an hour, it is still an odd choice to be made for this genre and I don't see how this improves the game, except making the work for the developers easier, which is a fair point.  I appreciate both, but I also like to go for achievements when I can. Having an achievement saying "don't skip dialogue" - when it holds up the whole game when there is any kind of dialogue happening - and one that says "don't use hints" - when your puzzles are often very abstruse/confusing, is not very nice. And still with the hints, I had to look up a guide anyway. I enjoyed the game a lot. While it frustrated me and got me completely lost to a point I had to look up a guide several times, the overall experience was wonderful and I am glad I experienced it fully. Looking forward to more games of these devs and I hope they continue to improve and experiment. 8.5/10, Moses is a very brave and strong bear now, and Hope's best friend.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Was hooked from the very start.Top notch environmental storytelling, intriguing storyline up until the last minute, heart wrenching moments,   level cutscenes, all through twenty hours of isometric goodness.Also... this game's characters have some heavy ♥♥♥♥ going on I can relate to.  I like how it's treated here.It was a wild ride.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I love atmospheric story-driven games, especially of the horror / sci-fi genres, but I've rarely been turned off by a game so fast. This is an unbelievably clunky and unintuitive game that is simply not fun to play. I'm sure there's good storytelling beneath it but when I'm having to fight with the game controls to advance it's simply not worth my time. Within the first 30-minutes I was stuck and even though I followed a video guide to the letter absolutely nothing worked as it was supposed to and I couldn't advance. This game is not fun and even for a low budget, indie game this level of jank is simply unacceptable.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still not a very smart bear, but I'm delighted with this horror story. At first, the oppressive atmosphere did not promise a happy ending, however positive it actually was. Pain and death at every step and in nice graphics. Sometimes I worry about another diary full of text, fortunately always an engaging story. Interesting way of sharing objects. Some moments were clearly expected, but I was looking forward to how they would be depicted. The amount of optional animations and descriptions refers to the effort with which the game was created. The affinity with the main characters has been building for quite a long time and they are not black and white either, fortunately. I am satisfied, 100% prediction.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!If you are into classic point & click adventure games, this game is for you.Pros: - Great story that keeps you engaged and is both horrifying and heartwarming. - Great world building & lore that makes you want you to know more. - Many interesting themes explored like excessive corporate greed, cyberpunk dystopia, trans-humanism, religion, ancient civilizations, personal grief, existential dread and more- Great visuals. Much like the first game it's a very atmospheric.- Good music and sound effects- Multiple characters you can play as.- The characters are all likable(*).- Each different character gives a different description of inventory items depending on their personality.- Interesting puzzles.(**) Most are clever or at least quite logical. They are generally easy and accessible enough (not "11th hour" or "7th guest" level of difficulty) to not be too frustrating to the more casual player.- Story is different from the original game, it's not just a rehash of the same plot points and - It's true HORROR.It does not have annoying jump scares. The dread comes from the storytelling. Cons are really just minor nitpicks for me:- (*) It seems some people dislike Charlie. I agree that at the beginning she appears to make foolish decisions which might bring some annoyance to the player, however later in the game you will come to understand why she made those decisions. I think she is a good character.- Some people complain there is (or was as some say it was removed?) some AI art. Frankly, I think it's not a problem. The Devs team is small. While AI art might be an unforgivable sin for AAA Devs, it is also a tool that allows small indie Devs who are strapped for cash to make a good game.- Sometimes the descriptions in the environment use purple prose (maybe AI generated?), but overall it was good.- (**)Some puzzles are a bit obscure. None really fall under the "moon logic"  some 90s point & click games featured, though, there are occasion where you might have to try every inventory item with every intractable if you are stuck. Devs however were kind to provide an official walkthrough.===========One common complaint I read in negative reviews is "too much dialogue", but frankly I thought the dialogue added to the game.I like the interaction between the characters and the NPCs. I feel too many people have no patience and just skipped the dialogue. (I know I failed to get the achievement for never skipping it, but that's because at some point I reloaded a save and skipped though dialogue I already heard)===========In conclusion, I think this is a must play for any fan of point & click adventure games. I also think this is better than the original Stasis overall. I also hope it will be a success commercially and the Devs will make more! I really want to know more about Cayne, Cayne Corp and the rest of the lore!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Totally recommended.The good-Amazing story-The voice acting.-Amazing Soundtrack and sound effects.-Artstyle-Worldbuilding that encourages you to check the developers previous works.-It easily keeps you engaged in the gameplay/story.Mixed opinions-You control several characters, each one is in different locations but they can switch items between them. In my opinion, it lends itself for some interesting puzzles that not all the time hit the mark and are unintuitive.-The main characters are good but their dialogues are often times repetitive and can annoy a bit.The bad-Too dark sometimes, I get it that it is a dark and gritty game but the great body horror sometimes gets wasted in the dark.-The PDAs have too pointless dialogue and a couple puzzles have clues in them so you kinda HAVE TO engage with them.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: It's an edge case, whether to recommend or not. I strongly dislike the gameplay and the puzzles. But I love the atmosphere, and the story is good. The story contains a lot of classical tropes that I have seen in plenty of movies and games before, so it's nothing special in that regard, just a new mix of everything (a bit inspiration from zombie movies, the Alien franchise, a tiny bit Indiana Jones perhaps, The Last of Us, The Abyss, and so on), but still interesting enough to keep me engaged.The reason why I dislike the gameplay is because it relies too much on searching through everything and take notes (literally, with pen and paper), pay attention to details (to get the solution to puzzles), going back and forth between different characters, areas and items, and so forth. It also relies too much on trial and error, using random items with other random items.There are not enough actual puzzles where you get to use your brain. Everything is just convoluted but not intelligent.A few times you are also supposed to combine items that barely makes sense, to create yet another item you didn't think was possible to create with that combination. Or how about using a bear trap to open a door? How does that make sense? I still don't know. A couple of times you are supposed to go through a doorway which you can't see, because it's hidden at the edge of the screen behind darkness. So... Yeah. It's not exactly fantastic.The game thankfully came with a complete walkthrough (a PDF in the installation folder), which saved me from hours of boredom. But there are some poorly written sections that makes you scratch your head. So get the game on sale only for the sake of the atmosphere and the story, and use a walkthrough whenever you get stuck, because the so called puzzles aren't worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not entirely sure how far into this game I am, but it is very good. It has some abstract puzzles but nothing too complex. I just wish the game wasn't so damn dark, I can barely see the environments that I KNOW look really good. It's too dark for the sake of being scary I guess. The characters flashlights basically light up the floor infront of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Original was better. Bone Totem starts very promising, but in the end becomes a mess of too much of everything. And first half of the game really works.But closer to the end I realized I really no longer cared.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: If someone else had told us a story filled to the brim with corporate greed, implant-induced transcendence, deadly microorganisms, resentful ancient civilisations practising cannibalism and bloodthirsty ritual sacrifices, impossible settings, the history of humanity being an awkward family reunion, and the ever-present yearning of human nature there is a good chance some of us would have stopped them right there saying “That’s enough!”.The way THE BROTHERHOOD are doing it, though, you just can’t get enough of it!

_childDocuments_.review: What a story!Show me the way moses,i love this universe of stasis i hope the story continues,the pacing is great the answers to the puzzles can be tough at times but in forces you to explore the enviroment and its a great enviroment to survive in,makes you stop and smell the corpsesi had a great time with this game and moses is hands down one of the best characters in a video game love how he just grins and Bears it

_childDocuments_.review: the brotherhood has done it again. a horror point n click set in a terrifying stasis universe with intriguing puzzles that provide hints and a story that becomes more disturbing with progression. sometimes difficult to figure out which of the 3 characters to use in order to pass along items but user friendly indicators is very useful to spot objects in the detailed environments.
