_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I had been waiting this game for a long time since Stasis was a surprise hit for me. Cayne was not so much. The story is alright and engaging, but in the end it gets a bit too much, like "are you serious". What is impressive that this game was done by such a small team. In the age of not having enough good PnC adventure games, I just couldn't put this game down. The game is also surprisingly long, I was awaiting for it to end around end of chapter 3 but I was pleasantly surprised.What I have most complaints is maybe the puzzles. Some of them are a bit annoying, and you kinda move from a roughly similar puzzle to another and in time it gets repetitive and a bit tedious. Those puzzles where you need to search for clues are a bit annoying since in reality there could be a number of correct solutions to some of them and you need to use trial-and-error to overcome them. Especially that chromosome puzzle was really annoying. That's why I played this game for over 20 hours as I didn't want to seek any hints. I used my phone camera to take screenshots so I didn't have to travel constantly between the puzzle and some computer screens.I used ping all the time, and sometimes when I read the descriptions of the green markers, I didn't really even see that myself on the screen. Like there is a description of something and its hard to even understand what that is on the screen. Anyway these are not any major flaws and would definitely recommend this one, although the original Stasis story and environment clicked better for me.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Good game never heard of it before until i got it in my humble bundle, but was surprised at how good it was. Story and atmosphere was really good. There are definitely some complaints though. Like in some areas the character you control moves SOOOOO SLOOOOW. Like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I ended up watching youtube on the side when the place I was trying to get to was really far. Other small thing is kinda wish there was some qol with interacting items and clicking on stuff when inspecting. It just didn't feel good or snappy felt really unresponsive. overall I'd give it a 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a safe place for children to play, 100% accuracy prediction.9/10 (+/- 1)A huge step up from Stasis, story was top tier. I was nervous that it was going to be too familiar during the first 1/4...I don't want to comment too much on the pros... My criticisms below are ultimately minor and do not detract in any major way from what makes it great.While the 3D cutscenes are overall very cool, some of the animations are distracting and disingenuous.I preferred Stasis' style of terminal and PDA presentation, Stasis' terminals were more gritty and felt more true to the environment.I also missed the occasional focus on interpersonal relationships between the crew members, this is still present but not to the same extent and not as clearly defined.There is something.. strange about the assets and presentation of this game. The PDA UI and font seemed off, almost cartoonish (not the bear's, that is clearly intentional). 90% of the time it did not bother me.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Sure if you like point and click adventures, I don't really like them, but I think the game is ok at best. I wanted to see where the story went, so that's why this review is positive.Too much clicking, would have been solved with other forms of movement. Also a plain old shared inventory would have helped to.Too much reading, I ignored most of the green info.Too much unnecessary dialogue that I wouldn't be complaining about if it didn't stop me from progressing and played in the background. "restricted area"....for the 5th time.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: AN amazing game! Please do play it. I loved the characters and the story was pretty dang cool. Designs were neat as well! I loved many aspects of this game, but the A.i. art was super distracting and didn't add anything to the game other than making me wonder why everyone has high cheek bones in the far future? Additionally, the bouncing heads for the logs were also distracting. If the A.i. art was removed and replace or just taken out things would be set.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I am Moses. I am a very brave and strong bear.The Brotherhood is a small studio that just keeps upping the ante with each release. I would say this game should take you about 10-15 hours, has seamless character switching, maybe one puzzle that actually confused me for longer than 15min, excellent world building that isn't just corny hamfisted exposition, a downright gruesome atmosphere at times that actually got to me at one point, devastating emotional moments, interesting inventory mechanics, oh look I'm rambling... lol. Look, this game has gore horror, sure, but the psychological horror is really up there. The strong storytelling, voice acting, and psychological horror are the pillars of a Stasis game and this 3rd installment excels in all three.100%ing this game won't be too difficult. Currently in the process of doing that.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game. A 3 character point and click game in the style of Day of the Tentacle meets unknowable horror below the sea. It's a more refined experience compared to the first game. The atmosphere is excellent, and great voice acting goes a long way to make it so.The story is well laid out. Not yet finished but very attached to the characters and afraid what may happen to them. Especially Moses. How did they manage to make a creepy AI(?) bear toy the most likable character in the game?If I had to complain, I'd argue that the logs you find laying around are too verbose for what they are by now I tend just to skim them for clues.Amazing that a game of this level of quality was produced by such a small studio. You rock.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Character dynamics are what make this game. Really the horror just serves as something to bring those out to the full, even if the setting has some really cool stuff in it.I've a few things to complain about but I know it's a small company so I'll just mix them in with things I like:- Sometimes, partially because of the openness of the order you can do certain things, the tone of the dialogue (which is pretty much all very well read) will not match things that have just happened very well. It's noticeable but forgivable, I think the quality of the line reads makes it stand out more- I might've missed some things but I'm not sure how some plot devices and exact details make sense but again it's fine since the story is mostly about the characters and the art direction is generally quite good- Some lines feel superfluous (restating things that have already been established)- Some mild controversy that I get why we don't talk about- Pretty alright puzzles, nothing too challenging but the game's more about the story/tone so I'm fine with not getting stuck on esoteric logic traps- The third section feels a bit underdeveloped in some ways, even if it has plenty of good moments and fits into the overall mystery- Moses is one of the most interesting characters I've seen recently in fiction, and his friendship with Faran is something I'll be thinking about for a while. The other character relations are pretty great too (Mac/Charlie's strain and love for one another)
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: played this immediately after finishing Stasis, it has completely ruined that game in my mind. Such an incredibly moving narrative with some of the most exciting and horrific sci-fi concepts combined with critiques of anthropological misconceptions I love it. 10/10 I cried like a baby. also some of the best and most coherent puzzle designs in a point-and-click adventure, I've played my fair share of lucas arts games and the whole double fine catalogue and this one did it the best.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, most of its flaws get washed away with writing, genuine character moments and wonderful visuals, I bought this game basically at random, I saw the image and went "why not?", I am not a fan of point and click adventure games, heck I tend to avoid them due to things like moon logic puzzles and stories for the insane, but this, this was something special, the puzzles were relatively intuitive and the story was fantastic but the true selling point is the stand out character writing and performances; the story is a conglomeration of sci fi horror, have a spooky science place, chuck in some lovecraft add one very brave bear and you have an engaging story throughout with some genuine heartfelt moments and reveals.Gameplay is simple, point click, you play as multiple characters in different spaces capable of manipulating environments and items in a unique manner, its standard for the genre and does it very well, how it contextualises and makes everything relatively logical is what makes it a stand out, this isn't Halligans puzzles for the clinically insane, this is well thought out, logical puzzles and with a bit of looking about you can usually figure out what you need to do, and if your a brainlet like me, now and again the game will throw you a lifeline with a question mark you call on for a hint, as well as this you can activate a "ping", this highlights interactable items so finally, we have a solution for pixel hunting in point and clicks! Its simple, it works, and its fun, gameplay is solid.Despite this, the game is still worth getting, and I will be waiting patiently for The Brotherhoods next game, and even be going back for the others.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: A thumbs up to support the devs. Those that like Soma, Disco Elysium and body horror (a la Cronenberg) will enjoy this game, because it feels similar to play and experience.Fantastic setting, atmosphere, story and characters; a very gory, somber, and to my surprise, moving narrative. The puzzles are not too hard, though the solutions to some of them can feel a bit random. In any case, there are hints and a manual if you need it to progress.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the game. Some puzzles felt out of place, like why the hell would item x and x go together?Also the fact you get locked out of intractables during dialogue is rough. Makes the “don’t skip dialogue” trophy weird, like the devs knew that it would annoy people so they made it a trophy? Regardless I loved the characters and the voice acting was great. Super cool setting. Moses 10/10. Also I’m not sure I’m as sensitive as other people in the comments about AI art, either I played too late and missed the updates where some of it was removed, or I just didn’t notice. I thought the art style was amazing even if some of the items looked a bit funny I thought it was just the vibe.Good job devs, let the haters hate. Gonna go play the other games because the Cayne universe sounds very interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is The Brotherhood’s fourth release, and it looks to have taken all the best elements from their previous games while building on lesson’s learned to give us a deep sea derelict danger-filled point and click.Can’t wait to dive into it further!Works well with weird aspect ratios and old hardware.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: It's stunning just how much there is in Stasis: Bone Totem. For the immense quality of the visuals alone I expected this to a quarter of its length. Point & Click is not a genre I know well or usually enjoy, but I feel like S:BT will stick with me for a long time. If you're even at least a little bit curious, you owe it to yourself to pick it up. No aspect of the game feels weak: there are so many high quality models and art assets, the story is gripping and harrowing, the puzzles are challenging but (mostly) reasonable, the music is phenomenal, and I really want to give props to the voice acting for bringing the writing to life: Charlie, Mac, and Moses are some of the most engaging characters I've seen in a while (not just in video-games). It's rare to see a game centred around characters in a relationship, and even rarer for that relationship to feel believable. Thanks to this, the descent into pure madness has so much more weight to it. I want to gush more but that would mean spoilers. What a fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Bought in on recommendation from MandaloreGaming, and it's easily one of the best stories I've experienced in a long time. Puzzle games aren't normally my thing, so I struggled a little with some of the more obscure ones, but the setting and story easily made up for any momentary frustration. Really good, would whole-heartedly recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short and sweet this is a great point and click with a great story, I cannot find many faults with it at all. I'm not the sort to generally write reviews but I was intrigued by the setting and dragged in to the plot very quickly. It held me for the entirety of it's run time (at about ten-ish hours). That being said there is some minor adventure game puzzle oddities but they are few and far between. I cannot recommend this game enough if you think the setting is interesting. I'm a very smart bear now.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Stasis: Bone Totem has a great story.  It is mostly isometric like the old Baldur's Gate Games but it does have some very nice 3D cut-scenes in a few places.  I enjoyed my time with this game because the story was so good, however, the game play itself was only okay.  I needed to use a walk through guide several times to figure out what the next step was as it was sometimes not obvious.  This is the kind of game that makes you remember something from 30-45 minutes ago that you then need to go back to and solve in some obscure way.  Most of the puzzles were fun and did make sense though.  I'd give the story a 9/10 and the game play a 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: Point-and-click game with a really cool, fresh and intriguing story. The characters are fleshed out very well and the world's lore is original and interesting (read all the logs!!!). The art and setpieces/level design is really great and the puzzles are very engaging and require good logic and patience to solve.In all it's a very strong narrative game that deserves to be played. Be brave and strong!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: A great follow up to Stasis with an even more ambitious scope and story. I am awe struck by the amount and quality of those prerendered backgrounds, the real star of the show for me.I liked the themes of the story and it mostly landed when it needed to. I was surprised at how effective some of the more unlikely character relationships ended up being.My biggest gripe was probably that some of the gameplay interaction could have been fleshed out more. Rooms will have tons of highlighted markers with no real interaction just descriptions and the "real" points of interest are often very sparse in comparison.Using the wrong items prompts no feedback from the characters or the game which often feels a bit lacking. Even point and click games in the 90's would catch those moments and elicit responses that could tell if you were on the right track with what you doing, or just add to the vibe. As such, Bone Totem is simple a lot less "playful" than it could have been, but I can excuse it somewhat considering the sheer amount of stuff in this game with such a small team.Its still a great (and disturbing) experience that both builds on and adds scifi ideas and themes to consider.By Cayne I hope to see more Stasis!
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: This is an indie masterpiece. It's a character-driven adventure game, punctuated by intense moments of drama, horror, and disgust. Everything is executed nearly flawlessly; even the cutscenes were surprisingly good for such a small team. It's one of those games that lingers in your mind long after the credits roll.However, it's not without flaws. There are occasional moments of 'moon logic,' where the puzzle solutions seem illogical. Additionally, the accompanying logs for the faces appear visually jarring.
_childDocuments_.name: STASIS: BONE TOTEM

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a neutral option for this one.  First, the positives: This game really breaks some boundaries with point and click adventures.  The way you have to use the multiple characters to coordinate and solve problems was extremely clever and well done, and really helps with both the immersion and intensity of the game.  The artwork is superb, as is the voice acting and sound effects.Where this game really falls short for me is the storyline.  All of the later portions of the game just don't make any logical sense.  If this took place on an alien world, it would have made much more sense, but an , especially as depicted, surviving for centuries is completely implausible.  If they subsisted on some form of hydroponics or aquaculture, I could buy in a little more.  As is, it just felt gratuitous, excessive, fabricated and unreasonable.  I've played all of the other games by The Brotherhood, and as gross as Statis and Cayne were, they were at least somewhat plausible.  There were also a couple of puzzles and actions that just didn't make sense to a seasoned adventure game player.  All in all it felt like the second half of the game was slapped together rather than enjoying the same care as the first half.  Considering that some of the descriptive tags were significantly displaced from the image target in several of the latter locations, to the point of not making sense, that's the only logical explanation I can come up with.Bottom line, if you really like point and click adventures, definitely give this one a try.  The gameplay is very refreshing.  But expect to have to suspend disbelief a lot the further you get into the game.

name: It Takes Two
detailed_description: Embark on the craziest journey of your life in It Takes Two, a genre-bending platform adventure created purely for co-op. Invite a friend to join for free with Friend’s Pass and work together across a huge variety of gleefully disruptive gameplay challenges. Play as the clashing couple Cody and May, two humans turned into dolls by a magic spell. Together, trapped in a fantastical world where the unpredictable hides around every corner, they are reluctantly challenged with saving their fractured relationship. Master unique and connected character abilities in every new level. Help each other across an abundance of unexpected obstacles and laugh-out-loud moments. Kick gangster squirrels’ furry tails, pilot a pair of underpants, DJ a buzzing night club, and bobsleigh through a magical snow globe. Embrace a heartfelt and hilarious story where narrative and gameplay weave into a uniquely metaphorical experience. It Takes Two is developed by the award-winning studio Hazelight, the industry leader of cooperative play. They’re about to take you on a wild and wondrous ride where only one thing is for certain: we’re better together. KEY FEATURES Pure co-op perfection — Invite a friend to join for free with Remote Play Together**, and experience a thrilling adventure built purely for two. Choose from couch or online co-op with split-screen play, and face ever-changing challenges where working together is the only way forward. Gleefully disruptive gameplay — From rampaging vacuum cleaners to suave love gurus, you never know what you’ll be up against next. Filled with genre-bending challenges and new character abilities to master in every level, experience a metaphorical merging of gameplay and narrative that pushes the boundaries of interactive storytelling. A universal tale of relationships — Discover a touching and heartfelt story of the challenges in getting along. Help Cody and May learn how to overcome their differences. Meet a diverse cast of strange and endearing characters. Join forces and go on an adventure you’ll treasure — together! ABOUT HAZELIGHT Hazelight is an award-winning independent game development studio based in Stockholm, Sweden. Founded in 2014 by Josef Fares (film director and creator of the award-winning game Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons), Hazelight is committed to pushing the creative boundaries of what is possible in games. In 2018, Hazelight released the BAFTA award-winning A Way Out — the first-ever co-op only, third-person action-adventure — as part of the EA Originals program. ABOUT EA ORIGINALS EA Originals helps shine a light on some of the most passionate, independent, and talented game studios across the globe. Discover innovative and unforgettable gaming experiences from highly creative game makers who love to enchant and inspire.

From Hazelight comes It Takes Two an innovative co-op adventure where uniquely varied gameplay and emotional storytelling intertwine in a fantastical journey. Founded to push the creative boundaries of what's possible in games, Hazelight is the award-winning studio behind the critically acclaimed A Way Out and Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons.

Something out of the ordinary

name: Dread Nautical
detailed_description: Your cruise was so relaxing until the monsters from another dimension showed up to kill everyone. Fight them off, manage your resources effectively, and convince scattered survivors to join your efforts. Supernatural forces have overwhelmed a cruise liner called Hope with mysterious monstrosities. Fight them off as one of four unlikely heroes. Manage your scarce resources effectively , and convince scattered survivors to fight alongside you. You’ll need them for any hope of escaping this “vacation” alive. Traverse all 20 decks to unlock the mysteries of the Hope. Think several steps ahead during each battle, plotting the optimal use of each character’s action points. Your weapons, bandages, and other items deteriorate , and your resources are very limited. Make sure your companions rest, or panic may overtake them. Oh… And expect to die. A lot.

_childDocuments_.review: Dread Nautical is a turn-based rogue-like strategy game with survival mechanics. You choose one of three characters, each with their personality, stats, and ability. You wake up on a ship. Someone is standing in front of you and tells you to go to deck one. As you do, you quickly find yourself fighting against an enemy who kind of looks like a zombie. After beating him, you search for any useful items on deck one and find a foghorn. You blow it and everything goes dark. You pass out...The story is interesting so far and the voice acting adds to it. Finding loot is always fun in a game. Early on, you have to manage your equipment, since you can't carry more than 4 items at a time (in the beginning). Every item can break after using it too many times, resulting in swapping items on a deck many times. The good thing is, you'll find many items when killing enemies since every enemy drops loot. The bad thing is, this all makes it unnecessarily complicated. You basically don't run out of items since you'll find new stuff quick, it's just annoying to swap them every few minutes. Every item you carry when blowing the horn will be in your base. You will unlock different stations, which will let you build new beds (to recruit new survivors in your team), upgrade and repair items, leveling up your survivors, and more. You can also upgrade every station for scrap. Scrap is one of two currencies. The other one is ruin and lets you upgrade survivors. Scrap is basically for everything else. Speaking of recruiting new survivors. On every deck, there is a chance to find survivors. You'll talk to them and need to strengthen your relationship with them, so they'll join your team. You do that through talking to them and saying the right thing (you have the choice of what to say and can choose between 2 to 4 answeres) or doing something for them (finding an item, beating a monster, etc.).After visiting a deck, your team gets hungry. You need food to satisfy their hunger. If you don't have enough food and someone is too hungry, they'll lose Health Points. Losing too many health points results in death - so be careful. You also can lose a team member going on a mission when just one or two of your members reach the horn and blow it. Sometimes your member can survive and find back to the base, other times you have the chance to find him again on a deck. But let's talk about the most important thing in the game: the turn-based fights. There is almost nothing to describe here because.. the fighting system is pretty barebones. Let's be honest. These turn-based fights are a JOKE to everyone who played ANY XCOM game (or similar ones in the genre). There is almost no strategically thinking involved besides moving to the enemy, choosing a weapon, and attacking. That's it. Sure, you have the choice to fight on a long-range (with a gun, etc.) or close range. Besides that, there is nothing to think about really. Either you're character is strong enough and has enough health points or not. And even then, most of the time enemies can't move more than two squares, so you'll easily outrun them. The story promises to be something special in the genre, but the fighting system is just boring. Add the breaking mechanic of items and you'll even get annoyed with these survival mechanics since it doesn't really require strategically thinking. I can't recommend the game to anyone who ever played turn-based strategy games. Buy it if you're new to the genre or on a sale for nothing more than 5€/USD.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Nautical

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, if you can get over some annoyances.  The story is good.  The battles are fun. Bad things:Low replay value.Part of your party can get stuck outside of a room when you get "ambushed".  This makes for the annoying practice of "rushing characters into a room at the start of a fight".  Gotta do that as fast as possible... and it is very silly and annoying.A threat system starts up when you hit floor 10.  The game is way more fun without it.  I don't want to think about how to collect loot after a battle in the least possible amount of steps (because threat goes up with every move)  It doesn't make the runs more interesting,  it just makes it more annoying, and you have to keep going straight towards the exit on every map. Repair costs are different for every item.  Some of the costs are too high.  It sucks when you get a new more powerful item, only to figure out that it just costs too much to actually use.  While in battle you start thinking "should I shoot it with my rifle?  Each shot costs me 30 scraps, I think I'll just attack it with my dagger"Stuns last for 2 turns. (on both sides)  Like why?  1 turn stuns are overpowered in every game already.  Why go with 2 turn stuns?One armor slot.  So annoying when the only way you can pick up an item, is to drop your current item.  You can't pick up any piece of armor, because you wear one already.  I picked up an armor piece thinking it would be better than my current one, but after upgrading it to lvl 10, I find out it is worse.  That's because upgrades also make zero sense and add have different benefits for different items.
_childDocuments_.name: Dread Nautical

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed thoughts about Dread Nautical. I like how you can collect survivors depending on how your relationship progresses with them. The lovecraftian graphics are vector-style and it really suits the game. As much as I would recommend this game, the cons are frustrating and somewhat a grind to enhance your survivors. PROS: Tactical challenge, skill tree, storylineCONS: Limited equipment slots, expensive repair, feeding survivors

_childDocuments_.review: If you really enjoy this genre of games and this game is at least 50% off, then I'd say to go for it. Otherwise, the game isnt worth it. So far, the story and graphics are nice but the controls make it difficult to truly have fun playing. I have a touchscreen computer, so some controls require that I touch my screen and others work with the mouse. I cannot look at the details of the items I find so Im just blindly consuming them to see what they do. Unless I press the weapon in inventory exactly in the middle of the icon, it registers as a move command and in the middle of a battle, it's extremely annoying. Speaking of annoying, the voice acting doesnt add to the game imo. I considered asking for a refund but I doubt steam will allow me to at this point. This game has been out since April 2020 and just released on steam, I assume to recuperate as much losses as possible since there's virtually no fan base, no wiki page for more info, and barely any playthroughs.

name: Sumerian Six
detailed_description: Sumerian Six follows the Enigma Squad, a team of commandos composed of the world’s greatest scientists who combine their skills to conduct secret missions in their fight against the Third Reich. Together, you seek to thwart ex-member Hans Kammler's nefarious plans involving a powerful, mystical substance named Geiststoff. Embark on a thrilling journey across multiple continents alongside allies such as the exiled chemist Rosa Reznick, Wojtek the Werebear, and the esoteric psychoanalyst Siegfried von Adelsberg. Dispose of your enemies by using each team member’s unique set of abilities inspired by their fields of expertise, and learn to master the art of chaining them together for devastating effects if you hope to be successful. As you delve deeper into the Nazi plot, you’ll encounter occult-scientific weapons and ancient Sumerian artifacts linked to Kammler's machinations. A grim future awaits you should the Nazis be victorious, so do your best to prevent that dark timeline from coming true in this real-time tactical stealth adventure. Demon Nazis Led by Hans Kammler, a former member of your Squad, the Nazis tap into the occult to create the ultimate Wunderwaffe. Face off against heavily armed, mutated, and supernaturally charged forces, and put your strategic abilities and dexterity to the ultimate test. Playful Violence Meets Super Science Sneak your way around Nazi strongholds and dispatch the ever-present watchmen in a variety of ways before taking on the more serious threats before you. Combine your team's dynamic powers in creative displays of tactical might. Travel the World Inspired by real places and events, Sumerian Six takes you on a journey through an alternate history where folk stories and conspiracy theories are as real as the Nazi threat.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really enjoying . I don't think I am the best at these types of games, having to reduce the difficulty to easy early on in the campaign and still finding it challenging, but I have been impressed with the sheer vastness of some of the levels and the tactical thinking needed to overcome the obstacles. I like to sit back and study the environments, try out some of the more obscure ways of killing foes, like electrocuting them in water, running them over with moving vehicles, or dropping freight on their heads. That is the beauty of this game though, you can approach it in many different ways. There are additional objectives for you to try and aim for, which can make things much harder, like not using certain skills, or finishing below a certain time, or not killing certain enemies, or you can forget about them and just try to get through the level and continue the story. Along with the three difficulty levels, these extra components can increase difficulty further if you wish. The six characters you will play with are introduced in stages and they will change with the story as you progress. They all have different skills to bring to the party and you can switch between the ones in play whenever you like. Certain situations will require a certain character to solve the problem and others will have a more experimental feel with a combination of characters used. You will probably have a favourite character in your group, and mine was Roza Reznick, who could dissolve characters instead of hiding the bodies; incapacitate enemies with a toxic drip; disperse enemies using a poison gas; and the most fun of all, attaching bombs to soldiers and detonating them from afar. This was especially satisfying when attached to a soldier doing his rounds and then exploding it as he approached a group of soldiers, taking them all out. That never got tired, and all deaths come with a comical quip by the character like "This will hurt, a lot." as she dissolved them where they stood. Other characters had cool skills like changing into a mutated bear that can kill enemies that other characters cannot; an electrocution skill that bounces from enemy to enemy; a skill that possesses characters so that you can walk around in their bodies and hop out when you want; a swap mechanic that switches the character's positions; a temporary invisibility cloak; and a trampoline type gadget that launches enemies into the air. Then there are the usual distraction techniques like whistling or throwing bottles to distract enemies so that you can sneak past them, or if you want to go Rambo there are various weapons to use, which obviously attracts a lot of attention. I thought the range of skills were varied and interesting and let you approach situations in many different ways. The game is a stealth game in essence with soldiers posted at various points looking in certain directions, or having patrols moving in a set pattern. Sneaking around can evade the gaze of some enemies but as soon as you stand up to kill someone, you become visible, and have a certain amount of time before you are discovered, represented by a traffic light system. Sometimes, you can just about get in there, eliminate an enemy, and get out before the alarms are set off and other times you just don't make it and if you are not shot on sight you will need to run away and hide somewhere. Quite often you have to be mindful where your team are situated because the alerted soldiers will find one of your team mates if they are not sufficiently hidden. In some cases, I purposely triggered the alarm so that the soldiers came looking for me whilst I waited around a corner to kill them. It doesn't always work, as you can easily get outnumbered, but it is another example at how you can approach things from different angles. The characters can obtain upgrades to their skills and health by locating crates which are shown on the mini-map along with your teammates and enemy locations amongst other things. I did find that when switching characters though it wasn’t always obvious where they were and you have to go looking for them. It would be nice if when switching, the game took you to the character you select. I got killed quite a lot when soldiers were on high alert because I moved the wrong character out of hiding by accident, and taking you to the correct character would have solved this. Enemies get more advanced as you continue and the Nazis unleash more twisted experimental foes that can use the supernatural to teleport or become invincible apart from an Achilles heel you need to take advantage of. For example, the Geist has a tether which you must break which makes them temporarily vulnerable to attack. This means you will need one character to turn off the tether, and because you only have a few seconds to act, another character needs to kill him quickly. There is an option to plan attacks by using the action planner which allows more than one character to attack at the same time, useful for taking out a couple of guards simultaneously, or using one character to distract a guard whilst the other one sneaks up and kills him. There's lots of things to think about, like planning the best route, or where you can retreat to if things go wrong. At the start of each level, you are given a debrief of the situation and offered some alternative routes to take, but ultimately, it's up to you how you approach the mission and whether you want to try and obtain some of the secondary objectives. The levels are very large. One level took me three hours to complete. There are regular autosaves and the option to manually save whenever you want too though so it easy to dip in and out of. If one of your team perishes, you will start again from where you died, although this can throw you in the thick of things sometimes, but if you find you are continually getting killed because of this you can easily access another save. I loved the mixture of supernatural and Indiana Jones type archaeology with the Nazis trying to turn the tide of the war through abominable experiments on creatures and soldiers. There are some nice cut scenes after each level furthering the story, and the voice acting is very good when they are acting out the story or talking whilst in the game.  The maps look great, with imaginative scenery and well drawn objects, and although there are a few issues with the controls, like having difficulty getting onto ladders sometimes, or picking up dead bodies lying near ladders by mistake, I found it very easy to navigate my gang around the different areas with a controller.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I was given a free key for this game before release by Devolver Digital and Artificer.Thanks for letting me stream and review the game early.I have completed the game twice now. First playthrough on hard and the second playthrough on normal to get all the challenges and achievements.Before this game I was worried that we wouldn't get any more high quality games in this genre after Mimimi Games shut down. After playing this game I must say - this game proved me wrong.It feels like the developers understood what made Mimimi's games so special and tried to recapture their magic with this game. I don't mean this in a bad way at all. I think this is the best thing they could have done and it worked out great.Pretty much everything feels high quality about this game and it feels like a lot of love and effort was put into this game.tl;dr if you liked the games that Mimimi created then you will most likely like this too. If you are on the fence about this game then you should download the demo and give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: The newest modern tactical/strategy stealth game, following the fantastic Mimimi Games releases (Shadow Tactics, Desperados 3, and Shadow Gambit), and it's truly great to see this genre come back so strong.This new entry is also excellent. It looks great, plays great, the setting is fun, and the voice acting is surprisingly excellent.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Artificer has done a superb job with Sumerian Six. It takes the core mechanics from the Mimimi games, mixes it with the Nazis from the Commandos series, and spikes it with a fun supernatural element. The levels are large, fun sandboxes and it is rewarding to pick apart guard patrols and clear areas before grabbing XP crates that improve skills for subsequent missions. Each individual squad member has a good repertoire of skills, but tougher Nazis pose enough challenge and vision cones are still important to avoid. While the story is basic, it does an okay job at keeping the Enigma Squad on target. It is a pity that Mimimi are no more, but Sumerian Six definitely keeps their spirit alive.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: If you are reading this review it's because you already have an interest in Tactical-stealth games. This plays like almost all the other ones and I love it. The story is interesting, enemy types are familiar with a couple of new ones and the abilities feel good. Each area of the map feels like you can beat it in several different ways and it's fun to find your own way of forcing a square peg through a round hole.Thoroughly enjoyed this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell that Sumerian Six took a lot of inspirations from the games made by Mimimi. This becomes really obvious when you look at the enemy types: You have the standard enemy that can be easily distracted, a enemy who ignores most distractions and an elite enemy who's immune to most attacks but can be easily killed by a specific party member. The game, however, does spice things up a bit by adding two additional enemies types that requires different tactics.The levels look great and each team member has a distinct personality. Only Wojtek was bit disappointing because he neither has a history with any of the other team members nor do we learn anything about his past. The games also has one mechanic that's rather uncommon in real-time strategy games: experience points. Most skills have an XP bar and can be leveled up by completing side objectives, collecting XP boosters scattered around the map or by killing enemies. Thankfully the game doesn't force you to grind  (unless you want all the achievements) and you are never be “underleveled” as long as you do side objectives and keep an eye out for the XP boosters.So if you like the Mimimi games and want more of the same I can wholeheartedly recommend this game to you.  But if you are looking for something that adds some new mechanics or ideas to the "Mimimi formula" you are probably going to be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game!If you miss Mimimi Games and their team, you should definitely play this game. The gameplay design is very similar because it was directly handed down from Mimimi Games, which unfortunately had to shut down. Whether it's the incredibly fun Desperados III, Shadow Tactics, or Shadow Gambit, you should not miss this. This game is not easy to play; it requires strategic planning, making it a brain-teasing and enjoyable experience just like those games. Plus, it's reasonably priced. Let's come together to support great games like this one for future installments.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I discovered Sumerian Six by chance, thanks to a Mimimi endorsement, which suggested to all stealth tactics fans to try the demo and help the developer in keeping this genre alive. It is indeed a difficult time for players that love this kind of games, after the closure of the best in class, Mimimi, and I wanted to support this game on launch, while I wait for the return of Commandos later this year.Sumerian Six took indeed everything good from Mimimi, and excellent titles like Desperados 3 and Shadow Gambit, literally copying those game mechanics while introducing new characters in an alternate WW2 setting, where magic and special weapons are the ordinary. Think Wolfenstein with stealth tactics, an isometric camera and an Avengers team of special ops, and you'll have a pretty good idea of what is offered here.I liked the game, which does not revolutionise the genre, and while the story is a bit convoluted and not that original, the kind of powers and abilities at your disposal let you beat all 10 levels in new and fun ways. Graphics are good, level design excellent, together with its musical score, but don't expect anything more. This is a game for players that already played all the other stealth tactics games out there, and want more of it. If you are new to the genre, I would suggest to start from Desperados 3 and maybe try the Sumerian Six demo first, like I did.In the end I would give Sumerian Six a very good 7 out of 10 score, hoping that new games will still come to this genre. While I don't think stealth tactics can evolve much more, I still think many new stories, characters and settings can exploit a niche but strong community of dedicated players!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six is not just a love letter to the stealth RTT games, mainly Mimimi's, but brings new things too. There is so much creativity within the lore and the gameplay, which is more often seen in the special skills. I played tens of hours of the demo, and I'm already immersed into the game after counting days to the release. Sumerian Six is a must go to all fans of the RTT genre, and I can see in the near future it will get overwhelmingly positive reviews, just like the Mimimi's games had.
