_childDocuments_.review: ***: If you've beaten Desperados III or Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun on normal difficulty, you will likely want to play Sumerian Six on Hard -- otherwise you may not feel sufficiently challenged.***Review version. 1.02: Good stealth tactics title that plays with the established formula in some interesting ways. However, at time of writing the production quality is not polished enough to compete with Desperados III or Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun. I would recommend mostly to players who have already exhausted the Minimi library.This review is mostly going to be aimed at the developers, because I believe that they have a lot of potential. However, they still have a long way to go until they can rightfully claim the now-vacant Minimi throne. ******One of the strengths of Sumerian Six are the player-character mechanics. They feel powerful, they can be combined in interesting ways, and allow for plenty of creativity on the part of the player. The enemy mechanics, by contrast, feel very weak and unimaginative. Beyond the basic archetypes of Soldier, Officer, and Heavy, the game only offers the Geist and the Demon, plus a stationary "magic inhibitor". That is a tragically low amount of enemy types for a game set in an 'anything-goes' Nazi-magic universe. The enemy AI is very basic as well: soldiers don't investigate suspicious activities enough, which leads to bizarre situations e.g. where soldiers see their colleague saluting to a ghost or in a Rosa-induced stupor but don't think that they should look into it.  From an artistic point of view, the levels are beautiful. From a structural point of view, they lack depth. Part of this is because some key environmental mechanics are missing: no footsteps in snow/sand, no light/dark viewcones, no swimming. The options for encounter design are limited by the lack of enemy variety -- there are only so many ways that five different entities can be combined. Without a proper Minimi-style challenge system (the current "don't use X skill" is insufficient), the level designers weren't forced to accommodate a healthy variety of paths to victory. Corpse management is janky and requires a lot of fiddling to find a suitable cliff -- often corpse recepticles are missing entirely -- which will drive the hard-core fans of the genre crazy. The addition of optional objectives to incentivize players to beat the whole map is cute, but when these are tied to XP gain then they become mandatory.  I chose to play Sumerian Six on "Normal" because that is the difficulty setting I had chosen in Desperados III and Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun.  This is a communication issue -- when selecting difficulty at the beginning, I thought I was getting Minimi difficulty so I naturally didn't select "Hard". I kept expecting the "Normal" difficulty to spike but it didn't -- in the end I played through the game on a difficulty setting that wasn't intended for me. Reading other player's reviews, however, I began to get a clearer sense of the problem: there is a massive skill gulf between Stealth-RTT veterans and first time players.For someone comfortable with Stealth-RTT mechanics, "Normal" is pretty trivial. There are massive gaps in the guards covering each other. If there is mutual coverage, then the 'overseer' guard is usually pretty easy to remove. The guards have very limited random head movements or zigzag patrol routes, which makes incidental detection rare. By contrast, the tools of the Enigma Squad are extremely powerful: Rosa's stun is completely overpowered (especially since she can crouch while doing it, and the target won't draw attention unless spoken to); Siegfried's invisibility beam and distraction ghost (no need to get a disguise!) are similarly strong. It rarely took me more than two tries to solve any one guard, and I am far from being an Stealth-RTT pro. However, for a relative novice who isn't aware or confident in using these powerful skills, the game can be punishingly hard -- once the alarm goes off a character can die instantly. In response to this, the enemy density seems to have been reduced so that these players are not constantly drowning in waves of Nazi guards. From the outside, the solution to this problem seems to be: reduce the penalty of triggering an alarm (to help the newer players) while increasing the reward for completing the level in full stealth. This would allow for more interesting problem solving on a moment to moment basis (more guards covering each other) but not result in an completely un-fun alarm state if a mistake has been made.The most interesting new thing that Sumerian Six tries is the XP system for the character skills. It is a good idea but it was not implemented in a way that truly motivates the player. For one, it was missing the "anticipation" phase, where the player sees their unrealized skills (e.g. via a skill tree) and thinks about how cool it would be to have such power. Secondly, it is missing choice, because the type of upgrade to the skill is determined by the game and not chosen by the player. Yes, one can selectively level-up one character over another, but the gains from enemies pale in comparison to the 150xp crates, so the feeling of agency is minimal. Finally, the impact of the skills is often hard to feel because there is no A/B comparison to how it was before.    The devil is in the details, and there were a lot of small inconsistencies that ate at the overall impression. The tooltips keep popping up even after the 75th time walking over them -- players should be able to mute them. The repository of these tooltips is also needlessly difficult to find if you miss them the first time (if it exists at all). If a crucial line of dialog occured during a fight, there doesn't seem to be any place to find it. The same goes for the XP gains from optional quests -- if the trigger was met during a frantic fight, you have no idea what just got upgraded. Ladders shouldn't be used as greebles to make the environment nicer, they should only be included if they are usable. Rosa's green outline and Sid's cyan outline don't read well on green bushes of Lilleby, the same goes for the green view-cones on green grass. The color palette within Kammler's Secret Base makes it very hard to read at a glance where the guards are. Nazi officers addressing each other as "du" is highly questionable. Rosa-stunned soldiers grunting loudly and incessantly is really distracting. Sid's voice makes him sound like the assistant social media intern for One Direction, not a man who can casually sling a Panzerwolf over his shoulder.For the first effort of a young studio under a lot of time pressure, Sumerian Six came out remarkably well, which is why I think it deserves a thumbs up. That said, I don't think serious fans of the genre will be as patient a second time around -- this is a very detail-oriented group of gamers that are accustomed to a high degree of polish. It is my hope that with more time for iteration, the next title will be a true classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I love the real time stealth tactics genre and I'm happy to say that Sumerian Six is really good addition to it.Let's get the negatives first as there are only few of those:-Controlling units isn't as precise as in Mimimi's games. It's easy to accidentally order your characters to run or not to drop dead body etc. Nothing too crazy, you just have to be mindful when issuing orders.-Sometimes some minor visual glitches after reloading a save.-Game would sometimes crash when using pink character's abilities. Not too frequent though, not even once in a mission.And then the positives:+The character abilities are fresh and the characters feel powerful. Only the trapper archetype felt lackluster and it's probably because other characters were much more fun to use. But no character felt useless.+Two new enemy types were unique and the game had clever spin on the heavy can't-melee-me-outright enemy type which along the fun player abilities kept the gameplay and the puzzles interesting.+The game kept shuffling the player character roster so every level (well apart from 4th and 5th, as you use the same four characters on those missions) felt compelling and the gameplay didn't feel repetitive.I played on hard difficulty and it was a decent challenge from start to finish. Ten levels which took about 2 hours each. All in all good game and more importantly a fun game. If you like this genre then this is easy recommendation on full price and must buy from sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I have played basically all the main stealth games of this like since Commandos 2 and was very sad when Mimimi Games folded last year.But this, this is a beautifully done spiritual successor (so much so that if you know Shadow Tatics/Gambit, you will not even have to re-learn keyboard bindings). It's gorgeous to look at, has a nice nearly upbeat sound track and is even somewhat playful in its over-the-top'ness. There was love behind this game and it shows.If you liked Desperados III, Shadow Tactics, Shadow Gambit etc., you will also love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Great entry into the real time tactics genre. Character abilities in Sumerian Six are what really set this game apart. Might seem a bit over-the-top for some, but it's pure unadulterated fun to play & experiment with those skills. Love how the abilities get upgraded as well.Story wise, it's nothing fancy, but it works. Gameplay is my first priority for this type of stealth strategy games & Sumerian Six delivers on that front from the beginning till the last. The only thing I didn't like much is the music/soundtracks, personally.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six is a blast! It’s like Indiana Jones went sci-fi with a team of quirky scientists and a werebear, all set on stopping Nazis from using mystical powers. (think Commandos but with more personality and bizarre powers).The game’s got great style, fun characters, and loads of ways to creatively take down enemies. It doesn’t reinvent the wheel, but who cares when you’re wrecking Nazis with poison and paw swipes? Aside from a few sound glitches, it runs smoothly and is just plain fun. A solid pick if you enjoy mixing strategy with some good old-fashioned Nazi-smashing action "à la Commandos"
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Fellow refugees from Mimimi Games would feel right at home with Sumerian Six. It's a very high quality game that you would even mistake Mimimi Games as the devs. It does have weird performance issues and bugs that can severely hinder your progress. Outside of that, It very much differentiates itself with the characters and their abilities than any games in the genre instead of falling in the trap of copy pasting, which a challenging thing to accomplish especially as a tactical stealth game.Highly Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: At the moment of this review (version 1.0.2), the bugs might prevent you from having a good time."Sumerian Six" is about punching supernatural nazis. It's also a real-time stealth tactics — the genre we don't get much anymore, so a point of appreciation goes to the developers by default.Since I'm a fan of the genre, the game will be compared to the standouts like the ones from Mimimi Games. And while there are some interesting choices like unusual abilities and an XP system (unrefined and grindy, but an intriguing concept nonetheless), it's lacking what I'm used to: enemies don't search hideouts, ground types don't influence stealth at all, triggering an alarm leaves next to zero ways for an escape.Regarding bugs… there's a lot. The biggest issue is quickloading: it might leave an alarm sound, it might keep showing visual effects that are no longer there, it will restart dialogs from random moments of time, it might not even be quick (won't interrupt defeat animations). On top of that, playable characters have pathfinding issues to the degree of being stuck alone in a corner; the player can execute infinite mind controls by singular characters (it's a balance issue, but was weird to discover); I even got a BSOD in the original demo and a full reboot in the current version of the game.But with all that, the soundtrack is awesome, some of the encounters are extra demanding on the hardest difficulty, and I enjoyed the gameplay enough.18 hours to clear every map. 26 hours of struggling through the bugs to complete achievements. I wish the team success, but "Sumerian Six" really needs to get a stable version.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: You get to murder nazis with a hammer: 10/10 dead nazis.  The demo's still available so I recommend playing that, since it'll give a better idea of whether you'll enjoy this than anything the reviews say. (Also it might encourage more companies to keep the demos around after release.)This is a great spin on ideas championed by the Mimimi series of stealth-tactics games, this one feeling like it'd be a great fit for an "Atomic Robo" videogame if anyone's familiar with that comic: Action-Scientists versus Occult Nazis.And we get into weird technology and how you can use it to solve (nazi) problems almost immediately, which is nice to see.My only minor issue so far isn't a game problem so much as a brain problem: the UI and interface is *almost* identical to the Mimimi games I've played, which means I keep brain-farting and using the shortcuts in ways which have changed here.  The main one is that you hold ctrl and click corpses to carry them, rather than double-clicking them: the game tells you clearly what to do in the tutorial, which is why I think this is a brain problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: While the game seems promising, it still has game breaking bugs that shouldn't have passed any normal QA, like the skills not getting restored after being blocked by a disruptor. Devs acknowledged the bug, but clearly not a in a rush to throw a hotfix for it, leaving everyone to have their save file corrupted. Right now feels like an Early Access rather than a full release.Until this is resolved, I give up playing and cannot in good conscience recommend it.EDIT: a patch from yesterday did solve the said game breaking bug, but had to restart the map for the game to acknowledge it, the save was already corrupted. I'm reluctantly changing this to a positive review because the game is otherwise great, love it. Hopefully I don't have to come back and send it back to negative again.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like Mimimi's 'first pancake'. Very easy on hard, with super OP skills, mediocre story and characters. Challenges are boring and the same in every mission: three of them (complete all optional objectives, collect all XP, and don't raise the alarm) are just my usual play style; the fourth is 'not use X skill'; and the fifth is just a boring timer. Devs copied Mimimi's visual style but for some reason decided to implement only the bare minimum mechanics (no footsteps sounds on any surface, no footprints, no dark/light difference in vision cones, no swimming, etc.).The game is not that bad by itself, but inferior in every way to Mimimi's games. I can only recommend it on a big sale and if you don't mind easy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six does not invent the wheel by adding anything new to this genre. However since the revitalization of this genre by Mimimi games, many others are picking up the torch after they have left the development; and that is good news. Sum Six drops you into the fictional world of WWII (unlike Commandos) where you get to play using heroes with superpowers that are reasonable and fun to play with. Using this formula any setting could be used with unique heroes to make a game. That also is a good thing! It has enough to satiate your hunger for strange and fun, while you wait for Commandos: Origins and the like.Don't get me wrong, this is fantastic. It was obvious what direction they are taking and Mimimi inspired Showdown mode (from Desperados) that was in Shadow Tactics and Shadow Gambit makes a return here. It's good to see that everyone is taking note of what Mimimi did (who were inspired by Commanods franchise partly) and implementing it into their system. Even the upcoming Commandos: Origins have the same method that Mimimi left for us. So credit is where credit is due. Putting that aside, this game is also a breath of fresh air. At the time of release it runs just like the demo, but with a bit of stuttering. Nothing a patch or two can't solve. Overall it's an easy pick for lover of tactical RPG. Devolver Digital knows how to pick their cherries.+ Diverse 6 heroes with their strange, weird and fun abilities. Imagine WWII heroes but with superpowers; better than just having a hero with a shield I say!+ Campaign missions where you are tested to see how fast and efficient you are in clearing out the stage of all enemies or skip them all, while trying to beat the best score. + Nice jazzy music, though it sometimes get repetitive if you play a mission for too long. Needed more variations.+ The fun you get by planning and executing orders using given heroes that we all know from previous titles.Now there are some issues, some will hopefully be patched out but some are inherent to the game itself.- Music and ambient sound have clicking, chirping and stuttering in them. This is a huge annoyance since music and sound plays critical role for immersion. This needs to be fixed with patch asap.- What you see is what you get, this game does not invent or add anything new to this genre. Once again, Artificer had the chance to do something more to surpass Mimimi devs by adding things like "pick your own hero to play already beaten stages" or "have any hero with another heroes abilities, mix and match, and give it a go." All opportunities are missed here.- For some heroes, some abilities don't seem to synergize with each other. This is a nit pick on my part but it feels like some abilities are meant to be used with another hero's ability only. As difficult as it may be, being able to have that invisible chain linking every ability of every hero together would've been nice, albeit very hard to execute. So not a big issue. This is something we all saw in previous titles, so you can take or as it is or pick on it. It however does not hinder gameplay.- Game as of now runs with a bit of frame rate drops and stutters. Combine that with the issue with music/sound, it's pretty jarring, but again, a patch or two should fix this.Overall it's a nice game. Sum Six did not change the dish but rather cook the same one differently. If you are into this genre or love this style of gameplay, no reason not to pick this one up. Price is reasonable and gameplay is fun. Let's see where Artificer goes from here. The potential is huge and branching out into different settings, themes and powers would make for some new games in years to come. Who knows, maybe Artificer would be the next Mimimi devs' successor.Here is to their journey...
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of all Mimimi (R.I.P.) games - Shadow Tactics, Desperados III, Shadow Gambit, so the news about the demise of this amazing studio left me grieving - I would buy a stealth tactics game from them in any setting and would love them to develop their style. Sadly, it looks like there are not too many of us fans of this genre. For a while it seemed that the only exit would be to replay the above mentioned titles over and over again, but then Sumerian Six demo appeared on the horizon. I played it and... felt at home. The controls are exactly the same, the level-building and approach to the design is almost identical. Yes, I would like to see the gameplay rely on lights and shadows, this feature added a lot of depth, also more synergy between characters' abilities would be welcome. But I loved the originality of abilities, liked the story and the setting. Mystic Nazi fighters are more interesting to me than fantasy pirates. All in all, I loved Sumerian Six and would welcome a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game a lot!! It's a bit simpler than mimimi games, but it's a lot of fun to play! And visually is very very similar.Playing as a team with super powers makes it feel fresh and opens up a lot of possibilities for creative problem solving. One downside of the game is that it doesn't have a functional/simulation type coding for the environments. For example you can't just throw the enemy corpse off any ledge, or jump down from any high point. These things only work at pre-determined locations and it can get a bit annoying sometimes. The game is absolutely worth a buy if you're into tactical games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: this game proves that Artificer has everything in their hands to carry on Mimimi Games' legacy and keep the Stealth Strategy genre alive and kicking. has a very Mimimi Games' flair, in the best way possible. Even some character abilities are wildly similar to the ones from their previous games (,  and ).✅ The game is set in WW2 with an unique "weird science" setting, as the devs themselves state. It has this very eldritch vibe to it while rooted in Sumerian mythology, particularly in the Epic of Gilgamesh.✅ The game's cutscenes play within the limitations of the budget in a very stylistic way. They come in two flavors: hand-drawn black and white illustrations and in-game models. Both cutscenes types are minimally animated but still feel dynamic and entertaining.✅ Very well crafted level design. There is a total of 10 stages; later levels are particularly longer and larger.✅ Distinct cast of playable characters, each with their own set of abilities that can be upgraded by killing enemies and collecting special items present in each level. Characters also have funny banters that ooze personality. The dynamic reminds me a lot of the  crew.✅ Lots of unique mechanics to make the game more challenging.✅ Clean UI and sleek graphic design for the menus.✅ Fantastic music. I wish they'd actually sell the digital soundtrack here on Steam because I really loved it.✅ The enemy hierarchy is similar to that of the Mimimi titles, but with new distinct enemies with their own unique mechanics.✅ The dev team is very transparent and communicative, and there is even an in-game feature for direct bug report.❌ The game has a few performance issues that lead to high GPU and CPU utilization, as well FPS drops; most of those issues can be fixed by capping the FPS and forcing V-Sync both in-game and in the Graphics Card settings. There were also some very rare and random crashes on my side that are probably related to the engine.❌ Some very minor issues like sometimes the music becoming quieter, or the game briefly freezing when opening the menu, or sometimes characters getting stuck on ladders. I've read that some users experienced crashes but I personally haven't got a single one.❌ Hard Mode's extra enemies only start appearing on later maps and not by much.Overall, I really loved this game. It was instant purchase for me because Devolver Digital is arguably the best Indie publisher out there, and all the games they support are certified bangers.Maybe this could be my veteran Mimimi speaking (I have over 100 hours in each of their games), but I felt that this game is significantly easy, even on Hard Mode. But I don't think this hinders the experience at all.If you like the Stealth Strategy games from the now defunct Mimimi (RIP), you'll love . It has everything that makes Mimimi great. I'm hoping they'll add some Challenge Missions like Mimimi did with .
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six is a tactical stealth game that is nearly identical to Mimimi Games' stellar Shadow Tactics, Desperados III, and Shadow Gambit, and while I mourn the loss of Mimimi and the quality of video games they were releasing, Artificer has stepped up to produce yet another great tactical stealth game in Mimimi's wake. Sumerian Six has a unique occult WWII-era setting that easily sets itself apart from the other games in this genre. The stealth puzzles it presents you with are clever and satisfying to solve, while the myriad occult abilities are loads of fun to experiment with. The characters are so far very entertaining and not just slapstick chatterboxes. The game also looks fantastic, it's stylish and the world is well-realized with stunningly vibrant environments.The game has some rougher edges, but these are mostly things to do with occasional control responsiveness which do not ruin the overall experience in this type of game and can easily be sanded down with patches. If you were a fan of what Mimimi was doing or even if this game just piques your interest, it's well worth a look!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who hasn’t finished a real-time tactics game since Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood (which I loved), I was pleasantly surprised by Sumerian Six. I dipped into Shadow Tactics but didn’t get far due to its difficulty and slow pacing, but Sumerian Six kept me hooked thanks to its vibrant characters and unique abilities. Each character feels distinct, and their powers are fun to experiment with, making the game challenging but never frustrating. The challenges for each level add an extra layer of difficulty, but you can always adjust the difficulty or focus on these challenges if you want more of a test.The plot is a bit much at times, but the mechanics are solid, and I found myself enjoying the game more and more as I progressed. Some characters feel a bit overpowered, but you can always adjust things to keep the game balanced. Whether you’re a tactics game veteran or a newcomer to the genre, the diverse abilities make it accessible while still offering enough depth for seasoned players.I played on Steam Deck, so I won’t get into the graphics much (it looked good, though), but I do really like the art style. The audio and voice acting are fantastic, and the characters are genuinely fun to interact with.After finishing the game, I dove straight into a second playthrough and am working toward 100% achievements, which speaks volumes about how much I enjoyed it.I highly recommend Sumerian Six to fans of the genre, newcomers, and even also for those whose only exposure to the genre was The Legend of Sherwood (I see you and I respect your previous choices, but really give Sumerian Six a try).Also, Wojtek forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I am in love.I have played this game now for 4 hours and I think that this is enough playtime to give my opinion already. And I simply fricking love this game.Combined, I sank more than 150 hours into the Mimimi Games (Desperados 3, Shadow Gambit, Shadow Tactics) and I'm pleased to say that this game is as great as those. I love that your characters have these crazy strong abilities. This makes for a very satisfying gameplay loop, just like it did in Shadow Gambit. I'm playing this game on Hard and in some areas it could be a bit too easy for a veteran like me, but in a way, this is also the fun of it. It just feels awesome to pick off enemies one by one. And while I love the Mimimi games, they had a lot of levels and scenarios where you were scratching your head and wondering if the developers actually playtested their game, that's how difficult some of these were. (Yes, I played all of them on Hard and with Challenges; don't start.) Samurian Six feels more respectable towards the player in that regard.Speaking of Shadow Gambit: Where that game pooped the bed with its weird story and "humour", Samurian Six feels closer to Desperados 3. The characters are charming and have banter going on, and the relationships between them are interesting.I'm impressed by this game's polish (no pun intended). So far, I didn't encounter a singe bug yet and the game runs tremendously well on my machine: On 4k and High graphic settings, I hit 60FPS every second. For comparison: Shadow Gambit on High only got me to 45 FPS in 4k. My rig: AMD Radeon RX 6700 [comparable to Nvidia 3060Ti], AMD Ryzen 5 5600X, 32GB RAM. (Just to be clear: I have the FPS limited to 60 for this game.)Also, I have to say: the amount of voice lines "taken over" from the Mimimi games is beyond stunning. I noted down a few: "I got the tools for the job", "A nice little stroll", "Not worth my time", "Don't waste my time", "Let's find you a better spot", "There, there", "Wise choice", "Just say the word", "I'm ready", "I know what needs to be done", "Consider it done", "Just tell me" -- it's staggering :D If I was to make suggestions, I would love to see a possibility to set the fast-forward ability via toggling the X button instead of holding it. Thank you for such an amazing game, Artificer. I hope that you will either make a sequel or make some DLC. I truly hope that you will have lots of success with this game and that it will make you rich. I'll probably also get Showgunners, that's how impressed I am with the quality at display here.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Finished the game and loved it. It became even better as I was playing, with more interesting abilities and enemy types. Hope to see more games like this from Artificer. I couldn't wait until I finish the game. I had to write a review now. As a kid I really loved Desperados and Commandos. Then as I was growing up no more games like those were coming out. So I thought the genre is dead. But then one day I saw Shadow Tactics from Mimimi and was surprised but excited to see a same type of game like those old ones. Bought it, finished it, loved it. After that I bought Mimimi's other two games as well on release (Desperados 3, Shadow Gambit) and loved both. So I was really sad when they closed up. First time I heard about Sumerian Six is actually thanks to them. They mentioned the game on their Discord server and after seeing the store page screenshots I got really excited. Luckily there was a demo, downloaded it, completed it and knew Artificer know what they are doing. So bought the full game and had to write this review after a few hours. The setting is Word War 2 with some sci-fi but to be honest as far as I'm concerned I don't really care about the setting that much in a game like this and more about the gameplay. And it is good, really good. The character abilities are interesting, it has the mandatory different enemy types that react differently to distractions and/or are harder to kill. It also has the thing that Mimimi brought in: you can pause the time, give commands to multiple characters at the same time and with one button activate them. And you need to use this often to succeed. Plus it has interesting stuff like devices that block your abilities and you need to sneak around without them until you turn the device off and interesting side objectives that make the game even harder (not allowed to kill specific enemies because they are double agents, etc.)If the game turns horrible suddenly my review is going to change. But I highly doubt that is going to happen. I'm really glad we got Artificer carrying on with this genre that I thought had died with Mimimi. If you miss Mimimi or if you loved Commandos or Desperados as a kid buy this. Support the devs. Show them there is demand for games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: The spiritual successor to Mimimi (RIP) games. I'm only on the first few missions but a downside for me so far is the writing. It's like Mimimi characters "Marvelified" and turned to 11 where every character (especially the main one) is a sarcastic, quippy, joker. Obviously, story and characters come second to the gameplay, but the writing is afraid to take itself seriously. Mimimi can be lighthearted while still taking the plot with at least some semblance of tension.Still a good game in a niche genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: The demo has the first two full levels so it's extremely generous and you'll know if this is a game for you. And the demo progress carries over to the actual game. I went in thinking this would be a janky example of stealth tactics. But this game stands up there with some of the best in the genre. It's great. No, it doesn't add much. But there's something to be said for making a great version of an existing formula. And actually the character skills lean on the more powerful side so I think it's one of the easier games in the genre- maybe a great starting point for people new to stealth tactics. I also recommend this developer's take on XCOM called Showgunners.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of reviews saying that this could be a Mimimi-title. But that is not entirely true. The Mimimi-games are a little bit more polished. And it is in the details, but it is there. I'm not saying that this is a bad game, because it is not. It is great, and as a fan of the Mimimi-games, this is still a very enjoyable game for me. And I do hope that this is not the last game in this genre from this studio.Let me give some examples of what I mean. With the Mimimi-games, when you double-click somewhere to get a character moving there fast, it would outline the route the character is taking. This one does not. The camera-movement is just a bit clunky at times (especially with some terrain elevation). When you hide in bushes, enemies won't find you. Even if they walk over you. Raising an alarm is penalty-free, just wait a couple of seconds and everything returns to normal, where as by the Mimimi-titles, often a group of 3 enemies would remain patrolling the area.The "super powers" of the characters are great, and also the other abilities of the characters feel balanced to me. I've enjoyed every minute of playing so far and I will make it to the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Shadow Tactics / Desperados III / Commandos2 / Shadow Gambit / War Mongrels Real Time Tactics genre type of game, then this is your kind of game.  Stylized, atmospheric, easy controls, interesting story.  Cast of six characters that you operate, each with very unique abilities, not replicated in other Real Time Tactics games I have played.  A little on the easier side in normal mode than others in this genre.  I hope that this game sells well so that we have more releases in this genre of this high quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazingly worthy successor to Mimimi's legacy of RT stealth strategy. I've played many, but this one is the one that really comes closest to the spirit, the creativity, and the map layouts that make these kinds of games special. Honestly, I would have paid a lot more for a game of this quality, so the price is also amazing as it is. And it is definitely the full works - handcrafted maps, voice acting, really detailed everything, balanced skills (so far), a really useful and good skill EXP system, and while it is RATHER much a clone of Shadow Tactics, it expands on it with some new mechanics and some borrowed ideas from other Mimimi Titles all in a very good way. And I know that comparing this endlessly against Mimimi is a bit reductive, but the game really is just a Mimimi game in spirit, form and function, and thus the comparison is very apt.Ultimately, I genuinely hope this company can continue to make more of these and continue the legacy. I hope they will be able to use more ideas from other Mimimi Games, especially what DIDN'T work about Shadow Gambit and make it work. I hope they can also incorporate the idea of base building and more interesting/unique skills in the future, too. I hope they will be able to think of more really fun, interesting settings (Sumerian Six has an amazing one already as is) and not just do sequels - I really like the idea of the Mimimi model of each game being thoroughly new but still be a 'spiritual successor' to the previous one. (Lovecraftian Mythos, anyone? Hint Hint?)Either way, extremely good job, Devs. I'm loving the heck out of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Being a big fan of Mimimi Games that recently closed its business I followed their announcement of Sumerian Six in their discord. I played the demo and was immediately hooked to buy the full game on release. And I don't regret the investment.Sumerian Six has huge similarities while avoiding being just a cheap copy. It has its own charme and different abilities for its characters. The setting of the story is well done and gives you Indiana Jones vibes. The maps are fantastic and in my opinion a little bit better in terms of love for the detail but also in the big picture. I've played 12 hours so far and I would totally recommend it if you like those games, especially when having played the latest Mimimi Games. After finishing the campaign I will come back here and finalize my review.Edit:After having completed the game I totally recommend buying this piece of beauty. The end is a little bit science fiction heavy in terms of story but fine for me. The game is in a very good shape and since it is the first time they took a foot in this genre I have to say: "Very well done!" I could imagine that they will add another one - the story arc leaves room for that and because I like those type of games I would buy that immediately. I'd love to see 2-3 more characters with other/different skills althoug the existing ones were pretty much fun.Overall I hope that the studio remains (even if they develop completely different games in the future), can go a healthy way and does not overextend by themselves, doesn't take unneeded risks or is driven into something by the publisher although Devolver Digital seems to be kind of reasonable and rational acting. Keep going folks, it was a pleasure to play! And gamers: Buy this!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: This is the second game I've enjoyed tremendously this year by Artificer. Summerian Six has some of the most polished and fun gameplay of the Stealth Tactics genre. It has reasonable length, great sound tracks and very well-written banters between the characters - just like Showgunners. The fully upgraded MC Sid provides lots of micro opportunities and loads of fun solo clearing an area with careful timing, vision control and swift clicking. The other characters are equally fun to play and seemingly OP compared to the character ability kits in Mimimi's titles. However, SS guarantees a good time if you don't care about the fact that even at the highest difficulty it doesn't provide much challenge to the hardcore veterans. I recommend it as a must-buy if you enjoy this genre casually.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game for the action stealth genre of Commandos, Desperados, Mimimi games. Great start by the studio, couple of bugs to be ironed out but nothing stopping me or most from enjoying the game.Difficulty is decent and not too easy for veterans of the genre.Hope to see more from the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game for free for being involved in beta testing.I really enjoyed the setting, characterst and atmosphere. The voice acting is great! The gameplay is very solid stealth tactics gameplay. I like how we get to use supernatural abilities due to the setting - this makes it more interesting than "realistic" Commandos.It did not keep me motivated for very long, though. It is just not my favorite type of genre. I am certain that people who like the genre, will have lots of fun with it.I am a big fan of the developer of the game, Artificer, and their previous title Showgunners. I wish them much success with this and hope they will also make some more turn-based games in the future, which are my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Artificer, with Sumerian Six, properly picked up the baton after Mimimi Games in keeping the Stealth Strategy genre alive. Sumerian Six has all the necessary elements of the genre but lacks the complexity that Mimimi had achieved over time. The game plays exactly like the ones that came before it although the genocidal path seems to be encouraged more than the stealth path, justifiably so because you're offing Nazis. Problems:Optional Challenges are severely limited in scope and diversity which hurts replayability Performance is not perfect and requires optimisation Strengths:Fastest quick save and quick load I have seen in the genre Map design and art style are beautiful and unobtrusive in gameplayNazi occult setting brings with it interesting locations & character abilitiesThank you, Artificer, for developing this game to completion despite the layoffs. Hope to see more of your work. Wholehearted recommendation!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun tacticla stealth game, similar to Commandos, Desperados or Shadow Tactics. Graphics and performance were good, cast was REALLY likable and gameplay was top notch. You might find it a bit easier if you're used to the genre(especially the old games like Commandos 1), but it's still not a walk in the park. Each character have some real nice skills and I've found them to be balanced (other than Alistair feeling a bit weak, but that might be just me). I hope Artificer keeps making games in this genre, I think they have what it takes to take the torch from Mimimi Games.I've played the first 2 levels on the Steam Next fest demo, so add 3-ish hours to my hours played if you want to find about my playtime. _childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough. If you're looking to scratch that itch after beating Desperado 3, then this is your game. I am of the sort that believes, if you off everyone on the map, then you can complete all the objectives without issue. So it took me 48 hours to beat on hard difficulty. I enjoyed every second of it and would do it again. I actually plan on starting a youtube channel and replaying the game so I can upload the full thing of how I completed all of the objectives. It plays very similarly to Desperado 3, which I also loved but I enjoyed this game more. If you're on the fence about buying it, don't think about it. Just do it. You will not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked any of the Mimimi stealth real time tactics games (Desperados 3, Shadow Tactics, Shadow Gambit), this a copy of the beloved format.  Sumerian Six lets you level up your skills for increased range, or a larger area of effect.  You can level them up by gaining experience from either getting kills or opening certain chests scattered throughout the maps.  This is a welcome addition that drives you to get stronger abilities as the game progresses.   If you liked any of the previously mentioned games, or War Mongrels, Partisans 1941, or something like Hard West 2, I believe you will enjoy the tactical game play and the magic/steampunk/alternate WW2 history theme.

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six is a captivating adventure game that offers a unique blend of exploration, puzzle-solving, and combat. The demo provides a generous taste of the full experience, giving players access to the first two levels and three distinct characters. This is a great way to gauge whether the game's style and mechanics align with your preferences before investing in the full version.One of Sumerian Six's standout features is its artistic direction. The game's vibrant and stylized visuals create a visually appealing world that is both enchanting and immersive. The diverse cast of characters, each with their own unique abilities, adds depth and replayability to the experience.While the gameplay is enjoyable and the character abilities are well-balanced, the camera system could benefit from some adjustments. The current method of controlling the camera with the arrow keys can feel a bit clunky, especially during intense combat or exploration. The option to use WASD for camera movement would significantly enhance the overall control scheme.Despite this minor drawback, Sumerian Six is a thoroughly enjoyable game with a lot to offer. If you're a fan of adventure games with a unique aesthetic and engaging gameplay, I highly recommend giving the demo a try, and purchasing if it's your cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and creative gameplay, high quality visuals via UE5, excellent soundtrack and sfx and an engaging story. Plays just like Mimimi Games' tactical stealth games with an XP system built on top and set in a sci-fi WW2 backdrop. Still, it stands on its own merits and has plenty of content. It took me about 30 hours to complete the campaign on Normal, but I like to take my time with games like this. So for the average playthrough, without too much perfectionism I'd say 25 hours at least.I encountered a few bugs, but nothing critical. The in-game bug report system is very easy to use. I'm sure the devs will resolve them in due course.Overall, highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Only played the demo a short time, however, I already knew after a few minutes, i wanted this game. Love the Mimimi Games. Similar feel to this. Feels like good quality, decent voice acting. Good game engine, good UI. I might update this when I get more playtime. For now it is a recommend!Ok, so my full review after completion. Overall loved the game, it is not quite as polished as the Mimimi latest games (only marginal, so done let that put you off. It is a little bit easier. I loved the different skills and how each character complement each other. Decent storytelling and a fair play length. I can 100% recommend this game if you even slightly like this genre of game. Bring on the sequel please!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the sort of stealth tactics games mimimi used to make then you owe it to yourself to check this out. It's certainly not shy about taking its influences from those games, right down to the design of the controls and sight cone indicators. It almost feels like mimimi got to make another game after all, so it's impossible to talk about this game without invoking that studio. It sounds like there have been a lot of layoffs at Artificer too and the dev might not be long for this world, and this game has been released without much fanfare. That's too bad because I would love this team to have had more chances to take a swing at this genre and maybe put a little more of their own stamp on it. I'm not very far in, at the moment, but the game ramps up from tutorial mode to some fairly sticky stealth scenarios quite quickly. That's good, because these levels feel  quite large so far, and dense with optional objectives to get bonuses to improve your abilities. I'm a pretty cautious player of these kinds of games, spending a long time scoping out an area, figuring out patrols before trying out a plans. In Desperados 3 or Shadow Gambit I was routinely taking 30-60 minutes to finish levels, but here the first couple have  easily swallowed well over an hour - your mileage may vary, of course. Like I said, I play these slow and deliberate.With all the wacky powers you get access to I'm getting strong Shadow Gambit vibes from this in terms of the weird and wonderful options you get for stealthing (but at least not yet in terms of the structure, so far it has been more linear like the previous mimimi titles), and some of these have been similar to those in that game, while others are completely fresh and unique to this one. I've only met about half the characters so far, and I'm looking forward to what the rest have to offer. Maybe this game will fall off a cliff later and if it does I'll update my review. But it seems unlikely. This team knows what makes this genre tick and have created a very worthy homage.Update: I think I'm about halfway through the game now and I think the main difference between this and other similar games is just how long I'm staying in the levels. I usually had the habit of playing through levels in one sitting and taking a break between them, but some of these are taking me hours because of my fairly methodical way of playing. The sizes vary but for example you might have a map which is a large section of a town which then becomes a large enemy base in another part, so it's almost like two levels stuck together, and there are many optional XP bonuses (used to level up skills to improve their effects) that I don't want to miss, so I'm being pretty thorough too. The last level I played had a speed-completion goal of *45 minutes*, and by contrast in many of these games levels might take 45 minutes for my leisurely, I don't care about speed kinda pace. So this level took me hours. They were very rewarding hours, it felt like trying to solve a very intricate puzzle box in a way. But your mileage may vary if you want your stealth strategy in more bitesize chunks. I think redoing these levels to go after optional objectives could be quite a time consuming process.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the mimimi games (Desperados 3, Shadow Tactics, Shadow Gambit...) you will like this too. This is a solid stealth strategy from a different company which plays very similar to the above mentioned ones. However it has a new world, new characters and setting. It has also a bit more complex upgrade skill system. There are not many such games nowadays, I really enjoy this one. I find the price also very reasonable, you can buy it in bundle too. I do not have a very performant PC but the game is running well, I have not met any major bugs either.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game on Hard/No Alarms triggered, very fun.To anyone who is in doubt about buying try the demo, if you are in doubt about even trying the game because you have been told this genre is difficult then ignore that and just try it. Reality of this genre is that the way you tend to go through the game is by dealing with an enemy at a time and quicksaving right after, there is also never a time limit so you have all the time in the world to clear the game.I'm mentioning this because a lot of people insist that these games are Very Difficult and it's why they play them, but I've honestly always found them quite the chill "puzzle" solving experience, just remember F5 to quicksave F8 to quickload(all these types of games are made expecting you to do this).

_childDocuments_.review: presents a fascinating and unique setting, blending elements of Nazi Germany during World War II with extraordinary powers, which adds an intriguing twist to a familiar historical backdrop. While the story is simple, it remains engaging, largely due to its roster of highly unique characters who bring the world to life in unexpected ways.Visually, the game delivers well. The graphics are solid, providing an immersive experience without pushing the boundaries of the genre, but certainly good enough to keep players invested in the game's atmosphere.As for gameplay, I found it relatively easy, even on harder difficulty settings. This could be subjective, of course, as I've been playing games in this genre for quite a while. That said, if you're someone who has been waiting for something similar to  and need something to fill the gap since ,  is a very solid choice. One of the highlights is the . With just two playthroughs, you're likely to grab all of them without much hassle, which is a nice bonus for completionists.On the downside, . There are abilities that I found myself never using, which makes certain aspects of gameplay feel less balanced. Despite that, the overall experience is enjoyable.If you're a fan of tactical games set in unique alternate histories,  is definitely worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six is very much what it looks like: a modern take on Commandos: Behind Enemy Lines, with a Hellboy-inspired twist. It closely (maybe too closely) follows the template established by Mimimi Games, which will be dearly missed. While a little rougher than either Shadow Tactics or Desperados III, Sumerian Six remains a very enjoyable Real Time Tactics title, and hopefully it sold enough to justify a sequel. Now, if only I put as much effort into cleaning my apartment I invest into cleaning vast, gorgeous maps of Nazis...
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: This superb real-time tactics game is worthy of being considered alongside the best that Mimimi (RIP) had to offer.  Well designed character skills, inventive enemies and engaging level design combine to create a memorable experience and one that has clearly had a great deal of love poured into it.If you enjoyed the likes of Shadow Tactics, Desperados and Shadow Gambit, then be sure to check this one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: - Felt extremely close to Mimimi's games to the extent that I though it might be using the same framework (this is a good thing). Not quite as polished at times, but the very fast save/load times make up for it.- Pretty good set of characters and abilities. Even if I didn't use all of them it wouldn't surprise me if even the "bad" ones could be used in ways I didn't think of.- Banger soundtrack- Difficulty balancing was a bit off. Sometimes you could effortlessly clear entirely rooms with a single character, sometimes you needed extra precise timing with the entire team. Might be at least partially an issue with Hard mode where enemies spot you so fast that the setting that slows down time when you're about to be spotted becomes useless.- The challenges were uninteresting. Getting experience pickups from missions was a good way to make the player explore most of the map, but also in a way defeated the idea of having multiple paths through the maps.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: For all fans of old Commandos games or the games from the late Mimimi Studios this is an instant buy IMO. Artificer studio created a perfect spiritual successor to the Desperados, Shadow Tactics and others in the genre. It plays like them and is fun like them. The game has 10 levels which doesn't seem much at first glance but those levels are massive. The game runs fine on steamdeck, some people have requested better ui scaling which I can understand. I was fine. At launch, the game couldn't run with the newest proton and we had to use 8.0-5 version but it should be fine now. If not, switch to it and you'll be set.The only criticism I have is the music which didn't fit IMO to the setting. Most of it was forgettable.Overall it's a fun stealth tactics game. Hopefully there will be a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Good game overall. Characters have some crazy abilities which is a good change if you come from the more 'realistic' stealth games. Mission design is good, character voice acting and the story is all good. Only small issues. And some abilities are useless like Izabella Swap-ability is literally un-usable because it stuns her and the enemy after swapping their locations so basically you must use it together with another hero and it leaves her standing stunned where the enemy was so in other words you can only use it against enemies are that not visible to any other enemies, sooo why not just go knife them instead? Yeah, swap 100% useless. And there are also some weaker abilities that dont get much use but mostly a lot of good fun abilities.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me say that Artificer can easily call them self successors of Mimimi Games. Great job! I hope you make more games in this genre in the future.The level graphics are beautiful. The character design is also interesting, although in this type of games we don't get to admire them up close very often. The only minor thing I can complain about here is the occasional graphical and animation glitches in our team. Siegfried is especially unlucky in this regard.Let me move on to the most important thing, the gameplay.Additional types of enemies are a great addition and greatly enhance the experience. Similar games often have a problem here that you managed to avoid to a large extent. However in the future, you might want to consider adding "connected" enemies that appeared in Shadow Gambit to spice things up a bit more.The only annoying bug I encountered during gameplay were small freezes when triggering alarms or being killed by certain enemies.The skills of our characters are very interesting and diverse, unfortunately some of them are very situational and less useful ( or much harder use ) than others. Siegfried again in particular. I think this may be due to the relatively easy difficulty level. Even on hard we are rarely forced to plan an action using more than one character at a time. We need to have more stuff like the last room which was quite an interesting puzzle.It also seems to me that you, as a creator, think that higher enemy types are more difficult than they actually are. Demons really didn't need short line of sight.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: A nice addition to the stealth strategy genre. Sure, it's no Mimimi game and is a bit bare bones around the edges with no darkness mechanics in the night and no foot prints in the snow. Apart from this obvious smaller scope, I found it enjoyable. The characters abilities are interesting, making a new playthrough with different strategy an enjoyment. I found it to be on the easier side of the genre, but obviously YMMV.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Some rough path finding but everything is really fun. Great entry, I used every character in every level possible and there's a lot of paths to choose when solving levels. Story is okay, graphics are okay. Kinda heavy on the PC but nothing jarring. I would put it between old Desperados and Shadow Tactics in terms of quality.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a huge fan of this style of RTS/Stealth games since the original desperadoes released in 2001. I had played Commandos prior to that, but Desperadoes really hooked me with its setting and larger-than-life characters. Gameplay wise, its exactly what you would expect, using several characters with their own unique skills and playstyles. Figuring out puzzles with careful planning and lots of trial and error. Abusing AI to the absolute max. Fundamentally, these games haven't changed since 2001, and that's absolutely fine because its such a great system.Sumerian Six's Weird WWII and Sumerian mythology combination is an absolute winner as far as stories go. You fight a teleporting nazi scientist fueled by "geistoff." There's nothing new or original here, just a lot of good ole fun. There have been some bugs, only one really bad crash after running the game for like 12 hours. Mostly fine. The game autosaves so often I think I might have lost a few minutes of progress, honestly.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six is hands down a great game.  The mechanics and play ability are wonderful.  As in Shadow Gambit, there are new and interesting characters with unique abilities allowing for very diverse strategic play.  As a fan of RTS and RPG games, I love the very slow pace of this game.  When playing it's a bit like Commandos 3 with camera rotation, and even more enjoyable.  I hope this developer continues to roll with the WW2 genre and expand on those possibilities in both the European and Pacific theaters.  Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Don't look at my hours, I played the demo and there you can see with the naked eye with what diligence the guys carefully transferred all the gameplay features from the MiMiMi games. _childDocuments_.review: I recieved a free review copy, provided by the publisher Devolver Digital. Thank you so much for that!Sadly, when I accepted the key for review I was not aware of the sheer mass of swastika textures in the game. They are everywhere and very prominent. I wish there was a disclaimer for content creators. Now, I stream from germany and I live stream my review content, which means I can't blur the symbols out. There is no option for a texture flip, the iron cross in place of the swastika would be the obvious choice here. As a player from germany I am used to geo locked games that either remove all swastikas or give me the option of a texture flip. This game sadly does neither.I played about 30 minutes of it and really enjoyed myself. As a commandos veteran it felt very nostalgic to me and I like the occult aspect which keeps the scenario fresh. Again, I'd absolutely love to review this, but with the swastikas I can't nor do I want to.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: The game is like a Commandos in the Wolfenstein universe. Meaning it's a diesel punk or ww2 punk game where technology mixes a bit with magic. I played the demo and the save continued to the main game at release so i played the first mission again on Hard Difficulty Pros: looks great, voice acting and character design is good( in the first 2 hours), story is nice(stop evil army that is well dressed and likes eagle symbols), the characters have skills that gain experience and when leveled up they are more efficient.Very cool big maps with a Plan moves for squad, quick save, great map with explanations and pass time faster buttonIt's what you expect from a commandos game with the exception that you have limited ammo to shot and there are ammo,healing and experience crates(a crate can be used only by the character that was meant for) on the levels. There are also challenges on every mission, i don't know what they gives when you complete all for a mission but usually it's Finish mission in XX amount of time wich is stupid.Cons: Only 10 missions and the first ones are like an introduction, suffers from the problem of "do this area like this or you get suck on it", gameplay loop is a bit broken since you abuse a few characters to just kill everyone, there is no "non-lethal" option wich seems weird in a stealth game, some character designs or skills are bad.To be honest, there are 2 main problems: 1) is this game worth 30 euros? you can finish it in about 10-12 hours on easy/normal difficulty if you dont care about alarms.2) Does the game have enough variety in the gameplay loop? yes and no, there will be great moments later but for the biggest part of the game you do mostly the same thing.Overall, the lack of content is somewhat fixed by skills geting experience that increases even if you repeat the same mission(skill boxes are only  active once) and the challenges.So to complete everything it's probably 30 hours.I am giving the game a positive review mostly because it adopted more RPG elements than Commands but i hope future games will have even more RPG elements with proper inventory management, loot, a player base to upgrade and use materials/money.The game also has all the quality of life that Desperados 3 had. It really feels like this is the Mimimi studio so it gets some credit from me because of all the QoL
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: If you're really into the genre you'll probably enjoy this game well enough.  There are however several things working against it such that I can't actually recommend it though.  First, it's pretty buggy.  Random crashes (on my 1080ti anyway), visual bugs, characters getting caught trying to path around other characters to name the ones that come to mind immediately.  Second, it's similar enough to shadow gambit in terms of how it approached the genre that it's a bit stale/derivative already.  There are some interesting new abilities and one interesting new enemy but that's mostly it.  Third, it gave the nazis aesthetics that appeal to nazis and most of the care in terms of art and creative direction seems to have gone into the nazis which gives it an off flavor.  Shadow gambit made the enemy faction look bumbling and rule-obsessed, which complimented the game mechanics of the genre so well.  The world is otherwise thematically inconsistent and feels a bit put together in a rush and perhaps like it's just trying to cash in on mimimi's legacy instead of actually increasing the strength of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun but towards mission 6 it gets frustratingly hard (on normal mode) to a point where I was no longer having fun. I simply quit during mission 8, I was almost 1h15 into the mission and barely made it to half. I think the game needs some balancing or at least warn you that normal mode is extremely difficult. I am by no means the best players on hearth but I am certainly not the worst, I cannot imagine the average player managing to finish the game without frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: There's no neutral option, but that's what it should have been. The game is a copy-paste of the Mimimi games (which is good), but they do everything a bit worse. _childDocuments_.review: I think this is overall a solid game. If you like this genre, give it a try.I feel that some missions have the "Too many character" problem, where I often use 2 or 3 and the rest is just there doing nothing.Skills are quite unique and cool designed as well.The little tutorials to learn your characters are simple, yet effective.Played it only on hard difficulty and some missions really need brain power. I like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Artificer has done a superb job with Sumerian Six. It takes the core mechanics from the Mimimi games, mixes it with the Nazis from the Commandos series, and spikes it with a fun supernatural element. The levels are large, fun sandboxes and it is rewarding to pick apart guard patrols and clear areas before grabbing XP crates that improve skills for subsequent missions. Each individual squad member has a good repertoire of skills, but tougher Nazis pose enough challenge and vision cones are still important to avoid. While the story is basic, it does an okay job at keeping the Enigma Squad on target. It is a pity that Mimimi are no more, but Sumerian Six definitely keeps their spirit alive.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to Mimimi's games.  And honestly, I just kind of love that there's a game that's unapologetically pro-killing Nazis.  You've got a nice variety of powers and characters.  I didn't care much for the skill progression.  I never really noticed any difference.  But everything else in the game was fantastic.  If you enjoy the genre, check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: To put it simply, if you like this genre you will like this game. It does suffer from alot of minor issues that I think prevent it from reaching the same level as mimimi's best: several audio-visual glitches, sometimes sluggish menus, Alistair sucks compared to the other characters, unclear level design in part, not as many bonus challenges. That being said, it nails the parts that matter most. There are alot of interesting abilities to play around with, varied levels and enemies. The story is competent(although no voice acting for the final scene was  a let down). If you play on hard the difficulty is is quite challenging even for veterans. Soundtrack and graphics are both nice, especially environmental art, which matters more for this type of game.It really breaks my heart that this genre isn't more popular as there really is nothing like it. Even if you haven't tried it before you are likely to enjoy it if you like open ended puzzles, stealth games or setting up complex abushes. i'd really recomend at least giving the demo a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. It looks and feels like Mimimi games.Pros:- this is a classic set of levels without any unnecessary hub, character selection like in Shadow Gambit;- excellent graphics (and you can turn off cartoon outlines and cell shading);- excellent game design, there are many unique character abilities;- excellent balanced level design, levels are completed not too fast and not too slow;- the controls are the same as in Mimimi games;Small cons:- there are small bugs that they promise to fix;- the music does not quite match the setting (in Mimimi games, you can immediately understand what place and time the game is about when you hear the music)- in Mimimi games, the enemies are more lively and funnier, they discuss something, complain about life, etc.I prefer historical settings, but this setting also turned out to be interesting, because it gives more freedom to the game designer.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Very, very impressive game, which I wasn't expecting at all with their lack of marketing, nor at this price.The characters are amazing (the Six team members), the story is a crazy , with a cool rock/blues-y music them that got me from the beginning.The gameplay is very solid, very satisfying combination of skills, terribly addictive. You have your  in the protagonist, if you are a Commandos fan. in the team, which I thought was very important, if you every caught yourself playing Commandos and thought "I wish I had a bear". Developers being Polish, I wish Wojtek got a bit more focus as a character, but that's just me.It's an Unreal Engine game, good performance, no crashes to report. _childDocuments_.review: Great game! As everyone else says, if you like stealth strategy games... particularly Mimimi's Shadow Tactics, Desperados, or Shadow Gambit, you'll like this one! _childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant. Fantastic. If you like killing Nazis, you'll like this game. If you like action-strategy or stealth-action, you'll like this game. And if you liked Commandos, Shadow Tactics or anything of that ilk, you'll like this game.This game is easily as good as Shadow Tactics, and I think better than both Desperados 3 and Mimimi's pirate outing. The characters are likeable and amusing. The art is gorgeous. The level design interesting and the set-dressing beautiful. The powers feel genuinely original from a mechanics perspective: even though there are "super power" abilities, they are NOT overpowered and outside of the very first level, I rapidly found myself having to think carefully about how to proceed.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game! fun characters, beautiful changing scenery (something I really like in these games), interesting abilities (sometimes can feel overpowered), good variety of enemies with some innovations for the genre (the demon, geist) and great music too. One downside - there is no water/no swimming/ it's a small thing, but I like the possibilities it adds (ex. Desperados 3). I really look forward to what this studio does next - I hope they take the 'baton' from Mimimi and produce more real-time-tactics games.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard not to be reminded of the three games produced by Mimimi Games. When Mimimi Games disbanded, I didn't think I would see a similar and well-made RTT game in such a short time. However, Sumerian Six did it. After I spent 26 hours to complete the game on the highest difficulty, I think I like it very much.I would like to talk about what fascinates me about this game:1. Excellent visual design: The whole game is very well made from a visual perspective. Whether it is art style, character design, or map modeling, it fully demonstrates its own characteristics. The design level is first-tier among all RTT games;2. Exciting music design: Good music is crucial for a game, especially it strengthens the storytelling of Sumerian Six, it gives me a strong sense of immersion, by the way, I like the music of Mission 9 very much;3. Exquisite and grand map design: When I learned that Sumerian Six only has ten levels, I was a little disappointed because I thought it was a bit short, but after I experienced the game in its entirety, I found that its ten maps are quite grand and exquisitely designed, and the relatively large number of enemies, the patrols with tight vision chains, and the difficulty of the levels reminded me of Commandos: Beyond The Call Of Duty, which is exactly what I need.A few years ago, there were rumors of another RTT game, its name is Fog & Silver, and from the leaked pictures and videos, it incorporates many supernatural elements, but there has been no new news about the follow-up of this game, and it is not known whether this project still exists. But surprisingly, although the story of Sumerian Six is based on World War II, it incorporates many supernatural elements and gives characters skills, such as the invisibility of character 2, the human bomb of character 3, the transformation of character 4 into a bear man, the chain lightning of character 5, and the invisible area of character 6. These skills are used to design the clearance route combination, which is very well combined.In addition, Sumerian Six has added a character skill upgrade system, which is really unexpected. This is something new that has not been seen in RTT games in the past 20 years, except for Partisans 1941, but I think their design, including character backpacks, item design, and skill upgrades, is not good enough. On the contrary, it weakens the stealth element of RTT games. Sumerian Six may have borrowed from such a design, but it focuses more on stealth and is more clever. This is very surprising.Then let me say some things that I think are not good enough:1.	The design of the level difficulty is a bit anticlimactic: As I said before, I think the level design of Sumerian Six is very clever, but I don’t know if the production team is inexperienced because it is the first time to make an RTT game, or for some other reason, the difficulty of missions 7, 9, and 10 is a bit too easy. In mission 9, I almost didn’t trigger the alarm many times when I played through it for the first time, and the most disappointing was the final mission. I thought the final boss would have a big fight with us after gaining new power, but after I pushed three pillars, everything was over. After that, I thought I would have a battle with the ancient demon, but it just returned to the end of the first mission, added more enemies, and other than that, the battle took place in the cutscene. I can’t say this kind of game design is bad, and maybe this is just my personal opinion, but the way the story is designed does remind me of the last mission of the first generation Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive. The thrilling battle between John Cooper and the sheriff is still very clear in my mind, but I haven’t seen such a final level design in subsequent RTT games, which is really disappointing.2.	Sumerian Six has indoor level design, but there is no related design after the character enters a house: for example, when I accidentally get discovered by the enemy during stealth and hide in a house, the enemy will chase me in and I can't do anything but wait to be killed. I have only seen such a design once in Commandos 2: Men of Courage. Indeed, if such a design is added, perhaps the logic of the entire level needs to be redesigned, which is undoubtedly a huge workload, but as an old player with 20 years of RTT game experience, I really look forward to seeing elements similar to Commandos 2 one day in the future, which is also my little expectation for the Sumerian Six production team.3.	Some characters have overlapping skills: for example, character 3's human-ground bomb, character 4's bear-man attack, and character 5's chain lightning, they are all range attacks. Although the supernatural elements are well combined with the level's decryption, I think there shouldn't be too many range attacks, otherwise it will reduce the difficulty of the level.These areas that I think are not good enough are just my attitude and suggestions as a senior RTT game player. This type of game itself is already very niche, and Commandos 2 has brought RTT to a very high level. Even the three classic works produced by Mimimi Games in the past, including War Mongrels, are almost all about patching up the shortcomings and unreasonableness of Commandos: Behind Enemy Lines, with almost no major innovation. This is indeed not a problem for any production team. In this day and age, it is a great comfort for me to continue to see new RTT works. For RTT game production teams that want to develop new games, it is a difficult problem to make a hardcore stealth game for old RTT users, or to reduce the difficulty of the game while taking into account both new and old users.I'd like to thank the Sumerian Sixt team for bringing such a wonderful and exciting new game. If you continue to develop new RTT games in the future, I will be very, very, very grateful to you!Out of 10, I would give Sumerian Six an 8.5! Very Wonderful game!

_childDocuments_.review: Done 2 missions on demo, those demo missions save carry over to main game and have done 2 missions on main game. If you care about FPS, I'll have it below. Tho it being strategy, its not huge deal imo.Few things first, this is NOT mimimi games' game - Mimimi was German studio while Artificer is, I believe, Polish. Also Mimimi used Unity while this is Unreal engine. Otherwise I can see why people get confused, they are really similar.The amount of combinations the characters can do is insane to the point it feels really amazing when you pull them off.For example just two:1) One of the characters has a unique ability to "hitchhike" into an enemy's body undetected. And then have another character throw a "smelly gas" at the enemy, forcing them to move. This way, you can jump from enemy thats otherwise out of reach for "hitchhike" jump, or even use a "hitchhiked" enemy to bypass security gates that only enemies can access with said gas.2) One character can lay traps that make the enemy fly to certain position. This can be used in a way that enemy flies on top of another enemy, or explosive, giving you multi-kill! This character also has the classic "whistle to lure enemy" skill but that's risky as enemy will turn towards you, potentially seeing you. So what to do? Why, use the gas move the enemy instead!And that's just things I've done in 4 missions! I havent met everyone in one mission yet!My PC specs: i5-12th gen / rtx3060 (12gb) / 32gb ramALL ULTRA, DLAA (no upscale): 70-80 fps depending on effects on screen.One UE crash made me restart one level, but haven't encountered it after that.
