_childDocuments_.review: After 12h of gameplay (pretty much half if not a bit more of the game) I can safely say that we have here a very enjoyable new release of Commandos like game. The game does not innovate in any way but it is more due to game genre that has reach its limit with the few innovations that Mimimi brought but this game reuse all the good things.There are very few technical problems (crash, maybe optimization could be slightly improved), but otherwise the games runs smoothly and those problems are not (in my case) detrimental to the gameplay.The game cements for me Artificer as a very solid studio that are able to deliver solid games (Showgunners, Sumerian Six) in different genres. I will definitely keep an eye on their next release. I hope considering the unfortunate fate of Mimimi that they will not stick to the genre (despite being a huge fan of it) and try to do something different next time.Pricing seems fair to me so if you are a fan of Commandos-like, you can safely go for it.EDIT : After finishing the game in roughly 18h, I'd revise my previous judgment on the pricing after comparison of playtime with Mimimi games. I'd say that 30€ is maybe a bit pricy related to the game lenght (Shadows tactics was 40-45 iirc for 40h of gameplay to similar level of completion challenge wise) so up to you if you consider to buy it full price to support the studio.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: There's still hope for stealth tactics genre!As an avid stealth tactics fan, I was pleasantly surprised by this new offering from Artificer.In short - Sumerian Six is a worthy successor to Mimimi's games (Shadow Tactics, Desperados 3, Shadow Gambit). While it doesn't quite reach the mechanical heights of Shadow Gambit, Sumerian Six has quality gameplay and bombastic presentation to make it interesting for veterans of the genre and approachable for newcomers. A bit more in depth:Pros:+ Character variety: it seemed like Mimimi explored all there was to do with character skills in Shadow Gambit, but Artificer managed to find new niches and creative ideas on what characters can be about. They are fun to play and interesting to solve levels with. Gameplay is tight, fun and engaging. Enemies, likewise, are varied, explore interesting mechanical designs, and present fun challenges to solve. + Overall presentation: theming, visual style, sounds, concept - while stealth tactics genre was born with WW2 games, Sumerian Six feels both familiar and fresh - it can be summed up as "weird science meets WW2". Theme stays consistent in character/enemy art, sound design and story presentation, making Sumerian Six a memorable game. + Level design: levels are varied and beatifully crafted. There are european castles, desert bases, ancient cities and more.+ Small things: loading time is extremely quick (which is important for the genre). I also really appreciated how speedrun challenges work - reloading returns the timer to what it was when you made the save, thus speedrun challenges are about devising a clever and quick path, and not about how many mechanical mistakes you made along the way. Cons:- Length: with only 10 levels to explore, game felt a bit short. The length is fair for the price point, but the campaign left me wanting more.- Replayability: while there are a few challenges to add replayability, they are very bare bones compared to Mimimi games, and especially Shadow Gambit. So while the game works amazingly as a one-off experience, fans of the genre might find it quickly runs out of things to do after the first playthrough. - Mechanical depth: while character/enemy design is great, the game omits any variations to gameplay specific to levels (i.e. leaving tracks in snow/dirt, or nighttime enemy vision being worse overall and better in lit areas). Those provided variety to levels, unique challenges to solve. - Difficulty: there are two aspects to that - difficulty curve and overall difficulty. I felt that difficulty peaked at level 8, and levels 9-10 were just victory laps. The finale of the campaign could use some love in terms of beefing it up. In terms of overall difficulty, subjectively it felt rather easy (playing on hardest difficulty). This might be attributable to my experience with the genre (I'm one of those people doing every last challenge in stealth tactics games). Compounded with the lack of extra badges/challenges, there were very few things to properly tickle my puzzle-solving desire. P.S. Apart from Stealth Tactics, I really enjoy Turn Based Tactics genre. If you do as well - please check out Showgunners by the same developer. It's a well made and well presented turn-based tactics game, one of the best I played in the genre recently. P.P.S. Artificer, I'm eagerly looking forward to DLC for Sumerian Six. Don't forget challenges/replayability features this time!
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: Sumerian Six is a good Stealth/Real TIme Tactics game that is definitely worth buying.There are some good and bad things but if you are a fan of the genre and games from Mimimi you will enjoy it and if you are new to it, the difficulty level will not cause you to stop playing due to frustration. Few important points after finishing the game:- you can see inspiration from Mimimi games, the art is on par with those games and if I didn't knew I would have though that it's theirs new game which is a big plus, also the gameplay mechanics work pretty much the same, so if you had played for example Desperados III you will feel like at home,- it's murder sudoku game, a genre that I adore and Artificier did a really good job in creating an overall good game,- game is a bit short (only 10 missions) but when you take into the account its price its definitely worth every penny,- it has pretty standard enemy variety. If you played these type of games you know that they sometimes lack in that department. Here we have solid 5 types which is fair enough. They could maybe add some snipers with long and narrow view cones (like in Shadow Gambit).- there are some bugs and game crashed or froze couple times but keep in mind that this review is written less than a week after the game premier, also in those few days developers already managed to release first hot fix so I'm going to give them benefit of a doubt on that seeing how they already are patching things- if I had to critique something it would be difficulty levels and enemy setups. I was playing on Hard difficulty (with this point I would like you to keep in mind that I have over 200 hours playing Mimimi games so I'm pretty familiar with the genre) and while for someone new to the genre the difficulty levels will be spot on for me the game wasn't challenging enough. It's probably due easy enemy setups and/or to OP abilities of our characters. There where only few moments/enemy setups that really stumped me and made me really use my brain. A lot of enemies can be killed without even bothering with the view cones, you can just run around the enemy setup or use Izzy's invisibility and just kill off enemies on the edges so half of enemies are gone and only then there is some figuring out how to get rid of the rest - in other words enemies were often not covered or barely covered by other enemies. Also the character abilities are too OP in my opinion. That is something that was often mentioned with the demo and unfortunately it seems that they weren't nerfed enough. Izzy's invisibility - is allowing for too much when it comes to avoiding enemies, Rosa's link - gives ability to 'turn off' an enemy but again it was to easy to find a place where she could use it against the enemy that is covering the one that is difficult to kill, Alistair's chain lightning - killing 3-5 enemies that are standing close to each other with one click of a mouse button makes some enemy setups useless, Sigfried's thing for setting invisibility zones - there is no need to worry that anyone will see you killing, yes sometimes you couldn't use it because enemies would notice you standing but again enemy setups were way too forgiving in that matter, Wojtek's wearbear form rampage - similar to chain lightning but with some restrictions, Sid's hitchhiking - no need to worry about view cones just move through the setups freely. Those are some examples of too OP abilities, Unfortunately those abilities also progress with time and are becoming even more powerful. The progression system would be nice with weaker abilities.To summarize - Summerian Six is a really good game that is worth buying.

_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: First there is no Yuki in here, so I should give the game a bad review, right? Let's see!I love stealth tactic games and I love the mimimi games.You can see the similarities everywhere. Most shortcuts and even the art style are basically the same. The base mechanics work like mimimi taught us.And for me that's great.I don't want to learn everything from scratch each time I try a new game from this genre.At the same time Sumerian Six is not a copy of any mimimi game, the setting is way different (killing evil Germans is always a great activity isn't it?), the characters are way different, most of the abilities are creative and fresh and I hope later in the game I will see some new enemies as well.And that's good, that's how it should be. These games are about the puzzles and the tools you get to solve them, not about reinventing the wheel from scratch.I'm playing the game on hard, because that's what I like to do, and I had no issues so far navigating the levels or managing my characters I'm so used to it thanks to the guys from Munich and I love it, I can focus on playing the game rather then learning the controls.So if you are a fan of the mimimi games, you will have an easy time getting into this game.But I must admit for me this game feels less polished then what I'm used to get out of Bavaria, it's very well done, I had no bugs or crashes so far, everything works like intended, it just feels a bit rough at the edges compared to shadow gambit or desperados 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Sumerian Six

_childDocuments_.review: O.m.g. yes! I was so so sad when Mimimi games was shutting down. I just adore their games. And then - out of the blue for me - there was Artificer with Sumerian Six and wow, just wow! It has - in my opinion - exactly the same (smooth) gameplay, approach and looks as Shadow Tactics, Desperados III and Shadow gambit! It's like...  a very (very!) good clone (in a very good way!) with just a different setting, new characters and skills. Just amazing! Sumerian Six will, without a doubt, fill the emptiness (if) that was left behind with Mimimi shutting down. So glad there is still hope for these types of RTT games after all!No need to type a book with my explanations why this game is so great, because the ones who played Mimimi games, know how this game will be (yeah, freakin' good), because it is just like ST, DIII and SG. So just a summary:- Beautifully designed levels;- Gameplay exactly like Mimimi games; and yes that is amazing (still can't believe this, I just love it!);- Replayability is high (many different approaches/tactics/achievements are able);- Funny characters and phrases throughout the game (you will even recognize some phrases from Mimimi characters, lol;- I came across 5 types of different enemies (dont know if there will be more because I yet have to advance further. _childDocuments_.review: At the moment, there is a great number of bugs, but I'm honestly willing to overlook those (they're annoying more than they're gamebreaking) because what is there is a promise of great things to come if the studio can continue to make games.The base, quite obviously, is mimimi games and they recreate those more faithfully than anyone else so far, but they introduce enough new things in terms of abilities and enemies (some setups on hard are quite a challenge) to stand out in a great way. _childDocuments_.review: Strategy games often hold a reputation for giving players the luxury of time. Enough time to rethink their moves, plan their moves and execute game-changing maneuver. Artificer’s Sumerian Six manages to do all of that and more.The game’s complex stealth systems and character abilities nonchalantly blend a meticulously woven narrative with an art style that mixes arcane elements along with a WWII backdrop.Despite certain game-breaking bugs, Sumerian Six offers a highly challenging strategy game that will be loved by fans of genres that mix stealth and action with a clever retelling of historical fragments only science fiction can mess with.Time is an all-too-valuable resource in this game, and that’s pretty evident from its mechanics as well as narrative direction. Right from the beginning, there are a couple of neatly sketched-out cutscenes and voice lines that introduce you to the game.Then, you’re stepping right into the action. You move your character by clicking at places, stay aware of enemies’ lines of sight, and use the best of your abilities to kill, investigate, and shift through spaces.But, that’s just the beginning! When you unlock a new character, you’re introduced to a strategic landscape where making decisions will feel highly personal to each character.One can go throw stun grenades and transfer his consciousness into an enemy. The other can swap places with an enemy, while also going completely invisible, and so on.I started wondering, “Wait, how is this even possible?”, and then nodded to the game’s supernatural themes mixed with realistic ones. And, that’s when I realized – the most realistic part of this game was my skillset. Otherwise, these characters would gladly conquer the world and destroy evil if it were up to them.But, no. My knack for strategic-action prowess made me replay a level perhaps ten times until I figured out the best way to get things done. That’s just part of the process.Despite the impressive tools and tactics I could apply in hopes of completing mission objectives, I struggled quite a bit. It’s almost as if the developers were mocking my stealth skills and asking me if I was up to this task. I was, trust me. Just… one more try (after my 20th attempt).There’s no point in trying to make things simple for yourself in this game because Sumerian Six’s deft gameplay design ensures that enemies aren’t dumb, even though sometimes the AI can be questionable.Especially when I’ve hidden a body right behind a desk, and the dead guy’s friend is likely wondering where he went. Yet, he chooses to patrol the area. Duty calls, eh?Again, time is valuable here. So, with the simple press-and-hold of the X button, I could fast-forward time until my characters felt safe enough to take someone down. The game’s pacing also takes this opportunity to tell a story.Between different locations and strategic maneuvers, characters would often talk to each other and have brief conversations. They would even talk to me! Yes, breaking the fourth wall is part of this game. That truly makes me wonder if these virtual personalities have a disheartening opinion about my skills.As pretty, clever, and enticing as Sumerian Six is, it also has its problems. Some of them can feel a little game-breaking, but others feel like design decisions taken by Artificer for the sake of immersion.For instance, one character’s abilities can completely make the other character feel useless. However, this is how you strategize in a way that makes it feel like teamwork, rather than solo play.On the other hand, there was a bug I encountered where no matter how many times I loaded into the game, it would freeze the camera at a place where I couldn’t select any characters. I hope the developers fix this soon.Finally, a character would sometimes keep moving toward an extremely risky place, even though I didn’t want them to. This happened whenever I wasn’t careful about my clicks, and was wrapping my head around all the available keyboard and mouse inputs.Fortunately these things don’t paint the game’s essence in a bad light. The more you play Sumerian Six, the more you want to keep playing. If you’ve adored games like Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun and Desperados III, then Sumerian Six is going to impress you.A fantastic gameplay loop, fascinating characters, and a historically inaccurate sci-fi journey are everything that makes this one worthy of your time.. .Review originally written for

_childDocuments_.review: Now that Mimi is gone (sniff, tears), this seems like a very good successor. It seems a bit more 'arcade-y' at first, but that flattens out over time as you play and you're left with some head-scratching scenarios to chew on. I am really enjoying the wide variety of skills each member of your team gets, and the progression into more powerful upgrades encourages you to solve areas you might otherwise pass by.In the end, I think these real-time tactics stealth games are all about presenting great scenarios to tease your brain... nothing better than solving a really difficult area after trying a bunch of different combinations. I haven't so far experienced any stealth game breakers where detection was glitchy (looking at you, 1942 Partisans) - it's been predictable and good.It's stable on release day - not a single crash, and that's something in today's game world. The quick-saves are lightning fast, as are the restores. The music is delightful too - actually kept that on this time.I think a lot of love and care went into this, and I hope there's a lot more coming. I got the bundle deal for $26 or so, which seems like a pretty good deal.

_childDocuments_.review:
Sumerian Six follows the Enigma Squad, a team of scientist commandos composed of the world’s greatest scientists who combine their skills to conduct secret missions in their fight against the Third Reich. Together, you seek to thwart ex-member Hans Kammler's nefarious plans involving a powerful, mystical substance named Geiststoff.

Embark on a thrilling journey across multiple continents alongside allies such as the exiled chemist Rosa Reznick, Wojtek the Werebear, and the esoteric psychoanalyst Siegfried von Adelsberg. Dispose of your enemies by using each team member’s unique set of abilities inspired by their fields of expertise, and learn to master the art of chaining them together for devastating effects if you hope to be successful.

As you delve deeper into the Nazi plot, you’ll encounter occult-scientific weapons and ancient Sumerian artifacts linked to Kammler's machinations. A grim future awaits you should the Nazis be victorious, so do your best to prevent that dark timeline from coming true in this real-time tactical stealth adventure.

name: Singularity
detailed_description: ‘Singularity’ is an immersive virtual reality experience that combines technologies including 3D scanning, head-mounted display, and immersive sound design. Creating an abandoned and forgotten world by designing a decentralized order, it invites the audience to rethink the relationship between living organism and inorganic intelligence. The inspiration for this work grows from the artist's personal experience of living an accelerating digitized world. She creatively associates the relationship between racing games and Moore's Law, also The Law of Accelerating Returns that appeared in the human’s technology development history. In racing games, users can usually accelerate by collecting props. According to The Law of Accelerating Returns, every time new technology is invented, the acceleration curve rose exponentially. The two phenomena coincide. This work uses the rationale of racing game as the basis of designing the experience’s structure. The audience will be able to explore many technical metaphors that we once used, as well as ones we are currently using, including mobile phones, Bluetooth, Information superhighway, chatbots, etc. The audience will experience the accelerating virtual reality world through observing and collecting the metaphors, and finally achieve the 'singularity'. Ray Kurzweil claims that the singularity will happen by 2045. Also, Steven Shaviro states that ‘like it or not, we are all accelerationists now’. Artist & Creative Director - Jingjing Shen Developer - Cody Wren. Music / Sound - Michael Tree. Producer - David Tree Exec Producer - Peter Richardson, Joseph Amoah - BBC RnD New Creatives South East Producer - Jo Nolan

_childDocuments_.review: On a clandestine mission deep into Russian territory, an American black ops team crash lands on an island research base that was mysteriously abandoned in the 1950’s. Cut off from the outside and under attack by an army of nightmarish creatures, Captain Nathaniel Renko is forced to battle his way through the hostile territory armed with the TMD (Time Manipulation Device) – a time altering weapon created over 50 years ago. Who created the TMD and why is just one of the many Cold War secrets Renko must uncover as he is thrown back and forth across time, making choices that will alter the course of world history. [Raven Software]

name: BIOMORPH
detailed_description: In BIOMORPH, players must use their skills to explore a vast, varied world. Solve puzzles and platforming challenges, fight deadly monsters and take their shapes to use their powers. But beware – every conquered creature can come back with new and even more threatening powers. Players will level-up their character as they fight through the vast areas around the city, collecting new abilities, mementos and chips. The journey will reveal surprising and alarming truths about our hero’s own origins. Play as the enemies by killing them and taking their shape. You will be able to use their skills to fight other enemies or use their powers to navigate in uncharted territories. Fight your way through a challenging AI system where previously mimicked creatures unlock new powers to create a unique experience while revisiting areas of the game. Choose your fighting style by using an arsenal of melee and range weapons, each of them having its own upgrade tree, to bash and shoot enemies. Create different builds in support of your play style by equipping and mixing different unique skills that you can upgrade. Explore a vast non-linear, interconnected world composed of many different environments, home of optional boss fights, eccentric NPCs, tons of secrets and upgrades to reward the most daring explorer. Rebuild the city of Blightmoor and befriend it's inhabitants, learning more about their daily life and the town’s origins. Customize the look of the city to make it your own.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had the game for over a week now, I've got 20 hours on it and I'm at 86% completion. I'd recommend the game without hesitation for anyone who likes Metroidvania and as a first Metroidvania for people who don't know much about the genre. It's definitely an S-Tier in terms of Metroidvanias. Positive points:- The concept of metamorphosis- Environments and art direction- Gameplay and combat, which are very tight and responsive- Variety of mechanics and builds- Biomes offering different gameplay elements each time- Plenty of content for the price- A mini-map!!!! In short, an excellent game!Suggestions for additions to the game (which may already be in the pipeline):- An item to return to the last SAFE, even if that means that we are gonna lose our ferrox (useful if you want to 100% all the pieces without too much backtracking)- A NG+ mode- A speedrun mode- An integrated randomizer- Boss Rush modeRating: 9/10The devs gave me a key because I've known them for a while. I did not receive any compensation for playing or reviewing the game. Also, I would not have done this review if I did not love the game ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, but with a few caveats.  The gameplay and biomes are in my opinion wonderful.  There's a lot to do, with a huge, sprawling, map, filled with NPC's and sidequests.  However, there are a couple of huge problems for me - Contact damage, with almost no invincibility frames.  I just cannot for the life of me, understand why devs feel the need to have contact damage.  One of the stupidest and most annoying gameplay choices.Other than for traversal purposes, transforming into the creatures you kill is practically useless, as the majority of their combat means are slow, plodding, and weak.  It's just not fun controlling any of them.  None.Please stop throwing in the soulslike ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of losing all of your acquired money when you die and then having to go on a corpse run.  You don't have to do it because you saw another successful game do it.  You really don't.That being said, I wish there was a neutral option, but I don't feel like this game deserves a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: , from the boss fights to the platforming.You can equip 3 Biomorphs at a save point.  It is mildly annoying when you are scouring the map for 100% and encounter a barrier that requires a specific Biomorph power, because now you're forced to run back to the save point to equip the correct Biomorph, then run all the way back and use it (And then possibly all the way back to the save point again so you can teleport to your next area to work on).    Completed rooms are surrounded in a Yellow border and that's a little harder to spot than say, if incomplete rooms had an exclamation point instead in games like Ender Lilies.  Alternatively I wish the yellow colour that is used to surround the rooms could have had some more detail to stand out more.  I was actually missing 1 collectable at the end of the game and I checked my map 10 times and could not discern the room that was incomplete.  I eventually uploaded my map and another player was able to spot my incomplete room.  The only tune that really did anything for me was the sad and somewhat moody town theme (Which sounds a tiny bit like "No Man's Land" from Aeterna Noctis").  This comes down to me preferring melodic music that plays in the foreground, as opposed to gentler music that plays it safer hiding in the background.  I much prefer soundtracks like Castlevania, Astalon or Monster Boy than the style that games like Biomorph and Ori use.  To me its all just safe, subtle background music that doesn't really get me going.I won't speak in any detail about the story.  There was too much dialogue for my liking that I just ended up skipping through it all (Game lets you skip it).  I much prefer succinct and to the point with some quirkyness, which you find in games like Astalon.   ..So despite Biomorph not having a banger soundtrack, being very challenging or roping me in with its story, , ahead of Rebel Transmute, Prince of Persia, Ultros and The Mobius Machine. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT FINAL: This review is getting long with all the edits, although I don't like removing them to retain history. If you'd like to see my final review of the game, I'll post it in the discussions. Overall, I am very happy with the updates, but still find the later half of the game to be disappointing enough that I can't recommend the game in good conscience. EDIT: I hate to say it but what was before a review that teetered on the (unfortunately) nonexistent edge of positive vs negative review (steam please add a neutral option), awaiting important updates to improve the late-game experience, has now become a firmly negative review. It seems that the CEO of the company has decided to respond to negative reviews by guilt tripping their players for giving their honest feedback. As a developer myself, I know how it feels to get negative reviews on a game you've worked hard on. That being said, I don't go responding to all of our negative reviews making people feel bad for expressing their opinion. Something that can hurt your sales even more than a negative review is negative PR. Congratulations to the rest of the team though for what was clearly hard work. This game started off really strong for me. The morphs feel fresh and fun. There's a lot of unique mechanics in the game, and each biome feels completely different. The bosses are decent, most of them are way too easy in general, though, but this isn't necessarily bad. Unfortunately in the late-game the game really starts to stumble. I think a few minor tweaks to the game could help a LOT. First thing the game absolutely needs is some sort of way to warp back to S.A.F.E stations. The amount of time I waste running back and forth across huge areas of the game after having cleared almost all of the rooms just to clear 1 more room is causing so much fatigue for me.Second thing is some sort of morph that makes getting around the map faster and more fun. I would LOVE a morph with no combat abilities that allows you to travel through the map in a way that isn't just dash-dash-dash-dash-dash-dash over and over until I have to turn the sfx off because i'm losing my mind hearing the repetitive sound. Third thing is the inventory tab swap speed. The tabs in the inventory menus are too slow, especially when wrapping around from first to last tab. It's noticeably slow. I don't know how to rate this game right now because I went from a 9/10 amazing experience to what now feels like such a chore that i'm not sure I have the energy to keep playing. I think with some more QoL features I may be willing to return but I think for now I'm just going to take a break. I have to give it a downvote because even though the first several hours are really a joy, the game just kinda fell flat.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the game extensively (did a 23h stream getting the 100% completion and a whole day of speedrun), here is my review:Biomorph is a Metroidvania, its hook and gameplay loop is a Kirby-like mechanic where you have the ability to morph into the enemies you have dispatched, which helps you do puzzle solving and further your exploration of the many different biomes you will be encountering in the game. This mechanic is extremely well implemented and checks all the boxes when it comes to variety and addictiveness.There is a LOT to see here as there are an inordinate amount of locales to see. Once you realize the size of the whole map, you'll realize how daunting a task it will be to explore it all, yet, it is a joy all throughout.Graphics are fantastic for this style of game. All 2D hand drawn animated and very endearing.. Also, for a game like this and a studio of this size, you will be impressed and thrilled to see that there are cutscenes throughout all the game to carry the story.The story in and of itself is a spin on the classic tale of ressource gathering, but at what cost to the inhabitants of the planet. It's nothing too revolutionary but there are nice twists and turns along the way to keep the formula fresh.On the music side, you're looking at a game with a very modest soundtrack (1 song per location), yet throughout all my time with the game, I've never grown tired of it. Songs do a nice job of conveying the mood and story behind the biome you are in.Finally, gameplay wise, aside the main hook of the game, which is to borrow the powers of your enemies, I'm pleased to report that the game controls extremely well. Inputs are responsive and snappy, no floatiness in running/jumping/sliding. Gunplay is fantastic as the controls allow for creativity and precision in the way you choose to tackle the challenges ahead.All in all, a fantastic package, which is diametrically opposed to the kind price to experience ratio you get in today's AAA gaming landscape. At its launch price, this game is a steal in all aspects and I do not think you will regret any minute of your adventure while also feeling financially respected.On a numerical scale, this game is a solid 8.5!@Mrleledg on Twitch.tv

_childDocuments_.review: It's not hard to see where Biomorph draws its inspiration from, mostly Hollow Knight and Ender Lilies. The game puts all the familiar ideas together and on top of that, adding a little twist into formula. You can become the enemy you just defeat. While the mechanic certainly makes the experience solid and bends the rule of gating-abilities, the execution feels off for me. Biomorphing doesn't streamline your combo and the overall combat. And a lot of monster forms are treated as one-trick ponies, a one-and-done deal. That being said, I cannot just down vote the game and move on. Despite my negativity, I still have fun exploring the big alien worlds the developers created. Tons of secrets and scavenge hunts encourage you to use all of your abilities to the fullest. Overall, Biomorph is a solid metroidvania to playthrough. It's just that I think the mechanic could've been better or at least well-used.→I like the western cartoon art style.→Quite a few interesting NPCs and side quests.→Exploration is often rewarding despite the terrible map system.→All 39 Scargatoes have their own cute description.→: There are actually two types of gating-abilities: first type is the usual reward that players can find at the end of the level or after the boss fight, and the other type is related to the biomorphing. For the first type, I am glad and actually surprised to find out Biomorph doesn't just hand out the regular gating-abilities like Double Jump right away. The design choice immediately sets the game apart from other metroidvania. Of course making your protagonist less mobile means the level design cannot be too difficult to navigate, but Biomorph circumvents this issue by introducing biomorphing, in other words, a second set of gating abilities. Each monster forms have their unique attacks and special quirks to help you on your journey when transform. You may not walk through a long spike trap, but Scarbyttle can hover any of them; when the level gets too big, Oddwing allows you to fly for a few seconds to places you otherwise cannot reach. This mechanic makes me feel very excited every time I see a new monster, wondering what abilities will it grant me once I slaughter I mean morphing into it.→: Three things really bothers me about the biomorphing. First, biomorphing doesn't feel smooth to use in combat. Most of the monster forms are clunky to use. You can hardly combo your chip attack into biomorphing Ben Ten style. Second, every monster form is a one-trick pony. Their usage only last for their responding level. Outside of said level, there really isn't any incentive to use them beyond you liking their look or their attack pattern. Some do possess valuable quirks like Ombre Blanche has triple jump and Jawfish can swim under water, yet this design reinforces my last point: some monster forms should just be enhancement for existing ones instead of being a standalone. Jetrunner's ability to swim against the stream should just be integrated into Jawfish swimming capability; any wall-bashing monsters should just be one being with upgrades. Same deal goes with any secrets-revealing monsters. By combining monsters together, it would be much better to organize the equipped biomorphs. Players wouldn't run into the awkward situation which they would find a secret area that requires a certain ability of a certain biomorph, only to find out they don't have the right one equipped. So they would have to teleport back to save point, equip the right one, and go all the way back to the point of interest.→Biomorph upgrades do not convey clear information.→The map system is the worst. Tons of plain rectangles really doesn't make me realize what I miss, especially when a portion of the area can only be accessed from another area that I have no way to know because the map is unclear about it.→Some secrets do not have any subtle hints at all.中文小簡評→一款內容實在的類銀河系惡魔城，只是其中的機制可以做得更好。→雖然主要機制的設計我覺得沒有很好，但是光就本作完整性，還是值得一玩。→西洋卡通畫風很有特色。→許多有趣的NPC及支線任務。→地圖中藏有許多秘密和道具，探索起來很充實。→39隻史來喵有各自的個性小簡介。→關鍵技能分為兩種，角色本身的技能沒有像其他同行一樣直接屈服於二段跳，而是巧妙地運用怪物變身間接的讓關卡逛起來更有趣，同時鼓勵玩家多多運用及蒐集不同怪物化身。→然而變身怪物這個系統個人覺得做得不好，戰鬥中不太能隨時切換打連擊，諸多變身功能僅限其會出現的關卡有用，其他地方毫無用處，僅有少數變身有好用的技能。→許多變身的能力太過單一，應該設計成其他變身的升級版。如此不但能方便玩家選擇想要的變身，也能解決玩家要來回跑存檔點換變身的窘境。→變身升級給的資訊過少。→地圖看來很糟，僅用大方框來標示關卡而沒有多一點細節，容易導致玩家繞了半天找不到興趣點，而那興趣竟然是要從另一個地方才能到達...→完全沒有提示說這牆可以被打壞。
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Buy this game if:✅ You're into metroidvania games, focused on switching and optimizing builds;✅ You like exploring and backtracking, by also "bio-morphing" yourself into other creatures, each one of them has their own set of movement and abilities;✅ You enjoy doing sidequests and optimizing / experimenting with your builds and weapons;Don't buy if:❌ you don't like changing builds often, as this will be required to overcome mandatory obstacles along the main story;❌ you like to receive weapons, trinkets and abilities not too far into the main game;Biomorph it's fun and aesthetically pleasing, even the cutscenes are animated like a cartoon...Let's talk about Biomorphing!You can transform yourself into 18 different creatures, each one with their own set of abilites and mobility options, allowing you to experience a different gameplay experience and as a result...making boss fights more diverse, making them much harder or easier, depending on your equipment of choice. a) Boss fights are way too easy, especially with the "right" build and/or weapon;b) Fast-travel points in few instances could have been placed in a more convenient way;c) Some biomorphs, especially the slugghish ones, aren't suited for boss fights at all, as contact damage against you exists...and it's not lenient at all as you'll lose lots of HP when being touched by the bosses' hitboxes.d) There aren't big secrets or heavy lore hidden or locked into sidequests, except for one;e) The last boss and the wrapping up of the ending part of the game feel rushed, which is a shame as the main character and her sidekicks are quite compelling;f) Some weapons and skills are being received and found too late in the game in order to allow them to be tested properly;Verdict: 7,5Time required to finish the main game: 13/15 hrs Time required to complete it at 100%: 20-22 hours (no missable achievements, the game map will track automatically cleared areas)Thanks for reading, leave a comment below if you have any questions or observations, feel free to follow my other reviews at:
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: I wish every metroidvania had the QoL stuff Biomorph did. Biomorph has one of the best maps I've seen, fast travel from every save, warp back to saves from anywhere, they added a run so you don't have to spam dash to get around "fastest", and rooms are highllighted when you've completed them. For the game itself, it's quite fun. I think the forms end up being less of a big deal than they seem at first, 95% of the time you are better off running around and fighting in your base form with the customizable chip loadouts which are nice to help deal with specific enemy types in different biomes. The bioforms CAN be helpful in combat or certain bosses, but mostly they're for getting around in my experience, which is fine since your normal form is fast and responsive and fun.I don't really have much negative to say about it. So many metroidvanias get fundamentals like movement or exploring wrong or make them tedious, but in Biomorph it's quite fun, pretty clearly telegraphed, AND you can even get around some of the intended ways to get upgrades with some creative approaches / exploring. I 100% it in 16 hours and it didn't drag or feel grindy, and I definitely feel like I got my money's worth.The only criticism I can really point at it are that the tone and atmosphere feel a little off - the world and story are quite bleak but the cartoony graphics and light music sorta fight with that. Not that in the real world, bleak situations are without hope and lightness - it just doesn't quite resonate in tone like some other games do for me, which is OK. I hope more games take the lack of tedium and nice QoL present here as inspiration, sometimes it's the difference between great fun and great misery.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic, polished MV experience, with a sizeable map, multiple playstyle possibilities, a Kirby-like morphing mechanic, and lashings of quality of life that show this is a game made by a team who know what they're doing. I went in expecting it to be my kind of thing from the demo, but was consistently amazed by how many times I had to stop and say to myself "These guys really know what fans like me want from a game like this."I'm sure it isn't going to be for so-called "metroidvania purists" or those that insist that all games need to be excruciatingly arduous and challenging so that they can feel some validation — but you can't please all of the people, all of the time. The game has a solid difficulty curve, and while I explored a lot, I expect people who just try and power through the critical path might find themselves with some reasonably-challenged boss fights on their hands. But difficulty is very subjective.I got 21 hours out of Biomorph to get all the endings and 100% file completion, and apart from a few nitpicks about contact damage, I had a really fun time with the game. Great artstyle, monstrous foes, fun bossfights, cool gimmicks, surprisingly nuanced story, fun characters. S-Tier quality work from people who clearly love the genre.And all for an excellent price too!
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. The map is huge but level design feels completely aimless and uninspired. Devs went for an Ender Lilies map style so I can't figure out where in a room I am or how to get to a specific exit. Combat doesn't have any weight and there is contact damage for no reason, which leads to getting juggled and multi-hit by larger enemies. Nothing feels particularly rewarding or worth spending my time on. It's pretty and I love the comic-style cut scenes, but there isn't anything to hold my interest here.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Hollow Knight and Ender Lilies, BIOMORPH caught my attention. I saw a review by Demajen that ranked BIOMORPH as S-tier, alongside Hollow Knight, Ori and the Will of the Wisps, and Ender Lilies. I've already been on my PC for 1.5 hours, battling and exploring as much as possible.The universe is truly immersive — the dialogues between Harlo, Eny, and Zeki genuinely make me laugh. I'm taking my first steps in Ilios, barely stepping out of Blightmoor, and already discovering breathtaking panoramas in Mezzo Skyway! So far, it's a flawless experience with the art, soundtracks, and cutscenes!! Honestly, I'm fully immersed thanks to these aspects.Not to mention the BIOMORPH ability. I've become a monster hunter so I can transform into all the monsters in the game — I'm filling up my Pokédex. Their gameplay is really diverse, and I enjoy being able to strategize which ones to choose to progress optimally during my playthrough.BIOMORPH IS BIG FUN !
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: An underrated gem for Metrodvania series. (but not souls-like though)Very solid experience in terms of exploration aspect. I was surprised how good the game turns out at around mid-point of the game when the map branches out into so many huge areas.Pros:- Good variety of bioms and aesthetic (almost on par with Hollow Knight)- Interesting world building and lore- Very solid map design and good traversal (on par with Hollow Knight/ Ori)- Addictive and worthwhile collectibles in terms of character progression- Very useful map feature to help you reach 100% without any tediumCons:- Bosses a bit too weak , lack the satisfaction of beating them- Monster transformation balance is poor. 2/3 of them are pretty useless , and maps that requires using specific transformation becomes a handicap toward your exploration rather than making the game fun.- Story telling and dialogues are kinda weak despite having very solid world building and lore- Art is pretty good but art-style is not very attractive. It's not bad but it doesn't leave an impression - A bit too many fetch quests running from A to B to C, especially when its given all at once.Overall a solid 8/10 Metodvania game. But do note this is not a Souls-like, unlike Hollow Knight/ Blasphemous and such.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Second update @16 hours in: Once the abilities start rolling in, moving around is a sheer joy.  I'll be 100%ing this and gifting a few copies to friends to help sales and word of mouth even a little bit, the devs put great heart in and it's a fantastic first game.  It's a phenomenal entry in the genre, it's already so criminally underrated and underplayed.  With experience and lessons learned, I can't wait to see what this team puts out next.So this came completely out of left field for me, not on my radar at all.  I tried the demo for 20 minutes before launch day and went from 0 to 100 hype, making Biomorph an instabuy the second it was available.  While I'm not an expert on Metroidvanias, I could very quickly feel the DNA of some of my favorites like Megaman ZX/Advent in this and I'll always give games like that a shot.The morphing part is genuinely integral to Biomorph, which may seem obvious given the name but could easily have been just a throwaway mechanic after hooking players in.  2 bosses in and I'm feeling really good about the responsive gameplay and world overall; it's quirky, melancholic, but with sparks of hope and witty writing all around.  From the demo version compared to launch, Harlo feels more floaty yet snappy in the best of ways, so it seems like a lot was tuned under the hood up 'til the last minute.  My main gripe is that hitboxes have felt a liiiittle cheap with being able to take repeated damage very rapidly, specifically on the 2nd boss, but I'm going to chalk that up to still learning.I'll keep this updated as I play, but definitely a recommend if you've ever played the ZX/A games and enjoyed them.Update: Additional movement capabilities and some other abilities have increased my enjoyment significantly.  There's a little awkwardness with the camera snapping sometimes with the movement one but it's not too bad.  It's worth mentioning the map system is pretty robust as well, though maybe I'm missing it but a % completion would be welcome.  Otherwise yeah, I just needed a little dose of getting good, I'm having a blast and maaaaybe slightly ignoring work to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Wow I feel bad for the monsters in this game. In the first 5 minutes of gameplay I had both of my tiny blue futuristic fists asking me to beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of mutants. Next thing I know, I'm feeding one of them the biscuit, giving them the knuckle sandwich, 1 - 2 combo. BOOM - I BIO MORPHED into the mutant I just killed, and then I start using his abilities to beat his mutant friends. How embarrassing.My favourite one so far is the Scarbyttle, their special ability is ''GIGA FART'', it rips a fat one and does tons of damage.I was reading the game descriptions and they insist it's some sort of dark smoke, but I know what I was doing.I was giga farting.The 3C feels tight, controls are responsive.The art style and visuals are fantastic.I highly recommend this metroidvania gem.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, the game is all about transformation and adaptability, letting you morph into enemies you've defeated to solve puzzles and explore the world.The main hook in "Biomorph" is your ability to take on the forms of the enemies you beat. Each form has its own unique abilities that you need to use to get past obstacles and figure out puzzles. This keeps things exciting and constantly makes you think on your feet.Combat is fast and requires a good mix of skill and quick thinking. Each enemy has its own attack style and weaknesses, so you have to be strategic about which form you use to take them down. This makes every fight feel fresh and rewarding.The story in "Biomorph" is a compelling mix of self-discovery and mystery. You get pieces of the story through dialogue, environmental clues, and cutscenes, all of which are well done and engaging. As your character grows, so does the world around you, making for a deeply immersive experience.The characters you meet are well-developed and add a lot to the story. Each has their own backstory and motives, revealed through your interactions with them. This makes the world feel alive and gives you plenty of reasons to explore and talk to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Another Metroidvania in the endless sea of Metroidvanias.But, is it good?Yes, it is!I have to admit, at first I was kind of skeptic. Right from the get go I could tell that I would like the music. And I was right. This was pretty good. Not exceptional but really good.Then I got into the Game and then came some reservations. I don't know what it was, but after ~1-2 hours of playing I needed a break. Glad I got back to it. The Game looks good. Certainly not the best looking Metroidvania but good enough. I think at first I was kind of mixed with the Animations. But I got used to it and in the end it was fine.After halfway through the Game I thought: Well, this is competent in everything. Not astounding or the next big hit but if you like Metroidvanias you can do no wrong here.After a while longer I began really enjoying the Game. I have to say that the Game is more on the easy side but I found that pretty chill for a change. Bosses took me at the most 2 tries, most of them I got first try. Even the last boss(es) were a first try.What I really liked was also that you really don't need a walkthrough or guide for anything here. First off, they have the feature from Prince of Persia - The Lost Crown, where you can take a Screenshot and it gets pinned on the map. Very helpful.Apropos map, the map is really good as well. Clear to read and it tells you if an area is completed and puts a gold border around that area.Game ran perfectly fine apart from one time where I actually had one hard crash that forced me to restart my PC. And the Game has exactly the right length. Not too short, not too long. It took me ~22hours to fully complete the Game and 100% all the Achievements. Just perfect.Also the Morphing into the creatures you kill, all with different abilities (you will probably use them mostly for traversal) was pretty cool and at least something kind of new in this Genre.Overall: This is not the next Hollow Knight. But it is a damn fine Metroidvania. If you like this Genre at all, I think this is a must play. (Also kind of impressive for an indie team.)Go get it...
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Completed it 100% in ~25 hours entirely on the Deck. Relatively easy by metroidvania standards.Art style and direction is consistent and inventive, as is the main gameplay hook. I really enjoyed the 2D animated cutscenes. My only complaint is that there can be some annoying backtracking if you make a mistake and bring the wrong creature along. Funnily enough, mid-way through my playthrough, the devs added a "return to save point" function which cuts that backtrack in half. The only bug I encountered is an inability to delete pins on the map screen. Not a big deal.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game. The style is great and the mechanics are interesting.There are just small things that make it feel incomplete. The map is huge but feels very empty and repetitive. You only get a few types of enemies per biome. The dialog in most cases is just shallow puns.There are some small improvements that can also make the experience better. You can't even quit the game without going through unskippable intros.EDIT: changed to positive since it looks like the devs are listening to the community and the QOL changes make the game experience more enjoyable.Having finished the game I still feel somewhat disappointed though, as per my original review.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: From the epic music to the dark mysterious lore, BIOMORPH has my full attention at the moment.The BIOMORPH mechanic itself (transforming into enemies) is what caught my eye when I first read about it a few months ago. It's a cool feature that allows you to experiment with different abilities like speed, power, range (so far), but I'm anticipating that different monsters will offer different things later on and that you'll have to use this mechanic to solve platforming puzzles as well. Judging by the size of the inventory and abilities tab, I can deduce that I've barely scratched the surface and unfortunately, that means I'll have to cancel my plans with my gf in order to get 100% by the end of the weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Biomorph was alright.The morphing power is a lot more novel at the start and you occasionally need it to progress and get secrets.I wish you didn't have to return to a safe point, to swap the powers though. It just artificially lengthens the game time, this game does not need this at all. The exploration is on point for a metroidvania, free pins and even golden border around completed maps make 100%-ing this very comfortable. Also being able to pick endings and not being locked out of any content is just good design.Combat-wise and Difficulty-wise this game is so-so. Combat does not feel bad or amazing but it just works.  I had to occasionally repeat bosses but honestly the boss fights are pretty forgetable. Music is fine, endings are kinda short and pointless. Even the true ending.Solid 7 or 6 out of 10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: The "become the enemy you defeated" gameplay mechanic is very well crafted. The game is fluid, fun and challenging. The first hour was a bit confusing and a bit too much exposition all at the same time (personal taste), but after that, the gameplay really steal the show and it's a lot of fun!Also, you can pet the cats. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Lucid Dreams Studio nailed Biomorph. This is a fantastic addition to the Metroidvania genre. From its impressive designs, to the challenging and varied combat, and the incredible hook of the Biomorph skill, this game deserves a lot of praise. I’m glad they took their time to put on such an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very average. If you're looking for a laid back easy Metroidvania, this game is for you. You can biomorph into your defeated enemies. However, the combat is basic.  The enemies in this game have 1-2 attacks and simple attacks like cause a cloud, punch, or shoot a blast. The main character is the most fleshed out by far is generic too. The bosses took me 1-2 tries top beat.Overall if you're looking for a cheap Metroidvania and have some time to kill or are looking for something relaxing, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun Metroidvania with a "become your enemies" gimmick, which are two things I immensely enjoy. The visuals are smooth like they're straight out of a cartoon, although I will admit that the environments don't leave a very strong first impression. The first few areas you go through are kind of bland looking and use a kind of reserved colour palette. It makes sense in the story, but visually they're really nothing special.That gets remedied later in the game, though, when they start using brighter and more lively colours. I was really impressed when I reached the Forbidden Plains for the first time. It blew everything that came before it out of the water, and the visuals were consistently very nice from then on.Difficulty wise, it's definitely at its hardest at the very start. Enemy damage is a bit high, and before you gain any more health or ways to mitigate the damage you receive, it can feel like everything kills you in two or three hits. Again though, once you're through with the rough earlygame, it's pretty smooth sailing. I don't think I experienced any deaths that felt more like the game's fault than my own. As with any game in this genre, there's a fair bit of backtracking with later upgrades or enemy transformations to pick up items you couldn't reach before. I'm a sucker for it, but it could feel like a slog to some people, so I thought I'd mention it.Two of the enemy transformations in particular - one of them can fly, one of them has a triple jump - can feel a bit wrong to use. They can bypass puzzles that they probably shouldn't be able to just by how far and high they can take you. A bit of sequence breaking can be fun, though, and you have to use them a little skilfully to actually get those early items, so it's not too bad.Another tip for you people that like doing things out of order: The Toroth can jump a really long distance with its charge attack, and you get it far earlier than either of those other two morphs. You can get a bunch of goodies just by abusing that.One thing I would really like to see is an option to refight bosses you've already defeated, as aside from the final boss, there isn't any way to do that beyond making a new save file. Maybe have them deal a bit more damage and have a bit more health, maybe move a bit faster, on the refights. Most bosses weren't too hard initially, so I think that extra bit of challenge on a potential rematch would do a world of good!Overall, I really enjoyed my time with Biomorph. It was exactly the kind of game I was looking for. I completed it 100% in just under 18 hours, so it's not an incredibly long game either. It's definitely worth your time if you're a fan of the genre, and I'm already craving even more!
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very fun game to play with some great quality of life features that make it accessible throughout all the backtracking. Art, music, and story are all great and there is plenty to explore in this game, along with the best part of course, . In fact, I would like to say that the story in this game was definitely a lot clearer than in many metroidvanias I have played. Additionally, the different abilities in the game make movement fun and it is satisfying to use them and chain them. Although I would tweak a few things in terms of knockback chain damage, and I have a few minor nitpicks about combat and some enemies, overall this game had solid fights. Also the biomorphing part of the game does make a slightly unique twist to the game, though I feel with more thought I could have integrated them better in combat. I would definitely recommend this game for those who like metroidvanias and the associated exploration and backtracking that goes along with it.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, albeit average, metroidvania. I have my issues with it but I've played so many of those that I might be pickier than most. It's a far cry from the pinnacle of the genre like Hollow knight or Lost Crown, but it's a decent time until Silksong comes. It just doesn't do anything that hasn't been done better elsewhere already. If you're looking for a decent metroidvania for a weekend, you could do worse. I give this a thumbs up a bit reluctantly.the good:- music is top notch, seriously great stuff- combat sfx are punchy and satisfying- pretty big map and decent biome variety- very distinct visual identity.the bad:- pretty much all the forms I unlocked so far (12-ish) are flat out boring to play as and pretty much useless in combat. They're used constantly for traversal and then you ditch em to actually fight. People calling this a "kirby-like" are completely off track, in those games, the transformations are the star of the show IN AND OUT of combat. Here, I end up never using them unless I'm strictly forced to and glad when I'm done using most of em. They are slow, cumbersome and many have such ultra specific abilities for specific obstacles that they feel forced. Would've much preferred to have like... 10 forms with more varied movesets and allowing a variety of playstyles. *People expecting kirby-like powerups will be very disappointed*- Not enjoying having only 3 slots for the memorised forms too, you always end up having to backtrack to a save point, change your loadout to get the form you need for a specific obstacle then go back. It gets old very fast.. and since pretty much all the forms are useless in combat, I'm never using them and I see no point at ALL to keep levelling them up just to run 10% faster or jump 1/4th of inch higher.- map / area design is painfully average. The 5-6 biomes I've explored so far feel like every other average metroidvania I've played. I usually really enjoy exploring every nook and cranny in these games, here, not so much unfortunately... there's just very little surprises to be had, it's all very .... average. - Bosses are boring: Their movesets are SO limited. They do 2-3 things on loop till 50% HP then add a new move or two. That's it... unless it changes later.... Their visual design is original, but the fight themselves are just "meh". They go down in no time flat with very little resistance. You can figure them out in the first 20 seconds of a fight. As far as metroivania bossfights go, it's pretty low tier. - Could change later but the powerups you find are also not very exciting. Riding powerlines is not bad though.- Story is quite forgettable so far and does nothing to push me forward. NPCs talk a lot but little substance, didn't take long before they veered into insta-skip territory.So much more could've been done with this concept. Feels like a missed opportunity. It's not a bad game by any stretch of the imagination, clearly a lot of love was poured into this game... but with the flood of metroidvanias in the last decade and them saying they took inspiration from things like Hollow Knight, I'm saddened that they couldn't transfer what made these games so revered. Once I finish it I'll update my review if my feelings change. **** Update after 10 more hours ****Well, sadly I won’t finish this because I’m bored out of my mind. Changing my review to thumbs downThis simply is the most by-the-numbers average metroidvania I’ve played in a long time. I’m usually 1:1 in agreement with Demajen’s rankings but here I’m just baffled. This is near bottom of the barrel for me. I feel most of the positives reviews come from the visuals, which are pretty good… but peel that layer off and it’s a bland uninspired mess. The world is just so boring to explore. Every zone nearly feels the same to navigate or just tedious to go through. It’s just a very blocky architecture that borderline feels procedurally generated at times. My opinion on the forms after getting all of them has not changed, they all uniformly suck and are not fun to use. Upgrading them is pointless and is barely noticeable outside a few very specific cases. These shouldve been the star of the show. It’s so unfortunate.The chips and mementos too, every one I unlocked I was curious to try but always came back to the first three (fist, gun, lance) because it’s just what’s most effective. The mementos effects are not thst exciting either. Upgrading either is just …. Making then a bit stronger, more charges, etc. No new effect or anything exciting.The bosses somehow got worse. This has to be the worst set of bosses I’ve seen in a game of this genre. No challenge, none of them impressive in the slightest. Practically all of them left me a “that’s it?” impression. Basic, uninspired and incredibly limited movesets.The needing to find those blueprints to get the mats needed to upgrade the save points for fast travel is a mind boggling design choice. There is zero point to it, it’s useless friction with no purpose. Now i’m missing a blueprint to get another set of upgrade mats and all the new save points I’m discovering, I can’t fast travel to, causing tedious backtracking that has just no reason to be. You should be able to fast travel to previously discovered SAFE spots. Anybody looking for a good metroidvania, look elsewhere, this is absolutely not it and misses the mark on practically every metric outside visual and sound.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Played on OG 512 steam deck without any major issues but from mid game on skipping dialogue caused a short freeze that would resolve itself and most annoyingly , putting deck in sleep mode would cause the game to search for connection and synchronize with steam when turned back on, like I said, annoying. That being said this is a great game, good fun from the begging to end with accessibility options, lovely graphics, satisfying traversal, large interconnected map with so many secrets. Has the screeenshot pin like POPTLC. Amazing good time and I highly recommend this wonderful game! Don’t wait for a sale, it’s worth full ask! This is a game I slept on for a while as the demo turned me off actually but the game can’t be judged by that in this case.Check out where I placed this game on my Metroidvania tier list
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I really wish had a neutral option. There were a lot of positives, but for me, there were some equally questionable items as well.I saw a lot of potential with the morphing abilities and story, however there were some (in my opinion) odd decisions made. With morphing, one of the oddities I ran into was when you morph from a corpse, there doesn't appear to be any ammo limitation with abilities. However if you morph from "memory" then you have ammo counts to deal with. With the story I didn't get too far, but from what I saw, character interactions felt a little unnatural. Like my character appears to be the only type of character in the world, but everyone reacts as if they're common. Maybe I just didn't get far enough into the game to find out why.Music, general sound design, and biome art was very cool and I really enjoyed the monster/character designs as well, but something felt lacking when it came to the actual character animations. For me, things felt like it was moving in slow motion, even though the speed/pacing was pretty ordinary. It's hard to describe.Overall, I'd say give the demo a try before you buy. Actual exploration was fun with all the different creatures you could morph into and it was a pleasure to discover new creatures and unlock new areas. Unfortunately it just didn't capture me like it did for others.

Should really let us change it anywhere, no good reasons to not and wouldn't cause any balance issues.- visual acuity with blue enemies blending too much into the background. Might want to consider adding need more colors for those enemies or adjust with lighter blue for better contrast against dark background.- too many sidequests make for excessive backtracking, the main hub is unnecessarily large and bloated to deal with- few annoying bugs at this time but nothing gamebreakingOverall, I'd say it's 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations for this game and that probably is killing it for me. I'm holding my breath, but so far it's just boring combat, very annoying quest system/large and confusing main hub, completely uninteresting story. It has good art though.The boss fights so far have been trivial (first try or at most second try) and very not-fun. The main mechanic is interesting (morphing), but for some reason, it doesn't make the game that fun, it forces the traveling to be slow (forced killing monsters).There is also way too much farming: grab materials, kill monsters to obtain powers, kill monsters for money.So far, I'm disappointed. Coming from Nine Sols and DOOMBLADE, this game is just not there, the depth of the combat is not.The biggest sin as somebody pointed out, is contact damage. Given the dodge is an extremely long slide on the floor, most monster attacks are easy to dodge due to the very generous invul frame, just to pop in the face of the monster and take contact damage. Very frustrating, especially when trash mobs are on narrow platforms.EDIT: I dropped it. I thought it was "me" the problem, but I grabbed a different metroidvania called Noreya: The Gold Project and was hooked hard (20 hours in 3 days).I confirm what's in this review, the problem is not with me, the gameplay is slow, full of open-world "stupid" quests which make it bad from my perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: The music is nice and catchy, the combat has good variation between the weapon chips and biomorphs, both the characters and enemies have charming designs. _childDocuments_.review: Seriously, excellent game for anyone liking metroidvania games. _childDocuments_.review: You can read my other reviews Visually appealing, with an intriguing premise centered around a sci-fi plot, Biomorph emerges as a standout in the Metroidvania Platforming genre.Following the story of Harlo, it quickly becomes apparent that this peculiar character suffers from a memory lapse regarding the events leading up to waking from cryo sleep in a mysterious spaceship. Upon reuniting with his friend, Kleio, the adventure begins to free him and uncover the mystery surrounding the area where they landed and why they ended up there.Although the story is linear, it allows for a journey filled with unexpected allies, flashbacks of small memory fragments, all encapsulated in charming little cutscenes.Harlo’s combat system is quite captivating. It is highly responsive to controls, features satisfying combos, and offers a plethora of interesting attack combinations, allowing each player to tailor their gameplay style to a specific build. This is all thanks to the Chip feature, which can be discovered throughout the adventure or purchased from a specialized shop, each with its own unique ability, including ranged attacks and more. These Chips have a cooldown period, preventing infinite use. Additionally, there are Mementos, which are passive abilities offering benefits like healing, critical damage, and increased damage, among others.The most interesting concept of Biomorph is directly tied to its name. Inspired by Kirby-like mechanics, where it is possible to acquire the abilities of others through enemy absorption, in Biomorph, the main character can also absorb the DNA of monsters and control their abilities, whether they are offensive or mobility-related like higher jumps to reach elevated areas. Another intriguing aspect of this mechanic is the ability to become stronger in a specific monster’s body the more times you capture its DNA, allowing for the freedom to transform into that form with the press of a button.As with all Metroidvanias, there are many areas to explore, and many of them cannot be accessed until certain abilities, in this case, monster Morphs, are acquired. Another interesting aspect is the premise of repairing the city to unlock new areas, giving a sense of community to a zone plagued by sad news and serving as a refuge for a pair of interesting characters.Unfortunately, the boss encounters are not memorable enough to mark a significant point in this adventure. Once you recognize each one’s attack pattern, it becomes tremendously easy to adjust your combat style.Biomorph exudes a special charm. From its animations, cutscenes, characters, to its engaging combat, it becomes an experience that will delight fans of this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed my play through. My X-box controller worked great and the game was easy to navigate. There was a lot to do and the different forms were the highlight. There is an enormous amount to discover and the map is big, clear and helpful. The 38 hours on my record is not correct, I would estimate I have spent around 24 hours for 97% completion. This will be longer than average since I am very methodical. The added accessibility options in a later update were great for me, I am not a die hard player and happily used them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some of the absolute best exploration in a Metroidvania I've seen. If you're into that part of this genre, this game is gonna be an absolute treat for you!This game also has some of the absolute weakest bossfights I have seen from this genre, and it really never gets any better. For something this game does remarkable well, the plot is frankly very well-executed. Much of the early game is spent introducing things that end up heavily re-framed later as you learn more about the world. It's just legitimately good story writing at a macro-scale.Overall, this game is solidly in my A-Tier of games. Not the best of the best, but still does a ton very well and overall had me hooked to the point I was thinking about potential plot threads and secrets even while I wasn't playing it.It's getting to the point now where I have played a  of Metroidvanias. I have quite a few thoughts with this one, as it does quite a bit well, but also massively misses in a couple key areas.As with most entries to the genre, Biomorph tries to bring something new to the table, this time in the form of creature morphs. But does it work?On the platforming/exploration side?  yes! On top of morphing into creatures you kill in their immediate vicinity, Biomorph also lets you keep three morphs "equipped" at any time, allowing you to freely transform into them to bypass challenges in creative ways if you know how to use them. However, on the combat front, I tended to find the morphs to be more of a nuisance than anything, and by the end of the game, I was frequently un-morphing to fight before re-morphing to continue traversal. The few times I needed to use morphs for boss fights, I would only briefly equip the morph for the gimmick attack of that fight, then morph back. Speaking of bosses...This aspect of the game was so weak in my opinion that it deserves its own category. If good bossfights in games is a necessity for you, frankly, I'd recommend looking elsewhere. It's technically not the worst I've seen in any game, but it's sure close.Most bosses are limited to two attacks they alternate between very consistently, and they gain a third once their HP drops below half. Pretty much every attack is trivial to dodge once you've seen it once just by dashing away, then back, and whacking the boss a few times. Repeat until it dies.The combat in this game is still generally good, with several enemies making for decent challenges rewarded by easier traversal of their respective biomes. And on that note...I said it in the short version, and I'll say it again here. Exploration in Biomorph is an absolute treat. The map system is legitimately one of the best I've ever seen for keeping track of and remembering secrets, and the satisfaction that comes with golden-ing a room cannot be overstated. Having a carefully-curated set of equipped morphs for the biomes you're coming up to can help this even more, allowing you to bypass quite a few challenges in creative ways that just feels fantastic. The secret-hiding is stellar, and exploring around basically always felt rewarding. You can tell the devs absolutely  this part of the genre, as they just nailed it in a way few others have.There's also tons of little QOL details that make the game super satisfying to play in the moment to moment, such as holding the dash button to run after dashing, making crossing large rooms way faster. Little things like that add up to making the experience feel a ton better, and there's a lot of little things that were clearly put in to make the game flow just that much better.Of course, there's always more to be said, but at some point, I have to stop and just let you experience some of it for yourself. If you've made it this far, you're probably interested in this game, and all I can say now is that it's a really strong entry in the genre! Had an absolute blast basically 100%'ing this one as I played it, and I look forward to seeing what these devs get up to next!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of metroidvania games, "Biomorph" captivated me with its innovative biomorphing mechanic and immersive exploration. Here's my take: The ability to transform into different creatures adds a refreshing layer of depth to both combat and exploration. Each biomorph offers unique abilities and mobility options, making every boss fight a diverse and dynamic experience. However, some sluggish biomorphs may pose challenges in boss battles due to contact damage, highlighting the importance of strategic planning. The game excels in exploration, with charming designs, catchy music, and well-crafted combat. Using biomorphs and exploration abilities to uncover secrets and traverse the map felt rewarding and immersive. "Biomorph" shines as a standout example of the metroidvania genre, offering fluid controls, a compelling story, and entertaining gameplay throughout. The unique biomorph mechanic, reminiscent of "Hollow Knight" and "Ori," adds depth and surprises while maintaining the essence of character progression. Visually stunning and creatively designed, the game showcases the talent and dedication of its development team. From vibrant biomes to intricate character designs, every aspect of the game reflects the care and craftsmanship poured into its creation. With its engaging gameplay, innovative biomorphing mechanic, and captivating world, the game offers a compelling metroidvania experience. Despite minor flaws such as easy boss fights and rushed ending segments, the game's overall charm and depth make it a must-play for fans of the genre. For those seeking a fresh take on the metroidvania genre and a captivating journey through biomorphing adventures, "Biomorph" is a delightful choice that deserves recognition and support for its indie studio craftsmanship.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing. For me it is on paar with Hollow Knight. The ability to morph into different enemies gives you a lot of possibility to traverse through the world. It is usually a lot more efficient to just smack away on the boss with you normal weapons. I think there are only two bosses that actually need a specific morph.I also would have wished for more possibilities to use those morphs in other areas than the ones where you find the enemies. Like alternative routes based on the morphs you have acquired. And the game also is for the most part very linear. As you need certain abilities to get through the whole area and to the boss.
