_childDocuments_.review: Biomorph is a decent metroidvania that's worth your time, so long as you play it with a few expectations tempered.Biomorph is a beautiful game. It absolutely nails its own artstyle, and each biome have their own distinct personality. Enemies and bosses are well put together, and it manages to make an alien world feel familiar somehow. Animation and game feel is crisp and responsive; no complaints there. Harlo, the main protagonist, moves like a dream in this game.Exploration is a mixed bag. The early game is fairly linear (for good reasons), and the world opens up slowly, perhaps a little too slow for veteran metroidvania players, but within reason. The abilities you get are pretty lacklustre; most abilities are context-dependant, meaning they require the right terrain to exist in order for you to make good use of them. Some of the abilities are only relevant in specific biomes. In general, strictly talking about the abilities you get in the game, they're quite bad, and boring. That said, you do get biomorphs - as you kill enemies, you can take their form and abilities, and more often than not they will come with unique traversal abilities. So even when your basic abilities are pretty meh, with the addition of these biomorphs, you won't be missing much mobility in the mid to late game.Exploration is mediocre. Sure, the world opens up, and yes, there're "secret" biomes that are particularly well done, but in general you won't see any level design that will make you go "oh yeah, this is smart". Don't expect good platforming until the late game (and they're actually pretty decent, though slightly on the easier side).Harlo handles like a boss. He's fast, mobile, and very responsive. You get a bunch of weapons that each have their own usages, though you'll likely stick with a few favourites for the vast majority of the game. Biomorph forms that you get have combat capabilities, but most of them handle like ♥♥♥♥ so likely you won't be using them much outside of a few boss fights.Now, bosses. They're on the easy side. They're slow, ponderous, and have very limited movesets that are easy to predict and handle. The final bosses are kind of a let down being how easy they are compared to what you can do at that point. That said, for players looking for easy bosses, this is definitely the kind of game for you. They're not total pushovers, but rewards you well for learning their patterns.I would say Biomorph is a solid A-tier game: well put together, enjoyable throughout, and barring a few issues here and there, it's a solid metroidvania to get your hands on. Real easy to 100% too.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been playing a lot more metroidvanias in the last 6 months or so and I will definitely keep Biomorph high up on my recent memory.It was different enough to be a memorable experience throughout the 15 hours of gaming. I particularly liked the atmosphere as it was still harsh but still light enough to crack a few jokes here and there. You could feel humanity in the cast as they tried to make the best of the hand dealt.Mechanically, using defeated enemies to aid in traversal and combat was definitely novel and the variety kept things fresh to avoid monotony and the feeling of repeated content.Even content-wise there is a lot of optional content to chase, be it additional gear, side quests, or get the shiny gold border on every single room of the map to keep your inner completionist  at peace. It is also tempting to go back after the final boss to unlock the other endings without having to replay the entire game - the game saves just before you enter the arena.I no longer have the free time to complete games to 100%, but I can genuinely say that I get the urge to go back and complete it every time I talk about Biomorph. It you are a fan of metroidvanias then I definitely recommend to give the demo a chance. The best praise I can give it as a demo is that it will provide you enough arguments to decide if you want to pay for the rest or not. And if you do play the full game, then you're in for a fresh metroidvania experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Great Metroidvania. Very impressive for such a small team. Atmosphere is stellar, Gameplay is spot on and there's a great variety of weapons, powers and equipment.It's heavily inspired by Hollow Knight, but with its own spin and improvements. If you liked HK, you're going to love this one. It's easier, but still offers a reasonable challenge.I was skeptical at first of the game's special mechanics, which lets you transform into enemies, but it turned out to be a blast. All enemies have a specific moveset you can borrow and many open new passages. It elevates the gameplay quite nicely.I 100% the game in 17 hours, without rushing, but without taking too much time either.I have to make a special mention of the gold border feature : when you've got everything a room has to offer (items, quests, enemies), the border becomes golden, letting you know exactly where to search for secrets and when to stop looking. It really helped motivate me to get 100%, as I knew where to search. However, it would be better if it did not require completing every quest step in the area, including future steps, as I sometimes spent a couple of minutes searching for a secret passage that didn't exist.All in all, I had a blast. Great game that I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: I love metroidvania style games, and this fits the bill for me. I played about 5 minutes of the demo and purchased right away.The movement feels nice, combat is just fair and challenging enough to be enjoyable for most players, and the art style and humor of the characters is excellent. I'm only just under 20 hours in (I've been attempting to clear rooms as I go since I got a bit lost at a time or two), and there's still more to explore and discover.That being said, I do have a couple critiques. The first one is the map/pin system. While I do appreciate having pins to mark locations on the map to check out later, I'm not a fan of just having the ability to change the pin color. I think that having different icons like a treasure chest, a door/lock, or a question mark would be nice so the player has an easier time remembering why the symbol is on the map in the first place. I realize this is maybe a little too forgiving to the player, but I think this sort of thing can be completely optional and can be used if they want. Definitely not a deal breaker, just a small thing.The other critique is there is not really any faster way to traverse other than spamming dash. Either I haven't uncovered any sort of speed boost yet, or it just doesn't exist. There isn't an easy or quick way to fast travel TO save points so you do need to be cautious especially if you're low on health. The good news there are plenty of fast travel points spread throughout the map, so you're maybe 2-3 rooms away from each one.Overall, I'm really enjoying this game, and I'm happy to see that this genre is still alive and producing quality titles. If you're still on the fence after reading reviews, give the demo a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really deep into this game and it’s like digital crack.  I can’t put it down.  It is so fun and so much stuff to do.  And haven’t even begun to really experiment with the weapons.  Because each morph is a weapon of its own anyway and there are tons of them.  You also get plenty of normal mv ability upgrades.  Then it has a charm system to boot.  Game is absolutely loaded with quests and marks the locations on the map for you to help keep track of them all.  Has an ender lilies style map with blocks and they get a yellow border when you have found all the secrets in a block.  But you can see where you are within the block unlike ender lilies, so I don’t see people having problems with it.  Boss battles are fun.  This game is a must play for any metroidvania fan.

_childDocuments_.review: You can pet the cat 10/10EDIT: Now that I've played through the game and am almost at 100%, I want to give a real review. This is the best metroidvania I've ever played.Levels:Every zone-based game I have played has some area that either feels like a chore or just sucks to go through. Biomorph doesn't have that problem. Each zone in the game feels fair and never a slog to go through.Controls/Handling:I've played games with a similar style, like Salt and Sanctuary or Hollow Knight, where platforming is stiff and takes a backseat to the combat system. From the beginning every action felt completely fluid. There was never a time where movement or attacking felt clunky. Every new traversal ability you obtain felt equally important and added a new layer of reactions to the environment.Combat:I was surprised that all the monsters you could morph into mattered. I will say that only a few of them felt good to use in combat, but the chip system already handles the combat side of the game and I see the monsters as a bonus.Story:I think Biomorph struck a solid balance with having the plot told to you directly, while the worldbuilding itself is something you have to actively seek out. Not everyone plays games because they care about the lore, and I like the option of this either being a mindless "hit things and parkour" type of game or a "explore and experience the world and learn its history" type of game.I again give this a 10/10, and not just because of the cats, but they do help.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see the developer is very obsessed with path of pain and Celeste. Late game areas are mostly like combination of those.The art style, puzzle mechanics and musics are good. _childDocuments_.review: Fun game, interesting premise, decent controls, and game play. BUT FOR THE LOVE OF GOD. Please stop sticking "souls-like" mechanics into every indie metroidvania. It's just an un-fun element to foist on players. It punishes risk and exploration.  Even if recovering your stash of cash isn't all the consequential it feels like a heavy handed punishment especially in tough situations. Especially in areas that have a lot of cheap contact damage (of which there are a lot). As I've reach harder and harder areas I already feel this game wearing on my nerves. There is no way I'm 100%ing this game and that's a real shame because it seems very interesting. And it's all because this game play element seems to show up everywhere to justify some difficulty check box. Also power progression feels pretty limited. You only have the same punch that is unlimited, everything else is shot counted between visits to the bonfires, even melee weapons. Another mechanic that couldn't die fast enough in my opinion. Something even Elden Ring got rid of. I really really wanted to finish this game but I'm almost certainly going to move on before getting much deeper. Big thanks to the devs for making the demo saves portable to the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: I won't criticize the game for unoriginality because I would have to apply the same critique to nearly every modern MV that employs similar tropes. It's proficient at what it does, it's fun to play, and is compact and accessible. But it should be noted that it skews on the easier side. I liked the boss designs but they could usually be defeated in 2 or 3 attempts, although the final boss sequence proved a bit tougher. The story isn't super compelling but there are some fun characters and cute/clever dialogue in the game.One thing I can praise is the fluid movement of your character. A handful of the creatures you transform into are really fun to control, however, there are too many to choose from and most aren't mechanically distinct enough from your character to be interesting. Transformations would be better if there were less overall—keeping only the most useful ones—and you could use any one at any time, instead of being limited to 3 in your loadout. Going along with that, more creature-specific puzzles throughout the world would've been welcomed. My other main complaint is I wish the challenge rooms had been more...challenging, and more complex in terms of enemy placement, attack patterns, etc., especially considering most are optional.On another note, this game has some pretty cool QOL features, such as the ability to screenshot anywhere on the map (previously seen in Prince of Persia TLC but refined here), ability to return instantly to the last save point, and the ability to go back and access all the alternate endings (each with a unique boss sequence). I'd recommend Biomorph for a laid back experience with enjoyable traversal and exploration gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: A solid game overall with great graphics and setting that I enjoyed (mostly) over the course of one weekend. Most of the fights were pretty tame in comparison to some other titles, but that made for a nice playthrough for a casual gamer like myself that didn't want to spend several attempts just for one clear. Definitely worth checking out if you're new to the genre or just want a casual Metroidvania either as a side-game filler or weekend-binger.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: VERY happy I finally picked this game up. I have pretty much always enjoyed MetroidVania style games, and this one was also a treat.The hand drawn art style of all the assets and scenes adds a very nice touch to the games overall aesthetic. Fully animated cutscenes are the icing on the cake in that department. Very nice to see this kind of thing. Kudos to the art team.Combat is certainly kept very interesting and different thanks to your own skills but also the 'borrowed' abilities of the creatures you morph into. Their abilities are often used for overcoming obstacles in the level, but many also come in handy with certain boss fights.The boss fights themselves are tricky at first, but once you nail down their moves and pick the right skills and biomorphs to use, it makes the fights much simpler. Very nice touch to make you think a bit more about these fights outside of just button mashing.Audio is solid all around. Musical score for each of the biomes fits perfectly. Not much to say here.Gameplay wise everything also feels very good. At no point did I ever feel frustrated or annoyed with any of the platforming. As mentioned about the biomorph abilities, it's nice that you are still kept thinking while moving through each level about what to use and when.The story felt a little slow at the beginning, but as each plot point was reached, it certainly got more interesting, especially the end. I felt a little odd about how eager Harlo was to help literally everyone that he came across. I figured he'd be a bit more.....angsty or moody given what happened to him, more on par with Kleio I guess.Overall if you're looking for a good platforming game in the Metroidvania style, ABSOLUTELY pick this one up. Worth it even without a sale.I love the character design, the variation in skills and biomorphs keep things fresh and interesting.Took me overall 24 hours of gameplay to 100% it and I feel that's a good amount of time to do it all.Really really hoping they make a second game <3
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania where the hook is transforming into enemies Andean using their special abilities for traversal. There's about 8-10 biomes, each one has 3 unique enemy types. You need to defeat a certain number of each enemy before you can scan their DNA and morph into them. The one downside is that you can only have 3 active morph choices at a time, and re-shuffling your “loadout” can only be done at a checkpoint. Level design is quite clever as it's built around this core system. There' sa decent amount of optional tasks and exploration to flesh out the world and its characters. As you explore, you find blueprints from time to time that allow you to expand the central hub town. There are several optional bosses to test out your combat skills, and you do get some choice in the order in which you want to tackle some levels. Provided you've explored everything, the final area offers you some choices that determine your final ending- but you can reload the save before the final sequence and make different choices to see all the endings in sequence. The game is a very interesting and well-executed entry in the genre, and is definitely a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting a souls-like masterpiece, then I'd say go play Hollow Knight, but I think that BIOMORPH is a really good game and a good introduction to the Metroidvania genre. This game has its flaws, as do all games, but it does a lot of things right that I think outweigh its flaws.First off, I love the ost of BIOMORPH, and it's a shame that the entire soundtrack isn't posted on youtube. Although the soundtrack is good, the boss music doesn't change except for one boss. Even the final (and hidden) boss had the generic boss battle theme and it made it a little underwhelming.The combat system is relatively solid. The boss battles never got stale, which was nice. I do like that the enemies you kill will adapt to you and add an extra attack into their arsenal, but they became so easy to take care of as more upgrades piled on. The main gimmick didn't overstay its welcome, either. It was really fun to run around as all these different well designed creatures. Each area felt really well crafted, and each area had decent parkour challenges too! I personally had no issues with any of them EXCEPT the Sentinel Complex (which was probably a skill issue on my part.) Some of the challenges felt a little misleading, though, and a lot of the parkour felt a little bit more tight than I was expecting (especially if a beginner was playing this game.) I am happy to report that BIOMORPH has the coveted pogo, but its not as polished as Hollow Knight's or Bo's.I think the story is definitely solid, and the animations were all super well done. I liked the characters, and I think Harlo is a good take on a not silent protagonist, which is harder to do in a Metroidvania.There is so much to do in regards to sidequests, but to get the Golden Explorer achievement, you have to do all of the sidequests, which caused me to run around for hours trying to find which NPC I forgot to talk to (looking at you Ramiro). It was pretty annoying near the end, but most of the rooms are easy to solve. If you like puzzles, you'll definitely be fine with them in this game. Also, I REALLY LIKED that there was an indicator at all regarding a room being completely explored. More games need to do this.In conclusion, BIOMORPH is an incredibly solid entry to the Metroidvania genre, has enough content to deserve its price, but does have some flaws. I wish Lucid Dreams Studio luck in future developments, and I will be waiting eager for the next entry.

_childDocuments_.review: BIOMORPH serves as an excellent entry point into the Metroidvania genre, offering a captivating experience for newcomers and seasoned players alike. Although it may not match Hollow Knight's high standards in terms of quality and design, BIOMORPH still stands out as a solid title, surpassing many other games in the genre currently available on the market.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent indie Metroidvania with a brilliant and unique mechanic of transforming into enemies.The relatively popular in this genre hand-drawn art style blends wonderfully with the created world of BIOMORPH. The story presented is interesting, though not groundbreaking. The developers also added the possibility of choosing the ending, which is a nice touch. A big plus for adding indicators that show when a level has been 100% completed (golden border).There are many enemies, each with different and interesting mechanics. The boss fights are challenging, but not excessively so - they are difficult enough that you need a few attempts while learning their attack patterns and defeating them is very satisfying, yet simple enough that you don't need to spend several days on the fights alone. Personally, I think the developers found the perfect balance.As always, adding cats to the game and the ability to pet them (actually find them, but it’s connected) is a big advantage :)The map layout and level design are very well thought out, althought a few times I felt stuck. For me, that's probably one of the best maps from all metroivdanias I've played. Adding fast travel points (which you need to unlock) is SO F*CKING GREAT - I wish more games would implement this, instead of making the player to run endlessly in every direction 😏Hopefully, there will be a DLC or a sequel.Chapeau bas, one of the best Metroidvanias I've played ✌️P.S.Fairly easy to achieve 100%; it took about 20-21 hours of actual gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: It's genuinely one of my favorite Metroidvanias. The story, game-play, mechanics, and art style all make for a wonderful experience. The art style is also really wonderful and satisfying to look at. The rooms and areas to enter also all felt unique and never felt "samey." I also appreciate the fact that we're dealing with actual societies. Some MVs I've played have the basic premise of exploring an old civilization with few survivors, and while this isn't inherently a problem as I've enjoyed them, this game puts a twist on that. There was still a catastrophic event but many are still alive and trying to survive. I could go on for hours for my praise for this game, but I do wish to address some criticisms I have. The first main criticism I have is with regard to the morphing mechanic. It was a wonderful way to solve puzzles, but I would have loved it if more of the boss fights incorporated this technique. Only two bosses off the top of my head really required you to rely on morphing, which adds to the overall experience. The next criticism I have does go into spoiler territory, so be warned.The Devouts and their overall environment were a lot of fun to explore. The church, the vibe, and especially the music were wonderful. I just wish there was a little more, as I was expecting a sort of gauntlet when meeting their god. Finally, I felt the ending was a bit rushed. Maybe it was because I didn't want it to end, but I was hoping to explore the core a lot more and maybe get some additional lore. Each of the endings was wonderful but felt a little too short with the way they wrapped up. Again, more spoilers in the conclusion.All in all, an excellent game that I'm sad is over. The second ending implies there could be more to come, possibly DLC or even a sequel, tho I'm not really sure how either would work since the game did have definitive endings, but either way, I don't regret buying or playing this game in the slightest!

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to really come up with a big enough word count to make this review more professional sounding, I'm pretty much speechless.So what I  say is that this is a  game. From feels, to mechanics, to sound design, everything about this is amazing. It's blended all of it's inspirations into a fine, hearty soup, but with enough distinction to set itself apart somewhat.After having spent the good last portion of 2 1/2 days playing (20.9 on record because breaks), getting to a 100% completion in-game (with only 5 achievements left to possibly get) as of the publishing of this review, I say this game is a 10/10.Some after-thoughts;Being an indie game that is self-published, the only sad part about the whole thing is that it probably won't get as huge of a following, potentially doomed to the life of a cult classic. Though that isn't a bad thing, and might in turn be better for the developers. Last thing I'd want for them to deal with is a bunch of nonsense contractual obligations for impossible review scores and to get screwed out on royalties. I just hope whatever community has been formed around these devs will at most suggest to them to keep going, because dammit, there needs to be more of  level of quality in games. Additionally, my only complaint is that I wish the ghost town area was completely razed to the ground.  A scorched landscape probably would have been a lot cooler looking and fun to navigate instead of dreary, haunted houses with an equally bleak and depressing color palette. (Obviously it's difficult to make 'Death' seem appealing, and a ghastly area does wonders for setting in that 'Something bad happened here' atmosphere. But boy-oh-boy, magnificent location for story; terrible location for gameplay.) I almost don't recommend 100%'ing just for that place alone. It  worth it in the end though.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was one of my personal favorites! I really loved the artstyle, fluidity, animation, and gameplay in Biomorph. The concept of transforming into the monsters you defeat added a lot of variety to the game. The level design was great, and the main character's design was really cool.The only issue I had with the game was that the story and characters' personalities were rather dull. _childDocuments_.review: This is a good Metroidvania! Cleared it 100%It takes a core from Hollow Knight and adds Kriby's transformations.+ Great visuals+ Good story+ Dialogues are interesting to read+ Multiple well written endings+ 10+ locations to investigate+ Map, that marks important quests and which room you cleared for 100%+ Bosses are fun to fight against, not unique, but fun+ Most people say that transformations are only useful only in one location.I won't dany it for half of them, however some of them are very useful.When you go investigate some unreachable areas, i always recommend picking 1 flying TF and 1 hard hitting TF.With some of them i could bypass some designed restrictions to reach, like i could jump on enemy, transform into flying robot, dash, and now i no longer need to get TF from pre-final location.This is a big thumbs up from me, i adore when devs allow you to break their own rules.- Due to similarity to Hollow Knight, this game unfortunately exaggerates problems from HK.Late side-quests are annoying to do, most of them are escorting item to different chracters in certain order one at a time.... and there are 6 of them for each quest.When i reached 50% completion, i had 15 quests active, because i didnt reach other areas yet. I felt overwhelmed at that point.- Also There are places where you have no idea what you are missing to reach certain areas.It becomes really annoying in second half game, i had to take 2 week break from game.- To add salt to injury, there is a terrible manual marking system for map.You can only use literaly pins of different colors. This is not informative at all, because i have to mark places where i needed a key and places that need certain transformation.Crosscode for example uses same mechanic, but it has icons like chest, cross and arrows, which is far more informative.- Do you remember charms from Hollow Knight, that let you get coins from further distance and heal faster? They are also here.Half of them rely on your certain remaining health percentage, either you should have full HP or low HP.I hate this type of passive abilities in most games, because you have to be perfect at dodging, otherwise your weapon turn into a small fork, enjoy sticking it at enemy to lower his health by 1 hp.+ Other half is good, that does not rely on your health percentage.- Dark souls death system, where you have to collect your coins in the same place where you died.I disliked it in HK as well, because DS was hard enough to squeeze through enemies, so this intense mechanic worked. It doesn't work in metroidvania where you can pass through most enemies.- Dear devs, please add animations which building I upgrade. I am wasting time figuring out which shopper gets new items for sale.Overall, solid 8/10, most downsides are fixable and upsides outshines them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly amazing, I played the demo and fell in love with it instantly and after finishing it 100%, It still holds upIt has some issues that bothered me but it's nothing that can't be fixed but I'll talk about them later, now, the positives:This game is strongest in its gameplay, its main mechanic is unlike any other and is fun to use, the combat can take a bit to get used to but it's also really good, especially with you being ablr to equip 3 diferent combat abilities at a time, it really lets you customize it very much, though some abilities you won't find until kinda late into the game which is a shame as they can't be put to good use Now for the neutral stuff, the game has some very unique and pretty areas but at the same time it has a few that have nothing going on and are really forgettably, mainly the early ones, another thing I feel neutral about is the story, it's good and I enjoyed it really much but it's kinda just surface level, nothing hidden, even in the collectible lore entries don't add much if anything to the world. Another thing this game does kinda good are the controls, the way Harlo controls is very fun, especially with all the abilities unlocked but it can feel kinda junky at times like dashing or attacking cancelling your glide even tho you're still holding the glide button. Also, moving on magnetic surfaces is way too slow as is walking, you get the ability to sprint later in game but it should have been either a part of the starting moveset or a memento plus, it still feels really slow.Lastly, the problems. Biggest problem the game has is talking with NPCs. There's no sound when they speak and the have the same portrait all the time. This makes characters feel shallow and doesn't let you know their personality well.Second problem, the endings. Oh the endings... I won't get into them to avoid spoilers but I'm just gonna say, they're really underwhelming. The ending cutscenes fall flat compared to all other cutscenes in the game which are usually intense or impactful. But not the endings for some reason. Also, what's the deal with the 2nd ending?!?!?!?!! Who in their right mind would actually choose it?!?! It goes against everything the game tells you. The game spends a lot of time portraying this thing as the most evil thing ever and you side with it while also going againts the thing your character has been working towars the entire game. WTF?!?!  The thing I hate the most about this ending is that you have to do it to get all the achievements.Last of the problems is lack of post game content/optional challanges. No boss arena to put all these different abilities to use, no hard mode, no secret bosses, no difficult platforming areas, nothing. There's some collectables that are hidden behind slighty challenging platforming sections but I'm talking about a whole area dedicated to it, a platforming trial.All these issues seem easy to fixand I hope at least some of them will be. this game has a potential to be a 10/10 for me but currently it is only an 8

_childDocuments_.review: It's rough around the edges, but I liked it.  I think more than anything else, it's the world they made.  It's admittedly very subjective, but I thought they did a really good job putting something together that, while sharing a number of traits with others of the genre, carves out its own place.  It feels like it has a history, without necessarily making you read through lines of text to have a sense of what's going on.Game mechanics play into this.  At it's core the game is a metroidvania, but it takes some odd approaches in places.  Some typical upgrade types never show up, while there are some others appear that didn't match what I'm familiar with.  Obstacles are traversed and overcome with a mix of abilities core to the character, monster forms you equip, or monster forms you find in the field, making it an interesting mix of innate upgrades, options equipped to limited slots, and in-field options.  This is built on top of more familiar systems, healing charges that take time to use and refill on dealing damage, and passive abilities that can be swapped out at rest points.  Though your active combat abilities using the same system is more new.Combat is an interesting affair.  The game is arguably melee focused, with for the most part the only unlimited use abilities being melee, the rest (including quick shots, explosives, and some melee options with notably long reach or wide arcs) having charges which are refilled at rest points.  Truth be told I'm not sure they needed them, while a few notably powerful weapons are worth restricting, for the most part it seems like you have too many charges to really risk running out unless things are going particularly badly.  It added a bit of unnecessary anxiety without really changing the tactical situation, I mostly relied on the unlimited melee options anyways.  I think they're generally balanced by windup frames and cooldowns, so it doesn't seem necessary.Most interesting is the creature forms, which are also usable in combat.  One could even go through most of the game playing as a favorite creature.  Each have their own movesets, with abilities and drawbacks.  Conceptually, this is probably my favorite part of the game.  In practice, it was something I had a lot of fun with, I just wish the monster forms were broadly a little more important in combat.  Your regular shape is generally better at fighting, with more customization, smaller size (easier time dodging) and responsiveness, with creature forms tending to be more about clearing obstacles than combat.  They're still great fun to play around with, just not quite everything they could be.It's a running theme almost, of ideas I really like not quite realized to their fullest.  Limited weapon charges, but neither in-field ways to recover them nor enough pressure on them to make the limitation relevant.  Creature forms are used to open up paths to collectibles, but rather than a puzzle or challenge of how to get a given form to where it needs to be it mostly comes down to heading to the nearest save point to shuffle your loadout to add the one or two you need to it.  I did have fun with the platforming challenges presented, there's just a version of the game in my head that makes more use of the game's more unique mechanics.The visuals I really liked, a good mix of colours that make each region feel unique without being inconsistent, and the cartoonish style is used very effectively for some really alien elements and to show horrific history to the place without needing to fall back on conventional gore.The music I wasn't amazed by, but it fits well.Overall, I had a good time with it.  If you're interested in a metroidvania that's experimental and don't mind it being a bit rough around the edges, it's a good pick.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty fun game and certainly worth the price. The transforming into enemies function to solve puzzles in or out of combat is enjoyable. The actual combat? Pretty fun but way too easy. If you want a challenge, you're gonna need to limit your use of chips (charms) and maybe don't upgrade your weapons. Possibly the charm that reduces damage but removes healing might make this game feel more balanced, I never tested it thoughI don't get why there's a limit to how many fast travels you can create (by upgrading save points), when you are very likely to increase that limit way before ever hitting it. It seems kinda like just a totally unnecessary thing. Don't be afraid to spend those fast travel upgradesThe home base customisation is neat. Not complicated or annoying, not very deep, but still cool.I did manage to reach and kill the final boss without getting two abilities - or at the very least I finished it without ever figuring out which two abilities were necessary to solve a few puzzles. There's a lotta map to explore

For me which already finish dozen of metroidvanie there was no challenge but it was still pleasant experience. If you have some free money this game definitly deserves more attention.I hope that devs or some mod add "path of pain" because in this game is so much move options  for masochistic jumping sequence
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very well designed game, the chips (weapons) and mementos (passives) give a wide variety of builds to use.The mechanic that allows you to transform into the enemies you kill is very well implemented in all the areas of the map, you rarely need to morph into an enemy from a previous area to find an item or some plaques (money).The platforming was the most enjoyable part to me, you can clear many paths in a non intended way, since you can use some chips to move around, or even some of the morphs from enemies can allow you to travel through a section of the map where you would need a specific ability to do so.I find that the bosses where the weakest part of the game, since they have few moves and they quickly  become punching bags, i only died on the final boss of the game.The music helps the ambiance of every area you visit, but i didn't find it to be anything revolutionary. It does its work, sometimes becoming more sombre or melancholic at certain areas to set a certain mood on the player.A small complain i have would be that the cinematics that play every now and then for telling certain events of the story feel rather short, sometimes we get a few seconds showing something that might seem rather random, but eventually everything seems to fall in place.There are some parts of the story that aren't explained at all. .Overall its a very entertaining game, i kind of speedran it but i enjoyed all the time that i spent playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: What a ride Biomorph is! I'm writing this review after reaching 100% completion. It does a lot of the good hollow knight/metroid(vania) stuff, with unique areas, powerups that gradually unlock more and more of the map, and a mysterious overarching narrative that slowly unfolds to the player.Where Biomorph has innovated is in the core mechanic of being able to become the creatures that you kill. Each area hosts its own unique creatures, whose abilities enable you to navigate the challenges that are also unique to that area. However, the creatures are not one-off gimicks, and you're able to make use of their strengths as you explore beyond their native zones. Another place where Biomorph shines is in he characters. You are not wandering a deserted world, there are many people who you can run into who have their own stories, and in some cases, quests for you to fulfill. Combat reminds me the most of Ender Lilies, where instead of having a main weapon, you instead are able to equip from a pool of attack techniques. It's a really neat way of allowing people to develop their own play style.Finally, I have to call out the in-game screenshot feature, where if you hold down the right stick it will pin a screenshot of your surroundings to the map for you to review later. Super helpful for figuring out where you can go once you unlock a new ability.Anyways if you like this genre at all, I highly recommend Biomorph.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Biomorph is yet another great Metroidvania with beautiful artwork and character design, precise controls, cool weapons and abilities and a large, well-designed world to explore. This time also with some NPCs, side-quests, upleveling of weapons and gadgets and just the right amount of story and background to discover without outstaying its welcome. But Biomorph is more than that, because it has a stand-out feature which leads to its name: After killing an enemy you can scan its corpse and then morph into its body using all its abilities. Having scanned enough corpses of one enemy type it becomes available to you everywhere and whenever you want – if you have it equipped in one of 3 available slots. This is no small gimmick – each of the creatively designed enemies (I think there are about 30) you can become is as lovingly animated and precisely controlled as your character. There’s a sharklike creature that alone can swim up waterfalls, a sphere-like thingy than can fly for a bit, a huge berserker that can smash stuff no-one else can and many more – some with very unique features I won’t spoil. In essence these enemies provide the abilities to unlock secrets or reach new areas that make a Metroidvania what it is. Or at least they should. Because instead of relying on this brilliant idea and fresh approach to wield abilities the game mostly goes the conventional way of enhancing your character with his own set of special abilities which are in fact far more important for progress than the enemy abilities you “borrow”. What sadly takes the edge out of biomorphing and makes the game much more common than it could have been. Don’t get me wrong, it’s a very good game, it just could have been a lot smarter and more special if all your abilities came from biomorphing (then without the restriction of having to choose 3 types at a save point) and I think it would have been great fun to quickly transform from one weird looking creature to another to perform some of the more complex platforming challenges. But as it is most creature abilities are just required in its own habitat and only a few times outside for some small extra loot. This often is infuriating as you must remember/mark the position, go back to a save point, equip the required creature and return. It’s one of a few poor decisions which don’t enhance the gameplay but rather annoy the player. Nothing is gained by restricting the number of types you can biomorph into but additional backtracking. More freedom is often better. Same goes for weapon selection (again 3 slots) and the necessity to repair found teleportation stations with a limited number of repair kits which must be found first. Let me quickly switch and experiment, let me get around as fast as I want. I also don’t get why only some rooms on the map have more detailed information or why I cannot instantly teleport to any teleport station I found (and repaired) instead of first having to teleport to the last one to then select another. Sadly, the bosses - again with great character designs - are a bit disappointing. If you know how to learn a few patterns you can beat each of them in 1-3 tries (only exception may be the optional final boss). The fights are very similar and not very memorable.On the positive side I really liked how almost every room has at least one secret (or creature to kill and scan) and how the rooms turn golden on the map once you've completed them. It gives a good sense of accomplishment and helps a lot to reach 100%. I also liked the story and the characters you meet and the perfect controls. In the end I was thoroughly entertained for about 30 hours, but the game missed the chance to be outstanding. 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little Metroidvania to fill the time.This game is on the easier side for the most part - bosses have little to no randomness. If you are looking for a super challenge, this game won't give it to you. But, it tries something different and I really liked how it came up with a new mechanic rather than the boring old "find X to progress to Y" rut that most Metroidvanias fall in to. The story is pretty forgettable with typical tropes. I'd say this game is perfect for your kid who is 12 who wants to get into the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Having just 100%'ed the game, I can wholeheartedly say, that it was totally worth it. The only fault of the game's that it's quite short.Don't get fooled by my steam timer, left the game in the background and forgot about it for like, half a day. According to the in-game timer, 100%'ing the game took me a little over 22 hours.And yeah, that's pretty much the only fault of it. The fact it's this short. But then it's priced accordingly, so I guess I can't fault the devs for it either. Hah.But seriously, animation, story segments, movement, skills, artstyle, story, characters, I loved everything here. Game consumed me for the past few days, and I binged it pretty much start to finish.As with a delicious cake, u just wish there was more.Like, legit, go get it. It's amazing. If you loved Hollow Knight or Will of the Wisps, then you'll 100% love Biomorph.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: A well done metroidvania. Fun boss fights, good exploration, decent movement. One small complaint is that sometimes you'll get items or unlock something and its not so clear as to what you actually just did, for instance, I unlocked something to do with the map and I have no idea what exactly changed about the map- this sort of thing happens often, but  other than that I'm having fun with this game
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never 100% a game, but I couldn't not with BIOMORPH! The character writing is incredible, and environment-wise the world feels broad and invites curiosity. The music and sound design fabulous, and the gameplay is engaging: moving between boss combat, platforming, and puzzles.Hallmarks of the genre apply: expect a few deaths, some backtracking and some head scratching. But and excellent experience all round.If you loved Ori and Hollow Knight, you're in for a treat (difficulty sits between them I think)
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: "Hollow Knight mixed with Kirby"That's what the devs were advertising this as when I first saw the game demo'd at PAX in 2023, and it's a fitting description. The inspiration from Hollow Knight is clear - large map, lots of ability progression, tough (though somewhat more forgiving) combat, and always more secrets to go back for.While the inspiration from Kirby, the central 'Biomorph' mechanic, can see like a gimmick at first, it highlights one of the core strengths of the game, the wide variety of player options. In addition to mementos (which function like HK's charms), players can equip 3 different primary weapons and 3 different Biomorph abilities at a time, letting everyone choose a loadout that fits their play style.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: It's good but I think a lot of bloat gets in the way. There's an awful lot of generic and forgettable  NPCs tied to important hub mechanics and functions that it all feels a little unnecessary for a metroidvania. The level design is good for the most part, but can make back tracking quite tedious. Whereas games like Metroid and Hollow Knight eventually give you abilities that allow you to blitz through levels you previously couldn't, it genuinely feels like Biomorph just wanted to keep you forever navigating the platforming sections throughout. This again leads to a feeling of bloat, considering how often you find paths blocked, and you have to manually check other areas for any clue how to progress. Tying actual progression to an Order of Ecclesia-esque morph system is pretty fine, but it also seems kinda shallow. Area gimmicks can mostly be traversed by enemies left intentionally there for that purpose. Certain areas force you to equip the morphs to find secrets or progress. But in the end having to go to a SAFE just to equip the useless monkey morpg to get through one hole to find a secret is kinda meh level mechanics. And as for general play, the Muttler seemed by far the most OP thing to use at least at the midgame. I didn't bother using anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: I just got done 100%-ing this game and I had a blast throughout. The difficulty of this game is somewhat on the easier side (except for the first few bosses as at that point you dont have many abilites and the bosses hit hard), the game does look pretty good, the story and characters are interesting, the rather huge map is well connected and with the abilities and movement options you have it is fun to move throughout it. The Biomorph mechanic (As in, being able to take control of your enemies) also is well fitted into the game, being used for puzzle solving as well as for combat, a few of those also allow for some sequence breaking. The only minor issue I have with this game is the neccesary currency you need to upgrade your chips (weapons) and mementos (passive abilities), though in a normal playthrough this will likely not be a problem, but if you go for 100% you will likely have to grind a bitBut all in all this is a 10/10 game, which is on par with the big name Metroidvanias like Ori, Hollow Knight and Blasphemous
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Let it be 3.5 outta 5, here's why:- Art/Animation definitely received lots of luv during development- While playing 1.2.26470 I've met no game breaking bugs, just one or two camera glitches. - (it's weird personal one) Game plays noice with a keyboard and takes advantage of additional buttons.BUT morphing mechanic is simultaneously cool and kinda problematic:Good: It's fun to discover new monsters, gets ya kinda excited about what you could do.Bad: Even though there are many monsters, only 2-3 are worth coming back to, rest are highly specialized and are pretty much useless outside their habitat.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished getting 100% - I really enjoyed the game. Ambience, music and art are key to a good metroidvania and this one sure delivers. The gameplay is also fun, tight and full of different abilities. Being able to transform into any single monster in the game is also a pretty cool mechanic that I had not seen before. Each biome has unique mechanics, enemies and a distinct visual signature. I love the rooms getting a golden border when you have found every secret, it makes getting 100% very achievable without having to resort to guides.My only minor complain is that I wish there was a hard setting. Not that the default difficulty is too easy but this is the kind of game that benefits from a tougher challenge.Absolutely recommend !
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Really excellent game.  It is beautiful, the game-play is excellent and it provided enough challenge for my tastes without being frustrating.  The biomorph system could have been more useful in combat but the main character offers plenty of combat customization in chips and mementos.  It is a bit short, but I will certainly play through again.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty nice game with fun gimick. Shame they didn't fully comit into that morph ability and gave too much offensive abilities to main character form, making others form feel more like key-to-door usage, rather then being usefull both in combat and exploration.Story also weak, but this is more case of fun gameplay over story.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, I had a blast with it!The only downside I could find is enemy contact damage, but it's nothing serious and does not ruin the overall experience.That said, Biomorph is a truly fun metroidvania with an interesting concept. Reading other's reviews it seems to me that many miss the point of biomoprhing; it's not something which is supposed to be useful in battle, but rather an alternative way to give the player power-ups. I'd recommend this title to any metroidvania fan, it'd be a shame to miss it.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a fun metroidvania with some cool ideas. It started off a bit slow for me, but once you start getting access to actual customization it really opened up. You can "equip" up to three transformations that come with their own attacks and abilites and three default form attacks, and then stat modifiers with more options becoming available over time. I really enjoyed one of the first monsters you can acquire which shoots a boomerang ball weapon. They really nailed the aesthetic (feels like a scifi Hollowknight / Ori). It wasn't until I got past the first section that I realized just how big the map is (originally I felt it was quite small).There are some minor gripes as well. The map's lack of details can be frustrating. Sometimes one "room" might have multiple levels, but you can only access those parts by entering from a different room (there's literally a ceiling) which made it confusing. For completionists, the map only tells you if you cleared out a room so you have no idea what you're still missing.And there is a ton of backtracking once you get to an obstacle and realize you need to equip a different transformation. I understand why they don't want you to be able to swap into all of them on the fly, but it was a little annoying getting somewhere only to realize I would have to go back several rooms to equip something different.Some of the monster transformations had very limited use case, which was disappointing. Many of the transformations were only useful for one particular obstacle in one small part of the map.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Best metroidvania I've seen since Hollow Knight.  Solid mechanics and good modern quality of life features that HK was sorely lacking.  Nice lore, as well.  Devs have been extremely responsive to player feedback, adding even more quality of life and in particular offering a lot of behind-the-scenes support for the nascent speedrunning community.  On that topic, this is shaping up to be an excellent speed game, as the morphs add a ton of movement and combat options.  The game is not super difficult if you get all the upgrades (so you're not forced to learn morph combat at all), but once you're optimizing for low loadout play (like a speedrun), you really get to explore what the various tools give you.  My Steam hours played are a bit misleading, since I'm mostly a tooling developer for the speedrunning scene, but I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun Metroidvania that flows pretty well. The biomes feel different from each other , with unique enemies and different platforming required to fully clear the maps. The story is fun and easy to follow, though not very surprising. The combat is flowy and enjoyable, but not particularly challenging . I actually didn't have any problems with the late game traversal, there are enough fast travel points that you're never too far away from a room you want to go back to when you're completing collections at the end.  I'm not a very fast player in any way and managed to fully clear the map in 27 hours so the game is not that long (which I count as a plus). Definitely recommended
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Biomorph is a very large game that packs a ton in. In checks every modern Metroidvania box- abilities, badges, secrets, lots of biomes, solid boss fights? etc etc. But it also incorporates enemy morphing (thus the namesake), quests, and a very polished art style.I liked it a lot, but I wouldn’t say it skyrocketed to an absolute favorite. The platforming felt a bit easy and underwhelming. It doesn’t a very strong atmosphere or unique identity. Sometimes, the game could drag.But I still wouldn’t hesitate to recommend it. It clearly had a ton of effort and love put into it, and altogether is an impressive package. I would put it right at the B- tier for me!
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome, no question. The movement feels good, the enemies are varied, the abilities are cool, the progression and quests are worth doing, and the art style and atmosphere are great. Highly recommended. My only nitpick, and this is purely personal, is that the game tends to be a bit too easy especially with the bosses. I think every boss I fought was well designed, and none of their attacks were annoying, but I was able to first try most of them without much difficulty and I wouldn't say i'm a skilled player. Tbh, I do think this game would GREATLY benefit from a hard mode and it wouldn't take too many tweaks. Even simple changes like only getting more recovery from killing enemies and not just hitting them, making it impossible to get more health during boss fights, making some normal mobs a bit stronger, giving bosses more hp but also maybe a third phase with one or two more attacks. These kind of things alone would be great, even make it a slider option with custom difficulty. Overall, everything else felt basically perfect, fast travel points are plentiful and traversal is never frustrating. The game doesn't really do a single thing wrong, it's just a tad easy and that's more a personal preference than a criticism.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Liked the overall game. It took me around 18 hours to complete most of the content.Here are some things I didn't like or would like to see improved:1.Morphing into other creatures is fun, but later-game creatures are a bit boring. (Maybe a creature that turns invisible to assassinate enemies would be cool. It could be integrated with your combos and have a longer cooldown.)2.I wish there was a button to toggle all interactable NPCs on the map. Traversing the map takes time, and not knowing where they are can be annoying. Alternatively, offering the option to purchase a completion compass (introduced later in the game) would be helpful for players searching for remaining items in stages.3.Adding a new ability to increase running speed later in the game would be nice so I wouldn't have to rely on constantly dashing. (I heard this might be included in patch 1, but unfortunately, I finished the game before it arrived.)4.The mid-to-late game bosses could use more variation. I was hoping to fight some human-like bosses alongside large monsters, or even a combination of both. Unfortunately, this wasn't the case.5. For your next game, consider making creatures visually blend in better with their environments. Additionally, it would be great to see abilities used more naturally by the creatures. Many biomorphs currently only serve a one-time puzzle-solving purpose, which feels like a missed opportunity
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Very reminiscent of Hollow Knight - and I mean that entirely as a compliment. It's got some pretty standard metroidvania stuff that you've come to expect but executes it all quite well. Then it adds just enough in terms of unique aspects (the morphing into enemies, namely) to differentiate it. Everything it does is competent - it does not reinvent the genre, but it's a stellar contribution to it.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Alot of Backtracking for some quest and puzzle related to the biomorph transfomations to complete the puzzle, but still had a amazing time playing this superbe metroidvania from a Quebec Studio, that I had the chance to play the demo early over a year ago during the Carravan Event in Chicoutimi.Id give it a note of 7.5 / 10 :)
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that gets you hooked pretty easily! This was my latest addiction and I decided to write a review even though I still got some tasks left in game.The gameplay is amazing and I barely had any issues,Especially LOVE the designs of the creatures and stargatos, I hope I'll find them all :3 ,I catch myself whistling along some of the tunes, Love the puns,an overall 8.7/10 for me :)Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Very good combat-focused metroidvania.  Strong hollow knight vibes.  Took 25 hrs to 100%, but i'm slow - Some of the cats were hard to find :/Great sprites/environments, tight controls.  If i'm being nitpicky, it could've  been just slightly harder.  Difficulty seemed a tad uneven.  The 'true' final boss was less of a challenge than some earlier bosses - maybe scaling could be tweaked, or maybe my build was broken, idk.  This really isn't a huge gripe - i'm struggling to think of anything that really bugged me, but coming up with nothing, so I guess it's a pretty great game then :P
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! This is definitely one of my favorite Metroidvanias, up there with Prince of Persia and Hollow Knight. While I wasn't that crazy into the narrative the gameplay was incredibly fun and like Prince of Persia I found myself using every mechanic through the games run time. If you're a fan of the genre this is a definite buy.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game worth waiting 4 years for! My only complaint is that the game was slightly too easy; all the bosses took me at most 5 attempts to beat. However, the platforming is enjoyable, it's nice to find secrets, and the biomorphing mechanic is very well-used during exploration and boss fights. 9.5/10UPDATED ON MAY 22ND 2024:Game updates have added more options based on people's feedback:-You can now teleport to your last save point FROM THE PAUSE MENU, so there's no need for backtracking (there go half of the negative reviews)- Accessibility options, like being able to reduce the damage that enemies do, or increasing your damage output (no more complaints about enemies being sponges or your character being underpowered)- I'm sure there's plenty of other things, I don't have time to read every patch noteIf I have one complaint, it's that the game felt a bit too easy at times. First off, I don't think I ever died to a boss (except final and true final bosses) more than 3 times before I beat them. That may be a good thing for some people, and personally it gave me a relaxing experience, but it also led to the game being a bit too easy. I would like it if the game had more difficulty levels or NG+.Expanding on what I said about the game being too short: it literally took me 18 hours to get every achievement for this game. Now, I play a lot of metroidvanias, but I didn't expect to find every single thing in the game in under 20 hours. I did get the game for $18 during launch sale, so that's a ratio of $1: 1 hour of playtime.There is one other thing I can agree with on the negative reviews: the Biomorphs could be SO MUCH MORE. Truly I love the idea of biomorphing for traversal purposes, but they really suck in combat, besides a few (Roltys, the late game area guy with the gun, village ghost). Also, their movesets are really good-looking when you're fighting the enemy, but then you turn into the enemy and suddenly you're too slow to do anything. It's like a "Boss vs. Boss as a playable character" kind of thing.TL,DR: As someone who played this game on day 1, I can say it has vastly improved since then. More accessibility, QoL features, glitch fixes, and all the other good stuff has happened since then. I love the story and the art style; when I read a negative review about finding it hard to bond with Harlo, I can get that. Honestly I think it's more of an Ori thing where you're not really trying to feel the same way they do, but rather just imagine how you'd feel in their scenario. Still love the art and the area design, those things DO remind me of Hollow Knight. (Also, quick tip: Roltys (did I spell that right?) gets I-frames on its dash, so if you have trouble with an enemy/boss just get that morph and dash through it until it dies.)Still a 9.5/10 and PLEASE MAKE A FREE DLC, I need more of this game <3
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: A Straight forward Metroidvania which is not too hard but also not too easy also, beautiful design of the characters and the world, it is very polished, and I have not faced any game breaking bugs.- Nice variety of weapons, skills and settings.- Music is decent, nothing too memorable for me tho.- Easy to manage completion due to marked rooms, similar to games like Ender Lillies.- Short but well-made cutscenes that tell the story well without dialogue, while in-game dialogue with NPC's and Lore are well written.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Only a small portion of the way through this game but I'm already obsessed.  Loving the character and world design, feels well balanced, and even though they suggest a controller, this maps onto my keyboard well.  If you were a fan of the gritty mystery of hollow knight but found it too difficult, AND you want some steampunk alien vibes, this is the game for you.  PLUS the free demo has loads of content in it, which gave me a good sense of the vibes, and was ultimately why I decided to buy the game.  The mechanic of transforming into the enemies you find along the way makes the mundane combat of any given room feel meaningful, especially when the enemies then come back stronger.  My only gripe is it is sometimes hard to tell your bio morphed character from the monster you are fighting if its of the same type.  Overall though, I'm having lots of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best platform/metroidvania type games I have ever played.  To some people this may not matter, but the game does come with ultrawide support which looks great on this type of game.  All of the hand drawn animations and small puzzles are pretty cool.  This is the best platforming game that I have played since Ori - Will of the Wisps.  I hold that game in pretty high regard as I have played through it free on game pass and liked it so much I bought on Steam.  Anyway just do yourself a favor and at least play the demo - it took me less than 5 minutes to decide I was going to purchase.  Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: Biomorph is a great new metroidvania with wonderful art and music, a good collection of unique areas/enemies and a great overall feel to the game. I've played a lot of modern metroidvanias and this one is definitely one of my favorites!The core mechanic of "biomorphing" - optionally temporarily transforming into your enemies after you defeat them - is very well done and resulted in a ton of really interesting and unique enemies both to defeat and to play as. It makes exploration extremely fun and rewarding, as you know with each new area you'll have new enemies to learn about, and then be able to put their abilities to use.I'd definitely recommend this game to any metroidvania fan, it feels great to play, and exploration especially is a real high point between the biomorphing and the solid quest system. Reaching 100% in this game was a lot of fun, with nothing too difficult or laborious to do, and instead including a lot of wonderful cat descriptions. Try it out if you're on the fence!
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: BIOMORPH is a fantastic addition to any metroidvania gamer's collection. The game's captivating world is an absolute joy to explore, brimming with secrets and surprises around every corner. The gameplay is tight and responsive, with the ability to transform into a variety of unique creatures adding a delightful layer of diversity to the experience. Remarkable visuals, with a level of detail that draws you deeper into the fantastical world, along with polished animations and an immersive soundtrack, further elevate the experience. For metroidvania fans, this is a must-play adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMORPH

_childDocuments_.review: The main mechanic of morphing into your enemies is a clever addition to a metroidvania. Being able to take control of enemies changes combat, traversal and exploration in very significant ways. Once you've found enough enemies of a type, you get the ability to transform into them anytime which lets you solve a lot of the challenges in creative ways. ✨The game is pretty big, I was surprised! The minimap is also very well made, making it very satisfying to 100% zones and leaving markers to come back to with new powers & Monster abilties.

The morphing mechanic is super intuitive and offers a wide variety of new game mechanics. Kudos for the attention to detail. name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos
detailed_description: ZENO EDITION About the Game You play as Pseudo, a master of martial arts who lives as a recluse in the strange land of Zenozoik. When you cross paths with the Boy, a small creature whose mysterious powers have attracted the attention of Gemini, the Mistress of the Artifacts, you decide to protect him, unaware that much greater forces are involved. EXPLORE ZENOZOIK Drawing upon both surreal and punk fantasy influences, the world and civilisations of Zenozoik are brimming with fascinating characters, creatures and landscapes. Roam this intriguing land and discover its paths, inhabitants and ancient secrets. CRUSH YOUR OPPONENTS Your fists and speed are your greatest weapons. Attack, dodge, stun, block, counter a parry to land a special attack, switch to first-person view to perform unique techniques: each time, it's up to you to seize the occasion to achieve victory and avoid mistakes that could quickly prove fatal. CUSTOMISE YOUR COMBAT STYLE Learn various martial arts during your adventure and alternate freely between them based on the situation, types of enemies and your preference. Victories will enable you to improve your characteristics and upgrade your attacks, so you can develop your own unique style. RISE TO THE CHALLENGE OF THE RITUAL Before fighting, you can challenge your opponent to a game of dice, with the winner defining the rules of the encounter – often to their advantage. Summoning a monster as an ally, covering the area in fog, having shackles limit movement… far from determining the outcome of the combat, the Ritual represents an opportunity to exploit if you win it or a challenge to cleverly overcome if you lose. A RICH STORYLINE Your search for the Great Artifacts that will help you defeat Gemini will take you farther than you ever imagined. While taking on the mercenaries pursuing you and developing your friendship with the Boy, you must confront your past and delve into the sources of the chaotic society of Zenozoik. Clash: Artifacts of Chaos takes place in the same universe as Zeno Clash and Zeno Clash II, but the game is entirely independent.
