_childDocuments_.review: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is an action game with some souls-like elements.  You play as Pseudo, who meets a helpless character named The Boy in the intro, and decides to protect him.  It is set in the same universe as Zeno Clash & Zeno Clash 2, but was designed to make sense without playing either of those games.The gameplay is satisfying, though with some minor flaws that might make it frustrating.1) To start with, this game has RPG elements, so you need to level your character to keep up with the fights.  The numbers that are used in the stats are a mostly smooth experience, with tangible (though small) boosts with the points spent.  The only problem was that in the early game I felt I did so little damage to the enemies, I spent nearly all of the points in boosting damage until the fights didn’t feel like a slog.  Then I had to boost the other stats so I actually had some defence in the fights.  Though with the updated patch that came out after I started the game, they do make it more clear in the tutorial that the parry increases your damage, so I might have relied upon that more in the early game if I had known about it.2) You can perform a dodge or parry after an attack animation is complete, but not during.  The problem is your standard attacks can take longer than an enemy takes to start and finish one of their attacks. This would suggest you should play reactively and not aggressively, but you do not do enough damage to play defensively all the time.  As a result, tanking attacks seems optimal, but you can take a lot of damage quite quickly, especially in the early parts of the game.  This problem seems unlikely to be resolved, as it would change the combat system at its core to do so.3) The stances you get early will be your stances for the rest of the game.  You can upgrade your stances using figurines you find in the environment, except you need to level up your beginning stances to do any actual damage, then you won’t find enough to really level up stances you find later.4) The giant enemies are a bit of a problem, it is possible to cheese them by getting close and being too close for some of their attack animations, but you do too little damage to them to play defensively like you are probably meant to.5) There are quite a few fights in the game where you fight one bigger enemy and a few smaller enemies.  Maybe three of those fights have the problem of the little enemies constantly hide behind the bigger enemy, so no amount manoeuvring around will single an enemy out.  These fights were quite annoying as a result.6) Battle spaces are usual spacious, however in some fights you can get caught on the scenery (and not realise it until you are trapped there).EDIT:Playing some more of the endgame content, the parry is very powerful in terms of boosting your damage for a few seconds after a successful parry.  The parries seem relatively forgiving in terms of timing, and do allow you to play defensively (addressing issue 4 above), and I presume would make the early game easier (addressing issue 1).  I feel the parries make the game easier as a result.These aren’t flaws but they may not be clear from the promotional material1) As a souls-like, you spend a lot of time walking around trying to find the path forward.  The areas are dense, and you need a good sense of direction to navigate this complex labyrinth.  To make it more complicated, sometimes you need to turn into night-time Pseudo to open the path for day Pseudo.  Often, this game felt like an exploration game with a bit of fighting.2) Crafting is a part of this game, and that means finding things in the complex environment.  Most of the time it is tricky to tell if you can pick something up without walking up to it and seeing if the button prompt appears.  Probably half of the things you can craft don’t matter, but the other half will help you become more powerful and you’ll probably need.3) The game only auto-saves around campfires, which are not that frequent.  It made it difficult to play this game in short bursts, and may be frustrating to play if you often get pulled away by real life.4) If you die as day-time Pseudo, you have chance to return and win the fight with night-time Pseudo.  If you lose as night-time Pseudo, it’s game over.Difficulty is a tricky thing to talk about, so I can’t really give any concrete comparison guides as to how hard this game is.  The community for when this game first came out as mostly people who played Zeno Clash 1+2, and some found this game too difficult compared to the previous games, and some found it easier.  Personally, I found it a bit easier.  The RPG elements can mean that you can go elsewhere to try and level your character up for a fight if you want, or to trade materials for weapons.  Unfortunately, there is one tough boss fight in this game that blocks you into the fight, so you can’t really do other things once that event is triggered.  It is a serious oversight from the developers, and I hope they do something about it.  Additionally, this game, unlike the Zeno Clashes, has no difficulty setting.  You can only play the game on one difficulty.  Crafting can be used to make more potent healing potions, or weapons, which can mitigate the difficulty if needed.The story was one of the best parts of Zeno Clash 1+2, but it is sorely lacking here.  After an interesting introductory section that goes for perhaps 2 hours (most of which is gameplay), there is maybe three cutscenes of any interest before the end of the game.  While the story does end up having some interesting concepts, it prefers to keep most things a mystery, as opposed to the detailed thoroughness of the previous games.  I know having vague mysteries where each audience member can just invent the story they like is the popular thing to do, but I hoped for better after the interesting intricacies of the previous games.  Most of the dialogue you hear is just incidental dialogue between the two main characters, and while it does show them bonding, it just isn’t very interesting.  There is some dialogue between Pseudo and his opponents before most of the key fights, but it’s mostly just generic trash talk.One thing that really bothered me was how much nearly everybody sounded like a regular person, as opposed to the sort-of broken & primitive lexicon, yet still clever dialogue of the previous games.  The voice acting for the non-main characters is similar to the previous games, with strange voices and inflections used to define the character.  But when everybody speaks Contemporary English, it just sounds like the voice actors making funny voices.  The dialogue written for Pseudo also makes him like one those flippant, smartass heroes, which leads him to not caring at all about the bigger picture of the story, and on multiple occasions, talks over or walks away from the more interesting parts of the story.I understand that Zeno Clash 2 contained most of the details of the story for the first two Zeno Clashes, so it is possible that this game was designed to lead straight into a sequel.  I would accept the mysteries introduced in this game if that were the case.  But by itself, the story was a disappointment.With the other technical specs of the game, everything visual is an absolute feast, just like every other ACE Team game.  I don’t know what the visual designers get paid, but I am convinced it is not enough.  The music is also incredible, having that staple ACE Team greatness, while still having its own identity to differentiate it from the Zeno Clashes.I really enjoyed playing the game.  With everything but the story being top-notch, I can highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Absolutely Phenomenal game! So good that I even bought it for my friends so they could experience it too plus to support the devs! 9/10 for me. This is coming from someone who has not played the Zeno Clash games, though that is something I'll have to change!Pros: - Very tight, punchy combat. I love how your different attacks flow into each other, and there wasn't a style or weapon I didn't think had some use.- Heartfelt story. I was not expecting the story to be a strong point going in. After experience in other souls games I was expecting it to be vague, but it is anything but! The writing was engaging and was even more enhanced by the phenomenal voice acting.- Exploration. The world has so much for you to find both at day and night. While the game completely lacks fast travel, the world is small and dense with content compared to other open worlds, which makes it satisfying to explore without things grating. - Art Direction. This was probably what first sold me into giving this a shot. Everyone looks so weird and wacky in a really charming way, that's the obvious point. However, every nook and cranny in the world is also fleshed out ranging from the craggly mountains to the worn, lived-in villages. There's just so much to appreciate.- Music. Dear god I don't think I've listened to a soundtrack as consistently amazing as this in a long, long time. From the somber melodies to the upbeat action music. When I found out this soundtrack was on ITunes, it was a guarenteed buy for me.Cons: - Slight Jank. This was rare, but there were occasionally points I encountered some jank in combat.- Relatively short length. I think you can beat the story in only a few hours, especially if you rush past all the exploration. While there is a NG+ that was added post-launch, I would have enjoyed a few more hours, especially for the price point. That being said, I very much enjoyed every one of those hours I put in.Overall, I recommend this game to anyone looking for a shorter game to try out, especially if you're a fan of soulslikes or are just looking for a good story to grip you! I'm very much looking forwards to a follow-up and until then will be satiating my hunger with the Zeno Clash Games!

_childDocuments_.review: Clash is a weird, ugly, beautiful game! It looks WILD, the voice acting is (almost without exception) superb, and the combat feels great.That said, I did almost quit the game a couple of times in the opening few hours -- it's just so hard to navigate at first. The game world mostly made up of series of interconnected corridors, and getting from point A to point B can often be a very different experience than from B to A. There is also no fast travel, which the devs have said was an explicit design choice. Interestingly, as someone who gets lost very easily in games, I found it happening less frequently as the game progressed. There was an adjustment period for sure, but after a good dozen or so hours I was able to follow the flow of the corridors a lot better. After nearly 22 hours I am so happy that I stuck with it, and am hoping for a sequel. Pseudo and The Boy are such loveable characters.Hopefully we can get another game in this universe someday!

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent game. A hidden gem I did not expect to find. However I do not agree it is soul-like. Imo it is nothing like Dark Souls. It is its own unique gamePros:- Great story-telling- Abstract world full of unique lore- Great graphics and performance on Steam Deck- The game will keep you interested and occupied from beginning to the very end- Interesting day/night mechanics with 2 different worlds to explore- A lot of secrets you really want to find- Great map building- Unique and excellent music that made me want to download the soundtrack (does not happen very often in fact I think it is the first time it happened to me with a game)- No grindCons:- Really no point in going to NG+ after you acquired all achievements. The game was already easy so I imagine if you are going to NG+ with all these levels it will be walk in the park- Too easy - after you gain few levels and learn how the fighting works (pick your best style) most of the fights are becoming trivial. I think I became too OP maybe because I was putting all points in resistance and not damage. So by the end no bosses were a challange to me. I beat the final boss on my second try. And the one before that on my 1st.Definitely try out 10/10. An unique experience!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin. Genuinely.Literally, I beat this game within the last 5 minutes, and I still feel speechless; and I'm struggling to articulate why.I have been in a gaming rut for about a year now. Most games that release just seem to be empty, soulless, unfinished, greedy, boring, or any combination of the above. I didn't think Clash: Artifacts of Chaos would be the game to hold my attention, completely, from start to finish. But it did.See, I first came across this game from a YouTuber called IronPineapple. He reviewed Clash as an early access title, and gave it a tentative thumbs up. Though, I had completely forgotten about that review until a few weeks ago when I randomly saw this game pop up on the steam store. I honestly felt like I had nothing to lose at this point ...considering I was struggling to find anything else entertaining at that time; and I reminded myself that I could always attempt a refund if I wasn't thrilled with the game.Expecting to be once again bored, I booted up Clash and was met with ...a pretty ugly character in a pretty 'interesting' world (The stylistic art design took some getting used to, I'll admit.)Not immediately impressed, I decided to push on for another hour. "Just one hour, and I'll probably refund.", I thought.Nope.Hour after hour I found myself enjoying the game more and more. I was hooked....and before I knew it, I felt more connected to this world than any other gaming world I'd stepped into over the previous year....and I still can't articulate exactly why.Sure, the aforementioned positives are as genuine as I can proclaim, though Clash still has it's flaws.But in a strange way,  of these flaws added to the game's charm; Traversal became a fun memory and spatial awareness exercise. Combat became a chance to hone my reaction time. Potion recipes, artefacts, stats, and the ritual all became fun examples of trial, error, and adaptation. Eventually the game made sense, and all within a reasonable amount of time too.In essence, I didn't feel like Clash held my hand. And I think that's what won me over at the end of the day; I'm a 36 year old gamer, and it felt genuinely good to just sit down and play a game that I had to figure out. I had to improve myself, learn, and become better. And in this way, I overcame the challenge.By the end of the story, I felt invested in the relationship between Pseudo and the Boy, even though their dialogue are actually kept to a minimum.I had some struggles, some smiles, some genuine heartfelt moments, and even some honest laughs at some of the character interactions.If you go into the game with an open mind (it is made by an indie team), and give it the old college try, I don't think you'll be disappointed.There's a lot of good things in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Very much a hidden gem of a game, it is a souls-esk game with semi open world, and a heavy focus on combat and narrative.Gameplay, involves exploration as your progress the story, combat is great with a multitude of martial arts and special moves that you have to upgrade as acquire new sets of armor, though combos did get a little stale at the end, but that's expected after learning everything if your a thorough observer. In the game you will also have two bodies your eatheral body in night time and corporeal body in day time, both day and night have different things you must explore and find secrets. The dice system is very unique, as you approach beings you can challenge them to the "One Rule" where you can put aliments on ememies if you win a game of dice, besides that there's also a light ver. of potion making.The graphics are one of a kind mixing cell-shade with comic like etching i honestly haven't seen it done this way before personally, very pleasant on the eyes.Music was very on theme and was well made, the last part really got me emotional.Story? i wouldn't say it's the most complex out there, but really it doesn't have to if it's well done, and man it is for sure a treat. What caught me off guard is this is actually a prequel to the OLD Zeno clash games, i was surprise to find out they were related and definitely gonna be playing them again for that reason.Setting is very weird, it gave me a lot of odd world vibes which was awesome.Conclusion? if you wanna emerse your self in a beautiful yet weird world full of combat, story development and dice rolling then it's a must play.Happy Hunting ^v^

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of this developer and loved the previous two Zeno Clash games. This is the weakest entry in the series, despite the obviously bigger budget and more modernized game design. I'm hardly a luddite and appreciate the care the developer has taken to update their sensibilities, but in this case they've lost more than they've gained IMO.Combat never really clicked. Feedback is low both from incoming and outgoing hits, it's very easy to get knocked out of your combo, and flowing between offense and defense is difficult. Even when you do well in battle and parry, dodge, and strike your way to unlocking the (very fun) first-person punching, it completely ignores the rest of the systems that the game spends so much time teaching and improving: your stances, weapons, and special moves don't have any bearing on it. There's neither the sense of engagement than the previous games had, nor a deep and interesting new combat system to replace it.The shift to third person really disconnects from the visceral combat and the detailed world. Looking enemies in the eyes, bobbing around their firsts, and getting up close to all the weird little structures and people in Zenozoik was a huge part of the charm of the first games, and it just doesn't hit right in third person. It was very easy to get lost or betrayed by the camera in the twisting canyons and tunnels, and miss landmarks in a way that wouldn't have happened in first person.For as much gameplay and narrative space as the Ritual takes up, its presence felt vestigial to the rest of the experience. It's possible to entirely ignore the mechanic and just get by on your fists, without needing to risk drinking poison or getting tied up. I really wanted to enjoy this mechanic (I'm a board game maker IRL and playing a little board game before fighting for a boost is conceptually perfect for me), but it was just not satisfying to interact with.I'm still looking forward to supporting the devs and this series in the future, and I applaud them for trying to make a different game with this new entry. I just don't feel like it's a better game for it.

_childDocuments_.review: ACE Team has done it again. Returning to Zenozoik, the world from the games that put them on the map, they've put together another banger. It's a weird, sincere tale of incredibly punchable people and animals being punched really really hard to protect the things that are important to you. As with the Zeno Clash games it has that great tone of being chock full of the ugliest, most alarming stuff you've ever seen in your life but for the inhabitants of this world it's just another Tuesday. The plot is a well-executed Lone Wolf and Cub style tale that just happens to be awash in ACE Teams incredibly strong art direction and character design. The gameplay evolves the Zeno Clash format into a kind of open world brawler, with some neat new elements like camp fire potion mixing, a pre-fight dice game that adds modifiers to each fight and a haunted night time alternate vision of the world. It even has some pretty crazy lore for the people like me who are invested in the setting. Play it! Go ACE Team!

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really enjoyed my time with this game. I've grown to love how ACE Team presents their games' weirdness as completely normal within the universes they create.The combat was satisfying, the story with Pseudo and the Boy was fulfilling and somber.My only complaint is that I wish there was a fast-travel at times, but this might've taken away from the exploration and bonding aspect between the characters. _childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to Zeno Clash. In fact, I found myself actually enjoying it more than Zeno Clash, which surprised me.The world design is absolutely beautiful. Every single area in the game looks like something out of this world, and I never found myself growing tired of the scenery.Combat is pretty standard, punch things and dodge when the enemy attacks, nothing really mindblowing. I found it good enough to keep me entertained, but it's not very deep. There's different combat stances and special attacks you can choose from, but ultimately fights still will boil down to simply mashing attack then dodging away once the enemy is about to attack.I'll note, don't spend your Lv3/Lv4 stance upgrade figurines until near the end. In my playthrough, I was only able to max 2 of my stances (and got a bunch of stuff to mid level), and ended up in an awkward situation where I unlocked some stances I wanted to use near the end of the game but was unable to upgrade them. I wish there was some way to respec so that there's more room for experimentation.My playthrough took me 17 hours. Could probably be beaten in 10-12 hours, since I spent a lot of time backtracking through the map to search every nook and cranny for collectibles.Overall a solid recommend, definitely worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I want this game to be good because I like this developer and I think this project had heart put into it, but fact is that it doesn't feel finished. The game takes the already strange and divisive combat of Zeno Clash (which I liked) and sets it in an "open world" (what looks like open space but is actually corridors and invisible walls) which just chews up time. I could see someone really enjoying this game if they liked the combat system and could tolerate the jankiness, but that is going to be a very particular person.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid brawler with incredible art direction, fun level design, and a heartfelt story with a character lead and sidekick. My biggest gripes with the game came with its map, it's far too opaque where the zone borders are, which can make progression and even backtracking more annoying that it needed to be. The parry is fun to master, and the game offers plenty of combat styles and super moves to play with. Some boss fights can be quite tough, which was neat b/c those were the only moments I felt like I really needed to master the parry system. I enjoyed exploring the levels, buying new armor, and the general progression. I do kinda wish the combat had more edge with blood or some effects like that. The game doesn't outstay its welcome either, it's a solid sub-10 hour experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Weirdly weird little gem. Exploration is very fun, and starting with a linear level design only for it to interconnect and back-loop so that at the end of the game you finish with a quasi-open-world was unexpected and quite reminiscent of Dark Souls 1 's map design.Combat takes some time to get used to and for me never exceeded to be merely serviceable. Having played soulslike games before definitely helped getting into it, although the core combat is quite different from them.The story was ... there, and despite of immaculate voice acting and an abundance of cutscenes, I couldn't recite it save for the basics and the general gist of it. But that might be due to the fact that the developers tried to be as weird with the world building as with the art design. Speaking of which, the distinct art style and oddball characters was what initially drove me to Clash, but I must confess that it always felt short from being truly bizarre, only managing to be mildly peculiar and most times even familiar.Music is top-notch and fitting for the odd setting.And although I mentioned Dark Souls before, Clash is far from being a soulslike and for itself a unique experience, which might be the strongest reason for me to recommend it.Yes, it's clunky at times, the gameplay is not as innovative or as engaging to justify the runtime, and it maybe overstays its welcome a bit timewise, but as a whole package it surly is one of a kind and worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a sequel to Zeno Clash 2 for almost a decade, the world of Zenozoik is fascinating and beautiful. This game is more than anything I expected. _childDocuments_.review: Just astounding. As a AA game this is punching so far above its weight, it's genuinely unbelievable. Haven't written a review in a long time but I seriously hope this game becomes the next indie darling because it's an absolute masterpiece. A true testament to the unique power of video games to provide an otherworldly experience. I wish more video games were this bold. PROS:Outstanding SoundtrackCompletely unique world and visual styleVery well optimizedGenuinely great story with ridiculously charming characters and voice actingNuanced gameplay with a lot of subtle hidden mechanicsRewarding explorationOld school style map design, pretty complex and creative with lots of organic in-world navigation toolsReally weird and neat death/night mechanic which in effect gives the entire worldspace 2 layersLots of weird ♥♥♥♥ that just makes you go "what"CONSMinor bugs here and there, nothing game breaking or unusualIt's too goodI'm kind of obsessed with it nowSeriously this game rules buy itIt took about 5 minutes for this game to totally capture me; the world, the soundtrack, the characters, all of it. This game gets right what so many AAA titles just get completely wrong. Genuinely one of the best voice acted games I've played recently and that's in no small part due to a script that isn't annoying as hell and is charming and clever with nearly every line. No pointless chitchat from obnoxious characters, almost every conversation is a delight.Some people might be turned off by the combat, it looks like a souls game but plays more like a fighting game as stringing together 6 attacks using animation cancelling to pump out damage as quickly as possible is how you bring down the tough enemies. If you're worried about it being too hard or frustrating I'd recommend just pumping defensive stats early on and looking up some guides. This game is definitely more on the Hard side with no difficulty options, but as per usual with souls type games you set your own difficulty, level Constitution and Endurance first. I don't really know how else to convince you to buy this other than to say that every once in a while you get something that restores your faith in video games. Modern AAA games are so bad so often and sometimes I just wonder why I bother. This is why. It's $30 without a sale, come on, it's a no-brainer. Buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: As I get older there are fewer and fewer games that genuinely excite me when I hear about them and play them. This game is a rare exception: It is so full of heart, and the world so full of utterly bizarre character (and characters), that it is a pleasure to experience. this takes place in the same world as Zeno Clash 1 & 2 (both amazing games), and follows a parallel story to that of Ghat from the previous games. It advances the lore of the world by introducing areas outside of the Corwid zones (and gives more background on the Corwids themselves), and introduces more characters with their own inscrutable objectives in this strange world. I love that even though the characters are totally bizarre, they all follow their own logic, and so it all  makes sense how they behave! The story is poignant, and kept me engaged throughout.The  are good and unique -- I don't know quite how to describe it, but there is a use of moving lines that makes the world feel like a giant art canvas that you are travelling through. The use of colour is superb: From drab mountains to colourful forests, and even more colourful inhabitants, the designs pop and are memorable. Colour is also used to highlight paths in times of urgency, which was a beautiful touch, especially when combined with the music...The  is excellent. Truly excellent. In certain areas, especially some mid-game and late-game areas, the vocals are fantastic. Every zone has different music, from thumping tones to beat your enemies up to, through to light choral pieces when traversing the different areas. My hats-off to the music director. This also extends to the  for the characters as well: Pseudo in particular really conveys his emotions and growth as a person.The  is fun, and an evolution of the fighter dynamics from Zeno Clash 1 & 2. As you fight and become more proficient, there are light RPG elements to upgrade your character's stats. The map is a helpful addition, and it was never unclear what my next objective was. "The Ritual", which is the only law of the world, is very fun to play, although I do feel it was under-utilised a bit, especially towards the end-game., I absolutely love this game, as I did the previous Zeno Clashes. It is fun, brimming with character and heart, and with amazing sound design. I cannot recommend it enough.PS: Dear ACE Team -- I massively look forward to Zeno Clash 3!!! :-D

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 03/12/2023:Just got the credit. Things I should emphasize- the soundtrack is awesome and there are real banger moments. The writing and voice acting is really good even if the story is just "Dad of War with carrotman." The exploration can drag on a bit after the initial "whoa" factor of an area lose it appeal and platforming can be aggravating but nothing overstays it welcome too long.The most endearing thing I can say is that for all the weirdness in this game, it was able to make feel connected (if you know you know) enough with the game and world to see it to the end.Original Review:Clash is an unique game that is worth experiencing for people who want to experience a game that isn't chasing the bandwagon like soulslike, roguelite, or survivor game. The game does have flaws such as semi-uninteresting maps, long traversal sections, and some questionable combat design. However, the game itself is worth it cause it tries to be unique and different and for the most part it works. People are probably going to complain about stuff like "no fast travel" or "no map compass marker" or "no direction." But these are just nice to haves. The game has the essential like a compelling story, interesting world and visuals, and for the most part solid and engaging combat. Even though the fighting can be a bit simplistic, it still visceral and fun just to wail on your enemy.Clash is more than worth the asking price just to try a Double A game that isn't just another soulslike.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll update my review once more when I finish the game. My stance at the moment is that this a very particular kind of game not suited to the tastes of most gamers. Very tough to recommend. ----"Clash: Artifacts of Chaos" is one of the most unique games that you've probably never heard about. It is reminiscent of early 2000's titles like "Jak and Daxter" and similar to the "Dark Souls" franchise in other ways. It's like if Kratos were butt ugly and Atreus became a winged creature. The setting is interesting and the characters you find within are both strange and alluring. Prepare yourself for a very weird game here. Every single character seems to have been designed with the idea that they have to be as revolting as possible. I wouldn't say the gameplay is the title's strong suit. It's honestly quite weak and finicky most of the time. A player can genuinely coast by nearly ALL of this game's combat encounters, bosses included, by spamming the Uppercut special attack. Solid damage, it will reposition Pseudo after every use, and it stunlocks almost every single enemy you can encounter in this game. If that fails, you can genuinely just outmaneuver them and spam the Projectile special attack instead.The Ritual minigame is quite boring. It's a nice concept, but not one that you should be encountering with such frequency.  Oh well, at least you can have The Boy do it for you.Around 50% of players beat the first boss of the game. Only ~25% of players beat the game's second boss. Every single Nightmare boss has a completion rate of under 10% and we're supposed to beat them all in order to face Nightmare Gemini for the last piece of North Armor. Player engagement is absolutely abysmal, especially when it comes to the 'secret' stuff. In my opinion, this is because the combat is weak, the fighting feels unresponsive at times, and the story doesn't pick up fast enough to pique player interest. Personally, I almost tapped out after the first boss because I encountered a section of the game where 2 minibosses repeatedly ran my pockets after I spent 5 minutes walking there and also picking up everything on the way. Whenever I lost, I'd have to completely repeat everything I just did because I did not realize that I could backtrack 3 levels and save at that old campfire. The campfire scarcity is a little ridiculous and they could do with some better tips for the players that will struggle even more than I did in that regard. There are a decent amount of shortcuts to be opened up in the game, but I would've appreciated a fast travel system. It's as though the developers WANT you to have a guide open on the side telling you exactly where to go. Trying to backtrack for collectibles, stances, etc. that you may have missed is a real pain. Sooooo much pointless walking around in these mazelike maps... Foregoing quality of life features like a proper map do not make a game charming!!! Taking a few days off from playing this game means you completely lose your bearings. I like the variety of pieces available for the Night Mode avatar, but the traversal makes it a pain to hunt for the hidden costume bits. You can't actually see where these pieces are in the daytime, so you basically have to walk the whole map over again on foot in the hopes you find something new to equip. Some sets aren't even in the same location and those particular pieces are thereby useless by the time you actually find them.

_childDocuments_.review: It's gorgeous to look at, beautiful to listen to, it's creative and the combat is amazingly fun and addictive - they kinda combined the basics of Zeno Clash's one-two-punch with a more complex combo and stances system reminiscent of Abyss Odyssey. It felt a bit too difficult at first, but once I got the hang of it, it flows amazingly well. The key is knowing that you can dodge or combo straight out of an attack animation, even before the animation finishes - but only if the attack hits. So being aggressive, but quick to dodge in and out of range inbetween attacks is key. The rhythm of it almost feels a tiny bit like Bloodborne at times, though I had to unlearn to try and dodge into incoming attacks - no iframes here, apparently, where there is a fist, there is pain! The stamina mechanic is also more forgiving, you can still attack without it, you just take more damage if you get hit. Also, there is friendly fire between enemies, which is not only funny, but also serves to balance those fights where you are outnumbered quite well. Nothing more satisfying than baiting the big guys into charging right through their allies, sending them flying!Yeah it's a bit rough around the edges here and there, but the little quirks and annoyances never once got in the way of my fun. For example, the levels can be a bit labyrinthian and they certainly have a bad case of shin-high barriers everywhere, but so far I never got stuck finding the way forward for long.Overall, I'm very happy to be back in Zenozoik after the long wait and will certainly take 10 more hours to explore every nook and cranny of this lovely world!

_childDocuments_.review: + Unique artstyle -> this is probably the biggest positive for me+ Challenging difficulty+ The combat is (mostly) fun- Map traversal (this is the most frustrating part of the game)- Combat can be slow (why I said it was 'mostly' fun)- Items are hard to find (again other players have mentioned making items glow to make them more noticeable)This game is pretty good from just the four hours I've played so far. The artstyle and design of the world is so unique and far apart from any other series that it will immediately stand out to players. The game started out slow initially and at first I almost refunded it because I had no idea what the hell I was supposed to be doing. Thankfully I stuck it out and had an amazing experience as I continued. The game would definitely benefit from having a minimap as checking the map requires pausing which takes me out a little bit. Fast travel would be a great quality of life change and would make the game a hell of a lot less tedious. I get that the devs wanted players to traverse through a maze-like environment, but why not award us with a fast travel point with each area we unlock? We'd still be forced to traverse but this way it'd only be necessary the first time and the rest would be optional. Making items glow would also be much appreciated as I only realised how much I missed once I bothered to read a guide on the community page.Despite these negatives I still recommend giving this game a try as the alien world that these devs have designed would truly have to be considered one of a kind. The enemies, the landscape and the architecture of the world of Clash is just so intriguing to me and it's why I bought the game to begin with. It's a real shame that these devs are not getting the attention they deserve. Hopefully this game will becoming more popular in the coming months so that the publisher can justify making a bigger budget sequel or some other instalment in the Zeno Clash franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: I was on board the moment I found out this is a successor to Zeno Clash. Just like the Zeno Clash games, it has very good brawler combat. This one is a bit souls-like, in that it has healing flasks that refill at campfires and if you die you get a chance to go collect your body to not lose your progress, but it's definitely more of a brawler than a souls-like still. This actually reminds me more of God Hand than Dark Souls, if anything. In particular you find equip different fighting stances and special moves to customize your moveset, which reminded me a lot of God Hand's customization.Zenozoik is a surreal alien-like world just like in the Zeno Clash games, filled with characters who have unique and interesting designs. It's always a treat to play a game with such a strong style to it. I think that Pseudo and Boy are more interesting characters than Ghat and Daedra or Rimat from Zeno Clash, too, since they're more inhuman like the other inhabitants of Zenozoik.The only problem with the game is that navigation is a bit difficult. The map only vaguely tells you the relative positions of different zones, so exploring the actual paths in each zone can take a while and involve a lot of circling around. It's not a deal killer but definitely something to be aware of.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of both the original Zeno Clash (and, to a lesser extent, Zeno Clash 2) and soulslikes in general. Clash: Artifacts of Chaos combines the two to make a really interesting soulslike brawler. It has a few problems, but overall I got quite a lot out of it. I am excited to continue my game in NG+.The cool stuff:- When you die, you go unconscious and you possess a mannequin. If you defeat the enemy that knocked you out as the mannequin, then you can wake up your unconscious self and continue. I find this to be a really interesting take on the "bloodstain" mechanic of other soulslikes.- The stances, special moves, and general combat mechanics are _mostly_ great. See drawbacks for some of the areas that combat falls shy of perfect; but overall, it's rewarding and results in some really cool moments.- The world building and story are engaging. This game has more of a story than most soulslikes - maybe more along the lines of Remnant: From the Ashes? The game is mostly about fighting, but there's a neat story to keep you engaged when the combat gets a little frustrating.- The only real collect-a-thon in the game involves collecting body parts for your mannequin at night. This collection aspect is really neat - it doesn't feel tedious or pointless, the dreamcatchers that the body parts are attached to are visible from a fair distance, and if you don't go around collecting the parts it won't hinder you in the majority of the game (night mode isn't required very often). It mostly helps you recover when your fleshy body gets knocked unconscious.Drawbacks:- Some bugs. Most notably, sometimes the game registers a quick mouse click as a charge attack instead of a quick attack, and you get locked into the full charge attack animation. There was also one point where the climbing animation was happening too far away from a climbable surface, so I would fall back down every time I climbed it. walking away for a few moments and then approaching the surface fresh seemed to solve it.- Hitboxes don't seem to be balanced against the dodge distance as well as I'd like. A few enemy types have attack animations with very wide hitboxes (so you can't dodge to the side) that happen too quickly for you to dodge out of range before they hit. Generally, once an attack animation starts, I would like to have enough time to dodge out of range.- Animation cancels are very tight, even with dodges. I really like how animation cancels work with combos, but trying to use animation cancelling for a dodge is extremely difficult. I am _fairly_ certain that animation cancels are only allowed in a small window after your attack makes contact with an enemy. If the enemy is winding up for an attack, the timing of the dodge is critical - but since you can only animation cancel into a dodge when you connect with an attack, there's no real way to time your dodge accurately. In the end, I gave up trying to use a dodge-and-weave playstyle and switched to a more hit-and-run playstyle, doing a lot of one- or two-hit combos before rushing back out of attack range.- Weapons auto-equip every time you pick them up. Weapons are useful early game, but since they only have one set of animations, they're not nearly as interesting mid- to late-game when you've heavily upgraded your stances. Especially late game, it gets a little annoying to accidentally pick up a weapon while trying to pick up all the resources in an area and not realizing it auto-equipped until you're in the next fight.Despite the drawbacks, this was a very enjoyable experience. My favorite game in quite some time.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game! A compact open world martial arts souls-like, with incredible visuals, a touching story, and deep combat mechanics with lots of unlockables. While you don't need to have played Zeno Clash 1 & 2 to enjoy this game, playing those games will deepen your enjoyment of this one (and this one is a satisfying entry in the series for long-time fans).
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to summarize what Clash: Artifact of Chaos is but, if you are like me and love martial arts stories with a hermit master turned into father figure as the protagonist, you sure are going to love this game.Seriously though, this is a really well told story, with gameplay and narrative perfectly fusing to tell the player a really emotional story about two souls linked by fate. With some martial arts thrown into the mix, a good combat system and AMAZING soundtrack and voice acting.The main downside, though, is that the game doesn't hold your hand, it's hard in practically every single aspect of it. Some enemies are really tough, and there are no waypoints or quest markes, and you'll probably will be lost a couple of times... Zenozoik is really a harsh world to traverse.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: ACE Team's best game yet.Don't let the mobile-game-tier title put you off, this is a really in-depth martial arts RPG that takes the incredibly satisfying bareknuckle brawling combat of Zeno Clash and adapts it to a 3rd-person gameplay style.Given that the last game in this world came out a decade ago, you can certainly see where some inspiration has been taken from games that have come out since ZC2. The most prominent of which is From Software's Souls series. You can see this influence in the Estus-like healing system, the day/night forms and the bonfire-esque campsites scattered around the map.The music, world and character designs are fantastic, even for ACE Team's already high standard. my only real criticism is that some of the areas can be a little confusing and mazelike, and that sometimes enemy attacks would glitch me halfway into the wall a level leaving me helpless and unable to move.Please don't sleep on this game. It's really good
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I had tons of fun with this game. For starters, I absolutely loved the graphics. It's like playing inside a graphic novel. The combat was lots of fun. Maybe some die-hard Dark Souls fan will find it lacking in some aspect I can't fathom, but for me, it was just the right amount of challenge: I couldn't breeze through it with mindless button-mashing, but it didn't make me want to hurl a controller at the wall, either. I loved the story, too. Jonas Kyratzes is a master of the art, and it shows in this game, too.Of course, it wouldn't be a proper review without looking at the not-so-good aspects. I bought the game as soon as it was released, so inevitably I ran into some bugs and glitches, but nothing game-breaking. The weapons are, in my opinion, completely superfluous. I got through the whole game without trying them more than a couple of times, and my own hands and feet ended up superior in each of those attempts.All in all, I recommend this game wholeheartedly.

_childDocuments_.review: Great, we get to go to Zenozoik again! That alone makes it worth it.The exploration, fighting and story are all very nice.But I have some complaints.- Ghat actually had a personal plot. Pseudo just seems to slot himself into the story for no reason other than it needing a protagonist. Does he have any motivations? Not sure. Not a bad character, but very opaque. Overall the characters seem to all be either nice or nasty, which is a downgrade over Zeno Clash, where the characters were seemingly more complex and simply had conflicts of interest.- Third-person instead of first-person is a straight loss for me. It may allow for fancier spin-kicks and so on, but I think the fighting loses a lot from the distance.- The night form, the corpse runs, and saving only at campsites are mechanics that all encourage one thing: backtracking. You backtrack to get back to your corpse, or you backtrack to get back to camp to heal up and then you backtrack back to where you backtracked from again. Sometimes you backtrack just to save so in case you die and then fail your corpse run, which forces you to reload, you needn't explore the entire area all over again. When you encounter a thorn bush, you backtrack to the campsite to switch to the night form, then backtrack to the bush, then explore behind the bush, then backtrack to the campsite again, switch to the day form, then backtrack back to the bush again and proceed along the other path. So much backtracking. And what for? This is a very frustrating design decision, wasting my time for no discernible improvement to the gameplay. This annoys me to no end. I do not exaggerate when I say that most of my playtime is spent going back and forth between the campfire and where I actually want to go.- The Stamina Guard mechanic, i.e., blocking 50% of incoming damage as long as you still have stamina, is underpowered and not worth using. Instead of taking 50% damage, you're almost always best off just taking 0% by dodging or stunlocking your opponents. IMO this needs to be buffed to block all damage, else it's just useless.- There are bugs. There are even game-breaking bugs. I for one can't finish the game thanks to one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into Martial Arts, particularly kickboxing such as K-1 and Muay Thai (the other "stances" I've encountered so far are fictional martial arts but still fun to use) and games with TPARPG mechanics, then I definitely recommend this game. It's surprisingly deep, somewhere between Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order and Sekiro, but definitely closer to Fallen Order. As of writing this review I haven't finished the game yet, but considering how much I have played it (including offline time) I decided I had to give it a recommend as the amount of content on offer here for the price is, in my opinion, very good value if you like this type of game, so from here I'll just ramble about what I like a little. While it doesn't look like your typical AA game thanks to it's brilliant, cohesive and fully-realised art design, it does play like one. It's not buggy or anything like that, just not as smooth and seamless as the premier offerings of the genre, but it honestly gets the job done and never hinders the art design with janky animations. In terms of the world itself, Zenozoic reminds me of a significantly more lush and primal version of Kenshi, from the primitive make-shift weapons and still operational ancient tech to the small wooden huts built in the footprint of decaying stone ruins, you get the same sense on Zenozoic as you do on Kenshi, that this world has not survived just one civilization-ending cataclysm, but many.The combat system isn't without it's flaws, but it's a fun and strong first attempt at an almost exclusively hand-to-hand version of the basic mechanics we've come to expect from TPARPG games. In place of the weapons you would have in Elden Ring or Nioh, you have stances, the first of which you acquire is selected from an option of three and two can be equipped at any one time which can be freely switched between with left and right on the D-pad. Each stance has a light attack which is performed by tapping the attack button that can be chained together for a basic combo, a heavy attack that must be charged by holding down the attack button, a jumping attack that can be triggered by pressing the attack button while still airborne after a jump and alternate attacks that can be performed by dodging in one of the cardinal directions followed immediately by the attack button. There are also special attacks, with their own dedicated face button, a maximum of three may be equipped at any time, each slot corresponding to the button combination needed to perform them, either by pressing the special attack button alone or in combination with moving the analogue stick up or down. Weapons also feature in the game, but work somewhat more like a brawler in that they have item HP (called "durability" in game) and replace your basic light combo while leaving the rest of the hand-to-hand moveset intact, their primary use seems to be in boss fights or when facing similarly tough enemies. TL;DR a very solid first attempt at a hand-to-hand TPARPG combat system.The progression system is, again, going to sound very familiar to those who play TPARPGs. You defeat enemies to earn XP, which is then spent at the campsite on the training dummy to upgrade Pseudo's base stats such as health, attack power, stamina, etc. Stances and special attacks, on the other hand, are upgraded by consumable figurines scattered all throughout the world, the figurines themselves coming in a variety of sizes, meaning the first few upgrade levels are purchased with the smallest type of figurine, then the next few upgrade levels with the successive size of figurine and so on. Stances and special attacks are upgraded at shrines located throughout the map, separately from upgrading Pseudo's base stats.That's all I have for now as I'm still working my way through my first playthrough. If anything I've mentioned in this review has piqued your interest then I sincerely implore you to try out this game. Even though it's rough, a gem is still a gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Clash is game where you beat people up --and shoot dice.ACE Team have fully embraced their inner gangster and have faithfully represented the harsh realities of street life in Zenozoik. _childDocuments_.review: A surreal martial arts brawler with some souls-ish elements. The bizarre style of the world is grounded by its story and characters. The combat is satisfying once you get the hang of it, and you can mix and match upgrades to create your own style. Exploration feels rewarding, but the lack of a map to help navigate is a bit annoying, particularly when everything looks so surreal I ended up just trying to memorize the terrain. I loved the Zenoclash games, and wasn't sure if I would like the transition to 3rd person, but ACE Team knocked it out the park imo! It's a bit rough around the edges, but the fun combat and unique style is well worth it.I see reviews complaining this isn't another Zenoclash or a first person brawler. You weren't tricked, you could have watched literally any gameplay before you bought the game... And yes, it's more difficult, that comes with being a souls-like. This is the same world but a very different game.Edit: Maybe I missed it, or its an update, but there's markers on the map now making navigation (my main gripe) significantly better!
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: A very tentative thumbs up, mostly because if you're looking at this title chances are you're a fan of the first two.  The artstyle is still great, story is a little less weird but still out there, but the gameplay is still the weak part of the equation.  There are several cardinal sins that a developer that's been around this long should know to avoid, some big, some small, but all stick in your craw trying to play.  The map may be gorgous but it's a maze you'll find yourself constantly back tracking.  Apparently there are several optional zones i've already missed with no clear indication.   There is a flask system with nonrenewable ingredients, so guess what you'll be hoarding until they are useless.  A pointless crafting system, a progression system that even once you figure out what the ingredients are translate into game mechanics that are never explained.  Several key buttons are not documented nor are they remappable, so I hope you remember your inventory even exists.  I feel like I could go on, but the point is this is a title you have to fight the game itself to actually enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Zeno Clash 2.5 - Krakos & ChildsonThe third in the Zeno/Clash series, this game still has a heavy focus on melee combat within the whacky world of Zenozoik. Highly recommend you install on an SSD and turn on the seamless loading option before playing, it makes the whole world just one big place to adventure through, and you'll probably be sick of the loading screens otherwise from backtracking.The night mode was a cool addition, though at some points it was easy to get lost for a bit with some of the area layouts.I had a glitch that would erase my special attack upgrades but the combat stances were fine. Not sure what that was about but thankfully there are utility specials like teleport that you don't need much upgrading from anyway.The new line art style was really neat, you can customize the line size to make it more or less noticeable.Fun time, felt pretty well paced, satisfying to get the combat system down and just wail on the Dr Seuss rejects until they ragdoll across the floor!8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game that really deserves a thumbs sideways. As far as the Zeno Clash games go, this is easily the weakest. Its a flawed game, but not without its charms. While its great to be back in Zenozoik, the lack of story is a bummer. There is some story, but its just not as well fleshed out as in ZC 1 & 2 with minimal cutscenes and few memorable characters. But overall it doesn't have the same level of weirdness of the original ZC games because there just isn't a lot of interaction with the world, most NPCs are just there to be fought, the rest are shopkeepers.The level design is, well, not good. Its incredibly easy to get lost and the first few areas all look identical so its easy to feel like you're running around in circles. Its vaguely souls-like, complete with corpse runs, but at the same time if you die while in "soul form", its game over, which can get pretty annoying as its not an easy game. Why it doesn't just continue the game but with the loss of XP/souls is beyond me. There's also a dice game before some fights that you can use to gain an advantage in combat, but more often than not it comes down to pure luck, it slows down the pace of the game, and maybe 60-70% of the time it'll just end up leaving you at a disadvantage.I cant quite bring myself to leave a thumbs down as its a game made with a lot of love, and i adore almost everything ACE team does. Clash's art design is still completely insane, and its OST is banging. The combat can be fun too, so its definitely not a bad game, its just... incredibly janky. I just hope by buying this, we can fund a proper, first person Zeno Clash 3 and continue the story of Ghat and Rimat.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I could recommend this game enough, it's one of the best I've played in years. I enjoyed everything about this game from the game play, the story, the characters, the soundtrack, etc. My only real issue is that it's sometimes easy to get lost, but this often just leads you to new secrets to find. This game is something special and the world is one of the most unique, immersive, and creative that I've had the pleasure of spending some time in. I wish the game was longer, but that's really a non-issue considering it gave me a good 12 hours of playtime. Even if you didn't play the original Zeno Clash games, you should absolutely give this one a try, the developer's put so much into this game and it would be a shame if you didn't get to experience it!

_childDocuments_.review: If you can punch it, you can defeat it!So far I'm 10 hours into the game and I love it. The games art style, world and story are unique and give me a feel of wonder and exploration I think I didn't have since I was a child. Everything is bizarr and strange but also beautiful.The fighting is very fun and unlocking new stances and special attacks, and switching between them mid fight opens up lots of possibillites to try out. Especially as soon as NG+ is added with the next patch. I also love the interconnected souls-like open world style the game has where you unlock shortcuts the further you progress. It doesn't set markers on your map or HUD to show you where to go next and you'll have to do some exploration which I like. Still I never really got lost for long so far. But I can imagine this 'lack of direction' be confusing at times for some.Also great soundtrack! Just listen to "The Amokuali" track of the Clash: Artifacts of Chaos OST on youtube :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the juice. The soundtrack is top notch, I found myself listening to it out of game frequently. The visuals are crisp and engaging with palettes that change up frequently enough to keep things fresh. The character design is as fascinating as it is fun to look at. Speaking of characters, the interactions between the protagonist and everyone else in the game was a joy to experience. From beginning to end the way he treats others and carries himself made me giggle in joy. The voice acting is at its best here as well. Every character has a unique delivery that reminds me of fairy-tales. It really adds to the personality of each character.With all the heart that went into this game I would easily recommend it. _childDocuments_.review: Being a fan of ACE Team's Zeno Clash games and the surreal world of Zenezoik, Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is another very welcome addition to the series. While this addition takes a much different approach to the formula; it still brings the player very kinetic, beat 'em up gameplay, unique art direction and compelling storytelling and characters. It is also non-linear, levels are split up in segments and you can explore them however you see fit as long as you have the abilities and progression to do so. The game also alters the combat system, asserting you to dodge and parry to overcome the numerous battles ahead.Clash also offers one very interesting feature that occurs just before said battles, should the player choose to; and that is The Ritual dice game. This is a pretty fun if a little simple dice game of chance and strategy where the ultimate goal is to have the higher value of rolled dice at the end. Should the player win, they can place a condition on the opponent/s of their choosing (this is chosen before the dice game actually begins), to gain an edge in the battle that follows. However, the vice-versa occurs if the player loses, so be careful. The game world really doesn't navigate the player that well and places a lot of trust in them to do so themselves. Some players (even myself, at times) may get lost from time to time as they try to collect and encounter all that there is in the areas. The combat scenarios are not perfect, either, as some of the arenas generated can cause bottlenecks and other nuisances. The map provides some basic info on the world but still leaves a lot up to the player to figure out where they're going, or even supposed to be going. , but I do think some minor changes could be implemented just for the sake of making it a little less daunting. For example, when the player approaches a transition point to the next level, it basically says [RB to the next area] or something to that effect. I think specifying what that area actually is would be a simple fix but an appreciated one.With all that said however, I can't recommend Clash: Artifacts of Chaos enough. A game that I can enjoy to the point where I can ignore its faults is definitely a game worth your time, and Clash achieves this very well.EDIT: I realised I left out what really sets this game apart from others, and that's the art direction, story and characters. There are few games these days that put in this much creativity and thought into the game's world and the characters that inhabit it. My mind goes to series like Oddworld (with an air of Heavy Metal magazine) if I'm to find something to compare this to. Truly incredible work.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is something truly unique. in the sea of mediocrity that is the gaming industry, it's always a breath of fresh air to experience a game that clearly had a lot of love and passion poured into it, and this game is exactly that.everything about it is refreshing. the art style is extremely striking, bizarre, and gorgeous all at the same time. even when you're looking at the most horrific and disgusting creature you've ever seen, you can't deny that they are extremely visually interesting. a lot of games just take the most sanitized and literal definition of "eldritch horrors" and spit out an incoherent design. in this game though, things look and feel TRULY alien and bizarre, but they also WORK. they don't feel out of place, which helps to really sell this crazy world and make it all fit togetherthe combat is extremely tight and satisfying. your blows are weighty, but they don't feel burdensome unless you're purposefully using the heavier and slower combat styles. it's an easy to learn and difficult to master system, and while the game isn't extremely difficult (for me, at least, though there were a few points where i struggled), you go from simply surviving your fights to thriving in your fights. mastering the dodge attacks and parries and when to chain your special moves into your combo can give you this state of perfect focus where you're locked in, constantly landing attacks without giving your enemy a single second to recover, and the fight is over in seconds. it feels AMAZING once you get really good at your chosen style.the music is consistently mindblowing. seriously, it constantly elevates every scene where the music is prevalent. scaling a treacherous cliffside, exploring abandoned ruins, taking a well deserved break in town, it doesn't matter the scenario, the music will really pull you in and keep you fully immersed. especially in fights, when pseudo's theme plays, you know it's time to lock in and beat whatever poor creature you're up against to death. it's amazing.the characters are another gigantic draw for me, and i'm gonna have a lot to say about them. pseudo is an incredibly well written character, because he's the antithesis of a typical protagonist. he really doesn't even want to be here half the time, he's doing what he's doing because of a moral obligation that develops into a genuine connection. the dialogue repeatedly sells this idea, with pseudo confidently saying something extremely jaded because he's a cynical hermit, and the boy poking the perfect hole in his argument with a question that stems from his childlike innocence and optimism, and all pseudo can say about it is "...i don't know." i love their dynamic. though pseudo can be extremely brutal to people he doesn't like, a lot of his philosophy and jaded nature comes from his solitude as a hermit, internalizing the ideas and building the walls that allowed him to survive in this difficult world, they don't tend to work well with other philosophies. despite this, he's not a bad guy at all. in fact, he's a good man (if you can call him that, look at the state of that weird thumb creature). like i said before, the entire game starts because of his moral obligation to not leave a child alone with nowhere to go. it just takes someone to actually talk to pseudo for that cold dead hard to warm up, and i love his character progression.i think i've said enough to get the point across that i really like this game, and if you also want your life to spiral out of control by having to constantly think about a giant hairy thumb man and his little owl son, buy the game. it's an incredible experience, and it's one of the few games i'd even recommend at full price. there's a lot of meat to it, room for multiple playthroughs (especially since they added NG+), and it has an extremely satisfying combat system.plus you can buy a little winter coat for your little owl son and he looks precious in it.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: FANTASTIC.The game is just great from angle; efficient loading times (Max 10 seconds from booting and already playing),  awesome combat with very unique fighting styles that you can mix midcombo to a degree, multiple special finishing moves, unique animations for the first person for every enemy so far, and a wonderful world that you are tossed into. The game looks, feels, and sounds awesome. Voice acting is a touch clunky but I think it adds to the charm of this disjointed world. Great game, worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: A prequel to the Zeno Clash games from some time ago, with a lot of queues taken from Dark Souls.In most ways, this is an excellent game. The combat flows fantastically and so many moves and techniques are thoroughly satisfying. Hits all feel like they have impact, and there's a high skill ceiling. Much like Elden Ring, the difficulty is in what you choose to use, and you can make the game much easier by mixing health brews and using weapons, or you can slam your skull into enemies exclusively.The visuals are fantastic, every character design is interesting and unique and even the most bizarre can still move and fight. The hatching shader is a wonderful thing that accentuates the entire world, and it's just lovely. The voice acting is superb with well written characters you can easily become attached to, and though the story itself is rather simple, everything surrounding it is unique, and the emotional points are delivered excellently. There is a lot of bird suicide to punctuate that point.However, the main villain, Gemini, is not fleshed out enough. The focus of the story is kept on Pseudo, the player character, the entire time, so we're not given much of a feel of what Gemini is going through the entire time we're denying her anything.Once you really get good, there isn't much of anything that can challenge you either, no NG+, no hard mode, no challenges. While others complain about how difficult Moon-Sun is, I kind of just knocked him around and it left me wanting.All in all, a fantastic game. I look forward to Pseudo's next adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Overall solid gameplay, definitely needs to learn the movesets of enemies to beat the game. Character designs are great, with them performing moves according to their body composition: for example, the moose-headed Picasso dude will kick with his third leg. We can also see the recurring mob characters being associated with the body guards of Gemini from their attack animations.The subtle touch goes beyond this. The conversations between Pseudo and the Boy indicating their different attitudes towards their situations of the world, where the Boy always shows inclination to understand more, while Pseudo displaying hesitation. Thus, the ending, despite looking a bit rough, suits how the general narrative flows.The navigation is a bit difficult for me since some landscapes, particularly in the mountain and swamp regions, is too visually extravagant for me to remember the marks for tracking. Some moves from enemies are a bit too fast to react. There are ledges that misleadingly suggests areas to explore, however when I died a couple of times from falling I quit that mentality for good. Besides,Clash is a wonderful sequel to the Zeno Clash games I was not able to finish as a kid, revoking beautiful memories I've never had.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an impressive evolution in the Clash series. The combat system features customizable movesets, attack cancels, craftable weapons, and buffs/debuffs you can dole out through winning pre-fight "ritual" dice games (which are almost completely optional). Also new to the series is a more expansive semi-open world to explore--much more so than Zeno Clash 2--and a narrative that has more developed characters and dialogue. Think Lone Wolf and Cub filtered through the Clash series' signature Boschean lens and you're pretty much there. There are even some sorta interesting themes about the state of nature and philosophy of law! Granted, it's all a bit on the nose, but given the stonepunk aesthetic of the game and the gruff Perlman-esque protagonist, it feels appropriate.Oh, and don't forget about the banger soundtrack, which is one of the best game OSTs I've heard in loooong time.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played the first 2 parts, so I won't compare. But here's what I'll say. Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is a wonderful adventure on a very unusual prehistoric planet. I would call the game - Beat 'em up RPG. Very colorful, fun, especially if you like hand-to-hand combat. The graphics are not ordinary, and perhaps not for everyone, but I liked it. The story is rustic, but... fights .... oh yes .. here you have fun to the limit!
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, creativity here is off the charts. Its a very strange game, but I embrace its weirdness and recommend you do the same.World and characters of Zenozoik are stunning to look at. Art design and visual presentation are like nothing I have ever seen before. Game uses this great filter that makes every frame look like a super detailed drawing. Every location and character is unique and rich with details that made me both chuckle and scratch my head, wondering what is it I'm looking at.Sound is just as great, music is all killer no filler. All the tracks set just the right mood and tone. There are a few especially great tracks that play at important story moments that simply slay. So glad I bought the version with OST. Gameplay wise there is a lot here to enjoy. Exploration is very unguided, there is no minimap, no signposts and no objective markers. You are meant to explore the world and pay attention to the landmarks, making it very satisfying to find hidden treasures and shortcuts.Combat in Clash is pretty deep and fun to master. It feels very "punchy" and satisfying. There are many combat styles you can use and special attacks to aid you in combat. All of these are tied to your attributes that you can assign on level ups. You gain experience by winning combat, but you'll also need to keep an eye out for wooden dolls you can find while exploring. These are used to upgrade your techniques and serve as a sort of "titanite" from Dark Souls.Combat is accompanied by Ritual minigame that can help you or burden you before fighting starts, depending on whether you win the dice game or not. I found it pretty fun and a nice distraction.Story can be a bit confusing, but it kept me interested, mostly because of wonderfully colorful cast of characters. Kudos to the voice actors, they sound spot on, which couldn't be easy to pull off with world and characters so bonkers.Game runs buttery smooth with several options to customize your experience, including settings to change the colour palette of the game. I found it especially enjoyable when playing on mouse and  keyboard, control layout is perfect and feels snappy and responsive.Overall I found no major issues with the game and enjoyed it throughly. If I had to complain about something, it would be that a few locations feel like a maze and can be difficult to find your way around. Other than this minor complaint I just love this game and can't get enough of the world of Zenozoik. Its a must play game, especially in an industry that got so stale and boring recently. Reasonable price, smooth performance and good length are just a cherry on top of this amazing package. Nominated for Outstanding Visual Style Award in 2023!
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: This game is my favourite by far. The unique visual style makes this game in a league of its own, and in the best way possible. The story is immersive and fantastically made, so don't skip a single cut-scene. The vastness of the world and detail and design of each different biome/area is one of my favourite parts, especially because those who venture to the deep corners and hidden pathways are rewarded with secret goodies and useful items, making it well worth your time to not only take the less obvious routes, but to also appreciate the scenery and beautiful map. I hope this game takes off, because I think it is an experience everyone should enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable, very original designs and a great art style. Pretty lovely story going on too. The combat gets a bit samey over time but the game isn't overly long where it becomes a real problem. The soundtrack is also pretty damn good.As someone who's only played Zeno Clash 2 four years ago and barely remembered anything from it apart that it was a huge trip full of just really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥  stuff, I wasn't quite sure how to go into this. After playing it I definitely felt that it tried to go for something a bit more grounded, while keeping a bunch of odd character designs and a beautifully odd setting. This has benefitted the story elements greatly, as I was often barely aware of what the ♥♥♥♥ was going on in Zeno Clash 2.Playing this made me want to get Zeno Clash 1 and replay 2, because I honestly can't get enough of the sheer originality and weirdness that radiates from ACE Team's games, and I can honestly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pleasant surprise. While I didn't expect the game to be bad, I went in with middling expectations, and came out loving it. It's easily one of the best Souls-inspired indie games I've ever played.The art direction is fantastic (and the stylized aspects can be adjusted in the menu, always a plus.)The music SLAPS, buy the OST if you can.Gameplay is great, with a lot of flexibility when it comes to combos and customization. I'm blown away by the number of unique animations for attacks.Story doesn't take up a lot of time in the campaign, but its pretty good and has some good lore for fans of the prior Zeno Clash games. The voice performances from the main character and his companion were both spot on.Performance was consistently great, no stutter or frame dips.My only current criticism is that some of the checkpoints are not well placed, specifically ones that are before cutscenes. While you can skip cutscenes, being stuck on a boss can mean running from the last bonfire to the boss arena, starting the cutscene, skipping it, playing the ritual, then finally the fight itself.I'd rate it 9/10, but I'd gladly bump it up to a 10 if they updated with a New Game +.

_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: It's everything I hoped for and more. Fluid combat where you can really feel the impact, with plenty of customization too, including stances and special moves that completely change how you approach fights.
