_childDocuments_.review: 2023's definitive sleeper hit.Gorgeous visual style and storytelling. Gameplay that scratches a very specific action game itch. Clash is the kind of thing that makes me glad video games like it can exist.If you are one of those people who craves highly technical martial arts action games, and/or likes getting invested in really freakin' surreal and cool worlds, you might want to give this one a shot.More people should be fans of this!!
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos is a tight and polished experience. The combat is mechanically simple but is kept fresh by creative enemy design and snappy encounters that don't overstay their welcome. Visually and musically, the world of Zenozoik is impressive, bizarre, and beautiful. All this is tied together by a powerful story with simple themes and complex characters. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Clash is the third title based in the absolute bonkers, anarchy world of Zenozoik. It is a completely standalone game and does not require knowledge of previous games. I absolutely adore it. I never liked fighting games so that is saying much that I actually am so in love with it. Of course it is not only a fighting game because it is also an adventure game with exploration and very basic puzzles. It shines in story and world building. I am a big fan of the other worldly feeling that comes with playing all the titles from ACE Studios. They put you into the worlds that are completely unapologetic about how absurd they seem, they live by their own rules and you as a player are a tourist taken along for the ride. If you like being in foreign places, experiencing a completely different world and worldview Zeno Clash will provide. I recommend all titles from this developer as they are very unique and do things differently from other studios. That being sad I have to leave also some negatives:1. There is no need for parrying in game - it is a completely useless technique.2. The legibility of items to pick up is non existent - you might end up licking every inch of the map to see if there is something there you can pick up. That is a bad design.3. The map is only available when going into inventory. It breaks the flow of game and the world is not exactly easy to navigate. It's an inconvenience but not a deal breaker.4. No difficulty setting.I cannot say that the fighting system is good or bad, I know it is difficult in the beginning but it gets easier as you learn how it works. I know also that many people didn't get through this game because it was too difficult, so keep that in mind.What kept me playing is the need to see more of the Zenozoik which is my personal buffet of art and awe inspiring views. Oh and MUSIC. The music in this game is an integral part of my life now. It is that good and I rarely notice the music in games but this is sth else...
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Keeping it short, this is an absolute recommend at full price. Pros- great art- fun combat- GREAT animations in combat- the One Law minigame is fun and quite polished- very nice narrative- great worldbuilding- good VA (but some odd choices for some characters)- some very nice music- very nice dialogue and character interactionsMid:- level design is just eh, secrets can be fun but the main path is uninteresting to traverse- dreamwalking mechanic can be tedious- some poor direction that is saved by the linearity of the map- walk-and-talk sectionsCons:- there are consistent bugs with getting stuck in walls from animations and some issues with the pickups, nothing game breaking- checkpoints suck idc what game theyre in- progression is slow and makes it hard to get into the game initiallyWhatever bugs or menial issues I had with this game were mitigated by the absolute peaks that were the highs in this experience. May be my fav clash game, I will have to replay 2, but this was an absolute blast and was well worth my time. Thank you, ACE.

_childDocuments_.review: Great 3D brawler with RPG elements and an interconnected open world that isn't just a field with things dotted across a map.Perfectly weird and funky in ways that just are, without need for explanation. You have a nightitme form made of wood. You fight animal people. You play a goofy dice game to determine whose buff takes effect before the start of important fights.The story beats become clearer at the halfway point through the game, Great ending (assuming it was the only one).

_childDocuments_.review: Really good experience overall with a few minor moments of frustration. The over world and how you traverse the map reminds me a lot of Dark Souls one in that you can see key locations you've been to and places you need to go which really helped immerse me in the world and of course having flasks and campsites which are similar to bonfires. _childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: It is totally crazy and utterly sad, that this game has not received more attention. It's amazing, beautiful, enchanting, unique and weird. It combines the best elements of Metroidvanias, soulslikes, brawlers into a unique mix. The combat system seems a bit complicated at first, but it quickly becomes really engaging. Like a dance. And the world is more than amazing. It doesn't hold your hand, but the level design guides you through it nicely. It's free, but it's just enough to keep you from getting lost.The game is full of heart. The story and characters are made with as much soul, care, and dedication as the amazing art style and world itself. The last time I took this many screenshots was in Elden Ring.I bought it on sale, sadly too late (it should have been a day 1 purchase) but I'd give the full price for it without hesitation.I can only hope that this world can continue to be built because it deserves a better closure (for me, this game is the culmination of what the first two parts of Zeno Clash started)A one-of-a-kind experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews but felt compelled to for this one since the game seems to have zero marketing.I loved the Zeno Clash games and was pleasantly surprised to see a new entry in the series. But where the first two games were more awkward experiences, this one is much more polished and a just plain good game. The previous games had memorably bad voice acting and localization, but this they really improved on this front and I actually found myself growing attached to the main character despite how freakish he looks. The game has also changed from first person melee to third person and feels more like a "soulslike". The world is big without being padded and it has a lot to explore with the day and night world variants. The combat gives you a lot of flexibility in mixing styles and moves and is satisfying.  In summary, it's a fun, surprisingly engaging game so long as you can appreciate the distinctive, bizarre art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: A truly amazing, wonderful game. You will get far more out of this from ACE, then most triple AAA studios. Return to the world of Zenozoik with all its surrealism, madness, exploration, and martial prowess.A third person, explorative, adventures story with a unique setting. You do not need to play Xeno Clash 1 or 2 to play this one. Though, both are great games in their own right worth playing.Pros:Fun martial arts combat.Lots to unlock in game for character growth and your style.Good music.Marvelous setting and character design.Good story.Exploration worth purpose as it only aids you. The open map and setting really does compel you.Price to play time ration: Perfect.Neutral:One can debate of splitting hairs on such an excellent game. There were simply things that could have been cut to save on time and resources. They drank hard from the Dark Souls vine here and a lot of it was unnecessary. The night sequences simply led to exploring the same area twice and getting through a gimmicky unlock new area portion (just slows down the pace).Night armor, again what is the point?The whole retrieve your body after you die (and cannot grab the body having to defeat whatever is in front of it that killed you first), when you can reload from the next check point with everything takes about the same about of time.The one law (the mini game of chance) before every fight just takes time. There is no penalty for not doing it and far faster to beat someone then take the time to play it with the chance of getting hose by losing it. It also eats the artifact used.Short cuts are fine, but there are moments where shortcuts are just stacked on top of one another and it becomes why have so many in the same space a hop jump from one another.The crafting environment does not resapwn for potion brewing. Respawning enemies drop supplies for weapon crafting  instead. Thus, make good use of your potions. Kind of backwards in importance.Pretty much anything I have to gripe about can be ignored in game which is why the remain neutral and not cons and why this thing remained great and fun and a positive experience.Con:Some character stuck bugs, but can get out of it via return to last check point. Note: The standard Dark Souls Stamina Bar works differently here: Pay attention to it: but you can keep attacking and Dodgeing, but will take more damage if you do not have  stamina.

"I didn't mean to hurt him," "Bring me the boy!" that kinda thing. There's visual imagination but little narrative imagination.

_childDocuments_.review: It's excellent. The combat is often a little obtuse in a way I feel like I have trouble describing. Maybe the best way to put it is that nothing feels "snappy." I bought this game because I saw a blog post saying that it was similar in concept to SIFU, which I think is roughly fair. The fighting aspect is really as close as the two games get; however, SIFU's combat is far superior in my opinion. The real selling point of Clash AOC is it's incredible art style, story and soundtrack. It is superb in every feature of its design other than the sometimes unresponsive combat. The games artistic direction alone makes AAA  games look like chump change, it's just gorgeous and unique--something sorely lacking in big budget, mechanically produced, emotionless AAA  games. The sound track is excellent, makes you feel badass (one area where I think it generally bests SIFU as well, whose soundtrack was slightly lacking in comparison to it's slick and stylized graphics). Story is excellent as well, I've not finished it but I find it endearing even at its worst parts so far, which is more  than I can say for a lot of other, more story driven, games. I'd highly recommend it, with the caveat that it is a difficult fighting game and that might turn some people off from it (the dice game challenge is also tremendously difficult to naturally win at first, probably wait to do it until you buy at least one or two more dice around two hours in). If anything, you should buy the soundtrack and play other games listening to it, it's just that good.EDIT: The story is a 10/10, Just finished the game, excellent. Love the ideas, love the writing, love the execution. Play it just for that.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEW: I changed from recommend to not recommend after getting 100% achievements.  There are way too many negative things about this game.  Only get it if you just want to support ACE Team and Zenozoik (which is what I'm doing). This game is barely related to Zeno Clash 1 and 2, but it's set in the same world of Zenozoik.  You don't have to play Zeno Clash to play this game at all, but I recommend you go play Zeno Clash anyway because it's great.- Returning to Zenozoik.  I will always play any game set in Zenozoik, one of the most creative and interesting worlds ever made.- Character design is top notch still- Dialogue performance for everyone other than Pseudo and the boy is pretty good- The Ritual is a really fun minigame and I find myself challenging people even if I don't want to punish them- Combat works well.  It's more like Absolver than a Zeno Clash game, though- There's a rage mode that turns the game first person, which is awesome and makes me wish the whole game was like that- If you hit the enemy enough times without missing or getting hit, you can execute a neat God of War style animation beat down that feels unique to the creatures you're fighting.  Super easy to do because you get some stun from a full light attack combo and you just circle a little bit to dodge anything they might attack you with. - Weapons are good if you're having a hard time with fights as a good.  Once you get the hang of parries, your aggressive meter fills up crazy fast and weapons are no longer needed.  I ended with a huge amount of weapons in my inventory because I forgot about them, really.- Exploration and night mode go hand in hand in their ruining of the game.- The night mode is when you sleep at a tent checkpoint from flesh Pseudo to a wooden version of Pseudo that can pass through brambles and see hidden chests and armor pieces and best of all, doesn't have the boy saying stupid things.  Sounds cool at first, but then you realize it just exists to waste your time.- The exploration sucks.  Bad.  Do you like staring at corners and just running alongside the wall for any ingredients for potions or figurines you use to upgrade your skills and stances?  Do you like multiple dead ends that may or may not have chest in them?  Sometimes, yeah?  Well do it twice the exact same way because you're missing stuff from night mode, maybe.- Even if you're like me and just wanted to see the story and not mess with night mode, too bad.  You find brambles and get to make the most laborious decision in a video game; do you backtrack now to the previous camp and go wooden Pseudo and go through the brambles now or try and go a little further and hope that the next tent is close by?  Either way, you've got to backtrack.  Then what if once you go through the brambles, you kill a thorn guardian that clears the brambles so flesh Pseudo can go through and interact with a totem that only flesh Pseudo can interact with?  You got it, more backtracking to get to the same place you're standing in.- Bloodborne style, you can knock down a ladder (a boulder in this case) or open a door to unlock a shortcut once you've gotten far enough, but the shortcuts are also put in strange places where it's not even clear if they help or not.  You've also likely gotten another tent checkpoint before the shortcut, so it becomes even more forgettable.- There's a kid.  He whines and says the dumbest things possible.  One of the most irritating things is you go into the mountains all nice and it isn't until you get high up that the kid starts consistently whining it's too freezy and he feels sick.  What?  You didn't get the warm fur outfit from the trader at the bottom of the mountain? You guessed it, go backtrack!  I chose not too in hopes that the boy would get sick and die, but unfortunately that didn't happen.  Looking forward to an upcoming patch, I guess.- The boy, again.  I get it, they wanted to add a foil to a story so Pseudo has someone to explain the world to.  However, by making it a kid, it's so painfully obvious that when Pseudo talks to the kid, he's talking to the player and treating you like a kid.  Even simple things like trying to tell the player what an enemy is called isn't done in a natural way in items that clearly come from those enemies or someone talking about it and trusting the player is smart enough to connect dots.  The boy instead randomly says the enemy's name.  "Watch out, a cave crab!" Yeah, I know.  We just killed like 5 of them a couple seconds ago.- Pseudo is a jerk to everyone except the boy.  The dialogue between the other characters is great and pulls you into this weird world of Zenozoik where even the way of speaking sounds unique, only for Pseudo to say something bland and faux intimidating.  Then the boy asks some of the dumbest questions and Pseudo's all invested and earnest. - The story is only interesting with  and talking to Word, which Pseudo shuts down, because why wouldn't he?  Aside from that, it's pretty much find the things to defeat the person.  That's the whole game in a nutshell.- By the time you get the third flask, you'll never really run out and the game gets real easy- Stats feel like they don't mean anything.  I put like 5 in power, 5 in constitution and 15 in aggressiveness and was good for the rest of the game.  Seriously, I ended the game with over 50 unallocated stat points.  I guess that's better than stat screwing yourself over, but I was always waiting to see if I could tell the difference between them all, but it just never really mattered.- Builds don't really matter.  Pseudo gets clothing and wood pseudo gets body parts, neither really mattered when I played.  You get different stances and special moves that you can burn figurines to improve.  I ended up leaving my favored stances and special attacks with low level figurines because FOMO and I just felt like there was going to be some great stance or special attack, but it never came.  I just ended up using boxing exclusively and spin kick mostly.  I tried some other specials, but they didn't work with how I liked playing.- The world is far too colorful for me.  The gritty dark and weird worlds of Zeno Clash 1/2 fit way better for characters.  Zenozoik was brutal feeling, this game feels too welcoming and kid friendly- Zeno Clash's first person combat was far more unique and satisfying than this game's third person combat.  In first person, it added another level of uniqueness since I can't recall many first person brawlers in addition to the added benefit of seeing the enemy character models closer and feel like they're focusing on you, not your character model.  The third person combat of this game is more like Absolver than Zeno Clash, it's too karate/kung fu artsy, which might fit the new bright arty landscape but feels slightly contradictory from the brutal and primal design of characters and buildings. The reason I said it was less satisfying in third person is because there needed to be some way to control the number of enemies you're currently fighting.  Zeno Clash did this by strong attacks that sent enemies flying and ragdolling and could even hit into other enemies.  That was very fun and satisfying.  I feel less powerful as Pseudo.- Melee weapons felt better to use in Zeno Clash, I can hardly tell if I'm using some of the weapons here unless the enemy's health bar starts dropping faster than normal.I wish I could recommend this game, but it's just not very compelling for most people not invested in Zenozoik with the amount of backtracking and the weak story.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this series, and even most of this game's design ideas, but I can't be bothered to finish it. _childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic action game that takes elements of games like Dark Souls and modern God of War and puts them in a melee brawling system that has a slight pinch of Street Fighter and God Hand. It takes all of these and bundles them together in a gameplay system that has it's own unique Zeno Clash spin and overall is a very satisfying and unique gamplay loop. This is all brought together by the classic surreal world of Zenozoik that Zeno Clash created and is still one of the most unique and interesting settings I have ever seen.This could have been a very simple "souls-like" game that took place in a strange world but was instead a very unique brawling game that delivers on it's remarkably unusual, yet coherent and uncompromising setting.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit clunky at times, and at one point I was entirely lost as to where to go next. The game does not offer a real navigation system, just a crude outline for a map, and you're supposed to figure it out yourself. The area are designed in a way to naturally guide you as to where you're supposed to go next, but it was still hard for me on some specific areas. It has been a common complaint, and I believe the developer launched an update to clarify some of these areas. I overall like the choice of not holding our hand in navigation with any UI or anything, but I can see how that could be a turn off for some people.The gameplay is overall fun, but very clunky at times, which can be frustating. I think the team at ACE has a good concept here, and I hope they'll expand on it on a sequel. There's a really good core here.The game isn't very long, but it is a good time. There's some extra, stronger versions of certain bosses that you can optionally fight around the world if you find them. These are pretty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game, all of the positive reviews stand up. However.I wouldn't call it a Souls-like, I believe it has been a bit mislabelled, don't go into this game thinking you'll have infinite respawns with low consequences. Each time you fully die you reset back to your last save, all progress made between death and that save is erased. The game doesn't save after major boss fights so you will have to figure out a way to save (there is a cheesy way but you can figure it out pretty easily), levelling up doesn't save and neither does sleeping / passing time. There were multiple times I failed to 'git gud' and had to repeat major boss fights due to dying after the fight to a regular enemy, this also led to losing multiple hours worth of progress.It's more of a beat 'em up where the odds are always stacked against you, except for the final bosses and some sneaky bosses the vast majority of bosses fight alongside multiple subordinates that function to muddy the fight. Depending on how you save you can sometimes have to go through multiple fights with groups of enemies before you reach a boss fight, draining your resources and tiring you out. There are a lot of upgrade materials laying around so you'll have a great time customising your build.Overall the way the map is laid out and shortcuts are utilised is exemplary, the gradual progression prevents stagnation and there is less backtracking than I initially thought, especially for some hidden bosses that require you to traverse the whole map all over again to catch all the bosses that are available before the final boss fight.The combat is great, I have a love hate relationship with this game due to the bosses having subordinates to increase the fight difficulty, on the other hand the dice game is very fun and an interesting way to rig a fight in your favour.I have 100% this game and won't play it again.(Spoiler below)There is a section where the boy displays the ability to link your enemies, thus any damage to one damages another. This would be extremely helpful during the boss fights and fights where you are fighting a group of enemies that are overwhelming but alas I never saw the ability trigger. That may be on my part, maybe there was a way to control its use but the game doesn't teach you how to do it properly if that is the case.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played and loved Clash 1 and 2, it was an immense letdown.More like a prototype than an actual gamePros: * The world of Clash: grotesque / wacky characters, unique flora and cities * Dark souls meets Clash is a promising combination * Different world for after-deathCons: * The dark souls formula was poorly adapted. Reminds me of (old) Lords of the Fallen with the clumsiness slow paced fights. * Now that you are obliged to scour the map for materials, it's linearity and emptiness is painfully obvious * Jump mechanic exists for no apparent reason. There is nothing you can jump on even though everything seems jumpable. * Music is mostly barely there. It is noticable, when the music finally starts that there was none beforehand. * The ritual minigame is just not fun. Like you are just always chose the best outcome and hope it is enough. The worst is that the ritual is a core mechanic related to the story and the lore. And since the rituals have one usage, so you are better of not using them. Shame. * The FPS playstyle which made previous Clash titles fun are now behind a fillup bar. Why? Like removing the fun deliberately. Outrageous.

_childDocuments_.review: A game where you play an ugly hermit helping a little bird kid in a weird world full of violent mutant combatants. I played and beat the original Zeno Clash and I love the strange setting and culture the games explore. I just wish the combat didn't feel so bad. There's a cool combo system that I always get knocked out of because opponents are almost never staggered. There's a dodge system where I swear every time I see the enemy winding up to attack and press dodge, I get hit before the dodge animation fires or because the dodge doesn't actually get you out of the enemy's reach. Add on top of that a difficult to navigate map that you can end up circling trying to figure out where you're supposed to go next, and it's like the game was designed to frustrate me personally. I think if you have more patience than I do for map exploration and clunky combat systems, it's worth your time and like I said I love the weirdo setting. But not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried to stick with it, but it just went downhill the more I played. Game would have benefited from being far shorter. This is more or less the case with Zeno Clash 1 and 2, previous games of ACE Team that I played years back, that belong to the same world setting. Bit of a pattern, sadly.Think I made it roughly a bit past half of the game.+ Visuals are pretty wild, easily the best thing about the game+ World lore is intriguing+ OST is pretty good* Voice acting is pretty alright most of the time, but subjective* Ritual minigame, which is big part of lore, I'm pretty mixed on, it seems completely unnecessary most of the time, I played it only when it was forced. There's upgrades for it and everything, but it just seems completely unnecessary...- Combat can easily be cheesed. I was able to take down any opponent I saw by dropkicking them in the face, not utilising any other move. There are also other moves to utilise that enable this to work better- Dialogue script is pretty bad- Same goes for cutscenes that feel a bit off at times- Story is pretty forgettable- Jank, you'll see some weird stuff pop up the more you play, nothing game-breaking yet- No manual saving, a SINGLE auto-save slot for when you make it to campfire. Better hope your save doesn't corrupt?- Unnecessary crafting that takes away from the game- Lots of stuff to find in the world but at the same time you don't need nearly as much as there is available, yet if you want max upgrades you'll find yourself scavenging every corner anyway for the actually rare items, which is made worse by having...- ...NO MAP! If you ever put this game on hold, you won't have a clue where to go or what to do when you are back. This is not helped by the fact that there ain't...- ...NO FAST TRAVEL either! Backtracking is what we're all about, here. But this problem is further amplified by...- ..."Night mode". Playing through the areas again. There are some unique drops for "Night mode" only that show up there, but you can't see where they are during the day. If you are a completionist, better get used to walking through maps multiple times. There's quite a lot of them. With no map or fast travel, of course. Mercy is that the drops aren't at least required and barely affect stats.Unfortunately the negatives far outweight the positives.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, but also quite confused.Aesthetically very distinct, with the unique shading effects and outerworldly characters designs. Environmental design is pretty good, but gets a little stale after a while. Animations are decent. The whole game is clearly a homage to ACE's earlier works like Zenoclash, and might, for all I know, be set in the same universe.Sound design is passable. OST is good. Voice acting is decent. Story is passable. I really enjoy the characters and both Psuedo (protagonist) and The Boy (deuteragonist) are likable.Gameplay is a mixed bag. It seems very confused about what to commit to, and despite being quite elaborate it doesn't really achieve much. Enemies have different attack patterns but only very rarely force the player to actually mix things up. Blocking exists by idling, which goes completely against what the game teaches and incentivizes you to do. You can animation-cancel by dodging exactly as the strike lands which adds to the pace of the game - but again it's fairly flat and doesn't go anywhere besides just repeating itself. Parrying feels very unrewarding except for projectiles (which you get to toss back at the assailant). There is no concept of high or low attacks, nor their respective defense. Some enemies have rare attacks like jumping, which can be countered by inputting the appropriate "special move". A lot of special attacks don't seem to tie into anything; they don't deal more damage and are usually slow on the recovery. Since you can't cancel them by dodging either they just seem inferior to regular stance attacks. Stances give the player access to a lot of things: a new running attack, a new jumping attack, new directional (dodging) attacks and a new regular attack chain. None of which achieve anything but just existing. The only use I found for combining stances is because some stance might have a better variation of some attack - so you just input 1 thing from 1 stance, then swap over to the other one for your regular chain. For a game that goes so wild on the amount of different angles you'd expect it would do more with it. Combat feels as just repeating the same trick over and over and is very easy once you cross the initial barrier of acclimating yourself to it.The "ritual", a small dice game with some modifiers, is actually quite fun and a nice way to break the pace. It's fast and simple and gives the player some time to breathe. It would have served more of a purpose if the combat were actually stressful, but alas.Very ambitious and honestly fun title, but also disappointing in how little is actually achieved with what feels like a great setup for a combat system.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for the newer generation that enjoys Souls-like torment above storytelling, exploration or fun gameplay in general. The environment and presentation showcase the beloved and twisted ACE Team creativity and there are a few neat ideas, but the combat system is NOWHERE near as fun as it was in the previous games. Maybe it's the inconsistent combo-interruptions (or lack thereof), the irrationally difficult fights, or that every single encounter feels the same and they don't have that "weight" or "depth" like in the previous games..I just realised that now there are people who never played Zeno Clash 1-2 before (why? how?), and for them this game could be a decent experience, but for us, nostalgic boomers, the adventures in Zenozoik seem to have ultimately ended with Zeno Clash 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so you KNOW I would love to give this game a 10/10 GOTY. Zeno clash 1 was basically a perfect game, it was a masterpiece. But this game has some problems. Let's start off with the one that has made me want to stop playing most: Since atlus got involved in publishing the 360 edition, they've had this half in half out with anime style voiceover artists. And it just does not fit the world at all. For the original release of zeno clash one, they had probalby friends of the developers in chile doing the voices, and it matched this alien world perfectly, but the anime voice actors, it's just obnoxious. I could deal with it in ZC2 because it was only a couple of characters who you admittedly don't spend much time with unless you chose to take them with you. But in this one, your companion throughout the entire game has a shrill, ear-splitting voice. The other characters of this character's species have similarly anime voices, despite being related to the giant bird monster that talks like a bird monster in ZC 1&2. And there will be segments of the game where this little bird baby fathermother is going to go IM COLD! THE AIR IS TOO FREEZY! Every 3 seconds, it will clip out actual game dialogue, it will even play during battles or when you are doing the ritual minigame. This occurs for about a third of the game. It's barbaric. Why anyone would subject their customers to this, i don't know. It might actually violate the geneva convention. They give you an out, you have to purchase a little ugly snowsuit for your cute little bird pal, and it will shut him up about how cold it is. Thank heavens. It's just awful. I don't know why they would do that and I hope it gets patched out.Now onto the substance of the game. This is a soulsborne adaptation of the zeno clash universe. Which is fine, I hope it doesn't mean a permanent departure from the first person beatemup, but it's very fun. The combat system is about what you'd expect from this franchise, a lot of depth to it but also simple and easy to master. Very fun, the fight animations are well done, you can really feel each blow as you bash some dude in the head. People have complained about not knowing where to go, but really if you just follow wherever the fights are, it's not too difficult to know where you're going, and there is a map in the menu with your current location. Is it mwah chef's kiss perfection, probably not, but it's 100% serviceable, because the point of the gameplay in zeno clash is to take you around this alien world so you can beat the crap out of the bizarre people who live there. Which brings me to my next section: VisualsAs with literally every game ace team has put out, this game is visually very good. The character design is bizarre but fascinating as always. You can see the dadaist, bosch, and MC escher roots of whoever is the visual director come to life again. It's always a treat to enter the world of zenozoik and this is no different. They have gone with some kind of semi-cel shaded filter and it really lets the warty details of this alien world pop. Rocks resemble fused megaliths, trees and buildings have their idiosyncrasies highlighted in all their glory. If I had one complaint it's that you don't see enough architecture in this game, as the architecture being so bizarre is one of the better elements of the visual design in zeno clash 1 & 2. This is a very minor complaint, as if you are looking to walk around zenozoik and beat up its diverse and mutated inhabitants, this will scratch that itch. Other than the aforementioned voice acting issues, this game is more than fine in terms of audio. The theme of the main character, Pseudo, is especially a banger and it gets you riled up when it plays during some of the emotional battles in this game. The voice actors that are not shrill whining anime characters are very, very well done. The mammoth boss, and the two recurring traders stuck out as having very fitting and memorable voices. I like the music that plays when you are buying from a trader. The ambient noise is fine, everything about the audio is fine except the voice acting for maybe 2-3 characters. Pseudo's voice acting is great too, actually. It fits him well.There's some really wacky bugs that I just couldn't understand. For example, if you use the tether artifact on the mammoth boss, he will just rocket around the fight arena like sonic the hedgehog, glitching out until the tether breaks. Was able to replicate this a few times.The ritual system is a good idea but maybe not implemented well. The two lives thing, I could take it or leave it. The plot is fine, and it will make you soyface if you are a fan of the original since it ties into it a bit.Anyways, that said, as it is now, I have to give the game a 6/10. If you're a Zeno clash fan, yes pick this up! You'll like it even with the issues I laid out. If you're just now entering into the zeno clash franchise, I'd maybe wait until it gets patched up a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, after putting some actual time into this game, it's not worth your time or money. Wait for 75% sale. Great optimization, fluid (one on one) combat, detected my PS5 controller off the bat. Definitely not the caseThis game has MANY shortcomings. Here is a quick list : 1.) You have no idea how strong your opponent is or if you're in the right area. There is no way to gauge your opponent's strength prior to engaging and the auto-save feature is useless, therefore it forces you to constantly go back to a campfire prior to engaging unless you wish to risk getting 1-shot and starting anew at your last camp. 2.) Your levels mean nothing, adding to power or endurance does not seem to affect the damage you do or the amount of  endurance you have / Stamina. 3.) You have no map, just a very high level useless loading screen apparatus. 4.) The ritual mechanic is nigh useless, if you win, you get a very minor buff that barely affects the outcome of the fight. If you lose, it can be devastating. Again, you have no idea how many dice or rituals your opponents can play prior to fighting them. 5.) The developers seem to have a lack of imagination when it comes to fighting styles or different enemy combat mechanics, instead, they just add more people to fight in a confined space. The fighting mechanics and view are absolutely dog**** for fighting multiple mobs at the same time. 6.) When you die, you wake up at your campfire and for some reason the developers think you'll be able to fight the 2-3-4 mobs that killed you without your flasks. What's worse, I've had two occasions where I could not reach my corpse due to the area being "unplayable" at night. The voice acting is great though and so is the environment albeit the horrendous amount of invisible walls. 4/10 from me.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat feels awful, win or lose. Either I'm being shredded to pieces by enemies who attack with telegraphs so short that I can't consistently react to many of them or I feel like I'm cheesing everything to death by keeping them at range and repeatedly using special attacks that both act as a gap closer and stun them. I'm not sure if it's intended; you're clearly meant to use mobility and speed, but like...they're just attacking empty air, or not attacking at all as I jump kick, back up, jump kick, repeat.Other annoying bits include:-To get to the first boss (or at least, first enemy with a second phase), you need to go through a load screen, then walk slowly across the arena you fight them in, then watch a short cut scene, then hold enter to skip a longer cutscene. Why tho?-Nothing whatsoever is explained, and the player is expected to make impactful decisions like what base moveset you'll use before you have a chance to understand how combat works or even see all the moves associated with that moveset. -Once you do get more movesets, you have to visit a totem to change them out, and I cannot friggin find these things. They're not at every camp/bonfire, so I guess if you decide you want to use something different you're just stuck with whatever you have on or get to play backtrack simulator 9000?-The controls feel bad, jumping and attacking especially. Jumping doesn't preserve your momentum; you just stop in place and leap and it feels awkward. Attacks are just inconsistent; you'll press the button and sometimes the game just...won't. Like, standing there in the idle state, try to attack, and nothing. I have no clue why, because it works most of the time, just not all the time.-Edit 1: The first boss broke when I beat their first phase with the first-person attack mode. They regenerated their health but kept using the first phase moveset instead of doing their transition and attacking with both hands.I dunno, maybe I just suck. Take the advice from people who have more hours over mine; I'm going to stick with it and see if this is all just skill issue on my end (and update the review based on what I find). But the beginning has been deeply unpleasant to play, and I'm continuing on right now because I hope it will get better and not because I'm enjoying playing it at present.

_childDocuments_.review: fire the QA team.i genuinely believe there was a cumulative test time of less than 10 hours.one of the very few games i have had the regret of playing.but the worst of it, I don't think i single developer actually stepped in and said "hold on guys, have we considered that this game isn't actually in the least enjoyable to play?"i have never played a single game where 90% of fights you encounter is both a reskin AND a sandbag.where every area is identical to the last, with the only mechanic being opening closed paths with NOTHING else.where every enemy be it at night or day are entirely non-threatening past the first 30 minutes.this game is the epitome of going through the motions and arriving at an abysmal game.you could have removed everything except for the dice, and arrived at a game actually worth playing because that is the only part that feels like it had an ounce of thought put into it.this game is bloated beyond belief scattering mechanics around that have no real impact when roped together.writing this review hurts me greatly, because making games takes an unreal amount of money, time and effort.All three of which seems to have been squandered.game looks visually interesting, props to the art team and shader people, but that is where my praise begins and ends.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get how this game has a 95% approval rating. Maybe I'm missing something. This game feels like a jumble of ideas that are all mid to poorly executed. The only redeeming factor is the music and art style (performance on mid range PC's blows though). The combat feels sluggish, awful with most enemies feeling like brain dead punching bags. The world is awful to navigate with terrible direction and has repeating environments that give you no cues on where to go. The day/night/corpse retrieval/whatever you want to call it makes no sense at all. I guess it's supposed to mimic dark souls but it's so poorly implemented. This game tries to copy a lot of dark souls designs but the devs could not implement them in a way that makes the game more compelling. It just seems to have stats for the sake of having stats. Same with crafting, cooking and this stupid f***ing dice roll game that makes NO sense at all. It's like they were drunk when they designed this dumb ass dice game. The outcome makes no difference again because the enemy AI is so bad. Again I have to repeat this, all of these additional systems make the game worse, rather than better. If this was just a straight up brawler like the first 2 games it might have good but the devs just had to try and be derivative rather than original.I love the first two Zeno Clash games but this, this is just awful and frustrating to play. If you want a good 3rd person martial arts game get Sifu instead. If you like this game more power to you but I think there are much better action/brawler games out there. Refunded. I do hope the devs can make more games based in the Zeno Clash universe but please ACE go back to your roots and cut out all souls stuff because it just doesn't work here.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly, truly, truly a gem. It can't be overstated how bold ACE Team's attempts are each and every time they try to deliver something new, different and untapped to us fans. Sure, it doesn't always work out to the full extent, but in a world where regurgitation in all forms of entertainment media became a devil safe bet, I will always support those who strive to break through the monotony. The gameplay offers a wide variety of different stances and special attacks which you can freely combine into all forms of combos to dominate the various battlefields. Single-target, area-damage, teleporting ninja! Even the dice-game attached to the battles, "The Ritual" as it were, did not get on my nerves as initially suspected.The world, as is common with ACE Team's games, is understatedly unique, vibrant and full of secrets and mystery. A lore that tries to buck all clichés and introduce something distinctive, yes maybe even a little bit quirky and eccentric! But this is why I love their games. It has tons of jank, tons of bugs, but I think at this point, I wouldn't have it any other way. If this is the cost to get games with their very own characteristic and soul, unrepeatable and idiosyncratic, then this is how it's gotta be.And again I have to say, there is something uncustomary going on here with ACE Team's soundtracks. Whoever does those, please give this person more attention. Eternal Cylinder had this going for it aswell, it's out of this world.  Bliss! Definitely something I will listen to in my spare time. But then comes the voice work. What a thoroughly insane undertaking. This is Triple-AAA level of voice work for SOME characters, but then a lot of mid-tier work for others. The main character clearly and audibly stands out among the pack, closely followed by the engrossing "Boy". What a cute little character! The random banter and conversations that appeared all throughout the game brought me close to these endearing personalities, wanted me to care and - and it did work on me without the shadow of a doubt ...   - It is definitely the first Zeno game that had me emotional, I won't lie.Definitely a must buy for people who want to try something original, albeit quirky and mesmerizingly profound.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BE FOOLED BY THE ABUNDANCE OF ONE-SENTENCE REVIEWS.  THIS IS NOT A SOULS-LIKE.Clash is an adventure game that preempts fights with major characters with a dice game (there's lore for this for some reason), and the combat is rather bland compared to significantly better games.  The combat has you spamming the same combo with the inclusion of a one-button special.  You dodge attacks typically and attacks are easily telegraphed so if you just distance yourself or strafe around, you just won't get hit by enemies in the early fights.  "So easy it's boring" is how I'd describe the combat.  It's listed as a Souls-like but it is not one.  It's really a beat-em-up with a simple dodge mechanic borrowed from Souls-likes.  The "big finish" is the meter that fills that puts you in first-person mode and lets you box your opponent, which is satisfying the first two or three times, but once you realize you're still just spamming combos in this mode just as you were in the third-person view, it loses its luster quick.The art style is fine but it is done zero favors by the cluttered, ugly environments that look like pieces of different game worlds patched together awkwardly.  The world is too busy and the world objects aren't cohesive enough to make it all make sense, so large chunks of the world end up looking like balled-up chunks of newspaper.The writing for the first area of the game, what little there is, is cheesy and bland.  It's basically a Spaghetti Western, and that's fine, it's just odd and unconvincing in its setting.I don't know what's with all the positive one-sentence reviews with this game, but it definitely doesn't warrant its Overwhelmingly Positive score.  Is it a bad game?  Not really.  It's effectively just bland and mediocre in all aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of my eagerness to derive pleasure from the offerings of "Clash: Artifacts of Chaos," it is incumbent upon me to disillusion myself and convey to both consumers and the development team my profound disappointment with the product. Evidently, the game's elongated duration is needlessly achieved through the utilization of recycled adversaries, an overabundance of locked pathways and doors, and seemingly nonsensical obstacles. How can a video game encourage players to explore the environment for experience points and resource gathering, yet exhibit an indifferent attitude towards populating the area with inaccessible doorways? It is an act of sheer madness, I must declare.Another notable flaw in this game lies in the dearth of comprehensive quality assurance testing that it underwent. In fact, I was compelled to cease playing entirely when, upon reaching the final boss, I was unexpectedly subjected to the commencement of the opening cutscene due to a technical failure or some other such mishap. Consequently, I was compelled to recommence the game from the very beginning, bereft of any prospect of reloading a saved position. Furthermore, there exist several locations within the game where players may become permanently trapped, and the ritual artifacts frequently suffer from glitches arising from technical or logical oversights.Undeniably, the underlying planning of what could have been a masterpiece exhibited a multitude of commendable ideas and ambitious aspirations. However, it is untenable to release a product that overtly relies on its fluid combat, captivating atmosphere, and intriguing characters while concurrently expecting consumers to disregard the monotonous repetition, game-breaking technical flaws, and an overall deficiency in refinement. Thankfully, ongoing efforts to debug and update the game provide potential buyers with a glimmer of hope. Nonetheless, it is imperative for prospective buyers to exercise caution, as this game stands as a hit-or-miss endeavor. Furthermore, it is saddening that the aforementioned issues primarily stem from a lack of foresight and proficient programming.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but it is a very love it or hate it kind of experience.The whole game revolves around being in this relative open world filled with shortcuts and there's a lot of backtracking to areas you've already been. The game is also quite challenging with no option to turn down the difficulty, and the combat -while good-, also has a learning curve; it takes a while until you get really good at it or you do any damage to enemies. It would've been nice to have some modular difficulty settings or more control over the actual challenge of the experience.I personally don't like the level design a lot, I find it very restrictive for the type of open world the game is trying to be, there are a lot of shorcuts, but the game uses a similar system to that of the Souls series so that, when you inevitably die, you respawn in the last checkpoint (or camp) this serve as this game's version of bonfires, you can customize your moves and sleep through the night.The night is a catch in this game that is a really cool system, but I think it could've been improved a bit, basically the way it works is that you turn into another version of yourself when you die, or wait till night in the encampments, if you die, you have to track your body where you got killed and revive as yourself in the day... but if you wait for the night you can just explore around without worrying about retrieving your body.Playing during the night allows you to access to different parts of the game that you wouldn't otherwise be allowed to access when playing during the daytime, then you can fight a special enemy in those areas during the night in order to open that area for your character during the day.Is a good system, albeit a bit of a convoluted one to explain, but I think it would've been better if -outside of combat-, you could switch between night and day on the fly, that could've helped the game's pacing and exploration. It's good.There's also NG+ which is a nice feature, but according to the devs themselves -after I politely asked them-, they don't even know if you can NG++ this title, because "they didn't tested it".Even then though, I think is a nice game and most people -sadly- won't even play the game through NG+, most people just finish the game and move on, but I personally like that the game mode is there for people like me who do enjoy replaying this titles.The game also has a cool dice game that's entirely optional but you can trigger it when before an encounter to give yourself advantages as you fight enemies, it's a good system.The game has crafting and even flasks that you can create with animals and plants and the like, there's also vendors that trade armor for materials, but some of these materials are very finnicky to get, almost to the point where they feel a bit scripted.I like the main two characters of the story, but overall, I didn't really care much about the story, I look at it as a backdrop for the gameplay to take place in, and while I do like the interaction between the main character and the bird like boy creature he has, there are other elements of the story I couldn't have care less about.Even then, really nice game, but beware, it might be for you or not at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game! The art style and music are great. I loved just listening to music playing. Pseudo's main theme being my favorite. _childDocuments_.review: Clash is a very unique game, which managed to positively surprise me multiple times throughout the ~14 h it takes to finish the story. The focus of the game is the fighting system, which is fleshed-out and varied both in terms of moveset and enemy variety. Exploration is rewarded with materials for weapons (which i didn't use) and upgrade materials for your skills. It is possible to upgrade multiple ones to the lower tiers before deciding on which to upgrade fully. Within the first playthough, it is not possible to become too overpowered, which i also appreciated. The general difficulty is strongly dependent on learning your moveset, which can be customized with two styles and three special attacks. I couldn't hit the parry timings for some attacks, but all encounters were manageable.Dying or sleeping sets you into night mode, in which different enemies and repeats of defeated bosses spawn. Additionally, sets of night-only armour can be found. You can also wake up from the menu and spawn back at camp in this mode, which cuts down on backtracking immensely.Despite most of the reviews, it is not a soulslike. You get up to three heals (one to start out), and dying i night form is a game over. There is no roll, and combos depend on acting when you hit the enemy. RPG elements are also absent beyond level-ups allowing you to allocate three points to four skills. The world is also not nearly as open, with many invisible walls and killplanes. This does not detract from the game, unless you come in with the expectation of jumping on things and over barriers. Jumps serve as a gap closer in combat and for some signposted places in the world.The story was neat, but feels unfinished. It still manages to present some concepts which are exotic enough to remain interesting for the runtime and is not in thematic conflict with a game about beating various opponents to death, which i appreciate. In some areas i got stuck in geometry after being thrown by enemies and using attacks that move you, and in one small region i occasionally had stuttering. Otherwise, there were no glaring technical issues besides sometimes a third moveset being equipped after obtaining it. I can very much recommend Clash and find it somewhat sad that it has so few reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It has innovative and unique gameplay mechanics such as a first person feature allowing you to do extra damage along with cutscene moves in some cases, as well as a sort of minigame type thing where you fight against whether you get a positive or a negative, this made for some fun strategizing both inside and outside the actual fighting part of the game. While I liked the direction the fighting mechanics went it ended up falling flat for me, it was janky and often times pretty glitchy. Nonetheless, fights were fun and the difficulty was at a pretty standard level with most bosses taking a few tries at least to defeat. But, this also made for a (definitely not on purpose) side of the game that I really enjoyed. Due to how janky and weird it was to play I managed to figure out several ways to defeat bosses by getting them stuck or abusing certain combos by mapping them to specific buttons. This was very fun for me as I am horrid at these types of games so figuring out how I would cheese the next boss was fun. The art direction of the game, including character design, GUI, etc was very interesting and the absurdness of all of it was fun and enjoyable to look at during my playthrough. However, the map design was probably one of the worst aspects of this game. While it was good and exploring was something you are encouraged to do multiple times through different paths and areas only accessed through certain conditions, it was confusing what areas were meant to be accessible and what wasn't. Some areas looked very similar so there were several times I would be going in circles expecting something new to show up only to find out I was still within the same path. The music varied greatly in my opinion, but I am also the only person who listens to music 24 hours a day but can't tell you what sound is a guitar and what sound is a drum. Sometimes the game would have scary and exciting music in a completely random and barren part of the map, whilst other times you would barely hear any at all while fighting a boss. In general, I loved some areas themes while others were just 'alright'. While we're on the topic of sounds the voice acting is also a strong suit. Almost every characters voice is emotive and plays well into the current scene and actions going on. Finally, one of the best parts of this game: the writing. The character development of the two main characters Psuedo and The Boy (If I recall correctly?) was a highlight watching and finding out about throughout my time playing the game. The small lines of dialogue the two have randomly, albeit it annoying at times, is enjoyable and compelling to listen to. Overall, this game has some great pieces from gameplay mechanics, to art direction, animations, writing, etc but also falls flat in certain areas such as the fighting and map design. (ps: game only took me about 17 hours to finish, I left it on overnight once)

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda liked this game. Very unique artstyle and uniquely designed characters, monsters and NPC's. Combat is decent, with focus on martial arts. Story was pretty good and I liked the relationship between man and "the boy". The biggest downside I found is the constant invisible walls everywhere. The game is very linear with only one choice of which of the two available areas you want to go first (the other will be afterwards regardless), which happens around mid-game.Despite its "cartoony" artstyle, the graphics were pretty demanding on 4k with max settings even on high-end hardware, with some dips in fps and plenty of microstutters when running through areas.Overall i'd recommend this for what it is, and its decent price.

_childDocuments_.review: not perfect, but a worthy sequel of sorts to the now-classic Zeno Clash games! Patricio Meneses' score is excellent as always toocombat is solid & satisfying, however the endgame gets very easy. however it's pretty satisfying smashing enemies that used to be a PITA!the ritual mechanic is fun, but it's a shame enemies never invoke it on the player, & later in the game it's very difficult to winanother positive is great art and worldbuilding as always! while it's a bit "sanitized" vs. the other two Zeno Clash games, it still very much feels like Zenozoikthe map is large and doesn't have any fast travel, but it's easy and fun to traverse However navigation can be confusing & needs better signposting, I got lost in some areas for ages before finding the obvious-in-hindsight way forward.there's also a lot of backtracking, especially in the later part of the game and it gets very tiring - especially when getting lost on where to go! Don't 100% finding every night armor piece etc. unless you're an achievement hunter, it only adds to the fatiguethe plot is a bit thin and there's large chunks of gameplay before the story moves forward, but it's enough to keep things moving.there's also some unfortunate bugs such as prompts or bosses not appearing, necessitating a save reload or sleeping/waking up to reload the worldI could go on, but definitely recommended when on sale - Clash has its flaws, but it's still a lot of fun and the land of Zenozoik is endlessly captivating!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the game had some cool ideas, specifically around the ritual combat. I loved the idea of combining gambling with combat incentives and punishments. If you are looking for something a bit different than your standard single player game this one is worth a shot. With that being said I will say the game play gets somewhat repetitive and I find the art style loses its magic pretty quick. This might just be my own fault but I found the environments to be very similar through out most of the early game causing me to get lost and give the feeling of running in circles. I also found the day and night cycle to be a bit tedious. Overall my final thoughts in this one are positive but I would recommend putting this game on your wishlist and wait to pick it up on the low.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a unique personality that can be hard to get on with at first. The combat mechanics are really fun and they have a flow to them that is unlike most other games out there, but in a way that is very rewarding once you get it down. The game is not good at explaining itself though, and trying to get to grips with everything at the start can be troublesome. But it’s definitely worth pushing through to understand the kind of mindset it expects from the player. It’s also got a fantastic aesthetic, and a really cool and surreal setting full of weird characters and environments that are a joy to explore. It’s a great follow-up to the Zeno Clash games that evolves and deepens what those games were attempting really well.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: My short review would be that, despite the each gameplay element (combat, level design, dice roll mini game, upgrades) has something more to be desired, as a whole package, it’s a weird and funky experience that not many other games can provide. Such a shame that this game flew over the radar of so-called “double A experiment” enthusiasts. Also, can I say the music carried the game really hard?
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, there's a lot wrong with it. Everything from animations being bugged to a huge lack of tutorial/explanation for any of the mechanics to the game just slowing to an absolute halt to pad out the runtime. But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I love it. Pseudo is going to go down as one of the protagonists that I love for at least the next decade. The story (so far) is great. The thing that really snagged me is the art style. I don't think I've ever seen a game that has this look.I just really wish things weren't so slow. Finding your way is one thing, but constantly having to loop around every five seconds because you can't remember which of the 100 branching paths leads to the objective is just annoying. Couple this with bugged out animations (getting stuck inside Pseudo's body for example and having to reset) and it just becomes a headache.Once you get a handle on the combat, it feels really good. It felt a bit different at first, because I can't think of a game that utilizes this kind of combat (outside of Sifu, but Sifu is it's own beast.)  Overall, I feel like I'll end up doing multiple runs through the game, though I think there's only technically one ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: While the games run time may be short It is a beautiful experience in a rather unique world with a great combat system & it deserves more recognition that it is getting. At first I was put of by how difficult the fights seem to be but as time went on things got more manageable so if like me you struggle at the start do not be put off as the combat in this game is very fun and rewarding once you get used to it.The story is pretty simple for the most part but the world of the game itself follows a rule, "the one law" where if you are challenged to the game the one law presides over you MUST take part and answer the challenge. This take place before any fight where you can invoke the one law and force your opponent to sit down and play a fun little game of dice. WITH CONSEQUENCES! (Though if you are boring you can auto resolve the game)Before the dice game begins your enemy will select a relic that will take effect if they win, Effects like, getting stung by wasps constantly if you ever stop moving, you must drink poison before the fight begins, get smashed over the head with a big wooden stick before the fight begins, Get tethered to the ground for the entire fight, the list goes on. Once your opponent has picked there win condition relic you can than do the same and select a relic you own that give the enemy a negative effect if you win the game. once a winner has been decided, the winners relic effect takes place and the fight begins.Speaking of fighting there are 3 Initial fighting styles to choose from to begin with but as you explore the world you can find the other 2 styles you did not select and a wide variety of other styles you can find to be used in combat. these can vary from lightning fast strikes and kicks to big heavy blows and body checks so there is bound to be a style you prefer hidden somewhere out in the world. During combat you will be able to hot-swap between 2 fighting styles you have selected at the pres of a button to suit however you want to approach a fight at any given moment. this also extends to special attacks that you can have 3 equiped at once that are sepperate from you fighting styles with simple forward, back or neutral inputs to execute them so pick what you like and go ham. and speaking of going ham Pseudo has a fury state he build up during combat and once it is used the game will go into fist person mode where you will absolutely wail on a target with succesive punches, and after landing so many will go into a unique finisher for every opponent in the game.there is also gear to collect and craft stats and upgrades to help Pseudo grow on there journey as well as the ability to mix potions at camps to refill & increase effectivness by mixing in various plants and wildlife.If this all sounds like its fun that's because it is! I have not covered everything because I don't want to spoil any surprises but if it seems like you might like it give it a go, I promise you wont find many games that are quite like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a straight recommend tbh. If the art style looks good to you then just get it because it is worth it just to see the wild stuff that goes on and it is all rendered wonderfully. It is a game of very lofty ambitions and it fails at atleast half of what it tries to do- but you have to respect the love that has gone in to this project. I really wish some gameplay decisions were a bit more 'normal' for want of a better word. Sometimes it frustrates because they come up with some idiosyncratic solution to a gameplay design problem that has been solved long ago- just for the sake of being wierd. VERY ALMOST THE BEST SOULSLIKE OUTSIDE DARKSOULS (not saying much)
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 9/10 game. The world was great and I really liked Pseudo's character. The martial arts system was really fun. I hope they expand upon the martials arts system in future games. I tried out Zeno Clash 1 and 2  last week and they both were pretty good but this game is definitely a massive step up in story and gameplay. I would strongly recommend this game.As for issues I ran into, there are some bugs with climbing stuff and getting stuck in walls but none were game breaking. I crashed twice in my playthrough which was a bit more of an issue but I did not lose much progress in either instance. I have 2 suggestions for the developers. First please add fast travel in future titles. It was not enjoyable for me to spend 2 hours running back through areas I had before. Second adding multiplayer in a similar future game like in Zeno Clash 2 did would be amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10... This game was a trip and an adventure. Clash: AoC is an inspired take on the souls-like genre set in the charming word of Zeno Clash. I was stunned to learn about this game so late since I enjoy both of those things quite a bit. There are times where the dialogue seems a bit Joss Whedon "erm... that just happened", but the characters were overall fun and had distinct personalities, even the minor bosses. Most mechanics in the game rely on elements that players will find familiar, while also adding intuitive new features that enrich the experience. Clash is a metroidvania souls-like that does things it's own way and does it well."You will learn to fear me... I'm almost certain of it"
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: A much better experience than I was expecting from this game. The art direction, the music, the story and the gameplay in this are all absolutely spectacular. I came into this expecting to be bashing heads in, but was pleasantly surprised by the depth of the characters, the extensive story and the beautiful music that accompanies you along your journey through this wacky and wonderful world. A hidden little gem here. Beautifully made.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: High level AA gaming. There is no fast travel so keep your brain on when navigating or you will divebomb the pacing of your experience. I got stuck on geometry about five times so you may encounter a bit of jank. The game might feel about 2 hours too long to the average player but I had a great time. Blocking and Dodging are both very viable defense options and the enemies can hit each other. No fight in the game is unfair and you can progress very rapidly if you play well. I had a great time overall and believe this entry is punching well above its weight.
_childDocuments_.name: Clash: Artifacts of Chaos

_childDocuments_.review: I have played this game for 18 hours. And I love it. However, it's important to mention that every individual's enjoyment from this game will vary depending on how much effort they want to put in this game.About 5 hours into the game I found a ranged technique which allowed me to cheese multiple opponents. Initially I loved it cause it allowed me to progress quickly through the game, but now, 18 hours in, I hate it because I have invested figurines in it and it's actually less fun.I am now restarting the game to learn to play it properly (with parries and dodge-attacks).If there is 1 thing to fix in this game it is to add practice mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Clash is a unique experience that is very well made. The story is engaging. The more you play the more you become attached to the characters.The world is very vibrant and full of details, also fairly huge. The game can be considered linear with how you progress through the different areas, you unlock areas and shortcuts that connect previous unlocked areas and so on. Some areas can be hard to navigate and you may lose your path, there is a map but it is not detailed and simple.There is also night and day, you wake up at night to traverse areas you cannot cross in the day. You also fight different variation of enemies in the night.The combat is pretty good with the different fighting stances you unlock throughout the game, there are also special moves you can use and ultimate mode where you punch your foes in first person and then finishes with a cool animation. Also combat is smooth and fast paced. There are also different armors and weapons you can use, weapons can be slow but some of them land huge damage. In addition, weapons break after their durability is depleted.The game is not particularly difficult, some fights can be a bit challenging since you are mostly faced with multiple enemies at once, but nothing impossible. It has the Souls-like tag, but you can think of it as the light version of what a souls-like is. When you sleep (a tent is used as save point), not all enemies re-spawn, only regular enemies do, but the stronger enemies don't.Enemy variety is decent and fun to tackle each enemy differently. The art style is the most unique feature of the game and while it can be pretty weird, you will grow fund of it and actually like the characters.Totally recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting things can happen when the dev team throws out the modern gaming rule book. Clash is a very interesting game that feels like a game from 15 years ago. The game definitely has some problems, but some of those problems are what make it interesting and an unique in the modernize gaming space.First, the great. The visuals are simply outstanding, from character design to art direction, the game is simply beautiful to look at, filled with creatures so strange that you've never seen anything like it. The music is also outstanding, it has a fantastic musical score.  The characters and voice acting are wonderful and you will fall in love with Pseudo and the Boy.  It's the characters, world, and story that are going to hook you the most.The game play itself is good. This is a beat'em up. Game play revolves around carefully timed attacks,dodges, and blocks. Combat feels pretty solid, with a pacing more attune to the the methodical combat of a Souls Game. There are some strange choices.  The opening tutorial really doesn't help much either. It takes time to get use to the combat.The dice game is more of  hindrance and I found my self simply not playing it. Some times there are long chunks of game play time where you go long stretches without fighting. The game play systems can easily be abused to make quite a bit of the fighting fairly easy.The game has barely any in-game map, and doesn't hold your hand.   Combined with the maze like nature of the open world, figuring out where to go next is actually the hardest part of the game. You can wind up in areas with powerful enemies that you aren't strong enough to deal with, and then the game can be very difficult, but that simply means you are in the wrong place and should backtrack. If you can find things in the intended order, this game is not that difficult.There are some minor bugs in the UI, and the UI and menu system are on whole terrible. You can simply ignore and not use several gameplay systems like crafting and the dice game.  Still, if you give Clash a chance, and really spend  about 5 hours with it, you'll start to get a feel for it's gameplay and visual language. You'll come to love the characters, and be interested in the world and the story. Clash is not a perfect game, but despite it's flaws, it has a ton of heart.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Clash is another great entry in the Zeno Clash series that only manages to be held back by some dated design choices.I'm a huge fan of Zeno Clash and Zeno Clash 2. The world of Zenozoik and the overarching story is both compelling and unique, and made me follow everything that ACE TEAM puts out super closely. Clash is the first of the games to take place in a different era entirely (although still within Zenozoik), and I wasn't as in love with the story as I was with the first two, but it was still very fun and thematic for the universe.The game is also the first of the three to make the switch to third person, as well as implementing a far more in-depth combat system. Previously, the combat was fun, simple and servicable and felt primarily like a vehicle to experience the world and the story. In Clash, the combat is a complex and sometimes difficult stance/combo system that feels much more akin to a fighting game. It's still accessible and fun, but wildly different. My main issue with the game is hard to put into words - the best way I can put it is that many aspects of it feel like a game that came out 5-10 years ago. There are mechanics and design choices at play that just feel dated and odd in a modern game. For instance, there is no inventory sorting, so even if you have full sets of matching gear, they'll be spread about based on when you picked them up - rather than having sets together, or same-slot items together, etc. You can rebind keys, but not all keys, so some commonly used mechanics are stuck to the default, for some reason. The entire game is one big map you unlock, and you can have it seamless, but it's off by default, and has serious performance issues if you don't split it up into chunks that each need a loading screen, which is not an optimization issue we should be having in a game that has a relatively low graphics.My only other nitpick is that the game doesn't really feel as surreal as its predecessors. There were no environments that blew me away or felt truly alien. Another reviewer said it best when they said that it didn't seem that unique, with some things even feeling familiar. It felt a lot more like a fantasy game than the previously mind-blowing surrealism of Zeno Clash and Zeno Clash 2. Overall, this is a great, fun game. The issues don't keep it from being an unenjoyable experience, and if you liked the first two games, chances are you will enjoy this one.
