_childDocuments_.review: I think that this game is well made and the combat is also fun but it was clear from the very start that this is essentially a grinding game. I had to do the tutorial(!) dungeon 3(!!!) times in order to unlock the next stage (=have to use abilities to unlock levels to unlock stars to unlock gates). It didnt' feel that bad because it taught me how to effectively use the ability of my charcter but imagine playing Diablo 2 in the beginning and you'd have to mindlessly do the starting cave with the goblins three times in a row.I distinctly remember back when I was a child that I even got annoyed looking for the last goblin for maybe a minute. This game goes all in, it makes you do entire dungeons many times just to unlock meaningless stars which are the equivalent of a time gate on the next content. Because I'm level 6 and the dungeon was level 3 but I simply have to keep farming more stars.I could theoretically forgive this and keep playing it for the gameplay itself but on top of everything this is an ARPG...without any items. I mean normally I would say that getting item drops is at least 50% of the fun of an ARPG. Then on top of *that* there is also honestly not really a story here. I mean sure, there's some infestation of mushrooms and I have to gather all the crystals to make the world nice again. This is on the level of a flash game, this is not a story. Maybe this would be enough for kids and in their defense this game does look like a kids game. But I was also a kid when I played Diablo 2.. so I don't really see a full excuse here.So pros:+ Good combat+ Good graphics/style+ Grinding, even at the tutorial level+ No items+ No storyBottom line for me is that I'm not giving a positive vote because while it's obviously a well made game, I already feel this uncomfortable feeling above my stomach that feels like I'm wasting my time on an epic level if I kept playing this. There is no payoff with the story, no payoff with items and no not really a payoff with character levels or epic abilities (ala skill trees) either. In comparison I just finished the warhammer 40k  martyr game and while it was only an average game in total, at least it had all the components of a real arpg and a very cool story and item looting and character building.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah this one's gonna be a no for me chief.Nobody Saves the world is a top down adventure game where you can switch between different forms to gain new abilities inside and outside of battle. The artstyle and overall tone of the game is very appealing but the gameplay has some issues.I started off playing Multiplayer with one of me lads and I had a blast... for the first 1 or 2 hours. After you unlock a few forms by completing quests as other forms, the sheer size of the game starts to take effect. All of a sudden you're unlocking way too many forms way too quickly and you have to balance, upgrade, and customize all of them between 2 people. It just ended up being too much for me.Switching to single player provided an opposite issue, because the gameplay got stale QUICKLY. Combat basically boils down to holding down an attack button until the bad people fall over, barely requiring any other sort of input from the player. And there's also the issue of some forms just becoming obsolete when you gain the ability to customize them. Now you can take an ability from one form and give it to a different form completely taking away what made that form unique. With this system why would you even bother playing as all the different forms aside from using them to unlocking more forms that you might ALSO not use at all.Maybe this is just a matter if taste, maybe I need to spend more time on it, but as it stands I don't see myself wanting to go back anytime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where the devs managed to crack the code for pure fun. I love the art style and the music is BANGIN'!! But the best part of all is the ability to mix and match active/passive abilities between different forms. The mix and match mechanic of different forms is fun and adaptable to different situations/playstyles, but the level up mechanic for the forms requires you to use specific combinations if you want to improve the forms, which I found a bit restrictive. They do have some dungeons where the form leveling is turned off, meaning there’s no incentive not to use your preferred combos, but I still think they didn’t really find a good balance between forcing the player out of their comfort zone and giving them the freedom to play as they wanted to. _childDocuments_.review: A fun top-down hack-n-slash action game with a wacky asthetic.If you watched the trailer, you'll already know if you'll like this game or not. It's a funny, wacky little action game with about 10-20h of content, depending on how much non-mainquest stuff you do.If you're on the fence and don't mind using a gamepad, you should buy it.Here's some responses to the complaints other reviewers have made. Feel free to skip :)These are my personal experiences, so ymmv.As mentioned, you WILL want to use a gamepad (any model will probably do). I started using one a few years ago, due to RSI in my fingers from decades of pc gaming, so the shoddy kbm controls didn't bother me at all.The porting job they did is ok, but it lacks some of the usual pc-specific features you usually expect from a title on steam, like fullscreen borderless (for some reason).Also, the grind others are talking about is completely honestly no big deal at all. Yes, there is a very small bit of it in the mid-game to unlock the other half of the forms, I just re-ran a few already cleared dungeons.The the level-synching of dungeons and open world areas is also not a big deal. The game syncs areas only in certain intervals, so if you keep playing you will eventually outlevel most dungeons and make them trivial, if that's what you're after. Also, you can buy and equip the money+ ability and later buy all the stat-buffs from the vendor. These are never compensated for by the level sync, so is pure power for you.In truth, though, with only a few exceptions all the dungeons are fairly easy as long as you set up your forms right. Sure, you can overcome all the game's challenges by skill, but the right abilities slotted into the right forms will do the job much better. I cleared every single dungeon and only had trouble with 2 of them, and I'm definitely NOT very good at dodging or timing (I mostly play colony sims).

Moreover during late game some combos are out right broken as I found myself just overhealing all the damage received.But this all did not take away from fun in this game as It was still very enjoyable to slaughter hoards of enemies.Graphics are simple yet still pleasant to look at and the game runs extremely smoothAll the monsters and npc's have fun designs and the story is interesting enough to keep you going but the gameplay is definitely where the team focus was.Recommend this game for everyone who enjoys dungeon crawler type of minigames.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game for the right person.Nobody Saves the World is a grind-based progression game with quirky characters and eccentric humor. It may not tell the most complicated story, but the writing is bound to pull a laugh. The core gameplay involves mixing and matching abilities from over a dozen forms to traverse an explorable map and procedurally generated dungeons. Some would consider the game's biggest selling point as its biggest flaw. You unlock new forms and upgrade existing ones by progressing through a massive list of quests, most of which involve killing a number of enemies in specific ways using certain abilities. This is always encouraging you to try out new unique combinations from thousands of options. What may feel grindy for some feels fun through-and-through for others. The more quests you complete, the higher your level and base stats rise. Maximum satisfaction for every accomplishment through its roughly 35 hours of gameplay if you include its new game plus mode.There are a couple issues relating to unfair enemy combinations in dungeons with particular game modifiers, and a few of the escort related side quests were not well designed, but nothing truly took away from the core experience.If you like leveling and progression systems, and can appreciate a cheesy joke, give this one a shot.

The NPCs even react to your forms in different ways and i liked that.The game can be a bit grindy if you want to get S rank on all forms especially the later quests from B to S, but hey more fun gameplay.Had some mix and matching of passive abilities and active abilities from the other forms on your favorite form.Really glad i bought this not just to support the developers but to have fun with the game. _childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for December 2023, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before January 2nd, 2023, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Achievement hunting the game. You know what’s better than Achievements, lots of them, and in quest form, with multiple different characters, and abilities that you’ll have to use to complete the quests.  You then tie the completion of those achievements into progression in the game, so players are constantly pushed to beat more of the game’s meta quests.   And while this sounds like a sick fantasy of people who care about achievements too much (which I do)... it’s also how Nobody Saves the World works.  Players will change their form to use different abilities and constantly switch what attacks they’re using so they can beat these mini-quests.  In addition, the game has an interesting and often funny story.  There’s a lot to do in the game, taking about 20 hours for me to beat and I was having a great time throughout. Still, this is very meta quest and achievement style gameplay, so players who want to focus on the large epic journey and get annoyed by achievements in games should steer clear, that’s most of what the game does.  The art style is a take-or-leave-it number, and while I like it, it took me a while to get comfortable with those empty eyes. Pick this up if, I keep saying it, but if you like metagaming.  This was an engaging title, and I even picked it up myself because I wanted to play the whole thing after seeing it on Game Pass, but I’m also thrilled more people will get the chance to check this out. _childDocuments_.review: Nobody Saves the World is a well-animated game that is best served up as a coop experience. The coop is fairly seamless and the entire game can be completed with a friend. The variety of classes as well as the subquests each class gets provides a lot of play time (I was close to about 24 hours when I finished the game, though I could have easily stretched it to ~30 hours if I went full completionist on this game).My only gripes with the game are the UI - you have a radial wheel that you use to swap between the classes/jobs, but there are more classes in the game than selections on the wheel. Unless I'm missing something, there is  to assign which class shows up on the wheel. So if you have a perfect radial menu setup and have to swap to, say, the Rat job to complete an optional sidequest? Uh oh, better hope whatever it replaced wasn't important! It seems sort of random which one it might replace, too. There's no discernible logic there. Similarly, you cannot view quests for other classes unless you're currently that class. As you'd guess, this compounds the annoyance that is the radial wheel so if you want to set up skills on a class - either passive or active skills - you'll need to swap to that class and start assigning stuff.Thankfully these are easily overlooked by the gameplay and lighthearted storytelling. Good amount of content to work with and a great game to span multiple game sessions. Overall I recommend this title at the current price and look forward to playing DLC in the future.Easy 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody Saves The World is a top-down action adventure game. Players take on the role of a hueless "nobody" with a magic wand which allow him to transform into a rat, an archer, a bodybuilder, a necromancer, even a dragon. A total of 19 forms are offered to players with every each of them contain their own unique way to fight ferocious foes. As you complete quests and explore the world to level up all the forms, you can unlock more abilities/passives for customization. Select a preferred form, make a build around said form, and you may triumph in battles against the Corruption, ultimately saving the world! From metroidvania to action RPG, the devs of Guacamelee successfully pull out another great game. The character builds are the star of the show. The open world and many little funny encounters elevate the delightful experience. Though personally I do have some gripes about some features, I still recommend Nobody Save The World.Again, the star of the show. 19 forms, 4 active abilities slots and 4 passives slots provide you with utmost freedom to create your own builds with each characters. Every form offers you a passive and 3 original active abilities as you level up. These abilities can be replaced with those from other forms to create more interesting interactions. Wanna make the ultimate summoner? Pick The Magician equipped with Hat Trick(Summon rabbit, occasionally tiger), Zombite(Infect enemies and turn them into zombies when death), Summon Demon(Summon demon from corpses), and Blood Pact(Heal familiar when you attack). By doing so you already have a solid loop for creating your long-lasting army, and yet you still have two passive slots to add on either more utility or more aggressive approach(Form-specific passive is locked and cannot be switched). My favorite two builds are what I called "Passive-aggressive Ghost" with damaging aura that can inflict poison, stun and fear all the while can be invincible, can both heal and deal damage with light aura; and "Care-free-chad Bodybuilder" who can Tokyo-Drift the arena, slowing and bumping enemies onto walls in the meantime healing and recovering mana when he attacks.Nobody Saves The World offers various quests to fulfill your sense of completion. Quests can be divided into three categories: form-related, side-quests, and repeatable. Form-related quests are introduction for newly-unlocked form to help the players understand the basics of the form in question. Later on as players level up, these quests will offer some official abilities combo to give players a taste of how each form benefit more from specific types of abilities; Side-quests are the delightful cherry on top of the interesting open world. They give charm to the zone they are in, like the one in Mutant Town, where you need to help the rogue buy more than one dagger from a mutant merchant. The funny part is that this merchant will commentate on your form differently depending on it being human or not. This is a tiny thing but it add so much personality to the world; lastly, repeatable quests are the level fodders that allow you to increase the general level faster, by just playing the game. There is no need to farm for it.→Dialogues are fun to read.→Secrets all over the world.→Dungeons have distinct visual designs.→Soundtrack is bopping.→Interesting enemies design.→Under-leveled won`t detriment gameplay too much. _childDocuments_.review: Took me 14 hours to beat while also spending a decent amount of time leveling and getting 100% on each of the guilds. I enjoyed the music, writing, progression mechanics, and visual aesthetics, but the game play is pretty badly lacking, especially for mouse and keyboard users. It uses the direction you are facing as opposed to twin stick aiming for some reason and there is no mouse support, even in menus. That said, I got used to it, but I think I would have enjoyed the game more if it weren't for this moderate annoyance. The biggest issue I had was swapping forms, as the quick swap menu is borderline unusable on keyboard. Having to constantly hop back into the menu every so often got to be a moderate pain.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Saves the World

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the most well rounded games i've played on steam in many years. Ticks a lot of boxes if you are into this genre, humor is simple and fun. Combat is responsive and simple , a bunch of enemy types and a couple of bosses to learn. Music flows well with the game and keeps the charisma of the scenery. Loads of characters to progress through and abilities to figure out. Overall just an absolute rock and or stone of a game. One of the downfall's would certainly be the design behind basically needing a gamepad, but I can speak to the fact that I did use a keyboard only for the first couple of hours and its completely do-able, I think the issue comes in where we are hardwired to use a keyboard AND mouse in PC gaming so for most people adapting to that style isn't going to fly. Once again you can play the game completely fine on keyboard, but gamepad just clearly feels like the design and is much more comfortable. As a side note, I do hope there can be some fun added content to the game, but for the price of the base game , you will get enough hours to justify it .

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, but there are so many small gripes that add up to my decision to leave it.In shortFirst 2-3 hours of game are fantastic - the humour, the locations, mechanics, everything feels like new.Past that time schematics in gameplay rear their ugly head. Basically after you're done with initial charm, you're left with repetitive gameplay that's similar to those found on Android games - you know, do a quest, get some fast XP, etc.I 100% agree with a review by herbesdeprovence, you can find it under negative ones.Imagine that - you have many forms that you can play as and switch them at any time. Ok, but you need to grind every one of those separately. Pointless waste of time.Later on you have an option to mix & match abilities from different classes and do some build optimization but I mean... it's not an action RPG, it's not an adventure game.I'd say that the authors should focus on one genre and master it but it's only my opinion and the game has scored a massively successful reception so well, not my cup of tea._An afterthoughtLook, if you want to do do a mechanic that aims at mastering various classes do it like Final Fantasy Tactics - it was to fun to learn new skills, spells, abilities while being more and more powerful. Here it's a chore, no matter what location you want to grind it's only a resking of a very boring locale where you toil.Video games should not use toil as a game mechanic!If I want to toil, I can do that in my work. I want to relax when playing a game, not treat it as a chore and grinding is definitely a chore. That's why I've left Diablo 3 and many other games, including this one.A wasted potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Saves the World

_childDocuments_.review: You need to know one important thing before you know my opinion: I was looking for mindless fun. And it's exactly what I got. What Nobody Saves the World has going for it is the ability to change your characters appearance and abilities on the fly. It elevates a pretty straightforward and mundane combat into something enjoyable. Of course in order to fully utilise the character's (other known as form) abilities, you need to unlock them first by completing a series of challenges. All of the challenges were pretty cool, making gameplay a lot more interesting than it was. At higher levels it takes use of the fact that you can mix and match some of your forms' passive and activity abilities creating a much stronger build. Magician spawning rabbits out of a hat and turning people into zombies with a bite is pretty OP and heavy on the framerate :)There's some humor in the game, one could say a lot, but it's really subjectively funny. Story is pretty standard, but it didn't annoy me.Difficulty level becomes a thing of the past pretty much in the middle of the game as your forms become stronger and stronger, but if you're looking for a challenge, you could try finishing the game with the basic form if that's even possible. That's the only useless one. Maybe add an egg to it, but at least I defeated some enemies with it and it's critical to the highest form.Nothing groundbreaking, but I enjoyed the world and defeating new hordes of enemies, especially in the more difficult dungeons. Unlocking new forms was pretty exhilarating ,too.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Saves the World

They are quick and easy to complete and elicit a strong feeling of "just one more" that made hours disappear.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda fun game up until I have to do this stupid ranger challenge where I have to hit all targets or fail, you have to use an ability that doesn't belong to ranger, have charge time and small AoE to hit 5 fast moving targets, most of the time it will just miss 1 target even though on the screen it looks like it should have hit and I have to start over because some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ability doesn't have big enough hitbox like the animation show ???Constantly changing forms to do what the game want you to do but have no control over the quickswap wheel, you can't customize which character and where you want them to be on the wheel, there's no pause while you're using the wheel, enemies will still attack you while you're looking for the form you need so the wheel is basically useless in combat.The entire game is like a checklist, do this 100 time, do that 20 time while you have no motivation to do so, you just have to do it to progress your characters because it's the only way and the quests get very repetitive. This game is too casual and the gameplay loop isn't interesting enough to have this kind of grindy quests.Enemies feel the same from the beginning to the end, they have 1 or 2 attacks at best, bosses feel exactly the same as normal enemies, stats are there for show they don't even matter, there's no loots or equipments so all you do is grind quests to progress characters and clear dungeons to get money, so many forms to unlock and yet they all feel the same, some abilities feels terrible to use, range character gameplay feels clunky because you have to be locked in a direction to hit the enemies, melee character basic attack have no forward movements so you're locked in a position and if the enemy got pushed then you have to release the attack button to move forward, the game look like it give you freedom on how you want to play, but if you don't play the way the game want you to play then good luck, you are not allowed to be creative and clear a challenge the way you want, you have to use specific forms with specific abilities otherwise you won't make it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, this game is alright, but it drags on with tedious chores to have your characters reach their potential rather than have it be a fun system.Here're the pros:1. Each form feels unique and fun.2. Biomes look and feel very different3. You can customize characters to do things very different from their original purpose4. For how short the game was, the story was very nice5. Movement and how abilities worked all felt very good. I did enjoy how abilities and characters played out alongside their visual effectsHere're the cons:1. There's only one real boss fight in the entire game, and it was tedious rather than fun. The base enemy playstyles are disappointing and simple. Also there were just very few enemies, making this game feel more rushed and slapped together rather than a deep labor of love.2. Unlocking abilities and forms was a chore, and I had to waste 4 extra hours just playing to unlock more abilities for forms I liked to use them to their B-rank potential. 3. Some forms just weren't even touched by end game because others did the same archetype but better4. Progression doesn't feel like progression. The "new" elements drop off in rate given to you by 8 hours in, monsters don't really get more complicated in attack patterns or movement as you get further in the game, and additional mechanics don't really matterI got it on sale, and if you don't mind these cons all too much, I'd recommend you also get it on sale alongside the DLC, but I wouldn't recommend it at full price, and I probably should've stopped playing 10 hours in regardless

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game that really scratches that Secret of Mana itch of overhead 2D combat with lots of weapon choices. It was a lot of fun leveling up all the classes. The major issue with this game is the awful interface designed around switching characters. In a game that wants you to use all 16 classes at different moments and with different niches, the game fights you tooth and nail trying to do that in any consistent, reliable way, with only 8 storage slots for said 16 characters, which can't even be consistently set, and which instead are constantly shifting all over the place. It's a massive and frustrating miss. I've beaten this game with my 6 year old, and while he had fun with the combat, my needing to pick up his controller every 15 minutes to reorganize both of our class selection wheels every 15 minutes really drained the fun from the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The highlight of this game to me was experimenting with character builds and abilities to figure out how to beat dungeons with particularly complicated special conditions included. Two examples that particularly stuck out was one spot that had all damage sources multiplied by x9999 and another that made it so that any healing abilities you used were reflected on all enemies on screen. The immense amount of customization and puzzle aspects described above make this game stand out from other 2D action RPGs, and if the art/concept description interests you I think you'll more than get your money's worth with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody Saves the World is a great top-down, action-adventure that blends the exploration from something like a Zelda game with the action seen in a ARPG. It may seem like one big checklist (which it can be at times), but it's still a lot of fun.If you'd like to hear my full thoughts then you can check out my review here:

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody saves the world is a pretty darn great Action RPG by the guys who brought you Guacamelee, Drinkbox. The hand-drawn art style oozes charm, very reminescent of games like Rogue Legacy 2 and of course their own previous games, Guacamelee 1&2.  NSTW doesn't reinvent the wheel or anything but what it executes it does pretty well for the most part. The form switching mechanic at first seems a bit gimmicky but it does result in some pretty in depth customization where you can take skills from one class and apply them on another. This allows you to create a lot of bizarre and funny combos, like a horse using a bow or an egg leaving a trail of slime.The writing has the right amount of funny without trying too hard which helps prop up the simple premise of the game, a calamity has befallen the world yada yada, you know the deal. The characters you'll meet are colorful individuals who have some really comical things to say. The dungeons you'll enter are procedurally generated, and for the most part seem simple enough in design, but feel very balanced. Some contain special parameters like everything can one-shot or everyone heals at the same time, which adds a nice bit of spice to the dungeon crawling. Usually it's all the standard procedure, you'll be fighting through hordes of enemies until you reach the boss room. The randomly generated nature of the dungeons almost gives the game a roguelite feel.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Saves the World

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is almost a hidden gem because I'd never heard of it before randomly finding it on steam. It's got pretty fun gameplay, especially in coop with lots of builds and creativity encouraged. It has fun comedic writing and occasional voice acting that's normally just funny sounds but it's appreciated. I think the issues people generally have with it are either to do with wards, form challenges or length of the game. These are very minor issues in my eyes and I don't think they take away from the game being pretty good. Read their reviews for the details on those issues but they're honestly not worth making a review negative in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is on the cute side, both in graphics and story. (The form's appearance doesn't change though. It would be just amazing if forms could visually reflect the skill loadout.) This is quite fun and NG+ provides an additional challenge from added dungeon modifiers.The game overall is a bit short, but a bit of time is required to max out your forms. A bit of a grind.

_childDocuments_.review: A pint sized ARPG where you can go from a slug that summons the dead to a horse that fires missiles in an instant, and that's very much the vanilla side of this game. Through the wide array of classes and the mix and match gameplay, the build variety on offer here is astounding, and the dungeons encourage you to experiment to see what works.The moment to moment activities constantly spur you on with levelling up, completing class challenges  and unlocking something new, giving that sweet flood of endorphins this genre is known for that make you want to play just a little bit more.To top it off, the game can be completed in 15-20 hours easy, and doesn't overstay it's welcome.Great game, great time.

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of fun. The combat is unique which makes it enjoyable. The world is well done, (the world) kind of reminds me of pokemon. The one thing I am not the biggest fan of is that you have to use certain characters some times. I like using the one that works for me, then maybe later I will try out some others. Especially when they all kind of function differenty, it makes it weird to switch mid fight. It does have the "enemy is immune until they are shot with the specific weapon type"  which is annoying. Everything else is great. The characters are fun. Some of them are more practical than others.  As for upgrades, and such, I haven't really gotten far enough to really notice yet. Leveling up characters is solely reliant on completing challenges for that specific character, also, not the biggest fan of this, but it isn't horrible. Just when they force you to equip certain attributes that I would not want.  Having played Guacamelee a lot (and not really liking Guacamelee 2 as much) I was looking for another game that felt retro, but also new. This game hit the mark. I was skeptical seeing the trailers but it really is fun from the jump. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game.  I think it has a fantastic foundation, giving you a bunch of different forms with different abilities and gameplay, little missions to let you power up and unlock new stuff, a solid sense of humor and good writing.  But there are some QoL issues that make this game frustrating to play.  The biggest offender for me is the quick swap wheel for your different forms, which is a good feature implemented in the worst way possible.  There is no way for you to manually customize it to put which forms you want on the wheel, instead it's just the 8 most recent ones you used.  If you go into a menu to pick a new form, it replaces the one it's been the longest since you've used, which means that it's constantly mixing them up and getting them out of order, killing any muscle memory you might develop.  Also you pick a form with the wheel open using the left stick, which is the same one used for movement (right stick isn't used at all), and the wheel doesn't pause combat, meaning if you open it in combat you're gonna stop dead in your tracks while you figure out where the form you want is, letting enemies hit you while you flounder around.  It's such an easy fix to make that work better, I have no idea why they made it that way.There's also some smaller issues, like some story dungeons locking progress for your quests for seemingly no reason.  I also have some issues with the sense of progression in the game and not really feeling like I'm getting any stronger as I level up, but I think that one is more about personal preference and I'm guessing plenty of people like the way the game handles progression and leveling up.This is a neat game that no doubt works for a lot of people, but it just falls a little short for me personally.  Also worth mentioning I only played the single player, so I can't judge how good the co-op is.

_childDocuments_.review: * Multiplayer review *Nobody Saves the World is a great game that offers online co-op. The problem is the online mode works just like a couch co-op, meaning both players view the same screen at any time, and that also includes shared progression, inventory, and even menu navigation. So you play with a friend on 2 PCs, but everything acts like playing on same PC. In fact, after realizing this, I ended up playing it online with my girlfriend in the same room using 2 PCs, both watching one screen and turning the other one off. Just like couch co-op, something the game does not support.I have nothing against a multiplayer mode that is "online only" by design, if properly implemented. But this is more the case of a couch multiplayer design forced to be online only. It feels weird and unnatural.I'm a big fan of DrinkBox Studios and their Guacamelee series. I would blindly buy anything they release.This game is very fun to play, but even more with a partner. The multiplayer design fell a bit short this time.If developer adds the couch co-op option (which is already perfectly implemented as the online option), I will change this review to positive.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked that game of the bat. It doesnt take itself serious but still serious enough for a nice experience. Every character is unique and there are a bunch of them. You start with a standart quest for a specific char but get combinated quests later on which often differ from each char. You can combinate the most skills with any char and get your own playstyle going.I play it on medium difficulty with a controller (its recommended and optimized for it. So you better use one). There are some retries but nothing exhausting if you know to combinate your skills or to use your characters. The game can be pretty clear what you have to do for a quest if you dont get it. Or are in the wrong transformation.Every location has its own theme. Its own idea behind it and some rules who might follow. Every side quest dungeon has its own properties and sometimes you need to change your char and skills to adapt to it.The game has a good enemy diversity. And the game uses the different enemy abilities and enemy type for some interesting dungeons.It has a unique and nice art style. The animations are nice and funny. As well as the dialogues.Over all its not a big game. I think 30 hours max. And it doesent exceeds in any aspects beyond imagination. But I was surprised by the detail the well made world and experience. For an indie game it has all what I expect off of it. A fun and nice experience. Its one of a few indie games I would recomment even for its full price.

_childDocuments_.review: DrinkBox does it again. This time the hero (Nobody) gets to go on a fun action adventure (with some rogue-like elements) with a wacky band of forms. The art style brought me to this game, reminding me of Keli's style of characters, but the gameplay lived up to my expectations. Have fun playing as various forms and taking on dungeon after dungeon of enemies, all while learning about yourself and the Calamity.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this game for a couple of hours and for a majority of that, I've been bored out of my mind. Yeah, I just gained the ability to mix powers across classes, which is interesting, but beyond that, there has been nothing distinctly remarkable about this game. There's barely a plot and there aren't any interesting characters that I've seen so far. The gameplay basically boils down to going into dungeons and farming mobs for EXP. In fact, this game very brazenly embraces EXP farming as a core element of its gameplay and I can't say it's all that interesting. Even with the ability to mix and match powers, nothing removes the tedium of having to farm kills or meet specific requirements to level up each class individually. I'd say if you're looking for a solid RPG with lots to experience, you should look somewhere else and if all you want is a simple action game where you just endlessly kill groups of enemies over and over again...... you should still look somewhere else. I am certain there are plenty of horde shooters, roguelikes, or other action staples like Doom or Devil May Cry that will offer far superior combat experiences than this.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost - Nobody saves the world is funny. All that NPCs, scattered through the game, very often say or do realy hilarious stuff. Very nice thing is that devs actually managed to incorporate gameplay base (that thing about form changing) into that stuff in a very smooth way. Things like  happen often enough, and they give the game nice and refreshing feeling of... IDK, integrity? Great music and visuals add a lot to overall impression too. But what may or may not be problem - it's gameplay. It greatly depends on your ability to pace yourself in the way developers intend you. Which means balancing world exploration and form progression. When at some point you receive a dozen or so "form quests", it's easy to go full completionist mode and start finishing them on the first encountered dungeon - even one that fits that particular form poorly. And then you are stuck with boring and unpleasent "YOU CURRENT FORM IS OUT OF QUESTS" streak, mindlessly clearing repetitive dungeons.If you keep yourslef under control, though, and progress forms while exploring - those two things will nicely balance themselves for a relatively enjoyable experience, with constant influx of new cool abilities that will keep you busy.This, however, means that completing NG+ to get those last two achievements... Well THAT would be excruciating task for everyone except grind lovers. No way I'm trying that!

_childDocuments_.review: Cautious yes..Control scheme is just bonkers considering its released on Steam (the part in start up that says "controller recommended" really should say "controller highly preferred, we really really insist" - kb+mouse while possible is so garbage no sane person should even try it. That is okay.. I like to have some pc games I'd refer to as couch games. I did however play this on my main pc and had to rumble through some hidey holes to find myself an old 360 controller. That did help.. however parts to the GUI/mechanics are still poorly implemented and there's no way for player to fix any of those issues. Also no local coop means it really isn't a proper couch game either..My biggest gripe with the game is how it completely breaks down after playing from 1½ minutes to 1½ hours - which is unacceptable for a game that relies on saving at checkpoints you visit. First time this happened I had to re-do some of the tutorial because I assumed the game would had saved when I got outside.. This happens constantly in the dungeons making it very frustrating to play a game that runs at <90 fps (I should clarify the game is capped at 111 which is very smooth; for no apparent reason fps sometimes drops to 60~90 range and the game stutters so badly it feels like its really running at <1 fps...), being stuck between check-point outside the dungeon and finishing it without knowing how long that'll take... Especially later in the game when you need to re-configure one character to get their quests done making it very annoying that I can't just restart the game and continue where I was but instead would lose sometimes good 30 minutes of progress - or suffer through the game being an absolute d' for no apparent reason. Later on there's some pacing issues such as some high level content available in lower level areas (which would make sense in a mmo.. here, not so much) and game really doesn't tell you where's what level contents other than going to an area.. so I ended up "grinding" a dungeon to finish most of character specific quests to point of game not giving new quests and not explaining where I should go.. Following the main quest "fixed" the issue, although the main quest dungeons at the point were so easy I could had looked meanly at enemies to make them die - so again, pacing issues.. Those higher level dungeons would had made more sense if they were locked behind a quest or something.. So assuming your specific setup won't have stuttering issues, and don't mind playing with a controller its.. okay. Nothing amazing, but okay. Solid 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has fun aspects, but there's so little streamlining in any mechanics that it really hinders the overall enjoyment. I WANT to utilize more forms, but I find myself only changing forms when I have to in order to progress, or beat a certain enemy. The game provides a "quick swap" button, but it is very clunky, and leaves you vulnerable while you struggle to get a grasp on it. The alternative to this is opening the menus (Which pause the game, something the quick menu does not, and going over 3 tabs to traverse your form tree. While leveling up forms is interesting, I'm barely 2 hours in and I'm already starting to get annoyed by it. You're arbitrarily locked out of further progression in any given form when it stop giving you quests for that form (At the beginning, this seems to be half way through C-Rank. The controls themselves are also fairly clunky. The quick menu requires you input a direction, CONTINUE TO HOLD THAT DIRECTION, and then close the menu WHILE STILL HOLDING THE DIRECTION in order to change forms. You also attack in the direction you are moving. It may be more of a personal thing, but I just find it to not feel very good. There is an entirely unused stick on my controller that could have functioned as a way to change attack direction (Also, the mouse for keyboard players). The mouse actually seems to have no function at all, requiring KBM players to navigate using the arrow keys (The default move buttons). As for controllers, there is only rigid omni-directional movement, restricting you to the 4 cardinal directions and their diagonals. It was a bit jarring to get used to, personally.Overall. The game's alright, but there's a lot that make me want to stop playing. It's a shame too. The game in concept and art is really neat. I highly recommend utilizing Steam's 2 hour return window to see if you enjoy the game. You can get a pretty good feel for it within the first 2 hours. I will probably keep playing it, but really wouldn't recommend it to people.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Saves the World

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly got bored not even after 1 hour of play. On paper the concept sounds nice: You're a "nobody" transforming into various other characters. The potential. I've unlocked a rat. Cool. Then an archer and a knight. Done 2 "demi-dungeons". The rat just heals, the knight just tanks all the damage and the archer is useless until you actually need him, because you can't get to an enemy. Melee combat is either "just tank it" or "stutter step", i.e. attack, move, attack, move, only ever so slightly, since the enemies so far don't seem to do much. Ranged combat is abysmal. Instead of being able to free aim or at least aim AFTER moving you have to actually face in the direction you want your projectile to go WHILE you're shooting/holding the aim button. That means you're constantly moving to avoid enemies, but when you get an opportunity to finally shoot you have to go TOWARDS the enemies before you can actually shoot, instead of just quick turning to let loose an arrow. Irritating.Combat is boring, the story is pointless and irritating so far, and the game already shows you how grind it's going to get. Quest 1: Kill 20 bad guys. Quest 2: Kill 50 bad guys. Yeah, I think I know where this is going. The repeatable quest from the vendor started with 50. Now it's 250. It took me about half an hour to kill 50 guys, so 250 will be over 2 hours unless enemy density GREATLY increases, but then I doubt the game will be fun at all. And since that quest is repeatable so you can get XP I just know the next stage is going to be sth like "kill 1,000 guys". No, thanks.A game can be grind if the gameplay is super engaging. Here that's not the case imho. Everything in this game is tedious. Menus, switching forms, unlocking new stuff. It's just not very well designed from a UI/UX perspective. Fine, it's an indie game? Sure, an indie game that costs a whopping 25 bucks... got it via Humble, but... meh. Then there's the DLC that adds stuff that's apparently pointless, judging by the reviews, since you've already completed the game when you can finally get those forms. But what does it matter if the basic combat system is so boring and flawed that no matter how many forms you have you just know how the game is going to play?

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game this early after its release after reading every single one of the negative reviews. 100% of the reviews were complaining about key bindings and controller support. If you prefer using a controller, please pick up this game if it looks interesting. I use a PlayStation 5 controller and it works great. Through Steam Big Picture mode, I configured the right analog stick to mode shift as a left analog input when pressing the right shoulder button (this is the quick-change button and I'm used to using the right stick for circular menu designs) and I remapped the right side of the track pad click to the "options" button (I'm not used to using the options/share button and it's used a lot). There's also an option to change the button prompts to match PlayStation controllers (it's option 3 in the in-game menus).As far as the game itself, I can't put it down. It's creative and fun, and rewards varied play styles through its leveling system.

_childDocuments_.review: Distinctive artwork. Very addictive gameplay loop with the quest resolution system giving small boosts of endorphins every few minutes which also serve to spice up combat as you're always encouraged to try different strategies and mix and match your moveset to find combinations that hopefully work for you.The one critique I have is that some forms don't get the spotlight shone of them as they should as objectively better ones are unlocked immediately after. Personally, I would love three stages of unlocks instead of two. Or even more, honestly.The challenges are... challenging. The classic "you have to fail again and again until you learn the pattern" gameplay, which is pretty popular nowadays due to Soul-like games springing everywhere. Not a fan, but I know many will be.The variety of forms and the freedom to customize what you want depending on the situation is the main appeal of the game. It is so well done to the point is hard to argue there is "strongest build" you should 100% go to where many forms can be customized to tackle a myriad of challenges as they come to you. Maybe you can set up one for healing and mana recovery, one for dealing with a particularly annoying summoning baddie that gets exploded by this one strategy, and one to clean up little guys. Oh, and one for travel.All-in-all, pretty good game. Story is not that bad, and the last boss design? Glorious. Both in appearance and how to fight it.

_childDocuments_.review: Chill, silly and fun.I don't know how the game is experienced solo, as I played with a friend, but we had a great time with the game overall. The game has given us plenty of laughs, had chill OSTs and the transformation system was a lot of fun to play with. The story isn't like super great, but the silliness is what makes the game. It is a bit on the short side, but then again, the game isn't that expensive. New Game + is available with mobs scaling to your level and new dungeon modifiers (sometimes requiring you to get a bit creative with forms and abilities). However, none of the dialogues can be skipped, which felt like a drag the second time around.While fun, I can imagine that a lot of people might not enjoy the transformation system. You will have to be actively working on various forms to unlock new passive and active skills, as well as new forms. This is something me and my friend found enjoyable, but some forms can be annoying to play early on and Form Quests can sometime be hard to complete unless you have a dungeon with proper modifiers unlocked. Aside from that, me and my friend have ran into disconnection issues a handful of times. When it happens, the host stays in the game, so they can just walk back to a checkpoint to save any quest progression made and remake the lobby. Slight annoyance. Again, I have no idea how the game is balanced solo, but the online coop was fun and definitely worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed feelings on this one. The thing about expectations, right? I feel this one could have been awesome, it has all the ingredients for it. But it falls a bit short and is merely very good.Let me ramble about it for a bit.There's much to be liked in here:  the art in great, the music is all bangers, it's silly and funny, the core gameplay of mixing powers and changing forms is very fun. Sounds great, right?The thing is that they take all that and make something a bit too shallow. The core loop of completing quests to unlock and progress the forms is fine, but you can easily complete the game before unlocking them all. And bear in mind that I'm a filthy completionist. I did everything. In the end you feel there's not enough game to properly play with and mix all classes and powers.But then, new game plus is for that, right? Well, kinda...The dungeons are simply too easy. NG+ mix stuff a bit, but in truth you can basically steamroll everything with one or two forms. There's no much incentive to use most of the forms.The overworld has a bit of use of the different forms via the side missions. But after unlocking a form that can swim, exploration became an afterthought.The DLC fixes this a bit. They have 12 challenges that force you to pick the right form with the right abilities to complete them. This was very fun and makes you truly go through the forms and powers to make builds for specific challenges.Also, we  need to talk about the controls... how can they be so bad? Walking and hitting stuff is fine, but menuing and specially changing forms is terrible. The game is about changing forms. How can they make actually changing the damn things so bad? We need to be able to pin some in the wheel. Also the game should pause when you open the wheel. We should be able to pin 4 to the d-pad... I can't comprehend the devs playing this and not realizing this. Bizarre.In the end I fell a big cheated I guess. They made a very good game. But it is plain it could have been a great one. Hopefully a second instalment achieves the full potential this could have.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game with some minor flaws.Story:It is a comedy, a bunch of crazy things happen and fun at that, after the character stole a wizards wand. At the very least, you can gather that the character and the conflict are tied together. As in they are more directly related as far as I can tell.MechanicsThe character can transform into different classes. These classes upgrades in rank by completing their questline. This is also how the player levels overall as well. You get some permanent side quests on top of this. At some point, you can mix together abilities which becomes a must to tackle the hardest dungeons. Exploration:This is a must for a few reasons. To find mana potions to increase your overall amount, to find chicken nest for an egg. The game is very wide, and there is quite a bit to unlock. It also leads to some entertaining scenarios.Upgrades:Aside from class upgrades, you can also buy at a merchant stat increase items as well as some passives.Cons:1. Tips never go away, it isn't even in the settings. This seriously needs to be added, as it is just annoying.2. Side Quests, it can start to feel like busy work. This is an instant where less is more, and the amount of time needed is quite a lot. Which knocks down the game a bit, this and the tips were very stupid features. The side quests could have been done better, a lot better.Overall:It is a really good game, and I can recommended. Despite the flaws, it is a really good experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Verdict: Acceptable, but feels very rogue-lite in name only. Did not play the online co-op.Positives: - Amusing characters / quests, interesting premise with changing forms & mixing/matching active/passive skills between mastered forms to maximize your potential. - They do a decent job of balancing things initially, but once you start getting late in the game, if you combine things correctly you're effectively unkillable, may be seen as a positive or negative.- Nice colourful world, with a surprising number of enemy sprites (though lacking in mechanical differences, everything is just a damage sponge in one way or another). Very much what I'd expect from folks behind Guacamelee. Negatives:- LOTS of re-use and time-stretching mechanisms, like mini-quests to level up your form by doing odd things. - These were initially used to good extent, but very much overstayed their welcome. I really started feeling it around rank A, when there were fewer and fewer actual rewards for ranking up a form.- Indicates best controls with controller, but did not work with PS4 controller, only XBOX.- LOTS of grinding to little advantage, You lose nothing on death, so finding a respawn point near a large enemy spawn point quickly desensitizes you to just doing X to complete a class quest, then dying, reloading (5-8 seconds) and repeating with no negative drawbacks- Game commits cardinal sin of having the last two achievements locked behind completing the game on New game plus- Lack of bossesFinal Notes:The only reason it seems to be called a rogue-lite is because every time you enter a "mini dungeon" (there's around one and a half dozen of these) It's layout changes. It's side-status effects, enemy spawns / immunities, and tileset/puzzles do not change at all. I suppose the "lose nothing on death" could be considered an aspect of it, but that honestly felt more like an exploit on my part than "progression".It's a decent purchase if you just want to waste some time while doing something requiring relatively little focus like listening to a podcast, but don't expect a super deep gaming experience. I had fun, but not enough to engage in new-game plus.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. Very difficult but also very achievable. Anytime I found myself frustrated with multiple failed attempts to defeat certain dungeons or caves, all I needed to do was try out a recently acquired form. Each form is unique and useful for specific battles and enemies. The map is very large which lends itself to hours of game play. However, the many side quests which send you all over the map and even into unknown territory can lead to confusing and tedious navigation. Although fast travel portals do limit the tireless walking to a minimum.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally purchased this game because I was a fan of their previous game Guacamelee and trusted this would be fun. I was instantly hooked in the first hour. _childDocuments_.review: "Nobody Saves the World" is a visually appealing game with a unique and charming graphic style. The world is vast and full of interesting sights, though it lacks hidden paths and secret areas that could enhance exploration.One of the standout features is the ability to transform into different forms, each with its own set of moves. This mechanic is incredibly fun, allowing players to mix and match skills from various forms, which keeps the gameplay fresh and exciting.While some say the game can become repetitive, I haven't experienced that much myself. There are moments of repetition, but the fun of unlocking new forms and experimenting with different abilities keeps things engaging.In summary, "Nobody Saves the World" offers a delightful and creative adventure. Its impressive graphics and innovative gameplay mechanics make up for the minor lack of hidden exploration areas. It's a game that provides a lot of fun and variety, making it a memorable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun and witty game to be played with a controller, it is a fast paced top down action RPG with a huge humorous Zelda likes world, gameplay has innovative elements (mixing up several mechanics such as roguelike) and core mechanics is centered around switching between characters (classes) in real time each with noticeably different play style that you can mix around, it offers a lot of versatility, you unlock them by doing quests and leveling up.Some may find the game grindy and it is somehow but it is not the typical repetitive grind as the world is huge with many quests and huge amount of dungeons so the grind feels distilled into the progression, the progression is a bit non linear as well, you also have to level up your characters which provide different play style and unlock more characters so it does not feel boring at all if you like that, the game does not seem to enforce a play style, overall difficulty is high.Gameplay may become repetitive after some hours even though new forms and abilities provide variations, i was still hooked due to the world content and overall feeling on the steamdeck, high end dungeons may seem generic after a while also.The game world is witty with several references, has ok graphics with good amount of content and is polished overall.Although i didn't test it i can see it being a blast in COOP !

_childDocuments_.review: Completely Solo review: Honestly this game has captivated me for the last 24 hours and I've truly been having a blast playing this game. I think for anyone who has played Pokemon should be able to relate to the feeling of slowly evolving your team, gaining new abilities, ranks and customisation. This game sort of scratches that same sort of itch. All while having an enjoyable laid back story that you can pretty much tune your brain out to but still enjoy? If that makes any sense at all. Regardless this games major selling point in the customisation options. Sticking to the Pokemon analogy, its sort of like fusing your different Pokemon's (forms in this game) abilities and attacks together. Ever wanted to give Magikarp Dragon Claw? Well you pretty much can in this game. Not to mention the countless well thought out Forms this game has. Honestly I think its worth the money, the graphics, the mechanics and the vibe all feel pretty good in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody Saves the World is an incredible game. Although short, in the little time you play is extremely fun.You start the game off waking up in a shack with no recollection of who you are. You venture off to figure out who you are and help fight the calamity and save the world. As you explore and level up you unlock different forms that allow you to shape shift. That's pretty much the story summed up but there's a lot of side quests you can do that are really fun. There's stuff like thieves guild and knights round table too which have their own side story line. The gameplay is very well done. As you unlock more forms you get more missions for that form and it helps you level up your overall stats. Each from has their own unique abilities and passive but you can actually mix and match abilities from other forms. It's pretty wacky having a turtle shoot a bow or a horse shoot a fireball but mixing up the builds is extremely fun and essential to leveling up the different forms. The game does a good job of spreading the levels of dungeons so that you don't feel too overpowered or under-leveled. I'm not sure if it scales with co-op but it felt pretty easy beating it with 2 players. Some of the dungeons have set modifiers which I think kinda ruin it. This one dungeon has all damage dealt and received multiplied by 9999 and so you basically always 1 shot the boss. I think it's a interesting modifier but I think they should be randomized because it totally ruins that dungeon.Some of my complaints are in co-op, inventory menus is shared so if someone has it open then both players are paused which is pretty inconvenient. Also the aiming in the game is a bit weird because it wants you to lock the direction you're aiming with right trigger instead of aiming with the joystick.The soundtrack and graphics are pretty good. We encountered very little bugs despite the game only recently coming out. Overall it's a great game. It's kinda short. We beat it in about 17 hours and did every single side quest. We didn't 100% it but we were pretty close. Might be a bit pricey for how short it is but I had a lot of fun so I would say it's worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Nobody Saves the World

_childDocuments_.review: The game is funny, nice to look at and it's central gameplay idea of mix&matching forms and abilities is fairly interesting and well executed most of the time (the pacing of some of the ability quests is wierd though).In the way it plays the game more often actually resembles a puzzle game more than what you'd think it would be from the way it looks, but a lot of the challenges and combat encounter are just about flat out impossible if you don't understand what abilities they want you to bring. I personally liked that, but you should definitely keep that in mind when playing this game.The systems aren't deep enough to warrant a very long playtime, but the game is fairly short anyway and for the low asking price its definitely a fun waste of time.

This game combines what I would call a old style jrpg (dragon quest, legend of zelda, final fantasy I,II,III) with a rogue-like and does it very well. _childDocuments_.review: Great game! The art style is absolutely hilarious and had me laughing quite a lot at the character designs, especially at the people near the power plant. The game runs and plays pretty smoothly to boot. Every form you can switch to has it's own spin on the combat and once you get to a certain point in the game, you can customize all these forms to match whatever playstyle suits you. My personal favorite was the zombie form. You get a skill that lets you turn enemies into zombies who can infect other other monsters and basically fill the screen with a zombie army. Grab some skills from other forms that let you heal and power up your zombies and you can basically make an unstoppable army. Every form has a surprising amount of depth to them which I felt was this game's greatest strong point. I had a great time playing this game and it doesn't overstay it's welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: The save system is purely save points which means if you need to stop playing for whatever reason you will lose progress if you quit the game (no save on quit).Which is a shame because it's a fun game but this design choice does make it difficult to recommend for playing on Steam Deck or if you have responsibilities that might pull you away from the game for extended periods of time.I wish I could list this as a neutral review but as I can't and I can't really positively recommend it because of this (and I've dropped it after just an hour and a half of play for this reason).However if you love this kind of save system, then imagine my review says "Yes I recommend this game!" because otherwise it's a cool concept, great art and fun progression system and you'd probably enjoy it if you don't need a save on quit feature!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent and I hope there will be a follow up game or expansions(s) for it, as I find it that good. It's leans into ARPGs like Diablo and Grim Dawn, but also has a heavy Zelda feel, especially the SNES Zelda game; Link to the Past, with its own silly humor.My only real complaints with the game are the form quick select wheel to swap between them is limited and a bit awkward to use, and that the controls for certain characters like the Ranger are a bit clunky. I'm getting used to how they work, and depending on which form and abilities you use, it will be a larger or smaller issue, but it is definitely something to note.Barring those 2 mostly minor issues I've had an absolute blast with the game. The main world is very open, and there's a lot of exploring to do, with some opening up after you can travel on or over water, In some ways the game is also like the Elder Scrolls games in which you can ignore the main quest to a point, although to unlock more advanced forms/quests, you'll have to be sure to advance it, but you can go off and run dungeons to get those form quests done, break stuff because you can, and find quests via NPCs instead of focusing on the main quest pretty much all you want.The forms are the key to the game and I love how you can swap between them virtually at will, and barring each forms signature attack and passive ability, you'll discover a quest to be able to swap thing around between forms, and in fact have to solve some of the more difficult quests and as required to upgrade your forms and open new ones. I have not tried multiplayer yet, so cannot judge how that works out, as far as dungeons or over world enemies would be affected. The dungeons start out relatively easy, but they can ramp up in a hurry and you'll often encounter warded enemies that are immune to all damage barring one of the 4 types (dark, light, slashing, blunt), so you need to use that type to break the ward so you can defeat them.The enemy variety has been robust, I'm not sure how far into the game I am yet, I've been focused on getting forms open and getting them their abilities unlocked, but so far I've seen a decent amount of distinct enemies with various attacks and abilities that can really change things up, especially in some of the dungeons with extra rules that can really make you be very particular in your loadout and chosen form.This one is a winner for sure; a great mix of humor, solid game play, and challenge. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost. This is an almost good game.Fighting promises to be amazing because of the constant evolution of your forms and the ability to mix and match. The world promises to be huge and full of exciting places and dungeons. Even the story gives you a mystery of sorts to solve, although you probably wouldn't play this for the story...Promises, promises. Now, does the game deliver on them? Almost. You assume a form. That form has a default (signature) attack and a passive ability. As you complete little form-based quests (kill X guys with ability Y, heal Z hp, etc) you level the forms up and gain new abilities. Most of those abilities can be switched around to other forms. Doesn't that sound amazing?It is! Until it isn't.Eventually the progression slows down, mainly because it's locked behind story progress. It's not well-paced at all. But that's ok - you hit a progression wall in one form so you switch to another, right? Ah, that's often not possible either, because of elemental wards.See, pretty much all attacks have some kind of element. Light, dark, sharp, blunt, whatever. And almost all dungeons have specific elements to them - so that means that you need to use this particular element against them, or else you won't deal any damage. So chances are you'll want to play as the horse who primarily deals blunt damage, but the dungeon you've entered is light elemental. Now, you could simply take a light-based ability for your horse... but that costs mana, which you won't be able to gain if you can't hit your enemies with the blunt attack!And of course enemies are everywhere. Exploration is limited by two things: enemies' level, and required abilities (such as swimming). That's fine; but sadly it's less exploration and more finding crowds of enemies to fight. It almost feels like an old-school hack'n'slash with its approach to baddies. You won't get a lot of quiet walking, taking in the scenery, unless you've killed everything in the area.Like I said before, the world is huge. And there are dungeons everywhere. Their level is often not quite matching their location, so you find yourself going back to them. I don't mind that - there are fast travel crystals available, so you can just go right back. But you know what those dungeons contain? More bad guys to fight! But in a corridor this time.Everything looks great - the dungeons often have some kind of theme (such as a gingerbread house), so the walls of the dungeon feel distinct from walls of another dungeon. Enemies, not so much. There are a few types and they pretty much repeat everywhere, with some very minor exceptions. Even bosses feel like normal fights, rather than those puzzle encounters you probably remember from Zelda. Oh, and the dungeons are randomly generated. If you die or leave the dungeon reshuffles. Like I always say - after a while you stop looking at the pretty graphics and start looking past them, and all you see then is a procedurally generated corridor with some dead ends and a boss at the finish line.The game doesn't take itself seriously, and that's a good thing. But if you do that, then make sure your humour is funny. Admittedly, falling in love with a horse gave me a chuckle, but otherwise everything is just... annoying rather than funny. For example, there's an area which is all about a nuclear power plant that went all Chernobyl on the area around it, including the local village - and everyone is horribly mutated to the point they barely resemble human beings. And all they say is "oh, the plant is super safe! Nothing wrong happened, we're all fine. See?". I don't know, that's not very funny to me.The main story is all about finding a missing super-wizard: Nostramagus. Where is he? Why isn't he helping against the calamity? Well, he might not be around, but at least there's... you. A strange, featureless being who happened to find Nostramagus' wand - so that's who will have to do. And the enemy - the calamity - is a force of nature, but it's also somewhat sentient. And it talks to you. Those are the only moments where the story gets kinda interesting.I didn't beat the game. Playing started to feel like a chore at some point, and that's where I draw the line. This might be a good game to play while listening to podcasts or something, but that's not what I'm looking for.Oh, and I also played solo. The game might have been more fun if I played with a friend, but... eh. I don't know. I had some fun, and when the fun ran out, I stopped playing. That's why I'm calling it an almost good game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best designed video games I have ever played. A game which understands its unique gameplay mechanic so well that every facet of the game falls into sync with it. I walked into it expecting a decent indie game with a bunch of character choices (and definitely expecting to find a favorite and never switch from them). But what I found was a magnificently rich game filled with challenges for each of the characters, encouraging exploration of all of the move sets and unique play styles to complement them. Even while playing cooperatively, I felt fulfilled with the progression of each of the characters, never needing to resort to grinding and never feeling over-leveled. Truly, the design of this game is impeccable: everything lands exactly where it needs to. (Plus, it has a simple humor and charm which remains endearing and odd from start to finish).Everybody should buy this game. I don't care how much it costs. It would be worth it for $60, so buy it at the amazingly reasonable price it's offered at.

_childDocuments_.review: what a great take on the arpg genrethe art-style is very destinct and looks great in both quality of picture and animationthe soundeffects are charming and the OST is extremly well producedthe U.I. is tight, althought i wish there was a quicker way to change forms (something akin to favorites, perhaps for the directional buttons as an added tool to the shouldbutton menu)the plot is more tongue and cheek, but mixed with the pun(y) writing works to keep the game going.there's some pretty funny stuff around, like you would expect from an adult comedy cartoon show. (avoiding spoilers) imagine beeing able to turn into a horse (why not?) and experience love at first sight for horses...i mean where can you do that? or run around as the hell-mouse suffering infinite appetite. the gameplay is where it's at. the genre has been milked to infinity by now, ever since Diablo 1 became popular.but Nobody is mixing things up nicely. first off: you don't grind for loot-drops or exp.you basicaly get a constant influx of mini-quest (like use X attack X number of times for example) tied to each "form" (everything from a turtle to a robot) you chose on the fly. these mini-quest mixed with side and main quest is what keeps your charackter progression going. similiar to a Zelda you also find more permanent upgrades like an increased mana-pool through fairies, or do enviromental puzzles tied to your forms to unlock further upgrades and treasure. chests and enemies also drop currency which you can exchange at traders for upgrades to your stats or skills.there's also some Mario-elements thrown in the mix, like unlocking paths by collecting "wands", paths beeing blocked by requisites, etc. . similiar to Metroidvanias new forms and abilities unlock new paths and treasures. Diablo, Mario, Zelda, Metroid it's all here in different amounts of dosage.it starts rather boring, but quickly grows into a frenetic mix of beats, mass murder and menu-hopping to apply all your upgrades or rewards.certain enemy types also need specific damage types (each of your forms got their own set of passive and active abilites, often beeing tied to specific "elements") which ads another layer of complexety without getting overbearing. changing forms comes as easy as holding the right shoulderbutton (radial menu); this quick-change also ads more tools to your toolset: one form might be able to quickly apply status effects to enemies while another form might get very high dps-boots attacking enemies suffering ailments; one form might be able to easily slow enemies at range, while another is a high-dps yet fragile ranged-dps, etc. . there's a lot and i do mean A LOT here. and as a whole package it's very well done: dungeons are grindable and repeatable, formchanging puzzles mixed with combat is designed quite competent; it's a little bit Diablo, a little bit Zelda, traces of a Mario and a very polished and competent game all around.a game which was not on my radar at all; which never interested me. then i bought it on console, spend probably 200 hours with it and now impulse bought it again on steam. it's just a very pleasant game all around. bad day? start the game and everything from the OST to the visuals, the gameplay and progression loop might lighten your load.(takes a while to come toghter, i would guess the point where the game becomes "good" is after you clear the first major dungeon/castle, which might be 1 to 2 hours in depending on your playstyle).

_childDocuments_.review: When I think of the Steamdeck, a game like Nobody Saves the World should always come to mind. This is an absolute gem of a 15hr dungeon crawler/action RPG that doesn't take itself serious, both in its story and its gameplay.It's great that we have complex ARPG titles like Path of Exile, but it's also heart warming that we have easy to understand systems like the ones found in NStW. No armor, no items, no weapons. Just skills and talents. EXP? Get it through questing and using your skills and talents in certain ways! Such a simple idea, but the execution is perfection.I'd put this on a must play list for fans of the genre, or anyone looking for their next pickup and go game on the device of their choice.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a top-down action RPG for 1 or 2 players.GOOD:- The multiplayer is really fun! The very tough stuff is optional (it's there for completionists).- Cute animation- The story is simple but effective- Funny- Levelling up the different forms is surprisingly challenging and fun.- The different dungeons and challenges have unique limitations that force you to use your brain a bitTHE BAD:- The game includes an in-game demand for real-world money. For a game I paid to buy, I didn't appreciate this at all. _childDocuments_.review: This game oozes charm. The art style is just the right balance of cute and gross. The game play is just simple enough it is easy to pick up and play, and just in depth enough that you can play around with weird builds. All in all I had a really good time with this game.My favorite part is how different each form is from the others. It really is like having a bunch of different characters. They have their own pluses and minuses and some are much better suited in some situations than others. Along with that there are forms that you unlock and you think there's no way I'm going to use that. And then you just do all the time. The egg has great abilities to use on other forms and the turtle is a dungeon clearing BOSS. I spent most of my time as the ranger because it made things more challenging.One thing that really rubbed me the wrong way in this game though is the level scaling. Most of the hours I put into this game was from leveling up each form. I put in so much work and I felt just as weak at the end of the game as I did at the beginning. That just didn't feel good. I'm not a fan of level scaling in a game like this. With that much work to level up I feel like I should be allowed to just curb stomp the final boss. That's just me and mileage may vary. That's really the only thing I didn't enjoy in this game. Everything else was great!I recommend this game. The level scaling is a bummer, but everything else is worth seeing. Playing this brought me back to playing NES Zelda once upon a time. This game is just generally a good time and there's plenty of fun and challenge to be had if you look for it.
