_childDocuments_.review: I am so glad I got this game on sale because it is so LAME. It feels like playing a bad multiplayer game online. The single player  campaign objectives and gameplay are very co-op multiplayer based such as capturing and securing an area by fighting off waves of enemies in chaotic multiplayer battles. I didn't really care for the cell-shaded graphics or dithered textured skies and I also experienced jittery camera movement that was not smooth at all. I also found the combat to be extremely repetitive to the point that it became boring real quick. The whole experience felt very arcady and lame to me. I cannot recommend this game at all.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Operation Blackout

_childDocuments_.review: Solid run and gun shooter that gives you plenty of ammo but has a short campaign. I liked the comic book art style and the cheesy dialogue too. Alternating between playing as both Cobra and the Joes gave a slight nuance to the otherwise conventional gameplay structure. The missions that give you the option of playing Storm Shadow/Snake Eyes were my personal favorites, as I got some poor man's Warframe vibes. The story gets more interesting when you find out that Cobra Commander gets betrayed by his own people. My biggest gripe of the game is how most enemies constantly run around while shooting, making it difficult to land shots even with auto aim enabled. This made the sniper and other slow firing weapons useless. My advice is just go for the automatic weapons only. I used assault rifles and machine pistols for the vast majority of the game. The lack of a shoulder switch button was also annoying during the linear corridor levels. Worth getting on a steep sale for any shooter fan.
_childDocuments_.name: G.I. Joe: Operation Blackout

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one. There's obviously a love of the 80's comics and cartoons present here and you can tell they really wanted to capture that feeling and were sincere in their effort. I especially loved the 80's/90's Marvel GI Joe comic series and wanted to love the game. The problem is the actual game itself. It's a 3rd person shooter and it's only a shooter. You won't be doing anything else and despite Snake Eyes and Storm Shadow talking about sneaking into places, there is no stealth. There are 16 campaign levels, but you're only going to see 4 or 5 because most are reused, some multiple times. There are vehicle sections in a couple spots, but they're repetitive and it's an on rails experience. You usually have an AI companion if you don't want to do co-op, but they're absolutely brain dead. They run around in circles and only occasionally even shoot back. Along with that all the enemies will zero in on you so the companion usually just gets in the way. The story isn't anywhere near the level of the cartoons, let alone the comics and the cut scenes aren't fully animated. It's a series of still shots with voice over. If this game had a AAA or even a AA budget I think we could have had something special. Something like the newer Hitman trilogy level design and the ability to have open/multi path levels would have been spectacular and I would have loved to have seen fully animated cut scenes, but obviously this is a low budget game. I want to hit the like button so badly just because they clearly care for the IP and it's not the worst game I've ever played, but I can't in good conscience tell consumers this is worth 30 dollars. If it gets down to the 5 dollar range and you're a super fan that can handle all the negatives, then it would still be a hard maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up watching GI Joe as a kid. it was one of my main shows with Transformers, Mask, Garfield and Friends, Smurfs, Voltron, Visionaries, and lots more. So i am probably the target audience for this game.So finding it for like $4, why not give it a go?Completed the training mission. I've played enough games that are like this that the controls felt natural. Got ready.,..and lets go into Mission 1.YO JO.......hey wait a minute! So the first mission is me playing as Cobra, attacking the Joes? This feels a bit off...and seems like something that should be cut scenes.But this should be where the red flags start.Honestly this game is not very good. I have played a handful of games that play third this person style and this one plays...well..the worst. Aiming is just super poor. I know in the show that the Joes couldn't hit anyone in Cobra with their lasers (which always made me wonder why Cobra ever bothered retreating), but I didn't expect that aspect to carry over to the game too. Also talk about unresponsive.....slamming my R key to reload, and nothing.But don't get me started on the controls for the Rattler mission....oh boy.... I am pretty sure they lifted the controls from a boat game....Also there is a real issue with key remapping. I remapped change weapon to 1, but forgot to apply. When I went back to set it again..I couldn't choose 1. the game simply ignored the key when I hit it. So I chose 2. Then I reset all the controls and then I still couldn't choose 1, and now couldn't choose 2. So I chose `. After not liking that and resetting again, I now couldn't choose 1, 2, or `. That is a big issue. No Joe...:(Finally...I am sorry but this game cheats. Really bad I might add. The computer knows to strafe the moment you hit fire. Most of the time it is better to just run into the battle and slash them to death...er...explosion.And yes like others have said..the AI partner can be a little stupid.So to recap with the theme song:He'll fight for freedom wherever there's trouble (like fight with this whole game?)G.I. Joe is there (not sure I would call these ones "Joes")It's G.I. Joe against Cobra the enemy (and the horrible controls)Fighting to save the day! (Its going to be a long fight...)He never gives up (He probably hasn't really played the game then)He's always there! (He has more forgiveness and determination than I do)Fighting for freedom over land and air! (Should be fighting the poor coding)G.I. Joe is the code name for America's daring highly trained special mission force. (I guess you haven't met my AI partner then.....)It's purpose: to defend human freedom against Cobra, a ruthless terrorist organization determined to rule the world! (So the programmers are Cobra after all?)He never gives up. He'll stay til the fight's won. (My heart goes out to him then....he has a lot of work to do.)G.I. Joe will dare! (But you shouldn't)G.I. Joe, A Real American Hero (I'm not so sure "hero" is the word I would use to describe the characters in this game....)G.I. Joe is there! (I really wish they weren't)

_childDocuments_.review: At the end of the day all G.I. Joe: Operation Blackout really had to do was be a good third person shooter. It failed, badly. Think about it, if this game had the exact same story and art design but had Splinter Cell: Blacklist's gunplay it would have been a far better game. Controls are bad, guns are weak and sound awful, even for a GI: Joe game where the guns shoot lasers and not bullets. Laser guns can have good punchy sounds as well, see Doom. AI sucks on both sides but is far worse on the player side because your AI partner does NOTHING and I mean NOTHING!!! Enemy AI had base level programming, all they do is move and shoot, that's it. All in all this game was a let down because I loved GI: JOE as a kid growing up in the 90's.

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend this game if you can get it on a sale and you are a really big G.I. Joe fan and want to play simply for the novelty. I did enjoy the game. Didn't love it but I had some fun, But compared to other games that are similar I can't say this is great in comparison. The graphics although stylised still aren't great especially for the time it came out. The aiming on controller feels really off and I switched to mouse and key most of the time (I'm usually a controller player). Many of the levels are just replaying a previous level but just in reverse. There isn't much enemy variety in terms of tactics all of them either rush you or just dance in one spot trying to shoot you (because the ai can't figure out where to go). Also, in terms of lore almost all the enemies are variety's of B.A.T.s (Battle Android Troopers) even if you play Cobra you fight Joe variants of B.A.T.s. Which is a shame considering how many types of troopers there are in G.I. Joe.That being said as a fan of G.I. Joe i did enjoy this game. All the different Easter eggs and the novelty of playing as some of my favourite characters. The story is nothing special but still feels like it could've fit in the old cartoon and they really try to give off that vibe while staying with the classified (toy line) art style. They also did a good job of making each character play differently (aside from that character's counter part on the other faction). The characters do feel very similar to their versions in the 80's show in terms of their personality and I feel this was a game where the developers wanted to be authentic to the brand and just had a shoe string budget and not enough time to do what they wanted for the game (example: there are chest high walls everywhere but no cover system). Also seeing things like skystrikers, Hiss tanks and other Joe things in game just makes me geek out a bit.If you made it this far and are enough of a Joe fan that you collect the current toy line (classified) I recommend getting on sale. I got it for about $6 CAD and in comparison, to a figure ($34,99CAD) that's nothing for a little Joe novelty. Which is a huge reason you would get the toys anyway. I enjoyed playing it and got some ideas for my own displays whiles playing it so for me it was worth it,If you are not a huge G.I. Joe fan or even a casual one then save your money. There's no real reason to buy the game. Try a game like Ghost Recon, Gears of War, Splinter Cell or Spec Ops: the Line instead.

_childDocuments_.review: G.I. Joe was always awesome in my eyes. Growing up with the first two badass films with a ton of action and combat in them both. Snake Eyes was my favourite like majority of fans. I never did grow up with the 80's version of G.I. Joe despite growing up with the 80's Transformers show and movie. But nonetheless this game is definitely worthy of a try, I will admit I wasn't blown away by this game, but it was fun to play all of these different characters. Duke and Cobra Commander are probably the best to play for me personally. But Playing Scarlet and Snake Eyes were pretty good as well. The soundtrack is pretty good for the type of G.I. Joe its based on, I love the cutscenes being a comic book style as well, showing the partial source material they made from it. You can definitely see some inspiration from the movies as well, as one of Snake Eyes' moves is called "Vow of Silence" which is from the movies. In the comics he was in a helicopter crash which scarred him. I do like the mix between movie inspiration and comic book inspiration the game contains, the second last mission even has a GIF image of Cobra Commander from the 80s cartoon which I think is a Great easter egg. I will say though a lot of the characters' faces look ugly, especially Duke, they were trying to go for a comic/toony look for the game with what looks like cell shading etc. But the face models themselves look ugly or odd for some characters.The game is fun but other than the campaign the game doesn't really have anything else going for it. Not a bad game at all, but it could have been better. Overall its a Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Soundtrack is good.Art is good.Gameplay is good, like playing with figure actions in childhood. Like the animation.Voices is good.Scenarios is good.Characters design is good.Level design is good.Story is good.Very faithful to the original, tanks, scenarios, airships, characters...Very funny! Cobra Commander send me to say this. (joke, in these days...)Cobraaaaaaaaa!

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with G.I.Joe and it was a major influence of my childhood, together with Star Wars and He-Man. Personally, I associate G.I.Joe mostly with the first 4-5 years of the toys and the first season of the cartoons. This is also about the timeframe they concentrate on in this game. So, as the main target audience, how is it?Its OK.Without my nostalgia glasses on, I would have certainly quit playing half way. Gameplay is fine, story is typical cliche nonsense, which is fine and fitting also.The different characters feel rather samey, but at least theres a few of them.There is a bit of fanservice hidden, like Snake Eyes incredibly good disguise, which can be unlocked.Overall, my two main critique points are:While keeping to early G.I.Joe in characters, they changed the design quite a bit. Everything looks as if someone designed it by hear-say, without knowing the original. I would have prefered a full on old school look and feel.Also, you only fight BATs in all sorts and colors... I get that this is aimed at children and you can't kill humans, but the old cartoon managed that very well. While shooting at soldiers with lasers and rockets, somehow noone got hurt. There is always a parachute. This limited enemy range makes the game a bit boring.G.I.Joe fan - get it.Never heard of G.I.Joe - search elsewhere.

name: Farewell North
detailed_description: Restore Color to the World In Farewell North you take on the unique role of a border collie restoring color to your human's world. Explore the hand-crafted, atmospheric islands inspired by the Scottish highlands and embark on a journey of companionship, trust and loss. A Spark of Life Whether it's herding flocks of sheep, highland coos, chickens or other animals, playing an impromptu game of fetch, helping the local farmers with their livestock, reuniting a trapped whale with its pod, finding lost ducklings, and much more, you're always finding ways to bring sparks of happiness to your human. Discover Hidden Paths Solve puzzles based on perspective and coloring to reveal hidden objects and paths in the environment. Find the perfect vantage point to reveal the secrets of the islands. Explore Land and Sea Journey at your own pace, running through lush grassy fields, hiking steep cliffs, and canoeing the ocean between an open world chain of islands inspired by the Scottish archipelagos of St. Kilda and Orkney. Uncover a Unique Story About Saying Farewell Unravel a unique story about saying farewell as memories reveal a glimpse into the life of the characters. Discover the events in the past which have led the characters to the archipelago, and caused all color to leave their world. Key Features Restore color to a vibrant, hand crafted world, inspired by the Scottish highlands and the famous isles of Orkney and St. Kilda Play as a loyal border collie helping a young woman recover the memories of her life Enjoy a beautiful, adaptive orchestral soundtrack featuring singing by Siobhan Miller Discover creatures and wildlife inspired by the rich history of Scottish folklore Travel by paw and by canoe as you make your way through the atmospheric isles For fans of games like Journey , Firewatch and Lost Ember

_childDocuments_.review: If you are avoiding playing this game because you're worried it'll make you feel sad, this review is for you. Yes, the game will make you feel sad. It is about grief after all. However, it's also about joy, happiness, delight, fear, curiosity and a myriad of other emotions that come from having a relationship. Grief is ultimately a pain we feel at the loss of a loved one, and the greater the love, the more pain we feel. This doesn't mean we should close ourselves off from the world though. As the pain from loss dulls, we remember the other emotions that we had with that person. The joy of their antics. The content we felt in their company. The fear when they were missing and the relief when they make it back safe and sound. This is what Farewell North is about and unfortunately to really feel the impact of these memories and emotions, we need a little sadness. Will you feel sad? Yes. Will you cry? Probably. Will you regret playing it? Never.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I started  I thought it was going to be very similar to  and and in many ways it was, with its main character being an animal you control, solving puzzles within the great outdoors wrapped up in a story about nature.  feels much less linear though. In fact, the game did a wonderful job of providing an open air feel where you could kayak around the lochs and waterways in search of islands to stop off at and explore. It is so open that it is quite easy to lose your bearings, and there is no map, compass, or any form of guidance whatsoever, so it really does feel like an adventure into the unknown. On the other hand this freedom can cause confusion and disorientation, not knowing if you were heading in the right direction, or whether you had already visited somewhere or not. After the game finishes, you are able to jump back in your boat and explore some more, picking up achievements you missed, and this is where the lack of direction and guidance becomes a little frustrating. There are indicators which tell you how many of each collectible you have acquired, but they just don't tell you where they are within the vast area of island chains. Once you are on an island there is also no location help for collectibles, so exploration is a large part of the game if you are interested in collecting these. I'm not quite sure of this but I think the story continues in a linear fashion no matter where you go, so there is a continuity of story. That's what happened in my play through anyway, although there were gold beacons and silver beacons visible when I paddled around and I went for the gold ones, so maybe the gold beacons represented story islands and the silver ones provided supporting stories? It was never explained but that might be the case. The story was well done and nicely voice acted by the daughter, reminiscing on her life with her loved ones and contemplating the future. It is a very emotional story and heavily entwined around nature and the solitude of being a shepherd in the highlands.  There are some well produced scenes with a great music track throughout and it is sure to tug at the heart strings. There are a few puzzles that need to be solved throughout your journey and some of them can be quite tricky, or at least much harder than the usual walking simulator puzzles you normally get. There is the possibility that you might get stuck on one, and there is no option to skip these puzzles, so I guess it could stop you in your tracks without a walkthrough. Most of the puzzles are the same, so once you get the idea of what to do it is just a case of finding the right items. Travelling around the islands on foot is fun, and the dog's movements are very realistic in the main, although the platforming elements to the game did feel a little cumbersome. When the dog jumps on a series of rocks, which is a common puzzle element, he does quite easily fall off, or the camera feels a little askew and you feel like you are battling with it a little. When he jumps it sometimes breaks immersion as it doesn't look right, especially if he gets stuck on something. The camera can bring about a little motion sickness and although not evident at the time I did feel a bit sick and got a headache from playing, and my friend also had this trouble playing the demo so it's just something to be aware of. Paddling on the water can also bring about a little sickness as the kayaking is quite realistic and very well done. There are two methods to the paddling, either advanced or basic, and you can choose which one you like. The game will take you around seven hours to complete, but probably double that if you want to explore and try to earn the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: I could say a lot about this game.This game is beautiful, and has a wonderful fitting score and a story with wonderful pacing and depth.This game may not be for everyone, but a lot of people will enjoy it and some may shed a few tears in the process.There is a lot to explore here and a lot of interactive gameplay, some light puzzles, and a few funny stories.The different islands and skerries you will explore are unique and some are really memorable. There are at least 12 hours of unique gameplay to do. Doing 100% in this game is a lot of fun and easy to do, even in post main game. Thinking about it, this is more of an interactive experience than a game you play when you are bored, this is an art piece.Also, the community behind this game and all the wonderful pet pictures that got shared are amazing. The bond between you as the pet and your human and the exploration of that is something a lot of people can relate to.Overall I think this game is a must-play, so stop reading and buy or wishlist the game!I promise, that if this game gives you good vibes, you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful game with a strong emotional core, and you get to play as a border collie!What made Farewell North special to me, and something that I wanted to highlight is that it joins the collective of games with positive Scottish representation, and is probably my favourite example in anything I've played. It was always is a nice surprise for things like munros and Hogmanay in Edinburgh to be referenced, and I thought the exploration of cultural erasure and feeling compelled to modify aspects of yourself to make your identity more palatable e.g , was a really great inclusion.I love story games that can make me cry and Farewell North had me in tears basically from beginning to end - it's really clear that the developers cared a lot about this project and absolutely poured everything they had into it, with stellar results. Would recommend to fans of story games and dog lovers everywhere!

_childDocuments_.review: Farewell North has touched my soul. The atmosphere is beautiful, the graphics are colorful that they fill up your soul every time the colors appear. The dialogue, music and events really capture the beauty of grief. You play a collie, so it's already a plus in my book considering I am man's best friend. The plus? You get lots and lots of pets by your owner. I streamed this game and I couldn't contain my tears on stream. That is how powerful both the dialogue mixed in the with the atmosphere and music work on you. You need to play this game at least once and real soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a 54yo dad sobbing at a video game. Maybe it's because it's so beautifully crafted with such atmospheric musical accompaniment - maybe it's because I'm both a proud Scot and a dog lover...but this hit me in the soul on so many levels.This isn't a game...it's a shared experience, it's storytelling at it's finest. Simple, honest and heartfelt.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly beautiful, from the story to the music to the visuals. I've only played about 2 hours so far and I can truly say that I don't think i've cried this much from a game in my entire life. The story is gut punching in the best possible way, and seeing everything through the eyes of the dog just makes those hard hitting moments more potent. Everything about this game is absolutely stunning.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: Farewell North is an absolute delight. You can tell it was crafted with love. I praise Kyle Banks with the quality of work put into the game--from its pleasing graphics, soul-stirring music, and touching tale.I also appreciate the emphasis on Scottish culture. I learned a lot about Cèilidh and her reasons why she moved away from her roots. It is thanks to her dog, Chesley, that brings her back and helps her process her grief. Farewell North is an excellent example of video games as an art, and there is little critique I could add.Farewell North is fairly lengthy for an indie game if you choose to explore everything. From a story standpoint, it was quite lovely, and I was thoroughly engrossed. Although from a gameplay standpoint, it sometimes was a slog to continue to the next point. However, that is negligible compared to the overall experience that I recommend to many who are looking for a heartfelt story and a taste of Scottish culture.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, has the kind of heart you can only get from an indie dev passion project. The Gameplay has just enough going on to avoid being a walking simulator; the mechanics can get a bit dull sometimes. The art and music are gorgeous, and the story made me sob at least twice, been a few days since I played and I still find myself thinking about every day. If you're looking for a pretty story based game that makes you feel feelings I would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so delicate, beautiful and moving. The visuals are stunning and createdt in a way that really enhances the emotion of the story - which had me ugly crying by the end. I love the music too and grew so fond of Chesley and all the subtle ways that he was able to bring colour into his owners life (sob). My only complaint is that I wish the game had a map, sometimes I would get lost in the skerries or on the canoe and be going round and round looking for the whisps or achievements - a map would have really helped to get a sense of what I had explored and I hadn't - since I didn't want to miss out on any detail of this wonderful piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I Cried, and I would recommend it; warning; it deals with the loss of loved ones.My thoughts on this are that it is a fantastic game that Captures what it's trying to get so well that it is packed and will make you Tear up by the halfway point and ball at the end. The colors are unique and give life to the world so well. Exploring was fun. The mechanics are Varied, and none of them are Overdone, besides maybe the canoe Mechanics, but that's just because I found them a little clunky. Overall i would Highly Recommend it The only issues I had were that the Collision for platforming was a little weird, and the Canoe Controls were Awkward.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting roughly two years for this game I was worried it wouldn't live up to the expectations I had for it, I'm incredibly happy to say I wrong but goodness, I did not expect this to hit me as hard as it did. I was a blubbering mess upon completing this, but for all the right reasons. The story is beautiful, sad but beautiful, and one so many of us are familiar with. The graphics - also perfect for the story being told and the inclusion of Gaelic truly makes it. The exploration of grief and emotion wasn't something I expected, and as mentioned hit me square in the chest and brought up a lot of things I've pushed away, love and grief go hand in hand, there is no one without the other. But if anything that should teach us to cherish what we have/have had and not hide away from it. You are a genius Mr Banks, but I think you certainly need to pay my next therapy bill. Above all else I think the main thing to take from this is the fact that often our truest friends are the ones who go through their lives without ever saying a word to us. Right, I'm going to go bury my face in my dogs fur and look up cheap trips to Scotland.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but for this I'm gonna make an exception. It's been a while since a game genuinely made me cry, but this one did. First sad tears, then happy tears. It's been an awesome roller coaster.The gameplay is fun and relaxing, not too repetitive or dull and you can unleash your inner dog in many ways that personally brought me a lot of joy.The story is very well told. Since you can explore the islands at your own discretion to a degree, it can happen that some events are a little bit out of order. There's one part where you have to herd sheep, and your human stresses out about remembering your commands, and whatnot. Only if you've been doing the optional stuff before that, you've herded sheep at least twice before without her having any trouble whatsoever, so that felt a bit... out of sequence.The world is beautiful, the switch between grays and colors is very fluid and never feels off. It was a joy to run around the hills and fields and mountains and just take in the amazing vistas and places.The graphics can be hit and miss for some I imagine, but the art style works well for the vibe and tone of the game. You can fine tune stuff like exposure, bloom and contrast to make the graphics feel a bit more or less surreal just as you prefer it.The sound design is just perfect. The ambience, the music, the sound your collar makes when you run around, the soothing voice of your human. It really transports you into the world. Not to mention the wonderful rendition of My heart's in the Highlands.If you like short but impactful games, and you're looking for something in the vein of Gone Home, Dear Esther, What Remains of Edith Finch (minus the first person, obviously), get this. You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, I wasn't prepared for this. It's a wonderful game with very serious themes that are tackled with excellent symbolism. I love the deep appreciation of nature and the deep bond between human and dog - makes me think back wistfully to our dog Jule at the time. The gameplay so far feels very polished. Exploring is fun and I get goosebumps every time I bring color back into the world. The voice actress conveys the emotions of the main protagonist very well and believably. The whole thing is accompanied by an excellent soundtrack. Visually, I find the game beautiful and the stylized art style also suits the game.And one more thing has to be said: COMFY BOY!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: This game rocked my world in the best possible way. It's a testament to a game designer who has a vision, and executes it flawlessly. I originally found this game when Kyle Banks released his first devlog on YouTube, and the mechanics he was working with looked interesting. As I continued to follow his development, it was clear to me that this was a game worth playing, and I completely stopped following it to avoid spoilers.Boy was it worth it. The story that is told in this game is executed so perfectly, especially relative to most other games I have played recently. It's the perfect embodiment of show don't tell, and it works immensely in it's favor. The gameplay is fun, interesting, and unique, and honestly the gorgeous story and impressive amount of polish on the game allowed me to overlook a few moments of clunky platforming. I cannot recommend this game more, and will be telling everyone I know who I think would enjoy this kind of game to give it a shot. Easy to finish in 3 hours if you aren't going for a 100% completion run. Easy 10/10 for me, a video game hasn't made me cry in years and this one sure did.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: This game was one of the most amazing experiences I've ever had with a game. A) I'm a dog, B) I have the ability to achievement hunt, and C) emotions. That's all I'll say. A beautiful story with such amazing game mechanics. six and a half hours was all it took to finish the majority of the game, minus a handful of achievements that I'll be going after in the coming days. If you just want to focus on the story, you'll get a solid 4 hours, maybe more, out of it. Short, but so sweet and absolutely beautiful to look at and play. 10/10, would recommend and despite it being a very straight forward game, would and will absolutely play again!
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I've followed this game and Kyle's dev journey bringing it to life with keen interest. There is something special about the vibes this game produces. I absolutely love it and have recommended it to many friends. Earlier this year, I lost my dog and since then, it's been incredibly difficult not having her around. This game has helped me cope with grief and missing my pup. I've cried during some cut scenes and during some of the game play because it touches on deep feelings. Thank you Kyle for making this game. It's truly beautiful and a healing experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: i don't have the words to truly describe this game. it is everything i hoped it would be and so much more. it is beautiful visually and as a traditional folk music enjoyer the soundtrack is really special. the gameplay is fairly straight forward but with some really well thought out and enjoyable mechanics, but the story is the stand out - it draws you in and makes you feel so connected to the both dog and the human, i was not prepared for being as emotional as i was by the endi've been following the development for a long time but it exceeded my expectations ten fold. it's a must play for anyone with connections to scotland
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I never leave reviews really. As the owner of a collie, I though "oooh! a collie game!" and bought straight away before really knowing what the game is about, and it has turned out to be my favourite game in quite a while. Aside from the fact we finally have a great game where a border collie is the main character, this game tells such an emotional story with really enjoyable gameplay and visuals that you really would require a heart of stone to not appreciate the beautiful messages spread throughout. While trying to piece together various puzzles and riddles from some dialogue, the gameplay of the puzzles and tasks themselves are really fun. I had a blast doing so many of the tasks that I was delighted to realise after I "completed" the game that I have quite a way to go with non-story aspects. It's hard to give a proper review of this game without spoiling it, but no game has ever made such an impact on me in all my years. Kyle Banks and his team took a story and presented it in such a unique and heartwarming way that you can't help but feel yourself immersed in many of the different parts of this game. John Konsolakis' score is out of this world, one of the few times that the marriage between the visuals onscreen and the sounds you are hearing is absolutely flawless and has become a favourite to listen to on it's own. As others have said, this is a sad game. But it's only sad because it helps bring up some pain in your past - which in a way is a beautiful reminder that to feel so sad, we need to have felt so much more in the first place. This game will leave you thinking for quite some time after finishing it, but eventually you will see that through the sadness is a truly gorgeous reminder of how beautiful life and relationships are.Fun, sad, challenging, heartwarming, reassuring, gorgeous. Good boy!
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: An emotional trip down memory lane. Farewell North is more than a walking simulator, similar to Anzu or Journey. It's on the shorter side, so expect around 4h - 6h of gameplay, if you just stick to the story path. There are side activities though, and with all the (easy to get) achievements to collect, one can get easily 10h - 14h worth of content.PRO+ Emotional story+ Voice acting+ OST+ Border Collie+ Good visuals+ No technical issues+ Edutainment (Scotland, Gaelic)I had a smooth experience from start to finish, so no CONs. Total recommendation 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I have only just started this game but felt compelled to make sure others know: this game is wonderful.So far, this game is truly an experience. A beautiful one. The soundscape and graphics work together to create an evocative, aesthetic, and immersive environment. This game manages to be both a calming and emotional journey and makes me want to smile and weep in equal measure. The use of colour and music is very charming (left clicking creates brief flashes of both and I find myself constantly clicking for the sensation) and the use of greyscale vs colour to carry emotions adds depth to the story. So far, the soundtrack is lovely.As for game play, occasionally you need to be closer than you think to interact with some objects but other than that I have no qualms and haven't noticed any bugs. The puzzles/challenges so far are enjoyable but not complex, which I have no issues with. This is about the journey. (This could also change as the game progresses)To Kyle. I was not born in Scotland but I have lived here for a few very happy years. And I will sadly be leaving again soon. Playing this game feels like a form of therapy as I not only grieve leaving this wonderful place I have called home, but also feel the warmth and hope inspired by the game play and story. Thank you for this wonderful little piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a poetic, soulful love letter to the Orkney Isles. A strong story explores grief. I think very highly of this game, I was very grateful I experienced it. Gameplay is intuitive and joyful puzzle solving as you control Chesley, the dog.Not challenging but enough to get into and feel you are pushing the story along. Herding sheep is a delight, as is playing fetch.The music and voice acting are excellent. This authenticity evokes emotions along the way and helps to make this a memorable experience. There is so much love poured into this, it is truly a wonderful work of art. If you love dogs and short, narrative driven indie games, don't miss Farewell North. ~Superchuffer
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: The short version: If you've read the product description and the review blurbs above and are just checking that this game is in fact worth your time, go buy it now and start exploring.I had no awareness of this game at all prior to it hitting the New Releases page of Steam, but something about the art design and the story overview sold me on it immediately. Once playing, I loved the design of the world with its eventually-revealed vibrant colors, and the variety of ways in which you bring life to that world.Farewell North to me is a game of caveats - the gameplay has its slower moments where you are just waiting to traverse from one point to another, but it also has moments where simply moving through the world brings its own joy because of the mechanics it gives you. The music might not have a technically wide variety of songs, but the main motif is well performed and the climactic song is the first game song to make me emotional on repeated listens since the Outer Wilds soundtrack. The story has some predictable points, but it also caught me off guard in how it approached some of those moments and ultimately had some very strong emotional resonance with me.There's a strong emotional core to the game that, yes as described hits on "saying farewell", but also to me said a lot about how we say "hello" after a long time away. Returning home isn't always as easy as just popping across town, physically or mentally. Farewell North was able to make a land-locked US Midwesterner feel right at home embodying the emotions and experiences of a Gaelic woman canoeing about some skerries, and overall I absolutely recommend this game to anyone who has already found themselves down in the reviews section.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, the images, the music, the feelings we can have during playing.It is a cool game with some deep thoughts inside. I like that.Anyway, I am an old man and my fingers are not at ease with the mouse and keyboard. May I suggest you to implement an easier game way in the preferences, by increasing the time to accomplish missions with the dog ? I am stuck after the sheeps, unable to bring back in time the flower to cross the bridge. And probably I'll be obliged to stop playing there. That is really sad because I like it. But it is too difficult. I know what to do, just unable to do it quickly enough...
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a lot of emotional games. So many games about loss and letting go and moving forward...but there was something so magical about Farewell North. Perhaps it was the relaxing journey across Scottish skerries or perhaps it was the connection between a border collie and his loving human companion, but I became so engrossed in this adventure. The balance between exploration on land, traveling by canoe, and interacting with the animals made the story of this pairing so much more engaging. The game does, admittedly, have it's weak points, mostly graphically it can struggle at times (clipping and getting stuck because of it) plus there are sections where collectibles are spaced pretty far out, but those didn't take away from the heartfelt experience. I definitely recommend this to any players who love games like Spirit of the North or Lost Ember or basically any player who love to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it!A wonderful story that had the same heart strings as Bridge of Teribithia.    The artistic form of graphics blended well into the story. I think the only thing i felt was missing, is maybe have the theme song performed in Gaelic as a treat, during the end game credits.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the making of this game for two years. It sat on my wishlist from August 27th, 2022. I kept up with it in the discord and now it's finally here. The premise of a game where you play to restore colour to the world is such a wonderful idea that has now been put to practice. As someone who has struggled with depression, this game is a glimpse into what that can be like and how things can bring colour back into life. It's beautiful and so incredibly well done. About a year ago I played the demo and that just made me more excited to play it. Now it's finally here and I can't wait to discover the whole story and all that comes with it. Well done, Kyle!
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply touching and humane story, even though you play most of the time as a Border Collie. I find it incredible how high the production quality is considering how few people were involved in the development.It looks beautiful, the music is great, and it's well-written and voiced. Above all, it has an incredible atmosphere that strongly reminded me of last year's Season: A Letter to the Future.The puzzles and gameplay are simpler and slightly repetitive, but it didn't bother me at all.I enjoyed exploring optional islands or just go for a hike on the surrounding hills and always learn something more about the story. I didn’t see absolutely everything, but after finishing the game, there’s an option to continue exploring, which is a nice touch.There's a photo mode and I really appreciate that! (Although I had to get used to the controls a bit). The technical state is good; apart from one stuck sheep and minor collision glitches, I didn’t have any issues.Finished in one day, almost in one sitting. I highly recommend Farewell North to anyone who enjoys slice-of-life games, touching stories, and artistic video games! Be prepared to cry!Kyle, thank you so much; you’ve created a beautiful piece of art, that I’ll remember for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: farewell north is one of the rare indie games where the entire experience feels like one cohesive idea. the music, the environment, the visual effects, the gameplay; everything you experience contributes to the story it tells. its clear how much heart and soul was put into making this. farewell north is more than an experience worth having; i feel it's one thats important to have.

_childDocuments_.name: Farewell North

_childDocuments_.review: To be completely fair to this game, I won't be able to finish it because of a personal problem: motion sickness. Something about the way this game's camera moves made me well and truly sick (especially the canoe sections), and I had to stop after just a few play sessions. With that out of the way - the parts of the game that I did get to play were absolutely *gorgeous*. I think that's the biggest strength of this game, that the visual aspect is really beautiful and unique. I also thought the perspective of the dog was a fun twist, and I especially enjoyed the way certain things were portrayed because you were a dog. The additional language subtitles were also a really nice touch.My only disappointment with the game (and again, I only got to play like 2 hours) was that the story seemed pretty basic/heavy-handed. _childDocuments_.review: This is a very emotional game that will certainly do best with people fully capable of feeling the spectrum of emotions humans typically feel.  I've long since forgotten what that's like, but I can still appreciate the story that is being told here.At its core it's a story of loss, love, and friendship.  It's very touching, even if you're not a dog person.  I think most people have had a pet at some point,so it'll likely tug at your heart strings at least a few times.  The story plays out through various moments of chit-chat between our main characters, and a few memory type elements tossed in as well.  You have your main story modes, but you also have a lot of things off the beaten path that serve as a type of side quest.Gameplay is mostly you as Chesley running around doing dog things.  You have the ability to bring color back to the world, which will open up paths and open up some story elements.  It works fairly well, though there's a bit of jank going on.  Occasionally you may find yourself with some sort of strange slow motion jumps, and other times you might be curious enough to try to climb up mountains to see how much of an area you can explore for real.The pacing is great.  The gameplay loop never becomes difficult and rarely introduces new elements, but the pacing of the story and exploration makes the game feel incredibly smooth progress wise.

_childDocuments_.review: As I started playing "Farewell North", I didn’t find it very adventurey. Sure, it was cool running around as a dog chasing a little blue light around, but the otherwise colorless setting didn’t warm my heart. Then I faced the first obstacles and things got more interesting, and even a little tricky here and there. And when I succeeded in returning color to the first island I visited, it was as if the entire game came to life for me, and the shared magical journey of Chesley and Cailey touched a chord inside me. It’s a very serious game, uncovering deep emotions, but it includes just enough comic relief, like Chesley’s interactions with the wildlife. What at first seemed little more than a cozy exploration game became something resembling a real-life adventure through a jaw-droppingly beautiful land I’d love to visit personally. The narrative builds up to a bittersweet finale through a variety of fun gameplay styles as you feel ever more invested in the deep love between woman and dog, making it ideal for animal lovers, nature fans, or anyone who could use a little more color in their own lives.

_childDocuments_.review: I know this publisher from having played  a while back. I'm really glad to see they published for another developer this time and under a similar style of game.Firstly I didn't go full completion on this, I wanted to play through the story and not be distracted by the collectibles. It does limit some of the experiences I guess, but from what I could tell it wasn't really necessary. Besides you can go back at the end of the game and free roam to collect them later.Having played games like RiME I felt like I knew what was coming, but the developer did a good job of keeping the truth hidden until it was time. The story was very sad but not in a bad way, it handles topics around loss and closure so be prepared. I really enjoyed the way in which you were tasked with helping the woman in this story with the limitations of being a dog. How I interpreted the style of the world is what the dog understands through its eyes, this is made more apparent in the city chapters where buildings zig-zag and distort and traffic filled roads are shown as a loud blurry obstacle.There's a ton of dialogue in this game as you progress through the land and visit all the various landmarks. The music is quite good, it has a memorable theme song that you discover/remember as you journey around. The song lyrics have hints that reveal what's behind the curtain in the story.My only gripes are that the controls can be clunky at times, the dog feels floaty when trying to platform. Some puzzles guide you well, and others are too obscure. The herding can turn into a nightmare when the flock breaks apart and they path towards cliff ledges. Sometimes you can get away with herding just one animal, say to open a path, but other puzzles require all of them. The wisp collectibles should have been a single activation to collect, or maybe two in some areas with fewer of them, three felt like a bit much and to me was just a heavy distraction from the story at the time.

_childDocuments_.review: Short summary: Phenomenal experience all around! Pleasing aesthetics, beautiful music, interesting gaelic setting, engaging and believeable story, with an ending to shed a tear or two.The game is mostly a walking/running game accompanied by narrative and exploration, with minor jumping sections and puzzles, and it's set around several islands off the northern coast of scotland.Between the islands your main means of transportation is a canoe, with some interesting physics/mechanics, basically you can control when to paddle left and right, and it behaves pretty much like it would RL, you have to alternate the paddling in a rythm to stay on course.Takes a little getting used to, but gets surprisingly intuitive pretty fast. If that's not your thing, you can enable simplified controls in the options menu.The order in which you visit the islands to discover new side stories is mostly up to you and non-linear, but may be locked until you progress enough. Only the "main" story islands have to be visited in order, which unlocks new "side story" islands each time.There is some similarities to other similar games, mainly "Spirit of the North" and maybe "Lost Ember".The dev also stated inspiration from Journey, The First Tree and Flower.If you liked those games, this will most certainly also appeal to you.There are already a lot of other games with these same characteristics around, but only few manage to captivate all the way through to the end like Farewell North does, and then culminates in one of the most heartfelt endings I have yet witnessed in such games.The game deals with many feelings of loss and it's acceptance, uncertainty, finding our place in the world while taking pride in where we came from and where we are headed.From a technical standpoint, there is nothing to complain about, it runs good, looks good and sounds good. I didn't encounter any noticeable bugs, BUT the game did crash twice, always when canooing. However the last save was never more than a minute away, so it's not that bad.There isn't really much else to say really, the playtime may "just" be 8-10 hours, but that is a good thing in books.Time is valueable, and this game feels like it really valued my time all the way through, the pacing was perfect, and it never got dull.For that, I will glady recommend it at full price, both Kyle Banks (mostly solo dev) and John Konsolakis (composer) deserve it for this masterpiece.Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: Farewell North - 9/10Completion Time - 9 Hours (Completionist)An emotional journey through the Scottish Highlands. In Farewell North, you’ll follow Cailey and her border collie, Chesley, as they explore the islands of the Scottish Highlands. You’ll play as Chesley who helps restore the color to Cailey’s world as she struggles to say farewell. Each island will have unique puzzles to solve from herding sheep, to finding new pathways, tracking wild animals, etc. in order to reintroduce that spark of color and discover little details about the past and why they have revisited the highlands.Farewell North is such an incredibly beautiful game that the developer poured so much love and care into. I had such an amazing time exploring each island and uncovering Cailey and Chesley’s story. As someone who has three dogs of her own and sometimes finds myself wading through a colorless world, I definitely connected to the idea that dogs truly bring that color back into our lives. The puzzles weren’t overly challenging and I loved the little checklist of finding all of the collectables on a particular island. This really helped with achievement hunting since you knew exactly what island had how many of what collectable, but it also made you want to set off and explore more - really taking your time and soaking in the beauty of the game. Additionally, the soundtrack was absolutely beautiful. One of the collectibles were music notes scattered across the water accessible by kayaking to them. Each music note you picked up would play a small bit of a lovely song about the highlands. Now, I didn’t really care for the kayaking in the game, mostly because I just wasn’t very coordinated with it (even when I switched the controls to simple kayaking). But let’s face it, I’m not very coordinated with it in real life either. The only thing that prevented it from getting a perfect score were a few bugs and glitches I encountered. Although you are able to jump as Chesley, if you go outside of the perimeters of where you were meant to be, the game didn’t really like that and would stutter step you and become a bit glitchy. There were some instances where I was trying to take a quicker route because I saw a collectable and would get a little stuck in certain places. There was a path up one of the steep mountains and although I could clearly see the brown pathway, there was some type of wall not allowing me to continue on the trail. Eventually, I kept pushing through it and got through so it wasn’t a game breaking fault. I also fell through the floor when Chesley went to dig up something. We just dug a little too far, and that’s okay. Again, none of the bugs I encountered were game breaking, and I’m sure a patch will come out to address these if it hasn’t already. I am a part of their discord, and Kyle is incredibly responsive. I can’t emphasize how wonderful of a game this is and feel like everyone should go on this small journey. Games rarely bring me to tears, but this one had me sobbing…in a happy way. In fact, I was still tearing up a little as I wrote this. I’m so incredibly happy I got to know a little more about Cailey and Chesley and highly recommend giving Farewell North a try. It’s worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful, gentle and deeply moving story/exploration/casual puzzle game about loss, the impermanence of the world we know and the way life must continue regardless - with a truly adorable protagonist.The gameplay is straightforward and unlikely to present a serious challenge to most gamers, although there are a few puzzles which require a bit of lateral thinking. The controls are generally good and frustration is low. I did manage to get myself stuck at one point in my playthrough requiring a reload.Visuals are excellent for a game with such a small crew - evocative and genuinely beautiful at times. However, audio work was the absolute standout for me - superb music and really excellent voice work.The story is emotional and sensitively told. If you are dealing with recent loss it may hit you hard though, be warned.If you like the sound of the above, I strongly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot emphasize how well written the story is in Farewell North. Throughout the game, you learn of the relationship between Chesley (the dog), Cailey (the protagonist), and Cailey's mom. Though it focuses on loss, the relationship between the three characters is one that anyone can relate to even if they have not lost a loved one of their own. The story is even further enhanced by the atmospheric and occasionally intense music, the stunning visuals, and the brilliant use of the main gameplay mechanic of reviving color to the world. The puzzles are quite well-made, and don't take away from the main focus of the story.I will say there are things for the game to improve on. The game could have made it a little clearer on how much progress I was making towards the actual story, so I accidentally finished the actual story before actually having done all the lighthouses, benches (not sure what their use is yet, will report back once I do), and song lyrics. However, not having 100% in the game before ending it did not take away from the actual ending, and the game does return you to the world afterwards to go back and continue exploring.I've been following Kyle Banks on TikTok for a couple years or so, and I fully anticipated that when Farewell North would release it would immediately become one of my favorite indie games. However, I could never have anticipated losing my own childhood dog two months ago, nor could I have anticipated the emotional impact of this game following my dog's death (I've been writing this review through tears). If that doesn't say something about how good this game is, I don't know what will. The story alone puts this game at an 8, however taking everything into account I would rate this game a solid 9 out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely story.The gameplay elements are basic with a heavy emphasis on story and exploration. Minor puzzles with platforming elements. Definitely would purchase a sound track of this game since they would just bring me back into the moments found within the game. The gameplay itself isn't the smoothest, some minor bugs may occur if you try to play it like a standard puzzle platformer (quick jumps and thinking too deeply on a puzzle) take it slow and enjoy the story instead.Overall, if you like Story Games, this is definitely a keeper. Try to avoid spoilers for your first playthrough.

As a victim you must use your wits and stealth to stay out of the Family's reach and find the tools you need to lead to your eventual freedom. Slaughter Family players must seek out, track down, and stop their guests from escaping. Players of The Texas Chain Saw Massacre can finally find out if they have what it takes to survive. Experience the mad and macabre for yourself in The Texas Chain Saw Massacre.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting years for another fun asymmetrical horror game to launch, and finally my prayers have been answered with Texas Chain Saw Massacre. TCM cuts out a lot of the padding other asymmetrical horror games contain and makes both roles (victim and family) enjoyable to play. Matches often don't take long to finish (~10 minutes/match), but in that time you're granted a tense, blood pumping, challenge to escape/kill. Too often do games in this genre become action games with a horror theme after the fear begins to wash away. With about 50 hours under my belt it's still pretty scary thanks to hard work and time spent in audio and visual design.GUN Interactive and Sumo Digital did a great job at giving this horror classic a proper video game release.

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst the game is fun, I really just can't recommend it at it's current price point.I'll list my pros and cons and reasons why:Pros:-Game feels relatively balanced so far (albeit a little killer sided)-Playing killer (family) with friends is incredibly entertaining-Diverse characters and skills/abilities-Graphics are pretty good and general game-play is fine.Cons:-No option to remap the key-binds (seriously? It's 2023) making it kinda difficult to play for a leftie-RNG with which character you get given, you're thrown into a game with a random character, and if you don't like it, tough, rematch and hope you get your character next game- Crashes and bugs GALORE. I've crashed too many times to count, and had a game-losing bug where my tab menu got stuck on my screen- The price (What???)-Feels kinda luck based whether you escape as a Victim or not - if you find the fuse, you're sorted and can escape relatively fast, any other escapes feel fruitless.-This is a unique con, but I have been held CAPTIVE in a game before by a survivor that kept abusing the wells, jumping down, looping up and round, then jumping down again. (Possibly could have been remedied by not having a family member DC, but i'm not sure.) - This kept me in the game for 45 minutes, until my game bugged out and she escaped because of it. - a game timer would easily fix this.-Tutorials teach you mechanics but not other essential skills.Overall, i'm enjoying the game play, and I will be playing more, but due to the cons outweighing and the game being generally somewhat difficult if not infuriating to play at times, I really cannot recommend it. I borrowed half from a good friend to buy this game but would've been incredibly disappointing at the full price point. The game feels like an early access mess and is honestly pretty bare bones. Playing solo is not worth my time and playing with a +1 is entertaining, but does not negate all the cons. TLDR ; Bugs, scuffed gameplay, and lack of control mapping makes this game not worth the price. Feels like an overpriced early access game ATM.

_childDocuments_.review: Lacks players. Despite being a co-op game, there is absolutely no communication in lobbies. The player base also routinely quits, sometimes prolonging the ability to find the necessary number of players to even start a match. In addition, there is a timer feature for lobbies. This means if you only have 6/7 of the required players by the end of the countdown, everyone is sent back to relaunch at the title screen to repeat the process again. My first three lobbies were unable to produce a playable match. This burnout of a game is a joke for 30$ (price on sale) because there is no indication that the development will adequately rectify the situation. The player base is rapidly declining, (which is a death sentence for a multiplayer game) and definitely not something you can change with the latest patch. Looking at the 10$ skins and neglect to balance the game in favor of P2W characters, the absurd asking price is part of some short-term effort to help milk all possible profit from this knowingly dying project. Just play it on gamepass.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a thorough review but as a lifelong fan of the franchise and gaming I think you'll find my perspective a worthwhile read. At the time of writing, (4/2024) I have almost 250 hours in TCM, over 4k hours in DBD and countless hours on other games in this genre, so I'll be coming at this review fairly seasoned... with quite a bit of salt. As an online only game I waited awhile to post a review to see how the game was shaping up and unfortunately it's unlikely I'll be needing to update this review in the future. However, if there are vast improvements I will do so. Let's get into it.The graphics are what you'd expect from a modern game, very nice visuals and uncommon for the Asym horror genre most of the action is taking place in the daylight. As with Gun's previous attempt there is a lot of attention to detail from the first movie in the game, namely the family house map. The additional maps they designed from scratch also feel like they belong in this universe. Playing the game at launch was a surreal experience, prior to the community fully understanding the games mechanics the game felt like you were thrown into the movie.  Leatherface performs as you'd expect him to, the creative license they took with the cook and the hitchhiker's abilities felt reasonably lore accurate. Sadly, that's where the positives end.The meta for the survivor side has essentially destroyed the game concept, and nearly every match you will get you will see this in action. As a survivor there is no reason to silently hide in the shadows, waiting for an opportunity to escape. Instead, you will be spamming your action key to unbind yourself at the start of the match and race to get a door open from the lower level to make your way up and outside as quickly as possible. This strategy is used for multiple reasons. First, the family gets stronger as the match progresses. Most of the killers, aside from Leatherface, start far away from the survivors and most require some setup time in order to be productive. By racing the exit you deny the killers the ability to get in position and also to stop them from gathering blood to level up grandpa.. which both stops you from getting aura detected and denies the killers unique 'grandpa perks'. Characters like Cook, Hitchhiker and the new addition, Nancy have to quickly sprint to setup their traps and locks. Youtube search 'fastest tcm escape' and you'll find that it's possible to escape in under  When you consider how long it takes to get into a match you realize how futile this whole experience is, more on that later. Survivors abilities and perks can completely hard counter certain killers whereas this is not true the other way around. For example, the perk 'bomb squad' denies both the hitchhiker and nancy their traps as you no longer need to gather bone scraps to disarm them while also giving you up to a 50% increase in speed. Perk 'immunity' denies sissy her poison, Virginia not only blinds all killers with her ability but can take Leatherface out of his chainsaw sprint and can also remove all blood gathered by any killer who walks into it.  If you actually manage to get into a chase escaping is a breeze once you learn your way around each map. There are gaps, crawl spaces, barricades and wells you can utilize that can guarantee you an escape if the killer is closing in. Only Leatherface can destroy barricades and crawl spaces, while hitchhiker and sissy can utilize crawl spaces and gaps. Even still, there are so many gaps located on every map you can run these an infinite amount of times to where it is not feasible for ANY one killer to dedicate time to the chase, as the average match today lasts five minutes or less and the greater priority for killer is to secure exits from the remaining survivors, which there are four. As there are only 3 killers vs 4 survivors it's already impossible to guard all exits let alone dedicate time to a long chase; putting the killer in a lose/lose scenario. Communication and teamwork is essential to succeed as killer while a survivor can escape on their own in seconds. I'm not even going to get into the door slamming... The only exception to all of this is the family map. If the original cast is selected the cook can lock all three doors leading to the exterior while hitchhiker can trap both staircases and front window as leatherface sprints in a circle on the first floor. Due to the small profile of the house this map is the only exception for the family team where they can have advantage.GUN felt it a good design decision to make this game exist prior to the first movie. Not only is this game locked into one franchise but character's from the sequels are unlikely to make an appearance. This is a pretty foolish decision considering it's primary competitor has over a dozen franchises full of characters already... including this one. It's been said this is due to licensing restrictions but this is something that should have been both addressed and resolved in pre-production. Unless you were a fan of the series you probably wouldn't care about being able to play as chop-top, lefty, stretch, benny or alfredo; but you should. The 'new' characters they've added to the game have either no depth or don't belong. Sissy and Johnny are clearly based on real life killers involved in the Tate/LaBianca murders. They've conflated the Sawyer family with the Manson's, which is both uninspired and in poor taste. And yes, TCM was inspired by Ed Gein but at least Tobe Hooper made the characters his own. 'Nancy' is a generic knock off of mama from TCM3 and Tea lady from TCM2k3. The less said about that the better.Aside from the balance of the game, there's even bigger issues. Actually getting to play the game! It took me hours to get this game to run on my 4090 setup. Continual crashes after I somehow managed to get a successful lobby had me tinkering away with graphical settings until I finally got it to load into a match. But let's talk about those lobbies though... what a horrid design. Killers often leave with nobody wanting to join and replace them (again, largely due to poor balance for the family). This often times takes 5-15 minutes to get into a match, making wanting to play the game feel absolutely brutal when the matches are guaranteed to be shorter than the lobby wait time. If a killer doesn't join the lobby to replace whoever left within a certain period all players are kicked back to the main screen. GREAT! If you click 'quick join' you are guaranteed to be picked as family, as I can count on one hand how many times it picked me as survivor over the last month.Does this game have a future? Unfortunately it's highly unlikely. Sumo has abandoned ship and Gun has once again decided to call forth the talent of Black Tower Studios. If you are unaware of this company that's probably not too surprising. They were brought on to continue development of Friday the 13th: The game to continue maintenance patches. They fixed almost nothing. Instead, the game suffered from more issues that it had during it's launch. Today, F13 has less than 100 concurrent players on steam. TCM has less than 1,000, which is a far cry from it's competitor, which teeters anywhere between 30,000-40,000 players on average. Unless there is some dramatic turn of events I expect TCM will lose half of it's steam playerbase or more by this time next year at which point this game will go into the sunset.If you haven't purchased and played the game yet there is little reason why you should. The DLC packs are ridiculously priced for what you get compared to DBD. In the coming month's the game+DLC's will likely drop from it's retail to 50% off or lower.  Just wait and see if GUN proves me wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Well what i will say is it not a terrible game like a lot of people say it is, sure its a game with limited content at the moment but it does have some great moments especially if you have friends that will play with you as well. I started playing survivor and was shocked just how much fun i was having i don't usually play survivor in theses types of games but here it felt right, the atmosphere coupled with the claustrophobic environments and the relentless killers and their psychotic babble truly makes a great little horror experience and a consistent challenge. Killers are no less fun as hell to play, CHALLENGING but fun!  and to me the characters distinct personalities, kills, dialog, and voice acting all good for the most part here other me hope that the new all the new characters become part of the lore.  Playing online solo IS fun...at times, and that brings me to the CONS of this game.  There are issues here as with any asymmetrical in regards to balancing, people disconnecting, not working together, some stages being funner than others with the few that there are. Lobby's also take a min to fill up so prepare for the possibility of a wait in some cases. I do worry for the future content as well taking a little long to roll out, things like cosmetics, weapons, balancing etc. REGARDLESS i personally am having alot of fun in the game and want to continue playing. For all that it does right in my opinion its pretty well worth it, especially if there is a discount which is something i would also recommend holding out for.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just gonna say straight up there is one big reason I'm leaving a negative review: Paid DLC characters without anyway to purchase with earned in-game. (I don't care about paid skins, chainsaw noises or executions. If the TCM devs want to make money through that I'd wholeheartedly defend that.) Just don't block two of the arguably top tiers characters behind a paywall...I rarely purchase new games full price, especially such a bare-bones that had a sudden burst of success, but I watched enough youtubers playing it, looked at reviews and character build videos then finally just thought "What the hell might as well buy it while it has a decent player base." No point in buying a discounted dead game in a years time, right? It had a lot of things I think are great potential for an upcoming game, a great fan base who praise the game, unlockables which reward grinding different characters, a lot of perks (some are useless, but i get a kick out of constantly leveling up even them.), different play styles, generally good looking game without performance issues, etc...It has a decent amount of technical issues: 1) If you get caught in a trap and jump out a window simultaneously the window breaks, but you stay in the trap, sometimes it works out for the victim because family members get caught in a cool-down animation hitting air, sometimes it just gets you 3 way gang-ganged by the family either side.2) Hitting victims can be a pain if the game decides you're somehow missing and revving up a full leatherface chainsaw swing and watching it go through a victim without doing anything is frustrating.3) Back stabs are a pain because the have the same button as grappling, so 50% of the time a back stab prompt ends up grappling when you're clearly behind that family member. (Sometimes you don't even get either options...)4) Connection issues are definitely a thing, I don't have them, but a lot of people do and it ends up leaving games dead if for example two of the killers DC'ed randomly. When combined with lobby waiting times it can make finding a decent game pretty tedious.5) Related to the last point and this review in general: Lobby dodging is a bad thing in TCM, which is made worse by people who want to play the content that they paid for and leave as soon as they figure out they can't play the character they want because someone else is in the same position. Something needs to be done about lobby dodging, increased lobby wait times or lower que priority, not being able to play the same character two in a row, etc... All in all it's a fun game, it's like any asymmetrical game (mainly DBD from my experience), it has issues, but for the most part it's a fun mess that you knew what you were getting into. I'm by no means a fan of Behaviour (DBD dev's) I do not pay money for skins and I use in-game currency to buy characters, but at least they have an understandable excuse for making licensed characters unbuyable with in-game currency as they need to purchase the rights and come to agreements to branded content which obviously brings in fresh new players. What is the excuse for TCM? Apparently the devs do not have full TCM licencing, so why not either make a content you've got the rights to or just make new unlicensed content as long as its TCM related. Until new playable content is free/can be earned I will not change this negative review because that's just how disappointed I feel with the direction the devs have taken this game.

_childDocuments_.review: While I had a great time for the first 40 or so hours of playing it, major flaws started to emerge once family and victim players reached level 10 and the meta was established. There's a perk in this game that allows you to incapacitate grandpa and take him from level 5 down to level 1, which breaks a major game mechanic. Victims are able to easily leave the basement and easily escape since there are 4 exit points, 2 of which are incredibly easy, and the other 2 are moderately easy with a second player and coms. The game has only 3 maps, so games have started becoming repetitive. I'd wait for a deep discount towards the end of 2023 before picking this one up. It's good, don't get me wrong... but it'll need a lot more content and a lot more balancing. I cannot recommend it in its current state. Will change my review to positive when the game gets properly balanced for both family and victim, and when we have more than just 3 maps.

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed playing this game, but some issues have been mentioned in other reviews that I should address. Firstly, the game has a steep learning curve, and it may not be easy for beginners who don't have friends to play with. You may find yourself dying frequently.In addition, it can take a long time to get into a match as a victim vs. family since more people are playing victims. This can be discouraging. However, if you have a full party of three for "The Family", you're set and your matches should pair up pretty quickly.I've seen some complaints that you have to pay for cosmetics, but I don't see that as any different from DBD. If anything, this game gives you 5 or 6 outfits per pack (recolors) for a 4.99-6.99 price range, while one outfit in DBD may cost as much as $10. So, I'm not sure why people are complaining about that.Overall, the game is fun and has much more replayability than DBD. Don't get me wrong, I enjoy DBD from time to time, but it does have a measure of monotony to it. You have to repair 5 gens or escape from a hatch. There's no real variation even with a map change.With this game, there are multiple ways to escape: Steam Gate, Car Battery, Generator, Exit Gates, or Fuse Box. Each of these is generated in a couple of different places at random. There's also much more strategy involved since you might want to start to open a steam gate to divert attention to another exit, as an example.Victims can fight back using bone scraps or, with the upcoming victim,  use poison against the family. All of these things make this game much more enjoyable to me than repairing five gens and escaping. Especially since the family can replace fuses, turn gens, or car batteries back on...assuming Danny hasn't tampered with them.Lastly, Leatherface is a total beast and, yes, a good player can get a critical hit and KO with one swing of his chainsaw. He's Leatherface. If you don't like dying...do gooder, ♥♥♥♥♥.
