_childDocuments_.review: Well this is awkward...My review used to be positive, but currently I would not recommend tcm. At it's core, it's still a great game. If you were to start playing, you'd probably enjoy it. So why the bad review?This game lacks a lot of content and it's future is very unclear. In comparison, their other game Friday the 13th took awhile to get new dlc out as well. However, there was a LOT of base game content to keep you interested. Lots of UNLOCKABLE counselors and Jasons to keep the game fresh for a long time. Because of this, it had a playerbase up until the end.I understand TCM wants to be it's own separate game, but they abandoned all of the things that made F13th so successful. All future content is locked behind expensive paywalls which is basically the kiss of death. With nothing to look forward to unless you pay ten dollars for a singular character (excluding cosmetics and extra kills for family), why keep playing? The new characters also conveniently have very strong powers that are game changing. The more dlc they release, the more you'll be pressured into buying it since people want to play the meta game. This does not bode well when it comes to longetivity.The lack of a roadmap is worrisome. I understand they didnt want to fail to deliver and that a roadmap can cause this to happen due to pressure. I would still like there to be more communication than whatever is going on now. I have no idea where this game is headed and that's a little worrying. They could very well surprise us all and begin releasing good updates but as to when that could happen, I have zero clue. It's been very quiet.I really hate saying this because I want this game to succeed, but I feel like I'm just waiting for them to drop a white text post any day now. It's not the end yet, but I'd say this game is definitely in trouble at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Woo boy. Was looking forward to this one and even gave them a week to iron out issues but there's just too much wrong with the game to recommend it in its current form. Refunded it after 4 hours or so.Leatherface just isn't fun to play. Most of your gameplay is running around, getting a hit occasionally and then being stuck in destruction animations. On top of that there's currently a rev bug which makes your chainsaw overheat every time the grandpa cutscene happens and you're actively revving. You'll overheat and your chainsaw will sometimes be bugged for the rest of the match. My GF has said this sometimes happens with other family members too; some weird animation thing will happen and she can't attack anymore.The grandpa awakened animation IN GENERAL takes about 5 seconds, interrupts the gameplay for everyone and is a pain. The devs clearly never played Castlevania 2 Simon's Quest. What a horrible night to have a curse! Yeah, it sucked in the 80s and it sucks now. Come on.There's a victim build that lets you get stun locked by Leland and it is very unfun, and again, you're just stuck in an animation, waiting. Killers shouldn't feel like the victims, and this aspect clearly wasn't playtested.The skill tree is bad. We can't see what we are specing into, meaning you have to blindly go down a tree and then respec to SEE the other parts of the trees that get locked off.On the victim side once you know what you're doing you can escape very quickly. I'm talking in under 3, maybe 2 minutes.As a Friday the 13th and DBD player I'm pretty disappointed here. It's not bad but it's very mid, buggy and shallow in its current form. Save your money or try it out on Gamepass for free.EDIT: Actually went back and tried it again on Gamepass. Sadly the game gets worse the more you play. I forgot to mention that the basements are maze like and confusing (and depending on your killer you have to navigate it differently, meaning you'll run into many dead ends, and half the time you'll struggle to find the door to the upstairs), the gameplay in general can sometimes leave you wandering around aimlessly for several minutes doing nothing as killer and there's glitches and bugs galore on both sides. I'm not trying to be a hater here but Jesus, what a fall from grace this was from Friday the 13th.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is extremely unbalanced at the moment, it is fun but it is so hard to win as victim without spending hours memorizing every aspect of the map. The door close mechanic is straight up broken, anytime you try to slam a door or close a metal one, the killers just glitch right through. Once you're alone as victim it is impossible to do anything, the game actually punishes you by having grandpa at max level where no matter what you cannot run or do any objectives, like ten seconds after everyone dies. There are multiple exits but the only viable ones include kicking a generator and then running out of a gate, which of course the killers all just camp every game. I've seen people complain it is too easy for victims to win, but it's only easy for hardcore victims who learn the best path to take every time. If there is only one viable escape in the game, what's even the point of having more? Anytime I have ever even seen someone escape or myself escape, it is always through the same escape every single time, assuming the killers aren't camping it. If there is three killers, why not put like 5-6 victims in one match to balance it out? 3v4 doesn't seem very fair as the killer can just all focus on one or two people at a time, screwing them over. The killers have plenty of advantages, Grandpa will see you even if you start an animation before he is active, still seen. Killers just have to camp objectives and they will win, or at least get 3/4 of them consistently. Family mains will always complain, but then get surprised when everyone rushes the one viable route in the entire game. Put more victims in and give us a fighting chance, then it would be more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I previously gave this game a positive review but I sadly gotta make it a negative one.The game is absolutely fun, especially with friends, but it struggles in many critical areas.With the same gameplay loop with each objective always being in the same place, no possibility to change keybinds, a struggle minigame that is practically impossible to win as a killer unless you want to destroy your finger, an exit which is practically a guarantee for survivors to escape through (fuse box) and a level system that locks you from creating the build that you'd like, I simply can not recommend the game.  Furthermore, it's difficult to see how the game can provide new content in the future since they only got the rights to the 1973 movie. I believe that by addressing the issues above and finding a reliable way to provide new content and battle toxicity, this game can live for a long time. Without that, I think it might suffer the same fate as others within the genre.If you got some friends to play with I'd recommend paying no more than 20eur.

Then you unhook yourself in the basement of some house and try to find find your way out of the basement. After that you are just roaming around doing some random tasks to escape that hillbilly hellhole  Hillbilly family members are all crazed lunatics who will stab/bash/smack/bang the living sh*t out of you while you are just trying to get away from there. Being part of the hillbilly gangbang squad was pretty straight forward, stab stab stab/saw them to bits and feed your grandpa with blood of the poor victims. We mostly played against experienced players with maxed out traits, so matches were stomps as we were just confused toddlers trying to make it. Everytime I managed to get into the puzzle solving, almost instantly these fanatical hillbillies had surrounded me and beating me together like I was a piñata.  As if these things weren't enough, my 2 teammates (teenage girls) are mocking and laughing at my poor puzzle performance. To top it off they said something similar to this like: "We shouldn't mock him, he is an old man".The f*ck ?As I was calmly panicking trying to find a button to open up my mic (to politely inform them that isn't very nice thing to say to people), it was too late, they were gone.If you 2 teammates read this, I just want to say: I'm perfectly fine-aged, thank you.All in all, experiences on this game left me with sour taste in my mouth accompanied by existential crisis. _childDocuments_.review: There's plenty of other reviews that highlight what bugs are present, some game breaking, some just dumb that they're in place at all so I won't bother with them, just be aware that they exist without any sort of tracking. They have also confirmed no road-map, take of that what you will.  Even assuming the game was free of bugs (which it isn't) the balance just really isn't there, every game seems to be heavily one sided. Against uncoordinated survivors, there's no real challenge, just rush towards them and you win. Against coordinated survivors they're out and free before the gramp cut scene has played and stunned Bubba. Although it's difficult to fully blame balance due to the subtle hacks people have freely been using. The perk system in the game is a little strange, allowing people to freely respec their trees but having random perk nodes that could be any perk. Which essentially results in repeated respecing until you get the perks you want, I'm unsure why a 'choose your own perk' system isn't utilised rather than wasting 20 minutes for something useful. Not to mention a few perks don't seem to work at all. The matchmaking system seems to be a trial and error approach from the devs, rather than any actual system for matchmaking they recommend leaving lobbies if you don't want to risk a 6 player game. I can't imagine the long wait time for a game isn't due to play count, rather than seemingly randomly throwing players into half full lobbies without any sort of 'pending' time to work out where best to place 7 people at once. A lot of the good reviews for this game are saying 'It needs some polish but it'll get there. Have some patience'. It's a $40 game that has had 3 months from tech tests to resolve these issues and an additional 3 weeks of it being live. Instead they shipped a game with debug functions and without any sort of anti cheat on one of its platforms. I'm not even going to mention cross play removal since it never should have been an answer to a hacking problem they created.Aside from the above issues, there is a solid foundation for a fun game with friends (unless they're on console.) If they start to resolve the bugs that people have been raising for months then perhaps it will be more enjoyable I wouldn't part with your money in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: The release day was somewhat bad with couple of nearly game breaking bugs: unable to find a match, error during joining a match or launching the game, servers kicking you out because of "timed out connection" or any other weird reason, if at least one person leaves a lobby then it becomes nearly impossible to fill that gap and find one freaking player out of 10k people, not to mention console players which are not included in here. Also there are some minor visual bugs too but nothing really worth of mentioning, except animations when sometimes killing a player leads to his character's body to be broken in every was possible. Sometimes it's fun to see and not really a big deal if you ask me. Introduced skill tree and perk system is okay but requires a bit of balancing with character abilities as well, since some characters are obviously stronger than the others. Every time you level up any character using a skill tree, you get attribute points to upgrade that particular character's characteristics. The only thing you can't manipulate by those points is a character's speed, other than that you can do whatever and make an absolute monster with busted characteristics(tons of stamina or absurd amount of damage if playing as a killer, etc).While playing as victims(survivors) you will see Sonny getting hooked and slashed by Bubba in a cutscene every match because of his inability to do something good enough, so rarely anyone plays him. As a victim, the game awards you for being aggressive which could be a good and a bad thing at the same time, depends on how you see it. Stealth is meh, except in some situations when you really want to lose a killer(to finish an objective or heal for example). The more people will get better in this game, the less you will see someone use this mechanic a lot. Despite clunky release, the game is lots of fun, especially when playing with friends. Great graphics, good audio/sounds, entertaining gameplay for both sides(better than holding down left mouse button on a generator, if you know you know). The only thing that keeps me worried at this moment is the content they can potentially add to the game or I should say the lack of that content. Developers are really tied to a license which doesn't allow them to add whatever or things that they would like to. So sooner or later everyone is going to get bored with the same 3 maps and couple of characters everyone plays over and over again(most likely with some leveled up busted characteristics as I said before), which will lead to drastic playerbase decrease in about a year or so. I hope developers will figure everything out and get a clear vision of their product at least for couple of years ahead. Other than that this game is a solid product, 8/10.Edit: Lately I had a game where 2 or 3 survivor friends tried to speedrun the escape from family map using basement exit(via fuse box). Unfortunately for them I was ready and trapped it with hitchhiker's bone trap. They gave their best to run me around and slam me with doors. Sometime it was really sus how they knew every time when I was approaching the doors in general and which doors exactly, so they were slamming them on me from inside(and running outside from the room while I was laying on the ground). I learned my lesson and after couple of stuns they couldn't do anything or disarm the trap on fuse box, so eventually they gave up and just crushed the server. Cheating was an issue during beta but on release everything seemed good so far. Looks like cheating is going to be on the issues list again soon. These are the times I wish Steam had mixed review button.Upd: DLC-s cost more than they should and game became boring really soon. Since release, playerbase is decreasing every single month and keeps going that way. As I said earlier in this review, in about a year the game will be dead. Buy it if you really liked a gameplay or you are a big fan of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Thought I would chime in with a realistic, perhaps non-emotionally-charged review. A lot of the reviews here tend to be hysterical and exaggerate.This game is brilliantly brilliantly made. I think, visually, thematically and horrifically, it's what we're all craving Dead by Daylight was. We want a genre of game that is gritty, intense, skulking and scary, and the motion capture movements and animations alone make this immersive and impressive. Not to mention, the game is fluid and visually stunning and really satisfying to play.There is a really big downside though... the family. Understandably, no one wants to play them. I myself am a family main, but I still feel the imbalance of the game. If you want to play victim, you will have to wait 5-10 minutes to get a game, but as a family player, queue-times are instant.This should show you immediately how imbalanced the game is.My first gripe is that the game doesn't seem to disincentivize rushed play, which sucks so badly because the FUNNEST matches are tense, sneaky and have you shaking. But if you watch any of the victim streamers, you come to realize that skilled victims don't give a damn about killers. They can do whatever they like, they don't need to sneak around, and they can just power through the game, building perks to bully and beat up the family. And a lot of games are over as soon as they begin, with victims brazenly breaking out their restraints, immediately slamming through the doors, ignoring the killers and rushing for the exits as soon as the game starts.Secondly, another huge flaw with the game is that, as a victim, there is little incentive to play as a team. I mean, I don't really see the point. There isn't much to do to help each other. You can technically heal each other, but you can't see each others health, and there's no benefit to doing so since they can just heal themselves. And you can't really engage with the killers if they're brawling with a survivor, so there isn't much point in working together. Almost always, you just split up and have a single player experience.Even as the family, it's actually bad to stick together. Even in the loading screens, it advises you to stay apart from each other.I absolutely love this game, so it makes me sad that there are these huge flaws are present.In my opinion, strongly disincentivize rushed play by adding a penalty to rushed, loud actions, perhaps by leveling up grandpa or something, make the door locks even more robust so that it takes longer for them them to be broken by the victims, and add mechanics to the game that encourage a true multiplayer experience through teamwork. Allow victims to help each other and interact with each other.Irrespective of these major flaws, the game is still fantastic, but you will experience many unfun matches (most likely as a killer), but you will still get to experience some brilliant and funny games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fine up to this current update. Cook, Hitchhiker AND Nancy can play together??? Are you f'n kidding me!? For the rookies who don't know the level of B.S. this creates let me explain.There are 4 exits, 2 main, 1 power, 1 pressure. Now, they have a player called "Hitch hiker" who can place 3 traps down that ensnare you and highlights you for all to see. Another Character is "Cook" and he is able to hear you, highlight you and place 3 locks on doors so you'd have to pick twice to get through 1 door. These two combined was a pickle if played right, but fun enough it wasn't broken. Now the balancing part of this was you NEEDED "Leather Face" to balance it out.So, onto what I am not playing this game for and not recommending the game to anyone is.... They allowed Killers to not be required to have Leather Face, which is fine to a degree but it's not just that, its now the combination of "Nancy" being thrown into the broken mix. For the new players again, Nancy is able to SEE where you are AND place 3 barbed traps down and with a perk you can get through the upgrade tree, you can have it so she has a 35% chance not consume one of her abilities. SOOO, she can technically place up to sky's the limit based on her luck, I've counted 7 traps before. So to put it into perspective. YOU as a VICTIM must exit through 4 options, within those options you must dodge 3 traps, 3 locks, 7 barbed wire snares, cook being able to hear you and highlight you for up to a minute, grandpa yelling forcing you to stop or you're highlighted AND Nancy being able to see exactly where you are. BRAVO, You f*cked your game. How to fix this?? Forcing a player to play Leatherface definitely made the matchmaking frustrating because no one wanted to play him so you were left waiting in dead lobbies so dont revert it back. I'd say make it so Leatherface isnt mandatory but put the characters into a class (heavy, Medium, Light) and you cant have more than 2 of the same class. Heavy = Leather Face, JohnyMedium = Nancy, Cook, HitchhikerLight = SissyThen for future updates you can further catagorize into assassins or brutes or whatever if this game sticks around to further add balancing. If NON of this suites your fancy, double the healing items around the map or let them respawn after some time, possibly limit the blood piles Family can pick up or the refresh rate of which they fill up. When I play with my boys we max Grandpa out in 4minutes on every map.... Yea, thats WITH me playing Leatherface lmfao. Imagine a Nancy. Anyways, fix this issue before you kill your game!UpVote if you agree with some of my ideas so the devs can fix this

_childDocuments_.review: I'd been considering buying this game but for the €38.99 price tag I needed to be sure it would be a good investment. Coincidentally, the game went free for the weekend and I got to try it out finally.- The game is not beginner-friendly. No in-game tutorials, just videos with captions. You are forced to play PVP from the beginning, and if you're looking to get into the game, don't even bother because you will be a punching bag for the experienced players. If you're a beginner victim, family will rush down to the basement and take you out of the game in 2-3 minutes into the game; and if you're a beginner family, the experienced victims will rush car battery or the generator, and grapple (which has no consequences) and t-bag you.- Lack of variety. The spawn points are always the same. Cosmetics are not customisable to the same extent as in DbD or even in F13 - you can't just change your character's t-shirt or shoes. 90% of the time the map will be Abandoned Mill.- Character VO lines are limited and you will hear like the same 4-5 lines the whole game. Also, killer lines can be very misleading - Hitchhiker will say 'I found them' when there's no one around.- Long lobby times. With the free weekend, the game hit its , and even then it struggled to find players, typically family. Often the game will fail to find a 7th player and disband the whole lobby when a certain amount of time has passed, kicking the 6 people it managed to scrape together.- Lack of updates. There have only been 2 updates to the game this year, with the second one being the most recent, so if the devs follow this pattern, you can't expect another update for another month or two. This is a bad look for an online game as you can't expect regular bug fixes like you would for Dead by Daylight, which received 3 bugfix patches in March alone. If something breaks with a new update, that bug is likely to stay around till the next patch a month or two later.- Terrible communication and lack of transparency from the devs. As of writing this, the devs have been selling for 5 days, for real money, a critically bugged character whose skill tree is broken, and have made no public announcements or disclosures to warn potential buyers. There are also several other bugs on Reddit users have reported to the devs, but it's always just the same 'Stay tuned' and 'I've passed it along to the dev team' every time. This is not at all comforting with the infrequent updates. Also, some of the community representatives tend to argue provocatively with other members of the community. Like, I get it, some people are rude to you. I myself have been a moderator for a big game in the past and there is no handbook for moderation, but there's this thing called professionalism. They are in a unique position to make a positive change within the community, but they decide to act childish instead of leading by example. I have never seen such shockingly unprofessional behaviour from any other big developer. The fact that this hasn't been dealt with shows that this is acceptable behaviour, and it reflects badly on the company.The only good thing I have to say about this game is its visual and sound design. Its atmosphere is immersive and it does a good job of making its maps feel like home.With all this mind, while TCM has the potential to be a good game, it is cursed with poor game design choices (e.g. lack of in-game tutorials) and terrible mismanagement based on my gameplay experience, community interactions and background research this weekend, and I cannot in good faith recommend it while it offers such a subpar experience for its hefty price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: A) PROS:1. Refreshing from Dead by Daylight as far as the concept/objective of the victims (survivors) vs. family members (killers). At first I was afraid of it being 4v3 since DBD is a very unforgiving game, but the idea of having multiple ways to escape the map justifies having multiple killers on a team. This brings a unrelenting effort of wanting to escape the map as a victim from leather face, which is insanely satisfying. 2. Every victim & family member is very unique to their own style of play based on their core attributes, perks and special abilities. This is very refreshing from DBD allowing players to focus on multiple builds and play styles based on their characters personal level and how they executed their skill tree. 3. UNREAL ENGINE makes this game absolutely enjoyable making it feel modern and with the times. The quality of the graphics is beautiful. The game is brutal, chaotic, dark and insanely gory. Every victim and family member has their own unique style of movement, which makes this game very unique during gameplay via PVP.4. Crossplay is a huge PLUS for easy matchmaking across the board between all gaming platforms.B) CONS:1. Server crashes/errors are very common after a few matches. You constantly need to restart the game just to make sure you don't get kicked out from the next match from a server error issue. This can get quite annoying, because at times it may feel as if you're spending more time restarting the game than playing it.2. During matchmaking while you're waiting for everyone to ready up the timer to start the match is way too long. It should be drastically reduced, so we can begin a match asap. Players being ready is a common issue, which causes a huge delay starting the match. Since there has to be one leather face as a family member at all times, this can cause players to leave quite often by players not being ready and taking too long to begin a match. If one person has to be leather face than there should be a default feature that permanently makes one person as leather face, so there isn't people constantly exiting the match. 3. Not enough victims to select when matchmaking. For instance, if your victim is selected, which 7/10 times in most cases will be, a lot of players back out of the matchmaking, which causes a huge delay finding a replacement to begin a match. I understand the game just came out and it's catering towards the actual story, but if they added 3 more victims it would make the biggest difference from the survivors aspect/pov. C) OVERALL:1. YES, I would highly recommend anyone to purchase this game. It's very challenging on both ends between the victims and family members. The concept is drastically different between both teams. In addition, the concept of the game is very unique to its own style, which is very refreshing from most common horror survivor games. Overall, I give this game a 9/10. It would be a 10/10 if it didn't have server issues while matchmaking.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a tentative yes. This is going to be a game whose quality is ultimately determined by how the meta develops and how the developers handle that. At it's core, it's an incredibly impressive asymmetric horror game that has the intelligence to build around voice chat. Team work is imperative. The real impressive element to me as opposed to games like, say, Dead By Daylight, is the complexity. While Dead by Daylight is two or three real gameplay elements copy and pasted onto a map with the "gameplay" being holding a button and doing skill checks, TCSM is complex. There are three stages to every map and four escape goals. You need to forage for supplies, to open doors, to get to the main objective which involves getting it done sneakily to escape. The victims have defining, original abilities and I find the chase/escape balance kind of nice. In a 1 on 1, you should be fine unless you screw up, but in a 2 on 1 (There are three killers) then its sheer panic. The killer side of things is great too. There are a plethora of spinning plates to keep up, tools to track the victims, and a diversity that necessitates team play. Critique time. Are there red flags? Oh you bet you. The ability for the victims to just disappear or instantly win is shocking. It's too soon to tell how it will shake out, but I'm concerned. For example, on the short end there are three doors before the final objective needing you to scavenge three tools. Even solo, there is a character who's ability is to break a lock every five minutes, so that's 25% of the game done instantly and again in 5 minutes. Not to mention that three door three lock thing? There are four victims, good coordination can almost instantly win and while there are tools to track the victims, they are laborious requiring manually checking which locks have broken down. It seems horribly victim sided with a modicum of coordination. And here's the big one for me that makes me question the talent designing the game. It seems small but stay with me. There is a cutscene that plays for killers when this event happens. Completely interrupts the game. If you're in the middle of something like chasing or evening attacking, it will screw you up. You say, "No problem, they can patch that out on week one." Yes, sure. But here's the thing, they NEEDED to be told that. It was plainly infuriating in the first hour of play to the point where I don't understand how someone at any point in development didn't say, "Let's not do that."So what I'm worried about is a game that soley dictated by the community. If the developers just hate playing games so much and don't understand what they like/ what makes it fun, then it's going to be pushed off on the community, and that's a fast way to offsett the trajectory of your game and make bland and uninteresting choices.Like I said, we'll see.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've spent over 60 hours in the game, I have even more bad things to say about it.First of all, it's price. 38.99€ for a game without local matchmaking, lack of content and many other problems is too much. Don't repeat my mistakes and don't waste your time on this game. There are better options for games where you can go in, quickly play a couple of matches and leave. Games with higher quality content and a decent local matchmaking (at least for EU players). I haven't played for a month, but I've been following the updates. Nothing major happened (saw changelogs). No more illusions of a bright future. There's no point in going back. I'm finally free. Thank You, Gun Interactive!. Perks and abilities are designed for people with disabilities. Highlight player/door/whatever. Increase damage/stun time. Increase stamina/health etc. The designers took the worst of asymmetric games. Many perks are useless junk. Characters have no restrictions on individual attributes. You can increase damage, stamina, etc.The character's last ability is usually strong, but the levels before it are mediocre. You're grinding just for that one ability.. Each map has an optimal family team composition. If you play against more or less experienced victims using the wrong character, then the match will turn into a nightmare and all hope will be on your teammates. Too many holes in the wall, exits too far away, etc.. No communication wheel (voice commands with or without animation). Most players in my gaming experience had bad microphones, bad settings, or something else that resulted in poor audio quality. There are also shy people or those without a microphone. Communication is extremely important in this game. A voice command wheel is essential.. No regional filters or simply lack of local players. As a European, you play against players from countries far away from you. In my experience, it was about 85% of the matches. This creates not only a communication problem, but also a problem with the quality of the Internet connection. You won't see the country, ping, or any other data. However, you may see delays in actions, strange behavior/bugs, etc. It can be extremely annoying. There are many players from the USA, Asia and South America. There are also players with stolen Wi-Fi and other connection issues. Here are a couple of examples of my ping in the following cities. Hangzhou - 265.403ms, Hong Kong - 228.058ms, Los Angeles - 166.295ms, San Diego - 176.732ms, Shanghai - 276.733ms, New York - 90.945ms, Philadelphia - 116.991ms, Brasilia - 235.052ms, Buenos Aires - 250.822ms, Mexico City - 138.783ms.Ping can change constantly. 90 can become 110 etc. All of the above figures exceed the limit for decent connection.. It's difficult to gather a full lobby as a Victim (fewer players want to play as killers). Quick match is always Family.. Most of the cosmetics are just simple recolors. Including DLC.. There are a lot of trolls who are either trying to stun you for no reason or are just wasting your time standing near the exit. I am not a psychiatrist or psychologist. It’s not my job to deal with other people’s complexes and failures. It's not my job to fine them either. However, normal people have to suffer from these garbage monkeys. I don't want to insult the developers, but they either don't care or are doing a bad job. If you remember F13, then this is probably the second option.. The process of playing as a victim is boring and simple. Compared to the previous GUN game, this is a step forward and a few steps back. No searching for items, no hiding in closets (it’s possible, but this is a very niche mechanic), no melee weapons. Free escape is also possible.. The escape methods are simple and boring. This is also a step forward and a few steps back. You either rush and run away, or act slowly and stealthily and then die. Only the fusebox has a mini game. Other objects - just press "E" to finish.. No dismemberment! No severed limbs or pierced heads. I'm not even talking about internal organs. This is also a step back.. Problems with the interface. The "Start" button is "E" instead of the popular, classic and famous "Enter" (and/or LMB). Is this a console port? _childDocuments_.review: So, let's start with the most glaring problem, which is that it uses Easy Anti-Cheat. You know, the easiest Anti-Cheat to bypass. I've had multiple games in my short time playing in which the basement is immediately open and the victims are walking upstairs. The fact that companies still use this specific anti-cheat should be condemned, as it makes the online PVP an overall worse experience, and that has been the case for a very long time. I'm not sure if it's cheaper, or if it requires minimal work to implement, but what I do know is that other games that have used it are a good enough example that developers should know by now. Secondly, the survivors, if they bring the right character, they can escape within five minutes due to enhanced lockpicking. It's reasonable to still be working through the balancing since the game was just released, we all know that League of Legends just doesn't try, so we can give the devs of this game some time to make an attempt. Leland is also a frustrating aspect of the game, since he can stun you for inordinate amounts of time and lock down sprinting and attacking after you've stood up from being knocked completely prone, and this is clearly not okay. Other than those points, the team-based killer gameplay is pretty fun. All of the killers bring something unique to the match, and seeing how those teams mesh if very interesting. Dead by Daylight could probably stand to learn something from that since Survivors are overall meta in that game, and it could benefit from a 2v6 mode. I also don't know how this game can build off of what it has, since it's specifically Texas Chainsaw Massacre, and there's not much to that.EDIT: They had time to make Connie less ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ when they kicked PC out of crossplay(Which they wouldn't have to do if they weren't using one of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ known anti-cheats), and left her the same. That's a critical failure. If they had play-tested this game at all, they'd know how dumb her power to unblock anything instantly is.EDIT2: So, there's also the pressure exits to talk about. Opening a pressure exit is automatic victory for survivors, because the moment they walk through, they win, and there's no way for killers to prevent them from doing so. Further horrifically bad design is the fact that the killers can be stunned every ten seconds, and it takes longer than ten seconds to shut a pressure valve. Leland is also capable of stunning you for inordinate amounts of time, guaranteeing victory for his team. They also still haven't sufficiently nerfed Connie, and Ana can break through the window of the family house map while suffering little damage and just win the game for her team automatically. The lack of balance in this game is embarrassing.

The Texas Chain Saw Massacre is really fun for the most part in spite of its many gameplay flaws and balancing issues. However it also suffers from a ton of jank and technical problems at the moment that make the game far more difficult to enjoy.Visually and audio wise, the game is very solid. It matches the style and tone of the original film very well and is incredibly faithful.Where the cracks begin is in some of its design and the fact that the game was clearly launched way too early.Despite having a beta before launch, it suffers from many problems that do their best to constantly disrupt the experience. The invalid credentials error will occur every hour or two of playing and requires a restart to fix otherwise it will completely prevent you from playing. On top of this, there are many issues with disconnects, especially when playing in a party. The game has also crashed on me randomly, there are issues with animations breaking, characters appearing in cutscene's where they shouldn't, cutscene's not playing at the right time entirely, the game stutters a ton, especially when playing as the killers.In general, I think the game needed an entire additional QA pass before being released, because right now it is a hot mess. Not the worst launch I have ever seen, but far from stable.As for the game itself, its incredibly fun for the first hours but once you start to understand more how it all works, the cracks show fast. Connie is still overpowered despite her changes from the beta, some killers are clearly better than others, spamming the door stuns on killers is still possible to exploit and incredibly annoying. Succeeding at killers requires a lot of communication meaning solo queue as a killer on gets less and less enjoyable with each day as survivor players get better at the game and the survivor role requires very little teamwork at all to succeed. Maps are kinda samey looking and can be difficult to navigate. I found it incredibly easy to get lost in the basement in all of the maps and even just getting back into the basement can also be incredibly difficult resulting in a lot of screwing around. Matches are often over in 1 minute or 15 depending on various factors. The family house map has a giant open area outside of the main exit before you have to leave, allowing players to just camp the exit and hold the game hostage like with dbd exits, allowing for incredibly toxic behaviour and overdrawn games.All in all, there are plenty of good moments to be had here, but I fear even if the bugs are fixed, this is a game that will only get worse and worse as the players get better and matches become more stale. That's even taking into account the fact that the Texas Chainsaw Massacre license limitations will have a big effect on future updates and the games overall longevity. If you are going to play this game, now would be the time, because I have a feeling that its only going to get worse from here.Should things improve, I will update my review to reflect that, otherwise, these are my thoughts right now.

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran of both the Friday The 13th and Dead By Daylight communities stretching all the way back to 2016, I was needlessly excited for a fresh take on the asymmetrical horror genre. While this isn't the most original game ever as it bares likeness to both Friday The 13th and Home Sweet Home Survive, it is definitely a breath of fresh air. After about 30 hours of playtime, I believe this is the one true successor to the Friday The 13th game. The game play loop seems comfortably familiar in a good way and veterans of F13 will find themselves at home here. There have been various tweaks to that familiar formula, some good, some not so great. For instance, survivor players have multiple means of escaping, but at the same time they don't feel as unique as the escape routes in F13. There is no car or boat escape, which led to lots of hilarious and highly entertaining moments in F13. I would have liked to have seen them bring vehicles back, but the maps are not designed for that vehicular game play. That said, what is here for survivor is pretty exciting when compared to something like doing generators in DBD (BLEH).On the killer side, the addition of having multiple killers feels like a much more fun experience compared to the 1 vs. all style that both F13 and DBD have. It is absolutely a rush to coordinate with friends and trap victims. At the same time, it makes it not feel as bad if your team gets absolutely rocked because you get to share in that experience. The kill animations are also really great, but some of the fun overly gory animations in the style of F13 would be welcome in the future. Leatherface kicking victims heads off, soccer style anyone? Each killer also has a unique power and game play style. It's almost more like a class system, rather than a power system a la DBD. You have support killers, chase killers, and tracking killers at present with more coming in the future. Each role is important in securing a win and all the roles feel satisfying to play. That said, Johnny and Hitchhiker currently need some changed. Johnny just straight feels unnecessary at this point, as his power is bested by other characters that do similar things better.All this said, there are a couple of major issues. The first is that the game is rather victim sided and once victims learn the game, there will be no stopping them. It's not rare to run across a high level team that manages to escape in 90 seconds. I believe this really boils down to a singular victim: Connie. She can instantly pop open doors and there is really no stopping her if she has a good Leland at her back to tank hits and stun the family members.Lastly, I feel like the vibe I got playing F13 is missing a key ingredient: COMMUNICATION. One of the stand out memories I have of F13 is goofing around with the other players in my match over voice chat. In fact, VC was so great in that game that I ended making tons of friends. In TCM, almost NO ONE talks over voice chat. It makes the experience feel way less fun and it makes the matches feel empty and devoid of humanity at points. I know the DBD community is largely against the idea of VC, as I have watched them fight VC being added to DBD over the years and also going out of their way to limit post game text chat, which could be the reason for the lack of active voice chatters in TCM (Spoiler: lots of DBD players are playing this game). In fact, I have heard from many new TCM players that one of the first things they did when they booted up the game was to turn off voice chat. Here's the thing people, there are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everywhere in games and in real life. They make the mute button for a reason and if someone is being really toxic, then you should use it. That said, I beg you all to turn on voice chat and try to make some friends in game. It makes for a way more fun experience and a better TCM community overall. If you don't want to make friends, that is fine, but I can tell you as someone that has played the game for a while with and without comms, VC is crucial to playing family and very helpful to victim teams as well. So maybe at least turn it back on so you can win the game?In conclusion, I look forward to years of content in TCM because I truly think it is THE spiritual successor to, in my opinion, the best asymmetrical game of all time F13 and it is absolutely worth a look if you were into that game/community.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, it's the classic Gun issue. They make an incredibly good looking game that really caters to everything that makes a slasher game good. Beautiful executions, solid gameplay loop, visually pleasing to look at. Then what do they do, oh right they say "We've done our part time to abandon it and hand it off to another studio that didn't actually have anything to do with making the game in the first place". So the obvious thing happens, everyone leaves the game because why stick around with a game that the devs no longer care about. Gun makes their money on sales then just walks away. At least with Friday the 13th they had the excuse of Victor Miller and his lawsuit putting an end to the game. But this was just them blatantly getting paid and then leaving to start yet another game that I'm sure will be a great looking game that they'll rinse and repeat with just like they did here. This game isn't even a year old and it's completely dead. This game is so dead there's only 3K people playing it on a free weekend no less. So what do I do I sit in a lobby for 15 minutes waiting to get one more player on killer side so we can actually play a match. This was after playing a match where everyone on victims team was level 0 against 3 level 10 killers. Match was over in about 90 seconds. So I wait 15 minutes hoping to try again but alas after the 15 minutes it starts the match starting countdown and then says "Network Error unable to find enough players to play the game" and kicks me back to the main menu. All of this mind you is with crossplay enabled too. I am so glad I didn't buy this game at full price a month ago when I was really thinking about finally getting it. This free weekend has showed me all I need to know about how dead this game really is.Edited to add: The fact there's $90 worth of DLC is just another disgusting part about this game. How do you have $90 worth of DLC in the first year of release yet you abandon the game and the player base is non-existent. But hey they'll still gladly accept people who pay $40 for the game and then $90 for the DLC for a game people can't even play half the time because of how low the player base is. Seriously don't waste any of your money on this game.

The maps are bigger and there are multiple ways to escape from each map.You can level up specific stats of your character, causing a killer to do more damage on each attack for instance. _childDocuments_.review: The game has an incredibly good attention to detail and clearly has a lot of love and passion put into it from the developers, and you can clearly see that they love the source material a lot. However, I cannot recommend this game. As someone new trying to get into it a month after the game has released, this game *really* sucks to try to learn. For one, there is zero report system whatsoever in this game, so toxic and problem-causing players can just do what they want with zero punishment. I have played a couple of matches where victim teammates end up drawing the killers to the exit you're headed towards, intentionally, simply to BM them, which also inadvertently (or even worse, intentionally) causes the killers to close off and camp that exit, forcing you to have to completely reset your progress and find another one. I have been told to kill myself because of my voice. I have had at least one Family member who was very likely cheating, unable to be reported and thus able to continue doing so. It is very frustrating to deal with.Secondly, the game is very unforgiving to newer players and there is, as it seems, zero weighted matchmaking beyond getting people into matches ASAP. My first game was a lobby full of max level characters, and a few games later I had a lobby with 6 other people that had never played the game before, with me being the most experienced one there with a whole 86 minutes of gameplay under my belt. A lot of players who regularly play the game are very devoted to the game, which makes learning either side obscenely difficult without watching tutorials on youtube or *requiring* you to pair up with friends in order to have any sort of cooperation, as few people use communication, and those that do are very often toxic in my experience.I am sure this game was an absolute blast to play on release day, with all the players who didn't know what they were doing. Now, seemingly only a month later, it feels too late to even try. I want to like this game, but sadly right now it is very difficult to. If none of these things bother you, by all means give it a shot, it is a very faithful spin on the original films and is probably very fun to play with friends. I will be holding off on playing this for now. I wish I didn't regret buying this.

There was a major hacking problem that occurred and the developers handled it poorly by turning off cross play that did nothing but isolate the remaining issue and then in return punished all PC players. Cross play has been turned back on and the hacker issue seems to be a bit better but you may still encounter cheaters here and there. As i stated above this game has balancing issues, some of the maps are either more family sided or more victim sided, this can lead to a terrible experience. (resulting in longer lobby times) Most people seem to play victims since it can be very easy to escape and rack up points if you know what you are doing. Yet ANOTHER silly choice made by the developers was to hide player levels along with hiding the icon that would show if players were in a party/group. This does not solve any kind of skill gap between players, all it does is make it to where people have no idea what the lobby skill gap is now. There are plenty more issues that i could go on and on about but i think i got the message across. Sadly this game could be great but i have a feeling if things keep going this way it may result in the games death/shutdown.UPDATE: After playing more last night and today i started noticing that major issues that should have been fixed are still NOT fixed, for example you can STILL become glitched in the ground and when this happens you can not do anything at all so you might as well just leave the match, you can also still become stuck inside walls or the stairs if you kill a victim on the stairs when to close to the wall. _childDocuments_.review: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre game draws inspiration from the iconic horror film, offering players a survival horror experience that mirrors the intense atmosphere of the original.Players can take on the role of victims trying to escape Leatherface and his family, or as the horrific family themselves, creating a tense and suspenseful gameplay centered around puzzles and evasion. The environments and sound design contribute significantly to the game's eerie and horrifying ambiance.While the graphics pay homage to the film's gritty visuals, the game prioritizes raw horror over a complex narrative. The experience successfully captures the source material's essence, delivering an anxiety-inducing gameplay.However, the reliance on jump scares and repetitive elements might lead to desensitization over time. Personally, I found the gameplay of the Friday the 13th game more appealing due to its emphasis on teamwork, objectives, and the unique role of Jason Voorhees.Fans of the franchise will find themselves immersed in the world of The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, appreciating the authenticity the game strives to achieve. While I did prefer the Friday the 13th game more, I do still enjoy TSCM very much and think it's a must have for any fans of this genre of games.

_childDocuments_.review: The Team Behind the F13 game has done it again and created a game that truly respects its IP and manages to put the players into the world delivering a horror fan a great experience.  This game has a very, very, steep learning curve.  While there is tutorials that provide some basic information it barely scratches the  surface on the all game play and game sense that comes when playing this.   When you start out If you Play Victim expect to die... alot, if you play family expect them to escape. To quote something from an unrelated franchise, "Losing is Fun".  :You will still learning some of the mechanics and nuances to game play. Play with different build and learn to adapt your strategies.  Also pay attention to which characters are in your game and respec your perks if needed.    the willingness to have a flexible build is what will increase your chances of winning. Also, YouTube will become your friend on understanding some of the mechanics. 1. Captures sense of dread that the "Original" 1974 Texas Chain Massacre.  2. Games are tense and winning feels very, very good. 3. The maps are gorgeous, they capture the look and feel of the movies.  4.  Maps feel balanced, the Family cannot camp all of the exits and just prevent the victims from winning.  There are multiple items needed to open exits scattered around the map allowing for different strategies.5. Steep Learning Curve that rewards trying new things in order to win.6. Lots of Lessons were learned from   to avoid trolling and team killing. 7. Built in Coms that make the game session much more approachable to solo players.1. Steep, Steep,  Learning Curve, the new player experience is going to be rough for the first 10-15 matches.  2. The Meta Game progression system upgrades character abilities, perks, and allows you adjust stats of the characters in the game.  While the intent was to create interesting and unique builds, stacking leveled up perks onto leveled up building is going to also negatively impact the new user experience.    It will be interesting to see how this plays out over the next few months as players begin to figure out the Meta.3. Comparing this to F13 and its Perk system, even without being able to adjust stats certain perks became very, very, very strong when used on certain characters.  4. Hopefully this game doesn't go the way of Evil Dead, who's Meta Game Progression system makes it almost impossible for new players to pick it up and play.5. The game play experiencing is very, very, different for those who do not an in game coms. The Game is designed that team is communicating. Expanding the UI that tells the other teammates where the other players area and what they are doing would smooth out the experience.1. Bugs when gaining experience, sometimes you don't get the XP earned in the match.2. Interaction Bugs (Fighting Family Members, getting stuck in closets, causing people to fall through the wall).3. Hackers using 3rd Party cheats.4. Character Balancing or Bugs causing certain character to be overtuned.5. Game stuttering (I have not experienced this, but i'm running a 4090 GPU and a powerful PC)6. In game coms are not working correctly, other applications are muffling or blocking microphones. Simply put:   1. the game mechanics between the two are too different both games promote two vastly different type of play styles.  Personally, I enjoy both games.  However,  I put more time into games that have multiple win conditions and require strategy in order to win.  Friday the 13 was and still is, one of my all time favorite games. As stated above,  the developer has taken most of the hard lessons learned from that game and inserted them into this one.   I strongly recommend this game to anyone who loves horror and enjoys asymmetrical games.

_childDocuments_.review: Is a fun hide and seek game, but people are going to drain the fun out of it by being too efficient.If the family or survivors don't play like chainsaw killers or scared survivors, it starts getting way less fun.  I expect the game will need some changes if it wants to live for more than a year.On the subject of balance, for Family, Sissy is by FAR the best killer, with speed, stamina, slow poison stumble attacks, follow through tight spaces, poison attack into crevices, traps, and blood collection.  She's best compared to... hitchiker, who has follow through tight spaces, traps that are hard countered by a survivor perk, and... yeah thats it.  Much shorter list.  If you're still unconvinced Sissy is out of line, imagine if Sissy started in basement instead of Bubba.Meanwhile for survivors: Connie instantly can pick a lock.  To escape, you need to pick 4 locks total, and typically one generator.  she can skip 1/4 of the main objective.   No other survivor can compare.For for the metagame:  The levelup system is just, bad.  Because skillpoints are character agnostic and respecs are free, a level 10 person can respec around their basket of points to max any one character, spending a tediuos amount of time doing so, making them need to leave any lobby they can't get them in or play a level 0 character.  This naturally leads to toxicity and weird standoff lobbies, especially when Leatherface is considered the least fun family, and is required to start the match.My suggested changes are simple.  Sissy cannot poison/slow/stumble via basic attacks, Connie starts without her character power, and make it so you queue with a specific character at a specific level where trait points are character specific to match with characters of your level.  This would also allow people to opt into low power level games.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 1,000 hrs in DBD so at it's base core yeah this game has similarities but let me tell ya its completely different. Honestly a lot more engaging as a player and overall a much more enjoyable experience. I love the fact there are multiple ways of escape not just one. You make a plan and suddenly your path becomes too dangerous so you gotta have a back up plan. "Yes, got the fuse gotta get that box open...oh wait its being patrolled k gonna grab some lock picks and try the back exit." I put far more thought into my plays and actions than I did in DBD. There is so much more to this game which is absolutely refreshing. Each character has their own unique ability which makes playing them fun and allows for more variety in the gameplay vs just buying a character for their perks and unlocking a new character skin. Honestly as a fan of this franchise I gotta say that the devs put so much love and care into every inch of detail into this game. From the sound design to the accuracy of the maps in respect to the films sets, the character voices and animations...list could go on. Love that Kane Hodder came back to do the body capture for Leatherface. Love that Sissy and Johnny were both concept characters from the og film. Love that they brought on Kim Henkel the original writer for the first film to work with them on the character design, they even were able to have Edwin Neal come back to reprise his role as The Hitchhiker, it's absolutely incredible. Its amazing to imagine almost 50 years after its conception that this franchise would be brought to life again through a whole new medium.  I highly recommend this game. It embodies so much of the horror and terror that was The Texas Chain Saw Massacre. It's new and feels fresh. I hope that the devs keep giving it love and keep it afloat with good updates and additional content. Some things I would like to see fixed: Animation for grandpa should not be so overwhelming. Should be a notification on the side or top of the screen. It should not interrupt the games motion. Skill trees while being very detailed and an interesting approach needs a bit of work. Multiple load outs is nice but I would like more variety to choose from with my perks. I get locked to certain paths on the tree and often times the perks are subpar or don't fit my play style. Then I need to refund the points and try a different route to try and get better perks...so why have multiple load outs if I am only changing one perk depending on which family members I am going up against? At this point I feel the system is a bit off but I am sure it will be tweaked. Fingers crossed the devs listen to the community. Disclaimer: At the moment there are two level systems; a player level and a character level. Your xp will affect both levels. So starting out new your xp level requirements will be low so you will level fast. This is normal for pretty much all games. I was able to get a character to level 10 within the first 3-4 hours of playing. Not too shabby. Then it took me around 5 hours to get another character to 10. I currently only have two at levels 10 and one at level 3. The grind seems to be a big one. This is either seen as good or bad for some players. Good because it gives reason to play and level everyone to 10 or bad for the more casual players who might feel stuck with playing certain characters cause they are only leveling one or two. Good thing the game has the skill point refund option so yes you can move points around. Just be ready to grind this game if you want to hit max level for everything. Okay, I've said enough. Buy this game and let the terror begin! Be good to each other and stay safe out there!

_childDocuments_.review: Really tense and fun gameplay with a surprising amount of depth. The 4v3 formula works really well- both sides have a lot of potential for teamwork but you can just as well win a victim game by yourself even if your teammates are all dead. Plenty of room for player expression- you can play aggressive and speedrun an exit if you catch the killers off guard or you can play immersed and hide until an opportunity opens to escape. Killer powers are varied and work really well with teamwork but you're not screwed if you play by yourself either.

_childDocuments_.review: After hitting 600 hours, I felt compelled to share my opinion about the game for newcomers, especially since I keep seeing the game on sale. The game is not beginner-friendly whatsoever. You start at an extreme disadvantage not having any map knowledge or sufficient accessible perks or skill points to use. There's no MMR ranking, so on your first game, you will probably load in against people who have been playing since day one. Beginners spend about 6-10 hours leveling up basic characters and learning how to escape the basement. I wouldn't recommend playing the game solo, especially if you aren't going to utilize a mic. The introduction of paid characters such as Danny, Virginia, Hands, and Maria all add gameplay advantages. My biggest strife is that the game lacks character customization, even though the devs keep releasing more paid cosmetics. There's no motivation to necessarily grind because when you reach level 99, you get some blacked-out cosmetics, and then that's that. They added lobby penalties, however, there still aren't any in-game dc penalties. I don't really have any issues with perk changes/skill tree reworks; I think it's helped to balance out the game on both sides. Overall, it's a game with a lot of potential, but don't go into it with high hopes if you're a beginner. You have a long road ahead in decently learning the mechanics and team play aspects of the game before it really becomes fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (Game)Rating: 3.5/5If you’ve ever dreamed of being chased by a maniac wielding a chainsaw in the middle of Texas while desperately trying to escape with your skin intact (literally), then congratulations, you’ve found your game! The Texas Chain Saw Massacre is a chaotic multiplayer horror fest that asks one simple question: "How long can you run while screaming?"Pros:Authentic Texas Chainsaw Experience: You can practically feel the BBQ sauce and terror in the air.Multiple Killers, Multiple Ways to Die: If Leatherface isn’t enough, don’t worry—his creepy family is here to help ruin your day.Teamwork (or Lack Thereof): Nothing bonds you to strangers like frantically yelling over voice chat, “He’s behind me! HELP!”Grim '70s Vibes: The setting perfectly captures that gritty, sweaty atmosphere where you know the AC is broken, but so are your chances of surviving.Cons:Survivor Fragility: Everyone seems to have the endurance of a 90-year-old with asthma. One sprint and they’re done for.Inconsistent Kill Animations: Sometimes Leatherface just tickles you with the chainsaw, other times it’s an instant gory mess."Texas Traffic Simulator": Occasionally feels like the family is playing the game while you're stuck in a cornfield somewhere trying to find the exit for 20 minutes.Friendly Fire: Sure, the family wants to kill you, but sometimes, the worst enemy is your own clumsy teammate locking you in a room with a chainsaw-wielding psycho.All in all, The Texas Chain Saw Massacre is great if you love stress, sudden death, and Texas. It’s basically a barbecue party where the main course is you, and the only sauce is ketchup. Good luck out there—you’ll need it.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game right now, it has too many bugs and flaws that drive me crazy to the point where I'm just not enjoying my time playing. To name a few: - I literally can't voice chat because its bugged and they said they fixed it last patch, but its not, so that's already a MAJOR hindrance as I don't have any friends who play this game, solo queue is my only option.- When Sissy hits you it puts you into an inescapable vortex spin driving me absolutely nuts, that HAS to be a bug right? If its intentional it needs to be removed, she's already strong enough and she has poison to make you wobbly like that already. It is infuriating getting hit by her even one time.- Lobbies take forever to start, everyone wants to play your character or they leave, and often nobody wants to play leatherface. So then you start letting people play your character, and then you're playing a lvl 0 victim vs lvl 10 killers which feels like a huge gap in power.-Matchmaking is horrible. It constantly feels like its either A. a really competent team of family vs victims who are somehow lvl 30 but act like they've never played the game before, or B. victims who are actually good, work together, and all escape through the same door in the first 30 seconds vs a family that has no idea what they're doing and don't even turn on the car battery or a leatherface who doesn't break a single barrier. Also nobody talks, likely due to the voice chat bugs still in effect. Only way around it I think is to go open mic and some people do that and then you can't hear anything cause their trash mic is fuzzy or playing all kinds of background noise.- Cheating is still a big issue. Also the being infinitely stunned as leatherface is a huge problem and probably why nobody wants to play him, although I do know a somewhat of a fix is coming for that.- We still can't customize our key binds. Unreal to me that it was not implemented at release. I am just beyond frustrated and am not having fun 70% of the time anymore. It feels 30/70 on whether I'm gonna enjoy the match or not. I'm okay with "losing" or "dying" if the match actually felt fair and playable, its not like I'm a sore loser. But due to all of these issues I feel like, in some matches, I cannot even play the game.Most of my comments are playing as victim, which I have played a bit more of than family. I'd say I've played 60/40. As family I feel like I'm extremely powerful. Rarely do any victims give me problems and usually if they do its because I'm outnumbered. But the killers move fast and get around quickly, even without comms I'm usually not too irritated playing as family, though being able to speak in game would fix any issues I had.I do love the concept of the game, and it has so much potential to be fun, and I keep convincing myself to play because of that, but I am just so often not having fun while playing due to all of these extremely necessary fixes that I can't recommend it until most of these are patched. _childDocuments_.review: After giving this game it's fair shake I just can't recommend it. At least not at the price point it's at. The game suffers from an extreme amount of bugs/jankiness. I played this with my wife and we both didn't have any fun with it.We suffered so many technical issues during our play session and both of our PCs well-exceed the recommended requirements for the game. The game stutters like crazy, especially when you play as "The Family" (Killers). We got kicked out mid-match multiple times, and mid-queue multiple times due to a "Credentials Invalid" error which seems to be plaguing everyone. We had a couple matches randomly disconnect. Outside of the technical issues the gameplay starts out VERY fun and the presentation is very good and faithful to the original film...but that peters out pretty fast. Really fast. Games start feeling the same, the few maps within the game don't have nearly enough randomization to make the games ever feel different. The killers are barely different from eachother and the survivors even less so with some survivors abilities only working against a specific killer. The killers and survivors have different stat points which helps them feel diverse but that goes out the window here in the next segment.As far as progression goes levelling up gives you an "attribute point". You know how earlier I said different characters have different stats? Like you have one character who is a bit stronger than others so they can perform certain tasks faster, and you have others who are really stealthy. That's kinda cool, right? Well it is until you realize that you earn attribute points, a lot of them. And you can just strengthen your characters to be amazing at everything which lets you straight up ignore certain elements of the game. There's just so little diversity in the characters, especially the survivors, that it hurts the experience.The game is also clearly a console game ported to PC. All of the menus are designed to be navigated with a controller. The most obvious example of this is the progression screen. The progression screen has to be zoomed out with the keyboard and navigated with WASD as the mouse works really wonky on it. There's also no key rebind feature which is pretty unacceptable in 2023. The thing that really killed the fun for me though is how cumbersome performing actions in the game is. It gives you a button mashing minigame similar to games from the mid 2,000s. Wanna open a little door to crawl through? You better be ready to mash E 100 times and you better not mash it too fast or you'll make noise, doesn't that sound fun? Wanna search a box? Mash E at just the right pace! Wanna picklock a door? Oh yeah, you guessed it. Mash E for 30 seconds straight but mash TOO fast and you break your lockpick and then you're gonna need to go mash E on the container that contains lockpicks again!The bugs, the gameplay, the lack of diversity all adds up to a really miserable experience. And certainly not one worth $39.99 with a day 1 cosmertic DLC which is already steep for an online-only game that's not doing anything new. As a final note I wanna say I'm concerned about future content rollout for the game. The game is going to be inherently limited by it's license. The maps in the game already feel thematically the exact same and gameplay wise very similar, and I'm not really sure where they can go given the licenses restrictions and needing to stay within the boundaries of the TCM universe.I don't recommend it if you're looking for a game with legs or a game with longevity. The gameplay is just too stale even after 2 hours for me to want to continue playing and the problematic and annoying metas I already see developing are enough to put me off it and stamp it with my seal of disapproval. The only situation I recommend it is if you're a hardcore TCM fan and you want to feel like you're in the movies because outside of the weird OC characters they added it's very, very loyal to the original film.

_childDocuments_.review: It's got some issues (matchmaking being a pain with everyone being sent back to the main menu after one player doesn't get the character they want, and the "supplied credentials are invalid" bug being the most prevalent), but the pros outweigh the cons. Both roles are fun to play and have different strengths and weaknesses. The matches shift in favor from one side to another depending on who you play and how you choose to play them, and with there being multiple family members, victims, maps, and ways to escape, no match plays the same way twice. My favorite part about the game is that it isn't balanced in favored of a competitive scene (at least for now), and it just embraces the fact that it's a silly party game. Sometimes you get rolled, sometimes you do the rolling, and sometimes it's so close that you have no idea whether  you're going to win or not.  The decision to include voice coms is also excellent, giving both sides a chance to use teamwork and come up with strategies on the go based on how the match plays out. It may not have thousands of hours worth of content, but TCM is a very fun game that will keep you plenty entertained regardless. If the devs can fix the day one bugs and the matchmaking system, they have a real winner here.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a bunch of beta, then this launch version and my initial suspicions unfortunately checked out.First and foremost, I don't want to deceive you from buying this game and giving it a try. This is a pretty well crafted cinematic experience, graphics are great, so is the performance (for the most part, just fix the freezing), and audio is even better. First few matches feel AWESOME.But then, when novelty wears off, you start to see how shallow this game really is. This game feels very complex but that's because it's confusing, once you understand what to do and where to go you can end the game in 2 minutes consistently, and that is what more experienced Victims are already doing, 2 days into the game's lifespan.My main problem is that there's nothing to keep you here for the long term, which is problematic considering this is a $35 asym multiplayer online only game. Well except for the tree progression, that's actually kinda good, but I'm talking mechanical things - once you learn the maps there's nothing else to master here. After you've played a couple of matches you kind of had enough. There's no movement you can perfect, as a Victim you just run away, as a Family Member you just run after them and click LMB when you're close, that's the whole gameplay loop. In fact, for Family Member it's probably even worse cause their gameplay boils down to being locked in an animation 50% of the time. You break the vent, you break the bench, you close something, you lock something, all these animation will take you 5 to 10 seconds, so out of 7 minutes of gameplay, 3.5 is spent watching your guy do something and the rest is running around looking for victim or feeding grandpa.Victims are a bit more fun in my opinion but they face a similar problem, except this time half your time spent will be doing the minigames. They boil down to holding the button down until you fill the bar, and you also fill a bar that you don't want to get filled that usually fills up faster and you have to go back and forth to balance that or risk getting detected (or worse).  Not every bar fills up the same way, vent starts with a huge spike in both bars when you start holding the button and it can lead to some fun rush interactions, but again - novelty quickly wears off. I definitely prefer it over holding M1 from DBD, but the major difference between this two games is that in DBD on average 2 or more survivors have some kind of interaction with the killer for the most time, so yes someone's gameplay boils down to holding down M1 which is boring, but on average people spend more time doing other things. In this game there's no escape from it, every single victim has to spend half their time doing this stuff cause that's what the game is about. You have to search for tools to escape, both the basement and first escape route (which requires 3 searches total!). Other escapes are basically the same cup of tea, you need to "skill check" something but instead it being a tool it is a valve now.As for controls they feel awful. Victims have plenty of i-frames, because they have to, some prompts are hold only, other are press, and obviously you need to wait for the prompt to show up for the game to care about your input and it feels just awful, the gameplay is not fluid at all. Not to mention you can't rebind your keybindings on launch, although I personally found default keybindings satisfying, though in my opinion this is unacceptable. This is not a freebie from 1995, this is an expensive indie title for PC.
