_childDocuments_.review: My review of the game: Pro's:A very enjoyable game to play as survivor. I haven't tried playing as the killer's yet but i've enjoyed my role immensely. It has a unique level of challenge and different ways to escape that make it enjoyable. The killers are unique and are, quite frankly, terrifying to encounter much akin to the real movies. The diversity and versatility of the system is fantastic, as you can cut-down noise detectors, if you have the appropriate weapon, and can even fight back against the killer's -which is a realistic component-. I enjoy the bleeding out mechanic as it makes it more difficult and paramount to find medicine scattered around the map, to avoid becoming temporarily incapacitated. The dialogue when encountering other player's is refreshing and feels immersive, I too would be overjoyed and relieved to see my friend during a situation like that, and the developers made sure to incorporate that. Team-work is another thing that makes this fun, you don't need to rely only on yourself, and much of the objectives can be accomplished as a group, now coordinating those tactics is another story as I believe the mic is global so any instruction offered the killers can hear as well -if im not mistaken- and vice-versa -this will be elaborated in the suggestions tab-. I like the beginning feature of being tied up in the basement and having to escape from the ground up, it adds to the challenge. I love working as a group, and seeing some things accomplished and being able to build off of one another. Suggestions/what i'd like to see in the future:-Chat box for AFTER you win, I don't use a mic, and it would be nice to talk to other players about the experience-being able to "friend" cross platform players before and after the match to develop continuous parties (if you can i haven't figured out how) it is a function similar to dead by daylight -New character: For killers, grandma, whether playable or not, she would be an interesting addition, she could be in the kitchen in the house butchering bodies, and you have to sneak around her once you get upstairs, if not playable she can act as a moving sentry, similar to grandpa but more challenging because she's capable of moving, however perhaps she is limited to a scope of eyesight or vision to detect a player instead of a, "don't move" aura in order to make the game more balanced. It would be funny if she saw the player and started yelling for back-up which highlights the victim character. If playable maybe she could lay traps, or plant slow-acting poisons along the map that act as decoys to medicine that damage stamina or health and progressionally gets worse without an antidote or real medicine , it'll be like russian roulette. -more costumes for the characters, that are unlockable as you progress to give us something to look forward to, maybe a level cap or point system to "buy" the costumes could be implemented to add layers. I hate what Dead by Daylight does hiding a lot of costumes behind paywalls, however they did something right with making some costumes unlockable with iridescent shards, or currency one gets from leveling up. It keeps the game fresh, and something to strive for. -More skills/better perk tree, or a simpler more digestible format to implement them. I find myself not using them to the fullest and just go into playing. Maybe making something adjacent to a, "blood web" from DBD or a perk tree that is fleshed out and incremental, just building on top of one another. -More survivors so that players don't have to, "fight" over getting their favorite, even if they are not unique statistically the cosmetic differences make it interesting. I'm hoping new survivors will be free updates, however if not, I think that there should be level caps to play as them or an experience system to unlock things. This idea stems from Friday the 13th, you had to reach certain levels to play as particular survivors or wear cosmetic items. There is a nebulous feature of this in the game however, it is a superficial change -for example, colors of the same clothes-. _childDocuments_.review: I like this game, I really do.Texas Chain Saw Massacre has a great foundation, very similar to the beloved Friday the 13th: The Game, with a very unique twist in the asym genre where there is more than one killer actively hunting you, all doing different things and different abilities to utilise, as well as some being better to keep up with in chase than others. Mechanically it plays similar to F13 with a big map and multiple objectives available for victims to do, sprinkled with some RNG.Graphics and atmosphere here are gorgeous, very well complimented with the animations for both the victims and family members.All this is even more underlined with a fantastic audio design ranging from immersive, film-like music, various grunts, screaming and other voice lines in the game.Overall, very immersive experience, that will often feel like a literal TCM movie!Family gameplay is heavily oriented toward patrolling the few objectives around the massive maps and working together in a chase, because victims are a lot more agile than the family. It's a nice and fun approach.As victims, for some reason I can't shake off the feeling like I'm playing a PuppetCombo game :D I mean it in a good way. It's a very cinematic, film-like experience. One where you don't always get a good glimpse of the killer, hide around the bush as they walk around taunting you with some blood-chilling lines that fit in their character very well. All this time a chainsaw being constantly revved in the background, mixed with screaming. It's a thing of beauty!Although, a thing I need to bring up - for some reason whatever GunMedia touches is prone to 2 ailments:1: Broken a*s voice-chat(find some player utterly annoying because they keep open-mic or perhaps got some angry russian kid in your team screaming throughout the game, telling you his life-story in his mother-tongue that SURELY the rest of the world can speak fluently? Too bad, because muting people in games touched by Gun's hand is purely cosmetic for some f*****g reason)2: Those games always die.In regards to the latter - majority of the time you're just looking for a lobby, or in a lobby waiting for people to join. In the actual game, who's to say you won't happen to die first in the 2 minutes from the start? You may, you may not, and then back to the lobby you go. Issue not really applicable to family members naturally, and just to clarify - it do be like this sometimes, from time to time you will die quick, and that's okay, the issue here is the enormous amount of waiting you have to do, and trust me when I say that people are very quick to take their leave, nothing new for an asym I suppose, just sucks to have a perfectly fine, immersive game be completely ruined by entitled people.You can really tell they had issues actually getting people into the game, given they were forced to put on restrictions on people for dodging lobbies before games even start. That's sad.Now, despite F13 having an Offline mode, TCM simply doesn't have it, so there's like NO preservation or future-proofing this game. If servers die one day (just like F13) or you simply get bored of people and would like to just chill out against bots - you can't do that. One day you just won't be able to play this game at all :VAnother BIG thing I wanted to talk about, something that pushed me away HARD from this game, is how competitive it is. In an interview with the developers (or publishers, can't remember) before the game released, we were assured this is not going to have a competitive approach, but apparently that was just a straight up lie? I played TCM for a while when it released, eventually took a break because I was mentally exhausted from the constant competition due to the nature of the game and the mechanics, and that break lasted for far longer than I anticipated, and I just couldn't bring myself to return despite missing the general theme of the game and it's gameplay.To give you an example: why the need for global voice-coms? Why the need for removal of proxy-chat? Part of the fun in F13 was the proximity chat, and the devs recognised it, literally saying that they quickly came to realise how much fun the community was having with the proximity chat. Now, they completely removed walkie-talkies, removed proxy-chat so that no victim can talk to a family member (for whatever reason?) and now both sides are just constantly in each others ears. It makes sense for the family I suppose, but victims? It removes a lot of the horror... Victims (characters) will talk to each other when they come close together, greeting each other and all, almost oblivious to the fact that we can telepathically communicate with each other the whole time. Oh, and you can also communicate just fine with people who either escaped or died just fine too. Like, it's stupid, doesn't make sense and takes away from the experience, as well as takes away from the casual aspect of the game and pushes it toward the more competive side.It's simply not the experience I was told I was going to get.Overall, a great game that's sadly going to die :(

_childDocuments_.review: The beta was VERY fun but it didn't take long for every match to turn into an absolute sweatfest when it went live. I had to upgrade my GPU to even be able to play the live game without constant lag, freezes, stutters and crashes. Victim objectives are too risky half the time and take too long to do sometimes. If a family member finds you, forget doing objectives. You're pretty much just going to be running the whole time until you run out of stamina then its game over. If 2 family members find you then they can easily corner you or cut you off and eliminate you leaving you feeling like you didn't have a chance. For me it felt like if you didn't make a fast escape then you're not going to escape. This wasn't the case during the beta but now that everyone playing pretty much has the whole game figured out its just all about the speedrun strats.Other things I don't like about the game:Your character as victim is auto placed into crouching all the time. The last time I played there was no way to turn this off and it was literally the most annoying thing about it. I lost many matches because I wasn't able to sprint because the game decided to crouch for me and prevent me from sprinting when I needed to. LET US TURN THIS OFF!You die too fast. A common experience for me in this game was getting hit by one family member a couple times just to run into another who hits me and then I die. I just feel so limited in what I can do to survive. Yea you have things to counter them like Leland's stun and the bone shards, but those only go so far when the family has infinite life and infinite attacks. If victims could actually work together to kill family members the game would be a whole lot better. That should actually be an alternative way to escape. The family has way too much power when all you can do to stop them is stun them for a moment in certain situations.Confusing maps. After playing all of the maps several times I only really learned 2 of them with still a few things I don't always remember. It seems like if you don't know exactly where to go at all times you're doomed. The whole "what do I do? where do I go?" feeling kicks in and you just feel hopeless.Overall the experience seems to be you either win fast as family or escape fast as victim. The long game doesn't really happen anymore in my experience. Family knows where survivors need to go and so they camp those places all the time. Sometimes other survivors will find a way to escape very fast, leaving their team behind to die instead of finding them to show them the way out. I think maybe the game could be fun if you play it with friends. If I am able to do that one day and have fun with it then I will update this review to reflect that. Until then, I can't recommend this game. Its not worth $40. This game should be $10, maybe $15. It needs WAY more content to be worth $40.

_childDocuments_.review: Texas Chain Saw Massacre is exciting, intense, and could use some improvements. Worth playing? Lets review. POSITIVES1) Despite all thats been said below, I do enjoy the game. Its fun and exciting to play with friends and it gets me on the edge of my seat pretty consistently. It creates a great atmosphere of horror and I love that. I think there's definitely room for some balancing and tweaks to make the matches a bit more even but in general I think the games worth getting. More so if you have like minded friends who will also enjoy the genre.FEEDBACK 1) Mechanics feel geared towards the family at this point. Double locks, traps, insta kill hits, sounds coming from hiding places making them essentially worthless, and a recent patch gave the killers an even bigger head start. 2) A maxed level Grandpa should do 3 yells in a row that auto-reveal you, and then be dropped back down a few levels. A maxed out Grandpa is essentially a game over. 3) Feels like theirs cheating or exploits occasionally. I'll be hiding in a dark corner and a leather face will charge straight to my position without hesitation like he knows I'm already there. I've spent entire games just roaming from hiding spot to hiding spot with a leather face constantly charging my exact position. 4) When you run through a door, you should never have to turn around to make it close without putting you on the wrong side of the door. You can do this with wooden doors but not others and that just feels weird. 5) This game, from a survivors perspective, is all about staying together. Thats one of the only ways to win. Communicate, work together and win. The issue is, the second someone is caught, everyone near them has to book it or hide wherever possible since you all can't move down similar paths without someone dying guarenteed. This isn't an issue if you can allow people to ping each other or communicate somehow. Maybe do a trail of personal items that helps people follow or get back to their friends. But yeah its extremely hard to stay together or work together without memorizing the exact paths on each map which seems extreme.

_childDocuments_.review: Gun Interactive, the publishers, have 14 employees according to wikipedia. They have managed to acquire the intellectual property for this first film in the franchise, but failed to design a fun game play loop for the developers they contract out to make the game. They had an entire year (original release August 2023) in which the game was free on a different paid subscription platform, to fix core issues with the game design. Now that the game is no longer free with that subscription, they have still failed to deliver a fun and balanced gameplay design. The game has now gone through two different developers and the newest patch, which was to be a minor one released today, has led to majorly broken gameplay and lots of new bugs. At it's core, the game doesn't have a fun loop. You can sit in a queue for ten minutes and a match lasts two minutes and you learn nothing. Whether the survivors rush the objective in two minutes or the family rushes the basement, the game has no clear direction of how it wants matches to be played when they quickly end within 2-3 minutes of starting or have people disconnecting due to feelings that the match up was unfair.Loading screens still show old and inaccurate tooltips based on gameplay logic before new DLC characters were introduced. _childDocuments_.review: Is the developer team even listening to their playerbase at this point? What is happening at GUN Interactive & Sumo Digital?Here's a handful of things that bother me:- The developers shipped the game with debug functions on launch. This makes it very easy for cheaters to hijack these functions and completely ruin matches — really just the game as a whole. Of course, these functions were not removed until today, weeks after launch. They could have had a patch out just days after launch.- The Microsoft Store PC version did not ship with an anti-cheat at all. You can imagine how this worked out. Anti-cheat was added in today's update (thankfully), but I have doubts in its competency. The developers promised to have cheating issues mostly under control on launch when the tech test was happening, including adding more server-side checks for various functions but that did not happen. Mostly everything is still client-side.- Crossplay was "temporarily" removed on the PC platform today. Who knows how long this change will last for, seeing how a developer on Twitter said "hopefully weeks or less," I am led to believe this will be for possibly a month or more. People can no longer play with their friends on different platforms such as Xbox and PS5. This was done in order to give the developers more time to "perfect" their anti-cheat and protect the precious console playerbase, while leaving the PC playerbase to deal with these cheaters in tenfold. Shows how confident they are in their new anti-cheat measures. - Lobby countdown timer was 5 minutes in the tech test, 3 minutes at launch, and now back to 5 minutes as of today. Who asked for this? If anything, people were complaining that even 3 minutes was too long because there would always be that one moron in the lobby who would not ready up, and we would have to wait the entire 3 minutes. 3 minutes really wasn't that bad, but now it's back to 5 minutes? I don't know if this is somehow supposed to compensate for the change that allows lobbies to start with 6 people, but even that's ridiculous. Really, the 6-player lobby change just leads to more sweat. I want to play semi-casual, not feel like I'm competing in a tournament for $2,000. It was fine with 7.- The request for keybinding has been a big thing among the PC playerbase since launch. Players mainly wanted to remap the text chat key because it was just so easy to accidentally press and completely get screwed in a chase. Never really happened to me, but I understand where others are coming from. Keybinding was added to today's update and I believe everything was added except for text chat rebinding, one of the big reasons players wanted a keybinding feature in the first place. Was this done on purpose or are the developers really just not listening?I hope I can recommend this game in the future, but as of right now that is not the case.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally reaching level 99 in the game, I can provide my final review of this game:Firstly, this game isn't particularly beginner-friendly. If you found it on Steam, have no knowledge of the movie, or have never seen any content about the game, or even played similar titles like DBD or Friday the 13th, don't buy it. I don't recommend it because you need to know at least the basics to play decently.However, if you're intrigued and would like to give it a shot, the game does offer tutorials with well-explained cinematics that perfectly cover all its basic aspects, from victims to the family. But again, if you want to have fun, you should have at least watched game content on YouTube and know the basic mechanics; otherwise, you won't enjoy trying to learn the basics.If you're new and familiar with the game beforehand, I recommend playing as the Family first. Maximize all the family characters with their builds and abilities to the fullest before moving on to playing with the victims. Trust me, it's easier to understand the game from the killers' side than from the victims'.What's often talked about in this game regarding the lobby and the issue of finding matches is 50% true. If you play as the family, you can have hours of uninterrupted fun. But if you play as a victim, you'll have to wait a little longer between each round. However, I want to mention that DBD does something similar, and people don't complain. What I mean is that when one round ends, the game can immediately search for another match. In DBD, you have to return to the lobby and wait for the game to reload everything and rematch with other players. And now that I touch on this topic, THIS GAME LOADS VERY QUICKLY. Maps load in less than 10 seconds, and you don't have to wait for anything during other loading times. But the fact that it takes a few seconds longer to find a match as a victim doesn't make it a lobby simulator like 85% of the people who play this game claim.In conclusion, if you're a FAN of asymmetrical horror games or you like slasher and/or horror movies, YOU MUST GIVE THIS GAME A CHANCE because this game is the biggest waste of potential I've seen over the years and it needs people's opportunity. Believe me, you'll feel like you're in an 80s movie, and your heart will beat fast when a maniac with a chainsaw chases you from behind.This game is an 8/10 for me, as a lover of horror genre in video games and slasher movies.Pros:-Incredible atmosphere that transports you to the 70s with its sound graphics and audiovisual effects.-Asymmetrical 3 vs 4, team up with your friends for both sides of the game.-Multiplatform Crossplay: it doesn't matter if you have friends on Xbox, PlayStation, or PC Game Pass, you can play with them.Cons:- Not very beginner-friendly without much experience, however, very detailed tutorials are available to learn the simplest things.-The wait time per match for victims is slightly longer than for the Family.It has bugs that can damage the gaming experience, but they don't occur very often and ultimately, it's being polished and fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the original film, or the franchise in general, you'll enjoy The Texas Chainsaw Massacre a lot. But, at launch (at time of writing), it comes with some fairly serious caveats to consider:1) Matchmaking:a) Bugs that result in you being kicked from lobbies that are still forming. Really needs to be sorted, fast.b) Lobbies that struggle to fill, particularly when you get to higher ranks.c) A wait timer that adds a surprising amount of delay to the experience, between matches that can be very, very short indeed.2) Progression is a mixed bag. It's impossible to tell which actions contribute to score proper, so you're shooting in the dark from match to match. On top of that, perks are levelled per-character - meaning you can have a Tier 3 perk for one character and go through the same levelling work with another, just because. Knowing that going through matches quickly, by escaping, isn't doing all that much to further my levelling, doesn't appeal all that much to me.3) Co-ordination. Really obvious, but it's critical when you're at higher ranks and up against teams. Particularly as a victim, you won't stand a chance. There's been plenty of times where I've just quit out of the game (which generously grants you the gained XP, that you'd otherwise expect to lose, anyway) - knowing that I have 0 chances of making it any further. Coupled with the XP issue, it's difficult to feel there's much to play for when you're behind.4) All of these issues contribute to the most prominent question for newcomers: the price. Do I think it's worth it, given my caveats? Yes, but tentatively so.There's an undeniable buzz to victory that only asymmetrical horror games can give you, along with the sweat-inducing panic of being pursued by Leatherface or breezy high of avoiding being spotted in plain sight. The aesthetics are great, if a bit limited in the cosmetics that the game hopes for you to earn. For some, it certainly won't be rewarding enough - but I still think, having played 6+ hours of the technical test as well, there's a lot to enjoy here.I will say, for those claiming TCM as a challenger to DBD, you're sorely mistaken. There's a game that really set itself apart over time, the devs learning, adapting and incorporating new content over time. TCM is fresh and doesn't have the firepower to compete. Maybe, with time, it will - but it feels far more of a niche product than the big, new horror title. And, that's okay.TL;DR - Game is good fun but has some issues that will put off newcomers. It has my vote, but it may be worth waiting for new content/issues to get fixed/balancing to dive in, especially at the current price (£25 is more reasonable to me).

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from a long time Dead By Daylight player, this game has a lot more variety in gameplay and I've been having a blast with my first 100 hours. I love how from a Victim perspective, the gameplay feels more like a game of hide and seek, rather than a game of cat and mouse. Though I end up getting killed more often than not, I still get a huge kick out of the challenge of trying to stay out of sight from the Family and finding a way out of the map. As a Family member, I like how you're working with a team and each member has a definable role. The fact that they can find and kill a Victim easily makes the stealth aspects of the game feel much more important. There's a lot of timing involved with making your movements and any noise you make, from foot prints to grunting, can easily give away your position. The maps, while they are a bit labyrinth-esq, are absolutely stunning and give the game a gruesome, oppressive atmosphere. The fact that they've designed everything, from the buildings to the bushes, based on actual on-site locations in Texas, shows how much of a labor of love this game truly is. The sound design and soundtrack are really damn effective too. If you're a fan of the original TCM movie, I think you will appreciate this game as an authentic tribute. The only problems I can think of that I have with it are the current lobby system they have for matchmaking. Considering people can only play one character at a time, and the match HAS to have a Leatherface player, you might have to search for new lobbies as people will hop in and out because they either can't get the character they want or nobody wants to play Bubba. If you're going into this game, it's probably best to learn the mechanics of each character, Family and Victim. Each character has something different about them, and I would argue that none of them are horrendously stronger over other characters.If I could mention one more gripe that doesn't have anything to do with how the game plays currently, I feel like I should mention the monetization system they're implementing into the game. First off, $40 is a pretty steep base price for a new multiplayer only game. That and I think the current monetization system they've proposed is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Upcoming singular Victim and Family characters are supposed to be priced at $9.99. Not in a character bundle, but as SEPARATE. Hopefully, if the game can last long enough, they can offer a more elaborate system for unlockable outfits, characters, executions, etc. I understand that microtransactions can be a way to help support developers. But when you already have a game that's 3/4 full price and only offers a multiplayer experience, it's hard to justify putting a high price point on extra content. Cosmetics and alternative executions are one thing, but if it comes to characters that could potentially make a noticeable impact on the overall gameplay that could make it a "pay to win" situation, that's where most of us could draw the line. Ultimately, it's anti-consumer and I hope they can find a way to make modifications to what they're proposing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is superb and fun. It's impossible not to compare this to DBD and F13, the game is a perfect mix of them both, killers can quickly kill survivours if they mess up, but survivours can actually do things in this game. There are 3 maps, 5 survivours and 5 killers and you are playing 3 killers vs 4 survivours. On one hand this feels unfair, but actually the game is well balanced, more than that, I played for over 20 hours already and I have fun as both survs and killers and I feel everyone is OP in their own right with some mild exceptions. The game feels very fresh, chases are very thrilling and very fair, always. Killers are all cool, I never watched the movies and I didn't like the idea of runnign with a razor or a scalpel, yet here I am having a time of my life, the game makes you always feel powerful as a killer and always vulnurable as a surv. Matches are fast and intense, chances for your escapr are always unknown and I just want to keep playing and having fun. Plus the game feels very alive, waiting times are very short, just making everyone go ready in lobby does. You also have perks and attributes, but this time you have points you gain per account, not per character, you can also always respec so you can play anyone at any time you want. Maps are very detailed, just like in B or even AAA class game and it's just a joy to play it. Whether you are running from leatherface or chasing as him you will have fun and that's what matters the most.

_childDocuments_.review: Assume the role of one of the notorious Slaughter family, or their victims, in The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, a 3rd-person asymmetrical horror experience based on the groundbreaking and iconic 1974 horror film. Texas. Early 1973. Ana and a group of close friends embark on a journey to the small dusty town of Newt, TX, the last known location of Ana's missing sister, Maria. The group's search quickly turns into a nightmare of unimaginable proportions when they mistakenly invade the home of Leatherface and his cannibalistic family. Tied up, tortured, and left for dead, the group must find the strength to fight back and escape before it's too late. Featuring strategic 3v4 team-based multiplayer gameplay, The Texas Chain Saw Massacre will allow players to truly experience this iconic franchise. The only question is, who will survive and what will be left of them?

name: HighFleet
detailed_description: Join our Discord About the Game In a world with no memory of its past. The House of Sayadi sends its thousand-ton military ships to the skies. Stirring the peace of nations inhabiting the earth they strive to bring back what they have lost. As a commander of the Sayadi Task Force you’ve been sent to regain control of the rebellious Kingdom of Gerat by whatever means necessary. To succeed will require careful exploration, clever resource management, cautious diplomacy and building a fleet capable of ruling the skies unchallenged. But maybe a much greater destiny awaits you in this journey. As this forsaken land still hides the mysterious prophecies of a long forgotten past. Killer combat At the heart of HighFleet is a unique form of combat in which giant ships bristling with weaponry duel above the desert. This is no mindless button mashing, however. Far from it. Battles are won by skilfully moving into positions that allow you to exploit your enemies' weak spots. Serious strategy Mastering HighFleet requires much more than winning battles. You must explore the mysterious lands of Gerat. You must manage your ships, men, fuel and other resources. You must engage in diplomacy with the various factions. And then there’s the prophecy to be unravelled… Freedom to fly Thanks to HighFleet’s in-game ship editor, you can build the perfect fleet to suit your style of fighting. The many distinctive ship options and upgrade paths ensure the game will provide plenty of replay value. One-of-a-kind world The “dieselpunk” visual aesthetic, immersive music and sounds, and underlying mystery of HighFleet combine to create a truly unique and unforgettable atmosphere. This is a world you won’t want to leave until you’ve uncovered every secret and followed your destiny to the very end.

There is a system that supposedly allows management of ships fuel, it does absolutely nothing; making things very difficult if you want to have any tactics more complex than keeping all your ships together and hop from city to city. _childDocuments_.review: Don't let the shipbuilder intimidate you, if you save a ship in there it can show up as recruitable mercs or even enemies and you will get destroyed by your own optimizations. Unless you are really into that sort of thing the game is 100% playable with the vanilla ships. However those vanilla ships (even your flagship) are designed with modification in mind. You eventually should learn to modify each ship in your fleet as your campaign progresses, upgrading them and supplementing your needs. Even the description for your flagship mentions that it is not fully outfitted (hint hint), however modifications made in a campaign at a shipyard are exclusively saved to the ship modified and the blueprints cannot even be transferred to other ships of the same type in your fleet. This means you won't see enemies sporting your on the fly blueprints but you also lose them every campaign or even when the modified ship is completely destroyed. Why is my review just talking about one small aspect of the game? This is what I wanted to talk about and the game has so many aspects I am not gonna cover them all. I honestly love this game, it reminds me of the upcoming UBOAT and older FTL which are both games I already love but then it adds this depth of sci-fi lore and immersion that I cannot get enough of. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome, it has a retro Cold War inspired presentation, the main screen is a navigation map with all sorts of fun little gadgets and gizmos inspired by Soviet aviation and technology, it plays like a fidget spinner except full screen. Many of the interface devices are functional and can be played with, the airship combat is super fun and immersive with thundering guns and rocket engines lighting up the post-apocalyptic sky. Play a few dozen hours and realize it's basically Harpoon 4 on the strategic layer with functional long range cruise missiles and aircraft - you're not provided with an aircraft carrier but you can easily modify the flagship or anything with a flat deck into one. This game certainly requires patience and technical knowledge of real world naval and aircraft systems of the 1960s-1990s to fully appreciate, and is not for the casual gamer - thumbs up from me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of a hard game to review, not cause it's a bad or unfinished game, but because it's just unforgiving. Let's break it into two things; where it excels, and where it's flawed. Excels:-Art work is incredible and original, it's fresh and the game feels dark and gritty-Story is engaging, and the dialogue options give you a sense of having a bigger purpose than just "go here, blow up these people"-Game mechanics feel original and while it's easy to compare to games like Barotrauma, it's still in its own niche that fits-Combat is intense, difficult and drives you to test new strategies and understand when to retreat or risk losing it all(thank god for the retry button)Flaws:-UI is a little clunky(not terrible but it's a lot going on), and at times it felt like the radio didn't serve much purpose other than when it tells you "you've picked up a signal". Spent probably 30 minutes trying just to see if there's any just random signals, but you mainly just get static(or maybe it's in morse code and I'm just not understanding it?)-Combat feels overwhelming at times; like I said, Thank god for a retry button. While you're given a set of ships at the beginning of combat, you only deploy one ship at a time....against four other ships. Obviously no one would be able to operate all four ships, but because it's just one ship against the world, your first two ships you deploy are most likely going to get trashed after each combat, especially if you don't retreat when nearly destroyed. I've lost many a good crew.... So with that in mind, I've got really only one suggestion for the devs; CO-OP! Sure, let the host(Duke) of the game pick all the dialogue and routes, but when combat begins, if ships could be assigned to other players(call them captains or something), and all players deploy at the same time, this would balance the odds, make things more manageable, while turning combat into a real dog-fight! Especially if you kept collateral damage, that way, players had to work together rather than just "spray and pray". Long story short; This game has some serious potential to grow and continue shaking up the traditional arcade shooter, and I would definitely recommend for someone looking for something fresh, so keep up the good work, Devs! Don't take the negative as a reason not to enjoy this, while hopefully the devs see this as a reason to keep this awesome project going and growing.

_childDocuments_.review: MicroProse returns in a frenetic kinetic explosive manner! Dead and recently revived, the team behind absolute wonders of gaming by the name of MechWarrior are back at it once more. And. My. WORD!! I've rarely enjoyed something so much and I've only just reached the 'end' after about 100 hours already on it. No, I'm not inept though I do choose to take a low range fleet so I can afford a ship I made myself. Hard to get a handle on, it certainly has its quirks and demands precision, efficiency, understanding of a dialogue system that is fairly unpolished. At best it is just aimless and confusing, but having seen the end and how it plays out shows me that the dialogue isn't wasted. Combat is unnaturally satisfying, the on screen effects are everything I could want it just reminds me of the onboard computers in the Aliens films and i LOVE it so much! I almost wish you were with the ability to command 6+ significant ships more often but it's just so hard to manage fuel, range and repairs unless you have anything resembling a Nomad or Sevestapol. It's a very good example of a game of which your choices matter and change how just about everything plays out. Every random sidestop you wiggle in is with reward more often than not, figuring out the map, radars, what guns you like and going as far as to make your own ships you can add to your fleet!The ship builder is rather enjoyable, as one who doesn't really even enjoy simple, fruitless building like that. I found myself getting lost on making my own ships for dozens of hours! I clearly have alot to say on this, the game's impressed and awed me in ways nothing else really has since Original Sin 2 and its Epic Encounters moddy. I hope MicroProse can get more under their belts, the person to revive them is a fan himself. Very interesting story there as well! ><Big applause, all my love. Well effing done.

_childDocuments_.review: For a while, I have had the desire to play a fleet command game. Something where you command a fleet (not a single ship) and this game scratched that itch perfectly. +Commanding the fleet is a blast thanks to a smart AI and clever rules. Stay in a city too long and the enemy will come crush you but at the same time refueling and repairing ships can take hours or days. You have to think tactically+Designing ships is great and easy to learn. Once you get good at it you can make some insane monsters that crush everything +Combat is deceptively simple. Every inch of your ship is a real part so ships take damage realistically. Using the right ship for the job, using missiles when in correct range, and managing the fleet are all keys to victory+There is a ton of choice tactically. Say I spot a large fleet a few hours out. Well, I can turn off my radars and fly "under the radar" and run away. Or I could order bombers to strike the enemy fleet and do some damage, or I could charge in. +The atmosphere is amazing. It's like part Dune, part Russia. Like a Middle East owned by the USSR. It's interested and engrossingThere are flaws. The game is not easy at all, the controls are complex, and only having 1 ship vs the entire enemy fleet is annoying. That said it's a solid 9/10 and worth every penny

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I want to love this game. The aesthetic is great. The story exists and some care has been taken to make you want to see what happens next. The actual fighting is kinda fun, too.Do you know what's not fun? 4,567 different mechanics for different phases of gameplay. There is a minigame for pretty much anything in this game and it is very intrusive to the goal of "fun." I'm not joking... there is a minigame for interrupting comms signals. The trick is to... wait for it... wiggle dials until the signal is strong. There is a minigame for landing ships, which involves using thrusters to control a fall so you land on the right landing pad. For the record... this is needlessly fiddly and difficult. Honestly, it's just needless. It does not have to exist and adds nothing to the game.There are separate mechanics for radar, infrared, missile defense, travel, and ship design. No matter where you are in the game they are going to toss a fresh system or mechanic at you. It's as if the designers knew that they had a really fun and solid $10.00 game on their hands, so they stuffed it with useless filler to bloat out the price. Because this game is really just a very fun aerial combat game with some customization elements saddled with a lot of $.99 minigames to muddy the experience. I suppose if you added up all the content you could get to a $20.00 game here, but it just does not come together into a rewarding gaming experience the way it ought to.With that being said, the parts of the game that are fun are very fun. The combat is brutally challenging, but also really satisfying. The enemy AI has nearly flawless aim and gets to field as many ships as it wants to at a time. You only control one ship at a time and your aim better be perfect or you're toast fast. Even losing is fun, and that is how you know you've got a good combat system. You can alter your ships to some degree with different parts. This is not intuitive but once you figure it out it adds a well-honed layer of complexity. This is where the game shines, and by itself is worth messing around with.The rest of the stuff? I swear it just exists to annoy the player. I suspect there was a sincere attempt to add dimension to this game, I really do. Unfortunately, after 2 hours of crashing onto landing pads, trying to outrun strike groups, and cursing at the stupid tutorial every time it pops up to tell me about yet another process I need to master that has nothing to do with giant airships blasting each other, I'm ready to quit.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game is nothing like I expected.What I thought I was getting was something like Airships, with strategy and building cool machines and some legit air to air combat. With the appearance and the price point I was like, OK, this must be a really solid and deep title.But what I got was like an online flash game or series of online flash games, like what you'd see on Kongregate or something like that.First thing you had to do is land your ship. Whenever you get to a new place, you have to land your ship using WASD, like one of those really primitive lunar lander games. When it told me what to do I was seriously like, "Wait, you want me to do what? What year do you think this is?"Then when you fight, you're also moving around your ship with WASD and pressing the left mouse button to shoot in a really cheesy 2d combat session, literally just like a flash game. All of those little combat scenes you see in the video? You're controlling one ship with WASD which moves like the ship in a Lunar Lander game while moving a little shooting directional pointer with a mouse, and all the other ships you see on the screen are enemies. Then when your ship gets beat up you have to fly to a certain place on the map and call in your next ship to replace it. The enemy has their whole fleet out there. Your side only gets one ship a time because you have to control everything.The graphics and UI LOOK impressive. This game works very hard on trying to create atmosphere to make it seem like it is more than it is. But then you get to this city map and click on 'supplies'. Instead of just listing whatever is there for sale and you pick from the list, you have to scroll around, moving your screen, and find missiles that are on shelves and that sort of thing. It's a waste of time and pointless to do it that way, but it is atmospheric.Maybe if this was $5 I'd say, OK, this isn't my type of game but it's not claiming to be more than what it is. At $30 it is not what you're expecting to receive.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a challenging, but fun game with a lot of depth. There's twin-stick combat, strategic cruise missile combat that's more like submarine warfare, ship design, radar, planning, etc. It's a bit rogue-like, in that you're expected to fail many times before winning. There are many ways to fight and you choose what methods you prefer. Choose to improve the vanilla ships designs or create your own from scratch. Maybe take a mix of the two.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible.Have you ever wonder what it would feel like if you were rudely awakened on a Monday morning, extremely hung over, and thrown into a broken soviet time machine?This game will show you what that feels like.  I bought this while hung over on a Monday morning. Suddenly it was 7pm and i realized i hadn't eaten all day. The art style is impeccable. It's the most dieselpunk thing you will ever witness. In game technology is a glorious blend of tech spanning from 1910 to what seems like the mid 80s. Nixie bulbs, grainy radar screens, old school radio sets, dirty gas masks, and lots of oil. Ships look like some sort of mashup of WW1 tanks with radar antennas and modern russian CIWS jutting off of them. All of that brutal looking tech thrown into basically fictional Afghanistan. The main map is amazing to look at and the weather effects in battles are beautiful. Clouds and rain streaming off your ships as they blast away at each other. This game sucks you in. You feel like you are playing a part in history. It plays like you are in control of a Soviet Afghan war documentary in a parallel universe.Everything feels right. The tone is perfect. Nationalism, duty, the cold death counts at the end of a battle. You lose a ship and see a hundred little skulls. one for each person who died on it. Experience nuclear war too.Combat is amazing. Difficult to master but very rewarding and incredible to watch. Difficulty is high even on easier settings. Learn to use your tools or die. Get this game. You wont be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.8/10. It has some interface issues, and some minor bugs so far (current release), but the game it's outstanding. Immersive like no other, complex, and logical in the sense that... enemy patrols and fleets track you down by search and elimination patterns. You have to decrypt enemy comunications to gather intel about their patrolling rotation and so on, i'm surprised by the amount of detail that the game projects. Never expected to be so engaged into this type of genre.  Yes i do. I fully recommend the game. If you are into post-apocalyptic games or diesel-punk style subgenre, this will be a great addition to your collection and a great experience. But be aware, it's a hard game with a marked learning curve, not a good idea if you want to rush things up. If the devs fix most of the little things that i mentioned earlier, i surely will give this game without any doubt whatsoever, 9.1/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommended this game because I love the premise and the combat but honestly this game is not fun about a quarter way into the first main mission. There are far too many aircraft carriers that intercept you at every turn preventing you from progressing due to the simple fact that you are out matched and out classed by enemy units. Until this gets balanced for normal play through I just can't play anymore, I have raged and restarted too many times to be having a good time playing the game. If you like a game that makes you quit because it is so hard to progress then this game is for you, it is probably the hardest rogue like game I have ever played in my 30 years of gaming. _childDocuments_.review: Nice strategy game in a unique "fussionpunk" setting with a great story. The setting mixes classical storytelling of Foundation, Homeworld, and KinDzaDza with the desolate landscape of a 40K hiveworld. There is also some taste of Dune's universe, especially in the technology , that is far ahead of our current (at least at free interplanetary flight level), but it's applications, designed to replace human brain seem to be either banned or completely avoided for another reason (Could their grimy existence be the final result of mankind's degradation due to abuse of "smart" technologies?) . Everything is simplistic, resilient and made to last (including during a all-out nuclear exchange). To make things even more immersive, game universe limitations briliantly reflect on the player. You won't be lead by hand or even guided in any way. After briefly showing you what you can do (sometimes jus as a timed message like "use space to launch missile") the game will never tell you if or when to do it, leaving you to think on your own (this may really frustrate some "modern" gamers). The gameplay itself also can be pretty unforgiving until mastered, especially at latest stages. You will most likely be defeated during your first runs.Game lore is quite deep for the way they present it and in same time leaves a lot said in between the lines, those to lazy to think on what they read may miss significant part of it (the amount of people who cal the it's setting "post-apocalyptic dieselpunk" is good demonstration of this). Story is decent, but it is the well thought, believable setting that makes it really impressive.Unfortunately game is not without some bugs (including one that made it unplayable for me until next patch), but is good enough to be worth waiting fixes. And it is good that they do fix is, as High Fleet is game that you will either hate soon or play for years.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat and damage system is really satisfying, visuals are awesome, sound effects are great. People said landing is a chore but I think strategizing which craft and where to land to maximize repair speed bonuses is a neat concept to add to your tactical decision. Radio interception, on the other hand, is quite annoying after some time.Now for the bad parts. Games like these are always difficult by nature. I hope they could give us options for easier difficulty because not everyone have time to grind to git gud. The thing with difficult games are, what the game designed as bonuses for doing well stopped being bonuses if you absolutely have to stack it most of the time to win the game. You either have to perform excellently almost all of the time, or you will be struggling to win the game.Also, the game have fantastic design mechanics, and I hope it would evolve in the future. But with the game as difficult as it is, why bother considerably changing a ship design on the campaign? You aren't going to have the funds, nor the mercy to see if your design works because, well, you have to do excellent to win.But all in all, I am a masochist who enjoys being punished for trying to have a relaxing evening in the weekends so I'll give it 8/10. It's a cheap game. Buy it whenever. Don't wait for discount.Edit: Ok there's apparently easy mode now but it just enables you to save the game whenever you want. Oh well its something, I can save scum now.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, challenging and very rewarding at the same time. You can make your own ships to use in the campaign, or test them in the shipbuilder for fun. This game is for everyone.If you're a nerd or autistic this game has 5 different types of highly detailed electronics to choose from.If you enjoy exploring there is a decent story and 6 hidden cities to find. If you're an arsonist and enjoy blowing ♥♥♥♥ up there is at least 10 guaranteed giant explosions per battle.If you're Serbian and enjoy killing innocent people there is 4 different types of nuclear munitions to choose from. If you're an aesthete and hate modern art then this game is for you. If you enjoy dieselpunk but are tired of all dieselpunk games being closeted steampunk then this game is for you.If you have 10 hours to burn and enjoy RTS games then this game is for you. If you want to fight in one of the hardest endings in video game history then this is for you. Enjoy micromanaging against 40 nuclear warheads. If you're not a troglodyte and have a basic understanding of geometry then this game is for you. If you wan't a game that has a soundtrack good enough that you don't have to play your own music then this game is for you. Or, if you're someone who just wants to mess around in shipbuilder and make a giant leviathan that can absorb several direct nuclear warheads, then this game is also for you.This game is NOT for you if;You have epilepsy (won't survive the menu)You're impatient (good luck with campaign and shipbuilding) You have the reading comprehension of a 1st graderYou can't accept minor losses You don't like RTS's or if you're an athiestenjoy

_childDocuments_.review: It's as if FTL had some good s*x with Starsector in a parallel universe of Dune where instead of getting high on some drug, everyone was high on gas fumes. It really feels like Dune but dieselpunk. Someone decided that planes are too small to be aircrafts so they now became ordinance for a much larger aircraft. And by aircraft I mean a f*cking flying oil rig guzzling thousands of tons of pressurized methane in order to a thousand kilometers.I calculated the price of Sevastopol moving from my city to my capital. I used the french exchange rate for a liter of methane (~1.2 Euro at the time of writing this) and it turns out that it would cost ~1,130,911 Euros. Not to mention that the planet the game takes place on is already a f*cking desert. This game is Greta Thunberg's nightmare right next to Factorio.All in all, great game, I got it for free, but honestly, I'd buy it myself, It's been like 2 days and I'm already half the way from hitting the 1 Euro per 1 hour of fun mark and I believe I'll go beyond that with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a 10-second-long air combat animation and immediately bought the game. Man, did I not expect how deep this game would turn out to be.The author throws you into a very difficult position of a clunky diesel flying machine commander. Story-wise, it's new for the character - the game conveys the difficulty of the plot in difficulty of the mechanics. The game does not teach you much - only the bare minimum to survive. I'll be honest, I spent about 10-15 minutes googling about various mechanics, but I absolutely cannot blame the game for not being accessible enough. Simply because it has SO MANY other virtues.The game has SOUL. Every blip on the radar, every accidentally pressed tumbler, every roaring cannon barrage resonates with your brain. Having finished the game, I have also listened to the main battle track, Tanc a Lelek, about two hundred times in two days. Simply because I can not let this game go. When you finish the game for the first time, it feels like the replay value would be quite low. Give it a day - you will ABSOLUTELY want to fly the clunky, flying diesel machine again. And again. 13 Thermal Signature Detected / 10

_childDocuments_.review: The art, fx, and feel of the game are amazing.  It's pretty much in 2 modes, a 2 view action phase where you fly your ship around and try to dodge or mitigate incoming attacks while you take out a few enemy ships.  There is also a sort of mini game of the side view where you just land your ships in the cities to gain faster repair bonuses.  The 2nd part of the game is the map view where you navigate and try to dodge enemies to avoid battles.   I feel like if you really got invested in this game there would be a lot more depth in the strategy of using the map.  I just didn't feel the drive to push further into the game.  You can also build your own ships, but I really didn't enjoy the building interface and soon the game just didn't feel right for me and I dropped it a few hours in.  It's cool, but just not for me i suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It is extremely difficult and addictive. It combines a dynamic, fast tactical combat where you must always keep a step ahead of your enemies and react in seconds with a slow but steady strategic overlay, where you play cat and mouse with a stronger enemy, using scraps of inromation to figure out the few narrow paths that will allow you to survive. People compare it to FTL and there are certainly elements of this game on the surface, but to me it feels more like Darkest Dungeon in Dieselpunk Afghanistan - the odds stacked against you, multiple enemies, not having control over everything and having to fight against RNG with superior tactics. Also the part when you have to fail multiple times to learn the game :D All in all, I would say - watch some videos before you buy. To me this is a rare shining gem of gamecraft, but as you can see from the several negative reviews - this game is not for everyoneI also want to add a bit about the aesthetics - it's a beautiful, creative game that created a unique universe and shows it to you rather than describes it, as games sometimes do. I also love how the ships you fly feel and look like enormous beasts.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant to purchase because I'm not into arcade games, but the arcade portion appeared to be combined with a very interesting strategic game so i went for it.  At only 27 hours in, I'm really impressed with the creativity and thoughtfulness of the game play.  Highfleet has a unique feel that is missing from many new games. I believe the development team is very small, so there are some quirks about the execution and features that will hopefully improve over time.Some improvement suggestions:Key remapping is not currently implementedBizarre game exit issuesArcade mode auto retreat is annoying.  A pop-up should be required to verify.Arcade mode HUD overlays obscure the screen corners.  Should go auto transparent when your ship moves over them.Arcade mode should have an optional low altitude warning,  The ground height varies and is very easily obscured by smoke and explosions.Being able to customize the size and shape of the aiming and turret cue indicators would be a nice feature.Update:  72 hours in.   I stopped and read a bunch of guides on how the game works.  If you are frustrated by the learning curve, understanding the basic concepts will make the game much more enjoyable.  Highfleet is a fantasy air/naval warfare sim with an arcade "combat" battle resolution.After trying the campaign several times, I see two main weaknesses in the gameplay.It's not that it's too hard, it's that your resources are so meager that you have to win all the time.  You just don't have any extra resources to spare to make up for losses in pitched battles.  The second is the morale system.  A nice concept, but I lose morale just asking my ships to fight.  They seem to lose morale at the drop of a hat.  And if you restart a battle your morale drops every restart.  Morale affects crew efficiency, so if you had a hard time before the battle restart your chances just got lower.This is compounded by a restrictive save game system.  The game is saved after every battle, so if you restart you lose any work you did at that city before your next battle.  Which is tedious and annoying.These two issues are unnecessarily sucking the fun out of a really fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated for 1.1 updateThe Jank:Navigatable by humans mostly. Some esoteric stuff like 50fps (This is covered a lot already, but resolution has been fixed since initial reviews.) and lack of keymappings. Tutorials could be better compartmentalized into the prologue but will show up when relevant in the actual game.  UI needs some TLC but otherwise works.(UI bugs addressed recently!)  *I saw some comments about mouse issues but haven't ran into them. (People with accel issues check 1.1 notes!)AI needs better multi-target handling. See carrier usage in tactical combat.The incredible:Battles are weighty and visceral with a plethora of player options on how to address a situation and their own faults/strengths. Successful macro-play allows you to take heavier, more immediately deadly options into battle like anti-ship missiles or even speedy bombers to dazzle garrisons and heavy cruisers alike. Successful micro-play allows you to slip a lightly armored knife of a fighter into Touhou like bullet hells and precisely destroy ship by ship in the deadliest game of tag. The music. The SFX. The work put into the sound of this game and how it captures the setting, the weird foreign land and the sheer raw hatred of the vehicles on display. Every sound used is a joy to hear even as the RWR sends dread down your spine.  Listen to Tanc a lelek when you get a chance. I want to comment a lot about the strategic layer and how giddy having a protractor and ruler makes me but that's on the niche side of appreciation. What I will say is that it offers players the ability to play Battleship with much more frightening results should they correctly use the intelligence tools on display. Every, single, button, is clickable and has a function. Players will learn to love/fear anti-radiation missiles and the consequence of nukes in warfare. In summary I adore this game and have a high tolerance for jank. I think it offers an experience that you won't get elsewhere, but you need to be aware that the game needs polish and will likely see it in time. This is Konstantin's labor of love and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been on many people's radars since it was teased. The premise is certainly an interesting one, hitting notes of post-apocalypse dieselpunk airships on a mission to... something? Very Dune-esque, which at time of writing has recently been released in theaters.Anyways: The game falls into the aesthetics of simulator games, but the mechanics are still arcade-y enough for a casual player to understand. This comes with the caveat that a lot of mechanics are unintuitive or poorly explained, so new players can be left confused.Combat is suitably meaty - heavy cannon fire is bassy and impacts are met with clouds of debris and shrapnel. Conversely, getting hit is a UI nightmare even with updates. Getting hit is disorienting.Music is probably the game's high point if you were to ask me. The music truely sells this mixture of Imperial Russia and the Middle East.Finally, the story is rather disappointing. It is an interesting one, but not enough to sell the sequel it clearly is trying to sell. Overall - get it on sale. I think it is a wonderful, innovative game with beautiful sounds but it is repetitive as desert dunes mechanically.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Utterly unique. Deep but fun mechanics, an enthralling plot, and gorgeous sound and visual design put Highfleet among my favorite games. The developer, Konstantin Koshutin, has kept up the development of the game over the years and plans further additions. I have 301 hours as of today and would buy a DLC or a sequel in a heartbeat.This game is absolutely worth the money. The replayability factor is very high with randomly generated map layouts, enemy compositions, and multiple difficulties--not to mention the intricate but incredibly rewarding shipbuilding aspect. The three separate difficulty settings are well-executed and are not just simple enemy stat buffs, but make deeper and interesting changes to enemy distribution and game mechanics.I adore shipbuilding games and Highfleet is my favorite 2D shipbuilder of all time. The game itself can be played and won on the hardest difficulty without ever touching the Shipworks, so if shipbuilding isn't your thing you still have access to most of the more than 80 unique vanilla ship designs. The ships are relatively simple in principle, with some smaller vessels comprised of fewer than 20 parts, and yet the art of arranging these components in aesthetic, useful, efficient shapes takes many hours of play and practice to develop.You can make a ship which is just a fuel tank, engine, and series of nuclear missiles. You can develop super-cruisers capable of crushing every enemy in the game back-to-back, and play the campaign with it. You can craft a fleet of fast maneuverable frigates and sneak your way from town to town, attacking before the enemy can raise the alarm. You can build an aircraft carrier and engage in jet-to-jet dogfights before bombing enemy capital ships into the ground with a single strike. Or you could just tweak the vanilla designs to your heart's content, optimizing--or worsening--some of your favorites.When you've selected or custom-built your fleet, you are thrown into a beautifully-rendered landscape with a realistic-looking interface fit for a Soviet naval captain in the late 20th century. You cross the deserts of Gerat with a fleet of nuclear-powered liquid-methane-fueled sky battleships, wresting cities from the hands of enemy squadrons one at a time. All the while, you are pursued by 5 large fleets of enemy capital ships, supported by aircraft and missile carriers scattered across the map or accompanying large fleets. Rogue commanders can be persuaded to join your cause with their ship and support, but you will always be outnumbered by the enemy.Combat is fought with you against 3 enemy ships, all wielding a number of unique and grievously wounding weapons. The damage from every shell, ship-to-ship missile, and collision is deeply modeled. You can strategically take hits on armored or less-important areas of the ship, e.g. crew quarters, or you can screw up and take a single bad hit to your magazine and watch your ship detonate from the inside with all hands. Strikes from planes or strategic missiles are fought (& often lost) on a separate battle screen where your maneuverability, armor, CIWS, and anti-air missile abilities will make or break your campaign. Every enemy poses a unique threat and has an interesting design. Different combinations of three enemy ships can either be hilariously easy (three tiny corvettes with peashooters) or terrifying (multiple armored cruisers with 7-inch repeating cannons and vast stores of anti-ship missiles). The tactical and strategic combat is still fresh and fun after all these hours--I just started a new campaign this evening!I can't recommend Highfleet enough. 10/10. You will burn and explode and die and it will be awesome and beautiful the whole time. Good luck out there, Tarkhan!

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my first serious feedback on Steam. After spending up to 300 hours in the game, I pretty much owe the developer my positive review, right?:) But this goes beyond than just a sense of obligation.This is, by far, the best video game I've played in my whole life. Someone might find such statement too pompous or emotional one. But I'm just being completely honest here. I've simply multiplied the total amount of time, I spent, playing the game, by total amount of fun I've had, while doing it. Before "Highfleet", there were just a couple of games, I've devoted THIS much time to: "Football Manager" and games of "TES" series ("Morrowind" and "Skyrim"). Most of these experiences happened in my childhood/youth, and, despite how great they were, it's important to note, that I've never considered any of them as "The Best of the Best". Before "Highfleet" there was no such video game for me.This game took me completely by surprise. By the age of 36, owning more than a 100 titles on Steam and other digital stores, I've lately found myself slowly abstaining from computer gaming, and shifting towards tabletop games more and more. Video games just didn't thrill me enough anymore, and it seemed like I've just lost the ability to fully enjoy them. But then a close friend of mine told me about "Highfleet", saying something like "It's coolest game, just take it an enjoy". And so I did."Highfleet" completely blown my mind. Why I loved it so much? Well, basically, because this game consists of everything I happen to like. I like a good strategy (most of the games in my library are strategic), but I also enjoy an occasional action. "Highfleet" effectively combines both of these aspects: deep and thoughtful strategy on the global map, along with super-fun and engaging arcade-style combat (God, I love it!).  I like a good theme - and I found Highfleet's alternative-history diesel-punk approach to be darn stylish and sexy.I generally love, when the game consist of different smaller-sized games. I consider mini-games a very powerful game-design tool, because, in the right hands, they provide a multi-dimensional sense of gameplay - and that's exactly what "Highfleet" does. Here you have 2 "big" games: global-map strategy and action-combat, along with 3 "smaller" ones: rpg/storytelling card game of diplomacy, radio-comm interception and ship-landing. Blended together, everything provide the STRONGEST sense of immersion, which is probably the major characteristic of "Highfleet" as a game. And the immersion IS why I play games in the first place. I especially like, that this game is pretty HARDCORE, even on normal difficulty - it's not a picnic. There is a tutorial, but it only teaches you as much as key-binding, basically. You really have to invest your time to learn stuff here, which, I assume, might be a deal-breaker for a lot of people. But if you are ready to do it - it's totally worth it.  This is not a flawless game, of course, even in the eyes of a crazy fan, like me. It has some questionable UI/game-design features, which can be rather frustrating. It also contains a range of bugs, which I believe, I encountered all, during my last playthrough on hard difficulty. At first, I was planning to point out some of them here, but then I figured that would be unnecessary. Most of them are very obvious things, which, I hope, will be identified and fixed anyway. Still, it looks much better, than some of the so-called "AAA" games, which costs like 5 times more, and just crash on the game start - no finger-pointing here, of course. But note, that, over 300 ours, "Highfleet" only crashed once for me.In conclusion. This is a great game, a neatest piece of game-design. It's definitely NOT for everyone - considering the hardcore nature of the game. But it's absolutely worth trying and find this out for yourself. If it appears to strike your chords, just as it happened with me, you will have tons of fun. I'm particularly proud of the fact, that it was developed by a fellow-russian guy, Konstantin Koshutin, almost on it's own! To him I wish, first of all, to keep up this enormous level of creativity, he's already showed. This project has a potential to become something really big and great, and totally deserve it. If this happens, I will be keeping my eyes closely, and be happy to take any part in it's future development. Meanwhile, I kindly wish all the dev team a good luck, and happy New Year!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game but I bounced off hard. I hate to judge it without having played it through but I figure anyone who reads this has to get through that initial hump one way or the other. My opinion is more subjective than I would like for a game I'm reviewing, so take it with a grain of salt. I'll keep it to pros and cons: The pros:- The art direction is really good and very unique. The best way to describe it is post-Soviet dieselpunk. - The story and setting seem pretty interesting, very bleak. Like the art style it's very unique, in a good way.  The cons:- The combat is interesting but it's basically your ships feeding in piecemeal against multiple enemies. Didn't feel like much of a fleet to me. That really turned me off.- The ship editor and the potential of custom ships seems great but I found the UI confusing and unintuitive. It's hard to explain, something about the way it looks and is presented just doesn't do it for me. I've played many games about building ships, vehicles, colonies, etc., in 2D and 3D, so this kind of thing is normally right up my alley. The UI was just repellent to me. - The UI in the strategic layer looks awesome but it can be confusing and almost overwhelming. It's very in your face. - The strategic layer itself is basically hopping from settlement to settlement for fuel. You fight the enemy at the settlement, you land, repair, refuel then head toward the next settlement. Meanwhile your motivation as to which settlement you're going to go towards is determined by intelligence you gather via UI minigames. These will give you hints to the movement of the enemy doom fleets that will crush you or enemy supply vessels. I'll admit, I didn't get very far into it but it didn't really grab me and make me want to get into it.In summary, this game isn't necessarily bad, there was just some things about its style and UI that really didn't work for me. It does do some things really well, especially its artwork and setting, but it wasn't enough to save it for me. I'd say if you're iffy on whether or not to get it then pass, or at least wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know that I've ever so quickly fallen in love with a game. Straightforward yet just-lush-enough storytelling, incredible tone and atmosphere, and gameplay that feels harsh and heavy like its ships. Its core mechanics are simple and match the overall tone of the game incredibly well. Everything around that simple gameplay builds upon that framework to create a simulation of operating a fleet of powerful, heaving ships with a solid backing of beautiful-yet-gritty sound and visual design.HighFleet does have its odd quirks like a dialogue system I could love a little more and what feels like some opaqueness with the fleet management system which has the player come out of the tutorial not quite as ready as one might like, but it's a deep game which heavily rewards time being open to the game and its systems and, in fact, cracking open the manual. That depth not being immediately apparent makes early failure feel like a learning process and success feel earned through shrewdness and attention to a surprisingly nuanced system of... well, systems.It's a great game that, years ago, would have come in a good-looking box with a nicely-bound little manual with some short stories tucked along with the instructions.Get HighFleet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of a kind. It offers extremely immersive strategic gameplay that is very hard to describe or compare to any other game. It has the deepest and most immersive strategic gameplay I've ever seen, coupled with a fun tactical combat mini-game, with a very well done custom ship designer.The strategic mechanics are all about maneuvering a fleet that is something like a modern carrier strike group. You have to manage fuel, ammo, planes, tactical missiles, repairs, and spare parts. While doing this you need to pay attention to several different types of sensors from radar, infrared, other radar emissions, and scout planes to avoid or attack the enemy. The game does not hold your hand, so you have to literally write notes on the map and use an in-game ruler and protractor to plot movements based on last known positions and speeds of enemies.The actual tactical combat is also very well done with lots of decisions needing to be made about how and where to attack based on enemy weak points and your own strengths. With custom ship designs this can get very complex and fun.The ship designer is very well thought out and lots of fun to balance, speed, armor, utilities, strategic assets (planes, missiles), and firepower. Every choice matters.Overall, highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: The moment when you can't find the quit game button before a battle destined to doom, you can be certain that this is a game designed to put you in there. An Immersive Sim, as we might put it.The stress was real. So was the relief when you survived against the odds. Then you realized three more of a Strike Group, a Missile Group, and an Aircraft Carrier were heading towards your solely remaining flagship, that no longer resembled itself at the beginning of the campaign. And as a commander, it was entirely your fault.The lore about prophecy is well written and worth investigating. Resembling; but while knockoffs can be described as terrible, this work is not. The story of HighFleet is a love letter to Frank Herbert's legacy.edit : This review has been written from memory. Later, I checked, and the quit game button during battle was patched-in in some updates when I was away. My opinion on the game doesn't change, because I'd Alt-F4 when it comes to that anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend Highfleet to those who enjoy meticulously planning their strategy and to those who have an abundance of patience. There are a number of game mechanics in Highfleet. You won't need to be good at all of them but you will need to be good at the majority of them in order for you to succeed. The dogfighting mechanics are exactly like Hammerfight(an older game the devs made) but with a plethora of armaments(including nukes) instead of melee weapons. The landing mechanics work like a complex physics based Lunar Landing game. The map works similar to a naval war simulator, with an emphasis placed on guerrilla warfare since you are outnumbered and out-supplied. This map mode uses a number of different radar-like devices that you would need to become accustomed to. Knowledge is power in Highfleet. If you know where your enemy is and where they are going then you are at a decisive advantage and vice versa. The recruiting and  storyline campaign mechanics uses a mixture of card based and rpg-like mechanics. Reputation is gained by being nice or not and will consequently improve your chances at succeeding for your chosen play-style (E.G. if you're feared then you'll find it easier to recruit these types of characters and succeed at dictatorship type decisions). Finally, the building and editing of your ships works like Starsector or Reassembly, with tons of customisation and the ability to completely create your own ship.Your ships needs a variety of things for them to function and there is always a trade off. For instance, a larger, more powerful ship is slower, an easy target and requires a ton more fuel to move around. The attention to detail in Highfleet is absolutely astonishing, but Highfleet does have its problems. First, they do not have ultrawidescreen support, so unless you like viewing the game stretched then get used to some black sides. Second, the learning curve is incredibly steep and is not intuitive but the payoff for understanding the mechanics is definitely worth it. Unfortunately, since there is only campaign mode, you'll always be bombarded with storyline interruptions, which I find incredibly annoying when I only want to focus on strategy. Third, always refuelling, repairing and resupplying can get incredibly tedious; frustration to the extreme. Fourth(pro+con) One wrong move may get your fleet blown up or worse, slightly damaged(yes, I can't stand always repairing).The game has to be played in small doses or it would drive anyone up the wall unless you're the type of person that enjoys meticulously planning your strategy with god-like patience. I salute you.
