_childDocuments_.review: Going to get this out of the way - The combat is AMAZING. The Soviet inspiration for HUD and parts is pretty much a dream for me. However, this game is so PAINFULLY UNBALANCED and the ship designer is so bad it ruins it. This'll be a long one...To start a game, you MUST equip the Sevastopol as your capital ship. This is an interesting design choice because it kills you. Think I'm joking? It guzzles 20 times the fuel of a light frigate and is so slow you are guaranteed to get missile spammed and gunned down by a strike group. Fuel is king - you need it to fly, you need it to fight - and it's expensive. To get that fuel money you have to capture trade ships, which are pretty fun to track down, but these will only give you 10,000-20,000 credits. If you follow the game's advice and take mostly medium combat ships and a tanker or two at the beginning, this will be enough money to fly your fleet 3-4 cities. Your objective is probably 30 cities away and a straight-line path is suicide. Now here's the real issue: each map has 30 trade ship convoys and they don't respawn. Ignore all those big ships with heavy armor you see, you can never afford to fuel them until the last attack of your campaign.Speaking of armor, it's pointless to use and incredibly frustrating to fight against. Repairs are expensive, and as I explained above, you're broke. If you use armor you're slow, and you get money chipped off your vessels by weapons fire. To deal with armor you need specialized ammunition or insane amounts of concentrated firepower, which is another expense. AP shells sound good, but lose so much damage over distance you practically have to ram your target, and if you're right next to a heavy cruiser, you're medically f***ed. Incendiary shells supposedly light fires more than regular shells (which light a lot of fires) but I barely notice a difference. Airburst/Proxy Fuse shells can be used to shoot down missiles and large shells (which you can just dodge but neat), rip apart unarmored targets, easily engage fast-movers, and for some ungodly reason they can also strip armor better than any other shell type. One of these things is not like the others. Oh, and did I mention the AI will be spamming these at you with no limit? Have fun <3Another force homogenizing ship design is the AI detection. If you get seen by a trade convoy or missile group or strike group or random stray aircraft they now have a timer above them. If you don't kill them before the timer expires you have alerted the horde and EVERY CRUISER STRIKE GROUP IS NOW COMING FOR YOU. Your only option is to run and pray you can avoid the net of radar around you. I use a stripped down, 2 gun corvette made of engines to get 700km/h (for reference Sevastopol is 90km/h and most fleets top out at 150) and it still only gets to them 3/4 the time, and it's always close. Also, turning on a radar to try to find your target better means any ship with a RWR/ELINT within 2 cities (double the range of your radar) can see you, so that's a death sentence as well. As for ship design, even if you suck it up and decide you'll start a new campaign every 3 hours because running an actual fleet is economically impossible, you can't load your own designs in the campaign, so have fun retrofitting the Sevastopol into a light tanker every time. There's an editor on the menu but I don't know why, I'm guessing just so you can save a ship to file and share it. The worst part is, if you take something off a ship the game doesn't consider that a new ship, it considers it a damaged version of it and will add that part back if you click the repair button because you got shot to s**t. So in order to save a new design to be repaired easily you have to strip off several wanted parts and add some unwanted ones, switch to another ship in the designer to get a prompt to save the ship, then add back the desired parts, strip off the unwanted ones, switch ships, and congratulations - you have added a save ship button in for the developers. Identifying parts is also difficult as it's done entirely by eye and then cursor, leaving you searching every inch of your ship to find where you accidentally buried that nuke.EDIT: No clue where to put this, but I have to add that your ships always fight 1v3. There are no fleet tactics. Okay that's a bit of a lie it's obviously best to concentrate fuel and sensors on non combat ships and other ships can help defend when the AI fires cruise missiles at you, but it really sucks that you can't go full wolfpack on them.The fact that this game's ship designer has no save button might make you think the UI is bad but no... it's horrendous. In order to change settings you have to be on the main menu. Weird, but fine, at least it isn't like 2005-2015 where we have to exit to the launcher. Here's the thing though, unless you play on easy you can only save at specific cities. A save point might be 30 minutes and a few good fights away if you're unlucky because as far as I can tell they are completely random in position AND NUMBER. WHY?! So imagine you play for an hour with the adaptive crosshair, then decide you want the extended one instead. Looks like you'll be clearing the next 4 cities and a known strike and carrier group just to get to the settings screen.It really hurt to make this review because the core art and combat of this game are so great, but the problems with English localization, UI, and balance really ruin it.Although I'm sad to say this, I don't foresee any of these being fixed, as this game has a single developer who has not updated the game in half a year at time of writing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is hostile to new players, missing such trivial things like a list of key bindings, let alone being able to change them, and yet having at least a dozen various keys for individual systems. The UI is interesting to look at, but awful to actually use, and the campaign is riddled with "you lose" silent triggers. Once you stuble upon them, it's over. Would be fine if it offered autosave at least on the easiest difficulty, which it doesn't. It does allow you to save your game manually on the easiest difficulty, though. You just have to remember to keep doing that because who cares about good game design.These things could be understandable on the hardest difficulty, passable on the normal one, but on the easiest it's just a bad joke. You are thrown in the game without any real tutorial (the prologue can't be called that even by a long shot), to use weapons you know nothing about, in a game where a single mistake can end your whole game. The game expects new players to already have 500h in-game time and know every mechanic, as well as having perfect mastery over them. It's just frustrating and not fun. Awful ship designer that boils down to "how to make the most efficient borg-cube," lacking any real creativity freedom, because either you design an efficient cube, or you are handicapping yourself for no real reason. The controls in the ship designer feel like something out of early Win95 era game that was made by a single guy in his basement in the afternoons. Well for all I know, it was created by a single guy in his spare time in the evenings.The actual combat, when it works and is well balanced, is fun. Watching ships dish it out. But actually using them in the combat is again unintuitive and you are thrown in unfair matches over and over again, designed to make you lose, and if not tactically, then strategically. "Oh, you killed those 10 much bigger and stronger ships in the last match without losing a single ship of yours? Pity now you can't repair any of those. Wouldn't it be sad if I threw in 10 more at your now badly damaged ones? You sold one to have credits for repairs of the rest? Wouldn't it be bad if I just threw 50 missiles at you to finish you off while you repair? Oh no, I guess it's game over for you."There also seems to be no difference in the difficulty settings, you can pick between "hard" and "no-save hard" mode.Long story short, nice to look at, bad to play. Might as well play in the in-game test mode. You don't have to care about the cripping in-game economy and can actually enjoy those 1v20 fights the game throws at you because you know a tiny mistake won't erase several hours of your progress. The campaign, though, is just terrible, the UI, the balancing, everything about it.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to say this when I first looked at the game, but this is truly a classic.The experience, to me, feels like I get to play the original X-com (1994) again, despite being substantially different. I have some minor complaints that'll probably keep me from putting in another 2-300 hours, but these really only show up when you start min-maxing and playing at the hard difficulties.Namely these (small) complaints are: player built ships that you can start with are far superior to the ships offered during the campaign. This isn't too much of a problem; however, fuel consumption prevented me from really expanding my fleet to make use of any extra ships. Other than a couple of support ships I mostly played through the hard difficulty with my starting fleet, and trying to mix it up with other ships was often more trouble than it was worth. Getting bad RNG on the available mercenaries isn't very fun either. Quite frustrating when all you want is a skylark or tanker or anything with good fuel capacity only to be met with stuff like paladins and feneks.Another issue is that killing enemies with cruise missiles, or aircraft, doesn't give you the opportunity to scrap the wreckage. Annoying since these are some of the funnest tools on the strategic layer, but you're heavily discouraged from using them as they're also quite expensive to use themselves, so losing out on the scrap is a double punishment.On the hard difficulty I felt that most of the ammo types were far far to expensive to even bother with. The enemy meanwhile gets to use them quite liberally. Somewhat frustrating not being able to afford them, but then having an enemy decide to blow up your magazine with some near unavoidable AP ammo. A rare occurance, but feels wildly unfair when it does happen. Ship editor could use some stream-lining, and it'd be really nice to have a better template system during the campaign, as trying to change anything can quickly add up to so many hours you'll finish the game before you get that Negev shaped up into something battle-worthy. I'd personally reccomend either a shipyard where you can just commission your saved designs, or maybe a base hull and variant system e.g. a lighting has 6 or so fixed blocks and anything else added to those blocks is a variant.

_childDocuments_.review: Lemme tell you a story.Many years ago I found this little WIP game called Hammerfall. It was on a website focusing on physics games and was among the abolute best things there. Even tho it wasn't yet completed I found a lot of fun in playing it. A *LOT* of fun. In short - Hammerfall was about fighting mighty arcade battles in which you controlled an airship with melee weapons and possibly a gun swaying down from it. Slashing, stabbing, slamming, crushing and bashing opponents was very satisfying, explosions were pretty. There was a lot of hidden stuff as well. And I played it a lot.Finally the game was released as Hammerfight. Completed, kinda buggy but OH SO FUN. I played it less at that point due to already having hundreds and hundreds of hours in it but it was great knowing it never was abandoned and that it's creator delivered the completed thing. I was happy to pay for it.Many years later I saw this game called Highfleet. I thought to myself 'I might like this.' I shall buy this for Christmas aaand I closed the window. But then I was like 'Hey, what did I see written there, who made this game? That name looks familiar.' So I reopened the page and behold: Highfleet was made by Konstantin Koshutin. Creator of my beloved Hammerfall. He made a new game.I Instabough Highfleet and oh my gosh, this is great, this is perfect. Visuals are so damn impressive, flying airships armed with guns feels so satisfying, combat is flashy and yet arcade'y. This literally feels like a battlefield of an era that never was, I love this, Konstantin delivered something deserving multiple awards. And he did this all by himself.The game is following a trend started by FTL. You move from a node to node developing your fleet and fighting battles while moving towards your ultimate goal and a big battle. You can shot, crash, land, fail to land. Oh and you can launch nukes. This is Hammerfall on steroids.After playing these two games by Konstantin Koshutin I'm under impression he's one of the most talented game designers in the world. He must also have such a strong selfdiscipline to build these games on his own.I'm trully impressed by this and I strongly encourage you to play.I'm waiting for your next release dear creator. I know it will take a few years, but when it's here it will be instabuy for me again.

_childDocuments_.review: Highfleet excels at 3 pillars that are very fun to play around:From modifying vanilla designs to making your own customs ships from scratch, the ship building system is easily one of the most fun and creative parts of the game. It is quite simple actually, and although making an effective ship can be somewhat tricky, it is a joy to see it in action, like my custom "Bomber Class" Rook ship, able to move at +300 Km/h while holding 10 tons of bombs. Parked enemy ships that saw it fly above them could only pray they weren't the ones about to face total annihilation.The combat is quick, stressful, and deadly, yet incredibly fair. It requires careful positioning, swift and well-timed movements, predicting the trajectory of your shots according to your speed and direction, anticipating your enemy, and more. A single mistake can imply your ship's doom, but if you master the game, you can take on gargantuan enemies with a single ship and win. Every success, mistake, victory, and defeat largely depends on your skill to outmanoeuvre the enemy.Arguably the most complex part of the game: managing your fleet, its resources, and the path that it takes to your destination. It is a risky endeavour that requires foresight and strategy, as it strongly punishes mistakes, but the tension and risk behind every decision is part of the game's fun. Also, the game is very authentic, forcing you to use tools such as the radar or the radio transmissions to gather information on enemies and predict their movements to ambush or avoid them.The game is very fun, however be advised that the learning curve is very steep, a lot of lessons are learned by trial and error, and it heavily punishes mistakes, so the road to learning and enjoying the game is, initially, quite painful. Nevertheless, if you're in for the challenge, overcoming it can be a really rewarding experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing.It combines strategy-game elements with fast-paced ship to ship combat.And a healthy dose of resource management and naval intelligence gathering.It has some RPG elements as well where you interact with your own officers and local leaders.Pros: -Great story-design/modify your own ships-brutal ship to ship combat.-Graphically, it looks great.-Great voice acting/crew reports.-great UI, it is one screen with an strategic map with all the sensors/panels you need.I absolutely love the sattelite view zoomed in.-Good strategic AI.As much i love this game and i would throw money to the developer to fix just a few minor things.Cons:-no manual save and loads.The game has none. its annoying.It auto-saves at points, but you never know when.-sometimes crashes in the ship editor. especially combined with not being able to load/save you lose a lot of progress.-Make the repair/ship editor screen remember the modifications you did to ships.Nothing is as annoying spending a lot of time modifying ships, take them to battle once and when you want to repair them they revert to their original layout.Outside of these points, the game is really immersive and fun to play.I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game.  Its completely unique to anything else I've played.  About 90% of my playtime is actually spent in the strategic portion, just planning movements, managing fuel, and using aircraft-carriers and ballistic missiles.  Only about 10% of the time is spent in the 2D realtime fights which can be really tense and are extremely fun to look at.Everyone mentioning that the game has a steep learning curve is correct, but I will tell you that once it clicks (after a few vids and a couple steam guides and reading the manual that comes with the game) its extremely rewarding to just nail everything.  It has great atmosphere, music, writing for a game this niche in its gameplay.  Everything is sort of based off of 60s or 70s soviet avionics except its set in a dune-like world with a lot of nuclear tensions.  It honestly helps knowing things in air combat such as ELINT and RWR, though the manual gives you enough of an idea.I beat the game for the first time on my 4th run of it, with all vanilla ships.  After that I took some time to craft my own ships (my own interceptor, carrier/tanker, AA-defense/radar ships) in the shipyard and immediately beat the game again.  Like I said, once it clicks, it just all makes sense and functions really well.  I would say it took me about 20-30 hours of failing to get it right though and really learn all the behaviors and mechanics.  So if you aren't enthralled by the world enough to keep trying, it might not be for you.  There is a small rouge-lite element to it in that every time you play it gives you a bonus based on your performance that is converted to extra starting cash for your next run.  So the more you keep trying technically the easier it gets.  After my current 70ish hours, I'm going to try the new Hard mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I can't recommend this game (yet), the premise is awesome but it's so damn hard to get into itLet's start with the pros:- The combat loops really tight and punishing (maybe too much?) - The art direction is really awesome. It reminds me a bit of a lo-fi version of Desert Of Kharak/Homeworld- The level of customization you can apply to your ships is ridiculous- The UI is pretty but not really "functionnal"The cons:- The out of combat UI is really, really pretty but SUPER weird: finding anything in the supply shop is a chore, upgrading your ship is really complicated (but the the possibilities are endless). It's pretty hard to understand what some modules do. The repair/refuel process is a bit obscure (especially if you want to fine tune the repairing)- The game doesn't support high resolution (huge black bars when playing at 1440p, unless you enable some kind of monitor stretching)- The strategic map is SUPER cramped (maybe because of the limitation in resolution)- The controls in the strategic map are really clunky: you can't dezoom a lot, no drag and drop of the map, the tuning knobs in the radio receiver thingy is super weird and not coherent (you can slide the tuning knob with a right click but not the direction finder for example)- Way too much graphical glitching to my taste (that you can disable)- The tutorial resetting messages resetting each time you relaunch a campaign (which happened 3-4 times to me already in 4h of playing)The unsure:- The game is extremely hard, it forces stealth on you, but if you get spotted on the strategic map it's pretty much gameover, you get missile spammed and the strike groups will come ruin your day.- Repairing is extremely slow, so if you don't perfectly manage a fight you are going to be stuck at the shipyard for hours trying to repair your tiny corvettes- By design the combats are unfair, you are always 1 VS X  so your ships are bound to take damage.I like the game, I like the concept, but some polish is missing somewhere maybe ?

_childDocuments_.review: ABSOLUTELY RECOMMEND THIS GAMEI have read reviews on steam and online which complain of features of the game and all i can really say is that the people writing those reviews must suck at this game. IT IS a difficult game even once you start to grasp the mechanics but what are we here for? A walk in the park? no. One review complained that they didn't have enough information on the enemy to  make the correct choices...yeah that's because you have to equip your ships properly and use the equipment to find the enemy/intercept and decode radio messages lolAs for 1440p, mine is fine. Out of the box, fine. Not a problem due to my aspect ratio being standard 16:9. No issues.No windowed mode, no funny mouse issues, nothing. So don't let that stop you. (2560x1440 32" monitor @ 59hz)Their are small bits of the UI which need refined but it could be patched up within weeks of release and I am sure it will be.Absolutely none of it has stopped me enjoying the game.Combat is chaotic, exploration is frighteningly tense and the story is downright beautiful.Ship customisation is baffling at first but once you start to understand how they all go together and how you can better equip your fleet, a whole world opens up and it is awesome.The game also lends itself to future DLC quite well and given that it was not too expensive to buy, a series of smaller £5 (or there abouts) DLCs would be quite acceptable to me. The only thing I would appreciate from the developers is to add the ability to set up your own custom battles. **Though having read the manual it would seem skirmish mode is planned for a future update already!**Like in the shipbuilding menu you can test your designs but you just get a load of random ships thrown at you so sometimes you are outweighed by the enemy so don't have the time to fully test on your own terms.That and it would be nice to properly practice combat outwith the story/campaign mode. Overall though I would say a firm 8.5/10 for me so far and I am sure it will only improve.Well done!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most enjoyable games I've had the pleasure of discovering in a long time.It is extremely compelling and immersive for a mostly 2D game, and shows some incredibly fine work by the creators, from the game designers, the artists, FX and developers, this is truly a work of art,  I am in awe.The game thrusts you into the position of a fleet admiral, and features a wide variety of strategic and time pressured mini-games. It puts your strategic thinking, intelligence and battle hardness all to the test in so many ways that it creates a great sense of achievement for making it through. The radical level of customisability and simulated dynamics seems like they wildly surpass what you'd expect from something like this. There's some very impressive programming under the hood!This game is truly a gem, brings back a lot of nostalgic good feels from Dos and 90's games of which the care and attention, until now I thought I could never find in a game anymore. _childDocuments_.review: The game is good, and fun, but it definitely has its flaws. I'll probably keep playing it. I can't recommend this game in its current state however. I'll give you a good example why - the game AI cheats. I was in a dangerous situation (enemy fighters coming at me, missiles coming in as well) and my radar picked up a missile. The game pauses when this happens. I also had an enemy fleet coming at me. So, I launched a nuke at the enemy fleet. I blew them up, and when you launch nukes, that gives the enemy the ability to use nukes too. So after I nuked that fleet, the missiles (which were in flight and coming at me) turned out to be nukes as well. What happened was the game changed the missiles in flight to nukes after I had enabled nuclear war. So those missiles which were just conventional warhead all of a sudden had their warhead changed? B.S. *** screen grabs on the store page show someone shooting at the ground on the landing screen - something you'll never need or want to do, and may do by accident, the warfare is nothing like that.The "prize ships" all seem to have missiles, which if they are cargo ships with a CAP squad would probably not have. The 'pick what ground thing to focus on or something blows up' part is dumb - might as well just randomly give us rewards than having us click on a radial menu and just randomly blowing stuff up. Landing craft is difficult - do you have landing gear? There's no warning until you're up in the air falling to your doom. Having a 'repair landing gear' or a warning for no landing gear might help. Also having an 'auto landing' option where it'll pick the safest place and land you (no bonus for getting the sweet spots) would be great. All this manual get a pencil put an x on a map just isn't worth it. The game needs to help out more, and the work of intercepting messages just to get 'make sure you have 1000 tubes' messages is not worth it. And on top of that, messages are encrypted - which, sure it was great that first time I guessed a key, but all the useless messages make me just ignore the radio.IR signatures detected - even when I have a spike on IR, turning the sensor towards something specific doesn't reveal anything. And if I get a warning saying an IR spike is detected, the game pauses, and I see nothing until they get a lot closer and I might get a little bit of a spike on it, but by then it's too late to change anything. FCR - fire control radars - I don't see any point to having one of these on a ship, they don't seem to help with targeting, and there aren't any short range (battle screen) missiles other than the IR ones. It's pointless to have in the game.Strike groups - left click sends the selected ships, right click does something else - the UI - aka the buttons you click have different meaning depending on what you clicked on, for example the main way you move your fleet is right clicking, but to move a strike group you left click, unless you have the strike group selected separately then its right click, but don't right click on your fleet... its confusing and frustrating, and needs a rework.Ship editor - this is awful and painful to use. Everything snaps, and it's not right - have a shadow snap where your mouse isn't being stuck like honey to the spot, instead use a shadow or outline and snap that instead of making it so difficult. Got a little concave part where you want to put something there? good luck getting it to not snap to the sides, anywhere you don't want it to go. How can I dissect the ship and see all the generators, or all the ammo - give me a filter where it grays out or darkens the parts I don't want to see (checkboxes, radios, whatever). I need a way to filter what I see on my ship. Placing the landing gear - its really fiddly and sometimes the legs don't flip the right way and there doesn't seem to be a way to change the orientation other than rotating something. Give me a LR control, where I can switch to a mirror image of something.  The weapons don't seem to show the firepower in the tooltips in some situations, for example the most important place - buying. The 700 radar if it's on the top of a vehicle, you cannot read the tooltip at all because it goes off the screen.  Put that tooltip on the lower right corner or something, some standard place with a line drawn to it, collapsable, and make ALL the info appear, and make it work for the buy screen as well. Overall gameplay - it gets very difficult to play the game as it goes on, money becomes a major issue, and the looting mechanic means stuff can just randomly blow up and you won't get any money. I feel like even if the map showed where all the enemies are at, it wouldn't make any difference, because the of the missile strikes, and the fuel issues are a concern. Where is the enemy getting all this money to be able to buy the fuel to move all their ships around all the time? Why does the enemy get to cheat the mechanics of the system? Does turning your radar off affect your detectability? because there's no feedback in the game. Missiles are few and far between, when I had jets, I couldn't find any place that sold bombs for them, but they always seemed to show up when I didn't have any jets. When you hover over them it says 'not suitable for anything' but rockets and bombs are suitable for your jets, and that tooltip prevented me from understanding I could buy those and use them in my strikes. Sending a strike of aircraft seems like a last minute addition, because clicking something under something else is strange, and there's limits which don't make sense. Your rocket ships won't have guns, so as soon as they're out of rockets they're evacuating. Air to air missiles are only for shooting other aircraft (the little ones on your carrier) not the other aircraft that you fight. If I am sending a strike group, why do my guys not have their guns loaded and ready? They're a strike group, I send them directly to a target I want them to strike, there's no reason those guns would not be loaded. It's a hostile city, there was enemy seen in the area, their guns would be loaded and ready. Don't make that a perk for winning a good fight, that's basic military doctrine. The only time your gun should be unloaded is if it's in storage, or you're in a well protected, friendly zone not engaged in combat.With all these issues, I cannot recommend anyone get this game in its current state. It's obtuse, the ai cheats, its clunky. It can give you hours of fun, but until the game gets better, the UI and the core game design / minigames design it's not getting a 'yes' from me.

_childDocuments_.review: At last, there is a game to fulfill an innermost craving that many of us have; the intrinsic yet deeply buried itch any game hitherto has yet to scratch: it is, of course, the desire to pilot massive neo-dieselpunk airships in battle high above the Arabian desert.This game is amazing. It's also incredibly difficult. There's no explanation for anything at all, but there is a forty page long manual on Steam that you have to read if you want a basic understanding of the mechanics. At every point in the campaign you will be forced to juggle a multitude of threats, objectives, supplies, map reports, random events, and the slowly-accumulating weight of your past mistakes. There are two parts to Highfleet, and each has great depth to it. The first is the high-adrenaline aerial combat which requires excellent maneuvering, tactical positioning, precise fire, and correct use of assets and weaponry. All warships are completely modular and all of their stats depend on their composition. Destroying a generator will cut off power from certain modules and losing the bridge will send you straight into the desert dunes.The second part relies on strategic decision-making, careful resource management and the ability to assess threats and pick battles. You will be staring at the map, using your intelligence equipment to amass all the info you can about enemy fleets, their locations, and compositions while also manipulating the enemy’s knowledge of you. With your fleet initially being composed of only a few standard ships, you’ll need to get any advantage possible while maintaining stealth before crushing the enemy with a decisive blow.Highfleet’s atmosphere is rather unique, combining the aesthetics of the Middle East & central Asia, imperial Russia, and, uh, Arrakis?.. The music is glorious and the battle visuals are… highly explosive.On the downside, this game can get very frustrating very quickly. You WILL need to go out of your way to search up how various mechanics really work because the game won’t tell you and the manual only explains the bare minimum. If you don’t, you will keep making the same mistakes over and over not even knowing that you’re making mistakes while the campaign mercilessly beats you with a stick. The UI is quite messy; I’m not sure if it’s meant to add to the atmosphere but it does make your life a little harder.Highfleet is a fantastic game. It’s extremely unique and very compelling. I would not say this game is for everyone but if you like what’s written here and in other reviews, it might be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of features, but none of them really mesh together to make a cohesive and satisfying experience.You will do the same thing, over and over again, until the game is over. You have an entire fleet, and only field one vessel at a time. If that ship takes too much damage, retreat and get a new one from your lineup. It's very odd to have many ships, and have the enemy use many ships at the same time, but you only use one.Ship design ends up boiling down to just put as much firepower with as much armor as you possibly can. There's not much need for creativity.Overall, the game advertises much but all it delivers is just short of being good, and just borderline on decent.Not for $30. At all.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Just beat the game for the first time, my recommendation only grows. If you're worried about how it'll look on your display, I'd say get it anyway and if you can't stand it refund it before 2 hours. _childDocuments_.review: I'll first say that this game is very good for reasons you already know. For me, the most disappointing part is the Devs.I even bought this game for 3 friends, so what i say is not me just hatin'. Instead of lifting this game up after its success, the devs (for some reason) just kept deciding to mix up the battle mechanics invalidating many ships and fleets that took players hours to make. From what i've seen, the devs had a huge problem with players making heavy cruisers and battleships (not even a very viable strat) so they blanket changed the system. not only does that break many player ships it also broke some of the AI ships that were made without the changes in mind. This mindset really misses the bigger picture since they could have added more content to the overworld map to increase the replay value. They also could have added more weapons to the sandbox, fix the weapons that are garbage and no one uses, or make the A.I. more tactical. This game is close to being a 10/10 for me but once you understand the simple AI logic the game becomes a cake walk even on the hardest difficulty, and once you have beaten the game a couple of times you've seen everything the game has to offer. I used to do challenge runs where i would try to beat the game with a ♥♥♥♥ off big ship (very difficult) now i have to redesign ships that took hours to make and i dont find it worth it anymore. I enjoyed the game a lot so ill give it a thumbs up, but man there is some missed potential that would make this game G O A T.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Throw in lots of money and enemies, money generation, unlimited ships to buy and construct, automate repair and refueling. no radio messages pls. Someone up for a mod?I have mixed feelings about this game.The visual style is stunning and beautiful. I love how the narrative feels.The game fails to communicate underlying mechanics or rules and provide suitable tools for solving problems which is the main reason for the apparent difficulty. The machinery soundscape stresses me.I love starting a new game and think about fleet composition. Spent a lot of time learning to build ships. Finished one, just one campaign to the end on hard. At first overwhelmingly difficult, once you understand the underlying mechanics, I find it not very difficult, but tedious and grindy. Admittedly, I created my own ship designs, which makes things a lot easier. While I think the fighting vehicles are mature and there is nothing really to optimize other than adapting to playstyle/role, i.e. changing guns, the Sevastopol flagship is fuel guzzeling monstrosity. In a game, where money is scarce and fuel expensive, that certainly is a bad design. This is the biggest challange, dragging this monster 20.000 miles north. The smartest thing you can do is completely stripping the ship for parts ending up with a tiny ship basicly recovering 175.000$. Time is not really a thing in this game on a strategic level. For comparisom, you could build a starting flagship that  acts as aircraft and missile carrier with twice the speed that consumes half of the fuel and cost half of the Sevastopol.So basicly, the Sevastopol is you biggest enemy, not the enemy.The biggest bummer for me is that needed to go through a lot of frustration and research to lern that this game is not very difficult, but slow and repetitive. But not the good kind repetition. I fully understand people who dont want sink so much time into research and are frustrated by the apparent difficulty,I dont mind so much that I am really bad at the bullet-hell fighting minigame, where it feels like fireing guns and flying the ship are jobs for two people at least. The constant beeping and machinery noise stress me al lot. Admittedly, its part of the immersion. But it sucks.Here are my userstories:- I want a way to confirm/silence alarms; - I want to get rid of all the message icons that clutter the screen and create navigation problems (crafts prefer message position over cities)- I want to fold away the left part of the UI-overlay to see the map, dammit.- Parts (from hull deconstruction) and shipparts (the stuff you buy from shipyard) both accumulate on detachment level, which not necessarily what you want. I end up doing back and fouths sorting this mess out. Also, there is no way of splitting parts, so you end up with 999 parts at your flagship and non where you need them. This makes only sense if the most boringest doomstack strategy is used. That is not how I want to play the game.- The shipyard UI is clunky. Add an repair all button next to each ship. - Show the ship veteran level in shipyard and fighting screens.Since a neutral stance cannot be taken, I recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS VERY HARDSeriously, the reviews saying that the mechanics are confusing or that the game is dull are playing the game in 2 ways:Single fleet to single locations or have Radar onThis game is very realistic in terms of strategy and planning, having radar on is suicide in the early stages where strike fleets will detect you and not using reconnaissance ships to reduce fuel usage will slow down progress.Shipbuilding is very fun and not limited in any way, build a sword plane if you want or a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WALL.Story and world-building is rich, feels like I'm in Arabian setting but it's clearly with soviet style artwork and machinery and the general depth of immersion you get is very high.My issue with the game is simply that it's an A to B game... _childDocuments_.review: FTL but 10x better, and expanded in all aspects. Fun combat, deep strategy, ship building. A work of love.On the map, I've plotted the target - a civilian convoy's route, based off a 5hr-old radio intercept. Sent a strong strike group, including a tanker, at max range. The strike stumbled into another civ convoy enroute. I could not divert - no range margin vs primary target. As the original strike package continued its mission, I launched an additional fast interceptor. And redirected my main cruiser to attempt to get radar coverage over the intercept area. (think Silent Hunter + Harpoon-lite)While the interceptor screamed towards the new target, the civilian convoy immediately altered course, reported my position to enemy fleet HQ and fell out of my sensor range. With no radar or IRST on the interceptor, I plotted a visual search pattern based off the last known enemy position and speed. Covering part of the search area by the radar of the (slowly) approaching cruiser.The interceptor found its mark. At 700 km/h vs the convoy's 150 km/h - little chance of escape. Combat begins - 2 light combat vessels, a lightly armed transporter vs my single interceptor. Great odds for an unarmored fighter if the crew is willing to spend the whole battle g-locked, and does not mind that the first hit can be fatal.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I like a game that doesn't hold your hand, but due to the interface not giving you a clear indication of anything, you really do need an intro to tell you what you need to know. Is a process automatic? No? Is that the button? No? It'd be one thing if this was a cookie cutter game that had the same core mechanics as a dozen other FPS or RTS games, or if there was a clearly defined interface, but this is fairly unique and they leaned way too hard into form over function. The mechanics and button placement need at least a hint of what and where they are for you to know that they exist. I won't refund in case I might get back into it at some point, but despite the awesome art style, nice combat, and interesting beginnings of a plot, I haven't been able to progress far enough to get hooked before I lose interest. Scroll up... Scroll down... Seriously, where is the button?
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: I have played 8 hours in this game when writing this, and it feels like I still have lot to learn.It is a unique game, with a feeling of being hunted. It is hard as well, I guess until you learn how to sneak through the strike-ships, and learn how the weapons work. I.e. the long-range missiles I am still unsure of how they work, as there is no detailed description of them, one type did work as I intended and killed two targets on site, another type just flew by my targets, the third one was extremely fast and just disappeared on the map, not engaging at all. So it would be nice to have detailed references on different types of weapons, they where expensive when I bought them.Anyway, I would recommend this game as it is so unique, and I really like the radar and the other enemy-detection-systems. If you like U-Boats, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game - there's nothing else out there with this aesthetic, style & immersiveness. It's definitely clunky at times, hard to figure out & hard to survive. The systems can be pretty opaque so that it's hard to deduce cause & effect from what you're doing and how the enemies react.But it's a labor of love, the combat is absolutely incredible, and for those that like to sink their teeth into a complicated, immersive game/sim, this is absolute must, especially if it gets some post-release support, which I hope it does :)
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome combat system plagued by awful campaign mechanics. You build a "fleet", AKA a line of fodder ships that 1v3's AIs that has infinite missiles, near-perfect aim, and has no fog-of-war. If you survive that, good luck dealing with the expensive repairs and expensive fuel. After that, pray that you survive the next enemy cruiser strike group already on its way.Hard pass. I regret getting this.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very good if you're willing to read all the forums in the world about how to play it. Otherwise it's pretty raw. How do rockets work on the global map? How to create a link from generator to a rocket launcher? How do you descypher intercepted messages? How to check your ships before a battle? Why aren't your ships, equiped with rocket launchers, shooting rockets? The game's mechanics are vast and complicated. The game's explanations for those mechanics are basic at best and non existent at worst. But the punishment for any mistake is allways brutal. Wich does feel very unfair: you're punished for the gemedesigner's inability to explain how the game works.And that's a real shame. The game looks gorgeous! The textures, the particles, the shaders, the overall style - it's very good. It sounds great - both music and effects are awesome. It has a lot of minigames, that looks invredibly organic. The plot is intriguing! The characters are intresting! For now, putting the game on hold untill the creator will put more effort in ingame tutorials - even some text would be enough. Or untill there's an "easy" mode that doesn't require to read heaps of tutorials before playing.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another game where everyone seems to confuse "difficult and obtuse" with challenging and engaging.Every aspect of this game feels like it is designed to be as asinine as possible. Why, exactly, is it that the fleet admiral is the one needing to pinpoint signals intelligence and coordinate air and missile strikes? Why can nobody ever understand when making these types of games that it isn't the highest commander's goal in life to do everyone else's job!?The world genuinely seems cool and I'd love to explore it but the campaign is more like a series of barely functional minigames strung together than a coherent game, so yeah I am freely announcing I barely touched it.Most of the time I had in game came from the shipworks, where you used to make a ship and test it out in what was basically a wave combat horde mode. It was actually neat to see what worked and what didn't in pure ship to ship aerial combat...At least until an update that caused ships to consume fuel during battles and not just on the overworld map. This update basically rendered everybody's curbstomping, no nonsense having superships into worthless paperweights that literally couldn't fight for more than a minute because then they'd run out of fuel. Great job game, my favorite mode, if only because it was actually playable, now assassinated.Make no mistake, I am not belittling the effort that went into this. I'm not crushing the passion and spirit of the makers. Yet, the end result is a mess that seems engineered from the ground up to frustrate the player at every turn. I was suckered in by all of those blue thumb reviews and we need more people willing to go against the mob who are saying "this is a good game, I don't understand it, but it's great" or "me like ships, ships go phwaa, guns go drrrrt."
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Top notch development and gameplay, Highfleet mixes gameplay styles from several different genres to create something that might look simple, is in fact complex enough to challenge most brains. The simplest comparison would be: Asteroids + Missile Command + FTL + Battleship + Chess = Highfleet (though that doesn't include the PTSD you get from the "glitch low/high" nor the ship customization which also has it's own test mode).Currently on about 265 hours and have completed the main campaign at least twice on each difficulty. Looking forwards to future developments/Expansions/DLC as just like Ssethtzeentach I want more!
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: This is the hybrid operational level fleet simulator, Sci-fi, Diesel-punk, Central Asia flavoured, RPG, 2D airship combat game I've been daydreaming about for years made real.Does it have some bugs, UI quirks, many other quirks and a learning curve?  Yes. Was this studio's previous game, Hammerfight, an absolute mess in bug and design terms? Yes. Did I play 800 hours of it over 10 years? Yes, because that game provided an utterly unique gaming experience you can't find anywhere else - I'm still waiting for the next skill and physics based helicopter melee combat game. This game appears to be following in the finest traditions of Konstantin Koshutin Studios.Every frame of this product from manual to title screen drips with atmosphere and style. It is already something I'm edging towards calling a masterpiece. If any of this sounds remotely interesting to you, you owe it to yourself to at least try it, especially at this price point.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: The developer released a major update, without any release notes! It broke many pre-existing ship designs.The game has a lot of potential but is mostly frustrating and obtuse. The story elements and realism are great, but the interface for ship design is terrible and so are all the pre-built ships so trying to get started isn't very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: This game for me is a perfect mix of gritty action and deep strategical decision making.There are many concepts learned in other simulation type games which I found translated perfectly here, such as radar discipline and electronic warfare. I found it a real pleasure to be able to reapply those skills here.You play the game very much as the underdog from the start and have to choose your path, tactics and battles carefully, with a constant pressure to not sit still too long, you must keep moving. I think the balance here is perfect, you have enough time and space to consider your next moves, but not so much that you can sit back an chill out in one spot on the map.Don't be put off by the fact that this is essentially 2D and to be honest I am not one to worry too much about graphics anyway, but I will say that the graphics are outstanding and go a long way to bringing forth the atmosphere of the game. I am stunned that a 2D game can look and feel this good.There is so much more to this game than meets the eye and I don't think a Steam review can cover it all. I suggest you check out the manual on the store page and watch a few videos if you have not done so already.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game and experience. While the visual style is well done and looks great, my favorite part of the game is the sound design. Everything sounds so satisfying, including the outside of combat noises. All the little clicks and buzzes immerses you into the cockpit. If you like ship fleet simulators combined with FTL all set in Dune, then maybe grab your vodka and jump in.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of DUNE the movie. I have been playing this game before the movie came out but there are so many similarities it feels so true to it. With out the worms and green planets but that is besides the point.Anyway now about the review. Honestly, it takes time to learn all the workings of this game. There are many buttons to interact with on the display. So the learning curve is a medium slope but once you get it you can traverse it rather easily. It can span from radio chatter and encryption to flight maps and strategy. You can make marks on the screen to plan a route or intercept enemies. I can't do math so I just run until a strike group obliterates my fleet. Like missile carries and aircraft carries wear me down and then 3 strike groups just bury me into the sand and call it a day. Which happens a lot. I haven't beaten this game yet but many others have. Do not let that discourage you.The ships feel like they have weight depending on how big or small you make them. Sadly there is not Steam Workshop for this, which would have made this game and lifespan of it infinitely better. If you make the wrong move you will crash. If you lose a few engines well you are screwed. You lost your landing gear last battle, well just don't land on your fuel tanks when you are touching the landing pad. Just weave and dodge. Or Weave and bob. Whatever you say.The visuals and sound are fantastic! It's gritty, it's blasty. and it's sandy! If your ship goes close to the ground you will blow up dust and create some fires. (dont hit the ground though, metal doesn't like the ground coming too fast, it will go crunch and then you lose your ship).When you shoot it creates a bang, even small caliber rounds can pack a punch. Parts of ships fly off if damaged, catch fire if hit, and explode if penetrated. The EXPLOSIONS go BOOOM. Heeheehe that ship and its crew are burning and falling to the ground to their painful deaths. Uh (cough cough) I meant shoot the escape pods (Which you can)! None shall survive! Wait (clears throat) hmmm Death to the invaders who stole our homeland..... Uhhhhhh I'll just stop now....The story is creative but somewhat complex. Knowing the different factions and who likes who and who hates who scrambles my brain. But hey that guy has a cool uniform :D OOOOO look at her dress how fancy. And do not forget to be cordial. You may get smacked. When you do negotiations with NPCs you either have the choice to insult your fatherland which your crew will hate you, or you get the choice to insult the one you are speaking to. Which can cost you a ship that was being offered or less status with ones that can help you. So good luck in the SEA OF SANDs

_childDocuments_.review: The concept of this game is great, and the mix of strategic and tactical play is well thought-out.  Unfortunately for me, I'm simply not good enough to enjoy it, so I'm also pretty bummed about the whole experience.  I know 'dark souls'-like difficulty is all the rage these days, but the tutorials are lacking, and the difficulty spike means that I'm always dead before I get better.A begrudged thumbs up.Review update: After reading community guides on how to optimize your ships' armour, and how to aim for vital points on heavy cruisers, I'm now surviving long enough to enjoy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a strange game in many ways. The people who made Hammerfight made this game, and it has some of the same hallmarks. Undoubtedly rough around the edges and having a few persistent bugs and crashes, but if you can get past that, it's really fun.This game's strength is its combat. It has a lot of other stuff going on that you do between fights, some of which is hit or miss, but the core combat game is very fun. The gimmick of WWII radio and radar technology isn't really as deep as it seems on the surface, but it is functional.This game is undoubtedly beautiful, and you could be forgiven for forgetting that this is all spritework. The sound is fantastic as well. The campaign is marketed as a roguelite but this is not the case. There is no tree to build between runs or any improvements that can be made: you have the same power in your first game as you do in your last. This isn't a problem really, you should just know that this is the case.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastically detailed game, flipping between something akin to an old school sub sim, plotting you strategy and intercepting communications whilst marking out contacts on a map, choosing to attack transport convoys or avoid strike groups the story pushes you along but you have an incredible amount of player agency, the AI doesn't cheat, it doesn't know where you are unless you do something stupid. The combat is fast paced and has significant depth brought about by fleet composition and ship designs.It is however a hard game, you will fail a lot, you will have no money and morale will be low, then you'll pull off the fight of your life.Oh and it looks awesome in motion.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a new favorite for me - I will be playing this game for a long, long time. Visually, it's one of the most pleasing Dieselpunk titles I've seen in the genre. The rougelike elements of this game add to the mystique and  to the fun, but they do not make this game feel like FTL at all. There are many more parallels to Dune. Gameplay is split between the Strategy Map, the Combat instances, and the Docks (when landed). The only downside is the lack of wider documentation - strategy and shipbuilding concepts outside of the manual are scarce. To get the most out of the game requires proper use of the Shipbuilder. Also, it's worth noting that you can split your fleet as many times as you like, granted you have enough fuel. Inventory management is critical and you will lose your first few fleets as much due to wastefulness as to incaution.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made for a very specific crowd, to deliver on a very specific genre not generally seen elsewhere. And holy hell MicroPose is really coming in hard with their releases.I'm not saying people generally can't enjoy this game, but the best way I can describe it is that you have to have liked FTL, Luftrausers, Ace Combat 7, Airships Conquer the Skies, Papers Please, and Homeworld, not in this order and not necessarily all of them, let alone played them. But I sorely believe FTL is a hard requirement, with Homeworld a close second if only because None of these really have anything in common, but follow me here. You have FTL with it's Rouge-Like gameplay with all the hard decision making and stress that comes with it. Luftrausers plays hard and fast, but is kept incredibly simple with only room for you to get better at the game. Ace Combat 7, is very pretty but loves its incesssant radio chatter and the romantic idea of being an ace pilot in the not so far future. Airships is just dumb love for making your steampunk airship and making it fight other steampunk stuff. Papers Please has the over designed menu you spend almost all of the game at. Homeworld has its audio, its universe, and that oh so satisfying feeling of a space opera because of everything you can hear, IN SPACE. Nevermind that's not how it works, it just does.High Fleet just mashes everything above into one, neat but obtuse package, albeit with a few shortcomings that may break or make your experience depending on your personal standards. The game at large is a Rouge-Like, highly tactical, management action arcade-sim that just stinks of the late 90's. It's a game that takes the best elements without making it too complicated but still tries to find something people will absolutely sink time into. But oh lord the audio deign and pixel animations are GORGEOUS-------------------That rant aside here's the laydownThe game is very arcade at its core; to keep things simple but complex enough that the user will appreciate. This isn't a simulation, but it isn't arcade enough where you can just dive right in.Right off the bat you're met with the admittedly very dense, but very detailed commanders view. The entirety of fleet operations, which includes early warning radar, navigation tools, intercepting communications, and maybe committing warcrimes if you happen to come by nukes. You will spend a good third of your time here, as management of your fleet is key, whether it be moving from location to the next or intercepting a convoy after you determined the information from an encrypted message is good.Soon after you're met with your first sortie, which involves flying your ship and fighting another ship, possibly multiple. This is where some people may find it off putting. This part is decidedly hard, maybe artificially so, and much more arcade. Aiming is basically looking at a very small radial around the ship and determining where the guns are pointing. Missiles are easy to lock-on but are incredibly few, save for a missile boat. Your ship characteristics determine if you're truly dogfighting or just trying to position properly as you brute force your way against the opposition.You will not be doing fleet on fleet engagements, at least not fully. I don't know if it's a hard limitation set by the dev's, whether in scope of the project or just the nature of balancing a game around actual fleet engagements. Nonetheless, I had fun, because at least the game is balanced properly around one ship at a time. There are tells for everything that happens, when a ship is about to line up and fire its guns or when a missile is coming your way. If your ship is too damaged or expended all of its munitions, it can retreat and the next ship in line will fly in.The next part is visiting cities. This is actually a smaller part of the game, where you spend time rearming and refueling. Important dialogue and events also happen here. You can do a minigame to land the ship at the Docks to speed up repairs, but it's not required. But there's also the Docks.You may or may not spend an obscene amount of time here. Most will be content with repairs and refits, others might just do a full teardown and rebuild. At that point the game does provide a shipbuilding separate from the campaign. It's both dense and seemingly limited, while obtuse at the same time. The editor is more than enough to get a ship built, but it's missing a lot of quality of life features most other ship building games would have. At the same time building is super simple, as there are only a hard rules to follow when actually putting things together. There's no serious pathing limitations, it mostly comes down to whether or not your ship can be considered airworthy by satisfying corresponding requirements like crew population and if enough generators exist. Engine symmetry is important but the game otherwise doesn't really care the radar is getting melted by the engine exhaust. The editor goes so far as to procedurally generate shapes so it doesn't just look like you slapped two trusses onto each other, because you did.Audio design is on point. Everywhere to interfaces to ambiance to the very ships themselves, it exudes its presence. It might be subtle or it might be deafening as the lightning storm that you have to fight in. Evading a missile is as awful as the experience of getting hit by one.---------------------------With all those highlights, I cannot stress enough the game is under one thick layer of frustration in that the game just assumes you . You won't know how long is too long spent at a city. You're not exactly sure if the ship has countermeasures, and you definitely don't know how much ammo is left unless you check a very specific register detailing the fleet's supplies. You generally don't know your men is losing morale, despite winning the battle. Maybe it has to do with their magical ability to know that you may have restarted the battle four times. You won't know the difference between 2 very similar looking radar masts. You aren't even sure if the optical sensors help you aim, because you've been manually aiming your guns in the worst way possible the whole time. Did you know that if you skip the prologue you keep all the money that gets wasted on the tutorial, the much needed funds for your fleet? You just will not know, unless you try.By the way, , for you adults who remember when the manual that came with the game told you how to play darn game! I appreciate the commitment to writing a full, and well detailed manual, but at least slap that link on the main menu for the player to see. The admiral is actually super helpful in guiding you, but he can only do so much.Oh and saving only happens at cities, and it's not even obvious. Not a deal breaker for me but for a game that happens at your pace, it's incredibly frustrating for other players that would prefer to save when they please. And I don't just mean save scummingShip fights, despite the core mechanic, can be incredibly and artificially hard. Especially in storms there's so much to look at but it's so tempting to say that the game just tosses so much visual garbage at you. So, all in all, this is an extraordinarily unique game, from an older time brought forward to a modern age, for both its efforts and what it strives to be. But holy hell not everything from the 90's is the gold standard.As a side note, for the technical aspect, I think it's fine the game literally renders at only 1080P. But a borderless option, and generally more friendly windowed options would be good too. I wouldn't mind it if the game properly upscaled to 4K, stretching and all. I will update this as I get more hours in

_childDocuments_.review: This is more than a rogue like, it's riddled with poor choices.No cursor during flight makes it insanely difficult to aim your shots, and I don't care for it one bit. Doubly so for the fact that you can barely see the aiming arrow in the first place. This is a great story game, but it's poor in game play. The "survival" mechanics are easy enough, though they haven't even explained them at all. (How to switch ammo types, etc.) The radio "tutorial" is worthless as it ushers you out of it before you've got the proper tuning. The game is rife with a total lack of explanation that clearly marks it as "no fun for newbies."If you're new to this studio's games, as this must be a trend, do NOT purchase.Graphically, musically, narrative-wise, the game isn't bad. Game play, lack of modding support, and lack of difficulty control in the game settings and difficulty even at the start of a game marks this as poor in thought, lacking in UI design, and generally unenjoyable especially to people with poor eyesight like me.4/10, should have thought about the game play far more before they even touched anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly well made and fun game. It is hard, beware, but very satisfying. It has two layers of gameplay. Strategic and the battles itself.The strategic layer is moving fleets around, managing your fuel and scouting the enemy, mostly by using signals inteligence and intercepting them whenever you decide you have the most advantage. You can also refit and adapt your ships to fit roles, the shipyard is like another game itself, and opens up a million of iterations that suit your needs best.The battles itself are wonderful, they require skill, because you have to aim at the same time you blast around on a x00 tons ship. This is very well modeled, you can somehow feel the ship's weight while maneuvering around, and the amount of engines you put on it compared to it's weight determines how agile your ship is. The big guns are amazing, hits go boom and explosions are the best I have seen in a while, landing shots feels very satisfying.And all this made by 3 dudes over 5 years. For 25 bucks it is very worth it's money, I would say it is even cheap considering the amount of garbage floating around for 50+DLC.Also, THAT song, you will know which one if you play it.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: So much about this game is amazing but you REALLY have to dig through bugs and quality of life issues to get to it. A lot of features of the game are buggy and broken and can easily ruin your game or at least set you back a lot through no fault of your own when they do something glitchy and weird. That wouldn't be as much of a problem if the game allowed manual saving so you could revert when something bad happens, but it's strictly autosave-only. That means when you encounter weird bugs your best bet is just alt-f4 and hope it hasn't autosaved since that happened. The game is also majorly lacking in settings and options as many other reviews have pointed out, including always-on mouse acceleration and a fixed resolution.This isn't really a negative review because this is a bad game, it's more just a recommendation that you don't buy this game AS IT IS NOW. If you're willing to fight through the bugs and quality of life issues you can definitely still have a lot of fun with the game, but I think a lot of players would find it more frustrating than enjoyable. Hopefully there will be some post-launch support to iron out the issues because the core tactical combat gameplay is incredibly fun and stylish, the campaign map mechanics are really deep and engaging, and the visuals are gorgeous. I look forward to changing this review to a wholehearted recommendation if and when that happens.

_childDocuments_.review: Needs a neutral ratingShort: Imagine you're playing asteroids as an aircraft carrier but the rocks shoot back and they are also the entire united states military. Long: First thing; I'm honestly not sure if I like this game. It is very interesting and thus I give it a positive review, so be warned. Also this game is difficult and it seems to want you to die trying to learn things. There is a very FTL-inspired/adjacent game-play loop. Still similar to FTL, it feels like there are a few different play-styles but I have not completed the game so maybe some of the things I have tried are really sub-optimal. The immersive nature of the game is well done. There are a lot of things you do radar sweeping, infrared scanning, radio intercepts ect. that can be all done by turning nobs and flipping switches. I am sure this is not for everyone but to me it indicates a well thought-out vision for the game. The execution does miss a bit at times. For instance when it is raining during combat it can be hard to see your ship. There's water droplets all over the screen!  Speaking of the combat I think that is the thing that misses the most for me. It seems like the game does a great job explaining and showing how the world is a vast nothingness and you feel the weight of these massive airships whenever you take off and land BUT suddenly you are placed in a box. In that box is a very small scaled down model of your ship. A ship which could in reality be huge. You can't leave the box during combat besides to retreat. The bare minimum it feels like the combat should have a way to zoom in and out. If I could redesign the combat system some I would prefer a turn-based system or maybe something inspired by battlefleet gothic or battlestar galactica deadlock   so you could control multiple ships. Anyway I am not sure I like the game but for how unique it is maybe it's something you will.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR at the bottom:Alright, so, I've never left a review of a game before, and this is coming from someone with 3k+ hours in War Thunder (on Steam alone) and like 300+ hours on Rimworld.Starting with the negatives:The game will crash when you try certain configurations in the ship builder, like putting 4 large fuel tanks on all sides connected to the bridge (the game seems to be trying to make a composite version, like it does when you combine 2 like pieces), and can't so it crashes. There've also been numerous other crashes like when trying to send a certain amount of planes to ♥♥♥♥ up an enemy's day, or sometimes trying to load up a town.All in all, the crashes are only really frequent if you're trying to recreate them, which I was able to several times. Other negatives include a lack of certain UI elements. Like flares. I know the button to use them, but every time I've pressed it with a flare module, it shows they're empty. Nothing I've tried has fixed it. The Jammer module doesn't have a name to it, and I've never seen it in a store, but you can make ships with it, and encounter ships with it. Certain other things as well, like there being no 300mm gun, but there being incendiary ammo for it? Weird, or the R-6 Nadir missile - some ships have it, but you will never find it in a store, at least on normal mode....When navigating the menus in town like the shipping dock, it's annoying that you have to use the mouse 100% of the time. Buying and selling things en mass is also a bit strange. You can buy bulk items with ctrl + right click, but can't sell multiple items at once. Buying or selling special ammo is also weird, as you have to subtract the total amount to gain money, rather than a simple + or - value to input.As for the positives:This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ *amazing*. I was a little hyped for this game when I saw someone cover it a bit, as it had a lot of unique mechanics, but the thing that got me the most was the ship combat. It's a 2d aerial combat system where you basically need to destroy the enemy ships in a 1v1, 2, or 3. it's deceptively easy ... at first. After that? You'll find that it's increasingly difficult to keep your ship from getting ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up in a 3v1 if there's an enemy frigate or even cruisers. The more armor and weight your ship has? The slower it moves unless you put even more engines on it, which you then have to compensate for in other ways.Not to mention the combat is immensely immersive and satisfying. All the sounds make you feel like you're right there in the action, and you'll find yourself just wanting to move to the next town, and the next town, and the next, ad nauseum until you reach Khiva.It took me 5 tries before I could even beat the campaign. The mechanic for dying and losing the campaign is what's the most interesting. You start with 100k to buy ships for your assault on Khiva, the main city you gotta get to, and every time you lose the campaign, you get extra points (money) to use to buy ships the next time, so after losing so much or even winning the game, you'll be able to field an increasingly larger fleet.The UI has like ... 27 different things going on, from possible radio signals you have to intercept to launching a quad-salvo of (nuclear) radar guided missiles on an enemy strike group to hurt them enough to be able to fight them in a ship battle, to sending your own fleet of fighters to bomb or rocket an enemy aircraft carrier group or missile carrier group, to sending out your own strike groups.There's a lot going on with the game's UI when you're not in town or in a ship battle, but it's cluttered in the best way possible. It really feels like there's a lot going on. My biggest gripes really are that there's not enough tooltips, and no place in-game to really look to find out everything. I found almost everything out by experimentation, but that was fun in itself.As for the ship builder: it's actually really satisfying. You can make colossal structures and test them out, and can even buy them for your fleets in-game, though it doesn't seem like you can find them in towns to buy, which is unfortunate, so make sure to load them up in the initial selection!All in all, even with the slight annoyances some of the design choices make, and the crashes, you're set back in almost no progress when that happens, but if you lose the game? GG time to restart and try again.This game is a solid 10/10 for me. It's honestly such a unique game that I don't think anything else scratches the itch quite like this one. It actually gave me the chills several times over as I found out something new and progressed. It's one of those games that truly makes you feel like a kid again - no woes or worries - at least until you start getting raped by a strike group. Would recommend any day. Waiting for expansions or other content to come out already.TL;DR - 9/10 game, makes you feel like a kid again. Amazing combat, and very immersive and busy UI. Ship building is hella fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I freaking love this game! At it's core is a very atmospheric two d-shooter/shump and fleet management simulator. Graphics, sounds, visual effects, and environment come together very well to make this a real masterpiece. Pretty challenging and very, very fun. It is a bit rough around the edges in terms of code and documentation, and some of the undocumented features can drive you to madness. Let me get you started off on the right foot:You can put down multiple copies of the same item in ship builder by holding shift.Do not try to use single strut landing gear, L shape or claws will absorb shock alot better. When you give a gift to someone depending on the type it has an associated trait, pretty obvious once you know but you can really piss people off finding this out. You can split your fleet by selecting a few ships from the drop down and clicking a destination. Big guns are not always best guns. Make sure you have some chain fire guns in your fleet for plane and cruise missile interceptionAdding ships with external fuel tanks can extend a groups range up to a point. Internal tanks cannot be shared. Auto intercept points the direction that a message comes from and you'll usually be able to tell what type of message it is. from the part you can read.Lastly Always keep your mask on while in flight you never know when an explosive decompression will occur!If your on the fence get it it's a blast! (no nuclear puns intended).
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: The game gives kinda mixed feelings. At first, you are in awe at all the systems and possibilities. You try to use whatever options are given by the developer to be that stealthy pirate fleet that you are supposed to. And you succeed. Until you fail and you don't know why. You learn and repeat, cool yeah?But then you discover a ship editor and figure out that with a couple of custom ships you don't need to be THAT stealthy. You can build economic ships that can fight strike groups from the very first nodes on the map. And you start to play more aggressively. And the game just falls apart. It loses a ton of charm because instead of running you just fight head on. Evading foes? Not necessary. You can kinda just run around not knowing where anyone is and not intercepting any messages. You are discovered? Just send your 2 fleet killer ships to end the enemy fleet. Special munitions, planes, strategic missiles, radar jammer, splitting the fleet and other tactics - all this can be ignored and never used. Which is sad because I feel they deserve to be used. I just never found the reason to do so.In the end, it becomes a fly-fight-refuel-repair grind. I hope there's a third stage of discovery which is unlocked by adopting a different strategy and which makes the game fun again.

_childDocuments_.review: According to all known laws of aviation, there is no way that a steel brick should be able to fly. And a brick is a brick, not many people know this, its thrusters are too small to get its fat little body off the ground. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most soulful and unique games I have ever played. If the screenshots appeal to you, they catch the vibe really well. Game has 2 primary modes, strategic planning and management of the fleet and go time dogfighting. In planning, the game has one of the most in depth information warfare systems I have ever seen, with highly rewarding planning, prediction, and execution on said information. Dogfights are the final blow bayonet charge of the game, either high speed greyout manuvers against impossible odds or beautiful broadside exchanges under the roar of phalanx guns

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I've had a great time with Highfleet - there was some serious love that went into this title. You kind of know it when you see it, right? The slavic-steam-punk feel just appeals to me - and though I still need more play time, I'm greatly looking forward to putting more time into the game map.Pros:- Absolutely Dripping with Style- Complex Fleet Management- Very Appealing Visuals (to me at least)- Interesting (if not a-typical) Revolt v Establishment Story line through Character Diplomacy and choice of actionCons:- Sometimes a little too busy- Unsure how effective the tutorial is at explaining ALL of the mechanics- Lack of out of the box mod support (I could only imagine what the Community could add)I need to know more about this Konstantin Koshutin Dev team, this feels like a love letter to carrier command in a whole different way - but I'm very eager to see more. And if Microprose continues to publish titles with this much soul during its return from the dead - then I can't wait to see them publish a whole catalog of titles.Great work! Looking forward to more!

_childDocuments_.review: Remember the moon lander game you may have played as a kid on some old console, flash website, or perhaps even coded in an Intro To Programming course?
