_childDocuments_.review: A strong recommend; although I think this is much more a management/strategy/sim game than a 2d action game.Have not seen a cohesion of vision in design like this in any game I can think of. The universe it's set in is extremely compelling; and the game's disinterest in explaining more than you need to know only makes you want more games to come out of the setting. The UI is completely dedicated to maintaining the impression that you are a in charge of this flotilla of warships. Some may find it off-putting but I appreciate the dedication to their vision.The game is also satisfyingly difficult. The story has you stranded in enemy territory and it feels like it. Even when you do everything right, there is never any 'snowballing' tipping point where engagements become trivial. My criticism for the game has to do with how little it prepares you for what you face. You learn the broad strokes in addition to how to operate things, but many minor but important details are left out of the in-game tutorial. As an example, the game teaches you about missiles, but doesn't explain that where you click is where their tracking systems will activate. There's also a spike in difficulty at the end of a campaign that makes sense in the context of the game, but may catch you off guard on your first run.As a caveat, the manual has detail about the mechanics to satisfy my complaints, but in the age of digital distribution I doubt many users will even realize that there is a manual that came with their purchase.Lastly - admittedly a nitpick - but the map tools are ineffectual in the broader campaign. I find myself eyeballing trajectories and estimating positions as opposed to using the tools, which would require manual calculation. Trigonometry isn't my idea of fun, although you might feel differently.

_childDocuments_.review: At launch, really would have a hard time recommending this game.What make it almost unplayable for me is the 1 vs. an enemy fleet combat system. How it currently works is that you bring your fleet to a fight vs an enemy fleet, but you are only able to fight one of your ships, vs an enemy fleet at a time. What ends up happening, is that 3 enemy ships shoot at you, then you can either loose your ship and then another 1 of your ships will respawn and then fight 3 ships. Either that, or you have to move your 1 ship to a small "retreat" window, then another one of your ships will respawn. I don't understand why this was decided upon, but that fact kills the game for me. The game had / had AMAZING potential, but at present, that just sucks the life out of enjoying the game for me. I brought the game, and glad to see MicroProse back... but that kills it for me. sorry, thumbs down review.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat looks nice, but everything else is just plain infuriating.- The UI fights you every step of the way. Slow/clunky transitions between screens where you have to click&drag or use WSAD, have to drag ship part lists on the refit screen, can't load designs in campaign, campaign map wobbles around, base settings have various effects (dithering, glitching, whatever) that make it annoying to just look at the screen- Basically no information/tooltips about base mechanics in game- Combat crosshair doesn't behave like you'd expect from any number of games you've played before. Mouse movement rotates it, no way to make it track mouse position- Campaign robs your time with a silly, pointless radio minigame- No fleet fights, it's always 1 ship from the player against many AIs. Deploying anything slow is a waste of materials, evasion saves on repairs- Load button simply doesn't work, it gives you your total score (WTF?)- "normal saves" are restricted to easy mode, otherwise you have forced autosaves at checkpoints. Retrying battles resurrects your ships but still drops morale (WTF?)- Lots of various other annoyancesThe thing that finally broke me is the soundtrack. It has a malfunctioning hurdy-gurdy on loop. I can only assume it was put into the game on a dare. It's hard to believe just how bad it is. It actually, physically hurts to listen to it.Look up Turjan Aylahn - Tanc a Lelek if you are feeling brave.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is surprisingly deep and varied. Not only is it a ship combat game, but the overall game is composed of several interconnected 'mini-games' that compose the whole:-Ship repair and customisation can be done at the docks in cities, optionally there's a whole 'build your own ship' mode.-To get in to the repair docks in the cities there's a ship landing mini-game which gives optional bonuses to your work there-There's an interesting story set against a procedurally generated map, so no two play-through runs will be the same-You can intercept radio communications from the enemy. Even if you can't decode them it lets you know the direction of an enemy formation. The encryption can be broken by either gathering code fragments from downed ships or by manually solving it in the game using 'cribbing' or other attacks (the code is meant to be breakable)-You can go sneaky and use electronic intelligence receivers to locate fleets running active radar, or go active with your own radar and invite attention-You can go looking for hidden cities in the desert using your ground scanning radar and your eyes.-You can make use of bomber groups, fighter groups, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles of various types to weaken enemy formations or defend your ships-Diplomacy matters when dealing with the warlords you will find, and they will react to you differently depending on how you have treated the world around you to that point and how you talk to them.Again, I am impressed by how these disparate mini-games come together to make a whole that is more than the sum of its parts. Be warned, there is a pretty steep learning curve and you're not meant to win on your first or even second attempt. When your run ends you receive a bonus to your funds for future attempts, so your first attempt can be the hardest.

_childDocuments_.review: I only have 45 hours at the time of review, but I'm sure I'll add many more. You might think that this is steeply priced for a video game, but it is without a doubt worth every penny. It may seem intimidating and cryptic, and that is because it is. Once you learn how to understand the information the game gives you, it becomes much, much more manageable. There are many moving parts, many systems masterfully woven together. It WILL take you time and effort to learn to use the UI and the tools the game gives you. It is worth that time investment. Watch youtube videos if you must.I also have to mention just how fun, robust, and rewarding using the in-game ship builder is. Sure there's no steam workshop support YET, but copy pasting .seria files from the unofficial high fleet discord, or from youtubers and other sources, is EASY and a NO BRAINER. Its great for people whose mind's aren't geared towards creating things like this, but still want to get a taste beyond the huge array of vanilla ships offered.Speaking as someone who never likes to build my own ships/designs, I have found the ship building both IN campaign AND just using the shipworks itself, to be so enjoyable, so rewarding, and it has given me more confidence in being creative and building things in general. Start with modding existing ships. Swapping out guns, taking out some fuel and adding ammo. Soon you'll be building ships from scratch at 2 in the morning wondering where you life went wrong and why you didn't try harder in school so you too could be an aeronautical engineer. Because dragging and dropping lego blocks is the exact same as designing aircraft capable of warfare, right?Last point, the immersion is unreal. 10/10 sound design. For a game where you're using a radar and staring at a map for a good chunk of your time, I have never been so immersed. No other strategy game TOUCHES Highfleet in the realm of immersion. Your heart will sink when one of your beloved ships gets torn in half by a missile and you watch it disintegrate into a million blazing chunks. Your blood pressure will rise, your muscles will tighten, when get the pre-battle screen and hear -THAT- song and know this is a battle that will make or break your whole campaign. For the love of all that is good in the world, support this one man dev team who created something so polished, so clearly visioned, and so unique. Even if you ignore the campaign and just play with the ship builder and the "arcade" battles, you can definitely get your money's worth. Buck an hour, that's all we ask.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, but I can't. I was attracted by the strategic layers of the game, being a commander that plays cat-and-mouse with mighty fleets as you plan your journey until you meet your destiny. The graphics, sound effects, music, it is all fine. The problem is the ships, or the way the Devs decided the components should be. And in a game where building ships is one of the most attractive factors, this is a serious problem.Also, as you can see, I played more than 80 hours and never managed to get near the objective for problems with bugs and events related to the story that I didn't know until time passed and the events unfolded. I wanted to enjoy my time making my strategic plans, but the game doesn't care. Rushing to the objective is the word of order, and that is really not my taste in a strategy game. But going back to ships, you see, when people decide that covering a ship with a reinforced 2-blocks spaced hull frame is more effective and cost-efficient than using proper armor, than you have a design problem. Never should armor be a burden so big you don't want to pay for it and go for alternatives. Armor is meant to be expensive AND better, not worse, than steel frames in rectangular shapes around a ship. Right now, armor is so heavy and its repair cost so much it is unwise to use it, and with enemies using infinite AP ammo, why should you bother anyway? But armor is not the only problem while building ships. I will not bore you with more details, just know this is a mess right now. It kills creativity for the sake of rectangular ships surrounded with steel frames in a desire to use the distorted rules determined by the devs to create a more efficient ship that has nothing to do with making a ship in real life. Until these problems are properly addressed by the devs, just stay away from this and keep watching if the problems will ever be adressed.

_childDocuments_.review: A very stylistic game that is dripping in atmosphere and fantastic art. Its a game that is 100% rough around its edges as many other users report you have to do quite a bit of fiddling to get it to run on resolutions that aren't 1080p and in 16:9 aspect ratio, there isn't a way to change your keybindings outside of messing with external programs, and finally has an absolutely terrible new player experience. These are things I hope are addressed in the future but this game is clearly a game of passion and is very interesting and requires its players to think in a more guerrilla sense since you aren't going to win a straight up fight with the big bads in this game. You piss them off and they will send your ass to the stone age then send a heavily armed strike force to clean up if the missiles didn't do their jobs. The ship builder is fantastic even though I'm not typically a person who like building things (wished there was more we can change cosmetically for the ships but seeing as you are playing an alt Russian empire, it does make sense on how you design your ships). Its a fresh take on the rougelite since you can design and build up a fleet of custom ships and each run rewards you money for future campaigns. This is the type of game I want to see succeed it. Its a game from someone's heart and it should be reward but I do agree with many other players that on the technical side it does have issues that need to be fixed and the new player experience might need to be touched up a bit since what it provides was very basic.Edit: Still love the game but it should be kept in mind that there hasn't been a great many updates at all for this game and its clear there was some content cut from the game. I just wanted to make this noted even though I support this game it is something to keep in mind

_childDocuments_.review: Game has a cool feel to it, both in graphics and setting, but the gameplay kinda puts me off. It's mostly little things like having to constantly do stuff with the radio. Sometimes 3-5 times in one trip. While it's a cool mechanic, it's gets kind of tedious when you have to do it so much. Then all the different keys you have to manage for different things, like F to send flairs/chaff, B to put stop fuel fires, C to fire anti aa stuff. i feel like some of this stuff should just be managed automatically by your crew  All this while trying to pilot your ship, and attack other ships. I'm also not to wild how it's always 1 vs xxx, Like why does the enemy get to bring all their ships in one go, but I have to go one at a time?While it is fun, it pretty quickly can get frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: This game. My gosh. Starts off and it's actually pretty good. Get involved and I'm enjoying it. But as the game progressed there were just gameplay elements that got so absurdly asenine. For example. You can have a radar but you can't ever use it otherwise the enemy will know where you are. So you're forced to essentially always be in the dark. No worries you have the handy dandy radio intercepts that you can use to figure things out as well and intel stations. Except all of a sudden those are useless too because they start cyphering them. No problem you can decipher the cypher. No more than 3 - 4 messages after figuring out the cypher are the messages recoded. Making it essentially useless.And then I'm constantly scurrying around trying to get fuel and and resorting to being a raider (its really the only way to play it) which is quite effective except that the only way to save the game is to take Fleet HQ's. Ohh wait those are all guarded by armies of enemy strike forces just waiting for you. But even with all of this I could deal with it mostly. What was utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ was the carrier strike groups nuking me (not with actual nukes) but these tactical missiles that would zoom in at 800-900 mph along with bomber that were nigh impossible to avoid in any real possible way. Meaning I might be minding my business and then all of a sudden a slew of supersonic missiles would fly in and murder the hell out of my ships. Now the normal strike fleets I could avoid and generally I tried to keep a low profile but it always seemed like SOMEHOW the computer would find a way an whack me from a mile away. No chance to salvage, no chance to repair. Just dead straight up. So I get ANTI-missile ships. They do nothing against the missiles. Meanwhile the carrier groups well I can't kill them as they're impossible to kill. I barely killed one strike group and that was because I HAD to. And then there were the myriads of other problems I ran into with the gameplay itself. For example I consider myself a pretty decent gamer but having your aiming reticle be literally right in front of your ship instead of idk being able to actually aim further aim shooting enemy ships at range or close up a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare. So then I was forced into a playstyle that heavily relied on guided missiles and sneak attacks coupled with armored paladin ships so I could come in and sweep the field. Altogether I found it ridiculous. Then there is the fleet aspect itself that annoyed the hell out of me. The ships and the way they are designed are supposed to work in tandem but never are you able to effectively USE your own ships to actually work together because you can ONLY ever have one on the field at a time. This makes it near impossible to actually have any real fleet engagements and so you're forced to become a missile assassin that swoops in and kills everything on the ground just to keep the game going. But yeah overall just the worst targeting and camera I've ever seen. I would have loved to design ships and give them general orders and watch them as they duke it out like some admiral instead of basically having to constantly dodge and play the missile is lava for the 100th time. But there is 0 fleet component and the camera is so far away and bad you can't even effing see your ships when they fight. Which leads to my next problem. The rain. Good lord the rain. I can't tell you how many battles I was in the rain made it night impossible to effing see anything going on. It's one thing if you want to make a game atmospheric, its another thing when every other battle is a literally gobs of rain that can't be removed blocking me from seeing anything. The game could have honestly been amazing but as such it's just so damn shoddy that I can't even believe it's getting any praise. The story is cool, the design elements are awesome. The visuals at times can be stunning but good lord is this game frustrating and not in any reasonable way.

As for the game itself? I suck at it :D But it's a lot of fun to blunder around with your fleet. _childDocuments_.review: Only 7 hours in but I don't care if it's too early to review or not-- HighFleet is single-handily the most beautifully atmospheric game I have played in the 22 years I have lived on this planet. That and it's the most innovative game I played ever since the market became stagnant with shovelling the same genera. It's a bold thing to say, but I'm being brutally honest. Games don't do much for me nowadays apart from ETS2 and SnowRunner, but this is the first time in years I was sucked into a game to such a degree.As someone who was practically brought up on World War documentaries, grew up in post-soviet blocks surrounded by post-soviet technologies to boot, the UI and art style is nothing but pure nostalgia. The tribal Slavic music and heavy, booming sound design for such a calibre of game is truly astounding-- all complimented by the gameplay loop which is a genius blend of FTL, RTS and pre-planning akin to CMANO-lite, with combat being a direct upgrade of Luftrausers. If you took away the combat and only left the RTS intact, I would still rate this game extremely highly on my personal top-favourites list simply due to how everything was tackled where things aren't told to you-- but shown.There are FPS drops, bugs, odd gameplay mechanics (such as card-based diplomacy) and some hard to gauge actions you need to take to survive-- but honestly for a love-child project of a singular man with a vision, HighFleet is a true unequivocal masterpiece in my mind in the ocean of mediocrity of the current video game market. A flawed masterpiece, but one nonetheless.Honestly-- if you're on the fence, just get it. The passion the developer has for this game oozes from every crevice. To not write a novel- a straight up 10/10 and a full-hearted recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: HighFleet. _childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry. In a good way. What could I say, it is once-in-a-while experience, to be honest. First five minutes when you try to land your ships without crashing them, you think "What the hell is going on here?", but then you start to get it. And after the first battle (and a few restarts of, actually), you start to immerse yourself into process, which, I should notice, is not really hard but offers decent challenge. The game has its unique aesthetics and a charm inspired by a history of Russian Khivan Campaign of 1873 and mixed with dieselpunk nuclear warfare. Graphics are pretty decent for a genre. And the sound of explosions and artillery shots is very, and I mean it, VERY vivid indeed: it feels like you are shooting these monster cannons yourself. Ship controls differ from what you choose/build. Something heavy will fly and maneuver as it should, without any fast, interceptor-style barrel rolls.I will add couple of bitter words though: sometimes game is a bit glitchy and unresponsive, especially in Shipworks section, but that's really a minor issue.In short: the game gives a very comfy and cozy vibe of an old-time legends like Fallout or Arcanum. It forces a player to use not just reflexes, but brains too. And that's what I find awesome. 9.2/10, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: In HighFleet you command your fledgling dieselpunk Sky Navy against a usurping Governor's forces in order to make him pay for his Sky Crimes.  It is an unusual and multi-faceted game which not only requires strategic thinking, but WASD & Mouse blasting and evading.I'm not normally a fan of a mini-game collection in one title, but HighFleet has so much going for it regarding the strategy and overall presentation.  You are basically waging an insurgent war with a fleet of air ships, and must use your fleet's sensors and intelligence gathering in your planning.  It is fortunately quite dynamic in that sense, and encourages you to be inventive with your approach.  It's often best to use stealth and intelligence to avoid strong enemy fleets early on while you are building your strength and conquering cities.Those who are familiar with modern naval and air sims would also be familiar with much of the equipment and terminology used for the equipment as they're almost direct copies of Russian military hardware.  Even the "ELINT" indicator looks like the radar warning receiver in Russian/Soviet aircraft cockpits.  The strategic gameplay involving ESM is recognizable, for example, and you'll be utilizing EMCON (emissions control) quite a bit to stay silent and keep off enemy sensors as long as possible.  Mixed with things like cruise missiles, aircraft from carriers & their armament loadout, CIWS/missile defense, etc, it's like managing a semi-apocalyptic naval fleet of Sky Pirates.I do have a few complaints, although they pale in comparison to the enjoyment I've had with this game.  The text interactions with NPCs is often a guessing game.  Although you can finger out a few beneficial replies for each NPC based on the limited info you're given, many of your cards & replies are still a guessing game at the start of each.  They can be quite beneficial if you get them to join, however.I'm also a bit disappointed in the lack of a keybinding option.  The default layout is sensible, but I'd prefer being able re-bind, and especially add a second key command to certain ones for things like the landing mini-game in which you don't use the mouse.  Adding a second set of key commands for Rotating the ship would allow me to use both hands to pilot those bucking beasts on the way down.Thankfully they added options to reduce the screen flashing and such in an update.  While I don't have epilepsy, the default settings could give me motion sickness to some degree.  After turning those settings all the way down, it is mostly fine now.The ship customization is great, giving you free reign to modify your ships how you want.  I hope they add a checkbox option for setting a large ship as a selectable flagship inside the game, but you can currently do that with a little info and text edit.I'd recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a strategy game which encourages and rewards sneaky craftiness with a healthy dose of customizable blastin' in between.  Once you get into it and understand everything, it's the kind of game you'll be brainstorming or looking up strategies for even when not playing.  The presentation is excellent icing, too.  Good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: It's a surprisingly deep strategy, tactical, rogue-like game set in a post-apocalyptic Persian/Arabian setting giving it a bit of a Dune, Metro 2033, steampunk vibe -- quite refreshing actually.2D arcade-like combat is ballistic based -- Think back to the WW2 navy days but with flying Mechs. Various loadouts including but not limited to gatling guns, artillery guns and the big  kahuna guns, then throw in fighters & bombers and finally guided AA/cruise/tactical missiles (some nuclear tipped). Put it all together and you got yourself a quite explosive display of firepower and sound -- quite fun!Ship design is generic at first but gets real deep (almost tactical) as you advance into the Campaign -- all with their own set of strengths and trade-offs.  Full ship customization is an option and I utilize it but you can't make the ultimate unstoppable armada - fuel/resource/objective management is a real thing here.  Radio interception + Intel gathering will net you some real juicy convoys but you'll still have to work for these using the tactical map with rulers and calculations with the added benefit of sensors like radar and infrared...I love it, try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is 100% a labor of love from the developers and they have crafted such a phenomenal game.Here's the PDF by the way for the game's manual, since I wasn't able to find it easily.-SPOILERS BELOW-It had been a long month of trekking city to city, but I finally had information from a caravan that a tarkan was nearby. North of me, the city of Shethe. Headed there, I immediately saw an ETHIL warning 4. I turned my primary radar system off and manually swapped over to IR search, detecting two incoming signatures. Given their speed and bearing, we immediately deduced they were missiles but there was no time to alter course. We opened up with 12 collective 37mm rapidly firing CIWS cannons with many auxillary weapon systems, but were only able to intercept 5 of the 8 missiles, the other 3 decimated half of my fleet.With only two ships remaining and no aircraft, we redoubled our efforts into Shethe, but not before the main force of the 4th enemy strike fleet found me. It was a desperate battle, four light cruisers against my single heavy cruiser. But during our entire journey, I was using my carrier strike group to do the heavy lifting. This would be my flagship Sevastapol's first taste of combat. I opened up with a barrage of 180mm shells and guided missiles, obliterating one of their light cruisers and damaging two more. With accurate, sustained cannon fire, I ripped apart the remaining 3 with ammo running low.Just as I was picking through the rubble and wreckage, relieved that I had beaten off their fleet, my radar began to ping me again, with my adjutant warning me that there were more incoming ships. Three more light cruisers, they must've been straggling behind the main force which had sped up in order to catch me. I tried to escape into the city but the fires from the earlier battle prevented me from doing so, and so we staged for yet another battle.This was bad, they had full ammo racks and fresh crew while I only had my auxillary cannons and main guns. They opened with a barrage of missiles, and despite the heavy duty CIWS fire I was able to bring, there were multiple impacts. I had lost half of my main guns and 3/4 of my starboard engines. The ships port engines overheated and shut down temporarily, causing me to freefall for several hundred feet. As they recovered, my only remaining 5 engines were barely adequate enough to keep me afloat, and I had to punch the afterburners in order to stay afloat. There was only one light cruiser left, them versus me.Through a desperate fight, I was able to maintain my altitude with my last engines, barely staying off the ground as I fired literally everything I had, the smaller missiles, my main cannons and my secondary armaments. Through a miracle, I had won that battle.This game is so hard, but this single encounter was worth it all. I can tell with the extreme depth of mechanics that the developers have really poured so much love into this game, its amazing.I then landed in Shethe, but due to my damaged engines, I had to use full power the entire time to slow my landing. Luckily a merchant's ship was below on the landing pad and cushioned my landing - to their detriment. Their entire ship was lost but hey, I landed safely and on only half of my engines.(deadass, this was so funny

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really cool. the setting of the game, the storyline, the mechanics. I even love the retro look of the game, which reminds me of the olden days. Yes I'm that old, that I remember playing in CGA graphics. I also love the shipbuilding option, which reminds me of Masters of Orion (also MicroProse!) The battles look cool and have some nifty mechanics, like reloading and manual aiming. Also, when you’re hit by bullets, you see the impact as if it were in your monitor screen. It adds to the drama, while in battle. The game itself reminds me of Deserts of Kharak, Dune (the Ye Olden one) with a dash of Masters of Orion. A truly MicroProse worthy game.And since MicroProse was the company from whom I bought every game, I would love to recommend this MicroProse game as well. But sadly I cannot do this, because for me this game is way, way too hard. Let me tell you why.There are two issues with this game. The first one is that you have no ability to save the game. This may be cool for the hardcore gamers who want the reality level turned to the max. But for the casual gamer, like me, this is really annoying and even a deal breaker.You have to land somewhere, where the game will auto save, I guess but I'm not really sure, because there is no mention of it. A save option is recommended, because the battles are very hard to do. And when I mean hard, it’s way too hard for the casual gamer. (or maybe I’m just an idiot gamer :D) Let me go into further detail.You start off with some basic ships, which you may upgrade with cool stuff later on. With this basic fleet you likely will run into a strike group from the start. These groups are made up of very powerful ships that will eat you for breakfast. Nearly every time I start a new game, I run into them at the first, second or third village. Now you need to land in a village, in order to get fuel. There is no getting around it. So, while landing, taking off or refueling, my fleet is always destroyed. That’s mainly because I can only fire with a BB gun hanging out the window, and they bring nukes to the battle. And you have to restart again. And again. And again. Until the morale of your crew is gone and your fleet is destroyed. So you need to start a new game. And again. And again. So if you have made any progress at all, say making it to the fourth village, and your fleet is destroyed for the gazillions time, any progress is gone too.Then there is the money issue. Yes you can salvage parts for money or your own use, which is a cool idea, but of the 4,5,6,7 parts that you have the option to salvage, you only have enough time for one or maybe two salvages. So you have to make a choice: crew, intel, parts or fuel. You always need to go for the crew because half of them are already dead from the past battle. Or go for the fuel salvage to at least go somewhere. So there are no parts left to salvage for you to sell and in turn, you cannot buy more fuel, let alone repair your fleet thats already moving like some old people with a walker. So, in the end you need to sell ships to pay for some gas. Ships from an already tiny crippled fleet.But that’s all relatively easy to overcome. The hardest part is the battles. Although I love the idea behind the battle mechanics, it’s way too difficult. I see videos of other guys shooting everything out of the sky, but I just can't do it. Maybe I’m getting too old, or I’m just an idiot, but I just cannot do the strike groups when they attack me at village number 4.I can do the city ships! Which is a nice challenge. I actually have the feeling you make a chance. But when you have several of the heavy ships from a strike group raining down on you with a constant hailstorm of bullets, while you are trying to move your baby carriage (i.e. a ship like a corvette) around the map, it’s a real challenge. Aiming, dodging bullets, shooting down missles, putting out fires and the endless waiting for 3 shells ammo to be ready to fire is a real challenge. And you are bound to miss them anyway. Now I really love a challenge, but this is impossible.So for me this game is unplayable and I asked for a refund. The ideas are really cool and I would love to recommend Highfleet, but in this state I cannot. If you are that average player, who just wants to at least make a chance, skip this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm old... not OLD old... but ... yeah ... old. ... 30s and such .... Grew up with DOS games like CIV, GP, XCOM UFO Defense, Railroad Tycoon ... etc. Most if not all of these spearheaded entire franchises, genres and/or lay the foundations for a good portion of modern games today.All of the games mentioned above were developed and/or published by MicroProse.Highfleet certainly holds up to the standards, and while MicroProse may never again rise to that level (seeing as though it's technically a completely different company now)... it undoubtedly has its priorities straight.Looking forward to seeing more.As far as Highfleet is concerned ... yeah... it's a good game ... currently ... it WAS great back before the developer screwed around with the balancing and suddenly allmost all ship components are 50% more crap.Dev, if you're reading this ... you're shooting yourself in the foot. The more fun this game is, the more money you make. The more fun it is, the more stuff about it will happen on YouTube... the more money you make... etc.The more you insist on russian-ing-it-up because you people just have to insist on complicating everything for no reason, the more difficult you make it to enjoy this game, therefore, the less fun it is ... and therefore the less money you'll make.Be warned ... if you continue to ignore the "fun" aspect in favor of " i want this done this way because life sucks in general and this should be life-like ' ... .... well ... I'm sure you can work it out for yoursef.Congrats on what you've accomplished though. It's pretty awesome. Just don't turn it into a piece of junk for no reason.TLDR : better-than-good game (at review time) ... could be better if dev would stop making every ship component half as effective for no reason.Negative review because reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an incredibly unique Fleet Management / Combat game with a rather steep learning curve.Pros:- Interesting Setting and Story- Excellent sound design- Excellent effects (absolutely love the ship explosions and falling burning debries)- Full ship editor with your own creations fully usable in the campaign- Deep strategic layer with many options to manage (Intel, Electronic Warfare, Suprise attacks, intercepting messages)- Very immersive setup, every button in you command room is usable- Can obliterate entire Fleets with mass cruise missile attacks (unless the enemy does it to you)- Can obliterate entire Fleets with mass fighter attacks (unless the enemy does it to you)- Can obliterate entire Fleets with Nukes (unless the enemy does it to you)Cons:- Sometimes the effects are just too much to see anything (Rain at night hitting your screen and explosions going off) - Initially very punishing, you can get into a death spiral very quickly as beginnerPro Tip:You can start the Nuclear War at any time but the enemy will end it.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art and detailed scenery. Post apocalyptic setting is very well done, not cheesy or overdone or unbelievable. The art style is unique as is the gameplay. It's sort of like FTL meets moon lander. Learning curve is slightly lower than Starsector, but comparable ship customization. The combat is very satisfying. Ammo is finite as is money, fuel, and crew lives. Radio gameplay is kind of annoying and you have to do it quite often. I would like to upgrade radar equipment gradually so that you eventually dont need to do it manually. Or hire specialized crew to do it for me. But overall it's very good.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: There is no sweeter feeling than seeing the structural diagram of the enemy ship you're firing at slowly melt under artillery fire. It's like a much more complicated FTL, where the enemy fleet isn't just a red line creeping across the map, but is instead intelligently hunting you. At some point in a run, you'll be cornered, and you need to decide whether to sacrifice a ship to distract the enemy fleets, or to grit your teeth, weather 10 tactical missiles pointed at your face, and then face down some thicc bois.This game is incredible. It is incredibly punishing. If one of your splinter fleets without adequate anti-air protection wanders into missile range of one of the thicc fleets hunting you, you will be rewarded with the real-time display of a tactical cruise missile yeeting your precious ships into oblivion. If you nuke a fleet hunting you, the other 4 fleets will launch their nukes at you.This is immediately one of my favourite games, even *despite* the jankiness. Reviews commonly point out some significant UI problems. Those are easy to fix and the developer is actively working on them. This game has gotten the hardest part right - an incredible combination of a tense strategic layer with creative and fun ship-to-ship combat.I'll finish where I started. You have not fully tasted life until you've seen a perfectly lined up arc of artillery shells yeet the unprotected topside of an enemy behemoth while its counter-fire whistles by you or is absorbed by your armour.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played much yet but reading some comments i want to give my own experience.The game is incredibly appealing to me sounds and visuals wise ; everything is seriously amazing. The dieselpunk/early-mid coldwar aesthetic plays a lot into this for me ; the setting is also really interesting, I am very fond of Gerat and its heavily influenced aesthetic. The story so far is really enthralling and I love meeting new Tarkhans, groups and special events.Gameplay wise it reminds me of Starsector a lot, a game that is also developped by a single russian man and really is worth a play ; I naturally am going to draw some comparisons. What I really noticed firsthand was that you cannot deploy more than one ship in battle, which wouldn't be such a problem if the enemy wasn't able to send at least three ships at you instantly. This unbalance is frustrating and pretty annoying in my opinion because it renders most support ships useless ; I'd absolutely love being able to send out heavily gunned ships covering a tinier point defense missile frigate. This is for me the main issue with the game. Apart of that and minus some polishing issues the game feels amazing to play. All of the UI is gorgeous and made to look like their real life counterparts while not being a mess to use, everything is unexpectedly practical.The customisation is also huge. Every single ship is an assemblage of blocks and you are free to build anything you'd like flying either in the shipworks of the main menu or during a campaign, scrap your flagship if you want to ! The ship editor needs a bit more polishing still and a lot of quality of life features (unless i haven't discovered them yet). I also think there's not enough complexity and that the part number is pretty low, but that serves the simplicity of the editor ; it is way more accessible than another comment made it seem, and if you have trouble, read the stats on the left of the screen and take a prebuilt ship apart to understand how they are built.Highfleet is imo an outstanding piece of an indie game, needing polishing but very good nonetheless. There's a lot I probably forgot or decided not to talk about but I'm not a game journalist, go play it. I'd love to see the original Glitch High option, for optimal chaos :) and maybe a sequel or massive updates. <3A warm thanks to the many members of the Merchant's Guild
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Visually if you enjoy playing old school games from the early 90s when highest level of visuals were sprites this should be up your alley. Problems I had with the game is a very key portion of the game which is aerial combat mechanic. The camera and hud doesn't really help you determine how to properly aim your weapons to hit your target. More often than not, it feels like pure luck that you land your cannon shots. Your main way of taking out enemies are your missiles and that assumes the enemy doesn't shoot those out of the sky and/or doesn't use chaff. What would feel like a 2D twin stick shooter to help you figure out if your gun shots are going were they need to go and adjust.  Your instead constantly adjusting with no feedback if your volley would hit making shooting aspect frustrating instead of fun. Seeing your rounds just miss because you under estimated your enemy position to only re-adjust and again fail to hit because you over estimated your shots is what you spend 90% of your time in combat doing.  There is no cross-hairs to help you determine where your volley will go. Instead you're shooting what feels like aimlessly or a spray and pray tactic as your only indication is tiny arrow that goes around your ship. Assuming you have also figured out where your ship is on the screen. You spawn at random on either corner of your screen for every combat scenario. Sadly it feels very indie despite the main developer is a seasoned pro from the late 1980s / 90s. The Indie feel in this game is not a good thing, in fact, it feels like they didn't bother have it play tested in a public environment. The game's trailer paints a picture that should feel like Luftrausers and instead plays like Lunar Lander (from 1979) with guns. Sadly all the talent from the team that made Mechcommander didn't translate very well in this game at all except for their visual direction. It's not worth your time, until the fix/ improve the shooting mechanic in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine, but the combat system is utterly broken. Misbalanced difficulty and brainless. It's all abount using the keyboard + mouse faster than you enemy. You can only use one ship at a time but the AI comes with 3 - a f* real xp ruiner. The battle screen is also overpoluted with visual effects, so you can barely see where you're aiming at. Dozen of alarms sounding at the same time. Music is also not good at all.No immersion, no tatics, no fun. Great idea cast through the window. Just buy during some sale and you're good.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Meh...yes the ambiance and graphics are nice and reminiscent of the 90s era, but the game is unbalanced and confusing. The combat system will allow the AI to get 90% shots on your ship while you'll be lucky to get 10% hits. You'll spend most of your time fighting gravity than landing shots, on the other hand the AI can predict your movement very accurately.Only the bare minimum is explained to you, what's the purpose of the IR sensor? How to use the carriers? Why is there 2 kinds of planes? What's the purpose of nuclear missiles? What's the difference between refueling your strike group vs. your main group? How can I reload missiles on my ships? How can I know which ships are assaults ships if I want to create a strike group?Also, the landing system is boring and too repetitive, need to land 5 ships? better pray the last one is not in too bad shape otherwise you'll crash and have to redo everything, why no auto land? This is not an enjoyable game mechanic, yes, lunar lander was cool in the 80s but not 4 times in a row and 10 times per game session.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A truly unique and well-themed ship-based tactical and strategic RTS that has a sharp difficulty curve and limited replay value.Pros:- Incredible theme with music, visuals and UI. I never thought 2D combat could feel so "realistic" just from the visuals and sound effects.- Very good balance between strategic map work, fleet building, and tactical gameplay. There is steep learning curve for each of these areas, but once you get a feel for it, it's pretty rewarding. - The games use of electronic warfare (ELINT, radar, infrared sensors, jamming) is really well done. A large part of the strategic map battle is using these tools to find the enemy fleets without giving away your position.- The custom fleet editor is great for trying different combat stategies.- Game isn't very resource intensive and seems well optimized. Cons:- A lot of the difficulty comes from not knowing what is going to happen and how the game's systems work. Once you figure out the game is "meant" to be played, it becomes much easier, especially when you know the plot of the campaign. Even though new campaigns have randomized maps, each game pretty much plays out the same every time, so for me there's not a lot of replay value other than building your own ships and trying them out. The enemy and plot never changes though.- The diplomacy and public opinion systems seem very empty. There is a lot of RNG involved and there seems to be no in game consequence for doing or even avoiding certain actions. A lot of actions will reduce your "kindness" rating, but there are few ways to increase it and it seems like a negative kindness rating doesn't matter anyway?- There is no way to access custom ships built in the editor after starting a new campaign. It would be nice to quickly retrofit default ships bought during the campaign with those already made in the editor, but this is currently not possible. Conclusion: Despite the difficulty curve, I do think this game is definitely worth buying if "modern" ship/fleet based combat seems interesting to you. I wish there were more campaign options to extend the replay value, but for it's price point the quality and quantity of the content available is very good.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: You are the spearhead of a special military operation to maintain the sphere of influence of the Russian state over the breakaway nation of Gerat, which is aligning itself with NATO dogs.Unfortunately it appears that the duplicitous Yankees have been arming these kolkhozniki, because they respond to this justified de-Nazification operation by annihilating the rest of the fleet and indeed Holy Mother Russia herself.Now you and your other officers, cosplaying as the Baltic Fleet of 1905, must push your Z-adorned vessels straight to Kyiva to seize the President and his family and force Gerat to commit itself to non-alignment and block its entry to NATO.Can you fulfill the prophecy and make Vladimir Vladimirovich proud? Or will you, like Shoigu, blow all your money on flying yachts?
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: After 50 hours in this game, I've finally beat it (on normal), and I can confidently say I enjoyed every single hour spent on this game. The story is compelling filled with interesting twists, characters, ships, decision and a couple mountains of challenges, which are all somehow topped by the finale; which really adds a sense of desperation to the mission. The Tarkhans (potential allies) are really interesting and have their own story, likes and dislikes, if you play enough you'll learn them all by heart (until you find one you haven't seen before); and they're all interesting and are pivotal to the end game. I'm still finding new Tarkhans after 50 hours. Building ships is fun and can be intimidating at first, but you're going to need to build you're own or at least make modifications to base ships, which you will find you are naturally more comfortable doing as you play more and more. Highfleet is truly a gem, and I don't see myself putting it down anytime soon. There is still much to see, ships to build, ships to crash, people to meet, and war crimes to commit. Pick it up, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: This game was surprisingly great. Funnily enough, I spend almost as much time trying to design the best ship as I did actually playing the campaign. The more you play it the more you realise how all of the detection systems, missile types and ships have a unique role which will make the game hard to beat without mastering them. Highly Recommended
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Got a mission to find a hidden city. Found said city who welcomed me as saviours, but I didn't keep track of a nuclear strike group.It sent missiles at me whilst I was landed.I didn't even see them until they were on radar.Eight missiles later I had brought doom to the city, their home an irradiated ruin and my fleet and flagship destroyed.The campaign had ended but now my new quest to find a new hidden city and evac my existing ships. Several nail biting battles and tense moments later I found the city and saved the remaining crew. 660 men escaped alive. I was rewarded in bonus points for my performance thus far and the mens lives I saved, which would be converted into funds to give me the edge for my next shot at the campaign. 8/8 Nuclear sub-sonic missiles that you don't see coming.

_childDocuments_.review: I like Barotrauma. This game has very similar styling(if you play Captain a lot).Unlike Barotrauma, the process of moving through the map feels more important, and the map feels lived in.Intercepting comms and mapping out fleet paths is amazing, and hunting them down on occasion is fun.Cipher cracking may not appeal to many but I make it a personal mission to try and crack it without finding more cipher keys.The ship designer being built in is fun, I just wish I could designate flagships without having to do file edits.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much detail and you can tell there's definitely love put into this game. I enjoy it immensely. Elements of Diplomacy, Resource Management, Choices that affect the world around you. It's definitely challenging and its not easy for sure but the scaling difficulty is something you have to prepare your own ships for. Everything is in an ironman mode, you lose a ship? It's gone, no reloads, no resets. It makes everything much more tense and gives you several situations where you're like "I think my run is over." and you somehow nail-bitingly squeak out a victory. Though it is forgiving as it lets you retry battles you lost in case you want to try and do it better than the first go.All in all. I have high hopes.

_childDocuments_.review: So, after ~7-8 hours with the game I'm pretty sure I love it. It's like re-living the 90's again - it's hard (but fair) and really appealing with it's artstyle. And the transition from prologue to regular game is awesome. In general it's a hybrid of strategy, rpg, U-boat sim (yes, my first thought of tactical map was Silent Hunter) and Lander.+ very nice art-style (think Dune)+ very immersive+ fair combat+ makes you think and plan ahead- sometimes the amount of things happening in combat can be overwhelming- it's hard- I mean it's really hard

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been playing video games for over 30 years, my relationship with the hobby has been deteriorating for at least the last decade. I keep asking myself why I still bother to play games - what was the last game that actually brought me joy, surprised me, or did something truly unique? Highfleet is the kind of game that reminds me what I love about the hobby.If you're looking at this game's store page and wondering if you should buy it, the short answer is that you owe it to yourself to at least try it out and refund it in two hours if it's not your jam. This is a truly unique game that brings back a lot of what has been missing from videogames for the past ~15 years (and I don't just mean 'having a manual'). The visuals are absolutely top notch, the immersive interface is fun to play with, the combat is meaty and crunchy with a high skill ceiling. The multitude of ways that you can interact with the campaign and your enemy, the freedom of diverse strategies, the lack of hand-holding all go a long way toward taking video games back to the way they were before the days of "streamlining" everything into simplicity. But the beauty of Highfleet is that it remains both a simple game, and an incredibly deep one. It's not nearly as overwhelming as it looks, but you can dive in just as deep as you'd assume from looking at it.For the record - I bought it, played for an hour and a half and got frustrated at the campaign, then refunded it. But I kept thinking about it for the next two days so I bought it again and gave it another shot, and I'm glad I did!
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Simply one of the best strategy-rouguelike games I've played. A must if you enjoy these two types of tytles, and enjoy shipbuilding mechanic.You are always at a numerical disadvantage, though there is a number of ways you can get other advantages, and you'll need to learn how to. Multiple mechanics that you can't always use are present to save you from a massive headache of fighting a large strike group, carrier group, or cruise missiles, that can all take you down quickly, or make your ships broken down enough that you lose a lot of progress to get them back in working order.Its a constant chore to track nearby ships, so much so you need pen and paper to know names of every encounter and information, and do yuor best to decrypt radio mssages to get updates and know your next move.TL;DR, easy to learn, hard to master and actually win. Absolute thunderingly painful to win.Must play.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like the videos for this game are misleading, often showing gameplay extremely zoomed in and cutting very fast to hide one essential fact - this is basically a flash game, very similar to ones you might have played back in the day where you move your little ship around like in asteroids and click on things to shoot at them.  Sure, you can make a load out for your ships but you can only field one ship at a time and the gameplay is pretty simple and yet still somehow manages to be a bit fiddly.  Everything about this game feels like it was built by people who really didn't have any experience with game design, like a bunch of folks just came up with a concept they thought was cool but didn't know how to execute on it, and made a pretty but simplistic game where everything is just a bit off and just doesn't quite work right.Now if this were a dollar game for your phone I would be saying solid game, worth trying out, but charging $30 for this just seems absolutely criminal.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Hoooooo boy do I like this game, guys. Truly amazing. Beautiful.Combat is hard to describe. Ponderous, tense dogfights. Intricate ship flying and building mechanics. Landing your airships at the dock is like the old Lunar Lander game from the 70s. It all takes place in a futuristic arabic dieselpunk setting - like Game of Thones with nukes. There's also a diplomatic element, as you attempt to unite a bunch of disaffected warlords to go after the central power.Oh, and navigating around the world map is like Silent Scope. You have a radar that you use - like you can pick up a pencil and draw an X to represent a radar ping. You decode enemy messages and avoid their fleets while going after lightly-guarded targets.The graphics in general are probably the best representation of an aesthetic I've ever seen in a video game. Rain beads against the glass of your ship - storms blind you. Your digital display flickers and warps. It's ugly and beautiful.Also it's Russian so it's a bit buggy. But in a sea of shlock, you really can't let that stop you.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game, if you like fleet command games, or just generaly want a game that actually makes you feel like an admiral go for this, it has probably become my favorite game ever. The music is fantastic, the atmosphere is on point. Gameplay is super enjoyable and the setting is very well written.It also has a great gameplay/skill curve, as you begin you will be afraid of strike fleets and the enemy but as you get to know the game and upgrade you will fight then head on, not afraid. the ship designer is also very fun, sometimes i get so into designing ships that i forget to actually get out of the designer and play.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Too much to say about this game. 10/10 without a doubt, even if its got a few hiccups.   Imagine FTL on soviet crack and taking place in a setting and story inspired by DUNE, probably the best way I can attempt to summarize it. Easily one of the best games I have ever played. The combat, story, shipbuilding; all of it flow seamlessly and it always continues to surprise. Love the radio system, which allows you to intercept enemy messages by finding the right frequency, adjusting the bearing, and at times using a cipher for encrypted messages. Radar types are a whole different beast.Everything is done from your cockpit, up until combat and/or landing. The combat is fun and strategic, and you've got soooooo many options for ships (many different types with combat roles but also an extensive list of modifications to existing ones). The shipbuilding alone in this game deserves a review. I never mess around with shipbuilding but i spent a good few hours playing around with designs and concepts.It can seem very overwhelming at first. But the tutorials are incredibly helpful and unobtrusive (Basically your badass General will remind you of certain things or tell you how to manage a new threat. this can be disabled too). Overall there's a few bugs but nothing major and it would be nice to have the ship list available in game. But theres a beautifully done Manual PDF under additional content (really, the artwork and everything is just great and it has a little notes section at the end like they used to) so RTFM.The story is very well done and yet again, flows seamlessly throughout the gameplay.P.S. If you don't know what 'RTFM' means you might wanna ask around, comrade.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: This game have surprising strategic depth. It combines elements of (pseudo-naval) combat, where intel about enemy positions is quite vital as you need to be a step ahead of strong enemy. Electronic warfare like sensors, jamming and intercepting enemy radio messages is important part of the game.You decide technical designs, composition, and employment of your forces as. You can also deploy tactical missiles or carrier aircraft in both offensive and defensive roles. You plan logistics and you play a game of survival against superior force. Strike and run is the key. Remember that you need fuel to run. Meeting superior force with empty tanks can be fatal as refuelling takes precious time!Battles play like a 2D shooter, with physics involved giving it another layer of difficulty. Situational awareness, good positioning and anticipation pays of more than super fast reactions as maneuvres are effected by inertia.It has rogue-like mechanic in that you can unlock more funds and stock ships by progressing and then losing in campaign.There are some quality of life issues, like lack of information on ship parts to quickly see performance to weight or cost ratios. II tried to mitigate that in partial guide. Be sure to check other guides as well, for example ability to make your own flagship (requires simple 'hack') is super useful if the default one does not fit your play style. Also info about missile types performance is useful.1.1 brought some QoL improvements, so team seems to be responsive for players requests.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: I have tried really hard to enjoy this game. I get that the UI is supposed to be part of the fun, and for the most part it is, however there are times when the status of the game is just too opaque. Specifically things like changing a ship during play as an example. Also, this game presents itself as a wide road to win, but really, there is a very specific sets of options to how to win. Sometimes that is part of the fun of a rougelike game, but here you are just suddenly going down in flames and there is no chance to recover and not really any clear explanation as to why. It would be one thing if there was some sort of between playthough progression, but now that bonuses are gone mostly. I would understand no bonus in a hard mode, but that is not what I want to play and it is not what I baught, it changed after I purchased the game.Really, the only fun part of the game is testing out ships you make. But it is kind of depressing as for the most part, those ships are really not great. I hope to see this game get better, but right now it is not fun. I'll come back to this in the winter time and hope for it to be more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: A very impressive game both mechanically and visually. It's rare to see something that's truly unique and stands out from the crowd and does it in a way that still has fun and mentally engaging gameplay. Highfleet's blend of strategic and tactical gameplay and management of fuel, repair parts, ships, planes, money, allies, reputation, and ballistic/nuclear missile stock seems daunting at first but had less of a learning curve than it first appeared for me, and is just enough to be rewarding without being overly frustrating. I would appreciate some more graphics options, like the ability to remove/reduce weather effects that cover the screen. while cool at times the number of water droplets on the screen in rainy weather certainly seems excessive. The game is also rather oddly locked at 50 fps, and like any good PC gamer i'm a frame junkie so that's less than optimal to me and my 3070, though there may be some technical reason for it. aside from that the game needs some polishing and I experienced some random crashes at times but I still recommend the game and think it is worth the price if it looks at all interesting to you.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Such an underrated hidden gem of a game. LOVE the strategy and lack of hand holding. If you wanna win and get far, you have to dive deeper into the systems and play and learn to use all the tools made available to you. Taking things at surface level wont get you too far. I think that's highfleet's biggest strength. I also love the chaotic, explosive, fun combat systems here. Alotta others saying it doesnt fit with the rest of the theme but fail to see how strategy and planning ahead play a direct role in how combat is approached or even avoided entirely. The only downside i see is there aren't more frequent updates. It could also do with some fresh content to up replayability but. Still a solid game.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a combination of exploration et super satisfying maneuvering combats. The art is gorgeous and the story is very well written. If you don't care for the srategic part, there is a highly customizable shipbuilding mod which can be use to just experience the combat in all its glorry.This is a labor of love and you can feel it in all aspects of the game!
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a perfect atmosphere.All from the graphics and sounds, to the characters are well thought out and I would honestly say that the atmosphere is what makes this game as a whole. You really feel like you're in a tight, cramped cockpit with instruments of all kinds with blinking buttons and sounds all around you. Every UI-element has a function and isn't just eye-candy and it just feels like you're there!Game-play wise, it's a tough start but once you've got the hang of it you will quickly start seeing more and more progress done by yourself. Just be ready for the first session to be rough... LIKE, REAL ROUGH. It's like riding a bike, impossible at start but suddenly it clicks.Story-wise I like it, but the ending is... abrupt? Way to abrupt. I honestly thought the game bugged out and skipped the ending. I even went to search for the ending, but nope, that WAS the ending.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: No doubt - it's an excelent game, made with lot-a-love, oldschool style! Welcome, youngsters,Re-live the golden years of gaming, when not every title was a classic, but some became gems, inventing new genres, mechanics and are well remmembered by most of us! Just give it a go. I do not want to spoil your first experiance with Highfleet and I am deffinately sure you will love it.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I've left the game running a few times so playtime is slightly inflated, but I've definitely put a lot of hours into this game.Highfleet is easily my game of the year. It's made by a small team (I think two people?), So can be a little rough around the edges, there have been some bugs and one or two gripes from the community but the Devs are active in addressing them.The game is HARD, but when it clicks you feel like a god (at least until a cruise missile puts you back in your place). The game has a lot of moving parts that fit together incredibly well. The tutorial does a reasonable enough job of showing you how things work, but you have to figure out the actual stratergies on your own.There are no 'hitpoints' or stats for ships, everything is made out of the same parts, it's about how they are put together. The enemy has the same weapons, ships and tools you do, just more of them.Brilliant game, nothing else quite like it, must play for strategy game fans
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: I love "TacMans", games with interrelated strategic and tactical layers like XCOM, BATTLETECH. I suggest getting to know the built-in ships and weapons in the campaign before attempting to design your own. I also suggest "playing to discover" - if you aren't sure about a decision, ship or weapon, try it! You can always reload or try again if it doesn't work out. The game isn't totally clear and sometimes it's best to Google something.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: Sound Design: GOD tier. Look the game is a bit for the people on the spectrum, BUT it doesnt stop it from being a very solid game. Once you get to the constructor... "This is where the fun begins". Because it does! Landing ships for immersion sake however is pain. Especially since i always forget to get them landing gear when making my own ships.The weather effects are good, the ost is fantastic, the game is really immersive especially when you are trying to pull some high G manuevres and your pilots are losing consiousness. In fact i am convinced that for the 80% duration of some of the best air battles i had the crew was either blacked out or puking. There are a few immersion sake 'unfun' mechanics im not a fan of but that is the creative vision of the developer. Should you buy this? Absolutely. Its fun and unique.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: After eventually getting the game to run via Proton, I found a game with a huge learning curve which is not clearly explained. Trying to modify ships is impossible, and the fight sequences are near impossible, enemies have perfect aim, perfect tracking and able to swivel their weapons instantly, while you are one single ship with huge restrictions up against many enemies scoring direct hits from every possible angle.First few levels seem extremely repetitive too.The whole "speed up time" thing is also somewhat strange, if it is possible to speed up time (and nobody is going to hang around for 12hrs for a refuel) why even include those huge time delays at all.Game looked very interesting and rather unique, but without huge amounts of time to invest in it, it is just not worth it. Not a bad game, just not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say that there's a decent learning curve to this game but the tutorial prepares you decently well with the basics and leaves you to work out the rest, though a knowledge of secondary-school level math is helpful.This game is unique, fun and very engaging; It's no lie that I've lost track of time so badly at times that when I shut down the game it was already 4 am. It would probably help if on 'normal' difficulty it was explained that the 'save' points didn't mean that you'd actually lose all your progress if you closed the game, you just can't go back except to those 'save points' (it would probably be clearer if they were renamed to checkpoints as that explains it better).Anyhow, the ship designer provides a decent level of depth to the game, though most would agree that the default designs are flawed for a reason, so you can fix them up during the campaign with all the considerations that sitting in a ship-works for a few hours hold. If you ever get bored the format/game-play loop is good enough that you could just do a modded play-through, whether it's changing the enemy's designs to be more challenging or give yourself different weapons; hell, I've heard there are some total conversion/map mods out right now though I've never used them myself.10/10 - Have recommended it to every gamer I know.
_childDocuments_.name: HighFleet

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a complete farce. Too much unfairness and useless complications for the sake of being artificial difficult. It's a meme, it's not even difficult to be fun, it's difficult because "haha, start over, your time is worth nothing".You avoid a strike fleet and another warp in your face a single city later even if they should patrol way far one from another. Your missiles get shot down outside the screen, airplanes are completely useless, 10 bombers didn't manage to clear 2 ships parked with 250kg bombs, enemy missiles and airplanes snipe your ships even if you are pointing four guns at them. Also if you kill ships with airplanes you can't loot them, this is beyond ridicolous. Also, the alarm will always be raised even if you clear all the enemy ships parked. Also, a single bomb from an enemy airplane can ONESHOT a full health Sevastopol. Those are just only few of the fun occurrence in this perfectly balanced game.I can't really imagine how someone can play this game for fun or relaxing, it's an act of aggression on the human senses. All the noise, the confusion, the unreadable UI and having to do litterally everything in the grasp of seconds or it's a game over it's painful. And everything it's just artificial difficulty, nothing adds to the ambience or the general game.After the first half of the map everything becomes dark, for some reason dark outside means you can't see your own instruments, because yeah why not more artificial difficulty. Your enemy of course don't have this handicap and in the most of the cases you just stop seeing your ship and you lose. You don't even see what kills you.Just for fun, the rule of 3v1 applies to you, not the enemy. The platforms are not included in the count, so your average fight after the first half of the map is always 5 or 6 vs 1 with swarm of infinite missiles, because of course the enemy has infinite missiles.Icing on the cake, after the onslaught on the last city you have to stop 5 strike forces that can hit from EIGHT different places, all out of your radar, three of those have INFINITE NUCLEAR MISSILES (all in a 3 day tops) or it's game over. This is a farce, not a game. I regret not being able to refund after seeing this.On principle, if a game is unwinnable unless you pass hours online looking for guides just to grasp basic machanics is a bad game. Here is this, and all the rest.Giving you pre-built ships which becomes useless after the first half of the game is sincerely an insult to the player.No thanks. Plot and lore are very interesting, but the mechanics and gameplay are the worst I've ever seen in my long career as a gamer.This game is just not fun to play, is a complete waste of your time and you get nothing from it except frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very appealing and the combat can be quite good in a challanging way too. Money is very hard to come by, enemy fleets are unavoidable with stronger units (not enough travel distance) and an utter lack of practical save oprions.PS-PS: I guess that the game is super hard but like with other tites by the same company you have to learn a lot first. _childDocuments_.review: There's a trick when it comes to difficult games. They need to be fair, there needs to be a reasoning behind  the game screws you so hard. Otherwise your game will be plagued with moments that will make the player say: "That's bull, how did that happen?"  Even if you haven't alerted any enemies in the entire run (though alerting enemies ramps up the bombardment). This wouldn't be that big of deal if there were more reliable ways to deal with missiles, but after your 5th missile attack in a row, you'll be out of countermeasures other than your guns. It also wouldn't be that big of a deal if the missiles didn't do that much damage, but a single missile can destroy one of your light frigates.So, ok, you're getting your booty rocked by random missiles, maybe playing on an easier difficulty will fix that. . The damage will be less, but the enemies can detect you  on the easy difficulty. So, less damage, but more missiles.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: These are my personal opinions, i might be wrong about some stuff, correct me if you guys can.WARNING: THIS GAME INCLUDES FLASHING LIGHTS AND MAY TRIGGER SEIZURES FOR PEOPLE WITH PHOTOSENSETIVE EPILEPSY. BE CAREFUL OUT THERE GAMERS.I would call Highfleet a strategy fleet management sim where you manage your squadron to reach the city Khiva, a city with a HUGE reactor. I will talk abut some pros and cons, critical mechanics that you should learn if you want to play it, and some stuff that i dont know if those stuff intended or not.MUSIC/SOUNDSThe music and the sounds for me are great. The music really fits well both on combat and events. The crew got some good voice acting too, They sound a lot more stressed when your fuel is low, when you lost an engine and abandoning your ship. (some games doesnt really capture this feeling too well)COMBATI will be talking about how combat works and tell you some strategies. (PLEASE SET YOUR CROSSHAIR TO LONG BEFORE YOU ENTER INTO COMBAT)You only have one ship to use in combat while the enemy can have up to 3 or 4. You can see if the enemy switchs ammo or when its about to shoot.All ships does NOT have a hp bar, they are made out of parts for example if you get hit by your engine it can die causing you to go slower and make it harder to keep the ship stable. A wise man once said:Think of every ship in this game as a crab, penetrate through its all just exoskeleton and its soft, tender flesh.If you can punch through their armor or hit them on a vulnerable angle, it will deal a lot of damage or even kill the damn thing on one hit. Thats why positioning and strategy is critical on combat.We have main batteries and secondary guns. Secondary guns are mostly for chopping up aircraft or missiles while main batteries hit ships real hard. We got 100mm, 130mm, 180mm cannons for our primary damage output and 37mm AUTOCANNON or 57mm HMG's for missilies and planes.We can also launch missiles which track the enemy that we were targeting (which shows up on the bottom right) when we fire it. we also have Air to Air missiles to intercept other missiles and planes.Missiles are good to use but i didnt see them be good on strike groups due to them having an insane amount of AAM. (air to air missiles) Flares are much less effective on 1.16 for some reason.MECHANICS(PLEASE LEARN THE MECHANICS IF YOU WANT TO PLAY THIS GAME)Lets talk about our Radar on Sevastopol, it has a long range and can spot trade convoys (i dont know if it can spot strile groups or carriers) I normally turn it on when im close to a city so a random trade convoy doesnt report our position and send strike groups and missiles to end our lives.ELINTReally good for detecting strike groups, its undetectable, has a good range and shows the direction of Strike groups, it has 5 stages, ELINT 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 the closer a strike group gets, the higher the number. If you are going to a city and get  this alarm on the direction of the city, you can turn off your radar and hide on the desert until they pass or TAKE THEM HEAD ON (like me) and question your decisions.Infared Search and Track SystemISTS is used for spotting planes and rockets, it has a short range that is around i think 300 km. So you better prepare yourself. Air to Air missiles are good for them.Jammerthis thing doesnt seem to work in my runs, i dont even know how it works so please someone tell me. It seems useless for me.Radio InterceptionThis is really good on early game where you can literally loacate everything just by rotating a few stuff. But they get encrypted on around mid-game which can be a problem but sometimes you can solve it entierly just by knowing its callsign or a single key word. Rockets (not the ones in combat)They have a long range and they can critically damage an airship if it hits on just the right spot. strike groups also has rockets so if your position has been reported, i would prefer getting aa missiles or proximity fuze ammo, because a rocket might be traveling as you repair and refuel your ships. I saw them one shotting my aircraft carriers and a light ship like lightning.NUCLEAR ROCKETSYes, you can nuke cities and strike groups as you want but keep in mind that the enemy has A LOT MORE than you, so i dont prefer using one, however you might need them so dont sell them yet :)AIRCRAFT(PLANES)Planes seems to have a good range to launch them and you can put unguided missiles and bombs in them, or a 37 mm gun that isnt as fast as the 37 mm autocannon. Bombs and UGM's are really good and they deal a good amount of damage. Really good for strike groups on the ground. (Sometimes they call for help when they get bombed sometimes they dont i have no idea why.)TARKHANSTarkhans are outlaws that can give you their ships and money and can even help you get hidden cities, funds, or faster repairs. You can recruit them by talking what they like and reach a certain point where they can join you or you can keep going and ♥♥♥♥ it up or increase it even more to get even more money.They really help you a lot so get them.VISUALSGREAT! The thrusters the guns the rain everything looks really good since its 2d! However your eyes might hurt a little because damn the flashing a lot. Not much more to say honestly its just great and really fits the theme.EXTRASOn easy mode you can save anytime and you can use this to load your save before entering a city to keep talking to an tarkhan and reload the save if you ♥♥♥♥ up which is really good.I dont know why but sometimes this game can run really slow and i dont know how and why it happens.Alright, thats it, i probably missed some stuff.FINAL SCORE: 8/10(i might edit the review later on to improve some stuff or correct stuff.)Great visualsFun combatNice music and soundsYou can nuke citiesIts not that easy to learn but itsn ot that much of a problem but REALLY HARD to master it.The game is a little complicated, due to the amount of mechanics this game has.I recommend buying it if it gets on sale but you can still buy it without it being on sale just to support them more.
