_childDocuments_.review: A hit-or-miss game that is both better and worse than it deserves.The game is not quite a metroidvania, not quite a zelda-like, not quite a JRPG.The exploration pattern is akin to a metroidvania, but the mobility upgrades aren't super revolutionary.The level design is reminiscent of Zelda-style action adventures in the combination of puzzles and semi-involved combat. But there's no true Zelda-style dungeons to speak of.It's got some JRPG vibes in how the story progresses through the world, but a lack of story-relevant bossfights and a comparatively low power gain throughout the game.The game has a lot of charm and an engaging story. With well-executed but not supremely great pixel art and a good-to-great soundtrack.The real tipping point is the combat and mobility. Both of which feel somewhat clunky, with more inertia to your movements than is common, and to a degree punishing knockback/ragdolling. Playing keyboard only didn't help my experience, though putting in more work on finding good keybinds for a Mouse & Keyboard setup might've helped the combat feel a lot more fluid.Still, combat upgrades like weapons and skills are overall pretty low impact compared to health and stamina upgrades. Not that they aren't impactful, but to a large degree, it felt like stocking the right amounts of healing items and just gaining a larger health reserve did more for combat than half the available upgrades. The lack of core mobility upgrades throughout the game also didn't help.The game has a lot of collectibles. More than warranted in my opinion, though a map and better mobility upgrades for backtracking would've done a lot to help as well.The world/story and the combat/exploration is what the game is about, and how enjoyable you find them is gonna be what decides if the game is enjoyable overall.In conclusion:The setting and story are very unique and well-constructed. Truly the highlight of the game.The graphics are pretty decent, though not overly spectacular. And the soundtrack is overall very good with some great pieces here and there.The combat is kinda unique, a lot more measured than the norm, and if you don't master the controls it can feel more punishing and clunky than it maybe should, largely due to inertia and knockback-ragdolling.The exploration and general gameplay is for the most part well-executed; there's a decent variety in kinds of puzzles and challenges, some of them felt really frustrating to me (in particular the ones involving enemy AI manipulation) and I expect someone else might be frustrated by something I enjoyed. The game is missing a map given the amount of backtracing for collectibles and secrets, and it's very light on mobility upgrades for it's format.It also has a really chill yet engaging fishing minigame.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: For all the deathtrap dungeons you have to surpass through the game, the ending is freaking terrible. I don't want to spoiler anything but it feels incomplete, and while the game has a lot of content most of it is just puzzles, and the general enjoyment of the game is determined by how much you can tolerate the clunky controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: I am heart broken about this game. I loved the first 16 hours, discovering new areas. Going back to the first dungeon with new items to discover new secrets. Doing some relaxing fishing. Doing side quests that are have pretty good dialog and world building. Just chatting to NPCs to get little flavor text that adds character. It is a joy to just experience, sadly that wasn't the whole game.The last 10 hours has slowly grown from just annoying with enemies that spam range attacks and challenges that are just a bit too tight for the game's controls. To the last major boss, that was spamming 12 enemies at a time while the boss charges. So it becomes impossible to avoid damage, and the whole combat system falls apart.I pushed pass that, and into the next visually interesting area, sadly I now had a sense of dread for the game. The enemies have been more annoying flyers, tiny hard to hit enemies, and towers that basically stun lock you if you get close to them. Plus more annoying design elements like platforms that are just high enough that you need a perfect jump to reach them or putting 5 plus enemies into a tight arena with you while you are encouraged to use a ineffective gimmick weapon.These harder elements reveal how clunky the controls are, how limited your attacks are, how quickly your stamina runs out, and the fact that you don't have I-frames after being hit so it's easy to eat 4 or 5 attacks from different enemies. The game mechanics don't hold up when the going gets tough, sadly even having the best equipment in the game doesn't help that.Now I hate playing the game. A single mistake might mean I get juggled halfway across the screen for 60+ damage(you start the game with 30 health). I miss playing the first 16 hours of the game. I don't have faith that the game will get any better from here. I'll just watch the rest of story online.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Never has a game captured me in the way Phoenotopia: Awakening did, from the moment I picked it up all I could do when I wasn't playing it was to think about continuing where I left off previously. I wonder if I even dreamt about it? It is an overlooked gem, very underrated. The game has a difficulty setting but I implore you to at least attempt to get used to the way it was meant to be played.If you value  in games then you can't go wrong here. There are many secrets to find, puzzles to complete and side quests to do. I even found myself talking to every single NPC! I wonder how many hours were put into the dialogue, it certainly was not lacking. It is a very charming game, colourful, vibrant. Very easy to lose yourself in this world and feel immersed. The pixel art looks great, and the music is stunning.The game can be quite frustrating at times (especially so when you are learning how the combat system works), it is challenging but never unfair. My only nitpick with this game would be how its story ended.All in all, Phoenotopia: Awakening is an amazing experience. Definitely one of the better metroidvanias out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: This game does a lot of things well but I felt like it was ultimately ruined by its poor combat and enemy design. It's not as difficult as games like Hollow Knight or Celeste but it is much, much more frustrating. Enemies feel like they were designed around a far more nimble and capable player character, and the Souls-style stamina system generally only forces you to waste time waiting around every so often rather than adding any real tactical tradeoffs. Certain critical combat abilities are hidden behind optional upgrades, which is great if you find them but makes the game even more frustrating if you don't. The difficulty/accessibility options make the game a little less tedious and frustrating in some aspects but they don't address the core problems with the design and controls.That said, if you can tolerate frustrating combat and some general gameplay jankiness then there's a lot to like here. There's a huge world that is fun to explore, with lots of secrets to find. The various environments are visually distinct and look great. The character animations also look great. The soundtrack is very good. Towns are lively and full of NPCs that have more interesting dialogue than most games of this type. There's some Metroidvania-like ability progression, where tools from later in the game let you find new things in earlier areas. In general you can tell that the game had a lot of heart put into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, amazing tribute to the old Zelda titles and an overall really enjoyable Metroidvania.+ tons of content (for real, the game is huge)+ great graphics and animations+ the soundtrack is epic+ dialogues are legit funny and enjoyable+ challenging gameplay+ tons of anime vibes- combat can feel a little slow and clunkyOverall this is a 10/10 game. A must-play for everyone who enjoys the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece of a game. The puzzlesI absolutely loved the puzzles in the game. A lot of them are physics based, timing based, and scattered all through out the world that it feels natural and immersive. I also particularly like the puzzles that use your arsenal to solve. The sliding puzzles were a bit meh, but that might just be my preference. Most of them are not too difficult, but they're hard enough to make you feel clever for solving them, either by deduction, skill, or being observant of the clues in the room. Hell they integrate puzzles in their world with the GEO club, which is a very fun idea.The dialogueI don't think I've consistently laughed at a game in a while, and this game's dialogue got me laughing throughout the whole adventure. It was probably one of the most charming things that kept me wanting to play more. Absolutely delighted when I got to a new area and have a new batch of NPCs I can talk to, and they can deliver some great one liners.The musicOh god is the music good. Sillythewilly did an awesome job, Stone Angel, Panselo, Caves of Mul, Moonlight Ravine, they are all peaceful melodic pieces I would listen outside the game. Some of the chiptune can be a bit annoying at first (like Thomas' theme) but it grows on you as you play the area. The battle music (especially the boss musics) perfectly captures the hectic feeling you get from fighting a new strong enemy, and made me feel hyped as hell to fight the bossesThe usability of your tight arsenalHaving no wall jumps, the spear is the main method for you to gain some verticality. I always like it whenever a weapon is also used for platforming, and the spear can also work as an explosive once you get the explosive upgrade. You can also use your bombs to use as a tiny platform, stacking two ticking bombs to gain some height, with a built in time limit before the bomb explodes. The aestheticWhile the pixel work itself seems to lack a bit of polish (for example the character sprites are a bit minimalsitic), the overall game aesthetic is very well designed. A lively desert city is adorned with decorations, colorful pots, carts, goods being sold, and colorful cloths hanged everywhere. They did an excellent job making a usually monotonous brown desert city stage looking colorful and pleasant to look at. A worn down abandoned bridge has tasteful debris scattered everywhere, walls crumbling, old statues falling apart, old mossy crates you can smash to get a few pennies. They create a very believable and natural amount of clutter to make the area look nice and realistic, like what'd you expect from say a club house, a laboratory, or a beautiful ravineThe cutenessThe game overall is very cute. From the frog, bee and slime enemies, characters like Fran, and of course the actions you can do. Crawling gives you a cute pacing sound, and if you bonk your head with a headbutt attack your character will rub her head in pain. And if you failed at cooking, it will blow up in your face.Other positive qualities I could think of-the touching aspects of the story (where Gail first came from, or when you find the young king's deceased parent's gift for him)-the accessibility options (because using stamina on normal attacks seem annoying as hell. I prefer eating in real time as it adds more challenge though. A lot of people had complained about the difficulty, and the devs themselves had admitted that they did an error on playtesting, by recruiting highly skilled playtesters (think Smash tourney regulars, and hardcore Dark Souls fans), but with the help of the accessibility options, you can smoothen the experience.What I didn't like much about the game-the later parts of the game My favorite aspects of the game, the funny dialogue and the colorful settings, decreased in the later parts of the game. These areas are:the Last Wall a wasteland of a once prosperous city, littered with ghoulish robots of ancient technology. While scary, fitting, and a good testament of the player's skill, I missed the more colorful areas while I was playing it. And zero funny dialogue in that area.E.D.E.N.a cold and heavily guarded laboratory. A difficult area of the game (which makes sense because it's the final area). But once again I miss the more colorful and cheerful areas. But at least there are some funny dialogues in the old entry logs. Between those two areas there are the Mul Caves and Aurantia however, two more colorful and lighthearted areas, so not all of the late game areas are like that.Overall I highly recommend this game. It is a very underrated gem, a very nice experience and my favorite game I played in 2021 so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10A long, long time ago humanity was quite developed and with vast knowledge, unfortunately people decided to use this knowledge to wage a war, the biggest war ever seen where practically all types of weapons were used, including the creation of artificial creatures just for combat. When the war finally ended, the few humans left decided to move to underground shelters and stay there, while nature recovered, now with its new residents created by humanity. ^^Many years later, humanity returns to the surface and begins to re-colonize this world, so familiar and yet so different. In this new world lives a young orphan girl with pink hair named Gail who lives in the orphanage in the small village of Panselo, having a quiet life helping to take care of the other children as she is one of the oldest. Everything was going well until one day that Gail needs to go to the forest in search of the other children who went to play, and which some of the children convince her to enter an ancient temple in search of a meteor that fell inside the temple, request which Gail answers, after all she really wants a new stuffed pony. But nothing prepared her for what she and the other children would see as they left the temple, a ship far more advanced than anything they had ever seen, appearing out of nowhere and capturing every adult in the village. ^^+ A vibrant and colorful world with all kinds of places to explore, from caves to forests, from hot deserts to villages with cherry blossoms, all very beautiful and lived with their own inhabitants and creatures.+ Well done Pixelated art, which combined with good animations makes the world even more alive and unique.+ Very funny and charismatic characters, everyone always has at least two dialogues to say, so I recommend talking to everyone at least twice and having fun with their lines and ideas.+ Music suitable for each environment that combine very well, in addition to being relaxing and helping to set the tone of each location.+ Many items to find and use during the adventure, as well as many ingredients that can be cooked to create various gastronomic delicacies, some of the description had make my mouth water.+ An unusual and very fun story, which takes our young protagonist to explore the most different corners of the world, encountering dangers and challenges but never losing her good humor and fun.- Achievements need to be redeemed within the game's achievements menu to be unlocked on Steam, so it's possible, as happened to me, to end up forgetting about them until you have several accumulated.- Manual save and only at certain points, which can be a little stressful, when we explore many places but we run out of life and because we haven't made a recent save, we have to explore everything again.This is how Gail's adventure begins, in a mix of adventure with platform, having to leave her small village while the other children take care of the place, leaving Gail free to go to the most varied places, from forests to caves, from sparkling lakes. to scorching deserts, always looking for information about the mysterious ship that took all the adults in the village, always accompanied by his faithful bat to protect herself, after all the world is full of monsters and creatures, but nothing that a few well-placed blows can't solve. ^^But this doesn't have to be a solitary adventure, after all along the journey Gail will meet the most varied types of people with the most varied types of personalities, some of which are quite fun, including the vast majority of these people having two options for dialogue, being for so I recommend always talking to everyone at least twice, who knows what they will have to say. It's something as good as good conversation is good food, and Gail can find several ingredients along the journey that she can cook when she finds a fire and make the most diverse dishes to recover life, and I must say that the description of some really left me hungry. ^^Produced by the Cape Cosmic studio that produced a very beautiful pixelated art, in which it is possible to recognize each of the characters being some of them very unique, as well as each of the cities with its own charm, and also the animations, many of them pretty and cute, my sincere congratulations to the team that took care of the art. In the soundtrack part we have light and fun songs that in my opinion match the light theme of the story, making a good combination of music with art. ^^Phoenotopia: Awakening was a fun surprise for me, I started a short time ago, but I really liked what I've seen so far of this world that has a somewhat dark story at the beginning, but then brightens up in a fun and colorful world where we explore looking to bring back the normality of the village and home of our little but brave protagonist with pink hair, who despite her young age already knows how to defend herself from monsters, and loves stuffed ponies. ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: It makes me genuinely sad that more people have not yet discovered this absolute gem.Beautiful visuals.Wonderfull score.Excellent puzzles.Tight gameplay that perfectly merges fast paced action with the more strategic elemets of rpg's.Worldbuilding, dialogue, story, exploration, bossfights, the list of elements that Phoenotopia absolutly nails is incredible.A huge amount of content, especially if you choose to explore the vast amount of optional quests and areas.The only thing I could see being off putting to some would be the difficulty. Luckily the game allows some tweaking in this regard both in togglable options and through gameplay, but an easy mode to allow more people to enjoy Phoenotopia would be welcome.Phoenotopia: Awakening is by all measurements of quality a true masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: So far i had only made it to the Ouroborous trials, so maybe later some upgrades will change some of the problems game have for the better, but, nevertheless, problems there are.The game is very good in terms of visual design, music and exploration.But, unfortunately, it is full of questionable game design decisions.First - it is controls. It is overcomplicated and, through that, somewhat irritating. I can understand stamina management, it was in many games like Secret of Mana. I can understand, that charge attack is supposed to slow you down. But there are many enemies, that move incredibly abruptly - and that invalidates using charge attack for anything but crushing the crates.Second - cooking minigame. It is fun on it's own, but you either have to tediously do it with every next item, reequipping each next stack, or stay with inferior healing items.Third - incredibly high health of many "random encounter" enemies. It is not, that you cannot just escape them, it is when you are going to get some ingredients/money from them - each of this encounters feels like it is miniboss at least.Fourth - VERY strange dash and dash jump. Dash itself just stops, when you jump, when you fall to the lower surface, any second you are disconnected from the ground - and it does not continue/start, if you still hold dash button. More than that - it is not a modifier button as in "hold dash and right to run right", it is a movement button, that moves you in the direction, that character is faced - so, in several platforming moments, when you need to dash jump betweer branches quickly, because they break under the character, in many cases you just fly away in the wrong direction. And because of all of that, dash jump itself works equally bad.Fifth - most enemies and enemies combinations are designed with intention to trick you - beginning with mentioned earlier  abrupt movement and attacks, followed by combination, when there is "sniper" enemies, that throw their projecties aiming at you - not just in your direction as in left-right-up-down, but actually aiming. And this enemies are usually go in packs of 2 to 4 or combined with melee's, that actively and very aggressively follow you.Shooting is also quite questionable - aiming the crossbow just feels wrong - combined with much less predictable and abrupt movement of enemies and high stamina consumption with not that high damage against said enemies.Towns - they are overloaded, It is cool, when there are details, when there are lore NPCs, but there are just too many of everything. Maybe developers had tried to create the effect of "lost in the city, exploring", but it just feel tedious.So, the game itself is not that hard on it's own, yet combination of controls, enemy behaviour, overuse of minigames, too many NPCs, that look like they are quest ones, but actually not, makes this game somewhat tiring. It have many puzzles involving crates, jumping, using the sling etc, but the gameplay itself just feels wrong. Again, should at least controls would be less strange, this game would be much better and less irritating, but so far it have very good world, but very bad means to explore it - unique experiment, yes, but not a good one.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game! It's such a unique and interesting mix of an RPG and Metroidvania. There's a world map you can walk around with towns and dungeons and sidequests and everything but the towns and dungeons are all setup in a metroidvania style. There's no exp, you power up by finding hidden items that raise your health or stamina. The game really focuses on exploration and puzzle solving which I really loved. There's literally hundreds of secrets to find. The combat can maybe be a bit janky at times. Some of the boss fights felt really difficult and unfair. But other than that this game was an absolute masterpiece. It was 100% right up my alley and I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much ever since the original released on newgrounds.its got creative enemies. cool locations and dungeons. fun puzzles. a zelda 2 overworld. fishing. fun bosses. cool upgrade progression and lots of sidequests and optional content and locations. fun achievements... great story and npc dialogue...i love it so much and it genuinely hurts me seeing these negative reviews i just....i love it man
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my all-time favorite game, it feels like a love letter to what games can be: soothing, fun, challenging, and rewarding. Everything from the music to the environmental design to the gameplay mechanics and associated animations are thoughtful and meticulously crafted. It's a clear passion piece and testimant to the skill of everyone involved without being pretentious or losing its sense of humor. If you played the Newgrounds version, you'll appreciate the outstanding new content and updated redraft, if you're new to it welcome to a real gem.The biggest general quibble with it is the difficulty level (there are no autosaves and combat is hard), but as a pretty casual gamer who tends to play on storymode and quit when things get tough, I can say that the accessibility settings on this make it much more manageable, and so long as you're exploring all the areas have to offer (which is fun! you should do it regardless because there's just so many layers of eastereggs!), you'll find it progresses at a very reasonable pace and never becomes unplayably hard. I think it's important to remember during that this is a slow-paced game about timing, attention to detail, and exploration . These principles are applied to everything, including combat, so a little bit of patience will get you pretty far when it comes to understanding the gameplay mechanics. I'm super excited to see what's next for this series and this studio, a truly fantastic debut title!
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 for sure. Maybe 11/10 just to be safe. Definitely recommended. This game has incredible spirit. It feels like the old 2D zelda games if only the developers had access to better technology. The game design here is immaculate, every pixel thought through. I realize that many people will find the combat system annoying, and will call it too difficult. But they don't get it. That's the point! You are a little girl against monsters and war machines. OF COURSE combat is difficult! The difficulty is part of what I love! A video game that doesn't coddle it's players to make it more accessible. But it doesn't just make it crazy difficult and leave it, like so many other games have done. Instead, if you allow yourself to be invested in the story, the game will make you WANT to continue, and WANT to develop the skills necessary to be good at the game. This is a point where many other games fail. Now, to be fair, I have not played a great deal of indie games, yet somehow I do feel confident that this is a game that stands out for its game design. Here's hoping for a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Phoenotopia expecting a short, generic, fairy tale-like game with typical RPG elements. But, within the first 2-5 hours of the game, I found myself constantly stopping to appreciate the extensiveness, charm and quality this game has. Every area is varied and full of life, the beautifully composed music scores range from sombre to exhilarating, the NPC's all have unique and interesting dialogues that make them worth stopping to read, every corner is full of secrets to find. There's a reason to explore and take in the world Phoenotopia has given you, like its an adventure in its own right.It wasn't just that it surpassed my initially low expectations, making me give favour to it. It matched the quality of so many other games I've played and loved, on par with titles like Momodora/Minoria, CrossCode, Hollow Knight, Starbound, Katana Zero, etc. While maybe not in quantity, definitely in quality. Even during the down times of being lost for hours, to getting a headache over trying to figure out the puzzles, every second of the game was absorbing, fun, gorgeous, well designed and interesting. From the tight, engaging combat with clearly telegraphed but difficult bosses, to the quirky and adorable animations, to the beauty of the world itself, the multitude of varied and unique areas, themes, races and people. All of this beautifully weaved together without them feeling out of place, forced together or overly inspired (except the few blatant references to other games, which honestly, I'm a fan of it). While it's story was quite simplistic, it still had unexpected turns and twists that lead down paths I didn't think most games like it would, keeping me interested and making it all feel satisfying. Not to mention that the dialogues and events outside the story bits only added to the emotional investment in world itself and the characters. There was never a plain or dull moment.Phoenotopia is one of those games that occasionally pops up to remind me why I love games so much. The quality, allure and immersion a game can generate, how it can suck you in and take you on an adventure in a world full of life and charm, all from the amount of care, passion and thoughtful design the developers put into it. I genuinely couldn't have asked for better, only for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: This game delivers every promise it makes. It improves on every aspect of the original (flash) game and sets up a complete world to explore, with enough stuff to do to make it as rewarding as a game like this can be.The art style is beautiful, the music is amazing, the story is enjoyable and immersive, the dialogues are very well written. There are a variety of moods throughout the story, where the more emotional bits are surprisingly well achieved.As an early follower of the creator's dev blog, I'm no stranger to the effort they've put into this and, in my opinion, it's been more than worth it. Congratulations to the team for making this jewel of a game!The only downsides I can think of are probably regarding the difficulty of a few puzzles, which may seem a bit unfair if not properly equipped. Other than that, I have nothing to say.The story may be similar to the flash game's, but this version has a lot more to offer. More characters, organizations, areas to explore, music, engaging dialogues... I played the flash version and this one surprised me a lot nevertheless. It's definitely something different.With an expected minimum playtime of 30 hours and given the experience it offers, I'd say it's totally worth the shot. Buy this and spread the word, up until now it's been criminally overlooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: The game I've been waiting for for a few good years.I should start off with the artstyle. I consider it a great extension of the OG flash game's - featuring softer lighting and brighter colours, it really has this "soft and cozy" feel to it. It's fun to see how prettier everything got - from locations, now having certainly more details to themselves, both lore-wise and aesthetic-wise, through NPCs who got a major overhaul, where even ones with two lines have more "visual personality" and UIs, ending on the grand non-pixel images like the start menu background or the first cutscene.Hearing many of the old tracks mixed with the new ones was fun too! The way they expand on visuals' climate really cements a location's feel. (As you can see, I don't know how to discuss music)The plot is engaging, and formerly sort of dull personalities of the flash were changed and built upon, too! Lore can be digested both via dialogue and via environment - my favourite piece was an ancient building in south-east of Atai, it had such an interesting puzzle not because of its "puzzle" elements (though I liked them too, even if I kept failing) - it was just jam-packed with history despite only using maybe 30 words overall.Puzzles can be hard at times, though. That needs to be said. Lots of them require quite specific, fast movement. Even though most of them aren't required, I believe that it may be helpful for people. I don't believe it's a bad thing! It can just get a bit frustrating, at times.I know that a lot of people said it, but while I adore the effort, the locations are. HUGE. It's very easy to get lost in your average city, and the amount of NPCs can be a bit overwhelming. And I say it as a person who loves talking to them for lore. After some time I just stop caring, unfortunately. And I can't shake off the feeling that I'm missing out on something important...The combat is usually enjoyable. The beginning of Doki Forest feels quite hard at the beginning, even now when I'd estimate I'm 33% through the game with decent gear for this level, but it gets better after that. I mean, I am playing with all the Accessibility Options on, because I'm not very experienced in that sort of stuff, so I don't really know what the game is like without them, haha. I struggled with one boss after that, but that's more because I didn't have a lot of food on myself, so it's more my fault anyway.Overall, the game is very pleasant to play, even if it can be overwhelming at times. But don't let that discourage you, I can absolutely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: This game is difficult to review for me. I love the artstyle, the characters/writing, and then sheer amount of heart just put into the world  building and design. But the controls are very dated. From my understanding this is a remake of a flash game, which would make sense considering the game design is full of harsh and punishing mechanics that cause you to have to backtrack and grind a whole lot. In my teenage years I would have put 100 hours into minmaxing and searching out the secrets and collecting everything. At my current point in life, I have to meter the amount of time I put into this game to be able to enjoy it, which I definitely do. It heavily reminds me of cavestory and old zelda game, but with perhaps even more dated combat clunkiness. Overall I would say that I love this game, but would only recommend this to people who are good at not being frustrated about game design and are fine with backtracking a whole bunch. IF you can look past these lacking design choices then this is the perfect game for you because it is truly a masterfully crafted game if you get past all the oldschool bloat.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece for me. It's like Zelda 2 on a scale that is beyond big.  36 hours I spent to beat the main story, took what I thought was a lot of time doing side stuff.  Ending tells me only 55% completion!  This is a deceptively large game overflowing with content.  The core gameplay is great, the music is fantastic, and exploring every inch of this world is delight.  Highly recommend this if you like metroidvanias or Zelda 2 from the old NES.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wasn't expecting the game to be as long as it was. Took me roughly 35 hours to finish it and I didn't even get to collect everything. I absolutely loved the minor things that Gail does. The little bop and yawn after you rest, the sounds she makes when she goes for the headbutt, and especially the random teleport collapse. All very cute.That said, the game definitely could have played a bit better. I did enjoy playing through it but there was enough mechanics that irked me that made it frustrating at time. For starters, your sprint cancels if you fall off a platform or land a jump. It felt like an unnecessary mechanic and really should have just let you keep sprinting. Jumping was also frustrating at times since the direction Gail is facing is locked after you jump and you can't turn to face the other way mid jump. The game defaulting to no i-frames is also a really weird game design choice. If you aren't careful you could end up getting combo'd until you die. There are gameplay accessibility options that you can turn on and one of them is getting some i-frames after getting hit twice in succession but it really should have been the default.As for non-mechanical things, the puzzles in the game were for the most part pretty simple or easy to figure out. There were only a few puzzles that actually required me to whip out a notepad to jot things down for. Nothing a bit of trial and error couldn't fix. The character dialogue was really enjoyable. I found myself actually laughing at some of the things that the NPCs said or did. The story was interesting but a bit lackluster and anti-climatic. I didn't realize the final boss fight was even happening because it didn't really give off a "final boss" vibe. I'm aware this is a remaster of the original game and there is an original Phoenotopia 2 so hopefully they'll remaster that as well to resolve the story.The one thing that REALLY bothered me was the secret boss. I wanted to fight it but the game locks you out of fighting it until you have max HP and Stamina. There's in-game way to check which HP/Stamina upgrades you've found and needing to find all of them just to fight the secret boss seems like an excessive lockout. I really didn't want to go find a guide to get all the upgrades and go check each spot to make sure I had the upgrade.Overall: 8.5/10. Despite the minor annoyances the game was still an overall enjoyable experience and I would 100% play a remaster of the second game if they ever did one. Definitely worth picking up if you want a game to kill some hours with.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: PHoenotopia has a lot going for it: Charm, interesting story, decent characters, an enormous yet full world, lots of good puzzles, good inventory system, lots of side-quests, good pixel graphics and animation, varied monsters. But somehow, it totally sucks to play, in a way that's hard to pin down. Most obviously, the combat feels off, and there is a TON of combat. The controls feel like you're fighting your character, and struggling to get your attacks out, more than facilitating your skill. It's very hard to avoid getting pinged by the numerous traps and enemy ranged attacks, which are all over the place.As a result, you're constantly getting drained, chipped-away at. This leads to the murkier problem: The math is just off. You take too much damage, there are too many sources of damage, and healing is too little and too far between. You have to be constantly hunting up food items, and then spend time cooking them, just to stay at a safe level of health. The inns are very few and far between, and save points don't restore you. I can easily see getting stuck in the middle of a dungeon or cave, not able to move forward or even back out, because you've run out of food, your health is low, and there's stuff just pinging you all over the place.The end result is very strange--this seems like mostly a kids' game, by tone, by story, by graphics. But it's far too long and complex to be fun at that level, and the frustration at getting constantly battered about and desperate for health sources is far too aggravating to appeal to a young player. Even the challenges are too closely-timed, considering the muddy controls. Players, especially young players, don't like being confronted with constant failure.It would take a nigh-total overhaul to fix this. Hopefully these problems can get tuned for another game, because what's good here is very good. But the bad makes it borderline unplayable. I found myself dreading booting the game up to take another crack at advancing; that's never a good sign.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original, Awakening is EVERYTHING you want in a remake. If you haven't played the original Phoenotopia... well, it was really good for a flash game; easily one of the best out there. This game checks all the boxes for me: challenging gameplay (with a unique modular method of handling difficulty to allow less-skilled players to enjoy it), wonderful storytelling, and a beautiful musical score. If you're into Metroidvania type games but also like heavy stories, I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Phoenotopia Awakening is a gorgeous, intricately designed video game. It's something like a Zelda title infused with a certain amount of Cave Story and - somehow - a smattering of Dark Souls... but there's honestly nothing quite like it.Phoenotopia started out as a Flash game on Newgrounds almost a decade ago. I think it's fair to say that the content appearing on Newgrounds during its heyday was... somewhat variable: a lot of games uploaded there were janky, forgettable or just plain bad, with a few gems standing out as interesting proofs of concept. And then there was Phoenotopia: innovative in its own right, but more than just a proof of concept - it knew its influences and could see a gaping void where a game of its sort really *ought* to exist. It felt like cheating to be given that game for free.I was delighted to learn that a remake was in the works. The developer considers the Flash game a first draft, and having finally played the commercial release, I am once again blown away by the breadth and quality of the vision behind this project. Phoenotopia Awakening provides a fully-realised world with a far more substantial and expansive challenge than I had anticipated, even after fully expecting a far grander work than the earlier iteration of Phoenotopia.Its dungeons are artfully designed, each one unique and interesting; its puzzles are similarly well-constructed, developing in complexity in a highly engaging manner; its combat, while not perhaps as fluid as I might have initially hoped for, proved extremely satisfying to master, such that I'm not sure in retrospect that I'd want any tweaks to it; there was that special sense of achievement at overcoming each of the later bosses that fans of the likes of Hollow Knight ought to appreciate.The pixel art and music are utterly beautiful - I've been listening to the latter fairly obsessively over the last month, while the former shows a facility for colour that left me gawking in sheer wonder at several of the game's environments. In gameplay, world building and aesthetics alike, the level of detail is illustrative of just how much care went into this passion project.The difficulty curve of Phoenotopia Awakening is smooth but perhaps a little steep for some. I enjoyed the challenge, but the game does include a decent range of accessibility options for those who would benefit from them. I loved every minute of my playthrough, and heartily recommend this game to any fan of classic Zelda, metroidvania, or well-conceived 2D action games generally.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: In my days I've played a LOT of metroidvanias. They're by far my favorite genre of game. I own probably most of the metroidvanias on steam. And throughout all of that, Phoenotopia: Awakening is probably one of the best ones I've ever played. It does some things better than some of the greats like Hollow Knight, Super Metroid, Ori. Of course all of those are greater in certain parts than this, that's for sure. But I think the fact that this game that's flown under the radar can-- in my opinion-- compete with the greats of the genre is incredible.Pros:+Art strikes a perfect balance between detail and simplicity with the art style. And it's cute as hell.+Puzzles are great. There are very few times in the game where a puzzle is actually repeated. It always kept fresh. And for the most part they're good and have fun AHA moments. throughout the game there was maybe 3 puzzles that I couldn't figure out, and had to look up, and with only 1 of them did the solution not make sense.+Music is pretty good. Not the best, I'd say others have it better, but they do a great job of setting the mood, and there's some tracks that are incredible.+Above just about any other metroidvania i've played, it REALLY rewards exploration. There's been a lot of neat moments of exploring someplace and finding something neat, or exploring all the side paths.+Character interactions are great, just about every npc has at least 2 unique lines that you can chat with them with. And there's a lot of NPC's+A LOT of stuff. I'm about 35 hours in, and I just finished the final boss with 80% completion. And it's been fresh the entire time.+There's a fishing minigame. As time goes on I think any games is incomplete if you don't have a fishing minigame.Not cons, not pros: Some of these may be cons to you, but to me, they weren't.  But weren't pro's eithero There's no map. Usually that really sucks for metroidvanias for me, but as I kept playing the game I didn't really find that an issue. That's usually a lot of points off for me, but the levels and such are designed in a way it's very difficult to actually get lost (probably mostly because there's an overworld to go to different areas. But even in the most complicated areas i never really got lost.o The story isn't incredible. It serves it's purpose well, but it's not especially hard hitting.o Combat. It's very basic. You have smack, heavy smack, and then some side weapons that there's only really 2 that have much function in combat unless there's a puzzle element to a boss that requires using one of the others. There's also an energy system that I don't know if it added to the game. I won't say whether the game is better without it, especially because one can lower difficulty to minimize that.o Grinding. I had to do very little, but it's still something that I needed to do at one point, and to 100% the game there's more to be done. I'm not putting this as a negative only because i had to do it so little. Otherwise exploration and side quests kept my wallet decently full.o No quest tracker. This one is very close to being a purely con, but again, it never really was an issue for me.o A purely personal one, but I think a smidge more lore would have been great. There's just still some questions and or details that I think would really bring the world just that step higher. There's enough details to get a nice bit of lore... but just a bit more would have been great. Maybe in the sequel that's probably going to happen?o Difficulty. It was a very comfortable level of difficult for me, but I'm very experienced in these types of games, this may differ for you.Con:Aside from the ones that for YOU might be a con? None. A couple of things were close, but just... weren't enough of a problem to really be a con. This game is very well designed. If i had to pick something, some enemies were kinda annoying to deal with.And finally to address some complaints that I've seen, and my perspective.Combat is bad: It's a bit limited, but It's functional. It's roughest in the early game, but even then the short range and stamina didn't feel BAD. It's not like i kept accidentally running into enemies because the range is short, when you get hit you get knocked back, but especially if you learn to ukemi it's barely a loss of time. Juggling is very rare, and that usually happens when you let yourself get surrounded.Enemies are tanky: I don't particularly understand this one. So long as you don't completely ignore weapon upgrades, i never felt there was a point where there was any enemy that took too many hits. Except maybe boars in the overworld encounters. They kinda take too many hits for being as slippery as they are, but they're also completely and easily avoidable. It's not like other ones where after a point all early enemies die from one hit, but I really wouldn't regard it as bad.Movement is clunky: I didn't get this, sprinting and rolling takes a little bit of a learning curve, but soon enough it's easy. It's no La-Mulana or early castlevania level of jumping. There were only a few points where I felt it was a bit too hard to get the precision I needed with the movement options. otherwise I was able to be as precise as needed to properly platform as needed.Grind: I only grinded at one point. There's only really one point of the game that gates continuing the main story behind money. I grinded a bit to get more money, and then never after that. I just collected, sold, and explored.No Map: I didn't find it an issue as explained above.Though a bit of disclaimer: Like I said, I've played a ton of metroidvanias, from the clunkiest to the smoothest, so in some of these my perspective may greatly differ from the other player's experience. But this is the game that I played and enjoyed, in my mind.TL:DR: An absolutely incredible metroidvania, at least for me. 8.5-9.0/10 for a normal game, 10/10 metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying this is a game I really liked, and I can understand why some people might find it too annoying or difficult at the beginning (or during their whole playthrough). I didn't particularly enjoy the combat and the stamina system at the beginning. There're some difficulty settings to make it less annoying but I wanted to experience the game without them. I would also recommend the devs disable the "you might want to lower the difficulty" message post-death after a few times (or make it appear every X deaths), which was one of the reasons I could've seriously dropped it for (it took me a while to find there's a setting that turns it off forever).Now, imo this game has something not many titles can claim: it has a certain charm of its own. Every character has a personality or quirk that sets them apart. The world might come up as "tiny" until you realize there're plenty of places to explore and things to do. Some of the side quests might have you helping a random character and later seeing little changes on some of the areas; or sometimes there's not a noticeable change in the world but they still feel meaningful. There's one particular cutscene on the desert town that is very endearing and I would've loved to see it again later. Thankfully, there's YouTube.The music is top tier and I really like most of the soundtrack. The battle pieces are epic and don't get boring, the calm music is relaxing, and each place has its own thing. There're plenty of tracks I got to love, sometimes ending up staying in an area just to hear them for a bit. You later get an instrument which lets you play some of the pieces for different effects, much like Ocarina of Time.There're also many puzzles, whether to traverse an area or to get an item. Some are clearly shown as puzzles (a specific type of dungeon), and others are not plain to the eyes. A few of them involve playing specific notes on the instrument, others require moving boxes, and some intended solutions might involve using the enemies. I might've done several of the puzzles in a non-intended way, oops.While yes, sometimes the combat or the platforming were a bit too annoying, the bosses often have a special "thing" you can do which makes the fight less brute-forcey. I do suggest going for a max health / stamina run if you're going with the higher difficulty (a hard requirement for the hardest, optional boss), and trying to max out / get most of the equipment available.The main weapon is a melee bat which takes a bit getting used to (not sure I got used to it tbh), and later you'll find some secondary weapons which you might find easier to use.Overall, I think the game is really good once it gets going. There're plenty of places to explore, things to do, people to get to know. I found myself wanting to know what came "next", what was at the end of the dungeon, what else to learn about the world. I was surprised when I learned it didn't sell well, but I also happened to found it by accident. I hope this review helps bump it up and convinces more people to get lost in this wonderful world.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a metroidvania. It is more akin to a (mostly) side-scrolling action RPG, with a big world and linear area progression with a bit of open-world questing and exploration in each area. Some have compared it to classic Zelda games and it's definitely got that vibe. Pros are nice presentation, some lovely character designs and animation work. The music mix is deceptively variable and some of the tracks are fantastic. It is a really nice world to explore, full of flavourful NPCs. This is a game I really wanted to like as it is clearly a labour of love... which may be the problem. Reason why I don't recommend it is combat and platforming difficulty on 'challenges'. It is not 'hard' as such, but it is unforgiving and requires a certain level of technical skill. The player is expected to experiment to learn the techniques that you won't find out about in game until after you need them (yes, you can go wiki-diving instead). Uneven difficulty jumps encountered in only the first two areas do not help. Difficulty options are available (if a bit obtuse to understand initially) but they do not help the fundamental areas that make it feel so frustrating for me. Veterans and devs have clearly spent a lot of time polishing this gem but in doing so they have overtuned things to their (high) ability. I have not finished this game and have given up in frustration in the second area (bandit combat trial). Yes, it is possible to 'master' the game to proceed but if you lack the technical and precise skills that this game demands then, like me, you find find it frustrating rather than challenging. If you do enjoy or are able to overlook the skill demanded then there is a lot to like. I cannot recommend it though; not without first trying a demo and seeing if the combat 'clicks' with you first, because if it doesn't, it will bar your enjoyment of the rest of this seemingly lovely game.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a crime that this game isn't more popular. There is a lot of game play and it's really fun and unique. Don't let the art style fool you. This game is NOT easy, but it's also not brutally difficult. The game uses the Breath of the Wild healing mechanic where you find food and then cook it to get more health from it, but there's a little cooking mini game you have to do in order to successfully cook the food, which gets harder the stronger the food is.The bosses are fun and challenging, but my only real gripe is that a couple bosses require you to do pixel perfect jumps to avoid their attacks which can get pretty frustrating. Maybe it's because I have been playing souls-likes, but it would be cool if the roll had invisibility frames so it felt more useful especially when you are in a tight situation. Other than that, I feel like the bosses require a good amount of skill, but aren't like souls bosses where you need 10+ attempts depending on the boss.There are a lot of items to collect and a lot of lore to find. The game really rewards you for going out of your way. All the towns feel alive and exciting. The soundtrack for the game is excellent. Some real bangers in it. Something the game does that I have never seen before in a metroidvania is have a Golden Sun/JRPG type of map where when you have a chance to encounter enemies as you travel from place to place. It's very unique and it's not as random as something like Pokemon battle encounters. If you play it, you will see what I mean.Overall, even though I haven't gotten every single item or 100% the game (I have beaten the final boss), I totally recommend this game. It will scratch that metroidvania itch you may have and definitely require you to use your brain!I give it an 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence with this game due to it's current "Mixed" reviews, hopefully I can convince you it's worth your time and money. While some of the Negative reviews have some justifiable reasons to rate the game where they did, ultimately I believe this game has more positive, and it's got a nice charm to it that you can't miss out on. I highly recommend it!=====THE GOOD=====1. Fantastic pixel art, maps are vibrant and well-decorated, nice animations and attention to detail.2. Each map is laid out well, fun platforming, and some fun sliding block puzzles and traps to keep the game interesting.3. You slowly unlock new items to keep the game fresh from a slingshot, bomb, crank lamp, fishing rod, flute, and a few more. The flute is especially fun. You have 5 notes you can enter (based on the direction you press), and each tune you play has different effects.4. While combat is pretty bland and repetitive for melee with no special attacks outside of a heavy charged attack, you do eventually get a slingshot and bow (to purchase). This can help switch up combat. I'm enjoying it so far, and I don't think it's as bad as some are saying (with the exception of the few gripes below).5. Slight customization! You play the same character, but you do have the ability to purchase new hair colors, and when you buy new clothing/armor, your appearance changes further. This is a nice feature to keep the game interesting if you're like me and love changing up your character's look :-)6. Tons of side content, hidden treasures, and puzzles to keep the game interesting. You might stumble across an abandoned tower with a sliding block puzzle while you navigate to the top. Your reward is a boost to stamina. It's nice the devs put in extra effort for some side content.7. The overworld map is fun to navigate, random battles can be easily avoided (if you don't want to take part), and there's a ton of additional side locations to explore!8. The game has fishing, and it's fun! It also has cooking... which is also enjoyable :-)9. Boss fights are a blast! They have unique abilities you must overcome, and a lot of thought and time went into creating them. For example... the armored toad that you can't just melee hit from the front. You can attack from behind for small damage, but it also does a vacuum attack where it's attempting to suck you up and eat you for high damage. If you throw a bomb, it'll suck that up and take increased damage, plus get stunned. Very fun battle!=====MY GRIPES=====1. There is NO map or quest log, which is the game's biggest downfall IMO. It feels very old school (NES days) where you have to actually pay attention to what NPC's say and figure things out on your own.2. While you can get used to combat, the range of your melee weapon is very short, which can get pretty frustrating, and you only have a quick attack and slower charged attack. You can't attack out of a sprint, rolling doesn't do much, and combat can get a bit repetitive IF you focus on melee only. Your only weapon (even with upgrades) is a bat, and the jump attack is slow and takes some getting used to. However, if you take the time to learn, it can be a lot of fun.3. There's no auto-save, which takes you way back to the old school days. This can get extremely annoying if you forget to save. Not sure why the devs chose to keep this really convenient feature that a majority of games have out of their game.4. Occasionally you come across a cat. You're not allowed to pet it... -_- Rude!Overall this has been a fun little adventure, there's a lot of content and it's a decent sized game! I feel it's well worth the price and time to try it out. Maybe you can't look past some of the wonky combat, but I got used to it, and love it. There's also a pretty steep learning curve to the dash and platform jumping, but once you master it... you'll do fine and it's enjoyable. I love this game, and I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: To really enjoy my RPGs, they need to have two things: far more adventuring than fighting, and having new places to explore in old areas once new abilities are unlocked. What can I say: I love the exploring. Give me a huge map over boss battles any day.And Phoenotopia delivers on this in droves. Not only is there a lot to explore (and re-explore), but there's also a huge diversity in each area. When you have a game set in the post-apocalyptic future of a scientifically created fantasy world, you can have the best of all settings. Whether it's a pastoral town, a futuristic city built underwater, a village deep in the woods inhabited by trolls & harpies, a bombed out hellscape, or a cave full of giant mutant bugs, this game has it!And the gameplay is pretty fun too, I guess. There's one extremely overpowered boss in the middle, which was infuriating. Plus the difficulty to execute attacks that seem like they should be standard can be a bit frustrating. But the limitation of movesets can offer fun unique experiences, too. (You're never able to double jump, for instance, but you can hover laterally for quite a long time.)I definitely recommend this game to anyone who likes adventure-heavy RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Has good level design, tons of puzzles and secrets. The combat can be a bit clunky, but it has its charm and you'll get used to it, also can get quite involved after you get new weapons and learn new moves. The bosses are good too, though I found some of them having almost unavoidable attacks a bit annoying, but you can tank through them fine.Also I recommend using a pen and paper to make notes, cause the game has no quest log or map, and there's a lot of areas that can't be accessed without an ability you'll learn later, and remembering every single one is pretty much impossible. Also useful for solving some of the puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an underrated gem, and my favorite game of the past few years.The controls and combat can be a bit clunky, especially early on, but if you can get past that, everything else about this game is brilliant - the soundtrack, the art, the world design, the secrets and puzzles - it's just a really fantastic experience to constantly stumble into deep and totally unexpected new areas. Secrets are everywhere - I was shocked how much I had missed in certain areas when I went for 100% using the hint system. Entire subareas with unique art and music hidden behind easily-missable secret doors. If that style of exploration appeals to you, I strongly recommend Phoenotopia, and urge you to push past any initial struggles.As an aside, I do think the combat in Phoenotopia is a lot of fun once you get used to it. The special techniques and additional weapons you pick up add a lot of depth to the combat system that isn't present at the beginning when you're just whacking enemies with a bat and pelting them with your slingshot. There's a particular late-game item that made the melee combat *significantly* more fun for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: I was a fan of the original Flash game, so I've been following the development of this remake for what felt like ages. I'm very pleasantly surprised with how much new content there is so far! All of the additional puzzles are fun, and I like the addition of the fishing, cooking, and flute mechanics. I feel like the combat was also improved so that it relies more on learning enemy behavior and dodging attacks than the original did. The beautiful graphics and music have created an enchanting world full of new discoveries~
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Phoenotopia Awakening was a delight to play. The game exudes charm with its lovely pixel art, soundtrack, and characters. The game's main strength is its world that is filled to the brim with exciting areas to explore, useful collectibles to grab, side quests that earn you new abilities, and puzzles that are a step above most indie, Zelda styled games that I've played.The story is pretty interesting and not what you'd expect from the cheerful and colorful world you explore in the beginning. Once I got to a certain point in the plot; I realized that this is, basically,  which is not a complaint by any means.Its main weakness is the combat which is not bad but a bit wonky. I sometimes found it difficult to aim with the bow or land a hit with the needlessly short ranged melee weapon, which was frustrating, but it wasn't a big enough problem to impact my enjoyment of the game.I put in about 60 hours into Phoenotopia and it was a joy to play from start to finish. I'm a big fan of these retro styled indie games and this is definitely one of the better ones on Steam. If you're even a little interested in this game, buy it. its worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best metroidvania games around, at the top level in almost all aspects including storytelling, visual design, music, level design, exploration, puzzle etc., while most other good games usually fail in one or more. The playtime is also the longest in the genre, providing ~70 hours of gameplay for completionists and none of it is brainless grinding. One thing I like is the Zelda-like exploration rewards here because everyone is useful; contrast to castlevania-like rewards which usually come in the form of weapons or equipment that don't suit your character and are eventually useless in the playthrough. Also the game offers many abilities to play with but doesn't focus on one ability in any part of the game, so all the abilities gathered and upgraded are useful. These two are perhaps among many other thoughts put into the brilliant game design here.The combat system is the only part that receives mixed review among the player base, but I think it's an expectation issue because the combat is designed to rely more on planning and strategy instead of quick reflexes. This remake has allowed more freedom in enemy encounters compared to the original flash game where every enemy is to be dealt with exactly one pixel- and time-precise way, and many accessible options are available if players prefer a different playstyle. Bosses can be challenging in the first try but recovery items should be abundant enough for the player to beat them.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of the best games that I've never seen anyone talking about.  Absolute MASTERCLASS of gaming here folks.  Music, Sound Effects, Spritework, Design, Background Art, Dialog and Story, EVERYTHING.  10/10 if you like games you will like Phoenotopia.  This is up there with hollow knight for me after only 3 hours played.After 45 hours, this has been an experience.  I used to think gameplay hailed above all, and Phoenotopia has it down to a notch, but it has a charm that many great games fall short of.  There can be a lot of backtracking, but there doesn't have to be.  There can be a lot of frustration with puzzles but most of those are optional.  This is a tough game, but not a hard game.  Even the hardest platforming segments will become routine faster than a fromsoft boss, and the combat can easily be overcome with enough food or just being patient.  I reccommend playing on medium difficulty the first time through.  This makes normal attacks take no stamina, and food items take no time to recover HP.
