_childDocuments_.review: If there was a netural rating, I would probably give this game that. I don't use positive rating values for games that are meh or just "not bad". People don't seek out games that are meh or not bad, they want games that are fantastic, games that are mediocre but get positive ratings dilute the ability to sort through what's great and what's not. In any case, my neutral / bad rating is based on a few of the game's, imho, biggest problems.1. The first is the checkpoint system. When you die in the game, you can only return back to where you last saved, and if that save point is before a really annoying (though a game shouldn't have really annoying, challenging sure, but not really annoying -- there's a difference) point and you die and there was not a place you could save up to that point, guess what? Yup, you're doing that really annoying part again.2. The first city you come across after the initial starting city is WAY WAY too big, it's overwhelming the number of people to talk to, the number of buildings you can go in, etc. This would be fine if each building and person had a purpose, but it's mostly just fluff. You're told to come to the city to find someone, so you wander the city for massive periods of time going in and out of each room and building trying to find the person, talking to each person, JUST to find this specific person you're supposed to talk to. It feels like such a damn chore and is torture. It wouldn't be so bad if the city itself wasn't so cluttered with background decoration and it was more obvious who to talk to and the other people and buildings had a purpose but for side-quest type of things. However, to be -forced- into talking to every single person and going in and out of every room in every building is just obnoxious and wears the player out pretty quick. Bad design. Do NOT force a player into your extra fluff, allow them to explore that should they want to.2 b? . You spend so much time in the city mentioned in #2 that you get sick of hearing the same music and sick of seeing the same motif. Once you've managed to move the game forward a little you're still stuck in that same "theme". I think the title of this number could be called "Pacing is completely off". If that's not bad enough, just getting TO that second town feels like a real slog. 3. The game is VERY grindy in terms of coins (called Rin in the game). Items, that are abilities, are locked behind purchases at vendors requiring lots of coins. Coins only drop from things like boxes being destroyed or chests. Even then, while the chests don't reappear after being destroyed, the boxes do but they then only drop a single coin.4. The sprint mechanic. Wow is this bad. You hit shift and your character dashes forward. Continue holding down the direction and your character keeps moving, but jump and land and you go back to walking despite holding down shift still. You have to release shift, land, then hold down shift again. This is absolutely horrendous and becomes obvious how bad that is pretty early on in the game when you're introduced to the spring mechanic and have a timed zig-zag vertical jumping bit. Just imagine that. You hit shift and your character dashes and you can't jump without it toggling back off as soon as you land. This is absolute hell for a tight /small area to move in and a very small amount of time zig-zag obstacle course where you're switching directions multiple times. Overall, the game really just fell flat for me. The game just wasn't fun for me. I don't know what it was but it just wasn't "fun". The story was "meh", and trying to at least just get a good story out of the game, and forget about the game not being "fun", by moving the game forward was a chore due to the problems mentioned above. What story I could get was not nearly interesting enough to make me want to keep pushing through. (Though, why should any game make the player feel they are just "pushing through"?) I feel like the game was missing "something" but I can't figure out what specifically it was beyond just saying it wasn't "fun". I guess this is one of those times where someone would label a game as "uninspiring" and the problems mentioned above only detract from an already very mediocre experience.

_childDocuments_.review: allright i went in blind..i kinda looked at the screenshots and it looked like an interesting vania.so i've played it for 10 hours got to the 3rd zone and im losing interest.Couple of things i do wanna give credit that it's not a straight foward vania, it's very Adventure based i do like that, however the pacing is really slow, i wish there was some form of assistance sometimes then some vague hints. the  physics based puzzling is a + as wellThe goodSense of adventure and explorationPhysics based puzzles and mechanicsnot too hand-holdynow on to the bad, the combat is the most basic and boring i've seen so far most of the weapons you get dont have a quick response like the crossbow aim, and load speed is slow. and the slingshot doesnt do enough damage in fights to be reliable weapon of sorts. then theres the absence of music just some pieces are DEAD silent, nothing not even ambience. Also this game FOR Some reason has a Stamina bar.its leaning allot in the " realism " like you need to cook your food and eat to regain hp and you have a stamina bar.. and to top all that off its trying to be clever with some of its pieces. i really am losing my interest to continue playing this. and i think the reason is just as simple as the game is just too boring.The bad- the background music is sometimes just dead silent- the combat is pretty basic and boring- the food items got all a unique design but boil down to - Cooked greens - or -fruit jam-  or the favoritemystery meat- the game is trying to reinvent the wheel a couple of times- the world is pretty boring- monsters in the overworld zelda 2 stylei wasnt expecting gold here. but to be ultimately just bored by a video game isnt the goal right? like let me  have some interesting weapons, give me some meaningfull upgrades instead of like a Floatie.. i just cant get myself to finish this one.. i had kind of some fun tho.. 6/10if you can get through the games blandness and straight up not telling you much to go on. it might be  the game for you however for me i think adventure ends at the 3rd zone.. sorry

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, boy! I really , REALLY wanted to like this game. The art style is beautiful, is great, and the dialogues are both funny and endearing. The towns alone are full with color and motion, and really feels like the world is alive, and keeps you engeged... but unfortunately, games are an interactive media, and you also need to play it.It takes moving around after waking up to already have alarms ringing in your head, as you're automatically going to notice a 0.25-0.5 second delay between imput an action, and that's just the beginning. This delay is pretty brutal as the game goes on, since it messes up with the running in small spaces and aerial melee attacks become unreliable at low altitudes. This last part in particular is a serious problem since flying explosive robots like to ram at you at a low angle, which is hard to defend against with melee aerial and takes too much time with the crossbow due to how the reticle is stuck in horizontal position and ignores small increases (for example, if you want to shot at 15º up, the reticle will remain horizontal until you reach the 30º, and from there you lower to 15º, wasting your time in corrections). Also, Gail  lacks iframes when hurt and has a deceptively large hurtbox, which will become a bigger problem in certain rooms as you move on. Been reading some comments after finding myself in this situation, and find it rather hilarious that the game shills even acnowledge this situation by saying everyone's approach to the game is wrong and you're actually supposed to pick an area where you can use ranged attacks and move as little as possible.Probably the thing that finally broke the camel's back is the last stretch, where you're supposed to fight a gauntlet of 2.5 bosses, in which failing results in having to go through an annoying text each time in the first, and the last one sends you to credits regardless if you won or not. Everything good the game did with it's presentation and flow are basically wasted by the dev's approach to action being about testing the player's patience and tolerance to annoyance. I'm certain that someone with the patience of a saint and undying loyalty to the game will find a way to go against the controls and manage to zero hit run all bosses, that's a given and always happens; but for most people, if the game feels like it doesn't want to be played, trying to tame those bad controls are not a fun activity, and having fun (or rather, lack of it) is what this all ultimately boils down to.

Well, there are a lot of other choices for you to choose. I would say, the game has a lot of replayability and development potential.In conclusion: A wholesome metroidvania mixed with legend of zelda game. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. I played the flash version so I was hyped when I heard about the remake. With that said, I can't recommend this game. It feels like the best worst game I've ever played. Much of this review, such as the points about fantastic music and art and the clunky mechanics, echoes other negative reviews so I won't go into much detail there.The Good (great, even)-Sound and music. Whether lighthearted, cheery, wacky, intense, creepy, or somber, the music and sound fx do a great job setting the atmosphere.-Visual design, both characters and the world. I'm a huge fan of the pixel art style. The enemy design is reminiscent of Cave Story, one of my favorite games.-Cute characters with endearing and/or funny dialogue. The various antagonists don't do bad stuff just for kicks.-World building. There's a lot of interesting stuff going on, like the idea of humanity getting back on their feet and rebuilding after a calamitous war and the existence of a faction that controls the progression of tech so such a war doesn't happen again.The Bad-Clunky controls, making for awkward/frustrating combat and movement. You have to come to a full stop to charge your heavy attack or to make a ranged attack.-Getting knocked around every time you stub your toe. Incredibly painful when trying to do platforming while turrets are shooting or enemies are jumping at you, and the aforementioned clunky controls mean you can't jump while shooting your crossbow or slingshot at enemies, compounding the issue.-MASSIVELY disappointing ending. -A nitpick: This was clearly a passion project. I'd be proud of myself if I made a game like this, but it unfortunately drops the ball hard in a lot of places that matter most.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Not just by indie standards but it's really outstanding on par with the best. The best way to describe it is that it recreates the feel of playing and old Zelda game (most notably LttP) but with much more modern game design and pretty clever puzzles and combat. Not found a game that sells the sense of adventure as well as this. It's not as focused as something like Hollow Knight but the world is much grander and way more lived in. In fact, it feels like there's even more life in this game's towns than open world games like Skyrim and BotW. There are actually more of these towns than you'd expect and each one is filled with puzzles, side quests and more. The music and pixel art is all really good too. Not the best but definitely up there.

_childDocuments_.review: I hope you lose $5 on the bus so my money goes somewhere else.Where to even begin with this mess. In short: the platforming is godawful and finicky, there is not a single enemy in the game that was enjoyable to fight, everything is designed to waste your time, and the story gets resolved in a text box at the end of two rehashed bosses.Every dash jump resets your dash, when you land you'll be in walk mode again even holding down the button. The direction you jump gets locked in strange ways I still can't grasp which matters when trying to lob bombs at things. There's very little room for error in a lot of the platforming. It's not quite pixel perfect nonsense but the timings get kind of strict and this also carried over into COMBAT with jumping over charging enemies and holy hell there is a LOT of charging and jumping enemies.Enemies. Every single one is designed to be as absolutely annoying as possible, even the bosses. ESPECIALLY the kobold bosses. Combat in general was clearly designed around the stamina system despite you being able to turn that off which then turns bosses into "go ape on them and they die immediately", and even with that crutch they are just zero percent fun to deal with.Towards the end of the game you get a regen ring which lets you pretty much ignore overworld danger and just sprint through traps, mobs, everything, because you'll just regen it back during the next segment of reading or puzzles.Speaking of puzzles, the design is... okayish. Push boxes, play music, at a couple points they just make you do Sudoku which is a weird choice and further cements the "everything here is wasting your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time" category. Especially the rewards. Oh boy you went out of your way to get this hidden chest? Enjoy 45 coins. If you're lucky its a stamina gem, which lets you not have to waste slightly time waiting for that to regen after regular platforming or minor combat. Sidequests are the WORST, item fetching nonsense that gives a pittance of a payout. By the way you often have to talk to an NPC multiple times before they give you the quest, and no indication that they have a sidequest so enjoy talking to EVERYBODY multiple times just in case!Getting to what is now apparently the final two bosses, both were just rehashes of two bosses you fought earlier! So clearly that was filler before the actual resolution of the game, right?WRONG. The moment you finish it off, the game ends and you're left with several text boxes explaining how you and your friends save the world. Not even cutscenes, or animations. Just text. A cute panorama of the towns. Credit roll. Honestly i'm just glad I don't have to play this anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Lovingly designed game world with lots of details and full of interesting characters. The story is engaging to keep you going.BUT! Unfortunately the game play is completely off the rails. The player is punished by almost every mechanic:You can't change the facing direction during a jump, your weapon range is a joke, the attack needs an eternity for build up, when you land the character pauses, you get stun-locked and thrown around by attacks, the crossbow has recoil! the enemies have no collision, which means you have to position yourself pixelperfect because of the nonexistent weapon range. The dash mechanic was already mentioned enough. All these elements and more lead to a completely learn-by-heart fighting style instead of reflex based play-style. There's almost no situation where you can react accordingly without having it memorized. That applies both to level design and boss battles. The game could have been great but the claim of being annoyingly difficult destroys the otherwise lighthearted experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks beautiful, and the music is good, but ultimately have some fatal flaws in the combat system that made it a very bad and frustrating experience, and is the main reason that I chose not to finish this game, despite really trying to look around these flaws. Like a see a few other mention: I really wanted to like the game, but in the end it ended up being a bad experience.I'll start with the good:- The pixel art is wonderful!- The music is nice.- The game has quite a few interesting mini-games and puzzles that I enjoyed.- Has content that makes it more versatile, and not just all combat. - The story itself is not too bad, but the execution could have been better.- The movement (walking / running) alone feels fluid.The bad:- The combat is sluggish, and your main weapon, a baseball bat, is borderline useless in many scenarios due to horrible range and a startup lag (especially when trying to use it in air) that really makes it hard to utilize for anything that is not just a sitting duck. You can charge it, but it will make you move in 1/4th of your walking speed, and the charge is gone if you try to jump. I really do like a challenge, but this game is challenging because your lack of control with your character, and not the enemies themselves. I really don't mind dying if I feel like I die because I am simply not skilled enough, but here I feel the frustration of dying due to a horrible combat experience. I ended up rarely using the bat in any combat where the enemies are in motion due to this problem, and in general I ended up just wanting to avoid any combat when possible.- There are a lot of characters, but they doesn't seem to be relevant for a long time, and most of them are forgettable.- There is an energy gauge that is required for everything. When you run, or just do a basic attack, you use some of your energy. When the energy is gone you have to wait 1-2 seconds before it starts to recharge. If this was designed in a good way, I would have nothing against it, but since everything except walking requires it, it simply just ruins the whole experience. The gauge can be upgraded by finding gems, but it doesn't fix the main issue.- I found that some parts of the game just simply did not give enough hints on how to proceed to get forward in the story, which made me stuck.- The hide'n'seek parts where you have to search around for characters were just boring, but they were necessary to proceed in the story.I could go on and on here, but you get my point: The overall experience was not great, but at the same time I feel like the game had a lot of potential, with a lot of great ideas. Sadly it did not deliver for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: There's a reason why I gave it a low score, and it's a single thing, but very important one.Let's start with the good: The visuals are great for a pixel game, and it helps because my computer can't handle big games like assassins' creed. The music was also pleasant, and very atmospheric depending on the location. The dialogue was entertaining, and with a lot of humor.The only thing that I would complain about, would be the gameplay. I know what some would say, "you can change the difficulty of the game." Well, that's not the point, and I don't think changing the difficulty would help either. The fact of the matter is, if you can't stun your enemies with one hit, you're at a disadvantage. I don't even know what was the point of adding the ability to roll, if it doesn't help dodge the attack. Combat is simply frustrating or slow, and I can't recommend this game in good faith.

_childDocuments_.review: I desperately want to love this game, but after completing it I can't bring myself to. This is a game that clearly had a lot of ideas in production, but the ones they chose to focus on for the final product were all of the wrong choices. The first indicator that the game was built on the wrong idea is combat, which is a chore, especially early on. Your stamina recovers so slowly that you spend far too much time running around waiting for a chance to actually attack. Stamina only drains on attacking or dashing, so you can run and jump to your hearts content. There is no dodge mechanic, so your only option is to jump to avoid attacks, many of which are either very fast or have splash damage in the form of very small rubble. Damage can combo up quickly, and with no aerial recovery you are at the mercy of the game if you get hit. To add insult to all of this, most combat in the game gives no real reward. Enemies might drop a small amount of money or the occasional item (which is almost always food), but with a criminally small inventory space you will find yourself either tossing items or leaving them behind regularly. The second is made clear by looking at the splash art for the game. The characters shown there are almost all insignificant to the story. Birdy plays almost no role in the game and only appears once. The kobold is the same and only appears twice. Bart is not physically seen until the very last scene of game. And these are the characters they chose to be the front page? The artwork in the game also prominently features characters who all disappear at the beginning. This, plus the ending of the game, speak to the devs having a grand idea for an overarching story, but the story we actually play is mismatched and taped together. Which is a shame, because the game looks and sounds great. But the ending of the game basically nixes all of the progress that you made. If that was the direction the devs wanted to go, then they should have made a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Game has all the potential of being a solid game, but is let down by repetitive, uninteresting enemies, combat and puzzles, barely passable controls and platforming mechanics, and a distinct lack of basic QoL stuff like being able to travel from one side of a town to the other at any decent speed without leaving the town and just going to the other entrance. No particularly good way to grind money. Easy to burn it at times, easy to get it back at others.There's nothing particularly redeemable about the experience, and it very quickly has an overinflated opinion of it's own competency making one of the early boss fights janky as all ♥♥♥♥, and each time you have to redo several fights beforehand, one of which has a tiny element of RNG you cant do a whole lot about.Not remarkably fun. Not memorable. Not really worth your money unless you've played pretty much every other side scroller out there and you're just looking for something else to play. 20 year old flash games feel better to play than this.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does get a lot of things right.The music is very good. I usually turn that to zero or almost-zero in these games, but I left it on here (with a few exceptions, like the meeting the kids music that forces me to listen to that tune too long for their too-long conversation).Being able to choose your difficulty and change it at any time is great. The game is very customisable in that way, but even the way the difficulties are presented to you are noticeably inefficient. First you are just given a choice of 5 star ratings for difficulty with no indication of what they mean. Then when you select one, the star menu disappears and you are given a character-by-character description of what your choice means for you, and you need to confirm it. You can cancel out of that if you like, and select a different difficulty and then read another character-by-character description. Why is it laid out this way instead of just giving you an instant description in the star menu as you hover the choices? I don't know, but this problem is a sign of things to come, as everything in the game seems to be set up with this mindset.The combat is okay but generally below average. The melee combat, which you'll be using most of the time, is fairly straight forward and not super smooth. I was playing on the difficulty level that doesn't require energy most of the time (I tried it with energy being used at first, and that annoyed me a lot). The slingshot aiming is extremely weird - effectively like Yoshi's Island 2 aiming eggs, but the aim is slower and cannot be controlled in any way, and the shots you fire are slow and have a weird arc that I don't think the angry video game nerd would approve of.The pacing sucks. This game has a lot of talking to NPCs and at first their conversations don't seem too long, but slightly more important NPCs have a lot more dialog and very little of that dialog is important. You start out just having to talk to your way around the opening town and it is very boring. I found my way out of that town by accident and I was grateful that I did. Then I had to learn some very complex moves very quickly, notably one that involved sprint-leaping repeatedly across 6 platforms, 2 or 3 of which were timed before they disappeared and I'd have to reset the puzzle. The problem here is sprint-leaping is not a matter of just holding sprint, there is a weird button combination of sprint-leap-land-sprint-leap-land that you have to do consecutively - but on short platforms, that is timed, at the beginning of the game. To begin with I thought this room was optional with some big gold at the top, but it is not optional. The buttons to perform all sorts of actions, not even complex ones are varied, odd choices. If I want to take a week-long break from the game, I will probably not remember how to pick up a box, and while I did place boxes down at my feet instead of throwing them a few times, I am still not sure how I did it.The second biggest red flag for this negative review is a big one - there is no map. I got lost, and so will you, and no decent metroidvania should be without one. Ultimately though, there is one last flaw which is going to prevent me playing this game entirely - I cannot work out cooking. I tried cooking about 10 different things over 3 separate cooking sessions, and everything I try to cook turns to poisonous fertilizer because I failed to cook it. I tried googling to work out the cooking minigame but I can't tell what I'm doing wrong. And if I can't cook, I can barely heal, and healing in this game is already not easy as it is. Cooking appears to be all but required for any casual player.

_childDocuments_.review: So disapointing!+ The music! I just could listen to like 3 or 4 music for the little time I played but I really liked them.+ Characters are cute from afar... but just from afar because...- ...the graphics/the pixel art are quite lazy. My fault, I had seen a few videos of the game and though it looked pretty but I guess I didn't pay attention close enough, because besides the characters and their animations, the pixel art is quite lazy and ugly (backgrounds look cheap and lack detaisl, everything look very flat/one dimensional etc.)- The clunky controls, omg! That's a torture! Everything you wanna do is sooooo tedious. Some of the controls don't make any sense like pressing LT to run... but it runs by itself when you press the button... why? The floaty jumps are frustrating (including especially the run + jump) and super approximate, you miss constantly the platforms.  Even Snes games had better controlled better on the snes controller.- The combats are bad, really bad. The hitbox is terrible and because the controls are so cluncky and everything you wanna do so tedious, it's a real chore. Also, once you jump and hit you can't turn away mid air to change the direction of your hit, like in what, 99% of games?, the hit goes in the direction you faced when you initiated the jump even.- The backtracking/metroidvania elements. Plenty awful. Suprisingly, the first boss (the water blob) was super easy to beat, i stood on him and mashed to hit he died in like 8 seconds... almost as fast as it takes to beat a basic ennemy like a frog etc. go figure...- Sometimes the music stops suddenly, just like that, for many seconds... do'nt know if it's a bug or supposed to happenI was roughly 1 hour in the game but everything so so frustrating that I'm giving up already, I don't feel like wasting 29 more hours (because according to this page that's a 30 hours game) fighting with the controls and not enjoying the game.Bought it for less than 5$ but that's still a waste of money for a game that I will never finish because of all the cons mentionned above. I wish I had played the game sooner so I could refund it, but now I'm past the 2 weeks delay for the refund by jsut a few days.Don't be fooled by the apparent cuteness of the game (from afar only), you might regret buying that game too.Though if you like movies/anime OST definitely check the soundtrack (it's on spotify). _childDocuments_.review: I suppose "Metroidvania" is a broad genre with an elastic meaning, but I personally wouldn't call this game a Metroidvania. It's more like an RPG with an overworld map and side-scrolling subareas. That would be fine, but the combat in this game is abysmal: the weapon hit box barely extends past your main character's sprite (the teensiest range imaginable), you cannot change your facing direction mid-air, the mid-air attack is too delayed to actually hit anything mid-air, and the action stamina bar makes you feel unduly fettered in a game that's already difficult. Although I have my complaints about the battle system, it's funny because I didn't spend a lot of time in this game fighting. I would guess about 3.5 of these 5 hours were spent running around town talking to NPCs just trying to move the story along so I could even experience the exploration and combat aspects of this game. Again, I personally would hesitate to call this a Metroidvania because so far the emphasis is on the RPG elements of dialogue, towns, and wasting time talking to every NPC to find out which one of them in the enormous sprawl moves the game forward. (I did everything in Atai Town to get to the desert hideout beyond the cave, but I got bored backtracking to town to heal, managing my extremely limited inventory, and looking for where to find/purchase recovery items that were worth a damn.)

_childDocuments_.review: Phenotopia: Awakening is a great game, and worth your while if you find it's mechanics to be up your alley...Phenotopia's story is a tale about generations carrying on in the wake of crisis. Sure, the inciting incident is pretty On-the-nose (let's just say), but, there's a lot of emotion, and dramatic subtext layered into the plot and soundtrack.Many of your usual Zelda tropes are here in their cutesy, pixellated glory - bombs, slingshot and bow, lantern, etc., but they're used to an overall, unique effect in the world. Phenotopia's iteration on traditional Metroidvania dungeons and zelda II styled overworlds are refreshing in a sea of other similar games.  The biggest star in Phenotopia is the animation/ platforming mechanics. Jumps and swings of your weapon are snappy & there are several techs which the designers expect you to grow proficient in as you progress (Ie. the jump attack, which causes more damage than standard, but not as much as a home run swing, which is slow but powerful when fully charged). The bosses sometimes feel a little on the cheap side, but once you get their patterns down, beating them becomes pretty epic. Save points are plentiful, though health isn't  as easy to find as you'd expect (primarily via cooking food, and sleeping in beds (where available.) Overall, the game is Tropy as heck, but has a presentation and depth that make up for it several times over. 👍

_childDocuments_.review: Probably favourite game of all time. 100%ed on switch, then bought the game just to put this review/play on PC.The main draw of the game is exploring the world. There is a huge amount of content in the game. The way its laid out builds a great sense of scale - when you explore/find something new in the game, it often breaks your previous notion of where the boundary of the world may have been. So the game keeps you guessing as to just how large the world really is, which greatly adds to the fun of exploration.In addition to having plenty of secrets and unique locales, the game has a very strong sense of place. Npc dialogue, game mechanics, puzzles, characters, and quests, often self reference/explain one another, and is very well integrated into the world's numerous settings. Every NPC you come across either gives a hint towards quests/combat, interesting lore about the world, or well written and funny dialogue. So you naturally learn that NPCs (at least in this game) are always worth interacting with.There's no map or quest log. I found that this made the game more immersive, as I'd pay more attention to the dialogue and my surroundings. Recalling locations/information becomes fun, as most of them are unique and memorable enough to do so.All of this makes the world feel alive and immersive.I see most complaints are about the combat and movement. From what I can tell, the influences come from Smash Bros (ex. no turning around in the air, landing lag, teching, dashing/sprinting being very committal, long startup times for melee attacks, small melee range). For some people, these mechanics aren't intuitive, and is a barrier to entry.If you're struggling with this, I'd recommend taking a small amount of time just playing around to notice these limitations. Ex. sprinting is committal, locking you out of most options and aerial control if you jump, so its not something to constantly do during combat. If you start the aerial attack too late, no hitbox will come out so you jump in the air doing nothing.Regardless, observing the enemy attack patterns, then waiting for openings/baiting attacks before engaging is something you'd want to do for most combat encounters. If you understand the mechanics, the combat isn't amazing, but decent enough. Overall, if you enjoy exploring a detailed and immersive world, and have some flexibility to learn the nuances in the combat/movement (or have played enough platformers/fighters), this is an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very leisurely platformer RPG, of the type where the plot is barely there and it's mostly an excuse to go exploring and do sidequests. For all that, it's well-written and has a good amount of humor, as well as plenty of varied environments and interesting puzzles. I will say that it's very slow-paced, though. It took me 36 hours to get through, and that's with a 74% completion rating. You should also be aware that combat is a little clunky. Your primary weapon is short-ranged, and enemies have only brief windups before their attacks. You're meant to get in after they perform an attack (after which they have some "invisible" recovery time), get some hits in, and then get out *before* they start their windup, which is a little weird compared to how most games do things. It works out once you figure out how the game wants you to play.I played on the middle difficulty. If I recall correctly, at this difficulty I can spam healing items from the menu (which would otherwise need several seconds each to consume, making them hard to use in combat), and basic attacks don't consume stamina. Spamming healing feels a little cheap, but then a lot of fights would be extraordinarily hard to do "fairly", so I'll take it.

The story and world is more fleshed out; and if you're the type of person who enjoys talking with NPCs and reading descriptions, the dialogue and flavor text in this game is such fun to read. As with Zelda games, more than half the fun of the game is combing through past sections using newfound powers or tools, of which you'll get plenty. For completionists, I cleared Phoenotopia Awakening the first time at 83%. The remaining 17 I think I would've been unable to get without the help of the very helpful online walkthroughs and Gsheets.A minor gripe is that the initial version's duri fruits (which obviously looked like durian) were turned into berries. Please release a duri fruit patch thank you.Also, boy am I glad that  was taken out 'cause that ♥♥♥♥ was nerve wracking.I really enjoyed the , and the computer journal entries. Overall, such an adorable but challenging 2D game that is super nostalgic for me. Would still definitely recommend to those who haven't played the newgrounds version.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game? Absolutely. I am an avid RPG and anything with a good lore fan, so I instantly took to this game. I digress. This game has difficulty for those who want it, story for people like me, and gameplay and small minigame aspects for others. I don't know how I ever missed this game when it first came out; I would have played this so much earlier if I had known. If you are reading this review, I highly recommend buying the game, even if you want to wait for a discount. Just play the game, I am sure that you, whoever you are, will love it. _childDocuments_.review: This hidden Gem is easily one of the best Metroidvania in my list. The third hidden gem I found after Kingdom Come Deliverance at its early release, and Valdis story. It is very underappreciated that it is almost a crime.This game has a lot to offer for its price. It has wholesome story, exploration, hidden powerup, puzzle, platforming. pixel graphic and great OST. I can see the developers put their heart and mind in this game....which unfortunately it has few flaws.Positive:1. Gorgeous OST. The song are nice done and match each map and atmosphere. I wish the same composer composes for Phoenotopia sequel.2. Beautiful Pixel art. City and dungeon are drawn goregeous, although I feel character pixel art can be improved a bit, maybe like Momodora.3. Wholesome story. I am tired with current trend of dark and backstab story, this game is a such fresh change. I also like how main character is actually a special character, not just a lucky normal person.4. Difficulty level. This difficulty level patch is a blessing. Without it, this game would be too difficult for me. I want to play this game like Zelda where it is Fun to play, not Souls like. I also appreciate that whatever difficulty player chose to finish the game, the ending is still the same.5. World map with visible enemies. I hate invisible random enemies, this unique map is more realistic where it is possible to avoid enemies.6. Many exploration and hidden power up to find.7. Many puzzles and platforming, although a bit too many for me.Negative:1. No Dungeon map. Although it is do-able to beat this game without dungeon map, but a dungeon map would be helpful.2. No quest notes. In pause menu, there is no quest notes. A notes would be helpful to remind or confirm player where player need to go to continue main or side quests.3. Related with quest. Especially at beginning, the game sometimes does not convey properly direction where player need to go. The game helps by writing blue line in NPC dialogue but there is no confirmation whether that should be the next place to go. In later part of the game, character Bart does confirm direction where player need to go.Neutral:1. Although the gameplay and battle are not bad. I think the gameplay can be improved to be more smooth like Hollow knight. 2. The platform and puzzle might need to be toned down a bit to suit beginner player, even for a veteran, some are challenging. 3. Different weapon and armor should have different sprite and art.Overall I really recommend this game. I would actually grade this game as 9 ish but since it lacks dungeon map and other negatives, I grade this game to be 8.5/10. Having read that during initial release that some players critic this game to be difficult with stamina usage, and no pause eating etc. These difficulty issue may be a factor why this game initially not received and sales not that good. When I see the title artwork initially, I immediately thought this game to be Zelda like which suppose to be Fun to play, and not that Souls like difficult. I will not hold my breath but I dearly wish the developer and composer continue developing for the sequel, Phoenotopia has great potentials if better executed.

_childDocuments_.review: Look overall, this game is brilliant. I'm also playing on a laptop, with my keyboard, which might be making things more difficult for me. If you have any kind of issues with your hands and reflexes this game might not be for you. Despite finding myself disappointed by the game and lacking the motivation to complete it, I am going to recommend the game. _childDocuments_.review: Phoenotopia is an exercise in player/game friction and as such won't be tolerable for everyone, and while I think the devs flew a little too close to the sun with this design philosophy, on balance I really enjoyed this game that was created with passion and clear intent. It's a side scrolling action rpg in open homage to Zelda II, that might also scratch some of the itches that Metroidvania fans look for. There's combat, platforming, puzzles, fishing, deep exploration, side quests and an okay story with charming characters and well written dialogue. The visuals boast simple yet expressive sprites and incredible backgrounds with notably high attention to detail in the environments, and the music is a standout. It's lengthy too, clocking in at 60 hours for me to complete the game with still around 20% collectables to find.There's no doubt that this game has the capacity to frustrate, it's baked in to the sometimes seemingly mean-spirited design. The cute exterior belies a pretty tough experience but the pros outweighed the cons for me. Those that click with this will probably love it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed my time with this hidden gem. The game plays a lot like a 2D Zelda-like, so there's a huge focus on platforming, exploration, and puzzle-solving. The games dungeons are well designed, and the world is jam-packed with all sorts of characters and secrets. There's a load of side-quests to keep busy with, so much so that the game almost feels like an RPG at times. As for the games combat, it has a significant learning curve parred with some difficult and unforgiving encounters. If the game ever gets too difficult, don't be afraid to tweak the difficulty options. I personally always play with the "Items usable in menu" and "standard attacks don't consume stamina" options enabled, and I heavily recommend these for newcomers. Regardless of what difficulty settings you use, once you get used to the controls and unlock more items, the game really opens up and becomes something truly special. If you love platformers and love Zelda-likes, give this game a try. If it clicks, it may just become one of your favorite games of all time, just as its become one of mine.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. I had been waiting for its release long ago when I first played this game when it was still a flash game so it has a sacred space in my heart. The music makes me feel good, the combat makes me feel accomplished, and the exploration makes me so happy. I'm just hoping maybe more people will find this gem of a game (and maybe it'll increase our chances of getting Phoenotopia 2)
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a criminally low review ratio so I'm doing my part. One of my absolute favs, like one of those really special games that sucked me in for the whole play time. A really rare adventure game that runs so much deeper than you initially expect. Awesome puzzles, awesome combat, awesome lore. Yes, the combat is challenging, but I never once felt like it was unfair. It's actually just the right level where the first time you fight a boss you might think "Damn, that seems impossible!" But you give it a few tries, work out the patterns, think about the tools at your disposal, and you can eek out victory every time. I find that really rewarding, but if you want a game where you just mash attack to progress this may not be the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: The main story isn't particularly amazing—at least not without a sequel that doesn't seem to be coming—but it serves the setting, and the setting is very well-done. It's an unusual take on a post-apocalyptic Earth, where some of the land has recovered after centuries since the Great War that ravaged the planet, but there's deadly machines still lurking outside the protective walls...The puzzles are numerous and highly interesting. They range in difficulty somewhat, but usually provide a fair challenge. I particularly like the flute and the puzzles tied to it. The combat is pretty great too—boss fights are hardcore enough even if you actively engage in exploration. Without it, it would be absolutely insane, because you start with 30 max health and low max stamina, and can go up to 250 health and, what, 4 times as much stamina? Basically, exploration and questing is a must. But it's really well-made in Phoenotopia, so I don't think there's any reason you'd want to avoid it—it's the meat of this game.The writing is witty and funny when appropriate, while the amount of dialogue is pretty insane. The BGM is great and highly varied—60 tracks in total. The pixel art (especially the protagonist's sprite and animations) is cute. Also, near the end of the game you can choose to ask for leads on health/energy/other upgrades you've missed—it's made very nicely, as it isn't too direct and thus maintains the fun of exploration.I guess if there's one thing I could maybe complain about, it's that there's no quest log, so it can be easy to forget that some NPC talked about something quest-relevant or asked you about something, especially if it happened dozens of hours ago. Granted, you'll eventually be led back to those quests if you ask for leads on missing items near the end of the game, but I still recommend binging this game instead of playing it "on and off".
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game not too long ago. It's a great game, however it is prohibitively difficult. Those who are not used to (or didn't grow up with) old school games that punish you for failure to execute in-game timings and techniques will quickly become frustrated with this title. I do recommend to the developers that they add the tag "difficult" to this one as many on various forums put this one down after a relatively short time playing due to abrupt difficulty spikes. That being said, I do love this game, but much of what we love causes us to overlook their shortcomings, especially by the end of the game's story and this game's got some stinkers for sure (SPOILERS):-pulls us in with a gripping narrative about growing up in a small village then-- HOLY JEEBUS ALIENZ/SPACE PIRATES R HERE AND THEY TOOK MAI FAMILY (this is never expanded upon until the very end and only very briefly do the writers state that nobody knows what happened to them lol)-you're told that the reason Gail is so good at fighting is because she was a "Pheonix"/test tube baby/super soldier/cyber messiah stolen from an underground lab (by whom and for why? we'll never tell.. maybe in a sequel? wink-wink :3)-the final battle(s) are just clones of other fights from earlier in the game (a second clone of Mother Brain from Super Metroid, a hastily inserted Dark Link style battle, then another annoying fight with a boss you already beat from earlier in the game but this time you aren't supposed to beat him.... instead a superhuman wakes up and punches him dead for you)-then, OFFSCREEN, there is a super-duper war with aliens for control of the Earth and the Pheonixes (other super soldiers whose narrative use amounts to that of Akira's orbital lasers/win-buttons)-just before the credits roll, Gail takes off into the sky all Superman-like with little explanation other than she was just ignorant of her own powers up to this point and we can only speculate as to the answers for all the questions the hastily written endgame has left us with So, what I'm trying to say is this game is good, but the sour (rushed) writing can leave one feeling snubbed by the end of the experience. However, if you want a decent time exploring a traditional RPG world that's not-so-secretely a post-post apocalypse (one of my favorite settings honestly) you should give this one a go. Just know that you're in for a :/ at times.

_childDocuments_.review: This starts as a cute action platformer but it evolves into so much more. Great touching story, world design, character design, music, challenges and secrets. And it is massive. A lot of love must have went into the making of this game, it will reward you if you give it your time.The game is very difficult. Item management is a pain and healing during fights is trouble. A lot of the tools get very finicky on the timing. Dodging attacks during some fights is near impossible and once you are hit, you ragdoll through every source of hurt possible until you manage to gain control. Somehow, most of this trouble can be dealt with by immersing in the many systems the game has. It is there by design and not oversight (I hope), it forces the player to use everything at their disposal and gives the gameplay a lot of satisfying weight.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is lovingly crafted, and is one of the only attempts I have seen to improve and expand the format of Zelda 2. As someone who has very nostalgic and frustrated memories of Phoenotopia's predecessor, I took the kind of unforgiving difficulty of this game in stride. To be honest, even though I have at least 30 hours in this game, I found the ending kind of lacking. I do understand that there were plans to continue this series, and it makes me sad that we might not get a continuation of this world.

_childDocuments_.review: A very challenging 2D adventure, that can be really frustrating. You are constantly trying to keep up with not dying, as your tools are limited in the harsh environment.However, the (retro) charm and the reward if you succeed keep you going and on track.It has exceptionally good soundtrack and good riddles. The game mechanics are diverse and super cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  All in all I'd have to reccommend it. One of the more solid metroidvanias I've played personally. Some of the bosses are annoying (looking at you, bubbles). And some of the puzzles are pointlessly obtuse. Good execution on the minigames. Cooking was great once I figured it out (you can't use joystick for it)The music is also wonderful.Gameplay has a few weird decisions and unfair design bits. I would have to recommend you to turn on fast stamina regen. Base regen isn't fun. Area design is great. Only about halfway through the game, but I have the sneaking suspicion that 100% is going to be a nightmare. TL;DR: Great game. Would recommend playing it if you like 2D platformer metroidvanias (the platforming's alright). Don't treat the combat anything like a platform fighter, it's meant for you to play careful and slowly.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest Flash games ever made - up there with MARDEK and Epic Battle Fantasy.The progression feels really nice, exploring the different areas and how they all connect to the world's ancient history/war, until you make your way to the final sections where it really starts to blend together.For me, the best thing was that the world still felt full of mysteries, so many areas were left to the player to interpret and wonder what happened - the first dungeon being a great example.The only thing I could seriously criticise is that some of the weapons feel redundant for combat, at least the secret one. Unless it's for a puzzle, the spear + crossbow usually takes care of anything. They'll all regularly get a use instead of only being limited to their area however.Ultimately, there's just a certain charm to the game with its fantastic music, setting, tons of secrets and challenging but fun control system.

_childDocuments_.review: This game took a place in my top 5 games of all time. The gameplay is challenging and feels really rewarding. The puzzles are really clever. It looks beautiful all the way through. The story is pretty good but it really shines in the well written dialog. I found myself talking to every NPC at least once just because all of them had character or atleast cracked a smile on my face. The music is absolutely incredible. And after learning the speedrun it added even more depth to a game I already loved. If I'd have to be critical, then I'd say completing it can be a bit tedious but it was absolutely worth it. _childDocuments_.review: The exploration in this game is a pure joy. Exploring every little corner for more dialog and upgrades was a lot of fun.  Solving lots of little puzzles, most of which are pretty intuitive (it helps to take notes!).  The exploration, music, humor (maybe its strongest trait), animation, lush environments all had me thinking this might be my second favorite platformer after Hollow Knight.The combat is frequently difficult.  Rather than being a hack and slash game where spamming attack will carry you, the fights are kind of puzzles to solve where you examine the enemy's patterns for occasional windows of opportunity.  I died a lot. I feel like anyone with the patience to beat SNES platformers like Megaman X can preserve here, if they are so inclined. Just don't go in expecting "snappy" combat, it is very methodical.  There was definitely one zone later in the game where monsters would rapidly respawn that tested my patience.I'd strongly recommend this game to any zelda/metroidvania fan willing to push through a few old-school hard bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game years ago on newgrounds and played through to almost the end but never beat it. Now I'm at the final boss and I have so many mixed feelings. The puzzle elements in this game are wonderful and where it shines the most but the combat against bosses is so bad. I'm not talking about the charge system or the stamina, I actually quite like those systems a lot. When you get hit in this game, you ragdoll and there is no getting out of this. Sometimes you have immunity frames in the ragdoll and sometimes you don't. What this leads to is enemies or hazards hitting you especially hard, ragdolling across the arena, and getting hit again once you're out of the ragdoll leading to being stun locked until the attack ends. Some attacks require you to dodge with more agility than have, some attacks will lead to hazards that you can't avoid if you mess up once, etc. The game is stacked against you in a way that not only doesn't feel fair but doesn't feel fun.I'm only recommending this for the puzzles and progression. Play on the standard difficulty or easy.

_childDocuments_.review: I will say this game is good (Seriously Steam update your review system) but would put this at a lower rate if that existed.The game is pretty good overall.- Story: Decent. Has some light tones and a little humor but doesn't overdo it.- World: Really cool design for the different areas. A lot of detail ranging from fields, forests and swamps to cities and their cluttered design (Intentional to give off that cramped city vibe). Many areas utilize doorways on both sides (Basically front and back to give it more depth). I'll also put the quest and sidequest content in here which gives you a lot to do with the collection of things and puzzles. The overworld what I relate to as the Zelda 2 with enemies spawning on a map and if encountered you get a small sidescrolling map with a few enemies and maybe an item or two.- Music: Very nice overall. I put the volume down pretty low so I may not be hearing it on most maps but the boss music absolutely slaps and really has that "It's go time" vibe (It's on Youtube!). While gameplay related there is a music component in the game (Key Item) and the notes are icons which are mapped to directions. It's cool that they have these notes to give more immersion but it does make a little hard to remember what you have to push to remember the note on top of the sequence (I just put together a reference that I can go off of instead of that).- Combat: This is the part I actually dislike the most and it's a shame because there is so much combat involved. Read some of negative comments and some point out this too.- Combat Movement: Your character movement is oddly clunky but it seems intentional. Most movements or attacks you do have to fulfill their animation which seems to carry on for a few frames too many and that is what leaves you exposed. This means you have to account for that extra delay at the end and consider even doing it. Another component to this that puts you at a disadvantage is the controls which I'll cover seperately since it also involves non combat.- Combat Difficulty: Enemies can absolutely juggle you and some attacks sends you bouncing off walls and it's kind of ridiculous. I've been playing this on easy but really the difficulty spikes with some area and bosses you're really playing on a higher difficulty whether you like it or not. Bosses have a noticeable progression but where I am at the time of this review (3rd storyline boss) was absolutely off the walls absurd (If you don't avoid one particular attack you're paralyzed for nearly 10 seconds - The boss doesn't attack during this time but it's just frustrating). - Controls: Some control input seems to have poor response ingame. I've been playing with an Xbox controller but for things like crawling prone or cooking I switch to the keyboard for that. With combat though I would not even dare try a keyboard with all teh other things you have going against you in combat. Using some ranged weapons that has aim is also limited and doesn't seem to accept the full 360 range of a joystick so you will have difficulty aiming to fire accurately (Of course enemies do not have to worry about this and will fire ranged attacks with better precision than you).Overall: If you want to try this because you like the genre just know you will most likely get a little or very frustrated with it's downfalls.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the game's tags is "metroidvania", so I went in expecting a metroidvania. I quickly realized this was not a metroidvania, so at first I was a bit disappointed, and yet, the game was a pleasant surprise.I don't even know how to categorize it, it has elements from a lot of genres, platformer, RPG, puzzle, I would say it would be close to an action RPG, think of Zelda 2, where you have an overhead map but when you go into places it goes to a 2d view with real time battles. Still, it's not really an RPG, there's no leveling, and there's a lot of platforming, but it's not a platformer either, and while there are many puzzles, they're mostly optional, but still very good, so you get the idea, it's a lot of things, and they're well implemented.It seems not many people know this game, which is a shame, because I thought it was very good, I had a blast with it, it has a charming style, the music is great, the gameplay is fun, and it has some interesting mechanics, I played it at the highest difficulty, which I found out later it's the original difficulty, but was later given the option to be tuned down, still, I would recommend playing it that way, the way the devs intended, because that makes it stand out from other games, it's its own experience.The only thing I would "criticize" is the fact that the game seems to be longer, and then it suddenly ends with things unresolved, that is not to say the game is short, it took me 31 hours to finish and I still only got 51%, so there's plenty of game here, but it really left me craving for more, mainly because the premise of the game, the thing you set out to do in the first place, doesn't get done by the end, but it's clear that this was planned as only a part of a bigger story comprising one or more games.And that's also part of why I'm making this review, because apparently the game didn't do so well unfortunately, so the devs went on to other projects and the possible sequel is not a priority, which is a shame, because, again, the game is very good, so I hope more people find out about this game and give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: Vague spoilers ahead - nothing outright, but stuff is hinted atWhat to say about this game.Well, for starters, I didn't think the end was quite...enough? It felt like there should have been more after the final boss. The resolution was melancholy and left me feeling somewhat empty...Probably like Gail. I was disappointed when the credits started rolling, which in some ways can be seen as a compliment, because the game was so good I wanted it to keep going! Plus I wasn't able to resolve some of the plot/quest threads that happened near the end.And then I saw my completion percentage40%My Metroid hackles rose.There is 60% of this game that, in some way or other, I haven't experienced.Not yet. I'm tired. This game took me almost 40 hours to finish, I'm not about to start all over again this soon. But someday. And, I hope, not after too long. One thing that could help with that, though, would be a New Game+ mode, but maybe the New Game+ is the stuff we collected along the way. :PI don't know if I should hope for a sequel. It would be difficult to balance the game considering the big reveal at the end. But who knows, maybe it's possible.A simple binary yes or no system makes reviews like these difficult to say. Do I recommend it? Yeah, absolutely, if you're into this kind of game, you will adore it. Not 100% sure of the criticisms either, like bad combat; felt pretty desperate at times, if you ask me, but a larger weapon variety, especially in the realm of ranged weapons, and more upgrade paths might improve it. But I probably haven't play enough games of its kind to really know why people had problems with it.I did like the combat difficulty accessibility system, and I will probably be utilizing it more in my next playthrough.The story was....almost *kind of* Undertale-esque, in like it has a surface level narrative, but the backstory and lore both contexualize the plot, but also give some pretty dark, unsettling, and depressing implications. I like those kinds of stories because they play on those feelings.==Actual Spoilers beyond this point==To elaborate on the ending, I didn't realize that the awakening of the Deus Ex Machina (the Phoenixes - grammar bro in me is disappointed they didn't use Phoenices, but what're ya gonna do ¯\_(ツ)_/¯) would actually *end the story.* I don't know how they could have finished the game in a better way, mind you, and I'm not really in a place where I could offer an alternative. Maybe it got a bit too grandiose for the game's scope and they had to make the war a paragraph or so, so there would be *some* resolution.==Spoilers end here==I don't usually write reviews. This game compelled me to, for some reason. I'm not sure if I've actually said all I want to say; I might make some addendums in the comments if I'm so inclined, but I did like the game. I enjoyed Gail's journey. I wanted more. I WANT more. Hoping for a sequel, Cape Cosmic! Thank you for this experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Woah. This game is sooo good.. but also weirdly bad lol. Phoenotopia has some of the most rewarding exploration I've ever played, but.. why the heck is there no map, ya won't be finding all those moonstones without it.. or maybe even beating the game. Adding to this problem is the disrespectful backtracking. Why does this game keep locking me in mandatory tunnels with no food and no easy way out?! AND when I take 15 min to go get food and come back the tunnels reset part way. Cool. The core of this game is great, art, exploration, platforming, puzzles, upgrades, stamina gauging combat, music, and even the dialogue at times, but wow are there some glaring basic issues that a game designer should have seen. I sure hope a nice QoL patch comes out for this game that adds a map, as well as ways to acquire more food in the difficult tunnel sections. Sadly I don't expect that to ever happen.The more I think about this game, the more I love it and wonder what happened with the "dungeons". The first dungeon,  was PERFECT, well.. it just needed a map, that would have actually made for a cool item to find. But anyway, this first dungeon, it wasn't linear, there was food to find, it had a central saving point, unique rooms, lots of lore details, stuff to come back to when I had upgrades, oh and even multiple bosses. If the other "dungeons" were this good, I'd be giving the game an ez nine. All in all a really eye opening game for me, and hopefully the metroidvania genre at large. Shout out to Zelda II and, shout out to Legend of Swordia VIII.7 /  10Please make more metroidvanias like this y’all, I love going town to town and finding the hidden spots between!

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the original flash version of this from 2014, and I was amazed at the quality and quantity of the content. After a few years I happened upon the news of the remake and followed its development with cautious optimism, and I'm happy to say I think it turned out great. This was one of the most enjoyable games I've played recently. It was the kind of game that I enjoyed beginning to end, I was always looking forward to coming back to it. I 100%ed and then went for the finale, and I was left with that bittersweet "satisfied and happy it happened, depressed that it's over" feeling, and I went back and scoured the game for every last drop of content.The game world is full of charm and sincerity; well animated pixel graphics and smooth weighty movement, loads of different in-game environments, lots of amusing dialogue throughout the game (more the kind that makes you smile, rather than the kind that makes you laugh), a cool setting with lots of satisfying world-building to be found in exploring, talking, and item descriptions, and a well told sincere story that is lighthearted and optimistic but also doesn't undermine itself with silliness. The game has a great balance of lightheartedness and seriousness, and the music is fantastic and catchy with loads of variety; I was always looking forward to hearing a new track in every new environment.Puzzling and platforming gameplay are very enjoyable; there's a huge number of puzzles and challenges all over the map, lots of different types: logic puzzles, timing puzzles, riddles, some well hidden ones involving background details and such. The platforming is usually tied to the puzzles, and while it occasionally requires some dexterity, the game rarely calls for pixel-perfect finger-crunching platforming (I recognise this  be seen a mark against the game). I will note however: For people who enjoy acquiring new movement abilities in metroid-vania style games; that isn't a huge feature in this game. While you  acquire abilities that let you traverse more environments and move around in new ways, the majority of your character's acrobatic abilities are available to you right from the start of the game and aren't altered or upgraded significantly from their original form. Dungeons in-game somewhat resemble puzzle dungeons in some Zelda games, rather than the more maze-like dungeons you can find in some metroid-vania games. While the dungeons and levels have several optional off-shoots and hidden areas (and the same is true for the world map), most dungeons are fairly straightforward in design. The game lacks in-game maps, but in my opinion it doesn't need any as the dungeons aren't sprawling or confusing enough, and the cities are also often quite well signposted. The world is big enough that you might forget the exact location where you found a specific item/puzzle/room/npc you couldn't reach or interact with before, but you'll probably know which area it was in, and I'd say you are very unlikely to be completely lost at any point.The combat gameplay is the most common point of contention in reviews, but I found it pretty enjoyable in most encounters. In my opinion, the gameplay in general feels very tightly designed, and I think that the claims of ultra-difficulty are extremely overblown; the game isn't anywhere near as crushingly difficult as many reviews (positive or negative) imply. The combat is often negatively compared to Hollow Knight (another game I enjoy), but the two games are only superficially similar, both in combat and other design and gameplay aspects. Compared to something like HK, the combat is slower paced; enemies move slower or more clumsily, both their and the player's attacks have more wind-up and wind-down, most enemies have no collision damage so you can move in closer and stay there longer, most enemies can be knocked back/interrupted if you hit them with a charged attack, there isn't any mercy invincibility after being hit so a single big strike can put you on the backfoot, and you have less aerial control than in something like HK. Then there's the stamina system where basic movement (running, jumping, crawling) costs nothing, but most other moves - sprinting, rolling, melee (both fast and charged attacks), and secondary weapons/equipment - cost stamina, and you can't be relentless with your attacks and must manage your stamina. Finally, there's healing, which typically has to be done mid combat without pausing  so you have to quickly stop and eat a healing item during a lull in the fight, with a choice between quick low healing items and slow high healing ones. All this combines to give the combat a slightly slower pace, so for example after a few short bursts of sprinting you'll dodge with a jump or roll, then get only a few hits and a charged hit in and run out of stamina, then focus on dodging/healing again, and so on. As you get used to the combat, you learn how best to use up your stamina and which weapons/items are most effective against different types of enemies, when you can sneak hits in during the dodging periods, and when it's best to use the faster or slower healing items. You'll rarely need to hyper-focus on intense stamina management, since most attack dodging doesn't require much (if-any) stamina so there's less pressure if you run out.  I found that most combat encounters were designed well with all this in mind, especially when alongside Gail's (the player character) really well animated and weighty movement and combat motions, so you get lots of cool and satisfying moments where you're rolling under enemy attacks, smacking multiple enemies with charged hits and sending them flying, or being sent flying yourself but using a smooth recovery cancel and getting right back to the fight.I will say that there are a few cases where the game puts too many of one type of enemy in too tight a space or too many aerial enemies and only small platforms to stand on, so due to your relatively limited aerial control it can make for some frustrating moments where you're forced to just tank a lot of hits and burn through healing supplies fast, but these moments don't come along often and the game is reasonably generous with save points so you can usually try again pretty quickly if you fail.The game is quite slowly paced and one could probably say that around 90% of the game is optional content, so if you don't have time for long games or you prefer to jump in and play something to completion in a shorter time, then this game is not ideal for that. I found the game to be extremely engrossing and satisfying, and if you enjoy long form games with lots of exploration and are the type to go around talking to everyone and looking at everything in games then I'd say I can recommend this to you.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game. It has an interesting plot, awesome art style, some really cool puzzles and mechanics, and a very simple combat system. It is, by all objective standards, a well made and fully produced game.However, as much as I would recommend people getting this game, I also equally have to express immense annoyance with it. It seems to push. Every. Single. Button. I have. It has parkour challenges that are designed to be pretty simple and easy, yet are incredibly difficult purely due to one of those simple mechanics being super weird timing that clashes with the slightly clunky movement of the character. It has fights that are cool, very interesting boss fights! Until you figure out what the pattern is you need to use to attack them. Then it's just a matter of sitting there, bored and annoyed, as I annihilate the boss in a long and boring period of time. There isn't a large amount of skill or timing that's necessary for most of these bosses, it's just figuring out where your character should be positioned for any given attack, and being patient. I am not a patient person. Being required to wait like three seconds between hits doing nothing but jumping over easily dodged attacks and then my hits doing minimal damage because you can't really effectively upgrade your gear, that's not fun to me. That's annoying. I've gotten lost as to where I'm meant to go many times because there isn't any real solid way for you to know what the next plot thing you've got to do is in multiple points in the game. A lot of the places you have to travel through to progress aren't even really designed in any interesting way: It's not a "challenging fight" or a "difficult parkour" or a "beautiful path," it's just an amalgamation of the three that makes for me being distracted from the beauty of the path by the enemies, all while being knocked off the parkour and having to start all over again because one of them broke the thing I needed to bring with me.All in all, this game, more than most, makes me annoyed and frustrated. It's a big shame, because I genuinely think this is a good game with only a select few flaws. It's just that those flaws seem to be EXACTLY the flaws that I find annoying and frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: I had cautiously-optimistic expectations for Phoenotopia: Awakening, and it blew those expectations out of the water. I don't understand how I haven't heard more about this game. It's a really fun, engaging, and challenging Zelda-inspired adventure with a TON to do. The playtime estimates in the official description are accurate: my first completion-ish playthrough took me 35 hours, and full completion took me a total of 55 hours.I really enjoyed it!- The game has a bunch of varied challenges, and they're all pretty great. Besides combat it's got logic puzzle challenges, observation challenges, jumping challenges, timing challenges. A few puzzles required me to take notes, but no puzzle was a complete stumper.- I really enjoyed the combat, both against normal enemies and bosses. Your movement feels good to play, you get a bunch of fun tools and items, and the types of enemies you encounter are varied. I know there's plenty of folks out there who really dislike an aggressive stamina system, but I really appreciate how the stamina system makes you consider when to strike and when to back off and rest (and there does exist an accessibility setting to let you attack without using stamina, if you truly hate it). In all, the combat comes together in a super enjoyable way.- The bosses were intimidating and challenging in a way I really enjoyed. More than once I'd fight a boss and get destroyed, and wonder how the heck I'd ever possibly be able to defeat them, only to learn their moves over another three or four attempts, and beat them without much frustration.- The platforming's great. Running around as Gail is fun, many of your tools have traversal applications as well as combat applications. There's even a small Breath-of-the-Wild-ish aspect, where I was able to figure out how to combine my tools in interesting, probably-not-intended ways to sequence break a little, but in a way that felt like the game was rewarding me more than it felt like I was breaking the game.- The level design is fantastic, and really elevates both the platforming and exploration. In particular the towns: every town is fairly large, but every town past the first one is dense and layered and just, very fun to run around in and search for secrets.- There's a ton to explore. In addition to zones being dense, there's hundreds of upgrades to find, with unique quests and requirements for finding them. I was playing pretty completionist, and I only found around 2/3s of the upgrades without the use of the in-game hint system.- The plot is on-par with a Zelda: every beat has good stakes, with plenty to keep me engaged.- The setting and worldbuilding are very cool and deep without being overbearing.- The characters are all fun, and the game knows when to be a little serious and when to be a little silly with them (and importantly is able to pull off both effectively).- The pixel art is quite nice: simple and clear but intricate enough to hide cool secrets in. And the animation is very strong: it's all totally expressive, and every so often it flexes with something super impressive.- There's a bunch of different minigames, and they're all very cute, and just the right amount of challenging and engaging. Mostly I just want to call out the cooking minigame, which you'll probably end up doing a lot. It's the perfect amount of engaging, with real risks (burning your healing items) and real rewards (better healing items), while being short enough that it's a nice brief bit of downtime between fights and exploring, instead of being a huge chore.It's good! Again, I don't know how this one flew under my radar for so long! If you like the idea of a Zelda-adjacent sidescroller adventure, Phoenotopia: Awakening is better than any I've seen. Big recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Phoenotopia: Awakening

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, it's got a demo, and the demo is extremely representative of the game as a whole. Try it, and if you like the demo, buy it!Phoenotopia is a hard-to-spell game that mashes up concepts from several games: Its gameplay generally closely resembles Zelda II, especially with the overworld. It has a Dark Souls style stamina bar as well, and songs a la other Zelda games. But it brings plenty of original ideas too: most items have to be consumed in real time, though you can mash the button to eat them faster, so healing in combat requires waiting for an opportunity. You have a wide variety of tools available and even your mobility techniques are often usable for fighting too.The game is also gorgeous (Moonlight Ravine in particular) and has an amazing OST. It's good about providing save points and does give you a fast-travel option for getting around more easily later. It's well-written, the fun sort of difficult, and rewards exploration - the game is stuffed to the brim with secrets and items for you to find if you go hunting around for them.The biggest downside is that there's no map, but I'm sure you can find some online if you really need them. The areas generally are not complicated enough to really need one, it would just be a real nice-to-have.Still, absolutely great game, and definitely recommended.
