_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game that hearkens back to early SNES days with a ton of modern polish. This is my game of the year all things considered, but I can acknowledge that there are some issues that people will have with the game if you didn't grow up in that SNES era.Examples include - no map system outside of the world map, "awkward" combat that takes getting used to, and the sprint-jump system. The combat and sprint system can be mitigated by experimenting with how it works and playing around it once you figure it out instead of trying to fight it. I personally didn't have a problem with no map, but I do wish they'd add one in an update as it would be a fantastic accessibility feature to help others.I've outlined some tips farther down below to help you get around some of these issues!I think the game's art direction, world building, general platforming, and music make this game a masterpiece for me. Every area has it's own music and distinct style which both fit together incredibly well. Some of my favorite tracks are "Boss Battle" "The White Towers", and "Merry Fellowship".A few tips that I thought I'd share based on what people really dislike about the game based off other comments.~Exploration~- The game is focused on exploration and adventure over all other aspects! If you don't like to talk to NPCs or go off the normal path, the game probably isn't for you.- The game has a ton of secret areas which are referenced by NPCs. You can miss ~50% of combat tools  if you ignore NPCs hints or don't go looking for secret platforming areas.- Enemies and combat stats seem to be heavily weighted towards getting ~25-50% of the hidden items in the world when you can. The early game is a little difficult, but if you explore and get 50-75% of items, it quickly becomes quite easy.~Combat~- 99% of enemies do not have contact damage. Your short range isn't as detrimental as you might think because you can get right on top of enemies and not take damage.- Most enemies attack in front of them. If you're right on top of them, it's easy to jump behind them when their attack indicator shows to dodge the attack. Running backwards will likely get you hit, and the first few enemies (mainly frogs) are designed to teach you this mechanic.- Like early 2d platformer games, there is animation cancelling when your jump attack reaches the ground. Try to implement hop attacks often! They do ~1.5x normal hit damage. Early game, a short-hop jump attack > either power attack or normal attack does a lot of burst damage with little stamina consumption. - If you really do not like the stamina mechanic, there is an option to turn it off in the settings. With jump attacks or charging, it is easy to play around it, but some people still might not like it.~Sprinting/Stamina~- You can perfectly control yourself in the air after jumping when NOT sprinting.- Sprint jumps take you a fixed distance and should be reserved for combat ONLY. Maybe 1 or 2 jumps in the game require sprint. Otherwise it is just a massive lack of control and you'll be much better off doing a walking jump.- Walking jumps are great for repositioning, dodging attacks, or doing general platforming.-  Sprint jumps are a "get outta dodge" panic button in combat. Maybe you need to get away from an enemy quickly or get behind them. - In towns/general stretches of land, sprint > immediate jump > sprint immediately after landing > repeat is a fantastic way to preserve stamina compared to sprinting everywhere. You should be able to get the groove of this very quickly.- Spamming normal attack in combat does good damage, but will run you out of stamina quickly. Implement the jump attack animation cancel into your fights!Honestly this is one of the best games I've played and it was hard seeing the lower rating on steam due to people not experimenting with some of these mechanics and giving up early. Hopefully some of these tips help you on your adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: Exploration and puzzles are definitely the strong points of Phoenotopia Awakening, but it's got a bit of everything, really - combat, bosses, platforming, fishing, collectibles, a bit of humor, dozens of sidequests and something like a few hundred major and minor characters (and I have yet to find two NPCs that would have the same dialogue).Just a sheer WEALTH of things to do in this game is staggering - you can easily spend an hour or three away from the story, searching for moonstones, backtracking to previous locations or getting prizes at the shooting range. There is always something more to do, some remote cave or forest patch to explore.And the best thing is - the game respects you enough to make most of it non-mandatory. You could blaze through this game in like 10 hours, but explorers are constantly rewarded with little secrets hidden in every nook and cranny. As of writing this review, I'm 15 hours in, and will probably spend another 15 before I finish the main story... and yet it still feels like I've skipped a lot of stuff.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review:
Join Gail, a simple villager, who must heed the call for adventure when a great star ship appears in the night sky and abducts all the adults. As the new oldest member of her fragmented community, she must set out to solve this great mystery. Little does she know of the grand adventure before her, the evil lurking in the shadows, and the role she would play in the fight for Earth’s very existence!

Features:
- A narrative-driven single player adventure filled with charming characters, vibrant towns, and dangerous dungeons.
- Over 10 different weapons & tools with which to combat enemies and solve puzzles. Fly with rocket boots! Blast with bombs! Play the flute!
- Fight against over 50 different enemy types and 12 boss encounters.
- A world brimming with secrets! Find 33 Energy Gems, 55 Heart Pieces and 111 Moonstones.
- An achievement system, with 33 badges to earn, for players seeking extra challenge and replayability.
- Over 60 original songs ranging from mellow piano and orchestra to raging synth/metal rockers and bagpipes!
- A main campaign length estimated at 25 hours of playtime. 50 hours for completionists.

Solve the great mystery of the Phoenix!

name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy
detailed_description: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy will take Amadeus the Wizard, Zoya the Thief, and Pontius the Knight on their most action-packed journey yet! With their reputations tarnished, loved ones in danger, and their own magical powers at stake, the Heroes of Trine must reunite to push back a fearsome Clockwork army and bring peace and justice to the land! Traverse breathtaking 2.5D landscapes in Trine's deepest and visually richest chapter to date, with an all new cast of characters - some friends, some foes, but all unforgettable. Whether by yourself or playing with up to three friends in online and local co-op, the upgraded puzzle difficulty system keeps things fresh, adapting the challenge to the number of players. Level up the heroes' abilities with the all-new skill quest system, growing their legend as they are once again united by… the Trine! 2.5D adventure with world-renowned puzzle platformer action Combine forces in 1-4 players (single player, local and online co-op) Accessibility and replayability through an adaptive difficulty system for both combat and puzzles Beautiful fantasy world with stunning visuals New combat system and tense boss encounters Fairytale soundtrack, as well as a voice cast of returning favourites and charming new additions Character-specific skill quest system adds greater depth and playstyle variety than ever before Trine's most epic tale yet, with more levels, puzzles, and battles than previous entries Express yourself - deck the heroes of Trine out in customisable outfits Bring the kingdom back from the verge of clockwork oblivion in Trine's most magical story, with fiendish villains and memorable allies

_childDocuments_.review: Everytime a new Trine game comes out, I play it in coop with a long-time online friend with whom I have played through and 100%ed all of the previous Trine titles. This is sadly the only interaction we have nowadays, but I'm always happy we still have something common to enjoy.So, thanks, Frozenbyte, for still delivering titles, so the contact between my friend and me doesn't completely vanish. :)EDIT: Thank you for all the love, people.💜 We have now 100%ed this Trine game as well and greatly enjoyed it. We are looking forward to a potential DLC.I noticed this review did not include anything about the game itself, so I should add some things here.It's a new Trine game. Being the fifth in the series, one might think it actually could start to become boring and dull, but it honestly brought a lot of fresh air to the franchise. There are now new abilities for each hero to learn throughout the story which actually add a lot of depth to the gameplay. Especially Pontius is now a useful character outside of fights. Zoyas nerf from Trine 4 still applies, but I honestly do not care too much at this point, the first two Trine games could have very much been called "Zoya and Friends" for how OP her character was. Now the characters feel a lot more balanced. Furthermore, the game is obviously again way more optimized for controller and although I played the previous 3 2D titles with keyboard and mouse, this one was the first I exclusively used a controller for and it didn't feel wrong or weird for a second.The game's story dares to change the status quo on the series much more than I had anticipated but mainly the narrative serves the gameplay just well enough. I did not play this game, expecting complex writing, so I am quite content with what we got in the end.There is the occasional physics based puzzle that you're trying to solve that, maybe because of a bad connection to the host, completely glitches out, some mechanics feel a little janky here and there and I am not sure how many of the puzzles we actually solved or which ones we solved with cheese. But honestly, this is by now an integral part of the Trine experience and I would almost be suprised if it played completely smoothly and tightly all of a sudden.Overall, great addition to the Trine series. It is certinaly not the hardest game in the series, but   still challenging enough. if you enjoyed the previous games, this is definitely for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the original Trine back in 2009.I've played Trine 2 in 2012.I've played Trine 3 in 2015, but we don't talk about that one ;-)I've played Trine 4 in 2019, but only few days ago actually played through the Melody of Mystery DLC.And now I'm playing Trine 5 for the first time, and I must say that it is the absolute best Trine game of them all.It brings a tear of joy to see the best ideas of all the games brought together in such beautiful and perfectly designed game:1. Unlocking core skills as you progress through the game, just like Trine 1 and Trine 4 did...2. Having short sections where only a single hero can participate, just like Trine 3 did...3. A plethora of optional upgrades which can be refunded as needed (T2 and T4)...4. Beautiful physics puzzles5. And a significantly improved combat system, which is less constrained than the confusing and chaotic Trine 4, but not as exploitable as Trine 2.Apparently taking advantage of the same fundamental engine as Trine 4, the developers could truly focus on the environments, which are absolutely epic, with the smart camera movement showing you the grand vistas, but also on great puzzle design and combat encounters. Unlike Trine 4, where combat was a chaotic clickfest with endless resurrections of your heroes as they would inevitably die, here, the camera tends to pull back a bit, giving you a wider view of the battlefield, and even allowing moving to the sides (Trine 4 was locked into a single screen and at later levels, it felt seriously cramped). Enemies also nicely telegraph their intentions and it's much easier to recognize who should be prioritized and how to avoid taking too much damage.All the little secrets hidden throughout the levels are a staple of Trine games, and the option to return to any checkpoint from the map screen and chase the missing experience or items is great - this feature makes a return from Trine 4.

_childDocuments_.review: I like Trine I do. I wish I was allowed to give a middle review to games however steam refuses to let me do so. In which I will have to give this game a thumbs up, yet there are still things I have to say about this game. Trine is a great series, a great game, a great group of people who make wholesome and fun games. Yet the more Trines they come out with the more it becomes apparent that this game has strayed further from what it is origin.Allow me to explain the thing that made Trine 1 so interesting and amazing was that it was a game that you could be played in any of the three ways they gave to you. It allowed you to play your way, to find your own solutions to the problems the game puts before you. Enemies? Kill them, avoid them, trap them, crush them. You could do many different things without being forced to change your own play style. A large pit ahead? Jump it, build around it, fly above it. Each character had a solution to a problem in their own way, sometimes somewhere easier to get to than other for certain situations. Trine 2 was also a improvement on this, though it became more puzzle like and instead of a challenging platformer which is fine.This brings me to Trine 4 and 5 (We dont talk about 3). It goes from playing your way to playing the way that is provided to you. Puzzles are mandatory, you have to find a certain solution to already developed problem in your path. You are not allowed to progress until you discover the solution they want you to discover. There is nothing wrong with this, it is just a shift in gameplay compared to the first two games. I like Trine, I have played every game they have put out. But I do miss the days of fun exploration that Trine 1 and 2 provided to us. Instead of being forced to engage in puzzles to pad out play time. I wish to explore the world of Trine freely and unhindered. The world you have made is a joy and sometimes I feel bogged down being forced engage in ways I wouldnt normally. Yet still I persist. This game. It is good. It is worth your time. I am just rambling upon days gone by, things change, nothing always stays the same and this is fine. There is passion in this project and it shows as always. I hope Trine continues to succeed.

This terrible behavior also exists in Trine 3 and 4 but you can fix it yourself for all the current Trine games, including this one.How to:1. On your deck, switch to Desktop2. In the file manager go to Home3. in the top right hamburger menu, select "Show Hidden Files"4. click through .steam/steam/steamapps/compdata/1436700/pfx/drive_c/users/steamuser/Application Data/Trine 55. Open options.txt6. add the line :or depending on whether you want to run this at 40 or 60 fps when running on battery. Note that it is renderingModule even though all the other options use rendererModule!7. Save options.txtNow you can switch back to Gaming Mode and the game should now run at the fps you chose. I recommend 40 btw.For Trine 3 and 4 this works basically the same, but you have to choose the app number in the file path. It's 319910 for Trine 3 and 690640 for Trine 4. You can also find these numbers in the URL for their respective Steam Store pages. For Trine 3 and 4 you also don't need to add the line to option.txt, you have to change the existing one from 30 to 40 or 60.I hope this helps someone :)

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been waiting for Trine 5 for almost three years, I have to say the wait has been absolutely worthwhile.After playing the first four Trine games in a row three years ago, I felt as if I had discovered a hidden gem. Trine 1 was a game that was released in 2009. It felt magical and unbelievable in many ways. The physics and sound design of the game was top-notch, creating a realistic and immersive experience. The combat was incredibly fun combined with amazing sound design. The art was vibrant and stunning, and the characters were all unique and had their own special abilities. Versatile characters and how they could all handle each puzzle was genius, making every puzzle solvable with every single one of them and combining their abilities. The music was beautiful and perfectly complemented the game. All of these elements combined made the game incredibly enjoyable and memorable, and are carried through to the later games, excluding Trine 3. They went in another direction with that game. It didn't fit Trine but it was a decent game anyway.As each new release came out, they implemented incredible new game mechanics while upgrading the physics engine. Throughout its 10-15 hour playtime, they introduce new mechanics and dynamics to the gameplay, which keeps the game flowing without boring the player once. That's Trine 5 for you. Everything is perfect except for combat, which I think they handled way better in terms of the feel in all of the previous titles. Trine 5 looks god-tier beautiful, very similar to Ori and the Will of the Wisps level art. I think that describes how beautiful this game, and this series look. The Trine series is the best puzzle-platformer series out there with Little Nightmares. Thank you so much to everyone at THQ Nordic and Frozenbyte for making this kind of niche series continue. Also giving each game the attention, the budget, and the time it needs to develop. You guys raise the bar for the genre every single time.  It's a testament to the power of creative thinking and commitment to excellence.Follow My Curator Page:

_childDocuments_.review: While I was initially excited, this is the first Trine entry which didn't make me actively anticipate the next level. Trine 5's visuals are serious eye-candy but that's synonymous with the series at the point. What Frozenbyte did differently this time is make levels longer and puzzles more convoluted. Perfect for those looking for a challenge but *not* ideal for players who want balance. Many of the gameplay staples (Amadeus' conjuring abilities, Zoya's elemental arrows and Pontius' Shield of Light) are reprised but Zoya has a cool new teleportation ability (fox rope) and Amadeus can double-jump (wind burst leap-extremely useful). I revere Pulkkinen's music but a lot of the compositions here didn't make a splash other than 'The Royal Castle', 'Gemstone Caverns' (personal favourite), 'The Astral Observatory' and 'The Magnificent Airship'. The mechanical clockwork theme is used to great effect in both enemy and level design and I appreciate this creative risk. Trine 5's combat is ok (although I feel Amadeus gets underutilised) and the story won't have you on the edge of your seat but it's serviceable. Overall decent but missing some magic. Would rate neutral if possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Good but not great.As always in this series, fantastic graphics and fine details. Which makes you go crazy wondering why would you go through all this trouble to make a stunning scenery or room which you spend five seconds on and move on in the game. It's really not necessary, spend the resources to make more actual content instead of filler - more puzzles and more complexity.Trine 5 did a great job introducing cool new skills that really create a great potential for interesting puzzles. Instead most puzzles require one or two characters doing basic things and moving on. It's so odd that you frequently check again and again to see if you've missed the point of this room/puzzle, it can't be that you are just supposed to jump on two platforms and move on, right? The room must have taken a few days to make. But yes, almost always that is the case.It's sad that a puzzle game has maybe 2-3 good puzzles that make you think logically instead of just do the obvious things you need to do and move on. Most of the game is a filler, gorgeous filler, but annoying nonetheless. I do recommend you play it, and it's definitely worth the cheap price it usually goes for, but I hope the focus shifts to interesting puzzles that use the many skills together. I'd rather have that than more art.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a new chapter and an absolutely wonderful journey in the series of Trine. I really didn't think I'd ike it so much just like I like it now that I completed it at 100%. My personal favourite is perhaps still the second game, but this one is very close to it. And actually it didn't do anything special, just delivered us stunning visuals, an epic and long story, and interesting puzzles and secrets to find. It was superb, fun, sometimes challenging, gorgeous and occasionally frustrating - but in a good way. I always loved to interact with animals, also loved to achieve nice achievements, so I was happy from this side as well.A bit of a downside:Firstly, I heard in the release version didn't have online co-op mode, which is kinda mehFurthermore, I would like to see that we are not getting and learning the same skills as before, it's just a bit disappointing after years of experience, and new ways would greatly help to improve the longevity of Trine highly, I believeLastly, I like the music, and basically in everything music always played a vital aspect to me, so I was disheartened that we didn't get more original tracks, however, I can understand the designers' choice behind it in that "Look, how far we've come", and liked the new arrangement of the older melodies, but I'm firmly believing Ari Pulkkinen can do way more than this.+1 for the fun, SPOILER: Pretty please, devs, give Amadeus Fireball spells!!! All in all, I can only and happily recommend this fantastic game, and even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those case where I wish I could leave a mixed review.Trine 5 has everything you love about Trine : the visuals are gorgeous and polished, the music and fairytale vibe, the characters and banter. What makes Trine good is here.However Trine 5 makes the mistake of trying way too hard to give new stuff to players. Trine 4 struck the perfect balance between being Trine and having new mechanics to toy with. Trine 5 goes way to far in terms of new mechanics.What I always loved about Trine is that it allows room for creativity when solving puzzle. You are given a set of tool, a puzzle, and it's up to you to figure out a (meaning one of the) solutions. Trine 5 gives you an arsenal of tool, and for a lot of puzzles, only one of those tool will allow you to complete the puzzle. Most of the new tools you are given are introduced, used for a few puzzles, then forgotten about until the next time you need them. But by that time you don't even remember you could do that. Each characters has like 6/7+ mechanics tied to them, that can or can not interact between them or with other characters. Being stuck on a puzzle because you couldn't remember that the clone of the warrior can use the sword that attach to the rope of the thieve while the wizard reverse gravity of the blah blah blah... feels fundamentally bad.I am roughly halfway through the main storyline (solo) and the games feels like a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Trine 5 is another stunningly beautiful and fantastic entry in the Trine series. Using the standard 2.5D perspective, it is similar to Trine 4, 2, and 1, just longer and more colorful. The three heroes return, along with the narrator, all with their same voices and cheesy humor. It has more cinematic flair than previous entries, with many fully-animated cutscenes that have close-up views of heroes and villains, although sometimes it pushes the view a bit too close.Levels are generally amazing, set across orange forests, murky swamps, dark sewers, gemstone caves, castle battlements, and more. Hidden rooms contain bonus gear that you can equip, and it is fun (and quick, due to the frequent checkpoints) to go back and find missed vials or extra narrative text. Short interludes have players taking control of a single hero through a small area to unlock a new skill. This helps pacing and aids skill introduction. There are some tricky brain teasers in levels that can halt progress. Some puzzles seemed impossible at first and a few were solved by glitching the physics system with twitchy ropes and bouncy boxes. But there are also multiple ways to get through puzzles, and optional side rooms are easier with all the abilities, so they can be left for later.Combat is marginally better than before, because of a few new abilities for Amadeus, and tempered enemy distribution. You are mostly fighting skeletons, rats, and the titular Clockwork Knights, and there are some okay boss battles thrown into the mix. Across 20 long levels, the game took about 16 hours to complete and required another four to get all experience vials. It does provide great value although it is also probably a bit long. That said, if you enjoyed previous entries then Trine 5 is a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: Teddy approved game!  would approve it too... if he only would have played it coop with me. ):Okay... the heroes of Trine are back in their 5th game of the series. Trine 5 is a side-scrolling platformer with let's call it parkour and logic puzzles and some fighting, paired with awesome, heartwarming graphics, an atmospheric soundtrack, a very good voiced narration and most of all easy to learn and very addicitve gameplay. Alone or in 2/3/4 player coop. I guess mostly everyone has played or at least heared of one of the Trine games in the past.  So let's concentrate here on what Trine 5 is doing better... and most sadly doing worse than its predecessors.The good things of Trine 5:- The graphics reached a new level. Most often absolutely stunning. Even better than the graphics of the Trine 4 DLC "Melody of Mystery"- Even more skills for each of the 3 heroes- Different logic puzzles for 1 or 2 player- Gameplay is the most addictive of all five Trine gamesThe bad things of Trine 5:- Most sadly the devs returned to implement "special" achievements (usually actions you would never do in normal gameplay) in addition to "finish a level" and "find all xp in a level", which are frustrating to complete (greetings to Trine 2) and most of all don't always trigger (big greetings to Trine 2). The glorious moment of Trine 2 when we've finished the game in hardcore mode in 3-coop... and the achievement only unlocked for 2 of the 3 players. Good job. A friend still tries to unlock Boreal Bowling in Trine 5, although many frozen enemies shattered into pieces with a ball... and the achievement still didn't unlock for him. Quite some people in the forums also seem to have problems to unlock "finish a level without taking any damage".@Devs: sometimes it is good to just ignore the trolls in the forums, who always ask for extra difficult achievements. Trine at least should be a fun game from the start to the end... like in Trine 3 and 4.- Perhaps it's only me, but I have the impression that there are much more logical puzzles in Trine 5 than parkour puzzles. - In addition the logical puzzles are much easier in single player than in 2 player coop for example. So if you play coop with one friend, you will make your life more difficult... not easier. Sometimes you wish you would have a gun and just shoot your way through this or that annoying 2-player coop puzzle (which was so easy in single player). Oh... while you're already here and we talk about having good fun... with a gun! :) Please take a wishlisting-and-following-look at the upcoming good game from a nice friend of mine: But anyway! The good things of Trine 5 outweigh the bad ones. So what more to say... rather than: Buy, buy, buy! (© and ® and ™ by )★★★★★5/5

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I played Trine 5 in unlimited mode, local multiplayer and easy difficulty. I've also played Trine 1, 2 and 4 twice (both single player and local multiplayer) and Trine 3 once (single player). With those in mind, here are my thoughts and comparison.* The story is somewhat fun, but not really memorable with 1 dimensional villain.* Beautiful visual and 2.5D environment.* Fairly good soundtrack.* The game runs well on my Linux device.* Better experience with generic controller, although I still prefer using keyboard and mouse.* Zoya and Pontius have more skills to help platforming. I also like the fact Amadeus now has skill .* Easy difficulty is more forgiving than previous Trine games, especially during the combat.* Many puzzles are easy, with the exception of a puzzle in act IV, chapter 13.Steam says my playtime is 15 hours, but our actual playtime is only 14 hours since we took a few small breaks without exiting the game. Overall Trine 5 remains fun, although I also agree it lacks innovation/some positive change which makes the game feel stale or boring for some Trine fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how much more there is to say than that it's more Trine. If you haven't played the rest of them, go do those first -- not because there's any real story relevance between them, but because most of them are great, and undoubtedly cheaper. If you have played the rest of them, you probably don't need to be told any of this. It's good Trine.For those who aren't familiar with this series, which despite only being known about by about 1000 people is still somehow getting one game after another, Trine is a puzzle platforming series with an emphasis on co-op. The newer games support four players, but they're meant for three, one for each character. The knight is good at fighting and can use his comically large shield for anything from gliding to using it as a platform for the others, the thief has a grappling hook that can tether items together, the wizard can conjure up various shapes and levitate things, and every game one of the three is laughably overpowered compared to the other two. The newer games also let you set the character swapping to unlimited, where you can have multiple players playing a particular character at once, but unless you have a four person group (which would require it) I prefer the classic setting that restricts you to one each. The puzzles do change to accommodate it in either case, with Unlimited mode sometimes requiring multiple of one character instead of just allowing it, but it loses the importance of being reliant on whichever player is playing a certain character and the chaos of coordinating three people.Trine 5 also has a puzzle difficulty toggle that I at least don't remember the previous games having. Nobody else seems to realize this, either -- I know this because the one time my group finally cracked and I tried to look up a walkthrough (I know, I know, but in our defense it was 2 AM), even the ones that said they were playing on hard mode only had the combat set to hard. The game warns you that it isn't meant for your first time, even if you've played the previous games, and quite frankly I agree, but in a game like this that just makes it that much funnier to play with a few friends. Coming across a puzzle you have no idea how to solve, breaking it in half with the combined efforts of three heroes and some thoughtfully applied physics, and moving on without ever figuring out what you were supposed to do is a cornerstone of the Trine experience, and the tradition is more alive than ever here.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Trine series since I was a kid but I will not be recommending this game due to repeating of itself too much. Actually Trine series is always about repeating itself with same game model in every game except Trine 3: The Artifacts of Power. I truly think that was a disappointing game with that 3D-ish experience. But atleast it was a short game I finished it something like in 3-4 hours with fully completion. After that game Trine left that design and returned to its origin with Trine 4: The Nightmare Prince which was a fun game to play. But Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy is repeating itself too much, for example there are unnecessary "Skill Levels" which is a tutorial for your new learned skills (Which we had these skills in the last game, by the way I don't have problem with learning same skills or similar skills in every Trine. This is Trine design of course they will introduce you new skills to solve difficult puzzles as you continue through the game) but even when I was playing Level 15 (There are 20) I had to play that totally unnecessary tutorial level to learn "How to cling two ropes at the same time with Zoya" Why am I forced to play these levels. I know Trine basics after all these 5 games. In level replays you can skip them but in original walkthrough you have to play tutorials. There needs to be a setting that can turn this off (If there is I couldn't find it).Story of this game is classical one for Trine but art-style, dialogs and characters reactions are kinda funny.Boss fights are good for Trine, don't expect much but it's satisfying.Puzzles are just puzzles there are hard ones and there are easy ones. But I can really say that puzzles force you to use most of the skills to solve it. (or you can cheese it with Amadeus' conjures if you fast enough to rope it and fly yourself)Above I mentioned how was Trine 3: The Artifacts of Power a really short game and I really can say that Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy is unnecessarily long. Its story can be told in 12-15 Levels. There are useless characters that was just there to be exist and mentioned only. Like, you are meeting a Necromancer in very early stages of game and what happens next do you think? You don't see him again like after 2 levels. There are characters like this. They are just there to be exist, developers probably think these characters would make you feel something exciting but I can't get excited for the characters that I know as nothing more than props. For short, game is pretty long for this repeating puzzles, level designs and story. If you like Trine series you can give it a chance but I don't recommend it. Probably, I will not be buying it if there will be a Trine 6 in the future atleast if it isn't be presenting something new and good.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Trine yet, combining the best elements of Trine 2 and 4 and adding some new ones.Most important improvements:- Greatest improvement: The puzzles. You really have to learn what each of the new skills does and learn to combine them properly. You can (usually) no longer bruteforce solutions with tons of boxes or planks (as in Trine) or by using the Faerie rope (Trine 4). Some levels also have segments which you have to solve with only one character, which helps to really learn the intracacies of each skill.- More levels than ever before, and most are quite long. Many levels also have mechanics (e.g. electricity, floating bubbles) which can only be found in that level, making each level memorable. - Combat is also improved over Trine 4. You no longer have to fight in a closed off arena which is separated with indestructible walls from normal gameplay. This allows you once again to use the environment to your advantage (e.g. kicking enemies into traps or levitating them into pits).If you liked any of the previous entries in the Trine series, you will like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Trine 5 continues the great series with more puzzle/platforming goodness.  If you've played Trine before in the series, you will be very comfortable in this game, as it does what this series does best.  In Trine you play as three characters, which you can switch to in single player, or play up to three players at a time each with a unique character.  The three characters are Zoya, the thief who uses arrows and a rappelling rope/hook to connect to things, you have Pontius the fighter who can use his sword and shield, and eventually his hammer, and finally you have Amadeus the wizard who can conjure up a box, a sphere.As you progress the game and collect bottles, you can eventually purchase new skills.  Or in this iteratin of the series, you will have special areas in certain levels where only one character goes off on their own and eventually find a skill during that portion of the level.  The skills are somewhat reminiscent of the past.  Zoya can now have frozen or fire arrows.  Pontius can use his shield like a kite, and Amadeus can conjure up more items.  But this iteration offers new skills which are both welcome additions and also make the game very easy if you're good at collecting the bottles.While the skills might make the game easier in the long run, the game does a great job, better than previous titles of the series in my opinion, of forcing you to  use the newly learned skills for puzzles.  There are so many puzzles in this game, a much larger amount than previous games in the series, but I thought they were really well done and really forced you to think through the new skills you had acquired and how to use them.  Eventually, as you got further on the story, you had to remember the skills you learned as now you had to mix them all up.  It really added to the game's puzzle portion, but the platforming was still king.Speaking of story, here you find a world being taken over by the Clockwork army, the enemies you will be fighting throughout the game.  Your goal is to defeat the army, its leaders, and save Amadeus' children.  There aren't too many variety of enemies to defeat, but the majority of the game is platforming and puzzles, so fighting has such distance between fight scenes that it's ok for the lack of variety.  There are some special enemies that show up, such as boss fights, but none of the fighting is too difficult.  The story as a whole is not really king in this game as it just creates a backdrop for why you are doing what you're doing, but the fun is in the platforming and the puzzles, not the story at all.I've already spoken of the beautiful gorgeous graphics, but Trine is famous for always pushing the envelope.  Here this is no different.  Each level, 20 in total, offers a different scenery and the details really show everywhere.  Frozenbyte always sets a standard that I feel other platformers rarely meet.The music was good, but nothing to speak of, the sound was actually really good, and especially as usual the dialogue of all characters were more than good enough to continue the immersion of the game.In my opinion Trine 2 is still the best in the series, but I would place Trine 5 second, with Trine 1, Trine 4, and Trine 3 to follow.  If you have not tried any of the others in the series, please do so as this series has been great since the beginning with one, albeit still fun, side step with Trine 3.Highly recommend you play this game, as it's a great puzzle platformer.  I did not play with anyone else in this game so I can't really say how much fun it would be as a multiplayer, and I also only played on a controller no keyboard.  The game feels smooth and should probably played on a controller for best experience.

_childDocuments_.review: + awesome gameplay mechanics with 3 characters+ cool level design+ fun skills of each character+ fairy tale story+ gorgeous visuals+ great soundtrack+ online co-op- couple of bugs/glitches- some flimsy combat encounters- stiffer movement/conjuring compared to the previous Trine games- (for some) no hard difficulty or hardcore modePlaying another entry in the Trine series is like visiting an old friend after a while. Some things might be different but it's still your old buddy. This time they really nailed the visuals but the new mechanics are nice too. And, surprisingly, also the story is rich and feels longer than it is. So much happens in it, lots of it surprisingly dark. Even character lore is expanded.While adventuring starts slow and clunky it gets better as you gain skills, especially for Pontius. Fights are a mixed bag. I LOVED the boss fights, figuring out the mechanics and then using all your skill is very cool and fun. What I did not enjoy were the fights where you have a big group of monsters flung at you. Mainly because majority of enemies have a ranged attack and so trying to position yourself became akin to bullet hell where 3-4 enemies shot at the same time, some having multiple projectiles. And because Pontius' shield breaks after 2-3 hits you cannot block it all so defensive play isn't encouraged. This ironically made Pontius less useful in fights because Zoya can swing, wall jump and has ranged fire arrows that ricochet. All making her my go-to for majority of fights. You would only use Pontius in boss fights where his mechanics (shield deflect, charge, etc.) are needed. Amadeus has some nice upgrades for fighting but the speed and amount of enemies simply makes him much less viable for combat.Now the game is clearly designed for co-op so most of the problems are circumvented by having more players split the roles and enemies. Default controls are console/gamepad so if you're on mouse & keyboard then go into the options and turn on stuff like conjuring by drawing shape or sword pointing at mouse cursor.Steam Deck gameplay is ...okay. To be great there would have to be a (non-user) fix for the 30fps lock when on battery. Also to be able to swap movement to arrow keys instead of left stick. Conjuring is done only on top of Amadeus instead of where the cursor is. So traversal is just fine but when fights or death traps start you see it lacking a bit.I did find some glitches like menu pop-up, letters/tidbits/fashion items closing when opened. Also sometimes the game crashed due to the GPU driver and wouldn't start until a PC restart. So Trine 2 is still king but I dare say this comes in as second best in the series. Definitely recommended!------------------------------------------------------------------

Try to guess the gender of the head of the Astral academy... Female. Wizards at the observatory? 2 females who are doing alright and a male who has made a blunder and has been sick ever since... _childDocuments_.review: Trine series are a weird beast. The original wasn’t good, but had a lot of really cool ideas. All of which got majorly improved in the sequel, which was the first genuinely enjoyable title in the series. Then Trine 3 was released in Early Access and remained unfinished, mixing lots of very bad ideas with some of the genuinely best ideas in the franchise. And then Trine 4 came along and was mostly a straight up improvement again returning to the formula of 2, but making it more fun and adding fresh ideas. First hours with Trine 5 felt like I was playing 4 again, but with some tweaks and changes. It was charming, as always, and quite fun to play. But the more I played, the less fun the game got. And almost at the end of the game I just gave up, feeling fed up with horrible design of the game.If you’ve never played a Trine title before, it’s a thematic continuation of titles like Lost Vikings or Gobliiins, played as a side scrolling platformer mixed with light action RPG mechanics. There are 3 characters, all with distinct abilities, and in smartly using those abilities alone or in combination, you overcome the problems and puzzles the game is constantly throwing at you. Game can be played in coop, where it’s a more silly fun experience, or it can be played solo (as I usually play these), where it’s more of a straight puzzle platformer game. But silly jank solutions are still possible solo, just more limited.Easily the worst offender of the series, that has not been fixed or changed whatsoever yet again, is the combat. Occasionally your jumping and puzzle solving is interrupted by an arena with enemies or a boss fight and they’re always just a slog to go through. None of them are ever difficult, but none of them are ever fun either and it’s something that the series never figured out. You do get a few more abilities to use in combat this time around, but they don’t really change the experience in a meaningful way.Speaking of abilities, that’s possibly the biggest issue Trine 5 has. As it goes along it stops being just Trine 4 again by adding more unique and curious abilities, which is great. Except, somewhere by the middle of the game your arsenal of possible actions becomes confusingly broad, whereas puzzles that the game presents (in solo) are very limited in how you can solve them. So it stops being about figuring out a fun combination of tools you use all the time and becomes a very slow and tedious process of eliminating which of all the tools are definitely not going to help you there.Which is not helped by the fact that the puzzle design in these games always bordered on almost never looking “as intended”. So when you do get to solve an issue, it looks like you’re exploiting some horrible bug in the game and not “solving a puzzle” a lot of the time. With previous games, this was often balanced out to feel relatively okay and most bizarre puzzles were relegated to optional objectives. But in Trine 5 you either get puzzles that are super clear or puzzles where “intended” solution is just indecipherable, even if they are required to progress.Even more strangely, the game adds a lives system on most difficulty levels, which feels… utterly pointless for things that it seems to be designed for? But frustrating for things that it shouldn’t have affected. Most times I died because I was trying to see if a particular hole in the ground that looks like any other hole in the ground is a bottomless pit or it has secrets – because there’s usually no visual indication at all. Or due to my character glitching out or simply not performing the move it should’ve. Some puzzle elements in the game work “just because” with no real explanation – you just learn it at some point. Some work extremely inconsistently and change based on what the designers felt that day. Sometimes weird glowing surfaces instantly kill you, some of them don’t… The game genuinely feels like a mess as far as the level and puzzle design goes. Which is a shame, because in terms of the story and presentation and music it feels as an improvement over the previous game.In some ways Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy to me felt like the Japanese Super Mario Bros. 2 (internationally known as The Lost Levels). Where the developers took the best the series was so far – Trine 4, – and then tried to make it harder and more-er. And if they just stuck to it being Trine 4 again, it would’ve been boring. But as it is – it switches between being boring and being frustrating. Maybe it’s a less obnoxious experience in coop, but if you like playing these games solo – I’d avoid this one. Play the fourth one instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This might actually be my new favorite of the Trine series -- mechanically, at least, I feel like everything fits together here beautifully.  It's nice and long (19 levels plus one "final boss" level), its story is (IMO) more engaging than the usual Trine storylines, and the puzzles feel nice and complex.  The levels, as usual, are absolutely gorgeous to look at, and the game is a treat on the eyes.Even though I quite liked the story in this one, I *do* feel like it was wrapped up very unsatisfactorily (spoilers follow):   There's also one boss battle and one in-level scenario which I personally found a little over-challenging on "normal" mode (I know, I know, git gud), but that's easily addressed by in-game difficulty settings which can both ease combat and the resurrection restrictions, so that hardly counts against the game.Overall I was quite pleased with the game, and I think it's spurred me to go play through the other installments again.  If you're a fan of the series, IMO you won't be at all disappointed with this one!

_childDocuments_.review: "Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy" is here to take you on another magical adventure. If you've played the previous Trine games, you know the drill: stunning visuals, clever puzzles, and a dash of humor thrown in for good measure. But does this fifth installment live up to the hype?Let's start with the visuals, because dang, they're gorgeous. From lush forests to intricate clockwork contraptions, every level is a feast for the eyes. Seriously, you'll want to stop and admire the scenery every few minutes.Gameplay-wise, Trine 5 keeps the formula fresh with new puzzles and challenges. Whether you're swinging on grappling hooks or conjuring boxes to solve environmental conundrums, there's never a dull moment. Plus, the addition of co-op multiplayer means you can team up with your buddies for even more fun.But it's not all sunshine and rainbows. Some of the puzzles can be a bit too tricky, leading to moments of frustration. And while the story is charming, it's nothing groundbreaking.Overall, "Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy" is a solid addition to the series. It's fun, it's beautiful, and it's perfect for a cozy night of gaming with friends. Grab your controllers and get ready for a magical journey like no other!

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful masterpiece of a platformer with puzzles. Despite the relatively simple powers of each character, it is mind-boggling how varying (and occasionally difficult) the puzzles in the game are. The character and environment design are gorgeous, and the game looks stunning in every instant.On the other hand, combat and story are relatively unexceptional. The story is extremely simple and straightforward; just enough to give some context to the levels you are passing. There are interesting combat encounters and new mechanics (both for enemies and player characters), but overall, it is still a weaker part of the game compared to puzzles. That said, the ability to set the difficulty of combat and puzzles separately is an amazing addition that allows you to tweak your experience to get the most out of the game. Want to challenge your brain with creative puzzles? Set combat to easy and puzzles to hard. You'll have a great time.

If you've never played Trine before, almost anyone would enjoy this game so go ahead and pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Trine 5: A clockwork Conspiracy is an ingenious sequel to the Trine-series that's almost able to reach the excellence of Trine 2. Once again, the new game offers various 2.5D-puzzles and also a few new, interesting game mechanics. Compared to Trine 4, it does stronger in the battle-side of the game, but on the puzzle-side it's a bit easier. It's probably needless to say that the atmosphere in this game is, once again, amazing.One thing I noticed instantly is that Trine 5 has way more fighting scenes than its predecessor Trine 4. Sadly,  even though the battles go frictionlessly, the different enemies lack in diversity and get boring quite fast. The balance between puzzles and battles is still well-thought and this upgrade is definitely gladly received.Another surely welcome thing that Trine 4 and Trine 3 didn't have is a long achievement list. Of course, getting all the xp and other collectibles gives you the basic achievements, but now we finally got back those fun little tasks including carrying a takeaway pie through the map. Still, the given extra achievements don't quite reach the difficulty levels of those in Trine 2, making the full playtime to be only around 20-25.So, to sum up the game: Trine 5 is closer to being the best game in the series than any Trine (excluding the best) before. In some aspects, it does actually beat Trine 2: it has modern animations and the bugs and broken physics are conspicuous by their absence. The only thing that drags the game down from the 1st place is the fact that it's easier and shorter than Trine 2. In general, it's still nearly a perfect puzzle platformer and definitely worth the money.9,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very Trine - cutesy and well it's Trine. That being said, this is a hard game to decide how to rate. It's Trine, but this one had some seriously more difficult puzzles than previous titles did. There were a few encounters that are harder than normal as well. The difficulty was Trine-like throughout most of the game (combat and puzzles), but there were insane spikes that featured non-intuitive solutions to problems, and then it would go back to normal Trine difficulty. I liked most of the new mechanics, but the co-op straight up just didn't work at times. Not that we couldn't play together, but that some of the puzzles were downright not doable in co-op. This was much more frequent towards the end of the game, where we'd have to leave co-op to solve them solo before rejoining each other after passing whichever puzzle it was. This happened 3 to 5 times total throughout the game. My co-op partner isn't sure he wants to play Trine games anymore, and I'm not sure either. This frustration absolutely killed the mood and feel or immersiveness of the game.I had issues with stat points not saving between sessions, whether I was the host or not. Every time I joined my only co-op partner for a session it would make a new save file requiring me to delete saves before being allowed to play again, once I hit the limit of 10. Deleting said saves didn't always work either. This was much more buggy than previous games. Also, why were all the other Trine games around or less than 10 hours and this one 20+? It was far too long and overstayed its welcome.TLDR: I'd say if you're playing these solo, then sure give Trine 5 a shot. However if you're playing them in co-op I may steer clear of this title and just replay one of the previous games. I've played all the Trine games, and this was my least favorite one. It was even worse than the weird 3d one.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics 10+Sound 9 Gameplay 9 Challenge 7.5 Replay factor 8An absolutely brilliant game and the best in the Trine series. The best aspect of the game is the by far though the graphics, a tremendously pretty pretty looking game with a outstanding animation, I will go on record in saying this is one of the best looking games of ALL time.The gameplay is top not notch, brilliant mix of platforming, physics based puzzles and light combat, it does not do anything really new now but what it does, it does fantastically well. Sound is great and managing to retain the same voice actors for all 5 games is actually quiet a feat, especially for Victoria Kruger who's the sultry voice of Zora is such a treat to listen too. But in all honesty the voice acting is some of the best ever in a game and really lends to the game well. Music is also especially top quality, with it's whimsical dream like quality to it very easy on the ears. Challenge depends who you are it is not really hard but can get quiet challenging later on, but is easier with 3 people, so reasonable but not Dark Souls level of frustration. Gameplay is awesome as everything is well designed especially the puzzles and locations make it so fun to play especially with 3 or more people certainly a great party game and a game that is a good ice breaker to get to know someone better.Overall an absolutely quality game with a supreme amount of love and dedication and polish gone into it, and the asking price is absolutely spot on. Well done Frozenbyte for this gem of a game I hope you many many sales as you deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: Be prepared to understand nothing of the characters, if you haven’t recently played the earlier games. I highly recommend checking a summary or something before playing.I love the series, and highly recommend the games. Trine 2 is still my favorite of the series.Love the music and game play graphics as always. Not sure how I feel about some of the more stylized choices made for the menus and other art.Boss fights are separated into stages, where you have to figure out a “puzzle” before you can do damage again. After you know what to do, the fights are super easy. It took me a frustratingly long time to figure out some of them. Towards the end I started just googling what to do instead of spending hours stuck.Sometimes the experience or hidden chest is in a place outside the map where you normally wouldn’t look (eg. top of a wall). Nothing wrong with this, but sometimes the maps aren’t designed for you to search or reach these areas. The game either glitches out a lot or the textures, hitboxes and background elements aren’t finished and just… end.I got myself stuck in mid air multiple times when looking for hidden things, and had to return to map to get unstuck.If your PC isn’t that beefy be prepared to suffer from horrible textures and the game running slow at times. Sometimes item hitboxes glitch out anyways. So be prepared to suffer from a seemingly still item suddenly launching a character into oblivion. Especially if using Amadeus’s locked objects near chains or ropes. Or that objects might sink into the environment or clip into each other…Also the automated functions can be annoying: eg. Zoya randomly grabbing onto random edges instead of using her grappling hook, or a character trying to use hanging Pontius clone as a platform and getting stuck inside him.Also, sometimes there are pieces of puzzles that you can’t figure out how you are supposed to use them. I watched a few walkthroughs, where players just ignored these objects and used unlocked skills to pass the obstacle without figuring out what you were supposed to do. I still have no idea about some of them.Even through all this criticism the game was obviously worth it, and I highly recommend. I will be replaying the series next!

_childDocuments_.review: ( TLDR for the people who don't want to read the full review )Skip that, the game is full woke, especially the ending and the "poor poor kids" (if I were Amadeus, I'd let them go and move on. Conveniently, his wife never appears in the game on screen to cover the fact what "his" kids are).The cringe trailer was not an accident.You don't get more PAYING customers with such a tactic.Edit: Well, after playing further in the game, *most* side characters are of color, even Amadeus' kids which raises very serious questions who the father of the three really are. Sorry, it is a shame that such a good game has been sacrified for that nonsense.( Gameplay; 3 out of 5 )Trine 5 shines in having fine-tuned gameplay to single-player and various coop scenarios, which makes it a great party game. Puzzles are mostly intuitive with some exceptions. Combat is now more prominent and more forced onto the player. There are arena battles like Trine 4 as well "organical" embedded enemies like Trine 2's Goblin Menace DLC. The whole skill tree is mostly combat orientated (and outright stated in its descriptions) and you get all the non-combat skills automatically as a reward for a small solo level.( Story; 2 out of 5 )The stories of Trine 5 is nearly nonsensical in that regard that the villains of the game already had all their power and would also have succeeded in their further plans if they would not have forcibly had the heroes of the Trine involved at all, but ... then this game would not have been a Trine game.At the midpoint of the game there is a noticable shift in the story and that is the reason that Trine 5 originally was a DLC for Trine 4, given its similarities in user interface, skill sets, graphic style and remixed music tracks from Trine 4. Perhaps it would have been better that being Trine 5's content up to that boss battle (and cinematic sequence after that) being a DLC for 4, as the DLC would have been concluded in that fashion, paving a way to a no hold back Trine 5.The sad part of the whole thing is that the games fails to explain who the heroes of Trine are. The tutorial levels don't explain their origin for newcomers, so the marketing falls flat on the face for trying to rope in new customers to the franchise.( Graphics; 5 out of 5 )Graphics is top-notch and very detailed, but sometimes too bright and washed out in some places. The animations and everything is fine, there are no glitches and the game has very fluid animations. The water looks a bit weird though.( Sound / Music; 3 out of 5 )The music consists of remixes of older tracks and some select new ones, I did not notice any outstanding music, perhaps it is generally softer in the ears and not a quality which connects to the game itself, like the predecessors did.( Verdict )Trine 5 is great game for returning Trine players or people who just want to have some good time with it, it overstays its welcome though and be prepared for a cringeworthy ending and final chapter, storywise.If you disliked Trine 4, you won't like 5, as for it is very similar to it.Edit 2023/11/20: A pity that these details drag the game down; but if you just wanna play, it is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: Trine 5 is probably the lengthiest adventure for the heroes of Trine yet.If you enjoyed Trine's 1, 2, or 4; you will most likely enjoy this game. Our 3 heroes bring some familiar abilities along with new ones but compared to Trine 1 and 2, You cannot box wizard your way through all puzzles.My main gripe with the game is the shared conjured item limit shared across all players; for example with 2 players you can only have 1 conjured item in the beginning of the game so you wind up de-spawning your friends' conjured items at inopportune moments; which while funny, can be frustrating.I played  the game through in its entirety and thoroughly enjoyed the experience.If you are looking for a fun 1-3 player game in the classic setting or 1-4 player game on the unlimited setting The Trine series is a great option and Trine 5 is no exception.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a fantastic game. Great variation of lots of mechanics, great puzzles, delightful visuals and sound design.Praises.- Lots and lots of mechanics that properly work together. New mechanics and fresh remixes of established constantly appear.- Puzzles are fun and very creative.- On HARD puzzles get even more interesting and difficult.- Wonderful visuals and sound design. Some levels are like paintings.- Great locations variation.Complaints.- Combat is a bit janky for how prevalent it is, but mostly fun.- Rope physics are wobbly and sometimes unstable.- Main story (I did try to get many optional chests and bottles) is 2-3 hours too long as it starts to drag in the last 4 levels. Despite great set pieces I started to really want to finish the story and felt like some sections and puzzles should've been moved to a new optional challenges thing. The Bastion of Hope honestly felt like it would be a good final level.- Towards the end some cutscenes and story overall felt unfinished. Ending is satisfying in concept but the cutscene is too short and abrupt.- Final boss should've had puzzle elements, not just straight up combat. Devs actually nailed this mix with that stone magic boss that has cannon in the arena.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a Trine loyal player from 1 to 5. Trine 5 is the most ambitious version of this series. Traditional features,  play-mode and art style are conserved and developed. Though some of the skills are a little bit of useless(gravity reverse of the wizard), some can be roughly used in almost all the puzzles(the double jump of the wizard) and some only play a role in a single type of the scenarios(the hook lock transfer of the thief), Trine 5 can be summarized as an abundant, diverting and substantial Puzzle Game among the industry. I'm expecting more complicated and designed with more kinds of pattern puzzles and a more sophisticated and attractive story script in the next work of Trine.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you want a fantastic adventure game to play solo or with friends, buy this one. If you are a fan of Trine, you will be a fan of this game. If you are not yet a fan of Trine, you are going to become one :)Trine is a series known for its co-op adventures, incredible visuals and an excellent soundtrack. After the dip that was Trine 3, Trine 4 brought it back. And Trine 5?Not much to say here, it's just marvellous. The game is breathtaking. The landscapes are incredible and you get to visit multiple gorgeous locales. The characters look good, everything is nicely animated, the lot.Once again, the soundtrack is bliss. Ari strikes back with an incredibly beautiful soundtrack. Unlike in previous games though, a lot of the songs seem to be slightly adjusted songs from the previous games. The other games had remixed songs as well (the obligatory Astral Academy remix comes to mind), but this game seems to have loads. Mind you, this is not a bad thing. And you still get new songs regardless.I only played in co-op, but I imagine my points will largely stand despite this. The gameplay feels nice. It's still got a whiff of the old Trine jank but it seems to have been ironed out rather nicely. The combat feels nice, the bosses feel satisfying and intuitive. The puzzles are nicely laid out and not too confusing. And, even on normal mode (yes, there is a hard mode for puzzles, I didn't play it tho), they can be challenging.They stuck with the basic idea from Trine 4. But they improved it. I don't know how, as it seems rather the same, but I felt much better with the skills in Trine 5. Talent points are back once again. You can choose where you spend them, but some skills are locked behind progression through the story, rather than being unlocked for talent points. Each story skill also has a dedicated section where you only play as that hero and get to try out your new skill and it isn't overly long, all of which is an amazing design choice. This progression system lets the developers make challenging puzzles with increasing complexity and difficulty as the game progresses, which is a plus. Each unlock also brings a new skill to spend talent points on, which is nice. In terms of skills gained, the major ones are, of course, the story related ones. If you're afraid that it's just going to be some sort of rehash of the old skills, don't worry. Many of the old skills are back, but each character gets new toys to play with. I won't spoil any story related skills, but I will say, that Amadeus' double jump is insanely broken and I love it. I will also say that Zoya definitely got the short end of the stick. The only really exciting skill is the very last story related one. I will also point out that you don't get skill points right away. You convert experience to skill points, but only at major checkpoints, not regular ones and definitely not at will. That is, of course, unless you just go back to that checkpoint via the 'Back to Map' button and then selecting to start at that checkpoint, or just simply walking back to it... I don't understand the idea behind them, to be honest. One last thing to mention is that you can respec skills at any point without any penalty, which is very nice.Once again, the potential for shenanigans is huge. The puzzles are adjusted to fit the co-op style so that you need to work together to solve the puzzles. Since each player has their own talent points, even with just 2 people, you can cover a pretty good chunk of the skills available to you. And with more players comes the potential for cheese. Creative use of another player's presence (or skills) can lead to puzzle solutions surely not intended by the developers. In other words, the Trine charm is definitely still here. Despite there being only 3 characters, you can play in 4 players. If you are playing with less than 4 people, you can opt to play "Classic" mode, where each character is only present once. Or, you can select the unlimited mode and just have 4 Pontiuses furiously pounding the ground, or 4 Zoyas pitifully chucking a sticky dynamite 5 cm in front of them and exploding it with the hilariously unsatifying explosion sound. Also, just like Trine 4, please note that to play on the same save with all your friends, you, rather confusingly, don't use the 'Multiplayer' button, but the 'Continue Game' button.It's quite good. It seems to be a lot more connected to the universe that Trine takes place in, there are a lot of references to past games (which you do not need to have played to play this one) and overall, it's enticing and doesn't have the weird "nothing's really happening" midpoint like Trine 4 does. We get to meet a lot of characters in the world and visit many different (all beautiful, obviously) locations. I like it, it's like a fairytale, so very Trine-like.One last thing to mention is my play time. At the time of writing this review, I finished the game exactly once, collecting every piece of experience and getting every Steam achievement. See for yourself, that is a lot of content for not that high of a price.PS: Some achivements are BS (I'm looking at you, 'As Luck Would Have It' and 'Boreal Bowling')

_childDocuments_.review: I played through all the way with a friend, so I am writing from a two-person co op perspective.Overall it is a good game. It looks gorgeous, the fairy tale aesthetic never fails, and the enviromental and character designs are all great, the puzzles are creative and the new powers are fun to mess around with, and can even be used to solve a puzzle in a completely different way than what the developers no doubt intended.However, I do feel like the game overstays its welcome a bit with its ~20 hour runtime, and some levels are genuinely insane difficulty spikes compared to others. I think there were like two occasions when it was basically impossible to tell what you could interact with in the enviroment, and the boss fight-puzzles combos were more annoying then rewarding for me (and I think for my friend too).If you are looking for a challenge, alone, or with a friend, I can highly recommend it. If you'd like to just chill out with a fairy tale-esque puzzle game, I recommend against it, cuz it will piss you off more than once, guaranteed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure I enjoyed playing this one as much as the last installment, but one reviewer put it perfectly: it's more Trine and more Trine is good. This is my favourite relax-after-work series and I felt like this game fit the bill again: the scenery is beautiful, the music is enchanting, the puzzles engage my brain without making me want to throw my computer out the window, and the little tidbits and letters provide some amusing flavor to the world. I loved the references to and inclusion of the Nine Parchment students and teachers! Another reviewer mentioned that you get so many abilities that by the end you forget half of them, and this was my issue as I progressed through the game as well. If I relied on a certain set of new abilities, then I had a tendency to forget the ones that either weren't present in previous games or weren't heavily used by me. Otherwise, I thought the abilities - when remembered - were fun to play around with.

_childDocuments_.review: Another fun and well-worthwhile entry, especially for couples.The stand-out highlight this time for us (with most other things up to the usual standard) is the puzzle difficulty taking a step up (you can adjust just the puzzle difficulty in a separate slider to say, combat, which is cool.)  The puzzles are often crunchy challenges, requiring testing and eventually arriving at a light-bulb moment and granting you a nice warm dose of smug satisfaction when solved. I feel like the puzzles were pitch perfect in difficulty. On 'hard' puzzles and multiplayer, this game shines - the multiplayer bit being important not just because working as a team is more fun, but it offers you more flexibility in solutions since multiple powers might be available at once. Often it felt like we solved a puzzle not in the primary way, and I love that this is allowed.The game is generously long but not tediously so.I can think of only two problems. Firstly, there's some lack of polish - there's the odd bug (e.g. camera glitches), one puzzle I'm sure you can't solve without one person dying (on hard MP), but they're not too bad. Secondly, the writing and cut-scenes and secondary characters are pretty cringey, awkward, and tedious; less would have been more here.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played Trine before so this was my first introduction to the series. I am not usually in to platforming type games but this is really a puzzle game with some platforming and boss battles thrown in.The art is fabulous in this game. They really did a great job with designing all of the different settings and rooms. Yes, some rooms you only spend a few seconds in but the attention to detail with the artwork just makes the whole experience more enjoyable. The puzzles are fair and some kind be quite tough to puzzle out. Especially when they introduce some new concepts without hinting at how it works like they do when they give you new powers. I had to look up the answer a couple time throughout my entire play through as I was stuck and starting to get frustrated. Overall though the puzzles were a fun challenge. The boss battles were probably my least favorite. For half of the game they are pretty easy but then the multi stage bosses at the end can start to get frustrating. Nothing worse than spending 5 minutes getting the boss down to very little health and then dying and having to start all over again multiple times.The story is a little corny but I think that was the intent. It wasn't overbearing and provided some filler between levels so I don't really have too many complaints there. Overall I think the game length was good. It says I played for 31 hours but some of that was in the pause menu while I was doing other things in real life so I would guess 20 hours to finish all 20 levels. I was starting to get tired of the game so I am kind of glad it ended when it did. I would definitely recommend this game if you like puzzle games set in a beautiful world, especially if you can pick it up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it and about halfway through the game, but I don't think it's quite as good as I remember Trine 4. Visually, it's great and the gameplay is all well and good, but my friends and I have run into puzzles that feel very very difficult. We've gotten stuck on them and tried everything including gimmicks and cheese and most of the time make it through. In the old game when you get stuck, the narrator would give a hint. There are no hints now. When we look up the solution online, it seems that the puzzles are fundamentally different from single to multi player, which is cool to be honest. But I guess my point is that the multiplayer versions of the puzzles feel impossible from time to time and we would have to get one person across and have the player left behind just kill themselves so they could respawn on the other side of the puzzle.With that said, some of the puzzles are really good. Some feel clunky. Still fun. Also feels like the longest Trine game yet which is good, but often I have little or no clue what's happening in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: are pretty stellar even on a machine with specs below the minimum requirements without any performance penalty (i.e. the game still runs smoothly without lag) is consistently good as was in the past have been split up into Fight Difficulty, Puzzle Difficulty, Resurrection Difficulty. This means that you can tweak each difficulty setting independently. For example, you can have Puzzle Difficulty on Hard while Fight Difficulty on Easy. However, take note that although you can change difficulty at any time - progress that you make is tied to that specific difficulty setting. In practice this means that the game discourages you from switching difficulties to get past a specific battle / puzzle in a level because you'd have to replay the level again from the beginning up to the point at which you changed difficulty. this time features a lot of callbacks to characters / events that have appeared in previous games. While you can still understand the story without having played the previous games, it would be quite a bit less enjoyable given how these previous characters / events are heavily featured throughout the story. wise there are a few nice abilities added - Zoya's fox rope, Pontius' clone which make the game feel fresh again. It's a pity that even on hard mode the puzzles don't have enough space / length to truly push the limits of the new abilities.Enemies feel less like damage sponges and boss fights feel a bit more varied compared to Trine 4. There is still a limited variety of enemy types which is similar to Trine 4. The balance between difficulty and reward is still off to me. Higher fight difficulty just feels like you face more enemies with increased hit points. It doesn't feel like there's much of payoff for playing a harder difficulty. Instead it leaves you feeling like you're getting penalized since it takes a longer time to get through. It would be nice to have some hard mode  achievements like in the past in Trine 1 / 2. In my own experience Trine 5 has been the most frustrating of the series so far. Part of it is because the entire game is built around understanding the visual cues. When you don't get it or when you did something which you think should have solved the puzzle / boss but didn't it leaves you wondering what went wrong.  Somehow I ran into more of these issues in Trine 5 than any of it's predecessors. Another part of it is for the issues that have persisted throughout the Trine series of games, namely the overall physics fails - items / characters going through rope / rails, the rope tying / untying working unexpectedly, arrows clipping through summoned objects instead of the displayed path, etc.The series feels stale in the sense that the core formula remains untouched throughout the years - co-op  puzzle platforming adventure with lots of possible way to solve each fight / puzzle or fail spectacularly.  While it's hard to fault Frozenbyte for not perfecting notoriously difficult tasks like balancing the game difficulty, giving players sufficient visual / audio feedback to solve puzzles / bosses, fixing the janky physics, it's also hard not to fault them when you see the exact same issues in the 5th game of the series. When the game is as good as it is most of the time, the weaknesses in the game stand out more. Such is the case with Trine 5.In Conclusion,If you're coming into the game fresh, this is as good of a starting point as it gets.If you've played the Trine 1 - 4, I would almost say that you can go without playing Trine 5 because there isn't enough new to recommend it. It is a worthy addition to the Trine series but unfortunately it doesn't raise the series to new heights.
