It's amazing how they still come up with new and fun abilities and talents, without changing the core of the three characters! fun puzzles and not too hard to collect everything. kinda sad that you have to do more than collect everything for 100% achievements, but I guess that adds replay value.we encountered a few minor glitches and lags plus some cinematics freezing. one of us with an old pc had very low frame rate and was freezing quite often. not much you can do in terms of settings sadly to fix that. the only annoying bug was the canon not working on the boss of the bastion of hope. but after a few restarts it worked.the story was ok, although I didn't really like the end and I'm not sure how they will be able to continue the story now. there was also some weird jumps sometimes that didn't make sense or I guess stuff was happening off screen.having only three lives is an interesting idea, if you want to make the game harder, but that doesn't really fit into the game and I think it should be off by default. we turned it off right away.overall enjoyable gameplay in coop and very pretty scenery as always. the artists did a great job again!
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I played and finished this one as well.It is a lovely game, BUT I can't get rid of the feeling it was made as a primary coop game - a lot of puzzles seems to be not polished to a standard I would expect.I can vividly imagine solving most of the puzzles in coop with a blink of an eye and making all those micro movements to try new solution instantly possible.I like 1,2,4 much better, but still, it's a nice experience and really long.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: This is so relaxing and remind me of the good times I playing Trine 2 and 4, but it get a little bit frustrating in the late levels as more combats and more ridiculous puzzles.- graphic and art style is fantastic- soundtrack is good- map is pretty big- story is average and boring- combat is interesting but also can be pretty chaos and frustrating- character can't interact with experience bottles sometimes that I have to restart from checkpoint to fix it7.0/10
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the Trine franchise. All of the games are light-hearted and fun, focusing on puzzles that require creativity more than a high level of skill. I also love that there is still a combat aspect to the game. Trine 5 continues with this trend of excellence, shaping the backstories and plots of our three heroes, as well as introducing a new struggle for them to overcome. I also find that the skill system has been refined since the last game, introducing varied ways to use a skill in multiple situations.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The Trine series never disappoints (except for the 3rd chapter, we all know that). It comprises some of the best games to play in coop and Trine 5 is maybe the best of them all.Throughout the 5 chapters of the series, Trine kept getting better, adding new skills to use to solve puzzles and interesting boss battles that requires both (little) skill and quick thinking.We even had some character development this time. Like, what do you want more from life? Maybe stunning settings? We got them. Adorable animal PNGs? We got them.Just buy this already and play it with your friends. You won't regret it. Even with some bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite game series, Trine!  The gameplay remains largely unchanged from Trine 4, but with some exciting new mechanics, seamless gameplay, and absolutely stunning art. While it doesn't reinvent the wheel, it's a more-than-satisfying continuation for me.The story and gimmicks are also enjoyable, even though they evoke similar vibes to Trine 4 (2019).If you're a fan of side-scrolling games with breathtaking visuals and challenging puzzles, Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy is a must-play! 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the previous games you are going to enjoy this one too. Zoya, Pontius and Amadeus are off on another adventure. The game delivers a familiar atmosphere and puzzles. In my opinion the third game was the weakest, with the fourth and this one is the series is on the rise again.If you want some light puzzle adventure with funny characters and fabulous music and design this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best in the series to date, but after playing four of these over the years (let's not talk about 3) there just isn't enough to make me as excited about these as I was in the past. If you've never played one of these games I'd definitely recommend to start with 5, which has everything great about the previous games with more interesting puzzles and variety. Follow with 2 and possibly 4 for more. I'm just starting to get burnt out with these titles, and not interested in playing a sixth game unless they do something new with the concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, easily one of my favorite games of the year.  The level of puzzle and gameplay variety, polish, and ingenuity on display in each level is honestly shocking and almost makes me feel bad for having paid them ONLY full price for this game.  I played through the entire thing in couch co-op and had a phenomenal time.  The presentation is also unreal - gorgeous graphics, lovely music, and great cut scenes.  I've played all 5 and I think this may be not only my favorite in the series, but possibly landed a spot in my top 5 games of all time.  I'm there day 1 for their next title.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The best game in the series by far!!! If you are a fan of the previous parts, you will enjoy it very much. They learned from their previous mistakes (cough Trine 3 cough) and they improved everything. The story is a little forced, but was still fun to play through (That's what really matters). This is my son's (5 years old) favorite game series (he Plays Pontius) and plays with me (Amadeus) and his mother (Zonya). Great Moments in Family. Thank you Frozenbyte!9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Trine 3 took a misstep with the attempted 3D game.Trine 4 fixed it by returning to the roots and back to 2D yet the game was overall quite easy as the puzzles were quite straight forward. Awesome boss fight though.Trine 5 once again follows a familiar formula but this time the team has really put some effort on the puzzles. I've played the game in co-op and multiple times we found ourselves just standing, thinking, "Umm how..."The game introduces bunch of new fun mechanics that really add up to the puzzles and I've had great fun with this game!Stunning, beautiful world, beautiful soundtrack, good story and our heroes seem more fleshed out then ever!
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Another action packed adventure with our three heroes of Trine (although when will those poor souls get to retire, one wonders)!  The devs continued with the tried and true puzzle-platformer formula they corrected in the previous game, and the visuals are stunning. I agree with other reviewers in that they seem to have ramped up the difficulty with this one. There are a lot of moving parts to the puzzles, especially later in the game when you have to use all the skills you've learned. Also, there is less tolerance for cheesing your way through puzzles unlike the first three games. One last thing - they didn't mess around with the achievements this time. Some of them are pretty brutal...but that's a compliment!
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Triumphant Trio Adventure in Trine 5Trine 5 takes the cooperative gaming experience to new heights, offering an exceptional journey for those who embark on it together. The magic of this game truly unfolds when played as a trio, enhancing the collaborative spirit that the series is renowned for.One of the standout features of Trine 5 is the mesmerizing visual spectacle it presents. Each character and setting is meticulously designed, creating a visually stunning backdrop for the epic adventure that unfolds.However, where Trine 5 truly shines is in its cooperative gameplay, especially when played with three players. The synergy between characters is not only crucial for overcoming challenges but also adds an extra layer of enjoyment. The seamless integration of the characters' unique abilities fosters a sense of camaraderie as players strategize and execute their plans to navigate the enchanting landscapes.The puzzles in Trine 5 are both challenging and rewarding. The game demands creative problem-solving skills from the players, and the variety of puzzles keeps the experience fresh and engaging. The cooperative aspect becomes pivotal here, as players must communicate effectively to conquer the intricate puzzles that stand in their way. The satisfaction of overcoming these challenges together is immensely gratifying and strengthens the bond between players.Trine 5 manages to strike a perfect balance between action and puzzle-solving, providing an experience that is not only visually stunning but also mentally stimulating. The cooperative gameplay elevates the overall enjoyment, turning the adventure into a memorable shared experience. Whether you're a fan of visually captivating worlds, engaging puzzles, or cooperative play, Trine 5 delivers on all fronts, making it a must-play for anyone seeking a magical and collaborative gaming escapade.

_childDocuments_.review: i kept asking myself if i've become more stupid since the last game bc the puzzles were harder than the other trine games but then realized the puzzles change a bit with the difficulty of the game now (i might be dumber now regardless tho)??? i think that's something new, if im not mistaken ,but i definitely enjoy it more this way. the game looks incredible as well, as usual. they seriously got the best aspects of each game and made this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm still not a fan of the wizard overhaul after Trine 2 (blocks only spawn above the head, free rotation of objects was removed), the developers did an amazing job. - The story is entertaining throughout. Hearing the characters constantly talk to each other while you play makes the game a lot more immersive.- Graphics are visually stunning, as was the case with all the previous games.- Epic soundtracks- Plenty of new skills that change the way you play and provide new solutions to puzzles. They are very creative and all of them are useful.- Replay value is there as you will definitely miss more XP than in the previous games and will need to track it down. The newly unlocked skills will make the next playthrough much easier. Also, the difficulty dynamically changes based on the number of players so the same puzzles may require a different solution.I definitely see myself buying Trine 6 in the future. Don't forget to nominate this game for Steam Awards. I can easily see it ticking multiple categories.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: It's more of the same, but it's more Trine! Somehow Frozenbyte keeps on finding new mechanics to play with in the familiar co-op puzzle solving landscape of the previous installments. If you love beautiful storybook vistas, enchanting fairy-tale melodies and figuring out puzzles with boxes and planks, this game will feel like your favorite warm, comfortable pullover sweater on a cold winter evening.Cozy AF.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Another dose of autumn antidepressant, the Trine series.  As always the visuals are colorful and detailed, on purpose bordering on kitch. This combined with the narrator and uplifting music builds up the trademark fairy tale atmosphere.  The gameplay is based on puzzles and platforming. Several abilities return from the previous installations and there are some new as well. Overall challenge level is moderate. On a rare occassion I had been stuck, because I forgot one of the abilities. This maybe one of the downsides - there are many abilities and some of them are relatively underutilised and can easily go forgotten. The combat is rare, but comparatively clumsy. Boss fights are more puzzle based and far more entertaining.  The story in the series was always simple, with characters being more of a straight archetypes. Even so the story of Trine 5 seemed weaker than that of Trine 4.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles seem very boring compared to all earlier entries in the series. Obviously limited to prevent you from solving them creatively instead of adapting the design to encourage experimentation. The developers continue to insist on having lots of combat encounters, but refuse to actually try and improve them in any way. Combat design is universally weak and it's just a part of the game you grind through to get to the better bits.Graphics are gorgeous as usual, and some of the voice acting stands out as excellent.If you're looking for a fun local or online co-op game to play with some friends, look at the earlier Trine games.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like the part where developers force you into solving puzzles in a very specific way and/or skill. Sometimes Zoya's arrow swap stops working, sometimes you cannot connect objects even though they appear to be made of metal, and sometimes you need environmental fire damage but somehow Zoya's fire arrows do not count. Zoya's dynamite does not break walls but gunpowder barrels do. Reverse gravity is so weak that it can't lift a single thing but Thieves' Aide is somehow rock solid. Some objects can be frozen but not stopped by light. Some objects can be stopped by light but not frozen. Some objects are unaffected by both. Towards the end I just started shooting randomly to see if anything freezes because if developers want it to be solved by freezing, the object is freezable, otherwise, it is not. Most of the puzzles towards the latter half of the game were like "So there is a ring, a grate and a glowing blue connector here so I should use this, this and this"It would probably be fun with friends but single-player feels a bit bland and railroaded.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so in love with the Trine series for many different reasons. Trine 5 is absolutely gorgeous, just like Trine 4, the artwork is just breathtaking. It's the coziest of games to get lost in, to take your mind off things and you can play it at your own pace. I hope new Trine games will keep being made infinitely!
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I like the Trine games but Trine 5 annoys me due to bugs/glitches, wonky physics, and some silly puzzles that make no sense to me and my pals (we play this game on 3-player co-op mode).On my system (Ryzen 5 3600, RX 5500 XT 8GB, 16 GBs DDR4) performance is fine, but shadows glitch by constantly flickering as I walk around. It's a baffling and distracting bug, and they still haven't fixed it. Changing settings doesn't help either. [edit 22/11/2023: a few days after posting my review, the game's been patched and the shadow flickering issue has been resolved by the developers]Otherwise the game is very enjoyable to play through and looks good. But some of the puzzles feel like they weren't properly tested for multiplayer mode, just like I saw on Trine 4. There are instances where we "break" the game's physics even though we ain't even purposely trying to do that.It's not possible to score a game neutrally on Steam, but I'll still recommend this game to Trine and puzzle fans. Hopefully they'll fix the bugs and wonky physics, but it's fat chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: Great instalment in an already amazing franchise. The puzzles seem to be a bit easier, but at the same time even funnier than in previous parts. Audiovisual side is as nice as it always was, making you feel like you're back in a fairy tale. Mechanics are easy to learn and familiar. There's not much groundbreaking content, but that doesn't matter, because the formula is very strong.So if you've played Trine previously, get this one, call your friends, and continue on your journey. And if not, buy all the previous "episodes" and play them, and then play this one. It is worth every cent and every second.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! It has all the good puzzles from Trine while having a much larger focus on story telling than the other games in the franchise, aside from introducing several new characters. The OST is also spetacular, and even has some remixed songs from Nine Parchments.Trine 5 is actually quite challeging too on Hard difficulty, and it has much longer levels than its predecessors. It is a problem on earlier levels since all the characters have their powers "nerfed" in order to not cheat the puzzles, but after unlocking new powers halfway through the game and buying their upgrades the levels start to be so much fun to navigate. It also has some very well hidden exp and collectibles for those who like to play without guides.While Trine 4 has a smoother and "floaty" gameplay, Trine 5 has a bit more of a technical gameplay, which is actually fitting for the game's theme. Each of the 3 characters also feels very unique, and all of them are useful throughout all the game's content.I would definitely recommend for those who like platform games and to play on co-op with friends (which I did, and it was really fun!).

_childDocuments_.review: This is another great entry in the Trine series. The locales and backgrounds are somehow even more gorgeous than previous games. Both the puzzle and combat difficulty have crept up steadily with each game, and both are now reasonably challenging on the default difficulty setting. Trine 5 feels like the longest game in the series so far; that 19 hours is for one playthrough.The heroes get a lot of abilities throughout the game this time around, and towards the end it can be a challenge just to remember them all. For some puzzles most of the challenge is remembering you have a particular ability that will solve the puzzle. Still, the large ability set gives many opportunities for creatively combining them, and a lot of the puzzle solutions are quite satisfying.The story is noticeably darker and more serious than prior entries in the series. The stakes are higher, and I felt genuine animosity toward the villains, which wasn't the case for any of the prior Trine games. This time around the plot also makes an effort to give voice to present-day anxieties, such as weaponized disinformation and replacement by AI. Trine 5's story is self-contained, so you won't be lost if you haven't played all the previous Trines.I encountered a few bugs (mostly objects that were freezable with Zoya's ice arrows but clearly weren't meant to be) but nothing game-breaking.Overall a step up from the already-enjoyable previous games in the series. Highly recommend especially if you liked the previous games.
_childDocuments_.name: Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy

_childDocuments_.review: I played Trine 2 with my girlfriend 10+ years ago and loved it then. I missed 3 and 4 although they seemed to have slightly mixed reviews. Recently been playing through Trine 5 with a friend and it seems they've absolutely nailed it for this instalment. It has all the best bits of Trine 2 while having improved mechanics, graphics, challenge ideas. For those that haven't played it, give it a try. Think 'escape room meets platformer'. This is a great game to play Solo and an essential game for anyone who has one or two mates (you can have up to three of you co-op) to play along with.

_childDocuments_.review: Like almost all the other Trine games, it is one of the best coop games you can get. Each character gets some cool skills that weren't in the other games, although it felt like Pontius got way more than the other characters this time. The villains in Trine 5 are absolute psychopaths and make all the other villains look tame. The levels are the most unique they have ever been with none of them feeling similar to one anotherI wish you could draw summon items but for some reason you can't draw boxes or planks to summon them with Amadeus. The enemies also feel less varied than the other games.However besides that it's just as good as the other ones if not better, I hope they make a DLC for this one9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Early review for me to help toward  as this is indeed a  game that meets the extremely high quality bar of this franchise.I am in the fan minority as a solo player and probably have a different reaction than most about the gameplay here, which is a return to form toward the beloved original games that started the series,  But I actually really enjoyed , and  felt like a really happy balance to me between old and new. This one though is back to harder puzzles with ambiguous solutions, which I do not enjoy nearly as much. Like yes, you can make it through, but was that the way you were supposed to do it? I'm missing that  moment when you realize how to solve a puzzle correctly. sees your heroes getting a lot more skills, and to me having so many more pieces on the board saps some of the enjoyment I took from the last couple of games. Structurally we are getting even more ways to solve the puzzles, and I know players have been vocal about enjoying that. It just isn't for me though.Thankfully, there are separate puzzle and combat difficulty options that can be adjusted during gameplay for players like me, and Frozenbyte has been active here in the Steam forums and helping to make sure players are getting the game experience they want. Gameplay has been smooth, my GPU is happy, and the game and animations as always are stunning, plus the game sounds amazing. The improved cinematic style and customization options in this entry really help with immersion. Easily worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all the Trine games with my wife on PC with controllers (PC projected to TV via HDMI). This is very much more of the same, which is a good thing overall. The visuals remain fantastic, and the puzzles and abilities you develop while advancing ramp up nicely. You can also set difficulty level on puzzles and fights separately, which I like because we plan to replay the game on the hard puzzle difficulty later on. They also do a nice job of occasionally having you branch off to solve puzzles as one character type, so 2 pontius characters playing at once is a fun change of pace.My only real complaint is that the story is really flat and boring. There's pointless angry mom type character that's the queen and wants all the power. She has no back story or complexity, and the narration lacks some of the whimsy of Trine 1 and 2. It really is a problem too, as the game is long and lacks the novelty of earlier games, so it starts to feel like a collection of levels you need to slog your way through to get to the queen and defeat her. The visuals and gameplay deserve better than that.Overall, a very fun game with creative puzzles in a spectacular visual world. Really the best couch coop game series there is. I'd rank this one ahead of Trine 3 and 4, but beneath Trine 1 and 2. I'm already looking forward to the expansion!

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Trine series, I'm very pleased with this fifth instalment. It’s a great 2.5D puzzle platformer that is a worthy sequel of "Trine 4: The Nightmare Prince".Visually, the game is gorgeous. From the level design, the character animations, the lighting, the bright colours, it truly is a feast for the eyes. You can't help but slow down now and then to just look around. Almost everywhere you look there are little details to spot in the back- or foreground.The soundtrack of Ari Pulkkinen is as magical as you might expect if you’ve played previous entries in the Trine-series. It enhances the atmosphere and together with the visuals helps you immerse yourself into the game's magical world. Besides new compositions, long-time fans may discover some new renditions of the most memorable tracks from the previous entries in the Trine series. Voice acting is well done and the sound effects are decent. The gameplay is where this game really shows an improvement in comparison to the previous titles. The three heroes – Zoya (Thief), Amadeus (Wizard) en Pontius (Knight) – each have many unique abilities to use in combat and to solve puzzles. The puzzles are in my experience more challenging than ever before, mainly because of them being designed to require thoughtful utilization and combining of all these abilities. And I have the feeling some obstacles require more skill in levitating objects and roping them together than was asked of me before. I feel that the three heroes are well balanced. Both inside and outside of combat I don’t feel a preference to mainly use one of them. Speaking of combat, fighting enemies feels incredibly satisfying. There are many ways to fight foes, besides your sword and shield, use your bow or stomping a box on their head. You can use for example exploding boxes, hailstorm planks, elemental arrows, sword throwing and stomping or swinging on enemies. And although the variety of enemies leaves something to be desired, the many unique multi-phase boss fights makes up for that and are a great spectacle. Finding and collecting green orbs/flasks of experience is a staple of the series. Many on the main route are hard to miss, some are more hidden with other collectables (letters expanding the lore or hats to change your look). The checkpoint system and level select shows how many you’ve missed (i.e. 5/7 at checkpoint 3). This makes it easier to jump back at that checkpoint in a level and search for those you've missed. Re-allocating your skills to suit the upcoming puzzles/fights is also easy. The checkpoint system and difficulty settings allows adjusting the game for new-comers as well as giving a challenge to more experienced players.The story is a light-hearted and at times comical. The narrative is mainly told through well animated and voiced cut-scenes between levels, a narrator before venturing into a level, but also through dialogue between the heroes during the 20 levels, in which your heroes will visit many different locations. The interactions between the three heroes and their adversaries are both endearing and comical. Although there are many nods to previous Trine games and Nine Parchments (a game by Frozen Byte set in the same universe), I don’t think your enjoyment is soured by not having played previous entries. The addition of up to four-player co-op (multiple players can play the same hero) or three-player classic (every player plays one of the three heroes) is a welcome feature, allowing friends to join in on the adventure. Since I haven’t played this mode myself, I can’t comment on how this affects the puzzles/combat.In conclusion, Trine 5: A Clockwork Conspiracy is in my opinion a great game. Whether you're newcomer of have played all previous in the Trine-series, this is an enchanting journey you don't want to miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it as good as Trine 2? That's really the benchmark that all future Trine games will get judged against. I'm currently 12 and half hours in and only halfway through the game, so it's certainly the longest Trine to-date. The puzzles are on a par with Trine 4, and the combat is significantly improved on the fourth entry, no more getting locked inside of battle arenas. It's very much built on the foundations of 4, so if you didn't like the slight different feel to the game compared to 2, you'll have the same issues here. The aesthetic is interesting and varied, not as pastel as 4, but not as vivid as Trine 1 or 2. Enemies are about as varied as you get in Trine games, complex combat systems are not a feature of this series. My biggest negative so far has been the occasional end of level boss encounter. None of these fights are really that hard, and tend to have a puzzle element to them, but one that requires a bit of co-ordination and dexterity to execute - neither of which are my strength and they feel quite juxtaposed to the unhurried nature of the rest of the game. Overall, highly recommended!

name: Tandem: A Tale of Shadows
detailed_description: Tandem : A Tale of Shadows redefines the puzzle platformer genre with a unique top down and side-scroller gameplay and exceptional aesthetics. Help Emma and the teddy bear Fenton solve the mystery of the disappearance of the famous magician Thomas Kane. Award-winning Tandem: A Tale of Shadows features five beautiful Victorian-inspired worlds inspired by Tim Burton, Jules Vernes, Conan Doyle. Players have to carefully alternate between Emma’s top-down view and Fenton’s horizontal side-scroller view if they hope to escape these chiaroscuro dimensions alive. As the duo navigates past intelligent obstacles and menacing horrors, they uncover clues regarding Thomas’ disappearance, the strange Kane family, and their place in this universe. Will Emma and Fenton escape the murderous manor filled with twists and turns, or has their fate already been sealed?

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like a Tim Burton version of Shady part of me.My wife’s boyfriend describes as it Alice madness return mixed with Limbo.Only few games are captivating to the point of making me to want to finish it in one go. The atmosphere of Tandem was just so wonderful, the main concept so inventive and discovering each new universe brought me so much satisfaction I couldn’t stop playing. The game is a visual marvel, I was immediately in love with the artstyle! The idea of having a character create new pathways and possibilities for another character through something as simple as casting shadows is very clever, and it made for very interesting puzzles and gameplay.The game has a very creepy yet charming atmosphere with its colors and music. It feels like a spooky game for a younger audience, sort of like Medievil for the PS One. Yes one of the main characters dress it's such a ridiculously exaggerated umbrella, she would fit better as a character in Courage the cowardly dog, but it still fits thematically with the rest.Tandem is a 2D puzzler platformer holding a dark atmosphere for its journey. How the game differs from other puzzle platformers is you play as two characters. With the ability to change characters you change perspectives from a top-down to side scroller to work together to solve the level puzzle. You will need to change in order to progress each character and reach the goal. There are about 5 world with 45 levels in total. Each level can take on average 10 mins to finish, with the later levels taking longer and some of them being real head scratchers. The story is sadly a bit lack luster, but it goes from 0 to 100 pretty damn fast. The main character first walks out on the streets to solve a mystery when suddenly a random teddybear falls out of a car, and things move on very fast from there. In the next scene she knows the name of the bear and acts like they been friends forever lol. At its core you’re here mostly for the puzzles and the atmosphere.If you like action and running 'n gunning, then this one may not be for you. This is more of a "push, pull, and aim things while switching back and forth between two characters and avoiding enemies until you forge a path to the exit" type of game. If you like puzzles that are challenging but not frustratingly difficult... if you like gameplay that doesn't make the veins pop out on your neck... and, most of all, if you like gorgeous graphics and music in the French style, with the aesthetics that feel like a cross between Little Nightmares and Shady Part of Me, then this could be right up your alley. I highly recommend it if you’re looking for something light to challenge yourself, and it’s specially worth it during a sale.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tandem: A Tale of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Tandem  is a puzzle platformer, the player controls two asymmetrical characters (Emma and Fenton) and navigates through the maze interiors of a great mansion, solving all riddles, puzzles and conundrums imaginable to progress within, while lying low wherever the world’s malcontents present themselves.  Emma is located on the ground, while Fenton, a living teddy bear, defies gravity and stands on the walls, and then defies gravity yet again and walks on shadows, in this game’s title – ‘Tandem’ refers to the tandem movement of Emma and Fenton are in tandem, ‘tale of shadows’ is in referral to Fenton’s ability to walk the shadows cast by the world, and by Emma’s lantern. This creative assembly (pun intended) to gameplay presides over a very unique experience for the player. This description sounds familiar? Perhaps you played the puzzle platformer game Contrast (2013). Just like in that game, you manipulate two worlds; the world of light, and the world of shadow. Your interactions with the real world affect the shadows cast by it, creating new opportunity for anyone who can transform themselves into a shadow. I have not played much puzzle games, I have played a few ‘hidden object’ games, and a few puzzle games such as The Room or House of Davinci (both I greatly recommend to the enthusiast of riddles). Tandem has 5 chapters, each possessing either 8, 9 or 11 levels, taking the game’s two protagonists through the Kane family manor in order to solve the mysterious disappearance of Thomas Kane - the family’s offspring. Each chapter corresponds to a different part of the manor (Starting with the Gardens, then progressing through the boiler rooms, the kitchens, the 'clockwork' and culminating at the greenhouse), each chapter has differentiation in level desig, challenges, puzzles, platforming and enemies. This variance aids in keeping monotony at bay.Each level, which in my opinion is to the game’s strength, does not overstay its welcome. You will be completing levels in times between 10 to perhaps a maximum 30 minutes. The puzzles to me felt a bit too simple and easy at times, but there was still great satisfaction and enjoyment to be had from platforming and solving conundrums, and in that thrill finishing each level left me wanting for more.One of Tandem’s strongest suits is the atmosphere - greatly reinforced by its musical score - and the camera angle. The player’s view herein comes directly from the top of the perspective. This means that the gameplay manifests two dimensions operating together in tandem (such an aptly named game), yet in this curious set-up each character traverses only two dimensions (X,Y), in a sense, it's a sidescroller - but one of the playable characters is viewed from a top-down angle: Emma’s gameplay and control are top-down, while playing with Fenton transforms the game into a true side-scrolling platformer. These visuals and gameplay style charmed me so greatly that I think I will hold fond memories for this game for a very long time.The game’s great weakness is its short length. As I reached the ending stages of Ch.5 I was left wanting for more, which to be completely fair is not exclusively due to the short length of the game, but due to the excitement that it had garnered in me. The passionate terms which unraveling the mystery of the Kane family secrets had spurred me to hurry across the game to finish it and reach that oh so desirable climax.My clock hours stands at 10, but in reality it is boosted from afk’ing and me unlocking all the secrets in the game after finishing it. The game’s true length should be perhaps around 6-8 hours.I have not encountered any bugs or glitches notwithstanding that sometimes Fenton (the teddy bear) will get stuck in the air after jumping, but the game does a good job of detecting and self-correcting such issues that if you get stuck in a jumping animation it will immediately offer a "reset" prompt where Fenton will be teleported a short distance away. In the technical side I did not like that the game lacked a resolution option but instead only a scale of percentages based on one's monitor resolution. Navigating the game's chapter map was also a bit tedious with M&Kb and some buttons have poor detection for your cursor. These are all very minor nitpicks and the is otherwise without hiccups.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really disappointed me. What started out as an interesting puzzle game with 2 different perspectives slowly becomes one of the worst platformers I've ever played. But the side scrolling teddy bear part is absolutely insufferable. The moment you switch controls the beautiful graphics are gone, replaced by the blandest black and white possible. And the controls... man, it's 2021, I wasn't expecting such bad controls. The jump has a fixed height and length, no matter if you press and hold or just tap the button. It's short and and lacks any sort of "air control". Even the jump sound effect is annoying. And to make matters worse, as the game progresses the platforming sections take center stage. Then it's all downhill from there. Such a pity. I absolutely cannot recommend this game. The entire teddy section needed to be revamped.

_childDocuments_.review: Fabulous shiny game that both made me over-complicate things, and left me confuzzled. These are great puzzles, and the concept works fantastic. I thought it might mess with my equilibrium switching between the two characters and points of view, but it’s seamless. Wonderful checkpoints, beautiful artwork, relaxing music, and clever puzzles. It’s rare that a game can take over my mind so much I forget to talk during stream, but this one had me just enjoying the game.Few people had trouble with some flashiness, and I was worried about that, too. The colorful part is VERY colorful, but it only bothered me in a few places. It’s a flashy success animation, which my friend said was acceptable since you know it’s coming. The spiders are the first mobile obstacle in the game and the worst, I think, so don’t give up if you don’t like them.I have two chapters left, and will update if something changes, Tandem is definitely worth the go.Edit: so chapter 4 introduced an adorable cube to be involved in the puzzle. I loved it. Levels got kinda dark, with the cubes locked up and chopping them in half... but they were jelly and they were still alive. I'm not sure why, but it got really dark at the end of Ch4. They were being tortured, and I immediately quit. Chat laughed at me, but they also understood and were shocked at the turn of tone. I glanced through a longer playthrough and I'm really not sure why the devs turned into vicious killers. I'm sensitive and love the characters. I do still recommend the game, it's worth the sale price for the first two chapters. But... don't get it if you don't want to see cute little creatures tortured. I even love horror games. I was not prepared for this.

_childDocuments_.review: The TL:DR of this review: good puzzles, AWFUL story, VERY off putting ending. Some gamers might retort: "meh, puzzle games don't need a STORY…do they?" Honestly...no, puzzle games do NOT need a story, though if you DO attempt one, make sure it's a good story, with NO plot holes (where did the "shadow teddy bear" come from, and WHY), and a great, rewarding ending. Play Tandem for the puzzles, NOT the story.The puzzles ARE good, at moments very good, and reminded me (in a good way) of a similar puzzle game, "Contrast," with a similar premise: half of the game in a 3D "real world," other half in a 2D side-scrolling “shadow world.” For the most part, these puzzles are fun, if you don't mind even the TINIEST "mistake" leads to instant death, where the little girl gets eaten by a giant spider while the teddy bear gets shredded to pieces.Which brings us to the story. A girl seeks a missing boy, in a mansion filled with death traps. What is so important about this missing boy? Why are no adults looking for this boy? Why does Emma have such an odd obsession to find him, after so many deadly and creepy death traps?!? If you want answers, get ready for none. This goes double for the ending, which is 50 percent "wow, that sucked" and 50 percent "What was the point of...any of this, if THAT is the way they ended it?" If you offer a puzzle game with no story, that's cool. Why offer a 'story' that explains...nothing? The random "hidden secrets" are fun to find, though do not  seek all secrets, expecting a "secret alternate ending" if you find them all. NOPE. This game has ONE ending. Well...darn.However, hey, good puzzles, with dozens of "instant death" at every turn, with unlimited lives, so if you like puzzles that more often than not lead to a little girl sliced in half or shredding a teddy bear to pieces, go for it. For me, the off-putting ending forced me into "marginal" thumbs down territory. Sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good puzzle-platformer. You play the two main characters simultaneously: Emma in a top-down 3D view and Fenton in a 2D side scrolling one. Both of them has to clear each others path of any obstruction to progress and finish each level. 40 of them to be precise, nicely packed in 5 sets. Each set has exactly 8 maps and vastly differs both in gameplay and theme from the others, tied to various locations within the mansion.The mansion looks great, it has a subtle creepy vibe to it and the relaxing ost really gives the locations a nice push in atmosphere. Story is alright, the cutscenes are well made and the ending was something I did not expect.Took me 5 hrs to beat it and find every collectible, honestly, it felt longer than that. It's not pricy either, so fans of the puzzle genre don't need to get bankrupt to buy this one, even without any discount. Curious fellas who aren't into puzzles should wait for a smaller sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Tandem: A Tale of Shadows offers a unique dual-perspective puzzle experience. Emma’s top-down world and Fenton’s 2D side-scrolling environment are intertwined, with light and shadow being the key to progressing. The mechanics are well-implemented, but the puzzles can become repetitive as the objectives remain largely the same across levels. The game’s world design is imaginative, with each region bringing something visually new and interesting. Not a difficult game to complete, but it does have several achievements that can be missed each level, but with a guide, you can easily find and get to the ones you missed.Hours to fully complete the game: 8Achievements: 24/24Playthroughs: 1Difficulty: 3/10Steam Hunter Points: ✪ 4,063 Visually, the game excels with its dark Victorian atmosphere. The environments are rich with detail, and the animations are generally smooth, though some minor bugs detract from the overall experience. Cutscenes have stutter both on Steam Deck and PC. The art style fits the eerie, fairy-tale vibe perfectly, enhancing the game’s mood. The sound design is atmospheric, with subtle music and well-crafted sound effects that deepen the immersion. Unfortunately, the voice acting falls flat. Emma’s lines lack emotion and feel stilted, making it hard to connect with the story. The narrative is one of the game’s weaker aspects. While the premise is intriguing, the delivery is lacking. The story doesn’t build much tension, and the voice acting does little to elevate it. The plot feels like an afterthought, serving more as a backdrop for the puzzles. The game offers 5-8 hours of content, with some challenging puzzles toward the end. The difficulty is balanced, offering a satisfying progression curve. However, once you’ve seen the core mechanics, the novelty wears off quickly, reducing the replayability. Tandem: A Tale of Shadows delivers a unique puzzle experience with inventive mechanics and a strong atmosphere. However, its repetitive gameplay, lackluster story, and stutter bugs prevent it from reaching its full potential. It’s a good pick for fans of puzzle-platformers, but might be better enjoyed during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tandem: A Tale of Shadows

_childDocuments_.review: Tandem: A Tale Of Shadows tries to mix overhead and side-scrolling perspectives to create a moderately competent puzzle platformer. While the graphics and atmosphere of the game is pretty solid even if unremarkable, the puzzle and platforming aspect of it just falls short of making it a good game. To be fair, Tandem isn’t a bad game but it doesn’t stand out in anything to be a worthwhile investment. Problems with controls also undermines the enjoyment of the game as well as low difficulty curve, 4 hours to finish the game and a story that is much too lackluster and wanting, makes recommending a hard sell. Despite that, the idea is pretty solid and if Monochrome Solid could improve on control and character movement, as well as expand the puzzles just a bit more, Tandem’s next iteration could be a thing to look forward to. As for this, it's best to get Tandem on sale. The graphics and atmosphere of the game evokes a sense of Brother’s Grimm scary fairy tale, the old Victorian kind. The use of light and shadow is put to good use here, and the soundtrack is very appropriate even if not outstanding. The concept of playing 2 separate characters - one side-scrolling and the other top-view -  is an interesting one and Monochrome Paris executed this moderately competently. Also using light and shadow as platforming is also interesting and is executed fairly well. The problem is that the concept wasn’t expanded further or use more creatively. It’s basically, make shadow, create platform, move to next area. After the first 10 levels, you’d start to want something a little more creative. The puzzles are interesting but truthfully, they’re not  clever. Of the 50 odd levels in the game, 40 of them are basically the same structure, making them very predictable. Basically, push button to open pathway, grab key to open doors, create shadows to make platform. It’s not until the last stage – Garden Stage – that things finally became more. and I would’ve preferred that this was introduce in the third stage and the puzzles were more elaborate. I am not implying in any way that puzzles should be difficult. But part of the being a good puzzle game is that it must challenge the player. For most of the play through, Tandem hardly ever has anything that is challenging. Every puzzle is basic even if the idea behind it has potential. It seems like such a waste. To be fair, the Garden stage gave a glimpse of that potentiality, with puzzles that are more elaborate, using timed mechanics, quick switching of characters and such. I just wish there was more of it. Also, a good platformer must –  – nail the controls. Movement is crucial in any 2D platform and in this regard, Tandem falls short. Controls are sluggish, lacks responsiveness and with limited move-set. All the Teddy Bear can do is move left and right and jump. So little so that calling this a “platform puzzle” is almost misleading even if technically correct. The Bear should have been given a bit more things to do. Lastly, the story in my opinion, also had good potential but it is so flimsily written. Why is the girl so enthralled with Thomas Kane? What is her relationship with the boy and the Kane family? Motivations of the protagonist and the antagonist are never explored. The characters themselves is unremarkable at best and forgettable at worst. I can’t even remember if the girl had a name, and I don’t remember what the bear is called either. It seems like the developers shoe-horned this story without much thought or concern, which is a waste because this story had a lot of potential to be a good dark fairy tale.As much as I would like to recommend this game, the flaws are much too glaring. It’s far too easy for any serious puzzle players, the platforming is much to janked for any 2D platforming player and the narrative is much too lacking for anyone wanting an immersive story. To be fair, the game isn’t bad. It’s just not good enough in my opinion. It sits in the middle where I might have recommended it but ultimately I didn't because none of the cutscenes are running on Linux and by extension, none of the cutscenes will run on Steam Deck. This means that a whole chunk of the games content is inaccessible for Linux and Steam Deck players. It is just not worth the investment. I am however, fairly optimistic of Monochrome Paris' next endeavor. There is enough good idea here in Tandem that warrants a second chance. I do hope they improve on their next iteration if it is greenlighted, and I'd be happy to give that a try. As for A Tale Of Shadows, I’d advise to get it on sale instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Making a paired puzzle game is a very difficult task, because you need to constantly keep in mind the balance between the characters so that playing for one of them does not become more boring compared to the other. In this game, we control two characters - a girl and a toy bear, who must combine their skills in the real world and the world of shadows in order to get through the confusing and mysterious spaces. The game has a rather calm pace, most of the time you can solve puzzles quite peacefully, but occasionally there are also limited-time challenges (not the best part of the game, to be honest). There are also platforming elements that are quite logical and accessible to any player, so do not be afraid. Here, the reasonable use of the trial and error method organically combined with the need to logically think out the solution to a particular puzzle.Pleases the great attention with which the creators approached the uniqueness of their design and gameplay solutions. The game has 5 different zones with 8 puzzles each, and each of these zones is unique. All of them have their own laws, interesting things, mechanisms for solving puzzles, and this constantly keeps your interest at a high level. After all, as soon as you start to get bored with this zone, you are already moving to the next one, where many surprises await you. The search for collectibles here becomes almost part of the main story. Good naivety so pleasantly creates an atmosphere of a fairy tale, some kind of pure childish force opposing something dark. And the weirder the ending looks... If it's so obvious about the sequel, then it's okay (although I don't like such cliffhangers), but if it's a complete ending, then it's strange. As I wrote above, I didn’t really like the time-limited puzzles, where you need to drag something from place to place. The drag and drop system in the game is not the most convenient, and even when you are also running out of time, it becomes generally torture. There are very few such tests, and at least this is good. I would also like to note a very cool variety of bosses in each zone, which are extremely interesting and exciting to fight."Tandem: a tale of shadows" excitingly combines two different worlds, leaving the player to choose which one he likes to be in. Interesting, fresh and charming.

_childDocuments_.review: "The disappearance of Thomas Kane, the only son of the famous Kane illusionists still hasn't been solved by Scotland Yard. Ten-year-old Emma, intrigued, is determined to investigate. As Emma walks the streets of London towards the mansion, a carriage passes by at full speed and a teddy bear falls out the window unexpectedly. Fenton the Teddy bear jumps onto his feet and sets off in pursuit of the vehicle. Without thinking twice, Emma joins the race launching after him. Okay, Fenton, we don't know each other much, but we're going to have to help each other find Thomas. Can I count on you?" You play as Emma and along with Fenton the Teddy Bear you arrive at the Kane mansion; your investigation begins in The Gardens (Chapter One Upside Down). You switch between Emma and Fenton as you make your way through each chapter. However, Emma moves around in the light, where you are looking down on her movements, while Fenton moves in the shadows and his movements are in the way of a side scrolling view.  Between the both of them you will have to use both the light and shadows as you look for a Crystal which can only be collected by Fenton. The collection of the Crystal will bring an end to the current chapter, allowing you to move onto the next chapter. There are five chapters, The Gardens, Boiler Room, The Kitchen, Clockwork and Greenhouse with a combined total of forty-four levels between them. As Emma you have a lantern which you use to create shadows so that Fenton can move safely around on the shadows produced. Each of the areas have their own theme and puzzles you will have to figure out how each of the puzzles is to be completed. This at first glance it might not be visible to you, you cannot move around the level to find the Crystal and plan your movements. You will also have to use the environment around you, this changes with each of the areas you visit. For example, the Boiler Room will have you dealing with pipes, turning the pipes on and off so that a liquid can flow through, this will then allow Fenton to walk on the liquid.  There are also other objects in your way, some of them will require you to stand on a button, which will then open a door or turn other objects on and off. There are some spiders which are able to scan in front of them and should you enter their field of vision they’ll rush after wrapping you up in a cocoon with their sticky web. They are hard to try and escape from once they get you in their sights but there are ways to get past them. You can also move some objects, such as Cubelings, which you can drag around by their tongue and be placed in certain to help you, they can also be used to eat through walls or carts which can only move on a rail, allowing you to create shadows. With each Crystal you gain, it will become part of a Key, once completed you will be able to enter the final level of the chapter. Completing the final level will allow you to then use the key and move on to the next area. You’ll have to keep your mince pies open for hidden secrets, there are eighteen hidden secrets scattered around the levels. Finding the secrets will also unlock Steam achievements and each of them can be found along with a picture in The Artworks, found on the main menu screen. In the settings there are options for Video - Quality, Post Process, Textures, Visual Effects, Resolution, Screen and V-Sync. Controls - Key Binds for both Keyboard & Mouse and Gamepad. Language - English, French, German, Chinese, Korean, Spanish, Italian, Japanese, Polish, Portugues and Russian. Audio - Music and Effects Volume Sliders. Tandem: A Tale of Shadows is a fun puzzle platformer game; I liked the little story which unlocks as you progress through each of the chapters as you investigate the disappearance of Thomas Kane. I did finish the game in about 8 hours or so, taking my time and getting stuck a few times on one or two of the levels. I liked the ending of the game; I didn’t expect that at all. The puzzles aren’t very hard for the most part, but sometimes you needed to be perfect in your application of swapping between characters back and forth, moving them around in order to complete the puzzle. Positives + Enjoyable game + Good graphics + Ambience and sounds + Unexpected ending + Full controller support + Has achievements Negatives  - No cards currently A fantastic puzzle platformer where you switch between the characters Emma and Fenton the Teddy Bear, light and shadows as you search for the missing Thomas Kane in Tandem: A Tale of Shadows. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Watch my 5 minute review here (or read below at your own pace): Gameplay-Tandem is one of the best puzzle platformers that I’ve played recently, even throwing in some challenging platforming sections that I had to try multiple times in order to complete.  As Emma, you’ll explore the lower areas of each location as you enter the Kane Mansion, from the gardens, ascending through the boiler room and kitchen, and so on, and she’ll have to avoid the many thematic hazards that impede her way.  In the gardens, strange spiders with laser eyes will try to wrap her up for a tasty treat, and in the boiler room, some strange liquid goo with eyes seems to be following her every move.Not only will you be trying to avoid these threats, but in every room of each location, there is a crystal key which Fenton will need to collect in order for the two to progress.  Fenton being a teddy bear destined to stay in the shadow realm, can only move in 2 dimensions, and can walk on top of shadows, but not in them.  And this is where the beauty of Tandem’s puzzle platforming really starts to shine.  Emma carries a handy lantern, and can cast shadows around each room in order to help Fenton reach the key.  You’ll be switching back and forth between the two characters frequently, but this mechanic is the basis of the game, and it works splendidly.  The solutions to each level weren’t evident at first glance, but at the same time, I never felt just stuck on a level.  At most, a level took me 10 minutes to complete, and never broke my brain, and all but a few early levels were rewarding to figure out.  Especially when you get to some of the later levels that require some faster platforming, and precise timing in switching between the characters and triggering actions simultaneously.  The more I played, the more I was having fun with the platforming, and feeling in a groove with the mechanics.Art-I think this game is launching at the perfect time of year, just before Halloween, as the entire setting is macabre, but in a cartoonish way, similar to movies by Tim Burton and Henry Selick like The Nightmare Before Christmas and Coraline.  The rich colors and the balance of light and shadows which pervades the gameplay all contribute to this spooky mood, not to mention the many dangers that lurk in the shadows and crevices of the landscape too.I’m not a horror fan, but I love this setting and style, creeping forward towards the red eyes of a spider, wondering how close is too close, until suddenly it’s chasing me, with nowhere to run.  And then you respawn and move forward with the knowledge, hoping not to encounter another giant spider anytime soon.  Hidden in the beautiful architecture and scenery are paintings, which you can collect to be showcased in your Gallery on the main menu.  In my couple hours of playing, I only managed to collect one, although I found a couple others and simply didn’t have the patience to pursue them.  There is an overworld map of sorts which shows off each area, and allows you to re-explore earlier levels for any hidden secrets or art pieces.Music-Also great, featuring dissonant tones with lots of chimes, kind of haunted music box vibes, and that’s just in the garden section.  As you progress to new areas and rooms of the house, the music changes to fit the mood, featuring heavy organ tones in the boiler room, which also for some reason features an organ in the overworld map.  Emma is voice-acted, if you’re curious, and if I have one minor complaint about the game, it’s that the story just doesn’t progress very quickly.  Or at all in the first couple hours.  Story-Through the first two locations, there is almost no mention of Thomas or revelations of his whereabouts, with most cutscenes focusing on how the characters are progressing to the next location, and a little speculation about it.  With the story being introduced in the opening minute of the game as an epilogue of sorts, I would have liked to see more of this story driving the narrative and focus of the game.  The story is fun, and while nothing revolutionary, it’s a good one that sets the stage for the mysterious mansion you’re exploring, and also gives credence to why this teddy bear can walk and help Emma.  He did fall out of the magician’s carriage after all.TL;DR-I recommend it.  The gameplay mechanics are solid and challenging, and the platforming especially just gets better with time.  The art is perfectly grim, and the soundtrack works well with it, changing to fit each new location, which I really love.  If you’re looking for a spooky game to settle down with this Halloween, but one that won’t make you run to bed after turning the lights off, look no further.

_childDocuments_.review: Sumptuous graphics, most of which you can't see because of the perspective, and can't interact with, embellish disappointingly linear problem-solving (often the only thing you can interact with removes the only barrier to progress).  The biggest challenge was often areas where dexterity with the controller was essential - which isn't really puzzle-solving and I found completing those areas to be more of a relief than a satisfaction.Having to sit through the opening narration every time the game starts was another annoyance.Nevertheless the game would have been charming enough if not for the final level which (unlike the rest of the game) appeared buggy (Emma wandered out of the playing area and couldn't get back, Fenton got stuck in shadows for no apparent reason) so that it took three attempts to complete, whereupon the downer ending, worthy of the League of Gentlemen, made me wish I'd not completed it, and robbed the game of any replay value.I thought there must be another ending - that would have been OK - but Internet seems to say "no".In hindsight the downer ending seems obvious, but one suspends disbelief in entertainment.

There are quite a number of mechanics, but they are not explored anywhere near their full potential, and I don't find them to be particularly creative as well. The platforming sections controls like a amateurish student project. There is no height variation depending on how long you hold the jump button, an industry standard dating back to the NES days. Another thing is that I can't get the game to change its resolution. It's stuck in a weird 1704 * 960 resolution for me. Even if I run it in windowed mode and have the window maximized (my desktop resolution is 3840 * 2160), it's still as blurry. Didn't bother with configuration files personally but I saw others reporting they can't change resolution even with configuration files.

A muddled color palette to communicate confusion or sadness would be considered highly rated here despite being uncomfortable to experience.1 - A total mess. The ability to pause or otherwise completely disengage from the game without detrimental impact to the gameplay. e.g. Turn-Based Strategy Games, Tactical Games, etc.1 - No ability to pause or stop gameplay.10 - Ability to pause or stop gameplay at any time.Autonomy of PaceThe ability for the player to choose the pace of the game and gameplay.1 - Basically no autonomy. _childDocuments_.review: Tandem: a tale of shadows is a short, but well crafted little puzzle platformer, in which you control two characters at once, while manipulating shadows to your advantage.Emma, a small girl finds the living teddy bear Fenton and follows him into a creepy looking villa, to solve the mystery of what happened to a kid named Thomas.While you control Emma from a topdown perspective, changing to Fenton let's you play like a sidescroller, as he walks on the walls of the level and on shadows that you cast using different objects and lights strewn about.This naturally leads to some great puzzles as you change the layout of the level by pushing around carts and different light sources so Fenton can reach new areas.Fenton also will have to clear the way for Emma, mainly through the use of switches.The puzzles were satisfying for the most part, though a little on the easier side.There were some headscrathers toward the end of the game, but nothing to get stuck on for too long :)While the characters and animations are a little stiff, i'd still say that this game looks really nice for the debut title of such a small team. Especially the environments have a lot of charme.The only thing i found a little lacking is the story or more so the lack thereof.It's passable to get the game going, but until the end of the game there's not really a lot going on.All in all, if you enjoy the idea of a puzzle platformer that's all about playing with light and shadows and got a few hours to spare, why not give Tandem: a tale of shadows a try?

_childDocuments_.review: Here is a video of my full review on my YouTube channel: The atmosphere is what struck me almost immediately. It’s Limbo vibes, it’s Darq vibes, it’s Inside vibes. It’s all the vibes! It’s a mix of colorful and whimsical yet dark and sinister. I’m sure many have made this comparison but it is very Tim Burton-esque. Clearly a lot of time and attention went into the fine details of the look of this game because even aspects of the game that are not able to be interacted with or, in some cases, you can’t even reach are beautifully rendered and pretty darn detailed. So much of this world seems alive…even things that shouldn’t be. But I very much enjoy this post Victorian steampunk/clock punk style aesthetic. And the music is a FANTASTIC addition to the ambiance. Every chapter has a signature music across it’s levels and the music really adds to a sense of unease and reminds you that this home is not a safe place. The sound design is pretty impressive and immersive, everything from Emma’s footsteps to the creaking, groaning, or squelching of obstacles or the sound that Fenton makes when he jumps are very well done.The gameplay was quite engaging. You play as both Emma and Fenton to solve environmental puzzles to clear each stage. Each chapter has 8 to 11 levels and is themed around a particular room in the mansion such as the boiler room, the kitchen, or the garden. Emma is played from a top down perspective and she is able to manipulate objects in order to cast shadows to allow Fenton, who walks on the walls in a 2D side scrolling manner, to move from place to place. This was a brilliant touch but be sure you remain aware of where each character is within their space. One neat way the game helps you keep track of who is control is that Emma plays in color while Fenton plays in black and white. Luckily controls are pretty responsive so that you can make those life and death decisions on the fly.  As far at the puzzles go, they hit the sweet spot: not too easy and not too challenging. I am a lover of puzzle games but I’m no expert so even an average Jo like me was able to figure out what to do in pretty reasonable timeframe. Now there were definitely moments where it took some brain power and good ole trial and error to figure out HOW to do those things that I needed to be done…but that’s all part of the fun, right? It should take you anywhere from 3 to 5 hours on a first run through, depending on how much secret hunting you do along the way.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Review on Youtube: Tandem A Tale of Shadows is set in London at the end of the 19th century and tells the story of Emma, a 10-year-old girl whoenters a mysterious manor on the search for a missing boy, Thomas Kane, the only child of a famous illusionist. And while Scotland Yard already gave up on the case Emma is determined to investigate. On her way to the Kane manor she meets Fenton, a magic teddy bear with mysterious abilities that allow him to bend perspectives and move within the shadows. Together they are ableto enter the manor and find clues and hints about Thomas disappearance by solving a variety of puzzles. You, as a player, control both of the characters by constantly switching between them and combining their unique skills and perspectives. Emma is played in top-down perspective and can only maneuver on the floor, while Fenton is played in side-scroller perspective and can only move on walls and between shadows. Emma lights up the scene with lanterns or other sources of light and has to use solid or moveable objects to create shadow paths for Fenton. This way the teddy bear can reach different switches and buttons that effect Emmas ground level and can collect the crystals they need to enter the next room.The game features five victorian inspired worlds with different topics and unique designs, that are parted into multiple levels with increasing difficulty. During your journey you have to solve more than 40 puzzles and will encounter a variety of mechanical toy-like enemies and bosses. Each chapter offers new ways to solve puzzles and also new and more challenging opponents tooutsmart. Some want you to think outside the box, while others need speed and dexterity. But one thing all puzzles have in common is, that Emma and Fenton have to work together to solve them.Tandem: A Tale of Shadows is a pretty solid and enjoyable game with challenging puzzles, interesting mechanics and a good balance in difficulty. The graphics and design fit the story pretty well and even though the scenery of Tandem is pretty dark and mystical, it's not too spooky as to not be suitable for kids. The controls are pretty simple, precise and intuitive and the music and sound effects add to the immersion. The only somewhat negative point for me are the graphics in the cutscenes, as they look a bit outdated. But they still manage to tell the story and at its core, the game is a puzzle adventure anyhow and it’s doing a great job with this.

_childDocuments_.review: Tandem : A Tale of Shadows redefines the puzzle platformer genre with a unique gameplay and exceptional aesthetics. Help Emma and the teddy bear Fenton solve the mystery of the disappearance of the famous magician Thomas Kane.

name: Salt and Sacrifice
detailed_description: Beyond sanctuary, a realm of elemental pandemonium awaits. A once-peaceful kingdom is plunged into chaos by encroaching tides of Mages: merciless embodiments of elemental chaos. The Marked Inquisitors, a doomed force of the condemned, once again mobilizes to stand against the existential threat of Magic. A buried secret threatens to bring an ancient empire to utter ruin. In a land plagued by powerful and twisted Mages, the condemned Marked Inquisitors take up the hunt. As a Marked Inquisitor, you’ll journey through the western frontier: pursuing, hunting, and obliterating the Mages that roam the realm. You may be bound to the Inquisition, but your choices are yours. Wield the Power of Your Foes Craft unique weapons and armor from the otherworldly flesh and bones of the Mages you destroy. Master dozens of powerful weapons and runic arts: “safe” manipulations of the corrupt Magic your foes wield. A Dense and Detailed World Explore a large and labyrinthine world filled with scavengers, secrets, traps, and powerful guardians. Online Multiplayer Team up with a fellow Inquisitor for full online co-op and drop-in quickplay online co-op, or engage in fast and chaotic PvP through various factions.

_childDocuments_.review: Massive downgrade compared to Salt and Sanctuary. The devs wanted to try too many new things all at once and EPIC (store) failed in most of them. The following review assume you have played the first game but some points make sense even for someone approaching this title for the first time. I'm going to stress some points very hard for the simple reason I've read reviews of the game before it was published on steam and boy do I wish I took them to heartGraphic is better, nothing to complain here and the use of colours and shades is far superior to Sanctuary. Hands down an improvement with no drawbacks Sound is good even if I like the BG of Sanctuary better but to each their own tastes. Each hit against shields sound "real" enough and the only one I really didn't like is the effect of lightning "magic" (again, you may like it, I didn't)Now for the plethora of flaws I really could not recommend the game. Many of these things have already been stressed by other players in their reviews and I wish I took them seriously enough but alas....- Forget weapon selection the way you knew it, want to use a specific weapon with a shield you like? NOPE, they come paired and there's nothing you can do about it.- Weapons are now tied to some specific elements and grades but they are fixed and cannot be altered in any way. Wanted to use a lightning greatsword in endgame? Think again. Oh and you also have to check if the weapon uses divine or arcane weapon arts since they need to be unlocked separately. It's a very restricitve system that massively limit build variety- Many players complained about how asinine was to assign weapons to a grade and being unable to use them unless you got their badge on the skill tree. You can have 40 strenght and being able to lift the best greatsword in the game but forget using the most basic club if you don't unlock it first- No weapon combo anymore unless for a basic system of light/strong attack.Now we get to the really bad stuff, those design choices that really left me staring at the screen trying to understand if I actually saw that happening- Some levels have a LOT of verticality, like a LOT LOT. No big deal if not for the fact that most enemies abuse the living ungodly hell of knockback and ragdoll. I'm confident in your intellective prowess to understand where I'm going or rather where you'll be plummeting - As I was saying, most enemies spam knockback and ragdoll attacks and can and totally will juggle you mid air. Don't believe me? The juggling damage alone has been nerfed twice, yes it was that freaking bad- Enemies have unlimited stamina BY THE WAY. Some players will tell you they don't but they do, they are just conveniently referring to the stamina to stagger them if you block them at exact time they hit you and you also need to block/parry multiple times to deplete their pseduo stamina in order to make a risposte. This mean that EVERY single enemy in the game can keep attacking indefinitely without pause - Related to the previous point but deserving of a spot of its own, enemies spam attack constantly. Not a figure of speech and I wrote "spam attacks" becuase it's what I meant. Bosses will be able to cast multiple attacks before the animation of the first one even completed. No, I'm not jokingI'm not even going to complain about chasing bosses around the map, that is forgivable...completely stupid since they teleport after 3 or 4 hits but that is really a minor problem compared the others.Ah yes, this has been fixed but I feel like I have to warn potential buyers. The game started with no sorting option for inventory despite the a vast amount of players complaining about it in the first one. they probably copy pasted from the source code of the first game...Never heard of a single game besides this with no way to sort inventory. Draw your own conclusions. I really cannot recommend this game in good conscience

_childDocuments_.review: I came into the game originally on PS5 two years ago. Tried it for a bit, wasn't the biggest fan and decided to come back to it.Here I am now having played much more of it than I originally did. Man, I so badly wanted to like this game. I am a massive fan of Salt and Sanctuary, love that game so much for its style, sound design, enemy design, boss design, level design, and weapon design. This game feels like such a massive step back in almost all of those regards. The random spawns of bosses, hazeburnt enemies during hunts, areas that don't feel designed to have bosses in them, enemies and traps that feel like complete and utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ so much of the time, and late game areas that don't feel like they have any reason to be there or are unfinished.The weapon crafting system feels so good, the player combat feels so good with the focus and rage systems of casting. Not being able to turn around while aiming is a massive downside though, lack of an attack speed indicator can turn a much anticipated weapon craft into a huge disappointment.Souls games work because there is a level of predictability with the enemy placement. Randomly spawning enemies don't mess with the enemy placement. Enemies don't appear one moment in just the worst place imaginable with almost no time to react to it. The traps are readable, even in Sanctuary the traps were much more fun to deal with. Monster Hunter games work because the areas have a lot of care put into them to make sure the levels interact with the monsters you hunt. Some even have special interactions with levels. You can also pick what monster to hunt in order to grind instead of loading into a level and hoping you get what you wanted to spawn.This game does both of those things wrong. I hate to say it feels like more of a rush job on an otherwise incredible concept for a game with the player systems all being there for a great experience. The world feels underdone. The enemies feel underdone. It's so frustrating to see a game come so close just to be held back by a very poor feeling world.I love Ska Studios, but man this feels like a dropped ball.
