_childDocuments_.review: Oh god where do I start.Firstly, I know I haven't played this game much, and I'm going to keep that in mind while writing my review. Like so many others in this review section, I'm an ABSOLUTE fan of Salt and Sanctuary. I've poured 300 hours of my lifetime into it, tried out every possible build (except magic because... well.. It's magic), killed every boss, nuked every boss, gotten every achievement... I just couldn't get enough.That being said, Salt and Sacrifice lost me after I killed the fourth electromancer in a row, and those aside, I think I've killed 4 unique bosses so far and all of them were just so forgettable.. I don't even remember their names... In comparism, I'm confident that everyone here who's played Salt and Sanctuary remembers The Sodden Knight.Back to the mages... Why do I have to play cat and mouse with them? ._. - I get you wanted to make a mage hunter, but it just feels so unrewarding running through an area you've already finished to find a boss you've already beaten, especially since some of the areas are ABSOLUTELY not fit for boss fights. Next point. Random enemy spawns... No... Learning fixed patterns and spawns and capitalizing on them is, imo,  an essential part of any (FUN) souls like. And random spawns just make that impossible. I've seen a lot of people complain about repetitive enemies, but tbh I for my part haven't noticed it... The combat actually feels smoother than S&S, I like the sprinting mechanic for example. It actually feels very fast paced, love it. I have one huge problem with the combat tho. No Iframes when you get knocked down is catastrophic. You can just get snowballed out of existance. I've died a couple times because an enemy launched me into the air and then homerunned me into oblivion.Lastly, I gotta point out the obvious pros. I absolutely adore your graphic style. Please never change it. Period. The skill tree is as good as ever, Ive found some good weapons for my style fairly early on, and multiple for other builds had I wanted to pick smth other than pure strength :D. I also like the charm system, adds a layer of complexity to builds. The built in throwing weapon was kinda useless to me, thenagain I haven't found any strong ones yet because I haven't played the game much. Lastly, the map designs are mostly good, very often built either linear or circular., I just felt like players who are new to no map games might get lost at one point or another. Thenagain that's just me assuming.Believe me when I say that I give this thumbs down with a heavy heart. I've played Dishwasher and Salt and Sanctuary and I absolutely loved both of them, and it hurts me seeing this game fail the fanbase as much as it does. I just feel Salt and Sacrifice got lost in ideas... I hope you're not discouraged to keep going by this game flopping, you both have a gift for making games, and I'd love to see  a real Salt and Sanctuary 2 someday. :3

_childDocuments_.review: Having almost 100%'d the first game, I wanted to wait until I beat this game to give a review. I can now say that I've done so. TL;DR, Salt and Sacrifice is a devolution compared to its predecessor. While the core mechanics behind combat, boss fights, and metroidvania style exploration are the same, almost everything that was changed did so for the worse. I cannot recommend Salt and Sacrifice in good faith, when you instead have the option to play Salt and Sanctuary.     1. Areas are less interconnected, as you travel to them through a central portal rather than finding them through exploration. Exploration within these areas is also typically rewarded with shortcuts that become obsolete due to the fact that you can teleport between beacons.     2. Combat is less fluid and clunkier, especially with ranged weapons, which had their ability to combo and parry removed. Just holding them out will also make your character a sitting duck. Spells are now tied to weapons instead of being mixed and matched at user discretion, staves are mostly useless since almost all of their spells can be found on better weapon types. Despite the relatively complex movesets that each melee weapon has, I almost always did nothing but spam running attacks.     3. There are fewer equipment options. Pistols no longer exist, axes have been scattered across multiple weapon types, and parrying and tower shields went the way of the dodo. The game places a heavy focus on having the right element to attack enemies, but not only does the bestiary not inform you of their weaknesses, many weapon categories also completely lack about half of the available damage types.     4. The mages are the main enemy of the game, which you'll be fighting once about every 5-15 minutes, and which are required for both exploration and equipment progression. The mages also universally have the most frustrating designs and movesets in the game, which is especially baffling since the non-respawning bosses still have the same tight and exhilarating gameplay of the first game's bossfights.     5. Almost the entire story is hastily crammed into the last area of the game, and told to you by a few nameless NPCs. The final boss is a nobody who you've never met or been told about before. The endings are devoid of a clear meaning. The NPC which gives you advice on progression throughout the game also mysteriously disappears at some point in the latter half and never comes back, which is acknowledged by no one.     6. The sense of allegiance and progression that the different factions had in Sanctuary is gone. All factions in Sacrifice are built around a completely dead multiplayer, and the only other way to progress through them is to mindlessly grind even more mages, as if you hadn't been swamped enough by their presence.

_childDocuments_.review: I fail to understand the thought process behind making one of the best indie souls-like into a monster-hunter-like. Actually, the game is labeled as "Monster-Hunter-like, Souls-like Metroidvania". I think to myself, maybe the developers find a way to mingle the merits from the three of them. After all, Salt And Sanctuary is a great souls-like metroidvania and probably the pioneer of this sub-genre. The result begs to differ, negatively. Salt and Sacrifice is a chimera. Developers borrow a lot of core ideas from the three genres, stitch them together, and somehow fail to breathe life into it. It's a shame because I really want to like this game. I like the iconic ska studio art style, and the animation is way smoother than Salt And Sanctuary. Everything else ruins the whole experience.→The iconic ska art style.→I like the mages and their lackeys' design.→Unique and fancy weapons, armors and trinkets to craft.→I guess Perfect Block is now a new standard for souls-like.→Seeing mages fighting each other is oddly satisfying.Like I said before, mashing genres together won't automatically make the game fun to play. You need to have the right mechanic and design to glue the features together.→: first, hunting mages does not feel good. Instead of you giving it all to take down a powerful being, the hunt plays out more like fighting the lackeys it summons until the mage stops running. The whole process before the showdown feels like a slog designing to stretch the length of the fight as much as possible; second, there is no real "hunting" involved. You find the residue the mage left behind, you accept the mission, and then you follow the guiding smoke till you find the culprit. No tracking. No collecting information. Just say yes to the mission and you are set; last, the most important part which was left behind, skills and set bonus each armor provides. I know the traditional level system and skill tree exist, but the lacking of those build varieties is such a missed opportunity to encourage players to hunt more mages and try out different build combinations.→: This is not even a downgrade, Salt And Sacrifice straight up ditches the level design in favor of the monster-hunter-like gameplay. None of the great design from previous title can be seen here. There is no actual mobility to unlock, and naturally there is no platforming or bosses' attacks to incentivize players to use those abilities more. The so-called gating abilities in this game are all just glorified keys to unlock shortcuts or activate hidden platforms. This issue won't be such hassle if the level design can properly use them. Alas, it doesn't.→: this is more of a rant about design philosophy rather than gameplay mechanic. Often time when other games try to imitate the magic of the Souls-series, they always focus on the gameplay only. Of course gameplay is a core feature, but other things are just as important. Coherent item descriptions, logical enemy placements, environmental story-telling, the list goes on and on. Somehow Salt And Sacrifice throws everything away. Item descriptions of the equipment provides nothing vital clues or some interesting story. Most of them feel like they were assembled by random word generator. Bosses have no identity at all since they don't even drop their equipment when they're defeated, therefore no lore to read through. The Mages do not fare well either. Despite the cool design, their roaming nature and the lacking of dedicated levels make them more of elite mobs rather than significant bosses. →Locking all the weapon ability behind one or two stat requirement is not a good idea.→Collecting resource to craft health potion does not fit souls-like.→Enemies late-game deal absurdly high damage.→The geyser/glider ability feels awkward to use.→A proper map will make navigating the world less confusing and frustrating.中文小簡評：→什麼都要加一點的大雜燴，到頭來什麼都做不好的遊戲。→真心不懂為何創造出首款獨立魂系類銀河系惡魔城的團隊，會把續作搞得一蹋糊塗。→製作團隊的美工依然別緻。→諸多巫師及其手下的設計特色十足。→多樣奇特武器、護甲及配件供玩家製作。→原來完美防禦已經是類魂的標配了。→巫師間會短兵相接，隔岸觀火特別有趣。→就類魔物獵人的部分，狩獵過程一點也不有趣、巫師在最終對決前只會刷小怪、裝備沒有專屬技能或搭配效果。→就類銀河系惡魔城的部分，沒有實質技能解鎖，幾乎都是變相的鑰匙，關卡設計也只把這些技能用作開捷徑的工具而已。→就類魂的部分，玩法有做到但其他特色都沒做好，道具敘述有講跟沒講一樣、敵人配置感覺較隨意、Boss和巫師沒有設計獨特的場景來烘托角色。→所有武器技能一定要點信仰及特定配點才能用....→類魂遊戲就不要設計什麼蒐集素材作補血道具了。→遊戲後期每個敵人都能兩下秒你。→降落傘詭異的難用。→探索時沒地圖看很容易迷路。

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first of all I've played only Dark Souls Remastered and Salt and Sanctuary and no other Soulsborne titles:Well, for starters, everyone thinking that Salt and Sancrifice is just another Soulsborne Carbon Copy; it's not. This isn't even Salt and Sanctuary 2, it may take place in the same universe, but it's no sequel. It's a stand alone game.In my opinion it's more of a 2D Monster Hunter with Bloodborne elements than a general Soulslike, but what do I mean by that? You hunt mages across certain levels and/or stages instead of beasts, with replenishable health items and ammo. The equipment crafted from materials gathered from mages possess attributes affiliated with said mage and most weapons have unique skills.While mentioning weapons, yes, only one weapon category comes with a shield and it's not exactly the most fun one, but blocking is not exclusive to shields and even though I have no on-hand experience, but I believe Bloodborne is also played without a shield.I've experienced a lot of the things many people have criticized about the game, like being juggled by enemies in mid-air, or being absolutely yeeted off of platforms, but in hindsight, after beating the game multiple times, that's pretty much just the Aeromancer. I'm not sure if people only played until that boss and just rage-quitted or anything, but of course there are other bosses like the Terramancers infamous bodycheck follow-up, or the Umbramancers quadruple shockwaves, or the Diablomancers relentless traps, but nothing really I couldn't handle and I'm not exactly the best player out there.Also, it's not like you've never been juggled or yeeted in Sanctuary before, just let me remind you of the Tree of Men, the Unskinnd and the Architect or the Knight, Judge and King. Not to mention the B**** of the Lake. Or just the Spindlebeasts.Another thing I've noticed is how much people revere Salt and Sanctuary, myself included, so after beating Sacrifice I replayed Sanctuary on enhanced mode to compare the two not just from memory:Walking speed is the first thing I noticed. In Sanctuary your speed depends heavily on your weight, while in Sacrifice not so much, but you move slower in general, except for sprinting, which is faster than anything in Sanctuary. There are other minor things, like wall-jumping feels better in sanctuary, but platforming in general felt smoother in sacrifice. I miss the mid-air dash from Sanctuary and the interconnected level design, but I love having a hub world where my stash, a smith and merchants are. Sometimes the controls aren't fast enough in Sacrifice, like I hit LB to drink after rolling and it just wouldn't do it, but Sanctuary wasn't any better in that regard either. Also people seem to complain about the random wandering mages you can find while exploring, sometimes even multiple ones at the same time and all I can say is; the more the merrier.I could go on, but who'd read all that? I love Salt and Sanctuary and Sacrifice alike, also, and that is just a thought, people complain about the two games not being similar enough, but how would we have reacted to Sacrifice just being a copy and paste of Sanctuary?

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first ever proper review of something so the formatting and stuff will probably be very rough but I really would like to share my thoughts on this game.I played Salt and Sacrifice before I ever played Sanctuary, and I didn't like the game from the moment I started playing it. Encounters often felt unfair and cheap, such as constant ganks or instant reactions from enemies that can juggle you for days without much you can really do about it. Attacks can be spammed out and the player movement doesn't really allow for the kind of manoeuvrability the game expects from you.To start with, the mage bosses in this game don't really feel like bosses at all, they spend most of the time running away and spawning mobs that suffer from a myriad of issues, such as said spawned mobs attacking you before they are even fully visible on screen or possessing cheap gimmicks (enemies that can block in this game are an absolute joke and take forever to guard break)Once you do get to the "boss fight" part of the actual fight, it typically goes one of two ways, either the mage is a complete joke and easy to demolish, or the mage suffers from a bunch of incredibly cheap, incredibly spammy moves that can just 1 shot you, it is very frustrating and such a downgrade from the quality of bosses that were present in Sanctuary.Speaking of Sanctuary, after I completed Sacrifice, I decided to give it a try and the difference between the games is night and day, sacrifice is bloated with issues that drag the game down that were never present in Sanctuary, and it's baffling some of the design choices when comparing the two.Things such as the quality of combat, weapons, level design are so much more inferior in Sacrifice, as it abandons the free flowing open world of Sanctuary in favour of a more linear stage selection-esque system present in alot of other games, but this causes the game world to feel far less interesting, and exploration is far less rewarding, as loot rewards are heavily gutted in this game, you will rarely find a new cool weapon or armour set, as 99% of the weapons etc you get are just crafted by beating bosses, the entire process of immersing yourself in the world and slowly exploring and discovering new and interesting items and weapons is completely absent in this game, yet in Sanctuary I'd say they really nailed the open world aspect, unsure why they changed this.Bosses and combat encounters in general compared to Sanctuary feel far more dumbed down and more luck dependant than skill, although the variety in moves in Sanctuary for enemies and bosses weren't the most deep, they were fair and thrilling as opposed to Sacrifice where it jumps between a joke and total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.The platforming in this game feels really janky and unresponsive, which admittedly was my least favourite part in Sanctuary too, but here enemies will constantly snipe you out of the air with the tiniest projectile which kills all your momentum, or you will get knocked about like a ragdoll and bounced around without having much say in the matter.On the more artistic side of things, personally I feel the art style is a complete downgrade from the more dark and unpleasant style of Sanctuary, and the music for this game feels far less inspired than that of Sanctuarys too, with no real standout tracks which is a massive shame.I could go on and on about the unsatisfying combat (weapons have far less reach than Sanctuary, making them feel far less satisfying, a lot of the weapons just have no forward momentum at all too, so you feel very static when attacking), or the boring level design (rip open world), ganky enemies (enemies that just pop into existence or combo you for days, cant forget that mobs can just be in mage boss fights too to make it even more of a cluster ♥♥♥♥), poor boss quality and so on, but I don't want to just drag on when this review is already a mess.Personally, I would like to see some more changes to the games balance, I've already come to terms that this game will never live up to the love I have for Sanctuary (one of my favourite games of all time), but I do think with some adjustments, this game could be decent, but it needs a lot of work, which makes it really difficult for me to recommend this game for anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: So while I do like this game. It just has a lot of issues that need to be addressed. Many of the core aspects of this game is extremely flawed compared to not only its predecessor Salt and Sanctuary, but even Souls games in general.One of the biggest main issues I noticed about this game are the bosses themselves. Bosses in this game are capable of relentlessly attacking you and are able to juggle you like it's a Tekken fighting game and because bosses attack so fast you often feel like you are dodging most of the time rather than attacking until eventually the boss catches up with you.Second issue is enemy and trap placement. Many traps I noticed usually have a trigger, but the triggers are purposely well hidden that it just feels obnoxious. Even certain enemies themselves are so well hidden they function as a trap themselves, but without any indicators other than dying and having to remember. Which is already a difficult task to do in a big, chaotic map.The loot system. Although the system isn't particularly bad. The main issue I noticed mostly when I was using twin daggers is that the RNG can actually halt your progress if you can't find a better weapon.Spellmark. It's a mechanic similar in old souls games where if you die you get a permanent reduction to your HP. An outdated mechanic that Fromsoft themselves got rid of in Elden Ring, but also rather punishing in a already punishing game. The only way you can remove it is using Guiltless Shards similar to Humanity in souls games, but with a few difference. In Souls games you can do that by killing bosses, helping players kill bosses, or invading players and killing them. You can not do any of that in Salt and Sacrifice other than Guiltless Shard. Instead Guiltless Shard was made as drops for the bosses you fight which you accumulate a lot of if you coop a lot, but...Online play. Even with the Steam release online play feel extremely limited almost to the point that online play is dead even with Cross-Play. Which makes farming weapons and armor from the factions really luck based and even then there are flaws I noticed rather quickly related to online play.First off is scaling. It doesn't feel like it was implemented properly or correctly and that could be based on a player's gear. I've joined games where basic enemies straight up one shot me and my guess is due to the gear and level disparity. This issue stands out because it can be seen as a problem in a very limited online population.Another issue is invader placement. In the first map there a spot where Invaders often spawn that basically can make them stuck simply because the player themselves haven't progressed enough yet. Meaning doors that are shut because the player hasn't opened yet means you are either stuck or have to find another route. The main problem is that the alternate route requires a grappling hook or jumping down a ledge and losing HP and for some reason I could not use my grappling hook. So RIP. So I listed the BAD things in Salt and Sacrifice and did play quite a bit of it so there must be something good right? Yes there are good things about the game. The combat itself is rather good when it wants to be. Many of the weapons have good movesets and I have just touched a bit on the magical side a bit and that's looking to be more hours I'll put into the game just to play around with.That alone is what makes the game good. If the devs could fix some of the issues it would be a solid game. Just tuning the bosses aggressive down alone would make a huge difference or giving players ways to farm seals for faction armor outside of online play would be a great benefit.And finally the game's base price is 20 dollars and right now on steam release being 10% off. I will say the price is worth it considering the amount of hours you can put it. I'm just putting it out there that the game itself does have potential, but due to some design choices. The game itself feels more unfair and frustrating if anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get misled by the art style, this is a very different experience from Sanctuary.First of all, I'm a huge fan of the previous game, over the years it has become one of my comfort games where I can easily sit down and enjoy going through the game once a year.Sacrifice is a much more focused, but at the same time un-focused, type of game. No interconnected levels (which could be a deal breaker for some) where you have a specific objective: Kill the Mages.These levels are not that complicated to explore but, whenever you return to the main hub of the game and want to go back to a previously explored level, the checkpoints are reset and you have to go through the whole level again. Since the exploration has been taken down by a notch I would have loved a handy map just to eliminate that sense of being lost every time you go back in some levels.Very nice additions to the combat system and to the traversal but the biggest downgrade comes from the enemy designs. This game was made to be played in Co-op, and it shows!Enemies usually are very tanky and most of the times they have some unfair and cheap attacks, like a very fast startup animation that goes instantly into an extremely fast grab which, of course, takes more than half of your health.When deciding if you want to buy this game, keep that in mind, you might need a friend to enjoy it at its fullest.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I kinda liked the good points of the game but absolutely HATED the bad ones.I bought and kept playing this game because I wanted a metroidvania so bad. Also the purchase had a discount so it was kinda worth it.The game has some okay highs and some ABYSSAL downs. I'll list some of them below:PROS:- The gameplay is very similar to salt and sanctuary but the builds are funnier to play and I tested a lot of them (Light armor is still terrible).- The game is short but if you take your time to look for and hunt the mages it can be quite a nice length.- Overall exploration was good.- Enemy variety was also good despite some repetitions here and there.CONS:- The Hub. The portal that takes you to other maps are SO FAR AWAY from the starting point. Why? You need to visit the hub everytime and EVERY SINGLE TIME YOU NEED TO RUN AROUND TO REACH THE PORTAL- Overall platforming. The platform movement in this game is terrible and the game has quite a lot of them.- FLYING F**KING ENEMIES. What's with those flying enemies that keep shooting you waaaay out of your reach and they also can fly through walls and even if you have projectiles (arrows, throwing axes etc) you STILL can't hit them if they want to hide behind a wall.- ENEMIES EDGE GUARDING. Sometimes the enemies will walk around and will choose to stay right at the edge of a platform that you want to climb. You have iframes in the edge grab animation but the enemies will start attacking as soon as you finish the animation. If you're able to try and jump over the edge, the enemy will still hit you and whatever hits you in the air COMPLETELY removes your momentum, so you fall straight down. It is even worse when a large enemy decides to edge camp you because in this case you're COMPLETELY unable to grab the edge or jump over. You need to wait for the enemy to leave the edge or kill them with a ranged weapon. The worst situation that happened to me was a mage in temple of embers that decided to edge camp a platform that you needed to use the grappling hook. There was no place to stay on so I could fire ranged weapons. I needed to constantly jump at him and use my melee attack only to fall and take 60% of my HP several times until the mage decided to teleport.- Enemies invading boss arenas. This one kinda explains itself.- Traps... just traps everywhere. Traps in this game are barely visible and they're simply everywhere. The damage that they deal gave me the impression that they're not designed to exactly kill you. Instead, their focus is to simply deal a considerable amount of damage and knock you off of a platform so you need to climb aaaaalll over again.- The mage system that is the core of the game. This is either love it or hate it because the mages are bosses that summon minions around the map and they keep teleporting around so you need to chase and kill them. The terrible thing is that they don't stay dead. They keep respawning even if you don't rest at the obelisks. Sometimes in the second map (Bol something) they even spawn exactly at the obelisk so you need to fight or avoid him right at the spawn point. And it's even worse when they decide to teleport near annoying enemies. The good news is that they'll fight each other but you still would need to wait for their fight to end or risk get ganked by all of them at once. Also it happened to me in one of the last maps (dragonsomething peak) that THREE mages spawned in the same area. It was a nightmare.- OST is just as lacking as salt and sanctuary but the first game at least had the still palace and nameless god ost which was kinda nice. This game doesn't have a single good song

_childDocuments_.review: For the first couple of hours, I wasn't entirely certain if I liked Salt and Sacrifice. Frustration after frustration mounted and I often felt like I was pushing my face against a wall to little progress. But then...I can't remember the exact moment I saw the cracks in the wall, worked my way into them and pulled it all tumbling down in front of me but I know it accompanied the sound of a clear thought in my head; "Wait, this isn't Dark Souls. It's Monster Hunter."I am now on a simultaneous NG+ playthrough and a separate brand new playthrough with the completely opposite build, 43 hours deep and one achievement from 100%. After that wall was long behind me, I found Salt and Sacrifice not to be the disappointment I had thought it was at the beginning but an enjoyable game with a great amount of fun you could often find for yourself.I dislike the moaning and groaning over reductionist takes on genre touchstones such as "Metroidvania" or "Soulslike." There's a reason we use these terms. In a limited time frame (such as a review on Steam with limited word counts) it conveys the necessary information so we can talk about more important things. If I tell you Salt and Sacrifice is a "2D soulslike" you know it has deliberate attack animations, difficult culminating boss battles, experience loss and recuperation, reusable healing flasks and so on; if I tell you it is also very much a "Monster Hunter-like" you know that you'll be hunting large enemies across the level, picking up their fallen bits and crafting new weapons and armor from them and sometimes you'll watch as they step into each other's territories and start fighting each other. The rest is the minutiae, the flavor of the game and how those pieces fit and move and the game's personal spin.Leveling importantly has numerous branches to follow that give you the ability to wield stronger weapons and magics you harvest off fallen Mages, and you will meet that same wall I referenced at the start if you stubbornly stick to one weapon type; the game desperately implores you to experiment and switch up your items all the time. If you put all your points into rapiers and the last rapier you made was ages ago, fire damage and had a weak weapon skill you're gonna run face first into that wall when the newest Mage you have to kill takes significantly less damage and stagger from fire weapons. I'll also say, personally, I find it a waste to not use a bunch of different weapons because the sheer variety of weapon skills, what they do and how they change your fighting strategies was a ton of fun. A favorite of mine was a hammer whose strong attack created a glowing blade and used the two-hand sword moveset which changed completely how I normally fought with a bludgeon.The story is reminiscent of normal "soulslike" storytelling, in mysterious subject matter with lots of vague terms and uncovering stuff as you go but I quite enjoyed it. It's not hard to follow (Mages bad, kill Mages), it's competently done and most importantly (and what I'd argue is more important in a game with Souls DNA) the world-building is very well thought-out and interesting. I am actually debating doing a lore-through video series. There's your surface plot and then a world bubbling under the surface that is hidden in skill and item descriptions, bestiary entries and dialogue. It's quite full and fleshed out.Unfortunately, I cannot comment on much more since review space is limited, but I'll sum up that the music was limited but good for the tone of the areas and game and I enjoyed the design of a lot of monsters and characters. There are so many good armor sets to play fashion with and monsters that I thought looked great. An important thing I will note is that there are a great number of different factions with different multiplayer goals so it is quite obvious the devs meant to have this game be played with heavy multiplayer involvement. Refer to the aformentioned Monster Hunter comparison where multiple people should be hunting Mages but also the Soulslike comparison in that some people might invade to kill you or maybe just steal your sweet sweet Haze juice.At the end of the day, I am extremely glad I played the game on it's terms and not the ones I wanted it to have.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this thinking the game will be somewhat disappointing based on the reception from other players. What I found instead was one of the most addictive metroidvania/action platformers I have played.Hunting mages with specific equipment in mind and finetuning the skilltree based on said equipment is a gameplay loop that kept me entertained for hours on end. The weapons themselves were also really fun, having unique weapon arts which are actually completely viable in all combat scenarios. Mage-hunting and platforming up till the specific boss encounters got enough enjoyment out of me and never overstayed its welcome, even after grinding several mages over and over. With some minor traversal and gravity-related nitpicks, I would still recommend this game. The only real shame lies in several equipment pieces being locked into covenant rewards and with the online participation being as dead as it is, they were unobtainable.Much like its predecessor, the game did not disappoint. _childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of Salt & Sanctuary (but not such a huge fan of splitting my game collection) I was waiting for what seemed like forever for this to come to Steam - and fans of the first game will be happy to know it doesn't disappoint.The hand-drawn graphical style is as sharp as ever and the enemies are fresh and new and not just retreads or skins of ones from the first game (for the most part....but spoilers so I won't elaborate).Combat feels good, but it has one downfall: it can get very frustrating being stagger-locked by 2 or 3 small, nearly trivial enemies at once and dying before you can get out to counterattack.The crafting system is robust and plentiful, with new items, and elemental tiers to craft opening up after you defeat certain Mages. Mage-farming is a bit odd, and sometimes when going back to farm one, it will blink to an area you can't access, which, I have to say, is also a bit frustrating, but it's usually a quick task to port back to camp and reset it for a better outcome.The music is fantastic and really lends itself to establishing the overall atmosphere of the game.The one major problem with the game is lack of much tutorial information. Most features and tasks are just mentioned once by an NPC and then it's up to you to figure out exactly how they work or where to go next, et. al., which is kind of a bother since there's more systems in Sacrifice than there were in Sanctuary. Luckily, since the game has been on Epic for over a year, there's already an established wiki and plenty of walkthroughs to get you up and on your feet.Overall, this is a great game and I'm having a really fun time playing through it. If you're fan of 2D Soulsborne games, this is hands down the best series of them out there and I highly recommend it. Overall I would give it a 9/10, but of course ymmv.I hope this review is helpful to anyone looking to dive into this franchise - or worried the sequel doesn't live up to the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this while currently replaying the game for a 3rd time, after a year of the game having been out or so, and getting it on steam after initially having it on Epic.to be clear: I never had an issue personally with Ska taking epic's money, I fully support the decision, money is being given to a team I like a lot.butThis is a game I feel nothing but contempt for.I loved the designs, art direction, and vibe of Salt & Sanctuary, ever since I played it on the xbox as a kid.I loved charlie & I loved vampire smile, primarily for the art, the style just felt so at home to me.This game feels like it was made by a completely different artist, not just one that'd grown up, but one that'd changed fundamentally. From the colors, to the design of the enemies, even the bosses; everything feels- IS weaker.I feel there are so many changes made in Sacrifice that almost come across as a slap to the face for someone that loved what made Sanctuary unique compared to other 2d metroidvania souls-likes. I can't even begin to understand why some changes were made at all. One that immediately stood out to me was the removal of parrying, in favor of perfect blocking, a much stingier and far less rewarding option. Parrying gave you a since of earned empowerment, a skill you'd hone with each enemy you fight, tagged with the reward of a finisher that gave you a massive lead in damage; this felt good. Perfect blocking, a significantly more time consuming and riskier option, would never be able to compete due to it's requirement being all the more demanding. Is there any reason this change needed to happen? All it's resulted in is some enemies, very few albeit, feeling mind numbing to fight due to their low attack cooldown. I suppose I could spend more time learning the perfect block timings on some of these enemies, but grueling through learning the timings and the amount of times I'd need to perfect block, just to do the damage I'd do in 2 hits anyways, is a little ridiculous? I felt similarly about elden rings approach to parrying, with the introduction of some bosses requiring multiple parries, albeit with that instance you are granted a moment to retaliate inbetween micro-parries.I feel I could tangent on about the removal of parries for a while, I guess I just liked the feeling it gave a lot and miss it's existence in this game. Another issue I take with the game is it's bosses, not mages, the bosses you fight in every area (like 2 every area...?) which have no reward to speak of. I remember first fighting the spider with the glaive in the desert, and thinking I'd get her glaive that has red lightning infused magic and play around with it, only to beat her and be rewarded with nothing but a single upgrade material I didn't even need. Not a single boss in this game, not including the first boss you fight in the lake, has any kind of gear to be rewarded to the player? Also, that first boss in the lake, a significant downgrade to the sodden knight. On the topic of boss design, all of them are incredibly weak and seemingly thoughtless in their design it feels. Maybe it's meant to capture a specific mythological aesthetic, but it had gone over my head throughout my time with the game. Almost every boss in Sanctuary, for me, was incredibly memorable and fun to fight, even if not all of them had a reward to speak of. Their designs carried the experience and made the fights all worth it,  yet in Sacrifice it feels as if several bosses lack any kind of strong, imposing detail to them that makes them either memorable or interesting. Especially the final boss. The final boss, felt very heavily like it was a knock off version of the first games final boss, with a significantly worse design, worse music, and no where NEAR as amazing a set-up as the first games. Walking through the upside down salt city to the final boss in Sanctuary felt incredible, it felt like I'd entered a palace of impossibility, sending all sorts of feelings up and down my body when I'd first reached it. I loved this moment with the first game, this final moment. I can hardly remember the final bosses design, let alone the introduction to them, as I recall it feeling abrupt and out of the blue, like I'd just been dropped into the final bosses room while still thinking I was only going through another normal area with nothing special to it. This was beyond disappointing after all this time.I just hopped in a call with my friend to play divinity OS2, and I can't bring myself to care to finish writing this.I love Ska and their work, but this is a stain in my eyes that I'd rather forget about. It makes me happy to see them still updating Sanctuary after all this time, adding new features to it, and I can only hope this game will continue to receive updates, maybe even some massive changes brought in that bring the combat and feel of the game closer to the first some day? That's a bit of a pipe dream. Please keep working on new things Ska and don't let this game be the last one. I believe in your team still, I know you have it in you.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great so far. Let me address the concerns for someone whose been playing 5 hours straight.1) Roaming bosses. Bosses will move around the map, but they'll only move to places that you've been. This isn't an issue, you can rest between chasing the bosses until you hit the point where it turns into an actual boss battle. This phase is actually pretty great as it drops the loot you need and another item that brings us to the next point. The only issue I've seen is when people want to farm said boss and it'll appear literally anywhere. I've come to just respect that it'll show up eventually, and really. They do, I'm not stressing.2) Health being taken when you die. At first this may be a stressing mechanic, but the enemies you fight as you chase the boss will drop these items enmass. I have 30 of them already and it's not going down by one bit. I'm not even worried about the mechanic anymore, I just die. Pop the item and continue.3) Limited amount of range option. That's fine honestly. Some people expect going into this game and corner warming with ranged weapons. I kind of do it against enemies I struggle to fight, but it's fine really. You'll obtain items that increase the amount of ammo you get.4) Flask / Ammo needing items. It does, but every enemy drops these same items and every corner these same items are gatherable. I have up to 300 of each item in my inventory already. This mechanic might as well have not been in the game. It's really funny.Really play the game yourself and see if it's for you. _childDocuments_.review: Great game, but Salt and Sanctuary is still better. The mage hunts and everything is fun, but I think the Demon Souls-esque hub isn't really my thing. Jumping into different worlds from the hub has always made the game feel more disjointed and like each area is a separate world. _childDocuments_.review: This review is in the experience of 2 player co-op. My friend and I beat the game together start to finish:Pros: Large amount of shortcuts most leading to the start of a map. Can revive each other if you or your companion have used a guiltless shard. The first half of the game's level design is fantastic. The skill tree layout is improved over the first game. Getting +1max hp every level up makes you feel like you are getting stronger every level. They got rid of the cancerous fatigue system.Cons: Players can NOT trade items. (if you did it to stop "twinking" then just make it so you can trade items if they were obtained while in a party) Unbearably tanky enemies with blue glowing eyes keep re-spawning whenever you look away. (and they drop blue pick ups that have a 1 sec uncancelable animation to loot 1-5 silver) Stat gain from leveling is very bad. (1 point in vitality gives you 2 max hp. 1 stat in endurance give you 1 carry weight)You have to invest 50 levels into endurance a necklace slot and a ring slot that increase carry weight just to wear a full set of heavy armor(not the heaviest armor ether) and mid roll(yellow back pack icon). Poise is a one sided lie. (trash mobs stun-lock you with every trike even if you are wearing a full set of heavy armor and have artifacts that increase max poise. While half of the enemies in the game ignore a great hammer bashing their skulls in like its a fresh breeze) Second half of the game have very sadistic level design. (multiple jumps of breaking platforms with interchanging jump distances with traps that will kill you at the beginning, middle and or end of the platforms along with enemies shooting at you to hit you mid-air and make you fall to your death to make you do it all over again) Blocking is a one sided lie. You lose your entire stamina bar for blocking(except perfect blocking) one attack from a boss while enemies can block from both sides indefinitely. Some weapons are LEAGUES stronger then most so there is very little actual choice. Mage hunting is ... annoying to say the least. Instead of making them near immortal while chasing them and making them have a balloon that's easy to pop of heath when the fight actually begins. I would recommend you just have them teleport to a battle arena on their second teleport(instead of chasing them for up to 11 teleport) and give them some more health or just straight up make them re-summonable by a totem in their arena and remove the entire chasing mechanic in general. (and yes I know about the "boss rush" in one of the optional maps. It gives you basically no items so its a waste of time) De-sync is a huge problem. (Both me and my friend have good internet and have low ping between each other yet it kept disconnecting us during boss fights causing us both to be teleported back to base and making us have to chase the mage again)It's not a bad game. But I would recommend Salt and Sanctuary over this.TL:DR:Armor is poop.Most weapons bad.No trade with friend.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is only worth it if you have a coop buddy or two to get one playthrough with. Aside from that there are ideas here that don't play nice with souls-like gameplay/balancing.It's fine and all getting juggled around by 2+ mages spam spawning adds for the first ~2/3rds of your NG playthough. But once you get to NG end game and dare venture into NG+ you realize how the balance and "fairness" goes out the window.Between the low soft caps and harsh penalties on increases afterwards, or defensive stats strictly being tied to your armor. If you aren't capable of abusing i-frames, you're going to have a bad time.Hopefully the game receives an "enhanced edition" balancing patch at some point like Salt and Sanctuary did to smooth out all the rough edges. Because in principal there's a good game underneath all of it, it's just poorly balanced and has a few annoyances that could be resolved. But given at the time of this review the game has not received an update in 4 months, I'd say it's unfortunately considered content complete by ska studios.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a very mixed bag. For every cool thing it does it does something equally bad.For every cool weapon moveset like rapiers or vanguard weapons, you get something terrible feeling for its weight like maces or glaives.For every cool bit of level design like the first area or Corivus mire, you get some borderline evil level design like the outdoor section of the temple of Eleven or The Twin Giants where enemies will knock you to your death constantly.For every cool mage like Hydromancers with their interesting moveset and attacks or Lumenmancers with their cool light aesthetic and good but not broken zoning moves, you get some real crap designs like Diablomancers and Electromancers with their absurd damage and odd movesets, or Neuromancers and Aeromancers with their absurd knockback and most common environments being areas full of insta-death ledges and similar pitfalls.Like, I want to love the game, but there's so many questionable decisions even beyond this and annoying encounters that I just can't recommend it. The back-and-forth and whiplash is real and it makes me dislike the game. That's not even to get into issues like how sparse the multiplayer is so you have to do absurd grinds for any of the cool faction rewards, especially the 50 token rewards. Or other things like how the silver economy is completely broken and renders the currency useless past super early game. This game does have these building blocks of some cool things though, especially the multiplayer with cool things like the blueheart runners and general functions when it DOES work. So I am not swearing these devs off because of this, and I want to see them do good and continue to make experimental works in the future, but this game just, wasn't it. The whole epic games deal didn't help either, putting greed before one's own legacy and all that. A lot of people still don't even know this game exists because of how much of a publicity and good-will-blackhole EGS is. In the end. It's a mixed bag. if you're willing to sift through the bad parts to get the gold, or just really REALLY want a 2D monster hunter like, this exists. Otherwise, don't get it, and I personally didn't enjoy it enough to recommend it to others outright, even if I did like a good half of it.Here's my build I finished the game with, as a show I genuinely interacted with the game's systems and am not just whining out of some sort of "skill issue" or related factor.

_childDocuments_.review: Up front, Salt and Sacrifice is NOT Salt and Sanctuary, despite what the store page, aesthetic and game feel may say because the game design is very different. While it wasn't really what I expected, even knowing it was a departure from Sanctuary, it's still a solid title if you are willing to meet it where it is... but some of those things you need to meet it on might be deal breakers.The game design is entirely different than how I remember Salt and Sanctuary, and I wasn't enamored with how Sacrifice does things. Instead of having one big sprawling world to explore you get a hub to go to one of ~5 maps. It's a shame then that the hub area that was specifically crafted to be your town is a nuisance to navigate and the portal out of it is annoyingly far from the leveling statue and where the game puts you in the hub after teleporting there. Instead of exploring and hitting new bosses being the primary gameplay loop like Sanctuary, the core progression is tied to "Mage Hunts" which weren't my favorite design choice. You'll come across something on the map to get the option to hunt a Mage and once you accept it you are now in a worse version of the map where there are enemies that keep spawning in that are associated with the Mages, you just cleared your way here? Well it's not clear anymore and nothing will be until the Mage is dead. Once you take down the Mage you can make gear from their drops... which means if you want to swap your armor set or get upgrade materials you are going to need to grind out "nameless" or "fated" versions of that same Mage, which are much more annoying to initiate. This Mage grind system is likely why I had heard the game be compared to Monster Hunster, which isn't a bad comparison complete with turf wars of sorts. The Mages do not get along with each other or the normal map monsters and in my experience mages will frequently end up in the same area which makes things a hit hectic. I think there is something to be said for trying out different designs, I'm pretty sure the maps here have more shortcuts than Sanctuary (I also haven't played that game for a while, so I could be wrong) and I could see them focusing on making self-contained areas enabling those kinds of choices. I don't think beating up enemies to craft gear is a bad idea at all, but I did find aspects of the Mage hunts to be an annoyance (especially when I started falling behind on gear) such as the constantly respawning enemies, and having those enemies even kill me at a respawn point when I had put my controller down to get a drink after dying to a Mage causing me to lose all of that salt. In my limited experience and research it does seem like Salt and Sacrifice is better balanced than Sanctuary was with no weapon type being outright bad here. Ultimately, I had some fun with Sacrifice but I wouldn't say it quite has the same Metroidvania feel or as much of a sense of exploration and mystery due to the map design differences, but the core combat is solid and once you understand what the game is, it's a good game that just isn't what a lot of people really wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Salt and Sanctuary. I beat the game twice and loved the art style and weapon variety. This game does not live up to the first one at all.There are so many major inconveniences and annoyances. For example, the game doesn't show you your class' starting stats. Why? The first game didn't show it either but at least it tells you the name of the starting item you select. Salt and Sacrifice does not. It tries to be quirky for the sake of being quirky and makes you choose a starting "crime" which influences your starting item. But you can't even hover over it or select it to see what the item even is. On that topic, Salt and Sacrifice doesn't tell you anything, just for the sake of being mysterious. Because it doesn't tell you your starting stats for a class, I had to start the game, then check what my stats are. Then I wanted to compare the stats to another class so I had to exit to the main menu and start a new save with another class to see their stats. There is no reason to withhold this information from the player, especially if they're gonna see these stats in literally a few seconds anyway. This is just one example, and this alone is enough to make players need to open up a wiki. You lose the sense of mystery you are trying to create if you withhold absolutely everything from the player because then it just becomes tedious and they'll have to resort to using a wiki.Some other annoyances in my limited playthrough:- You have to teleport all the way back to the hub area and walk up a non-trivial amount of steps to access your skill tree. In the first game you could do it from any checkpoint. Why do I have to fast travel to the camp to check my skill tree?- Skipping the opening cinematic skips the tutorial and the first boss (that you are supposed to die to, but still. If you are on a second playthrough and have already seen the cutscene but have the skills to take on the boss, you'd have to sit through the cutscene)- To use ranged weapons with a controller, you need to do some yoga with your fingers. You first hold the left bumper, aim with the thumbstick (do not let go of it or it will reset the aim to in front of you), and then press the X button. I don't understand this decision. Your hand is in such an awkward position that attempting to press the X button will cause the thumbstick to wiggle a bit and throw off your aim. Like, why can't it instead just be the right trigger to fire? You're already holding the left bumper so the game knows you're trying to aim, so it won't confuse it for you trying to dodge roll (also mapped to right trigger).- Massive lore dump at the start and huge hub area with locked doors and unclear paths everywhere, as opposed to the first games linear focused start and better interconnected world- The tutorial pop ups only show up when standing on a very tiny spot. If you move just a few steps they will disappear until you step back on the area. The problem is there are enemies here running towards you to attack you so you will be trying to fight them off instead of being able to read the popup- In fullscreen mode, if you tab out of the game (which you will do often to check guides because the game doesn't explain anything), theres a high chance it will bug out and not let you open the game. You'll have to force close it. In borderless, when you tab out of the game, if starts to flicker white really fast. 1000 flashbangs a second.I was really looking forward to this game. I waited for the Steam release because the EGS deal was a huge red flag and I wanted a platform with a better refund policy.

_childDocuments_.review: Salt and Sanctuary is one of my all time favorite games.Salt and Sacrifice is not a bad game, but compared to Sanctuary, it is a complete downgrade with some really weird design choices. - Enemies and bosses have some spammy juggling attacks that could kill you once you get hit- chasing mages throughout the map is tedious, boring and downright stupid idea.- the game is divided into 5 separated main areas, i prefer an interconnected world like the original.+ the movement here seems better and more fluid than the original+ graphics are better than the original.+ the world is still filled with lots of secrets to find.overall i really enjoyed the game, as long as you don't compare it to the original, you will find a lot to enjoy in this one. i really don't understand why the Devs decided to ruin a winning formula, the game could have been much much better. despite the issues, i would still recommend this game to the people who liked the original.

_childDocuments_.review: What in the Nameless God's name happened here? How did we move from an amazing game to this godless abomination? - equipment system was reworked, for the worse, main weapon and side weapon are now tied into one thing, for some reason, you cannot double hand nor equip shield as necessary, you have to make do with the pre-made combos; - world building was reworked, for the worse, there is no more "world", now we have a central hub from which we teleport to the locations, and those locations are completely separated from one another, unlike, say, Dark Souls 3; - enemies are now dirt cheap, there is no point in learning anything, it's best to just power through everything with reckless abandon, if you're dying too much, just grind levels and power through; - speaking of world building again, there is no organic roadblock anymore (a gap that needs double jump, for instance), they have made literal doors with "kill this many enemies first" message, and I cannot fathom anything cheaper than this, it's ridiculous; - checkpoint system was reworked, for the worse, now you no longer have access to sanctuaries to ressuply, upgrade, do quests, no, now you have totems and everything is done in the central hub, and ressuplying was reworked too, now you need a specific item to ressuply heals, so it's perfectly possible, and easy even, to completely run out of healing, which I don't know if I should laugh or cry about, and even better, you don't have access to teleport between totems, and ressuplying is done manualy instead of automatic like previous game; - storytelling was reworked, instead of organic learning via reading in-game descriptions and piecing together the story through NPC's quest, enemy name, locations and whatnot, now we have a billion NPCs that vomit exposition as needed, lovely; Not all is lost, though... - leveling and item buying are still the same; - art style and overall presentation are still the same; - combat stream and momentum are still the same, despite the disgusting equipment system and cheap enemies; But I don't know if that alone can salvage this mess... The game overall is not the end of the world, it's still somewhat fun, albeit with very annoying changes, so if you can stomach the new disgusting equipment system and the insane cheapness of the enemies, it's worth a 60% sale. 5.5/10 - don't buy it unless you are starved for a soulslike-platforming game and is absolutely bored of Salt and Sanctuary, otherwise just buy Salt and Sanctuary instead or wait for a big sale, at least 50%. As a final note, I hope Sweeney's money was worth it, because between EGS's terrible sales and game sub-mediocrity delivery, the sales won't save this tragedy of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get one thing out of the way first, if you loved salt and sanctuary you might not like this game since it is more akin to monster hunter when it comes to progression and game-play.Though with that being said the game feels and plays really really good, I can't really put it into words other than it just feels good. If you ever played dark souls we have all had that moment where it just felt like we shouldn't have been hit and it just feels frustrating despite you knowing that it was your fault however I have never felt that not even once while I was learning the game.I wish I had a better way to explain it but it just feels good. I really love being able to fight bosses that I have already killed again, I also really love being able to get unique relics with different stat buffs and unless you are trying to midmax it is just a really nice little boost to your build.I can't really think of anything bad to say other than it can be annoying to try and hunt down the mage you are looking for when it just won't spawn in. Though that would be an issue if the game-play wasn't so fun.So I guess to end this take what I said with a grain of salt since I think what I said has been very opinionated though if you like dark souls and don't mind it being 2D and the same with monster hunter then I can't see why you wouldn't enjoy this game.Edit: The game is still something I really enjoy but god is it stupid difficult in the later worlds and can totally see why people would still not enjoy this game. So one other thing that I want to add on to this review is that this game will require a lot of patience and determination to not give up from frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I *expected* to like this game but despite pushing through my initial dislike, I honestly grew to hate it. Everything about this game seems hostile to your enjoyment. So much so that I started to question if I was misremembering how much I enjoyed the first game. The level design is terrible. The combat is simplistic and bland. The levelling structure is weird and unsatisfying. The weapons are boring. The bosses are samey and limited in design. The main gameplay loop of chasing down said bosses as they teleport around the level is just a huge chore. The knockback and juggling on hit is such a bizarre instance of game design, it all just leaves me scratching my head. Poise of enemies seemed inconsistent and unpredictable and stamina was tuned in a way that killed the pace of fights. Maybe I could've steered my build in a way to mitigate these annoyances but honestly, the game didn't give me enough to ever care to try.I'm fine with trying something new but not if it sucks every last drop of fun out of the game. What a disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love Salt and Sanctuary, it handled that translation of Dark Souls into 2D really well, had satisfying progression, thick atmosphere, and interesting lore.This?  I don't even know.  This isn't Salt and Sanctuary 2 like I hoped, this is... nothing.  I don't know how else to better put it.  It's vapid.  Shallow.  Unremarkable.  It has none of the qualities which made the original exceptional, to the extent that I really don't know why this exists at all.The areas are uninspired, and too big for how little they offer.The enemies uninteresting, and bosses especially a huge disappointment.You're spoon fed lore and important terms by about a half dozen NPCs in the first hour which really takes away any of the setting's mystique.  I really had no interest in what was going on around me, unlike in the first game.  The mystery isn't engaging and everything just blends together to be really basic dark fantasy.Suffice it to say, my disappointment is immeasurable, and my day is ruined.Do NOT buy this game, it's a waste of your money.  Buy Salt and Sanctuary.  If you already have it, buy it for a friend.Do NOT play this game, it's a waste of your time.  Just play, or replay the original.  Or any other game which has more substance than this.A very tragic title.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a downgrade from Salt & Sanctuary. I understand trying to spice the formula by meshing mechanics from other games (Monster Hunter) but you can't just add things willy nilly.- The mages you hunt is basically the same with a different coat of paint;- The other bosses are all forgettable with simplistic moveset;- Bosses are simplistic, but they don't have stamina and spam the sh** out of their AoE high damaging attacks;- So, bosses spam attacks, your dodge consumes a lot of stamina and, the cherry on top, dodge covers a lot of ground, positioning you far from the boss so you can hit once, maybe twice before the boss start another attack;- 90% of the attacks will send you flying or juggle you for potential combos, Tekken style;- There's no map, which is not bad by itself, but when you need to chase mages around, it gets really tedious;- Since you have to chase mages around, you still have to deal with trash mobs that can still kill you easily;- Exploration is gutted, making the gear you use behind grinding mages materials;- Grappling hook is very inconsistent. Don't know if it's my controller, but I fell to my death so much from this because the hook flashed for 1s and it didn't register the input. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: Heavy Armor's good now, Hazeburnt just means grinding sucks a little more. Map's still confusing, but otherwise I'd actually recommend it now.It's good at a basic level, but dragged down by so many abstract gameplay decisions that turn trying to play it into a struggle as the game itself punches you in the balls with incredibly abstract, Lynchian mechanical ideas that didn't even really need to divert from the original as hard as it does. I don't have a problem with the basic ideas or the gameplay loop, but the game really throws the baby out down the stairs while drinking the bath water. Losing health permanently until you use a humanity equivalent is just blatantly outdated, even at this game's first release. There's no benefit to the system besides to arbitrarily twist your ♥♥♥♥. Enemy attack patterns are obfuscated, speed blitz nightmare fests where they just wildly flail at you until you die. Even more so for most bosses who have so little space between attacks that all hit like 67% of the screen that it's a hit trade simulator until somebody dies. Heavy armor, ooh boy. It's a slog, with how capacity upgrades in the skill tree only increase your weight by ONE (1) point, which isn't nearly enough to actually wear anything worthwhile without spending hours grinding out one stat. Poise is a joke, the smallest whiff of a gnarly fart will tekken floorbounce you like a bronze Xiaoyu main getting your ♥♥♥♥ rocked by a nolife Geese Howard, regardless of how big your armor is. There's literally no reason to wear anything bigger than a paper plate duct taped to party city chainmail, you'll just die anyway. The game wants to encourage blocking, but the block cost is like actually all of your stamina if you block a lethargic overhead. It's an unintuitive, unimpressive, unengaging playstyle to even attempt. And the map design is annoying with no minimap or overall map, I couldn't imagine flagellating myself with this game's level design at launch before fast travel. Only buy if you're so hungry for something like Sanctuary that you'll literally eat trash shaped like the Sodden Knight.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bad sequel…it’s just a downgrade in comparison with the first game in every way!The areas are huge and there’s NO MAP! _childDocuments_.review: All the worst BS of Sanctuary here is core gameplay, now with added salt.- One shots- HP sponges- Inflated damage- Unavoidable AOEs, stuns, grabs, and chains of stuns /grabs- Unavoidable spamming of AOEs, stuns, grabs, and chains of stuns /grabs- Unavoidable juggles and spamming of juggles (even in heavy sets)- Chained juggling/ grabs/ stuns/ AOEs + all of the above and below resulting in unavoidable death- Mages spamming unavoidable spells / AOEs- Mobs and Mages spamming juggles- Mobs and Mages spamming stuns- Mages spamming summons that prevent damage- Said summons being covered by the now immortal mage- Running around in slow mo trying to chase said summons while all of the above and below goes on- Enemies jumping 3/4 of the screen- Enemies jumping 3/4 of the screen through solid walls- Enemies floating / flying all over the screen and attacking you through solid walls (for real)- Enemies now being invisible because they are floating / flying through "black" solid walls, all the while attacking you with spells or melee, while all of the above and below goes on- Bonus: Enemies can juggle you through rolls and walls- Enemies have infinite stamina and projectiles/ fp- Enemies stuns, grabs, and juggles have no cooldown - Enemies stuns, grabs, and juggles can be chained by single enemies or groups- Enemies can block 100% of damage (minus 2 statuses that deal low damage over time)- Enemies will chase you across the whole map if they can pathfind a way, and chase you over other aggressors- A bat bites you for 1/4 of your HP at level 55 and wearing a full heavy set (like, wtf)- Your character moves like underwater, and the world is on speed (regardless of weight)- Clunky controls: you try to "jump down" to get on a lower platform, but you jump up, possibly into a trap...GG- Drinking a potion takes way too long for way too little gains + sitting duck syndrome- Your auto-targeting abilities can and will prioritise the mob half a screen away / entirely out of screen rather than the boss mauling your pretty face off- Rolling has both less frames and range than incoming attacks / chains of attacks, do your math- Enemies that guard ledges and hit you as you try to land/ grab on them so you fall to unavoidable death- Enemies that teleport you into burning chairs that deal high damage (as the hanging men is the older game, but worse due to mob gank squads)- You cannot "aim" at an enemy, the first one in line on a 2D plane gets the bullet- Later weapons (tier 3+) may have way worse skills than early/ mid-game variations, i.e. projectiles that will very rarely hit an enemy and for insignificant damage- This is especially bad considering the whole game is based on heavy grinding, and it fails to reward the player for the time invested- Heavy weapons force you to trade in a game where trading hits is a one-way ticket to stunlock-landia and reload-screen-o-landia- A number of cheats for enemies and limitations that are only applicable to the player- Dead PVE / PVP in a game -poorly- balanced around multiplayer (i.e. aggro management and pal revives)- Chasing mages through multiple sections of trap-filled, ganking-mobs infested, and bad platforming-heavy levels gets very old very fast; especially when each of these can and will one-shot you one way or the other + all of the above goes on, resulting in unavoidable death- So much deaf and relentless obnoxiousness that you won't stop playing for any other reason that you just don't care, you are not having fun, and you would rather do anything else, including the dishesThe Tireless Exalted and afterwards is one shot galore. Witch of the lake style. Finished Sanctuary and still enjoy it after 50+ hours. Here, I stopped having fun in 15 already.It's like they won't listen the community no matter what.Do you know the term "bait and switch"? You get five, maybe ten decent hours, then player trolling without irony.Quite possibly the worst experience I had in 30+ years of gaming (and I am a Souls enthusiast). It's not that the game is just "hard" (although all of the above doesn't make it easy); it's that is pure tedium and BS unending.It's a game where RNG is left unchecked, no cooldowns, no logic, so, rather than learning, you are getting either more or less lucky (oh, I got juggled/ grabbed through a roll/ one-shotted/ thrown to unavoidable death, ok, maybe next time I won't).I would like SKA to fix it, but you can't fix stupid and I cannot find another cause for the shameless mess I am putting up with.Since I bought it, I may as well try to power through and update my review; but you please learn from it.

_childDocuments_.review: I accidentally started this game instead of Sanctuary so I think oh well, might as well finish it. It was kinda weird at first, dark souls 1 combat with MonHun gameplay loop and dark souls 3 / Elden Ring endgame enemy aggression doesn't mix well, still don't at the end, it had some charms with the combat but that's about it, there's nothing else to "praise". _childDocuments_.review: 22 hours in now and pretty much everything about this game feels great! The only thing I've noticed is a little bit of a lack of non-boss enemy variety in some places.... people are mostly concerned about Mages being the only thing you fight though... Nah, those are recurring bosses you hunt down for items and story progression throughout the course of the game, THEY ARE NOT THE ONLY BOSS ENEMIES IN THE GAME THOUGH.  There's still plenty of unique non-boss enemies to encounter too, like these freaks that run at you on all fours if you get too far away from them, they'll pin you down if they catch you and repeatedly stab you.  All in all... I'm quite pleased by the gameplay, enemies, and all the hidden goodies I've been finding while exploring, I even fought some optional non-mage bosses last night that gave me a pretty good whipping before I beat them.  But yeah...  I think alot of the hate may come from people who are upset that whatever cheesy tactic they used in the first game doesn't work in this one. That or they go in already poisoned by the toxic "this game sucks" sheeple mindset and only play the first area a bit--maybe a little bit of the second--see everything in a negative light, and proceed to parrot what they heard to everyone else. STOP DOING THAT!!  Another complaint I see is that the multiplayer community is too small or inactive... hilariously/sadly enough these complaints oftentime come from the same people who dump on the game and say how bad it is. No... If you want more players then stop telling everyone the game is bad. ESPECIALLY if you're still trying to play it.     On that note, I would like to mention the pretty cool multiplayer options the game has, I've done a little bit of each so far and I can say I'm pleased with it.> First off you have the classic Salt option: Co-op. Great experience! Vastly improved from the first game in that both players can get unique loot and progress their stories, special NPCs won't dismissively one-line you and not give you the pleasure of a full conversation. You can't invade or join other players' worlds in co-op mode, but you can still be invaded or joined yourself. Pretty cool.> Next I'd like to mention the very souls-like "aid another player" and "ask for aid" options, they work great! You got candle things you can light when you are seeking to help somebody or looking for help and its pretty smooth sailing so long as whoever you connect to doesn't have a potato for a modem. There's also gestures available too! These are great, I always do a handshake and or a wave to somebody when I see them.> Then you got the other souls-like "hunt a player" option. Same thing pretty much, you can light a candle saying you are seeking a challenger, or you can drop a cursed page to look for someone to invade. You meet, you fight, someone emerges victorious, bam.> The last one is a very interesting one and probably my favorite: you have the runners and the sheriffs... Basically a game of cops and robbers; Runners invade other players' worlds to steal salt (exp) from the special enemies that spawn during mage hunts, in doing so they spawn dangerous enemies that attack the host player. Gather 9 times or kill the host and you win! If the mage hunt finishes before you do so however, you fail your mission.   The sheriff players on the other hand are dedicated to entering worlds being pillaged by runners to hunt them down. Kill the runner to win!> It is also worth noting that when you are in another player's world you have an indicator that regularly goes off that will show you the direction of your objective. If you're helping or trying to kill a player, the indicator shows you the direction of the host. If you're running, it will show you the direction of the sheriff, and the sheriff's indicator shows you the direction of the runner.I definitely recommend this game to anybody who is a fan of the original and soulslike games in general. Its a shame the game released on Epic first... But now that its here on Steam it finally feels like its where it belongs. I look forward to an eventual third installment of the series if the hackjobs don't ruin its rep.

_childDocuments_.review: Since the epic games launch this game has substantially improved in a lot but it still suffers from an identity crisis. It's a fusion of a Souls like and a Monster hunter like title ; in itself thats not the worst thing, but while trying to do both things equally it makes for an obtuse experience.Mages attack patterns seem wildly inconsistent with very high damage and knockback attached where even the toughest armor still sees you losing half your health to something the mage easily filled the screen with and is still doing. Due to the gameplay loop being following mages across awkwardly small and perilous stages until you arrive at a small arena to be quickly filled with attacks , projectiles, roll catches-you name it. All mages feel about the same with little variety, which is a shame and a let down from both angles of souls like and MH-like.Chase sequence take you through Souls-like maps which means filled with traps, lethal falls and high damage mobs; in later areas some mages will run away past a jump puzzle and once you reach it; it will run away back through it. When youre not dealing with hunting a mage, the maps themselves are decent the only issue with them is due to the comically strong knock back a lot of things have , youre often having to do that climb you just did all over again.Oddly enough the most well designed fights that make for the better experience are not the mages, but the other non mage bosses such as the dragon. Having a dedicated stage thats spacious or having attack patterns that are telegraphed and have space between themselves to breath makes for a fun experience- who wouldve guessed.Edit-The Final boss did play a different track this time? I had gone back to help a friend for the other ending and this time it wasnt the default mage theme. Probably a bug; leaving that bit in just incase someone else runs into itMusic is practically nonexistent ; Mages have 1 shared track which the final boss also uses.. Other bosses also have one shared track, most of the time you spend your time in awkward silence or very faint ambiance. Exceptions are the final map and a section of the new one they added in do have dedicated tracks but its strange seeing such a drastic drop in variety from the maker of Dishwasher series or Charlie murder. Its understandable wanting a more unsettling ambiance focused track for the tone and setting of the game- Monster Hunter World did not have constant tracks playing for every map for example; but that did have different battle themes for each map for small and big enemies alike- as well as a short intro theme for day and night- i had wished something similar was implemented as a break away from the unnerving silence.I want to love this game, SKA and specifically James Silva has made my favorite games and favorite sound tracks , and maybe this didnt have to be Salt and Sanctuary 2 or even similar; its own thing as he clearly wanted it to be- but i do wish It leaned more in one direction or the other. Trying to do both as is just doesnt work for me; unfortunate as i love both genres but i cant recommend it. Do try SKAs other games though its predecessor Salt and Sanctuary i cannot recommend enough, and Dishwasher vampire smile has a killer sound track.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second all-time dislike review... so you may understand the importance to me to write this.I loved the first game, and bought this one hands-down with not a single doubt. And... man, why is this game WAY worse than the first one? I loved the combat in the first one. In this one it feels slow and clunky. Why having a 3-attack combo when ALL enemies will straight attack you back after the second one? Only some enemies are staggered when attacked, but for the rest is just a matter of attacking once - rolling to the other slide- attacking once - rolling to the other side. If you dare to try to combo twice.. you will get damaged. Why don't make the enemies cooldown after attacks longer (or their animations), so you can dodge their attacks and give them hell back for a while when you see an opening. These enemies have NO openings. They just SPAM the attacks one after the other.  It is SO easily solvable: have an internal CD between attacks, or make the end of the attack animations much longer so you can use that moment to attack.Bosses are spamming all the time and are not fair. The bubble mage would spawn bubbles all over the place and you have no place to hide: if you stay on your toes you will be hit, but if you roll, you will end up on another's bubble landing zone. I cannot stressed more how many times I have rolled out of an attack just to end up on another attack's zone. ALL-THE-TIME. So the game should only be based on blocking-attacking, and only dodging to position. But if I block with my weapon I get damaged nonetheless, so it is counter-intuitive to do that.I really loved the first one, but I have stopped playing Salt and Sacrifice after 3 hours. And I am really, really bummed to do that. I wanted to finish the game, but I don't enjoy it.
