_childDocuments_.review: If you're an R-Type fan or shmup fan this is a must have.  It's basically exceeded my expectations in almost every way and I just can't put it down.  It's not a game for the faint of heart or for those easily frustrated.  This game will tear you apart but it's so rewarding to find a path forward and to find solutions as it's a shmup but each screen almost plays more like a puzzle that can only be passed with the tools available to you.I haven't played a shmup in years and it took me about 12 hours to beat the game finally on normal and there's 2 difficulties and a few unplayed branching stages I have yet to find.  I'm going to get well more than my 40 dollars worth.The soundtrack and most of the graphics are great, the level and enemy placement is designed tight and with a lot of thought and care.  The game runs great on my pc and I really don't have a lot of complaints.There's a few bugs Granzella has acknowledged and a stage or two where the graphics are a bit lacking compared to others.  There's a few muddy textures here and there but these are small complaints.Buy it.  If you're even here you're probably interested and know what you're getting into.  R-Type is back and it's fantastic.  Helluva job Granzella!

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is solid.  Graphics and music are cool.  The variety of ships and power ups allows for a lot of room for experimenting with loadouts to figure out the optimal build for each level.  My one major gripe is an aesthetic one.  R-Type Delta and R-Type Final both did amazing jobs of conveying a dread-inducing, creepy as hell sci-fi horror vibe through visual storytelling and lore--an impressive feat for sidescrolling shmup games.  Nothing in R-Type Final 2 even comes close to that, and for the most part the levels are just rehashes of the ones from previous games.  The few original levels are fine, but in general they feel phoned in compared to the trippy, nightmarish designs of the previous games.  The bydo just aren't scary this time around, and it was a letdown.  Still, it's worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: R-Type Final 2

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, hooking up a controller makes it far better now. I thought the intro was unskippable but that was because the game kept thinking it was the first launch thanks to the keybinding softlock issue I described. The game play is fun, but unforgiving as typical of SHMUPS games.Quality, simply put is the main flaw of the game. The difficulty tends to be all over the place. For example the difficulty in stages 2 and 3 are far beyond the difficulty in the underwater stage which is one the later stages, and this was on 'practice' mode, the easiest mode in the game. Some bosses are easier than the stage itself to be frank.When respawning at a checkpoint you lose all your upgrades, and this is often at some of the most difficult portions of the game, which at this point, respawning at the start of the stage would be easier, but isn't given as an option. Allowing this, even for some of the easier difficulties would make going through the game far easier, or just respawning without losing your upgrades on easier difficulties would be great.Graphically, it's nice to see the ships in HD, and stages look great, for the most part, however the AI battleship map is really rather simply graphically, and feels out of place compared to something like the fiery armoury map which is far more detailed in comparison. In fact in some cases it feels like a regression from R-Type Final's giant battleship(PS2), which feels more detailed in comparison despite being SD. R-Type Delta's triangular shield graphic that surrounds your ship at the start and end of stages feels like it has more effort than the generic static field that now surrounds your shipMusically, it too is generic, I mean it works, but Delta had better sound design, the first 3 stage sound tracks were far more distinct and memorable to this day.This review thus far has been negative, but it's really mostly improvements R-Type need to make to survive going forward in 2021, as there are plenty of other games now that either have better value or enjoyment for much less. As a R-Type fan, I'm just happy to even have this game, I thought the series was dead a decade ago, and I did have a blast navigating through the stages. The team critically still has the level design aspect down which is the core of the game, and that's what matters really. If you're a R-Type fan, chances are your mind was or is already made up about getting this. But to try to introduce newer gamers into this, R-Type has to do better, assuming it wants to continue the series, and simply just isn't a love letter follow up to Final and the games prior. My original review still stands, minus the intro cutscene, so I'll leave it below. And no I didn't get the keybinding set to the mouse, I'm just using the controller for now.DO NOT BUY YET, holy crap this game is unfinished, trying to change the unintuitive keyboard layout can get you trapped in the game with no way to back out and this is the first 10 minutes. I backed this wanting a future for R Type, but this 'launch' hurts it more than it helps. Even entering in your name is difficult, it brings up a text box with a keyboard layout below it, but it's unselected, so all your keyboard inputs go nowhere until you move the mouse to click it. I'll change this review once I figure out how to map the fire button to the mouse, if it even is possible to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it.The PC version has little-to-no issues currently (2023), and you can choose different frame-rates, and also different resolutions.The first several hours can turn you off from the game, and the game tells you little to get going, so I recommend a certain strategy to make things easier, so please read this paragraph if you want to know. The game will still remain brutal, but your beginning experience will be improved greatly. For this reason, I recommend playing through all the stages/campaign on Practice mode. Then, go into "Score Attack," and you can view your completed stages there. Score Attack allows you to learn each stage with full powerups at the start. If you want to grind out the bosses, you need to play the regular mode up until you reach that boss, and then you can use your many continues on it.If you're new to R-Type, you pilot a ship and you control a "Force," which is a ball that attaches to the front or back of your ship. It can block small shots, and fire additional lasers. R-Type is a game where you need "to move to the enemy." It makes more sense once you realize that each stage is a puzzle. Every stage plays out the same way, every time - enemy movements and patterns are deterministic.If you are new to shmups in general, or you want to improve your time with R-Type, here's a tip: Instead of always holding the direction to you want to go, try tapping to move. If you're playing on a controller with a standard layout, a firm grip with the right hand and a loose grip with the left will make it easier. There are keyboard controls available as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game? Yes, but.I backed the initial crowd funding campaign and paid ~£25; for that price I'd say it's pretty fair, but it seems the price on steam is currently ~£35 which is a little steep, and nearly £60 for a version of the game with some pointless DLC thrown in. I completed the game on the easiest difficulty setting in 3 hours, so there is certainly lots of replay value with all the unlockable ships, 3 higher difficulty settings and multiple routes/end stages to complete just like the original R-Type Final had. When you consider that, the current £35 price tag isn't too bad- it is a very pretty game but really that's all it offers largely, it doesn't bring anything new to the table at all besides a few new enemies and updated graphics, and a re-hash of previous stages/bosses.This could ( should.. ) have been a HD remake of R-Type Final and it would actually be a better game I dare say as a result. I'd happily pay to get a HD remake of that game and R-Type Delta, this game is 'fun enough' but it seems to have an identity crisis, not knowing if it's a partial remake or trying to be it's own thing, and not doing a great job of either- good enough to enjoy, but certainly didn't blow my mind either.I would certainly wait until it goes on sale, or the price drops etc etc- in the mean time, go and replay the original games and remind yourself of how great they were, and still are; sprites ftw!

_childDocuments_.name: R-Type Final 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is an overall decent shump, the ups and downs are all valid point form a stand of preference, Although a good game, that I highly recommend READ the user reviews or watch play video, do some homework before you buy. This is an offshoot remake of old arcade style game with modernized HD asset, it can be your dream game or a deal breaker, depend on your motivation, Not a cheap game amount indie titles. If you are used to modern gaming convention, this game can feel like a ripoff for the little content it has. Despite the dev being committed to pull off an honest effort, much of that did not translate into a great user experience, I think it has to do with the development direction of what this game should be.This game carry too much burden from the past, what they are doing is essentially make a new game from an old time. A motivation so arcane to a point of even faithfully replicate its flaws, Rtype in its tradition is balanced on the raizer edge, its a barely beatable game, that has a different learning curve in every encounter with a one hit death, also have to keep you comeback. This is not a system can be tuned by someone interested in develop shmup. Also In my opinion not a good direction for developing a modern game experience. Shmup in general is in many ways captivated by an outdated system that catering to a business model no longer exist. But for this game the biggest problem also is their biggest sales point: The DLC sets of recreated past stages. These beautiful remaster are the highlight of this entire project ATM. The main campaign in comparison feels rushed. They are causing a great problem however, is each remasters require a new set of assets to be created from ground up, the project need to dedicate a significant amount of resources for these assets. And in turn could cost their time in content creation for game play. A modern game format can allow them to use recycled assets to create variants and analogs and use most of the development resource in creative system and stage design. But all these are my speculation. After all this is a crowdfunded game, they maybe simply fulfilling their promise to give what the backers wanted.Rtype final 2 is an on going development, the game has become much eloberated sense its launch. A plan for Rtype final 3 is also being drafted, much of information is in their Japanese PPT. I think they do have something serious under their sleeve. Final 2 they get pass for that nostalgia card, by replicating the Final. They cant do this twice. In my review I chose to give a thumb up for Rtype being irreplaceable within the STG genre, however I do not recommend this game for anyone not already have attachment to old IPs.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great horizontal bullet hell with plenty of replay ability. You should start on normal difficulty or easier with the base ships, then as you unlock more ships you can use them on harder difficulties.  The ships are unique in what they can do too, along with your friend, the Force.  It's a mechanic that isn't present in much of anything else, which makes this very unique, as the force you use can block bullets, attack on its own, or enhance your own attacks if attached to the ship.  Makes for a great gameplay mechanic. Really like the game.  Would recommend to people who like Gradius or top down shooters, I personally like the horizontal nature this has though more than vertical though.  Just an opinion.If your easy to frustrate, just start on a lower difficulty like KIDS or PRACTICE, and you will likely really enjoy the small challenge till you get better ships.Recommended! :)

_childDocuments_.review: It is amazing to see R-Type return once again, and better than ever, loved it!Proud to see this game becoming a reality ever since from the April 2019 teaser tbh.The game has more extended difficulties, and has been made much easier for newcomers to get in to and enjoy the game casually. For veterans, this too is also a good pace of new things to try, as in higher difficulties, the game can get really punishing for your mistakes. Starting off again from a checkpoint is never an easy thing, but with , it makes you possible to pick up back from a checkpoint as they optimized it slightly convenient for you to pick up where you died off, even if your power ups are naked ( you lose all power ups if yo get shot )As someone that plays a lot of predecessor of R-Type games, Final 2 is an amazing take, felt almost like a concept combination of R-Type Delta (with their good stage designs), and R-Type Final 1 on the PS2 (good introduction to many usable fighters). So this is considered the state of the art of R-Type games, with a lot of good things to take in.The part that made it better with this PC port? You can game more than 60fps, and this is surprisingly something I have not really witnessed in other Shoot Em Up games in my life. This is certainly pleasing to look at, as I have a working 144hz monitor, and it works wonders. Resolution in game can go up beyond 1080p if you have a very beefy PC.

_childDocuments_.review: I expected a remaster of R-Type Final, and instead got a whole new game.I am both upset at this and really happy. The new game is awesome, it feels like R-Type, it has a ton of ships like the first "FINAL", and it's got great music/art. My disappointment for not having the original courses was quickly replaced.So with that, this is a SHMUPS game (Shoot-em-up game, where you fly). You have shot, charge, and force buttons as controls. Powerups give you a FORCE module that attaches to either side of your ship (front or back) and the force button launches it off. Your FORCE module also shoots additional lasers as you pick up upgrades. If you are charging your beam, your lasers won't fire, but you get a devastating charge attack in it's place. There's also missles and bits that fly with your ship as powerups you can get. This game feels great. I can't wait for the DLC too (more stages). Pick it up if you are into SHMUPS!

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who is old enough to be blown away by the original  arcade game - and who enjoyed the sequels just as much -  made me very happy when it came out.Several years later, and I'm not that enamored with it anymore. It's simply not as creative as this series used to be. The only good stages are the throwback ones in the DLC packs, the soundtrack is forgettable, the boss fights bland and uninspired. Production values are good, but inconsistent - did they forget to texture the third stage or something?...And instead of spending the development budget on improving the playable content, someone involved in decision making at Granzella insists on spending it on superfluous picture decoration nonsense nobody cares about.And while this game does have a lot of content - over a hundred nicely modeled, intricately detailed fighters to unlock and a lot of stages if you get all the DLC - it ultimately still feels restricted since the developers have failed to catch up with modern game design, restricting you to playing either a set of pre-designed stages (arcade mode) or a per-stage score attack. There's so much missed opportunity here it almost hurts.Not even Granzella seems to know what to do with this anymore. They where promising an upgrade to  but then they didn't and released an alternate version on PS5 instead. It's poorly planned and managed.But ultimately it still deserves a recommendation, because it does get a lot of things right.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute trash of a game that does not deserve this score or price. A game that looks like 4 3d game art students first project, where each one created assets for a different generation of console, and then combined them together into this game. Map number 3 was clearly never finished, stretched textures and a neon texture that looks like a place holder is used on 90% of that level. _childDocuments_.review: Do you love R-Type? Then you will love R-Type Final 2. Its that simple. The developers did not drop the ball.Think of this as "R-Type Final Remix". It isn't doing much wildly new or different, but if it ain't broke, don't fix it.If you don't know what R-Type is, its about the grace and satisfaction of pirouetting through a minefield while leaving an astonishing wake of destruction behind you. You must die many times before you learn that dance. If you're on the fence, here's what you need to know:- Difficulty is on par with previous R-Types (i.e. "Kids Mode" will still kick your butt). If you desperately need help, Practice Mode lets you respawn with your Force on already.- In-game music is very good. Don't be scared by the trailer video or narrator, which are a really bad fit for this game. The style is similar to III, Delta, and Final. Unfortunately you won't be hearing more than the first 15 seconds of each track because that's how long you will last before dying (again).- Graphics are bright and colorful, to a fault. Sometimes hard to tell the difference between foreground and background. There are so many explodey things going on that may need to stop firing just so that you can see the bullets coming towards you. That's bad game design, but good eye candy. You decide if thats okay.- The backstory fashions this as a catalog of war stories, so consider this an expandable game (R-Type Final 1 was the final battle). Developers may include more stages as DLC in the future depending on sales and demand.- Many elements are remixed from R-Type Final. There are many similarities. I don't think it hits the sublime highs of some of the previous games, but there are some fun twists at the end that will still make you smile. I wont spoil them.- The UI confusing and feels rushed, but i bought the game for the pew pew, not the clicky stuff.- Stages are relatively short and have many checkpoints to reduce the amount of cursing required to move forward.- There are 11 total stages, at least 3 retro DLC stages, and, yes, , not just 12 like screenshots might imply. There's a lot of replay value, just like Final 1.Verdict: I love all of my R-Type children and am happy to welcome the newborn!@Granzella: Please remaster R-Type III and Delta, too! I'll buy.

Same with R-type Delta etc etc. I never thought id see another R-type in my lifetime and this was a total surprise to me, if id have known id have backed it from day one. Anyway the price is more than fair for and arcade Shoot em up, loads of ships to try out, good old classic try and beat the game and surpass that high score. Graphics are great. Good Music, Good Difficulty settings etc Very faithful to the originals. I cannot wait for the R-type Delta DLC level a long with the others. It would have been great to see it on the PS Vita but ill grab it on the Switch too. If you loved the originals youll love this. Ignore the whining younger generations, they need to learn to save up and appreciate gaming history. Well done, thanks for the nostalgia!

_childDocuments_.review: The first name in Shoot Em' Up today. R-Type Final 2 gives you a futuristic setting that goes all the way back to 1987, when R-Type 1 first mesmerized a dedicated following. Spanning releases on most platforms: Arcade cabinets, home consoles, handheld, mobile phones, and best of all PC. In the future, an alien menace called the Bydo came to threaten humanity. In response the development of an advanced one man star fighter called R-Types were conceived. Thanks to advanced technology and the harnessing Bydo element called Force. Which can be attached to the front, rear, or even independently launched and attack on its own. Which is one of the defining gimmicks of this series, along with the use of the Wave Cannon. On top of having rapid firing guns, the Wave Cannon offers the most destructive power against the opposition.With a hundred ships, with multiple configurations and options for attachments and personalization to your ship. The only thing stopping you from achieving victory is your combat piloting skills.

_childDocuments_.review: I love me some R-Type and this game seriously nails it. After believing R-Type Final on the PS2 really would be the final R-Type, and then hearing about Irem going under, I didn't think I'd ever see this game. I wasn't holding out hope. This game was a day 1 purchase for me and I don't regret it in the slightest. The intro sequence gave me those excited goosebumps I only get on the best of occasions. The soundtrack has me hooked and I've barely scratched the surface of this game. I can't wait to dig in further. But based on what I've seen so far, I would recommend this game to fans of the series in a heartbeat. Is it perfect? I dunno, probably not. I'll admit I'm being a total fanboy over here. But I sincerely think the team behind this game have done an excellent job and have stayed faithful to series. This feels exactly like the kind of R-Type game I would want here and now.

_childDocuments_.review: Always been a fan since Final 1 on the PS2. this franchise has always been one of the best sidescrollers and I grew up playing R-Type Final 1 for hours on end, back when it was grittier in atmosphere and design and even harder to unlock the ships. _childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything else, I ought to put down a disclaimer: I'm absolutely terrible at R-Type, have been since I was a kid and in twenty years that hasn't changed much at all. But I love the look and feel of the games, and while it may be a departure from what some might expect (visually or otherwise), to me it still radiates those fantastic R-Type vibes.Outside of the sights and sounds, there's also that signature R-Type difficulty, probably the largest reason why I could never beat these games as a kid. Even today, I can still barely make it past the first few levels before the game kicks me in the teeth, but it feels like a fair difficulty to me, like every time I got shot down (or crushed by swarms of angry fish-things) it was because of poor planning on my part, especially when I forget to increase my ship's speed to improve my ability to dodge lolOverall, it's a fantastic experience, and if you're a fan of old-school shoot-'em-ups, you may well be, too!...If I had one gripe, I was expecting to hear some music that gave me a distinct throw-back sensation, but I didn't hear anything that I recognized (at least, not in my experience thus far) so that was a bit of a bummer. Music -is- great, don't get me wrong, and I'm gonna be listening to this soundtrack for quite some time, I just kinda wish I could've gotten just a smidge more fan-service in that department. Tiny little nitpick, that's all that is. :P

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of R-TYPE and have played every game in the series, so I was really looking forward to R-TYPE Final 2. However, it ended up being a major disappointment for me.The game is too expensive for the quality it offers.The enemy design, scenery, and model detailing are terrible. In fact, R-TYPE Delta still has better texture detailing, to the point where I felt like R-TYPE Final 2 looked like high school-level 3D work.The difficulty level can be described as "unfairly difficult." Enemies are placed in blind corners, often in such numbers that they force the player to hide in one area. This happens frequently. Even on the "Kid" difficulty level, it's still very challenging.Adding features like dressing up and decorating a room is absolutely ridiculous for this type of game. It felt out of place and didn't make any sense at all.And there are many other small issues as well.In conclusion, I really regret spending money on this game, even when it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice successor to one of my favorite PS2 games and one of my favorite franchises in shoot-em-ups. Plays very similarly to R-Type Final so nothing major has been changed. Tons of ships for you to unlock and branching paths in the levels (I'm assuming since stages are still called 1.0, 2.0 etc etc. Final did this as well with the branches being things like 1.1, 2.3, etc etc.) Very challenging so be ready for that. Also be warned that the game is a bit rough right now, hopefully it can get smoothed out as it's life goes on.A couple things I dislike about this game:1) Unlocking new ships in Final was just "Clear this stage" or "Play this long with the previous model". Now it's that but you also need to spend resources you collect by beating levels. There are way too many ships here to require that. Final's "Just do these things" was perfect because once you completed a requirement you didn't need to worry about if you had the resources to buy it then. Still tons of replayability in that situation, this just seems frivolous. At least no MTX where you can buy the resources for real-life money so you get the resources at a decent pace. Not all the ships are unlockable by spending resources, though, because...It seems they changed this up so the physical keyboard actually works. No longer a problem.Those are only problems I have so far. Otherwise I recommend this game. Haven't gotten very far yet but I plan on beating it soon. Just need to knock the dust off as it's been awhile. Will update as I discover more.EDIT:Am now noticing that hazards can just kind of blend in with the environment. Numerous times I've been playing, I die and I go "WTF just hit me." Your ship's spectacular explosion hide whatever it was that hit you so you might not ever know. I've said the same thing in some other shmups but not as much as I have here already. I could just be bad but it sure seems like nothing hit me most of the time. I KNOW something hit me but I can never find out what.

_childDocuments_.review: There is much to love here: Great graphics and cool stages (apart from a few bland ones), 100 different ships, ship customization in looks and weapons, branching stage paths......but there is also the old old school difficulty with endless cheap deaths. Which means, you will be stuck without powerups at a checkpoint, trying to claw yourself back into the game, again and again. In my first full playthrough (normal) I used 26 continues, each with three lifes, so I died 78 times... I guarantee you, you will curse and yell at the screen.Apparently, I'm a masochist, cause I do like the game and will continue to play it... but I can't help comparing it to something like Natsuki Chronicles, where you have similar ship upgrade gameplay, but virtually no cheap deaths, due to markers for entering ships and even for bullets. Feels much more fair and less infuriating.Overall, this R-Type is a game, which I love to hate and in that sense, it's very true to the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game perfect?    No.  What game is?  Final 2's levels are on the whole shorter than Final 1, but while Final 1's levels often feel a little sparse, Final 2's are packed.Is the price right?   Debatable.  I have clocked over a day so far.  Better value than the average COD single player campaign.Will this game punish you harshly for every mistake?  Definitely.  The often pretty GFX do a good job of pulling your attention away from where it should be!Is this game 'fair'?  Yes.  It's your own fault if you die.  You can change ships between levels.  Did this game compel me to keep trying until I succeeded?  YES!  You will start to see the patterns, you WILL 'git gud'.Can't wait for the upcoming updates.  More ships, more levels...Near rock solid performance on my Ryzen 1700x, 16GB RAM, RX6800, Win10 machine.This game is bast played with a controller.  One with two analogue sticks is required to control the Nanomachine wave cannon (carried by the WISE MAN) but otherwise a controller with a good D-Pad is recommended.Note:  I backed the Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.review: i Loved R-Type Final on the PS2 when i was a kid, and hoped this would be the same, and it is! the game-play, the difficulty, even on the easier difficulties, the ships, the satisfying game-play, all there and its a wonderful game, unfortunately the grind gets extremely brutal extremely fast, barely 7 to 9 ships in and your taking multiple hours to grind a single ship out, one that wont be significantly different to your previous, sometimes even the same but upgraded, and while many of the early ships have huge play-style variation and exciting new unlocks, the game doesn't respect your time once you invest a moderate amount of time into it, going from getting 1 ship every couple of runs to 1 every hour is jarring for some, and for some games that's okay, because its built for an audience that wants to play the game for a long time, however, this is not an experience i am interested in with a 2D shoot em uptruth be told, i expect the old ps2 version likely had just as much grinding, but it felt far better there because of its platform and era, nowadays games struggle to captivate people for long stretches of time, and without significant unlock-able or progression rewards, people don't stay interested, i have refunded this game as i don't feel it was worth the price, even on a 50% sale, due to the intense grinding and fun, but slightly repetitive game-play (due to many ships, or many in the same line, either playing the same or not having significant upgrades available in the form of bombs, bits or otherwise)pick this up if you have way too much free time, or really REALLY love R-Type, i don't think the game needs to change nor is it a bad game per-say, it just aged differently to my expectations

_childDocuments_.review: The good thing-and bad thing-about this game is it's an R-Type game. It looks fabulous, plays like the franchise should, but there are two big reasons this gets a thumbs down: One, like every other R-Type game, it's THE most difficult shooter out there. I've played tough bullet hell shooters that are easier than this, even on the lowest difficulty level. It will cause frustration to the point of rage quitting. Second, with the DLC this is now becoming a cash grab. I purchased the deluxe bundle and got all the first DLC with it, but now you have to pay for the second round separately.This isn't a bad game overall but it really disappointed me and on top of that, the so-called "adaptive difficulty" either doesn't work or i's garbage. If you like frustratingly impossible shooters and R-Type, this might be worth picking up on a good sale. But in part because of how the second set of DLC is being done, I can't recommend it now. I won't be sinking any more money into this until it's made at least a little bit easier.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most visually beautiful shmup games. Great soundtrack too. Not without flaws however. The Switch version's loading screen for a full playthrough takes up to a minute; after playing that port for dozens of hours I purchased the PC version hoping for even better graphics and faster loading times. I can attest that with a good enough graphics card, loading times are quite satisfactory! Unfortunately the screen jitters more than I'd hope for a game running on a PC with an RTX 2080 GPU. I typically receive lag upon loading a stage I haven't loaded in the current session. Seems like both Switch and PC versions could be further optimized.Level design is a mixed bag. Ranges from good to awful with a lot in between. Stage 6.1 resembles a pinball arena with destructible spinning triangles. It's unique and visually interesting, with a reasonable learning curve. Stage 6.2 on the other hand employs repetitive mecha assaults and debris attacks and the infamously ridiculous stream of POW Armors containing dozens of crystals but no bits nor missiles. It seems boringly easy until the difficult boss fight. To top it off, the spawn point if you die at the boss is very far from the boss, and the background is just one effect infinitely scrolling.Overall a recommend anyhow. Between starting and completing Final 2, I played the original R-Type I and II. If you are unfamiliar with the R-Type games and want to play one of them, I'd suggest also playing the original. It'll undoubtedly reward you when you play R-Type Final 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I've started R-Type with Super R-Type on the SNES. At first the game didn't really interest me as I was rather into lighthearted games like Super Mario, but one day I decided to take it more seriously. I chose the lowest difficulty - "Novice", it was still very hard and confusing for me as I was rather new to gaming and didn't know any ins and outs. It took me hundreds of tries to finally beat it, I was so intrigued that I even finished it in easy mode afterwards.As I got older I played through a plethora of games other than R-Type, this gives me a good insight into what makes a game work and what makes a game fail. I believe that a game is only worth it, if it creates a deep atmosphere - immersion. There is another very important thing to take into account: A game has to provide you with either relaxation or with adrenaline rushes, it has to decide on a sole focus.R-Type Final 2, although lacking in graphics, has an atmosphere that you can feel. It also has a set goal of providing you with adrenaline rushes.I've played many games in my life, some very hard games, many of them lacked what R-Type Final 2 offers, they were huge time sinks that tried to deliver the player a mixed bag of things. If a game is about the player getting sweaty hands and a fast heartbeat, it should never try to make the gamer exhausted, the two things don't go well together. Many games make you grind useless stuff for hours, wich is boring, takes away your time and eats away on your energy. Some games give the bosses too high health bars, or are so complex and incomprehensible that the player has to resort to seek out information on the internet. This all hampers the fun and the growth of a gamer which should evolve automatically either by the means of game-design and mechanics, or through minor hints provided in the game.R-Type on the other hand gives the player a huge adrenaline rush while not really making him lose time or a lot of energy. One does not have to click the mouse 400 times per minute to be good, neither is one forced to hit at a boss for 30 minutes for the 100th time, which is just exhausting and boring.With R-Type you get the perfect classic gaming mix, you fight relatively "easy" enemies to warm up and then destroy a  very hard boss in 10 seconds or 5 minutes. It is fun, it's a formula from older and simpler times that makes sense, no wasting of time and energy, no real exhaustion.R-Type Final 2 has graphics from around 2006, but with higher resolution and better lightning effects, one gets a nostalgic feeling from the 00's. The level designs are okay, they are not what you would expect for 2021 and I think most will agree that R-Type III and Delta are the flagships of R-Type, overall high fidelity pixel art has always worked very well for R-Type. When I first played R-Type Final I felt like it wasn't on par with the older games graphic-wise, but there is something to the art of the "Final" games too.Most levels look okay, some like level 7 look very nice. Level 3 though looks bare bones, it lacks many details, which is sad, as it is a beautiful idea of a level. Personally I dislike level 6 far more than 3. _childDocuments_.review: Do you like straight-forward arcade action? Do you like having a bad time? Do you like beating your head against a wall again and again and again until you eventually burst through the other side? Then R-Type Final 2 might be for you! While the presentation is rough around the edges in places to put it nicely, I've found a lot to like as I (attempt to) master each and every stage and unlock bigger and better ships. My recommendation does come with some asterisks, however. -This isn't a high-octane action packed romp. It's more of a trial and death exercise in focus and patience.-Not all ships are created equal. There will be over 100 in the playable roster when updates are complete and most of them will not be viable on R-Typer difficulty or above.-Honestly, the DLC stages are my favorites in the game. The main game isn't bad by any means, but DLC consistently has more interesting design and better music. Just beware that the default DLC stage order slaps you with the hardest two levels first before getting much more manageable.-If you're new to the series, try and engage with the community online. Getting tips and tricks from veterans can really improve your experience in more ways than simply beating a tough section.Should you decide to give this game a go, I wish you luck, Brave Soul.

_childDocuments_.review: Being a longtime fan of the series, I love this game although I recognize that it's far from perfect. The major issue I have with the game is the price tag. _childDocuments_.review: I've had quite alot of fun playing this, and I haven't even finished it yet (have gotten up to the last level in 1 of the 3 different ending paths). I was in the mood for a schmup for some reason, so snooped around and found this. I like the graphics, bright with large ships/things moving around, shiny and feeling polished to me, and your ship and lasers feel good. (There are some boring enemies like the big plants in the 2nd level but generally the enemies are interesting I think).I'm also a fan of the music, groovy dancy/techno that puts you in the groove (I'm a fan of that sort of music in general).It's very deliberate almost slow-paced gameplay for a shooter where as you make your way through the stages every section after the 2nd level or so becomes 'how the hell do I do that??' and then you try things and get further and further and its satisfying to conquer each section. On your first run you'll have just 3 continues or so, but afterwards you'll have much more (10?) and then much more again and so gradually with persistence you can get through more and more of the game.I've enjoyed all of the different bosses. The first one is very easy on normal (and even bydo) but apparently it has a different form on the highest difficulty? The 2nd one is ..ok but after that they become interesting challenges, quite unique where you develop a plan and need to execute it, its quite fun.I wasn't sure what I'd think when I bought it, looked at a handful of reviews but I'm glad I did, it is fun and I'm enjoying playing thought it again more than I thought i might. You unlock different ships too with different types of attack and force types etc as well and just starting to have fun trying out new combinations (they're a bit different - still trying them out).It's not cheap which is true but a modern schmup is a unique itch to scratch and if you like this sort of game, its fun to play. I think they've done a good job tbh, with the level design and the whole package. A solid 8-8.5/10.I'll point out I bought this first and also having loved Darius Twin back in the day on the SNES, grabbed DariusBurst Chronicles on Steam too. (I was tossing up between the two). Didnt see many comparisons between them - haven't played DariusBurst for too long but it's more in the style of abit more exhilarating reactionary play against swarmy enemies for short bursts (levels are short), with lots more bullet patterns etc, but this feels more focused and deliberate - every section a crafted enemy and environmental challenge to master as you go, where progress kind of feels more meaningful?. Both are very fun tho.UPDATE: Have finished 2 of the ending paths now, having heaps of fun with the game. It's very addictive and I keep wanting to play through it, unlocking new ships. Wow it gets hard in the last level in both paths (doable tho with persistence) but the final boss in one of them is creative, I've never played a boss like that in a schmup and its fun while being very challenging (and tense while you're trying to beat the game for the first time!) This is a quality game, I'm going to be playing more of it. Have upped the difficulty too and enjoying the differences in the levels that tweak it slightly to make it more difficult.UPDATE 2: This is a deeply rewarding shooter, with very skillful level design. You can tell in the tweaks they make to each level as you go up in diffculty the changes are lovingly made to improve the diffculty experience but remaining fair. Have played through each of the endings now and very much enjoyed the other path aswell, completed it on Bydo (the difficulty up) and the first stage in rtyper (2nd stage wow thats tough). Also got the stage pass and made it through the first 5 levels on normal, loved x2.0 which forums revealed horror stories of but worked it out blind even with a ship not considered to be all that great and it was very satisfying. And playing with all the different ships and unlocking more has been very enjoyable.All in all a fantastic game made with care and thanks to the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this with this: This game is not perfect.With that out of the way, let's move into the meat of this review.This is a game that has a reasonably-good ramp in difficulty among its various stages, and even among its difficulties. Even if you aren't the best at most shmups (I certainly am not), playing on Practice or Kids difficulty can help prepare you for later difficulties. By the time you complete all three routes on Kids, you should have the skills, knowledge, and ships to handle Normal. And so on.R-Type as a series is one that rewards memorization. It's hard. And it will kill you until you learn. In that sense, some things seem unfair at first blush, but there's the key-- it kills you... _until you learn._This game is an R-Type game at its core. It will kill you, but every checkpoint is recoverable (even That One Checkpoint-- those who've played, you know the one). Once you know how to handle a given area, it's just a matter of execution.In a nutshell, this game is hard, but learnable. And it is rewarding to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved R-Type as a kid.., wanted to love R-Type Final 1... buutt..., yeah there was a love hate relationship there with how the levels changed with each play through so I was a bit sceptical in regards to Final 2I shouldn't have beenIt feels like a nostaliga dream From the very first moment you start as the Arrowhead and then that classic feel... MMMM heaven.., then you go on to unlock the ships in what is in fact a better method than Final 1, you get resources.., so you can actually unlock the line of ships you prefer to play as first..Then it gets awesome, the variable stages at 6.0 and 7.0 where your choice in 5.0 decides the fate of the ending,, and sure there's only 4 options.. but the options feel good and it makes wanting to replay the levels over and over more funso... difficulty wise.. well this time it's a choice and not forced on you via the level mechanics, there's Practice to ease you in.. and for some levels to help learning them is a godsend.then we have Kids, Normal, Bydo and Rtyper.. the last being unforgiving and brutal.. as it should beWould I recommend this to anyone that loves classic space shootersHELL YEAHI am only 4 hours in from writing this.. but it plays great, it feels great and I wish I had more hours in a day to unlock stuff.. the hanger number reads 99.. and I hope the developers actually add all the ships which I think at last count was 102?.. I might be wrong though there..The DLC adds charms and throughly brutal as hell levels.. (You have been warned) but there from the older games where the difficulty was set to pretty much stealing your coins, and first timers might want to play the normal campaign first to at least Bydo before they attempt themGraphics 4/5 Sure it looks nice, some of the effects are a little pixelated at times but it's RTYPE as it should beSound 3/5 Some of the Music is forgettable but there some remastered classics in there Controls 5/5 It's a joy to play, the controls feel really responsive while I played on a X360 padOverall 4/5 A modern homage to a classic game.. _childDocuments_.review: The return of R-Type series brings me both nostalgic and modern feeling so there are both pros and cons to consider should buy this game.- GraphicFirst, due to Unreal Engine, this game has much dazzling in graphic but the main point is to be the difficult play in game mode. Enemies are nasty and combined with graphic, this is brutal for eyes especially colorblind players.- GameplayThank you for bringing the old style type; Revival Start. This type, to define what it is, is quite brutal for newcomers but for R-Type fans, it is the core of the game. When you die, it will not continue what you have done in the progress, instead it will restart into the accessed checkpoints. Additionally you will lose all powerups so if you would like to beat the game, practice more.For newcomers, the system is R-Type Final (PS2) in most cases, beat the game, collect the fighters, you have dose for SP.Attack, you can adjust speed-up by buttons, and even touch the environment but don't run over enemy big battleship surface.- DifficultyUnlike old classic version, R-Type Final 2 has only 1 loop game but instead there are many routes lead into different end scenes. But don't worry for newcomers, you can pick many difficulties in hangar before launch, from Practice to R-Typer (equivalent to Very Hard). Moreover, if you think R-Typer is boring, this game already brought beyond R-Typer, there are R-Typer 1 to 3 which change both enemies' strength and bullet patterns. Some bosses are totally different compared to easier difficulties.- ControlWould like to complain a bit for Keyboard due to low sensitivity, caused movement weird and also in menu command it is not quite fully supported. Recommend Joypad to play.- MiscBeside gameplay, yes, you can read all biographic in both R-Craft and Bydo enemies after beating the game (even Stage 1.0 you can read some of them). _childDocuments_.review: (Full disclosure: I was one of the game's backers)You got over 6 levels to conquer (including alternate endgame stages), around 101 ships to unlock (with more coming in teased updates) with their own unique play styles, difficulty levels for a wide range of players with plenty of surprises in the higher difficulties for daredevils to encounter, and plenty of deadly aliens to blast in this long-awaited sequel to one of the greatest ship-collecting STGs out there. The pacing for the levels feels great, the levels and enemies require you to combine the attacks of your ship and force unit effectively, and one major improvement from R-Type Final on the PS2: You no longer need to grind time to unlock ships, as you now collect materials from playing the game and use those to build ships! No more being stuck on a ship you're not too crazy for just to unlock something; just pick your favorite ship and kick some bydo butt!It's R-Type Final for the 2020s, What else can I say? The only issues I have is that the on-screen keyboard feels barely functional for the PC version (as of the time of this writing) but it's a real minor complaint. If you love shooting games, great atmosphere, and tons of things to collect then don't think twice. Get this game; just don't expect beating it to the a walk in the park!

_childDocuments_.review: Here are some of my early impressions and suggestions.Virtual Keyboard:Like most of the other reviews, the menu can definitely use some refinements. Allowing the controller to navigate the virtual keyboard and letting the physical ENTER key to confirm what is entered in the text-box will be a big improvement. Pause Menu:Using "Exit" for resuming the game is confusing. Replacing it with "Resume" would be much clearer.Displayed Controls:Automatically switching the displayed controls between keyboard+mouse and controller when the user presses a button on a different device would a good quality of life improvement.R-Museum:Titling a locked ship with "Coming Soon" is odd. It gives an impression that the ship is not released in the game yet. I believe replacing that text with "Locked" or "Not Purchased" would be clearer.Locking ships such as the Warhead behind a ship that requires a password, that as far as I know, is unobtainable in the game seems unfair. Maybe placing password locked ships in its own tree would be better.Navigating the R-Museum feels slow, although functional enough with a controller. For keyboard+mouse, unlocking the cursor to be controlled with the mouse would work better.Saving:Being forced to start over after exiting the game can be frustrating for someone who wants to continue where they left off. I understand saves can be abused though. Maybe implementing a save system similar to other game's ironman modes can work.

_childDocuments_.review: Not good, but good enough.The first R-Type Final had 101 ships that could be obtained through playing the game.This iteration uses a bizarre in-game currency system and has entire ship development paths locked behind a password for kickstarter backers.  I think it's kind of sad that fans of the first will miss out on ships they had access to previously.Also, the addition of an adaptive difficulty baffles me.  Why pick normal difficulty if it's going to get harder? Why pick bydo or r-typer difficulty if it's going to relent when the player hits a rough patch? I don't know who asked for that feature to be added, but the game doesn't seem to benefit from it in any way unless they plan on removing the difficulty selection altogether.  My opinion, not gospel.R-Type Final 2 manages to be prettier than Final 1, but I feel the level design leaves a lot to be desired.  To that end, if the player finds themselves using only 1 out of 99 available ships because the stage layout renders the others almost useless, there must be an issue with the level design.All that said, it's not bad, nor unplayable.  I just find myself unable to recommend it to anyone but fans of the series.I couldn't recommend it to all fans of the shmup genre as shmups tend to come in many incarnations -this title is a sort of niche within a niche.I would not recommend this game to anyone who isn't a fan of R-Type.Fans of R-Type who have not played R-Type Final will probably get a kick out it.To anyone who has played R-Type Final, skip it.  There's nothing new to see here.

_childDocuments_.review: [edit 6/19/21: they did an announcement saying they're going to give current owners of Final 2 a whole new sequel in Final 3 by the end of the year??? this is a crazy good deal if it's like a whole new campaign...]As an original backer on Kickstarter 2 years ago, I would say the wait was worth it and It's a fantastic shmup.  Anyone familiar with the R-Type franchise knows what they're getting into for the most part here.  It's not like the Danmakus and Gradius-like shmups that require super fast reflexes, but it's more about strategy, atmosphere, and the story-telling as told through the level design.  I remember still being in high school when I pre-ordered R-Type Final 1 for PS2 from Gamestop and I was so excited to discover all the levels and unlock all the ships.  A lot of those levels back then were a little too long, so it's nice to see the levels in this sequel shortened, similar to the very original R-Types in a way.  However, I do miss the bits of quotes and story that were in Final 1 to add a little more depth and intrigue into the gameplay.The graphics are gorgeous and everything runs smoothly on a decent machine.  Performance-wise, this is what R-Type FInal 1 should have been as I did go back to playing it last year on my PS2 and found everything so sluggish.  You basically have to emulate it on PCSX2 to get it to feel and play more like Final 2.Being such a fan of the series, I did pre-order the high end collector's edition for PS4 from the NIS America website mainly for the awesome R9-A metal earth model.  It was nice to receive it early and try out the game a couple days before release, but I can definitively say you must get it on Steam if you have a machine capable of running it smoothly 60-144fps with no hiccups.  At least your chances of dying due slight frame rate stutters will be lessened lol.At the backed price of $30, to get the game and all the DLC that was planned is a fantastic price.  At the price of $65ish for the complete package and digital copies of the OST and art book is still pretty good... 11 main stages and (I think) 6 planned DLC stages?  99 ships to unlock.  I mean, I bought Dariusburst Chronicles with all the DLC when it was on sale at some point, and have only played it a handful of times, finding everything to be just a little too generic.  You can always wait for a sale too, but it's definitely a must buy for anyone who's an R-Type fan or even a fan of shmups.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit wary of the switch to 3D graphics and the Unreal Engine, as one of the things I loved about R-Type was the excellent bitmap graphics, but they have really made it work here. The weird bio-mechanical Bydo aesthetic is captured perfectly, the levels themselves make great use of movement and depth, and most importantly, the reflective lasers glow powerfully against the dark corridors. The modern engine also allows for super high frame rates, which is a revelation in a game as twitchy as this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's gorgeous and a worthy successor to Irem's long line of shooters.   Plays solidly even on my 3-year-old, Intel I5 / midrange Geforce GTX gaming laptop. This one isn't for folks who aren't willing to fail -- and fail a LOT -- before getting good.The one thing I would change is adding an option to the settings to let the player select their own default ship speed.   It's not a deal-breaker, just something that would be real nice to have.

_childDocuments_.review: -Launch Day Review-As a kickstarter and a giant fan of R-Type and Shmups i was very eager to boot up the game and play this game. I've been waiting for years for another game that takes what previous R-Type games did but better and.....well. It's more R-Type but i think a good explanation is in order. First up, it feels and plays just like Delta/Final in a good way. Ship with a unforgiving hitbox, force core at the front. Speed up and down buttons to adjust movement. This is 100% a R-Type game, with plenty of ships to use and unlock. The problem is that it's trying to be the early R-Type games while also trying to be like Delta/Final, but it's drawing on too much from the former than the latter. Considering that this game was marketed like it was going to be more Delta/Final than R-Type 1/2/3 it's somewhat misleading.Two big examples is the OST and the Level design. There's too much energy in the music for the most part and it seems to have some pacing issues (perhaps a technical issue?). It's not bad music mind you, but it feels like it would had fit a more retro-themed or hard-core game. Now the Level design....OH BOY. This...this is a doozy for me. It doesn't make good use of it's '3D space'. It feels like you're always travelling on a line. "But R-Type games have you always travelling on a line."True for the early games but again, Delta and Final did things to compensate. Interesting Rotations of the background, moving the scenery about, water effects and it had enemies come in and out of the scene in cool ways. Final 2 meanwhile only uses it for the most part to rotate into another 'line'. It feels like a waste of the UT4 engine.In addition, some of the checkpoints and enemy placement are completely unforgiving. There's one point on stage 4 that is literal cancer if you don't have a weapon for it prior. And if you die at that point of the stage you have to do it without access to any weapon other than your wave cannon and if your wave cannon can't deal with what are basically solid objects then you're done, restart the game because it would be faster to get back to that area instead of trying to futilely throw yourself into what is essentially several walls made of angry flesh.Visuals are also mixed bag. On one hand you can get some really nice shots here and there with sweeping views of space, planets in the background with objects in-between to create a lovely setting. On the other you have objects close up that look like melted chocolate. I think something may be broke with the LoD on them. At least the game runs silky smooth (For me at least).All in all. I really wish there was a 'neutral' button for a review. The game is enjoyable enough with solid gameplay and tons of unlockables. You'll generally have a good time if you're a Shmup fan but it does seem to lack a bit of it's predecessors soul.

name: You Will Die Here Tonight
detailed_description: Play as each member of the elite Aries Division, separated by mysterious forces. Explore the mansion and seamlessly switch to pulse-pounding arcade combat when running is no longer an option. Your teammates will die, but their actions and decisions carry forward, empowering – or endangering – whoever remains. You Will Die Here Tonight is a survival horror game inspired by the golden age of the genre with a unique twist: Death is only the beginning of your story. A Modern Upgrade to a Classic Formula A love-letter to survival and action-horror classics, YWDHT seamlessly blends top-down exploration with visceral, heart-stopping first-person arcade shooter combat. A Cursed Estate Explore Breckenridge Estate, a cursed 19th century mansion with a tragic history. Uncover the sinister and cruel reality of the place, where nothing is what it seems. Life or Death Decisions Fight or flee deadly enemies. Carefully manage scarce resources. Solve challenging puzzles. Purchase weapons and upgrades. Your decisions will influence the rest of the game. Take what you need but leave some for the others. Death is Inevitable But with every death, your actions and decisions will carry forward to empower or endanger whoever remains. Can you embrace the death of your team to uncover the truth, or will all of their sacrifices have been in vain?

short_description: Immerse yourself in retro top-down visuals as you face the horrors of Breckenridge Hall through intense first-person combat. Scavenge, solve puzzles, and upgrade your gear. Do whatever it takes to survive—but remember: You Will Die Here Tonight.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so badly to like this game but in its current state I can't recommend it.Pros:- Really cool idea to change up combat by having it take place in first person while the rest of the game is top-down third person- Gorgeous low poly visualsCons:- Combat is trivial, in many cases you can avoid fighting entirely. When you do happen to get caught in combat, its usually against a single enemy that you can kill with the knife and mashing A to push them off of you, you will take no damage if you do it right.- Boss fights are designed to kill you so you just need to throw enough bodies (or health packs) at it until it goes down. Damage dealt to the boss is permanent. They also give you infinite ammo (at least for the pistol and SMG) so the resources and ammo upgrades you collected become useless.- Puzzles pretty scattered but not very deep, the clues are often written down in the exact order you need to do things. When it seems like there may be a challenge to solve, the game just outright TELLS you the solution to the puzzle.- The game is incredibly short and lacks depth. Just as the game feels like its going to get interesting, you get pushed right into the "true" ending on rails, get handed a big gun and blow things up until you reach the credits.There were so many cool things I thought I was going to have to figure out, maybe by playing through the mission with characters in a different order, or figuring things out overtime with some sort of meta progression, but the game was too short to do anything interesting with those ideas. This game has a survival horror coat of paint, but throws away any tension it builds up with insta-death mechanics and plentiful resources that end up being unnecessary.This game had a ton of potential on the surface and I hope the devs either add more content or make another game entirely building on what they tried to do here!
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Still semi early into the game but it's very fun and intense! you can take your time looting for ammo and health, looking for clues for puzzles and out of nowhere enemies will just swarm you and you have a few seconds to put them down before being killed, once you die it doesn't seem like you can go back since you move on to another character so it adds onto the fear of wanting to stay alive, this has already made me jump a few times from playing it at and the House of the Dead Combat is pretty cool too and fast paced, in the moment you wont know whether to heal or just keep shooting when you're literally one hit from death. If anything try it out for yourself and see if you enjoy it, I hope they add achievements down the road that will be cool, Thumbs up for me so far!
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: A shockingly short game that has a genuinely good concept and flow. In the early to mid game it hits that perfect resident evil feeling with unlocking the map and exploring puzzles. Though some of the puzzles are unbelievably confusing with almost no way to know you actually completed them. Not even completed correctly, just that they are completed. One has you clicking lights off in order, but there's no hint that they're in order, or if some are meant to be left on, etc. Completing it correctly and incorrectly has the exact same response from the game, except you die in one of them when you try to leave the room.Some puzzles can only be completed by specific people, but you can't change between them without getting them killed. Some puzzles can only be completed BY killing a teammate. The game tells you to get everyone out alive, but that's not actually possible. So you just feel like you're in a losing state the entire game.It's a good game, with a good gameplay loop, but it needs a lot of work if they make another one.

_childDocuments_.review: Resident Evil, Resident Evil Gaiden, House of the Dead, and Cabin in the Woods are all things I would use to describe quite what this game is like. A true gem, this title manages to be meta and subvert what people might assume to be a "Resident Evil 1 clone."I can only hope that they continue to expand on this game, as something truly special lies here for long time fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts out great and ends up being just okay. The premise is very good but the execution isn't. I would have loved if the different characters actually spawned in different locations and could meet up somewhere where you could switch between them for different tasks. Currently they all just take turns dying until one reaches the end, which feels disappointing after the tutorial run in which two character do meet up. It's really nice that all characters have comments for each others' deaths, but it isn't enough to feel satisfying.While it's a pretty cool idea to move the player into a House of the Dead style perspective in combat it falls flat with the complete lack of proper encounter design, which is the key to such games. In practice you mostly enter the first person view to kill a single zombie coming at you from the front, which quickly becomes rather tedious and feels mostly pointless. For a game presenting itself as inspired by Resident Evil I really cannot understand why you can freely refill your ammo at a certain place when there are collectible ammo boxes spread around the map (like in RE) and the enemies are mostly finite. It would have been much better if the player had to conserve his ammo and loot the corpses of the dead teammates.  The bosses felt mostly frustrating in my opinion as you cannot properly interrupt their attack like you can in HotD, even though you can use the shield which feels pretty silly.The story is mostly good even though I would have preferred something along the lines of a time paradox or simply having it be a single scenario without a meta game. The varied monologues for the different characters felt like a nice touch but it was largely ruined by the overuse of comedy, both the nerd and the stupid guy are almost exclusively written as joke characters which just ends up being cringe unfortunately.I would ultimately still recommend this game to people who are big fans of the first Resident Evil and want to try an interesting take on that general scenario. The game is short enough to not overstay its welcome after the strong start, otherwise I wouldn't have recommended it to RE fans either. I hope the developers or someone else gives this concept another try and does so more competently than they have done here.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: As everyone else has mentioned, this is very much Resident Evil meets House of the Dead The game took me about 5 hours to beat while taking my time to complete everything. Combat is fun, and ranges from easy to slightly challenging depending on the enemy. Puzzles are fun, slightly more difficult than modern RE games, but also more sensible than ye old games a la King's Quest.The part that really makes this game special, however, is the story. What starts as your cops in a haunted mansion develops into so much more, similar to Resident Evil, but the developers of this game have clearly gone their own way.I heavily recommend grabbing this gem of a game and look forward to what the developers plan on doing next.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, You Will Die Here Tonight isn't a bad game by any stretch but one that ultimately just made me want to pick up the Original RE1/Remake again. Visually the game looks great, with it's low-poly aesthetic and it clearly captures the Spencer Mansion vibe, but it's all over within two to three hours, and honestly there wasn't enough there to warrant another run-through. I felt the game deliberately sets you up to die to cheap deaths (clue is in the title sure...) but given I was carefully navigating the mansion to die to something you really wouldn't know your first play-through and with the intention of saving all the team-mates, just took away the apprehension to the extent I just thought well I am going to die regardless so what difference does it make. The manual save in my view lures you into that initial thought process but its effectively worthless other than taking a natural break from the game, because as soon as a character dies it automatically overwrites your save file. Story-wise, nothing ground breaking or particularly captivating, the puzzles were okay outside of the deaths you suffer if you make one mistake. Combat was "meh" and got repetitive quickly particularly with the grabbing and spamming of the mouse button, it would of been nice to see additional visual damage if I had shot a zombie in the arm holding an axe etc. for me to blow it off with a shotgun before it threw it, or shoot it in the legs to prevent it from chasing me, it's very easy to just run away from a fight. I honestly would of just preferred the traditional combat format of the Survival Horror genre. There is only four zombie models, a spider, and a knight enemy as well.Whilst I sound critical its entirely my view and as I said at the start it's not a bad game, and I do hope and look forward to see what the devs bring out in the future but unless you really want a Spencer Mansion nostalgia dose I would look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Only wish the "multiple character" aspect mattered. The only difference between the bunch is movement speed and their own "personal goals". Other than that, they all function rather the same, the old guy can melee kill pretty much anything in 4 swings. Story premise was really good, ended up feeling kinda flat towards the end. Other than that, great game, fun to play and cool aesthetic. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is not for everyone, but if you like this kind of thing, try it out!It's a complete love letter to RE1 and funhouse dungeon-style deaths in horror games. Deaths can feel (and are) brutal and unfair, which is the point of the game. It could be exasperating, but not to the point of ruining the game experience. There is an in-game mechanic to help soften the blow of losing your squad mates, though, so it's not entirely pointless. Combat isn't really intuitive and the puzzles are pretty basic. That being said, I actually think the shotgun puzzle was pretty clever.I will come out of the gate and say the whole 'teammates dying to help others' is more-or-less making sure you complete their small side missions so that their progress carries onto another character, or maintaining the previous damage done to a boss, not more involved than I used to hope. Not a highlight, but that's okay. I actually like the character writing a lot, each member of ARIES endeared themselves to me by the time I finished the game (some slower than others, Mike).My big issue is the controls are a bit buggy if you use PC controls. Reloading out of combat bugged out sometimes.I personally really liked the ending, but I can see why it doesn't jive with people. I can't really say much about it without revealing spoilers, but I think it comes down to your own personal genre tastes.That being said, the laser puzzle genuinely tilted me, wasted 5 minutes, and I hate it with every fibre of my being.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute love letter send up to Resident Evil and the survival horror genre, the game really keeps you on your toes and I greatly enjoyed the twist which was very well executed. There we're multiple explanations available for what was occurring, and the reveal of what was actually going on really impressed me. The developers clearly are fans of the genre and know the meta around it, played with it, and really created something unique. If you enjoy Resident Evil, and the survival horror genre I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: - Combines elements of RPG action and arcade shooters, resulting in challenging but fair gameplay.- The graphics give off personality and a pleasant nostalgic air that will transport you to the mid-90s.- The combat system is very original and fun.- The game has some unique surprises that make it stand out. in the genre.- The developers are preparing big and juicy new features ("professional mode", wink wink) to be added for free!- The game can be frustrating at first until you get used to its gameplay, which mixes a semi-isometric third-person view most of the time and first-person combat.- In some moments the death of our character is necessary. Luckily we have a team of six characters to play with.You Will Die Here Tonight is a game that defies the conventions of the horror genre. Its original combat system and excellent puzzles keep players on their toes, while its "unofficial" roguelike concept adds a layer of tension and strategy. If you fall in battle, it's not the end of the game, but the beginning of a new experience with a different character. Each character has unique abilities, from crafting med kits to upgrading weapons, which adds a dimension of customization and strategy. In addition, the fact that bulkier characters can inflict and take more damage but move slower adds a level of realism and depth to the game.e.8,5/10.You Will Die Here Tonight is a horror game with a unique blend of action and horror, which becomes a wonderful ode to classic survival horror. If you like the genre, and are captivated by its graphics, it's a must-have.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit (11.8.23): There was a bug report here, but the devs work fast and patched the game. You should now no longer softlock in the finale.I feel pretty confident calling this the Signalis of Resident Evils.It's not ethereal and relationshippy like Signalis, which Signalis gets from drawing on Silent Hill for inspiration. Instead, You Will Die Here Tonight is punishing and tactical and hammy, aligning with its Resident Evil DNA.Essentially, this is a game where you play as the entire team sent to the Spencer Mansion. Combat is extremely lethal. Traps often unilaterally oneshot you. Dying generally gives you clues on how to proceed, and each character picks up from where the last one left off.There's a lot of very good, very necessary convenience features baked in. You have a small home base with some limited heals and weapon refills. Different characters can interact with items brought back to the base to craft upgrades for the team. Progression is retained between characters, and if you find a teammate corpse (assuming they died in a way that left a corpse, and assuming they didn't reanimate) you can pick their supplies off of it.Controls are clunky but feel smooth once you've gotten accustomed to them. There aren't a lot of screen prompts, and there's a bunch of stuff to remember, so you'll absolutely take some deaths from getting the controls wrong, and it's simply part of the game's learning curve.Combat will also get you killed periodically (different characters have different hp pools,) but it's some of the most fun combat you'll get in a survival horror that isn't Condemned Criminal Origins. Instead of the typical resi snap aim system, where you just spend resources to down targets you don't feel like jinking, You Will Die Here Tonight puts you into a House Of The Dead style minigame. Enemies have attack patterns. You can rapid fire into vulnerable spots to cause knockback and interrupt attacks. Ammo *is* a concern, but there's a much higher skill cap than just appropriate ammo management.Now, as far as the game's writing goes, I wasn't expecting much, but it's honestly pretty solid. The tone and content are sort of what you'd expect from rpgmaker horror, but genuinely B+ tier rpgmaker horror. Each squadmate has a distinct personality and reacts differently to different events, and while the writing is never intrusive, the personalities are pretty charming.Now, at the time of my writing this, there isn't really a walkthrough. This means your enjoyment of the game may be ultimately linked to your tolerance for Resident Evil puzzles. However, if you like looking for double meanings in notes and repeatedly yeeting yourself into the spike pit under the shotgun, this might even be a plus.For me, You Will Die Here Tonight has been an absolute gem. I will update when I roll credits, but for now, based on what I've encountered, this is a must play. If you like classic resi, grab it at full price.Edit: There's multiple endings, finding secrets feels legitimately like discovering things you weren't meant to see, and people are starting to assemble walkthroughs. I now feel comfortable saying that even if resi puzzles aren't your thing, you can enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice idea. Its like something of a retro Resident Evil (and it wears its inspiration on its sleeve) with a little pinch of Rogue-Lite. Watch out for spoilers:You choose one of six characters and explore a Resident Evil 1 like mansion and when you die, you choose another character. Some characters have certain abilities. So one Character can upgrade your guns, another can hack computers etc. etc. Each character has slightly unique comments on everything that happens and you can often even find the dead teammates and have your character comment on it. When all your characters die you... start over. You lose all your key items, but you keep all equipment so subsequent runs become easier to a certain degree. Gameplay is mostly fine but a better defensive system would've been much appreciated. Against most enemies you can break free by just smashing buttons, but bosses are often very time sensitive in your chance to push them back and the game does not explain this well enough in my opinion. The boss in the attic is the worst offender in this, in my opinion.Most puzzles are completely fine, but sometimes there are puzzles that are just absolutely weird. The animal head puzzle is very weird and you can easily miss the way to find the true ending because you didn't use a certain character to do a certain thing. BUT - I still think this game was very well done and I had a lot of fun in playing.
