_childDocuments_.review: First, a video overview Stream subscribe to my channel and give me likes. I would like to start this review with one, at first glance, not quite unambiguous statement, which, however, you can hardly argue with - Resident Evil of 1996 is a perfect survival horror in a vacuum. It's a pillar of the genre that could very well stand in the House of Weights and Measures - by saying survival horror we mean Resident Evil, by saying Resident Evil we mean survival horror. Yes, it's not quite fair to the other forerunners of the genre - Alone in the Dark and Clock Tower, but now the influence of the latter has waned, but from Resident ideas are taken by almost everyone - from major publishers to single developers.That's why, due to the focus of the review, I would like to ask you one question - where is the border between inspiration by a great ideal and its mindless copying. I will probably be able to answer this question only by the end of this review, and that's why, in order to add worthy arguments to my final conclusion, I think it's necessary to thoroughly analyze all the elements of the new indie horror, which miraculously came to my review, You Will Die Here Tonight.Cycle I. The Delight of DiscoveryYou Will Die Here Tonight begins with an introduction to a reference to the STARS squad from Resident Evil, the ARIES squad. No, I'm lying. You Will Die Here Tonight starts with a direct reference to Resident Evil - a creepy voice with spoofed effects saying the name of the game. Getting acquainted with the team is quite pleasant - none of them take a character from the original, but have their own (albeit just as clichéd) . The developers didn't even skimp on creating racial diversity - the local Wesquero-substitute (in terms of performing the function of team captain) acquired a dark skin tone, and Barry-substitute - Mexican roots.The team of dummies, however, is not the only discovery that the introduction provides us with - here we are also taught a unique combat system - the shooting of evil with a first-person view in the manner of the well-known House of the Dead. The idea is undoubtedly fresh, but in my opinion, it could be formed only in some such situation:- So, our main source of inspiration is Resident Evil, but it seems to me that it is not enough to create a full-fledged game. What else do you think we could be inspired by?- Well, look. Resident is an abode, aka home. Evil is obviously evil. And the evil in our game will be zombies.- I haven't heard of Zombie House, to be honest.- Well, zombies are the walking dead, which makes them dead, which makes them dead.- And... House of the Dead?The shooting itself is done quite nicely - on pressing the key we stand on one place with the ability to rotate 360° - aiming in this way became much more convenient than when using the tank control from survival horror classics. Also in the game was added and quite interesting feature that helps to avoid permanent damage - the ability to push away any enemy with a quick press of a button. However, the most useful, to my taste, was another one - you can always escape from all battles, thus saving yourself ammo or changing the position to a more favorable one.Cycle II. Diving into the abyssStarting from this part of the review, the number of spoilers will exceed all imaginable and unthinkable limits, and therefore, if you have something against it - go to the very end, because for the sake of consistency of thought I will not hide separate pieces of text, but will consider the whole game.So, discovery #1, which the player makes after completing the prologue - You Will Die Here Tonight turns out to be a roguelike. However, not exactly a roguelike, but rather a roguelite or even a game with "rogue" elements. And this means only one thing - death is your main enemy and your main friend. However, it is expressed in a rather strange way - each character has a unique mechanics - one has the ability to pump weapons, another has the ability to create first aid kits, and the third has a separate quest chain, which opens when you perform certain actions. That's why there is a sense to change characters, but the problem is that regardless of that You Will Die Here Tonight is an extremely linear game (linear roguelike, it's about time), and gameplay for different characters feels absolutely the same.To summarize, I would like to say one thing - You Will Die Here Tonight is far from the best game, and far from the best survival horror. It really has enough flaws that prevent you from fully enjoying this project - the creators did not have enough imagination to bring the ideas that were put into the project to mind. And therefore, I give the game scores like this:Visual - 3/5 - a standard stylized retro picture that has a slightly unusual isometric perspective, which allowed to make the locations quite interesting.Story - 3/5 - not a bad postmodern statement that slightly reimagines Resident Evil, while often following the original stamps closely.Gameplay - 3/5 - I was originally going to give it a two due to the fact that most of the mechanics that are introduced in the game don't function at a decent level, but the rather original idea of mixing Resident Evil and House of the Dead gameplay still made me raise the grade slightly.Bottom line: 6/10. A mediocre game that brings almost no idea that introduces to mind. Also, it's very short. And, answering the question posed in the beginning - distinguishes mindless copying from deep inspiration the quality of execution of ideas brought from outside - from other projects or invented from scratch. And here, creaking my soul, I'm ready to say that You Will Die Here Tonight still has some merits that prevent me from calling it a mindless clone. But next time, if the developers from Spiral Bound Interactive don't rethink their approach to game creation - I would be careful to buy their next project.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, hear me out. The game is not the most (cough-cough) polished product ever. It may be overpriced for its ~4 hours runtime. But damn it is fun.All nods to RE1 are in place, some are subtle, some are incredibly over-the-top. Cross-over with House of The Dead worked for me, although I still have no idea how to use the shield. Exploration is smooth enough, only one puzzle saw me resorting to guessing and general flow was really nice.But you should be ready for trash (in all the best meanings) when you head in. The game knows it's trash and embraces it. I can only commend this dedication.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good, if a little frustrating at times with enemy encounters. This a full blown resident evil copy in terms of aesthetic and puzzles, which I don't know acts as a love letter to the series or just full on laziness to create something unique. Absolutely loved it. It's short but sweet! Give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic oldschool meets newschool survival horror title that absolutely knocks it out of the park on all fronts. This is the kind of game I hope to find when I go looking for indie horror games. Smart (and often funny) writing, great gameplay and an aesthetic that nails the retro look. _childDocuments_.review: As the title suggests, players will die many, many times in this game. However, while this may sound like a Souls-like type of challenge, failure and loss of life are tied into the main narrative of the game. Without spoiling much of the surprisingly intricate plot, You Will Die Here Tonight features an element of looping that takes into account the player’s actions in previous lives. Taking control of the various members of Aries, there are different parts of the level that can be explored, with each mistake or dangerous curiosity leading to new discoveries and understandings of the best course of action to take.The developer is definitely ambitious with this title, and Spiral Bound has to be commended for going in a different direction to make the game feel different from its peers. However, there is still quite a bit of polishing that needs to be done in order to make this as great as it can be. My experience featured a variety of bugs, from navigational issues (the characters kept getting stuck in the level geometry at odd angles) to unresponsive button prompts (it was impossible to switch to the knife as a primary weapon if I had anything else equipped) and soft locks (my character got stuck twice in different scenarios in which I entered combat way too soon, only to trigger an endless dialogue loop that could never proceed since the other subject was long dead).Spiral Bound is hard at work fixing You Will Die Here Tonight, taking into consideration player feedback of all kind to make sure that everyone who buys the title is getting an enjoyable experience. Despite some janky moments, this is a thrilling and inventive indie title that shows a lot of genuine passion for survival horror and underdog games like RE: Gaiden. Worth checking out for genre fans looking for something different and fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: There are some cool ideas to arcade-ify the classic survival horror experience here, but ultimately You Will Die Here Tonight is more fun to talk about, think about and look at...than it is to actually play. Putting RE1's Spencer Mansion under the lens of a faster action game where characters can die quickly but the game will continue with the next party member means that the puzzles are more stressful than usual because there are far more death traps to worry about. They have a lot of cheeky fun with suddenly killing you, but death is not the end of a playthrough by any means. Similarly, enemies hit hard and fast, and will chase you everywhere, but you get a lot more ammo than you normally would, so you're encouraged to stand your ground as much as run away. It adds up to a faster, leaner survival horror adventure, which is a neat idea but it's to a fault here.Without much delineation between characters besides combat prowess and some upgrade opportunities, it makes your choices in who to bring feel hollow. Only half the cast is required to be interacted with at all in order to beat the game. On the flipside, what equipment gets brought over between deaths feels entirely arbitrary and makes keeping track of what is ostensibly a "time loop" story much harder than it needs to be. Some key items are ditched while others are brought over and can lead to mild sequence breaking; however, there are also permanent ammo upgrades, and they're easy enough to get that just shooting the zombies is more manageable than tangling with the weird Doorkickers mechanics of checking keyholes and locking doors to force zombies through choke points. So with this game's wrinkles being as shallow as they are, all you're left with is a very basic survival horror throwback that has very little atmosphere or difficulty, even with some half-decent puzzles. The way the combat plays out in first person is a neat trick, echoing Gaiden and Dead Aim of all games, and the pixellated filter can hide monsters in plain sight for some surprising spooks, but it doesn't maintain its edge for long with how easy it is.It all culminates in a plot twist that kind of echoes DRV3 of all games, and it works to justify the gameplay mechanics tying each playthrough together and has enough foreshadowing to be an enjoyable reveal, but as with so many time loop stories, it also means some repetition is required to get the best ending. Even at five hours, it overstays its welcome. Recommended only if you really want a leaner, more action packed Resi clone. Otherwise, I would wait for both price drops and bug fixes before trying it out.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: This is basically Resident Evil Gaiden, but actually plays well.  As well as resurrecting a very interesting gameplay concept and giving it the polish to make it work, its a pretty decent game in its own right. The story has some interesting twists that give a narrative reason for the pseudo-roguelite style of gameplay and the survival horror nods are all there too. I do think that the game could have done with having maybe a couple more areas and the puzzles are quite hand-holdy, but its novel and entertaining and worthy of the survival horror throwback genre.It took me just under hours to 100 percent the game (achievements included) so if you're one of these quantity over quality gamers, you may want a very deep discount before buying, but it was certainly worth what I paid and I hope the devs go from strength to strength.  I'd love to see a sequel with the same gameplay style but with an expanded scope.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it STARTED fun, but after awhile it just became a bunch of unnecessarily convoluted nonesense.  What was once tense became punishment for wanting to actually progress.  I'm not even talking about difficulty, I'm talking about the game being just a chore in places.  I can kind of see what they were going for, but I ultimately feel punished for trying to play the game.  I honestly wish I was still in refund range, this game should not have been released yet.  It has some nasty bugs, it seems to have retroactively changed how people died mid playthrough leaving me to have to go on a scavenger hunt for bodies, and even the hints I tried to find from the devs seem to refer to stuff that doesn't exist.I really wanted to like this, I really did.  I love the premise, but it's an unfinished game at best, and a pointlessly frustrating one at worst.  I shouldn't be punished for not reading the devs minds on how to play the game, if I'm going to die let me die because I screwed up, not because I'm put into a stupidly fast paced situation with absolutely nothing to work with and nothing to learn from dying.  After 2 hours it became the smashing your head into brick wall simulator.  Maybe later I'll look up how I'm supposed to know how to get the shield and give it another go; right now, however, my interest is as dead as the several people I lost to a suit of armor.

_childDocuments_.review: Much like the games that inspired it; You Will Die Here Tonight has players stepping into the combat boots of a highly-trained police task force, investigating a '2spooky4them' mansion. It's a plotline that's been widely reused since 1996. I'll be honest, I never get tired of this style of setup for a survival horror game. In this case though, YWDHT takes your expectations and flips them on their head as  I can't say too much without spoiling key aspects of the story, but there are six characters to play as throughout the game, some of which have skills that you'll need in order to progress the story and get closer to the truth. Death is not a permanent end for any character, and not everyone is who they claim to be. The more I played, the more mysteries revealed themselves. While the game is loaded with twists and turns, it still remained somewhat predictable and it got pretty convuluted towards the end. It felt as though the game was trying a bit  hard to be unique. Regardless, it was enough to keep my attention and a pretty interesting take on an old plotline.The gameplay is actually how I heard about YWDHT, as it's a unique blend of a 2.5D third-person view during regular gameplay and a 3D first-person perspective during combat. On paper, that sounds pretty neato burrito and it certainly gets the blood flowing during the first handful of enemies. However, shifting into the combat perspective takes a bit of time and not all enemies on screen will appear in the first-person mode at once. This perspective shift eventually gets  and hella' disorienting as more enemies appear throughout the game. I found myself getting so tired of it that I would run straight through enemies and just take the hit instead. Interesting as it may be, I would have preferred the combat to take place in the 2.5D perspective. Apart from that - you'll be faced with the classic trope of trudging around and solving puzzles to find key items that grant access to new areas and elements of the story. Be careful though, most puzzles have deadly consequences if you fail to solve them. In the words of Peter Griffin, I quite enjoy the look of the old late-90's PC RPG game, and the backgrounds for pretty much every location are a delight. Although, the character models themselves appear to be even lower resolution than the backrounds, which is a bit peculiar. The 3D first-person perspective has a resolution-lowering filter applied to match the aesthetic of the rest of the game. Overall, there's nothing particularly remarkable here. The monster designs can be quite cartoonish, which sadly I found detracted from the horror elements. The graphics certainly aren't bad, but they aren't amazing either. That's all I got, comrades.Oh how my ears do so enjoy the spooky creaks and thunderstorms of a creepy old manor. Fortunately, that craving is pretty well satiated throughout the game. YWDHT's setting is appropriately suited for atmospheric horror, and I find that it benefits greatly from limiting the amount of music that plays in game. It adds more weight to the audio cues and rumblings of less-than-human creatures. There's a point or two where the rain, wind, and thunder completely stop; invoking a true "oh sh*tballs" moment that has you bracing for what happens next. The creatures throughout the game are surprisingly terrifying in terms of the noises they make - most notably the withered, starving zombies that you come across. The strained, painful groans they emit are on par with the disturbing breathing of a Regenerator from Resident Evil 4. A downside is that there is a complete lack of voice acting, however that missing element is reminiscent of games from the era that inspired YWDHT. I also want to mention that there are very noticeable audio balance issues during the first-person perspective combat. Things that should be loud are quiet, and things that should be quiet are loud. For example, gunfire is nearly silent - but not all the time. It's strange, I'm not sure what's going on there.In keeping with the games before it, You Will Die Here Tonight leans on it's replayability - to a point where it is pretty much completely necessary to do so in order to get the full story. There's a lot that a player can miss and would be none the wiser to; from dialogue to cutscenes to puzzles to boss battles. It's a deceptively large game and how attractive that replay value is will depend entirely on the individual. As for myself, I got the true ending and solved  all of the puzzles the game has to offer on my first playthrough. It's been a minute since I last played, but I don't recall unlocking any new modes, costumes, or anything that would otherwise incentivise a player to give it another go besides missed dialogue. I also couldn't stand the combat anymore, sorry lads.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe I almost missed this gem due to zero coverage in gaming sites. I have no words on how much I love this game.  Wait, that's not true, here are some words: If you grew up playing OG resident evil on the PS1, this is a beautifully crafted homage to Resident Evil 1 with fresh gameplay elements (House of the Dead inspired  combat system, different characters with different aptitudes representing your lives,) a ridiculously fun combat system, charming old school graphics, great puzzles, and OH MY GOD a story that is actually really good.  If you didn't grow up playing OG resident evil on the Playstation, this is still what I just wrote.  In a year full of amazing games this is, after BG3 of course, my GOTY.  After playing most if not all of the RE1 throwbacks, this is easily the best one hands down.  Run, not shamble, to your virtual gaming store and prepare to be very very happy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty great!A short (depending on how good you are at RE inspired by games) & sweet game, fun twist ending.Only complaints that I have are: the bosses can feel like you basically have to throw bodies at them to defeat them, use all your magnum rounds with one character, then die, come back restocked and reloaded, rinse repeat, and that (as far as I know) health kits/packs do not transfer over to the next character after death.But either way a fun little game, I fully recommend if you like OG Resident Evil style games.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game randomly browsing steam. The Idea is there and I was ready for a nice nostalgia fix. The peephole mechanic and the combat mechanic is a super interesting twist that i was looking forward to. Unfortunately I'm getting hit with soft-lock after soft-lock and it's only the first 10 minutes of the game. TLDR: Too many bugs so early on that make's the game unplayable. I can't recommend this game until there's some pretty significant patches to help the overall quality of the game. I'm not sure why no one else has come across this? or addressed it even. I killed him and after doing so, i walked forward which triggered her dialogue. Problem is Monroe is already dead so after closing out of the dialogue it just reappeared in an endless loop that left me having to restart. _childDocuments_.review: For what this game is, it does it really well, but there are a few issues that I hope get addressed if there's ever another game that's like this one.- Every character's running speed feels AT MOST maybe 0.01% faster- The idea that different characters have the ability to do unique objectives is very cool, but feels wasted by the fact that 1 or 2 characters don't have any sort of unique purpose. It would probably be forgiven if they at least had some noticeable buff like slightly higher melee damage or faster reload speed or higher damage resistance, but if they had those buffs I didn't notice them- I have no clue if I used the shield properly because it didn't seem to have any feedback from blocking attacks- Cringe dialogue. Particularly Mike, who spoke in a very "heh, aren't I self aware" style of quip.- The magnum puzzle. This puzzle needs to be done over as soon as possible, because the solution makes absolutely no sense when compared to the clue.- During the last few seconds of combat, I would often try to use the available time to reload my weapon, but the reload cancels in between the transition to the overhead gameplay. I played through the entire game and never once broke this habit and always felt very disappointed that I would have the reload animation 99% completed in the combat, but it never counted.- No option to rebind keysHope to see more from the makers of this game someday.

_childDocuments_.review: A loving twist on old-school Resident Evil.While the set-up might be very familiar, the execution is refreshingly unique. Gone are the saves of yore. Instead you play as each member of the team, utilizing their unique skills to advance the game until you win or die. All progress, unlocked doors, and items carry over to the next character.While the story is largely a parody of the original Resident Evil, it takes a few unique liberties that really liven up the experience and make it worth seeing through to the end.Embrace death. The title says it all. And as long as you're exploring thoroughly, you'll have a lot more chances at winning than you might think.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: A game inspired by Resident Evil 1, from the squad to the mansion, but the story quickly goes its own direction with some excellent twists and turns.The combat, rather than stick with tank controls, seamlessly goes into a first-person mode (shooting-gallery style), then back to top-downish exploration.The puzzles go farther than just find-the-item-and-put-it-in-the-thing and require some real thought to put all the pieces together (similar to Tortured Souls).  For those that enjoy a little brain challenge, these are great!Lastly, there are some very mild rogue-like elements that will keep you going as squad members fall but the rest of them are able to continue on in their stead.  More than that, I won't say.An excellent game that I played through in one day.  An automatic purchase for any Resident Evil 1 or Tortured Souls fan.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Step into a love letter to classic survival horror with 'You will die here tonight'. The sprawling Breckenridge Estate, with its cobwebbed corners and dusty secrets, oozes with the atmosphere of Resident Evil 1. Tense resource management keeps you on edge, each shot a gamble against the shambling horrors lurking in the shadows. Combat is a satisfying dance of headshots and critical hits, demanding precision and quick thinking.While the game embraces the spirit of its inspirations, some technical quirks might raise eyebrows. The lack of a frame rate cap can lead to occasional dips, strange looking animations, and the audio design during traversal phases can be frustrating. The eerie zombie groans are presented in a strangely panned "mono," offering no directional clues about where the imminent threat could arise. This reliance on trial and error can break the tension built by the game's other elements.Despite these minor setbacks, 'You will die here tonight' is a thrilling throwback to an era of creaky mansions and jump scares (due to the strange audio choice). It's rough around the edges, but its infectious charm and genuinely satisfying gameplay make it a must-play for any horror enthusiast. Just be prepared for a few hair-raising close calls (both from the monsters and the audio!). I eagerly await future updates to tighten the screws and see what this promising developer cooks up next.The achievements are also not really achievement-based in my opinion, they are from what I can see so far, mainly achievements for you falling for traps.TL;DR Resident Evil x House of the Dead with good ammo economy balancing.EDIT:Having played a bit more I can say that most of the puzzles aren't that well crafted, the boss fights are just an endurance round and you can't shoot projectiles out of the air. There is a certain "unfair" factor when it comes to the combat. I've just arrived to the garden and I don't know if I care to finish the game mainly because the puzzle quality just isn't there. I can't really elaborate more on that without spoilers so I'll rate the game as "Playable".

_childDocuments_.review: After the patch, with many of the progression blocker bugs of the early game cleaned up, I've been able to push a good distance into the game.  It captures the classic Resident Evil game feel and puzzles extremely well.  Lots of good variations on old memory and logic puzzles pop up, with some suitably grisly punishments for making mistakes on them.  Thanks to the multiple characters and lives conceit, with your past failures memorialized in bloody fashion throughout the mansion, failure can be an oddly entertaining thing.The first person combat is a bit of a mixed bag - it definitely can feel very gripping at moments, but it can also start to feel strangely routine, and with no ability to move during them, you quickly start feeling like some of the fights are more annoying than enjoyable.  The first time that you get smacked upside the head by a zombie's sledgehammer because you ran out of bullets before stunning him, with no real ability to just... step back will likely just feel frustrating.  There are moments when you think you've cleared the threats, and you anxiously swing your gun around to try to find the last foe that work very well, especially with the maids and some of the other later opponents.  The thing that makes this the most awkward, though, is the way that ammo and battles are ultimately handled; the zombies and other enemies appear to be fixed in number to a given mission and world state, so you can clear the area of opponents, run back to the ammo box, and replenish back up to a point.  This makes saving up ammo thoughtfully less of a practical necessity, and generally pushes you to carefully clear out the game world to let you focus your attention on the puzzles.  That seems like it fights some against the fundamental survivor horror feel, since that means that you can ensure a lot more safety, and the resource management angle is less of a contributor to the anxiety of the situation.Outside of puzzles and combat, some aspect of exploring the mansion prove overall awkward.  Controls can be a bit sticky at times, requiring you to try some inputs repeatedly or in slightly different locations - something of a general problem with the camera angle and positioning required for the game to verify what you're really interacting with, I'm sure, but in some spots it can be a bit of a nuisance.  There's some strange decisions around what is communicated where, such as not being able to see how many bullets you have for each gun in the inventory, only when it's equipped and you tap the R key.  Healing, likewise, feels like a strange interaction, since it's stuck into holding the E key and then selecting and applying a healing item; this feels clunkier than it really needs to be.  This does have the benefit of forcing you to intentionally heal, and it takes time in the world so doing so when there's zombies coming at you is a time and positioning management question, but in practice it mostly just means that you don't heal unless you're safe or you have no alternative.  It would make a bit more sense if it was bound to one of your weapon slots, so it was a bit more of a gear trade-off, and then you could simple switch to it and start applying, rather than it being a completely separate slot set.  This is further complicated by how many healing items you can carry being somewhat different between characters; most can carry 2, while the medic can carry 4, but the nature of the separate slots and the UI involved doesn't make that immediately apparent.  There's certainly logic there - the medic character getting to carry extra medical supplies absolutely follows - but it was definitely a head scratcher initially, until I'd made enough progress in to get a clear sense of each character's little benefits.Story and dialog is a highlight here, with each character having their own commentary and perspectives.  The game makes use of the multiple character conceit very well, and sells it with all the small details, including different characters moving at different speeds, each one having their particular bonuses, and so on.  It makes what might otherwise look like a pure RE nostalgia wank feel like its own distinct experience.Overall, pretty solid, worth the price if you like survival horror games.Game has some positive qualities and real potential, but there's a lot of sequence break bugs that are easy to run into, and they can stick you in infinite dialog loops, block forward progress, or otherwise screw with the experience in just plain stupid ways.  When you have to restart the game three times due to the autosave being AFTER your game has been progression blocked, and the tutorial is unskippable, you probably just stop caring.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: A familiar setting with some twists that make it worth your while.A team of six go into a mansion to apprehend a murderer, but as with most Survival Horror games, it does not go well. The team gets separated and is forced to try and survive.A top down exploration with a splash of what looks akin to a rail gun shooter combat system, its clear the game takes a few notes from Resident Evil 1, House of The Dead 1, and Resident Evil Gaiden. There is a slight camp to it that makes some of its characters and moments stand out. There is a level of "done this before", but that adds to the joy as it is a familiar setting and vibe, with some extra bits added to it so it doesn't feel like its copying other game while the art style of its world add to the retro aesthetic it means to have, and does so fantastically.The big 'gimmick' is that you take control of one of the team members, with each of them acting as a 'life' as you explore, solve puzzles, and fend off monsters. Resources are not shared in the run, so if you pick up ammo or healing as one character, it will not be there if you end up picking up another character, and any excess ammo will have to be picked up from the previous character corpse. However, progression is shared, as finding weapons, shortcuts, solved puzzles, and key items will have them stay in your inventory, remain unlocked, stay completed until a restart.The squad is expendable to a degree, and failing to properly solve a puzzle or poorly managing resources/combat encounters can leave you dead, making you switch to another team member. Each of them have their strengths, such as Mr. Eric Downs having the smallest healing inventory, but in exchange, he is the only character who can modify guns using kits you find to enhance your combat prowess. And upgrades are carried over when you switch to a new character, adding to that strategic value of who you play as.Overall, I enjoyed the game. It was a fun romp running through everything, and I managed to escape my first run through. My only "negative" is that as an indie game, it is on the short side of a few hours. It is clearly set up to be played through multiple times, trying to keep everyone alive, and multiple runs are very clearly a theme with this game. If anything, the length made me hungry for more, I would very much be down for another game.In the meantime, enjoy a quote from our resident gun nut Mr. Downs:"You thought being a giant spider would save you, but you forgot one thing: I'm an ******!"
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: You Will Die Here Tonight turned out to be a hidden gem of 2023, and an excellent example of the new wave of retro survival horrors that freshen up the classic formula with clever twists (the other recent examples being Alisa and SIGNALIS).YWDHT is a great love letter to Resident Evil 1 / Gaiden, combining very well paced top-down exploration with fast and aggressive first-person combat encounters. On top of that all there's a semi-permadeath mechanic, vaguely similar to ZombiU: you take control over the whole "Alpha team", one character at a time. If your character dies, you're moved on to the next one. But there's a twist... more than one, in fact (but I'm not going to spoil anything).The trailers alone were enough to capture my attention, but the actual game exceeded my expectations. Despite a few mild inconveniences (the controls cannot be rebound and may be just a bit awkward with KB&M, there's no mouse pointer in menus, and I did encounter a couple of bugs—no progress blockers, though), there was something fun to be had at every turn. Charming homages to the classics (including a "Barry", a "Rebecca", and a ridiculously over-the-top "Chris"), challenging combat (especially at early stages of the game), multi-layered mystery — YWDHT has it all.A definite must-play for all survival horror fans out there.P.S. The game is great on Steam Deck (even though it's not officially verified), and cloud saves work without a hitch.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, great puzzles. A brilliant homage to Resident Evil: Gaiden and a sound mix between Resident Evil and House of the Dead. I only wish there were more shooting galleries and the game had a little more length to it. Otherwise, hidden gem. Definitely not worth full price, but on sale: a fun day of enjoyment :)
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Criminally overlooked little gem of a game. Fully conscious that Survival Horror is a bit of a niche, specifically when looking at the classic camera perspective (fixed) games rather than the modern homogenised over-the-shoulder camera type popularised by the constant stream of remakes these days. Within this niche though I feel that the team at Spiral Bound have accomplished something quite unique. What this game is a remix of sorts of Resident Evil 1, borrowing most of its concepts, but adding their own interesting twists along the way. The puzzles are great and I personally love the devs leaning into this aspect as much as they did. Combat is well implemented, even if a tad tricky to get the hang of initially, but it looks good, controls well and does its job to keep the tension up (especially at the beginning). The way the game transitions from top-down to first person is very well done I feel. It feels crisp. All in all this one's a must play for any of the original RE enjoyers, and a solid recommendation for anyone else interested in a spooky and original little adventure filled with twists and turns of all sorts. A note on the difficulty. If it feels punishing initially, just stick with it as once you progress the tools and mechanics to make things easier will start falling into place. Think roguelike! Great job, Spiral Bound!
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: You Will Die Here Tonight is a nice homage to both the original Resident Evil and Cabin in the Woods, with a twist on both gameplay and story, and an amazing ending that makes one's brain truly fold onto itself. A sweet, but short little game that's wholeheartedly worth the money and the time spent on it. Well done, Spiral Bound!
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially Resident Evil Gaiden, but far more playable. Overall I enjoyed my experience: exploring the mansion is fun, combat works pretty well, and there were some decent puzzles. The negative: there were some puzzles that were logically unintuitive and the game is fairly short for its price. I wish the game did more with the shared progress/info from playing a succession of characters too.If the premise, trailer, and mechanics seem interesting to you, pick it up, but you may want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only about 2~ish hours into the game proper, but so far this game is a blast.If you like Classic Resident Evil, good chances are you'll like this game too. It offers a unique mesh of gameplay while throwing homage after homage to RE and feels like an darling love letter while still retaining its own identity. It plays like top-down RE and switches to House of the Dead style combat.The game opens up to more mechanics once you let yourself die and switch to another character (and seriously, the dialogue on blonde Redfield is just *chef's kiss*), so don't be afraid to die like I did.I've seen people complain about the controls, but other than not knowing how to switch weapons in the beginning (tutorial notes might need tweaking to address this), or learning that you can't reload if you're near an interactable, I never had any problems. They're very intuitive and I can't see how anyone thinks they're clunky.The puzzles so far are more classic RE than Remake RE, so expect a little more brain juice demand with the caveat of killing you if you mess up. And you'll probably need to mess up at certain puzzles to switch characters, because the game's combat is frighteningly easy if you're decent at FPS games, As long as you stick to a certain effective-but-tedious playstyle, you will have more than enough ammo. It's unfortunate that the game gives you this easy difficulty straight off the bat, but hopefully it ramps up later on.The writing is also solid. Usually with indie titles or even AAA games by new studios, I find myself rolling my eyes back into my throat at god-awful dialogue  That's not the case here. The game knows exactly what it is -- It's not trying to be on The Last Of Us' level, or win an Emmy. It's campy B-movie horror schlock that gives you a short burst of entertainment. Out of the 3 characters I've played, their personalities feel interesting enough to keep me from getting bored (or annoyed).However, I'd would like to suggest some things. The ability to store health items would be great since I don't want to waste my big health kits after finding a smaller one. Please god, make the ~5s cutscene of your character waking up every time you start the game skippable too. An FPS game not having a sensitivity slider is also mind-boggling to me in this day and age.All in all, I'm really loving this game. I'll likely continue my playthrough once I know certain save-file deleting bugs have been fixed. If you're an RE lover like I am, though, I wouldn't hesitate in buying this game right now and supporting the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Old Resi meets new Resi. Isometric exploration with first person combat, putting you in control of the headshots makes for a fun gameplay loop! Puzzles which don't go into the tedious to solve which is a nice change of pace from similar games with only a few taking a bit of time (or context) to wrap your head around. (also no need to fight with an inventory system.) Death not being the end of the run is a nice touch with going back in with another squad member, progress made being carried over from member to member.  The game is HEAVILY inspired by Resident Evil 1 (even mentioning biohazard a few too many times to not take notice). Whether this is a bad thing is up to you but it does throw it's own themes and ideas into the story and it's main twists and concepts seem to be unique with some direct throwbacks added in. All and all, definitely worth the asking price if you like the old resi/silent hill games!
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: To the point=====================A Survival Horror..... sorta Rougelite game ?! It all works so well and is definitely worth your time/moneyGood Stuff=====================- The core gameplay loop ( Try something, succeed, try something, die, repeat) is actually super enjoyable and you keep just enough between deaths that you can feel the sense of progression.- The puzzles are largely fine, barring one or two where even a poo-brain like myself could figure them out without a ton of difficulty.The game gives you good reason to play each character, aside from their unique traits, by putting things into the map that only they can use to make future runs easier. People can collect unique plants in the manor, for instance, that the Medic character can turn into multiple medpacks that spawn each run. These bonuses never feel overpowered with the exception of one or two of the gun upgrades.- The creators really understood what makes the early RE games so enjoyable and the game has a fantastic mix of great moments, cheesy dialogue and, yes, a ton of throwbacks and references in game for old bastards such as myself to stumble on.Bad Stuff=====================- The combat can be a bit difficult to get used to at first, I know I had issues switching between weapons in critical moments, but you'll get the hang of it- There's not a lot of enemy variety here and although the few that we get do have some small variants between them it's not strong enough to make them stand out much.- The game is pretty short, taking me roughly 4 hours and that was with a few re-attempts, this is more of a nitpick but some people might be turned off by it.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: "You Will Die Here Tonight" is a survival horror adventure game in which you control an entire set of characters 1 by 1! The retro graphics create a nostalgic feeling which will remind you of another time. It's a top-down game with first person combat and that makes for a fun mix! One of the best horror games in a long time! It combines adventure with action and some puzzle elements. Fight for survival and remember.. "You will die here tonight". That's a fact.. But will a death be in vain? Or will you make good use of the information? Death is only the beginning!The resources and ammo are scarse, so don't go wasting them pointlessly! Your actions and decisions will either help or endanger the remaining members of your unit. Take good aim, blast your enemies! Use your wits to figure out what's going on in the mansion, uncover the mystery and try to save yourself and whoever else you can. Can you do it? Are you up to the task? Will you solve the puzzles involved or die trying?Seeing the story through many perspectives of colorful characters is neat! It's also great how you combine information. The story is interesting and the horror has been done well. From the atmosphere, to the artwork, to the monsters and the storyline you will experience fear! You will like some and hate some.. But you will be glad all of them are at your disposal!Good soundtrack! Convenient and responsive controls! The game runs smoothly without any lag or anything that could get you killed. The aesthetics are awesome, same as the sounds used. Clever puzzles. Interesting characters, dialogue and plot.You'll want to replay it and try something else!  If you like what you see on the video, don't hesitate to buy it; it won't deceive you!It will keep you at the edge of your seat for the duration and you won't want to quit it!For more reviews, follow my curator

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big scaredy-cat, so I'm not faring the best against the evil zombies, but I am really enjoying the art in this game, the puzzles, and the intriguing storyline! _childDocuments_.review: A good take on survival horror with some rogue-lite elements. Don't be  afraid to die - it is part of the game. But the game is not  cruel - even if you run out of survivors, you still get a chance to continue without needed to restart the game from scratch.The puzzles were challenging enough without needing to resort to a guide and the unique shooting mechanic was pretty fun and tense. The story also had some nice twists along the way.A solid recommendation if you are in the mood for a medium length horror experience.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun zombie puzzle game that takes place in the  Breckenridge Estate. It starts out like your typical old school Resident Evil game, but adds a nice twist on the whole "You Will Die Here Tonight" theme. This makes the game a bit like Obscure meets Resident Evil with the game having 6 characters to play as. Each character has different stats and abilities that can assist the team. One character can make first aid kits, one character upgrades guns, etc. The gameplay throws you into FPS for combat. While this lets you get a good shot on enemies, you're locked into place. With regular enemies you can choose to run and reposition, but when it comes to bosses you're in it until you either win, or die. To offset this, bosses do not regenerate health. If party member A takes out 85 percent of a bosses health and dies, then party member B only needs to take out the remaining 15 percent to win. The only thing that annoyed me were some of the puzzles. They can be really poorly written and cause some headaches. My personal bug bear was the magnum puzzle. But luckily, only a couple of puzzles are like that and the rest tend to make sense. All in all, this is a fun, short, zombie game that is heavily inspired by the classic Resident Evil series. I recommend picking it up if you're a fan of that type.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: A very good top-down, classic Resident Evil inspired game with roguelite elements. Combat is unique as it shifts the perspective to first person mode when attacking and looks a bit like The House of the Dead. The only thing that annoyed me a bit was getting infected when zombies bite you, but there are systems to manage that.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: What the Hell?Resident Evil homage with House of the Dead gunplay, its an interesting mix. There are two problems with the game, one minor, one confusing. The small problem has to do with ammunition. Technically, you have infinite reserves. If you're ever low, just go back to base and restock. The reality of this is that, because there are so many enemies, you are constantly going back and forth between supply points to refill your ammunition. It makes the pacing tedious and stupid. Resident Evil balanced ammunition and enemies. This doesn't. They just peppered a bunch of enemies all over the place and let you do the work of deciding to run back or not. The confusing problem has to do with the ending. I'm pretty sure I somehow skipped some important exposition because I went from "Hmm, there's more to meet the eye here. What's really going on with this mansion?", to "Final Battle with the mastermind and blasting my way through with an infinite ammo grenade launcher". I don't think its a glitch. There was a key, I grabbed it, I opened the door, and *bam* - final chapter. I think the problem is that the game assumed I would die more and was preset to follow instructions in order, but, because I just went right to the key that triggered the ending, I skipped a bunch of important dialogue. Anyway, its still interesting, but not amazing. Grab it if you feel like it.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't feel mixing corridor shooter combat in a survival horror map with rougelite elements was a good combination. _childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: A good survival horror shooter rpg set in a mansion whose resident is evil.It is generally good and through its mechanic of dying and retrying as a new team member you keep coming closer to the true ending. Its combat is pretty unique - you enter a different "map" where you aim and shoot like in an old arcade shooting games, with enemies slowly approaching. Melee ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks when you have to use it - only one character can actually get anywhere with melee.Speaking of teammates you have six. They don't have clear stats given to you outright but they do have stats. All characters have a speed stat and melee damage stat. Shooting damage seems uniform, though some characters seem to aim faster. Maybe. Others have skills for very specific actions - one guy can upgrade weapons, one girl can create medkits. One guy has a sidequest because he is a nerd.Overall it's a pretty good game.However, i have to say the thing i say to 99% of horror games:FRUSTRATION IS NOT HORROR YOU IMBECILES!Making really obtuse puzzles that will 100% kill you the first time around? Making traps that some characters are bound to die to due to ♥♥♥♥ running speed? THAT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SHOTGUN TRAP ♥♥♥♥ YOU ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥?!!?No, this did not scare me, no matter what people stuck in the era of fixed camera angles and tank controls seem to prefer. There is no fear to frustration - there is only anger. Anger is antithetical to fear - it smothers fear. As well as any ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enjoyment at the moment. Which is why, the true ending was something i really didn't enjoy - a ton of awful laser puzzles that one hit kill you with hitboxes that aren't actually where they claim to be, combined with a time limit. A boss that's easy to stunlock and zombies that waste your time.Please - all the horror devs listening. PLEASE DO NOT CENTER YOUR HORROR ON FRUSTRATION. For the love of God or whatever force you worship.Still... i do recommend it as a game... especially since i know i'm somehow in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minority when it comes to seeing horror as something that's not meant to be a frustrating mess.10/10 would dump all the magnum ammo into the skull of the shotgun puzzle creator again.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed Resident Evil 2 Remake, you'll probably enjoy this game (I've never played the original RE1 & RE2). It's a good game and I enjoyed my time with it. _childDocuments_.review: As a Resident Evil enjoyer (Resident Evil 1 is my favorite game of all time) I really appreciated this game, the aesthetic mimics that game in what almost feels like plagiarism, but never really crosses that line, more of a nudge with the elbow with a smirk that gives an eye-roll in response, but in an endearing way, the developers knew how to scratch the itch that the lack of old school survivor horror left untouched.The story follows 6 different characters that you will kinda get to know depending on your choices, each one inspired heavily by the original Resident Evil 1, some almost reaching parody levels. But just like Resident Evil 1, the mansion itself is the main character and most memorable part of the experience. The death maze full of face-eating zombies ready for you to shoot is a delight to traverse and explore, puzzles and traps are the main attraction for me and what will most likely to kill you in this game. I don't want to spoil the twists this game offers, for even at the start, it drops you in a mysterious plot and it begs you to keep pushing yourself to see what the full picture is.Speak of dying in this game, start getting used to it. The 6 main characters in this story are your total lives, lose one in a gruesome way? The next ones are ready to pick up where they left off, either losing all inventory you had with that character until you pry it open from their dead (or not so dead) corpse, learning from their (or in that case, yours) mistake, like a Groundhog day style where you will start to learn the ways of the mansion after some trial and error. Although some times, the game feels rather cheap on the delivery of hints for certain puzzles, leaving it with more error than trial. Not being that clear on what to do or what you did wrong, especially in such a punishing game like this. My bane was the shotgun puzzle, the hint was there, but there were so many variables that I tried and failed through, that once I did it, I didn't feel accomplishment, but frustration of losing 4 characters over it.But traps aren't the only thing deadly in this mansion, neither is Resident Evil its only inspiration. It caught me by surprise when the first enemy combat, the top-down camera angle shifted to an arcade-like shooter, really unsubtle about the reference to House of the Dead, but again in an endearing way, for rail shooters are also a starving genre this day and age that I shamelessly gobbled up and enjoyed. The shooting is precise and it captures the panic of missing a shot while a zombie rushes you from across the room, throwing his head around and making it very difficult to hit, but is not a bad thing though, the mouse is way more precise than a lightgun and somewhat makes me wish there was a lightgun support for these kind of games. But going back to the "creatures", it has a small lack of variety, from buttles zombies, to maid zombies (those are terrifying btw), and zombies with weapons and no, different weapons do not change the moveset of said zombies. It's always fun to shoot in this game, but when you are at the end of the game and still see the enemies from the beginning, it makes the whole experience a bit unmemorable outside of some boss fights, which were a highlight but left me wanting more. All areas feature the same enemies and it takes a bit away from the overall experienceLong story short, this gameplay really touched on some areas of my childhood that I didn't realize I missed so much of. The graphics, the music, the story and the unconventional gameplay that mimics old-school games make this a must for the loves of this genre. There are a few negatives that are overshadowed by the goods that were mentioned, but can't go without saying that some puzzles are unsatisfying to resolve, characters can be a bit bland, not much enemy variety and the game overall is on a shorter side of things, leaving you wanting more, because it's really good, and you just don't want it to end here tonight.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, gave it another try and I actually had a good time.My major gripe was the cheap instakills but it turns the game is way more lenient than it wants you to think.The game has permadeath but there's a mechanic called "k coins" which revives all 6 characters and keeps all your progress, including killed enemies and damage dealt to bosses.I found 4 of them which means 24 extra lives so you have 30 lives to beat the game, maybe even more. So basically you are actually expected to lose a couple characters every bossfight or puzzle and just keep going like nothing happened.So all in all, it's a nice resident evil homage with its own twist.ORIGINAL REVIEW:I don't know, the deaths are pretty cheap plus it gets repetitive fast and it's already a short game. _childDocuments_.review: It's a cycle based game where you're meant to lose but learn things with each cycle and are allowed to make additional progress. Game has some Sweet Home elements where each character has specialties.The game is good enough for me to have played through the refund period and not regretted it, but the first person combat mechanics are my one issue with the game, so buyer beware;The combat encounters have an intentional jankiness around them that I kind of hate. I think it's meant to emulate the inefficiency of tank controls in a first person perspective but I feel it's way worse than tank controls would have been. The interface is intentionally obtuse and under explained, if you push an enemy off, you have to redraw your weapon and my first few deaths were related to not knowing how to redraw the pistol.Boss encounters are an absolute mound of ♥♥♥♥ where the intentional control jank meets Super Punchout style puzzle elements. The player meets heavy damage and an absolute necessity to memorize attack patterns. Some people may have a higher tolerance, but a 30 second enounter in which a boss beats you to a pulp while you wrestle with the interface is not my idea of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that one finds such an obscure release tied to this level of quality. YWDHT is an homage to the OG Resident Evil, and wears its inspiration on its sleeve. That might get misinterpreted as a lack of fresh ideas or innovation, but this little gem brings plenty to the table - be it QoL improvements or totally new, experimental elements. For the price asked, this is 100% a no-brainer for fans of the genre and of quality, puzzle-focused games in general.- FiOth

_childDocuments_.review: We've all done worse things with $10...Anyways, I have incredibly mixed feelings about this game. While I did have fun I also had an incredible amount of frustration. Thumbs down for now, because I could only recommend this to an incredibly small minority of people.Pros:- Classic old school Resident Evil vibe- Shooting/combat is fun for the most part- Game is short and easy to replayCons:- These controls suck, I switched back and forth between keyboard/Mouse and gamepad and both had their issues.- Bugs and glitches galore for a game that should be finished.- Manual saves don't always work. I lost progress over this- Game is short, feels like there should be more to this or more happening on the map or something more to the story, but it feels like we got some abridged version of the game instead.- RE bugs and glitches: I couldn't get the ending. I interacted with the chess board in both the office and the manor in every which way per existing guides, but could not start the ending sequence.Final notes: 5/10I eagerly hope the dev works on a new release of this with significant improvements because as a concept this has plenty of potential. For now its just poor execution.PS: If this review seems harsh, I'm still salty over not getting my ending.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface this game has everything going for it:- Oldschool survival horror gameplay * (more on that later...)- Great retro graphics- Interesting and innovative combat mechanics and roguelike aspects- Good puzzles and explorationBut sadly I still have to give this game a negative rating (would be neutral if Steam would allow it). In the first 2 hours I was truly impressed by the game. Then you start to realize that the game has cheap deaths...which is okay because...well "You Will Die Here Tonight" and you have other characters. Then you arrive at the boss fights and realize the game is designed in a way in which you basically have to throw bodies at the boss enemies loosing more characters no matter how careful you play. For some reason this kills the survival horror feeling, especially since after each death you just grab your ammo and run to the boss again to finally get it over with.But what really killed the fun for me was near the end when the game punishes you because you did not interact with a specific (background) item, with a specific character (!), while at the mansion and expects you to go back now. This is such bad design that reminds me of the Clock Tower games. The story is kind of a hot mess and not told in an engaging way so at this point I had no desire to finish the game and watched the ending on youtube.I think this game would have benefited from a more traditional survival horror and roguelike gameplay. All characters are dead? Game Over. No continues. But to balance that they should have done away with the cheap and unavoidable deaths. Give the player a fair chance even in the boss fights instead of multiplying them and making them bullet sponges just so to make sure at least one character dies during the fight. Even regular enemies can kill you with 3 hits sometimes and since at some point they start to swarm you in the mansion I just felt like the game was taking its name way to serious and  became a frustrating experience intended to kill the player again and again on a first blind playthrough. Throwing bodies at problems is not fun in a survival horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: A good fun game for being on sale. Why do I give it a down vote? Because it could have been more. It's great fun that gets you hooked, with a mix of horror and intuitive puzzles. The problem was the story is a little bit short, the twist really isn't fun, and the bosses are repetitive. With more varied fights, a few alternate endings, and not having to have all your characters die, it could be a really solid experience. Hope to see more from this developer
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Putting this at the top since it's important:LOOK UP THE SOLUTION FOR THE SHOTGUN IF YOU DON'T FIGURE IT OUT WITHIN A COUPLE OF MINUTESThe shotgun is the best weapon in the game for the large majority of the game, and is nigh-mandatory if you want to have a smooth experience.--Review Time--I'd give this game a perfect side-thumb if I could, but since I have to choose one or the other, I'm giving it a thumbs down. It's not BAD, it's just not good. It's merely okay.You play as a member of a Resident-Evil-esque, STARS-like team, infiltrating an oddly-familiar mansion filled with, you guessed it, zombies. But even if you know the story, things are not what they seem...The story is the high point of this, as even though it isn't long, it packs a decent number of twists and turns. I will warn you here, though. It's anticlimactic. Still, it is interesting while it lasts.The low point is the game's design. There's 6 characters on this team, and when one dies, they die "permanently" (no manual saves), to be replaced by the next person on the team who picks up where they left off. It's lenient enough, but if you're trying to get through with as few deaths as possible, you may become frustrated by the confusing number of instant deaths. Or deaths that were only avoidable if you picked up specific gear elsewhere in the mansion.Yes, I know the game is called "You Will Die Here", but there's actually only a few story-forced deaths. The rest is just regular gameplay, but taken to this weird place where bad game design is being apologized for by the game title.For example, regular enemies are essentially harmless, while boss health is overtuned specifically to kill you for no reason. In this game, you can't dodge while in combat. You can only stand and shoot, so if you don't shoot the right areas... or shoot them with a strong enough GUN... you will get hit and die quickly.I really feel like this game could have been improved by just beefing up the quantity of enemies in the mansion rather than trying to force the player to die through circumstances they couldn't have seen coming. If you actually go where the game tells you to go, when it tells you to go there, you will have a bad time.Again, not a bad game, just frustrating and ultimately unsatisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting mechanics but the pacing of the game is far too unintuitive. They throw you into the game without any idea of who you are or what's going on. It nails the nostalgia of Resident Evil 1 and House of the Dead, but unfortunately the game just feels like a shell of what those games were. At least their introductions gave you more information to go off of. All you get is that "You will die here tonight!" *cue spooky lightning* and left trying to figure out what is even happening without knowing who you are or why you're even there in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Short but charming Resident Evil pastiche. Because of the lightgun combat and ammo prevalence, you freely shoot all the zombies, but you did that in RE2 and 3 too. _childDocuments_.review: If I can describe this game in one sentence it will be; It's Resident Evil but with a twist.  This game seems to have roguelike elements where it is expected that you will die and then learn from the experience.  And if you are playing this game with no prior knowledge then oh boy... are you going to die... A LOT.Like RE, this game takes place in a huge mansion, filled with zombies, tension, puzzles, and gorgeous decor that you'd expect in a mansion deathtrap. What separates this game from RE however, is the seamless transition from top down exploration to first person shooting.  Fighting in combat especially the ammo discharge animation gives me a sense of nostalgia as it reminds me of Time Crisis.  And unlike RE games if you get bitten, you have a limited amount of time to "deal with it" or else you'll become the next survivors problem.As of this review I have just under three hours play time and am absolutely loving it.  A few negative points:1) I had experienced a softlock at headquarters at the very beginning as I'd entered the inventory but then could not exit from it  I had to quit out of the whole program which erased all progress.  But it was no biggy as like I said, it was at the very beginning. 2)  As far as I can tell, there is no way to rebind the controls.  I play on controller and the current control scheme is fine as it is, but it would be nice to have that option.3) There is a Chris Redfield like character and there is a boulder and he did not punch said boulder.  What a let down : )If you are a lover of the survival horror genre, then do yourself a favour and check this game out.
_childDocuments_.name: You Will Die Here Tonight

_childDocuments_.review: It's all right. Mixes a few genres. Has permadeath but also has scripted deaths for some reason. But you can continue? Graphics are retro so no problems running it. _childDocuments_.review: Man, I don’t know how I feel about this game. I want to love it, it’s reminiscent of Resident Evil and its PS1 look/feel. Like is this a roguelike or whatever? No idea.I Hardly know any of the characters because there’s rushed character development, if you can even call it that. Having text only, no audio dialogue doesn’t help bring personality to the characters either. If we could have full voiced characters in the 90s, you can do it today. Christ, just get your friends to voice them, it’s better than nothing.I dunno, it has potential. I might play it some more, but I really wish they’d have fleshed it out a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game.  The atmosphere is a great throwback to the original RE.  Perhaps too much.  What ruins it though are the controls.  This makes the tank controls of the original RE games feel like they're current.  Terrible, clunky movement, combat is beyond awful, and the menu and UI navigation is some of the worst I've experienced.  I will reconsider if the game gets updates in the future to refine the controls and we get better resolution options.  However, I cannot recommend this game, especially for the asking price.  There have been other tributes to the old school RE and Silent Hill games that have been way better and are much cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: Well done Resident Evil 1-inspired Survival Horror Game where your characters can and WILL die. That can potentially make it easier for the remaining characters, depending on what you did or didn't.It's sort of a side-top-down perspective, where as you initiate combat as soon as you see an enemy on the screen, the game switches to first person. The further the zombie was away in the top-down perspective, the further is it going to be away in combat. You can make use of that if you want to fight specifically ranged or melee. You can also turn 360 degrees in that mode, as you'll be attacked from multiple directions sometimes.There's 3 ranged weapons, gun, shotgun and SMG, and a knife for melee combat. You CAN defeat weak enemies with the knife without taking damage, consistently.If you like Retro Style Survival Horror Games, this one's for you. Controller works well with the game if you have one, and I think its the way its intended to be played. For good or bad: the game does NOT have tank controls.I'm currently playing through the whole game for my YouTube channel, free to check it out here: ---------UPDATE: The roguelike or -lite mechanics are pretty forgiving. Once your whole team is dead you get to restart, but keep all objects that you picked up, guns you upgraded, and so on.

_childDocuments_.review: UPD to the dev: By "borked" I don't mean actual bugs but rather when you lose a character prematurely/at all (not sure if you can save everyone). I.e. it's not really a rogue-lite and puzzles/levels always remain the same, so I see no point in being forced to replay it if you slip up.The game's "manual save" is actually a hoax since it can freely overwrite it on a whim to lock you into a borked playthrough. As a person who values their time, thanks but no thanks. I'm not going to waste hours upon hours replaying it just because the devs think it's fun to force me to. Refunded.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it feels like a neat little homage to classic survival horror like Resident Evil. If one of your six team members dies, you can take over one of the remaining characters and pick up from where you left off. Weapons and key items are kept, but anything extra needs to be grabbed from your previous character's corpse.The only major negative thing I have to say about the game, is that at certain times after combat the game bugs and you won't be able to reload for a short moment. So multiple fights in quick succession can be annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10A good and unique take on the survival horror genre, as the closes thing I can compare it to, is resident evil Gaiden on the gameboy of all things. In fact, this is probably what it would look like if that game had gotten a sequel on the ps1 or DS. The game has a solid art style and good visual design, that makes the mansion interesting to explore. The combat manages to find a nice balance between intentionally clunky but also fun to play.That said there are some issues that keep this as a good game instead of a great one.The story, writing and characters are.. bad. And not in the campy so bad its good way like classic RE, but just plain bad.Most of the characters have other attributes besides their role, such as speed, defense and resistance to infection. This is not explained well and turns character use into trial and error. It doesn't help that you have to intentionally get a character killed if you need to change them.Lastly, its pretty short. probably shorter than playing a classic RE for the first time. Doesn't help that there isn't a lot of enemies in the game, and most of them are just different types of zombies. it's also lacking in replay value, apart from if you want to see if you can do a full run with as little deaths as possible. Would have been nice if the pump shotgun and this games equivalent of the BFG, could have been unlocked to be used outside of the endgame, like how classic RE did with the rocket launcher.Still, despite its shortcomings this is a fun and unique survival horror that is certainly worth the time and money. I hope the devs learn from their shortcomings and make a squeal that truly delivers.

_childDocuments_.review: First off: my total playtime is inflated by a few hours because I left the game running when other stuff came up in my life, so the more accurate clear time is probably... four hours or so? And I could have shaved it down further if I was rushing it. So you're getting a pretty short game here. As for the TL;DR - it's a decent game, but I hesitate to recommend at full price.-Negatives-Survival Horror with combat this easy invalidates a major chunk of the tension. The regular zombies are slow and weak enough that mechanics like looking through keyholes to scout may as well not exist, and the only times where I felt like I was in any real danger from regular enemies were from the maids, who are entirely too rare. When most fights last barely long enough for the music to play a few notes before it cuts back to the isometric view again, there's an issue. The boss fights are an enjoyable exception for the most part - and when they're not, it's by virtue of the game doing something that undercuts their difficulty yet again. -While the game generally feels fair enough, some moments can be bizarrely confusing. For example, being given a large shield before immediately placed into a fight where it comes off as worthless because its damage reduction is poorly conveyed, or being told the key to an optional puzzle (with menacing deathtrap to make you think twice about meddling with it) is 'patience', which easily leads to setting it aside in hopes of finding the solution elsewhere until it turns out that, no, the clue meant something completely different. These two are the most egregious while the rest of the game is thankfully much more sensible, but it sticks out.-Having six unique agents is a fun idea, but the way the game plays out leaves most of them feeling vestigial besides serving as extra lives, and their sidequests don't really feel all that important, either - with one exception, anyway. I understand the game wants to kill you and it doesn't want any one character feeling vital, but then it undercuts it by making them all play close to the same, and the way the story focuses on one main character in particular also doesn't do it favors. The closest comparison point I have is Prey: Mooncrash, which gives you five different characters with their own unique stats and quests and multiple escape routes, so you're angling to eventually pull off a run where you get everyone's objectives done and all of them escape. I understand that designing a full survival horror sandbox to better utilize everyone's unique traits would be an unreasonable expectation for a small team, but it's the kind of thing a sequel might be better placed to attempt.-Positives-Despite how easy it generally is, the combat is satisfying. Weapons have solid effect and feel good to use, and when the game puts you in particularly hairy situations, whirling around scanning for threats and firing away or considering a retreat is a good time. -The writing is fun! Despite each agent's gameplay differences being pretty small, every member of the unit is entertaining and I'm invested in trying to keep them alive, as well as see how they react to the various perils of the mansion and the fates that can befall the other agents.-The mansion is an entertaining place to explore, and working around the various deathtraps and puzzles it has in place for you is usually a thoughtful, engaging experience.-I appreciate the limited continue system - having to reset entirely from scratch once I lost all my agents the first time is something I could have lived with, but having a few chances to just try and power through the story without my progress being totally undone is excellent quality of life that kept the pacing solid.Overall, the game does enough with its premise I don't feel like my money was wasted (though I got it on sale, which softens my opinion too). There's clearly love and soul put into this experience, and the core is solid enough that I was left satisfied by the time the credits roll, but the execution needs some polishing up and there should have been more to it overall. Twenty dollars is a bit of a high price for what you get in return, I feel, but despite my issues I still think it's a worthwhile ride.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually learn too much about games before I pick them up, as I want to give most of them a fair shot. In this scenario, I saw the retro survival horror style mixed with first-person gunplay and thought that would be enough to pull me in. It is, for the most part.However, there is one key narrative factor that turns this game into a game I would normally not enjoy very much. For spoiler reasons, I won't go into specifics, but I will say that the game expects you to die (the title is pretty accurate) and repetition is baked into the gameplay.Normally, I'm not a fan of this kind of gameplay; I don't enjoy replaying sequences over and over, but this game finds a way to avoid that (again, involves the story). There is also a somewhat generous continue system that helps negate some of the usual frustration or stress one might encounter with these mechanics, and that made it all far easier to enjoy.Overall, very fun game. The story is okay; the whole thing is very reminiscent of RE1 (to the point of one room even sharing almost the same puzzle/layout as RE1), but the execution is fairly novel, so it keeps you interested. I believe there is a secret ending, too, but I think I got it on my first attempt, so I don't know what would have happened otherwise. All I can say is to make sure each character plays to their strengths. If you think a character should be able to have a unique interaction with something that others might not, give it a shot.I'm glad I gave it a shot, because I honestly would probably not have picked it up if I knew what the premise was beforehand. That said, they took a concept I normally find annoying and found a way to make it far more palatable, and while I still stressed a little here and there, it's not nearly as punishing as the concept might have you believe.
