_childDocuments_.review: The brave/default battle system is interesting, letting you borrow against or store future turns while combining class roles for each of your party members. The game also gives you some passive experience through the exploration system, so your in-game time also contributes to some passive item gathering and experience gains. The game is a little tough though, it's not designed to just walk through the story. You'll have to do a little bit of grinding (apart from side quests) to reach the next point in the story, or, I could possibly just not be an expert in this combat system. Though, pacing wise, this is probably going to be a long time investment, as for me it was 3 hours to the title card, and 10 hours so far for maybe the 2nd major story mission 2/3rds done. Overall, it's a fun turn-based JRPG and the characters are pretty hilarious, both in an intentional and unintentional way. I don't mind English VA in general, but the random Scottish, medieval English, royal English, and modern day English dialect mixes are a little weird (and unexplained story-wise) in this game, so if you want to get immersed in the story switching to Japanese VA might improve your experience. My Japanese is not good enough to know if the dialects and accents are as varied. Also the items use Final Fantasy names like Echo Herbs, Phoenix Down, etc so if you are familiar with those games it's nice to not have to relearn the names of everything. All-in-all, the chibi characters and watercolor/pastel (maybe?) art-style of the backgrounds to me are beautiful and give life to the cities and environment. 10/10 would get as a birthday gift again.
_childDocuments_.name: BRAVELY DEFAULT II

_childDocuments_.review: If you've been dreaming that Final Fantasy would one day return to its roots, it has in the form of Bravely Default.This game released earlier this year as a Switch exclusive. As much as it hurt to walk away from my 20 hour save file on Switch to make the switch to this PC version, I can't say I'll ever think of going back. Its so much snappier, prettier, and load times are DRAMATICALLY cut down. Fantastic port as well, uncapped resolution and frame-rate, runs like a dream.As for the game itself, this is a great classic RPG with leveling systems that are very free-form and encourage experimentation. There are a ton of different Jobs (Classes) that you can mix and match between all of your characters, and there's a lot of variety. Hard Mode is a great, fair challenge and I recommend everyone try that mode at first. (You can always switch later) Story starts off pretty slow and character models could use some work. Also, the mouse cursor itself cannot be used to navigate the menu which is a huge bummer.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished both Bravely Default 1 and 2, and the sequel is the same high level of quality that I've come to expect from Square Enix. Every aspect of the game, from the graphics to the sound to the gameplay, is beautiful and engaging.I genuinely could not find fault with anything during my 57 hours of gameplay. I did not even find a single typo in the novel's worth of text this game has, and that's quite an achievement. Kudos to the writers and editors!The game has 3 different endings, and you can unlock them in sequence.JRPG fans will be right at home in BD2.

_childDocuments_.review: Bravely Default and Second are some of the first RPGs I've ever played, and are what got me into the genre. Additionally, they're also the reason I really seriously got into the anime dubbing scene. I have a lot of history with the franchise. On that note, this game is really lacking compared to everything that came before it.A lot of this is personal gripes, but I can't help but point them out.The art direction for the core 2D visuals are stunning, and everything I'd expect from this team, but when imagined in 3D it all falls apart. The models look like they cant quite decide if they want to retain the chibi style of the original games and go for a more realistic style, making it this total uncanny valley look that I just cannot get into.The visuals look like a amateur Unity game. I can't explain it but for some reason so much of the graphics just do not look like something that should be coming out of Square Enix. The best way to explain it is just that nobody really cared creating this game.The story doesn't have a good hook whatsoever, and I'm given like no reason to care about anyone here. They're all annoying to some degree and feel like bootlegs of the Default team. You have generic main character guy, girl in high standing, wildcard rowdy girl, and suave goofy guy. When I see the Default 2 cast I just want to see the OG cast more, honestly. None of it is interesting, and is completely by-the-books. Final Fantasy IV on the SNES had a more unique story than this and that game came out a lifetime ago.The gameplay is what you'd expect from the Bravely series, so really not much to note there.Overall, just play Bravely Default and Bravely Second if you want a Final Fantasy III-styled RPG with great stories and great presentation; both full of a lot of passion and heart. They're worth a try and a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the old Bravely Default games, you will not like this one. With that said, I had not played the old games (except 4 heroes of light) and this game is a huge upgrade compared to that one. Compared to the old ones, its a huge downgrade. There is no quest catalogue, so you have to use an open source website to find your missing quests. One item is miss-able if you don't steal it from a berserk boss during his fight. The worst part of this game is for sure the boss fights. This game stops being a JRPG and more of a puzzle turn based fighting game. Every boss has some gimmicky counter move that makes the fight way harder than it needs to be. You are never too overpowered unless you spend hours intentionally grinding. Every boss is more fun if you have a guide on the side telling you what to do. But even with that, they are still super gimmicky. They have bull crap counters for every situation, that are NEVER listed anywhere. Some enemies have immunities, which force you to play certain strategies. I have never felt so forced to play a certain way in my life. I really want to enjoy this game, but the boss fights are WAY too long and way too insanely hard. You are never too good for any boss fight, and I am not ever having any fun during the boss fights. Every side quest in this game is either "kill these enemies", "kill this boss", or a fetch quest. There is no variety. The ONLY part of this game I really enjoy is the B'n'D, but most people hate it. This game as a JRPG just sucks.EDIT: Just finished this game, and I will say it does get better towards the second half. The plot is still super cookie cutter, and even lacks a real story, but I think once youve gotten the better job classes and can get past the slog of the intro, grinding gets much faster and easier to do with certain abilities. If you like mindless grinding after getting stronger, it does eventually get better. I will say I absolutely dread the beginning of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Bravely Default II is a terrific game, it makes my taint tingle with the possibility of more.I won't complain.The basic idea of the game is interesting, simple and fascinating all at the same time.Bravely Second is just like Bravely Default, except you have to focus on your direction while you play.I noticed that, well, almost every time I attacked something, I would get enough Hit Points to dodge the incoming attacks.And, well, there was no real purpose to the more defensive / survivability type play of the game.I mean, there was quite a bit of wandering and talking about the past, stuff like that.That was kinda cool, but it was pretty much limited to three or four levels before the player level shot up.Oh, and there were the annoying roadblocks that you have to remove by finding people with the right item to do it.Since that doesn't make a whole lot of sense to me, I won't go into it in this post.What I will talk about is how engaging this game is.Well, now.I actually had a huge amount of fun with this game.I love a lot of Square - Enix games (Frozen, Kingdom Hearts), but Bravely Second is hands down the game I like most.The idea of playing against a game that can see your play style and try to counter it makes the game fresh and interesting.There were a few times I had to re - figure out how to beat a boss, but it made me really think about the design of the boss, and that was good for my preparation.Each of the main battles, which all had different mechanics, made me think, "How am I going to beat this?" Some things that I didn't consider at all were correct.That made my battles a lot of fun.One of my favorite bosses was a Tree Dragon that attacks with its vines.That stuff does suck, but it looked really cool and really frustrating to fight.The way the battles all work makes me wanna slap my testicles on the screen, repeatedly.The game even tries to tempt you into using the bosses from the previous game by sending a message that says "Get me the Heart That Touches the Sky!".Good job, Square - Enix.This game got a 4 out of 5 stars from me.I love the direction they took in this one.If they had done this back when they made the original, the game probably would have gotten 5 stars from me.Either way, I'm proud of them for making such a great game.Well, I could go on and on with other examples of flawed games, but that isn't really what this is supposed to be about.I'm sure I'll find some more games that fit in this category in the future.My favorite thing about this video is how he contrasts the show's two genres.Some people really think that the first two seasons of the show are pure fantasy, and that the third is pure fantasy + sci - fi.Well, we know that's not true, but I think he manages to get his point across fairly well.Take a look and let me know what you think!I've been thinking about music a lot lately.I haven't been following any particular kind of music, and I've been listening to pretty much anything I can.

_childDocuments_.review: I already reviewed the game on the Switch and very few of the issues have been resolved, but you can read that here"This review covers specifically the PC version.✅Performance, which was a huge issue on the Switch, is almost completely resolved here.  VSync seems to have some issues though, where there are inexplicable stutters at 1440p.  At 4k/60 it was fine.  There's really no need to go above 60fps with this game, because the visuals won't let you recognize a difference.✅Most of the graphics look much better than Switch.  Things like the character specifically do, and there are a few settings that can be tweaked in the config for slightly better effect.✅Load times, which was also a huge issue on Switch, are not here (assuming you have an SSD, and you should by now).✅It's not overly technically demanding.  My second PC, which is a business PC that doesn't have the strongest graphics card, was able to run the game at 1080p/60 with only minor issue.Note: if you're coming from Switch, you can "balance" the difficulty by simply "acquiring" more cash.  This will let you buy the items, weapons and armor that you need without completely "breaking" the game.I said it before: if it were named anything else, "Courageous Crystal Quest" or something, it'd be an 8 out of 10.  But it doesn't hold up to the Bravely name at all.  There were too many steps backward and even from the first demo, which I felt was the best experience overall and they removed the best features.That said, on PC you can apply QoL fixes to make the game decent...just IGNORE THE BRAVELY in the name.  It's not a Bravely game.  At all.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I never played Bravely Default 1 or this before it was ported to PC.I wanted to give this a positive review because I like the art and the voice acting, not the main character's voice though. The classes and abilities are fairly neat as well, nothing really new here in the realm of RPGs from what I've seen though. Although, judging from other reviews the starting class is probably one of the best.So, why wouldn't I recommend this game? Glad you asked, it's the game play. Running around on the world map is...okay enough. You're constantly swirling the camera around trying to navigate and the mini map is either too small or too big with its two modes. The camera refuses to ever level off so you can actually look where you're going. I'm guessing that was a design decision so you can't just run past all the enemies SINCE YOU CAN'T F'ING SEE THEM. It was enough to make me nauseous.The combat is awful. There's no real tactical decisions being made here. Are they vulnerable to a certain damage type? Use that. Not vulnerable to anything you use? Oh well, just spam your best attacks. It's almost not even worth the turn it takes to examine an enemy to figure out their vulnerabilities. Most of the time the damage is negligible enough that you would've killed them anyway. Any sort of debuff abilities or magic seemed to have no real effect that I noticed as every time I've tried using them the enemies are immune. I once used an ability to lower a bosses attack power by 7% 4 times in a row and it stacked (you can look at battle info on enemies during fights) and then they still 1 shot my healer without it being a critical. Even though they barely did that much last time with full attack power. Neat.You have two types of battles:-First type, your entire party spends all their "Battle Points" (you can spend future turns in advance during combat) to blitz down the enemy. This is the majority of encounters on the world map and in dungeons. It's super repetitive and uninteresting. You can increase the battle speed, WHICH YOU WILL, to save your sanity. There are just so...so so so many battles. Like a laughable amount. As soon as you're done with one, you zone back to the map, get attacked again. I started just running past every enemy possible, sometimes ending up in "linked" battles where you do multiple fights back to back.-Second type, boss fights. The bosses have a counter attack to most(all) abilities, especially the things they are vulnerable to. Melee Attack? Get slapped with a heavy counter attack. Magical Attack? We also counter those, with a hard hit or spell debuff on your party. Healing your party? No no, we don't do that here. COUNTER ATTACK. Using an item? You foolish fool you, counter attack. You're going to take turns spamming Default with the boss enemies. They'll store up battle points, you will also. Then you'll basically try to bankai each other and repeat. Bosses have vulnerabilities, but if you try to line up 3-4 vuln attacks, your character will get chopped down by counters before finishing them most of the time. Oh yeah, your main character gets hilariously weak limit break attacks that buff your party. A normal attack might do 200ish if you're lucky they aren't Default spamming like you. A vuln attack does like 300-400. Limit break? Maybe 800. The bosses hp? Oh, a cool 25k.The game is not hard. Battle Brothers is hard. This? It's tedious and downright not fun. They had a great recipe here, then decided to remove the key ingredient, fun, and replace it with repetition. I wouldn't recommend this one even on sale. If you really NEEDED to buy it, play it on Easy so you don't spend your entire life fighting some color palette shifted enemy for the 1,000th time in a dungeon.

_childDocuments_.review: I played 70 hours on the Switch version.Unless you are a hardcore RPG fan I would strongly advise against BD3.  It is by far the worst BD game in terms of story, characters, mechanics, and gmaeplay.   If you are an anime fan, consider how bad most filler episodes are and then imagine if the excellent BD1 and BD: EL were written by the same people.The plot is super generic, and the characters (sans Elvis) lack even a 1/10 of the charm of the previous cast.  The MC literally has no personality.  That's not how the previous BD games were at all.  The combat is solid, and messing around with jobs is as fun as ever, although the classes were far more interesting in BD: EL.It's also worth noting that adding monsters on the field actually INCREASES the amount of random battles you have to fight since BD1 and EL literally let you literally turn them off.   The loss of fine control over encounters is a huge loss.   Who thought that was a good idea?          It's obvious that the original BD team did not produce this steamy pile.  If you can enjoy a game purely for the turn based combat you might enjoy this.   But if you associated Bravely with fun characters, great dialog, witty writing, and a pile of charm then prepare to be disappointed.  None of that is here.Hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a joke, and many aspects of the game design make it seem like it was made in the early 2000s. The story seems to be a very trite "save the world from over-the-top evil villains" kind of thing and is nothing new. For more fleshed out characters, try Octopath Traveler instead.The gameplay is ok in that you appear to have many options to strategise overpowered combos and combinations of passive skills, but the combat is pretty stale. You just default to gain BP, buff yourself, and burst down the boss.The game also loves including overlevelled minibosses in every area so you have to keep remembering to come back and kill them later on. The first miniboss that you find (right outside your starting town where you're level 1) has a level 25+ miniboss. Completely ridiculous design that doesn't respect the player's time whatsoever.TLDR: Boring story, Terrible design, OK gameplay. Save your money for another game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the few times I am going to flip my thumb. I gave it another shot. And although the style still reminds me of Mister Rogers, Something clicked with me. I grew up on Final Fantasy and other old school RPGs, back to when the first FF game came out. Ever since FFXII that series has been going in the wrong direction for me. But this feels like what the FF series used to and still should be. It is very similar to what you would expect from the era of about III - IX. And that is what made me change my thumb's direction. Now i am digging it.As always though..i kept the original review under the dotted line.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I can't do it. I just can't do it.I tried  but I just can't do it. I can't take this game seriously.I am very much a non-graphic snob, and would happily play atari 2600 games...but this I can't figure out if it is trying to be serious or some elaborate joke expecting people to justify its greatness in because they see JRPG and Square Enix. The combat style reminds me too much of the DS remakes of FF3 and FF4, which is also now hard for me to take seriously. (I know what people will say: but the first ones of the series were 3DS. I get that but....)Every single cutscene I am just waiting for Mister Rogers to pop in...or the Thunderbirds. I expect at some point Rudolph or Yukon Cornelius will join my party. Actually I am pretty sure one of the characters in the early cutscenes is claymation Santa in disguise. Its so awful looking, that I can't even focus on the over-cliched story to even pretend like what is going on is interesting.Then there is the combat, which lets start with discussing what we were just talking about. Remember JRPGs that throw you into battle and you start selecting commands? Well this one has a quick little intro for each side when they line up. The moment i saw one of the enemies come into battle punching their open hand to pump themselves up in a cheesy saturday morning cartoon way....any seriousness of the combat was gone. They might as well go full wresting at this point and have an announcer bring them out, and have them trash talk each other.Then there is the backgrounds...especially the starting city....that was made to have a "DS look" to it. Its not mild either...I was running this at a 1280x720 window..and it looked like a DS screen pumped up to 1280x720 resolution. But the characters didn't look DS...so everything just felt really off. No..they still looked like they just got off the trolley from The Neighborhood of Make-Believe. (Upon reloading and going back to the city after getting a party...it dosent't have the same DS look. Maybe this was temporary for the very start...but that image will be forever burned into my mind in a very bad way.)I can tell that the job system in this one will be very complex and customization...but if the next Doom had Strawberry Shortcake world in it...it is not going to feel right.Now I will admit I am not a fan of the idea of the Brave and Default system...nor have I ever liked sacrificing turns for stocking attacks. BDII banks in it. And i am sure a lot of other types of JPGers will enjoy something like that. So it is worth mentioning now if you can get around the confusing look, and like stocking attacks, or risking loss for a big hit, you might just love this combat system.I think I would just rather go back to FF3 or FF5 for the job class system. i appreciate that it looks to take job classes to the next level, but i think the only way i could get through this game would be to play it with a blindfold.....

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a neutral review for me (If Steam had a neutral option)The game does not respect your time. The grinding is insane. I put about 80hrs in this game and most of it was grinding. Only at the very end do you finally get to relax and have a fun battle that focus more on the story and characters then being obliterated or one shotted if you are not leveled enough. Unlike Octopath Traveler 2,  job points (JP) in BD2 be accumulated for EACH INDIVIDUAL JOB. The only job that gets JP points is the job you assign as your main job. If you want to play as another job you have to then select that job as your main grind it to max also to get all the perks and abilities, instead of just counting JP exp towards all jobs. This makes the game an insane grind and makes it harder to mix and match between jobs, unless you want to grind for hours of course. You can unlock JP UP UP which makes it faster to accumulate JP but for all your characters you have to MAX OUT the freelancer roll for EACH CHARACTER. The grind was so insane, it got to the point where I was ready for this game to end.The story is ok. The ending is ok. The characters are interesting and I can tell the devs put a lot of work into this game. There are several endings and only once I got the true ending did I feel ok with the story. I changed my review from a negative to a neutral. Truly I am glad I am done with this game and I will never play another JRPG that requires this much grind. It really felt like a second job.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this a neutral rating I would.This game is a JRPG to the core and if you prefer your adventures with a job-system, this might be the perfect pick for you. Don't be fooled by the graphics and chibi style of this game though. It really doesn't hold your hand and you might die more often than you would expect. Boss battles expect you to switch around jobs and manage a feasible strategy that you can apply for that specific enemy, so you will never have a job build that will remain the same throughout your run. If that's not what you're looking for keep searching for something else (you may be able to do this at the end-game if ever). Some may find this intrusive and annoying, but I had my fun with it, and enjoyed the extra challenge that this brought. The reason as to why I still would give this a neutral rating is the fact that this game does a lot of good things, but nothing exceptionally well. The gameplay is fine, the music is fine, the characters are okay (if you ignore the fact that they feel like carbon copies of everyone in BD1) and the story is... there.I never finished a retro final fantasy game, but this story feels like something I would see in there, which would be fine in the 90s, but it never really tried to reinvent the wheel with anything I saw in there. Maybe Chapter 3, for a cool twist, but except that, nothing extraordinary, which is unfortunate if you are used to play Persona or Omori.It's not bad per se, but maybe there is a game out there that does these things a bit better. If you already played everything I described and just want more job-system RPGs then have fun with this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun in a basic kind of way. Fairly standard story with few to no choices to make.  The brave/default system is interesting. Picking your primary class, secondary class, and passives is interesting.However, early on you get the "Beastmaster" class and this thing seems broken. You get stat bonuses that scale with how many monsters you've ever captured. So from a small amount of leveling- mostly trying different jobs and just kind of zoning out- my party is extremely overpowered. Kind of sucks the fun out of it.  It might get better later, but right now it's a weird position to be in. The game is also very much a levels game.  Some monsters you just don't have the numbers to beat, and there's not much you can do strategy wise to turn that around. No level 1 runs here.Runs nice on the steam deck.  It has cloud saves. I think at some point it didn't, but as of 2024 it syncs fine between the deck and desktop.Combat has a fast forward option. Much appreciated.  No combat log that I found, so if you miss a message you're out of luck.Stealing is traditional FF style. It can be a little tedious just hitting steal steal steal until you finally get the item you want.  You can steal permanent stat boost items, but is it worth the time? Probably not.Pacing is pretty good. Doesn't take long to get to actually playing.Overall, as of chapter 2, it's fun but has some balance issues.Update: Finished it.  Beastmaster is completely broken the whole time.  Do not use beastmaster if you want a challenging playthrough.Overall a good time, but I sort of optimized the fun out of it by using beastmaster.
_childDocuments_.name: BRAVELY DEFAULT II

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its flaws, Bravely Default 2 continues to be among my favorite games of all time.After a 2nd playthrough now on steam I am still amazed at the depth and options of the combat system. No other game has made the job system this much fun.This is the end of the review, however I am also writing some personal suggestions for possible future games.Be warned as there may be spoilers below.- A slightly different visual style, as its clear the port from 3DS games to more modern consoles made the original's aesthetic pretty hard to copy. Town art is still beautiful however.- Keep Revo making the soundtrack, the games are not the same without him.- Bosses with more unique mechanics rather than just counter attacks.- PRESETS FOR JOBS. I can't tell you how much having to reassign all the passives and equipment disincentives an otherwise amazing job system.- Better character arcs. I think team Asano has gotten a lot better with writing characters after Octopath 2 and Triangle Strategy,  and I would love to see the same love being put to this series equally. Somehow this game had all these amazing villains whose frustrations you could relate to, but all the main characters felt really shallow. I couldn't tell you anything about Seth other than that he was a sailor. Gloria, just like Agnes, feels like she mostly doesn't contribute anything substantial to the plot other than the fact that "it's her task" to do the right thing. Just make characters have more meaningful struggles, and I know the team can do it since I have seen them do it.- Bosses should "pause" music when talking in battle. Because of the special attack system letting the boss talk actively makes you skip dialogue to keep the buffs up.- LESS talking in combat, especially when casting spells. Maybe make each character say one phrase per turn, instead of one per action. At times I had to mute voice volume just so I could play the game normally in grind sessions.- Items should be sortable. When playing classes that gain benefits for using items like the salve maker or thief its really annoying when you have to slowly scroll through the giant menu instead of letting yourself prepare your most commonly used items to be at the top. Just do it like the Final Fantasy pixel remasters did and it should be fine.- Don't make fairies the primary villains. I get that its been a norm for the series, but at this point it's a little on the nose.- Signify recommended enemy levels. This is just a small touch but it often was unclear if I was meant to come back later when fighting some optional bosses or if I was just having a bad strategy.- Remove godspeed strike. This move was busted in all 3 games and you get it so early that it doesn't feel like it should be as strong as it is.All in all I love this game but I think it has a lot of room to grow and become one of the leading games in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is decent, maybe like a 6/10. I love how each job has it's own character designs too. The art direction is nice and the story, though generic, was also enjoyable. There are numerous enemy designs and the open world part is really well done, even if small, but it gives you a slight sense of exploration, only to drop you back into the narrow corridors shortly after.The party system is nice cause it utilizes the typical RPG format, though you could probably drop the tank in most cases. Where the game really takes a hit for me personally is everything else. The areas you spend alot of the story parts in are mostly mazes and corridors. The grind is real towards the mid to late game. The bosses are very tanky, with HP exponentially rising compared to what you fought prior. Bosses require a bit of strategy as you can't brute force most of them, and you may need to swap jobs out, which you would then need to grind out levels on the job, and the job levels do not level universally, if you want 2 characters to be one job type, gotta level it twice. Alot of bosses utilize mechanics that just are there to ruin your time, and extend your time. Chapters 6 and 7 are part of the story, but require convoluted processes to unlock which if someone wasn't paying attention, may not even notice. The end of the game boss in CH6 to unlock the true ending in CH7 is also an absolute joke of a boss and requires some luck on top of frustration to beat, and it isn't even the end of the story boss. Even at near max level, that boss will wreck you.The Chapter 7 ending requires getting all the asterisks, and 2 of them are optional that you don't get via the story, and I had to go back and look up what I missed because I didn't do all the side quests. I unfortunately couldn't be bothered to do these and jsut chose to end my time here. The game kinda over stayed its welcome for me and I started to get fed up with it. EX: The optional mini-game card game you are required to play takes patience and exists to pad out the time instead of being optional content. It definitely looks like I didn't like the game, I'm just bitter about it, and I did enjoy the time I put in, just disappointed in how it's implemented, mainly the end game part, beginning and middle were good. Neutral thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Still feel pretty early into the game. Sometimes the game has been running in the background so real time might be more like 15 hrs at time of this review. Overall, really enjoy the game-- even if the story feels very wanting.Positives:-Wonderful class system. This class system is one of the best in a JRPG I have played. Allows you to have abilities hold over to create unique play styles and class combos that is hard to find in any other RPG. I feel like no two players are going to set up their party completely the same- and that really adds to the role-playing elements of the game. Probably the strongest point of the whole game.-Combat: the combat feels very good. As an avid hater of all things ATB I feel like this one actually does it in a way that isn't annoying to me. If you don't like ATB style combat, you might want to just test this one out first. -Difficulty: The game gives you so much to work with in classes that you could be going into a dungeon feeling like you for sure would overpower any enemies that the game throws at you. I feel like here the game does a good job increasing difficulty without it being some BS difficulty spike. You are definitely going to want to stock up on pheonix downs and potions and always have a healer in your party. It feels good to have a hard JRPG that actually forces you to think about item selection.-Great economy: of course you can grind and get more money through the game, but money doesn't just fly at you. There probably won't be a time where you have too much money to manage. Because of the point above, you are always having to evaluate if you'd rather have ethers or slightly better armor. Again so many AAA/AA JRPGs really struggle in making items feel meaningful on base difficulty. Negatives:-Art style: This is more of a taste thing, but man, this almost turned me off of the game before buying it. It doesn't seem like it does anything art wise great. Feels like the polar opposite of a persona game per say.-Not well optimized. On a 4070ti this game has quite a bit of frame stutters. It seems like this is a pretty common issue.. Also I have noticed some input lag when using controller. Not a big enough deal because it's not an action game, but it can be annoying. -Mouse and Keyboard sucks: look here, this is a PC game. In the 2020s why are we not allowing users to customize their M&K experience? Default on this game is that WASD is movement and the arrow keys are camera control. Would not recommend this game without a controller. -Story. The biggest negative. Man is this boring slop. I don't know how anyone could possibly like this story at all. It is hugely predictable and bores me to no end. I usually skip now or just sit on my phone while it plays. I mean, how is this so bad?This is a game for a JRPG fan who loves class builds. If you are not that I don't think I would dive into this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game and i kinda enjoyed it but it's very grindy and full of backtracking and the worst sidequest i've seen in a whileYou unlock a lot of jobs and you need to grind a lot to unlock skills and passives to make nice combos. You could probably just level a few jobs for every character and finish the game, but the core mechanic is the jobs and its passives so...And the sidequest and to a lesser extent the mainquest make you do a lot of backtrack, for example:- There is a mainquest that make you go to the end of a dungeon for a second time to gather an item. The dungeon and the enemies are exactly the same. They are just making you walk to add time to the game.- There is a mainquest when you are traveling to a city: the road is blocked so you have to go back to the previous city, talk to one guy and go back to remove the block. Reason? We need to add minutes to the gameplay, right?There is A LOT of sidequest and most of them are boring, repetitive and pointless: * go back to 3 places you have already been and gather 3 items in each one. (there is a lot of this kind of quest) * go to talk to a guy in a dungeon and deliver him something. Oh! They forget a second thing! Go back to city to receive it and go back to the dungeon to talk to the same guy and... believe or not, yeah, they forgot a third thing. Back to the city and back to the dungeon.* some woman is looking for his dad in the city. Find the dad, talk to him. He has a message for the woman. Go back to the woman and of course, she has a message for her dad. Go back to her dad to deliver the message and go back to the woman to finish the quest. (there is A LOT of this kind of quest)* Of course there is a lot of go and kill 5 rats king of quest.Also, almost all the dungeons are just mazes with no mechanics or puzzles. Just choose a path and maybe is the right path, maybe not. If not, go back and choose another. Repeat until you get to the end of the dungeon.if you have played the other 2 bravely default games, this is the worst of the series for a lot of reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic. Very unique game play for a turn based RPG. Good story, good characters, Some difficulty spikes, but not too bad. The game works well on Linux PC's and Steam Deck.Things to be aware of:* Story is quite linear, so if you want huge decision trees with massive consequences, this probably isn't what you're looking for.* Side quests can be completed at any time, so it's not like a tales game where it's easy to miss stuff. You don't much need a strategy guide for this, unless you need help finding every single chest or locating certain drops.* While there are lots of jobs (character classes) to choose, free lance (the starting job) becomes very over powered in my opinion and makes the other jobs kind of pointless in a lot of ways. Early in the game the jobs feel a lot more meaningful, late game, less so. Just my opinion though. However, there are jobs that I use instead of free lance for various reasons.* Outfits are tied to jobs, there's a mod that lets you use any outfit on any job though.* Really wish there was a way to hide the helmet/head gear/face masks, on some outfits. Some look really good, but I prefer to see the characters face during conversations, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Bravely Not-Third is an excellent JRPG with smart class combination builds. But, it does have several items that are worth nitpicking:- The Beastmaster's sub-job specialty 2 grants an absurdly broken increase in most stats on a character if you take the time to actually capture monsters as you encounter them. Hard Mode becomes Easy Mode if you don't pass up on this on at least one of your characters. There are other strategies that can completely ruin the challenge for most of the game, including the final story asterisk.- The game heavily disincentives using the luring items because of "useful; therefore, never use." And, the economy is poorly balanced such that you will have far too much money to even spend until after you gain the Chemist class half-way through the game. If luring items could be bought as soon as Savalon, then this would solve both problems at once.- The story loses a lot of its steam right when you finally defeat Adam. The side characters (outside of a small handful) get tossed to the side, and the main four characters become flanderized. Once you defeat the Conqueror, just skip all of the non-sidequest cutscenes--you're not missing out on anything.- The events which play out in Rimedhal (the Snowbound Land) calls back to incredibly important story elements from Bravely Default and Bravely Second, and ends off the chapter with a surprising twist. But when you visit a certain hidden village in the forest, ALL OF THAT BUILDUP from two-and-a-half games goes to waste, and is cheapened for the sake of reusing tired fantasy tropes. Once again: the execution flops horribly, and you're better off skipping the cutscenes once you're at this part of the game.- I miss the Exorcist class.- The endgame content where you re-fight the asterisk bosses are fun and interesting, but shortlived. If there was more of this difficult content and some of the class skills were more balanced so as to not be super broken, then the gameplay would be much better than it currently is.Anyway: play the first two games before this one, and select Hard Mode once you get to this title. Don't bother grinding for JP until you get JP Up and Up skill and earn the Beserker asterisk for all units, so that you can use Level Slash to make the process go by quicker.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good rpg with lots of content.  I find the art style very pleasing, and overall it's a classy production, very family friendly.  It has little downsides for every upside.  The dialogue is nicely written, but it's quite wordy, lots of clicking through short dialogue bubbles.  The story is traditional, and the heroes are good guys.  The writing and voice acting are good, but it's not gripping and full of tension.  It's just nice.  The game is very grindy - you will spend lots of hours fighting and fighting.  It gets to be a bit much.  This includes things like fighting a boss battle once to see what powers are used, then doing the whole thing again after changing your party and strategy.  You might be able to avoid this on normal difficulty, but then again maybe not.  The boss battles are hard.  On the other hand, combat and character development are pretty interesting.  Combat is turn-based.  On each character's turn, you choose a maneuver and a target.  If you're not familiar with the brave/default mechanic, you can borrow turns against yourself.  So you can take 3 turns at once with a character, but then you have a "debt" and can't do anything until you pay off those actions.  Conversely, you can store up extra turns and then release a chain of actions.  It's a good mechanic and puts nice strategy and choice into the fight.  "Defaulting" (passing for a turn and storing an action) also puts the character in defense mode, which makes the whole process feasible.  There is no penalty for ending a fight in "turn-debt", so if you think you've nearly won, you can have everyone go crazy with extra actions for a quick finish.  The bad guys can use this system too, so beware.  There is also a very annoying, confusing mechanic called "Chance to be Targeted", or CoBT.  It's a big mystery whether this mechanic is broken or flaky or just too hidden to be understood.  The idea is to create a tank by making his CoBT as high as possible, to attract hits from the enemy.  But in practice it's quite unpredictable.  It's theorized that all damage a character inflicts, including healing, secretly adds to their CoBT.  So it's quite unreliable.  My first playthrough I gave up in frustration.  Now with lower expectations for CoBT, I'm enjoying it more.  There is a flexible jobs system, reminiscent of the Final Fantasy Tactics games.  You will find lots of Final Fantasy influence, like job names, spells, and the importance of phoenix down.  Each class has its own colorful outfit, cute and nicely detailed.  You can mix and match abilities from different classes, once you've learned them.  Not all the classes appeal to me.  For example, the Monk inflicts high damage by reducing her own hit points - like doing the enemy's job for them, in the name of taking down one target quickly.  I don't care for that mechanic, but the monk is certainly effective (paired with a healer).I'm a bit annoyed by the many trips to the internet I've had to make, to understand how things work.  For example, there seems to be no in-game description of items, either things you find or that you can buy.  Who knew that clicking L3 turned on the item description tooltip?  Well, I know that now.  But you will likely spend time researching old threads, if you want to finish the game.The story is rather innocent and involves a princess (I mean, of course it does!  It's a classic tale) and a noble quest.  Everyone's a bit naive, even the villains.  All that said, I do recommend Bravely Default 2.  I have hit no bugs, everything works as it should (I think).  Combat requires some thought and characters require planning.  If you like that...err, if you like LOTS of that...you'll have a good time.  The whole thing is nicely crafted.  Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm getting near the end of this game and I'll update this if my feelings change about it.I think this game is a perfect 7. So perfect that it is actually a perfect 8, especially if you are looking for a job/class based JRPG. If you are like me and viewed this game 100 times thinking it is exactly what you want but the lukewarm reception keeps repelling you, I say go for it.Why a 7/8? Why not higher? Because this game doesn't aim higher. It doesn't attempt to excel anywhere except in having a really good, really solid JRPG Job progression.The art style was a HUGE turn off for me. I think BD1 is a visual masterpiece. The chibi didn't feel like it was cute to hide weak character design. It used it to great effect. I can't say BD2 uses its strange doll-like aesthetic nearly as well, though it DOES use it to some effect. Unfortunately, as I said, it does not excel here. You will get used to the doll-style, but every time I use one of the character supers I am left completely underwhelmed by the lack of effort put into them. One last note on the visuals: The lack of visual effort in a lot of the game would make BD2 a wonderful candidate to receive some beautiful pre-rendered cut-scenes as a reward for working through the story. I am at least 3/4's of the way through and many major events have happened. There are only in-engine scenes so far and I'm not expecting that to change.The music is very pleasant. This is somewhere I think BD2 lands right where it needs to. I really like the themes and motifs in the music and I would rather it be what it is than be over the top orchestral epics like some other JRPGs. The music is a nice peaceful ride.The characters are fine. Elvis is a great stand-out as are some of the side-cast. The main cast is nice, pleasant and inoffensive though the player character feels half-baked. I think I would have preferred a silent, nodding protagonist rather than... Seth, I think his name is.... Gloria is nice and sweet and Adele has a fun attitude.Stopping for now.

_childDocuments_.review: Great for casual gaming if you only get 30 minutes or so of playtime. Game's grindy after chapter 3.Generic in a lot of ways, re-uses Final Fantasy tropes since it's a spiritual successor, but once you unlock the fourth asterisk(job) things really open up. There's a lot to play with and work out. You'll find a lot of quests, sub-quests, optional enemies, hidden loot, and grass that wants to be cut.Nice little bonus, if you idle games, there's an idle boat feature that gives you items while the game is running and you're online. There's an Othello-like board/collectible card game as a distraction.If you're looking for mechanics that mix up the old JRPG formula, this is your standard turn based, job system JRPG... with a twist. The Brave/Default system. Which sounds more confusing than it is. Brave points are action points, which are the amount of actions you can take per turn. While the default action is an action used to defend and increment your brave points.You can have a maximum of 4 brave points, which means you can take a maximum of 4 actions per turn. You can take 4 actions per turn, even if you don't have the brave points... BUT... if your points go negative, your next turn is skipped and your BP counter increases. Your character's turn will be skipped until your BP are no longer negative.Otherwise, there are jobs with abilities that unlock the more experience you gain using them. You gain more classes/abilities as you progress, giving you more options to use in-game. I it's fun to think through what classes you'll want to use, or what class abilities synergize best per situation.

_childDocuments_.review: This series has meant so much to me ever since the first game, and I can say without a doubt, after over 500 hours with this game, that it is my favorite in the series. The combat is the best I've ever seen in any videogame with a ton of incredible, well designed jobs that you can mix and match to create devastating combos. It's very easy to get into with a relatively low skill floor, and has an incredibly high skill ceiling for anyone who wants to put in the effort to learn the different combinations that can beat bosses with relative ease. If that wasn't enough, this game was designed with low level in mind and it shows with how clever so many of the skills in this game are. They gave all the necessary tools to make low level fun and rewarding, without just throwing it in without any thought as to wether or not it might work. Ever since my second playthrough I've been doing nothing but low level runs and learning more about the game every time. If anyone wants to check out my Youtube channel, I have guides and boss fight videos showcasing level one strats. The channel is YewGeneolgia10x if you are interested in checking it out. I even have a tier list video where I go in depth on every job in the game and how strong I think they are relative to each other and the bosses in the game. I can't recommend this game enough. It has the best combat system ever, probably the best OST ever, some phenomenal characters, and a story that admittedly feels a bit rushed at the end but has an incredible theme throughout that they play off of perfectly. Easy 10/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast with this game. It is a throwback to the turn based RPGs of the 90's-2000's. It was a bit grindy at times but for some reason it didn't bother me. There are difficulty spikes but nothing that ever was too tough to get past. The story was fully voiced and had some interesting characters. They flesh out the world pretty well and bring some history to the land too.  The main theme for the story and the combat is the job system. You unlock new jobs that gives new roles to your party. Each job can level up on it's own and there are passive abilities in each job that give you utility even if you switch to a new job. You can also set a sub-job which gives you the "commands" from another job too. The system was really enjoyable for me as I looked for different fun combinations for my party. There are some very broken setups that destroy the difficulty but I didn't find those until I had basically beaten the game.Overall, I highly recommend this game - I thoroughly enjoyed it. The job system allows you to set things up how you want - although you will likely need a white mage most of the game. The story was engaging and had some fun moments. If you like turn based combat than  and give this game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game with a few shortcomings that you may or may not be able to tolerate. You will inevitably die to enemies whose counters and weaknesses are sometimes deliberately hidden from you. While the voice acting and character interactions are fun, the overall story falls apart at points and can be unintentionally funny, with attempts at seriousness falling flat thanks to wall-eyed character models and sometimes stiff animation. The dungeons are maze-like and uninspired. Less for the sake of levelling your characters and more for the sake of gaining new job abilities, you  have to grind a bit. This can be minimised if you know what you're doing with certain items and abilities though, especially in the late game. If all this sounds alright to you, I'd give this game a shot. The soundtrack and job system carry this game hard. Mixing and matching passive and active abilities to make your team untouchable, guarantee crits and regularly hit the damage cap(s) can be really satisfying, especially if you've been hitting a wall with a certain boss. Pushing myself to the next big boss just to hear one of their many unique themes was enough to get me through most of it. If you're skipping this one, keep an eye out for the sequel that we know is coming. This dev team have admirably been very eager to get feedback, and if they take the right criticisms on board I think BDIII has huge potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Spiritually akin to Final Fantasy 5, this game gets great mileage out of solid and varied gameplay, coherent plot, gorgeous scenery and incredible music.To elaborate:- The balance is well done - on the hardest difficulty, you can complete the game just by doing all available side quests before tackling the main story, without the need for intentional grinding.- The gear system (weight limits per job) uniquely makes you consider using items that aren't best-in-slot, so older gear remains meaningful much longer than just until you get an upgrade.- The combat system has some serious depth with the action-borrowing mechanics and a wide array of possible jobs (well, until you get that one late game job and the "borrowing" part goes out the window, but you need it by then).- All the spells are visually distinct and have good animations, and the town backdrops are absolutely gorgeous.- The music is amazing even in a vacuum, but also serves well for accenting characters and events. There's over an hour of battle themes alone, and all but two of them (IMO) are absolutely stellar - with the second half of the game having some proper facemelters.- The story/plot is simple, akin to FF5, mildly campy, but by that virtue it's easy to follow, and still allows for some emotionally intense moments.The few drawbacks are the player avatar having all the personality of a cardboard cutout and villains having some of the cheesiest writing/VA this side of the gaming industry (some accents are nails on the chalkboard).

_childDocuments_.review: This one's only for hardcore JRPG mechanics fans.  The bosses are very hard, and even the random encounters take time and effort.  The plot and characters are quite generic.  I've been comparing the plot to cafeteria food; it does the job but it's nothing exciting.  I'm also 85 hours in and have only seen the bad ending; this is a long game.The mechanics are the interesting part.  The Job system means you want to constantly be switching what skills your party has.  The Equipment Weight system means there's a reason to keep all your outdated weapons and armor around.  Passives synergize with other classes, equipment gets various special immunities, mastered Jobs get their own unique passives that make it worth keeping them equipped.  It's a customizer's dream.  Probably my favorite system.  (Having not played the previous Bravely Defaults.)The Brave/Default system is about turn-stacking; you can take up to four turns at once, and so can the enemies, so it's a tactical game of knowing when to attack and when to turtle up. In random encounters, it's heavily in your favor, but it's a different story in bossfights where the bosses can kill a character in two turns and also take four turns at once.I want to emphasize how hard the boss fights are on Normal; there have been six mainline boss fights I've had to rebuild my party to defeat, and that's not counting slog fights and close calls.  They hit hard, and they counterattack constantly.  Later on, they start counterattacking buffs and healing.  The good news is, once you defeat them, you get their Job Class.  Although the auto-counters don't come with it.The encounter rate is too high for how complicated the fights are.  One of the later dungeons took an hour to reach the first savepoint, of four.  Enemies are on the map, but the map is mainly tight corridors you can't really maneuver in, so you're just going to have to fight everything, or try to run away and despawn them.  I never had to go out of my way to grind, but that's poor comfort.  (There's also a lot of sidequests of "kill X number of this monster".  The latest endgame one wants 35 spider enemies.)So, this one's if you like Job Systems and hard fights.
_childDocuments_.name: BRAVELY DEFAULT II

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a lot of fun and one of my favorite jrpgs of recent years.  Difficulty can be erratic and you will probably die a few times along the way.  Even with that it's still my favorite in the series.  + Runs and looks much better than the switch version.+ Story and writing are better than previous entries and Octopath.  Far less tropey writing and the main story is at least halfway coherent.  Nothing amazing but it's decent.+ Can easily avoid most battles through avoiding enemies on screen, items, or in combat skills.  Low level mobs run away from you on the map.  Dungeons have waypoints.  Getting around and backtracking is easy, but you still need to fight a bit to get through a new area.  + Deep class system.  Fixes some of the balance problems of previous entries with the passive that lets you break the damage cap.  That 3BP move you buffed to the gills can now do more than 9999 damage.  There are a lot more ways to have decent damage as opposed to being forced into multihit attacks.+/- Takes some understanding of mechanics to progress smoothly.  If you're an RPG vet you'll figure it out easy enough but I can see newcomers making a lot of bad choices and being overwhelmed.  The difficulty settings don't seem to affect anything other than the enemies speed.  You will get destroyed by bosses even on easy if your party is a mess.  The game gives you lots of xp and jp boosts to use for when you hit a wall or need to quickly switch up your party for a boss.  The only way to progress is to git gud.  Simply grinding without a plan and using the same strategy with an extra level or two won't work.  +/- The bosses are tough even once you know what you're doing.  You will probably need a learning death on some of them.  The main thing that will get you are the counters.  Some of them take jobs out of the fight completely.  A bit of an issue in the first chapter when you don't have many jobs or time to level up alternative ones.  You will also likely need to change your gear to cover elemental resistances and status ailments.  It feels unfair when you go in blind, but once you've made the necessary adjustments it feels good.  Fortunately there's always a save point or autosave right before a boss.

_childDocuments_.review: "Isn't it too soon to review a JRPG?"Not in this case, no, because it can only get better. They managed to create a party with great chemistry, the most amazing OST ever, the best battle and level up systems (I mean those are the same as BD and BS but you get what I'm saying). It is both new and traditional, it makes you curious and nostalgic, as every franchise should be and do.Is it anything I don't like? Well, yes. Scripted battles are as lame and uninspired as the villain, but in the past games the villains became interesting much later on.Also the crystals of the elements. But I feel it's kinda on brand for this specific franchise, so yeah, it's totally forgivable.Do yourself a favor and play it on hard. Your boss fights will feel way more epic, trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is essentially a more modern take on classic JRPGs such as the early Final Fantasy titles. It features turn based battles against a plethora of enemies with distinct types and different strengths/weaknesses, and a robust job system that offers a lot of customization and the ability to have fun creating overpowered job combinations and builds. The plot is a bit stereotypical, but it does have quite a few interesting subplots and twists, and it's strengthened a lot by the superb voice acting. The art style is simply gorgeous, and the soundtrack features some really memorable music tracks.Lastly, as far as the PC port is concerned, I've encountered zero problems after 10 hours of playing and in general the game runs very smoothly. The only issue is that the game kind of expects you to play with a controller in typical JRPG fashion.Overall the game seems excellent so far, highly recommended for fans of classic JRPGs.

Enjoyable but also not as memorable as a lot of other JRPGs by Square Enix. _childDocuments_.review: Get Bravely Default II if you're a fan of the original Bravely Default or if you're looking for a story-rich JRPG like Final Fantasy, but with a twist in combat. Bravely default II's combat mechanics make for very interesting (and frustrating battles) thanks to the Brave/Default mechanic (allowing you to store 1 turn for an extra turn later, or use up extra turns so you forfeit later ones).Here's a quick overview:PROs+ Great Graphics (sadly, might not appeal to everyone)+ Amazing Voice Acting from Well Known Voice Actors!+ Quite a lot of cut scenes to add more depth to the story+ Strong character development+ Original Soundtracks are amazinggg+ Highly customisable builds – Ability to mix Classes, Equipments and Abilities make for very interesting builds and combat! (Probably the greatest selling point here)MEHs= Can be somewhat grindy= Story might not be super unique (think crystals and saving the world... sounds familiar?)= Not much guidance outside of story-related stuff= Hard to tell if monsters/bosses are too strong for you, so best to save often (at first)= Game has MULTIPLE endings= Monster encounters are not randomised and can be "controlled"!CONS- Quests are not super imaginative and can be quite repetitive- Certain classes/builds can be abusable and can easily trivialise HUGE parts of the game - Card mini-game doesn't offer too much of a challenge and you'll likely quickly get the hang of it- On harder difficulties, could be very hard to deal with certain bosses without having to grind/abuse certain mechanics (insane damage + multiple turns + status effects)Overall, a really solid game that should keep you entertain for hours if you're already a fan of JRPGs!Would recommend starting on "HARD" difficulty and completing ALL endings for those with a bit more experience in JRPGs! (You get an achievement for that too!)
_childDocuments_.name: BRAVELY DEFAULT II

_childDocuments_.review: PROS: - The combo of multi classes is great. - Fun battles and mostly decent music - Straight forward Fantasy game with the crystals and saving the world etc.. CONS:- (Pro if you are lazy) - Maxing out the Beastlord and just farming monsters once you get Beast Whisper makes the game really easy. Your stats will be insane.- It is kind of fun to play with the combo of classes and abilities to see just how massive you can make your damage. A lot of people get to the point where you can one round bosses. - The multiple endings can be confusing at first... but then once you get to the actual ending it feels a little underwhelming. - I am mixed about the graphics of the actual characters. Like if they were aiming for minimalism I almost would have liked an Octopath pixel style more than the weird Wii looking one. What makes the game is the class combo / abilities. Everything else is pretty straight forward. I had a lot of fun but it was not anything mind blowing. It feels like an updated old Final Fantasy game from the Super Nintendo.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely recommended. I really enjoyed Octopath Traveller so it's no surprise that I think this game is awesome as well. They're very similar to each other, and each have things they did better than the other.An example of something this game did better than Octopath Traveller was the achievements being less annoying, and overworld map improvements like being able to see un-looted chests in an area. I've also not run into any chests that were straight up invisible like I did in Octopath Traveller (basically that  game is completely isometric, so sometimes chests were in places that were not even visible - combine that with the fact that there was an achievement for looting every single chest and you have a very annoying thorn in the side). Another example of an annoying achievement in Octopath Traveller is the one for analyzing all enemies in the game. The way the scaling works, this is actually missable because some enemies no longer appear once your level is too high. No achievements like that in Bravely Default 2, thank god.A lot of the jobs in this game feel very irrelevant - there's almost too many. For instance, you get a job very early into the game that relies on spending the money you earn and it doesn't seem very viable...There's also a pretty mandatory grind that you should do to get all of your characters' Freelancer job maxed out ASAP, and 3 of your passive perk slots are taken up by leveling perks for a large part of the game, which is sort of annoying. You'll probably put 60-80 hrs in, maybe even more, before you can feel good about unequipping those leveling passives (JP Up/Up&Up)... I think that was an oversight.Overall this game has an interesting combat system and I really loved the card game that they put in it as well. Very similar to Triple Triad if you've ever played FFXIV. Loved that.Charming game with cringey dialogue sometimes, but I think it's worth buying on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Bravely Default II is a very standard JRPG in the style of 90's-era Final Fantasy. The brave/default system is an interesting changeup but otherwise if you've played any of the older FF games, you know exactly what to expect here.For some reason BDII, despite being a very simple game, works really well. The focus is on just four party members, all of whom will join the party very close to the start of the game. As a result, each character has time to develop and all four share the spotlight evenly; you won't have anyone joining at the eleventh hour and consequently having no time to develop. The voice acting is mostly very good (although without spoiling anything there is one boss enemy whose voice acting may be the worst I've ever heard, which is no doubt a matter of the direction of the voice acting being intentionally over-the-top in a way that just doesn't work). While the plot is simple, the writing is very good. There were a couple of twists that genuinely surprised me without feeling contrived, and the characters are refreshingly mature for a JRPG. I played this right after Persona 4 Golden and was pleased to see a total lack of hot springs scenes/characters changing personalities on a whim. The boss fights are a highlight; there are an impressive number of them, most of them have visually cool designs, and each of them has a clear gameplan that you're expected to analyze and adapt to. That adaptation is done in the form of jobs, another similarity to some of the old FF games. The job system is impressively diverse; each character can accept each job, and each job has a unique outfit and set of skills. Leveling up these jobs is a relatively simple affair, and the game gives you tools to speed it up further. There's an incredible amount of synchronicity between so many of the jobs at your disposal, and it's truly impressive how many different ways you can tackle each boss encounter. This synchronicity between jobs, and the game's expectation that you pay attention to the strategies used by each boss, is more important in clearing boss fights than grinding or min/maxing gear (although that will certainly make things easier).If any of this sounds like you would enjoy it, trust me and pick up BDII. It doesn't do anything revolutionary, but it does everything that it sets out to do incredibly well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played one of the old-school Dragon Quest / Final Fantasy games, you will know exactly what Bravely Default 2 is about.Heroes of light vs. armies of darkness, powerful crystals, villain with a "tragic" backstory, evil mastermind who's about to be unleashed, ridiculously powerful bosses, the option to speed up battles, game-breaking hero skills, the obligatory card game, base game ending, post-game ending, orchestral soundtrack... Bravely Default 2 has it all, plus it adds a really small number of modern JRPG features. So if you are ever in the mood for a classic, yet modern JRPG adventure, this is probably one of the finest choices that Steam currently has to offer. Would wait for a sale, even if it's not a big one, and get it!

_childDocuments_.review: As far as the old school RPG formula goes, Bravely Default 2 checks all the boxes. Unfortunately these exact same boxes have been ticked time and time again. This is yet another story of destined heroes of light charged with saving magic crystals from the Big Bad. It's all very run of the mill and has been done literally dozens of times before. You would think that Square Enix could at least change the formula somewhat from titles that are now 30 years old. We're stuck in an endless timeloop so bad that they should make a game about that instead. Final Fantasy meets the Neverending Story. Maybe they should title the next entrant in the arena The Neverending Fantasy. But with all that said, BD2 isn't a bad game. Square took time with this one to ensure there was plenty of character dialogue throughout. Unlike some of their other titles, the plentiful cutscenes seemed more balanced here. In general I didn't feel bombarded by them, and they made it easy to simply skip them if desired. Overall the story fits into a middle range. Just deep enough to pull you in and tell the tale, not deep enough to get too emotional about any particular thing. (Except for that whole scene with Adam which was just trash)Like some of the older Final Fantasy titles, there are a spate of different classes/jobs that you can assign to your characters throughout the course of the game. Having choices is a good thing, but half of them just seem redundant. Realistically most players will only be utilizing a handful of roles/abilities throughout their playthrough. Still, players aren't required to use any of the jobs at all if they don't want to. In that regard, this design choice doesn't really impede players. In fact, you can quite comfortably beat this game with only the Freelancer and Vanguard job roles, both of which are received within the first two hours of gameplay.Square did a good job on this title in several other key areas as well. Equipment choices are plentiful, with towns consistently refreshing stock based on player progression. There isn't much need to farm for equipment, but if you're the min-max type that wants to get your hands into the power leveling arena early, you can. Enemies have a decent range of different weaknesses and strengths, not only to elements but also to differing weapon types. This is important if you want to keep your character under-leveled for more of a challenge, but can be comfortably ignored if you want to steamroll the game by powerleveling. Towns and dungeons are standard faire here. Plenty of annoying labyrinths, with a puzzle or two thrown into the mix. There will be lots of traveling back and forth, both as part of the main plot as well as the very numerous side quests which are completely optional. Thankfully there is a fast travel option in every town, and warp portals in most dungeons, which makes getting around much easier. All in all, I don't really have anything negative to say about BD2, except for the title itself. Bravely...Default? What a stupid name. Why would they choose to name the very game after a game mechanic? This is like renaming a Tesla Model S to Big Battery. And speaking of this game mechanic.....why couldn't they just call it Defend instead of Default? Bravely Defend sounds a hell of a lot better than Bravely Default. This is definitely a design decision made in a boardroom of overpriced executives.

_childDocuments_.review: Bravely default II is what I had wished Bravely Default and Bravely second to have been. The game is solid and I am enjoying so far. Chapter 4 is a bit of a spike in difficulty, but that's fine. A criticism I have of this game is that the equip-able abilities seem sparse and the removal of weapon lore makes me sad, but this game is a game worth the 60.Edit 5/27/2024: I have beaten the game. I have seen it to the end, and I'd like to change what I've said while still having the above review. I like how they've handled the Weapon Lore abilities, while the equip-able abilities are sparse, what they lack in quantity they out do themselves in quality. I can see the vision. While I would've liked more magic-based abilities, relegating the spells to how they were in Bravely Default, I wouldn't say I hate this change. Some of the graphical issues I've experienced were a bit... weird, but they're not off-putting. I still stand by Bravely Default II is what I had wished Bravely Default and Bravely Second to have been. A new criticism I have is THE COUNTER SYSTEM. OH MY ♥♥♥♥. Look, I get it, you want to make sure people don't just steamroll, I get it... but my god, a lot of my frustration in the later half of the game comes from Counters, and while Counter-Savvy does exist, the fact that there's a counter that's basically "Counter literally breathing". Over all, I recommend this game, at 60 or on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first time playing the Bravely Default series and, overall, it did manage to satisfy my urge for some classic JRPG. The default system also adds a fairly interesting dynamic to the game as well, which puts it slightly apart from its peers - something that I believe most rpg lovers would come to appreciate.However, the game is not without its flaws. The story is, perhaps, the weakest aspect of it all as just like its name suggests, it is extremely defaultish. Perhaps that's the way developers planned it (hence the name of the game) but, damn, it sucks playing a game where you can pretty much guess every step along the way. The job system is both interesting and frustrating at the same time. Here's a tip for perspective players, do your best to fight temptation and not play your first walk through with a particular game-breaking class. You'll enjoy the game a lot more. _childDocuments_.review: Full confession: I thought this was a port of Bravely Second. I bought it anyway, because I love that game and I do hope they port those eventually. If you were living under a rock and didn't know that Bravely Default 2 even released for Switch, then just note that this is not Bravely Second.That said, you should definitely pick this game up if you're a fan of the series so far. Or even if you haven't played Bravely Default or the sequel (but never play Bravely Second without playing Bravely Default), it's worth the play through if you're into JRPGs.That being said, if you did play the first game(and the sequel), just note that this game doesn't have as much of a blatant twist as the other. It also takes itself more seriously than the previous games, which isn't all bad. The story is pretty solid, but it lost a lot of that humorous charm Bravely Default and Bravely Second had, and replaces it with drama.I do feel the game had a "smaller stage" than its predecessors, and it doesn't really go into depth as much either, but that's okay. Everything you experience, you experience in the now and you piece the rest together yourself. It felt somewhat nostalgic.I played a lot of the game in both Japanese and English, and I will say that certain characters feel like an entirely different person in the other language. I was a little critical of the English voice acting, at first, but it grew on me by the end. You can't go wrong playing it either way, but I suggest you pick one so you're not disillusioned by the different character types--especially if you understand Japanese.Game play is that of a standard RPG with the same elements brought to us in Bravely Default. Complete with a job system.Overall, I didn't like it as much as Bravely Default or Second, but it's a good game in it's own right, with its own tone.

_childDocuments_.review: This earlier Switch title suddenly dropped on steam without my prior knowledge. So I do think they both could and should have made a bit bigger splash to get some attention for the release.The short version of my experience with the game is as follows:Its a modern take on the classic job-system jrpgs (think ff5). ran perfect for me, no problems from start to finish, no console fps cap. is pretty mediocre, nothing special here. was good enough to keep me interested until the end. are usually short and sweet, with unlockable shortcut-teleporters. was never needed on my part, until I was trying to complete the equipment-guide. is more about finding the right job-combinations than stat-checks. was relatively easy, and can be completely crushed with some of the most powerful combinations.Bought it full-price and tbh I got my value out of it.
