_childDocuments_.review: Overall it's a good game, but world was wayyyyy better. There are a few things that I like a bit more with MHRise though. The switch skills are great and are a fantastic way to really customize your playstyle. I like the diversity of monsters that you are hunting, and the different weapons and styles there are. I like that I'm not fighting 3 different types of the same monster. I even enjoy certain aspects of the wirebug system. The buddy system is more in depth than World and you get a doggo, so that's cool. But that's where it really stops. Let's get the obvious ones out of the way, graphics, maps, and story. MHRise looks and feels like an arcade game with a very basic story. This is understandable as it was a game designed for the Switch and then ported over. With that said, now it's time to get into some more of the in depth issues I have with Rise. 1. The keyboard and mouse bindings for this game are atrocious. Probably the worst I've ever played with in a game. I tried rebinding it to where it made more sense but eventually gave up and just plugged in an xbox controller. The fact that it supports controller is the only reason why this issue is more forgiven than the others. 2. The decoration system, I wasn't really a fan of. Because it just added even more grind onto an already tedious grind. Surprisingly it felt easier to get decorations in World. In Rise you have to get specific materials per decoration, which means grinding the same monster over and over and over again. It gets boring fast especially early on. 3. The charm system. Geezus how do you mess that up that badly?? Instead of crafting charms you now have to meld them. To do so you have to sacrifice materials like you would for decorations in World. Except to get any of the good ones you have to select the higher melding process. Not only do you have to wait to then get said charms after doing hunts, it's random what you get. So you could sacrifice materials up to 3 times to try and get a divine protection charm, and it will give you 3 random charms for skills you didn't select, and then those 3 are completely random as to what level of those skills you get, with the majority of the time you get tier one useless charms. This whole system needs completely reversed into what it was in world. 4. The buddy system, while more in depth, is also kinda worse in some ways. Like the fact that you can't change your Palico's class. So if you're new to the game and make your Palico a healer but decide later on that you want them to be more of a fighter, you can't change it. You have to hire a completely different Palico and start taking them on quests with you. This may just be a personal preference but I absolutely hate that. I don't want to take some other Palico, I want to take mine. I don't care if you can change their name or gear, I want mine lol. That was one of the best parts of world was that I had this debonair extraordinaire cat named Dubois that joined me on my adventures. I could even have entire builds focused around Dubois and making him the star of the show, but all of that was just stripped away. Yeah I have a dog now, but there's just not that connection like there was in World. 5. Rampages. I absolutely hate rampages. It's pretty much like a small tower defense game, not crazy hard, just annoying mostly. Here's the thing though, I don't like tower defense games. I don't play Monster Hunter to play tower defense. It's one thing to simply add it, but to make these fights absolutely mandatory to progress is just horrible design, just awful. Make them optional, sure I don't care at that point, but don't make these boring af fights mandatory. They just take away from the actual fun parts of the game. World had this issue too though with Sieges and endgame fights. They'd make these sieges and bosses that almost required a full party of pretty good people to even beat, and then locked all the best weapons and armor behind them. I'd love a weapon I could customize more to my playstyle, but I'm not playing your shoddy missions just to get them. 6. My final and probably biggest issue with this game, and the only reason I almost couldn't recommend it, monster AI. Holy crap it is bad in this game. I like the new movesets, they're interesting and diverse. But the monster aggression is ridiculous. I get that you can do a bit more in Rise than you could in World as you've got switch skills and counters now. But that turned it up to maybe a 3-5, but the monsters were turned up to a 10. They don't hit harder, they're not a crazy amount faster, but the way they act over the course of the fight is just beyond what it should be. The will spam the same exact move multiple times repeatedly until they hit you. So you could dodge the first 3 times they do the move, but eventually you'll be out of stamina and they'll connect anyways. There's multiple monsters each with their own attack where they do this until it connects. Both Barioth's breath attack and dive attack. I had one fight where I counted the amount of times he went for his breath attack in a fight. In a hunt that lasted under 15 minutes he went for his breath attack over 26 times. The last fight I had with him he dive bombed 8 times in a row. No other moves, he would dive bomb repeatedly until he hit me. Rathalos' air tail swipe is like this, the spider things sweeping fire attack, zinogre's walking slam thing he does. You could dodge them every time, they're just going to keep doing it until it connects. This almost ruins the entire experience. One of the best things about World was studying the monster, learning their moveset. Knowing when they're going for different moves based upon their habits, and then being rewarded by taking less damage as your skills grew. This goes out the window in Rise. Now it doesn't matter if you know they're going for a certain move, because they're just going to keep doing it until they get you. It's a very unrewarding feeling and really takes away from the entire experience. It goes from being fun, to just tedious. It's less about "Am I skilled enough to do this?", to, "Did I bring enough healing items to do this?"I use DB and SNS too, I don't even use slower weapons. I can't imagine the feeling of being a GS user dealing with all of that lol. It's just made most of this game a slog for me and for the first time in a Monster Hunter game I find myself constantly asking the question, "How far am I from the end of the game so that I can just finish it and be done." I'm not excited about the end game, I'm not excited to try new builds or to farm different monsters or any of it, and that's a horrible feeling to have. Would I recommend this game? Sure, it's a monster hunter game, and if you're new to the series it's not a horrible place to start. However I would recommend Monster Hunter World a whole lot more lol. Make World 2, keep doggos and switch skills, and some of these other monsters, that it.

_childDocuments_.review: To start Rise is not world 2 so if your expecting that you will be slightly disappointed. But Rise and into sunbreak is fun amazing none the less. Rise delivers a fun fast paced hunting experience that is a really fun change of pace. you can 100% tell this game was made for the switch because the the features like a pause hunt function really allow you to play at your own pace. Negatives of base riseIn by no means is rise perfect. Rampages whale a nice change of pace from normal siege quests just become tiresome after 4-5. the tower defense horde combat just really becomes a slog and its a good thing they added the ability to fight the special monsters you get at base rise endgame without them. Base Rise also has a difficulty problem. to put it bluntly its easy. until you get to late end game monsters there is really no challenge. There is also no reason to grind the end game monsters no special armor, decos, or weapons.Positives of base risesilk bind allows for some weapons to play and a completely different style then they normal would. because of the lack of difficulty you really dont need to have the most optimized builds you can play and experiment how you want. take for instance LS(which is the most popular weapon) you can go the normal route of get to red gauge then preform helm splitter or you could do what i did on my switch play through and use sakura slash instead and get multiple hits that do tic damage on a monster and play elemental LS. Palamutes are also a amazing addition that allow you to get across the map way faster then walking. and the palico changes really allow you to customize them to do what you want having diffrent classes of them is fun. you also always even in multiplayer hunts have access to one of them and in single player you can choose to bring 2 of any combination. want 2 palicos you can do that want one of each you can do that too. one the the biggest things they added is that the whole world is a hub there is no more inviting people to your lobby to only be able to see them in the designated hub areas you can even go to the training area together. Sunbreak NegativesThe start is filled with a lot of powered up Base rise monsters its not until later you get to fight the new monsters. another thing I've noticed that is a (negative) is there are a lot of capture side quests witch can lead to a lot of your pub hunts to end in such, this can be really annoying for people grinding out parts. Sunbreak positivesthey turned everything up to 11. silk binds gained by every weapon are amazing. the ultimate moves for palicos are so fun to watch. palimutes had multiple changes that made them way more useful then just as a mount. the monsters they added from other games are s tier choices and when you get to them omg is it fun(they even added the frontier flagship espinath). Its also probably the best final boss we have got in awhile. the 2 new maps are fantastic. and we have at least another year+ worth of content coming. with the first new monster drop coming in august of 2022. the difficultly whale still not as hard as old game (probably do to so QOL updates) is amazing once you get to end game. the afflicted monsters are hit like trucks and can take a hit too. all in all i would give rise base a 8/10 and sunbreak a 9.5/10 neither are perfect but if you are looking for more monster hunter or a fun experience i highly recommend the game and expansion (a note with both rswitch and PC at the time of review i have a combined 400 hours having used 6/14 wepaons)

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter Rise is a refreshing reminder that simple ideas are sometimes the bestThe premise of the game is incredibly simple, there are giant monsters roaming about and you need to change that. You have 14 weapon types to choose from, each with a massive tree of craftable variants. As you go on hunting monsters you turn their hides and bones into your weapons and armour, each piece being styled after its respective monster, hunting a bird of prey will deck you in feathers, while a rock dragon drips you out in stony plate. Graphically the game is a switch port and looks the part, while not awful the graphical fidelity does leave something to be desired. I will concede that it's art direction more than makes up for it, quite frankly the armour and weapons you can make look appropriately overkill and obscene, and the fact that it only takes a few short hunts before you can start looking like a serious menace is a very welcome prospectThe monsters themselves are downright inspired, while there is certainly a lot of cross over between their general themes, there being a fair amount of dragons and such, each one looks and fights distinctive enough that it doesn’t feel like they are there for padding. Even if Rathalos looks like a generic western dragon, it is more than made up for with the rest of the cast, creatures like Almudron and Magnamalo being particular favourite designs of mine.In regards to the actual hunts, obviously not every fight is going to be able to be some big epic battle but the progression through the various monsters has so far kept each one feeling appropriately powerful. The difficulty has definitely been skewed to the low side however, while being able to make a lot of mistakes (especially as a new player like myself) is good to get into the swing of things, this ended up making a few fights frustratingly difficult rather than a proper challenge. That is probably more an issue of my own inexperience and veteran players will probably be fine, but the game has a learning curve for new players that seems inconsistent at its most generous reading. Despite the ease of some of the encounters I wouldn't honestly say any of them are boring. Even the easiest fight is still decently enjoyable with higher end gear if even not for the fact that pummeling a defenseless raptor ignites my caveman brain. After around 75 hours i’d say there aren't any fights that have been egregious enough for me to want to avoid entirely and despite simplicity they’ve all remained fairly entertainingBut what reason is there to hunt monsters if not for gear. The weapons and Armor of the game are mostly crafted through drops gathered from beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of the various monsters, if i'm not mistaken each monster has its own set of armor and a variety of weapons to go with it. And while a large part of the arsenal looks dope as hell, a lot of the weapons feel very awkward to use and switching between them can mean entirely different control schemes that are frustrating to grasp. If I want to switch between my bow and hunting horn several unrelated controls are thrown in that put general abilities, like sprinting or using the wirebug, on different keys or overlap them in a way that means I have to work against muscle memory. Why Melee weapons let you sheathe your weapon and hold for sprint while ranged makes you toggle sprint if you want to sheathe is strange to me but it’s just annoying enough to get to meIn terms of complaints I wont say the game is flawless. It’s price tag certainly seems a bit steep, and while I have 100% got my money's worth from it I can see it being a turn off for some. The combat is good and fluid, but despite comparisons to darksouls, lacks the immediate finesse. For a new player there is just so much ♥♥♥♥ thrown at you it can be incredibly overwhelming. You are given literally hundreds of various items right off the bat with not a great explanation on their uses. There are a large number of status effects the game doesn’t explain and it feels like I was constantly glancing at the wiki to figure out what they meant. The instant failure after 3 deaths on your team makes certain fights online far more stressful than they need to be.The Maps are all pretty good however there's only 5 (or technically 8 however 3 of them are more just single arenas) and you frequently fight monsters in the same areas each time and even when they move around it does feel kinda repetitive. You are able to join random hunts online or search for people doing a specific quest but there is no server browser, if there's a specific monster i want to fight in multiplayer i have to try and join one of the quests its in to see if anyones doing it, or start my own and hope the lobby fills up.Overall Monster Hunter Rise is a thoroughly enjoyable endeavor with some quirks and a bit of a curve to getting into but so far it has been well worth the effort. It is most certainly not for everyone but because of how it presents itself, if you think you’ll be into it there's a good chance you will, the game doesn’t hide how repetitive it may seem and I greatly respect that. The game definitely has its flaws but none of them are major enough to be a turn off and it is more than made up for in what it has going for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to other Monster Hunter games, this iteration is very accessible for new players. There is a distinction between Gathering Hub quests and Village Quests. The Village Quests are much lower in difficulty compared to the Gathering Hub quests, allowing you learn the patterns of a lot of monsters, without being too harshly punished (yet).By playing Village Quests you unlock Gathering Hub ranks doing an "exam", which is the equivalent of doing a number Gathering Hub quests on a certain rank and then doing the "Urgent quest" that follows. As such you can skip going through the early stages of the Gathering Hub by doing village quests and the associated exams. Whichever you fancy.Compared to Monster Hunter World, they added a Palamute mount to help you traverse maps faster. On top of that, they also introduced a Wirebugs mechanic. This allows you to verticially or horizontally traverse maps, but also incorporate them in your combos when dealing with monsters. I don't think I can go (or want to be) without these two things ever again... Going back to Monster Hunter World will be a pain, haha.Other than that, I feel the grind for gear is okay. There are a lot of monsters, but especially with the Village Quests you burn through a large portion of them very quickly. So by the time you start focusing on High Rank, most monsters they throw at you don't surprise anymore. I can imagine that for some people this would feel repetitive. It does for me in a sense. But on the other hand, it feels great to deal with monsters with great efficiency once you learn their patterns, which you can only really achieve by fighting against them often. So it's a love/hate relationship.Graphics are okay, it's visibly an upgraded Switch game, but personally I don't mind that. It's performance is very stable, which is the most important aspect to me when fighting monsters anyway. Monster design is great.Definately recommended for first time Monster Hunter players to get the hang of a lot of mechanics, and then go back to Monster Hunter World for more. You are really going to miss your Palamute/Wirebug though...One additional side-note though: There is a new Tower Defense like quest type called Rampage, and the game will from time to time force you to participate in one to progress your ranks. I don't like it as a solo player, but I understood it's great fun when played in a party.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't find any part of this game more enjoyable than World. There's more monsters from the start, but weapons feel mostly the same. The bow has some nice upgrades to it and is pretty fun, Insect Glaive somehow feels worse, everything else I tried seemed pretty much the same outside of wirebug stuff. Graphics are ok, but worse than World. Things get more aggravating than fun at higher ranks, and the community is annoying with all the manhood measuring and chest beating while reassuring each other how things aren't hard. If you enjoy the "git gud" crowd you might fit in, anyone else will probably hate it. I played World a lot, Iceborne wasn't my favorite because it starts in on the idea that cheap deaths are a desirable form of difficulty....monsters hit too hard, or too fast, or require specific items that take days to farm up, and it all just becomes a chore. MH Rise is just more of the same, basically, with worse graphics and wirebugs, most of the monsters feel exactly the same as in World, and as you progress the difficulty comes from things just hitting way too hard or insta-death combos that you can't avoid rather than being a fun kind of difficult. I just eventually stopped caring about progressing and grinding items.       Buddies are another issue. Take the special buddies you can hire; by the time I'd used them, and tried to level them after picking them up early, the same buddies become available only at a higher level on the vendor...so everything I did with them was a complete waste of time. My palico in World always felt useful, but here they're stingy with their special abilities and heals so they're rarely where you need them to be when you actually need them.   I don't like the maps, I don't really care for the wirebugs, weapon and armor progression feels way worse for some reason... it became a pain to try and find armor with stats I actually wanted, or to find upgrades for the weapon I was using after hours and hours of progress. Take the charge blade, where you're sort of stuck with a crappy version of it for way longer than you should be because it takes so long to get to monsters that give you a chance to farm up a decent one.     Rampage missions are so completely terrible that I wish I'd never played one and have no desire to ever even hear about them ever again. I hate Rampage missions. I cannot believe that anyone ever played these when they were being designed and thought they were fun or a good idea.     If you love MH games and want a new one because you ran out of content in another older version, Rise will probably be great for you. If you started with World, like so many people did, nothing about Rise feels like an upgrade. The story is virtually the same as World's.    I loved World and spent a ton of time with it, but I don't like MH Rise and can't honestly say I enjoyed much, if any, of my time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game’s visuals are stunning, with diverse environments that range from sunlit forests to treacherous mountains. The vibrant colours and refined details bring the world of Kamura Village to life, creating an immersive experience that’s beautiful yet expansive. The Japanese-inspired setting adds a unique look that distinguishes Rise from its predecessors, enriching the game’s atmosphere with traditional architecture and folklore-inspired creatures.Monster Hunter Rise introduces several new features that enhance the gameplay experience. The addition of the Wirebug revolutionizes mobility, allowing players to scale cliffs, dodge attacks, and execute aerial maneuvers. This newfound freedom adds a unique twist to the combat, making every hunt engaging and strategic. The inclusion of Palamutes, offers a new way to traverse the environment and adds another way to move around the map.The combat in Monster Hunter Rise is pretty much the same as the previous titles, with the addition of new weapon skills and a skill swap palette. There is a diverse roster of monsters, both familiar and new, each with its own unique behaviors and attacks, The improved fluidity and responsiveness of the combat system make battles more intense and satisfying. The game’s crafting system remains the same, with a plethora of weapon and armor options that cater to different playstyles.The game incorporates several quality-of-life improvements that streamline the hunting experience. The ability to fast-travel and the addition of a more user-friendly interface make preparation and exploration less cumbersome, allowing players to focus more on the thrill of the hunt.Monster Hunter Rise is a excellent addition to the series with exciting new elements. Its captivating world, innovative mechanics, and engaging multiplayer make it a must-play for both veterans and newcomers. Whether you're hunting monsters or exploring the vast landscapes, Rise delivers an unforgettable adventure that will keep you coming back for more.

It has some nice QoL features compared to older games in the series, and has a lot of interesting mechanics that I'd say make it worth playing if you enjoy this style of combat.Cons: The game was originally designed for the Nintendo Switch, and as such is designed more to be a portable game for better or worse. The biggest negatives with that come with that is the graphics and sound design, both of which pale in comparison to Monster Hunter: World. Combat is also a lot more fast paced, and this is widely considered the easiest game in the franchise.Old (Negative) Review: The latest update adds DRM software (called "enigma"), which breaks software compatibility with Linux (including steam deck)...

_childDocuments_.review: Rise/Sunbreak has definitely been one of my favorite games for the past 2 years. It has a lot of pros for me that I honestly can't even remember any shortcomings in comparison to other games (Now that it's a complete game, it really released in kind of a poor state) that aren't boiled down to "would be cool but i don't care they didn't do it".It's easy to get into it, weapons have incredible variety by themselves which means you can basically play more than 3 different ways with most weapons and by getting rid of set bonuses it opened up more armor variety throughout the whole game.If you're playing with friends you can all start the quest together and skip the cutscene if you're not interested, most of them are monster intros and they're short enough to not feel like you're losing time if you decide to watch them.My only real criticism is the fact it has region lock and with me living in Brazil it kinda messes up matchmaking so I do recommend downloading the  mod that just makes it so you can join ANYONE around the globe, and you don't need to worry as the netcode is pretty decent as It won't really disconnect you unless you're really REALLY laggy. (though you still need to change download region to host to a more populated region)

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to preface this review by stating I was very late to the Monster Hunter party and this is my first Monster Hunter game.  For someone new to the series, I was taken back by all the small nuisances, and content there was.  I had to ask a few friends to basically explain some "ins and outs" because either I missed during the beginning of the game or they were never brought up.  You definitely want to watch some guides on Youtube to make your life easier once you progress in this world. There is a weapon for everyone, I have spent so much time trying them all and attacking the training dummy.  I do play on Keyboard and mouse, and only the ranged weapons seem to run smooth on it but I have started to excel on the dual blades after refining my keys and learning muscle memory.Combat is visceral, and very twitchy giving you a real sense of pride and accomplishment when you finally take down a monster.  I have over 300 hours in this and I am progressing rather slowly but having a blast.  If you do not like to grind do not play this because you will fight, fight fight and improve your gear and weapons and it could be repetitive for some.I would love for Capcom to make an MMO of this game with just updates and expansions so all your progress is not lost when a new variation of the game comes out but I am not sure everyone would like that.  I highly recommend buying Monster Hunter Rise and Sunbreak.  I purchases Sunbreak when I reached Hunter Rank 100 but I wanted to complete it all before I took the plunge into Sunbreak.  Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: - New monsters are cool as ♥♥♥♥.- Monster hitboxes are significantly improved from previous games, especially good considering how fast monsters have gotten since World.- General gameplay feels very smooth.- Weapons have actually good and unique models again.- Valstrax- The environments are, to be honest, horribly ugly and bland, not even compared to World but compared to 4U and GU which had great color and skyboxes on a 3DS. Kamura Village, Shrine Ruins, and Flooded Forest are a desaturated mess of murky gray and green. Frost Islands are lifeless and the shin-high water across the entire map looks bad. The desert and volcano are both less bad but still aren't very creative or unique areas. All of the gameplay areas suffer heavily from being a bunch of big empty rooms with practically nothing in them aside from materials around the edges. There are occasionally actually cool setpieces but they are basically all secret areas accessed by wirebugs and you never actually fight monsters in them so they basically don't exist for 99% of gameplay.- Literally only two(2) sets of armor actually cover the face on female characters, like come on dude what the ♥♥♥♥ is that female death stench armor.- General difficulty is kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥ as weapon movesets have gotten so crazy that a bunch of the returning monsters can't keep up.- Wirefall further destroys returning monsters and while monsters that counter wirefalling is fine, there's also monsters that force wirefall or else you get combo'd which is stupid.- Charge Blade's entire flow was completely destroyed by Counter Peak Performance and Condensed Spinning Slash which let you ignore 75% of the weapon's moveset because someone saw the actually good loop of Savage Axe going from Axe to Sword to refill phials whenever it gets low and thought, "yeah, but what if we made it GAIN phials"- Hammer's Impact Crater is way too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ strong, doesn't destroy the entire flow of the weapon like CB's horrible changes but still does wayyyyyyyyyyyy too much damage.

_childDocuments_.review: "We're out of Ideas" - the devs. No ♥♥♥♥.The weakest monster hunter game to date. Extremely repetitive combat.The content is drip fed to us, every few months 1 or 2 "new" monsters, which are all variants of the exisiting roster, with 1 or 2 new attacks, and an element swap.I hope you like ""event quests"" that are just the same regular monster again, and rewards are cosmetic only.Overall Very little monster variety. You do the same ♥♥♥♥ every hunt, every game.The sad reality is all the new stuff added in Rise and Sunbreak are gimmicks, which don't improve the game or make it more replayable:- hunting helpers / birds are a pain to gather- wirebugging is fun at first, but quickly becomes abnoxious. I'm so sick of wire jumping all the time.- monster riding is extremely boring - it completely interrupts the flow of the fight and forces you to do the patronizingly easy minigame, and again its always the same repetitive ♥♥♥♥. Mounting monsters used to feel like a reward, because you had to work towards it, and it took work to do the damage. MHW's version of running monsters into the wall, was also quick and unintrusive to the main combat mechanics. Riding in Rise never feels earned, it usually just happens at random- Monster AI is extremely barebones. Their attack roster is very limited and they will use the same attack over-and-over. For difficulty all that is different is some attacks will hit x2, the animation speed is faster, and damage is higher. No creativity at all. Also all monsters will only fight in 3 or so areas in any given map. Even if you somehow end up in a different and interesting area, they will immediately leave.- The maps are pointless. Like I said, all monsters have their designated 3 or so areas, so you always fight in the same 4-5 areas of the map. Everything else is just a dress up, and there for gathering. All that verticallity and mobility  (wirebugs, etc) are rendered pointless. You never need to be anywhere.-The newest map is just a room, with a nice skybox - and all the new quests take place there, because the devs are literally out of ideas already.

_childDocuments_.review: In order to properly review this game I suppose I have to take into account the history of Monster Hunter which was if I recall correctly was PS2 followed by the PSP. I feel a little like this is a repeat of history with Rise following World. World was made for PS4 and XBox and Rise was made for Nintendo Switch. If you compared the two here on Steam you would think that World was the newer game. Graphics, Biomes and Storyline are all bigger and better in World because it was made for a more powerful console. It feels like everything was ‘dumbed down’ so Rise could be released on a portable system. But...I’m not saying the game is bad. It’s a good, solid Monster Hunter release. It has all the familiar creatures I enjoy hunting. All I’m saying is that I enjoyed World a lot better and I HOPE that if/when another Monster Hunter game is released they bring back the all detail I missed seeing in Rise.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who grew up with the Monster Hunter games (Monster Hunter on ps2, Monster Hunter Freedom Unite on PSP, up to the newly released MHR, having both Switch and PC) the gradual changes and new and old mechanics makes every release an enjoyment for me as a veteran player. Originally a Nintendo Switch release, you cannot compare the quality of Rise to Monster Hunter World due to the design and limitations of the Switch. If you can look past the cries of people who played Monster Hunter World as their first entry into the series who thinks this game looks like a Xbox 360/PS3 or whatever delusional comparison they pull out their ass, then you can enjoy the next iteration of Monster Hunter with this game.In terms of previous mechanics, you still progress through your "Village" and "Guild/Hub" storyline while increasing your Hunting Rank (HR) independently of each other. Like always, quests are split into the Low and High rank where the latter of the two allows for the expansion of the higher tier monsters and monster parts that can be crafted into the higher tier weapons and armor.Without going on a long tangent, the Rampage mechanic has me reminiscing about Overall, this game is more or less the same with previous titles in terms of your basic mechanics and progression. New players can easily jump in and go through the Village quests or go to the Gathering Hub to play solo or with friends online to complete Low to High Rank quests as you progress. Use the new skills and Switch Skills mechanic thanks to the addition of wirebugs and traverse the half a dozen locales available to explore and hunt new and old monsters in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster hunter rise is an excellent game, but it has issues, same as any other monster hunter game.The grind of monster hunter is never bad. Only when you're going for a specific armor set does it get absolutely abhorrent. It's the kind of game that you make with what you're given, but what you're given is almost never what you want.Regardless, the game play is incredible, but i feel that it's gotten so complex that it almost shuts out new players. Learning and mastering each individual monster's battle is the core of monster hunter, but in Rise, learning your own weapons move set is a much greater ordeal, one that one must spend hours on before even approaching a battle. I hope that in Monster hunter 6, we can revert back to the simpler times when it was about the monsters and not the weapon combos.I like the game, but it didn't hold me nearly as long as Monster Hunter World did, which for me, struck a perfect balance between learning your weapon, and learning the monster.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game.  I've played through all of the content it has to offer, beaten every monster, reached master rank 120+.  This game could easily be an 8/10 product, but the absolutely abysmal hitboxes brings this title down HARD to around a 4/10 experience.  I'd offer a cash reward to anyone that could find a game with worse hitboxes in it. Never, in any game in over 30 years, have I been hit by so many attacks that clearly missed me, nor missed by so many attacks that clearly should have hit me.  Attacks that are dodged, and even have the game tell you that you've dodged, still hit you.  One of Rise's main gimmicks is that you can use wirebugs to counter attacks, or add verticality to your attacks.  The issue with this is that your counters fail constantly because the monster's attacks just don't register properly.  Either they go straight through you, or hit you anyway with the character not performing the defensive action.  And if you thought you were safe in the air, guess again.  Currently flying more than twice the monster's height in the air?  You just got smacked by a low claw sweep not 1 foot off the ground.  Attacking the tail?  The bite attack at someone else in front of him just hit you.   Attacking the face?  The tail swipe just blew you away.  On the back left leg?  That right front claw just caught you.It feels like every single attack in the game creates a 20-foot dome around the monster, and you just take damage if you're anywhere in it.  Or if you prepare for it, you do nothing, because it decided not to register that time for no reason.  It's incredibly frustrating for the game to constantly punish the player for something they can't prevent, prepare, or adapt to in any way.  I simply can not, in good faith, recommend a product so janky and lacking in quality in such a critical area.Edit:  After putting in another 130 hours, I can firmly say it's even worse than initially written.  The hitboxes are unforgivably terrible.  Just cart after cart from attacks not even remotely in the same timezone as my character.  I've downgraded my initial 4/10 to a 2/10.  This game should be removed from the store due to being a literal broken product.Do Not Buy This Game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't just have monster it is a monster, especially with Sunbreak (Add-on).It has a lot of content, but everything repeats itself. Sometimes you stuck by a monster chain attacks and will faint/die (you can faint 2 times, the 3 leads to a fail (exceptions)), sometimes it feels the game wants it so. Also you have to learn the movements of the monster, so you can react to it. Sadly, the monster just minding its own business and then the hunter comes, who is the monster now? _childDocuments_.review: Remember finding Kut Ku scales randomly in the forest areas? What about being able to buy prey parts?You're in a middle of a fight but realized you forgot to bring extra mega potion for a hunt? Too bad! Now you have no choice but to complete the hunt with what you have or get triple carted and try again.Remember back in the PS2 days, where you had to use the damn analog stick to do attacks? Did you develop carpentunal from literally clutch claw gripping your PSP thumbstick just so you could efficiently use the arrow/bowgun correctly? Tools used to take up inventory spot?! How bout using paintball to tag monsters? Hey hunter, what about doing powderstone carrying quests, where the only accessible path is the longest one, the path with many Bullfangos along the way. >.>Those were the times, not sure if they were amazing times but they were something.5th fleet hunters really have it good. :')Shame Bazelgeuse is no longer an invading monster and Rajang is a former shell of its freedom/4 ult days, but hey.. at least Rathalos is no longer a pushover like how he was in World (remember flashpod spamming? h4h4h4) and he has a bit of Dreadking Rathalos moveset so he's way more aggressive in the air, so I guess that's something.In my opinion, by comparison, with how much risk/success Capcom took with MH World, by bringing back the series to the big boy consoles for the first time in ages since the PlayStation 2 days. Certain aspects of Rise felt like a graphical/mechanical downgrade. Besides turf wars, monsters no longer have cool interactions within the environment nor with other monsters. Other than just fighting hunters, they didn't feel like animals that had their own agenda. Seasonal themed hub rooms didnt return, small variety of collaborative armor/weapon sets (something this series is known for) nor collaborative monsters from other video game titles (despite what you think of.. leshen and behemoth *shivers*), also unlike all the past games, rise was a rushed game that had very little content during the first year of its release and more importantly.. WHERE'S THE MEAT!!? I'M TIRED OF EATING DANGO, I NEED NOURISHMENT!! AAA!! Jokes aside.. Although, despite all of its very apparent flaws, Rise has probably one of the best combat movements since Monster Frontier Z (rip) and the neat weapon designs (a staple within the  series) made their return after the very underwhelming bone/metal designs World kept plastering on their weapons. Some will argue that the old MH games were the best (and still are) but in all honesty, old world gameplay was more focused on positioning, waiting for opportunities to attack and due to strict controls, timing on when to heal or apply buffs, everything was punishing if you made even one error in your swings, while (the new world titles, especially from the pocket studio) is more about being active, going for the monster directly and humiliating them with a more refined movement system to back you up. This type of gameplay fits better with most (new) players and offers a new array of mechanics for old vet to abuse the monster even quicker with. I still think its the easiest game in the series but one thing is for sure, Rise (including MH World) is the best entry for newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: As my first monster hunter game i really enjoyed it.Starting the game you're bombarded with information about controls and other stuff, but as time passes you start to get those by yourself. Monsters did not feel unfair and the monster progression felt alright, though personally I don't like how shorts the hunts usually are (around 10-15 minutes, 20 if you're struggling). The soundtrack is amazing. The mobility is nice and the big open maps feel amazing (except flooded forest that one can burn). You don't really feel at danger because you can just use a wirebug to get back up and run away to heal. There isn't really a reason to use most hunting helpers. Grinding armours and weapons before end-game didn't feel really grindy - at most you'll grind for like an hour for a full set and weapon/s. End-game on the other hand has you grinding a bit more, but again it didn't really feel very long. Crafting your own sets is not hard, but you can just look at ones online too (which usually ends up being more optimal). Multiplayer is fun, but it makes fights incredibly easy, sometime feeling like you are just attacking a big wall until it collapses. The ones that don't feel like that are the end-game fights, but then you're better off hunting alone because the other players will cart 3 times and you will have to re-do the quest. After 200 hours I could say I've done pretty much everything I would like, and maybe i could spend another 20-30 hours to finish up my sets, hunt earlier monsters and maybe learn another weapon or two until the DLC drops.Also I have spent 4 full hours looking at which armours to mix and match to make myself look cool.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter Rise is my third Monster Hunter game. I've played on the 3DS and Monster Hunter World on PC. Rise comes across to me as a kind of blend of the two, removing some of the weirder, clunkier combat from the handheld era and further smoothing out the combat of World. The coop online experience of Rise is amazing, especially compared to World.  Levelling up alongside another player is great in Rise, it's the ideal Monster Hunter game to start with friends. I think start with Rise, and then consider playing some of the other games for a different vibe to combat.Combat in Rise is very good, but it can come across a bit arcadey, just do your moves and roll or block when attacked. Less punishment for mistakes, less time spent vulnerable (average shorter end lag on moves, lower end lag on item use, movement while using items, item cancelling etc) results in a game that feels like it has lower stakes.Monster Hunter Rise is a great game, but I would highly recommend playing it with friends. The game is ideal for people looking at getting into the Monster Hunter games.

_childDocuments_.review: There is this narrative surrounding this game that says it's a step backwards for the series. Everyone is entitled to their own opinions but, as someone who has played a majority of the entires including the original PS2 title, I feel like Monster Hunter Rise represents the distilation and culmination of this series'robust history. Following the queues set by World/Iceborne's developement, you spend less time managing micro systems, like the now-extinct hot/cold statuses, and more time in combat. Oh, how glorious the combat is. With the addition of wirebugs and silkbind skills, alongside a moveset update to many weapons, combat absolutely SINGS. There is an energy, a tempo, that is palpable during each fight, it is especially felt when you've mastered your weapon/class' moveset. Having the ability to zip away for a reprive or to reset is liberating, it helps to eliminate some of the frustrations felt when learning a new weapon or positioning. The monsters in the line up are fun, a neat menagerie of classic and newer beasts to fell, many with new moves to offset the advantages given by the wirebugs. The only knock I have is that the game feels rather short if you are a returning player. You'll hit the original ending within 25 hrs, then perhaps another 10 hrs with the additional content they added before Sunbreak was released. Another annoyance is the removal of items that boost your health and stamina, instead being replaced by spiritbirds that you have to pick up around the map. Kinda lame when you just want to get into the fight at hand, but this is only relevant during the later quests. Lastly, and this is probably the most nitpicky, the meal animation is a poor substitute for the grand feats they would feature in the past games. Bears nothing gameplay-wise, but it was neat flavor that they scaled back for...no reason? I'm sure Dango is culturally relevant to the overall Japanese theme, but it is boring.Get this on sale, or as a bundle including the DLC (Which I did not review here, but is a great addition to the base game). 9/10

First 5-10 hours after i picked it up again were very hard to keep going and i wanted to stop playing multiple times but kept playing to see the story and once i switched to sunbreak i actually started enjoying the game and playing more and more every day. Monsters were more fun to fight, new skills were very interesting and many of the base game systems were improved upon as well. It felt more like a new game than a dlc. and i actually enjoyed solo'ing the end game monsters this time around (world was a game i mainly played coop with friends but in rise i did almost the entire sunbreak end game solo(a friend of mine jumped on and hunted with me here and there but i was mostly solo from master rank 30 to 180) and it was a fun challenge (i went back and solo'd the monsters i originally hunted with my friend as well)One thing i didn't liked about the monsters in sunbreak is there is way too many variants. (i'm looking at you magala) you defeat a monster and it comes back 2 missions later with a stronger variant, you defeat that one and it comes back with even stronger variant. it felt cheap and unrewardingI also disliked the whole min-maxing systems being the melding talismans and the rng armor augmentation system and both of them being tied to anomaly research(a system i personally found very boring and uninteresting to grind for) in worlds when you didn't had the deco you needed you just ran at attack boost 5 instead of 7,who cares you'll upgrade it when you can but in rise your builds are made around the talismans you get and the augmentations you're able to roll so when you get an upgrade its not a simple just change the deco and done. you have to remake your build, craft new armors, augment them again etc.. its very annoying and if 2 of your builds are using the same armor, you have to craft a second one because most likely the augmentations you want will not line up and you'll have to roll 2 separate instances of augmentations. I disliked the rng deco system in worlds as well, certain decos were way too rare to make it realistic to obtain but i would take that system over the talisman/rng augments any day. I was very upset the first day i actually tried out the armor augmentation system and tried to get a skill i want on the armor, i wanted to alt f4 and uninstall the game. its straight up a slot machine, you load up the materials, pull the handle and hope it gives you the result you want. its suuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuch a dogsh*t system.Overall if i were to rate the game and the dlc separately it would be like this;Base rise: 5.5/10Sunbreak 7.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter: Rise is an odd crossbreed of high-quality and budget title. Tons of love has obviously been put into monster designs, weapon designs, descriptions, music and tons of things that give you a *feel* that you're about to head out on a super cool awesome hunt.At the same time, the game has that "budget" feel because of how constrained and limited its actual areas are. Five actual playzones(six if you count the arena, which I don't), and then the town area which is miniscule.How's it play, though? It plays... oddly. Like, it feels that more work has gone into how the monsters move and act than how the player does. Most of the monsters are amazingly designed, with really well-designed tells that allow you to have an idea of what sort of trickery they're about to pull even on your first fight, since a lot of their cues feel grounded in human or animal gestures and behavior. Most of their attacks allow you to pull off a dodge even at the last second, and the amount of attacks that are BOTH absurdly hard to dodge AND absurdly hard on you if you get hit, are low. Though they do exist and are a notable gap in an otherwise well-designed game.The game also loooooves hidden meters, which... occasionally just makes it really hard to tell how effective what you're doing is. I understand *why* it does it, and sometimes there are natural "tells" to compensate(like a badly wounded hunt target limping and starting to look ragged), but for plenty of things you just have to guess. Personally I feel like I could do with a few of the meters being unhidden, but your mileage may vary on that complaint.My main issue is that the player character really suffers from their controls being originally designed for a console controller. It means that almost every keybind does double duty(and no, these can't be yanked apart even if you're playing it on PC) and are occasionally contextual, there are still some moves and actions I don't have any idea how to pull off consistently or occasionally any idea why I'd want to do them. The second issue is that the high-quality action animations for the monsters are very cool, help build their tells... but for player characters they are INSANELY frustrating. Like, even if a dragon-monster the size of a truck and bristling with spikes is bearing down on them, your character is the most chill and unhurried person in existence. Oh no, can't hurry up folding away that bowgun, swallowing this potion or getting up. That might give them *stress*. And there's really no such thing as a dodge-cancel for anything you do, once you press that button, you are COMMITTED(unless of course the game's semi-sticky controls decide that you don't REALLY want to do what you just tried to do, and doesn't respond to your keypress).This unfortunately leads to a good number of hits, and occasionally even deaths, feeling exasparating, because it feels like it comes as a result of poorly designed/ported controls rather than your own lacking gameplay chops.Mind, by the point where I started hitting these, I was already something like 45 hours of gameplay in, it really only starts being an issue when you do the high-ranking hunts where a good few enemies can one-shot you.Ultimately MHRise is a game I enjoyed almost every moment of right up until that point. So get the game, get a buddy, and go wild playing the game in co-op which is absolutely where it's strongest. Note the *a* buddy, though. While the game supports up to four-player co-op, my experience is that it works best with two players, since once you have four players it turns from a tactical fight into a chaotic mess.

The combat has been expanded on, with the addition of customizable moves and wirebugs, which offer more mobility to all weapon classes, making them more viable and easier to pick up. Another positive change is more diverse weapon designs, which are unique to every weapon tree; or the option to take along a second, canine companion.(also I got rise cuz I probably won't be able to run wilds D: )

_childDocuments_.review: I made this review only now because I've beaten every monster in Monster Hunter Rise ONLY. I can finally move on and play Sunbreak since there's nothing new left for me to hunt in the base game.I only reviewed what I really noticed in Rise so I may miss some aspects.First off, Rampages f*cking suck. I don't know why CAPCOM even bothered with that sh!t. They couldn't come up with a good gimmick then better yet don't put any gimmick at all and let us just hunt monsters like we're used to. Though there are only 3-4 required rampages, some rampages need to be done for quests to unlock like the Apex Monsters which is ridiculous.The Wirebugs. I'd say they're a little bit better than Iceborne's clutch claw. I love the movement. Making me feel like a ninja. Covers more ground and can easily go to high areas to scout some buffs and gathering points.The Switch Skills. I'm indifferent about it. Coming from Iceborne, I got used to the usual controls of most weapons. But having different switch skills is like having to relearn it all over again including the new combos. For example, on the Charge Blade, if I have the Savage Axe switch skill, I can't have the charged sword and vice versa. However, it does open up to new playstyles that you can build around. Like having the Charge Blade use the Savage Axe mainly than a SAED build or vice versa.I'm glad that they removed the "tenderized" monster parts that was in Iceborne because it was so tedious to wound monsters from the beginning. Like it made hunts so easy that if you're just a casual hunter, you can try your hand at speedrunning. You'll feel just how easy it is to just hit on the tenderized part and deal a lot of damage.Surprisingly or unsurprisingly, most monsters are somewhat of a challenge once High Rank is reached. High Rank monsters have all the moves of the Low Ranks and new ones as well. So if you got used to how easy Magnamalo is in Low Rank, get ready to be two-shot in High Rank.The story. Like in World and Iceborne, I didn't pay attention to the story at all. I'm just here to fight monsters and carve them for parts either common or rare. The TRUE last boss fight in this story was meh. Felt like fighting Safi'jiiva's cousin. If you're a bow gun main, this is a walk in the park. If you're not, good luck hitting that thing once it's in the air. Not to mention the ballistae that only lasts 3-4 seconds most of the time. Just mounting it takes time and unmounts you then after before even firing and if you're lucky and early, you just hit it for a measly 10-20 damage. So frustratingly tedious this fight is. It's armor is supposed to be OP but it's really disappointing. And I know I've said this word before but I have to again. Underwhelming.The Apex Weapons/Monsters. A huge letdown on the weapon part. We don't even have armors for it. It's like having fully augmented weapons yet it's still weak as f*ck. Haven't tried the other Apex Weapons other than the Longsword and Charge Blade but it was so underwhelming. You're better off with non-Apex Weapons like Elder Dragon weapons. CAPCOM fumbled hard on this one.The monsters are good. Difficult fights especially the 'Emergency' ones. Apex Zinogre is by far the strongest of the Apex monsters. In emergency quests, Apex Monsters will f*ck you up like never before. So better get the best upgraded gear you can and watch out for their continuous attacks. If you think you just survived, think again fast. They might not be done with you yet.For the final update of Rise, they gave us Crimson Glow Valstrax. To be completely honest, I love the fight. It's super fast, hits hard, and looks absolutely cool. Those crimson wings with that dark scaly skin looks so epic. When it gets mad, it glows all over. After beating it numerous times in normal hunts and expeditions, I decided to hunt it in the Event Quest that has 'Advanced' in it. Surely enough, I was confident of facing it. Having known its moveset, I had almost no worries until I got my ass handed to me. His hunt on the Event Quest is basically a Master Rank fight. As usual, I don't play multiplayer against a monster I haven't beaten solo. So I solo'd it and I finally beat it at my third try. Having come so close on the last one too. Only to be f*cked by his follow up wing attack. To be completely honest again, for me, this hunt is the most difficult hunt in all of Rise base game. Before you know it, you'll be living in Cart City before you can superman jump an Ambush attack.It's a 7.5 out of 10 for me. Good monster hunter game. I had fun.Looking forward for World 2.Thanks CAPCOM

_childDocuments_.review: BLUF:  Not a 60$ entry, by any means.  Too many flaws, and too many giant steps backward for the series.  Still plenty of fun to be had here, especially for fans of the series, and in multiplayer.  Maybe at 40$.This is an excellent port of an overall "ho-hum" Switch game, with flaws, and some day one bugs.  If you don't have Monster Hunter World, go buy that instead, it was a steal even at full price, and is by far still the superior entry in the series, both in value, and fun.  Controller required.The Good:--Village visuals are excellent, sound and music is great. --60fps+ is a joy.  --Voices in Japanese are fantastic.  --Most weapons are mostly unchanged with a few tweaks.--The RE Engine change hasn't drastically changed the tight control feel, and gameplay and movement feel like a classic monster hunter game.--Can you pet the palamute?  Yes... you can pet the dog.The Bad:--Crappy maps.  Not a single one is great.  Most are passable at best.  They're not fun to traverse, and few have any charm except the Temple Ruins.--10 year old map design.  Hallway, to an arena, to a hallway, to an arena....  This game was designed for Switch, which has low 3D processing power.  To adjust, the Capcom team chose to obscure many open areas in canyons, or "arena" like areas with high walls on all sides, which tricks modern 3D into not rendering what's behind, or obscured.  This is a rather typical, if lazy, way to build for games and art.  How do we then adjust?  Wire bug.  Jumping in monster hunter.  So now you can jump, and run up these sheer canyon sides.--Abysmally bad on-hit 3D effects.  They obscure the fight, and in 4p, you can easily cover the entire screen.  The setting to tone this down helps greatly in single player, but 4p + 4 buddies is far too much screen clutter.The Ugly:--Cut scenes are locked to 30fps.--Progression is separated again into offline / online hub.  A massive step backwards.--Hunting Horn moves are less defined, it's all floaty swings, and some move backwards, which is an awful change for the weapon.--Due to differing movesets required, insect glaive's moves were ruined by the addition of Wirebug.--Evil microtransaction practices, once again.  The end boss isn't the last monster, it's you're wallet, and always has been.--Twitch launch week tie in: "Just gift two subs to eligible Twitch creators while they live stream Monster Hunter Rise, and you’ll receive your reward redemption code redeemable on Steam."  The greed here is palpable.Note:  I've played every monster hunter since Freedom Unite, including all 3DS and Wii entries.  I do call this series my favorite.  I am currently Hunter Rank 600+ in MHW, with 918 hours at post.

_childDocuments_.review: I dislike this game, but you probably won'tI think the game is amazing and i recommend it, but it has a few features that turn me away from it. i have already tried to play the game 3 times and i am barely forcing myself through it. don't get me wrong, most people enjoy the game and so will you most likely. Monster hunter is a phenomenal experience no matter which game you choose.but i don't find it enjoyable and here is why.The combat of rise feels way too fast and spammy for me. the methodical calculated movement from older games is basically gone and i find myself just wailing on the monster until i get hit then wirefalling (areal dodge when you get hit), healing and continuing. i don't interact that deeply with nether the monster nor my weapon. This also makes the hunts very easy. the base game in general is too easy in my opinion, with basically infinite healing options and healing just being better here than in world.The game also has a very arcade-y feel to it. There isn't as much hunting down the monster as you just load in, get to it and kill it, end quest and go next without giving much consideration to each of them. i don't think i even remember most of their names, which wasn't the case for me in worldLastly and for me most importantly: old hunting horn is gone. the new version is essentially a completely different weapon. I have around 400 hours of HH in world and iceborne and i really, REALLY hate the new version. Don't get me wrong, i think capcom did an amazing job at making the weapon more accessible and easy to use for new players, as well as more flashy and faster, which did increase it's popularity dramatically. and since it was unpopular in older games the change makes sense. but imo it has lost it's identity. no longer can you listen to the beautiful songs when playing different melodies. no longer can you bm the monster by playing a melody of death for them right in their face. your attacks are no longer methodical and thought out, used not only to attack but to play the correct notes as well. now you have an optimal combo with a 2 or 3 attack loop that you spam on the monster with occasional mix ups. the notes are an afterthought that might as well not be there. and since the weapon was so unpopular before i don't see a reason for them to change it in the upcoming mh games.I tried. I really really tried to love this weapon in rise. to play my doot. but my doot is gone. HH in rise is a different weapon. And if capcom doesn't revert the changes in new monster hunter games, i will never buy them again.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as big as Iceborne but it's a great game with a DLC that has improved it. There are new features never seen before. The random mechanic of augmentation is not the best but still a great improvement which is useful to make strong builds. Craftable decorations is something awesome too. Afterall this game was made for Nintendo Switch too so i couldn't expect a game like Monster Hunter World, created for PC so there are some limitations. Graphically is pretty good despite these limits. I miss the option to set the layered armor, the quick slots for crafting and the build set in a single loadout. With recent updates i miss the spamming gestures too. _childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review by saying although the graphics are worse than world, the gameplay more than makes up for this lack of graphical fidelity. Monster Hunter Rise is a game more focused on the combat than the graphics and the new wirebug mechanic makes combat feel much smoother than World. The lackluster Raider Ride has also gotten an upgrade with the Palamute, this dog companion is fully controllable unlike its world counterpart and also has some fun movement attached to it like drifting. Movement really is the core of this game, you can climb just about anywhere in bounds and there are secrets on every map to find for lore about the world. While this game may have been made for switch the game still has some impressive looking areas like the waterfall in the flooded forest. The one thing this game does lack in my opinion is a meaningful endgame grind, those of you who enjoyed the guiding lands will find that there isn't a time sink like that in this game. It's just kill monsters and get what set you want, and that makes the endgame just building the best set. Which isn't a very good motivator. So overall, while the game might have less graphical fidelity and a much shorter endgame. The gameplay makes up for that by allowing freer movement, smoother combat and more depth to environmental exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game more. Been an avid MH fan for years, but the direction this series is taking is not for me. It started out really fun and I think it is pretty nice to play for a first time. Was very happy to see original weapon designs return in Rise. Instead they cut out all the alt armours (They already cut Gunner armours in World, this time they cut Beta/Gamma/etc versions too). So I think, "Oh, since they're cutting all that, surely they'll put more work into other stuff, right?". Mostly just dripfeeding reskins of old monsters, grinds that get invalidated later on, 252 cosmetic DLC in the store. There's no real consistency in the monsters they decide to reintroduce either. Where is Agnaktor, where is Gigginox? Qurupeco? Not like his ability means anything anymore with the way how invading monsters are barely a threat. In the past you'd be like "Oh ♥♥♥♥, an invading Rajang". Now an invading Rajang just means free damage on the monster you're hunting. The threat of invaders is gone.Both World and Rise took like 2 years to complete their dripfeeding. The next MH game (actual game, not the meme mobile game that was announced), I'm going to wait until it's done with its 2 year long update cycle before I'll consider buying it.tl;dr Game is cool for casual gamers and first time players, game is an example of ongoing stagnation for old time players.

_childDocuments_.review: While not a big departure from Monster hunter world, Rise follows the tradition of incramental approval.Probably the biggest change is the focus on vertical movement, allowing you to climb or wall runs and the addition of wirebugs that can get you air born at any time.This makes the maps much more open to traverse and while you can still use camps to get around later in game there are rewards for traveling along different routes on foot or on mounts in the form of stat buffs for your hunter.You can now travel with a palico and a gaint dog, oddly they seem to get along just fine and in multiplyer you can choose between the two for different play styles.Story wise its the same song and dance, Surprise! Monsters are attacking a village so go save it! but they do tie it into a new game mode thats almost like tower defence only with huge monsters called a Rampage. These can be allot of fun and challanging with some good rewards. Weapon wise things are pretty the same with nothing new though with the new wirebugs and several tweeks to certain weapons some frustrating weapons have been made more appealing. Range weapons and hammer play for example are much more enjoyable.They continue to add to the content of the game and it's what you expect from a Monster hunter game. While this fails to evolve the online player experince  it is still enjoyable just like world.The real star of the game is of course the Monsters and like always they look amazing and while turf war's remain now you can get into the action to by actually riding monsters to use them against other monters in a fight for a brief time or positioning them to do more damage. Flying monters take a more center stage but there are plenty of memorable fights to have with both new and old foes.Over all if you loved world you will likely love Rise and if your new to Monter Hunter Rise this is a great introduction and probably the most player friendly version of the game to give people a gateway to the series has to offer.Still waiting on my monster hunter MMO.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely spectacular game, but it needs to have cross platform game saves.  I initially bought this for Nintendo Switch because it was going to be exclusive to the system, but once it was put on PC I had to get it for the myriad upgrades the PC platform allows.  ONE thing they completely neglected, and seem to have zero interest in implementing, is cross platform game saves.  Monster Hunter is such a massive experience as it is, that it feels really awful that I can't keep my experience between Switch and PC.  I don't see the point in having two entirely different saves for this game, when there could easily be a way to upload a save online and then download it for the other system whenever I need.  The Witcher 3 on Switch added this so you can play on Switch, and then continue later on PC.  When a game is this huge, and takes up this much time, there's really no excuse for devs to not implement this, especially when it's a major game company.  This isn't some small indie dev, it's one of the biggest game developers of all time.  They should be able to figure this out.Outside of this lack of a feature, the rest of the game is spectacular.  It doesn't have anywhere near as many monsters as Generations Ultimate, but no big deal.  This game keeps all the gameplay upgrades from Monster Hunter World, but now it doesn't require such higher end hardware.  This game runs on Switch nicely, and doesn't seem to tax my PC at all, even during the biggest battles.  Plus they added DLSS post launch!  Amazing game, and a great experience, if it's the kind of thing you're into.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, not what you're usually used to when playing MH but the systems fit and (mostly newer) monsters adapt to the new tools given to the players.They fixed the issue of having overly big maps that was in World, toned down the cinematic-ness of the game (cutscenes appear pre or post hunt, don't interrupt multiplayer anymore) and went back to the old system of charms being random and decorations being craftable, which is better in every imaginable way.The base game is quite easy for the most part but to be fair when do you ever really struggle with high rank, at least compared to g-rank? People complained about the lack of an endgame loop as opposed to Iceborne and of course that would be the case, the Iceborne equivalent wasn't even out until now.The new monsters introduced are all fantastic with some returners that were missing in World, but also sadly a lot of staple monsters that did make an appearance in World fading out again. (I really just want the MHG/U flagships to be together again)Going over to Sunbreak, G-Rank adds the usual complexity you want in your endgame and has monsters that tank more while dealing more damage, a higher emphasis on the latter at least seemingly in Sunbreak.The new switch skill swap lets you essentially bring two movesets with you, which can be a big game changer depending on how many different things and what situations you want to be able to do things for, but it can also be ignored as aside from the swap evade and a skill that later supports it there is no other benefit other than having multiple movesets.I've been having a great time with Sunbreak so far and while I'm not done yet I have a good feeling that it won't disappoint.Rise has taken a different direction of MH sort of building off a basis built by MHGU, one that I highly enjoy and expands the game in an interesting way.Will probably edit this once I've beaten the story/worked myself into the new endgame loop, but all I can say is that if the difficulty concerns you, Sunbreak has that to offer.If you played or tested Rise and didn't like the new mechanics then returning for Sunbreak will probably not change much, however I will say that once you're used to the mechanics you will probably forget about the issues they may pose to you.Also send help I have a crippling addiction to the Sword and Shield and I keep telling myself I want to try out more weapon types but I totalled like 400 hours combined with my Switch version time and still haven't gotten thereEdit 2:Now that I finished the "main story", I think this is my fav MH game, I still need to finish the deviant grind in GU but I want to ride the Rise wave for now.I was initially very concerned because of the rather low roster of new original monsters (haven't seen what MR100 has to offer), but I came to the conclusion that a massive roster is less important when you can have more quality fights rather than a ton of mediocre to sometimes good fights.All of the new additions to the roster including the returners are fantastic and have been given a coat of fresh paint, giving them all an almost new identity to how they feel.Afflicted monsters are something I wanted back too, something similar to hypers making any monster strong enough to be a fight you don't just autopilot, haven't done all of them yet but the buff to their speed really changes the way each fight feels while also giving you rewards for better weapons.While I still am unable to get my hands off SnS I can really tell and feel that this game has to have the most build variety and playstyles of any Monster Hunter game even surpassing GU, the game gives you an extreme amount of skills and movesets to work with to suit your playstyle and the new rampage decorations really make choosing weapons more interesting than before.The road to MR100 is a long one but one I am enjoying a lot and I can't wait to see what the end and free title updates will bring.Edit 3:I've beaten the MR100 monster and am reaching checkmark completion, and in my opinion Monster Hunter Rise is the peak of modern Monster Hunter.If you miss the survival-crafting aspect of MH then this game may not be as much for you but the quality of the new monsters is fantastic and there is more to come.Build variety is also at a peak here, with most armor sets providing their own playstyle and having many slots.MR Valstrax has ended up being my favourite fight in the series and the final monster may not be Yian Garuga but gave me a fill similar to it as I love monsters that feel like they're actually duelling you by being hyper aggressive and precise with its moves.10/10, may not be for everyone but if it clicks with you it just doesEdit: Minor spelling mistake, point and laughEdit 2:Road to MR100 additionsEdit 3:Post MR100

If you have played world you pretty much know what to expect from Rise.I am going to leave this review as negative but only because steam doesn't have a "maybe" or "Meh" option, yes the bug soured my taste for the game a lot and thats how things go but otherwise its a fairly well put together game. I also prefer World's ascetic over Rise.So I can't for or against getting Rise, if you got some bodies who want you to get it? Maybe ya its got a pretty nice co-op experience in the bit that I played. If your going to play almost exclusively solo and just want a monster hunter game? If you don't have MH: World I can recommend that, had a lot of fun with it and they play pretty close to the same so you should have some really good fun with it for less than it would cost you for Rise right now.Have fun gaming all.*Below is my struggles with the bug and my original review while affected by the bug*UPDATE3: They have just released a patch that has fixed the game for me. I am thinking I will post a proper review later but keep the below bit attached for posterity. If you are having the bug still, verify your files and hopefully it updates, if not fallow the instructions in the game's news feed. I will keep comments and the discussion below active for about the next week in case any other people still have the issue.Can't recommend buying the game until the they fixed the save game bug. Understand this isn't a loss of progress issue. You CAN NOT play the game at all if you are affected by the save game bug. Both my Desktop and gaming laptop are affected by this bug and currently as of posting there is no fix. If you want to gamble with your money that is your choice but personally I would wait to buy until this bug is patched out. If I find a fix that works for me I will attach a link to this review and will remove/change my review once/if they fix this bug.UPDATE2: It would appear that the bug may only be related to certain hardware (mainly Acer) so if you are afflicted by this bug try on other PCs you have but before turning the game on turn off steam cloud saving on the new pc to prevent using the bugged save from the initial bugged PC. Capcom is looking into it (so they say).UPDATE: I have fixed this bug on my laptop. It appears that the bug is caused by the game and steam cloud save not playing nice. I *THINK* this fix only works if you have the game on your main drive {usually (C:) } The way I fixed this bug was by turning off cloud save (stay with me those who are about to punch their monitor). This is under steam settings/cloud. Make sure "Enable Steam Cloud Sync..." is NOT checked. Close steam. Next go into Program Files (x86)/steam/Userdata. In there will be a file 191411892, copy that to your desktop for safety then delete the one in Userdata. Once thats done restart your PC. Then start the game. Hopefully that fixes it for you. I also hear that the demo has its own number file so you may need to delete that too. If anyone else finds fixes to the save game bug post them in a comment below. I will keep this review here (negative) until this bug is patched by the devs. GL guys.
