_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter: Rise... ooof this is a though one to review!Bit of background information:1st ever Monster Hunter Game was MH4:U, It was on the Nintendo, I was playing Hammer and I was not really that into the game. I truely started playing and loving Monster Hunter when Monster Hunter: World got announced and released on the PS4. I played MHW base game and returned even when Iceborne was released! My main weapon was Insect Glaive... Aerial Insect GlaiveMonster Hunter World was and still is an amazing game. But then compared to Rise... I feel like Rise is a dissapointment, I even dare to say a Failure to the Franchise!Don't get me wrong, every Monster Hunter Game, If I were to replay them on an Emulator or such would probably be worth the price and I do recommend Monster Hunter Rise as wel! It's like how a Pokemon game is hard to go wrong and even if it dissappoints, it's worth the money. And that's exactly the feeling I have with Monster Hunter Rise!Personal Frustrations:- Turf Wars were removed- Monster Riding in my opinion is only a good thing for solo hunts, not multiplayer hunts- The Massive Player Lobbies are reduced from 16 -> 4 Players- Aerial Insect Glaive is not Unique anymore. Silkbind Attacks granted every weapon Aerial Moveset which ruined the Uniqueness of the weapon- Aerial Insect Glaive Kinsects buffs are so limited in turns of duration. Even with Power Prolonger The Kinsect Buffs dissappear way to quickly while in Monster Hunter World, I don't even need a reason to use Power Prolonger yet.- Monster Move WAY to fast! It's very annoying as soon as you get all 3 buffs and land only 1 set of aerial insect glaive attacks that the monster just runs away! Every time I just aquire some buff or was just getting into thoughts of "finally a good fight, I got the high ground cuz I understands it's moveset/did crazy damage" it just runs away.- If 2 monsters see eachother! 1 scares away the other, without fighting, and more often then not the monster you are hunting is running away again!- Limited plants/bunches/mobs, in comparison with MHW, I feel like this game is a de-evolution of MHW, sure it's an evolution compared to previous entries because it's made specifically for the Switch, but this is bad- Spiribirds are the worst invention ever! It forced me to use mods (which I never use nornally) because of how much of a grind it is if you don't start with max stats!- When trying out new weapons, Ranged Weapons seem unplayable because of changed controlls/UI (I play with PS4 Console)Pro's:- It's still a Monster Hunter Game, A lot of the fights were cool, the new monsters were nice to have! return of some fan favorites that I couldn't even beat in the past: Gore Magala, I don't think Capcon can ever delivery a Monster Hunter Game that truely deserves a negative review! (this is the ONLY REASON Why I still recommend this game despite personally seeing it as a failure)- For some reason, the controls feel easier to use.... (except for ranged weapons- I like the idea of costumizable movesets HOWEVER Next time this is implemented, They should give moves suiting the current weapon and not steal from Aerial Insect Glaive- I played other weapons as well, for those weapons the game is great to play as, just sucks if you're an Aerial Insect Glaive Main because you feel weak, not unique, and forced to change weapon unless you play Ground Insect Glaive- The option to escape after getting pinned down is a nice things they tried. But In most cases feels to much like Aerial Insect Glaive regardless what weapon you are using.False Myth:There's a debate going on the Monster Hunter Rise's UI is better then Monster Hunter World's and honestly... I feel like nothing changed! Whoever is claiming this is probably Monster Hunter Rise biasedRatings:Graphics:                  5     /  10Gameplay:                6.5  /  10Replayability:            9     /  10Innovation:               7     /  10Multiplayer:              5    /   10Accesability:             5     /  10Costumization:         8     /  10Total Score (According to these):                                           6,5  /  10Personal Score (According to biased opinion)     Generous   4  /  10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great entry for those who are new to Monster Hunter as this to me is the easiest title to date. Compared to Freedom Unite and World, this game has relatively few monsters but the new mechanics make it very enjoyable even for those who are veterans of the franchise. The only thing that lets this down is the absence of the necessity of "Prep Time" before hunts as the environment and riding make the game a little too easy even for the elder dragon fights, which in the previous titles hold a lot of lore and require observation. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. There is so much content and new monsters there are more harder levels than I expected.  The weapons are all good in their own ways you can basically make your own playstyle with all those different abilities that weapons have and the ramp up skills that can also enchant your weapon. _childDocuments_.review: A faster-paced, more accessible entry in the Monster Hunter series.  Though I miss the atmospheric depth and stunning beauty of MH: World, Rise is tremendous fun.  If it starts to feel samey just pick up a new weapon and suddenly the rhythm of every fight is new and fresh.To have fun in Rampage quests, put villagers near the front and shoot down the flying monsters first.
_childDocuments_.name: MONSTER HUNTER RISE

_childDocuments_.review: Good game like many of the other monster hunters I've played. The only critique I do have is the talisman farming. During mid to endgame you'll unlock melding. These meldings include rebirth and wisp of mystery, these meldings are known by many to be the 'best odds' in the game. But it isn't the grind that annoys me, hell no. It's the fact that you have to put in monster parts or other precious materials to even get the meldings going in the first place. For wisp of mystery it requires way too much points.. people have *grinded* the last boss of the game (not the hr100 one) for parts just for these talismans. It gets incredibly boring and depressing. Especially considering the odds for a good/meta talisman people have said to be 1/3000+ odds.. and that's for the feasibly decent talisman. Meanwhile the top spectrum of talismans are like.. in the millions? Billions? Don't care enough to look it up myself but it's high. Lastly, I'm sure I'm only speaking for past monhun fans but Deviljho and Akantor/Ukanlos is not in the game. I miss pickle man.
_childDocuments_.name: MONSTER HUNTER RISE

_childDocuments_.review: My second favourite monster hunter (right after MH4) Amazingly stylish, looks gorgeous, plays fast. Still the same game with a more modern coat of paint. The content is a bit light (still enough for a hundred hours +) For now, but god, is it fun.----Years after release, this game has now more than 500€ of Microtransactions.big Yikes.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fun and amazing. After more than 100 hours of play, going through the story and carrying out most of the missions, testing weapons, etc., I can say that it is a good game but after Monster Hunter World, more was expected of it, there are those who say that MHW is better and it is in some aspects such as there is more diversity of activities (Well, it was a new world to discover of course), many improvements that were introduced in the World were eliminated, the game was more immersive due to the existence of climates and affectations Of the characters to these, the cloaks do not exist either, the combats with the monsters were more tactical, I feel that in the Rise at the moment it is not required to have a lot of tactics when hunting, the Cordo Amarre Vs the Retractable Claw I like both , the Claw was more tactical while the Cordo Grasp gave more speed to the game, depending on the weapons you use.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Hunter Rise is a phenomenal game. A great game for MH players and a great game for new players. If you are familiar with Monster Hunter this game is undoubtedly worthwhile. The wirebug changes work seamlessly and the game runs like a dream. If you are not familiar with the series, Monster Hunter is boss fight central. Great monsters with an array of weapons to hunt them with. Each monster feels totally different as well as each weapon. _childDocuments_.name: MONSTER HUNTER RISE

_childDocuments_.review: Just as usual Capcom takes previous MH titles, combines them, adds a bit of something new and we get new MH.-Setting, village, maps:Great. Very well done. Village is good and all maps are good, especially the remake ones.-Music:Groundbreaking. Proof of a Hero is just insane here.-Difficulty:It is extremely easy most of the game. Though by the end, by 6* quests it ramps up and elders deliver what they have to- pain.-Combat:Silk bugs are here, clutch claw and MH4 style riding is no more. Refreshing.Also game borrows even more moves from MHGenU than Iceborne imo. It adds variety of gameplay to weapons so you don't need to switch weapon and can just switch some of the moves.Also animation feel even more fluid and fast.-Equipment acquisition and farming:Very easy, probably even easier than World. Though gems and plates are hard to get at times.-Movement across the map:Maps are highly vertical now and feel bigger due to that. Though with the help of a hunter dog one can move very fast. Even silk bugs allow very fast movement so you won't get bored with boss fleeing.-Graphics:Switch++. Plausible. Effects are cool also.-Content:Idk, feels like usual non-G title. It took 100h+ to get to the last story boss and complete almost all quests in game except Apex and some Events. And there are new monsters after story end, so I expect 150 or 200h of total playtime to see everything.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially played it on the switch, I enjoy the better graphics and loading times.  The only thing is I wish they had cross play so I could play with folks who aren't on PC.  It'd also be nice to have my save data, but at the same time I don't mind playing through it again, it's kinda fun knowing the monsters and being able to jump back into high rank.  I would recommend this over world to new monster hunter players.

Rise to the challenge and join the hunt. The action-RPG series returns to the Nintendo Switch! Set in the ninja-inspired land of Kamura Village, explore lush ecosystems and battle fearsome monsters to become the ultimate hunter. It's been half a century since the last calamity struck, but a terrifying new monster has reared its head and threatens to plunge the land into chaos once again.

Hunt solo or in a party with friends to earn rewards that you can use to craft a huge variety of weapons and armor. Brand new gameplay systems such as the high-flying 'Wire Action' and your canine companion 'Palamute' will add exciting new layers to the already robust combat that Monster Hunter is known for.

Whether it's at home, on the go, online or offline - you'll always be ready for your next hunt on the Nintendo Switch!

name: Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty
detailed_description: Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty Complete Edition Worldwide praise of the dark Three Kingdoms action RPG 'Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty' has resulted in the creation of a complete edition of the game, including all three DLCs with a wide variety of additional content, from new weapons, to new scenarios and characters, to new Divine Beasts. The Complete Edition includes: - The base game 'Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty' - DLC 1, 'Battle of Zhongyuan' After the collapse of the anti-Dong Zhuo coalition, Cao Cao's forces strive to expand their influence throughout the Zhongyuan region. - DLC 2, 'Conqueror of Jiangdong' The warriors of the Sun clan fight to overcome the struggles they face following the death of Sun Jian. - DLC 3, 'Upheaval in Jingxiang' Liu Bei's forces fight back against the threat of Elixir that has gripped Jing Province since the death of Yu Ji. - In addition to the three in-game bonus items 'Qinglong Armor Set,' 'Zhuque Armor Set,' and 'Baihu Armor Set' that were distributed upon purchase of the base game, the Complete Edition will include a purchase bonus in the form of a small icon of 'The Records of the Grand Historian,' which will indicate the locations of Marking Flags on the minimap. Note: - Except for 'The Records of the Grand Historian,' all content is the same as in past and current releases. - You must have an internet connection in order to access various content. - Please see the official site for details Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty Complete Edition Demo This is the demo version of 'Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty Complete Edition,' an action RPG set in a dark fantasy version of the Three Kingdoms world. In this demo, players can enjoy the game from the beginning to the Mt. Dongshan stage. Notes: - Although this demo is a portion of the full game, it may differ from the retail version in some respects. - It is possible to carry over saved data from the demo to the full version of 'Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty Complete Edition.' However, it is not possible to do so for 'Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty' (the original version). - For multiplayer, players can only be matched with other demo version players. - Distribution of the demo may end without prior notice. - For more information, please visit the official homepage. About the Game From the depths of darkness, a dragon soars. A new dark fantasy Three Kingdoms action RPG from Team NINJA, the developers of Nioh. 184 AD, Later Han Dynasty China. The land is overcome by chaos and destruction. The imperial dynasty that prospered for many years is now about to collapse. Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty is a dramatic, action-packed story of a nameless militia soldier fighting for survival in a dark fantasy version of the Later Han Dynasty where demons plague the Three Kingdoms. Players fight off deadly creatures and enemy soldiers using swordplay based on the Chinese martial arts, attempting to overcome the odds by awakening the true power from within. Wo Long refers to a crouching dragon, and also refers to a hero or person of greatness who is not yet known. This is the story of officers, who will later become heroes, during their ‘unknown’ period, and also the story of a protagonist’s rise from being a ‘nobody’. Demons in the Kingdom A dark fantasy set during the chaotic Three Kingdoms period, the narrative vividly tells the tale of a militia soldier’s strenuous fight for survival during a Later Han Dynasty infested with demons. It’s madness in the Three Kingdoms like never before! Awaken the Power Within Defeat deadly enemies to boost morale and awaken the power from within! Overcome adversity through unique new strategies, including battle styles based on the “Five Phases”. Live by the Sword Renowned for ruthless strikes that can change the tide of battle in an instant, sword practitioners of the Chinese martial arts gracefully change pace as they shift between offensive and defensive maneuvers. Overwhelm opponents with a flurry of force in a series of intense and bloody battles while learning the precision and skill necessary to become a true master of the sword. Various Play Styles with Weapons and Wizardry Spells -Weapons Choose from a wide variety of weapons, from glaives to dual swords, to discover which fits your fighting style. -Wizardry Spells This secret art draws upon the power of the Five Phases, which allow for attacks using such elements as flames and ice. Upon achieving higher Morale Ranks, you can gain the ability to utilize even more powerful Wizardry Spells. -Divine Beasts Divine Beasts like Zhuque and Baihu are brought forth through alliances with other warriors. By calling upon these Divine Beasts, you are able to perform feats of great power. Character Creation The player's appearance can be freely set. Select from a wide variety of settings and use accessories to create your own unique protagonist. You can also download all of the equipment and missions from collaborations with 'NARAKA: BLADEPOINT,' 'Lies of P,' and 'Nioh 2.'

name: Very Very Valet
detailed_description: Up to 4 players must work together to solve the world's severe parking crisis! Your puppety crew of valets will redefine what 'parking space' means as you drive, boost, and crash your way to victory. It's time to buckle up and become a Very Very Valet! Madcap Couch Co-op Valet alone or with friends! Up to 4 players can work together to solve this parking shortage. Help each other and hitch a ride, or cause chaos launching your fellow valets wildly - the choice is yours! Party Game Palooza Throw an 8 Player party with new driving minigames! 'Knockout' is a bumper-to-bumper brawl to stay in the ring, and 'Rally Race' is a burning rubber boogie for first place - may the best Valet win! No License Necessary Driving has never been easier - just point and go! Accessible driving controls allow anyone to quickly become a valet, with plenty of hidden techniques for mastering your valet game and cornering the market. Check out the 'Drive Styles' options for even more ways to play! The World is your Parking Lot Show off your car corralling skills in over 20 unique levels! You’ll be helping out customers in a variety of locations and scenarios - city streets, cliffsides, bowling alleys, airports, and even trainyards. Become a Very Very Valet Join this elite squad of valets! Whatever the parking need, Very Very Valets are ready to accept the call. Grab your friends and leave no car unattended!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally played AI; Somnium Files and went, "wow! I sure want to play more!" And you find yourself here thinking about whether you want to invest more to play the sequel?I myself enjoyed the game however if you are ultimately looking at buying the game because you want to find out more about the characters, want to find out more about the world of AI:Somnium Files then it honestly isn't worth the money, especially at full price.  If you read lots of other reviews most of them will say the same thing and I will also say the same thing. There is a lot of absurd and nonsensical parts to the plot. The characters aren't all that fleshed out and there is little to no character development. Which is why I have, after all things considered, decided to say I don't really recommend it to other people just because I'm sure there are quite a few other games out there well worth the time and money. But if you're and idiot like me and buy it anyway despite reading more than enough reviews then you know what you're getting into. I just came for Date Kaname and honestly nothing else.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played the first game and loved it a lot, I think nirvana initiative is an alright game. I don't think it's especially good but I wouldn't say it's bad either.I have a lot of critiques about this game and I think the first game is a lot better overall if I'm honest. This game feels too reliant on jokes/reoccurring bits from the first game and god the story itself. It hurt my brain to try to comprehend for awhile there which made me a lot less immersed because I couldn't follow along anymore.  The random singing/dancing bits felt like they just wanted to make a callback to the  first game. Like I understand why all of it is the way it is but the big twist at the end felt kinda unsatisfying and I didn't get to really connect with the characters like I did with the first game. I'm honestly unsure what this game focused on? I can't say story and I can't say characters because both of them weren't explored as much as I wanted to. I think the main focus was on the twist and the story was built around it which when experiencing the game for the first time without knowing the twist.. makes it so hard to stay immersed and follow along. I had high hopes for this game but I feel like it missed the ball. I do want to see more from the somnium files series in the future but I want a greater focus on the characters again like in the first game while still having a good story-line. I think this game is very much for someone who has already played the first game. I personally bought this game on sale but with how lackluster the character development (minus ) and story beats were, I think the game isn't worth the $60. I'd only buy this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first game in this series you'll probably like this one too. It's got the same kind of gameplay and fun dialogue but for some reason didn't hit as hard for me. Though it was still a lot of fun to unravel the story of this game. Figuring out new mysteries is always fun! It does feel pretty linear but that's kind of what you get when you play visual novel games :P All in all it's a fun adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: This is... not Uchikoshi's best work.  The characters are less likable (particularly compared to 999 and VLR), the fight scenes feel more intrusive and annoying than in the original AI, the drama often feels silly and hokey rather than heartfelt (No highs like Luna from VLR or Mizuki's segments in the original AI), and even the plot, inarguably the strongest part of the game, is kind of...  Eh.I guess my biggest issue is it just feels very...  Marvel?  Apparently serious scenes are too close to goofiness for my liking.  I guess if you have a stronger suspension of disbelief than I'm capable of, you'll probably have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Plot twist for you, plot twist for me, plot twist for the plot twist, plot twist for everyone. If you've played and liked the first AI game there is no reason to not play this one too, fully recommended. You can even play this one first if you wanted to, it goes out of its way to not spoil the first game *too* much, but why would you do that.Now, some thoughts about the story after completing it (no spoilers, but don't read if you don't want a bias before playing the game), it's hard to say if it's better or worse than the first AI, the game took a very different turn in its narrative, kind of similar to how in the Zero Escape series VLR differs from 999 (by the same director), this sequel has a bigger scope with its story, and it aims to give huge twists at the risk of not always making complete sense, it also tries to confuse the player instead of the characters living through the story a lot of times, which is arguably a weaker narrative trick than making the characters share the same experience as the player, so it doesn't feel like a "complete package" like the first AI game, where once the story is over everything fell into place very smoothly, with all the reveals being a surprise for the characters AND the player. I'm still wondering if the sequel's story would hold up in a logical way in a second playthrough.  But at the same time, the twists are really mind blowing and actually make sense (overall) once they're revealed, so it ends up in a weird spot where it lives up to the first game's expectations of mind-bending turns but in a very different way, I could even say that as a pure murder mystery game it's weaker, but not as an overall experience.Aside from the story itself, the game has a ton of QOL improvements, a much improved UI, like the dialog instantly appearing on the screen fully instead of slowly fading in, cleaner animations and face expressions, smoother somnium gameplay (at the cost of not feeling as trippy as the first game's dream logic puzzles, so it could be a mixed bag there for some people), more extra content like a tamagotchi clone minigame, infinite time somnuims once you complete them, story tips that appear while playing instead of being hidden away in a submenu that you will rarely open, and more small things that I'm probably forgetting, so in the gameplay side of things it's an improvement overall.Anyway, I loved playing through the AI games this year, I'm gonna miss my time with them, they ruined my drive to play anything else lmao.

_childDocuments_.review: To sum up my review: This is a fantastic game, and an upgrade to the first in every way, but it doesn't serve well as a direct sequel, held back by its no-spoiler toggle, but to me that didn't ruin it. In fact this game made me want the next entree in the series more then the first game made me want a second. If the dev team's goal was to open up this series for more entries, then they really did succeed.  This game is made for people who want a fun to play sci-fi mystery, it's not really made for people who were only here for Date or other characters' stories.Pretty early in the game, when you have the spoiler toggle on, it sets it straight just how stupidly it’s going to write off inconsistencies with how the first game ended, and at that time I just laughed, because it really set my expectation right there on how this wasn’t going to be the story sequel people wanted, and honestly that moment is probably why I did end up content with the story. I set my expectations for a proper follow up to none right from the start, then all I had left was a very solid, super fun game, with a great story if you judge it by itself. Mechanically, AI: The Somnium Files Nirvana Initiative feels so much better to play.  I spent my first 10 hours just in wonder of how much it technically improved.  One of my biggest issues with the first game’s gameplay (other then any bugs or optimization issues) was that a lot of the Somniums (its main source of gameplay) just felt like trying to randomly pick the right option instead of any actual puzzle, with the idea that things in dreams don’t always make sense, but a puzzle that is based around not making sense doesn’t serve to be the best gameplay.In Nirvana Initiative, they were able to find the balance between Good Gameplay and still feeling like a dream. Each character’s Somnium has its own core gimmick, and I never felt lost like I did in the first game, and these somnium’s are for sure the highlight of this sequel. They also added more gameplay outside of Somniums, like VR investigations, which served well to round out the kinds of gameplay they had, as well as show off more of what the tech of this universe can do. Not to mention these VR segments do end up having some of the best character moments.  If you pair the more welcoming improvements to the main mechanics of the game along with the story being written so you can play it without playing the first, I do think this game succeeds the idea of being an entree point to this series. Not to mention its narrative does have a very strong start, almost the opposite of the first game, which I felt struggles with the early scenes of the game and introductions to a lot of the characters being hard to get through. The first AI is a game where you tell everyone “just keep going. It’s worth it.” and it is worth it, but Nirvana Initiative feels like the answer to the complaint “I don’t want to have to convince people to keep playing”, I’m sure the growth of fans can be attributed to that part. This change probably means nothing to players who were already invested. This sequel may have a stronger start then its predecessor, but in exchange it has a weaker ending. Though, it’s not easy to compete with the first game’s ending, and personally I went into this game not expecting it to be able to. A lot of sequels suffer from this. A new IP benefits from the player not knowing the rules of its universe, but that leaves follow-up entries to have to find the parts yet unexplained, or add on news ones, or just try to write entirely new twists unrelated to its origins completely. It can get messy. AI:NI was messy in the parts where AI:TSF wasn’t, but with how cleanly AI:TSF uses its new universe to set up and execute its mystery, it didn’t exactly leave the room for AI:NI to serve the same kind of twist successfully. After all of that; It would be a lie to say I didn’t care about AI:NI’s story, I cared about it deeply. I just didn’t care about it in the same way as the first game. The first game to me was a character story at its core, a personal one, with most of the sci-fi and big picture stuff just going over my head, and then Nirvana Initiative lost that personal touch, but I ended up way more invested in the big picture of the world created, and what kind of sci-fi this series wanted to be.  I had to replay it many times, and replay the first game again to properly put together why I felt the way I did. My feelings playing the first game were extreme lows and then extreme highs that make you forgive the lows, whereas Nirvana Initiative avoids the extremes, and is generally a solid Good to Great with a few meh moments and a couple moments that really excited me.“If I played the first game, will I enjoy the second?” is a question asked a lot on the various forums for this game, and its honest answer is that you won't know until you play, and it will probably entirely depend on what you're looking for in the sequel and how much you care going into it. If you're looking for a game that adds on to the story of the first game, this isn’t it, if you’re looking for another good Uchikoshi and AI team game, then this is one of their best yet.I wanted to answer honestly to the confusion of some fans as to how the game’s pre-release reviews were across the board 8/10-10/10 when on the fan base side of things, its much more divided. It’s a sentiment I saw a lot from people. It’s an easy answer; game reviewers are probably not playing this game for the same reason you are, and will have a different goal in mind for what they want from the game.  While a more fandom-oriented fan would probably be playing a game because of a character or a relationship or something core to the narrative, game reviewers and other fans will be searching in the game’s design for what they want.  You can’t professionally rate a video game by just how satisfied you were with what was done with the characters narratively, you have to consider things like narrative and characters more with how they function and serve the game’s design, then how said design works for the player. For those points, I think Nirvana Initiative really did deserve its 9/10s.  All of its twists and turns and how it laid itself out served its main theme this time around, it just didn’t end up being a narrative designed to explore and fully serve the characters like the first game, and if you were a fan just for characters, seeing the series take the turn into prioritizing its sci-fi elements and make its themes less personal probably was not the turn you wanted to see.  But for me, I think I was just happy enough letting these stories take me the direction they wanted to go.  If you're like me, and just thinking “I’d love to play another sci-fi mystery game”, then AI:NI is fantastic. That’s not to say you can’t be disappointed, thinking a game is good is entirely subjective and truly you can hate any game for whatever reason, this is just my feelings and I wanted to try to explain why I ended up enjoying it so much, and to maybe help people choose whether they think the game is worth it for them personally or not.Also, as a general statement, I just think it’s important to see the difference between a dev team’s goals and a players hopes, and even if you did come out of Nirvana Initiative being disappointed, I hope you can still see that this team has grown, and that they want to keep reaching for new ambitions, and above everything else that they deserve to do so.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I really liked this game, and if you played the first one and liked it, you'll probably like this one too. This review will overall seem very negative, but I don't want that to scare anyone into not buying this; I'm just frustrated because I think this game could have been basically perfect, but instead it's full of flaws that never should have existed. But, all in all, I did have a great time with it. I'll compare it to the original one a lot during this review too, and if you didn't play that one yet, I recommend you do so, and come back here after that. I'll keep the review spoiler free, though.The one area Nirvana Initiative is way better than its predecessor is in the actual investigation mechanics (Somnia and the new VR Recreations). Those are awesome! In the original game, a lot of (if not all) Somnia were really illogical and in many cases you'd just have to keep randomly trying until you got the right solution. In contrast, Nirvana Initiative's Somnia can be logically traversed and solved, and feel very satisfying. The new VR segments are also a welcome addition that actually make you feel like a detective. The problem with Nirvana Initiative is that pretty much everything else is either the same level at best or (more often than not) a straight downgrade from the first game. - Plot: this is the worst offender. The story of Nirvana Initiative is just so much worse than the one from the first game. I won't go into spoilers, but in the first one, everything felt right. Almost all endings were very satisfying, the conflict felt personal and made sense, the twist was well-executed (you could figure it out by yourself beforehand, all the hints were there, but it still felt great when revealed), etc. By comparison, Nirvana Initiative falls flat. The only ending I actually enjoyed was the secret ending (which, in fairness, is one the best things I've ever seen, but it's still the only one I liked; all others, even the true ending, are all mediocre at best), and the twist kinda sucks (I honestly saw it coming a mile away, but didn't give it that much thought because I believed it would be really contrived and they wouldn't do that... except they did and it is exactly that). - Protagonists: I came into this thinking Mizuki would be absolutely perfect as a protagonist and pretty much wishing Ryuki wasn't a part of it, since I wanted to spend my time with her and Aiba. By the end, I thought Ryuki was the interesting one and Mizuki was actually somewhat boring. How did the writers even manage to do that? And while that might not sound terrible still, the kicker is that Date was an AMAZING protagonist in the first one, and his chemistry with Aiba was such a joy to watch / play through... here, Ryuki/Tama pale in comparison, and Mizuki/Aiba almost feel disconnected even. - Other Characters: I fell in love with the cast of the original game, they were all amazing in their own ways. Here, Tokiko was the only character I was actually fascinated by. All others just felt like stereotypes or empty/one-dimensional. The killer in particular was a huge letdown for me in Nirvana Initiative, while they were such a fantastic part of the original. - Humour: now, the first game was 50/50 on me, and I didn't enjoy the over-reliance on dirty jokes. I thought they would do better this time, but now I'm not sure they did. And while the first had me howling some times, that rarely happened here. It's still good, but arguably a bit worse than before.- QTEs: "Wait a minute, the QTEs in the original game were bad!" Yes, dear reader, you are correct. And guess what? Instead of removing them, they doubled down! And now they are even worse, and more over-the-top, and more ridiculous!!! Seriously, what were they thinking?????For me, the original Somnium Files is somewhere between an 8 and a 9, and this one is more like a 7. That's still pretty good! But it falls way short of my expectations. I was hoping this game would be basically "first one, but with better investigations, better humour and no QTEs", which would have made it the perfect Visual Novel. Instead, for the two steps forward we got, we also walked three steps back. And that's kind of a shame.All that being said, let me end on a few high notes:- The soundtrack is, again, awesome!- Localization team did an INCREDIBLE job once again, super props to everyone that worked on the English version, both script translation/adaptation and voice actors!So, even if this wasn't perfect, I still look forward to more in this series, if the creators are up for it. They seem to have heard the criticisms of the first game, and if they do so again, then the third game absolutely still has the chance to be the game I wish this one was. We'll see. I'll continue to have hope.

_childDocuments_.review: The first AI Somnium is one of my favourite games of all time, with a single clean twist tying everything together in a satisfying conclusion. Years after finishing it, I could probably give you a fairly accurate summary of its plot.This one is an absolute mess. It's such a mess that as I sit here minutes after finishing the game, and even with the assistance/memory of a friend who played along with me, I am not capable of coherently summarizing the story, or remembering all the twists/mechanisms (re: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥) involved in its resolution.It's also difficult to capture all the ways in which this game is a regression from the first, here's a few: - None of the new characters are particularly compelling, and the characters carried over from the first game are flanderized to painful levels.- You are often forced to visit an absurd number of locations only to get little to no info from any of them.- Critical information is often hidden not by deliberate deception but by characters simply unnaturally not mentioning it.- Somniums are often required simply to force supposed allies to give us information they are refusing to share for no good reason- There are a dozen sub-plots, most of which do not feel like they tie in to the narrative whole, and some of which don't even get left feeling particularly resolved.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start by saying that I'm only giving the game a negative review because I feel like the game has a disproportionate amount of positive reviews considering the actual experience being sold in AI2, when I feel like given the opinions I've found online it should be more of a mixed rated game at best. I'm not going to enter specifics as many others have with their reviews, but as someone who has enjoyed the first AI game and also the entries from the ZE series, I am used to Uchikoshi's style of writing and it would have been impossible for me to jump into AI2 without expecting his signature touch to some extent. But it really just felt off in AI2, and I'm not even sure if I can explain why. Perhaps it was becuase of the pacing issues, which gave the player so little time to process the actual implications of the twists that they just fell flat, and the only interesting aspects of the story weren't developed in the slightest Pretty much every other twist felt badly implemented or downright unnecessary for the story All in all, I don't feel like the game was solely bad by any means. I thoroughly enjoyed the character interactions and the whole investigation experience which was something I loved from the first game; the dialogue was just as — if not more — witty and funny in the way that only AI seems to know how to deliver, and the gameplay was much better than the first game (the somnia were more interesting in my opinion, and the gameplay worked better for what they wanted to achieve, although there's my inner ZE fan who really just loved the escape room inspiration felt in some of them; the new investigation mechanic was pretty simple but also made the experience more fun, so I quite enjoyed it too). If we're solely talking about gameplay, I feel like the only questionable thing was how many QTEs we had when they were already something that wasn't too good in the first game. It could have been better for some of them to just be cutscenes. That said, those QTE cutscenes are just as absurd as they are in the first game, and I personally find that positive as I enjoyed that aspect from AI1. To conclude, I can't say that I would recommend AI2 at a full price to anyone, unless you're alright with the fact that you won't be getting a satisfying main plot — which for a mystery visual novel/adventure game, is a pretty unfortunate fact to be forced to overlook.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is from someone, who's played the first game. Sequel falls a little short in fleshing out some personalities and despite having a spoiler-free mode, the game assumes that you know the personalities and traits behind a lot of returning characters from the first game. Some backstory is developed, touched upon, but not too much. Some of the pros, having dual protagonists is great, since both characters are distinct and likable in their own ways. But as per usual the studio goes into ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ territory with their sequels, . However, since AI: Somnium already had a somewhat extra-ordinary theme going for it since the first game, the whiplash isn't as bad.  The whole idea of the series is chasing killers by diving into people's psyches and investigating their subconscious thoughts and memories. The sequel gives more variations of people to dive into, since two protagonists = more opportunities to dive into different people. They have a varied, even distribution on the investigations, so pacing is very good. The new voices and tracks to the OST were really amazing (Played in JP). The brain teasers they throw are really fun to work through. There are multiple endings, each revealing a nugget of the overall truth of the matter. There's replayability in experiencing both dubs (I think english is pretty decent), unlocking costumes, and concept art. My main issues with the game is that the story is on the slightly weaker side and is afraid to take more risks and they may have reused a little too many assets from the previous game. Overall, if you're a fan of the first game, you'll really love the second game and should consider buying it full price . If you aren't the hugest fan and you think it just looks interesting or something, get it on sale for 30 or 40 bucks. It's absolutely not worth 60 bucks unless you are a rabid fan of the first game or this genre of game.

_childDocuments_.review: (hereafter abbreviated as simply "nirvanA Initiative") is the second installment in Spike Chunsoft's AI franchise, a sequel to the also quite amazing detective visual novel AI: The Somnium Files. Like its predecessor, it is a horror visual novel soaked in dark humour, its zany and silly moments contrasting with and complementing the more horror-oriented plot and its darker elements.  is a twisting and turning ride through a series of murders, fraught with horror and mystery, and some comedy along the way. When Kuruto Ryuki, a rising star in the secret government agency of ABIS, is confronted with a series of murders where only half of the victims' bodies are found, the case leads him on a bizarre path of alternate realities, skewed time, madness, and so many other things. When six years later, the other halves of the bodies appear one by one, his successor Date Mizuki, now a grown woman, is the ABIS-agent who takes it upon herself to solve the mystery once and for all.As always with ABIS-operatives, their greatest weapon is the Psync, a way to enter the person-of-interest's dreams and search for answer that they themselves will not - or cannot - divulge. Somnium, the dream worls, is a twisted and warped version of the world, skewed and wrenched by the Psyncee's emotion and perception. Through its strange logic (and some trial-and-error), the Psyncee will reveal more and more information, leading to revelations impossible to obtain through regular police work. But can things sometimes play out differently depending on the choices the Psyncer makes during Somnium... ? There is a lot right with . Its winding, twisting and constantly remoulding plot will keep the player guessing and interested. The game throws mysteries at the player left and right, and yet never falls into the trap of turning the whole game into one bizarre heap of incomprehensibility. The plot is just the right amount of obscure, keeping you wondering without making you throw up your hands and give up trying to understand it. Its implementation of alternate timelines, like in the original game, makes it so that players will reveal new information to themselves, piecing things together while the characters themselves might not.The Somnia, too, are captivating and special, and while the game sometimes errs into trial-and-error play, like its predecessor, all the Somnia are able to be solved on the first try if the player is attentive and clever enough.Lastly, the humour is, as always, the right mix between dark and silly while still maintaining the overall mood of the game.As mentioned before, sometimes the game does dip its feet firmly into trial-and-error gameplay, and it can be frustrating to fail a Somnium even though you made the intuitively correct choices. Still, since every part of the story, and every Somnium, may be retried or skipped back to, this is a minor inconvenience.There are also some small plot holes, but that is only to be expected from a story this complex.Like its predecessor, nirvanA Initiative is great and you will not regret buying it unless your preferred way to play video games is running through the same maps over and over, clicking the shooty button and shouting racial slurs into your mic.

_childDocuments_.review: I played both AI: The Somnium Files visual novels back to back. The riveting story and likable characters meant I could not put them down until I finished.  I would compare this series favorably to Danganronpa or Ace Attorney, but better written, less choices, and higher production values.  But what The Somnium Files series does uniquely puts it in a class of its own.The first game left me with a better impression than nirvanA Initiative.  To facilitate the mystery, this sequel's story was deliberately less coherent than the first game.  Though they put in the effort of continuing the narrative from the first game, the characters and scenes reused lacked the same impact that I enjoyed before, even if I was happy to see them.  I was not driven to manly tears quite as often as the first game, but your mileage may vary.However, the features introduced by NirvanA Initiative are where the sequel comes into its own.  Numerous technical improvements, more challenging logic puzzles, and a nicely-extended cast of characters.  What the sequel lacks in impact, it makes up for in breadth enough to be a worthy successor in the series.  It's more than the sum of its parts.  I feel gifted to have had the opportunity to play something this good.If I see a third game come out, I'll buy it right away at full price.  I'm a big fan of this series now.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not review games often, but I loved this game so much that I feel compelled to share in hopes that someone else may decide to play it and enjoy it as much as I did.Collectively, the two AI: The Somnium Files games are by far my favorite story experiences of any medium (video game or otherwise) of the last several years.  Incredible writing that keeps you constantly guessing at what the answers to the various mysteries are, characters that have so much personality and I made genuine emotional attachments to, caring about what happened to them through the whole game, and an honestly great sense of humor that never feels forced, never misses its mark, and manages to brighten the mood of an otherwise very tense story without feeling like it is undermining the seriousness of it.I lost sleep, lying awake well after turning the game off each night, as I thought about all of the mysteries and desperately tried to come up with answers before the game actually provided them. My 31 hour playthrough was completed in 3 real world days because I simply was so hooked that I could not stop pushing through the story.Additionally, without spoiling anything, one of the endings for the game (people who have played will know which one Im referring to), was the most haunting and profound moment I've ever felt in a game.  The game manages to do something rare that no game has ever done on the same level, and it WILL stick with you for days, if not weeks or more after you've beat it.Play the original game first if you have the means to play both.  You can play this one on its own, but it is definitely a better experience with the context and prior knowledge from the first game.If you are even remotely interested in mystery, thriller, detective, or just visual novel stories in general, PLEASE give this game and the original AI Somnium Files a chance.  I want more people to feel the joy that I did playing this.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, I wish Steam had a "maybe" option for the recommendation.I didn't hate the game, but a lot of that was because of how much I liked Ryuki and Tama. Unfortunately, they get sidelined in the latter half of the game.Unlike the original Somnium Files, Nirvana Initiative is very, very linear. You're forced to do Ryuki's path first, and then you switch over to Mizuki's path after you've learned all the clues you need from the Ryuki path. I appreciated the easy/story mode so I didn't have to worry about beating the Somniums within the arbitrary time limit. The investigation sequences were nice but also kind of bizarre, in that... if Tama/Aiba scanned everything down to the molecular level like they did, why did they not realize a lot of things earlier? I feel like my AI buddy should have warned me about... well, most of the extra dumb things.Some of the puzzles got lost in translation, apparently, and I had to look up the answer to one that was pretty infuriating. Another set of puzzle frustrated me to the point where I just let the game handle "solving" it (thanks for that option, at least!).But I think I would have forgiven all that weirdness if I'd enjoyed the story more than I did. Because the twist--and let's face it, we're all waiting for a twist in Uchikoshi games--was awful. Just terrible. On top of that awful twist, the game also retcons a lot of Mizuki's backstory and adds an unnecessary character who continues to detract from Mizuki's everything. The thing I loved the most about the first game was the Date & Mizuki relationship. If you wanted more of that... forget it. Mizuki and Date barely interact with each other, and Date also gets a bunch of very dumb plot stuff shoved at him. They tried so hard to avoid spoilers for the first game, and I think it was to the detriment of the story. They would have been better off not using Date or Mizuki if the problem was spoilers. (You can turn spoilers on at the start of the game, btw, but it doesn't change much except a few lines of dialogue here and there.)I definitely wouldn't recommend this game to people who haven't played/didn't enjoy the first game. It's maybe a bit playable for fans of Somnium Files.... but be prepared for the retcons and for characters to not really be recognizable.... Ryuki and Tama are great though. I guess that's the only part of the game I truly enjoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: Story-wise, I like the prequel better because some aspects of this sequel felt somewhat anti-climatic and too far-fetched for me .But it was still a great story nonetheless. The mysteries were intriguing to follow, and while I am not someone who enjoys being spoked, the way this game (just like its prequel) could creep you out with the sheer bizarreness of the settings instead of unnecessary gore and horror, was an achievement in and out of itself.Even though there were a lot of physically and mentally disturbing themes in the story, this game did not fail in delivering some of the most emotional scenes I've seen in video games, both the tragic and heartwarming ones.I kinda wish they could choose a different trope than "cute and pure-hearted girls hiding big secrets" next time; feels like it's getting repetitive. That said, I actually think the characters here are less cliche than the prequel.Totally love Ryuki and Tama. I really didn't expect I will like them as much as I do now, but I love their chemistry and relationship. It felt like a reverse version of Date and Aiba; before, Aiba was usually the level-headed one despite her quirkiness and Date was the troublemaker, yet now we were presented with a Tama who looked like she had a screw loose and Ryuki who was helpless at stopping her antics.The Aiba/Tama's Room and the mini Tamagotchi features are also cute and fun to play with. Overall, great game. Totally recommended. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the first Somnium Files game and this sequel is, let's say, a nice sequel to an awesome first game. Let's explore the ups and downs of the game (+, +/-, -, ?):+ Nirvana Initiative's story is a bit confusing, but it's a great mystery story with many horrible and touching scenes in it. It's a sweet roller coaster ride of madness with a nice ending*+ The cast of the previous game returns, for the most part, and the new characters** fit in perfectly with the new story. Mizuki is always a treat, much like Iris, but the best character, who kinda doesn't fit in with the rest of the crew, Gen is the absolute best character. What a nice man! I would love to visit his restaurant in real life. Oh yeah, and the receptionist with big tits is back (vital to the plot?).+ Thank god, the gags are here again! WHAT'S YOUR NAME?!?+ The OST is awesome! I'd say  somnium theme is the best track here. A nice, 90's alt rock thing going and all!+ The new AI companion Tama is... way too hot! I never knew there'd be a "step-on me AI queen" here, but I'm not disappointed.+ You either love or hate the humour here. To me, this is the perfect balance of madness, anime and sexual innuendos.+ There are things that are never explained in the story. Some of them might be because there might be another sequel coming, but... Mama's new weird ball-related skill is... weird in the good way.+/-* I knew what to expect from the ending, but the new ending song is not as great, or off-key, as the Invincible Rainbow Arrow.+/- The somniums themselves are mostly easier than before. It does make the story move faster, but, maybe, increase the difficulty when playing this.+/- There's a love story in the game that feels a bit wrong. It's kinda good towards the end, but it could have also been used in a horror plot. There were some moments that felt weirdly threatening, while it was supposed to be sweet.+/- The game deceives you on purpose. Is it a good or a bad thing? Depends.+/- These minions are so useless the stormtroopers are laughing at them.-** So, Ryuki is... a boring whimp. I can't say he's totally pain in the ass, but being stuck with him for a long time in the story made time move slower.- I love story games and I love detailed explanations, but there's so much repetition that this feels like a Danganronpa game. Oh, wait...?  yeah, maybe a different plot would've been nicer right now.? I felt pained when philosophy and religion was discussed here, since I know the discussed topics well and I just wanted to skip the mountains of texts explaining all the different theories and such... Like being back at uni again... Really useful for most players thou.AI: The Somnium Files - nirvanA Initiative is a great story game that has some minor faults to it. Overall, it's a pretty damn enjoyable story game, but it just can't reach the same level of greatness as the first game. I recommend playing both of the games anyway since these stories with these characters, and humour, are damn awesome experiences. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: A good time ago, after completing AI:SF, I saw some reviewers saying "Just play nirvanA Initiative instead". Unfortunately, after clearing this game, I can't say that I feel as strongly about it as I do for the first installment.I didn't have anything that I explicitly disliked, but there were parts that left me feeling meh or even disappointed. ● Spike Chunsoft always nails their prologues and AI:SFNI was no exception. Strong and captivating.● The length of the game. One of the worst things a game can do is rush itself to abide a short time frame and pull a cliffhanger, much like how a stretched out game with useless fluff and filler scenes leaves the mind parched and yearning for another source of water. I do believe this game could have used a slightly longer runtime because of reasons mentioned in the "meh" list, but as things stand it is fine.● The game, much like the first installment, doesn't treat you like an idiot.● The fact that the game's plot isn't dependent on the first game. Alongside this, I must say that the new info and characters were decently integrated into the the game and don't (really) conflict with the previous information ().● The mystery was interesting. Trying to piece it together while making notes of theories and tangents like a madman was fun.● All the references, even if I don't get all of them, and how some are explained in the trivia/appendix (alongside some terms).● Good balance between serious and comical.● Normal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ auto-mode where the characters don't take 10 year long pauses between one voice line and another.● The audio aspects- from OST to voice acting (played with EN dub, relistened to some voicelines in JP) to sound effects and mixing. These things all contribute to the feel of the game, it's a shame only OST and voice acting gets heralded. Bad mixing can ruin any experience, poorly chosen sound effects can make you consider turning them off completely despite the potential consequences. There was none of that garbage in this game.● Amame. Amame Amame Amame. o Back to the "treating you like an idiot" aspect, there were a couple of questions/puzzles that, while obvious in hindsight, felt a little poorly explained (the worst offender being )o Some of the sex jokes were too ill-placed to overlook. The concentration diluted over the progression of the game, however.o The lack of interrogations! It feels like this game replaced them with Somniums. I love Somniums as much as the next person, but I was hoping for a little more conscious brain shaking, at least in Ryuki's segments.o Saw someone else mention this some time earlier, but Timies had disappointingly low significance.o To anyone that might be on the fence and reading this very line in this very review- the next 4 points are spoilers, but what they discuss boils down to the contents of this point... don't spoil yourself. Anyways, some characters felt underutilised/not fleshed properly. Same can be said about character relationships. o Similarly, I didn't build the same attachment towards Mizuki and Ryuji as protags in AI:NI like I did for Date in AI:SF. o This is a bit more of a side-tangent, but, speaking of Mizuki, o o o There were a bunch of things, plot-points and aesthetics laid down in the beginning that the game clearly wanted to pick up and flesh out that it never got around to doing, at least not properly. Personally, I would have loved to see a bit more of the  I also would have loved to see recurring exploration of In summary, I liked the case and the obvious effort that was put into the game and all of its artistic aspects. However, the game had a bit too many characters than it could handle and a little less than enough time to wrap it up as neatly as it clearly could have.Overall, the game was enjoyable. I don't regret the hours I sunk into it and I feel comfortable saying that I recommend it, but there was unmet potential.The game's ending was clearly egging on a 3rd installment- if it does come to be I'll definitely be playing and hoping to see it meet its potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I think a good analogy when comparing this game to the first Somnium Files game is the first two Zero Escape games. Both first games are relatively simple but are held up by a compelling story. The second games, on the other hand, expand on the gameplay and make more experiments with the structure. In both cases, I prefer the first games in the series. VLR wears out its welcome eventually (personally too much text/not a fan of long exposition dumps, I play the games for the mystery and puzzles  ), and this game, nirvanA Initiative takes directions I disagree with. Foremost of which is the big reveal. Not a fan of how it was revealed and not a fan of the reveal itself (there's like a plot hole in my head until now). Also, I don't think leaning more into the humorous side was a good decision, just not a fan of this humor and it just takes away from the atmosphere of a murder mystery.In any case, expect that it feels like step down from the previous game, despite the added features like improved somniums.

_childDocuments_.review: AI Somnium stories so far are brilliant thriller adventures but they fall short as detective adventures, they really want main antagonists to come out of left field so hard that it feels like they abandon more interesting stories in some red herrings. Learning about Van Dine's 20 rules and Knox's Decalogue from Umnieko hasn't done my feeling on the reasoning style favors, but you do get more puzzles you have to actively solve this game than AI1 which I found engaging if not held back by a very rigid interface to input puzzles without hints, on-the-fly clue cycling, or a notepad. Somniums this time are very mechanically unique from each other in fun ways with only a couple stinkers, sadly they don't lead to many branch endings like the first game. I appreciate the effort into reincorperating AI1 characters and creating relationships between them and the new cast. Fandom and theory building experience is great but I have a hunch the popular Ryuki/Date ship will be tainted by a reveal that might come in a next game. People found assets for a possible Episode Date DLC story in the files but my hopes aren't up with months passing and no new PR. I'm very excited for what could come next and hope Ryuki and Mizuki stay in the spotlight in an AI3.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not as good as the first game, but it's still good.I think it has a very underwhelming first half, and a very disappointing second half.It's still enjoyable but overall the structure of this game doesn't flow as well as the first game, which is ironic because the first game was stopping you and throwing you around multiple timelines constantly.You'd think a game where it doesn't do that anywhere near as much would be harder to follow, but this game's main huge plot twist just doesn't stick the landing, and comes off as super confusing as opposed to endearing.Don't get me wrong, it makes sense when you sit down and think about it and get further context clues, but it comes out of nowhere and is hard to follow. The amount of contrivances and coincidences to make such a plot twist happen overall brought down the quality of this game in my opinion.It's still worth playing, the new deuteragonist, Ryuki, is fun and so is Tama when she isn't being childish about sex jokes or having a screaming fit. _childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this if you liked the first game. Some people would say it's not as good as the first game - but I'd say I enjoyed it about the same. It's mostly more of the same stuff from the first game - but with a new mystery, new characters and new game mechanics. Once again it doesn't take itself too seriously, and the mystery will keep you in the dark for most of the game with an excellent reveal and a lot of cheesy scenes mixed in there as well. The game play is similar to the first game - a mix of visual novel dialogue with somnium sequences scattered throughout. In these somniums you will need to observe your surroundings for clues to help unravel the story. Don't be afraid to choose what seems to be the "silly" or "wrong" choice - sometimes it's actually the right choice. If it's not then it will probably be funny anyways!If you've never played the first game - go play it first. These are excellent mystery games from the creators of the zero escape (nonary games) series. Excellent mysteries. Excellent characters. Excellent writing. They are worth much more than you will pay for them.

_childDocuments_.review: Its been a while since I had completed AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES - nirvanA Initiative, But having Revisted the game and experiencing it from start to finish with the faintest bit of memory of the plot twists and the outcome of every ending, I can say without a doubt that this game is an absolutely amazing sequel to the somnium files.However, I do have a lot of major gripes, some of which will be discussed and lightly touched upon, but I'll start off with the gameplay.Visual Novel: As to be expected of an Uchikoshi game, The game is incredibly Dialogue heavy and tends to hide a lot of things from the reader, to some that can be very frustrating, but to this game it is incredibly fundamental that the game hides A LOT of stuff from you, lest the story's impact completely falls apart.However it doesn't come without its faults.The Somnium Puzzles: I hate to put it in a way that sounds rude, but in my personal perspective Ryuki has some of the best Somniums in the game, mostly from the impact and weight they have on the story and the difficulty not being hair pulling, The difficulty of Uchikoshi games have always been a point of contention, there are times where the solutions are very simple, to moderately difficult, to literally needing a degree in detective work to even know what the hell the solutions are.And these problems shine no further than _childDocuments_.review: A truly disappointing game, I wish I could recommend this game, and I wish I could like it, but I just cannot bring myself to say this is a good sequel. To start off with some of the positives before I get into more negative spoilery talk, I decently enjoy the new characters added. Ryuki, Tama, Kizuna, and Tokiko were some stand out additions, but at the same time there were a few characters I just could not bring myself to enjoy, like at all.I think the new additions to gameplay are good and were a good inclusion so the game didn't feel repetitive and stale by doing the exact same things as the first game. Virtual reality is a really neat addition that let's you feel more involved in the investigations, at least in a more typical way, but as always with good comes the bad. I feel like the new Somniums are very hit or miss not just in level design, but also in an artistic sense too, whereas I can recall each Somnium from the first game and how unique it's direction in both level structure and art was, I find this game often feeling lacking... The Somniums don't feel as striking often being verrry restrained in how abstract or unique they allow themselves to be, often just being real world locations with maybe a filter or two overlayed on top, not really changing all that much in all honesty.As I don't have much to say in the way of music or anything else, it's now time I detail by far my biggest grievance with this game which is of course it's narrative. So be warned for spoilers going forward if you do still plan to buy this game.No matter how much I ruminate on it I just well and truly dislike this games story, on a very deep level that relates to the games core themes and ideas it tries to get across. Riddled with retcons and mediocre to downright awful reveals this game left me so  It tries to replicate the first games storytelling structure of discovery and needing to play multiple routes to understand the greater picture yet does it in such a subpar way, by splitting the game across 6 years it's ability to make multiple branching routes gets absolutely gutted, whereas in the first game you'd often have routes branch off into other routes here they're less of "routes" and more like "endings" often only happening near the end of the games main story mostly just there to showcase some big interesting reveal wow!!! Overall the flowchart in this game feels utterly unnecessary, and I'd maybe go as far to say it actively hurts this games storytelling.This game seems to so desperately want to replicate what the first game did and how that game presented it's twists and reveals, yet what this game has to show is just uninteresting at best or just plain bad! Don't get me wrong the series has never been grounded or realistic, there's always been both cartoonish, and sci-fi elements to the story, but in the first game it never felt overpowering. In it's universe it did feel grounded, it felt like something you just accept whereas this game really jumps the sharks in some regards, actively hurting the first game in it's retcons and additions. The game seems to have no clue how to balance it's tone, again the first game most certainly had loads of comedy in it, yet that game knew how to take itself seriously when the time called for it, when something disturbing happened the characters would react realistically losing their joking tones and treating the situation with the seriousness it deserves. Whereas this game feels like it has no respect of it's own story, big major reveals and moments are often ruined by it being brushed off with some joke? Never actually taking the time to consider the ramifications of certain moments, because why actually take time to write something with substance when you can brush it aside with a mediocre porn joke.  Despite being a murder mystery this game seems to have no desire to actually tackle anything too sad, everything often being tied into a bow at the end. Here's a word of advice, if you need to directly tell the player what your game's twist is, it probably isn't a very good nor interesting or satisfying twist and is actually just obtuse and confusing for no real reason. I'm reaching character limit so I'll wrap up now even if I have so much more to say... but overall my ending thought is AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES - nirvanA Initiative is a pretty decent game on it's own, while being an incredibly disappointing and subpar sequel to the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Welp, if you disliked the first one, you are going to reallllly hate this game.  I would describe it as even more animey than the first one…which I did not think was humanely possible…but by god they did it!  I’m not sure if I would consider this a good thing.  While I loved the First Somnium a lot of the very animey content was grating.  The fact this is a game where constantly massive armies of people attack you and you magically never kill these people because you only use “rubber bullets” and somehow the massive physical damage you do to them causes no bodily harm or the fact multiple characters in this game basically have super powers…also multiple dance numbers.  I really could have done without a lot of that.  Still I think this is a pretty good game.I do think the puzzles are much more well done in this game as compared to the first game.  However, a lot of the psychnes like the first game still devolve into randomly picking options with no much logic connecting your choices.  Some do  seem more connected than others.  This game also adds much more actual puzzles you need to solve.  For the most part these are pretty decent, but every now and then there is a crazy number substitution puzzle which can get aggravating quite fast.  The game seems to realize this and your AI can just solve it for you.  I would have preferred puzzles that were far less number substitution related.  Still I’m glad they added more actual puzzles to the game and I’m glad they are still not as numerous or as mind bogglingly stupid as those found in the Zero Escape games.I will say I was pretty disappointed that this felt almost like an expansion then a true sequel.  For one a lot of assets from the first game just seem to be reused.  The most telling one is that Date is still in his original body from the first game, which realllllly makes no sense.  Also even though 6 years have passed since the first case everyone still looks the same age.  When this game later goes another 6 years in the future on top of that (12 years from the first game) the characters still look the same.  Characters make jokes about this fact…but still I find it lazy.  Mizuki, Ota, Iris all still look like children even though they are in their 20/30’s by now.  Even locations from the first game are the same…and there are a lot.  While it’s nice to have all these characters who I liked…the fact they opted to have this big time jump and have everyone remain the same just felt real lazy when they are asking for a $60 price.  On the plus side the game does have full English or Japanese voice acting, both of which are excellent.My real issues with this game though come down to story.  For one, I feel the game needed a lot more choices and branching paths.  There are really quite few here…which I understand why this was probably done…but I felt like it took away a lot from the game.  Visual Novel adventure games like this I feel need to have a lot of player choice options so that’s a problem.  I do like that you get to play as both Ryuki and Mizuki…but I think this took away from the ability to have so many more branching options.  I will also say I much preferred Ryuki and Tama as I dislike playing as children and no matter how much the game insists Mizuki is between 18-24…she looks like she is no older then 12 and her partner AI appears to be 6 years old.  It’s remarked on multiple times how weird it is that she is a police officer at her age…and on a serial killer murder investigation.  If a third one is made I think what I would prefer is a properly aged up Mizuki and Tama as a partner so the dialogue doesn’t constantly seem so childish.  Ryuki was an ok main character…but I drastically preferred Date to him.Overall, my problem with the story is, this is a murder mystery and it’s just not a very good one.  Who the serial killer is, is exceedingly obvious.  I’m not even sure if the game has a lot of clues pointing to it…in fact it’s the lack of clues and any real suspects that make it so easy to solve.  The game also wants to have a lot of action sequences…which I don’t understand.  The entire ending of the game is one big action sequence…I would prefer just presenting your findings to Boss and the person being arrested…you know like an actual detective would do.  I really think the developer/writer should have concentrated far more on the mystery aspect then the action/thriller aspects.  The rest is just going to be spoilers Look if the ultimate solution to this mystery wasn’t so fun I wouldn’t be recommending this game.  For so much of this I was very disappointed until that final solution was presented.  After this, I’m still excited to see what this developer can do as once again this is still drastically better than his zero escape games.  So I really do hope a third one is made, hopefully focusing more on Tama and with more player options, at least give some romance options!  Also the next game better have a far more intricate murder mystery and less of a focus on these absurd action sequences.  Due to the lack of real improvements on character models, locations, and with such few player choice options I would say #Worth $30.

_childDocuments_.review: Prime Uchikoshi f*ckery in this game, and that's as much of a compliment as it's criticism. nirvanA Initiative has much more substance than the first AI, but at the same time it seems to have little regard for its legacy many times, especially when it comes to the supporting cast, who was either relegated to near-total irrelevance (Iris being the worst offender. Her only showing up to say something about conspiracy theories that teeter near the antisemitic point of no return actually lowered my opinion of her character... sigh) or being made into annoying, repeated jokes. I think Boss and Mama were the only members of the first cast who fully escaped this fate (Date and Aiba had some... off things about them).To that end, the flanderisation example that hurt me the most was Moma. His gross tendencies toward Iris were the one part of his character in AI1 that prevented me from further liking him, and it only gets WORSE in this game. Every scene he's in has to have some sort of reminder that yeah, this middle-aged man has been wanting to get with this girl ever since she was a high schooler. He could've been so much more than that, ever since the first... just the thing with this old guy being a pop star fan was funny, you didn't need to go to me for every scene with this gross joke! (But again, I may be one of the only people on this Earth who cares about Moma more than a joke character... I needed to rant, though.)Mizuki as a protagonist is very good, even if her aggressive tendencies when she's exerting her profession are worrying — I know she has her heart in the right place, but seeing her lash out at people during interrogations... y'know. Her co-protagonist Ryuki was very fun to see, but I did get the impression that he got way less screentime in the grand scheme of things — either that, or his near-complete absence in Side Mizuki made me forget about the time I spent with him. To compensate for the either lack or ridicule of the old cast, the new cast is full of shining stars. Chikara felt like a natural evolution of Ace from 999; Tokiko's tragic antagonism had me hooked to the end; Tama was surprisingly relatable to me; Gen and Lien had missteps (especially the latter), but delivered some of the most important messages of AINI; and I can't believe I thought cube man was one of the best, but here I am. These people made me feel every emotion, I dare say. I laughed, I cried, I got angry, I fell in love; it was a human game, through and through.TL;DR: even with the issues all around it, AINI is a fantastic game, the culmination of Kotaro Uchikoshi's talent as a screenwriter. I hope they make Moma an actual character in AI3.
