_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game a while ago and didn't know what to write as I had mixed feelings about it. It is a step down from the first game, but still a good one to play. Six years after the first game ended, Mizuki became a special agent, along with a quiet young man named Ryuki, who has an artificial eye named Tama. Surprisingly, after an incident six years ago, Mizuki now has Aiba as her artificial eye and partner. The primary investigation will be after finding a half-corpse in the middle of a stadium, the same person they found his other half six years ago. The game will keep jumping for six years in the past and six years in the present. This might confuse you initially, but you'll get the hang of it.  The artwork and character design are excellent; I've played the game in Japanese and watched someone playing it in English, and I found both versions are perfect. There are some returning characters like Mizuki, Ammame, and, of course, Date, who I don't understand why he still looks like that; perhaps they didn't want to spoil the first game, which is understandable. Speaking of spoilers, when you start the game, they'll ask you a couple of questions about the previous game; if you answer them correctly, they'll let you proceed to play while they mention things about the previous game; if you don't answer them, they'll keep the game spoiler free. I found this genius move from them.The soundtracks and music are as good as the first game. The gameplay felt a little bit lacking. There are few interrogations and lots of moving around trying to find clues. I was not too fond of the QTE, of course; I should have disabled them to enjoy the game more; the random buttons they are promoting are tricky to mash on time. Unlike the previous game, the Somnium locations require lots of logic; you will not lose time while standing, but you'll have to be careful about what to interact with. There is also another mini-game in each investigation location, called VR, where you locate the evidence and try to recreate the murder scene. The film reel and director/actor scene were very corny as they kept repeating them in each location. They also added a side mini-game called Eyeballie, where you answer a question every 20 minutes to create a character; each answer will add points to Brave, loving, Impish, or Crazy. This mini-game doesn't impact the story; it only gives you an achievement. Tama/Aiba's room is also a mini-game, where you dress them up and answer questions. There is a paid DLC for the outfits, but you can also purchase them in-game with the eyeballs you collect throughout Somnium levels.   What I disliked the most in this game was the adult and sexual jokes; they were too much and unnecessary; they made the characters look bad and even forced them into some of the conversations. I didn't find joy in them. Also, some of the characters' relationships felt weird and forced, as well as what was written in their profiles.I didn't expect some of the twists we had in the game; it made me speechless in a good way. There are five endings, and one of them is a good ending. The good ending is locked until you finish the other endings, which you can choose from the flowchart to continue from where you've stopped. The sad part is that you only have one manual save file, meaning you must reset the section where you want to choose different questions or responses. As much as I liked some of the characters, I disliked at least four characters in this game, mainly Mama. They also didn't explain some things for a couple of the characters, such as why their personalities are like that and why Hitomi is still living 'alone' after what happened in the previous game. I also don't know why they decided to have a weird character design sometimes. Pros:+Interesting story with multiple twists.+Excellent writing.+Fully voiced (Choice between Japanese and English voice acting)+Interesting characters.+Good soundtracks.+Chellenging puzzles in Psync.+Multiple endings and routes.+Two side mini-game (Eyeballie, Tama/Aiba Room)+Good game length.+Steam achievements.Cons:-One manual save file.-QTE is tricky if you use a keyboard and mouse. A controller is highly recommended for the game.-A LOT of adult humor.I understand what they meant by the extra ending, but I don't comprehend the whole thing those 'evil' corporate are after. The game is a bit confusing, but I can't say I haven't enjoyed parts of it. I still prefer the first one better.

_childDocuments_.review: What a game. This game is probably up there with 999 in terms of story quality, and combined with everything else in the game, my opinion is that this game is easily the best Ushikoshi game.I will compare nirvanA with AI1 a lot because they are from the same series.Story comparison with AI1:When compared with AI1, in my opinion, nirvanA has weaker endings to almost every route. AI1's stories also feel much more personal and heart-wrenching than nirvanA. However, nirvanA is better than AI1 in literally everything else, story-wise. The mystery's build-up is far more well done, there are a lot more sub-plots (which are also well-written and integrated), and Ushikoshi really abused Chekov's Gun a lot as well here. The characters are also better written and have a lot more involvement in the story, and old ones like Chinpei gain a lot of character too.That being said, this is an Ushikoshi game, so as expected, there is an Ushikoshi moment in it as well. As for what an Ushikoshi moment is, Ushikoshi's writing style is back to front, so he imagines a twist (or more than 1 twist), then makes a story out of it. Below are some examples.In 999, it was the introduction of jumping timelines in Zero Escape. In VLR, it was , and in ZTD, it was . AI's was . nirvanA has a few, but there is one in particular that stands out. It's so mindbending that it literally stopped me for a solid ten minutes out of shock. And I usually can take twists quite well and continue playing. This Ushikoshi moment almost perfect in execution and also the most shocking by far. The only possible flaw with it is . This moment was also so good, it actually makes a repeat playthrough really tempting, just to see how the scenarios were cleverly written for the sake of the twist.OST: Just really good, as expected.Graphics: Slightly better than AI1. So, it's alright. Gameplay: The somniums in this game are far better than in AI1. The worst of nirvanA is nearly as good as the best of AI1, and that is amazing. Many somniums have completely unique ways of navigating them. Even the more normal ones are still really solid. The creativity of these somniums are also really great. Many of them really give you a sense that you are in a dream, not just some cobbled mish-mash of memories, which is most of what AI1's somniums are like. There were very few moments of frustration for me in nirvanA when it comes to somniums. Conclusion: Fantastic game, perhaps Ushikoshi's best. It's by no means flawless. However, it's a damn good Visual Novel.Also, Date is a great MC, but imo he actually is far better as a supporting cast member, and nirvanA proves it. I enjoyed Date a lot in AI1, but his presence in nirvanA is just so good.

_childDocuments_.review: Once is an inspiration, twice is an obligation. I'll start this review by saying the 1st game is probably my favourite game of all time. Almost everything I mentioned in that review applies to this, but not all of it. I also used a PC/Switch controller to play as I believe it is the better control scheme, just like the 1st game. And just like the 1st game, they have to reuse certain jokes and character gimmicks because they had to since they did it in the first game. So even though it's been roughly 5 years since I last played, I still remember and laughed at the recycled jokes that have new material now.What's not funny is most of the 1st game's cast is barely involved in the story. Unlike in the 1st game, most of them are just hanging around, not involved in the story. I'm questioning why they are even in this game, but once again, the line at the beginning of the review kept creeping back into my mind as I played. The designers of the new cast of characters in this game seem to have forgotten that while the character designs in the 1st game are colourful, they still looked like how most humans look in real life. We now have big headed but short scientist, a giant deformed man in a animal mascot costume and a man with a square head. One of those has a reason to look the way they do, the other 2 are just designed that way. It's incredibly distracting. While thankfully, there are normal looking cast members in this installment, can't say I find them very interesting.One of my favourite things to do in these games are to interact with the items in the various locations to see the funny banter between characters regarding the inspected item. Yet, I can't help but feel they didn't care as much this time around. The new areas and new characters rarely seem to bother giving a remark about the many items just stuffed into the area. Many times I'm just clicking everything hoping to see a scene but many times I'm left hanging. And yet, in the areas that are recycled from the 1st game, I'm having fun seeing the recycled interactions and jokes from familiar places that always had a reoccurring gag. It's almost as if they didn't have much to add in the new areas and just gave up. Like they said in game: "You don't have to say anything if you don't have anything to talk about." While true, it just feels like I'm wasting my time clicking all the items in this game, almost like an obligation instead of something fun to do while revisiting a new area.What I also liked about the 1st game is that it's very linear, you won't ever get stuck. Somehow they screwed that up this time. The game feels like it hasn't been play tested, during certain parts of the game they give out these fill in the blank questions that are seemingly designed to block the players from advancing the story. And it refuses to let me proceed unless I give them the exact answer they are looking for. The game thinks they have given you enough hints to comfortably answer them, but they have clearly not. When I looked up the answers online, my only thought was: "I would've never figured this out." Because that's what I want in my games, being asked to solve ridiculous puzzles that I don't think are even fair. What happened to my linear experience? I'm sorry I'm not a genius, so I have to ruin my immersion to look up a walkthrough.Now about that story, I enjoyed almost half of it. While I hated the other half. And most of it is due to the new cast of characters, more specifically the new team of Ryuki and Tama. These 2 are completely useless together and are not enjoyable to watch. Compared to the amazing pair that Date and Aiba were in the previous game, it's such a downgrade to be forced to sit through the new pair's investigations. Ryuki is a generic shounen protagonist. There's hardly anything to note about him except that he is annoying, not a great detective, and certainly isn't funny. He is clearly unfit for the investigation yet he's still on the case. He's constantly having delusions and passes out frequently. Clearly he isn't fit for duty, yet everyone around him seems to call him a genius or something.His partner is no better. Tama, the new Ai Ball AI partner, is an assistant/consultant. She barely fulfills either of those roles. For someone that looks like a dominatrix, her personality is of a massive pushover that allows Ryuki free reign to do whatever, despite how terrible of an idea that is. Her personality makes no sense, sometimes she bosses Ryuki around by shouting at him, rudely mind you. Yet when the going gets tough, she just rolls over. As an AI assistant, she somehow is of no help in warding off or confirming what is real or delusion despite being in his left eye. It's almost as if she doesn't even exist sometimes.I genuinely hated most of their segments, and the quality of writing in their routes are just bad. Inept duo aside, their investigation feels strangely bloated with horribly bland Somniums. There are exceptions but most of them felt really bland this time around. A lot of the joke choices don't give any funny results, instead we are reprimanded for not choosing the obvious answers. So much for a dream world. And the somnium design feels like they have gotten worse in some cases. A lot of them actively try to fail you right at the end, and if you spend too much time early on, you basically had to restart right at the end. They give out hints that eat up time, use them enough times and you were going to lose either way, so you had to restart.It also extends to the writing of the mystery, the contrivances they come up with to block technology like GPS tracking, voice/video calls and cloud saving investigation data is maddening. It's almost as if everybody in that world actively chooses to not charge their phones and turn off their GPS so nobody can find them in an emergency. To be fair, the 1st game did this sometimes, but it feels so much more commonplace here. By the end of the Ryuki route, I started to question why I even liked the 1st game, it's that bad.And yet, when I arrived at the Mizuki route, things changed. I really appreciated the dynamic between Mizuki and Aiba. They're fun to be around, Mizuki retains her super human strength and her personality is pretty much the same as before, very straight forward and gung ho about handling situations. Aiba returns and she's great! She's really useful and she's surprisingly thoughtful at times. It almost feels like a different writing team was responsible for their route. Most of the somniums for Mizuki's route feels a lot more creative and fun to play through. I was getting more banter when I checked items in areas. And in some of the somniums, the joke options in somniums yielded more funny outcomes. It reminded me of why I loved the 1st game, except it's just worse this time. I will say I enjoyed most of her route but at this point, it's already a worse game than the 1st one. There's no meaning in me recommending this game. It's more expensive than the 1st game, has worse writing, a lesser cast of side characters and main characters that are just not as interesting or funny as Date and Aiba, the 1st game's pairing. It has forced fill in the blank segments that are designed to stumble player progress. It introduced a difficulty slider for QTEs and Somniums because they didn't want casual players to be stuck, yet didn't bother giving better hints for all the quizzes and fill in the blank questions.  Even though it's been 5 years since my play through of the 1st game, there's this sense of deja vu as I'm constantly revisiting these areas from the 1st game. And with how few new areas there are, it just feels like I'm going back and forth in the same few areas. There's simply not enough new content to make this game feel like a sequel, despite the new mystery and cast.
_childDocuments_.name: AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES - nirvanA Initiative

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game a more than the last game.  Like all games written by Kotaro Uchikoshi, It's still mostly a bunch of puzzles, character backstories, infodumps, wacky action scenes, and plot twists loosely duct-taped together into something resembling a plot about a guy that kills people because he read a wikipedia article about some cool physics theory.  Relative to the first game, the pros are: you can play as Mizuki, the puzzle's and somniums are much better, there are a few bonus features, and you can play as Mizuki.I think the weak point is the story feels somewhat linear since the paths get locked, and Ryuki can be a somewhat dull protagonist that you play for the first part of the game. Narratively his character arc is a good idea, but I think his personality and mental health issues could have been written better.There is also a major "twist" that I really enjoyed, but I expect some people will dislike because it might feel cheap.
_childDocuments_.name: AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES - nirvanA Initiative

_childDocuments_.review: As a continuation of the AI series, it follows some recurring characters through an investigation that once again throws their lives into chaos. The game follows two new main characters, Mizuki from the first game and Ryuki, a newcomer to ABIS, and the Half-Body Case.  I won't give any more information, but it has everything the first game has and a little more, with a small tamagatchi-like system, a dress-up room for Aiba and Tama (Ryuki's partner), and multiple endings.  Some of the puzzles were actually difficult, there are now QTE's in some combat cutscenes, and there's even a special preview of Spike Chunsoft's Nonary Game after you beat the game.The endings themselves don't feel QUITE as good as they did in the first game, but two of the endings did nearly bring me to tears. The writing is well done, the voice acting is fantastic, and I personally give this game an 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game improves on a lot of things compared to its predecessor.Most notably Psyncs (the main gameplay sections) were heavily improved having both more variety and more in sheer quantity. Story tone goes up in insanity compared to its predecessor, which benifits the game as a whole. Ai: THE SOMNIUM FILES had a more grounded tone, which made the insanely stupid action scenes feels extremely jarring. They are still far from good scenes, but the tone of the story fits better now. In terms of story it's fine for the most part, but it does have some asinine twists. Though if you are familiar with Kotaro Uchikoshi's other works, it should be well within expectations.The story is also surprisingly mostly linear, which is shame since the game would benefit a lot from a little nonlinearity, but this is mostly small gripe. Overall I think nirvanA Initiative is an improvement on the previous entry, despite its obvious flaws. Though I don't think that is a high bar to pass. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think this game is pretty much exactly what I wanted from a follow up to the original Somnium Files. The game is even more of a mind♥♥♥♥ than the first one, the characters and writing are still as great as ever, and the Somnium segments are more interesting and involved this time imo. It was really enjoyable to try to piece together how the story was going to turn out, and I actually did manage to predict some stuff (e.g.  before it was actually revealed). I think the story is just very intelligently written as well, and when everything falls into place it really is one hell of a realization (not saying some points don't feel a bit contrived though). Also Tama best girl.For a bit more of a detailed breakdown, again, I think the Somnium segments are more interesting this time than they were in the first game. Still nothing on the level of ZE's puzzles (although there is ) but it was fun to interact with the Somniums and see how they changed. Adding swimming to some of them was a cute touch too. As for the writing and characterization, I think it's pretty on point here...for the most part. Don't get me wrong, Date being a perv was funny in the first game, but at least for me I was hoping after the end of the first game that he wasn't gonna be more of the same in this game...but he kinda was, when I expected him to be more serious. I guess this has to do with them not wanting to spoil the first game in the second one (this game actually has a quiz at the start that asks you some questions regarding the ending of the original AI to confirm you won't be spoiled, and you have to answer all the questions correctly), but hey they're the devs. Aside from the handling of Date, I loved pretty much all the other characters, and they even got me to respect Ota now which is something I didn't think I'd be able to do after the first game.Overall, I'd say if you were a fan of the first game, then definitely pick up Nirvana. Pretty much all the good parts about the original were polished and made even better here in Nirvana. Even if you didn't play the original (but for some reason are here looking at the sequel...) then you can truly play this game spoiler free even if you haven't played the original. However, there is one crime that is truly unforgivable, and that is Uchikoshi making me down horrendous for a thicc dom chick who makes pervy jokes, constantly flirts with me, and threatens to tie me up with rope. I hope you're happy with yourself Uchikoshi. For real though, 10/10 game, Tama best girl, and most importantly MIZUKI SAYS TRANS RIGHTS!

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was a very big surprise for me and become one of my favorite game of 2019! This didn't even touch the surface of the emotional impact that the first one made me feel. First thing: If you're expecting that this is gonna be directly connected to the first one and build on the True Ending that was established- don't buy it! The characters are basically acting like the first game never happened. We only have those small optional dialogues that give you- sometimes so stupid- explanation of why things are back to "default". There are a lot of reused jokes, locations, and plot points so sometimes I felt like I'm playing exactly the same game but with a different skin.I really don't understand what was the point of putting an original cast in the game if they're only there for background. And if they're part of the main plot, writers make them so over the top that it hurts me. Everything is over-complicated for the sake of being over-complicated.I like the new cast but they don't have the opportunity to shine- why not focus on them 100% if you don't want to do anything creative with the original cast anyway? Developers?For me, it looks like they wanted to kill two birds with one stone- have a new protagonist and new cast but at the same time, have Mizuki and the original cast come back. Which didn't serve any parts of the story.What happened to all the creepy/horror elements? Anybody remembers the last sommnia of the Annihilation Ending in the first game? or that people being stabbed or murdered were shown to the player? Yeah, nothing like that here... people are being cut in half but nothing is shown and even if we're examining the body it's conveniently placed on the side that's not showing any blood or insides. I know that even the original game had some over-the-top/very anime moments but here it's pushed to the max: one person fighting hundred goons, a character trying to stop the rocket on the fricking scooter that magically flies now, in one point one character grabs a minigun and starts shooting everything that moves. I just can't...5/10 so perfectly in half just like the half-body serial killings and this game's plot. Time to replay the first game to remember how good this franchise can be.

_childDocuments_.review: To start with, I do recommend AI:The Somnium Files - nirvanA initiate overall.The game reassures you that playing the first one is optional, which while I see how you could jump in here, I would still recommend playing the original first if nothing else for an explanation on some of the recurring jokes and you can see more of the character growth.Gameplay: AI:TSF NI makes a lot of smart changes over the original, as the Somnium puzzle logic feels a lot more forgiving than I remember the original being with the bonus of having a variety of difficulty options to give you more time if you want it. On the other hand though, I remember the Somnium designs being more surprising in the original but that was also a few years ago so it's hard to say if I'm just being pickier.Story: NI is a fun ride. It's definitely cut from the same cloth as the original in a lot of the minute-to-minute dialogue and style which I find more of a positive than a negative. Being that the story is the main attraction here I can't say much for specific pros and cons but I liked it. I still find the action sequences to be the weaker part of the series  but it does a better job of maintaining a tone than the original that I felt cut the tension of the serious moments a bit too often. The same style of humor from the original is still here, it just feels like it is better placed than before.Music - The music is very good, though a decent chunk of it will be familiar to those who played the original.Misc - There are a lot of weird odds and ends choices like bugging you to talk to your Ai-ball when you open up your menu, the UI in general takes a minute to get used to when suddenly you have have Trivia scrolling along the top that you can move with the D-pad which is also how you select a dialogue option and if you just so happen to be selected on someone when trivia pops in you'll end up picking a question when you wanted to just scroll through the trivia message. There are definitely some quirks to the design but nothing major I'd call out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm tired and stiff and no that's not Boss talking! Joking aside I'm here to write my review for the second and currently last game in the AI somnium files series, to me it's rare for a second game to be as good if not better than the first, especially modern day but AI2 (which is what I'll call it from here) is sequel and a half for sure, even if you liked the first one more in short this game is as good if not better at times than the first game dood.Now onto the full review for more details, so how the game plays for people skipping the first game (you reaaaally shouldn't though, first games stellar still) a point and click VN with other gameplay elements such as third person area searching which they've added to in this with another way of looking at things third person, QTE (quick time events) which there are quite a few more of and this time around puzzles dood.The story much like the first involves you being a detective with an AI-ball assistant but this time there's a new protagonist you play as, the game plays almost exactly the same as before with a few exceptions, first off it's easier, like much easier than the first game in terms of gameplay and the somnium (if ya haven't played yet you'll get to it lol) what's more there's a lot more just straight up inspecting rather than choices at times too, I think it worked well for the larger somniums myself but it did make timies hard to judge when to use, not that those even really mattered oh and if that wasn't easy enough for you? there's two lower difficulties that massively lower how much time is spent in somniums so fun for everyone dood!They have added a new third person mode, I won't spoil what it is exactly but just for now imagine how somnium plays but without a time limit and piecing together things in a different way, honestly I enjoyed this aspect a lot and it made for some great comedic moments as well as adding more detail to things and how they worked which is great, it can often be a detail left out in investigative stories and games dood.The QTE events are more abundant which is great because they are just a visual treat and so fun to do, so having more this time around is just an amazing time, what's that? you're bad at QTE? me too!! lol well maybe these days I'm a little better but even so they have you covered as they have like with the somnium, two lower difficulty versions for those of you who want to see things go in super slow-mo while you find whatever button prompts there are you need to press! I appreciate this because not all people probably came into these games for too much action so it's a great way for people to just roll with it for fun dood.Let's see...ah puzzles! now these were great but I did have issue with some, I can hear the "Git gud!" from here XD still I like to think I know my way around a puzzle or ten over the years, now to start I do want to say none of these puzzles were bad, they were creative and rather fun, the main issue is the visual representation and what they gave you to work with on about...I'd say three puzzles I think needed a little more to make sense, definitely 2 although I won't spoil, what I will give props for though is the devs realise we aren't all super great at puzzles and gives you either hints or right out answers (at the cost of a little more time) if you can't seem to grasp it, the game is very player friendly which for a mostly VN/story based game I feel is a must dood.The cast and music/songs were all outstanding as always, all lines bar very particular inner talk is voiced just like before and it remains a clever and insanely interesting game that much like the first, I'd suggest to anyone, casual or non casual players alike and I hope to see more from the devs in the future, whether it's a new AI somnium game or something else, I hope you all enjoy it as much as I have and thank you for reading dood ^-^7

_childDocuments_.review: nirvanA Iniviative is a sequel to AI: The Somnium Files, however they have made the game friendly for newcomers to try out without knowing about the first game, they even include a quiz at the beginning to test on whether or not you actually know about the first game, though these only really hide some specific trivia that shows up at the top of the screen. The game is mostly unconnected from the plot of the first, though this led to some choices that even though are explained, are a bit silly, just to reduce information from the first game, I'd still recommend actually playing the previous game before trying out this one.As for what this game itself is, its a visual novel styled adventure mystery game, where you'll take control of 2 different members of ABIS, a police department that dives into people's subconscious dreams to gather information for their investigations. This game follows a story that spans throughout a case that began 6 years prior and was unsolved, before signs of the culprit start showing up again.In classic Kotaro Uchikoshi style, the game features branching paths on the story that will lead to different endings, though this time around there is a more set order on how you can actually chose the branch you end up on, this is done for a narrative purpose, you can't always branch out freely unlike the previous game or the Zero Escape titles, but it works in the end. Eventually you'll reach a road block that requires other branches to be explored first, or on the contrary, be able to continue on a specific path once you reach an ending. There is not much more to say, but there will be surprises along the way.The game seems to use an enhanced engine from the previous game: loading, prompts and selections that used to take a little longer in the previous game now are quicker, which is a QoL enhancement for the player, I can't ignore this and I praise the upgrade that was done on the core system of the game.Additionally, my overall favorite feature that was added was the ability to revisit the Somnium scenarios without a time limit, this allows you to select all the funny alternate options within these scenarios without having to worry about time usage, or having to reset over and over, like what you had to do on the first game if you wanted to see the side scenarios.Overall if you are a fan of Uchikoshi's game you know what to expect, the entire game is a wild ride and it kept finding ways to surprise me all the way through.

_childDocuments_.review: A deeply disappointing sequel to the original Somnium Files.In part, this is because the sequel seems obliged to distort, overuse, or otherwise ruin key moments from the first game. The most dramatically refreshing twist from the first game - that all the mentions of cults or secret plots in a somnium were just caused by Iris' brain damage - is completely reversed. The Atami ending is repeated, despite not fitting one bit, presumably just because it was so memorable the first time. This problem is most jarringly notable when, after quoting a line from the first game that'd just been contradicting by the latest twist, Mizuki asks, "Did she mean the exact opposite?" No.No she didn't.But the problems with Nirvana are deeper and more structural that the annoyances that first left a bad taste. The Somniums, in particular, rely on too many gimmicks to match up to their counterparts from the first game. This has two consequences: first, there was never a moment where I felt like I'd finally grasped the dream-logic and therefore finally cracked the puzzle. In Nirvana, either the thread of logic was so obvious from the start as to allow only a single chain of answers, or the logic wasn't there at all. And second, where the first game made good work out of the decision points being contained within the puzzles, Nirvana initiative hardly uses them at all.Ironically, these two flaws are most displayed by what is otherwise the game's best somnium, by far: Lien's. It has the most rewarding dream-logic. It has a somnium choice, when I was feeling starved for them. And a narratively compelling choice at that: resolve Lien's dramatic arc for a favour, or dive deeper to uncover his secrets; either way get a different piece of information. But, at the crucial moment, the choice is presented as a pair of effectively identical safes.It is design oversights like this, and the mentality that resulted in them, that resulted in an underwhelming set of somniums.There are other flaws that could be mentioned. The fight scenes, for one, have more than I could easily list. And perhaps the problem is that Nirvana Initiative's flaws are front loaded and end loaded, leaving a more reasonable middle section hurt both by the bad taste going into it and a cynicism-tinted hindsight. Would I have appreciated that middle section more, and the controversial main twist, if it hadn't been for that? Maybe.But as it stands, this game comes across as a sequel that exists because they wanted a sequel, and not a game that wants to exist on its own merits. And that meant that Uchikoshi succumbed to the temptation of all his worst habits, without a structure to guide him away from them.(Plus, what on Earth did they do to Mizuki's hair?)

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, the mystery and the twists in the main plot is very interesting and while there are bound to be some holes with a premise this complex, Spike Chunsoft once again does a good job making the player believe the twist without resorting to anything ridiculous.However, the good part stops pretty much there. All the characters are there just to make the plot and the twists move forward. Characters that act intelligently one moment do something ridiculously stupid because otherwise the plot point can't occur. Characters are both omnipotent and can't do basic things. Characters solve extremely difficult riddle but then don't realize the most obvious things, all just so that the main plot can stay whole and move forward.There are also some good improvements to the somnium parts but unlike the previous game it is extremely straightforward and the gimmicks only make other elements superfluous. I don't want to get into gameplay element spoilers, so only mentioning something that existed in the previous game as an example, but what is the point of TIMEEs in this game? In the previous game they were things that you collected from obviously wrong objects so that you have leeway trying to find the right solution, but in this game they don't serve any purpose. 80% of the time you aren't even allowed to use them.In the previous game the somnium parts and the gameplay were there to enhance the experience as the player went to various routes on their own volition gathering information in an order that is unique to their experience. In this game the gameplay is there to say "hey look there is gameplay!!!" while offering almost nothing to contribute to enhance the story experience. There are even parts where it seems only natural that the target would tell the player the information and the psyncs are just there because gameplay needs to be added.Overall, the main twist is very solid again and if you enjoyed the twists of the first game without the supernatural flavor of Zero Escape series, the game isn't that bad but despite having so much more things than the first game, what you get is so much less in terms of getting engrossed in the story.There are more I want to complain about but that would start to creep into spoiler territory so I'll leave it at this.

_childDocuments_.review: A deep and mind-bending mystery where nothing is what it seems on the face, a lovable and quirky cast of flawed and eccentric characters, a very odd but endearing sense of humour, and a lot of heart. This was completely my jam and a real gem ^^

_childDocuments_.review: This is a weird game to rate. On reflection, I don't even see this as a Somnium Files game, but a love letter to the Zero Escape series, which is bizarre. I don't want to go too in-depth on any particular thing because story is so crucial to enjoyment (or lack thereof), so I'll keep this review a bit vague.From the puzzle design, to the story, to the twists, this doesn't strike me as more Somnium Files, but a Zero Escape game with a different skin. Though the first Somnium Files felt like the real, modern world with two twists: Psyncing and the power of AI, both explored very thorough within that game, this sequel just feels like ANYTHING can happen. And while that can make for some exciting and surprising moments, it also makes for some rather confusing moments because the rules of the in-game world just don't make sense anymore. This is classic for Zero Escape, since that series hinges on twisting the normal and expected so thoroughly that nothing makes sense anymore. But, for Somnium, it doesn't really work the same way. Things have to make sense in this kind of series because, at the end of the day, it's a mystery game where much of the enjoyment is putting the piece of the puzzle together for yourself. That's pretty hard to do when the game constantly derails itself and puts forth the most nonsensical things imaginable.I recommend this game if you like the Zero Escape series, but not really if you like the first Somnium Files. While this game does have its charms as a Somnium game, its true strengths are when you realize it's the secret fourth Zero Escape game.Tama is hot tho so 10/10 you got me there!

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original, I'm not sure how I feel about nirvanA Initiative. However, in some crucial ways, it falls behind the original. The story begins promising enough but the ending really left me unsatisfied with some cheap twists, the villain is pretty much the same guy from Zero Time Dilemma and was a pretty weak antagonist compared to the nail-biting tension of the first game, and having two protagonists, while it could certainly work, just kinda diluted the potency of the story due to its mediocre execution. Especially poor Ryuki is kinda shafted later on. I also wish games didn't block off pre-order bonuses for people who bought it later (just sell it separately). nirvanA Initiative also feels like more of an expansion than a proper sequel as it doesn't really build upon the original game's graphical and design foundation in any meaningful way.Overall, it's a 7/10 for me. I'm still excited to see more games in this universe but I'm hoping for a more coherent, more satisfying plot and some real innovations in how the game looks and plays.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a big reason why Steam needs a 'mixed' review.TL;DR: It's okay. Lots of potential but ultimately felt weak with some of the plot twists, explanations of said twists, tonal whiplash, and so forth honestly just being awful. If you liked the first game you should still play this game but it is not as good as the first.Let's start off with the positives:- The soundtrack is great, no complaints here.- The somniums are a great improvement over AI1, the puzzles are much more logical and while the key system wasn't really useful (they essentially just tell you the 'theme' of the somnium, which is pretty obvious and doesn't need to be spelled out most of the time), it still comes in handy a couple of times. Plus, they don't crash this time around! - The references to scientific phenomena and questioning the validity of them are key to Uchikoshi's works, and this game is no exception.- Tokiko.- 'Virtual Reality' sections were cool- The mystery itself was very compelling throughout the whole game- Spoilers for one of the bonuses (not a story spoiler): Now, the not so positive:- The tonal whiplash. The advertising for this game is DARK. The Hidden Bats ARG, the trailers, the description, even the main menu theme give you this really uncomfortable feeling. However, sometimes the game just decides to go balls to the wall with the most wacky unfitting action sequences. I'm talking characters seemingly jumping into the fight from the sky, enemies literally STARING AT OUR CHARACTERS with guns aimed as we beat their comrades to a pulp, characters lifting objects that are thousands of pounds that have no right lifting these objects (this is actually explained, but the explanation feels like a copout), so on and so forth. The game occasionally goes into some REALLY DARK subject matter, which I can't talk about without spoiling anything, but these moments are followed up with these god awful action sequences and it just ruins the tone of the whole game. The Zero Escape games kept a serious, dark tone throughout each title. Imagine if after a character's death in 999 or VLR the characters just started fortnite dancing and beating up a massive group of armed forces with a metal pipe. If this game just kept the dark tone they advertised, it would be better by a significant margin.- The plot twists. Obviously I'm not going into too much detail here. The plot twists themselves are okay (most of them are actually great), but the explanations for some of these plot twists, not so much. Some of the plot twists are great at the time of revelation, but any actual thought into them just raise so many questions and it begins to feel like they created this game BECAUSE they came up with a plot twist and did everything they could to make it work, which ends up making certain story elements feel shoehorned in just to allow the twist to happen.- I'm gonna be honest, this game not trying to spoil the first game was a huge mistake. I assume Spike Chunsoft wanted this game to sell really well and limiting it to those who already played AI1 would hinder that, but the game itself clearly suffered because of this. Some of the returning characters were honestly BUTCHERED in this, their personalities just feel way off to how they should be and a lot of character development from the first game just gets completely erased. One such character isn't even supposed to exist in this game because of the events of AI1 and the explanation for their existence is straight up garbage.-----Overall, the game is like a 6/10. The first half of the game had MASSIVE potential, it was mostly serious and the mystery was compelling, the theories running through your brain were crazy. The second half of the game just falls off significantly. Most of the tonal whiplash happens here, some of the major plot twists at this point just feel shoehorned in, the characters around you just aren't as interesting as the first half, etc. That's my main complaint of this game. Potential. This game isn't nearly as bad as World's End Club, that's for sure, but it's just not on the same level of Zero Escape or AI1. I genuinely pray that Uchikoshi can go back to more serious themes and stick to them. These wacky action scenes and tonal shifts are NOT IT. Should you buy it: yes. It's not a bad experience, it just could've been so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey this game is pretty good!... Except it wasn't.... Except it is!From the get-go I always heard this game got mixed reviews, and I can definitely see why.Let me clarify my opinion:I do not believe this game is bad, not by any means. Spike Chunsoft proved to us once again that they can continue to make absolute bangers of mystery visual novels, and this game is proof of their skills. Massive props to Uchikoshi and the team. However, I do believe this games plot to be far weaker than the first, which is a shame because it's what I love to experience in these kinds of games, and what they are mostly focused on.When I first started playing Nirvana Initiative, I was incredibly hooked, just like any other SC VN. But as I played on, I felt tired of the plot and certain scenes, namely the action scenes and the main ending. God the action scenes were painfully awkward to watch.This game pulls a lot of its plot from the whole cult cliche, which if you like that stuff, more power to you. I'm just kind of sick of it after it being prevalent in nearly all 3 Zero Escape games, and even Worlds End Club. The ultimate bad guy reveal isn't nearly as interesting as AI1, and the ending just feels... Well... cheesy and Hollywood-y.That being said though, everything up until the last stretch of the game (in my opinion) is fantastic. Characters are great as always. I especially loved Ryuki and Tama, and thought they were amazing, if not better than Mizuki and Aiba. They felt like a perfect fit for the world of AI:TSF. The somniums are amazing and are a lot more experimental than the first game, but I mean that in the best way possible. They were seriously A LOT of fun to solve and play through. It captures light hearted somniums well, and the dark somniums even better. And of course, the soundtrack is grooving to the max. Always a strong part of these games. The music used in somniums really captured the emotions well. I especially liked the music for "Need Info", and "Novel Ingress".And finally, what I  really loved was the amount of 999 references. The bonus 3rd class cabin somnium literally made me freak out with joy. I love Zero Escape so much and I'm so glad it got this much attention in another title.All in all, this game IS a good time, but left me feeling a bit disappointed with how they handled the ending. I still highly recommend this game regardless, illbeit, a very heavy hit or miss kind of game. However, I urge anyone who has played the first game to definitely give this a go whenever possible, perhaps on sale if you're unsure.Thanks for reading this review, I just wanted to state my opinions on the game, and hopefully give potential buyers an idea of what they are getting into!

_childDocuments_.review: A New Level of Insult, Buyer BewareIn my 30 years of gaming, this may have been the worst story experience I can recall. I simply was not prepared for just how much, or in what ways, a story could be so badly constructed.To say that the game is a slog to get through would be a massive understatement. As others have said, the characters and story beats are forced in order to justify a twist, which ultimately has no meaning or emotional impact whatsoever. You wont be able to learn anything intriguing or useful about the mystery until 40 hours in, and it doesn't hit in any way that is relevant. At this point, you will have lost all investment, and the twist and ending are completely trivial. You might as well have had the twist be "oh, the killer was actually a robot!" or something of equally no impact. I simply cannot overstate how "hurtful" this game is in the sense that it pulls you through excruciatingly long sequences of shouted child banter with the most trivial, forced psyncs at every turn, until the entire conclusion gives up in exhausted resignation--"We did it, we somehow made the game work," without any sense of progress or satisfaction. All I can say is that I will need a very long break from VNs to recover from this.  For Nakazawa fans, there is a small degree of philosophy in the game on the topic of 解脱 (probably moksha in English). The problem is that it feels like an afterthought and is completed wasted as it is not related to the story in any meaningful way. These topics have so much depth to them, but all we get here is a brief introduction while all the implications are ignored. In the end, these ideas were done better in Nakazawa's masterworks Remember 11 and I/O. It seems to me that Uchikoshi is a business man and not a writer. Most people don't realize that it was Nakazawa and his ideas that made the Infinity Series so good, not Uchikoshi. Without Nakazawa, 12 Riven was just as awful as AI.There is a certain frantic nature to Uchikoshi's writing, like a privileged child who just discovered thought. I can almost compare it to Yoko Taro, but in his case, there is absolutely is meaning in his stories and complex emotions are at play. AI Somnium files nirvana initiative is juvenile to the point of being repulsive, like the entire thing is a throw-away kitchen sink joke, which the game seems to even recognize in some of its dialog options. The problem there is that it doesn't make it any better.The only objective quality of the game is its high production value, but even this simply misleads you, like a beautifully wrapped gift with something distasteful inside. I recommend that one avoids this game at all costs. If you feel tempted, be honest with yourself about the reasons why you want to play it. Do not let the graphics, voice acting, and FOMO cause you to make the mistake I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming in from AI, which was a pretty goofy but fun and intriguing mystery game, I suppose I didn't really know what to expect. I came away feeling like this was the worst of both VLR and ZTD with ZTD's boring mystery, plot and characters and VLR's incredibly goofy and badly executed plot twists making this a thoroughly underwhelming playthrough. Only once it dropped all pretense of being a mystery game did I finally begin to have fun with it and I rode the goofiness of the end to a somewhat satisfying conclusion but that doesn't excuse the remaining 80-90% of the game where I was bored to tears.Getting it out of the way, the presentation is largely exactly the same as AI. They're serviceable with the fun character designs and goofy low-fi animations and extremely small environments. They're not trying to win you over with the graphics and that's perfectly fine. The music is great as ever with a lot of the same tracks from the first game but also a fair few new ones. I played it on Japanese and the voice acting is entertaining and I do hear good things about the English dub which was excellent in the first game.In terms of gameplay, you're still largely just following a VN story for most of it, punctuated by the Somniums which are the "escape room"-esque sections where you need to solve puzzles in moon logic to try and make sense of a subject's dreams to find things out about them. I largely enjoyed AI's Somniums so color me very surprised when I realised that the Somniums this time around almost all hilariously easy or unreasonably frustrating. There was ONE Somnium that was good, one that was decent. The rest were either walks in the park with incredibly obvious solutions requiring next to no thought or logic, or unreasonably frustrating with instant death mechanics and lots of frustrating trial and error. Most of the Somniums, save the one good one, don't really have puzzles any more. You're not really figuring out anything. You are given almost the entire solution right from the get go making large portions of some of them extremely linear affairs where you're just doing the next singular thing. I'm also really not a fan of the many times you are essentially forced into protracted sequences that reduce your time but give you no option to use the timies which is a huge departure from the first game. The Somniums were a serious downgrade in my opinion.And unfortunately, coming to the story, I did not like most of what was on display. The writer of this game, Kotaro Uchikoshi, loves his sci-fi and loves his plot twists. Unfortunately, in this case, the twists hurt the storytelling to the extent that it doesn't allow you to explore the characters and their tragedies which left me very unsympathetic to their situations and I cannot elaborate further without going into massive spoilers. The story structure is centered almost entirely around the core twist which leaves so much of the game shallow and bereft of any sense. Characters simply refuse to talk to you and elaborate on what they know, nonsensical explanations have to prop up and hurriedly stitch closed massive plot holes, characters aren't given the room to breathe and let their stories grow and so on. None of it hooked me until the very end when the game just lets loose in a blaze of unabashed and shameless glory and revels in the chaos. Rather than try and make sense, I really wish the game leaned more into how incredibly stupid it is. But the game is not really a mystery game and people who want an actual mystery to try and figure out, akin to a detective novel, will be thoroughly disappointed.While I did not enjoy myself playing this game, I am very glad it exists and will definitely pick up whatever the team makes next. I did not find myself enjoying the game as I played it but I am still glad that I played it, if for nothing else than to experience the sheer madness of these titles. There's truly nothing else quite like it.

_childDocuments_.review: A tentative recommendation. This game has...problems. But if you liked the first one maybe pick this up on sale and try to go with the flow. Thinking about the plot too much isn't a lot of fun, let it just carry you along. I don't regret having played it, but it was extremely frustrating as a game in the 'mystery' genre.I think the main issue with this game is that it isn't a well written mystery. The best mysteries show the audience all of the information so you could in theory work it out yourself. The story then makes you feel clever by either confirming your suspicions or walking you through it until you can get it before the big reveal. Nirvana initiative is somewhat dishonest with the way it presents information to the player. Characters withhold information for no good reason, they reveal it at times that are convenient to the plot but lack rationale for the characters themselves. Some information is actively withheld from the player in order to facilitate a 'clever reveal'. Other plot points are never clarified or explained, or are unsatisfactorily closed off  with one-liners. For people who like mystery plots this whole game is a real headache. There is also some fairly serious character assassination in parts in order to support plot contrivances. Lots of things happen conveniently at just the right time. That's generally a sign of poor writing.Outside of the plot issues, the game seems overly reliant on a strange combination of QTE fight scenes and the same dance sequence about 5 times. By the end the fights had really lost all impact which was a real shame. The puzzles are good and in some cases not easy, so there's definitely something to enjoy for puzzle fans.Mechanically the game works fine except for a graphical error toward the end involving Mizuki's hair(?) and one ending not completing properly which appeared to lock me out until I went online for a solution.However, some of the old fan favourites remain the same and still fun and likeable. The plot is...a ride...even if it isn't always a pleasant one, the intro is excellent. Some plot beats are really nice.TLDR: Rough plot for a plot driven game, dishonest mystery with clues hidden from player, some characters not well written, good puzzles. pretty charming in places, some same old lovable characters and some good new ones. Buy on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of AI Somnium 2 is awesome in the beginning and it's middle section. It does a great job of presenting mysteries to the reader in such a way and pace that makes them intrigued and curious to read further, to see what will happen next and how the author will explain everything. Unfortunately, the entire plot is basically a "house of cards" and its collapses in the endgame, so this time around Uchikoshi wasn't able to deliver great finale like he was able to in the previous AI:Somnium game. It is still one of his better games and its honestly great for like 80-90% of its duration, so it gets a recommendation from me. But if you like a great culmination in the story with a nice finale, it might be better to stay away from this game. Because it is, honestly, doesn't deliver in those aspects (better play the first AI:Somnium game if you haven't already, in that case).

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the limited edition Day 1, played through it, and then collected my thoughts for two months. I love AI1 to pieces, but NIrvana just feels... off. I'm mixed.Everything is polished, there are fun little minigames in the menu, the music is fantastic, voice acting is once again A1. The mystery hooks you well, everything is all over the place and that's an awesome place to start so that you can solve it bit by bit through the routes. The simulation scenes/walking around the crime scenes is a very cool additions and most, if not all of the new characters are great.The characters don't feel like they're the same people from the first game. It may just be the fact that you play in Mizuki's and Ryuki's perspectives, but it is different from before. As many others have already mentioned, the twist is... ehh. It's not really much of a payoff. You can tell that they thought it through really hard for it to work, but it doesn't come out as solving the case and more of a: "oh okay ig." Some might like it, some might not.On the topic of the mystery, without being too specific: It basically doesn't relate to Mizuki or Ryuki except for a few forced-in bits and pieces. Anyone could've solved it, and these two are just running around while the case solves itself. What truly gets to me isn't the twist, or even the personalities of the old characters. It's the fact that so many suspects from the first game show up in this game. AINI was advertised as containing no spoilers for the first game, but idk man. Imagine seeing them here and then going back to play the first game? It isn't hard to figure out.Things I personally liked:Things I personally disliked:Something to note:The routes in this game are more streamlined than the first. There is still somewhat of a butterfly effect, but not as much as in the first game. While I prefer the extreme butterfly effect from the first game, I have no problem with a streamlined story either as long as the mystery is banger. Just thought I'd give a heads-up.If you're coming from the first game, it's up to you. Just understand that it's very different from the first game. If you're new to the series, I highly recommend the first game before this one.

_childDocuments_.review: nirvanA Initiative is the sequel to 2019's AI:The Somnium Files. This review will attempt to assess the game on its gameplay, story, characters and music.The gameplay itself can be classified into two parts. The investigation part, where you have to go around asking people questions and investigate crime scenes with some minor puzzles and QTEs added on top. This part plays most like a typical visual novel with lots of reading. The sominum part, where you enter a suspect’s mind or somnium, and attempt to retrieve some vital information relative to the case in 360 seconds. This is where most of the gameplay lies. As you attempt to solve each sominium, you have to interact with objects in the room with little guidance in order to unlock mental locks. It’s interesting to see a world constructed out of the consciousness of a would-be criminal, and reminds me of ID:invaded, a show with a similar concept. Your interaction with a seemingly random object can alter the world around you to a great extent. Overall, the game focuses heavily on its story and gameplay is its weakest part. If you are not a fan of a book disguised as a game then this one is not for you. The story focuses on the HB killings where people were killed by this mysterious Tearer who chops them in half and leaves the body on display. It’s where this type of game mainly focuses on and sadly is the part where most of my complaints lie. The story starts strong, keeping the player on their toes as to why people are being killed in this way. Sadly it gradually began to fall off, some of the things that kept the players intrigued were just explained in a really underwhelming way. The big reveal to one of the biggest mysteries is just the game presenting the player with false information which in my opinion is somewhat lame for a murder mystery. The characters were never in any real danger, and there’s barely any sense of urgency. This problem is at its peak in one of the character’s routes since he/she literally has super strength.  It still suffers from some of the same problems that the first game has. The most glaring one being its tone. At one point you feel that the Tearer is still out there and the next potential victim could be any of the characters you’ve met, then the next moment, the characters were arguing about erohons. The game constantly fluctuates between a murder mystery and a rom-com, and refuses to stick to one. But I guess going from serious to goofy in a moment's notice is the staple of AI. With that said, the story is not without merit, Tearer’s motives really made the player feel somewhat sympathetic towards him. The characters broke through the fourth wall at times. It is terrifying to see how far someone would go to prove something that’s so deeply ingrained in them with no way of knowing if it’s real or not. The game does leave the player thinking, if we know we live in a simulation like a game character, since everything is fake, would anything we do still matter? Unlike the first game, this time we follow Ryuki and Mizuki. Ryuki being the newly introduced character with a bland personality who acts as a self-insert for the player. The only interesting thing I find about him is his curious mental condition. Mizuki on the other hand is a little more interesting. Players of the first game would be curious to find out how much she has grown. Both characters has to deal with the loss of someone important while trying to solve the murders, sadly the game did not explore that too much. The relationship between the duo protagonists and their AI balls reminds me mostly of the latter half of a buddy cop movie. It would be nice to see how their relationship developed. The only downside is that Tama and Ryuki’s relationship is not as strongly depicted as Date and Aiba’s. Speaking of Date, the perverted detective who turns into super saiyan when presented with an erohon is back. The cast of supporting characters are well rounded and quite likable. The performances the Japanese voice actors give are great. Fans of the first game would see a couple familiar faces.The music is not too memorable. Aside from Kizuna’s song which is heard throughout the entire game. In conclusion, AI:The Somnium Files nirvanA initiative is an enjoyable 50 hour or so experience. If you are a fan of the first game, you are likely to enjoy this one as well. If not, this game requires no previous knowledge and serves as a good entry into the AI franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal! There are so many twists and turns, and there is something revealed towards the end that is mind blowing! This game isn't as dark as the first one, which is a downside in some sense. I found the somniums in this game to overall be better than the first one; they felt more creative from an aesthetic point of view, and some of the mechanics were more interesting. However, some of the somniums were more straight forward than the ones in the first game. Sometimes you would interact with something, and there would just be one option. This might be an improvement for some people though as it reduced guess and check work. That being said, some of the puzzles were really interesting and did take some thinking. Minor spoilers ahead: Instead of interrogations, VR sections are used. While I did really enjoy the VR stuff, I do kind of miss the interrogations. Both serve similar functions though from a gameplay perspective though. However, there are more interactions with the VR sections, which I liked. The cast of characters is amazing! A lot of the characters from the first game are back. Some of them don't play major roles unfortunately, but they still pop up. One really cool thing is that Amame (the mermaid from Sunfish Pocket) gets more screen time than the first game. The new characters in this game are all really cool in their own aspects, and it is neat to see them interact with the old characters we all know and love. Also, the English VA for Gen is SungWon (i.e. ProZD)!!! Spoilers from the first game:One cool thing about this game is that it asks if you completed the first game in order to avoid spoiling it. I said that I did, but there were some things that I think they still censored. One obvious issue is Date not having his proper face, but that is understandable considering they would had to have paid an extra voice actor and redo a bunch of scenes (although the latter portion probably wouldn't be too bad). There are topics that I think would have been relevant too like talking more about the prototype psync machine,  Mizuki's parents, Date and Hitomi, and various other things. Obviously there isn't enough time for all of this, but there were a few scenes where an extra line or two of dialogue would have made logical sense and would have been a nice nod to the first game. Minor bugs/issues I noticed:There were a couple lines characters said that didn't have a voice for some reason (I even checked the log in game). This wasn't a big deal though since the examples I came across were one word lines. Another thing I noticed was that Mizuki's hair was doing some wild things towards the end in one the conversations haha. Other than that, the game ran smoothly. All in all, this game was amazing! The story kept me on the edge of my seat for pretty much the entire ride! I am very interested in checking out Spike Chunsoft's other games too. I really really really hope they make a third game in this series! I Highly recommend checking this out! If you haven't played the first one, definitely do so. While you don't need to, I think it just adds an extra layer of enjoyment if you do. First one is amazing too and you can usually find it on sale for $8 whenever steam does one of their sales.

_childDocuments_.review: An upgrade on all fronts in comparison with the first AI game. The gameplay isn't changed much. But the pacing has been improved by far, and that helped fix the main issue of the prequel: a feeling of disproportion. Now Somniums (they are still the best part of the game) are evenly located throughout the plot, and you don't get tired of point-and-click/investigation parts. An invention – quick VR parts – also bring some new activities and look suitable. Another good thing is the Unlimited Psync option where you can inspect locations with no rush after completing them for the first time. This is, on a whole, a massive improvement.I like that Chunsoft did not try to squeeze as much as possible from the main characters of the first game here. They just placed them in the background where they should be after finishing their stories. The new characters are vivid and fun to watch. Kizzy/Lien and Mame/Gen pairs fit into the story well. Not sure how I feel about Iris becoming a bimbo in a tracksuit though. The new protagonist is okay, and the new AI is a sexy rabbit. Aiba has grown up, and Mizuki did too. They look alright as a second protagonists duo ready to take action, then their evolution is nicely progressing as the story unfolds.The graphics and voice acting are the same (good), music too (mediocre) – but the grand finale dance here rocks! I like the AI skins too, now the player has more purpose to obtain scattered collectibles. THIS IS A NICE SEQUEL!All the issues I have are related to the story. And that be:  It's not like I expect answers, huh

_childDocuments_.review: If it was possible, I would choose a "Mixed" option to better describe my feelings on this game.I don't want to say it was bad though, so I'll still recommend it if only because Uchikoshi's games are one-of-a-kind and this game is no different.The characters are all still well-written and funny as always, fully fleshed out with nice arcs that are interwoven so well with the main story. And the mystery of half-body murders is a fascinating concept that is so entrancing to dig deeper and deeper. Albeit with little gore. I dunno, I feel like seeing corpses with their eyes literally gouged out was far more haunting than bloodless half-corpses lying on clean environments.The Somniums in this game are a BIT better. The Somniums from the first game, ironically, were the weakest part, as they came down to literal trial-and-error, which suits the theme of dreams, but doesn't make good adventure-style gameplay or puzzle-solving. The Somniums in this game were slightly better because they each had their own form of logic that you'd need to follow to solve them, but even then, they still resorted to trial-and-error a lot of the time. I do appreciate however that this game lets you adjust the difficulty of Somniums without punishment, so the time limit wouldn't be an issue if you set it to the lowest difficulty.My biggest problem with this game is like everyone else has been saying - the main plot "twist". I of course won't spoil anything but all I'll say is that instead of reaching an epiphany, all I felt was confusion and it feels like my suspension of disbelief was stretched to the far corners of the moon. Uchikoshi games often bend the rules of storytelling, even dare I say... cheat, in order for their big plot twists to work. But they are at least understandable and even a little clever. This game however pretty much had to lie to you the entire time to get the plot twist to work and it rightly feels cheap and unearned. I dunno if the twist was even necessary in order for the plot to be fully understandable, but I for one was not happy with it.I absolutely loved Date from the first game. His character and voice acting made him such an incredibly charming character despite how depraved he is. And his dynamic with Aiba was always fun. And when I saw the trailer that Mizuki would be the next hero, I was super stoked, I LOVED Mizuki!Disappointingly however, Mizuki isn't playable until 20 hours into the game. Or however long it takes for you to clear Ryuki's "Story Mode". Ryuki being the new character made just for this game. He's not a bad character by any means, and I loved his dynamic with his AI-Ball, Tama, but it was a shame that the pacing of the game made me wanting to play as Mizuki for the majority of Ryuki's story.When I finally got around to playing as Mizuki, my excitement quickly dissipated when we reach the revelation as to why she has superhuman strength and agility. I honestly never questioned why she had such powers in the first game and just accepted it as part of the game's cartoonish, almost dreamlike charm. But this game's explanation for it feels so standard and cliche that it pretty much takes the fun out of her character. Furthermore, she doesn't really have much of a character arc. I suppose with her being as overpowered and successful as she is, there's not much you can do with her as she is a literal Mary-Sue. But Date from the first game had to make sacrifices that made us fully understand his character. Mizuki... makes no such sacrifices and it feels underwhelming.Like I said, I'm very mixed on this game. The characters and humor are all on-point, and I certainly don't regret my time spent with it. In fact, I wouldn't mind playing it again someday.But out of all of Uchikoshi's games - including the Zero Escape Trilogy and the first Somnium Files - this is definitely the weakest entry. If it was possible to numerically score it, I would probably give it a 6/10. _childDocuments_.review: Okay where to start with this one. I loved the first AI game. In fact after playing the sequel I can absolutely recommend that you go play that first game. It's phenomenal! Being a person that never really got in to visual novels, it really gripped me. The plot was confusing at times but once you got through the story branches and unlocked new content, questions were answered and the payoff was satisfying. Characters mattered and were utilized in ways that really made you feel for them and had arcs that stuck with me. The puzzles in the Somniums were fun. Even the frustrating ones at least had funny outcomes and felt rewarding when you finally got through.So with that, I say definitely buy the first AI: The Somnium Files game. It's 100% worth the play.And don't even worry about playing this one. Because you won't find near as much of that here.Yes you can argue that my expectations were pretty high for this one. However I wasn't expecting them to come out so far below that they didn't even meet the originals standard. The best part of the first game was seeing how the strange plot all came together at the end. This game's plot twist and story climax feels so hollow, ending up with a couple of characters that you've made almost zero attachment to throughout the game that even during the 'epic' conclusion I didn't really care. By the end of the game I was told the same plot that I (and in game characters) figured out many chapters ago, over and over again. With the only answer being: insert character here because we need to wrap this up. You still don't get all the answers to some big questions in the game. Which the first game still answers more, if not most, of the important questions by the end of it. Somniums in the first game almost always had something unique to them. Like I said previously even making the wrong decisions still gave you something. Aside from a couple of standout Somniums it's mostly hand holding to the extreme. Selection 1 not it (nothing happens), Selection 2 not it (nothing happen), and here, now pick Selection 3, that's the right answer and now you get to see something happen, maybe. There were I'd say at least 3-4 Somniums that were at least interesting in this game, I'll give them that. However there are numerous Somniums that just feel like you're on rails and you get absolutely nothing out of them. The ones you do get something out of are on branching paths that also don't add to or connect the story like the first game does so well. Other than to get some keyword to a password puzzle to advance the main plot on a separate branch. At least the first game's branches connected in someway. These feel more like dead ends with an answer to use later. Even when they explain how the 'flow chart' comes together, it just comes off as a waste of time and lazy.The music is amazing! As always the tracks in this game slap. I have to bring some positives here. At least I could enjoy the music in this game just like the last one. One Somnium in particular with a 'thief' has one of the best tracks, in my opinion, of both games. I actually still listen to this.The concepts and new characters are very interesting and it's a shame they are totally under utilized. Ryuki and Tama are a great new addition. Some may find cringe (esp Ryuki's constant Half-Might/My Hero impersonation), but I rather enjoyed. Which makes me upset that most of their time is spent on the majority of the on rails Somniums. Without spoils Lien, Kizzy, and Gen are some of the best characters. However Komeji (Minecraft Steve man), Shoma, and Amame are less than interesting and it sucks because they become more integral to the plot later and I could have cared less. Some people could think the opposite and that's okay, however I just wish the game had focused on other characters instead.Mild spoiler: Date is barely used in this game. Mizuki is brought front and center along with the new character Ryuki and if the main plot wasn't so mediocre I would have enjoyed it more. In fact the new situations involving old characters were great even if for some are brief. Some slight twists and lore progressions from characters in first game are interesting but don't quite hit the mark.All in all I played this game to completion hoping for a satisfying end. The first half of the game is a slog to get through with less than interesting Somniums. The beginning of the second half really picks up. Filled with some of the best Somniums and really got me hoping some of the answers I would receive would propel me to a satisfying ending. But then you start to realize what's going on and then the rest of the game takes a giant nose dive in quality for me. I saw the potential and greatness this game could have been. Maybe that was due to the new director for the game? I'm not sure. Instead of feeling great by the end of the game I was honestly just ready for it to end. I critic this so sternly because I love the first game so much. It doesn't live up to the first game, however I'd love to see them actually take time to make something that can at least meet or exceed the first. Which is why I basically say, if you haven't played the first game. Please go play that. Here's hoping if a third game is made, it's much better than this.In the end AI: The Somnium Files - nirvanA Initiative, for me, get's a 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know, maybe I have just changed and become a lot less tolerant for nonsense, but in so many ways I was unhappy with the experience of playing through this game.
