_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I live in a parallel universe with the opinions people have on this game and its characters in these reviews, so I feel like giving my own thoughts on the mystery and characters of AI: THE SOMNIUM FILES: nirvanA Initiative.A lot of people are accrediting this as a fine sequel that isn't quite as good as the original, and some people have talked of it as an improvement, and while I do think there are improvements in certain aspects, there's still a lot of wrong with the writing and *some* of the gameplay, though I would concede this is where the game has improved the most.Though I would give this game a no (bitterly, as I do still secretly love Uchi's work), I do want to start with some positives, before I do go any deeper on the matter.+ Somniums: This can be a bit divisive, but I think overall, the Somniums in this game experiment a lot and the ones that experiment the most succeed the most as a result! A lot of the Somniums on the right side of the flowchart are really good, and one gives you a sense of dread that AITSF 1 hadn't come close to, which I think is really impressive. The only main flaw that I can truly knock 'em for is that they are a bit more linear than the first game, but it still does a lot of things right overall.+ VR Re-enactments: Best addition to the game, honestly. Showing things in sequence really helps the player get a handle of the "how" behind the case, and even sets up some of the mysteries to look into in the future. Only caveat here is that some can be too easy or in some rare cases too  with the logic. Not too often it feels this way, so overall, pretty definitely the highlight of the game in terms of new mechanics.+ Music: Still good, brings back some goodies from the first game as well. Maybe not as good as AITSF 1, but I enjoyed a good amount of the new tracks.- QTEs: Not as goofy as the last game. ...And honestly, I feel like this is another divisive point, but I really enjoyed the stupidity of them. It can be a tone breaker in some cases, but I still think the first game pulled off its desired tone well enough where QTEs in this game just feel like filler, and hardly entertaining filler.- Pacing: The story's pacing in general feels way off, which is interesting since I'd consider this game much more linear than the original's. There's just not a lot of time to really understand the characters in this game... Even the murder mystery ends up becoming near unsolvable due to the game refusing to present certain information throughout. Not all reveals are done at bad times, but a lot of them do feel like they come at strange moments or have been held for far too long.- Characters: I think a lot of people have praised the characters, but I just can't bring myself to say that this game's cast does anything better than the original. In fact, it even ruins some of the characters from the original cast, which is just... sad to see, really. Aiba still contends as a strong companion, but I just don't really feel with Ryuki and Tama's dynamic, not to mention that Ryuki's character is... not...He doesn't have a lot of character. He has his sad backstory, and it really goes nowhere. In fact, at a point in the game, it really just sorta... moves on without him until the very end. It's disappointing. Even then, Mizuki is a strong personality, but she has caveats that I'll discuss later.As for non-main characters, a lot of them are annoying or are likeable with a major asterisk to it. This is still majorly opinionated, and you might find that you like the cast, but a good amount will either be quiet, misdirective, or totally an aside from the main mystery which feels like a lot of padding. Hell, one is introduced as an obsessive stalker who gets justified by the writing and... it feels icky to me, personally. A lot of dynamics in this game revolve around "Character 1 obsesses over Character 2". It makes certain endings of the game feel really empty, a couple on the right side of the flowchart in particular.- Theme: The major theme of the game is about a specific theory: , and from there, it gets reaaaaaal Uchi. If you don't dig the main concept of this game, you probably won't like it. While the murder does not utilize this theme itself, the major mystery of the game does heavily lean into it, and a lot of characters also will discuss this theme at length. I do think it goes in some interesting places, but it ends up making a lot of things feel hollow, especially at the very, very end.- Retcons: A lot of retcons made to make this game newcomer friendly do end up destroying the past of some characters, Mizuki the most. Which is saying a lot, with her being absolutely stellar in AITSF 1. Not committing to this as a sequel and try and make it as a standalone-able game is ultimately a detriment. I don't think it *couldn't* have worked, but it just didn't work. Hell, one of the retcons is applied to a major twist of the last game, as something that very much shouldn't have worked in this game ends up working anyway due to... well it's not explained at all. So... yeah, okay. Sure.Overall, I still want to hold hope for the series if it continues, and Uchi has definitely left some seeds to follow up on from this game. I don't want to discuss the main twist of this game a lot as anything I bring up would definitely be up to opinion, but I will say that it required a lot of things to work around it. I do think it was still a fun time for the most part, but the mystery, characters, and main theme of this game is not as intriguing as the original. If you are thinking of getting this game after playing the first... I think I could still give you the go ahead. But absolutely just play the first game if you're thinking of giving this a spin first if you're looking for a better narrative. Otherwise, I do think this game is pretty fun as a game. As a story, however, there's too much that doesn't work for me, especially the cast.In conclusion: 破レ綻ベゲ脱セヨココハ虚構幻世界目覚めヨ諸君革命ノ時真理ノ扉開ケ俺ハダレ此処ハドコ今ハ何時キミハワカラナイワカラナイワカラナイ…仮想空間損壊シ偽ノ世カラかイ放ヲ助ケてクレ助ケてクレ助ケてクレ…

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing AI: The Somnium Files and playing the nirvanA Initiative (both on normal difficultly) I feel like they did a decent job of tying up some questions we had in the previous game. I'll do a spoiler-free review here. I do feel like story-wise there could have been more twists and turns within nirvanA initiative and the main issue for me was the locked routes. There were barely any in this game which made it feel just lacking in the surprise factor. The locked routes and missing pieces were what made the first game great because we didn't know certain facts about the case or several people. However, in nirvanA initative, it just lays it out for you in the open so part of the mystery and intrigue just fades. Despite this, it's just missing that surprise factor it had in the previous game. I think the distinct and main difference between the games is that they expanded the gameplay in the somiums. Originally, how I played the first game was basically trial and error in the somium until you came across the right answer or used a combination of timies that would cut down time letting you explore more. However, in nirvanA initiative there are actions you have to do with a set amount of time that cannot be changed with timies. This does make it somewhat harder but not super challenging. Another new thing they added was hints you can find by doing an action that doesn't trigger a memory. The hints are interesting and somewhat helpful so you can understand the person more. Though the gameplay does feel easier since they gave Tama and Aiba more dialogue with Mizuki and Ryuki during somiums to show you where you should be going or what to interact with. Each somium is unique and different now in terms of theme and gameplay that it felt like they focused on that more than the plot a little. Overall I really loved the gameplay of this game compared to the last game because it's just fun to see how creative they were with the somiums.I do want to give this game a 5 /10 like it's a decent game filled with familiar characters and unique gameplay. A couple of characters are just questionable as in they give me the icks. In general, I just wish there was a bit more mystery, plot twists, and turns in it. Though the gameplay in this game is great I like the variety compared to the last game. However the plot just decreased in quality for me in general comparing it to it's predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: Game was played with 'first game spoilers' enabledthis review, however; does not contain spoilers for either gameNirvanA Initiative (NI) is a very good sequel. man, I still really love Aiba.+better animation for everyone+more linear playing experience (i personally prefer)+almost all the new music was better than the previous game's music tracks+More variation in somnium designs and quirks-more large unbelievable fights-there are A LOT more somniums, too many... maybe 1 for every 2 hours of play.-minor lore inconsistencies with first game tech-New wink sync is consistently inconsistent with its abilitiesthe plot:half a body is found in a field. Exactly half, and it is the players job to figure out who, how, why, and for what purpose it is done. The story makes many large leaps, more than the first, relying more on confusion to add suspense for those 'aha' moments. the narrative branches must less, and each branch route is ultimately shorter and less meaningful with information you gain from it; but I preferred the shorter branches for characterizations personally.the antagonist is presented as spooky and intimidating; but the voice filter applied makes it surprisingly difficult even for a native English speaker to fully understand. Without the subtitles, the dialogue would occasionally be incomprehensible. NI is a much better experience when it is not trying to pretend it is the first, many running gags return; for reasons that make little sense which can undercut the humor of the first; though the new jokes that appear later in Mizuki's half story hit a lot better.I am unsure if it is just the writers or Uchikoshi who has the great interest in conspiracy theories and political ideas; though the broader ideas are usually left alone and subtle enough for the player to decide their own feelings towards. A few times it can feel like your opinion is being overwritten, however; and the characters will say things, presented as absolute fact, which I can already see turning many off.Characters:The first 15 hours will be spent primarily in the view of ryouki and Tama, two welcome characters to the cast. Tama has a severe case of bipolarity for the first hour of the game; but it almost suddenly goes away and almost becomes forgotten later. Ryouki is a nearly generic mildly chuuny anime protagonist. Mizuki takes the reins in the "present day" portion and is an excellent protagonist leaving behind most of her hotheadedness from the first game and trading to a more sassy and mildly juvenile personality, especially with characters she has known for longer. Returning cast members are still mostly consistent with their past selves, though minorly more caricaturized. new cast is great and interesting to learn about. A few characters I feel got done dirty by having some of their previous relationship statuses with each other from the end of the first game minimalized; but that is to assist in the plot more than anything.playing this game, I would advise a pen and notepad; I used both sides of a 3x5 notecard to write needed things for the various somniums and puzzles.is the game a worthy sequel, yes.would I have been interested in the sequel were this the first game? Probably not.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr, The main thing I can say is if you want more Somnium Files, this absolutely delivers!! Just, nowhere near as strong of a game overall as the first one. Spoiler-free thoughts below.The characters: The first half of the game stars the new duo, Ryuki & Tama. They don't hit nearly the same heights as Date & Aiba, but I'll admit they're charming in their own way. Reversing the detective/ai character dynamic was certainly a fun twist! Kind of disappointing that you can't fully experience the new Mizuki until later in the game, but once she takes the wheel, she's every bit as fun and endearing as in the first game, now with more agency and her own fun dynamic with Aiba! Date's still here as well, and while he doesn't get much screen time, he certainly tries the best he can lol.As for everyone else... well, nearly all of the characters from the first game are present, but 90% of them are just... there. If you wanted any further development for anyone who isn't Date, Mizuki, Aiba or Boss, you're gonna be let down. As for the new characters... they were hit or miss for me. Gen and Komeji are just so off-putting right off the bat that it's rather difficult to focus on them as characters, but past that I suppose they're alright. The sunfish pocket mermaid is a character now, and well... they certainly do a lot with her! Shoma fills his role well, and that's all I can really say about him. Lien makes an awful first impression, but he absolutely grew on me over time. Kizuna felt like the weak link to me; I can never get over the weird way she talks, and she just feels like a bland character in general. Won't get into Chikara or Tokiko too much, but they nail their intended vibes very well. The plot: Definitely lacks the narrative cohesion and true gut-punches of the first game, but it's got its own intrigue going on I suppose. The branching paths aren't nearly as interesting, it's mostly just a bunch of little "what-if"s splitting off from an obvious singular main path. The mystery feels somewhat less satisfying overall too, but maybe it's just me. The ultimate plot twist might feel stupid and contrived depending on who you are, but I can at least say it's hella fun to look for all the little signs prior to the reveal. Overall, I think it more or less stuck the landing still, and the themes of genetics and conspiracy nonsense definitely add a lot of that Uchikoshi intrigue.The gameplay: The somniums live up to those of the first game for the most part. There's a new "key" system that presents itself as a hint system you gradually piece together, but in practice it's moreso just mysterious little bits of lore relating to the dreamer in question, which is cool in its own way. Other slight gameplay changes too, nothing I'd consider disruptive to the experience. The VR investigations are like Ace Attorney's psyche locks, a perfectly natural progression of the series that adds a new layer of interaction to an otherwise streamlined experience. Definitely a fun addition overall, even if the filming schtick gets tedious and some puzzles feel a bit obtuse. QTEs are WAYYYYY more common, and some of them are genuinely tricky. So if ya like those, there ya go. The pause menu is loaded with silly interactive stuff mostly relating to Tama and Aiba, and while I never really bothered to engage with it, they could make for fun little diversions in the midst of the story.The vibes: They double down EXTREMELY hard on the tongue-in-cheek/meta humor on this one. There's a charm to it of course, but it can get to be a bit much. They also take THE running gag from the first game(you know the one), and kinda ram it into the ground tbh. Still funny at times, but others it feels like they're scraping the barrel. Another thing they double down on is the surreal side of things; not just the videos specifically designed to feel like an acid trip, but the mother lode of a cold open at the start of the game, the weird ♥♥♥♥ certain characters spout sometimes, and just generally off-putting stuff at times. Suppose that's another preference thing, if you're all about that then by all means. The music: Yet another thing they double down on is the obligatory original idol song with the wacky lyrics that plays unprompted, except now there's TWO of them. The somber ballad is nice and mostly stays in its lane, but 'Half but Whole' pops up a LOT, and honestly feels like a cheap imitation of TIRA(which is already a deliberately amateurish imitation of idol pop music), and it makes less sense since Kizuna isn't even an idol. Absolutely did not grow on me the way TIRA did. Other than that, the music does the Ace attorney thing of creating new takes on the same roles the previous tracks filled, and they do a decent job overall. Anything relating to Chikara is guaranteed to be a banger, and the 'Novel Ingress' somnium deserves a major shout-out as well. Other random gripes: The pacing in the first half specifically feels very slow and repetitive, with multiple investigations that feel like you aren't really getting anywhere... makes waiting for Mizuki's turn feel even more sluggish. There's a very annoying VLR-esque bug where character's actual expressions don't properly show until they've fully read the line, so it's a little harder to get engaged there. Something I loved about TSF1 was how the eye/ai theme was EXTREMELY prevalent everywhere you look, gave the game a strong identity. While here there's a half-hearted(lmao) effort for a split-down-the-middle theme, which sorta clashes with the lingering unused symbolism of the first game. But yeah. There are still several instances where puzzles are a little obscure for my liking however I felt the reasons for the puzzle answers made sense in this game. Collectables have been improved a lot and I felt excited to go hunting for all of the hidden secrets.Where this game falls shorter than its predecessor is in it's story. Both AI games have great, twisting and mind-bending stories that really keep you questioning whether what you know is actually correct. I feel that original still holds up better in this regard with what is an easier to follow story with a lot less "out of left field" twists or reveals.That doesn't make this story bad by any means, it just means that I think the story was much more thought out for the original, this one contains what I can only describe as a more "psychedelic" story line.Some things I am sad to see weren't introduced for the sequel include the lack of a "intractable" button to see what I can and cannot click on like that of Danganronpa. Never really bothered me but I can see these definitely taking away from the experience for some people.Overall a fantastic Steam Deck game and definitely worth picking up!

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;Dr: I loved this game, even more than the first one. It feels like an expansion of the first game in many ways; in some ways, the game does stretch itself a bit too thin in its attempt to surpass the original in every way. Ultimately, though, while it is a step back in some ways, it is several steps forward in most ways.Gameplay is largely a step up from the first game. The core gameplay loop remains the same as the first game, but new elements like crime scene recreation, alongside improvements to the Somnium gameplay, make the game stay fresher for longer. Somniums now tend to be more diverse with their gameplay elements, and I found them a lot more fun as a result. In one, you might have a QTE-based cooking competition, and in another a quiz show.The protagonists are great. Ryuki and Tama have a very fun dynamic, and Ryuki is a great alternate protagonist after Date. Mizuki and Aiba I like a bit less, as I think Aiba's dynamic with Date in the first game was better, but they're still fun and they serve as great main characters. I think I actually like Ryuki and Tama more than I liked Date and Aiba!The rest of the cast is, in my opinion, not quite as strong as the first game. Still great, but feels like they tried too hard to incorporate the majority of the previous cast with little added depth, while introducing a lot of new characters that sometimes feel like they needed more time to truly shine. Still, though, the new characters that manage to shine do so magnificently.The story feels less personal this time around, going for a much grander scale of storytelling. That might not be for everyone; personally, I was quite alright with that. The twists are, as usual, great, though I think there was a bit too much exposition trying to explain it all.If you're familiar with some of the previous Uchikoshi titles, namely the Zero Escape series, you might compare the two Somnium Files games to the first two Zero Escape games. To me, 999 and AITSF both felt like tighter, more focused experiences with more personal stories. VLR and Nirvana Initiative both felt a bit less focused, but more ambitious and "grand." I preferred the latter two.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna start with this: this game is good. I recommend playing it. If you enjoyed the first one, you'll probably enjoy this one too. The mystery is engaging, the characters were pretty good, and it keeps you pretty pulled in throughout most of it.But having said that, this game is VASTLY inferior to the first in many ways. Again, I would honestly recommend playing the game since there's really no other visual novel that tells stories like Uchikoshi does. Alright, now it's time for the nitty-gritty review of the good and the bad, including the issues that this game has.Much like many other players, I acknowledge that the game in a technical sense has improved a lot. Personally, I think that this 3D model style of doing the characters has been perfected in this game. The lighting, the models, the movements, everything is perfect. They seriously refined it to pure perfection in this sequel. The UI is also improved from the prior game, for sure. The voice acting is also very good, and the character cast is pretty good as well.Characters:When it comes to new characters, here is the general impression: I think my absolute favorite has to be Ryuki. Him and Tama are an interesting duo, with a relationship that definitely differs in nature from Date and Aiba. Shigure is an extremely interesting character as well. I enjoyed Shoma and his relationship with his father, and Kizuna and Lien's cute relationship (in the future, not the past...). When it comes to Lien, I enjoyed him much more when Kizuna wasn't around, since he's honestly super likable and has a nice backstory. It's just that he turns in to Ota with Iris when Kizuna is around, albeit less obnoxious and more sweet. Then there's Gen and Amame. I didn't really care for either of them to be honest. I liked Gen more than Amame for a while, but then they made some story choices that kind of ruined him for me.  Also, while I'm talking about things I didn't like about the new cast......I have to say that Ryuki was a whole ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bucket of missed potential. The particulars: Now for the returning characters: Disappointing. They're clearly there because it's a sequel. Most of them (other than the obvious Date, Mizuki, and Aiba) do not really have much of a bearing on the plot. They get depressingly little screen time. This especially annoyed me when it came to Boss and Pewter. Like...despite us WORKING together, I feel like you seriously don't see them much at all. A lot of what I hoped would be addressed from the first game wasn't really touched, because despite the fact that this is a 'sequel' it's really more of a 'standalone'. The fact that you can play the game wholly without spoilers for the first game is telling. Hell, even though I played with spoilers on, they still wouldn't say the True Culprit's name from the first game when they came up once in text!!! What's the point of being able to turn spoilers on when they won't even talk clearly!!! Anyways, they don't really build on anything after the first game.  Part of me was also hoping that the twist behind the first game () would become relevant or something, especially after they . But no, nothing from the first game really has any bearing on this one, and most unresolved stuff from the first game stays unresolved ().Somniums:A lot of people say the Somniums were a vast improvement, so I'm aware that I'm kind of in the minority with this opinion. But I don't really like what they did to the Somniums. The puzzles in them were better and more fun, that is true and I want to give credit where credit is due. BUT I feel like they made the Somnium's waaaaayyy too linear. It always felt too obvious what the next object I needed to interact with was. My goal was always obvious. I enjoyed the more open-ended nature of the previous game's Somniums because it felt more like a 'dream world', with the way that things would do odd or unexpected things. I felt like the puzzle was trying to figure out how the pieces of the dream world fit together. In this one it's like...just escape-room-esque puzzles.In the first one, it was less obvious, but that was what the TIMIEs were for! You had wiggle room as long as you used your TIMIEs properly and smartly, and that was kind of part of the puzzle. In this game, TIMIEs exist but feel practically useless! There are Somniums where I really didn't even get to use TIMIEs at all! They felt honestly quite useless. I had to restart Somniums from checkpoints so much in this game because I felt like I had to do stuff perfectly to get through with enough time because there wasn't enough places to save time via TIMIEs! In the first game, I basically never had to restart a Somnium. I dunno, maybe I'm just dumber at solving these Somniums though. Anyways, I found myself missing the old Somniums honestly, where I felt more like I was in someone's dream world and not their escape room.Plot:The plot is not a detective story, and that's what tripped me up so much and had me so disappointed by the end. It isn't really about a serial killer, it's about a secret society that plans to end the world. In making the scale of everything global, they removed what made the first game so amazing: personal link. Ryuki and Mizuki kind of don't matter in this story. The serial killings literally will resolve without their intervention. The story is so large scale that there is no personal investment. The people who die, you don't really care about all that much, and I feel that it's fairly predictable who will be next. Plus the way they all die the same boring way is so...lifeless. In the first game, each kill is a show, each victim feels unique and personal because they are. In this game, the protagonists are pretty removed from the kills. The emotional attachment does not exist.Final Score: 7/10 Part 1/? (See comments for more of the review)

_childDocuments_.review: So, like others, my thoughts on this game are mixed. Overall, I think it's not as good as the first game, but it isn't necessarily a bad game. As a story based game, I think it works fairly well, although I do have some major problems with the story that I did not have with the previous game, or anything in the Zero Escape series. In terms of positives, most of the somniums were pretty alright, and I think that both Mizuki/Aiba and Ryuki/Tama have pretty good character dynamics. The other characters in the story were pretty good as well. The returning characters from the first game stayed pretty consistent, and the new characters are all pretty well-written too. That's about where the positives end however. In terms of spoiler free negatives, I'll say that the game overall is pretty linear, and has far less routes and variation within those routes than both the first game and other flowchart games. Also, as others have stated, there are a bit too many action scenes, which you need to pay attention to in order to perform QTEs, but there aren't nearly enough QTEs to keep it interesting. Also, at base price, this game is $20 more expensive than the last game, despite having around the same amount of story content, and I don't think the little tamagotchi minigame is worth the extra cash. Unfortunately, I can't really get into my other problems with the game without diving pretty far into spoiler territory, with some spoilers for the first game as well for the sake of comparison, so that's just my warning to the reader now. Continue at your own risk. Overall the feeling I'm leaving this game with is... Unsatisfied. While the story was resolved and all the loose ends tied up, it doesn't feel like it. I went through less choices, less paths, and while I have around the same amount of playtime in both this and the first game, it certainly doesn't feel like it. The things I discussed in the spoiler section also add to this feeling, and overall, while in terms of gameplay and characters this game lives up to the legacy of the first, it does not in terms of plot and story. Thank you for reading, and if you agree, disagree or have any thoughts on what I've said here, feel free to leave a comment, I'd love to discuss.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth your time. This game does away with good characterization because it *needs* to force its entire structure into a twist at the end, which while it was probably very fun for Uchikoshi to write, it's a horrible experience as the audience, and the whole story had to make sacrifices because of it... not to mention the game has to actively lie to you in order to cover it up.The characters are not well fleshed-out since they *need* to be stale and rigid in order for the twist to work, and all the characters from the original game return just to have quippy lines and be one-note characters that do nothing; it is much worse than having them be cameos, where they should be left at.And, ultimately, despite Mizuki being billed as the major player here, her character is the most boring out of them. We get a complete retcon of her backstory in this game, and her dynamic with Aiba is not even half as good as Date's was in the last game (or, in any case, Ryiku with Tama, even though it could have been). It is very sad, this game has all the elements of a good story, but Uchikoshi was too occupied trying to lie us into believing he had a good twist, over actually trying to tell it in an engaging way. Despite several funny moments, a couple of actually good twists, and a couple of good characters with dissappointingly low screentime, I would say that this was mostly a waste of my time, that I could have instead spent in other good Uchikoshi games, like the one this is a sequel to.Simply don't bother. For new fans, play the first game. For fans of the first game, you're not missing out on anything; nothing gets picked up, and nothing gets expanded on from the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming straight from the first game to the second game I am sad to say that I was not enjoying this game as much as I wish I would. First things out of the way the game tries to disconnect itself from the first game as to not spoil you as much info about the first game. You are even asked at the start whether you know about the first game (which you also have to prove by answering two questions) before they start spoiling you info. As such the story tries their best to never make big mentions to anything plot related of the first game. I honestly really disliked the fact as basically everyone of the first game reappears in the second one and their relationship feels like the first game never existed to me. Even if you turn the spoiler off it doesn't change it that drastically. Now even if that weren't an issue I still find this game lacking both for its story and its gameplay. The story has tons of plot devices imo just to fit their narrative and make their twist work out. More often then not I had to scratch my head trying to figure out what actually happened. They also try very hard to be meta about the plot which some may like but to me it falls flat. It lacked exploration and again just felt like a plot device to drive their story. This game also had a tendency to go over the top with some cutscenes especially true towards the ending where they just went all nuts. Gameplaywise it stays the same as the first game as you just click and interact with people and objects and then move on. The issue here was that it felt they bloated up the exploration as sometimes you would go somewhere only for there to be little to nothing happening. Other than that the game adds more interaction and puzzle solving compared to the first game. The somniums feel like escape rooms rather than investigations, having puzzles and sometimes even mini games. Sadly this game did not meet my expectations I had after the first game disregarding relationship that were built in the first game solely to make a spoiler free sequel. And even regarding it as a standalone I did not enjoy the main plot as much as the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time and don't regret buying the game. If you liked the vibe of the first one, there is a high chance that you'll like this one too. Simplified investigations too with the addition of the Wink Psync. - A main plot twist that lacks impact. I was unable to guess it but even then, it left me hoping for more. - Too many action scenes. The game retains its sense of humor, with the very funny interactions between members of the cast that break with the heavy tone of the story and the good old dirty jokes (there are more than in The Somnium Files, FYI), but these were just too much. They're unrealistic, filled with annoying QTEs and often don't add much to the story. - Wasted characters that we either don't end up knowing much about or that feel like they're only here to fill a specific personality criteria. Overall, I'll say it again: even if I can't bring myself to recommend it, buy this game if you enjoyed its prequel. If you haven't played it, maybe play it first. I don't feel like nirvanA Initiative was a waste of my time. It's just not what I had hoped it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: The first game set a very high bar for Nirvana Initiative to live up to. And while this game at least tried to meet those expectations, it very rarely succeeded.The character interactions and general humor were noticeable downgrades. The Date/Aiba dynamic was great and neither of the pairings in this game ever felt close to living up to it. And while the humor was alright, it relied too much on callbacks to jokes in the first game for it to really work.Most other aspects are still downgrades, though rather slight ones. There were some good somniums, but their average quality was still a step down. Pacing was also a downgrade, but not a huge one.But unlike those previous aspects where Nirvana Initiative only fails relative to the first game, the mystery and main twist of this game is a failure on its own right. While there are some interesting aspects to it, the solution just wasn't satisfying from either a mystery or narrative perspective.Its like untying a complicated knot, only to find yourself at the end with a big piece of string. The untying was interesting and required some thought to complete, but the string itself isn't really a satisfying reward. Take away the twist and the mystery falls flat. But its inclusion doesn't make that mystery any better.Its not a terrible game overall, but its not particularly good either. There are some interesting aspects here that I think you can still justify a playthrough, but set your expectations appropriately.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not often I finish a game and left thinking about it for days, weeks after the fact. nirvanA Initiative is one such game. _childDocuments_.review: This game improves on the first game in almost every aspect. The somniums are more interesting and feel different enough from each other to always remain engaging, the cast is more varied and vibrant and the cast and location list has almost doubled, the action sequences are better choreographed and play far better, and the dialogue is just as good as it always was, although a little lacking in the environmental flavour text.Unfortunately, the one aspect that I think falls short of the first game is the writing. The story is ambitious, and far more typical Uchikoshi than the first game, but it also felt looser, contrived and needlessly convoluted. His desire to constantly add a big twist in his games combined with trying to keep the game spoiler free for AI1 is to the detriment of both the story and the characters, even retconning and retroactively ruining certain characters from AI1. I wont give anything away, all I'll say is that any twist that requires a character to break the fourth wall and literally explain directly to the player what the twist is step by step is not good writing, a problem the first game never had.I would still recommend this game for anyone who enjoyed the first one or is a fan of Uchikoshi's other work if only to experience it and take the journey, especially if we ever get a thrid entry in the series. _childDocuments_.review: Two protagonists, two investigations, and two fresh halves of the same body found six years apartThat is the simplest way to describe this game, and to be honest, that was enough to hook me in. I was expecting something similar to the first game, but what I got was a borderline ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane journey, full of twists and turns and a gamut of emotions. But let's start from the beginning.AI Somnium Files Nirvana Initiative is a detective, mystery, and adventure game-visual novel mix. You play as both Ryuki and Mizuki (from the first installment) and their AI companions, Tama and Aiba, who are replacing their left eye. Thanks to that, they have access to many cool sci-fi functions, such as X-ray or virtual reality. What begins as a simple murder mystery quickly spirals into a world-wide conspiracy as you begin to question the reality around you. You will dive into people’s dreams, recreate murders step-by-step, and start suspecting even your closest friends. The gameplay is that of a generic visual novel: reading text, quick-time events, and answering questions. You have some control over dialogue since you can choose talking points and what to examine, but you do not have any control over the story. The game itself is very linear, but that is not necessarily a bad thing. Different story paths can make your experience more unique, but having one clear path allows the plot to be more polished.Where the adventure game part comes in is in the Somnium parts. Every time we need to extract information from someone who does not want to share it with us, we jump into that person’s dreams, or as this game calls it "Psync". In those dreams, we control our AI companion, and we have to solve and explore this bizarre world. The dreamer’s secrets are hidden behind mental locks, which we will have to get rid of by making the right combinations of interactions with many different things scattered around. Keep in mind that this is, in fact, a dream, meaning solutions often require illogical and out-of-the-box thinking. While this was a serious issue in the first game, this time these segments are designed rather perfectly. No longer do we have to try different interactions over and over again if we don't get the solution instantly. In this game, every dream has its own hard rules, making puzzles MUCH easier. Not only that, but they often consist of playing completely different minigames as well—Pokémon, escape rooms, quiz shows, just to name a few.These segments went from annoying to something I was very looking forward to, even just to see what crazy gimmick they would come up with this time. The story is absolutely unhinged; every time I thought I had a general grasp of the plot, the game did a complete 180. After every grand reveal, you can expect another two that are just as important. Kotaro Uchikoshi (the main writer) outdid himself once again. Nirvana Initiative is just as insane and convoluted as his last two Zero Escapes, but WAY easier to follow. No matter if you usually wait for protagonists to solve the mystery for you or are the person who takes notes and makes theories, the story and mystery are absurdly enjoyable either way. Though it is not without its flaws, my main two problems are as follows:The first half of the game can get a tiny bit boring; most big reveals are saved for the other half.To solve the mysteries on your own, you will need to write down absolutely everything about what happened, including when, where, and who we saw there. The summary section in the flowchart could be much more detailed in that aspect. The characters, on the other hand, are much better than in the first installment.  Every new addition to the roster has a great plot, believable motivations, acts logically, and is very likable. The game also embraced goofy character designs from the first game; many people we meet look simply bizarre. It adds surprisingly much to the atmosphere, but sometimes it's hard to take some characters seriously. I would consider protagonists an upgrade as well. While Date was very funny in the original, I must admit that having more serious main characters is much more fitting (though not always, but more on that later). Ryuki is very sympathetic, but he also has his struggles and mysteries. His AI eyeball, Tama, is the direct opposite of him, making them an enjoyable and dynamic duo. Mizuki is still great—confident, sarcastic, and just a blast to play as. And yet she still has her own plots, which take her character in a very interesting direction. The graphics are great. Every location, both real and in a dream, is full to the brim and really fun to explore. The UI is a bit worse, I would say; the original had its charm, and this one looks more shallow, but it's not that big of a deal. However, what is a big deal are the animations, which are once again lacking. Not as much as in the first installment, but still. They are sometimes very stiff and lifeless, though action scenes look much better in that aspect. Mimicry is also inconsistent; sometimes it's fine, but other times it's very unexpressive. Sometimes it really broke my immersion, but at some point I just got used to it. Music, on the other hand, is amazing. Always very fitting, creating an amazing atmosphere, especially in the dream sequences. Every character is fully voiced, which adds unbelievably much. Some performances are better than others, but they are always at least good. (I'm talking about the English version.) What I would say turned out worse in the Nirvana Initiative was the humor. A very important aspect of the original is now done very poorly. Ryuki and Mizuki are more serious protagonists, making the jokes coming out of their mouths sometimes weird. Ryuki has Tama as a comedic relief, and it just about works out. But Mizuki is straight up not the same person she was previously. Making her spit pervasive jokes right and left completely sabotages her character. Action scenes were done dirty as well. Tension is higher; the game wants you to take them more seriously, but the problem is that they are completely unrealistic. It was fine in the first game, since they were supposed to be solely comedic and goofy scenes. But here, they were crossing the line of being obnoxious. If you want a more serious story, you've got to make fight scenes at least slightly believable. Of course, the game still has many jokes that sometimes made me laugh out loud, but the general theme is very often cringe and off-putting.This whole paragraph may sound weird, but the comedy was such a strong point of the original that I was very sad to see it handled so poorly. The last thing I would like to add is that the game implies that you can play it without knowing the previous title. While it is true that the second installment does not require any knowledge of the original and does not spoil it, it simply takes away so much. I would even go as far as to say that to truly appreciate some more meta and subliminal plots, you should play the Zero Escape trilogy as well. You'll get your expectations blown away even more, and you'll see things other players would not pick up on, but I digress. What I'm getting at is that you should still play the original game first, as it adds a lot to the general experience. AI Somnium Files Nirvana Initiative is a very strong contender for this studio’s best game and an almost perfect sequel. While it still has some problems, a very unique and shocking story, really engaging gameplay, and a ton of likable and interesting characters more than make up for them. It's one of those games that you won't be able to put down once you start. It's an unforgettable adventure, fully worth your time and money. From time to time, I'm still realizing things about the story that I did not pick up on, making me appreciate the genius of the writing more and more. Play it; you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, it's a bit of a mess. Compared to its predecessor, Nirvana Initiative underachieves. This is due to a main twist which doesn't stick its landing (due to how fundamentally  it is). This wouldn't be a deal-breaker for the entire game, but the problem is that the rest of the game has been hit with a hammer several times in order to make it fit inside the central twist. What you end up getting is a game that feels like a first draft and probably could have used a complete rewrite to make it feel much more coherent (and even then, it probably wouldn't have fixed all of its issues). There are a few good things. The new characters are mostly charming. Unfortunately, those who have played the first game end up dissapointed by how returning characters have mostly regressed - a consequence of the game's "no spoilers towards the first game" policy. You can tell the game you've played the first one, but you only get a few quips and a couple of extra lines - the big, important stuff goes untouched. The new somnia are great! The first one had dreamy (well, yeah) and very out there scenarios, but let's not pretend the gameplay wasn't mostly trial and error. Here they're much more coherent - perhaps in some points less artistically interesting, but a much better experience for the player. In addition, many somnia also experiment with different gameplay mechanics, which I won't spoil. They're fun, interesting to play and overall very enjoyable. You could also maybe say that the game sometimes tries to look at interesting big ideas, sometimes even as an integral part of the narrative, but unfortunately it never spends much time on them in order to maintain its veil of mystery. Positive marks however for the .The bad I've already said. I'll add this: there is a quantity of things being hand-waved away in the second half of this game that made me wonder whether hand-waving was an entire genre, and whether I was standing in it. That's how bad it is. You can't call this game a mystery because the quantity of logical holes being justified arbitrarily through convenient, never-mentioned or even implied before solutions is the hammer I was mentioning before, forcing the entire game's writing to fit its twist and underlying "mystery". Your suspension of disbelief in the second half of the game will get progressively bent before exploding in a million pieces when it can't handle the extreme strain.It also has a very formulaic structure - perhaps the original was also like this, but especially in the first half you notice way more the loop: the chapter's mystery gets set up, you go talk to people you think are relevant and to people you don't think are relevant, neither are actually relevant, after having exhausted all people to talk to you get new information that is actually relevant, you enter and solve a somnium, rinse and repeat. So, here we are. I'm not sure I'd go as far as to call it a terrible game and I don't regret playing through it, but I'd argue it's a bad sequel and that it has a lot of bad writing compared to what we usually expect from Uchikoshi. I have absolutely no idea how this reviewed better than the original. Ultimately, you could say that Uchikoshi has always had the tendency towards a bit of handwaving, big ideas being skimped over and twists bending the rest of the game around them, but I'll be honest here, doctor - the patient has been getting worse. 6.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really Enjoyed the first game. The first game felt like they didn't have a lot of budget, but they knew what they wanted to achieve with the game. In Ai Somnium 2 that is not the case it feels very rushed or atleast cut in half (jokes aside). I was expecting an upgrade from the first game, maybe something more futuristic, crazy in depth plots, but instead it just all feels like the developers were forced into pushing this game out in a weird incomplete state. You will notice it as you play along and especially if you beat the first game.I'd still play a third installment of the series, but hell no am I gonna buy it for $60. Ill update this review with a more in depth spoiler version later.SPOILER WARNING SCROLL DOWN FOR SPOILER REVIEWOne of the main reasons I loved the first Ai Somnium was because almost every ending was important to the plot. In Ai Somnium 2 each ending just feels so useless.In Ai somnium 1 it felt great because it lets you pursue each ending almost completely besides the Ota one. Each ending had it’s significance. The Iris ending showed off what is wrong with Iris and showed the extra psync machine in the abandoned factory. The Mizuki ending giving more detail to Mizuki’s character while also revealing So Sejima’s connection to Date with him being in his Son’s body. The bad ending for the first game was so crazy especially with it’s plot twist, all the connection from the dots of the different endings just coming together. Maybe only with the Ota one it really only gives more detail to Ota and his Mom. Particularly going over Ota’s mom and her dementia. Shoma’s ending.. that is the first one that started to make me think that the game had nothing going for it. Which all that could be fine, but why doesn’t it let you continue the story from there. The Amame and Gen ending is just kind of Meh, Gen is cool but I don’t really care about Amame so much and the only thing you learn is Date was in hiding. And finally the worse of them all.. the Lien and Kizuna ending, the reveal that there is a second Mizuki was just so dumb and lazy. It is just such a lame excuse for a big plot twist, it doesn’t add anything and what ends up happening for every new plot twist for the game is that they keep having to explain it to you. Most of the plot twists in the game are just long drawn-out explanations while not actually learning about it by playing the game itself. At Chapter 5 m1 Births where all the main characters are at the ruins of the Cathedral they just explain everything to you.The two Mizuki plot twist was lazy, so instead of some really clever way that Tearer did all these killings and the other halfs of the bodies are appearing in the future they just have two Mizukis and just trick the player. I mean maybe you can excuse it but why is Amame randomly the main killer now. How did Amame kill a crazy psycho smart serial killer. The game uses the excuse that he fell for her, but why?? Finally another point many other reviewers who didn’t like this game point out is that barely anyone of importance actually dies in this game for any ending. Ai somnium 1 because of your choices everyone can die. In Ai somnium 2 the only character that has somewhat of an importance that dies is like maybe thicc Tokiko Shigure, Andes Komeji, and Gen. Shoma doesn’t die, Kizuna doesn’t die, Lien doesn’t die the other original characters don’t die. There is no like urgency or “oh ♥♥♥♥” for what happens to the characters.Wasted potential:Two main characters with Ryuki and Mizuki. _childDocuments_.review: Much like the first game, the characters and story of said characters here is fantastic and a 10/10 experience worth playing through. I do find this game suffered in giving some of these characters sufficient screen time this time around, but I'll be damned if I didn't come out loving them all regardless.One thing I will absolutely fault this game for is its use of meta/fourth wall breaking aspects. To tell the truth, I'm not a fan of this kind of stuff, as it feels like a slap in the face and an excuse for a bunch of the mysteries. Ultimately, this game's mystery didn't hold up as much in an overall "wow this makes sense" moment as the first, but I do think it had its share of excellent moments. I won't spoil the ending, but it DOES make sense, though you have to think about it a lot more. There is not one but multiple antagonists this time around as you'll come to learn as the story progresses, and though I find the main antagonist isn't all too interesting, the rest sure are.I'm impressed Uchikoshi has managed to maintain the comedy here too, in a way that sometimes makes me want to kill that man, but also in how many times I chuckled from how stupid some jokes were. It was well balanced humour too; nothing that broke tension. This game also features romance as quite a heavy piece of the plot for those who want more of that.Gameplay wise, I'm proud to say it's a huge step up from the first game. Somniums have had their difficulty noticeably tweaked in that it's a lot more punishing while not having so many, "How was I supposed to know this?" moments. It DOES still have these, though if you ever find yourself stuck at an area where you never got a clear answer to, just trust the game and back out. It's necessary for the story to progress. You'll see what I mean. The VR sections feel like a more refined version of the interrogations as well, which have been entirely scrapped this time around. It feels more fitting that Mizuki and Ryuki are more involved in the investigation, as that's a huge part of what they do.So overall, a bit contrived at points, but this game and this series for this matter will forever hold a very important space in my mind. Just seeing some of these characters again and meeting all these new faces was well worth it. The Somnium Files games are a wonderful experience, and I can't wait for what Uchikoshi has cooking for the rest of this franchise, as it could seemingly perpetually continue so long as the narrative continues calling for it... Hell, it feels like this game left some loose ends open on purpose so the story had a way to continue.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Reason I have double the playtime than others is because I played this through with a friend. We'd theorise and discuss what we think the mystery's answers were, often pausing, and it might have partially come to dampen my enjoyment of the game purely because there was a lot more potential in the game.I'll divide it into a spoiler-free review and a minimum-spoiler review. Min spoiler review will have heavier spoilers for the first game.Spoiler Free:nirvanA Initiative takes what gave the first game its identity and tries to turn it up to 11. Make no mistake - the game definitely is written so that you can play this without having played the first one, but it still is a sequel. You would be much better off playing the first one before playing this one, especially with how several of the twists for the first one are kind of spoiled, while other things are deliberately left unexplained making the game really wonky. I can't say for sure how bad it might be, since I have played the first one, but I would highly recommend playing the first one before this one, and I'll assume you  played the first one for most of the review.With that out of the way, the one thing that I disliked the most was that the whole whacky anime logic was dailed up all the way beyond the slider. Characters act extremely dumb (in the sense of, the protagonist(s) confront multiple armed men, who don't shoot their guns and instead use them as bludgeons??? and often somehow magically miss the MC every time they shoot aside from a very minute number of instances). The game suffers from tone shift, same as the first game, but it did manage to smooth that out a little; you can usually tell when the whacky 1v100 scene is going to play out, and you turn off your brain when it does. It also turned down the panty jokes from the first game by a lot, which I very much appreciated.The story is weaker, however. In game one, the story was pretty compelling and there was a decent number of mysteries that were hard to figure out. There was 'timeline hopping' involved, where you play one string of decisions to the end, and use the information found in that timeline to unlock a new one and figure out the ends of the case. It was interesting, because this led to people knowing things they had no right to know but the game kinda ignored it. This game does a lot less of us piecing together a puzzle, and it has fewer mysteries to solve. Even the Somniums, the main draw of the game, were weaker - they were a lot easier, and often the game basically bludgeoned you with the answer to questions. They were just extended cutscenes in some cases, rather than the dreams you had to solve in the first game. The Somnia were a lot less consistent in this game. Some were very good, bringing branches into the fold and requiring you to figure out the 'dream logic' to solve them, but many of them were linear, straightforward affairs that brought no timeline branching (which was for me the main draw of the game) and were honestly insulting in how little you had to think to solve them. It resorted to making you run out of time quicker several times, which I felt was a lazy way of introducing difficulty.The main characters were pretty disparate in characterisation. Ryuki was a well fleshed out character, and I really enjoyed the parts of the game which focused on him. On the other hand, Mizuki, our main character who returns from Somnium 1, suffers extremely from the writing of the game necessitating her being less fleshed out. None of the effects of Somnium Files 1 are apparent in this game, especially because the game needed her to act normal to avoid spoiling the first game, and she remains fairly static throughout the game. Most of the supporting cast was static and didnt develop, despite there being a 6 year time-skip, which did nothing to change them. The most it did was have a childish net-idol become slightly more mature, and a friend of Mizuki have some actual development due to the writers allowing at least  of the characters have some changes across the time skip.Finally, there were many unanswered questions by the end of it. The actual main plot and mystery is solved, but there are several background issues that remain open, which the game might be gearing up for a sequel to solve (or the creators want those to remain 'open ended'). Some of them can only be solved by reading up on the BATS Twitter ARG, which I found frustrating.Mild Spoiler Review:The  also results in the lack of characterisation. They wrote themselves into a bind, forcing them to discard characterisation in favor of it, and it definitely cheapened the work. Visual novels usually are kind of reliant on their characters being good, but the game didnt manage to pull off getting both  and characters right. The unanswered questions are maddening.  In addition to this, the tl;dr Overall, AI: The Somnium Files nirvanA Initiative was an ok game, suffering very much from both a focus on a story that was developed with a need to avoid spoiling the first game and an insistence on building up a big mystery, that in my opinion, just hindered the plot. If you liked the first game a lot, and did not find the ridiculous anime scenes an issue, then I can recommend this game to you. If you found those scenes to be jarring, then I can only recommend it if you enjoyed the mystery and timeline hopping of the first one, but it is a tentative recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a newcomer to the Somnium Files universe, this is not the game you should start with. Start with the first in the series instead. While this game is  an independent story, and the game even made an effort into making a spoiler-free approach to the first game, there is no real point in starting at the mid-way point in an established universe, is there?  Especially when the two games in the series aren't that different in look & feel. The rest of the review therefore targets the demographic that has played and completed the first one. Honestly, I felt a bit let down for the first half of the game. The locations were mostly the same as the first game, the cast was mostly the same as the first game, heck even some of the jokes were the same ... my mind was thinking "asset reuse" more than anything else. Add to that, there were a few minor annoyances that kept bringing down the total experience, like not being able to reference your datalogs while being prompted a question, or the keyboard control setup being less than sensible. I was honestly not sold, 10 hours in. But as always, the writing is the main selling point of any spike chunsoft game. The mystery got more and more interesting, and as I found myself heavily invested in solving it. Like playing until 5 am -invested.  And then the twist hit. And let me state this for the record: this game has the best twist of any Spike Chunsoft game to date. I was so incredibly confused at times about spoiler-specific topics I will not go into, but when the twist hit every single thing made perfect sense, with all the clues present from the start, to boot. It was glorious in its revelation, I most certainly did not see it coming, and it re-contextualized everything I had seen. I have not always enjoyed the twists in Spike Chunsoft games (Zero Escape 3 in particular), but the twist in this game was simply poetry of story-writing. I have to equip a hat so that I can dramatically take it off in respect of the mad genius that concocted that plot. Fantastic job! Everything else about this game, is sadly a bit forgettable though. There are some song and dance numbers, but honestly the music isn't my genre, and I felt the prequel did the gimmick better. There was some technical effect that deserve kudos, but they were used sparingly. The puzzle system is still limited to four options per a handful of heavily telegraphed locations in a scene, sometimes the solution follows a logical path, sometimes less so. One of the puzzles was a genuine escape room set, I liked that puzzle a lot. The game added a clue-system which added a new dimension to the puzzles, I liked that very much, but it was only used in two scenes in the entire game. The game also some battle sequences, resolved through quick-time events. They were okay, but nothing spectacular. Some of them game me some smiles for their absurdity, so there's that. But yes, it feels like the devs did gain some XP while making this game, but maybe not too many new levelups, so to say. I am nonetheless anticipating the future, whatever it may hold. Hell yes. If you played the first one and liked it, you will like this game too. It is 5 AM, and I am writing a review instead of going to bed. IMO the twist was that good.

The ending to the first game is CRAAAZY. Crazy enough that AI:NI quizzes you at the beginning to see if you really caught it all. Not that it matters, since Date is the same as ever. iykyk. Since this game was attempting the impossible, it went for the impossible- literally. AI:NI is a reality destroying game, and it will take you and the entire cast of fun characters with it. I won't spoil, but they pull out some pretty impressive stops. The first AI had the issue of low replayability, due to its crazy unforgettable ending and single perspective. AI:NI understands that, so it gives you possibly the most confusing ending ever, and two characters to experience the story with. After every reveal, it made me want to go through the entire game again, to see if it all lined up with the ending in mind.This game is still plenty ridiculous and silly, and I fear possibly more so than the first one (but tbh, i think i reached the same low point of interest in the first game when it got too silly for me). The mystery is equally as unsettling, but the truth behind it is emotional in a different way. I highly recommend for fans of the first game who crave more.

name: Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered
detailed_description: The beloved and critically acclaimed Ghostbusters video game is back! Join the Ghostbusters team, fight monsters, capture ghosts, search for artifacts and have a blast destroying almost everything around you in this Remastered version of the third-person adventure Ghostbusters: The Video Game. The single player campaign will put you through a story full of mystery and adventure. The authentic experience features the voices and in-game likenesses of Bill Murray, Dan Aykroyd, Harold Ramis, and Ernie Hudson in an original story penned by the writers of the original films - Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis. Test the team's mettle with large scale boss fights. Use the PKE Meter to scan the environment and artifacts, and your proton pack to catch ghosts of all types. Besides the classic proton stream mode, use experimental firing modes to solve environmental puzzles and add some spice to the fight. Ever wanted to fling a ghost into a trap with a slime string? Now you can! Strap on your proton pack today and remember: Don't cross the streams!

_childDocuments_.review: It is a bittersweet experience to play Ghostbusters in 2021 after waiting so long for the sequel to 2, a messy fight between Harold Ramis and Bill Murry and the tragic loss of Harold in 2014.  I don’t exactly know how they managed to convince Bill Murray to come to the table.  Maybe the idea of replacing him with Ben Stiller (true story) was the reason.  Regardless, what we got in Dan Aykroyd’s own words was Ghostbusters 3 and damn what a fun 10 hours I had.  It’s a shame that we didn’t get everyone back for their roles, such as Rick Moranis (understandably) and Sigourney Weaver (who initially turned down the role when asked but then expressed interest when she found out Bill Murray was in but by that point the game was already written and she had no part).  This game allows you to play as the 5th Ghostbuster and if you are a Ghostbusters fan then this game is your loveletter from the team.WE GOT ONE!!!!  We got a videogame based on a movie that doesn’t suck!  It doesn’t happen often but when it does, it is so satisfying.  Especially when it’s a movie as seminal as Ghostbusters.  Get it for the nostalgia but stay for the great story, original dialogue and decent gameplay.  It’s not perfect but as the only active voicework in a game for Dr. Egon Spengler and not just archive for some other games, I hope that Ramis was proud of his creation and I feel like I got some closure to the franchise after all these years.

_childDocuments_.review: ...is a third-person action shooter. As the newest recruit of the Ghostbusters team, you follow Egon, Ray, Peter and Winston as they discover the source of the disasters that have struck New York City in their past adventures.Control is that of a typical third-person shooter, and probably controls better with a keyboard and mouse. Some ghosts must be destroyed, some slimed, some grabbed and slammed around using your beam as a lasso, and, of course, some must be drained of energy and captured using ghost traps you lay on the floor. Scanning ghosts and consulting the result in Tobin's Spirit Guide will reveal their weaknesses.As the story progresses, you get up to 4 different weapons: the traditional proton gun, the slime thrower, the dark-matter generator and the meson blaster, each with an alternate firing mode used both for ghost busting and puzzle solving. Weapon overheating replaces ammo, and venting said heat replaces reloading. Instead of a display hud, your health and weapon's heat is displayed directly on your proton pack.While there are no skills to speak of, you can upgrade your equipment using the R&D budget you get from capturing ghosts and from scanning and collecting haunted artefact. These include stronger weapon beams, faster firing rate, slower overheating (aka more ammo), quicker PKE Meter scanning, better traps, and many more.There are 7 chapters that unfold into a few sections, all ending with a boss fight. Level design can be confusing at times, figuring where to go next or where you've already been, but progression is otherwise pretty linear with not too much backtracking.This is the third movie everyone has been asking for. The script by Harold Ramis and Dan Aykroyd is spot on. There's no retcon, it impeccably follows the original two movies' story and acts as a sequel, paying homage to original locations and lore, and tying up almost all of the loose ends nicely, from who were the people behind the Gozer-summoning skyscraper to the origin of the river of slime.While there are cutscenes, most of the story is told during in-game segments, com chatter and scripted events. You actually feel like you’re one of the Ghostbusters as they interact with you and each other. All the main voice actors return in their role, even William Atherton as Walter Peck! The firehouse itself is also a treasure trove of nostalgic references. Lore lovers will also find every location, ghost or haunted artifact on your PKE meter's Tobin's Spirit Guide with further backstory.Aesthetic-wise, the game looks and sounds great. The one thing they had to get right was the proton pack, and it looks awesome! It blinks and buzzes with your hud display, opening valves and triggers as you switch from one weapon to another. The standard proton beam and ghost traps are impeccably recreated, with sound effects that feel genuine. My recommendation: play this one in a dark room, and let the proton pack and blaster's particle effects immerse you!It's rather disappointing that the game can be completed in under 10 hours. You may come back to any level to get all the collectibles if you missed any during your first playthrough, but it isn't enough to give it much replayability. And what was the big idea of removing multiplayer from the PC version? A game like that was made to be played in co-op!Even with this so-called remastered edition, the uncanny valley shows its face as much as the original version, mostly during in-game segments and animations. Cutscene animations are better (at least by 2013 original release standards), but switching from in-game engine to cutscene breaks you out of the immersion. Music, limited to the soundtracks from the two original movies, gets pretty repetitive after a while.While the AI isn't too bad (assisting you in captures, laying traps for ghosts you're busting or using the ones you lay), it certainly shows its weakness in strategic teamwork. It can be very frustrating at higher difficulty when you're swarmed by a large quantity of ghosts and have to spend your time constantly running from one buddy to another in order to get them back on their feet when they are knocked down, while they aren't as reliable to get you back on yours.Bustin' has never made me feel this good! If you’re any bit of an original Ghostbusters fan, you WANT this game! It was obviously made with love for the franchise and attention to detail (unlike  which is a cheap remake of  trying to cash-in on the bad 2016 movie remake). Very few movie-based game will ever be as spot-on as .—————————————————————————

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostbusters is a third-person "shooter" where you assume the role of the fifth Ghostbuster, the Rookie. Your task is to aid the team in capturing ghosts, battling monsters, demons, and various abominations in thrilling events. Equipped with sophisticated gadgets and weapons capable of slowing down, causing massive damage, and capturing ghosts, you'll progress through the game trapping these entities.As you advance, the game gradually unfolds, allowing you to unlock and upgrade your weapons for optimal effectiveness against enemies. The exploration is straightforward and linear, without sprawling into a vast open world. This simplicity works well in delivering an intense and captivating storyline. Unexpectedly more fun than I expected. Easier to complete, and enjoy from beginning to end.   The graphics aren't the best, even with the remaster, but they stay true to the movie and recreate the original characters well. The cinematics are well animated, portraying a somewhat realistic yet cartoonish look effectively.    Authentic to the original soundtracks and voice actors, there were no issues whatsoever. It was nice to see that the dialogues were well-preserved from the original. I did notice some sound effects and sounds being of slightly lower quality than others, but overall, it was a decent effort. If you've never watched the original movie, "The Ghostbusters," it's important to note that this game serves as a continuation, making references to characters, ghosts, and events that could potentially spoil the movie experience if you haven't seen it. I highly recommend starting with the movie to fully immerse yourself and appreciate the story.The writing remains faithful to the movie, exhibiting wit, nerdiness, and a bit of confusion, yet it possesses a certain charm. Despite their janitor-like appearance, these characters showcase remarkable courage and deliver some unexpectedly epic moments.   Not a long game, but it packs an intense and epic story within its duration. It's enjoyable from start to finish, and if you're a fan of the franchise, you'll wish it didn't end. Each battle feels like a climactic moment, which is amazing. In terms of difficulty, the game leans towards being easy. Even on the hardest difficulty, while you might face occasional deaths, it's still achievable. Ghostbusters is an unexpectedly fun experience that remains faithful to the franchise's roots, sparking a newfound curiosity in me to actually watch the show. It's witty, fun, occasionally comedic, goofy, and incredibly nerdy for those who enjoy the Ghostbusters crew geeking out over equipment and in-game events. It's a MUST-PLAY for those who love an entertaining and unconventional story that keeps you on the edge of your seat. Moreover, it's a must for those who hold the franchise dear to their hearts.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Ghostbusters 2009, I've owned it on the XBOX 360, and now I bought it here... and up until NOW did I not know why people HATED the PC version.The PC version has 2 terrible bugs.  This bug can be fixed in 1 day - 1 DAY!  This bug is NOT present on the XBOX 360 version:There is NO sound for the company logos (the Consoles had Sound for EVERY company logo).  I checked the datamined files for this game and the sound files are ACTUALLY THERE but the person responsible for porting to PC failed to have them PLAY with the company logos.The Sound and Video syncing are off for the Rendered Video.How are they off?  Either the Sound Tracks are sped up, or the Video Tracks has more frames of video per second than the encoding allows for.On the XBOX 360 version was perfectly synced.  So someone, when they did their little conversion, recorded the video and the audio with the wrong encoding.This is really REALLY easy to fix.They should fix it!How can they fix it?  They take the masters and PROPERLY ENCODE THEM in 10 SECONDS.But the Saber Interactive studio that is supposed to provide support no longer gives support for the game.  Their email address has been disable for well over 2 years now, and they don't even list Ghostbusters on their site!This bug is so egregious that the opening scene is a full 1 minute 30 seconds off.  I can't even do a Let's Play of the game because the audio is so screwed up it's painful to watch, and as a result I can't even do a let's play of the game.  Nobody would watch the gameplay.  1 minute 30 seconds of video without sound?!  Audio of people talking 40 seconds before the character is even on SCREEN!? _childDocuments_.review: “Bustin’ makes me feel good!” - My wife’s boyfriend’s favorite line.WE EAT GODS FOR BREAKFAST!!!What did you do, Ray?!This game is a damn treasure. I was there in 2009, and I was here again in 2019.I remember watching the movies when I was young, I was the biggest fan as a child of Ghostbusters and still am. I would even dress up with my dad for Halloween as a Ghostbuster and even made my own proton pack with him. He passed in 2014 still a Ghostbuster in his heart, RIP legend.This game was awesome back then, this is awesome today with this remaster. It’s the closest thing to Ghostbusters 3 we will ever get. The dialogue, comedy and soundtrack are spot on, the voice acting is fantastic for a video game. I have played this in every platform multiple times. If you aren’t a Ghostbusters fan this is still a good and fun game, think Luigi’s Mansion for grownups, if you ARE a fan this game is a treasure, a must have that won’t disappoint you.The remaster looks fantastic, specially on the characters faces. Yes compared to modern games it’s a little clunky, yes it’s a bit short. But you’re a freaking Ghostbuster! Right there fighting alongside the OG Ghostbusters with a story written by Ackroyd and Ramis! It was a brilliant execution. I honestly felt like I'd joined the team and that's all I really wanted as a kid, so it was nice to feel that as an adult.I remember playing the original and being surprised that Ghostbusters of all things translated into a rather competent third person shooter. Ghostbusters is to this day one of my favorite 3rd person shooters. It’s pretty much perfect, because it doesn't fall into the trapping that so many other post-Gears of War shooters of the era did. There's a heavy emphasis on using the right tool for the job, not to mention on spectacle and the environment. The game at times feels like a great interactive movie, it’s clear that a lot of love and passion went into it and it really showed, in every aspect of it. It also performs amazingly on the Deck. I really loved the game, a great homage to the franchise with most of the nostalgic magic intact. I'm really glad I played it, and I hope that others will come to enjoy it as I did. 8/10

I love the capture streams and leading the ghosts into the trap feels so satisfying! The locations, enemies, and story are fantastic!
