_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of Ghostbusters games but this one stands apart for it's authenticity - a return of the original cast, the 3rd film script on hand, and gameplay that lets you live the fantasy the movies sell.Almost all of the original cast are back (minus Rick Moranis and Sigourney Weaver) along with you playing a new recruit. You're lead through a variety of call-backs and scenes from the original film mixed into the new plot. The original voices add a lot to the story but the trainee you play feels shoe-horned into the script. The story ends up being fun in parts and functional overall, but the environments feel very phoned in. They clearly had original ideas but it's like they built them from cheap pre-made parts. The biggest effort went into re-creating locations, objects, and effects from the films. The entire thing plays out very cinematically and gameplay is very straightforward - you zap the ghost until it gets tired while dodging attacks, then you deploy a trap and pull it in. There's a few different beams and tools you'll get as you go, but it's really just 'zapping mode' or 'scanning mode' throughout. The scanning will let you find your way and unlock some achievements but that's about it. The combat can be brutal at times as ghosts do a lot of damage which makes you focus on dodging, that combined with health-sponge enemies results in some very drawn out sections.I'd say it's worth a play if you're looking for that 3rd movie experience or if you're a fan of the original films. It's hard to recommend this to newcomers because it's so closely tied to what came already. The gameplay feels like the films, you play scenes from the films, there's a lot of catchphrases. Lacking all that context you're walking into some very simplistic gameplay and a story-heavy experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Steam is the third platform I've bought this game on (original on some old console, remaster on Xbox One, and now, at last, PC). Not only is there a ton of fanservice -- numerous callbacks to, and elaborations on, the movies, plus heavy doses of new lovingly-pulled-out-of-the-nether-regions ecto-technobabble and spirit lore -- but the proton packs feel and work like you'd think proton packs should, and the snozzberries taste like snozzberries. Oops, wrong franchise.Every year or three I get an itch to revisit the stupid-smart world of the Ghostbusters, and at last I can do it on a rig that runs Cyberpunk 2077 decently well. _childDocuments_.review: Ghostbusters: The Video Game really is the third film in the series. The overall atmosphere, the writing and the story are all top-notch and there is also a very enjoyable game to accompany all of this. The creativity on display is here is simply astounding and it is something that only comes along every now and then.Yes, the game has some technical issues. Yes, some animations are still stuck in 30 fps. Yes, it looks and feels like a game from the X360/PS3 era. However, if you can look past all of these issues, then this is really one of the best movie to video game adaptations we've ever had.And the reason of this is quite simple: not only are you interacting and fighting alongside the original characters (voiced by the original cast) but the gameplay loop is fun and the game introduces new gameplay elements and weapons just at the right times. The graphics might be a bit dated but the art style and the game's own debris and destruction system really stand out and easily stood the test of time. You can expect to see some memorable set pieces while listening to well-written and often humourous banter between the characters.Overall, even if you are not a Ghostbusters fan but you enjoy solid TPS shooters with a good story and genuine humour, then you owe it to yourself to give this game a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: This is Ghostbusters 3. If you are a fan of Ghostbusters, Congratulations! You've found the official unofficial (basically canon) 3rd entry. The story is written by Dan Anykroyd and the late Harold Ramis and has been stated in many interviews to be the spiritual successor to the first two films. The game take off a few years after Ghostbusters II, where the team pick up a new cadet (you) to try out all the new gadgets so they don't harm the 'real' Ghostbusters. This game expands the lore of the many types of ghosts in the Ghostbusters world as well as the lore of the Gozer worshippers across New York. If you cared at all about the lore of the first movie and the implications of slime from the second, this is where you can find it. Gameplay is great, you slowly get access to different proton pack weapon types as you progress the story,  with different ghosts being weaker to the different weapon types. You can spend the money you get trapping ghosts buying upgrades for your weaponry and tools. If you aren't a fan of Ghostbusters, you might get lost on the ghost science talk and some parts of the plot, but you might still enjoy the gameplay. The game took me about 6 hours on the experienced (medium) difficulty to beat, so it's pretty short. Given it's essentially the 3rd movie in videogame format, that makes sense. The only other Issue to point out is the bugs. The game resets some of the settings every time you close the game, so I had to go into the settings every time I launched the game to get things back the way I wanted. Not a deal breaker, but doesn't look like the devs will update it soon. There are also a few times where parts of a level will stop working properly, like the characters won't follow you, the game doesn't register you've beaten all the ghosts in an area, etc. Luckily, there is a "restart from last checkpoint" option so you don't have to restart the level, but it's sometimes frustrating, especially after you've just trapped a ton of enemies. Overall, great game. Definitely worth a playthrough during a Ghostbusters marathon.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Ghostbusters so so much.  I am a massive fan of the original movie, so it is right in my wheelhouse.I should note here, I played the entire game on Steam Deck.  It runs fantastic on Deck, max settings and locked at 60fps.  Truly, an appropriate game for a commute through NYC.First and most importantly, Ghostbusters has all of the original talent involved.  It was written by Harold Ramis (rip)  and Dan Aykroyd.  All of the voice performances are from the original actors, and it is fantastic.  It is sort of the unofficial third Ghostbusters movie.As far as the game itself, I would say it has high highs and low lows.  There is an overwhelming amount of good, you can wander around the firehouse, and it is filled with fan service.  There are tons of great cutscenes.  Many of the missions have you returning to memorable locations from the films and dealing with familiar faces.  You proton pack is awesome, it looks great, and the sounds and effects are spot on.  You are a rookie, just starting your internship with the team.  The plot is fine, it pulls in stuff from both of the previous movies, there are lots of enjoyable moments, and again, fan service.  The gameplay is a mixed bag.  As previously stated, your proton pack is awesome.  Additionally, you are almost always fighting with at least one other 'buster by your side and they banter, and you need to help each other up when you are downed, its all pretty cool.  Its interesting, because a lot of the issues I have with the combat seem like deliberate choices to stay true to the source material, so I am torn when thinking about if I would have done it differently.  You are the team are a bunch of middle aged guys, you are not soldiers or athletes and it shows.  Your dodge is just a little hop, and you have no other movement options besides a roadie run type sprint.  You don't get "into cover" or anything like that.  You just kind of lumber around blasting ghosts.... but the ghosts are super agile, and it leads to getting knocked out a lot and feeling like there was nothing you can do about it.  In the same vein, blasting the ghosts is kinda loose, you just kinda keep your stream on them and hope you are doing good damage.  They have a little damage meter, but sometimes they would be so spongy I wasn't sure if I was doing damage, or if it was my teammates.  As you advance in the game it gets a little better, you power up your pack, and you get other pack modes and can scan the enemies to see which mode they are weakest against.  The environments are pretty awesome.  You can destroy a ton of the objects in the rooms, and you revisit a ton of great NYC locations from the films.  Levels where you are not in cool, real, NYC spaces, feel much more generic.   Ghostbusters is a great little remaster, I really loved playing through it.  I think its probably in the 7-8 range as a video game, but I am such a massive fan of the source material, it is a 10 for me.  10/10

It took several decades, but this game was the Ghostbusters 3 I've always wanted.  It was a grand reunion with all my favorite characters.Nostalgia aside, it's actually a great game.  Wrangling a ghost is not easy, but it's a whole lot of fun.  The enemies are varied, dynamic, and interesting, and some of the boss fights are insane.   Some battles require thinking outside the box, while others require constant movement.  Standing still can get you killed.My only two critiques are:1) Some fights do feel a little bit like whack-a-mole when everybody keeps getting knocked unconscious - and then I spend most of the fight running from one downed Ghostbuster to another, reviving them instead of fighting - but in a lot of ways it adds to the tension.  There's a lot going on.2) You can't not cross the streams.  It happens all the time, and more often than not it's one of the other Ghostbusters crossing streams with you, but then they give you grief for doing it.  It can be a bit repetitive hearing it a couple dozen times in one fight.I'd give it 9 out of 10, but now that I've finished it, I still want more.  Where's my Ghostbusters 4...?

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best movie based game I've ever played. Being written by Dan Aykroyd and the late Harold Ramis helped immensely, not to mention not having to rush production to release along the movie is another factor. The game perfectly captures the atmosphere of the movies, every ghost and every proton pack upgrade fits right in. The cutscenes alone are pretty much Ghostbusters 3 that never was, although whether this game is canon or now is up for debate. It doesn't have everybody in it, Dana Barret is all but mentioned and as far as I know, nobody even talks about Louis Tully (or I missed that), but at least Preck I mean Peck is still there being a pain in the ass. And it doesn't matter that you don't play as one of the main Ghostbusters. The Rookie, despite being a silent protagonist, doesn't feel out of place as he reacts visually to everything that happens.The gameplay is a little bit weaker part, mainly due to the stupid AI of your companions, who are incredibly incompetent at what they are doing. Other than that it's essentially a third person shooter where all the guns were replaced with proton pack modifications. Besides the regular proton stream you've got slime blower, boson darts and stuff like meson collider and you'll be switching between them quite a lot in the late game in order to be as efficient as possible. There is an upgrade system, but there's not much to it. There are tons of easter eggs and little references to the movies, you'll be visiting a lot of the movie locations like the Sedgewick hotel or the Public library and even cross into another dimension few times. The way they implemented the ghost catching is really immersive, first drain the ghost of its energy then slam it into the ground few times and finally slam it into the trap. Or use a slime tether to sling it into it, which is really fun, but almost impossible to do if there are other ghostbusters around.Then there are obligatory collectibles, most of which are haunted artifacts, which have humorous backstory to them. And if you want even more backstory on the individual ghosts, you can scan them, which also reveals their weaknessess.Then there are the more frustrating parts, for instance the framerate- in the options menu you can cap it to either 30 or 60FPS by checking respective box. You can uncheck both of them, which you'd think would allow you to uncap the framerate, but nope, still 60. Plus if you do that and quit the game, next time you open it it'll default to 30FPS. Annoying. Then there's the professional mode, which is the hardest  difficulty in the game, it should be renamed "Ghostbuster babysitter mode", because it highlights how bad the AI is. You'll be constantly reviving your colleagues instead of focusing on busting ghosts. And in the later levels you can be pretty much all instakilled by bosses. Not to mention if you need to be revived, you're in serious trouble as you'll be seeing Egon getting stuck on terrain and walking in one place for few seconds, or running away from you, or running to revive somebody else even though you were closer. There is also no coop option, this is a strictly singleplayer game.Anyway, I highly recommend you play this game. If you liked the movies, you'll love this. Just don't play on the professional difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: After seeing Ghostbusters: Afterlife I decided to pick up Ghostbusters The Video Game and this is one of those rare movie licensed games that actually has passion put into it and isn't just a cash grab. Of course being written by Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis (stars of the movie) it feels authentic. And if I'm not mistaken this was supposed to be Ghostbusters 3 but instead they took those ideas and made it into this game. The story is really good and even if some of the stuff at the beginning are retreads of the movie, it makes sense because of the context and there's so many new ghosts and monsters to fight. The gameplay may get repetitive for some but I was so invested in the story that I didn't really care and I just had so much fun reliving a game that I used to play when was little. It would've been nice if there were more puzzles or exploration in the levels but aside from that it's a really fun game that I recommend, especially if you're a Ghostbusters fan and you want a true continuation. $25 is a bit much though so I'd recommend buying it when its on sale, I got it for $6 from the autumn sale.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing way to experience something close to a direct sequel to the first two movies thanks to Harold Ramis(God bless him) and Dan Aykroyd's writing taking from a scrapped script of Ghostbusters III. The dialogue, characters, and story are on point, though Bill Murray seemed to have less of a presence most likely with his own personal stuff but showed more of Ernie Hudson because of it.Gameplay actually feels pretty nice for a 2009 game. The satisfying sounds of a proton pack and the mesmerizing waves of a particle stream is just how I pictured it to be. Wearing down the ghost may seem a bit tedious or slow, but actually feels thrilling especially when there's 3 other ways of wearing them down. Once you capture a ghost with the particle stream, you can wear them down even further by slamming them into walls once your slam meter builds up from latching on to them and may even slam them directly into the trap which traps them instantly with one of the upgrades. You may even just directly tether a ghost into a trap without having to wear them down.Because of how much I love the gameplay, it's sad that they didn't include the multiplayer modes in the remaster which would've been a great experience actually playing with other people and it seems Saber isn't going to be updating the game at all for it. Speaking of the remaster, there are apparently some video settings missing from the original PC version like a borderless or windowed option making fullscreen the only setting present. Settings will also automatically reset to default once you boot up the game, forcing you to switch the settings everytime you start it if you wanted anything to change. And while you have the option for 60FPS with the 60Hz settings, the character animations still play out in 30FPS most likely due to missing some parts of the original game which they can't change without it or not wanting to bother with it.Cutscenes constantly have a difference in quality too. Some will have been pre-rendered with really nice lighting while others are low quality videos of what seems to be in-game. Not exactly sure why they couldn't have been actual in-game instead of the low quality videos they put but I assume they lost some stuff from the archive.Also the music is pretty much straight from the movies which is great in making it feel like a genuine continuation, but it does start to get a bit boring when they keep reusing some of the same tracks due to not making any new soundtracks. Sure the second movie also reuses most of its staple music, but this is a video game story with multiple chapters which each have their tense moments. It would've been nice to hear something different every now and then.Overall, the game is still pretty solid over 10 years later. Definitely play if you're waiting for Afterlife to come out

_childDocuments_.review: The remake is a scam not to be bought, the game has no improvements.The graphics are the same, with a slight improvement in fluidity.Subtitles don't work and there are voice bugs in many scenes.The resolution worked properly in 2009, but today I run the 2009 game at 5760x1080 or 1920x1080.In 1920x1080, the game runs on a screen without any problem.On the pseudo remake, the game doesn't work in 5760x1080 because it automatically switches to 5760x3240 and in 1920x1080 the game automatically switches to all three screens and there's no window mode, the steam options "-windowed and -sw" don't work.The 2009 game was perfectly adapted to 2024 configurations and worked very well, but saber's goofy aren't competent to make a game in 2024 for 2024.The guys who made the original in 2009 were already more talented than the untalented people at saber today.Pitiful.The gameplay is faithful to the movie, and it's fun, with a bunch of goofy wasps who become heroes.The battle with the ghosts is very well done and respects the atmosphere of the movie.The level rises gradually, but the weapons need to be upgraded and purchased.As for the graphics, it's hard today, as the 2009 style lacks fluidity compared to what we're used to today.But the game runs smoothly and without bugs.Unfortunately, there are no longer any prizes, as the game has been replaced by a scam masquerading as a remake.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostbusters: The Video Game remastered by Saber who are best known for World War Z & Evil Dead The Game. The game was originally developed by Terminal Reality, best known for BloodRayne, back in 2009.This is third person shooter action/adventure in which you assume the role of a new recruit. The entire cast (except Rick Moranis & Sigourney Weaver) reprise their roles for the game. The story of the game being written by Aykrord & Ramis. This is essentially the third installment in franchise.There are 8 levels. Well 8 levels if you count the Firehouse hub as one. There are a tons of locals you visit in those 7 levels. From Sedgwick Hotel to the Library and to much more. The game is short but sweet. It can be beaten in one sitting.One unique thing that I liked and what the devs took from Dead Space is no hud. Everything you need to see is on your character (Proton Pack). Your health and your overheat meter. Though the health can be ignored because your screen gets more red as you're closer to death which I think is a better indicator. Now you don't die but you get downed like Left 4 Dead. Your NPC partners need to revive you and you need to do the same for them. When everyone is downed then that is a game over. The revive is a simple button press and the character is back on their feet immediately.I would fully recommend downloading the Ghostbusters Deluxe mod by sakis720. It fixes and tweaks some areas and aspects of the game to make the experience more enjoyable.Your Proton Pack has four different modes of fire. As in you fire something different out of it other than the Proton Stream. They spice up the gameplay and have ghosts affected by certain types.Solid game & solid experience for a Ghostbusters fan.Easy 100% for achievement hunters.Should only require two playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: finished the game on professional difficulty with aim assist off, it was fun.the first thing i noticed about this game was the tone, it is quite lighthearted at the start of the game with the help of the soundtrack but it does lean progressively more towards the horror in the later game, and i would consider the later game to be closest to a real ghostbusting experience, although throughout the whole game you are rarely alone to facilitate this horror experience.there are pros and cons the this game's approach to being a ghostbuster, i suppose it could have been a bit better to play as one of the main 4 ghostbusters or a rotating cast for each level instead of being a nameless cadet with a forgettable fresh face, especially since you do end up getting some of the best gear among the group as a guise for "testing" it, sometimes it doesn't really make sense for us to be a newbie but it also makes sense to make the player simply someone who comes along to the main cast's adventures.there are collectibles in this game but these are better than the usual video game collectible since these do show up in the ghostbusters office after you collect them, and you do get some money for finding them but this game is quite generous with money anyways so you won't have to worry about getting enough of it for upgrades.the game does have some cool physics which do get utilized quite well with items that let you pull and hold most physics items, as well as these things getting utilized in physics puzzles at certain points in the story.the navigation was quite solid, there wasn't really a point where i felt lost since most level designs are quite linear.it wasn't too hard to finish even on the hardest difficulty, save points do come quite often and all areas took less than 10 tries to beat.i've played the unremastered game on xbox 360 in the past which is why i decided to play this game on steam again, and it was well worth it, this is certainly the definitive ghostbusters video game experience.i would say it is worth a buy though it is pretty short so buying it on a sale is recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game to others... the answer is yes to some and no to others... Here is why. The game was a blast to revisit. I had just as much fun playing it again as I did when it was first released. Even the "replay-ability" is just as engaging when your hunting to get all the achievements that are in this game. At the time of review I already threw in 18hrs and have all but one achievement to get which is the most difficult and curse word inducing challenge of all... playing it on extreme difficulty. But alas the game and the fun factor is well worth every struggle. Now as for the remastered part. Whether the game is worth getting for the remastered version. Sadly for me the answer is no, Although the game looks exceptionally well on the cosmetics part, there are issues that I have with the game. Firstly there are parts of the game to where the FMV cut scenes are in low res, almost 480 to 720, where others are using the games engine that supports what standard I set it on, which was full! I get the pre-rendered cut scenes, yet why does it feel as though my game goes to standard definition from 2009 to suddenly back to the full just after?! Very tacky and distasteful. Secondly, there is one specific cut scene where Peck, at the museum, is scolding the GB'ers before being possessed, here the audio of music is missing for some reason, giving the impression that my copy is faulty or it was removed intentionally or by accident. Still the games ambiance is altered and removes you of being encapsulated by the story, because the scene is awkward with no ambient music, and it leaves you wondering if you did something or if your game is corrupt. Thirdly yes the infamous "NO Multiplayer" that all of us that once had, is missing, this makes the extended replay-ability sadly thwarted from growing or continuing. When you think of other games like "No Mans Sky, Astroneer, Mortal Kombat 11, and many others, that still sink DLC content to a game, you ponder on to how such a familiar and beloved franchise was diluted and abandoned so?! The game was released in 2009. Its been handed off from developer to publisher on and on so often, all it feels as though the game gets handed down and repackaged with little effort in branching it to other avenues. Look from what I hear the XBOX community still has servers available with multiplayer and fans still at times dive in to play the game. Multiplayer might have its controversy, something of how 6 or more coding parameters exist within the game, yet which was the one primarily used for multiplayer is still unsolved. Yet in all that time, no one pondered to develop another one? Seems odd. Luckily the modding community has been working on such issues, so for Ghostbuster fans, know this, if such a modding community exists to bring back 007 Golden Eye, so does a community working on bringing its talent to the GB franchise. I love this game, its worth to get if you are a die hard fan, but if you can, dust off the xbox 360 or dive into the XBLA and play it again, even with the extra of multiplayer. As to the Playstation fans go find your old copies and dust them off, as your not missing much aside from sharper/crisper gameplay. Trust me the fun factor is still as good from your consoles as it is for the remasterd PC version. But to those that have yet to experience this game and have the time and cash to invest. Your in for a treat. I think later this year when the latest expansion of the GB universe is released in theaters, there will be that love and hunger for this game again, and they wont be disappointed from the story and the gameplay, yet they will join us on how we feel when we are strung along with hopes on making it better or adding to the adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I said it before when I first played it on console and I'll say it again now that I have it on PC. Ghostbusters: The Video Game is the Ghostbusters 3 we all wanted and desired!Put yourself in the boots and strap on the proton pack as you play a rookie taken in under the wing of the famous ghostbusting crew, voiced by the original cast! Visit familiar venues seen in the movies, battle familiar ghost and newer ones as the makers of the video game expand on the legend of Gozor. Starting with the Good: Naturally, using the original actors gives you a feeling of being apart of the crew, with each actor nailing down their former roles with the same enthusiasms we see in the Ghostbusters movie. References flow just as freely as the slime - and boy there is a lot of slime - while the full personalities we fell in love with on screen are put on display.Artistically, the game is great to look at! Whether you are traversing the topsy-turvy dangers of the Ghostworld, or ruining a party at the Sedgewick Hotel. Each character model in the video game closely resembles their actors as they were portrayed in the movie.When it comes to the actual gameplay, Ghostbusting has never felt this good! Get the feel of a proton back with not just 1, but 4 different ways to capture ghost, unlocked and given to you through the gameplay. Create untold levels of property damage with the classic proton stream, or hose down your allies and ghost with the slime gun. Many ghost will be weak to a certain type of firing mode and you'll need all four of these to help the Ghostbusters, once again, save New York!Now some of the bad:Though they have brought back the same actors from the movie, a lot of their jokes still don't quite carry through and I've found that a lot of them miss more than they hit their target - however, this could just be my preference in humor.Pathfinding might be a bit of an issue. Having beaten the game, I can count at least four instances where a ghost got stuck in a corner somewhere, stuck under some debris, or otherwise becomes inaccessible to me. Considering you must actually capture these ghost instead of blowing them away with your proton pack, this can sometimes result in a very annoying lock where you have to just reload your last save.Your allies are usually very dependable... however, I have encountered moments where their pathfinders will sometimes break and they will either stand around and do nothing when they should be reviving me, or they just stand around and shoot at a ghost, taking massive damage and forcing you to spend a lot of time picking them up off the ground.In conclusion: The Ghostbusters: Video Game is a dedicated and faithful addition to the world of Ghostbusters. I would give it a pretty decent 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)When Ghostbusters: The Video Game originally hit consoles back in 2009, it was a delightful surprise for fans of the iconic movie franchise. Now, a decade later, Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered brings back the paranormal action and humor in a polished and updated form, serving as both a trip down memory lane and an enjoyable experience for new players.Visually, the remastered version of the game is a treat. The character models have been enhanced, and the environments are more detailed than ever, breathing new life into the ghost-infested corners of New York City. The animations are smoother, and the ghosts themselves exhibit a level of detail that was impossible to achieve in the original release. These improvements contribute to the game's overall immersion, making it easy to become absorbed in the Ghostbusters universe.The heart and soul of Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered lies in its story and writing. The game features a script penned by original Ghostbusters writers Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis, capturing the quirky humor and camaraderie that made the movies so beloved. Players step into the shoes of a new recruit on the Ghostbusters team, giving them a unique perspective on the established characters and their ghost-busting adventures. The inclusion of the original cast's voice acting, including Aykroyd, Ramis, Bill Murray, and Ernie Hudson, adds an extra layer of authenticity that fans will appreciate.Gameplay-wise, Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered successfully blends action, exploration, and puzzle-solving. Armed with the iconic proton pack, players battle a variety of supernatural foes, each requiring different strategies to defeat. The upgraded controls feel more responsive, making it easier to wrangle mischievous spirits and wear them down before capturing them. The inclusion of new mechanics and equipment adds depth to the gameplay experience, preventing it from feeling like a simple rehash of the original release.However, a few minor issues prevent Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered from reaching perfection. While the updated visuals are impressive, they still show their age in some areas, and occasional graphical glitches can briefly break the immersion. Additionally, the AI behavior of your fellow Ghostbusters during combat sequences can sometimes be a bit unpredictable, leading to moments of frustration when teamwork falters.In conclusion, Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered is a lovingly crafted homage to the beloved movie franchise. It successfully captures the essence of the Ghostbusters universe while providing a fresh and engaging experience for both newcomers and long-time fans. Despite a few technical hiccups, the game's nostalgic charm, excellent writing, and improved gameplay mechanics make it a worthy addition to any gamer's collection. Who you gonna call? Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered, for a hauntingly good time.

_childDocuments_.review: WE CAME! WE SAW! WE SHIDDED AND FARDED! Remasters are honestly trash most of the time. It’s either a soulless cash grab like Batman: Return to Arkham or a bastardized downgrade like GTA: The Trilogy -Definitive Edition.  Very rarely is a remaster the definitive way to revisit an old game, but sometimes a new coat of paint can make an old title feel brand new again. Saber Interactive’s remaster of Ghostbusters: The Video Game didn’t break the mold in regards to utilizing the latest hardware or giving us a 4K photo realistic rendering of Bill Murray, but it freshens up a rare licensed game that’s more than just a cash-in on a popular film. Ghostbuster: The Video Game serves as the third story in the film franchise and allows you to join the crew of paranormal exterminators. Shooting a proton stream and visiting familiar locations from the original film alone sells the nostalgia factor, but the gameplay is actually fun and challenging. Terminal Reality, the developer, really took great care to make this title indistinguishable from the films and with the influence of Dan Ackroyd and Harold Ramis’ script, everything is familiar but brand new. Gags are funny, logging intel from ghosts is brilliant, the cast does an incredible job, and the overall experience is good ol fun! The remaster is kind of a mixed bag. Gameplay itself is updated visually and looks superior to the 2009 release, but most cutscenes are untouched with terrible 720p quality. The controls are mostly in tact, but things are still very stilted like the original, which I wish was improved. Generally, the PC port for this is a mess! You can’t save your settings and you have to consult PCGamingWiki to fix that and other issues that may occur. Kinda inexcusable for a modern release, but I would take that headache over the nightmare glitches of the GTA trilogy remaster. If I were to grade this overhaul of graphics and what’s left of a 12 year old source code, I guess it would be a B-. Ghostbusters is a really good game and the remaster does just enough to renew it for a new audience. Like most remasters, it doesn’t improve anything of substance and focuses on visual stuff, which is passable at best. It probably plays better on the console, but I wouldn’t know.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, can you believe this game originally released 12 years ago. That means this video game is a nostalgic romp for someone who played it as a kid 12 years ago. That's wild to me, as a person who grew up with the original Ghostbusters movies and later the cartoon show (that really actually had so little to do with the movies it said the movies were just movies in that universe too which is why they were called the Real Ghostbusters because the movie was supposedly only based roughly on them).I originally played this when it came out, but since it was on XBOX 360, and I think I had an SD TV at the time, it was really dark (hard to see type dark) and it made it frustrating to play. I ended up stopping around the museum level. It's so weird to me that I remember that since it was apparently such a long time ago.The game is memorable because it does so much to reference it's past films, but also builds onto that a pretty decent trilogy of movie length set pieces of it's own (There's roughly 6 missions which amounts to about 3 movies worth of material) that are much more interesting than anything Sony pictures has done with the license in the last 12 years and fun to play along with at times.Long long before this game I played a Playstation 2 game called Ghosthunter. While the game felt unfinished at times (especially around the end which rushes you out the door with how lackluster it is plus it has things missing like sound/music for example that make you think they just didn't have time to add it) it is still the best Ghostbuster like video game to ever come out to date. The trap mechanic- while slightly different as in that it is a disc that you throw or can punch into a ghost to trap them- is way cooler than Ghostbusters does it because it causes what looks like a small black hole to erupt and suck everything in in a way that is similar but different to Ghostbusters. This game was clearly heavily inspired by Ghostbusters, and for some reason it remains incredibly obscure (very few to no people ever talk about it despite it being such a great game to play). The combat mechanics also feel really good, and there are puzzle elements that completely blows this game out of the water.I bring that game up because I wish it had studied that game at all. That game feels good to play, the various weapon types aren't a pain to use, and the only similarity is the trap mechanic which was clearly just parallel thinking. What I'm getting at is that it's just not fun to shoot at ghosts for the most part in this game. the concept is cool, and it's really awesome that they leaned into destructive set pieces so that you break stuff all the time when you fight ghosts, but it feels bad to do because they're beholden to the canon where the proton pack is not only inaccurate it apparently is also entirely unwieldy. While that is canon, that isn't fun to do with a controller as a mechanic. Ghost wrangling in this game is not fun, it's tedious and it never gets easier. The only way to make it slightly easier is trap dunking, but that is not intuitive to pull off and does not work reliably.Despite the mechanics not being fun, the story is great. Which is good because like I said there is about 3 movies worth of material here. I love that all the guys came back for this (except Rick Moranis) so we even got Egon since this was before the actor passed away. Bill Murray clearly was not easy to work with as, if you pay attention, as you get farther into the game you realize more and more he has less and less things to say and often starts just repeating his dialogue from earlier in the game. It's very clear Bill Murray did as little as possible on this. But it's cool they got him at all- to be fair. He is notoriously difficult.The other guys are all in on this, though, which is great. Dan, Harold, and Ernie are the same likable characters tehy played in the films, and much like Ghostbusters 2 they give Ernie even more to do which is cool as Winston may be my favorite Ghostbuster. Ernie Hudson is just too awesome.As with all games, this game becomes incredibly frustrating the farther you get in it. It's also from 2009 so that means when you die you have to replay the same dialogue and walk to a location over and over and over. The worst part is a lot of creatures one hit knock you down. As long as your'e with a team mate they pick you back up, but as you play single player the AI is often times clunky and just gets knocked out over and over and over so you constantly have to restart the checkpoint which is not fun at all. Moments when you're alone in the game just become a chore sometimes.The set pieces chosen for the game are great. You return to the Sedgewick twice, but it's slightly different both times. The first time is the most movie referencey, and the second changes it up a bit. There's also a museum, Times Square, A New York type public library, some ghost worlds, and a couple more locations. They are legitimately cool choices for the game.While some reviews I read in 2009 said the game relies too much on references, I did not really feel that way. It does make a lot of references, and talks about things that happen in the movies, it doesn't rely on these things. To me it felt more like it was expanding on a pre-existing canon- because it is.Bug wise there are two I can think of to mention. The game once or twice lost the trigger and would not advance after a long grueling fight and I had to restart the checkpoint and do it all over again to get the game to continue on. Also, you have to change the graphic settings every single time you play. The game does not remember your settings after you exit the game. These issues were irritating, but the trigger not activating thing only happened once or twice so it was not a game breaking thing. The settings issue is just irritating.Overall I only recommend this video game to Ghost Busters fans. The mechanics are aggravating, and often not fun to play, but the story is really good (basically it's Ghostbusters 3, 4, and 5 if you ask me) and they got the old team back together for one last hurrah which they will they will never be able to do again. It really is good for that, but you will at times have to struggle with the least interesting aspects (which is unfortunately the game play).If you like Ghostbusters this is definitely a must. The remaster is not bad- it looks better than it did on XBOX 360 (where I originally played it). Again, though, I played it on a SD TV at the time so I don't know what it looked like on an HD TV at the time- so is it improved? I don't know. Right now, though, in HD it looks great. The issues with it being too dark are not a problem. There are some animation lip sync issues where the voices do not line up with them talking in cut-scenes (pre-rendered, the in game looked fine) but overall the game looks fine for a game from 12 years ago.If you're not a fan of Ghostbusters I can't recommend it. You won't enjoy this game for it's mechanics alone. If you're interested in Ghostbusters- maybe a new fan or casual viewer- and want to check it out for the story you might like it, though. Play it on easy.

_childDocuments_.review: - I wasn't able to catch Ghostbusters: The Video Game when it was originally released (though I do remember wanting to play it), so I can't really compare the visuals to the original game. This 2019 remake does look pretty good, if just a touch dated. The lighting effects are nice, but some of the textures could have been a little more polished- The set pieces are diverse and well-crafted, except for the last level (more on that in a bit). I felt well-immersed in familiar locales like the Sedgewick Hotel and fire station, as well as the completely new sites- The music is quite good, but it's funny how little the developers were able to use of the iconic theme song. There's one moment in the game where you're riding in the ECTO-1 and the drum fill from the beginning starts, but it turns out to be a different song. At least they got to play part of the first verse at the top of the credits- The voice acting is, of course, the highlight here. Dan Aykroyd and Ernie Hudson were excellent. Harold Ramis does a pretty good rendition of Egon as well. As much as I was looking forward to hearing Bill Murray, some of his lines sound a little phoned-in. Maybe he was too busy thinking about that one time he dangled Seth Green over a garbage can- The story is actually pretty good, having been penned by Aykroyd and Ramis themselves- I was impressed with how well the game feels "Ghostbusters-y". They do a great job of capturing the feel of Ghostbusters I & II despite the difference in medium- Unfortunately, the one note this game can't hit is the humor of the films. None of the jokes land that well, except for the answering machine messages. Be sure to listen to those every time you're in the fire station- For the best laid-back time, kick down the difficulty if you're not trying to 100% the game. This gives you more time to soak in all the nostalgia- The game consists of a few long (1.5-2 hour) levels constrained to a distinct location. Just listen to what Ray and Egon say and enjoy the ride. All of the levels are fun except for the last one. It's really easy to get lost and turned around in the early parts of the level, and the section immediately before the final boss fight is a complete chore- Boss fights are pretty decent. Each one has its own quirks and requirements that they all feel unique- While the controls are sensible and the camera is well-behaved, doing some things in this game just feel janky. Capturing ghosts feels like a crapshoot most of the time until you unlock the slam dunk ability. The slime tethers also sometimes don't behave as expected- That said, it's smooth sailing most of the time. I kinda feel that certain moments could have been made more impactful with a tighter over-the-shoulder angle rather than the more distant 3rd-person perspective used in the game, though- I'm not feeling a second playthrough coming down the pipleline anytime soon. Maybe I'll return to pick up the other achievements someday- Coming in at only a little over 7 hours, the base price feels a little high. Luckily, this one goes on sale fairly often- If you love the first two films, you'll appreciate the game. It's definitely worth your time if you're a fan- I did have one weird crash out of nowhere in the cemetery level; the game had been running very well until that point. There was also an unusual bug on the same level where Ray just straight-up disappeared, requiring a checkpoint reload- . I'm so used to movie property games being dogwater that I didn't expect much from this. It was certainly a nice surprise. If you like the franchise, picking this one up is a no-brainer

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2009, long before there was any hope of a proper sequel movie to 1984's Ghostbusters and 1989's Ghostbusters 2, one of the best games ever released was made. Ghostbusters: The Video Game. A decade later, it was remastered in anticipation of the long awaited sequel, Ghostbusters Afterlife. Not related to the 1984 Ghostbusters the Video Game, made by malware developer Activision back when they actually made games instead, on the mighty and immortal Commodore 64 and every 8 bit computer and console known to man, and a few not known to man. GB:TVG has all the features of a great Ghostbusters game. Voice talents from the original talent from the movies, missing only Sigorney Weaver, Rick Moranis, and Bill Murray giving a damn. The plot derived from Ackroyd's GB3 script, and Dan and the late, great Harold Ramis having involvement in it's development. This game oozes atmosphere, making you feel like you are actually working along with the Ghostbusters, catching ghosts, blowing up half of New York City, and causing millions of dollars in damages. Like the OG movies, it treats the horror aspects somewhat seriously, and the humor comes from the interaction and response of the characters to the horrors they face. It is downright creepy at many points, especially in the Library level, though it never manages to have any real jump scares. As far as Ghostbusters, it hits all the high spots of the first movie, tying into it's plot and bringing it to a conclusion. It does have it's flaws; after all Bill Murray threw almost nothing into his lines, while cutting out early (and having the crew record what they did get at a golf course). While the proton pack and slime blower are lovingly used extensively, the additional weapons, which basically amount to a shotgun with a freeze ray, and an SMG with a LMG attachment, are basically useless. The PC version of the original release lacked online multiplayer for no good reason, and the remaster team was too lazy to bother even on consoles. Still, this is as close as you will get to playing a Ghostbuster and actually feeling like it in any video game. While it advertises as an HD remake, it really isn't. It locks up if you try to play in a resolution past 720p. Not a huge issue to me, since I still play Commodore 64 games and happily watch DVD-quality films (and VHS-quality home tapings of old wrestling shows). But if you're looking for 1080, forget it. 4k is just a dream for the next remaster in a decade or so. It really isn't any different than the original release, just slightly improved textures and a few minor changes here and there. It also seems to have messed with some of the triggers some, as I have had to run back and forth to get some to fire off after catching all the ghosts. A few times I also had ghosts get stuck behind walls or other objects, and stay there, necessitating me looking for them. Unfortunately, they've also broken the last stage of the game, making it impossible to complete. The stone angels one shot the Rookie or Ray, and the gate does not actually register being hit with the angels themselves. Thus, the game cannot be completed.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't write reviews but I had to come out for this one. To call this a "remaster" is really pushing it. The graphics are 2009, the game play is clunky and confusing. Voice acting is pretty decent, and it is cool to hear and see the original cast (except for Annie Potts -- it's her voice but the character looks NOTHING like her). What exactly is "remastered" about it?  The game throws far too much at you at once, in my opinion. You have sometimes 7 or 8 ghosts milling about throwing things at you and it takes far too long to grab one of them and trap it. If that's not enough, they will throw a bunch of "minions" at you at the same time that you have to destroy, not trap, and you have to let go of the ghost you are working on in order to take care of them, or you basically die. Seems like Doom with some Ghostbusters action added.  The fact that you cannot jump over debris is frustrating as well. and it is extremely difficult if not impossible to sprint while in combat, leaving you a sitting duck for most of the game. I spent more time waiting to be picked up off the ground by my teammates than actually fighting,  and if they all go down before you get up, it's game over. I had one point where I was down and not one but TWO of the other guys got hit and went down right as they were trying to revive me. And this is all on the medium difficulty setting. Can't imagine what it must be like to play on hard.  Your characters are too weak and go down much too easily. You have too little health and you can only shoot your proton stream for a view seconds before it gets too hot and you either have to "vent" (like reloading I guess) or else the pack "resets" which takes precious time. It's like firing a gun with three bullets that you have to keep reloading all the time.   Egon is constantly badgering you to scan everything. The scanning mechanism is clunky at best. If a ghost is attacking you, you basically have to absorb the damage, because you can't scan and fight at the same time. You have to hit X to switch back and forth. And speaking of the characters, Bill Murray is supposed to be the comedian of the group and throw out a bunch of witty on-liners, but he pretty much comes across as a jerk most of the time, not funny. This game really makes Venkman unlikeable, and he was my favorite character in the movie. If you play on ultra widescreen (3440x1440) you can't even see the entire screen. Text gets cut off on the top and bottom so you can't see what you are supposed to be doing. Best graphic setting I found is 2100x900 to resolve this, but even at full 3440x1440 the game feels like it's 640x480. You have little field of view and you can only see what's immediately in front of you. Very difficult to find flying ghosts to hit them with your proton pack. Reducing the resolution makes this effect even worse. There is no way to adjust the field of view either.  Overall I would not recommend this game. i got it on sale, which is fine, but if I had paid full price, I would have returned it after an hour. The fact that I didn't return it even at the sale price is probably motivated by the intense nostalgia I felt while playing it, which is one of the games only good qualities. Steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: Not much to be said about this game that hasn't been already stated in other reviews.  If you are a fan of the Original "Ghostbusters" movies, this is a must play.  The graphics are not amazing, but still hold up well if played in 4K with all settings on high.  And, due to it being an older game with just a facelift, you should be able to play it at 60 fps (which you have to enable in the options) without issue.  (I only have an RTX 2060 and i7 7700, and it ran flawlessly for me.)I found the controls to work pretty good, though there were some occasional camera issues that got in the way of aiming--but these were few and far between.  For the most part, your Ghostbusting pals will come to your aid when you get knocked down, and I didn't have too many instances where I had to revive them.I only encountered one "bug" in one of the missions, when a ghost decided to get stuck inside a wall, with two of the Ghostbusters attempting to walk through the wall to get at it.  It was pretty funny, tbh, but I had to go back to the last checkpoint to continue the game.  Overall, as just a fun game to waste some time, I give it an 8/10.  But, if you are a fan of the OG "Ghostbusters" who wants to relive your childhood dream of suiting up with Egon, Peter, Ray and Winston and blasting some spectral beings with an undocumented Nuclear Accelerator strapped to your back....this is a 10/10.Oh, Janine is in the game, too, snarky as ever. _childDocuments_.review: Its pretty good for an older game. in some places and cutscenes it looks pretty good while in others the older graphics falter. There are some minor bugs you may run into but typically quiting and restarting work. The only turnoffs are the relative lack of replayability unless you like achievement hunting which if you're good enough you'll get over half in your first playthrough. Other than that it does suffer from a lack of direction and some pacing issues. Sometimes it gets a little confusing because the solution to puzzles is either out of the way or not obvious. Sometimes the mechanics also get a bit confusing as you may succeed by just blasting your way through without actually knowing what you did or why it worked. The pacing difficulty is where sometimes the space between cutscenes and the actions you take around them do not always align. Also, sometimes the difficulty randomly spikes with a ton of small enemies being thrown at you at once. Though you'll really only struggle on the final mission with this. Other than these relatively small issues its a good game with a pretty good story. If you liked 1 and 2 you'll probably like the game. Its nice but also very strange that out of all the media franchises, its Ghostbusters to succeed at nearly everything. Good original and sequel movies with good script and effects a good cross media adaptations with comic books, cartoons, and a video game, a decent to good comeback sequel (afterlife), and finally a good healthy and growing fandom. Excluding the 2016 abomination, everything is coming up Ghostbusters.

_childDocuments_.review: I got and played the 'hell' out of the originals back when they came out as a kid for Christmas presents, both this realistic version on the Xbox360 and the stylized version on the original Wii, gotten 100% multiple times on both, and dumped hundreds of hours on both back in the day. I've always been a Ghostbusters fan and loved these games with a passion, coming back to it when I was bored or looking for something to do.Go to 2017, I re-bought the original as one of my first paid games on Steam, having to track down a key to redeem on steam just to play it 'one more time' thinking it was just going to be a nostalgia trip and that the game wasn't going to be as good as I remembered, boy was I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wrong. Graphics were a little dated, sound was as compressed as you'd expect from an early 2000's game, but the gameplay and story still stand up to this day.Got the remastered a week after it came out, and I play it the most. Pick it up, give it a try, I guarantee you'll enjoy it.P.S.The original actors were those to write and voice the game. _childDocuments_.review: Let me first make this clear that on the surface the game is actually pretty great! For a licensed adaptation of a classic franchise first relased in a past generation, Ghostbusters - The Videogame is actually a pretty faithful tribute to this classic, beloved IP and essentially functions as a sequel to the first 2 movies, complete with old actors returning to provide their voices and faces for the game. And you essentially play as a "self insert" mute character working as a new recruit in the team, working alongside your favourite characters and exploring (and ruining) iconic locations as you chase after ghosts & spooks from the movies (and a bunch of new freaks as well) - how cool is that?!Well, the thing is that while it's pretty cool that you get to actually zap some ghosts and suck them into traps, the problem is that the devs seemingly thought the players would get bored of just blasting ghosts and catching them into traps when... come on, it's Ghostbusters! This is what you're here for! But the dev team clearly did now have much confidence in that, because they start trying to... switch things up. And they do that by introducing alternative firing modes that essentially turn your blaster into a missile launcher, shotgun or SMG and even a LMG. And even though that's... fine, they also introduce a bunch of enemies like chandeliers turned into fireball-spitting spider like critters, violent animated globs of marshmallow goop, book-bats or pages of paper bound together with... ghost energy or something and turned into fast zombie-like things that try to claw you and give you mean papercuts. Basically just different types of critters to serve as cannon fooder attacking you en-masse and which you just zap to death instead of trying to wrangle them and drag them into traps like you do with normal ghosts. There's also these golem-things that essentially function as miniboss damage sponges, and which also just get "killed" rather than caught like ghosts. Whats worse is that shooting at those critters becomes more common as you go futher in the game, to the point where you'll get annoyed because you're just playing some cheap third-person shooter and not busting any ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ghosts. Matter of fact playing the game made me remember this weird ghost-busters game that was I think released on the Sega Genesis, where the Ghostbusters has weirdly big heads and rather than catch any ghosts you were just blasting a whole bunch of weird critters and animated objects. Were the devs inspired by that game? Because I don't think this is what I was asking for. Seriously, it's Ghostbusters! Why should I be just running around zapping random critters and wondering "man, when do I get to catch a ghost again" in a game that's supposed to be about catching ghosts?Another issue is that with all the fighting that you do in this game and with all the ghosts and gremlins that want to murder you... you and your fellow ghostbusters are just too frail. It's way too easy to get knocked down or even knocked out, and your companions really have a problem with staying on their feet in most fights - and if you get knocked out trying to get them up, its game over. It's pretty frustrating, especially with all sorts of enemies that can cheap shot you while you're trying to deal with another threat or revive another ghostbusterThen theres a bit of technical issues - other users mentioned various issues that didn't happen to me (or I just didn't notice them, alternatively they were fixed) however this "remaster" is a bit rough on the technical side - one issue I ran into first was that the game doesn't save any graphical settings because... it doesn't actually have anywhere to save them into. It's supposed to be a settings textfile located in a GHOSTBUSTERS directory in your AppData... but no such file exists, because theres no such folder either. The game is SUPPOSED to create the folder and the file, but it never actually does that on its own. You need to MANUALLY create the GHOSTBUSTERS folder inside the Local directory in your AppData - only then a file with the settings will actually be created. Its a weird problem, and the first time I run into something like this. Then there's stuff like the cutscenes running at 30 frames per second and non-HD resolution, and the fact that a lot of the animations (pay attention to other ghostbusters especially as they talk to somebody) are animated at 30 frames per second even if you run at 60, making them look choppy and janky. Opening the menu will also lock your game to 30 FPS. And even though this is a "remaster" there really isn't much graphical difference or any real changes compared with the original game - in fact the original game doesn't have the issues the remastered version brought. Huh.In short - worth it if you're a total GhostBusters maniac in need of a fix, but do be warned there's just not enough actual ghost busting. Anyone else - its pretty much a budget console third person shooter with the skin of a classic IP, buy at a big sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostbusters: The Video Game is a action-packed third person shooter in which you play as a new Ghostbuster recruit. While on a training exercise for said newbie, the Ghostbusters stumbleupon a new adventure and needs to save the world from yet another evil ghost. It takes place 2 years after the second movie. I don't really want to get too much into the story other than it's great, superb even. Main reason why, is that I feel this game can also double as a thrid Ghostbusters movie. The story of the game was writen by Dan Aykroyd and Harold Ramis, the game uses all the actors likeness and voices. There is a "in memory of" for Harold Ramis, which is a nice added touch. The voice acting is good, but you can tell that Bill Murray didn't try as hard. Gampeplay is solid and......YOU GET TO USE A PROTON PACK!!!!! _childDocuments_.review: Ghostbusters sounds familiar enough but I've never seen it before. The shooting is not exciting, your only gun feels like plastic without recoil and no need to reload, just don't keep shooting otherwise it will overheat, bullets are replaced by fire/thunderlight or toxic liquid squirt towards ghosts like you are a firefighter. For those ghosts that can only be defeated by traps, it becomes a bit tricky because your teammates are hopeless and mostly just drag ghosts everywhere except the traps on the ground, so you have to place the trap nearby then catch it yourself, and repeat it 100 times.It has some unique design, like there's a number that appears on the top right cover. At first I thought that's how much money you earn, but no, it turned out to be the amount of value you broke. So if you limit damage during the mission you will be appreciated by the owner and if not, you'll get sour scolding at the end. You also walk into another dimension through mystical item, or a time crack, and use a new kind of bullet which looks like a string that seams 2 floating lands closer so as to cross. Most of the time I'm busy shooting flying ghosts, other times I'm on the ground waiting to be revived, or holding a detector to find hidden encyclopedias. Can't say fun but not too boring.It's hard to rate this game, I played 3.5 hours and it feels like 7. By this way, I only recommend to people who are familiar with the title and want to extend experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is the REAL Ghostbusters 3!Originally coming out in 2009 when talks of a Ghostbusters sequel on the silver screen had all but faded outside of rumors and speculation, it served as a hell of a boost for the Ghostbuster’s series in the eyes of fans and newcomers alike! While some brushed it off as a cash-grab, those who actually played it were left speechless. It was straight up a legit sequel to Ghostbusters 2, featuring talent from the entire original cast! And while Rick Moranis was nothing but a reference and Dana was a no-show in the game, the devs managed to get the additional talent of William Atherton as Peck, Annie Potts as Jenine, the unmistakable Brian Murray as the Mayor and even the Legendary Max Von Sydow as Vigo the Carpathian! That’s a hell of a roster for a movie, let alone a videogame!Yet time moves on and eventually the original steam release disappeared and original copies became harder to come across. But eventually it reared it’s remastered head once more… as an Epic Games exclusive!But a year later, it finally lands on steam once more. Is this remaster all it’s cracked up to be considering it’s now 10 gigabytes larger? Oh yeah, you betcha!The game starts off 2 years after the events of Ghostbusters 2, the crew are facing increasing paranormal activity in New York City and decide to bring in a new recruit, a doughy-faced young lad who despite his fear and apprehension is more then willing to do anything to gain the trust and favor of his Childhood Heroes. Or at the very least, be a very good human guinea pig for all the new experimental proton-pack firemodes!Story-wise, it’s a damn treat! Every character feels so genuine, especially considering it was written by many of the actors! And while it’s no masterpiece, I can’t deny the quips and humor feel like such a breathe of fresh air compared to the disappointment of the 2016 reboot. Likewise, the tone, atmosphere and even the music feel so on-point with the Original 84’ classic!On the gameplay front, it’s a damn treat! While some have accused the game of being a Third-Person Shooter with a Ghostbuster’s paintjob, it downplays the fun design of the enemies you face with the help of your proton packs! While some levels are filled with physical enemies of everyday objects possessed by ghosts, you straight up go to town on rooms of specters (as well as the room itself, sheesh! This game is destructible!) who want nothing more then to drag you to hell! And with 8 new fire-modes in your proton pack, dozens of different foes to trap or shatter, your fight through New York City is anything but forgettable!So what’s wrong? Not much if you ask me!I’ve had times where the ridiculous destructibility snags me in tight spots, some arena’s are a bit tricky to trap ghost and face physical enemies at once who have a heavy tendency to knock the rookie down on his ass but that comes down to identifying the real threat first at the end of the day. Also, the last two levels no longer count your destruction bill which takes the fun out of wrecking rooms if you ask me!Perhaps the biggest gripe I have is that it’s too short at only 7 levels, one of which is a revisit. I’ve also encountered one crash but some folks had nothing but crashes so maybe I was just lucky.But after putting in so many hours just fiddling with arena’s and racking up millions of dollars in damage, I couldn’t recommend this remaster enough. After the death of Harold Ramis in 2014, I can’t help but feel this is the ultimate send-off to the original crew.Strap on that Unlicensed Nuclear Accelerator and start trapping some Ghosts, New-Blood!

_childDocuments_.review: Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered successfully captures the charm and spirit of the original films, offering fans what many consider to be the unofficial third movie in the series. When it first released, the game was lauded for its impressive graphics and immersive gameplay, which effectively brought the world of Ghostbusters to life. The character models, voice acting performed by the original actors, and the detailed environments all contributed to a richly authentic Ghostbusters experience.The remastered version, while still showcasing visuals that have aged reasonably well, brings enhancements that honor the original art style, ensuring that it feels undeniably Ghostbusters. It strikes a fine balance between maintaining the nostalgic essence of the 2009 release and updating elements to meet modern expectations. On the Steam Deck, this game performs exceptionally well, with controls and graphics that adapt smoothly to the portable format, allowing players to bust ghosts on the go. This combination of faithful adaptation and portability makes Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered a fantastic choice for both longtime fans and newcomers eager to step into the boots of their favorite paranormal investigators. The game also serves as a poignant tribute to Harold Ramis, preserving his iconic portrayal of Egon Spengler for new generations and longtime fans alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Twelve years ago Terminal Reality still existed as a game development company and were probably best known for their BloodRayne franchise. It was still a few years before Kinect Star Wars and The Walking Dead: Survival Instinct would become the final nails in their coffin, but even then they weren’t known to make good games. Often curious titles with some neat ideas, yes. But not what you’d call “good”. And Ghostbusters: The Video Game, originally released in 2009, wasn’t “good” either. But it wasn’t terrible and had some cool things about it. All these years later, the Remastered version of the game doesn’t get better.To start off, I need to mention that the possibly most notable part of Ghostbusters: The Video Game is the fact, that the story of the game is based around an unproduced script for a sequel to the original two Ghostbusters movies. That, and the fact that most of the original cast returned as voice actors and all, apart from Bill Murray who’s clearly there for the paycheck and nothing else, sound excited to be part of the story. This, given that the original movie still holds up as a fantastic mix of comedy, sci-fi and horror, should inspire confidence, but just as the sequel film, it’s very hard to justify this game’s story existence. In many ways, it is a repeat of the same story bits and locations from the original movies, but in a less interesting way and with far fewer jokes landing.Same goes for the gameplay, which works as a very primitive third person shooter from the era (except with no cover). Granted, shooting the proton pack and slime is exciting and both of these tools are actually fun to use for both combat and puzzle solving. But on practice they eventually become far less useful in comparison with basically a machine gun and a shotgun, which work as one would expect. Mostly because of how enemies rather quickly get switched from ghosts you need to trap to just hordes of fodder you shoot. There’s no nuance to the shooting, most locations are terrible gameplay-wise, mechanic of buying upgrades feels slapped on and most of the optional stuff is more often just a bother to do and isn’t worth it.Which is a shame, since there are cool ideas here. Visually the game wasn’t fantastic even for 2009, but the locations had style. Some of the sequences and gimmicks to the locations, ghosts and tools are genuinely inventive and fun. And a lot of the geeky speudo-scientific elements are, just like in the movies, really intriguing. When everything comes together, – the mechanics, the jokes, the situations, – the game is a blast. But Tron 2.0 this is not, as most of the time Ghostbusters: The Video Game is mediocre and sometimes it’s outright frustrating. Remastered edition, actually, doesn’t help much, if any. Settings resetting every launch of the game, awkward sound and music cuts everywhere, weird interface bugs… It’s not very good.Ghostbusters: The Video Game, original or Remastered, isn’t a terrible game. It has some curious things and can be interesting. But it’s not good either and it never was. If you’re a die-hard fan of the franchise, you probably played it back when it got released originally. Otherwise, I can’t really recommend playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I did have a harmless bug where the settings wouldn't save. This could've been caused by the couple of mods I installed but Idk. I resolved it by manually creating a "ghostbusters" folder in my %LOCALAPPDATA% and copying over "settings.ini".Aside from that, I HIGHLY recommend this game. As someone who loves the characters and comedy of the original movie and loves Luigi's Mansion, this game honestly couldn't be a better fusion of the two. You play as a silent protagonist, and each ghostbuster reacts to you appropriately. Venkman couldn't care less about you and wants to move on with the story, Stanz is highly eager to explain the intricacies of ghost capturing, Spengler is very blunt and focused on the research, and Winston feels like he respects you as a fellow employee just trying to earn a living and enjoy the spectacle.The game plays as you would expect with a nice handful of tools in addition to the proton beam. The upgrade system is unremarkable, but the money/destruction mechanic was great! The game isn't terribly long but has enough levels and story to feel worth the purchase for me. There are collectable objects in the levels and you can scan ghosts to get information about them. It's a focused game in that it's basically just the levels, brief intermissions in the firehouse, and a handful of extra secrets to find. That being said, the levels themselves each feel like climactic set pieces in their own way and the good character writing makes some of the encounters more memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game!  Pudgy highly recommends play in window mode, and to do so, follow instructions below. _childDocuments_.review: The nostalgia is incredibly strong and it's pretty great to have the main cast together for one last adventure. It definitly have the feel of the first two movies, it was after all written by Akroyd and Raimis and the entire cast is back. For the most part fairly solid, if a bit repetitive 3rd person shooter gameplay. The different weapons (shotgun stream, machine gun stream, rocket...) you had was a little silly, but i get why they where added to give a bit more gameplay and, lets face it, to apease the shooter demographics. I do feel it was a really bad choice to add a fifth, ghostbuster as the player that's just kind of there and at most does something goofy in the background, but with zero impact on the plot other than constant "-Oh look, the newbie found the way". it didn't add anything, at least have some minor character customization if you are going to make a player insert. It would have been much better to either switch between the main cast on missions or if you have to have a new character for the player, make them a character that actualy has an impact on the story. It's a minor complaint, but I really feel the game would have been better.The graphics is defintly starting to age, mostly in the character models, it's the typical seventh generation uncany valley where character models had this distinct look where graphical fidelity is starting to make the characters look like humans but mostly looks like manequinns. But all the minor complaints aside, it was a great time, and you will especially like it if you love the series.

_childDocuments_.review: It is rare for a movie-based game to not only retain their cast and likenesses but to also have a good storyline. For all intents and purposes, this is essentially the Ghostbusters 3 we never had. Bill Murray, Dan Aykroyd, Ernie Hudson and Harold Ramis all seemed to be quite enthusiastic with their delivery as well!The gameplay loop is pretty enjoyable. You play as a new recruit on the Ghostbusters team and things start to go sideways almost immediately after you sign up (Considering the character is not voiced, I would have liked if they had given us the option of choosing either a male or female character, but alas, male only here). The variety in enemies is pretty good and the locations you go to are great as well. We see a return of both well-known ghouls as well as new ones.My only real complaint is that the Ghostbusters treat you as a bit of an inexperienced grunt even though you prove yourself through the levels, time and time again. I suppose it was assumed that it would be seen as some sort of playful hazing, but it irked me a bit. Not enough for me to not recommend the game though.Recommended!

It turns into a run-and-gun FPS pretty quickly, and while it's got a unique twist on the formula, the game would be effectively unchanged if you had a few different guns instead of different wand attachments. If you're looking for interesting ghost hunting, this isn't really where you're going to find it. If your down for a solid, originally casted Ghost Buster game and are ok with the fact that it plays like a late 2000s sci-fi shooter, then I definitely recommend it. If not, this is probably a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a real tough one to review. I think part of it is the multitude of "streams" in the proton pack. It easily could have combined/eliminated the streams down to just two options. I generally prefer FPS but have nothing against a third person view, but this one was very wide/off-center view that had me running into walls and things because of it.Don't even get me started on the mechanics of capturing ghosts though. _childDocuments_.review: I'm compelled to write this review simply because it'll be therapeutic for me. How dare so many gamers give this game a glowing review?! For shame! Blast. Overheat. Repeat. Heaven forbid you would want to put the thing away (you know, to see better), but as soon as you do, the game prompts you to equip it again. And that's not the only prompt! The game also constantly harasses you to purchase upgrades... sometimes at the worst possible times. So far, I've failed more missions in this game than COD, Battlefield and HALO combined! Why so difficult? As I write these words, know that I'm only at the Azetlor boss battle (the first one), and it feels like I'll never defeat him. _childDocuments_.review: I cant really say anything about the remaster since I never played the original PS3, PC, or Xbox360 version, I only played the Wii version which was totally different compared to this one, it was technically a totally different game. It's not that great in terms of graphics: the hair on the characters look really bad,it's like looking at dark brown TV static, some cutscenes still use the old FMVs so they are grainy and blurry and some cutscenes have the camera and environment moving fluently while the NPCs move at 30 frames, game is locked at 30Hz by default every time you boot up the game, and on wider resolutions the on-screen messages and subtitles bleed off the screen. The game gets the job done at running fine, that's all i can really say.Talking about the game itself, busting really made me feel good. it's a fun third person shooter with proton packs and spirits. The gang's all here with the original actors portraying as themselves, Slimer escapes his little chamber and wreaks havoc at the hotel again, Stay Puft is resurrected, and the Ghostbusters revisit the library for redemption to capture the Grey Lady after failing to capture her on their first mission. This game screamed fan service by bringing back familiar faces, recalling past events, and expanding the Ghostbusters lore considering this game WAS Ghostbusters 3 when no one knew that another movie would come to fruition or existence. It's really worth a shot to play if you dont own the original. The price is for you to decide whether or not it's worth 25 dollars for a game that doesnt really look like a remaster.
