_childDocuments_.review: As someone has said already: this is the best ghostbusters game in existence.  But... it's far from being the best game in existence.Not too long ago i have played the "Terminator Resistance" game and it feels like the Ghostbusters fall in the same category as the "Resistance": fun for fans. If we take those games and swap the surroundings, sounds, protagonists and NPC for some other no-name/random assets, while leaving the levels and gameplay exactly the same - would those games still be cool? To be honest they would be "kinda playable/meh" at best. But return all the "trademarked" stuff in and suddenly you have an awesome nostalgia rollercoaster.What i want to say here, is that if you have seen and enjoyed the Ghostbusters 1-2 movies - then definitely get this game, i'm quite sure you will enjoy being the original 4's sidekick in a what is by all means "Ghostbusters 3" movie but in a videogame form.But if you have never seen the movie or did not like it, it is a different story. In such a case, tbh, i think you better pass this one, since purely from the gaming point of view i can't say it's a "must play" type of a game.As a Ghostbusters lover myself, I'm obviously giving this game a "thumbs up". But as for you - decide for yourself how much do you want to meet Peter, Ray, Winston, Egon and the Marshmallow Man to forgive the game's numerous shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a Ghostbusters game done right.  You play as the newest recruit alongside the iconic four, voiced by the original actors.  You track supernatural energy, shoot proton streams, and drag ghosts into traps and all the other stuff you would expect as a ghostbuster.  Though I do recommend this game, I also recommend that you do NOT play this game on pro difficulty.  I usually play games on hard mode, so I chose pro level at the beginning.  However, your character is very fragile and goes down after two or three hits.  Then you wait for one of your NPC companions to revive you.  Should all of you be defeated, you lose.  I actually like this idea of this mechanism as it emphasizes the camaraderie and teamwork between characters and adds a dimension of strategy, deciding whether to risk fighting without backup or risk trying to revive fallen companions.  However, the AI of the other ghostbusters is terrible.  They sometimes go on fighting rather than reviving you right away, or they walk right into an enemy AOE to get to you, joining you in defeat.  They are also picky about the angle they choose to revive you, sometimes navigating around debris to find just the right spot while taking damage all the while.  In some cases they charge ahead into swarms of enemies when a strategic use of cover would make a lot more sense.  This problem is compounded when you are on a mission with just one other ghostbuster, especially Ray who really seems to take his time to revive you.  The upshot of this is repeating levels over and over, losing because your companions keep making terrible choices and often fail to make reviving you their top priority.  Some boss fights were quite easy, but others took me literally days to defeat, and I gave up on the final boss fight where you spend half your time reviving fallen NPCs only to have them go down again almost immediately.  If repeating levels over and over waiting for an AI to make the right moves is your idea of fun, go ahead and crank the difficulty.  Otherwise, just enjoy the game on normal where the AI's blunders are less likely to create repeated defeats.

_childDocuments_.review: Third person shooters is one of my favorite genres of video games, and I had the original version of this Ghostbusters game on PC, but I never played it because the game would unfortunately always freeze on me (probably largely due to my terrible PC at that time). So my first experience with this game was October 2022 when I bought this remastered version on Steam, and I gotta say... This game hold up! I loved it!I had a blast with this game. The dialogue is just so good. It is not very often in games that I go out of my way to try to pay attention to every line of dialogue, but that is how I felt playing through this game. I'm not even a die-hard Ghostbusters fan. I like the movies, but I don't love them. This game made me actually care more about the franchise than the movies did.Now, I have only played through this game once on the "casual" difficulty, so when I try the harder difficulties I am expecting to find it a little more frustrating. So keep that in mind when you choose your difficulty. I have played tons of 3rd person shooters including RE2r, RE3r, RE4, RE5, RE6, RE-Rev, RE-Rev2, Vanquish, Dead Space, Evil Within, and Control... And as of this review, I would say that Ghostbusters is now up there among my favorite 3rd person shooters; I enjoyed it more than Dead Space, Evil Within, or Control. Ghostbusters doesn't beat the Resident Evil games, but the Resident Evil games are my favorite 3rd person shooters of all time (especially RE4), so coming in right after those should tell you I really like this game.I haven't run into a single crash like I used to with the original PC version of the game. :)

The characters, humor and the fact you're a ghostbuster is the driving point of the game, your proton pack is very fun to use and each mode has multiple fire modes, though I wish they implemented them more organically in the story, and that they used the slime tether to its full potential.There is a lot of references and fanservice and a good enough enemy variety. Game should last from 6 to 8 hours to the average player and its definitely worth a pickup on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun Ghostbusters adventure.  Also a very enjoyable story with good graphical enhancements to bring it up to modern times.  If the producers/writers of "Ghostbusters: Afterlife" had made a couple minor lore/story changes (and I really do mean small) in the movie, then "Ghostbusters The Video Game" could easily have been accepted as canon in the Ghostbusters story/franchise/lore, too bad it wasn't.  Would have been super cool.There were occasional glitches with event triggers activating to progress the game, but reloading from the last checkpoint always fixed the trouble.What really made the game for me was the return of the main actor core to voice their character's, Bill Murray, Dan Aykroyd, Harold Ramis (RIP), Ernie Hudson, Annie Potts and WIlliam Atherton.  Special shoutout to Brian Doyle-Murray as well; even though he was a psychiatric ward doctor in the original Ghostbusters, I instantly recognized his voice as the Mayor and it helped that the mayor's appearance was clearly modeled after him too.  He does so many movies with Dan Aykroyd and Bill Murray that it was a hoot to hear him in the game too.Really felt like I was a real Ghostbuster.  Would Ghostbust again!

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Ghostbusters fan, this game is such a treat to play every time, yet not alienating to anyone unfamiliar with the IP. Story is action packed, funny, full of charm, almost everyone from the original cast returns (minus Sigourney Weaver and Rick Moranis), tons of little details for long time fans to find, it's such a blast. Plays like a normal third person shooter but it can stand on it's own with the ghostbusting mechanics of making sure your pack doesn't overheat, throwing traps, switching between equipment, dodging and reviving, with tons of upgrades to unlock along the way. In remaster terms, this game isn't much different from the original 2009 release, higher fidelity textures, face models look clearer, especially in the more advanced cutscenes like the elevator in the Sedgewick level, but overall it's practically the same, can perform the same tricks and glitches. Only fault this remaster has is the developers weren't able to fulfill the rebuilt multiplayer, giving the game only the singleplayer story, different changes like loading screens being a static image with tips instead of the original's GB theme playing along with a 3D model of equipment along with gameplay in the background. In-game cutscenes weren't remastered and cuts to them are very noticeable with the quality dropping. Overall, this is a very faithful remaster with everything in-tact, a good distraction if you want to waste an afternoon.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely the best Ghostbusters video game of all time. If you're looking for fan service, this game provides it in spades! It's linear, but each level does allow for a bit of exploration, to find hidden artifacts. Besides the satisfaction of finding these hidden goodies, you get a big cash boost for each one you find, making it possible to buy all the upgrades barely halfway through the game if you're vigilant.As far as video games go in general, I'd say it's pretty good. Not great, not going to win any awards, but definitely worth your time and is enjoyable. There is ONE part that is pretty frustrating where the difficulty even on Casual spikes to an 11 for like no reason. I will try to keep this as spoiler free as I can but there's a point in the game where you have to smash flying enemies into a gate to break it down. The problem is you're swarmed from all sides, from the air and on the ground, and odds are you'll end up dying over and over...and over..and over..and rage quitting, then trying again a week later and dying over and over again until you either finally get lucky and pull it off, or get fed up and delete it. But there's a trick! Ignore what the Ghostbusters are suggesting and just run back and forth in front of the gate and focus solely on dodging and taking out the monsters swarming you from the ground. The flyers will attempt to ram into you, and most likely hit the gate instead as long as you keep moving. It still might take a couple tries, especially on Professional, but it's WAY easier than trying to play that scene as the developer intended.Anyway, it's a pretty short experience as far as PC games go, at around 15 hours if you make a point to explore. But if you grew up in the 80s and 90s and always wanted to shoot a proton pack as a kid, this is definitely the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Ghostbusters game ever made and still holds up today.With Ghostbusters Afterlife on the horizon to fill the role of "official third film" following this arc, prior to that this game was considered by many (myself included) to be our Ghostbusters III.  Written by Dan and Harold and voiced by the entire original cast, this is just excellent story telling.  This game not only tells its own independent story, but goes back to the original film and even parts of the second, with nods and references to both hidden all over.  For one, Slimer is here in the firehouse as is a certain painting some may be familiar with...One of the coolest aspects of this game is the firehouse and world of the Ghostbusters.  Finally you can walk around the entire firehouse and see some of those  easter eggs mentioned earlier, including an upgraded containment unit, packs being assembled, the dorm room and even have the ability to go down the fire pole...or roam the halls of the Sedgewick Hotel which feels straight out of the movie.Not only is this game voiced by the original cast, but, the sounds and music you remember from here are all present to.  Gameplay is exceptional.  Instead of stepping into the shoes of a veteran ghostbuster, you are "the rookie" trying out on his first day.  The gameplay is exceptional.  From walking around to using the proton pack, everything feels as authentic as you think it would.  The proton pack has some power and kick, you put down your own trap and even have to "wrangle" the ghosts you catch into the trap.  It can be challenging sometimes!  The pack itself is awesome.  It contains your HUD all in the pack and it doesnt distract but fits right in with the other gear.  SPOILER TERRITORY: Fans of the lore of the original film will know this story heavily follows Gozer lore and the Shandor family.  It builds on an already epic story and really gets you hooked.Cant recommend more for Ghostbusters fans or just people looking for a fun and well fleshed out game!

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR: Great game with a good story combining elements from the first two movies. Controls are a bit cumbersome and basic, but since it offers several hours of addictive gameplay, I recommend picking this up during a sale.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I remember when this was released on the PS3 in 2009. I thought it was a great concept, but I also thought the demo sucked, leaving a lot to be desired. So I never bothered buying it. But seeing it as a remastered version at a cheap-as-chips price during a sale, I had to grab it.I've read other reviews saying that this game could be considered an interactive version of the third movie we all wanted. Not the third movie we got. I disagree. The content in this game doesn't really bring anything new to the table. What it DOES do though, quite brilliantly, is reflect and expand on content from the first two movies we all know and love.We get a deeper glimpse into the world of Gozer. We get a bit of backstory on the library ghost from the first movie. And we see the proton packs upgraded to be able to spray caustic-neutralising green slime, with a spray gun reminiscent of the ones used in the second movie to coat the inside of the Statue of Liberty with pink slime.We also get voices from most of the original cast, which is a rare bonus by today's standards, never mind 12 years ago!The game is dedicated to the memory of Harold Ramis. A fitting tribute to one of the great minds behind the Ghostbusters movies, and the story for this game along with Dan Aykroyd.I have 4.5 hours logged at the time of writing this review, and if other reviews are anything to go by, I still have at least another 4 to go before completion. But here's what I like, and what I don't like so much, so far:The appearances of the ghosts and the proton streams are straight out of the movies. The effects are amazing. But graphics in other areas really let the visuals down. You can see all the lights on the proton packs flashing and running their sequences. But get close to one of those packs, and it looks like a kid's drawing. On the whole though, the graphics are certainly acceptable, and don’t ruin the experience in any way.I like that you play as an additional team member, not as one of the main four characters. It allows you to experience the game as a total rookie without impeding on the dialogues or banter between the others. And there are a few classic one-liners in those dialogues too. Ramis and Aykroyd did a splendid job penning the script for this game.Between missions, you can roam around the firehouse. In fact, I would encourage you to do so. See if you can spot any Easter eggs!The sounds and music from the movies have been used in the game too. Elmer Bernstein’s unmistakable score works fantastically well in creating the perfect atmosphere for the task in hand, especially when the odd ghosty appears out of nowhere!I like that we get to use a few different pieces of equipment too. The famous Spectrovisors (called Paragoggles in the game) are used in conjunction with the PKE meter to help you locate spooks and items of interest. Also, for decades we wondered what all of that equipment on the roof of Ecto-1 was for. In the game, you get to use at least one of those items. Additionally, one of the videos which can be unlocked during the game is a 15 minute documentary covering the refurbishment of the car in 2007, in which Dan Aykroyd test drives the finished project. He also explains that although the car setup was deliberately designed to have a comically overkill appearance, every item included on the roof was designed for a specific purpose. It wasn't just a collection of random objects.I feel this is one of those games where more available input commands would be hugely beneficial. Instead, what we have is essentially five controls: choose weapon, choose trigger, equip PKE meter/goggles, interact, and jump/evade (which rarely works). If you happen to have your PKE meter and goggles equipped, you need to UN-equip them before you can use your proton pack. There’s nothing automatic here. This puts you at a huge disadvantage if a ghost suddenly appears while attacking you.The temperamental jump action is about as much use as a lighthouse in the desert, especially since every ghost you encounter will spend 99% of its time attacking just you, only momentarily diverting its attention to the other characters if you run away. Constantly being smacked down when there’s very little you can do about it gets boring fast. And if you happen to be alone when that happens, with no other characters around to revive you, it’s Mission Failed! You can then respawn from the last checkpoint. Depending on which mission you are on though, that last checkpoint can be some time back, and I’m really not into lengthy repetition in procedural games!There’s not always a clear understanding of what you should be doing either. You can look at your PKE meter screen at any time to see your current objective, but more often than not, you find yourself just heading into one big shoot ‘em up scenario. Some of these seem to go on for hours too, with ghost after ghost appearing relentlessly – often in far too many numbers for you to handle alone – while the rest of your team stands there doing nothing but shouting unhelpful instructions at you. It becomes both tedious and uninteresting when these moments occur. Even more so if you happen to encounter the “untrappable ghost” bug. This often requires you to restart the game, at which point you’ll spawn back in at the last checkpoint.Some of the equipment upgrades seem to have very little to no effect. And many of them are not cheap!Being a casual modder, I was hoping to find some way of editing the game files in an attempt to “tune out” some of the clunkiness of the game mechanics and improve the overall experience. Although modding seems to have been achieved by other players, information on modding this title appears to be very limited, with downloads and resources only seemingly available from more questionable websites.The good and bad points about this game seem to be on an equal footing. I haven’t listed everything in this review. But for every good point I can think of, I can think of at least one bad one. That said, the game has had me coming back for more since I first launched it a few days ago, and despite the odd bug with untrappable ghosts, I would still highly recommend the game to anyone who is a fan of the original movies. I’m not sure I would have been happy paying the full price for it, but it’s a steal at less than 5 bucks during the Summer Sale. I’m looking forward to playing more of it around Halloween!

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute delight of a video game. As if someone read my mind and wanted to know exactly what I wanted to play, then proceeded to make it. Ghostbusters: The Video Games is basically a full third movie, which also happens to be playable. Very much in style of a third person shooter and it borrows its HUD from Dead Space, putting all necessary information on your proton pack. You're a fan of the movies and cartoons? You will find countless references to all of them inside the Firehouse, including a portrait of Vigo, once again voiced by the late Max von Sydow. It's also a game from 2009, so even with the Remaster don't expect any wonders. You can still see how the game aged, but the sound work is still amazing. Still, they did a lot of work, making previously console-only pre-order DLC available on PC for the first time. Finish the game on Normal to play in the grey jumpsuit from Ghostbusters II (sadly, with a covered up insignia) and on Hard to get a Golden Proton Pack. Too bad they never added the Multiplayer mode.Still, this is a love letter to Ghostbusters and one of the best games ever to be based on the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros - Original Ghostbusters images, voices, sound, and music.  If that is the essential selling point, then this game delivers.  Many of the levels are very well done.  Fairly detailed.  Ghostbusting is fun.Cons - Ghostbusters slapped on a middling FPS.  Levels can be repetitive.  Limited player interactions.  Story could have been refined.  The script can be slightly redundant at key segues.  Very short title.  I completed the game in 10.5 hours.  For comparison, I have 500 hours in Fallout 4 and have yet to complete the game.Overall - There is enough original Ghostbusters content to recommend the game to Ghostbusters fans.  If you are a fan, you will likely enjoy the show.  The music and sound are resplendent.  But the experience is somewhat lacking.  I want to play more Ghostbusters (even if just a retelling of Ghostbusters I & II) with similar original content, but in an open and interactive world, with role-playing expansion.

_childDocuments_.review: I can easily see how one might find Ghostbusters lacking. It's short, no new game + or other modes, has a paper-thin plot, and quite literally no character development. Venkman shares a kiss with the damsel of the story near the end, and it feels incredibly awkward, as we've spent little time with either character at all and have seen no relationship develop between the two. By no means a great or must-play title, but if you're a fan of the franchise and PS2-era game design you'll get a kick out of it. Fair asking price: $10-$20

_childDocuments_.review: A gameplay-rich story-driven movie-game sequel with a fitting amount of horror and humour. Inventive enemies and entertaining boss fights. Only two unbalanced fight sequences of note: one boss fight early game and one scripted ambush very late game are disproportionately difficult compared to the rest of the game, especially on Professional difficulty. Graphics are great, though the cutscenes can vary in quality. Contains 42 unique collectables that stick around for your playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Ghostbusters: The Video Game Remastered

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit, I am not the biggest fan of the Ghostbusters movies.  But this game was truly enjoyable.  After sitting through a long intro with no sound the next time I entered the game pressing ESC was able to skip it.  I play in wide screen and had zero problems.  I saw two other reviews mentioning problems with that so I thought I would mention them.  The original casts' voice talent was awesome to hear.  Their acting was on the mark for a movie but a tad bit off for a game...but it didn't really matter.  Each weapon had a purpose.  Each level was varied so the game didn't become repetitive.  There was just enough variation in enemy ghosts to make the game interesting though they did then to reuse.  Game mechanics were easy to learn and wrangling ghosts became second nature by the middle of the game.  Okay, that was the boring stuff.  Here is the bottom line.  This game was FUN.  It may not have been like walking into the movies but it was definitely the game version of it.  It brought back good memories and added to them with newer, fun memories.  Even if you aren't a big fan of the movies, like me, you will still enjoy this.  Definitely worth getting without a doubt!

name: Metro Exodus
detailed_description: Owners of Metro Exodus are also entitled to the Metro Exodus PC Enhanced Edition - a stunning visual upgrade that REQUIRES a Ray-Tracing Capable GPU as part of the minimum spec. The DLC for Metro Exodus is also Enhanced – purchasing the Metro Exodus Expansion Pass, or The Two Colonels / Sam’s Story individually, entitles you to the Enhanced version of that content, accessible via the Metro Exodus PC Enhanced Edition. Metro Exodus The year is 2036. A quarter-century after nuclear war devastated the earth, a few thousand survivors still cling to existence beneath the ruins of Moscow, in the tunnels of the Metro. They have struggled against the poisoned elements, fought mutated beasts and paranormal horrors, and suffered the flames of civil war. But now, as Artyom, you must flee the Metro and lead a band of Spartan Rangers on an incredible, continent-spanning journey across post-apocalyptic Russia in search of a new life in the East. Metro Exodus is an epic, story-driven first person shooter from 4A Games that blends deadly combat and stealth with exploration and survival horror in one of the most immersive game worlds ever created. Explore the Russian wilderness across vast, non-linear levels and follow a thrilling story-line that spans an entire year through spring, summer and autumn to the depths of nuclear winter. Inspired by the novels of Dmitry Glukhovsky, Metro Exodus continues Artyom’s story in the greatest Metro adventure yet. Features Embark on an incredible journey - board the Aurora, a heavily modified steam locomotive, and join a handful of survivors as they search for a new life in the East Experience Sandbox Survival - a gripping story links together classic Metro gameplay with new huge, non-linear levels A beautiful, hostile world - discover the post-apocalyptic Russian wilderness, brought to life with stunning day / night cycles and dynamic weather Deadly combat and stealth - scavenge and craft in the field to customize your arsenal of hand-made weaponry, and engage human and mutant foes in thrilling tactical combat Your choices determine your comrades’ fate - not all your companions will survive the journey; your decisions have consequence in a gripping storyline that offers massive re-playability The ultimate in atmosphere and immersion - a flickering candle in the darkness; a ragged gasp as your gasmask frosts over; the howl of a mutant on the night wind - Metro will immerse and terrify you like no other game…

_childDocuments_.review: "This is Moscow, do you hear me? ST，Petersburg? Vladivostok? Voronezh? Novosibirsk? Do you hear me? This is Moscow! We're alive! I don't know if you heard us before... we couldn't hear you. We thought we were the only ones left. We thought... there wasn't anyone else. Nobody and nothing, do you understand? How could you understand? You've been chattering to each other all this time... while we... oh lord, thank god that you're alive! That you're there. Out there... Singing songs. How are you out there? We've been here all these years. Underground. We were afraid even to stick our head out. We thought there was nowhere to go, can you believe that? We had no radio. There were no signals. Some bastard here set up jammers... in Moscow. In Balashikha. And they hid you from us. It was as if it was as if we were deaf. And blind. We sat here for twenty years... I've been here for twenty years, and im only twenty six... sitting here, down under the ground. My name's Artyom. Down in the basement, in the Metro. Did you at least try to find us? I tried to find you... we tried. We thought the whole world had been burnt up, the whole planet... That there ws nowhere to go, to crawl out to... But we still searched, we hoped. How are you... you have dances there... I want to come and see you so much. Can you breathe out there without gasmask? What's your air like? We don't know anything about you. We've spent twenty years here alone. I don't even know why. What for. Why did we sit here in the darkness? Surrounded by concrete? We'll find out who did this to us. We'll smash their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ jammers. We'll be together again. This is Moscow. We'll be with you, with the whole world. We're alive, do you understand? Everyone's alive, and so are we! Maybe you have relatives here. Forty thousand people survived here. How many of you are there? We'll be a country. We'll live on the surface, like before. Like human beings. I ... There was so much i wanted to say to you. I rehearsed what i was going to say a hundred times in my mind. And now i forgotten it all. I hope you can hear me, at least. I'll speak here for as long as i can. Then they'll probabily switch me off. The people who put up the jammers. Who cut us off from you. they'll come back. We'll try to hold out here for a while. But there are only two of us, and lots of them... The Reds. just don't think that you're imagining this. Or that this is all a joke. I'm real. my name is Artyom. If they kill me, others in Moscow will hear and they'll lead the rest of them out. are you there, Moscow? Hansa? Polis? Everyone who hasnt forgotten yet ... Who else is listening? I'm not the only one. we've been tricked. we've all been tricked. We could have left our shelter a long time ago. and gone wherever we wanted. driving or walking. Anywhere at all. even as far as Paris. Or Ekaterianburg. The Reds hid everything from us. What for? So there wouldn't be any hope? I don't know what for. I can't understand it. We can just ... we can just live now. All up on the surface-and live. Like before. Like human beings. The way people are suppose to live. Live! Do you hear me? There: I haven't gone insane. They're all there; they exist-all of Russia, and Europe, and America ... They're all real! Listen for yourselves! And now we exist, too!" -Artyom

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most immersive FPS with a fantastic level design. Instead of a overwhelming, bland open world, the game is divided into various areas, some of which are linear while others are open. There are no quest markers to show you where you should go, but you'll still be exploring the remains of the post-nuclear wasteland because it never gets repetitive or boring. The characters are well written and you'll be hooked up on the story, always wondering what the next destination of the crew is.

_childDocuments_.review: As with the previous titles in the Metro series, Metro Exodus continues to be one of the most immersive game experiences out there with gorgeous graphics and sound design.The gameplay is fun if not slightly easier than Metro Last Light. The weapon customization is fun yet I'll still never forgive them for making the third weapon slot locked to stealth weapon crossbow/pneumatic weapons. (I get it though, it's how they chose to balance the weapons/ammo)The more open world format is very fitting and works really well for the title. I enjoyed the extra dlc missions and can see them doing more if they wanted to. I know Dmitry Glukhovsky, the author of the original Metro books and narrative collaborator with developer 4A Games, revealed on his Instagram account that he's "working on the story" for further entries in the series, so I do hope they make more great single player experiences like this one.The story is great and I enjoy all the dialog with the characters. There was definitely much more attention paid to developing more of a rapport with the characters around you. You care about them more than in previous Metro games.

A great game up to this point but so disappointing that it has been stopped by a basic bug.

_childDocuments_.review: I should admit that I've always underrated Metro games until when I finally picked Metro 2033 and completed it. Fast forward to today, after having completed the entire Trilogy, it would be hard for me to not recommend them to anyone who'd appreciate a great story with well-written characters,amazing gameplay mechanics, and a truly memorable experience.Metro Exodus took all that we loved in the last two games and only improved it. _childDocuments_.review: Metro: Exodus, and the Metro series so far are among the best games I have played. The characters in it are the heart and soul of the game, each with their own distinct personality, motivations, and struggles. From Artyom's unwavering determination to Anna's resilience and the enigmatic Miller's leadership, the cast is a diverse mix of individuals that you can't help but become emotionally invested in. The voice acting is superb, bringing the characters to life with nuanced performances that add depth and believability to their stories.But for me, what sets Exodus apart is its ability to create genuine connections between the player and the characters. Through intimate conversations, personal moments, and moral choices, you develop relationships and attachments that shape the course of the narrative. The game presents you with tough decisions that have consequences, challenging your own moral compass and forcing you to confront the shades of gray in a harsh world. These moments of choice and consequence add a layer of emotional weight to the already compelling story. This game is a triumph of storytelling and character development. Its immersive narrative, memorable cast, and thought-provoking themes make it a standout title in the post-apocalyptic genre.

I got this on sale, it's a no brainer buy it, its an incredible game all around.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. I did just the main missions and it played pretty linearly--it worked out well. There are some cool weapons, enemies, and lots of stuff happens during the storyline. A lot of the areas felt oppressive and it had a good horror atmosphere. Game also didn't overstay its welcome.My only main complaint is the game wants you to play pretty stealthy / passively at times, and to be "moral" for the good ending, which doesn't make a lot of sense sometimes when the people you aren't supposed to kill shoot you on sight. If you enjoy stealth / slower game play that won't be an issue, but I'm not a huge stealth fan and wound up getting a bit too trigger happy, which got me the bad ending.Not a big deal though. This game goes on sale really cheap and is definitely worth a play.

Then the perfect settings, THE METRO, yes in another city and it's A LOT simpler than the original Metro, yet it was scary and i have to say, PERFECT.TBH, I rly didn't like the idea of going outside the Metro and make this game a free open world game, that's because i loved the first 2 Metros, but after experiencing the settings of the maps that Deep silver gave us, i can say it was awesome!The ending I personally think it's an open ending, we might get Metro part 4? who knows?All in all, this game is a must get!

For example, the player movement is inconsistent and you will sometimes slow down for no apparent reason.Somehow the game design feels like it's from the early 2000s. It's a shame the developer did not modernize the game play after Metro Last Light. I give the game 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I rented the original Metro 2033 on Xbox 360 from my local Blockbuster in 2009 based on nothing more but the blood red box art of a weird monster plastered across it and being told it was "like a Russian Fallout" game. Very thankful to the 4A crew for literally 15 years of memories now :)

_childDocuments_.review: Metro: Exodus is an uneven game. On one hand, the story can be kind of miserable (and not in the intended way); on the other, this is top-tier survival-crafting FPS gameplay.Let's rip the bandage off: both the story and storytelling aren't great. The idea of leaving the Metro is fine on its own, as it opens up environments that the previous two games couldn't touch...but the implementation is nonsensical and largely unnecessary. I understand that there are some ties to the larger book/game canon, but as someone who's only ever played the games, it feels like the worst possible implementation of a decent idea.Then there's the fact that Exodus ditches a lot of the series' identity as it leaves the metro behind, and all players are left with is a bland post-apocalypse that'll screech to a halt every ten minutes and talk at your face about trope-y characters doing boring, trope-y things. More-so than any other game in the franchise, Exodus' story feels like a checklist of story beats, and that only gets worse when you have to stop playing and watch a bunch of NPCs ramble on and on and on.The gameplay really is top-notch, though: if you're looking for Fallout-style "wander in X direction and see what you find", Exodus delivers in spades. The looting and shooting is still great, but there's a new layer of depth that elevates the gameplay passed the previous two games. Metro 2033 and Last Light both offered a bunch of mini-mechanics to immerse the player - switching out mask filters, charging your flashlight, etc. - and Exodus extends that same style to crafting and weapon customization, and it's fantastic. Gambling on changing up your loadout in the middle of a firefight is wonderfully on-brand, not to mention exhillirating (insert Revolver Ocelot speech about 'reloading in the middle of battle' here).The world is also surprisingly reactive. Sound propagates realistically, NPCs react to your weapons and gear, and the lighting is gorgeous (though your mileage will likely vary based on your hardware). Walking up to some random folks and watching as they thank you for not pointing a gun in their face never gets old, and it's a shame that features like this don't pop up in other shooters.Unfortunately, those big open levels with different factions and characters are a bit front-loaded. Exodus comes with both linear and non-linear levels, but there are only two open maps. Worse is that the last couple of missions leave a lot of potential on the table, and Exodus never really feels like it's building to anything. Last Light still takes the cake when it comes to underwhelming endings, but it's a shame that Exodus still can't top the original game all these years later.Basically, when Metro Exodus lets players off the leash and actually allows them to the explore, it's damn near perfection...but as soon as that leash comes back on, you may as well get up and grab a snack.

_childDocuments_.review: This one felt rough to play, and a hesitant thumbs up because only for the story to see it through since I've been invested for a while in it. I missed the more linear style story from the first 2 games. The open world in this feels like the game play took a quality hit to compensate for large areas it has to load. Hit registry seems to be poor at what would seem like a reasonable distance and enemy detection in this game is all over the place regardless of day/night and if you are behind a wall or not. RHC feels like a joke to play at times when trying to do stealth because anything can give you away. I enjoyed the story, but I think that's about it, just to see it through to the end. I like to try and get as much as I can in the first play, but besides difficulty, the game itself poses too much of a difficulty with its limitations and poor AI being unfair to make it worth an attempt and gave up a quarter of the way through.The game runs smooth though despite all the negative feelings I have, but I'd choose 2033 and last light any day over this. The Taiga stealth level in the swamp is near impossible to do with the shoddy AI detection if going for the Forest Child achievement on RHC, but...possible. After searching for a while, I found a comment from a youtube video that made the 2nd part (after getting lucky obtaining the rowboat) easier and does NOT require even interacting with teh gate house lever at all. ----- Quote below from YT user meeze_ : "If you get to the part where you have to get out of the boat to pull the lever but the guard never leaves the bridge ahead of you and you always get seen. I found a way. Get out of boat. Go up stairs. Turn right and go behind the shack and wait for the guard who is patrolling. Follow him across the bridge and look left. There's a broken rail that you can fall down onto some raised ground. Then run jump to the bus in front of you. Then run jump to the next bus. Then run jump to the shore. You're welcome."

_childDocuments_.review: "Flawed Masterpiece" comes to mind. This game tries to do everything and really doesn't quite succeed, but dang it's hard to give it a do not recommend. The problem is that it is absolutely beautiful. There are some scenes that will take your breath away, but then the character models will smoke a cigarette and it won't reach their lips. And that pretty much sums up the game. For every brilliant moment, there's a bug or a game design flaw that negates it. If you like stealth games, this has it in spades. However, if you don't, you're pretty much forced to for about half of the game. Unless you want the bad ending. And you DON'T want the bad ending. It's one of the most depressing endings to a game I've ever seen. The first part is pretty open world, but then becomes extremely linear. You're also forced to look for secrets while being stealthy which really doesn't work well as a mechanic. If you don't play your game just right, you could end up completely losing the end level in a never ending loop, because they only have quick save slots, and there's only four and the game auto saves often. Don't have enough resources for filters at the end and there would be no way to finish the game.They give you two gun slots, but tons of gun options and only rare moments to switch, so you always feel like you're missing out on a better load out. A mini-map would greatly improve the game or way point markers, but you have to keep pulling up the map to keep track of where you are. Sometimes the game is very confusing on what or where you're supposed to go to and that's even on some of the more linear levels.Also, a BIG WARNING!!! If you don't like spiders. do NOT play this game. There are times when giant mutated spiders will literally crawl over you and the screen. I almost uninstalled the first time this happened.However if you like story, this game has TONS of NPC comments at the beginning of every level. If you want to read and hear everything, you'll spend 30 minutes at the beginning of every level easily. This was fine at first but dragged the game's pacing down towards the end. TL;DR if you're willing to look over some flaws for some great graphics and a decent game AND you like stealth, this one's for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: This game truly takes you on a profound journey, exploring the depths of human nature and striking a balance between good and evil. The Novosibirsk level was especially haunting, immersing me in the terror of a desolate city. I was overwhelmed by the sight of countless bodies, their lights extinguished, trapped forever in the horror they experienced in their final moments. The despair and agony of those lost souls resonated deeply with me, leaving me to grapple with their silent cries for answers.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game, either on it's own (though you might miss some of the plot) and as the final instalment to the Metro trilogy. + The story had a good pacing, never felt boring or rushed, in my opinion.+ Graphics were quite decent and performance had a few hiccups here and there, but it was an overall smooth ride and I played with RT on all the time. (RTX 3060TI + Ryzen5 2600)+ Gameplay and gunplay was solid and felt satisfying. I love shooting with the Bulldog and Sammy.+ Semi-open world was cool and decently balanced in the sense that it was neither too linear, nor excessively open-ended. When games are too liberal I spend an unhealthy amout of time exploring everything, just so I don't miss out on anything important and end up neglecting the main quest - looking at you Witcher 3.+/- While I liked the fact that the game takes place outside and let's you touch grass on ocasion, I missed the claustrophobic metro tunnels and the ruthless and devastating effects of surface expeditions in the nuked cities.+ Monke. Several of them.+ Decisions matter to keep some of your crew mates alive and ultimately it will affect the ending you get.+ DLCs are good,  edit: Just finished Two Colonels DLC and it was amazing and very emotional, it really tied things together for me, I prefer it over Sam's Story. But both are quite good in their own way.- Enemies felt a bit repetitive. Oh, look! More humanoid mutants and/or bandits.- For some reason the main character physics are weird as hell. Sometimes I would be catapulted 5 meters when I tried to leap over tiny barrier. That killed me a couple of times.Stop reading this ♥♥♥♥ and go play Metro: Exodus.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, atmospheric and uniquely beautiful game that will hold a special place in my heart. A vast, vast improvement upon the previous Metro games. The biomes are all beautiful, gunplay and stealth are fun and the story is intriguing (obviously as it is based on a great book series). Hats off to the team at 4A and Deepsilver, although whoever amongst those teams designed the bear fight in Taiga should take a long hard look in the mirror and seriously consider killing themselves, as should all those who signed off on that insane idea. This game took me on a journey, one similar to Artyoms, and I feel now as though I am more monkey than man.

_childDocuments_.review: A good game that knows how to entertain, but it falls short of capturing the essence of the Metro series.The gameplay is solid, but the design decisions made by 4A for this game are questionable. Metro is known for its linear, claustrophobic and gloomy environments, which have been integral to the series' identity and atmosphere. Exodus has semi-open world elements that feels out of place and detract from the established tone of the franchise. While not inherently bad, this shift in design direction is a disappointment, as the game's atmosphere suffers as a result. It feels like a disconnected sequel that only uses the Metro name for marketing.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing graphics compared to the first 2 games specially with RT enabled but the little bugs that the game still has after so many years post launch are going to make you lose your patience:- Takeouts that don't activate and you end up healing (Q) or melee punch (V)- Headshots that don't register, there is something really wrong with hitboxes in this game.- Enemies that can see you out of nowhere and disable stealth play for the whole level/area.- Game introduces hold (E) to enter small passages, it doesn't work correctly sometimes in small passages which always leaves you with a doubt if you were suposed to go in there or not.But the most annoying thing is the bug that makes auto-saves to stop working when you deviate slightly from what the game expects you to do, this is specially bad when playing Ranger Hardcore as you can't F5 to save, you depend on the auto-save and losing 2 hours of progress and materials is surely going to make you insane.You can of course play in easier difficulties that allow for constant quick-saves but for me personally it makes    the game too easy and simply not worth it.I will skip this one, it's not the masterpiece that so many people said it would be.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some really cool aspects and others which I absolutely didn't like, which makes it difficult to classify as a good or a bad game since it isn't necessarily either but a bit of both.First of all, the setting of the game and the Metro franchise is very cool and immersive, and this becomes obvious from the first missions, which are really interesting and fun at the same time. However, my experience with the game changed completely as soon as the characters left Moscow and approached other locations, such as the bunker or the desert. These settings were very mediocre and provided most of the boring parts of the campaign. Things became much better only in the final mission in the abandoned city, which I think is by far the best mission in the game and was designed really well by the developers.Now, I know that all the other Metro games were set entirely in Moscow and that the developers may have wanted to change some things or experiment with different settings and scenarios, but I think that the game lost so much potential and interest on my side just because of the dull locations and missions which ended up filling a large chunk of the campaign.This brings me to my next biggest concern, which is the story. I had high expectations regarding this game's narrative as I had looked up the story of the previous Metro games and found them extremely cool and interesting, so I expected nothing less from Metro Exodus. I can say that I was massively disappointed by what I experienced.Already from the beginning I could sense that there was something wrong, as the interactions and dialogues between the characters were a bit empty and not a lot was happening. However, from the instant they left Moscow, the story completely fell apart. For the whole duration of the game, I still can't remember a useful or interesting mission in the whole campaign. It is as if no story was being narrated, and the only objective during missions was to gather resources and help get the train moving again in order to reach another location a few months later and repeat the process. After this incredibly useless and boring jorney brings us to the final mission of the game, things start to get a little more interesting and the mission itself is actually really cool. However, the ending of the game left me extremely disappointed as it was just so dull and unoriginal.Something which I don't have very clear thoughts on is the gameplay. I would say it was alright, a bit clunky but with some cool features and a decent pace, although the enemies' AI was quite poor and clumsy sometimes. Mainly in the snowy and radioactive regions, the gameplay blended really nicely with the atmosphere, which I think is the only reason that kept me playing the game (although I did take ages to complete it as I had no interest at all in continuing for weeks after I finished a mission).Actually, another strong aspect of the game are the graphics, which I felt were quite good overall but not as incredible and godlike as I saw other people say. I played on Ultra graphics quality and High ray tracing with an RTX 3060, and my FPS averaged between 80 and 140 depending on the location, and they were generally very stable, making the game feel quite smooth. There were some locations in which the graphics were awesome, such as the cities and the forest towards the end of the game, and others in which they seemed terrible to me, such as the desert, while the indoor sections were quite good-looking but nothing too special I would say.Overall, I believe that the game has many cool foundations and does some things really well, but the whole experience is ruined by the middle chunk of the campaign which is incredibly useless and boring. Also the rest of the story is pointless and unoriginal, but what saves those sections of the game is a much better setting and atmosphere which gave me something to hang onto, although not enough to save me from a generally negative experience with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The Metro franchise has always competed with STALKER for the best post-apocalyptic janky slav shooter title, but this time they completely missed the mark. Whereas previously Metro worked as a linear story-driven game, unlike STALKER which was fully open world, this time around Metro also wanted to experiment with more open-ended levels. However, they don't really know what they're doing, and it shows. The "open" parts are still heavily scripted, which ruins any immersion they try to establish. The levels themselves are mostly empty, with a few loot locations which are usually barely even worth mentioning. I liked the first two Metro games, but I really couldn't force myself to play through this one. I'll just wait for STALKER 2 and download STALKER Anomaly in the meantime.

_childDocuments_.review: Great story telling with graphics that are out of this world good!Occasionally, the rendering achieved a level of realism that I have not seen before in any video game (I played the "Enhanced" version). No stuttering and despite the outstanding graphics quality, the frame rate was much more than OK. The soundtrack is also very good; some really nice music features in this game. The overall sound design is also excellent; many sounds add to the realism and animal noises can be super scary. Player confinement is similar to the Tomb Raider reboot series, i.e., the story is very linear and movement is oftentimes very restricted. One often follows a path and now and then there are scripted sequences in which the player has to relinquish control. However, there are also sometimes opportunities to engage in optional activities in any order. While I really like open-world games where the player may roam freely at any point in time, in my view the more restrictive style works very well in "Metro Exodus" and is better suited to make sure the story is told with the intended pacing and dramatic effect. I had not played any "Metro" title before and found the game design to be very successful. For some reason I was expecting much less story and more FPS action, but was very pleasantly surprised about the captivating story, the rich characters, and the room the game reserved for atmospheric moments. The last chapter was a bit too gory for my liking, but it did not last that long. For fans of gore, there is more of that in the "Two Colonels" DLC. My favourite chapter was the "Taiga" episode which takes place in a lush environment and features a lot of stealth action. I played at the default difficulty and was a bit surprised how tight the resources were. I thought I was going over and above to look for resources (BTW, game designers really should have NPC characters look for resources as well; feels dumb if one is the only one who has to make an effort) but supplies ended up being pretty tight all the time. The game was very much playable, so there was no real problem; I just would have thought all my collections would have let to some abundance of resources, but it pretty much ended up being just enough (except in the "Two Colonels" DLC in which I ended up with plenty of ressources).The enemy AI isn't the most convincing, but playing the game was still a lot of fun. For anyone looking for a strong story, good action, and fantastic graphics, "Metro Exodus" is a very easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: + the atmosphere of the environment+ sounds and music+ weapon modifications- weak gunplay- stupid enemies- stealth is disappointingMetro Exodus continues what the series has always done, and that is the really high-quality atmosphere of the various environments in the game. Unlike its predecessors, it goes into an open world, and the game has freedom of movement within some environments and the order of places with tasks.Unfortunately, it also maintains a not very interesting stealth with stupid and deaf-blind enemies and this time also a very peculiar gunplay, which is not fun. Player can carry 3 weapons and combine them in different ways from the parts that the player found during the game. From revolvers, shotguns to pneumatic rifle or crossbow. Modification and production of items for survival such as filters, ammo or healing takes place in a limited way through a field backpack or through work tables scattered around the maps or in the train, which is your hub for operations.The story is quite nice, but nothing revolutionary, the game often uses relatively long cutscenes and optional conversations with various members of the train crew. There are also annoying QTEs to a small extent, but they are limited to the usual button mash in a few places of the game. The puzzles within the environment have very limited and simple solutions.With different difficulties, the availability of materials and the strength of the enemies changes, the maps are mostly quite straightforward, especially in more closed sections, and the solutions are the same.I didn't enjoy the game very much, I was always somehow excited by the atmosphere, and then some stupid passage with bad gunfights knocked me down, the occasional boss fights didn't really cut it either, they were boring.I recommend it only to people who like the atmosphere of the Metro, various environments and their details are sometimes really beautiful, but the gameplay is not really good.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus represents a bold step forward for the Metro series, with its more expansive, open-world design and refined gameplay mechanics. The shift towards a larger, more exploratory experience is largely successful, though some may miss the tighter, more confined levels of the earlier titles. The game is at its best when it allows players to soak in its atmospheric world, tackle challenges creatively, and become fully immersed in the harsh survivalist setting.Overall, Metro Exodus is an engaging and visually spectacular game that retains the dark, atmospheric storytelling of its predecessors while adding new elements to keep the experience fresh. If you're a fan of narrative-driven shooters with a focus on exploration, survival, and atmospheric world-building, this is a must-play title.

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been a lot scared to play any sort of horror games.Sometimes I buy them just due to the sale, but I never end up playing them past the first jump scare.The Metro series holds a special place in my heart as they are the only game for which I would keep playing even after being scared shi*less just to enjoy the story, the characters and the oh so superb environment of the series, I always felt that I was in the shoes of ARTYOM (The MC) and the decisions that I took always seem to matter and meant something. I've completed Metro 2033 and Last light twice when i was a student and a lot of time has passed since. I was anticipating exodus to be great, but I never expected it to be so phenomenal and engaging. Even the subtle hints and storytelling that this game does environmentally are a sight to behold.I played this first on a GTX 1050ti PC through Epic game store a long time ago and as soon as I got my hands on my new PC  I got the enhanced edition on steam.This game somehow manages to look more gorgeous than other AAA titles released years later. The Ray Tracing and Dlss help a lot too, The environments are dark, gritty, filled with atmosphere that keeps you as a player ALWAYS on your toes. This time the game is semi open world as the open world is segmented and it does WONDERS for the series. As in previous metro games the player can choose the type of play style they want to pursue, They can play the game rushing everywhere with guns or even play through the entirety using stealth and trying to keep the kill count as low as they can. All of that has an effect on the story and its events and how they pan out.The Crux of Metro Exodus is the story, and its told beautifully with the amalgamation of superb game-play that brings joy and terror to me at the same time. The Gun-play is smooth and feels impact-full.  Each and every weapon seems to be made with love and care and they keep becoming better throughout the game by getting upgrades.The story takes many turns and the endings as said above depend on you.I came out of the game as an emotional mess, while still being happy for my choices that I made yet regretting not being able to change some rather sad incidents.This game among other metro games will always be special for me so i urge anyone even slightly interested or scared please give them a try and i can guarantee you will fall in love.

_childDocuments_.review: A very different game from the previous two Metro games, but I didn't find myself disliking it. While the open world meant that a lot of the creepiness and atmosphere was lost from the tunnels that you travelled through in the first two games, the moments where you're suddenly in the dark are only made more intense.Metro Exodus felt immersive in the sense that you were rarely taken out of the game. Everything from crafting to checking your map was done in game time, you had a very minimal HUD (which I love, it really lends itself to letting your sink into the game). Rarely are you brought out of the game by a menu, but this does lead to making the survival aspect of the Metro games a bit easier this time. You're rewarded for being careful and looting everything as this means ammo, health syringes and air filters will never be a problem as you can just craft them at a work bench.Branching out from the immersion that this game is striving towards, you can feel the weight behind your actions, as Artyom trudges through the new world. Inputs need to be deliberate as they require you to hold down the button. It's slower and carries importance compared to other games where you can bring up an inventory screen with a single button press.Would highly recommend this game when it's on sale, and play on the PC Enhanced Edition.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It has a lot of good things going for it. It looks great, the atmosphere is there, the exploration is challenging, the plot seems interesting. But it's, at least in my opinion, unplayable, especially on higher difficulties, thanks to an attrocious save system. I decided to play on Ranger Hardcore, which is the highest difficulty. The ammo and resources are very scarce, the game forces you to sneak a lot, to constantly look around searching for resources, and you die from 1 - 2 shots. All of this is fine, that's what I wanted. The problem is I am not able to save the game manually, and have to rely on autosave. This would also be fine, if the autosave system worked well, but it rarely saves, and forces you to lose sometimes 15 - 20 minutes of progress.Imagine this: you are exploring the wilderness, your ammo is near depletion, so you slowly sneak around, trying to avoid monsters, searching every nook and cranny for any resources. You are slow and careful, completely immersed in the atmosphere. You take your time and you manage to gather some ammo, find a new gun attachement, and sneak past some wild beasts. Because you were forced to progress slowly it took you about 10 - 15 minutes. Than you enter a boat and some huge monster eats you. You reload, and you are forced to go through the exact same thing again, and pick up everything once more. You don't feel immersed anymore. You don't feel any tension. You only feel frustrated that you just wasted your time.What's funny I'm not even sure why the manual save isn't working. I can see the quicksave controls in the options, but they do nothing. Maybe it's just turned off at higher difficulties, but I don't know as the difficulty descriptions did not mention this at all. And even if it's so, I don't understand why can't I get the challenging gameplay with the option to save whenever I like? I considered lowering the difficulty, to see if it will allow manual saving, but the game introduction is about 2 hours long, full of unskipable in-engine cutscenes where the characters are spewing exposition, so I'd have to go through it again, and I just don't feel like it. What grinds my gears the most is that it is an "enhanced" edition. You'd think they had enough time to fix this stuff, but no. Instead I can have raytracing. Whoop-de-doo.I wanted to buy this game at launch, but I didn't because of the Epic Store debacle. So I bought it on sale a few years later. That's fortunate, at least I didn't lose as much money.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Hardcore ranger mode from 2033 and Last light Redux directly into this. Did a totally different team make this game? - The movement is terrible. The jumping is literally "low grav"... its not earth gravity.. if you sprint near something angular sometimes you launch off edges and die. - Enemies have broken aim, sometimes they will 1 shot you with a shotgun from 30m or an AK from 200m.- Enemies see you extremely easily, you can be spotted through a crack while in pitch black. - Auto saves are terrible, you can finish a side quest objective, and it does not save, then get 1 shot and have to load back 20 minutes.- The writing/acting compared to the first two is night and day. The things characters do make you face palm... really a shame, since this was the strong point of previous games and would excuse a lot of the other frustrations.Going from the first two and into this, I thought Metro would be one of my favorite gaming series of all time..  the first two on ranger hardcore were difficult and extremely immersive. You felt like the world was real. Everything in this is a constant reminder that you are playing a game. Dialogue is boring and endless, characters from the first two act completely different. Miller the epic squad leader from 2033 and Last Light is a bumbling old fool in this.Probably the biggest offender is the basic movement physics, it feels like low friction low grav in CS.

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like this game is 70% unskippable cut scene, 20% CoD/Halo style linear campaign and 10% free roam.If what you want is a first person movie with a reasonably compelling plot and beautiful lighting, this is the game for you. If you, like me, were looking for an open world Fallout style experience you might be very disappointed.By the end of the game I was questioning whether or not any of my decisions even impacted the outcome of the game. Are the gorillas invincible? Is there any point in even shooting them? In the previous mission the final fight with the bear ended after it killed me so I was left questioning whether there was even any point in shooting it at all, or if I just wasted almost all of my crossbow ammo for no reason (which carried over into having low ammo for the final mission). The final mission took me 2-3 hours to complete, of which maybe 30mins was actual unrestricted gameplay the rest was first person cutscenes and walking/paddling down hallways.For a game that is categorized as "Open world" I was left feeling frustrated and with no sense of agency for most of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The most visually stunning game I have ever played. No matter what level the settings were on, the game looked and performed great. My RTX 2060 on High Quality and Normal Raytracing was still able to pull over 120+ frames per second. The optimization is really good. Not only that, but I enjoyed everything about the gameplay. All the different weapons, customization, gadgets, etc. were all so fun to use. The trope of a grand safe haven turning out to be a death trap was also very fun. The ending was super creative, having Colonel Miller pulling you out of the metro towards the lake while all of the Spartans take turns keeping you alive with their blood. I understand people's views on Artyom not talking to any of the characters and only hearing his thoughts through the loading screens, however, I think it allowed the player to become Artyom, filling in the gaps of his character with yourself. It fits right in with the gameplay too, having the player decide whether they want to be stealthy or kill everyone they see. To top it all off, this game has an all around great soundtrack. Hearing "Premonition" play in the background while Colonel Miller briefs the mission to everyone, just great. Please buy the whole metro series, it's a great experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Really liked this game. Excellent graphics, voice acting, and sounds effects. The only thing better was the continuing story. The locations and tasks at hand were were fun (very linear like the previous games) and just couldn't wait for what was next. It did start slowly for me (and there are many changes made from the previous 2 games), but once it got going, it didn't stop.Some of the changes I didn't much care for like having to hold a button down to do certain tasks and the dialogue running over each other (which was a problem in the previous 2 games as well), but doesn't take away from the overall gameplay which I liked a lot.Achievement wise, you must buy the DLC's to get them all and you will have to play at least twice (which I didn't do :)). Did I mention I like this game. Just making sure.The DLC's are fun as well (will review them as well).If you have played the first 2, you gotta play this one. Definitely hits a lot of emotions and just really drew me in.Apparently, you can' review an individual DLC doe this version, so here goes:The Two Colonels: In the base game, you will split up with the colonel and have your own tasks to do. This DLC covers what the colonel (and another one from the main story) had to do. Was very cool seeing that side and I enjoyed the story and action involved. Highly recommend this, but at a discounted price as it is only 3-4 hours long.Sam's Story: This story takes part after the end of the base game. _childDocuments_.review: well its simple, this is how games are supposed to be built. Not rushed, not to fit some type of deadline or for anyone just to pick up and play. A game built for those who want to fall into a world to get lost in but still have enough direction to keep it moving at a perfect pace. A game that doesnt hold your hand but not beat you to death with a mistake, that said, how you choose to use resources weighs heavily on the player, even more so in higher difficulties. Combat overall is rewarding and fun with great variations in weapons and satisfying punchy sounds from weapons with impact. Pair that with the enviroment and all the things in it really gives the player that immersive feeling... every shot matters and has its proper weight. In the end the choice on what you do is the star of the game, allowing the player to explore options with risk and reward ever looming as the main driver in how you move through various situations in the game. To sum it all up the characters, voice acting, graphics and enemies make for an engaging story that brings this series to a point that any game should hope to match. While anything can be picked apart overall the Metro trilogy will forever be iconic with Exodus being the jewel, making it clear that single player games can and still reign supreme as the best medium to tell a story. For any player looking to slow down, enjoy tense moments, rewarding gameplay and a story that sticks with a game that can still look gorgeous...this is the game to fall into!

_childDocuments_.review: Survival games have captivated the hearts of gamers, offering a unique blend of tension, resource management, and immersive storytelling. Among the titles that have stood out in this genre, Metro Exodus shines as a remarkable achievement. Developed by 4A Games and published in 2019, Metro Exodus takes players on an unforgettable journey through a post-apocalyptic Russia. This essay will explore the various aspects that make Metro Exodus an exceptional survival game, including its atmospheric world, immersive gameplay mechanics, and compelling narrative. One of the standout features of Metro Exodus lies in its exceptionally crafted world, filled with a post-apocalyptic ambiance that is both haunting and beautiful. The game transports players into the bleak and desolate ruins of a nuclear-devastated Russia, where the remnants of humanity struggle to survive. The attention to detail in the environments, from the dilapidated buildings to the overgrown vegetation, creates a sense of authenticity and realism. The dynamic weather system further enhances the immersive experience, with changing seasons that affect gameplay and visuals. Snowstorms create limited visibility and force players to seek shelter, while rainy nights increase the tension as mutants and hostile factions lurk in the darkness. The day-night cycle, along with the dynamic lighting and shadow effects, adds to the overall atmosphere, allowing players to witness stunning sunsets and eerie moonlit landscapes. Metro Exodus offers a diverse range of gameplay mechanics that contribute to its immersive survival experience. The core mechanics involve resource management, scavenging for supplies, and crafting items essential for survival. Players must carefully ration ammunition, filters for gas masks, and medkits, fostering a sense of scarcity and tension. The weapon customization system adds depth to the gameplay, allowing players to modify their arsenal according to their playstyle and the challenges they face. From crafting makeshift suppressors to upgrading scopes, players have the freedom to adapt their weapons to suit different combat situations, whether it be stealthy infiltration or open gunfights. The game also features a robust stealth system, enabling players to navigate through dangerous territories unseen. Choosing between a stealthy approach or engaging in intense firefights presents players with strategic choices, adding an element of versatility to the gameplay. The enemy AI reacts intelligently, making it necessary for players to assess their surroundings and plan their actions carefully. Additionally, Metro Exodus incorporates open-world elements that diverge from its linear predecessors. The game offers vast sandbox-like environments, allowing players to explore and undertake side quests, uncovering hidden stories and resources. This departure from linearity provides a refreshing sense of freedom, making the world feel alive and offering numerous opportunities for emergent gameplay. Beyond its atmospheric world and immersive mechanics, Metro Exodus boasts a captivating narrative that drives the player's journey forward. Set in a post-apocalyptic Russia, the game follows the protagonist Artyom and his companions as they escape the Moscow Metro and embark on a cross-country journey in search of a new home. The narrative weaves a tale of hope, survival, and the pursuit of a better future. Along the way, players encounter various factions, each with their own ideologies and motivations, adding depth and complexity to the game's world. The characters players meet are richly developed, with their own personal stories and conflicts, immersing players in a world of moral ambiguity and difficult choices. Metro Exodus explores themes such as sacrifice, loyalty, and the consequences of human actions in the face of adversity. The game's narrative-driven approach ensures that players are emotionally invested in the story and its outcomes.
