_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus concludes the series ... for better or worse. It really depends on what you're looking for.The game takes a bit of a different approach to level design than the last two did. And for me, personally, Last Light will always be the best one.Good things first: The graphics are generally good and the game runs flawlessly (for me at least), not FPS drops, no stutters, nothing.Gunplay is just as you remember it from the other two games (at least the remastered ones).The atmosphere is at times once again eery and spine-tingling, sound design, graphics, shadows, light, limited ammo, enemies hiding in the dark (or you sneaking around in said darkness to ambush enemies) everything works together to create a great experience.Now for the things I didn't like as much.The story feels ... boring and it drags on. In the first game your mission was to destroy the Dark ones with nukes. In the 2nd game you had to find the "last surviving dark one" and then defend D6, which you found in the first game. Here you travel with a train through war-ravaged Russia. We still don't know WHAT exactly has happened or is happning, even at the end of Exodus.Anna (and to a very lesser extent your band of brothers) and her father have become the focal points of the narrative. And I'm sorry, but I just don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about Anna, I'm afraid. I liked her in Last Light, because she was strong, fierce, independent ... here she is clingy, whiny and weirdly incompetent for the most part. More would spoil the story, I guess, but damn ... she and her father irritated me.Speaking of irritating companions: In quite a few sections you have an AI companion ... who is constantly talking (we know that already from the other two games), but this time just takes AGES to move and is often deliberately blocking your path, so you can't just leave them behind. Annoying.The gameplay is also more "open world" now, well at least in the first half of the game. You get to play through 4 chapters basically, each at a different location and taking place during a different season. So far so good, some much needed visual differences, forests, deserts, swamps ... however, I'm just not a big fan of open world games. Crysis is the only one I really enjoyed, because it gave you a mission and then let you decide how to handle it. Here, however, you can explore a giant map, which is mainly pointless, because there's nothing here apart from crafting resources and the occasional story collectible (notes and such), and it just feels like a chore to get from point A to B, since Artyom, a seasoned Spartan, for some inexplicable reason, can't run for more than 50 meters without needing to SLOW WALK and catch his breath for TEN seconds! In the other games you sprint for as long as you wanted ... or I never encountered a situation where I would ever run out of breath. Here you get a huge open world and your guy just keels over every 10 seconds!The 1st chapter is the worst offender here, the 2nd one is alright, since you get a car, the 3rd one takes away all your stuff and puts you in survival mode, which I enjoyed, it was the only chapter I completed without killing any of the humans, and it was fairly linear. The 4th and final chapter is the Metro experience we know. And that one is also my favourite.That being said the actual set pieces (i.e. "instanced" levels) are great, even though you've mostly seen stuff like this before.Enemy design is lazy though. There's basically no new enemies to fight apart from some slugs later one and the new mutant humans ... the rest is just rehashed from the previous games as far as I can tell. And you will mostly be fighting humans anyway. Since humans are the biggest evil, of course.Gameplay is fine although I feel the constant scavenging and weapon maintenance doesn't really add to the game, rather it detracts. It's a colossal time sink to check every corner for crafting materials. In the previous two games ammo and filters were sparse, and there was a set amount available. No crafting. Since the levels were linear, exploring those areas you could felt actually rewarding, instead of finding "3 tools" on a workbench. It feels like a chore instead of actually engaging gameplay.All in all Exodus is definitely the "biggest" Metro game and the one that takes longest to complete (and the loading times are longer as well), but I wouldn't call it the best one. Still, it's a worthy end, I guess, even though many things remain unexplained.DLC thoughts:The Two Colonels: Mediocre. And a bit of a waste of time. Adds VERY MINOR backstory to a VERY MINOR character of the main game's last chapter. We basically already knew pretty much everything that happened in the first place.Adds 3 more short levels and a whoooole bunch of cutscenes (and more Anna this, Anna that at the end). 1st level has you cleaning out "slime" with a flamethrower. Extremely boring.2nd level is a very short "base defense" mission.3rd level is more flame thrower, this time against some mutants. Also very short and boring. Last Light already had a flamethrower level in its DLC, and that one was really good, creepy, not overly long, but entertaining. This DLC feels pointless and is executed worse than the base game or its predecessor.Sam's Story: Markedly better than the Two Colonels IF you liked the open area gameplay, because this DLC adds another big outdoor map (with too many invisible und visible walls though, so it is quite more linear than the main game's outdoor maps), but pretty much nothing else. Two new weapons that feel like old weapons, a new main character, who miraculously appeared out of nowhere, and a new story that, honestly, isn't too bad. The movement feels floatier though for some reason. Sam gets stuck on stairs, overshoots ramps more often, and the combat seems markedly harder.People keep complaining that they don't know where to go or what to do ... a) don't play on the hardest difficulty then, you get map icons, b) you can't really get lost all that much. People also keep complaining about the mines ... I've encountered these evil mines maybe twice or thrice in the entire DLC ... and for the most part you can just ignore them, even sprint past them without taking damage.The constant beeping of your new detector is a bit annoying though.All in all it's still solid and offers another 4 to 5 hours of gameplay. The boss fights are - as usual - ♥♥♥♥ though!

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is not just a great game but an amazing experience and currently is a strong contender for one of the best games I have ever played (up there with Elden Ring and Red Dead Redemption 2). The game is best experienced when played directly after Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light as it allows you to play the story back-to-back where the evolution of the series’ features, characters and gameplay features is clearly seen. This is, however, not mandatory as the intro includes a very brief but detailed visual synopsis of the story so far and would have been perfect as an exposition dump if this was the only game in the series.Metro Exodus is an ambitious departure from the previous two games’ claustrophobic and dark metro tunnels and instead takes the gang on a nomadic trip across the continent (hence the name Exodus). The game presents itself as consisting of non-linear levels and even includes the open world tag on steam. Although true on a technicality, only about 33% of the game’s levels meet this description and the remainder on missions still retain the linear structure of the previous games. To quantify, of the 7 main chapters, 2 are truly open areas, one is a linear mission with an extremely wide path and boarders on qualifying as an open world and the rest are all completely linear. So, technically it is an open world game at times but also not so for most of it. I can only hope that, should the studio release a sequel, (please guys!) it moves further into the open world aspects we’ve seen and further strengthen this component. As it stands, the game exists in this weird limbo area where both open world and linear aspects are sufficiently executed but leaves a lot to be desired in the former. To elaborate on these aspects:The “open world” nonlinear missions:The nonlinear missions take the form of two explorable areas much like the hub world area set up we saw in the 2007 Transformers game based on the first Michael Bay Movie. You are given a map and the story points you to specific spots on the map as required but apart from a few set situations, you are left to explore the area at your own leisure. The game does not utilize any quest markers, instead, you need to use bearings to get the direction you need to go using the various details on the map and the landmarks around you represented by these details. Traversal is aided by a boat in one area and a car in another. Each new transportation method introduced is extremely interesting, but all feel very short lived which I will get into shortly.Exploration is simply a joy as you are told nothing about any location at first. You enter the abandoned building, clear out any monsters keep exploring and then there may be a specific gear item to add to your collection. The game’s emphasis on immersion and resource scarcity also means that every encounter comes with a calculated risk, and you must choose either to run or fight. The considerations of whether the potential ammo gains from fighting through will exceed the expended ammo only adds to the game’s experience and, depending on your difficulty, you will feel things. At some point in these areas you will come across a vantage point where a character will explain the main locations in the area and any potential narrative advantages it may hold by going there. This then adds icons to your map but unlike other open world games, the icons are small hand scribbled symbols which in no way clutters your map. You are then free to explore these areas or not. This brings me to the biggest complaint I have with the open areas.Being a linear story, the open areas should not be seen as open worlds but instead, levels. Once an area’s story (which is relatively short) is concluded, you can never go back there again. This means, any unexplored areas you were going to get to after your current objective will remain untouched. This is especially frustrating as sometimes it was very unclear as to whether this mission would be the concluding point of no return mission for the area or just another mission to add to the current area’s progress. Maybe I just missed the subtle indications due to the characters speaking very quickly. So, my advice to make the most out of your experience, when you visit the character that marks the icons, go there as they appear. Certain characters will also have additional side quests which are mainly fetch quests.Although not confined to the cluttered metro tunnels, these new areas still resonate with majesty and atmosphere that one would quickly adjust to the sudden change in core setting. Where the previous games relied on darkness and the echoes of random sounds of which can suddenly manifest in the form of a monster jumping on you from behind, Metro Exodus takes a different approach, instead, relying on the silence of the dead environment and the ambient wind to generate its atmosphere and in this, the game excels and deserves the utmost praise. During your traversal of these areas, you will encounter monsters (some which will be very familiar to those who played the previous games but with an extreme facelift) and the area’s human faction enemies. Most encounters are scripted and there are no random encounters like other open world games but this is understandable given the scale of its areas. Each area offers enough of that exploration experience to satisfy you but still leaves you wanting more as the game as a heavy focus on Quality over Quantity. But exploration is not just something you do because you are naturally curious. Being a departure from the Metro colonies, merchants no longer exist to provide gear and ammo. Instead, all weapons are looted from enemies and a copy is stored in the train storage. Merchants have now been replaced with the crafting system and the bullet currency has been replaced with scrap and chemicals looted from the area to use in the crafting process. The materials are also specifically placed around the area so there is no system like fallout where any bottle or can can be picked up and scrapped. With the crafting system, you have your new backpack which is a mobile workshop. Being an immersive game, accessing this menu means you take off your backpack, zip it open and you select the crafting items. No mere toggling of menus for crafting. The backpack allows for crafting of the minor items while the work bench back at base opens up the entire crafting catalogue.GameplayOutside of the open world aspect, the gameplay is as you can come to expect from First person Shooters while disincentivizing running and gunning due to the ammo conservation you require to survive. My only gripe with the ammo system is that the game makes it clear in the difficulty selection that ammo is scarce and there is no guarantee of success in combat encounters but has some of the most spongey enemies in game. Being so immersive and realistic at times, it does take you out of it when an unarmoured enemy takes a slug to the chest and walks it off as if a mosquito bite. But outside of this, stealth and gunplay are excellent.Dislikes:Apart from the sometimes spongey enemies mentioned and the levels being short and leaving you wanting more as mentioned above, the absolute worst part about this game is that I can never look at Fallout in the same way again as this game absolutely goes above and beyond in delivering the experience and atmosphere one would want from a game like Fallout. If Fallout 5 is anything like Metro Exodus, then I will be very happy.Conclusion:This is a perfect example of a quality game without all the unwanted aspects plaguing the AAA Gaming industry today. On sale this is a must buy especially if you can get it bundled with 2033 and Last Light. I would even recommend it at full price. For the best experience, take it slow and explore thoroughly when map markers are added to the map and do not rush. You will be grateful for doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: Semi-open world FPS with crafting. Interesting concept, well made game overall, but missing the layers of polish to really make it great. My biggest criticism is that it's not a joy to explore. The enemy design is repetitive and boring. I'm never sure of exactly how many bullets I'm supposed to spend on killing the mutant dogs that are all over, but I know I'm going to have to explore for more bullets after fighting a few of them. I don't get anything useful from killing them so it's best to avoid them, but there's no clear stealth mechanics other than just crouching everywhere. The crafting is fun, and I like the idea of being able to customize my weapons, but it's too much of a chore to explore to figure out where all the weapon addons are which would undoubtedly make my life easier and I'd rather just run to the mission objective.I can see all the little dials on my arm that give me useful information, but I'm not going to look down at them since I know I always need more filters for my gas mask, more bullets, and that I'm probably going to die soon. It didn't feel more immersive to avoid putting that stuff in the UI since the gameplay itself isn't strategic enough to justify worrying about those details.As far as the story, I think if you're going to do a dystopian nuclear wasteland you have to figure out how to make it not so unrelentingly depressing, but Metro leans into it instead - which makes me avoid the little notes and tape recordings they leave around the world because I can't count on it being interesting or entertaining. The dialogue and voice acting is clunky, maybe too much lost in translation there, I'd be able to ignore it if there wasn't so much of it or I could skip through it to learn the important bits.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a love/hate relationship with this game. Mostly, because the tone and feel of the game drops off of a cliff as soon as you leave the first of 2 open areas in the game. You trade a surrene frozen coastline for a mad max style desert scenario. That's cool, but it was way more unpleasant to explore and just not nearly as visually appealing as the Volga. And then, once you leave the desert, that's it. The biggest aspect of the game that they marketed and told you the game was about is Over. It's a linear fps from there on. This is not the game that was advertised, plain and simple. The only reason I fought through the mundane gameplay and horrible bugs in that stupid desert was because I thought I was about to get an open world in the post-apocalyptic Taiga to explore, and I didn't. I'm struggling to understand what the thought process was here to make this happen. All those years in development, all that money, all that effort in making a whole game, to not only just cut it brutally short, but give us a taste of something so good just to throw it out the window. Once you leave the Volga, the best part of the game is over. If you're not interested int eh story, the game is over. It's just wading through sand and linear gameplay for there on. If Moscow, Volga, Caspian, Taiga, and the Dead City were all open world areas, this would've been stalker 2. But it's not. Guess we have to wait a few more days for the real deal. No idea why they didn't just release some new maps to explore, it didn't even need the story because Artyom doesn't speak anyway. I don't think they understood the absolute gold they struck with the raw gameplay of Volga and passed up the opportunity to make this one of those "Release a new chapter for $20-30 every few months", with some more of those classic metro "horror" elements to keep it interesting, and have kept people playing this game and spending money on it for YEARS. This game is just a really sad missed opportunity. This game just makes me sad cuz I'll let myself forget about how lame it get's and scrape the Volga AGAIN because it's sooooooo good, and then arrive in the Caspian desert and be like "ah why the F**k did I do this to myself again?"They released the SDK but I've only seen one custom map made. Just have a contest for who can make the Best custom map and give the winner $1000 and bam you have a ton of new content to market your game with, instead of just leaving it in the dirt to make a new game over 3/4 of your fanbase can't even play. Hello?The "Enhanced Edition" definitely has much much better performance, but introduces all sorts of bugs with the cutscenes like Krest smoking a cigarette and it teleporting to the other side of his mouth and then his hand, and that never happened in the original.The Volga is 100% worth the $5 I payed for it and it's 2 dlcs though, but not the $40 it was on Epic when I first played it.

_childDocuments_.review: Immersion don rightIn a post-apocalyptic world devastated by nuclear radiation, you will find yourself highly immersed in a game that does not handhold you.No quest markers, no handholding. Metro Exodus respects the player's intelligence. Planning and charting your course to a destination feel very atmospheric. But don't worry, you will have a quest log and a compass that you can refer to if you forget or get confused by what the characters want you to do.Characters and voice acting. The characters are, for the most part, mediocre, and it might come from the voice acting. A lot of the voices are flat, monotone, and, in general, kind of boring. The Russian accent makes it kinda difficult to pay attention for longer periods. Using Russian voice acting (with subtitles if needed) is supposedly better.Gameplay. The game rewards a stealthy tactical playstyle. Your character has very little health, so getting overrun by enemies is very dangerous. However, there are a lot of different weapons and weapon upgrades to make a more aggressive playstyle work.The story is the weakest aspect. The game starts strong, but the pacing and storyline are too slow and uninteresting. It would definitely be one of my favorite games of all time if the story and characters were more captivating.Is the game fun to play? The game is definitely not for everyone. The gameplay is slow, but playing the game feels very atmospheric and unique. The game oozes with detail and ambiance, making it one of the most atmospheric first-person shooters out there. The game is very worth playing if you find immersion and atmosphere important.
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. Exodus has a lot of differences compared to the previous games, with different chapters being in widely different settings, but narratively it makes sense as a journey of the main characters. The gameplay is pretty good, the graphics are great, the story is good and the atmosphere is incredible - that is probably the strongest element of the game. The two DLCs are also pretty good - one being similar to the prior Metro game and the other like an extra chapter of the main story of Exodus.There are some bits of jank, but these days you can't even call it "Eurojank" with AAA studios often putting out worse products than this. And the story and atmosphere only hit harder with the current times of 2023. Like prior games, you'll have to rely more on stealth and Han's old lessons to get the better ending, but stealth in this game is pretty forgiving. (And while it's a shame that Han or the Dark Ones aren't back for this game, it's kinda understandable with where the story goes and the book it's based on)All in all, this is a good game and a strong recommendation for anyone looking for a story-heavy shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: I just played through all 3 Metro games and this morning I panicked for a second after leaving for work as I realised I'd forgot my gas mask! I enjoyed all three games, each one stepping it up in graphical quality and immersion. Exodus has incredible visuals, each new environment completely different from the last and with amazing details and polish. The characters are voiced exceptionally well, and when paired with the top tier facial designs and expressions, the characters are very much alive. Gun play is amazing, you look forward to each enemy encounter and even reloading is cool to watch and listen to. I generally play the stealth route so when you get the opportunity to plink through some ammo its incredibly satisfying. As for the stealth, so far I've only played through the game on Ranger Hardcore. You get nothing on this mode, no HUD, tutorial or hints. I DO NOT recommend your first play through on this difficulty unless enjoy the challenge, however personally I thought the immersion was amazing with no HUD, and the frugality of resources ensured you played carefully. You strive for the perfect stealth sequence to both save resources and lead to the desired ending. Stealth again is very challenging but also fair. Only a few times I was frustrated when encountering a bug that prevents a stealthy take-down, but generally it wasn't an issue. The story is great, building up to a pretty climatic finish and a bittersweet ending typical of the Metro series. I'm going to play through a few more times to collect all the stuff and enjoy what are probably the best graphics I've seen in a game. Performance- 70-100 FPS approx (depending on environment) @ 1440p Extreme setting, RTX ultra, hair-works on, advanced phyX on, RTX reflections, DLSS on quality.       Pc -i9 9900K, RTX 3070, 16GB 3200mhz

_childDocuments_.review: Since this edition doesn't have its own store page, I'd presume you're reading this directly from the review section in Community Hub.This franchise is already well-known for its immersion, and Exodus takes that to another level, especially this edition. It features extremely-detailed graphics, even by today's standard. Also, this is the only one in the franchise with semi-open world sections in some levels, allowing for some freedom of exploration. And the story has always been about fighting and surviving in a post-apocalypse world, and eventually leads to finding ways to thrive in it. I personally like Exodus the most for its gameplay, but all 3 of them are superb, so if you're new here, I recommend starting with 2033.Of course, it also has its flaws here and there. But I'm just gonna bring up something that truly bothered me. And those are the graphical glitches, audio desyncs and some annoying bugs that can ruin your gameplay.Oh, and FYI, some of these bugs can be especially frustrating on harder difficulties and Iron Mode, which disable saving. It could cost you a run, two or even more if you're unlucky, I know I was.So just in case, be warned.But honestly, those cons aren't really a big deal, comparing to the quality this game has to offer. If you know that you're a sucker for immersion and also a fan of survival horror FPS games, definitely try this out.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun but I hate its morality system. A game about surviving in a world full of murderers, fanatics, and bandits judging if I kill them or not. That sucks. I had more things to say, but after knowing this at the end, it spoiled in retrospect the whole game. Like, for example, the game expects that I spare surrendering enemies. How do I know they will not kill me when I turn my back on them? I’m roleplaying and the game has a hidden rule that punishes the way I want to roleplay. You are a soldier, you want things to get done in an environment where every enemy is either a rapist, a bandit, a cannibal, or all together. Yeah, I’m going to leave them be if they say “I’ll surrender”.   Story: 7/10 (Very predictable but exciting).  Gameplay: 7/10Difficulty: Has difficulty options so this doesn’t apply. Characters: 7/10Music: 6/10Enjoyment: 7/10 (The hidden morality system spoiled the game in retrospect. Bad aftertaste)Replayability: 6/10 (I refuse to play by the hidden morality rules just to get a different ending).

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a Metro game before and maybe the game is for Metro die-hards only, but I found it a bit boring. The dialogue is clunky and boring, the combat is clunky and boring; the acting is clunky and boring; and the notes scattered around levels are just boring. If you found the previous sentence clunky and boring then you will not like this game.The graphics are typical East European developer fare, gorgeous vistas and ugly close up textures. Very S.T.A.L.K.E.R., ARMA, Operation Flashpoint etc.It's a stealth game in disguise despite there being an achievement for killing 300 humans, so be aware of that if you were expecting an all out killathon a la Far Cry 6 etc.Also be careful when driving the unstable van in the desert level because if you get it stuck on a slope or elsewhere early on, you will have to do a large portion of the level by foot (with one reset point after a mission) and it's the biggest map of the game. Get it stuck again after the reset point and the game turns into a walking simulator. Talking of maps, the last level is one of the most uneventful and pointless sections of a game I have played. Next time I see a gorilla in a zoo I am going to lash a poisoned banana at it. I'm not sure whether I got the good or bad ending but I was relieved it was the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games where you "take the skin" of every character. The world drives you and slowly takes you in. The characters and their stories feel connected and real, You are part of this world. Graphics are beautiful and the levels well designed. It has the feeling a real wasteland would have (something to learn here bethesda). It's a game to be appreciated, to be taken in.. slowly at it's meant to be played.Audio is ok. I mean ambient audio is very well done, voices and dialogue need a little work. The "fake" english russian accent is notably "forced". I would prefer russian with english subtitles in this regard. Game mechanics are some of the best I've seen in an FPS. Controls are easy to remember, nothing too fancy, but very well positioned and in a "logical" / "real" way (pump guns are my favourite).DLC's are worth playing, and worth every penny. They add to the story, and give us another insight of it's world.Metro Exodus is a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Having read all the books, I can say that the story of this one is roughly based on the plot of Metro 2035. If you’ve read the book, you’ll immediately know some of the story points from in the beginning of the game. However, the game takes it’s own path beyond the beginning section. As the title “Metro Exodus” alludes, the game takes place outside of the Moscow Metro, a refreshing change of pace from the first 2 games. Without spoiling anything, I can say that the game is about searching for a suitable place to live, you overcome obstacles and challenges along the way to a climax at the end. Personally I found the story to be good and has some emotional moments in it. The game has 2 endings and the choices you make along the way influence how the story plays out. Overall I give the story an 8.5/10. This game is a hybrid between open-world and linear. Certain sections of the game are very linear and others are very open. The Maps themselves were an ideal size, not too large but not that small at the same time. The devs did a nice job at filling the space they had, so there’s plenty to explore without the map feeling like there’s too much wasted space. The maps also capture the post-apocalyptic setting well. In contrast to games like Fallout, buildings have substantial levels of decay despite the game only taking place ~20 years after the bombs fell. Resources are also quite scant with scarcity scaling with the difficulty slider. You have to keep an eye out for these resources as they are used to make ammunition, filters, clean your weapons, and craft other consumables. The scarcity added a level of immersion and realism to the game, it also made me reconsider how I approached certain situations. When exploring the maps, you could run into a location that just has a bunch of mutants but no loot, making it a waste to clear them out. I found myself counting bullets, especially in the final section of the game. If you run out in the middle of a firefight, you’re pretty much done for so you have to make each shot count.The game itself doesn’t break immersion with menus and a cluttered hud. In fact the game has very minimal hud, almost non-existent which I liked a lot. The game doesn’t give you quest markers or objectives either aside from the main quests, where the game will mark your map and make a note of what you’re supposed to be doing on the back of the map. All side quests you’ve got to remember because a marker won’t be provided. You can recon the area using binoculars and it will add question marks to your map so you can go explore, but often times you won’t know what’s there till you go there. I really liked that about this game, It added an element of uncertainty, you could find a new item, more resources, or just a den of mutants or bandits.The last thing I’ll touch on is the morality system or karma system, whatever you want to call it. Throughout the game you’ve got to make choices about how you’re going to conduct yourself. If you have bad morality at the end of the game, you’ll get the bad ending. If you have good morality, you’ll get the good ending. The game makes it clear what you need to do to get the good ending, just listen to people and don’t be too bloodthirsty. The game distinguishes between enemies that are pure evil, misguided, and non-combatants so pay attention. I played through on the enhanced edition of the game, which uses ray tracing as its primary lighting method. My 2070 delivered good performance on high settings with ray tracing set to “normal” at 1440p resolution. I was getting 100-160 fps the whole game depending on how complex environments were. This is the first game I’ve experienced ray-tracing on, maybe its more noticeable on the higher ray-tracing settings but to me it just made the lighting look good. The game was well textured and the models were detailed. I enjoyed how the soundtrack was done in this game. When you’re out exploring the soundtrack doesn’t even sound like its there because it’s quiet and more ambient. During key moments like cutscenes and tense moments. The soundtrack isn’t anything special, but it does its job well. There are a lot of achievements in this game, certain achievements require certain styles of play. You’d have to play through the game 3 or 4 times to get all of them. Whilst this does add replayablility to the game, I do not plan on achievement hunting in this game and I’m not really able to give any estimation on how long this task would take.I enjoyed the books, I enjoyed the first two games, I enjoyed Metro Exodus a lot. The story, the setting, everything was well executed in my opinion. You can’t go wrong with this game, I can’t believe I let this game sit in my library this long before finally playing it. Since the author of the original trilogy has pivoted and will no longer write books, instead favoring other forms of media, I eagerly look forward to what adventures lie ahead Artyom and the rest of the Order in future installments of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: I Enjoy and Recommend this game. However I feel Im obliged to say Im having massive performance issues with this game. Occasionaly in smaller areas or in more controlled enviorments it's not an issue but several times games massive frame rate drops and lagspikes and stuttering. And from reading other's issues it seems to be when the game is attempting to load chunks of the map or something. Or the game using virtual memory instead of RAM. Im no PC expert so i can't comment more on it. Twice now i been forced to Reboot my PC since the game frozen so bad it forced a Hardboot on my PC. I left it on for 20 min with no result.  Im using 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12600K   3.69 GHz. 32,0 GB of RAM. On WIndows 10. Rocking a NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 TI. So i doubt it matter at this point how good your PC is. Mine are way above Requirments. I think the game just have a bit of bad port to PC as i did not experience any of this issues when playing the game on Console. Other then that The only issue i have is the game sorta losing It's soul. As much as I love the new enviorments and the Semi-Open world. I feel without the Metro the game lost allot of it's essence. And allot of it's core functions doesn't come togheter natrually without the more on-Rail story telling. you notice allot of the time how when approaching certain places from other directions then the main one the game sorta breaks. And cutscenes and dialogue doesn't come or flow natrually. I also am having issue with how the story is being delivered. Your just showerd with massive exposition and i feel the DIalogue even tho not the worse is way more Static and wierd. People dont talk like Humans they talk like they NPC in the matrix pretending to be Humans. Everyone is going in to such massive wastefull details about everything as it's clearly written for the sake of the player and not for the characters. Also I find it really hard that all the characters I loved from the earlier games. Khan, Ulhman. Bourbon. Any many others are just gone and only way to meet or see them or be reminded of them is to get the ♥♥♥♥♥ ending of the game. While they throw like 10 new Rangers at you acting like you all been friends for 10 years while i dont remember anyone of them. I understand they needed to flesh out things. I know Ulhman died at D6. I know bourbon died way before in metro 2033.  But It' still wierd. The game never been shy about forcing your hand. As your entire relationship with Anna came off as akward and wierd in Metro last light. She hated you. Told you that you suck. She ♥♥♥♥♥ up and lets you be captured. you dont see her for another 4h. Then she tells you she's sorry. You rescue her. She sleeps with you and now she's your wife. Even worse is how metro exodus uses her as a damsel in distress. She acts tough but allot of times your forced to rescue her. Even worse is that a big plot point is 100% based on her making a off character off screen Decision about going someplace alone. Combine that when you go there, There's skull signs of radiation and ♥♥♥♥ eveywhere. So why would she go there? Exploration is one thing but there's clearly monsters. And radiation and bandits. And everyone gave you ♥♥♥♥ for going dangerous places. Including her. And now she's doing it?  COmbine she talks about breathing fresh air yet goes to the like the only big hotspot in the first area? It just comes off as forced and wierd. Also combat is weird. Sure it's faster. More fluent. but allot of the AI just goes AImbot T-800 on you. They most likely programmed with hitscan. Sure stealth flanking and tricking them with last know location is key. but allot of the enviorments doesn't offer such variation to actually promote such a playstyle. Allot of the time your forced to sit behind 1 cover and take peak pot shot at aimbot AI. While they bum rush you. This become even more appearant in Higher difficulties. I feel the Aiming of weapons still more defined and created for corridors and narrow spaces. So when it turns in to a 360 Degree arena you notice the shortcomings. Last issue i have is the exploration. As much as It's fun 99% of the time it doesnt yield anything. you find some material you hardly need. And sometimes your forced to kill a mutant or two. And all you get is back the bullets you used for killing mutants. Since there's a max capacity to everything and no storage you quickly come to a point you stop bothering. but then you risk missing the unique upgrade loot. I feel this could been handled better.  Allot of features are just wierd. Day and night? Sure that's cool but since stealth is a must for any non lethal option and Light = your instantly spotted. It forces you to play allot of night time. And that would work if you could skip to Night wherever or at least outside of combat. But no your forced to go to safehouses to sleep. I get the changing guns or cleaning them but this just destroys the pacing of the game. And you notice quite soon that you could had removed like 60% of all map markers as they just pointless. Like why point out oww it's a nest there? theres no reason to go there and the only way to get it to change from a question mark to a Nest icon is to go and stand in the middle of it? So your map get's clogged up with dumb question marks you dont want to go to cause there's nothing but mutants and waste of resources there. Another big issue i have is how they dont make it clear what's bad or good. Somehow some people are 100% ok to kill and others are not. Of course sometimes it's obvious. Dont kill the prisoners or the scared women. Dont kill friendly people or slaves. but like sometimes you can slaughter an entire camp and other times your not allowed to. If you google it people have listed this and it's strange and just reinforces you to go non-lethal throughout the entire game. Which is sad cause the shooting is very satisfying when it works.Overall It's a good game and I feel if you enjoy metro you will love this one to. It expands allot about the game. Im just sad it feels like it sacrefices allot doing it. I would much rather had a semi open world inside the metro going between stations and doing missions and trading while clearing out Bandit stations and etc. Sure it sound a bit more like a far cry title then. And it has it's own issues and risks. But i feel you cant call it metro.. Without The Metro itself.I'm trying to 100% this game but holy hell. I did Metro 2033 Redux in 18 hours 100% and did last light in like 22h. And here I am 26h in and only managed to do what 40-50% of the achievments? It's insane. But still fun. Gonna pull through and get it done sometime.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually dont write reviews but this is one of my favorite games so i felt like i had to do it. First time i played the game was on PS4 and i bought it again on steam because of the gold edition which has he 2 DLCs that i never played and of course the enhanced edition that has Ray-Tracingand other graphic improvements. And the second reason was that i am a fan of STALKER and wanted something simillar in wait of STALKER 2. What i love most about this game is that it is very immersive. You have to change filters on your mask, the mask can pe put on or off depending on the purity of the air and the mask has to be manually whiped to keep it clean or if cracked it needs to be repaired. The map is a real map that you have to pull out and look at and marks appear on the map only if you spot a location with your binocualars. Flashlight has to be manually recharged with a pump like mechanism, you also have a lighter to burn spider webs and other things that slow down your movement. You have nightvision and there are very good stealth mechanics in game like moving in shadows, sneaky gameplay, distracting enemys, silencers, trowing knives and other objects. You have a watch to check normal time and the remaining air filter time, backpack for crafting and more. Oh and did i mention you have to clean your guns? they may shot slower or even ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ jam. Exploring feels amazing and the game makes you want to search every corner of the maps. You can have 1 minute of air left in your filters and no bullets then all of a suden 2 giant ape like mutants that are blind appear next to you. You cant move because they hear you, you cant shoot because you have no bullets, the air in the filter is running out. Also packs of wolf like beasts roam the world, maybe one is not a problem but if it sees you it howls and five more come running. I also saw a zombie like creature that was sticking to a wall using its skin like camouflage to blend in and have a jump on you. I usually play singleplayer games one time and im done with them but on my 2nd playtrough of the game i loved it the same as first, maybe even more. I feel like im on a rant so im stoping here. I LOVE THIS GAME! PLAY IT!

_childDocuments_.review: I played all Metro games before, Exodus is the only one that I wanted to replay and that stuck with me. The different zones you visit throughout the campaign are varied and tell fantastic stories about Russia after the war. This is a different post-apocalypse than Fallout or Last of Us, and it hits very close to home if you come from behind the former Iron Curtain. This PC enhanced edition is excellent and looks stunning. Still some jank from the base game, but overall I recommend it. Also play it with Russian VO.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sucked and its positive reception completely baffles me. I was basically agnostic regarding the original  and its sequel  and thought they were competent if somewhat unremarkable shooters, but this game felt a substantial step backwards on multiple fronts. It's a terrible stealth game and felt to me like a worse shooter than the previous two games. The sound design is awful and much of the game is filled with interminable poorly delivered dialogue spoken by a character cast of dullards. The bulk of the playtime felt to be comprised of quicktime events and ponderous cutscenes and the nonlinear "open world" components add absolutely nothing of value. To the very limited credit of , a few segments, such as a journey into a den of mutated spiders and an encounter with cannibals, still felt fun, but they are also mostly just rehashes of stuff from the previous two games. The  series, which is hardly the pinnacle of FPS gaming, still managed to do this exact game way better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is 6.5/10 for me.The story is nice and the ending is pretty emotional. However, most of the beginning section you are not engaged.The english voice acting is really mediocre, it is somewhere in the middle of a meme factory and decent acting. The gameplay is really enjoyable, especially shooting. Although, when doing stealth, you can tell your enemies are practically blind and deaf. Crafting is also a pretty fun thing, I liked it.The level design is good overall, it leads you well in most locations. However, almost everything is predictable. You can easily tell where a fight with a big enemy will take place or where a jumpscare will be.The game didn't have enough time to introduce you to the crew members. You don't feel attached to any of them. Only the main characters matter.The graphics are good, the devs utilized UE4 pretty well.Metro Exodus is worth playing, and I enjoyed it. You can see a lot of effort that have been put into the game. There are some hiccups here and there, but it's a good story with the diverse gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game. My favorite in the METRO trilogy, and compares favorably even against the great S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Shadow of Chernobyl. Some things I think this game does exceptionally well:Characters: The characters in this game are superb. The dialogue and backstory is so well done for each of them that I just stood around for probably several hours listening to everyone talk, until they truly ran out of all of their lines (which is a surprisingly long time). So much care and effort went into this and it shows.Ambiance and music: Exceptional all around. I cannot believe they licensed music from my favorite Soviet rock band Кино, and the guitar tracks throughout the game are well done too. If you go searching for it, you can find side stories which aren't even emphasized in the main game (such as listening to different people on the radio conversing with one another), which just adds so much to the ambiance. The ambient music is great too and I found myself turning it up in the settings.Graphics: The best I have ever seen from a video game. Absolutely stunning in the enhanced edition, especially with everything on its maximum and with HDR. I recommend using the steam launch option (-deependark) to make the game truly dark and not just gray in dark sequences (if using HDR).Compared to other METRO games: I thought the free roam aspect of most of the levels is excellent and reminds me so much of the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. series which I love. The game does it super well and I spent so much time exploring every nook and cranny throughout each of the levels, just as I did in S.T.A.L.K.E.R. The game is not as scary/spooky as the previous two METRO games which I personally didn't mind. It is also easier to play the game stealthily, most likely due to the large, free-roam maps. If the new S.T.A.L.K.E.R. game is anywhere near as good as this game, it will be a home run. Congrats to 4A Games for creating such a masterpiece. Two Colonels DLC:Fantastic, truly amazing addition to the game. As a Romanian, it reminds me of when the Russians installed a communist government in Romania after WWII, where everything belonged to the state and even things that are rightly yours. My great grandfather had built a house and several smaller buildings for my parents to live in, which were quickly stolen from him due to the communists. There were portions of the DLC which strongly reminded me of that, and how things were done "for the good of everyone" when it was really only for the good of the ones in the top of the party. Superb story telling and environments; I actually enjoyed the non-action portions of this DLC more than the ones with action.Sam's Story DLC:Much longer than I expected! Similar in feel to the main game with more open areas and places to explore. I actually think the exploration here is really good, and it guides you through a few pretty specific paths even though it feels like you are traveling all over. I actually had to make sure I went everywhere by checking the map due to how open it feels (there are places you can miss accidentally). I thought the story was great and the new characters that were introduced are quite genuine and well done. Two new weapons as well which are great. Overall, I would recommend getting it as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus provides an incredibly fun and engaging gameplay experience, coupled with one of the best stories ever created within video games. Exodus builds upon the foundation laid by 2033 and Last Light before it, and offers a far more polished and large scale experience with far better gameplay, visuals, and sound design to boot. The game provides an amazing amount of variety within the open levels of its 15-25 hour campaign and 2 DLCs, totaling another 8 hours in content. Metro Exodus brilliantly combines beautiful visuals, an amazing story, fantastic characters, varied content, fun level design, and an amazing in-depth gameplay system, which results in an incredible game that I think everyone should experience. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 is a first-person shooter with a suitable touch of survival. The story takes place after events of the previous game. Our protagonist is obsessed with finding persons living outside of Moscow. So he plumps for to surface, and with help of his radio he trusts to stumble on a signal. In one of his expeditions to the frozen outside with his wife Anna, they both spot a moving train. They’re captured by the Hansa soldiers. After all the hassle and snag by the militaries, Anna, Artyom and Yermak, they found out that signals were jammed to circumvent contact with the outside. They robbed the train —the future Aurora— and with Miller's assistance they run-away from Moscow. Our adventure takes Artyom's conjecture: It’s possible that there’re people outside of Moscow. If true, it’s possible to find a habitable place.This sequel to Artyom's story introduces us to an atypical world. Instead of going through each subway station, it takes as its plot substance some wrecked cities and villages in Russia through a story voiced on a train tour. Its story takes the form of a circle, whose station-like parts house social issues with a post-war context. Composed of chapters, seasons- stations, we do the hero's journey with that cause-consequence logic (tragedy and fate). Artyom is less introspective, but more involved with his friends. Like a table talk, we participate in scene where they’re rally round. The characters reveal charisma or loathing that ripens; but all of them always starring a part of story. An admirable work has been done on the script: they convey point of views and feelings, emotional moments, especially Anna's aphorisms or the potlucks where interesting topics of conversation are happened. The game makes us feel like living inside a film or a picture. The only negative is weakness of slowing down catharsis at climax to realize a good conclusion.Metro Exodus, as the Greek word indicates, is a departure and leaving precarious life in the subway. At the same time it’s the step to be an AAA game for the Metro franchise. We can notice this in a large number of graphical improvements that alludes the player experience. From the textures, the facial expressions or the lighting to the cinematics, change of weather or the artificial intelligence that we discovery in the game. Everything is revealed as we progress in the game. The locations are a unique, atmospheric and with a different colour palette. Play with biodiversity (forest or desert e.g.). Places offer a singular contexts, has a different rhythm, as well as convenience to halt for a while and just stare. The maps are open and every corner is worth judiciously exploring. The plot and art is dynamic, fluid and coherent. With a good optimization, the footage in real time, it’s always worth traveling with Artyom on Aurora. 9/10The gameplay of Metro is well known. Although here the difficulty mode changes a bit. The story mode allows us to appreciate its plot. While the difficulties are related to the gameplay. The higher the difficulty, the fewer resources we get. To this is combined weather and time changes, with which those affect and modify way a player performs. Each chapter is a large and different map. Being an almost open world, we arrange a compass and a map that indicates the direction of our primary objective. There are «secondary» missions that influence end of the plot. Binoculars are included to eye over zone, and that way it’ll be marked on the map. We can explore at the risk of losing supplies. So it’s better to be prepared and study the map.Regarding the gameplay, we can consider it in two ways: survival and action. Survival in turn we cogitate it in three ways: stealth, scavenger and recovery. Stealth is optional and a mode we know of. It’s important to take advantage of weather and time, as well as the usage of cans to distract or sidetrack enemies. We can incapacitate or kill them. In the case of the scavenger —or looting— it has been implemented with more eagerness. Furthermore to getting supplies in boxes and from enemies defeated, we also find attachments for weapons, weapons base, equipment upgrades and raw materials (chemicals and scrap). Our inventory is the backpack and with it we can craft basic items (filters or meds kits e.g.), store and modify our weapons. If we find supplies but we’re well provided, then they’re scrapped to be raw material. These materials are used to craft supplies, ammo, to clean weapons, and to maintain the train. By the way, everything is in real time in the game. So if we decide to open our backpack, we must do it in a safe place. Finally, in the case of survival, there are housings on each map where we can rest, sleep and have another time (day or night). All this to accomplish a mission in a determined time, equipment and strategy.The action part, i.e. the shooting mode, only the following is worth mentioning. Guns get dirty. It’s always good to scrub them with chemicals so that they don’t get stuck and are efficient. In the houses that are on the maps, as in the train, there will be a work table. There we can clean the weapons, manage resources and weapons, change our equipment and craft supplies. In several areas, we find equipment improvement: from upgrading for the flashlight, to a vest to carry more ammo, grenades or filters. We’ll carry 2 weapons, which we can modify at any time; and a weapon between Tikhar and Helsing. Finally, it’s good to be aware of what is happening in the scenario. We remember that to get the good ending, it’s enough to do good deeds, walk stealthily and complete secondary missions. 9/10 The soundtrack was composed by Alexey Omelchuk. We know him from the previous games and . The interesting thing about the substantial soundtrack of the game is the budget that has been given to him, since he offers us a symphonic soundtrack. In addition, ambient sound and music from the radio —a parallel soundtrack—enriches the game's drama.The theme of the soundtrack involves the fate and decision of Miller, Artyom and Anna. An excellent leitmotif that emphasizes isolated, friendless societies and their deterioration. The question of whether the exodus from the Metro was worth it finds its theme and refuge in music. Many of the times the music is vigorous, strong and lively. But solemn, convincing and euphoric adages preponderate on some occasions. Symphonic music is supported by other elements (rock, electronic, classical minimalism or film music) and tempos, but always reminding nostalgia and longing as an emotional motive. It achieves its task: to communicate the uncertainty of the characters, the destiny that awaits them.The other musical part is found in the scene sound. This may vary. It can be the ambient sounds, the dark ambient that accompanies it or the guitar that Stepan plays. The guitar has always been present, it dramatizes the characters through its homely warmth. While ambient music and sounds express the wildness of each biome. Although the sound of dialogue still implores the player to be in front of character to hear it well. And on the radio, a rebellious, expressive leitmotiv, above all willing to deal with the lies of the rulers. We listen to rock or post punk like the band Kino and their perfect song for the Spartans, . It’s a pity that the game has a short musical repertoire. 9/10In short, it's an amazing game. Although the closing of the plot is abrupt, as if the curtain of the theatre fell in full staging. A work that is atmospheric, rich in context, artistic and enjoyable. Includes DLC, such as Sam's that allows us to continue the adventure to Vladivostok. A game+, modifiers, so the limit is up to the player. Recommended for lovers of travel and stories.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very hard to not recommend this game, because with very little care it would have been amazing. The best part is the history of the characters and for a No-RPG game, they are very well developed. You can "talk" with them and know a lot about them, and with each interaction the history gets richer and you start to care about them. And say "talk" because you are mute. I know this isn't a RPG but it would have been great give some answers to your friends or tell Anna how much you care about her. But all in all, this is not why I can't recommend this game. The reason why I not recommend this game after 23hs of gameplay is the stealth. The game encorages you to play stealth and sometimes punish your friends for not doing so. And more often than not you break stealth because graphic glitches (people/dogs that appear in front or something but they are really behind something). And that sucks but still is not ultimately bad, because you KNOW that screw up and then load a quick save or something and try again. But the thing is the stealth is bugged beyond that. The game has an internal mechanic and if you where not "good", it punishes one of your friends. And THAT mechanic is bugged. For example:  And, like in this case, you are at the end of the chapter and you can't do nothing but start all over again. You don't have an indicator or something that let you know what the game though you did wrong, so maybe you can reload a check point or something before finish the wole thing and THEN notice it. And getting your friends dead or hurt, also alters the ending, so, it is annoyting but also y game breaking. That is why I can't recommend this game. Otherwise, is a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: For those who encounter the "Bug" called the flashlight:The actual solution:1) Replay Valley from the start2) Once you get to the dam (after the tea party) quit out of the game and make a backup of your save3) Try to get through the spider section without reloading (this is the section that bugs your entire save)4) If you make it out the other end and your charger doesn't work, delete your current save and reload the backup to try again(Credit to Forum User who gave me options for a fix but it wasn't worth the hassle)Game is still unplayable years later due to this specific bug that requires specific actions just to avoid it (yes unplayable, TLDR: you bring out the charger and you can't put it away)I'll change my review when I see patch notes about it being fixed.Very disappointed that I can't finish the series and I'm taking it personally, don't waste your time.I can't say much about the game outside of that due to being unable to progress passed 1h of the game bc it happens so early so.

_childDocuments_.review: Pacing of the game is not good. Much of the game is on rails and the game CONSTANTLY takes control over the player with no option to skip. It feels like a QTE simulator. Combat is also not great with enemies seemingly able to spot you in complete darkness behind cover. Movement is extremely limited with invisible walls everywhere.HDR is broken. Black levels are much too high giving a washed out look. Must use launch commands and reshade to get appropriate black levels. Gamma option in game do not help.Controls are broken as well. If you change the movement keys from default, you will get stuck in certain menus such as the radio or the map. The game does not remap those actions to the new keys, but also somehow removes the actions from the default keys - resulting in unbound actions despite all controls having a bound key in the options.

_childDocuments_.review: The Metro series has a level of immersion and attention to detail that is uncommonly seen in video games. Pick up 2033 first (probably the redux, though I'm still a fan of the OG 2010 release) and see how you like that. This is expands on everything Last Light did, and then somehow adds an insane level of detail and content on top of it. It's a massive game that will grab you and hold your attention the whole way through. Only issue for me is the pacing issues. There is a lot of unskippable cutscenes and meandering dialogue that bog the story down, with weird linear levels between amazing open levels. If you can forgive the weird pacing, it's very much worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: as with all of the entries into this series, the world and map design is spectacular. The level designers deserve props because the atmosphere and detail is top notch.The sound effects! Oh my, the glorious sound effects. They finally got it right. The first two games had horrific weapon sounds in particular but this game has some of the better sound effects out there. A+The human AI is quite nice and fights against them have the potential to be fun.You can finally adjust the FOV in game.Anna.Cons: much like the other games, they want it to feel like a survival experience so you never seem to have enough ammo. You can barely carry any ammo at all yet the enemies all seem to have infinite ammo. This is annoying and unbalanced in my opinion.There is a crafting system like all modern games seem to have and I'm not well versed in it to provide much of an opinion. But I think modifying weapons out in the field is a bit silly to a degree.The character movement is still too dang slow and fighting against monsters is annoying as a result.The performance is ok for the most part. I didn't have framerate issues at all but there is a tiny little micro-stutter that I notice mostly in the animations. It isn't as bad as in the previous titles so I wouldn't call it game-breaking but it is definitely annoying.Overall:The story seems to carry over from the previous titles and that is a problem for me since I didn't like the two previous titles at all. I will likely not finish this game right now. I think maybe one day I will watch some playthroughs of the first two or read a detailed synopsis of what all happened so that I can try this one again. It seems like a decent game. Nothing special but not a bad time. Worth checking out if it seems like it interests you.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the weakest entry in the series. Things I didn't like:There was absolutely no reason whatsoever to make this game open world. It adds absolutely nothing. The maps are empty and bland, and do not evolve in response to your actions. Honestly, it feels like the only reason they went open world was to inflate the game's playtime. Additionally, a lot of the game's engine-level issues become really apparent in an open world environment. An example of this is the player movement. It is the same as in the previous games, but because the previous games took place in a tight, closed environment, it seemed fine. In an open world, the movement is horrendous. You are constantly slipping and sliding on the ground. Multiple times I sprinted over a tiny hill only to go flying over the crest to my death. The story is a pile of hot garbage, and does not come close to being even slightly coherent. The storytelling is done by Artyom (the player character) who narrates current events during the loading screens. Then once in game, Artyom somehow forgets how to talk, and stands there blankly while the other characters chatter at him, pausing awkwardly every few seconds as if begging him to say something. It doesn't really help that all the Spartans have pretty much the same personality and are all equally bland. The silent protagonist trope is pretty common, but in Exodus it feels wrong because the other characters keep asking Artyom questions, and keep pausing as if to give him a chance to speak. It's like they forgot to record lines for Artyom, but didn't tell the writing team.Things I liked:The gunplay is solid, and ties in nicely with the crafting/maintenance mechanic. I especially liked how your traversal methods affected the state of your equipment (ie. falling in the water makes your gear dirty). On the other hand, the backpack is stupid. What is the point of the time limit on gas mask filters if you can whip out your pack and make more whenever you want? The game looks and runs amazing. There were definitely times where I paused to just look around and take screenshots. The sunset in the Taiga was quite something. They really did a great job with the Enhanced Edition. The linear levels, oooh the linear levels. They really drive home the fact that this game should not have been open world. Yamantau was great, and really gave a taste of what this game could have been. The last level of the game, The Dead City was absolutely fantastic, and finally for the first time in Exodus, captured the essence of what made the prior Metro games good, that eerie oppressive atmosphere that permeates through you as you play. I was honestly ready to give up on the game halfway through The Taiga, but I'm glad I stuck through because as forgettable as most of the game is, The Dead City made the whole thing worth it. In conclusion, it's alright. It does not hold a candle to 2033 or Last Light, but is worth playing just for the visuals and the linear levels. Grab it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a truly unique experience. It emphasizes all the aspects of a game that I personally gravitate to: immersion, attention to detail, player choice, and ambiance. The Metro Series at large has always excelled at these things which is why I'm a life-long fan since playing Metro 2033 back when it first released. Metro Exodus is a masterful execution of innovation and progression from a studio that knows their audience and loves their game. I am currently on my 4th playthrough! Even in 2023 the visuals and immersive aspects go unmatched. It remains one of the most highly-detailed games I've ever played. The semi-open world is JUST right. It provides player choice and exploration without allowing the player to get lost in hours of mindless copy+paste content. Everything in Metro Exodus is hand-crafted and highly detailed, even the throwaway encounters and side missions. What Metro Exodus may lack in quantity of content compared to a game like Skyrim, it makes up for in quality with everything you do feeling like someone put a lot of effort into ensuring it felt JUST right.My gripes with the game are minimal, though Metro Exodus is in fact a flawed game. While the RTX implementation is largely well-executed, it can be buggy at times and there are artifacts and light bleeding though surfaces that break your immersion a bit. The movement is a janky, and this above all things keeps me from fully losing myself in the world. Even the highest sensitivity on controller is too low, and your character seems to glide over the game world like a vehicle, even being launched into the air if you hit a rock going the right speed. It's odd, and detracts from an otherwise fluid gameplay experience. Things like filter management, gas mask repair, using your lighter to burn things, and the backpack system are all incredibly immersive and well-executed gameplay features. All in all, Metro Exodus is a MUST PLAY in my opinion. It's one of the highest quality gaming experiences you can have, with next-gen visuals and a compelling story line. The DLC are both amazing, with Sam's Story essentially playing out as a second game. The way character development is handled, paired with the Aurora serving as a home base where you have the choice to explore each character further and even complete side quests for them is akin to the campsite system in RDR2. If you haven't tried this game, do yourself a favor and pick it up. Sales are frequent, and it's a game world you might just find yourself liking enough to go back and play the older games which STILL hold up to this day.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent game so far. It uses the established mechanics well and stramlines them nicely for a semi-open world environment. It is also nice to see a diversity of locations and settings. The road-trip vibe is lots of fun. It absolutely retains the feel of Metro as opposed to other post-apocalyptic settings without having to keep everything in tunnels. Some very clever and varied gameplay too. The characters also seem more fleshed out. Anna seemed like a bit of a cardboard cutout in the last game and it is nice to see her character develop and have more to do. I also find it interesting that it shows an ongoing committed relationship in it's story. Many games either use the love interest to be a damsel or alternately have the protagonist losing their significant other at the start so they can go on brooding. TL;DR Can totally and completely recommend this game. Even if you have not played the previous games, the setup is clear enough that it would not be an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the main story after 29 hours. Time to write a review. I was initially going to compare Exodus to the first two games, but figured that would not be fair so I will be reviewing it on its own.Graphics and performance are solid. Ray tracing is properly done (PC Enhanced Edition) with good performance. I am playing on a Ryzen 2600 and RX 7600 8GB and can pull stable 60+fps with High Ray Tracing, VRS turned off, Hairworks and Advanced Physx on and High overall quality. Impressive optimization by 4A games. This is despite being CPU bottlenecked, where my GPU is running at 85% usage at the highest.All the mechanics you might know from the previous games are still there and further refined, with the addition mechanic where you need to clean-up your weapons after extensive use. This new mechanic was never a burden, instead increased immersion and prevented a guns-blazing approach and encouraged me to take a more grounded approach to the gameplay.NPCs are wonderfully done, each with their memorable personalities and quirks. They interact with you and talk to you as you progress in story, it feels like they are actual people that live and breathe. They are no longer "agents" that appear and disappear as the story dictates.The larger maps are--in my opinion--a good new approach. They did not go the open-world route but instead created hand crafted, meaningful areas of just the right size with each side quest serving a story telling purpose or contribute to the overall gameplay in a meaningful way. The larger maps also allow for more environmental storytelling, where you come across scenes that convey a strong story along with the notes you find in them (I won't give any examples to prevent spoilers). This larger map approach also gives way for more non-linear approach to missions. If you listen to enemies' chatter, for example, you can find a safer entrance to the objectives or you can simply scout the area to find alternate entrances. In general, I am happy with the large, hand crafted maps.This does not mean there aren't linear areas, however. Each large areas are accompanied with a small and linear objective like Yamantau or Novosibirsk level so you get a taste of both.Sound quality for weapons and environment are top notch. Yes there is no sound propagation simulated, which would be amazing if we had it but what we have is enough to complement the immersive quality of the game. I played the game in Russian voice with English subtitles so I can only talk for voice acting in Russian language and it was not bad. I found VA performance a bit flat and lacking at some parts but overall it gets a pass from me.That's pretty much it. 30 hours well spent, money well spent. Now I have two DLCs to get through and I hope they are just as good as well. Totally recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an ok survival game (I refuse to call it a fps), very story heavy but unfortunately let down by a very predictable plot filled with 2-dimensional characters and bland dialogues. Nothing wrong with the story per sè, it's just the way it's slowly narrated and how the characters talk that I find boring. Thus said, the game looks amazing, the ray tracing does make a difference for once, and the game has some good set-pieces here and there (the giant spiders levels definitely got my attention). I liked 2033 but hated Last Light, I'm glad they decided to completely change the setting with this semi-open world. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying I haven't quite finished the last part of the game yet, but i'm working on it. I will not mention any important spoilers in this review. If you are looking to buy this masterpiece ( which you totally should ) please go through and play the first two games redux & last light. Not only are those great games but they will complete the story. The graphics are gorgeous, this is one of the few games that has a atmosphere that just simply captivates me more then many others. I usually listen to music while playing games but I just cannot when playing this game, I'd rather be immersed in the environments. There are some amazing details in this series and this game in particular, your choices do matter as there is a moral system that can affect which ending you end up with. The relationship with Anna & Artyom is done really well. You can hear a character mention that they want a specific musical instrument, if you go out of your way to find and give them that instrument they then play it in different parts of the game and continuously thank you. I've had issues putting this game down as i've just enjoyed it so much, I'd recommend stealthily progressing your way through most of it and not running in guns blazing as there is lots to look at and do and I feel like running & gunning just isn't at all how this game was meant to be played ( but it can totally be done ) You are rewarded for exploring. Something else i'd like to mention is the phenomenal gun customization, you can select 3 guns to carry on you all of which you can swap parts out on the go depending the situation, for example There is an air compression rifle that shoots metal ball bearings, that's my main stealth weapon which I will constantly change sights & parts on as needed. Small details like patching your cracked gas mask & dirt & grime slowly affecting your weapons really helps to build the atmosphere. TL;DRI give the game a 9/10, there is an amazing atmosphere with great gun-play & small details that just complete the game to be one of my favorite Story driven FPS I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat and movement are sluggish, inferior in many ways to the 2 previous titles.I can definitely appreciate the dialogues, but the facial expression and models are just bad, even with raytracing and all the game looks passable, nvidia filters fortunately come in handy to fix that.Just no, the game doomed the series between the epic controversy and the objective low quality of the game.Even the section in the first 20mins feels absolutely written awfully, and comes from a novel too!Then i was frustrated when you literally have to throw an object in front of an enemy to distract them, or how comically high the game tries to railroad you towards the very obvious generator with green lights.The game is a mess, i'll play it because it's still a beloved series in my heart, but wouldn't give it the same love and care as the other titles.The movement is so bad that there's such a big inertia and low attrition in some points that you literally fall to your death because of it.A few guns literally have their laser pointers NOT parallel to the gun... jesus this is embarassing,So... there's a boss fight, or well you face the same boss twice, and it's invincible.I could have understood the first time, you're just not meant to take it down, but at the second encounter you take it down purely by luck??? It just doesn't make sense.Also like in previous instalments you have a sort of karma system, but there's no punishment for killing (my mistake, thought they were hostiles) villagers in the first area, now in another area much later i get punished with a companion death? Not cool.Two Generals DLC:Bad, like even spelling mistakes in the transcript, the core idea of fuel wasn't bad but the exploration is slow as hell.Had a dialogue even cutoff early, after the general meeting and the first requisition you witness outside the office, the whole DLC is a rushed cashgrab. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, so to get the first thing out of the way the game's Metro, but open world now, and everybody is delivering comically long monologues. Tone is farcically grimdark at places, but on the whole it's fine.Now, concerning the only reason anybody cares about this game: the RT implementation  good, but there's a number of problems lurking below the surface.To start with, there's a bunch of bad textures, and texture streaming is somehow handled poorly. Then there's a postprocessing white filter that maybe you can stand, but you'll probably want to remove with a launch options command (-deependark). Then, there's motion blur which does not play well with DLSS, so you'll want to edit the user.ini file to disable it completely; however, your problems will continue because the game loves using DoF, which DLSS  does not play well with. And you'll need to manually upgrade the DLSS, of course. Oh, and if you've got an HDR display on top of all that you might also be in for more tinkering with the .ini file.Overall, it's a mess. The kind we've gotten used to by now as developers don't seem to have a clue what they're doing on PC graphically, let alone the commitment to properly execute, and maintain their vision -- that's if they have a vision in the first place.

It's not bad, but I personally like more of a linear playstyle with these kind of games, however there are sections in the game where it does become linear.It really reminds me of the playstyle change from The Evil Within and The Evil Within 2.
