_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game on ranger hardcore. The game has several problems, mostly stemming from poorly designed sections in the caspian border part of the game, terrible checkpoint system, and half baked stealth mechanics. The eariler sections of the game aren't too bad and can be a good time on ranger hardcore, but after that, the game slowly become more and more annoying to play. These frustrations start in Caspain, and continue for the rest of the game. The big problem is the stealth system, or more specifically, the extremely inconsistent nature of your light indicator. This indicator is supposed to tell you when you're visible to enemies, but sometimes you'll be in complete darkness, with the indicator saying as much, and enemies across the room will still spot you. Or you'll be visible for half a second, which can sometimes mean that enemies get spooked, or they'll fully aggro and sound the alarm. Its a coin toss as to which will happen. Or you'll load a checkpoint, and suddenly every enemy will be aggro-ed before you take a step. To get the good ending you'll need to minimized the amount of people you kill who aren't bandits, so stealthing areas is encouraged (especially on ranger hardcore). So, basically, you'll have to engage with this stealth system often during your playthrough and simply deal with all of its frustrations. This wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for the god-awful checkpoint system. Its not uncommon to lose 15 to 20 minutes of progress due to a checkpoint not triggering when it was supposed to. In the Tiaga section of the game, the checkpoints are the absolute worst. I regularly lost 20+ minutes of progress because checkpoints were poorly placed or just that infrequent. This is also a section of the game where you need to avoid killing Pirates or Pioneers in order to get the good ending, so you also need to stealth most of this section (but not all of it). There's also issues with the story. The initial reason for why artyom and friends can't leave moscow is incredibly stupid. Why anyone would possibly believe that post-nuclear holocaust Russia was occupied by the americans everywhere outside of moscow is beyond me. This plot point is so full of holes that you'd think someone shot it with a quad-barrel shotgun. Thankfully, once the crew is outside of russia, the story basically becomes "Artyom and Friends try to find a place in the wasteland that isn't a hellhole, and live there." Its a simple story but it works. Overall, I wanted to recommend this game seeing how the previous 2 metro game were fantastic (and designed to be played on ranger hardcore from the outset), but I can't recommend this game at all. Its just frustrating to play, on nearly every level. The beginning sections of the game before the Caspain Desert are fun, the Caspian Desert is a chore, Tiaga is filled with horrid checkpoints, and the final section is almost good if it weren't really slow. This also isn't mentioning the bugs and 2 crashes I had while playing. Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played any of the other games so keep that in mind and I will try to keep this brief. I played the game, wouldn't say its anything amazing, definitely get it on sale. The DLCs is another matter entirely, they can't get rid of many of the problems in the game but they do to me present better and more interesting stories thats executed better and both also have speaking protaganists instead of just silent treatment so that is also a plus, to bad some of these designs didn't make it into the game.*** The main game* The good1. The levels/maps: Many of the open ended levels you can freely explore are quiet good, cool environments and places to check out. For me it faltered a bit as it seems the rest of the game didn't fit to well with this part because there are so few things to actually gather up. So in Fallout for example if you explore a ruin you expect to find some things, here if you explore what you usually just find is either Scrap og Lab stuff for crafting and maybe one weapon upgrade that's it.2. There where some very atmospheric levels in the game, especially the last level where you are searching in a medical building which was well made. But it did ruin the pace of these things when you had to open your backpack in the middle of it to craft more gas mask filters or more pellets for your gun.*The Meh1. Graphics: A lot of people are saying looks great but that was not my experience. From a distance it looks good but as soon as you get close to the environment it looks average or bad, especially the frozen maps. And this was with everything on max. Its not that the game is super ugly but its not anywhere near as pretty as everyone else is making it out to be.2. Monsters and enemies are for the most part okay but nothing special.3. Many things in the game seems to be missing that final polish that I was expecting in a title like this. The core is fine but could have been so much improved if more time or effort had been put into it.4. There is a car in the game for some reason, and it handles crap.5. No way to progress time outside of sleeping which on some maps are hard to find beds.6, Gameplay is okay but nothing super exciting.7. Crafting: its there but not much depth to it, which is probably for the best.*The bad1. Voice acting is poor. So they choose to have a big focus on it sounding Russian which I can respect with the game being set in Russia but I can't say any of the characters voices brought much to the table. This might also have been an issue based on the next 2 points.2. Dialog: Sometimes it does it job, but often when NPCs are talking together the voices almost overlap taking away any feeling of authenticity to the scene and other times its as if the dialog and characters aren't reacting to whats actually going on, feels robotic.3. NPCs: Most of them felt pretty bland to the point that I couldn't tell them apart or remember who was who. It also doesn't help that they where all morons. Most prominent is a point in the game where the decision is made to go to a place that is such an obvious trap a 5 year old could tell you but everyone is just "yeah okay gotta progress the plot and all".4. Still some crashes in the game 2 years later, especially around one specific level in the game.5. Spiders running over your screen when you walk through spiderweb, why? No sane person would like a creep the size of a fist run over their face without removing it. But apparently the main hero is both completely unphased by this and also an spider attractor as it doenst happen to anyone else.6. Almost no modding.7. Hitboxes are all over the place, often what you would expect is a headshot just passes straight through the enemy for no damage. Probably happens on other body parts too but is very obvious on headshots.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Metro game I've played and I'm definitely interested in checking out the rest after this! Never has a shooter asked me to consider the implications of every encounter quite like this one."Can I spare the bullets? Can I risk the noise? What will my comrades think if I kill these people? Should I neutralize everyone here? or just enough to sneak around? Should I risk looking around for materials? or should I make a mad dash for the exit while I can?"There are no levels to gain, no perks to unlock, and no loot to grind. There is gear to find, notes and journals for extra lore, and weapon attachments to scavenge from enemy weapons. For the most part the motivation to keep progressing is to get your crew to the next destination, and gather enough materials/scrap/gear to survive more effectively.The main things that hold the game back are the various visual errors that seem common, the sub-par dubbing/line delivery timing, and the sometimes clunky stealth/melee combat.Still a very unique experience worth the cost of entry, a strong 7/10!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a huge step up from 2033 and Last Light. Now there are many more persistent characters that get fleshed out and developed other than just Artyom. It seems like there must be hours and hours of dialogue in there and much that I haven't heard even after playing so long due to all the variations that react to what you do. Not only is there a lot of dialogue, but it's all well acted as well. I think this game is up there with Red Dead Redemption 2 in terms of the writing.As for the actual gameplay, it now has a handful of very open maps you go between throughout the game versus those two much more linear titles in the past that are almost entirely going from A to B in tunnels. The customization in this goes much more in depth while also sporting a few new weapons, especially in the Sam DLC. This level of customization also extends to your body suit and kit.There's also a huge variety of environments you play in, it's not all just snowy streets in Moscow or tunnels anymore. Lots of rewards for exploring these areas as well with lots to find veering off of your objective.Alright, now that I'm done praising this game, let me talk about some things that didn't work too well in this game. The stealth system in this is pretty bad. Thankfully it didn't have the bug from Last Light that disables your ability to knock out, but the lighting could use some work. Seeing some comparisons between this Enhanced Edition and the original release showed a huge difference in lighting and, after playing it, yeah the lighting in this Enhanced Edition is way too bright. When it was nighttime I could hardly tell if it was daylight or not because they're lit almost the same, the only difference is a light blue hue to the ground and the skybox changes. There's a couple of interiors that get properly dark where a flashlight is needed, but they're rare. Most interiors without lights are still very well lit. And it doesn't seem like the stealth system really takes into account the time of day and actual lighting all that well, which I think could be because that system might be relying on light placements from the original version and not what the raytraced lighting is showing. Sometimes I'll be standing in a pitch black room and it'll say I'm visible, other times I'll be in the light of a lantern and lit up but it'll say I'm not visible. It was near impossible to tell what areas are and are not in shadow because of this, unlike the previous two games where that was much more well defined and easy to see. And the physics, oh goodness the physics. If you're running up a slope and that slope has the tiniest of bumps on it, your character suddenly will slow way down as the engine is having you start to slip while you're in the process of running. I've have had a few times where just running through I'll enter into this slipping state and get flung or fall where I didn't mean to.But despite the criticisms, I think the good definitely outweighs the bad and this is my favorite game of the three. Highly recommend.(Oh and Sam's Story is great. They made a whole new highly detailed open map just for that one DLC filled with new mechanics and placements, many of which I wish were in the main story. Go check that one out. The Two Colone's DLC you can pass on though, not much there and no interesting.)

I should just reinstall STALKER and play through them for the hundredth time.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus was already one of my favourite games on release, ridiculously immersive, amazing environments, with a great mix of semi-open world maps, loaded with details and little secrets, and old-school more linear claustrophobic Metro levels. The enhanced edition with the amazing implementation of Ray Traced Global Illumination with infinite bounces, seriously adds to the immersion level IMO. Tunnels and the underground are so ridiculously dark now, using your torch and lighter have more of a strategic implementation, deciding to be blind, or risk using the torch and getting spotted and swarmed by mutants. It also runs better performance wise than the original did, whilst doing WAY more RT Heavy effects, that looks jaw-dropping honestly. I suggest doing a first run on a middle-ground kinda difficulty, and then replaying it on Ranger Hardcore, I feel like Metro plays best when you kill enemies in one shot, and they kill you in one shot. Makes resource management much more of a thing as well. I've played this game 3 times, and both DLC's which are both well worth playing. I really enjoyed Sam's Story, another semi-open world one following his path to try and get back home to America with a big choice to make at the end, just like the base game has a bunch of options and the moral system, IE killing too many people in certain levels, might make you end up losing a crew member. On my 2nd run I went all guns blazing, and ended up having the saddest ♥♥♥♥ happen over & over to me because of my homicidal actions hahaha. Anyway, if you want an immersive, post-apocalyptic FPS with resource management, semi open world levels coupled with old school linear levels. Pick this game up. My only complaint is that Artyom is still a voiceless character and it doesn't help with immersion when characters are talking directly to him and he just... says nothing. Sam's story DLC proved that having the main character have a voice works way better in this game then not. There's a great YT video where someone has overdubbed their own voice for Artyom and after watching that I seriously don't understand why the developers didn't add a voice for him. Regardless, 10/10 game for me and I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a continuation of the Metro story picking up shortly after the events of the canonical ending for Metro: Last Light. There are some notable changes for fans of the series. Some of the controls are slightly different, there is a slight open world aspect to certain chapters, and there is now an essential crafting component. I was a bit off-put by the control changes at first and the beginning made the protagonist seem like the bad guy, but (without spoiling anything), I soldiered on and I actually would consider this to be my favorite game in the series so far. I do not know if the publishers plan to continue the series beyond this, but I would be interested in continuing the story from the end of this one. I did not read the books so I cannot speak to how well they kept true to the source material. I am running this on a RTX 3090, Ryzen 7 5900x, and 64gb of DDR4 RAM played on maximum graphics settings with enhanced PhysX enabled. There are some notable glitches during gameplay which may have been attributed to enabling enhanced PhysX, but they were relatively minor (floating trees and debris mostly). I really did enjoy this game and the story so far.

_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: It is well known that sequels are usually worse than the original. This is one of those rare exceptions. This game is by far the best of the series. It has what Fallout 3+ is missing. A soul. Don't get me wrong, I love the Fallout games and the universe. I just think that this one has a spark that the others are missing. Being part of the Spartan team is like being part of the family. You care for all the characters.They really did an amazing job of story telling. If you want to be immersed this is a worthy world to spend a few hours of your life in. Sure like all games it has some bugs but how many games don't? I savored this world. I tried to get all the lore that it offered out of it and it never felt like a chore. All conversations were tied into the world and not random. You could even spend some time just standing on the running train watching the world pass you buy and just enjoy that while listening to the music on the radio.So many little details (small things like you smoking/drinking, playing the guitar, just listening to people talk or snatching random conversations on the radio that later even tied into the DLC) contributed to creating a wonderful immersive atmosphere.I wholly recommend that you play it in the original language. I know that for me it was extra enjoyable since I understand what was being said but the voice acting is so much better so do yourself a favour and don't go for the terrible English dubbing.
_childDocuments_.name: Metro Exodus

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect way to end the Trilogy, if 4A decides to make another Ill that one as well. If these ever come in a pack on a sale I thoroughly recommend these games, If you liked STALKER youll more than likely love this seriesExodus is a great way to end the Metro series, Artyom got his ending of wanting to escape the Metro and live a life different than what his peers wanted. At the start this game is a slow a burn; Learning how to craft, loot and explore a map before going to your next objective is a huge departure from the dark, restricting halls of the Metro Tunnels, while the game is open world I feel its a little over bearing at times with the amount of walking from point A to point B is but after gearing yourself to your playstyle this game is amazing.Exodus Improves on some of the Mechanics from the 2 Previous games while fudging some up; the AI being one of the things I didnt really enjoy from the last 2, they seem to be more absent minded and more willing to eat a bullet to the face in the event you have to actually fight in an encounter. Guns are nice with good visual and audio to make the player feel powerful not to mention all the crafting options available to you to make and build your guns to your liking while also offering a large enough arsenal to help make the game not feel as stale, so the times you make it back to the Aurora to change a gun or clean it if you dont supplies in the field is recommended. Though some combat encounters on Ranger Hardcore do feel cheap, since you die in 2 shotsGraphics are a top-notch, Ive yet to see a better game that is both visually clear and vibrant. After getting used to the various Grays, Browns and Greens, Exodus really shakes it up; After leaving the snowy levels you get to see the 4AEngine really knock it out of the park, My favorite being the Taiga chapter, a forest valley in the middle of Autumn really pop when you take the time to crank up your settings and really appreciate the amount of work 4A put into the world to make it look as good as it does. Crank up some music and sit by the camp fire and just really take in the sights.Audio is standard Metro fan fair, stock sounds for alot of the interactions. But im not an audio guy so what do I know.DLCs are pretty good too, I didnt care for SAMS STORY, but TWO COLONELS too you back to the Metro Tunnels one last time to watch a father do what he could for his son, and that ending really pulled at me.Overall Exodus is a great way to end the series off, if you want an experience worth playing and learning Play it on Ranger Hardcore then move to Iron mode for a real challenge. If you play any version of the Metro Exodus play the Enhanced Edition if your unsure, it offers the best visuals while giving you all the DLC to continue your journey,

_childDocuments_.review: Exodus represents a considerable change of pace from the previous games in the series. Out of the claustrophobic, dark tunnels of the Moscow metro, you are now set in open outdoor areas (for most of the game), and get to explore the outside world.While at first I was worried about how these "open areas" would affect the quality and pacing of the game, but they turned out to be just big enough to be fun to explore, while staying concize.Another aspect which had me worried was the crafting, but again, it's very streamlined and doesn't get in the way at all: there's only two types of materials, which work almost as if they were currency for you to buy ammo/clean your weapons, etc. No need to worry about finding a million different materials, or blueprints, or whatever.While the game can be played as a straight up FPS, like in previous Metro games, there's a lot of room for you to take a stealth approach, and you'll be rewarded for doing so, as most (human) enemies will be having conversations amongst themselves that you can listen in on. This also ties in some ways to the moral system: there will be some instances where the game confronts you with the thought that sometimes your enemies aren't necessarily wholly evil, but rather people who don't know any better, fighting to defend themselves.The story is alright, but it's the way in which it's presented that makes the most of it. The moments in between missions, where you're hanging out with your team at the train are very relaxing, and it feels great to have a moment to chill with your bros after each mission.Your actions and decisions have direct consequences for the story, and your playstyle reflects that: in a game/setting that explores humanity at the brink of extinction, you'll often be confronted with choosing between perpetuating the cycle of violence that has haunted humanity since the beginning of its history, and coming up with a more understanding point of view towards your enemies. In fact, a few times you and your team are actually the trespassers in someone else's land, and in this post apocalyptic world, trusting outsiders doesn't come easily.Finally, the game looks great, and delivers a good atmosphere, like the other Metro games got us used to. Each mission/level has a different setting, bringing a lot of variety to the table, with some stages being more open and others more linear. In my opinion they're all  very goodThe movement is very janky sometimes: feels like you're driving a car instead of being a person walking/running. This means that some times, if for example you run up stairs or some elevation, Artyom (your character) will be launched forwards like a car jumping on a ramp. Sometimes this is a bit annoying.For people new to the series, I'd recommend playing through the first two games before starting Exodus, as otherwise you won't really care about the main characters and how their past has brought them to where they are now.Metro Exodus is a very well made game. It's full of great moments and is definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Exodus is a meticulously crafted experience with unfortunately sluggish game play. This is the first open world Metro game but many design flaws make it frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus was a fantastic experience, boasting:1) Impressive Graphics & Visuals delivered with what was for me, fantastic performance at max settings 140+fps the whole ride with a 3080. The Audio design in this game was fantastic as well from top to bottom.2) Incredibly immersive gameplay with an emphasis on realism, tactics & preparation. 3) Solid story with an enjoyable group dynamic amongst the various characters. The Aurora (your base between zones) was one of the most cozy, immersive "HQs" I've seen executed in a game. Really cool. (Voice acting of all the characters was top notch as well)4) Well paced. The game isn't one massive open world, but instead divided into several smaller Open Worlds. Each of which containing several side quests & content alongside the main quest/mission of that zone, before moving on to the next. The game never felt like a slog like many modern open worlds can. Would 100% recommend anyone looking for a more immersive, mature/serious toned narrative shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly astounding. My two favorite aspects of this game other than what I just mentioned is the enemy AI and weapon customization. The human enemies are great in my opinion for the fact of their combat skills and communication, sure they have some dumb moments but no game is above that. What I loved the most is their communication during combat such as call outs to other npcs about your location often being very detailed.I think the world of METRO is great and brought to life amazingly in this game especially how they will often lead up to something like a boss fight in such great ways. _childDocuments_.review: Congratulations to 4A Games and Dmitry Glukhovsky.A monumental achievement. A great single player experience with heart, passion and a great story. Certainly in the realm of masterpieces not for it's technical mastery, but for delivering what story driven games are supposed to. An unforgettable experience. It's the little details that matter and there are plenty here.Thank you for allowing me to take the occasional smoke break on the train. For allowing me to sit with Anna and listen to her stories. For allowing me to drink with my comrades from time to time. For giving everyone a piece of dialogue in between missions that are relevant to what we are going through. For allowing me to naturally, without any queues, discovery hidden quirks, missions and interactions. Everything is worth exploring and everyone is worth approaching.It is without a doubt, especially after playing all three games in succession, a wonderful adventure that delivers in every way. Please make another one. And please keep the atmosphere the same. Don't give in to the mainstream trends. Metro is unique.If i could make one suggestion for the future: Expand the small things. Give us more to do so we can stick around after the fact. Don't go head first into multiplayer. Let us live a little longer in the Metro world before we have to leave.P.S. Read the books people. They're worth it too. And the audible narration is fantastic if you want to listen instead.

_childDocuments_.review: So many good ideas...  When this is game is doing what it does best, it's amazing.  The gunplay is fantastic, having to conserve your ammo gives it an edge that most shooters don't have.  The stealth is usually really, really good too.  The open maps are...  Well, generally pretty good.  Some small complaints, but nothing major.There's just so much of the stuff it really, really doesn't do well.There's a weapon cleaning mechanic that's a great idea, but you keep getting tossed in the mud, which takes it basically to zero, and it happens in scripted events.  Your reward for doing what the game keeps telling you to do is to have it be rendered useless by a cutscene.   You get injured in scripted events, too, and that's a real drag.The horror elements would be good if they didn't drag on so long.  I don't normally play games with horror elements, and in the early levels I was pretty on-edge most of the time.  A welcome new experience!  By the end of this game the enemies you're supposed to be worried about were just a drag.  Oh great, another ten bullet sponges.  Just like the last 8 rooms.  I think the devs wanted puzzles in the game.  There are no puzzles in the game.  There's just "Find the thing".  That's not a puzzle, and it's not fun.  I don't remember ever having to look for something in real life and thinking 'yay, this will be fun!'.  Especially when the lights stop working and I'm being attacked by stuff.I guess if I had to nail down the biggest problem, it's pacing.  Every new mechanic is invariably what you'll be doing for the next several hours.  Every single level had something going for it, was exciting and new, but by the end I was saying 'I'm SO done doing this same thing for last 8 hours.  Please, let me move on.  Oh, great, I've been knocked in the water in a scripted event.  AGAIN.'

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with an excellent story and an interesting take on the Metro formula. Story-wise,my favorite parts of the game are the transition levels between each open-world level as they really fleshed-out every member of the crew, particularly the relationship between Anna, Miller and Artyom. I especially liked the intimate moments between Anna and Artyom, however, the fact that Artyom is still a silent protagonist is quite an outdated choice considering the events that happen further in the game. Special mentions goes to the Two Colonels DLC, which may be the best part of the game in my opinion. The DLC has a great self-contained story that serves as a extension to the main story and has some tense moments which I highly recommend playing at least once.On the gameplay side of things, the gunplay is pretty good with each gun having a satisfying kick to it. However, Artyom's movement is pretty floaty, especially when sprinting as he will sometimes get launched off ledges which is a step back from Last Light's movement.Overall, I highly recommend this game for fans of the Metro series and it is definitely worth picking up for a quite long 40 hr experience.

If you are a masochist with a great deal of time to waste,  try it, but I'd recommend watching the grass grow in your backyard rather than invest a moment of your time on this.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first played Metro Exodus when it came out back in 2019, I finished the first 2 levels and put down the game with a disappointed exhale. 2 years later during quarantine I decided to pick it back up, and I told myself that I would finish it. I thought to myself it was the best game that I'd never finished - and I wanted to change that. So I sat down, and played it the whole way through. It turned out that Metro Exodus was not just the best game I'd never played, but one of the best games that should never go unplayed.I finally decided to get round to playing it once again and I love it every bit as much - and more. Playing on the enhanced edition has genuinely blown my mind - I'm playing with Ray Tracing at 100fps on high settings and it looks phenomenal - just how is this possible?? We all know how good Metro Exodus looks even in the standard edition so I won't get into it too much however, it's no understatement when I say that it is a serious sight to behold.Gameplay wise, Exodus totally reinvented what I thought an immersive experience was. I saw games like Far Cry 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 and thought that was what peak immersion looked like - now I look at Metro Exodus and say that nothing comes close to it at being as immersive. To put it simply, Exodus is a story driven, semi-open world, action shooter. What makes it unique though, is a heavy emphasis on player-driven exploration with little to no handholding (and yet, depending on the difficulty, it still feels totally fair). For example, during the first mission in the Volga there are a dozen or so places that you can choose to go, and just a few that you actually have to go to. Though I still felt compelled to do it all simply because I saw a destination and chose to go to it - after all, there might be some cool gear there right? Correct. Depending on how much you explore, you can gain access to all sorts of cool things from motion detectors to night vision goggles; it's excellent as it makes it very tempting and rewarding to simply explore. To further encourage exploration, similar to the old games, Metro Exodus restricts how much ammo you can carry. This at first might seem discouraging, but they cleverly utilise the crafting mechanic to allow you to use the resources you find to craft special bullets on the go, among other things. You can also swap out weapon parts on the fly - although to craft specific bullets you will have to find a craft bench. It may sound tedious but trust me, it's incredibly fun and spices up the gameplay by forcing you to try things you otherwise wouldn't.So what else makes Metro Exodus so immersive? Besides the mind-blowing, realistic graphics and animations, and deep-but-simple crafting and exploration mechanics, are the little things. For example: your map is an item you actually hold while walking around, your backpack is something you place down and use to craft instead of using a menu, walking into car doors moves them, etc. Something else you could easily ignore, yet I felt engaged enough to lookout for, is the conversations you can have with others, and the ones others have between themselves. It's hard to make dialogue sound natural, and yet they did it here near perfectly. Not only does this further your emotional investment in the story, but it seriously immerses you into this post-apocalyptic world by allowing you to naturally bond with the characters through just hanging out and watching them interact with each other. The game does an excellent job, almost like no other, at making your group genuinely feel like a real family.On the topic of conversations and characters - the story is phenomenal. There have only been 2 games that by the end had me 'going through the motions' and those games are none other than Red Dead Redemption 2 and this masterpiece - Metro Exodus. By the end of the game, assuming you've been paying attention, you really feel invested in the achievements and well-being of the crew (which in itself is quite the accomplishment). Obviously I won't spoil the ending but I think it's really important to make it clear that Exodus does a fantastic job at wrapping up the story in a way that not only leaves you to satisfied, but begging for more. Not many games pack enough punch to make a man cry but this one really does, especially depending on the ending you're served and the choices you made to get there.If you are interested in any of that, you will be thrilled to find out how long this game is - I estimate roughly 20-25 hours, maybe longer for completionists and even double the amount if you are an achievement hunter. If the length worries you, don't let it - there is no copy-pasted content here - every location and interaction is different and that is what solidifies Metro Exodus as one of the most impressive games to date.I must sound like a broken record by the end of my reviews because it seems like each one I do I'm handing out best game ever awards. However, Metro Exodus exceeded my expectations through and through - even a year after playing it for the first time - and still holds up against even the most high-budget titles out there. It is by all means a worthy contender for becoming your favourite game of all time and it damn well deserves it!I cannot recommend this enough.10/10I do also want to mention a few minor annoyances after I gave my score as to not put you off purchasing this as I do honestly believe that despite these few quirks that Exodus is one of the best games out there. To start with, while the enhanced edition does enhance the graphics with far superior lighting (despite the lighting already being amazing without ray-tracing), there are still persisting issues that there are no fixes for that don't exist within the regular edition. For example, what I thought originally to be a DLSS bug that made characters blurry when they moved actually turned out to be an issue with what I believe to be TAA or another graphical setting. The problem is made more troublesome by the fact that there isn't a detailed graphics option interface that lets you toggle specific graphical elements (such as TAA). So like I said, you cannot fix this bug. Another bug that I don't remember from old playthroughs is simply getting stuck on objects so small it's quite hard to avoid. On one specific occasion I had to reload a save to get unstuck, but there were maybe a dozen more times when more minor incidents happened on both visible and seemingly invisible objects. There were a few more bugs that I encountered but most (if not all) were minor - such as a floating chair which ultimately made me laugh. While I think that some of these bugs were somewhat annoying, it's important to make clear that they did not come close to ruining the experience or make me quit. There are enough bugs to stop me calling Exodus a polished game, but it's very close to it - all I will say is that if you intend on buying it, expect some bugs during your journey.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first play through of this game and these are my thoughts. This is one of those games I purchased several years ago while it was on sale and just never got around to playing it. Several years and a new PC later I decided that I wanted to start playing through a backlog of games I have on Steam that I've yet to touch and this brings to Metro Exodus Enhanced Edition. Overall I am very impressed with this game but it's not without some flaw.The game has you playing as Artyom, a competent member of a group known as the "Spartan Order" which boils down to special ops in the post apocalypse world of Metro Exodus. The formatting of the game essentially works like this, through a series of events you find yourself on a train named the Aurora headed east across the post nuclear wasteland that was once Russia. The train will stop for one reason or another in a new area and then after some cut scenes you will be given a series of optional and mandatory tasks to complete in a pseudo open world setting. Each map features a verity of different human and mutant types, not all humans are aggressive and the game has two different endings that can be altered based on your play style throughout.(The Good)I thoroughly enjoyed the different areas of exploration which ranged from a frozen over irradiated Moscow to a hot desert ruled by slave traders to a mountainous lush forest with tree people as well as a few others. I found myself eager to explore the different maps the game offers up. Much of the games lore and backstory can be found in audio logs, notes and people you will encounter in the wasteland so if learning the lore is your thing, be prepared to explore to get it all. The game play is smooth and tight, this is one of the rare games that get guns right, be sure to turn on spacial audio in the sound options when playing this game, it helped me feel more immersed with it on. Speaking of guns, the weapons in this game pack a nice punch, I found myself leaning heavily on the shotguns the game offers up as they we're great for taking on larger mutants and downright overkill in close proximity to any human opponent you may face outside of a few armored mini boss type variants. The weapons are largely customizable and you can craft your own ammunition for them, however if crafting is your thing, the system in place for Metro will probably seem a little weak to you as you really only collect two types of crafting material in the world and playing on normal difficulty I quickly found myself with an abundance of it, perhaps it's different on the higher difficulty settings.The enemy AI is competent, they will take cover and try to flank you, they will also speak to each other in mid combat outlining where they last saw you, lots of nice little touches like that add to the fun. Most of the mutants are pretty brainless as to be expected, depending on what kind of mutant they are they may just slowly shamble right up to you and practically let you put your gun in their mouth or they may just charge at you full head of steam. The one that stood out to me was one known as the demon, some kind of flying apex predator, it will grab you by the shoulders and attempted to carry you away if you are out in the open, in any case the baddies in this game are numerous and of nice verity.On top of it's fantastic sound effects this game is graphically beautiful, I am played it on a I7-13700K/4090 system and with the graphics maxed out the game was absolutely gorgeous, I averaged between 130fps and 200fps at max settings during my entire play through.(The Bad)Despite largely smooth game play I did experience a total of three crashes that booted me from the game, one of which required me to crtl/alt/del and reset my computer to escape it. Not a huge issue, but worth noting. Next up, the voice acting to me was hit and miss at times. This game is also pretty intense on your PC, despite having a powerful liquid cooled 4090 setup, at max graphics I found myself opening windows in my bedroom to cool things down, My PC normally doesn't blink and much of anything currently out there but  Metro definitely made sure my GPU fans for working full time.I played it in the English dub and some of the voice acting was a little hard to not snicker at, particularly the over sentimental dialogue given to you by your in game wife Anna. That may just be a personal nitpick but it was something that occasionally stood out to me during my experience, perhaps the Russian dub is better. On the subject of voice acting, strangely enough our guy Artyom is strangely a silent protagonist, I understand why games with heavy RPG elements make the player character a silent protagonist, I however found it an odd decision to go with in Metro as the game play loop of Metro is pretty liner with a well defined story and established protagonist, making Artyom silent led to some weird instances of silence when in conversation with other people.Despite praising the AI earlier it's sort of double edged, while I enjoyed my encounters with bandits and mutants, in some instances the AI allows itself to be easily exploited a sound method for taking them out in droves is to get into a position where all your enemy's can only reach you through a bottleneck, they'll come running right into the choke point guns blazing every time just to capped as soon as they enter your field of view, I on a couple of occasions wiped out an entire camps doing that. However, this wasn't a terribly consistent occurrence so it's not a huge issue.On normal difficulty I found the game quiet easy. I was generally able to easily mow through entire bandit camps without much fear of dying, same can be said for most of the boss encounters in the game, however in an effort to see the other ending and get more achievements I will be playing through it again after writing this review and will likely go with a higher difficulty setting which will hopefully make the experience more challenging.(Verdict)Overall I thoroughly enjoyed my first play through of Metro Exodus. While there are some nitpicks I had a long the way there was nothing that was a deal breaker to my enjoyment of this game, the worst of it being the three crashes I experienced during my nearly 15 hour first run of it. This game is worth every bit of the $30 its listed on Steam for. If you happen to catch it on sale than even better. If you like FPS shooters or the idea of a beautiful Russian wife simulator than this game is a no brainier, I am sorry that I took so long to pick it up and give it a go.(Pros)- Fantastic gun play.- Beautiful graphics.- Wonderful sound design.- Immersive and engaging game play.- Engaging AI "most of the time".- Surprisingly diverse environments.- $30 price tag without a sale "worth every penny of that" - Simple easy to use crafting/upgrading system(Cons)- Under performing voice acting at times.- Occasional crash.- Why is Artyom mute?- When AI is not engaging it can be a bit on the stupid side.- A bit on the easy side "speaking from normal difficulty".- Rudimentary crafting/upgrading system lacking somewhat in verity.(Final Score)8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow where to begin after beating a game like this. In short, I loved it. The game itself was breathtaking, and I highly recommend it to everyone who contemplates purchasing it. It's a well crafted, innovative, and beautiful game.Mechanically the game is very smooth. The effects, interactions, game play, and handling are for the most part seamless. With the very rare hiccup here and there that might through you off. However, these are to be expected when you try to make the game as mechanically complex as they did Metro. It's quite innovative, and the presentation of it all makes it feel incredibly immersive. The implementation of a resource management system in this game felt both right, and proper. Added some nice layering, made you pay more attention, did everything that it's supposed to do. UI was clean and I like the guns, though some are clearly better than others. A very important note is the utilization of stealth mechanics in this game. It is without a doubt crucial during certain points at minimum on hardcore (my chosen difficulty), to choose stealth over action. Especially so if you want good results in your story. The execution of stealth is in my opinion well done. Without much knowledge regarding the parameters set around the AI; I'd say that it felt consistent and reasonable in almost every situation. Cover felt real, the utilization of dark spaces felt effective, and noise levels felt correct. If you shot a silent weapon at a person they wouldn't be like "Ah yes I am being shot at", rather, "Huh, what was that noise? Is that an enemy?" Then they would begin sweeping the area. While if I shot my Kalash, they would very much so be like "Ah yes, enemy has shot his gun." In summary, I reiterate that the game play is very nice, interactions are phenomenal, and I loved every second of experiencing the game. Now my favorite part of this game, the story. This has got to be one of my favorite stories to play through. Not necessarily better then say Horizon, which I loved, but different. The utilization of a morality system, and a butterfly effect makes an otherwise linear plot, much more complex. Actions become incredibly heavy handed, and you need to choose your moves carefully. I became attached to the characters in an instant, and felt like Artyom while playing this game. The lore, depth of writing, pacing, attention to detail, progression, is all there. There were some instances that had me at the edge of my seat, others that had me jumping out of it. Metro Exodus, for all of my fellow story loving gamers, simply is a must play. Graphics wise, the game is showing it's age but on the enhanced edition with ray-tracing it looked very pleasing. Their chosen art direction is appealing to the eye and leaves nothing to be desired. I have an I5-13600K and 3080 12gb. Stock, I was able to achieve around 130fps with DLSS Quality on ULTRA quality RTX. The very rare render bug (I can account for 3, like a floating monitor where clearly a table failed to render in) is not worth mentioning. Optimization is excellent, stuttering, tearing, and drops where all rare/nonexistent. Overall the game runs very well on my rig when pushing for top graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Main Campaign:One of the best narrative driven shooters I've ever played. Exodus is a bit of a diversion from 2033 and Last Light as it introduces almost Far Cry levels of freedom in huge sand box stages, but you never feel lost and there's always a clear goal. The storyline running through the game and the cast of characters is really quite impressive overall. Initially you feel quite helpless but as time goes on and you master the tools supplied and learn how to adapt weapons for situations and how to know when all out gunfights or stealth is key. Looks great on 4K but I'm looking forward to the next gen update too. Special mention must also go the the AI who talk to each other and know where you are if you let yourself be seen...! Varied missions, lots of modifications to be made weapons and gear, lots of exploring, a brilliant story, superb voice cast and great pacing. Literally one of the best games I've ever played.      MainCampaign : 10/10DLC:1 : Sams Story : Sam's story seems amazing...if it's the first of a series of episodes featuring Sam's journey from Vladivostock to Los Angeles.The setting is very akin to Volga and Taiga, to which the first is not my favourite level and the second, whilst very interesting, was very linear by comparison. The swamp/flooded parts of the map are the worst experience, luckily the motorboat makes driving around a breeze than rowing clumsily around.Main questline feels very cheesy, and speaking of which seems to entirely dominate the game experience, whereas in the base game, the larger maps and open-world nature allowed you to scout out areas for goodies and upgrades. This would have been possible had the travelling part of the map was either water based (which in practicality limited the open world concept) and the few ground travelling was entire linear, and often scripted as well!I really wish 4A games makes some more DLC campaigns for Sam, he can travel north to find an ice crossing, bringing back an open-world winter/snow map that follows a story where he obtains passage to an ice crossing in Kamchatka; there he can cross the frozen sea and make stops at the islands for some side missions. A third chapter has him traversing down Alaska and Canada, where American, Canadian and others (including Russians) survivors can be encountered as enemies or friends. And of course mutated Alaskan wildlife battling non-mutated animals.Anyways enough rambling; Sam's Story is so-so, I just wish it was the beginning of a series of DLC chapters featuring Sam. DLC ;1  Sams Story : 9/10DLC: 2: The Two Colonels : A short, contained, classic Metro experience. Around 2 hours at it was all over. Some technical improvements were made to the already impressive ray tracing effects on PC. To showcase their prowess, the developers made the primary weapon of the player character, Colonel Khlebnikov, a flamethrower. And by primary weapon, I mean only weapon.Despite its condensed length, I found the combat felt pretty one note and repetitive by the end. Jump scare, spray flames until room clears, a few quiet tense, rusty corridors, repeat. The hammy English VO does contain some occasionally clumsy lines, but I did find the story to be entertaining. It's almost like a vignette, with the entire emotional arc of the main game but taking place over a much shorter time span. There's nothing groundbreaking here, but the parallel timelines of the two lead characters intersect cleverly, and I found the characterization and portrayal of fatherhood to be endearing, if a little overwrought at times.Without spoilers, the last few sections of the game lean heavily into the horror aspect of the survival horror experience found in the Metro series. The excellent sound design and clever gameplay balance choices made with the inclusion of the flamethrower create some genuinely tense sections. Your flashlight is removed, instead replaced by the flickering yellow flame of your weapons pilot light. The reduced visibility and arsenal, coupled with the slower aiming and reload times force a more cautious pace, even compared to the full games already contemplative speed. DLC ;2: The Two Colonels 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus is a beautiful, yet flawed game. For context, I've played every game in the Metro series around the time they came out, and they've all been a blast. In particular, I think the setting has always been a strong point throughout the whole series thanks to it's basis on the wonderful novels by Dmitry Glukhovsky.Having said that, it's actually still hard for me to tell how much rose-colored tint I'm peering through when thinking back to the older games. Because let me tell you, it sure wasn't all sunshine and rainbows when I first started Exodus. After a very long load screen with multiple janky resolution changes, followed by a game crash. I was finally able to get to the menu and actually start the campaign on the second try. Unfortunately, It's hard to call the first chapter anything but rushed though. One moment you're on the surface, "chasing" down ghosts in the ether, getting chewed out by all your friends and colleagues for needlessly irradiating yourself. Then not 5 minutes later, after everyone lambasted you for being a fool. Everyone is in a clamor, cheering and calling you a hero for discovering that there really is life outside Moscow. Maybe there's some ironic realism to this scenario, but I personally found the way the whole experience was put together to be quite jarring and amusement park ride-esque. I felt like I was going through a lot of important events and emotions far too quickly. I normally wouldn't harp on a game's opening chapter so much, but I think what really makes it impossible to ignore was the frankly awful dialogue. Thank goodness I remembered that these games have full original Russian voicing and subtitles because without that I may have actually quit the game before getting out of Moscow. I mention this specifically because I feel that while still not great, the writing comes across much better with the Russian voice acting. I think that's mostly due to the fact that many of the language's little limericks, proverbs, and other turns of phrase are almost impossible to translate. Thus, hearing the characters speak in their "native" language makes them sound a lot more human, especially as a fluent speaker of both Russian and English. Personally, I also found Anna went from intolerable to actually fairly likable. So that's all to say do yourself a favor, and switch the game to the correct language if you can right off the bat. Coincidentally, I think the narrative and character of the game was strongest in the last chapter. Even though gameplay then was more "traditional" like the older games, it was in this chapter that the writers did the most showing and the least telling. With great use of environments to convey stories and many cool moments where you are shown glimpses of the past in original and sometimes creepy ways. Some of the more spooky aspects of the franchise also come rearing their heads or lack thereof here. Which was sadly largely missing from the rest of the campaign. I think the odd radiation induced phenomena to be one of the more interesting concepts in the Metro universe. I'll also mention here that the ending did feel a little sudden, but not nearly as jarring as the beginning. Character writing was decent, but besides Artyom and a couple others, there isn't really much development. Yermak feels downright forgotten which is a shame since he had such an interesting introduction. Overall, the plot has a very original concept and good drive, even if told in a somewhat clumsy and unoriginal fashion. Having briefly touched on it earlier, let's talk about arguably the best part of the game. The world and environments. I find the premise of riding a massive armored locomotive with a bunch of your comrades through the irradiated wastes of post-apocalyptic Russia to be enthralling. You travel to several fresh and creative settings with a great variety of well designed and beautiful environments to explore. Each one making it's own unique and disturbing mark on your journey to a new home. This is very impressive for several reasons. Not the least of which being the fact that all the previous installments were entirely within claustrophobic tunnels under Moscow. This is the series' first shot at "open-world" environments and it's a blast! They're both artistically inspired, and well laid out to make exploration fun without being a chore to get around. In between each level, you also get a chance to walk around the train and talk to various characters and catch up on their threads. Actually, if there's one thing this game has no shortage of, it's dialogue. You can spend hours listening to everyone in the world which is really cool, but also a bit boring at times. I found a lot of conversations that just kept going about 3 times after I thought they were over. Nevertheless, I think these segments are great, and added a lot to the feeling of making progress especially as cars and characters were added to the train. see the rest here:

_childDocuments_.review: The only reason I'm recommending this game is because the DLCs make up for what a mess the main game is. I'm glad to have played those last as it would be the only memorable thing.I'd suggest buying Metro Exodus only when it's on sale or playing the first two Metro games instead to enjoy the true Metro experience.

_childDocuments_.review: The best post-apocalyptic first-person shooter there is. The first instalment was very good immersive action adventure , second one got top notch action epic pieces, more high stakes drama and layer complication in script writing. And now the third one is a masterfully crafted amalgamation of all those best features in semi-open world mechanic. Like if you played STALKER and wished METRO got same survival and ecosystem open world features, now your wishes came into reality and realised WAY better. Every nook and cranny has something to find and to see. Action is well paced and designed for open action encounters or stealth approach. Plot scenes are very much diversified and awesomely designed - one time you are hijacking full ahead steaming trains through desolate nuclear winter scenery, one time you are slowly rowing a rotting boat in a midst of mutant infested rainy swamp, or driving an old soviet van through sands of dried up sea bank in a middle of mad max like desert. Survival mechanics on highest difficulty are engaging and fair,  but always keep you on the edge of your seat for scavenging and saving resources, or finding other ways to solve the encounters. The negatives are some plot forced linear sections where stealth is vital for good ending, there are so much limitations and bugs in stealth comparing in contrast with well designed open world sections - they are truly infuriating sometimes... Although Taiga level is exception - it was so smoothly designed to finish it in complete stealth.And finally most important one is obviously immersive atmosphere, story and characters. The train hub idea was so good, it gives you a strong attachment to your companions and friends, your moving fortress, your common goal to find a new home. Magical experience!

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 but please keep reading. I've already finished this game once because I own it on EGS also. There are some things that you need to know since it seems a lot of people get the wrong idea going into this game because it is poorly marketed. This is a story driven FPS horror game with a heavy emphasis on stealth.There's no open world. There's no sandbox to play in. It's a shame those tags are applied to it. There are multiple levels. Some of them are decently large. Much larger than the areas in previous Metro titles. But this is a story driven game. Once you advance the story, there's no going back to explore. The game moves on and anything you missed might be gone forever.Gameplay wise... very fun. Super immersive. You won't be menuing. Guns, items, map, they're all mapped to buttons. Your HUD is basically on your wrist. Guns seem well weighted. Sneaking around is fun, has an MGS feel to it. Enemies are varied from area to area and new ones are introduced as you progress. Also imo this game has the best jump scares of any game I've ever played. You will make bird noises.The story is more or less you're hoping to find that there's life beyond the radioactive hellscape you currently inhabit. No spoilers here beyond that. There's plenty of between level cutscenes but they don't take forever. There are also optional side quests that tie in to NPCs.Graphics are still looking hot even 4 years later. How can you not appreciate the level of detail in the disgusting post apocalyptic sinks and toilets? I encountered a few graphical bugs in my first playthrough but nothing game breaking. A coupe of enemies still twitching after death, one time the sky didn't load after I died, nbd.The DLC is worth it overall. The Two Colonels is a walking simulator with a flame thrower. Short and simple. Great story addition, but skippable if you're looking for more action. Sam's Story is where the action is. You get new weapons, there's new enemies, traps to disarm, and a killer boss fight. And it isn't over quickly. There's a few hours of play time, not going to spoil how long though.So if you're looking for a great looking horror story first person stealth/shooter this is your jam. If you want an open world sandbox FPS then look elsewhere. I highly recommend this game.  It isn't perfect but I can't think of anything that was annoying or made me not want to continue playing. Highly improved over the previous titles, noticeable QOL additions, I'm looking forward to what this studio does next. 9/10 all day.

_childDocuments_.review: Ran into a game breaking bug 14 hours into the game. Tried to fix it for three more hours. Couldn't fix it, 4A doesn't patch the game anymore and it's a known issue. No solutions.Avoid this game like the plague! The gameplay is amazing, the graphics are great, BUT YOU CAN'T ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ FINISH THE GAME! What's the point in playing a game where you spend most of your time trying to load saves and fix bugs?I was looking forward to this game SO much... it spurred me to buy a new RTX 2060 so I could play it. And now they burned me and left me with an unplayable game. I don't think I'll ever buy a 4A/Deep Silver product ever again now, they do not care about their customers.Edit 4/13/22: I restarted the entire game and uninstall/reinstalled it, and played through the entire story successfully without running into any more game-breaking bugs. If you get the bug where you can't interact with anything... just restart everything. Completely. I highly recommend the use of a trainer or table (it's single player, no one has to know) in order to bypass certain pains in restarting the game, such as repetitive fights and world exploration to find all the item attachments. I used one to get through the Volga area in 1/4th the time it originally took so I could ensure the bug was gone when I reached Yamantau. In general, it made the game more enjoyable by being able to ignore many of the bugs and flaws present in the final release.It was a good game, with amazing graphics, gameplay mechanics, and characters. There were a few scenes where I cried because of how deep the characters are in this game, it was simply breathtaking.Gameplay - 9/10Story - 8/10Graphics - 10/10Re/Playability - 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to start with this. I haven't felt this attached to a single-player game like this since Red Dead Redemption 2, which was 4 years ago. This is my first introduction to the Metro series, which probably wasn't the smartest move but something about this game was just screaming at me to play it. But now, I'm 100% going to play the others to see how Artyom was before Exodus.Gameplay, sounds, dialogue, atmosphere, story, all phenomenal. Breathtaking visuals with great game optimization. This game feels superb and very polished and there wasn't a single dull moment in the game. The ending was truly unexpected and will leave you absolutely speechless. I do wish it was a bit longer than what it is, because of how amazing the story is, but that isn't saying that it's too short. It was just that good.I can't recommend this game enough. If you're looking for a single-player experience that has all the greats a AAA game should have, then this is definitely what you should go for.

_childDocuments_.review: My best experience playing Games so far!!!I've been wasting my time online for quite some time now and I really, really have to say that this is, by far, the greatest experience I've had in years. I recommend playing the first two games (Metro 2033 and Metro Last Light) before starting this beauty, since you will be introduced to the story the game is based on, as well as general mechanics and characters. Allthough this is a different take on the Metro universe (Not with as much "Metro") it just perfectly fits the feeling of the game. You are more free to do things -its a semi-open-world- while the first two games are more, but not only, linear. All three games together should add up to over 50 hours of playtime, if you're trying to get to all the sidequests and eastereggs (which are perfectly implemented in the story btw.) as well. For me, personally, the games are worth easily over 100€, despite the first two games being over 10 years old. The Metro universe is based on books and this really helps providing emotions and relations between characters; the end of exodus actually had me in tears. But if you buy it or not and for how much is up to you, I hope you'll enjoy the games as much as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels awesome in every aspect. Probably the best campaign game I have ever played.The gameplay is amazing. The combination of mutants, bandits and the occasional friendly people make the NPC variety diverse and immersive. Weapons have many upgrade options and you get a really nice overall progression throughout the entire playthrough. Having suit upgrades is the icing on the cake. Also being able to switch weapon attachments on the go and tune your gear before a mission is absolutely incredible. The stealth element is implemented very well to, with lights you can disable and the ability to switch the time of day by sleeping in safe locations.The story is, in my opinion, mind-blowing. Events are scattered nicely throughout the entire game. There are also lots of side missions which add to the lore. And getting the butterfly effect (decisions in the game that change the outcome) incorporated as well?! A ton of work has been put into this game, clearly. Collectibles are also found in the world and really expand on the story. Even just visually so much effort has been put for things like dead bodies and dusty rooms to tell a tale and add to the experience. I also want to mention that this game's finale made me tear up which is quite rare for any campaign game to pull off on grown men.Graphics-wise you won't be left disappointed. Every single texture is well detailed. There are sometimes particles in the air which add to the experience. Lighting is just stunning which is crucial for stealth games. Water is also realistic looking as well as the sky and clouds. Trees, grass and bushes don't fall behind as well.I could go about this game all day long but the final verdict is that this game is just out of this world. And at such a low price it's a steal. Definitely recommend this game to anyone who loves FPS, stealth and story. I honestly struggled to think of any flaws apart from the seemingly long time to change graphics settings. But that in itself is a minor inconvenience.Finally, I'll say it one last time: the game is must, 10 out of 10. Don't think, buy.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the main criticisms leveled at this game was that it wasn’t like the previous two metro games. I mean, a metro game...that doesn’t take place in the metro. Well, it’s called Metro Exodus for a reason: an exodus out of the moscow metro. And look, I get it, a franchise should be about a certain thing and people who like that thing will keep buying games about it. But we already had two full fledged games set in the moscow metro with plenty of stations – go replay them if you want to return to that environment, but at some point, the story has to move on, preferably to somewhere new. And when you put yourself back in the year 2019 when this game released, the last good STALKER games we had had were already almost a decade old. And since both franchises are somewhat related, the dev team decided to take inspiration from the STALKER franchise and actually give us a good spiritual sequel to those games with voiced characters and jaw dropping graphics. And that is exactly what Metro Exodus delivers. Less moscow metro, more STALKER tundra, taiga and even desert exploration. So how exactly does that happen? You and a small group of pals get aboard a train which takes you from location to location, and each location has a different environment and is basically a miniature open world bubble. Explore it, resolve the quests therein, then catch your train to the next bubble. Pretty genius game design. For the 2000s.One thing I didn’t like about Stalker Exodus, woops Metro Exodus, is that the game throws you right into the action with no slow buildup like in previous games which spend some time introducing you not just to the game mechanics but also to the setting, like waking up in the coziness of Exhibition station in Metro 2033 and walking your way through the lived in, zero privacy environment while admiring the graphics way back in 2010 when not even Crysis had created such realistic urban living spaces and had decided to focus on nature instead. And in Metro Last Light you do the same in Polis station. So in comparison to the previous two, I guess the third installment in the series really is meant to be played right after you finish Metro Last Light, have had enough of exploring underground tunnels, but like the lore and want to take the next step in the adventure. You start the game as veteran Artyom, returning from an outdoor trip exploring irradiated moscow and back into the canal system where you soon find yourself burning spiderwebs with your zippo and scrounging for ammunition before getting attacked by nosalis-like dog/bat creatures which are now called watchmen.After making it back to the station in a wounded state and having to receive blood transfusions to get rid of the radiation, you wake up to a furious Anna who you are now married to, the daughter of ranger captain Miller who tells you not to keep returning to the surface and listening to the radio static because there really is nobody out there, but you refuse to listen and are soon out exploring again, and this time, spot a train belonging to the Hansa faction and board it, realizing there may be life outside the moscow metro and this is your one chance to escape the city, so you seize the opportunity.Metro exodus offers a crafting system that uses two resources: parts and chemicals. You pick these up as you explore the map and can then spend them as resources to craft medkits, throwing knives, or molotovs, but also ammo for your weapons. Similarly, you have to periodically clean your weapons to reduce their risk of jamming. Another aspect is weapon customization. Think Fallout 4, but you can’t craft attachments from raw materials and must instead find them. You start the game with two different weapons, an assault rifle and a pistol, and as you progress in the game and come across dead enemies, you can either switch your weapon for theirs, or remove the ammo in its magazine and any attachments it has. These attachments can then be applied to your weapons when you are at a workbench. Scopes, grips, tubing, these attachments usually make your weapon better, but not all the time. Sometimes, they decrease the damage  but increase the rate of fire or silence the weapon. Enemies have a low detection radius and therefore can be avoided, as ammunition remains scarce – only defend yourself when attacked, don’t try picking a fight with everyone. As you explore each free roam bubble, main quests and side quests take you to various corners of said bubble. You can check where you are on a map you carry with you and left clicking it turns it around and shows you the quest entries. Main quests however also have a narration when you load the game, so playing for too long will make you miss out on some of the narration.Which brings me to another thing I didn’t like about this game: there is so much dialogue. Standing next to an NPC makes him chat with you almost constantly, and you don’t feel like moving away cause you may miss out on some of the lore related things he has to say, but you also don’t know when he’s done. And standing next to several characters will make all of them speak in turns and you quickly lose track of what they are saying. The mediocre voice actors and russian accents do their part in muddying the waters in terms of listening comprehension. And it also doesn’t help that the Metro universe has a rather complicated lore to start with.In terms of graphics, this is a relatively demanding game. Turning on ray tracing and all the settings to max can cripple even an 80 class 30 series card at 4k. However, DLSS quality offers a massive framerate boost, almost twice as much as it does in cyberpunk, so playing at native is really not advisable. The original version of Metro Exodus which released in 2019 came with DLSS 1 which made the game blurry and was not worth the framerate boost, but the Enhanced Edition comes with DLSS 2 with varying settings and quality is almost identical to native so definitely go for it. That being said, at 4k, 8GB cards will still run into VRAM issues, so I recommend midrange 30 series cards stick to 1440p dlss quality for a smooth >60fps ray traced experience. Speaking of ray tracing, I feel bad for AMD card owners, cause there definitely is a bigger difference in terms of visuals in this game than in e.g. cyberpunk where it gets relentless praise even though it doesn’t do much except e.g. make the reflections of neon signs stay in puddles even when you are no longer looking at the sign. But in Metro Exodus, raytracing definitely changes the look of the game. On one hand, people complain that it makes the game less dark and perhaps takes away a bit from the feel of realism when you stay in the shadows. On the other hand, there are many instances where even Metro’s engine looks rather flat and cartoonish but ray tracing hides this with global illumination, bathing everything in more volumetric and diffuse sunlight.So overall, I’d say this is definitely a triple A title and you should give it a go, especially if you played STALKER and wanted better graphics for it. If you prefer the underground tunnel exploration experience, then stick to the previous two titles in the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: + Complete Russian experience with desolate landscapes, fighting for survival, and smoke/vodka breaks.+ Global illumination lighting is *chefs kiss*+ High dedication to NPC interactions.+ Russian waifu ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)- Infinite enemy spawn. Why would they do this? The game is trying to make you feel like a survivor where you scout for supplies, keep your weapons clean, make your shots count... and then it throws wave after wave of bullet sponge enemies at you. This actively discourages exploration. Enemies will literally respawn 5 minutes after you clear an area / go into a building and go back outside.- You die in a couple hits, but enemies can take quite a few in their alert state.- NPC dialogue and exposition can be cheesy and boring. Especially during the first part of the game.- The last 20 minutes of gameplay, including the ending you are most likely to get, suck bad. The game keeps some kind of odd morality meter hidden away from you that counts toward getting a good or bad ending. If you kill someone who was 30 seconds earlier trying to knife you, this counts against you and somehow changes the ending? They could have made this clearer at the very least, but you would think the concept of "good" and "evil" actions get blurry in a post-apocalyptic world.- The game goes from frustrating, to cool and making you want more, back to frustrating again. Mainly due to the above complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: As my first game in the metro series, it was quite a solid game!it looks gorgeous, and there is clearly a lot of attention to detail.repairing / customizing weapons, handling radiation filters, charging electronic devicesthe options to shoot lights or turn them off adds to stealth significantlyoption to kill / knock out enemies, is a nice additionThe story is quite interesting, engaging and easy to put yourself into.cutscenes are a bit awkward, especially with the sound effects, but a welcome additionGameplay is where i'm somewhat divided. My playthrough was on hardcore.Ammo was quite comfortable around 5hrs in, in fact I never used the 3rd weapon once during my playthrough. My 2 primaries, which were the pistol + ak, after the first zone I was sitting around 100+ ammo each, using headshots in stealth sections and using knockdowns when I could. Could be just me but that ruined the immersion of "ammo is rare only use it when you MUST" post apocalyptic scenario, as I was quickscoping enemies left right and centre for basically 80% of the gameAnother waste is that there are so many weapon options + 4 ammo types but you can only actually carry 2 guns at onceThe alternative to the 3rd weapon is better but comes too late to matter.revolver + silencer = too overpoweredMy biggest disapointment is the the wasted potential by including a silent protagonist. It feels so weird as people dump dialogue on and on and you're just there absorbing it all, in some scenes it even looks like you replied, so the character actually continues a convo whilst you're only hearing 1 side of the conversation. It didn't even have to be anything special, just some simple voice lines here n there. TLDR; amazing graphics, solid story, varying gameplay experience depending on skill, worthwhile the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Metro Exodus had a lot of promise. A vast wasteland to explore after the claustrophobic Metro tunnels? Sign me up! But for fans of the previous Metro games, Exodus feels like a bit of a letdown. Here's why:- Wide as a lake, shallow as a puddle: The open world sections are expansive, but they lack the density and detail of the Metro tunnels. You spend a lot of time just traveling from point A to point B with not much interesting to find in between.- Farewell, claustrophobia: The tension that came from the tight spaces and limited resources in the Metro is gone. Exodus feels more like a standard shooter in a post-apocalyptic setting.- Characters Take a Hit: Exodus introduces a new cast, but they never quite reach the depth of the characters we met in the Moscow tunnels.  Their motivations feel underdeveloped, and their interactions repetitive. The dialogues are clunky and unnatural.- Forget Metro, follow the waypoint: The open world also hurts the story pacing. Metro Exodus often feels like a series of fetch quests strung together rather than a cohesive narrative. - Semi-Open, Mostly Linear: The desperation and moral ambiguity of the previous games are replaced by a more predictable good-versus-evil story.- Forced Stealth: The open world design often pushes you towards stealth, but the enemy AI can be janky and the detection feels inconsistent.Exodus isn't a terrible game by any means. The core gunplay is solid, and the weapon customization is good (although feels like a chore after the first hours). The environments, while empty, can be beautiful. But for those who loved the atmosphere and tension of the Metro games, Exodus feels like a different beast altogether.If you're looking for a wide-open wasteland shooter, there are better options out there.  If you crave the unique blend of survival horror and post-apocalyptic storytelling that made the first two Metro games great, you might want to stick with those instead.- You loved the claustrophobic dread of the Metro games.- You prefer open-world exploration over scripted sections.- You were invested in the character development and moral struggles of the Metro games.- You crave a story with a strong sense of player agency and choice.- You enjoyed the unique atmosphere and dialogue of the previous Metro games.
