_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to play story driven open world FPS games, I gave Fallout 4 a shot and got bored 2 hours in, but I had heard great things about this game and decided to get it since is was on sale. Let me say this game did not disappoint. I played the enhanced version with a RTX 3080 and cranked the settings and I'll tell you this game is gorgeous, textures are great, the ray-tracing while overrated still does make a difference in fidelity, the most impressive thing to me though was the water. I feel that most games cant get water right, the way it reflects and the waves and stuff I mean. 4A did a amazing job with the water here.The voice acting at least in the English version I feel could be better, the way that the characters convey emotion through the voice acting makes them sound monotone at times, but for the most part its good, just could be better.  Sound design is great, guns sound beefy as well as clear and bright if that makes sense. The footstep sounds also sound great no matter what material your traveling over which is a nice touch.The story and narrative is a win for me. Post Apocalyptic/Post Nuclear war Russia is a great sounding setting for any book, let alone video game.  The Mutants and beasts are unique and grotesque, although they can get annoying at times. I also like the atmosphere that they game can put off at times. (Minor Spoilers here) For example whenever Artyom and Miller get to the metro in the "Dead City", at one point you start walking past a lot of dead bodies, I don't know if it was just me but it really started to creep me out, it gave me the feeling of playing a horror game rather than an FPS which really hammered home the feeling of helplessness and horror these people felt before their death, it makes you feel more of the significance of what the effects of Nuclear war might look like in a creepy or scary way, which is the way it should be betrayed. All in all I give this game a 10/10 and I will definitely be playing more Metro games to come. One of the best games I have ever played to date.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the first 2 games, this does succeed in making more exciting story and characters that you get invested in than the first 2. A great positive was allowing you to continue to listen to people's stories and them talking which grants you the option to pace yourself your own way instead of filling the game with cutscenes. At first I thought the amount of characters might have made it confusing, but each character grows into their own personality as you progress. I also enjoyed the playstyle that they kept the option to get the good ending for only killing the bad guys, makes the gameplay more creative. The gripes I do have are the open world. I believe the linear gameplay of the first 2 games allowed for more polished levels where you enjoy getting through to get to the story. The open world of Metro Exodus makes it more of a chore to get to story parts because having to run around to different objectives that take a long time while also running into random enemies is very annoying and slows the pacing of the game. At the end of the game it becomes a linear again and I realized how much more I enjoyed it than the open expanses in the previous chapters. I do understand they went open world because, for the first time, we finally get to explore outside of Moscow and to show how limited the metro in Moscow really was. I hope for their next game they improve the open world and make it more enjoyable to move around. Other than that, it definitely is a great successor to the previous 2 amazing games. If you have not played the previous games, make sure you do, you will not understand the story as well if you don't.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has such high highs, that it way out balances the lows. I’m not going to say graphics, but the environmental detail. The exploration is great, and the zones are large enough to keep it interesting. The voice acting is superb as well. Downsides – confusing routing and quests. You never quite know if you’re going the right direction. Gunplay is a little flat, but the crossbow is super fun to use. Sometime get stuck in lengthy dialogue or singing when all I had to do was click something to move one. All in all I recommend, levels are all different and short enough to not overstay its welcome.

name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series
detailed_description: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series contains all 4 Seasons, 400 Days, and The Walking Dead: Michonne, which includes over 50 hours of gameplay across 23 unique episodes. With graphical enhancements, behind the scenes bonus features and faithful recreations of classic menus, this is the definitive way to experience Clementine’s journey and find out how her story ends. Graphical Enhancements: “Graphic Black” art style brings Season 4’s enhanced visual style to all previous seasons of the acclaimed series. Will also include full dynamic lighting to episodes that previously did not receive this upgrade. Behind the Scenes Bonuses: Exclusive looks at the making of the game from the developers, VO artists, and other team members that brought Clementine’s story to life. This includes over 10+ hours of developer commentary and “Return of the Walking Dead” documentary short. Gameplay Improvements: Character performances, lip syncing, and other gameplay and UI enhancements make this the definitive Telltale’s The Walking Dead experience. Even more digital bonuses: Music player that includes 40+ tracks across all seasons, art gallery, 3D model viewer with playable voice lines, and new 3D front end that still includes the original menus and music from all past seasons.

_childDocuments_.review: An Outstanding Example of Interactive Storytelling in The Walking Dead: Telltale Definitive SeriesAn absolute gem of interactive storytelling is The Walking Dead: Telltale Definitive Series. The Walking Dead: Michonne, 400 Days, and all four of Telltale's critically acclaimed seasons make up this collection, which is the best way to immerse yourself in one of the most moving and captivating storylines in video game history.Emotional and Immersion NarrationThe show throws you into a zombie apocalyptic world from the very first episode, where every decision you make counts and will follow you for the rest of your trip. With regard to forging emotional bonds with its characters, the game is particularly good at doing so with Lee Everett and Clementine.In his quest to keep young Clementine safe, Lee must make many difficult choices, painful sacrifices, and morally dubious decisions. Every language option seems dramatic and natural, and the writing is excellent. It's hard to stay emotionally detached from the characters' plight because of how skillfully the emotional highs and lows are written.Relationship Development and Character DevelopmentExemplary character growth can be found in The Walking Dead: Telltale Definitive Series. It takes amazing depth and detail to show Clementine's transformation from a terrified young child into a strong and resourceful survivor. The show excels at making you care about the individuals you encounter and giving the bonds you create a real sense of significance.Each character is well-developed, with their own backstories, motivations, and complexities. The bonds you form, whether they are friendships, rivalries, or something more complicated, add layers to the narrative that make every interaction feel meaningful.Impactful Choices and ConsequencesOne of the standout features of the series is its choice-based gameplay. The decisions you make, no matter how small they seem at the moment, can have far-reaching consequences. The game does not shy away from putting you in morally gray situations where there are no easy answers. This creates a sense of immersion and urgency that few other games can match.Not only can your decisions impact a scene's immediate result, but they can also have an impact on upcoming episodes and even seasons. Your journey seems distinctive and personalized because of this consistency, which allows you to sculpt the narrative to suit your goals and ideals.Improvements to the Audio and VisualThe audio and images are much improved in The Definitive Series. The Walking Dead universe is brought to life like never before thanks to the game's updated graphics, which also include better lighting, character models, and surroundings. The revised visual style adds a refined, contemporary touch while maintaining the original series' comic book appeal.The aural enhancements are similarly remarkable. The voice acting is excellent, evoking a variety of emotions and giving the characters more nuance. The eerie soundtrack and background sounds in the sound design help to fully transport you to the post-apocalyptic setting.Entire Bonus ContentFans will like the abundance of supplementary content that the Definitive Series offers in addition to the main episodes. This already comprehensive product gains further value from behind-the-scenes elements, developer commentary, and a music player that lets you listen to the game's eerily gorgeous soundtrack. These features let you appreciate the craftsmanship that went into creating the series and give you a deeper look at how it was made.In ConclusionAn outstanding example of interactive narrative is The Walking Dead: Telltale Definitive Series. Its rich characters, dramatic decisions, emotionally driven story, and engrossing atmosphere make it a truly remarkable experience. This compilation is essential for everyone, whether they are seasoned viewers reliving the series or first-time viewers taking it in.A prime example of the storytelling potential of video games is Telltale's The Walking Dead. It will pull at your emotions, test your moral compass, and stay with you long after the credits have rolled. It is, in a word, astounding.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't be telling you how amazing these games are - But yes, they are. They're wonderful, even if at times certain episodes had me scratching my head about their ideas. I'd recommend them to anyone. Rather want to look into the changes that the definitive edition brought. As a collection of 5 games, you also have music, art and such that you can look up anytime in the menu, it's really neat, also the music can be set to play while you're browsing the other menus. The original menus from the respective games are also there when you pick them from the season select which I really appreciate as that's a part of their identity.The main thing about the collection is the fact that the games are remastered with a new ''graphic black'' option.(and all 5 games are in one package) What this does is try to make the first 3 games(and Michonne's)'s graphics closer to the 4th by giving it a more comic-like artstyle. The idea is neat but execution not so much. There are graphical bugs, small ones but unfortunately I am reeeeeally good at spotting all the annoyances that will bug me forever after, there are moments where you simply can't see objects which may or may not be an issue. Mostly isn't, as the games aren't fast-paced and the issues are mostly present while exploring. To me it just feels like it was slapped over like a mod and it's not the intended art style and way to play by the devs who made the actual games long ago.My suggestion? Try and see for yourself if you like the option. The ''graphic black'' can be changed any time! It was not my thing but it was still a reason to replay these amazing games yet again. If you're new to the series this is the way to go as the 5 games are there all in one, as well as them just being discounted to like 20 euro every now and then which for all these games is neat. (Also since saves carry over between games there is less of a chance for one to actually lose them)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best gaming stories ever told.This version is a bit buggy, but it's still great.Season 1 of TWD is a masterpiece! It perfectly represents what we all love about TWD universe to begin with. Tons of walkers, hostile survivors, and lots of sad moments. This was the first game to ever make me cry. Easily a 10/10 from me.A pretty nice, albeit short, DLC for the first season. I remember playing it when it first came out and trying to figure out how to get all the characters to leave together. Lots of interesting characters and scenarios, definitely worth a play. A solid 9/10, plus it ties into season 2.Season 2 is just as good as season 1, and it happens to be my favorite of the Telltale TWD games. Season 2 deals more with the evil of men, but there are still lots of walkers constantly adding pressure to the group. It genuinely feels like every choice you make matters, and this season boasts around 7 different endings. I also give season 2 a 10/10 because I truly believe it is a masterpiece. Season 3 is where the series started to dip a little bit. The story focuses on a new set of characters and puts Clementine into the background. I do love the new characters, but this is supposed to be Clementine's story. We also never got any closure as to what happens to any of the surviving characters from this season apart from Clementine and. In addition, the choice you made at the end of Season 2 is only touched on for a few minutes at best, and that is one of the few downsides of this season. It's still a great season, but I would give it an 8/10.Season 4 really picked things back up. The setting is great, the new characters are pretty good, and it wraps Clementine's story up in a great way. The choices are tough and seem like they actually matter, plus, . I give Season 4 a 9/10.The Michonne miniseries was surprisingly really good! Michonne is one of my favorite characters from the TWD show and being able to play as her was so much fun. The story is actually unique and different from the show, because the Telltale games take place in the comics universe. Even though it is really short, the miniseries is absoultely incredible and I highly recommend you play it. I give it a 9/10.Also, A Rick Grimes or Negan TellTale game would work really well if it followed this format.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series is truly as definitive as the title says for this collection. You can experience the full journey of Clementine from humble beginnings with Lee in Season 1 to a final struggle with AJ at your side in Season 4 (The Final Season). The 400 Days DLC and The Walking Dead: Michonne are also included in this collection and are neat additions to The Telltale Walking Dead series. There are even additional goodies exclusive to this all-in-one series package, such as some behind the scenes videos, concept art, a model viewer, and music player. is an iconic masterpiece with the best cast of characters in the entire series. Every episode is a classic in this banger of a season. Just about everything in this game is sublime, really, which is why it's my favorite season in the entire series. Only thing I can think of that isn't great are the PC controls but otherwise it's practically perfect. Honestly this game could've worked as a one-off, but considering how The Final Season concludes, it's a good thing more games were made. is a great continuation of the first game with a brand new cast along with a few familiar faces that are nice to see for the time they are onscreen. The first three episodes are amazing but the season falls off in the last two episodes. The finale for this season is very good, though. Apparently Season 2 was supposed to be way darker than what we got, but I believe that the Season 2 we received in the end is better. is the weakest game in the Clementine Saga™, which appears to be a common take online. The overall story isn't bad, but the way it handled the two determinant characters from the finale of Season 2 was very poor. The biggest problem with A New Frontier is that it tries to do something new while also having to continue Clementine's arc, resulting in the weakest narrative overall for Clementine's 4-Season journey. honestly capped off the series the best way any series in a zombie apocalypse setting could've ended. AJ is by far the best character in this game and Clementine even has romance options in Violet and Louis. The Final Season is the perfect swan song for both Clementine and the series as a whole. It's nice to see a series come to an end when so many franchises with a multitude of entries refuse to die. is the weakest game in the collection, at least in my opinion. The fact that I've never read the comics (nor plan to) and the game being only 3 episodes long doesn't help much. My biggest gripe is that the "villain" doesn't really feel like an antagonist compared to other villains in the series. In fact, a certain character that you ally with feels more villainous than the actual "bad guy", which is pretty perplexing to say the least.Ultimately, The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series is the best way to experience these games. There are a few issues such as iffy character animations at times, quiet audio and a black screen of death, but these problems aren't prevalent and won't ruin the fantastic journey ahead. With 5 whole games, a DLC and bonus content exclusive to this game, there is no better way to experience the very best Telltale has to offer than with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played all the seasons one after another and I saw that in this game your choices are kind of an illusion because they don't change the main direction of the game. After a few seasons of the game, you start to understand how the game developers are playing with you, and you know when the end of the episode is coming. For example, why do you need to press a button, although the game will not allow you to press it all the way, switching to a staged action, so often pressing the button is meaningless. Why write that your choice affects the actions of the character, when the character takes and does everything that was already staged. Yes, it is possible to determine which character will leave the game, which will survive, but in the overall context it will not make any difference. I played the Definitive Edition, but I don't get the full existing content, like the comments from the video creators, which cannot be viewed due to a server problem. The developers were just lazy in this release to provide all the content in the already installed game. Looking at all 5 seasons of the game, I can give this game a maximum of 6 points out of 10. The first two seasons were interesting, and then it was just the same over the same, only with different characters, and the more you play, the more it becomes clear how the developers are playing with you . I can highlight the visual side of the game the most, it's very beautiful and I often saved the images, the soundtrack also deserves praise. The first two seasons are like a great TV series, but the more you play, the more the excitement wears off, the extra content seems to be done to fill the game time, if it wasn't there I wouldn't really miss it. Clementine is a great character, maybe the most interesting to watch in all the seasons and see how she changes, grows and becomes a woman with a lot of experience. However, everything is ruined by game clichés, with which the developers try to create drama, tragedy, inexplicable things, such as how it is possible for a character to survive who has been shot several times, bitten by zombies, etc. If you start thinking does it make sense? It means that something is wrong. It's definitely worth a try, but is it worth playing all the seasons? I dont think so.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead would probably be my favorite story in terms of zombie apocalypse. There was a time during my teenage years where I'd be obsessed with brain eaters movies, but it wouldn't be until I discovered the comic book series of Robert Kirkman that I realized what should be a great zombie narrative.I won't make a comparaison with the TV series, because I haven't seen all of it (probably stopped at season 4 or 5?), but what I can assure you is that Telltale definitly preserved the atmosphere you'd find in the comics. The Walking Dead isn't about zombies or how much walkers you can smash on the head. It's about human condition, how most of us lost the sense of community and trust, how we shattered a world and our souls, and yet people still try to build communities and make our lives better. But when survival is put first, the challenge to make the world a better place is very high, and can cost many lives.Telltale's The Walking Dead feels like watching a film, and as someone who's fond of cinema, you bet that I love that aspect. And you create your own story. Sure, the narration itself is already written down, and it'd be almost impossible to create a game with thousands of possibilities and choices, but I think that the options you're given are enough to create something that fits you. In the end, you still feel that your decisions have an impact, not only in the story, but on you too, which can influence your next outcomes.I think that The Walking Dead also brings more emotions. Movies affect me pretty easy, I'm the kind of guy who can have a tear or two if a scene gets emotional. But a video game empowers those feelings, and the only reason I can find is because you're litteraly part of it. And because The Walking Dead is done right, you'll feel a lot of emotions: you'll be angry, joyful, you'll have regrets or feel betrayed, you'll shed tears of joy or sadness. You'll feel all of that, and that's powerful.I'm not even gonna make a rank of each seasons, because all of them have their uniqueness and charm. All of those stories are about survival and hope of creating a better world, find good people and making a difference in an already shattered earth. Clementine, Lee, AJ, Javi, Michonne, all of those protagonists are amazing in their own way, and so are the people you'll encounter along the way (well maybe not all of them). You'll even find some familiar faces if you've read the comics!I loved Telltale's The Walking Dead for all the reasons I've said above, and I'd do anything if I could experience this gem again like the first time. It's the game that reminded me (with many other things) why I love stories. They bring us together, teach us to be better people. Thank you Telltale for this masterpiece.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: "Oh, Brother, Let Me Tell You About This Incredible Experience I Just Had! Initially, I Must Confess, I Had Reservations About Telltale Games. When I First Encountered Their Games And Saw Their Cartoonish Graphics, I Couldn't Help But Wonder What They Were Thinking. In An Era Dominated By Cutting-Edge Graphics, Their Choice Seemed Out Of Place To Me. I Often Overlooked Their Titles, Dismissing Them Without A Second Thought.However, Driven By The Overwhelmingly Positive Reviews, I Decided To Give Their Batman: The Telltale Series A Chance. To My Surprise, I Found Myself Enjoying It. As I Progressed To Batman: The Enemy Within, My Appreciation Only Grew. At That Point, I Believed Telltale Games Had Reached Their Peak.Then, I Stumbled Upon The Walking Dead, And Let Me Tell You, I Was Utterly Captivated By Its Story. Each Season Brought New Surprises, And I Must Say Skybound Games Truly Outdid Themselves With This Masterpiece.But Here's The Kicker: While The Walking Dead Is Exceptional In Its Own Right, I Can't Help But Imagine How It Would Be With The Gameplay And Graphics Akin To Detroit: Become Human. That, I Believe, Would Elevate It Even Further.In Conclusion, If You're A Gamer Who Values Storytelling Above All Else, The Walking Dead Is An Absolute Must-Play. Trust Me, It's A Masterpiece In Every Sense Of The Word."

_childDocuments_.review: Story - 10/10Voice acting - 9/10Atmosphere - 9.5/10Graphics - 9/10Characters - 8.5/10Clementine - 10/10An absolute masterpiece of a story. Although I'm a sensitive person, I don't tear up very often, I push through it. And it's been a long time since something squeezed a drop out of my eye. That series, from the very beginning, managed to draw emotions out of me like few games ever did. For that alone, I think it deserves high praise.Those telltale games are designed to be more of a movie than a game, but it still keeps you entertained, as it drops those often difficult choices to make. Every decision counts, to some extent. There's no telling where one may lead you.The story isn't completely rid of absurdities of illogical situations of course, but it's easy to look past those if you got a heart in the right place. From the first episode to the very end, it was an extremely entertaining journey. One, that I will surely remember forever.If you enjoy a good tearjerker, one that will detach you from everyday ugliness, I highly recommend you dip down into this one of a kind story.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic bundle for a fantastic series. You can't go wrong with this package, you get everything.Before going into each season in detail, it is note that with every first episode of each season, I ran into optimisation issues. I have heard this is the case with AMD CPUs, but it is something to be aware of as there will be constant stuttering throughout the first episode of each season, other than that, it runs perfectly.Now for the review. - Honestly, it's a masterpiece in storytelling. You begin to bond with the protagonist (Lee) easily as he approaches other survivors and groups. You bond with these people. Make friends. Trust one another. But things aren't always happy, and boy does Telltale do a fine job with this first season. 9/10 -We follow Clementine's story now after the events of Season 1. A new group of survivors, new friends to be made, new enemies as well. Not as strong as the first season in terms of the narrative, but the way that Clementine grows and matures as a character is apparent to the player. Still. Not. Bitten. 8/10. -I feel like Season 3 is underrated. Some see it as a wasted opportunity with the new protagonist, Javier. However, personally I believe he was a great addition to the TWD world and story. The new supporting characters actually surprised me, I bonded with them better than I thought, and therefore I think I enjoyed this one more than Season 2. The visuals are definitely improved, audio is great when kicking walker ass, dialogue is strong and so are the choices and partnerships along the way in this branching story. 9/10 - Wow. Where do I even begin with this season? I am still in awe with how this season was approached and how Skybound were able to bounce back from Telltale's departure. A fantastic, beautiful 'end' to our Walking Dead journey. We're back with Clementine, protecting AJ (absolute badass btw), and it is amazing to see how she has grown in not just age, but as a character with her morals. Teaching AJ throughout this season reminded me of Life Is Strange 2. It is a great way to show how choices really matter to the player as they are making an impact on AJ and his life. I loved this season. My favourite in my opinion. And for that I have to describe it as a perfect season. It brings closure, the best supporting cast, relationship decisions  . And for all of this, I give this final season a 10/10. And there you have it. A complete package for a complete, resolving and satisfying story. I hope that one day we can revisit these character, but that's wishful thinking. Thank you Telltale and Skybound.

_childDocuments_.review: is one of my favorite game so far. It's about the journey of a child name "Clementine" or known as "Clem" in the world after zombies apocalypse while trying to survive as long as she could in this tough world with various people whatever enemies or allies. This game make me realized that the true terror of this world both in game and real life is people, not such things as ghost, zombie, various animal or anything that we most scared of.   Because of it contains many products, I'm going to say only about overall.Like I said in the Introduction part. The story is set in the world after zombies apocalypse from unknown reason  and the only thing you know is there're zombies every where. So, you're going to see Clem growing up in this terrible environment that can be shifting based on the choices you made through each episodes. Each episode is represent each age and development of Clem in both physical and mental, since 8 years old in season 1 to about 17-18 years old in final season. The writing is . It contains all things that make some story is actually good and interesting at the same time. Characters have their own thought, perspective, habits. It makes you feel you want to know more things about them such as their back stories, secrets or the reason why they did something. Because it mostly have the answer for your question revealed more and more you play through. It also has some plot-twisted and plot itself makes you always thinking about what is just happening and what consequence is it going to be after this.This is the best way to describe game play of The Walking Dead Series. From small action like making someone angry or just taking something may even grounds to determine somebody to be dead or alive, it's all by your choices you made.Because of it's a Story rich - Choices matter genre, you will never be worry about difficulty. Most of gameplay is just examine items, interacting with peoples, and encounter quick time events. This make it can be enjoy with all skill level players by felling like watching series that depend on your own decision. But during this type of gameplay itcan be get bored in some sections.Graphics and UI are developing by time through all seasons by Season One and Two are basically the same but then in A New Frontier all things jump to be more modern, ambient, models, cut scenes, UI, etc. But you have a fundamental options in every seasons, that is Graphic Black. You can switch it on or off in every seasons setting. When it's on, it looks like Borderlands and I really loved that style. If it's off, it makes graphic looks more realistic.Audio is acceptable and voices over is the significant positive in The Walking Dead Series. You can truly feel the emotions of most characters by just listened to their voices because they really put it in to it. Completionist- 42 hours

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a review of all seasons, Since i have already played 1 and 2 before i bought this bundle I will mainly be focusing on the 3rd Season, 4th Season, and Michonne series. Spoilers will follow with this review, so if you have never played this and are wondering if this is worth it or not here is your short answer "YES BUY IT"1st Season: Probably one of the greatest interactive story games of all time, Getting emotionally attached to most of these characters is pretty easy, you feel something when your favorites have to bite the dust and actually get scared of certain choices while you play, will this person survive if i make this choice? Or will I risk their life doing something else. It's an excellent thrill ride from start to finish while simultaneously being an emotional Roller Coaster, something that Naughty Dog couldn't even compete with, even with TLOU Part 1. If you have NEVER played this before, it is worth a purchase for this season alone. 400 Days: Meh... that's pretty much all i gotta say about it, it does something Semi Important in Season 2 if you complete it and it really only takes an hour and a half ish to beat, so no reason not to play it before Season 2.2nd.  Things go from bad to worse for your main protagonist, finding a new group and some new faces to either hate or love. Building more relationships both within the game and personally as once again, you start to feel for these people you are with. It is absolutely an Incredible sequel to the 1st Season, which is a shocker because most developers will ruin their story adding new characters, and changing old characters to try manipulating the player into hating the old ones and trying to manipulate you into loving the newest character. *COUGH* TLOU PART II *COUGH* But Walking Dead Season 2 is an another ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slammer from beginning to end, you will feel emotions both happy and sad... more sad than anything. How they manage to smack us with two absolute bangers in a row is amazing and is not seen nowadays in gaming making Walking Dead Season 2 another amazing title and honestly, worth the asking price for the first two seasons alone. Michonne: I was honestly surprised by this one, it isn't special by any means or the very best experience ever especially comparing it too the first two seasons this is absolutely a C Tier game. But it was still interesting playing a mini story for Michonne which (without doing any research) I am going to guess the story is from the comics (which i have never read) But honestly a pretty solid game from the short three episodes available. I honestly made her a bit of a psychopath and it was real fun doing that.3rd: Ok, this is where i could see the cracks forming, I believe this was made around that time they were starting to lose a lot of their staff and i believe even went bankrupt for a while (could be wrong about that last part) But playing as your new protagonist 4th: A complete 180 from how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3 was. Adding some new mechanics overall with how you fight zombies, But i quickly realized how much colder I became trusting others since I played all of the other Walking Dead games before hand. The only ones I tried benefiting were  Now if The Wolf Among Us can somehow top every single season of The Walking Dead, I will be extremely impressed. Overall, hell yes, this is worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: The first season was enjoyable, although clunky. Good characters, good interactions, good writing. I played for 6hrs solid. I ploughed on though and stuck with the old crew. Until the game took away my choices. And then I considered not playing anymore. BS was clearly in play and I wasn't happy.Season 3, well hello wacky world. Plastic characters, I didn't care who died, the writing was dreadful, dialogue dreadful, and they turned the main character into Rambo. A kid, female, version. Ouch. This is where I stopped playing. The game had become a cheap copy of itself and all I was doing was pressing the odd button like a trained pigeon. Season 4 is utter tripe. The Sims V Zombies. I don't know who was the most frightening. The developers who produced series 1 left afterwards, and it is very obvious, never more so than in series 4.I don't recommend the definitive series. If you can get hold of season 1 at a very low price then do so.

_childDocuments_.review: Season 1: 9/10Overall: 8/10.Major spoiler warning.It was a little repetitive and cringe-worthy sometimes, but it's nothing fans of the TV series aren't accustomed to. Nevertheless, I adored the story and really cared for some of the characters. Every game has its cons, though.The Expendables (I just have to get this out) This game has some really cool choices and plot twists I didn't see coming, but the good story beats are treated as rewards for enduring through less engaging segments of the game, which may not be for everyone. The unengaging parts of the game are usually long, boring periods of time or flashbacks in which nothing of importance happens; it's more stagnant action than rising action. Which, again, TWD fans are no stranger to. These parts often involved walking back and forth between side characters and engaging in irrelevant little blurbs of stale dialogue like a checklist in order to trigger an event that I wasn't very interested in because it didn't progress the plot. For example, supper with the side characters, which was more often than not awkward, long, and boring. I understand it was Telltale's attempt to develop their many expendable side characters, but you can develop them in Rising Action. While I ate dinner or walked and talked nonsense with these meaningless side characters, I couldn't bring myself to care enough about characters who I knew were just going to get their heads blown off in the next episode. I was more concerned with how their deaths were going to affect the group's attitude towards me than the deaths of the characters themselves. I think it would have been more effective if there were fewer side characters so I could grow a personal relationship with them, like Louis and, notably, Kenny, whose death would not only affect the group's psyche but also my own, rather than nine shallow side characters who wouldn't make it long or characters whose sole purpose was to be used in "choose to save one of these two shallow characters, someone will get mad regardless" moments. Kenny was a great side character because I was able to watch him go through the motions of the story alongside me. I saw him experience grief, happiness, and grief again. I felt horrible watching him fall further and further, knowing the inevitable in my gut, that I'd have to make a choice and that there was nothing I could do anymore for him. The conversations I had with him were cherished as well because, unlike with every other side character, they moved past the trope of reminiscing about "the good ol' times" or indulging in futile chit-chats about what we were going to do "when the world goes back to normal."The Story - Despite what I mentioned above, this story is actually very good. I binged the hell out of it. Towards the end of it, I felt like I had actually spent 8 years as the character(s) in The Walking Dead's universe. After finishing the finale, exiting to the main menu, and seeing the house where it all started, I felt tired, nostalgic, and old, even though I had just started the game not too long ago. There were some surprising and very effective emotional moments, all the way from tear-jerker moments to rage-inducing ones. The story does a good job of making you feel like you can't catch a break, lol, to say the least. I also appreciate how the game goes into way more detail about different personalities in the apocalypse than the TV show, which I love. And the choose "your own adventure/your choices affect people" aspect of it just makes it that much more interesting.Conclusion - Despite a few flaws, this game is completely worth finishing all the way to the end. I find season 1 to the best, but that's just my opinion. This game is an 8/10, fairly priced, and unquestionably worth investing time in.

_childDocuments_.review: The year was 2016, it was a sunny day with just the right temperature outside. 16 year old me was sitting in my room playing the first free episode of the first season on the 4 inch screen of my smartphone thinking it was the best thing ever. It was just my type of game, . Everything was perfect, but unfortunately 16 year of me didn't have money to buy the rest of the episodes, so my wish of seeing the story to completion was something I held on to for many years, 6 to be exact. And it was only now, after my good friend  gifted me the Definitive Edition that I got to continue my journey.The first game got over 100+ game of the year awards and that says something. Right of the bat you are put into the shoes of Lee Everett, a convicted criminal on his way to jail. and you are left with the young Clementine, who is so innocent that you want to protect her at all cost. I don't think there is a single person who wouldn't give their life to protect her. Along the way you meet new survivors while you try to make sense of what is happening all around you. The game's dialogue system was revolutionary at the time and still holds amazingly well to this day. Not to mention  The game is amazing, and probably my favourite one among all the others. It touches on a lot of dark themes but still provides you with a little hope to hold on to. The crazy thing in my opinion is even if this game came out this year, it'll still be the game of the year because the game doesn't depend on any fancy gameplay gimmick, the whole game and every Telltale game for that matter is about the characters and story, which only deepens as the lore continues.The second one was heartbreaking to say the least. After the tear jerking ending of the first one, you're thrown into Clementines shoe who is desperately trying to survive not knowing who to trust. Weirdly enough, . As she tries to get by, she makes new friends and meet some old ones. Interestingly the whole game revolves around the dilemma of who you choose to trust, your old friends or new ones. I definitely had to pause the game several times and ponder on my next decision as the game gets really tense at times and most of the things always seems to be out of your control. Unlike the first one, this has a whooping 7 different endings and its amazing how they even pulled it off. The third one was weird. The first striking aspect is that you don't play as Clementine, but instead Javier, a washed off baseball player who is a disappointment in his brothers eyes. The game isn't flat out bad, it might be even good if it wasn't one of the main line entries and a separate one-shot like TWD Michonne. For what its worth, the visuals are definitely better, certain sections of shooting feels great and voice acting as always is amazing. Unfortunately coming to this after the second entry you have a hard time caring for the new characters as you barely know them. One of my biggest gripe I have, which I don't see mentioned often is the camera work. This whole game is shot like a freaking Michael bay movie and I don't know why. They tried making everything cinematic, by using different aspect ratios for cut scenes, depth of field and camera shake, all of which I despise. Clementine is still in this but for not long enough and from the last time you played as Clem in the previous game, she has drastically changed. She is bolder, stronger and more sure of herself.  In a way, I like to believe  and this third game was the necessary evil to facilitate that.The fourth and final one in the series is definitely the most innovative in terms of gameplay and visuals among all the others. You might have noticed, I've said little about the gameplay in these games, its because there's only a little of it. . The two biggest improvement is, you can move the camera to look around, and secondly the combat is in real time which I really, really love. Throughout this game, I felt a sense of pride and déjà vu as we become a guardian of sort, first with Clementine and now Clementine with AJ. With such a huge series, you can never make everyone happy, but it is what Telltale has successfully done. It is the best conclusion that I or anyone could have asked for. Not to mention the internal situation at telltale at the time. For those unaware, Telltale was shut down mid way through the final season and it was set to be cancelled. Hundreds of employees laid off overnight with no where else to go, it was a nightmare and I sincerely hope all those people got back on their feet and are making great games. Fortunately for us gamer, Skybound the company owned by the original creator of The Walking Dead came to the rescue and stoke a deal with Telltale to finish the final season. For that thank you Skybound, thank you for allowing all us to see Clementines journey to the end. TWD Michonne is probable the best game in the series in terms of gameplay and story telling. The first game is my favourite but objectively I think Michonne takes the cake. The combat is still the best in the series, the story telling keeps you on your toes and it has some great cinematic shots. Not to mention, . Like really, everything about this is amazing and I really think it deserves more praise.Final note: I highly recommend watching the Dev playthroughs of all the games with the voice actors, which was supposed to be viewable in-game but isn't available now as they took it down from their server. Fortunately there are a few heroes on YouTube who have recorded the entire thing, so check it out there. Finally, finishing this game series has reignited my love the zombie genre and I can't wait to go back into this world by reading the original comic.

_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: The game is pretty old by this point, so not much to be said be about the quality of the overall game that hasn't been said already. It's still a wonderful narrative. There's really only a few gripes with the game, and they're mainly technical. The animations obviously weren't intended for higher frame rates, so every now and then, they tend to get a bit jumpy, which is really not a big deal in the grand scheme of thing. It's not an FPS, some jumpy animations won't kill you. If you're like me and you chose to play this game on controller, be wary that every now and then the game freaks out a bit and likes to go back to the m+kb selector instead of the controller layout for options during dialogue. Just tap the left stick down and the game will flip back to the controller layout. As long as you're not super slow at reading, you'll be perfectly fine.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- The same amazing story from start to finish (with the exception of Michonne)- Graphics have been given a significant improvement especially with the addition of the graphic black setting, gives the older games a much better atmosphere- Much much less buggy than the original versions, frame rate dips are very rare and the scenes transition much more smoothlyCons:- The Michonne mini series, really not a fan- The price is a bit too high, better off buying it on sale
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: this is the first game to actually impact on me and hurt me mentally to the point that i cant stop thinking about it and i just feel sad and empty after i completed it. i love the characters so much and i want to be able to relive this game like i had never played it before. i will not recover from this one for a while but at least I know not alone on that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved TellTale's The Walking Dead. It gave me highs and lows and the compassionate story telling and humanity made me feel a wide variety of emotions. My only gripe is that it's all over now and that I don't get to play as Clementine anymore. She is by a wide margin my favorite video game character of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: This defines what Telltale games are all about, its such a shame there will be no more games by them.The story really draws you in, you feel a connection to the characters. _childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the game, I assumed that the game could have from itself. Especially when I then looked through the reviews, some of which were negative. But after I bought the game, I realized that I was not mistaken in my preferences about the game. But still the question remains: is the game created to specifically waste time in vain for the sake of passing all parts of the game, or to be nostalgic remembering what we played before?
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, combining all seasons in 1. But... there are some stuff that i don't like. First, You cannot "pick" chapter from the episodes. SO, in the previous installments, each episode has chapters (It's 4 or 6 chapters if i recall). Which means if you screw up your choice, you have to redo the whole episode. The second one is more of a bug/glitch. If you already played the episode in 1 of the save files, when you tried to replay it, the choices will remain the same. The game didn't rewrite your choices so that you have to play on a new save files. The third one is you can't copy your save files to another one past season 1. So if you screw up on episode 4 season 2, you have to replay the whole season on another save file FFS!!!! Just buy the game separately... Buy each season separately. It'll benefit you a lot. Even though it's more expensive, believe me...
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. Clementine felt like a daughter to me... I never thought I'd become so attached to characters that you really only spend 40 hours or so with but yeah, I did. What a game... don't think I'll ever get over not being able to play this for the first time again. And wow what a soundtrack... Take Us Back.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: This game collection is one of the best of all time. The story is gripping and heartbreaking, leaving you wanting for more. This game offers an infinite amount of replayability, each decision branching a new relationship or a new loss, every choice being left to the player to decide the fate of the characters and the outcome of your journey. The growth between characters is truly warming, and the goodbyes between them, in death or in separation, is a true pain. But most of all, The ending. Finding out what you have done, created, and lost in the end is what really separates this game from any other. Seeing your actions played out, seeing all that they come to be, It is what makes this game one of the best games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: Want to know the real reason all of these people survived the zombie apocalypse for so long? None of them have any brains to go after. The writing is so cringe it's unbelievable. Every single thing that happens in this game has already happened in other iterations of the Walking Dead. The only differences are small details and the characters. Not like the characters make much difference, though, because they are all stereotypes or one-dimensional.Then you get into the whole "the story adapts to your decisions" crap. It does, but in mostly meaningless ways. I have replayed multiple important scenes, choosing every option available, and nothing changes. Most of the time it just loops back into a singular path, and sometimes the difference shows up in a later episode, but every single time the decisions are between a dumb choice, a stupid choice, and a foolish choice.This game is the illusion of choice while getting railroaded through a bland story with attempted moments of shock and awe. It is boring.If you must see for yourself, at least get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The four games that make up the combined main series for Telltales The Walking Dead is nothing short of an artistic masterpiece. Few games come this close to wholly enveloping a player into it's world and cast of characters. Whilst the series is not without it's faults, and season three A New Frontier is certainly the odd one out. At no point did I want to stop playing. Only ever to pause and reflect on my journey so far and the let the consequences of my actions sink in.Having first played season one back in 2012, and only now coming around to find out how it all ends. Season four, the final season, left my heart broken. Not because of what had happened on screen, but because now I can only daydream whats happening off screen. And the harsh reality that I'm not going to get to see these much loved characters again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to play the whole Clementine story when this came up. A lot happened until I finally could purchased the game, I am still want to have a little girl, maybe sometime near future. IDK, Clementine, her journey, her transformation, this telltale make you feel how your guidance could transform someone into something else if we made wrong decissions, as any father IRL. I recommend everyone give a try. This kind of games are nice for people who want to listen/see a story but with a little of visual novel, not much effort to play it.However, probably nobody is gonna like what I am gonna say... but the worst decission of devs were use Michonne in the game as a conclusion of the telltale, that not even felt as TWD, was like an action game point & click. _childDocuments_.review: This game series is going to leave a memory on ANY player that will get their hands on it. It could be the boredom for the lack of real gameplay mechanics, disappointment for how many of your choices end up not mattering, bleakness for how many characters die (sometimes in the most stupid ways possible) just when you were starting to get attached to them, but for a subset of players, all those problems that are objectively true don't matter at all. I am one of them. Clementine's journey could easily be your little sister's or your daughter's depending on your age. You see her grow up, making decisions that would be difficoult for an adult, let alone a child, help and be helped, finding what little humanity is left of the people she finds. Is it all worth it in the end? Play this game and find out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: This may just be the best ever story game i have ever played. Your choices have REAL consequences and can get characters killed or saved. The way you follow a little girl named Clementine growing up in a apocalypse is just crazy with how much she has changed. She's become a fearless killer with morals to other humans. The game tries to make you connect to characters and then to eventually kill them off which makes this emotional bond even harder.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: It's crazy to think that some of these games are now considered classics. I remember playing the first episode in 2012, 8 years ago! Playing these classics with updated graphics (which look great by the way) is totally worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: Where do you even start? I got the game because I had heard so much about it. Being a fan of TWD, I thought maybe the majority of the reviews were just fans like me saying "it's good" because we just love post-apocalyptic horrors, but I would have never thought there would be so much more to these reviews. The game delivers a gut-wrenching emotions and difficult choices, and if you are not prepared to feel absolutely rotten for some of those choices, you better be prepared. Clementine is no longer just a character, she feels like a real human being and you want to protect her at all costs, but you WILL make mistakes. This is probably just ONE of the lingering emotions you will have to bear. Overall, if you are hesitating to get this game, what are you even waiting for? Begin this harrowing tale today... and good luck out there.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, because this is 5 games instead of one, it's kinda hard doin' a short review.My fav voicelines:"Hey, sweet pea.","Keep that hair short", "My little goofball".In my opinion, because i played Season1/2 in another platform, i didnt had a single one in steam. So getting the definitive was cheaper for me then getting each one as standalone+you have the enhanced graphics which it's worth? Guess so.You have a lot of cosmetic stuff like the osts/art gallery/ some animations, try Lee and rosie animations of final season, AJ riding them with guns it's hilarious. In another hand, standalone version you can choose the chapters in the season to change your choice.In player choices i would rate: TW4>TW1>New Frontier>TW2>MichonneOverall quality of story: TW1>TW4>TW2>New Frontier> MichonneAs a whole it's pretty solid storyline, Lee teachings and  even Kenny teachings, everything as a sacrifice to AJ and Clem to live in a dying world. There're a lot of moral decisions with consequences, i wish i could've saved some chars more then others, but in the end, i think that was the point, the world is dying and we need to enjoy the brief company we have with each other and sometimes no matter how much you dont want to sacrifice someone, you need to made the hard calls, and like AJ says the hard calls are unfair.The three bad things i have to complain is:1° There were choices not matter what you choose just change dialogues, you dont have the freedom of choice, but freedom of dialogues, that's why 4 and 1 are better then the others, New frontier even has this, but most of chars aren't remarkable and Tripp my fav... you cant change his fate. 2°The other thing, Minerva didnt make any sense, at the end of Season 4, she got a plot armor from the devs to fight Clem, and that was it, because was full of loopholes the fight at the bridge.3°Michonne it's bad overall, i guess it's worth play one time, but was a whole i didnt learn anything meaningful(every other season made me do an inner reflection on life)P.S: as i had my hand screwed by a nurse, i could only use one hand, and  while isnt a point and click game, it's pretty easy to do the QTE actions with only one hand.

_childDocuments_.review: Take this review with a grain of salt as of right now I only have 10 hours:This game is very good but that could be bias as I am a huge fan of The Walking Dead television show.This game will leave you feeling for other characters and immersed in the story telling.The options/choices the game gives you all feel like viable options depending on the person you are and the story/ outcome you wish to see.The parts of the game play where its not just cut scenes and storytelling are also very good.Like having to find objects and solutions to problems in locations I'd never think of without searching thoroughly.Overall I highly recommend this game to fans of TWD but also people who have never touched anything to do with the series.Alright Pt 2 of this review. I will edit this review after every season/chapter, as I feel it gives an accurate review on this great game:Season 2 expands on what season 1 had to offer and enhances it.The game play loop feels smooth as there is a lot less annoyances like having to always talk to characters and check in on them. The immersion is still present, you watch your favourites go through their character arcs and really feel for them and the story that's present. I felt sad watching my favourites die but they only died because of me and my choices. So there is a lot of immersion into the story. The options and choices are just as good as the first season as all choices feel like valid and reasonable options to choose. A great part of the dialogue choices is that you can try to please certain characters by taking to their side. Overall season 2 is a great expansion to the first season. Watching the previous events extend into season 2 feels really nice to see and refreshing in a way, leaving and starting right where you left off. Overall 9/10 Part 3:Season 3 is a very weird season in my opinion. It starts you of with an amazing cut scene introducing our setting and characters. For me personally, I didn't like the start of this season the characters seemed weird and unlikable at the start. I turned off the game before I was even 30 minutes in. However, when I picked up the game again I enjoyed it this time as events unfold very quickly and you are right back into the swing that the first two seasons had. One of the earliest choices that changes your story seems very minor when you first see it. Then later I noticed that with one action I had created a domino effect. I was amazed when I realised what I did and the consequences of that choice. Once again immersion is still present and you really feel a sense of attachment to the characters. The characters at the start seemed random as it didn't connect to previous events (spoilers, Clementines Story). But after just an hour or two, you see the events from season one and two connect into our new cast of characters lives. Dialogue is good as normal nothing seems bad at all about it. Watching characters develop and change through their arcs is so majestic to see, it just feels nice knowing that the characters have changed after your journey with them. Watching the characters you watched grow and develop die (some of them) really makes you feel like it isn't just watching/playing a story, you feel emotional at points. This game is truly great and the fact you can get this instead of getting all the games separately really enhances the connection between the stories, like the games were meant to be all together in the first place. You can continue your story from previous seasons or make a new backstory. Overall I really enjoyed this season, the characters designs and the game looked phenomenal, game play feels fun and really immersive.  I know people will think this isn't fair but I enjoyed it that much I have to give this season a... 10/10 or 9.9/10 as their can always be improvements to everything.

_childDocuments_.review: Telltale never fails to surprise me. I'm not that far into the game yet but I love it so far.Edit: Reliving the story of season 1 had me in my feels all over again, season two was great, deciding who clementine is, what people think of her, was great. _childDocuments_.review: While the game does have it's flaws and frustrating moments it's an experience and narrative driven adventure I think everyone should embark on. The story is one you can have fun with and be goofy with yet each game had their moments where you just cry. You truly connect with the main characters and side characters alike, having beaten the entire series twice now and choosing drastically different options each time, there were charters I loved in the first game that I quite simply didn't care for in the second. You truly feel your choices matter and your work is molded around what you do. I would say anyone who has time should try this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead series by Telltale Games is a poignant exploration of trauma and the bonds of chosen family in a post-apocalyptic world. Lee Everett's enduring presence and Kenny's complex relationships throughout the series underscore the profound impact of familial ties amidst chaos and hardships. It teaches many important life lessons while highlighting the glimpses of kindness throughout the Apocalypse.  Overall, "The Walking Dead" series transcends its genre, offering a profound look into humanity's resilience, and the enduring power of hope. I love this game so much, and it was honestly so sad leaving its world behind knowing I've finished. Thank you so much to Skybound Games for saving the series and remastering it for everyone to experience. If you could buy this game at a discount, this is definitely the best way to enjoy the series.and remember to keep that hair short.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead game series by Telltale offers a gripping narrative experience that blends intense decision-making with a post-apocalyptic world filled with zombies. Spread across multiple seasons, the game's emotional and character development make it a standout in the gaming industry and interactive storytelling.Season One introduces players to Lee Everett, a former university professor convicted of murder, as he navigates a world overrun by walkers. The player's choices shape Lee's relationships with a diverse group of survivors, most notably the young Clementine. The bond between Lee and Clementine forms the emotional core of the series, and the choices players make weigh heavily on the narrative.Season Two shifts the focus to Clementine, now a hardened survivor on her own. The game explores themes of trust, loyalty, and the consequences of one's actions. New characters add layers to the narrative, and the player's decisions continue to have far-reaching effects on the story.Season Three, subtitled "A New Frontier," introduces a new protagonist, Javier Garcia, while still weaving Clementine's story into the mix. This season delves into the complexities of family, duty, and morality, offering players a fresh perspective on the harsh realities of the apocalyptic world.The fourth and final season, titled "The Final Season," brings Clementine's journey full circle. The game introduces a new cast of characters and forces players to make difficult decisions that will ultimately shape the fate of Clementine and those around her. The emotional impact of this season is heightened by the sense of closure it provides for long-time fans of the series.Telltale's unique storytelling approach, which emphasizes player choice and consequence, sets The Walking Dead games apart. The episodic format allows for a more intimate connection with the characters, making every decision feel weighty and impactful. The use of a graphic novel art style complements the series' tone and helps create a visually engaging experience.However, the series is not without its criticisms. Some players may find the gameplay mechanics repetitive, and there have been occasional technical issues. Despite these minor drawbacks, the strength of the narrative and character development overshadows any shortcomings.The Walking Dead games by Telltale offer a masterclass in interactive storytelling. The series balances the tension of survival in a zombie apocalypse with emotionally resonant character arcs. Fans of the television show, as well as newcomers to the franchise, will find a memorable experience that challenges their morals and leaves a lasting impact.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth every penny for the combined hours of entertainment (and existential crisis) I've gotten from this game. This is a game that capitalizes on cell-shading techniques to give a comicbook-like touch to the visuals and QTEs as well as choices-mattering dialogue options to tell stories about a post-apocalyptic world infested by zombies, but more than that, individual human politics and reactions to said apocalypse that shapes surviving groups and communities, ultimately exposing the most primal of instincts and people's inclination to act on those at the cost of morals or survival. Over the years, I've played these games over and over again and cried my eyes out and felt a hole in my life everytime after finishing my playthroughs because while there are plenty of similar games to be played, there's nothing quite like this story out there. Where it all started. Lee, a convicted felon on his way to prison, stumbles onto a little girl called Clementine when the dead first start walking. Over the season, we see people hoping for everything to go back to normal soon while also trying to survive and adjust to a whole new way of living because the world has been plunged into chaos. Morals that once applied in the civilized world are tested, questioned and sometimes sacrificed for the sake of survival.   A grown up Clementine jumps from one sinking community to another, trying to stay alive, while witnessing said communities being pulled apart; sometimes by the dead, sometimes by hostile communities and other times from within. She rescues a new-born baby, AJ, from one such sinking community and forms a bond with him, trying to protect him and raise him right.Unlike most fans, I didn't have a problem with the game taking a break from Clementine's story and focusing on a completely different protagonist- Javier Garcias and his family. I feel like two seasons of Clementine on the move just trying to survive the world was getting really intense. And it's not like we completely abandon that arc because while playing as Javier, you ultimately do cross paths with Clem again and she plays a significant role in the season then onwards. I would have liked to discover what happens to Javier's community in Season 4  Brilliance. Almost. I loved this season and the fresh breath of air it brings about. By now, you can clearly see how much the graphics have improved, as well as the gameplay, although I had a few frustrating moments where the timer to choose the dialogues would run out extraordinarily quickly, forcing me to quit to main menu and hoping the game didn't save the choices. During one of the most important choices (of choosing your preferred romance), the game doesn't even give you a heads up and I had to restart the whole episode just because the last save was overwritten. And now, we come to the worst part of the whole season- the main antagonist. Holy crap that felt forced and really bad. As well as the ending. I couldn't believe that after having been part of Clementine's journey from the beginning, I'd have to go through this poorly executed and shoehorned "conflict". It didn't make any sense whatsoever because the game broke it's own rules just for the sake of being dramatic. I mean, seriously?  But all in all, the ending was very reminiscent of the circle of life and the end of Episode 1, in general, with Clem now standing in Lee's shoes.Eh, it was decent. I don't know why people hated this one. I found it was a nice break from the main story. Michonne is the protagonist for this season and she's this strong, silent type, unlike the other protagonists in the series. TWD Michonne has 3 episodes altogether apart from an interesting narrative arc, it has quite a satisfactory ending. It's a short standalone adventure.This one was actually worse than Michonne and should be played after you've played everything else because it's so insiginficant and short and fragmented with very little in the way of choices. In fact, I don't believe there are any impactful choices in this "season" whatsoever really. Both this and Michonne are standalone stories, only "400 days" is a collection of short stories of 5 different people who end up in a group together later on. And... that's it. One remarkable thing about "400 days" is that there are rather explicit easter eggs or throwbacks, if you will, to Season 1 and Season 2 and that since you're not given much time to acquaint yourself to the protagonists, you're put in black-and-white situations where you can make immoral choices on their behalf, which is far easier to do than in any of the main stories, if you have a conscience.

_childDocuments_.review: While I really, really, really wanted to like this whole game, and leave it a great review, I must leave it a negative one due to my frustration outweighing my enjoyment. In short, the first season was amazing, the second season made me wish it was the first again. The third season made me realize it was to late to get a refund from Steam. The forth season just made me puke in my mouth. If you want better detail read on...While the first season was the very foundation of enjoyment in this series, everything after just ruins it. The second season just ruins some great characters, does a complete 180 with them and tries to make you hate them, why? Because the writer says its time to, and if you still stick by those characters, you're considered the "bad guy". It was after the second season I started to feel things were going downhill, and I was very right...The third season is just filler, like someone stuck fan-fiction into my game then kept slapping me in the face with it, no choice shaped the story, it all would lead down one road that you couldn't change. No enjoyable characters, just annoying cringe characters. On top of all that I get some stupid romance that I cannot avoid, and gets forced on me, with the worst, most cringe-worthy character. I swear it was fan-fiction turned into a season.Finally, season 4. It was literally a repeat of season 1, just poorly done and with a lot of extra cringe, I literally missed quick-time events in cut-scenes in this chapter because my eyes were rolling back into my skull so hard they didn't want to see it anymore. Awful characters and it just felt like the writers had their own point of view they wanted to shove down your throat, instead of just creating interesting people in the game and letting you make your decisions. A lot of cut and paste in this season!To sum it all up, First season was the only good thing about this, it doesn't get better, only worse. They step on what was made in season one, then give you the most self-righteous, idiotic and cringe-worthy characters with choices that lead you nowhere except where they want you to be. If you do buy this, stick with the first season, unless you want to know what it feels like to be a walker.

(even if you dont trust AJ he wouldve cut off your leg) Also the same ending happening everytime and it being a good ending kills the whole vibe. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. _childDocuments_.review: I first started playing this game back when I was 7 or something, at first I hated the game, not much action, the art is weird, the controls are a bit janky. But after years passed, I slowly understand it, I figured out everything, and when I did, I fell in love with it. I don't intend to write anything long (this is already long) but I love this game. It made my childhood less harder. It was a welcoming sight. Seeing how Clementine changes from an innocent girl to a jaded thief and to a loving mum, I feel warm. The feeling that the character itself growing up alongside you made me feel as if I'm not alone. The game taught me a lot of things, things that I otherwise won't really care about, family. Family isn't someone that shares the same blood as you, it is someone that will make you tear through post-apocalyptic Georgia to find, someone that no matter what happens, you'll find a way to be there for them, someone you watched and supported grow. I thank you, thank you for being there for me. Clementine, Lee, Kenny, Javi, all of the characters, from the dead to the living, all of them. Thank you for making my childhood back then nice. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I once played almost all the walking dead games, except for the final one. So since I got a pc a couple of years later, I decided to snag this game and replay and finally complete the games.For starters, the story is probably the best part. Some don't reach the quality of the first and last season, but they do great with what they deliver, even the during rough parts. Clementine and Lee are a great parental/child figure for each other and they learn from mistakes and gain more knowledge in this world. The other characters also do fantastic in their roles, as I constantly remember them vividly after playing the games.The atmosphere is another great feature for this series. There was never one scene where I wasn't absorbed in the world, especially the final season with some great scenery. Not one game felt out of place in the world of decay and walking dead.The visuals are fantastic for the game's style, especially last season. It felt like flipping through a comic for the next scene almost. The older seasons did get a option to change the style similar to a comic feel. I wasn't the type to enjoy that style for the older seasons, so I kept it the same.The last note I should mention is the gameplay. If you are not a story type person, this game is hard to get used to. Up until the last season, the game have on-rail camera angles where you can't decide where the camera goes often. Getting used to this was difficult at first, but it grew on me. The final season is more so free camera perspective, with a few scenes being a forced camera angle, though it did good for those.Overall, this is a high recommend for story based games. _childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series contains all four main games, the 400 days dlc, and the Michonne spin-off. In the first game you play as Lee Everett, a man with a troubled past that finds himself having to protect and raise a little girl called Clementine, shortly after the onset of a zombie apocalypse. The sequel takes place roughly a year after the conclusion of the previous game. You now play as Clementine, as she tries to adapt and survive in the brutal world that has emerged. The remaining two games continue and conclude her story.The story told here is nothing short of phenomenal and gut-wrenching. The connection between Clementine and Lee, the struggles she faces, and the people she comes across in her journey, will not leave you indifferent by the end. Even though there is a decline in the quality of the story by the third game, the whole experience is still very much worth it. The story will change slightly depending on your choices.Despite being a point and click at its core, the characteristics you normally associate with the genre are less prevalent, having instead a more streamlined approach. The game also features many action scenes that involve quick time events.The graphics emulate a comic book style, which is fitting, as the games are based on The Walking Dead comic book series. The Definitive Series features various graphical enhancements in comparison with the original games.The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series is a classic and an achievement in storytelling. If you enjoy a good story, you must experience it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely nostalgic for me, one of the first games I ever wanted to complete back in 2012 when the first game came out, I was 12 years old, played every single one as it was being released, and having the chance to come back and play them remastered with the Graphic Black mode, is just pure nostalgia, I was ecstatic to play this game through again. And I'm only half way there. The idea to keep playing and get a complete a different story by just changing a few key decisions is why these types of games deserve so much credit. When telltale was going under I was so worried that the they'd never finish the series, and then why Skybound came in to finish the series I was so relieved. The developers have made games to stand out for over a decade, and I believe I'll be playing this game for years to come.
