_childDocuments_.review: The Story:Such a beautiful story. The last time I cried that hard in a video game was when I played "The Last of Us", which was ironically also about a man and his sergeant daughter in a zombie apocalypse setting. The characters are what really brought this game together, especially Clementine and Lee. Whenever I was in a room I made sure to check in with Clementine to make sure she was okay. When this game came out, you would have to wait for an episode every week like it was a TV show. The story may have been structured in a way to benefit of this, but as someone who just finished all of it in 2 days, I thought it was still one of the best.Choose your own adventure:In terms of diverse endings, there really is only one. But I think that was necessary if they were planning on multiple seasons (I only played season 1). I do think it was one of the best endings to a story like this. Then again, the "Choices are tailored to how you play" doesn't mean much. I still can't seem to find a game as diverse in its branching story line as "Detroit: Become Human". That's not to say nothing will change, we all know the dreaded "Character will remember that" notification on the side of the screen. Gameplay:As most telltale games, it's just a bunch of dialogue options with quick time events. It's not really fair to criticize it though since it's supposed to be dialogue driven, building relationships and deciding who lives and who dies is the main idea of this kind of gameplay. I usually find QTE's to be out of place in most games but I also think there's an exception for linear style games like this.Would I Recommend:Yes, you do not need to be good at any shooter game to appreciate this game for it's story and gameplay. You could watch this game on youtube and still get emotionally invested in the characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m at a loss for words when it comes to this game. This game touched me deeply and had me on the verge of tears. I love the story and side characters main characters, especially Clementine and Lee Everett. Their journeys are not just compelling; they are profoundly moving. The challenging part of this game but yet rewarding is the difficulty of making choices. Each decision carries weight, often leaving me second-guessing my responses and actions. This pressure to choose the right words or actions creates an intense and immersive experience, highlighting the moral dilemmas that arise in desperate situations.The Walking Dead offers a powerful narrative experience that highlights the significance of choice and the strength of community, all while exploring the complexities of human relationships. Each decision you make feels impactful, shaping not only the outcome of the story but also the characters’ development and their relationships with one another.The emotional storytelling and thought-provoking themes leave a lasting impression, transforming the experience into something more than just a game. It’s a reflective journey that stays with you long after the credits roll, making you ponder the choices you made and the lives you touched along the way. This is a game that resonates on a deeper level, and I can’t recommend it enough to anyone who appreciates a story that genuinely engages the heart and mind. ❤︎

Example: You can choose to save a certain character from dying or cut them loose. No matter which you choose, the character ends up dying anyway. There are many scenarios like this.- Action sequences are clunky and sometimes hard to understand. Many times I had to retry a sequence because it wasn't clear exactly what I was supposed to do, or the controls were janky. A little annoying, but not a dealbreaker.- Story is a bummer. No spoilers here, but there are exactly zero triumphant moments in Season 1. Just a slow march to doom with a dark, unsatisfying ending. You watch companions die continuously with almost no hope or joy to balance it out. When I finished Season 1, I just felt depressed.Worth your time if you like adventure games.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Nice 3d visuals with vivid colors and sketch lines that resemble perfectly comic's aesthetics. They are nor the best looking neither the most detailed graphics but they do the job.- Awesome post apocalyptic atmosphere. It manages to describe perfectly a deserted world taken over by the walkers. You'll feel the loneliness when walking through vast fields, silent forests and even more in empty cities. Without being a classical survival game it gives you strong survival vibes.- Well crafted protagonists with unique personalities. You'll attach emotionally to them. Clementine is absolutely fantastic and one of the most likable characters ever in a video game.- Interesting NPCs with rich backstories and complex relationships between them. Studying them is challenging, while most of them will quickly manage to make you care. Every death is important and will touch you.- Wonderfully written, fluid dialogues. Although there are hours and hours of conversations you'll never get bored. There is always something interesting or controversial that will force you to tell your personal opinion. Some dialogues are really poetic too.- Some of the best voice acting performances you'll find out there. So convincing, so emotional.- Interesting plot full of emotions, action and agony, although at some points it gets a bit repetitive or cliché. It packs many small stories form different perspectives, people and communities giving you a complete picture of the world that you're into.- Great direction and photography with cinematic shots, nice cameras' movement and good pace. In fact, it's more of an interactive movie than an actual video game.- There are many decisions that really affect the story's outcome. There are many more, smaller,  that don't. But the decision system is so well built that constantly gives you an illusion of having the power to affect everything, from characters' psychology to who is gonna die. In fact, you're much less powerful than you think and the alternatives are a lot fewer, but the key is to make you feel important, to feel heavier the controller buttons before each decision. Finally, it doesn't matter if there are two or ten more endings. What matters more is living it and giving you the motivation to craft multiple stories, relationships and alternatives inside your mind while playing. - If you want something splatter this is the game to go. I haven't seen so much blood, guts, decapitates and killing for a while now. And it's well implemented too.- Good overall sound design. It isn't spectacular by any means, but it's convincing and does the job in building tension. Music is nice and enhances the atmosphere when needed.- Good replayability value. Most episodes can be interesting after a second or even a third playthrough. There are many choices to try. - A great way to acquire all the seasons at once in a fairly good price when it goes on sales. There are also some extras and the graphics are slightly but obviously enhanced compared to the original versions. The bad- Although there are many little, interesting stories supporting the main plot, after a while it feels a bit repetitive. You get familiar with some characters, they die, some more appear, they die too and all over again. And it's so tiring to learn all the time new names and personalities and continuously evaluate them. Also this hustle, zombies killing or fighting each other, seems repetitive and after a while even certain deaths will be expected. Don't get me wrong. the story is good, but tends to run into circles.- Gameplay gets boring easily. Not only the QTE (quick time events) controls are well worn these days, but also there is no big variation of them. After a while it feels repetitive, while some QTEs make no sense at all. Killing zombies is too simplistic, lacks interest and if you die you'll just replay the scene starting from a few seconds before. No challenge at all.- There are some annoying graphics' issues. The comic effect is nice but not very sharp. It produces tons of dirty spots around the shadows and near the edges. This makes the visuals feel a bit amateurish. Also there is too much faulty blur effect during the last two seasons that constantly makes some characters or entire scenes complete unclear.- Clunky animations especially during the first two seasons. Both body movements and facial expressions seem robotic and that can cause some problems to navigation too.-  There is no skip button at all. You have to watch all the dialogues, cut scenes,  previously and next episode videos even if you are into your second playthrough.- "A New Frontier" and "Michonne" are mediocre. They have lost the balance and realism of characters and events. Deep conversations, survival struggle and those silent, poetic moments of loneliness have been replaces by epic battles between good and evil, big action scenes and cliché heroic moments. Also Michonne's illusions are so often that get tiring.- It's not exactly the game's fault but this version of zombies is problematic. They're just too slow, weak and dump to justify all the fear and agony, especially when the protagonists are not inside narrow and dark places. There are more than one obvious solutions for humanity to win this, but the most annoying part is the inconsistency. Sometimes one or two zombies are huge problem and others the protagonists easily kill dozens of them just because there are other more important things of the story to focus on. All these take their toll from realism and atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series contains 23 episodes across all 4 seasons and a mini-series.In order of when they were released before this collection was made, there's:The Walking Dead: Season 1 (5 Episodes & a DLC Episode)The Walking Dead: Season 2 (5 Episodes)The Walking Dead: Michonne - A Telltale Mini-Series (3 Episodes)The Walking Dead: Season 3 - A New Frontier (5 Episodes)The Walking Dead: Season 4 - The Final Season (4 Episodes)It also comes with some extra features like a new graphic black mode, a sprint button for Season 1 (but these two things are buggy, I'd recommend playing the game without them on a first playthrough and then using them if you do a second playthrough), character trophies that can play lines and animations, all the OST for every game and concept art.Season 1:The second best in the series and one of the best games of all time. The writing is off the charts. The Final Season may be my favorite season in the series but I have to admit that when it comes to the writing of characters, Season 1 is the best in the series. Lee and Clem are up there with the best characters in gaming, and the ending is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful.10/10Season 1 Bonus DLC Episode (400 Days):A very disappointing and skippable episode. A lot of the characters here are boring or annoying, and overall, as a one hour and thirty minute teaser for Season 2, it doesn't really connect all that much to Season 2 (which is entirely Season 2's fault). Only one character returns for good (and they aren't even that good of a character to begin with, in fact, they end up being really unlikable at the end of Season 2), and the rest of the characters only get 10 second cameos. If it ended up connecting more to Season 2, I might have given it some leeway, but as it is, this episode is pretty useless to the story overall. Like I said before, completely skippable.5/10Season 2:Although I still love this season, it's got a lot of faults. Starting off with the positives, the art style is great, an improvement from Season 1's already great art style. The OST is even better, with this Season having the best OST in the series, and some of the best OST from gaming in general. Episodes 1-3 range from great to amazing, it's got a lot of great characters and great writing as well, but once you hit episode 4, and episode 5 especially, you start to see the cracks in the writing that originally started to form in the first three episodes, that were caused by multiple rewrites and deadlines. Multiple character arcs or plot lines that get setup in the first few episodes are abruptly changed or cut off when certain characters are killed off too early. Some of the best characters are just completely sidelined for an entire episodes before getting killed off. They always find the most abrupt ways to write off certain characters that don't need to be written off in the first place. That's not to say that this season doesn't have good characters arcs or plot lines at all, one character specifically has an amazing arc but I don't want to spoil anything. The episodes are also noticeably shorter, with each episode being around an hour and thirty minutes, compared to each episode in Season 1 being around two hours and thirty minutes. If the episodes were given more time to cook before getting released, this season would've been much better than it already is, in fact, could've been on par with, or better than the first season. It's still an amazing game, but it had the potential to be better.9/10Michonne Mini-Series:If you're a fan of the comics, I'd say go for it. If you're here for the story of Clementine and nothing else I'd say skip it. Aside from Michonne, all the characters are either bland or very, VERY annoying (Sam makes me want to tear my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hair out every time she says a word). It's got the best choreography and QTE's in the series though. This story is in no way connected to Clem's story, which isn't a negative, but, like I said, if you're here for Clementine, you can just skip it. I kinda consider it it's own thing since I have a hard time grouping it in with the main series. There's not much to say other than this Mini-Series being overall meh.6/10Season 3 (A New Frontier):Absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Clem is completely sidelined and acts like a different character. The new characters here are either boring or just not likable in the slightest (Gabe is the most unlikable and worst character in the series). The OST is forgettable, which is very disappointing when coming off of Season 2, and the art style is gross to look at. The season is only 9 hours long, but it's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrible that it feels much longer than it actually is. Only around 20 minutes of the game are actually important to Clem's story. If these minutes worth of important scenes weren't so important, I would've recommend that you avoid this season at all cost and just skip to The Final Season. DO NOT let this season discourage you from getting to The Final Season. The Final Season is beautiful and, in my opinion, not only the best game in the series, but the best game of all time. On a more positive note, I think this game just goes to show how go the other games in the series are. They're so good that, at least for me, they complete make up for this train wreck of a season, to the point where this season doesn't really effect how I view the series as a whole.3/10The Final Season:The best game of all time. Every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scene is perfect. The final episode is the best thing in gaming. The perfect ending to the best video game series of all time.11/10Series Overview:It may have it's faults, but overall, I think this is the best video game series of all time. Season 1, 2 and the Final Season more than make up for some of the mistakes the series has made, with each of them having multiple amazing scenes and moments between characters. This is a series that I'd 100% recommend.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: season 1:the telltale point and click gameplay is so outdated it's not even funny. if you make a wrong move, take a wrong turn, talk to the wrong person, or walk in the wrong room, it takes a solid 10 seconds to get back where you were to go do the thing you wanted to do in the first place. on it's own it's fine, but after this happens 4-5 times in each chapter it gets really tedious. the fact that whenever lee walks in a room he constantly has to close the door even when there's no risk of zombies getting in REALLY pissed me off. some of the shooting gallery setpieces are a little fun, but they give you basically no challenge and are really just effortlessly clicking on heads. the graphics look really good for a 2012 game and really nails the feeling of a comic book the game is going for. the music is probably this game's only saving grace from how many memorable tracks there are. and the story... it's alright. lee and clementine's chemistry is pretty well written. his death at the end was pretty shocking which i liked. I wish they had focused more on his decent into maddness as he slowly became infected but they did what they could with it only being in one chapter. my main issue with the story is that so many characters take all these insanely stupid risks to get the story to where it's supposed to go. the one that really stands out to me is when Lee and Clementine are on a moving train going to the coast, and decide right then is a perfect time to do target practice when they know the zombies are sensitive to sound. also the voice acting in this game is not great. clementine's voice is so annoying it literally made me want to rip my hair out, and both her's and lee's lines get delievered poorly every once in a while and it breaks immersion. overall 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I first played this game a long time ago. I never finished it, because the release model was a bit bizarre and the price was expensive. This might have been the reason for why some players gave up on the studio and why it went bankrupt in the end... The studio itself is kind of legendary (Telltale Games). The game they made are like the pinnacle of point n' click type of games. Their 2 most well known games are a bit similar to Oddworld: Aby's Odyssey, but they have much more lore and story to them.This game and  are one of the best games ever made. They have some minor technical issues and could be better implemented technically (at least The Walking Dead), but story-wise...they are pretty amazing. In case of The Walking Dead, it's one of those games that has unique dialogues, story and choices that seem to matter. I would say that some dialogues are a bit too 'extreme', in the sense that you sometimes aren't given a choice in the 'middle', but this allows to build up a type of dramatic experience.I would personally be a tiny bit more realistic, but nonetheless - the game is entertaining.EDIT: I think that the "next" episodes (the ones after the 1st/2nd one) are actually very good and get better.This game could support windowed border-less mode and occasionally has got small issues like textures flickering, or (so far just one spot) characters 'teleporting' when moving around, but otherwise - it's pretty stable and solid.EDIT: It seems that each game "chapter" or "episode" has a different game engine, kind of. The newer ones run much better.The gameplay is unique. It isn't just a 'point and click' type of game. It has got elements of surprise, cinematic experience, quick events. It evolves even more in the final episode.It is very hard to find something similar to this game. I only dislike the graphical rework in this specific version of the game, it doesn't serve it that much in my opinion. It could be a bit more balanced - some areas seem over-exposed and just too bright or even with fake colors.It looks pretty good later into the game though.I believe that every person who enjoys playing games with interesting story, decent graphics (and the cartoonish style is pretty satisfying) and such a person that enjoys making choices and re-playing the game, or trying to play it differently - they will enjoy it.I think that it's one of the most interesting games ever, along with The Wolf Among Us, which I find to be even better in some ways.This game is great to get on a discount. You can play all the episodes one by one, finished and provided right at hand.

_childDocuments_.review: Season 1: Telltale at it's best. This is the game that brought back the genre from the dead. The story is great and emotional. It's one of the rare games that can make you cry. While the graphics are pretty bad, I didn't find it too distracting. The gameplay is fine. Soundtrack is not too bad as well. Season 2: If you liked the first one. You will like this one as well. I personally loved it. Gameplay remains simplistic but serviceable but that didn't bother me as I like the genre. But the story is top-tier. Just as emotional as the first one. The ending made me tear up.Season 3: If you are a fan of the series, you should get this one as well. They updated the gameplay to be smoother than previous entries and the improvement in graphics was noticeable too, especially facial expressions of the characters. I liked the new characters that they introduced, but I wished that we could play more as Clementine. Story is good but not as emotional as the first two seasons. Season 4: Probably the weakest season of the series but still good. They again updated the gameplay to be smoother than previous entries and the improvement in graphics was welcome, especially facial expressions of the characters which they refined from the previous entry. The new characters were hit or miss, there were some great ones and some very poor ones. I was happy that the focus was back on Clementine though. The story was less good compared to the first three seasons but the Clementine and AJ parts were more emotional than the entire New Frontier season.Michonne: The weakest part of the series for sure. The story is weak, characters are bland including the main character and it is too short. _childDocuments_.review: if you’ve never played it, it’s the best experience you’ll get collection as it’s literally the Definitive way to experience all of the main games, DLC and spin-off episodes. not only are you getting the whole story, but you’re also getting the remastered version of the original games, a new graphical setting that makes the game much more like the source material, a whole host of bonus features, and the games have supposedly been given a touch-up on the lipsyncing and overall visual effects. if you have, but you want to relive the story from start to finish, this is your chance to get the fullest experience possible. it’s a fitting, carefully curated send-off to an excellent series, and well worth your time to experience this amazing journey of trust, survival and friendships. visual style adds a whole new level to the storytelling, making scenes much more dramatic and intense thanks to the dark and gritty overall look. once you’ve completed all five stories, with over fifty hours of content, you can sit back and relax to over 150 music tracks, again, from every single title here – simply find which one it is and play it as many times as you wish.

_childDocuments_.review: Another perfect game, must play, 10/10.For new fans and old fans, this is a must play game. This is a series that will make you scream in fear from zombies or worse, laugh and goofy moments where you feel safe for a second later to get jumped, and cried in the sad times of your favorite character leaving. Far from the tv series and comic book, this story of the walking dead universe is by far the best one you can experience. Season 1 is by far my favorite. Choices you make feel like they matter, characters interact human enough to feel the stress in every conversation while zombies are trying to kill you. If not them, maybe it'll be raiders who follow you throughout the entire game. They start as ragtag teams of people with guns trying to mug you, and they evolve into full fledged organization by season 4. With new faces showing up and leaving every episode, the drama never ends. After every big win, there is some twisted event. This is a game you should beat a few times to see how the story changes, WARNING LIGHT SPOILERS, In the very first episode you meet a guy name Kenny and his family. He is just a nice dude who is trying to survive. I instantly hated him. From that point on, I was as mean or negative towards Kenny for the entire game. By the last episode his anger seemed to be nothing but rage or depression. In my 2nd play through I was nice to him and treated him much better and by the last episode he was more calmed down and easier to work with.If you want a fantastic zombie story with easy controls, the is a must play game. It is a literal point and click. I wont dive to deep into the rest of the seasons but they have everything the first season does and then more but it doesn't execute it as well as season 1. For the graphic update, the game looks light years better and the game already looked really good if you are into a comic book style of art. But this update make it look cleaner and make everything more recognizable. It feels so well done, I don't even notice until I love back at the old games. I plan on beating every episode all over again. I first did this on xbox and now I ready to do it all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: "Am I a good person, Clem?"The child you are looking after in season 4 asks this of your character. My friend Cole is not a good person. I wish I could've been the Clem to my friend Cole's AJ. Unfortunately, my friend Cole lives in Canada and I am in the US. Life got in the way, you know how it goes. My friend Cole and I lost touch for about a decade, give or take. He was a piece of ♥♥♥♥ before, and when we reconnected, my friend Cole was still a piece of ♥♥♥♥. I have atoned for my mistakes, I wish my friend Cole had. He just wants to keep bringing up how he had more Xbox 360 gamerscore than me. I mean, I get it. While he kept pounding away at gamerscore, I learned how to do things like drive cars and have a full time job - basic functional adult stuff, yknow? He broke 100k gamerscore and I bottomed out around 86k gamerscore and sold my xbox account to some guy on reddit who wanted my log in for some The Beatles: Rock Band DLC that wasn't available anymore.I really wish Cole had chased the gamerscore of Telltale's The Walking Dead back in the day. Sure, he met a great woman and is happy, but he could've probably been a lot happier if he was more like me, someone who played through Telltale's The Walking Dead. I'm proud of what he's achieved given his horrible choices and such, but I feel like if he had played through Telltale's The Walking Dead, I'd like him over his friends Ethan and Adam.

_childDocuments_.review: Words cannot describe how much of a work of art this game is. I decided to give this game a shot because I loved other games Telltale has put out, like The Wolf Among Us and Minecraft Story Mode, and I ended up liking The Walking Dead Telltale Series way more than any other Telltale experience ever. These characters that we interact with throughout the series actually feel like real people, people who were forced into the dark and ruthless world of The Walking Dead, which is more than I can say for the show. And the main characters, oh my god. The main characters some of the most likable characters in story telling ever. Lee, Clementine, Javier, you actually feel for these characters. Their pain, their happiness... you feel it because of the choices they make, and the choices you make. And the choices you make? They Matter a lot. The benefits, the consequences and your reputation matters. The Walking Dead Telltale Series is an experience that I think everyone deserves to have in their lifetime, because these types of experiences change you.

_childDocuments_.review: When the dead began to walk the earth... I was small and all alone. I lived in a treehouse that my father built for me, but she and my mother picked a bad time to travel to Savannah. One day a man came into my yard and asked for help, and I gave it to him. His name was Lee. From that moment he began to protect and protect me. He protected other people as well. But it's impossible to save everyone. The living were no less dangerous than the dead.A woman in our group, Lilly, lost her father. It was hard for her to come to terms with it. She killed the one whose life Lee had saved.Lee showed mercy, but she abused him later and betrayed us. Again.Lee taught me how to survive in this world and protected me for as long as he could. But he was bitten. Because of me.I still remember what Lee taught me. Even looking into the eyes of death and meeting her in his arms, he continued to instruct and teach me."Stay out of the cities, honey. It's too dangerous out there." - Lee was doomed. He knew it was the end for him. And he turned to me with one last request. He asked me to shoot him. And I did it.Then I met another group. Unfortunate and broken people who fled from their past. There was a woman in it who gave birth to a boy named Alvin Jr. Hey Jay. He survived. He survived thanks to the efforts of everyone who was with us then. But his mother is not. Something happened in the new group and Jane left AJ in the snow. We thought he was gone forever and we would never see him again. This was the last straw for Kenny. Kenny, who lost everything in this world, including the meaning of existence.Lee was no longer with me, so I had to make a decision. But I couldn't. Kenny killed Jane.It turned out that AJ is alive. Jane hid it to convince me that Kenny is no longer what he used to be. And even with what happened, I couldn't leave Kenny behind. I was too attached to him, he had already become a part of me. We tried to survive together.Until something happens that always happens. Until life took him from me.AJ and I went to the New Frontier base. I thought we had finally found a permanent home for us. But I was wrong again. They took AJ away from me saying I was too young to take care of him. I fought back. I wasn't going to put up with it and didn't agree with what they said. But I wasn't strong enough to defend myself. I spent a long time searching. And it wasn't until I gave up and lost all faith... that I found him.Now we are looking together - a place that would become our home. I am everything AJ has, and I only have him. And I will protect him with my life. Just like Lee did for me.

_childDocuments_.review: After binge-watching the entirety of The Walking Dead TV show and associated spin-offs, I decided it was timely to have a crack at the often-celebrated Telltale Series to see what all the fuss was about, and given that it offered all five entries under one reasonably priced title, The Definitive Series seemed to be the way to go about it. Season One is a great starting point, which unfortunately also means things don't get much better than that, but you begin the journey as you step into the shoes of Lee Everett; a former teacher with a dark past who takes a young girl, Clementine, under his wing at the onset of the zombie apocalypse. It's not the greatest story ever told, but it undoubtedly suckers you in as you get more and more invested in the characters and their fates, and I think it really demonstrates how well the Telltale formula works with the Walking Dead IP, thanks to the nature of the setting and how that feeds into the themes of the story and the difficult moral choices you face throughout the game. Season 2 is largely consistent in its quality as you now take up the role of a slightly older Clementine trying to make her way on her own through the world of the undead, but the dialogue begins to feel a little more awkward and expositional at times, and there is a developing sense that your choices matter less and less. That spills over into the Michonne mini-series that sits between Seasons 2 and 3 that, while offering a nice, self-contained moral dilemma with a major leap forward in its graphics and animation, suffers greatly from a lack of player agency stemming from the choices you're given feeling irrelevant or even antithetical to the outcomes the story arrives at. The same goes for Season 3, which also makes the bizarre decision to place a new set of characters, the Garcia family, at the forefront of the story with very limited Clementine segments that essentially strip her of any input you might have had for her characterisation, which damages the otherwise engaging story that A New Frontier has. Thankfully Season 4 walks this back by putting Clementine back in the role of the playable character, but it seems that there's a concerted effort for The Final Season to distance itself from the previous games that ultimately ends up causing it to feel strangely removed from the larger story. Still, even with Season 4's vast gameplay improvements and increased level of interactivity, it was truthfully a poor way to end the series as a whole thanks to a boring plot, weak dialogue, and an emotionally barren, cop-out conclusion. Overall, these were by no means the greatest games I've ever played, with the story failing to make up for the sparse gameplay offered by the Telltale formula, but they nevertheless captured my interest almost the entire way through thanks to the characters and the setting. Still, if Telltale games are your bag, if you're a Walking Dead fan, or both, I'd say the Definitive Series is worth picking up on sale, although I'm not sure how much it offers for returning players given the plentiful UI bugs, visual glitches and sound issues, not to mention the temperamental Graphic Black mode that I'd recommend switching off whenever you can.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be the longest review I've ever written for a game, but out of all the games, this one is the most deserving of it.  In my honest opinion, this is the best story game I’ve ever played, period. I’m not an emotional guy by any means, but MAN did the (seasonal) endings make me emotional. It was the perfect mixture of sadness and satisfaction, I honestly couldn’t ask for it to be any different. The emotional roller coaster this game takes you through is absolutely insane and something you can only experience yourself by playing the game.Before this game, I had never read or watched anything related to The Walking Dead, nor was I ever interested in it. I was recommended to play this game by a friend. Initially, I was hesitant, but he insisted it would be worth it, and oh boy was it.Almost everything about this game is brilliantly executed. The characters are memorable, the environments and situations feel real, and as you continue playing you feel more and more immersed.My only major complaint about this game is Season 3. I won’t go into specifics as to not spoil anything, however this specific season is definitely a downgrade compared to the others. I still recommend playing it thought. The story and various pieces of context are still applicable and are relevant in Season 4.I will note, do not go into this game with the expectation of “playing” a game, it’s more like “watching” a game, with various gameplay segments spread throughout it. Remember, it’s a Telltale game after all. This is not a bad thing however. I had initially thought it might have been, but the story makes up for any lack of gameplay. You will also make plenty of choices, a lot of which contribute to the story significantly.Check out to spoiler review for each season here:

_childDocuments_.review: What am I even supposed to say? A game I played throughout my childhood, having revisited it in my adulthood. Just like in the game, about changing, about ageing. As Clementine aged as well.Well... I'm certainly at a loss for words.While it's far from perfect - most notably, the fact that virtually all "choices" don't actually lead to alternative outcomes, something that only became more disappointing the further I played (which, expectedly, would be the opposite way around, as I should've typically gotten used to the lack of meaningful actions by that point. Yet, I was always continually disappointed as the writers felt the need to make my decisions meaningless even when it didn't require more animating, something that became more prevalent later into the game, showcasing poor writing abilities on the part of the creative team), I can't name a single game (or game franchise, in this case...?) that made me feel as much emotion, and generated as my tears, as this one.In particular, Season 1, Episode 5, Season 2 Episode 5, and Season 4, Episodes 3 and 4, I couldn't stop crying. There were so many more emotional moments in the other episodes, but these utterly destroyed me. I was just a mess for tears.Truth being told, I never played past (or even watched content of) Season 2. No spoilers, no YouTube let's plays. I only played, and watched content of, the first two seasons of The Walking Dead. Everything after that sort of felt like fanfiction, like it wasn't real, like it had already ended so long ago.Still, it was worth playing, finishing, those other seasons, and to see an end to Clementine's story. Or, at least, that which appears to have concluded itself.For those out there that truly want to feel something, something so strong, this game has so much of that, it's like a drug of its own. Be warned. And if you can stomach it... well... have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I would 100% recommend experiencing this game, the story is amazing and while is true that it has flaws like some decisions not feeling important, they do affect the story in a way that makes you feel responsible for your actions, making you immerse yourself in the world and it's characters.  Every season has it's flaws, but also have something that makes them unique and make it special and worth playing.  Talking about characters, some characters in this series feel like a lost opportunity, they could have been developed a lot more, BUT the characters that are developed really feel real, unique and special. I'm almost positive that if you play any of the seasons, they're gonna to be a character you will feel a strong connection or hate towards. The main characters in the series are also one of the strongest points of the series, they feel really flesh out like actual people, they are not just a empty husk for you to take control of them. Finally, to end this review, I have to say that while the game is far from perfect, what the game presents and lefts you with is 100% worth it. It is a unique experience that you will be glad you experienced, personally it has become one of my favorite story in gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: These games are pretty good and having them all in one together like this is great.My thoughts on each season:SEASON 1The first season is the best, in my opinion. It has good writing and good characters, too.SEASON 2The second is season is the worst of the 4. The writing is terrible, your decisions have little impact unless it's to piss somebody off. Clem is like 11 in this season and is somehow the most capable member of the group, which nobody acknowledges and the adults all feel useless.SEASON 3This season gets a lot of hate but I actually really liked it. It gives you an interesting perspective on who Clem is becoming from an exterior view. I think it's important to not just agree with/side with Clem on everything because that makes your experience as Javier feel a bit flat. Definitely better than Season 2.SEASON 4This is my second favorite season. The combat is different from the last 3 seasons and it's honestly pretty refreshing. The art style is really good and I love how Clem has turned out. My only complaint is that the system of teaching AJ morals is really black-and-white, which I guess makes sense considering he's 5 and doesn't understand nuance, but... other than that, this is a great season.MICHONNEAt the time I'm writing this, I have only completed 1 episode of the Michonne season. She was one of my favorite characters from the show (Until about season 8-9+) but this version of her does not even seem like quite the same person. If you thought the main 4 seasons had bad writing, this season will blow your mind; just when you thought it couldn't get any worse, it gets worse.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played all the separate games, but I bought this for the convenience of having all the seasons in one game plus all the extra visual enhancements. The game is super long, so price is worth it and you don't even need to be a fan of the TV show to enjoy it. The story in the game is a parallel story to the one in the TV Show, so it is unique to this game and you won't feel like playing the series, but the storytelling is amazing. You will get attached to the characters in this game more then you imagine. It is a must have game for anyone even if you are not so interested in zombies. This is not your usual shoot-and-kill game, it is an interactive animated movie with quick-time events, character movement and a lot, i mean a LOT of hard choices to make which decisions will stick with you till the end of the game. In this game the choices do matter the most of the times even tho sometimes you are forced to take a certain choice to be able to continue the game further.I recommend it at full price and it is a MUST have at a sale without hesitation.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece of a choice-driven, story-rich game that everyone should try. If you enjoy post-apocalyptic survival stories with zombies, compelling storytelling, and characters in the style of The Walking Dead, or if you’re already a fan of the series, this game is a must-play. Sure, if you compare it to newer choice-based games like those from Quantic Dream, you may find that the choices and impact aren’t as varied, but I think the game still holds up well. It’s got its own charm, a fascinating story, and an engaging narrative—sometimes it’s even better than the series.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a bad series, but the longer it lasted the worse it became.Going season by season: - First season was undoubtedly the best one. Good and diverse set of characters, decent story and overall satisfactory finish, making players ask for more. 8/10  - Second season had its ups and downs, and overall left a lot of holes in the story that could have been easily fixed with some more time, but never did. New characters felt short, and felt that they were just replacements for older ones, not bringing in much diversity. 6/10- Third season is just trash. Main character was annoying, the side cast was done really shallow, and the entire relationship between MC and others felt forced, like REALLY forced. Storyline started being extremely predictable, and ended in a very open way, which felt so...unfinished. 1/10- Fourth season tried something new, and somewhat succeeded. Decisions here made more sense, and impacted the game more, however, adding a `home base` and `collectibles` killed the `keep moving` vibe other seasons had, because the entire game is happening in a very small radius. Also, the season is shorter than the rest, and had a lot of filler and unnecessary content. It did had its moments, but they felt too confined to a small place and group of people. Could have been really good. 4/10- Michonne standalone story is just garbage. No sugarcoating here. Very short, very simple and very boring. Forgettable characters, unimportant decisions and a lot of filler content. 0/10Overall, 4/10TWD series are still best on comics, and had a decent run as a TV series, but it ultimately felt short as a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: Before I write my big ass paragraph, this game is 100% worth it, I bought this on the winter sale and I do not regret it the slightest, I'd buy it double the price if I had to.When I first bought this I just started watching The Walking Dead show and I've been enjoying it I thought this looked pretty good, I've come to learn that was a big understatement. This game is a masterpiece, from A New Day all the way to Take Us Back, I was so immersed in the story and by the end of the Final Season, I was upset that it was over. This game has (in my opinion) the most sad and depressing scenes in fiction. The story of Clementine and her growth is so amazing, and her story with raising AJ is so good and gives me season 1 vibes and I love it. Every friend Clem meets are *usually* so well done. I've never cared for so many characters in a game this much. Lee's redemption story from killing his ex-wife's lover to raising and teaching Clem how to survive was amazing. Lee is a fan favourite and for good reason, I can safely assume everyone fell into a deep depression after his "departure"Javier was also a good protagonist as well, not as good as Clem and Lee but good enough to care about him. I liked the dynamic with him, Kate, and David. Gabe was annoying, and Mariana was alright considering she had barely any time in the seasonI loved the story with the boarding school. The whole drama with AJ killing Marlon, Clem's relationship with Louis and raising AJ were all so good it would take to long to write about all of them.If you are interested on playing this game, please do yourself a favour and play it, one of the best things I've ever experienced. Thank you Skybound and Telltale for making this masterpiece and wrapping it up so nicelyMy Ratings of Each SeasonSeason 1: 10/10400 Days: 7/10Season 2: 9/10A New Frontier: 9.5/10The Final Season: 10/10Michonne: (coming soon)

_childDocuments_.review: This is my 2nd time in completing the First 2 seasons, and first time for the other 2.The first 3 Seasons are 10/10However, the Season Finale's story is just plain awful.First of all, how is a 6yr-old kid capable of a decision making and talks like an old man with 30 yrs of experience in the apocalypse, like a guru When even the MC's having troubles herself? It felt like AJ's the one who's got the memories of the MC in the past 3 Seasons and Clem is the baby. Did the devs think that that is how 6-yr old thinks and that's how a 16-17yr old would think in an apocalypse?Also, aside from Lee, it seems like the other season's memories were just plainly forgotten in the Season Finale to help you progress in the totality of the story, which was the main driving point of the first 3 seasons. Your "world building" for the past 3 season we're just wasted away and is clearly useless in the season Finale.Overall, the first 3 seasons are god-tier storytelling. 10/10Season Finale is meh, prolly 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so, first and probably only game review I'll do. This game is just such a masterpiece not to voice my opinion on.I cannot believe the journey this game takes you on, Clementine has possibly the best character development I've ever saw in a character and just bonds you to her that much more. Constant fear and anxiety, especially in Season 1, of her getting even the slightest scratch on her. Once you take control of her it eases it a tiny amount but boy do you still panic in some situations. Even replaying you will feel this anxiety. Season 2 sends you on a nostalgic trip reminiscing on the previous season talking about your adventures and partner in crime. However it never makes it any easier when the same result is replicated as the only thing you'll ever know in this is that it will not go well for long, don't grow too attached to anyone.. This is infact an impossible task and you will never be satisfied with how the episodes end. Season 3 is a bit of a iffy season, not the biggest fan of it nor the DLC's but theyre still done wellSeason 4... Felt sick to my stomach playing this one in both the worst and best ways, it is a work of art and nothing can be said otherwise. The devs give you the most freedom with the combat and dialogue. However this does mean you get attached even easier. The whole Clem being a mentor is stressful but makes you think 'WWLD' - What Would Lee Do. If you haven't played it, do so asap please.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. The story has you on the edge of your seat at every moment, guessing whether or not you made the right choice at every interaction. Clementine is such an amazing character, and to follow and assist her with her character development makes everything that happens much more emotional. Can't tell you how many times I was brought near to tears at the end of every episode. The final chapter is a big step from how the other games played out though; much more freedom of movement. It's kind of a shame though, I wish I never played this game so I could witness the magic all over again. Also, this isn't so much against the game, but I wish there was a way to theatricize your choices, so you could watch every episode like a movie. The art style is different, but imo it gave the writers much more room to worry about the story. 10/10 would recommend. I wonder if TTG would be able to top this or even come close to this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like the game but that doesn't mean the game is bad or something. I couldn't make myself finish the game is because of it's pacing and general gameplay. Many times you are just confined inside a small place and asked to talk to every person 1 by 1 to find tasks and progress further. While, this feels normal but the way it has to be done is kinda like chore to me. The movement speed is very slow at times and all characters feels lifeless all the time even in conversation.If anyone can sit through all these boring scenarios, I have a good feeling that story is gonna turn out great here. I couldn't do it but not everyone's like me.In my opinion, Life Is Strange-1 did a formidable job in keeping the general gameplay and pacing bearable. No fixed cameras, no slow movements, people having lot of charisma in their voices, much more vibrant world.To my best of optimism and understanding, this game can do a nice 8/10. Buy on sale only.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead by Telltale Games is an excellent adventure game that has received critical acclaim for its immersive storytelling, memorable characters, and engaging gameplay mechanics. The game is set in the universe of the popular comic book and TV series of the same name, and it follows the journey of Lee Everett and a young girl named Clementine as they navigate a post-apocalyptic world filled with zombies and other dangers.One of the strongest aspects of the game is its story, which is emotionally charged and full of tough decisions that have real consequences. The player's choices throughout the game affect the outcome of the story and the relationships between the characters, creating a deeply personalized experience. The characters themselves are well-developed and memorable, with unique personalities and backstories that make them feel like real people rather than just video game characters.The gameplay of The Walking Dead is also noteworthy, as it combines elements of adventure games and interactive storytelling to create a truly immersive experience. The game features challenging puzzles and tense action sequences, as well as dialogue trees and other interactive elements that allow the player to shape the story in their own way.Overall, The Walking Dead by Telltale Games is a fantastic game that is sure to delight fans of the comic book and TV series, as well as anyone who enjoys a good adventure game with a compelling story and memorable characters. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: As a Walking Dead fan, I couldn't wait for this to drop in price. So I coughed up $49, grabbed a root beer, and settled into my comfortable chair.While TWD doesn't follow the television series, it's still a satisfying game. The nice thing about it is that your decisions affect the game's outcome, more or less. The cel animation takes some getting used to. It feels like you're in the comic book, only animated. The game uses point-and-click to get things done. You're presented with several options when faced with a decision:  Truthfully, most decisions eventually drag you back to the linear story line.I have two negative issues with the game:1. The first one is the touchy-feely conversations that are blended into the scenes. While intended to flesh out the characters to make them more real, they seem to conflict with the ever-present danger.2. The second thing is  IOW, if you die at a certain point, you have to begin the scene again, which forces you to re-play tedious sections.  I was trying to kill this one zombie, and it was giving me grief. It took 10-12 attempts before succeeding. Having to replay the whole section the same number of times was an exercise in frustration.That said, TWD pulls off a satisfying journey into the apocalyptic story we've all come to embrace.

_childDocuments_.review: Telltale Games' The Walking Dead series is often regarded as one of the most powerful narrative-driven games ever made, and at the heart of this success lies the profound, emotional bond between Clementine and Lee Everett. Their relationship transcends the conventions of typical video game character dynamics, becoming the emotional core of the series, particularly in Season 1. Through their journey together, Telltale tells a story about survival, trust, and the complex human connections forged in the face of unimaginable circumstances.In The Definitive Edition, this bond is given even more weight as players experience the full arc of Clementine's growth across all four seasons. However, the foundation of her entire story—her transformation from an innocent child into a hardened survivor—is inextricably linked to Lee, whose impact on Clementine resonates throughout the series, even long after his death.Lee Everett: A Complicated HeroLee Everett is introduced as a man burdened by his past. In the opening scene of Season 1, Lee is being transported to prison after being convicted of murdering a man who was having an affair with his wife. From the outset, Lee is established as a morally complex character, and the player is given a unique opportunity to shape his personality and actions as the story progresses. Despite his troubled past, Lee quickly becomes a deeply sympathetic protagonist, one defined more by his desire for redemption than by the crime he committed.When Lee stumbles upon an abandoned house and discovers Clementine hiding in the backyard treehouse, the course of both their lives changes forever. What begins as a chance encounter evolves into a deep, paternal relationship that becomes the emotional backbone of the entire series. Lee, a man initially broken by his past, finds new purpose in protecting Clementine. His story is not just about surviving the apocalypse; it is about making peace with himself by ensuring Clementine’s safety and preparing her for the harsh world ahead.Throughout Season 1, players make decisions as Lee, shaping his actions and choices, but the heart of the narrative revolves around how Lee interacts with Clementine. The dialogue options the player selects not only influence how Lee is perceived by other characters but also how Clementine views him and, eventually, how she views the world.Clementine: An Innocent in a Cruel WorldWhen we first meet Clementine in Season 1, she is just eight years old. Frightened and alone, she is a symbol of innocence amidst the chaos of the zombie apocalypse. Her parents are missing, and she has been left to fend for herself, making her immediate connection with Lee both necessary and deeply emotional. Clementine’s vulnerability and trust in Lee set the stage for a bond that feels incredibly real and heartfelt, and players quickly become invested in her safety.Lee's role as Clementine's protector is the driving force behind many of the decisions players make. Should Lee shield her from the cruel realities of the world, or should he prepare her to survive in it? This tension between protecting Clementine’s innocence and ensuring her survival becomes one of the series' central themes, as the player is constantly reminded that the world is unforgiving, especially to children.Clementine starts the game as a beacon of hope in a world dominated by fear and death. Her wide-eyed innocence contrasts sharply with the horrors that Lee and the rest of the group encounter, and protecting that innocence becomes an emotional task for both Lee and the player. But as the game progresses, it becomes clear that Clementine cannot remain untouched by the world forever.Lee and Clementine’s Dynamic: Surrogate Father and DaughterOne of the most compelling aspects of Lee and Clementine's relationship is the way it evolves over time. Initially, Lee is simply trying to keep her safe, but their bond deepens as they come to depend on each other for emotional support. Lee becomes a surrogate father to Clementine, filling the void left by her absent parents. For Lee, this bond represents redemption—a chance to be a better man, to guide and protect someone who is completely dependent on him.The game excels at showing the subtle development of their relationship. In the beginning, Lee is responsible for teaching Clementine basic survival skills, such as how to shoot a gun or how to keep quiet and hide when danger approaches. These lessons, though simple at first, carry enormous emotional weight, as they represent the loss of her childhood. As the story progresses, Clementine comes to rely on Lee not only for physical protection but also for moral guidance. Every decision Lee makes is not only about immediate survival; it’s about shaping Clementine’s understanding of right and wrong.One of the most poignant aspects of their relationship is the way it reflects the broader theme of survival in The Walking Dead: in a world where death is constant, the real struggle is holding on to humanity. Lee, through his actions and choices, teaches Clementine what it means to be a good person in a world that constantly pushes people toward cruelty and violence. Whether it’s by showing her compassion, teaching her to defend herself, or simply giving her hope, Lee shapes Clementine into a survivor who is as empathetic as she is strong.The Heartbreaking Climax of Season 1The emotional climax of Season 1 comes in the final episode, when Lee is bitten by a walker and is slowly succumbing to the infection. The once-strong protector is now helpless, and the weight of everything he has taught Clementine comes to bear in this moment. For the first time, Clementine must fully take control, as Lee’s time is running out. This reversal of roles—from protector to protected—is both tragic and beautiful.In his final moments, Lee’s influence on Clementine is evident. The player, through Lee, must decide how Clementine will move forward—whether to shoot Lee to prevent him from turning into a walker, or to leave him behind, thereby sparing her from the emotional trauma of killing him. Both choices are devastating, but they illustrate the ultimate goal of Lee’s character arc: to ensure Clementine is prepared to survive in a world that offers no mercy.The farewell between Lee and Clementine is one of the most gut-wrenching moments in modern video games. Lee’s death is not just the loss of a beloved character; it’s the culmination of everything the player has invested in throughout the game. Lee’s final words to Clementine—"Keep that hair short" and "Stay strong"—are simple, but they carry the weight of their entire journey. This moment serves as the emotional foundation for the rest of the series, as Clementine carries Lee’s legacy with her long after he is gone.Clementine's Journey Beyond LeeThough Lee’s story ends with his death in Season 1, his influence on Clementine is felt throughout the entire series. As she grows older, Clementine reflects Lee’s teachings, and players see how their decisions in Season 1 shaped her worldview. In Season 2, A New Frontier, and The Final Season, Clementine evolves into a strong, independent survivor, but she never forgets the lessons Lee imparted.In many ways, Clementine’s journey is a direct continuation of Lee’s. Her relationship with AJ, the baby she takes care of starting in Season 2, mirrors the bond she had with Lee. Clementine becomes the protector, teaching AJ how to survive in the same way Lee taught her. The cycle of survival and mentorship that began with Lee continues through Clementine, making his presence felt even when he is no longer physically part of the story.ConclusionThe relationship between Clementine and Lee Everett is one of the most powerful and enduring in video game history. It’s a testament to the emotional depth of Telltale’s storytelling that their bond resonates so deeply with players.

_childDocuments_.review: To sum up, this game or this playable movie series is the masterpiece of all the story-rich games that I've ever played. I have always loved story telling games, Death Stranding,  Detroit: Become Human, and Chinese Paladin (a classic to Chinese 90s gen ), are all good games, all made me shed tears, but this game is different. Cause, gahh! jesus!  this game have touched something deeper, something made who I am, something like my soul. As advertised, the narrative of the story could be altered if you made a different choice, which is plenty druing the process of the game.Though the choices can be undone, you just need to reload, but that is not recommended,for a story tailored to your decisions is what you must live with.I can sense that the game encourages players to stick to their choices, to keep on going even the choice cause a bad out come, which is always someone got killed or moveing on a trajectory you don't want.But that is the point, it supposed to make you feel difficult at deciding who you want to keep or must sacrifice, for a dead walking world,nothing is simple.It dosen't mean the ending is gonna suck, though some choice may make you sad or regret for a while, but Telltale had done a good job making the narrative reasonable and keeping the mystery till the end.That is all I can say, more would spoil the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★☆☆☆As a long-time fan of Telltale's The Walking Dead series, I had high hopes for the Definitive Series. Unfortunately, this collection falls short of expectations in several key areas, making it a letdown for both seasoned players and newcomers.First and foremost, the visual upgrades promised are underwhelming. While some scenes do show slight improvements, the overall graphical enhancement is inconsistent, leaving many moments feeling just as dated as the original releases. The "graphic black" art style, meant to emulate the comic book feel, often ends up making scenes look murky and indistinct rather than sharp and stylized.Moreover, the performance issues that plagued the original games persist here. Frame rate drops, occasional crashes, and audio glitches disrupt the immersive experience, making it frustrating to play through extended sessions. It's disappointing to see that these technical problems were not adequately addressed in this definitive edition.The bonus content, while a nice gesture, adds little value. Behind-the-scenes footage and concept art are interesting for a quick glance but don't justify the premium price tag. Fans hoping for significant new content or enhanced gameplay features will be left wanting.Additionally, the controls remain clunky and outdated. Navigating characters and interacting with objects feels cumbersome, a stark reminder that these games were designed several years ago without significant modernization for current gaming standards.Overall, The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series feels like a missed opportunity. It neither offers a polished experience for returning fans nor an impressive introduction for new players. If you haven't played the series before, you're better off starting with the original releases and tempering your expectations. For those who have already experienced Clementine's journey, this collection does little to warrant a second trip.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will be updated as I play through the seasons.Season 1:Yep, if there's an actual zombie apocalypse, I'm not living through that stuff. The Walking Dead Season 1 will destroy you. Blow after blow after blow to your heart. But it is a necessary experience. We need experiences like these to remind us of how we're lucky. Sure, a zombie apocalypse is pretty much fiction, but the struggles shown in this brilliant piece of media is very real. The toll, of a situation where you have to do anything to survive, on the human mind. The horrible acts one is forced to do in order to get by. How bleak life can get. How small things, that we take for granted, are the most important. We NEED to be reminded of that to appreciate what we have now. This season is full of memorable characters, masterful writing, gorgeous execution and grotesque twists to truly give you a sense of hopelessness and pure dread. But even when it reaches rock bottom, things do eventually get better. Life is like that. I believe in that. No matter how bad it gets, we keep moving... I will never forget this game and it's effects will stay with me for years to come.Necessary to play10/10400 Days:Interesting setup for Season 2. How good of a setup it is, I'll only know in season 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was contemplating whether it should be positive or negative review, because the game is OK, but I think that the game is praised too much for it's story, which is not that great. Definitely it has some interesting episodes, but it feels too scripted, and unrealistic. I didn't feel like my decisions make any difference at all - characters that are meant to live will live despite all circumstances, and characters that are meant to die will die - you can save their live for one episode at most. Although the game itself states that the story is shaped by your actions it is simply not true, all decisions that you make are insignificant and in reality main course of actions is predefined. And when your decisions don't really fit into scenario you'll just see some absurd situations that don't make much sense. Another big downside is that the game really expects you to behave well and usually punishes you for making tough decisions, for example you can steal food or medicine from someone, which, despite your expectations (like saving life of your friend or preventing death from hunger or something like that) you don't get that much benefits and later will be punished while making morally good decisions usually is more beneficial. Because of that you don't really feel that it's tough surviving in post-apocaliptic world, because you can just always make good decisions, share you food, behave well, and everything will be just great. For me it's just poor writing. From a gameplay perspective the first two seasons are pretty boring, because there are very few actions that you should do: rare and simple QTE's and that's it. But it get's better and the final season is much more dynamic. In conclusion, while the game has its moments, it's just OK. but don't expect too much from it. It's worth mentioning that each season is better than the previous one, especially from gameplay perspective, game becomes more dynamic and involving. The Clementine is a great character and it was interesting to see how she grows up in this post-apocaliptic world.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 4.5 stars  Alright, so I just wrapped up The Walking Dead Definitive Edition (upto mich, and man, it's something else. If you're a fan of the series or just dig a solid story-driven game, this one's a winner.First off, the graphics got a facelift, and it's like seeing an old friend with a glow-up. The post-apocalyptic world looks both eerie and beautiful, and the characters? They look even more real, making the whole thing hit home a bit harder.What's cool about this edition is that it packs in everything - all four seasons, the 400 Days DLC, and Michonne's side story. It's like binge-watching a great series, but you're the one calling the shots. They ripple through the whole narrative, keeping you hooked from start to finish.And can we talk about the music? Seriously, the soundtrack is on point. It knows exactly when to kick in, cranking up the tension or hitting you right in the feels. It's like the icing on an already delicious cake.Plus, there's some behind-the-scenes stuff thrown in, giving you a peek at how the magic happened. It's cool to see the faces behind the characters and how they brought this whole emotional rollercoaster to life.Whether you're a die-hard fan or just looking for a gripping story, The Definitive Edition is worth a go. It's more than a game; it's an experience that'll stick with you. So, dive into the world of Lee, Clementine, and the gang. Trust me, you won't regret it.(Edit after 100%)Even though there's choices the story itself is linear. What you choose to do mostly affects how the characters view you and sometimes who lives or dies. Don't expect multiple endings or being able to change the course of the plot.

_childDocuments_.review: Telltale's The Walking Dead is a masterclass in story driven games.  With the definitive edition and its final season the magnum opus in their legendary legacy before shutting down. This game demonstrates that when it comes to enjoyable gaming, most times all you need is a well written, delightful and lovable main character and great set of secondary characters to support her.The game is an exodus, through all the 4 seasons + 1 spin off season. I experienced the 40+ hours of exciting story, unfolding carefully written stories and journey through the apocalypse with a band of people, either good, or evil.The choices you make will ultimate decide certain paths the story will take, the outcome of several characters. You shape who Clementine is, and seeing her grow from a cute, innocent, childful kid to a battle hardened survivor is great.I recommend everyone, who enjoys story driven games, with some the casualness in gameplay that exist in Telltale's games, to experience this great story of a survivor in the apocalypse that has meticulously crafted throughout 7+ years. Experience the masterpiece created by a legendary studio that people still wished was still around.

_childDocuments_.review: ILLUSION OF CHOICE. During the first season I really enjoyed this game and was totally hooked because I believed that my actions were shaping the story and I was creating my own game. But then I looked up a YouTube video one day and saw that no matter what option I chose, the ending stayed the same. After that I lost interest in choosing what I thought would be the best option. Now I understand that it would be impossible to create an unlimited number of scenarios and infinite dialog, scenes, etc. But the fact that its all an illusion from the game to make you believe you actually do something put me off. Now, above all that, this game is a masterpiece of storytelling and characters. It knows what it is and knows that is has a perfect formula to grasp the player to want me. Some of the characters were honestly annoying, but Clem, AJ and Lee were amazingly well written and voice acted. All the voice actors should be praised. Would I recommend you buy and play this game in 2023? Yes, definitely. But I wouldn't buy it for more than $15 considering the flaws, length and DLC.

You are not here to receive a gift, nor have you been called here by the individual you assume, although you have indeed been called. You have all been called here into a labyrinth of sounds and smells, misdirection and misfortune. A labyrinth with no exit, a maze with no prize. You don't even realize that you are trapped. Your lust for blood has driven you in endless circles chasing the cries of children in some unseen chamber, always seeming so near, yet somehow out of reach. But you will never find them. None of you will. This is where your story ends. And to you, my brave volunteer, who somehow found this job listing not intended for you. Although there was a way out planned for you, I have a feeling that's not what you want. I have a feeling that you are right where you want to be. I am remaining as well, I am nearby. This place will not be remembered and the memory of everything that started this can finally begin to fade away, as the agony of every tragedy should. And to you monsters trapped in the corridors, be still, and give up your spirits. They don't belong to you. For most of you, I believe there is peace and perhaps more, waiting for you after the smoke clears. Although for one of you, the darkest pit of Hell has opened to swallow you whole, so don't keep the devil waiting, old friend. My daughter, if you can hear me, I knew you would return as well. It's in your nature to protect the innocent. I'm sorry that on that day, the day you were shut out and left to die, no one was there to lift you up into their arms the way you lifted others into yours. And then, what became of you? I should have known you wouldn't be content to disappear. Not my daughter. I couldn't save you then. So let me save you now. It's time to rest, for you, and for those you have carried in your arms. This ends, for all of us. End Communication."

_childDocuments_.review: Rating each season, but first, an overall impression of the entire series: Never have I ever played something so emotionally captivating as The Walking Dead. I'm 10 years too late to the hype and release of Season 1 as well as all the proceeding seasons and spin-offs but my god, even 10 years later it still holds up to be one of the best gaming experiences I've had (it is no exception to flaws though, which I'll get into)Definitely recommend from the get-go, got this game on sale but even in full price is still cheaper than all seasons combined and bought separately.Now for the individual reviews! I'd ramble about each one but boo, Steam has a character limit so I'll keep them light:- fine, a bit of bias since this is where it all started and c'mon, Lee Everett is the G.O.A.T.- found family trope with a former felon being stand-in father to young girl, so emotional investment is already in the bag- the best survivor group across all seasons - a splendid story to serve as a foundation for all the other seasons- Episode 2 is the stand-out, Episode 3 is the weakest imo- 5 tears out of 5 tears ending, I knew what would happen but still bawled- decisions had weight and mostly left you feeling remorse and regret; effective storytelling- ... what was that?- more an interactive teaser than an episode (P.T managed to be its own game, why couldn't this)- concept of "collection of survivor stories spanning 400 days of the apocalypse" is interesting, but execution is poor- each character's story is so short I could barely care about their circumstances- saw this more as a freebie than anything to the Definitive edition- solid continuation from the first season- so many bittersweet and bleak moments that heightened immersion and intensity- Clementine's growth is heartbreaking- survivor group holds up on its own but compared to the first is a bit annoying- character writing inconsistencies - great antagonist - deaths feel super unnecessary and sour the overall story- delivers an amazing ending - contrary to popular belief, I'm part of the minority that actually liked this season- agree with general consensus though that this is the weakest one of all of them- was heavily invested in the "golden popular child vs. hardened military son" sibling dynamic- not so invested in the forced romance (just thinking about it gives me the ick)- also contrary to popular belief, Clementine's characterization this season was cool and I didn't mind not playing as her- started out great (opening cinematic was amazing) but fizzled out- better/more fluid animation in exchange for a horrible artstyle that meshes comic and realism- a great conclusion to the entire series- AJ is an amazingly well written character, especially for being only a 6 year old- a more grounded story which is welcome considering most of the "run from place to place" setting- an amazing step-up in terms of graphics and artstyle- better gameplay, much more interactive in fights and exploration than just being rapid clicking a button for quick time events- a desperate cop-out ending just to induce a few tears, could've been more original but it's aight- I didn't realize people disliked this so much- not as forgettable as everyone says it is- story was engaging, characters are lovable- runtime was way too short- decisions felt very restrictive and lackluster- a nice break from the main story- did what it could in just under 3 episodes- crush on Pete, damn he's fine

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game, especially the story. I always liked the aspect of the choices you make affecting the story. It barely does affect it though, but the choices I made made enough differences for me to enjoy it.The gameplay side of things though, it's terrible. The heads of the characters glitch out often, and, in episode 2 of season 1, going up the stairs in the people's house and then going back down the stairs without investigating in the other room will soft lock you. Lee will take a step down the stairs, Mark will say "help me", Lee will go back up and you're left back at the top of the stairs. Moving in any direction will push Lee towards the stairs and soft lock you with the same dialogue of Mark asking for help. This forced me to restart the entire house part.
