_childDocuments_.review: I have the utmost respect for Telltale games. So sad they were bankrupt, but glad they're back and making The Wolf Among Us 2. Anyways, the game.The Walking Dead Definitive series is a collection of 5 games, including all the stories: season 1, 2, a new frontier, Michonne and Final season. I'm gonna go across all the seasons in that particular order and say what my thoughts are of them.Season 1 is the crux which everyone remembers, its the Ironman of this The Walking Dead Universe. I'd like to thing this was the The Last of Us story, without having The Last of Us. The relationship of Lee and Clementine is so human and lifelike and that you can't help but feel the connection between them. It's a classic father and daughter story, which everyone should enjoy and have an experience in it. I can also appreciate 500 days "dlc" (I put in quotes cos its no longer dlc for people who buy the definitive edition) as a nice epilogue... kinda story. It's nice that Telltale put in the effort of another episode.Season 2 is the movie which you say "Oh, that was good." .... and never watch it again. But you still remember a key point from that movie. You control Clementine, and she meets a new bunch of survivors which you hopefully get to stay with and call your home. I'm certainly not saying that this is the worst, but if the last point is the part which really just matters, which makes other choices in the game kinda obsolete, I'm not sure I can enjoy the game. Also, most of the characters are annoying in this story (except Boat God). Not a memorable pick, but still something important to the whole enjoyment to the story of Clementine.Now, Season 3, aka The Walking Dead: A New Frontier, is actually my personal favorite, despite the fact that you rarely control Clementine even though it's Clementine's story, and they butchered Boat God's beard. Take control of Javi, and try to keep your already tight family alive. I haven't really talked about the graphics, but you can definitely tell it's a very different artstyle. I will admit, the cast of characters aren't the greatest bunch of characters, but like, it's certainly an interesting installment in the series, and I can respect that. Season Michonne is by far the worst and my least favorite. Take control of Michonne... and that's really the only good thing I can say about that- heck, I'm gonna get slander for this, I don't like Michonne. A samurai like woman who has a strange backstory and a badass- I dunno, I don't like that in a story where 1. The main story follows a girl with her own struggles and 2. She can overpower a lot of things. Strength is weakness and weakness is strength. You wanna see a person grow from struggles and learn from mistakes, whether from self or others. I'm glad it was only 3 episodes, but Steam doesn't recognize that I FREAKING FINISHED EPISODE 1 OF IT!!!! AGGGGGGGGGHHHHHH!Lastly, but not least, the one with the most depth and dedication to it, The final season. Take control of Clementine again, and uncover a hidden but familiar foe from the past. This game does a lot gameplay wise, such that a lot more depth in combat and exploration. I also like the collecting of items and the choice of having a romantic interest in the games... although I suppose technically season 3 kinda addressed that? I dunno. This is also the final story of Clementine, so I.... oh wait.... the comics..... huh. If you want more Clementine, I guess I would recommend the Clementine comics by Tillie Warden. I've never read it, but honestly, from the first few pages, it's kinda unlike Clementine. So, The Walking Dead. An amazing series spin-off formed by Telltale, a "choice" based game based around the story of Clementine. Verdict: This series is a definite get, but if you ask me, skip season Michonne. Also, wait for a sale, cos damn, that stuff kinda expensive. Or, go Steam CDkeys.

_childDocuments_.review: Great series in terms of story telling. For actual game play, it's a glorified "decision based" interactive movie. I would say the first and last seasons were some of my favorite stories ever. The first season left a very big impact when it first came out. The parts in between were honestly a bit bland and boring, but it was necessary to complete to complete the full story of Clementine. I really enjoyed the time you spend with her as she grows up.For its full retail price, this game is completely not worth it. Even though it is the entire collection of games, it almost has no replay value once you know the story(unless you forget it). Each season(Excluding the Michonne stuff) would take a maximum of 10 hours, so you're looking at 40 hours of game play. While this may look like an interesting proposition of 40 hours for whatever price it is, the game kind of drags on and has really slow moments that don't necessarily add to your enjoyment of playing the game. I would definitely get this on sale if you're willing to play through an awful game for story.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead is a truly beautiful game, up until recently I had never played it, but I had watched countless (and I mean, literally over 20) different playthroughs on Youtube, by countless different creators, and alot of the same creators too just because their reactions were so satisfying, and, with the definitive edition, I finally have a chance to play all of these incredibly touching games for my own without having to pay up to £90+ to play them all. The game series is so incredible, Season 1 is a perfect game in every single way, it focuses on character development, introduces all of these indepth characters and makes you care about their wellbeing so when faced with difficult choices, you feel more pressure and emotion if you regret your choice, and also in moments when you don't actually have a choice and something tragic happens, you feel so dreadfully sad. Season 2 accomplishes the same effect, by keeping familiar characters, and overall having a better story than Season 1. While some of the choices in Season 2 have absolutely no bearing on the story, it is the final choices in the game which truly matter, as you finally have a chance to shape the main character in a meaningful way, and you can choose what kind of person you'd like them to be. Season 3 feels fairly out of place, and more of a side-story to the main characters arc, as they are only a side character in this game, however, the story is so incredible apart from this, and so even though it does feel out of place in the series, it is still very fun to play and enjoyable to revisit. Now for Season 4, one I haven't had a chance to play on my own yet. From what I remember, the gameplay is incredibly different, however the formula is the same, with extra groundwork and structure to make it a better game. The story is incredible, following our main protagonist again, and we shape them in many more ways then technically possible throughout the entire game series up to this point. I love the collectable system, and the final decision is heart-wrenching. I've tried to keep this review as spoiler free as I can, but, if you're reading my review, you've almost definitely played the game series already or else you wouldn't have scrolled so far down to see this review. In short, The Walking Dead Definitive Edition features 4 incredible games, a side story for Michonne from the comics and the show, and tons more interesting features like development art, un-used assets, a music player, a model viewer, and so so so much more. I love this, so, I'm so happy to own it. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I'm probably the luckiest guy in the world to have experienced this story raw, and without spoilers.Honestly, it's beyond words, this game. From the Start to the end, I was fully invested in this world, it's characters, it's story, and it's unfiltered cruelty and honesty. I'm a sucker for story-based games, and this is easily my top pick. Being able to choose what you say and do is always hard, but it's even harder not knowing what the right choice is. I know lots of people say that your choices don't truly matter in this game, but they did for me. For someone who didn't want to look up the "answers," I learned what you say and do matters. That may be corny, but there's something about this series that struck me, and many others, to appreciate the weight of your consequences. Even if you made the wrong choice in the moment, that's the beauty of the story. There's more I could say, but I just want to thank the developers for perfectly crafting a story that I fell in love with.  I highly encourage anyone curious to give this story a try.  10/10, no regrets.

_childDocuments_.review: The game can serve as a valuable character study and you might learn a thing or two about group dynamics as well. No matter what choices you make along the way, the main story line seems pretty straightforward and there is always someone in the group who messes up things. Plus, silence counts as a valid response, and you'd be amazed how much people let out if you just let'em. Just like IRL.With all the smombies prowling the streets bumping into posts and people, I figured it'd be appropriate to replay The Walking Dead. A recent steam sale of this episodic screen journey beckoned me to delve into the apocalypse once more because previously I had only played through Season 1. It is great to see Clementine growing up and to live through the trials and hardships of an ever-changing group trying to survive an apocalypse.I found myself riding an emotional roller-coaster as I got more and more invested in this or that protagonist. With the story getting increasingly intricate with each season, I found it quite hard to decide whom to sacrifice to keep going. Don't worry about the seemingly hopeless situation, though ;) as the dialogues really get hilarious at times.The characters are easy to identify with... ok, most of them at least ;P Of course, first of all there is Lee, the main protagonist, as the guy who must not die since you as the player step into his shoes. He seems to be a decent guy with enough integrity and street knowledge to survive. But not alone. People join and leave the group, and as the player, you have to make quite a lot of tough decisions concerning this potpourri of hillbilly, journalist, geek, teenager, racist, military forces and their respective convictions, prejudices and opinionated views of how to proceed.These decisions play into the relationships that develop and, of course, affect the bond Lee has with Clementine, the big-eyed girl who stays at your side throughout the series, and for whom you act as caretaker. Even if you're not into zombie apocalypse and the such, it is absolutely worth to play because of the aforementioned funny dialogues, the plot twists, character development, and the heart-rending story of Lee and Clementine.☀☀☀ Much much more than a mere adaptation of the TV series☀☀☀ Relatable characters and heart-rending stories and mini-plots☀☀ Cartoon-ish, artsy visual style☀☀ Easy 100% Achievements☁☁ Linear story with your decisions not  having an impact in the long run☁☁ No Trading Cards☁☁ Limited replay valueIt is worth full price given the hours of game-play you gonna get for your buck.On steam sale, it's an absolute nobrainer - pun intended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: This story is amazing - the dialogue makes you care about your characters, which is nice because it feels like real people who are living in a nightmare. I could see normal people being in situations like this and understand the psychology of every person as well. It was so hard to make choices and it'll probably be even harder to go back and choose a different outcome. Makes you wonder who would survive in a zombie outbreak too - is it by chance? Luck? People around you? Your environment? Physicality? Mental durability? If you decide to play this game, I encourage you to use this for great life lessons - yes, you should be kind and try not to betray anyone, but why would people do the things that they do? If you can become understanding of behavior, you can become a worthy leader and calm everyone down; and if you can get everyone to work together, your survival should, ideally, be much higher.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Games, story real deep, a lot of emotions and many tough moral choices that we have to make. PS: And just to add that the graphics get better and there is a more interactive gameplay that is real cool.This game collection teaches many life lessons, people when in bad situations have to adapt but maintain humanity, caring and hope. In life you will have many consequences to your actions, bad or otherwise. In life there are some things that are out of your control, even if you try to change something, the result will be the same because you are not in control.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series ReviewThe Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series is an emotional rollercoaster that I wholeheartedly give 100% to on Steam! 🎮 This collection not only captures the essence of the original games but also presents a much better experience than the later seasons of the TV show.Characters That Stick With YouFrom the moment you step into Clementine's shoes, you're immersed in a world filled with unforgettable characters. Lee, AJ, and Kenny stand out, each with their own compelling stories that resonate on a deep emotional level. The choices you make shape their fates, making every interaction feel meaningful. Telltale's masterful writing brings these characters to life, and their development throughout the series is truly remarkable.Clem’s Journey with LeeOne of the most touching aspects of the series is Clementine's growth through her relationship with Lee. As she navigates the harsh realities of the apocalypse, the flashbacks featuring Lee provide warm, heartfelt moments that showcase the lessons she learns from him. These memories not only deepen the emotional impact but also highlight how Lee's guidance shapes Clem into a strong and resourceful survivor. Watching her evolve from a scared little girl to a capable leader is incredibly rewarding.A Better Experience Than the ShowWhile the TV show has its moments, it struggled in later seasons with pacing and character development. In contrast, The Telltale Series maintains a consistent quality that keeps you invested. The storytelling is tighter, the characters are richer, and the emotional weight of your decisions feels far more impactful. The game delves into themes of survival, morality, and the bonds we form, providing a deeper exploration of the zombie apocalypse than the show could achieve.Flaws and TriumphsOf course, the game isn’t without its flaws. Some technical issues, like occasional bugs or performance hiccups, can break immersion. However, these are minor compared to the emotional depth and narrative brilliance on display. The Definitive Series also includes enhanced visuals and all the DLCs, making it a complete package for both newcomers and long-time fans.ConclusionIn conclusion, The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series is a standout title that deserves every bit of praise it gets. With its strong characters, emotional storytelling, and impactful choices, it offers a gaming experience that surpasses much of what the later seasons of the TV show delivered. If you’re a fan of storytelling in games, this is an absolute must-play!

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I've played all the games as a kid and I've cried everytime. During the steam summer sale I thought I'd get the definitive series and play through all the seasons again. I'll edit the review each time I get through a season.02/07/2024 - Season 1I thought I'd never cry again to a video game but god was I wrong. I won't spoil anything about the game for anyone thinking of playing this for the first time but , make sure you have a box of tissue paper ready because you'll be needing them for the tears.The music in depressing yet beautiful , the art style and visuals are truly timeless and the story is gut - wrenching yet amazing. The story can be alter based on the decisions you make and the voice line options are quite good giving you the power to really do what you want. Saying that there are also decisions you can't make as they're inevitable. Each character in this season have their own pros and cons depending and what decision you make so think carefully about your choices!The "puzzles" of this game are quite straight forward and usually everything you need to know are either obvious or given to you by speaking to the characters available. Each level of the game takes you to a new environment which their own puzzles and choices to make , there are many times where I was zoned out or not paying attention since they balance action , story - telling and cut scenes pretty well in this season. Overall this game is great. This game is truly a masterpiece and I'm not saying that out of nostalgia. 9/10 for Season 1.05/07/2024 - Season 2God ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ damn it I am seriously in tears right now. I really really love this game so so much. After all these years almost more than a decade I find myself playing the same game not expecting much but man did this game deliver. I don't really like the Walking Dead TV Show but I really do really really love this game.Anyways time for some critique I guess! Season 2 , a whole new season! Which means new faces and what not. Personally I found myself having less of an attachment with the new characters , I'm not sure if that is due to the character design of some of them but I have to say unlike Season 1 I'm not really caring of the new cast. BUT! that does not mean I don't like any of the new cast there is one or two I absolutely LOVE! Although my views are of course subject to opinion. So you like find yourself liking more that is great!Trying not to spoil this game is quite hard.. but if I was to talk about this game without spoilers I'd firstly point out the amazing art which seems to be a staple with this series. The second season of this game brings a lot of new environmental elements to the visuals and some of them are absolutely breath taking! The music is subtle almost to the point where it just compliments the scenes but also parts where the music really gets me emotional during the scenes that need them most. An interesting thing is that you cannot change your sensitivity in-game which is peculiarly strange as you could in the first Season/Game from memory. I doubt this matters much to people who don't play competitive games and aren't used to a certain setting but even if you do you'll get used to it pretty quick!The very very few things about this Season that I'm not really a fan of are:- The Story feels very set in stone and don't play much of a drastic change in the story! The story is great by itself there is no disputing that. But sometimes there are things are want to do that aren't an option which is kind of a bummer. There are some very very Story changing options but very little. I just wished they added to option to do things that are very possible and logical sometimes like if I wanna to shoot a certain Russian!Well actually that's it.. There really isn't much that is remotely bad about this game! Its great :) I'f you're still thinking about getting this game but haven't make sure you do! You really wont regret it unless you hate crying which in that case I recommend setting up an appointment with your local GP to obtain some Lexpro @- @ Sorry jokes not funny..Either way a 9/10 for me again! Hope to finish the 3rd season soon :)

_childDocuments_.review: I remember watching playthroughs of this series on youtube when it first aired, and thankfully I could remember very little to nothing of what happened in season one and after. After seeing this on sale for 20€ (as to it usually being sold at 50€) and me not wanting to get every season seperately, I bought this collection. And I gotta say, it's worth every penny. So far I've finished the four main seasons with the michonne DLC still left, roughly 40 hours of gameplay in.. just 3 days. Yeah, I know. After finishing season one I was so invested in this whole story, I wanted to know how it ended so bad I finished the entire series in one weekend. Those were probably the saddest three days of my life. Enough to make a grown man cry.The story and characters are fairly well presented, for the most part, and they're very different from Kirkman's The Walking Dead TV Series you may be familiar with. Though honestly sometimes it feels like watching an Episode of The Walking Dead, just with extra steps and better characters. I was completely lost in this story because of how the game works and is written. My actions shaping the way the story unfolds, tough decesions I had to make in a matter of seconds, and dealing with the consequences was definenely a tough match. Prepare for emotional damage.Sure the overall gameplay quality varies from season to season, including graphics, controls, also characters and stuff, but I think overall it all works out quite okay. The devs had a really hard time finishing this series, with Skybound helping out to save the day eventually, and I'm really glad they did.Now after I've finished the game, I'm writing this knowing how it all ends, and feel kind of emtpy. Though not in a bad way I suppose. The last time I felt like this was when i finished Bioshock Infinite's story, just..? dunno. If I was able to forget all of what happened in my 40 hours of gameplay, just for the sake of enjoying all of it again like I did the first time, you bet your sweet bippy I would. Now go get it damn

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games to get me to cry. At the time this game was made, Telltale was practically a "no-name" studio. Nobody really cared what they were doing, they were seemingly making hollow tie-in games for films like Back to the Future and Jurassic Park. Which are big films, so it's odd they never gained traction. The Walking Dead, however, was just gaining its sea legs in pop culture when the first episode dropped. And suddenly the format Telltale had built for gameplay had been retooled for narrative, and the potential clicked. The game was good.This game should, in my opinion, serve as the blueprint for what a narrative-focused game should be. It gives you time to know characters, choices that impact the story and the characters in it. But it also gives time to explore, and find meaning in the story. It lets you take in what's wrong, what's right, and most importantly it lets you change those definitions as time goes on - something the second and third seasons are reluctant to do.Each episode is memorable, each episode is meaningful. There's no filler. There are puzzles. There are fun, interesting characters. Ben is there, too. And as the game builds towards the finale, the feelings of hope and dread and joy and sadness all mix together and create a unique experience unlike any other I've seen in a video game. This is a good game.Kenny is a racist, sexist psychopath that only wants to use Clementine to validate himself. I guess that's why so many "gamers" relate to him? Every moment he was on screen I was uncomfortable, but I guess it's important to show that trauma can change people - and that other people can neglect to see that pain. Be they Clementine or the people playing as her in this game. This one is a rollercoaster - no time is given to reflect. No time is given to converse. Everything simply happens, one major event after another. The time once given to connect and converse with other characters and explore is gone - a side effect of Telltale pushing this season to be dense with drama. This, of course, has the opposite effect. If you don't care about the characters, why would you care what happens to them? If they're all going to be killed 3 minutes after you meet them, is there really a reason to get to know them?The season is, in the end, alright. It brings together three key players: Clementine, the girl you protected throughout the first game. Kenny, an old friend. Jane, a new friend. The choices you make throughout the season simply don't matter. What matters is the choices you make at the end. Who you trust, who you don't. It all serves to set up Clementine's future, but at the expense of not caring about her present. It's fine.It's fine. Javi is a fine character, and his family make a good extension of that character, for what little they matter throughout the story. I think the game certainly has some of the most interesting supporting characters, but they're either swept under the rug or die. The game also pivots partway through from "I must take care of my family" to "I must save this settlement that fell prey to a power-hungry leader" - even if you  tell the game that you do not care about the settlement. You are fully railroaded into a story that makes no sense for the characters to be involved with.I also think the inclusion of Clementine was unnecessary. It added nothing really interesting to the story, and instead made me wish the entire game was about her, instead. Her inclusion as a whole just kind of highlights how everything in the game is kind of meaningless? Like her goal was to find out where AJ was and that could have happened without the events of the game transpiring. It's fine. It's just pointless. Nothing matters.One of the few games to get me to cry. Telltale (and later Skybound) really popped off with the final season. Not only did they bring the fidelity up to modern standards, but they introduced the stunning "graphic black" art style that has now been retrofitted into the past titles. This is on top of fun side content (collectibles), a proper third-person camera paired with the return of proper exploration sections, and truly meaningful choices and branching paths for the story.They keep the number of characters throughout this season consistent, each one (aside from Omar) getting time to shine and grow a meaningful connection to not just Clementine, but AJ, too. The choices you make truly matter and truly change the characters and the way they feel and interact. If the development of this game hadn't been interrupted by Telltale's going-out-of-business bonanza, I can only imagine that it'd be even better.This season alone makes playing through 2 and 3 worth it. This is a good game.You could not pay me to replay this one.This collection is worth checking out. It's two amazing games, one alright game, a serviceable game all wrapped into one. And the Michonne series is there.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played through all off the The walking dead tell tale series, I must say that it is totally worth it, to try these games. Maybe that is in part due to the fact that the first two seasons had Kenny and Lee, who were my favorite characters in the series beside Clementine, but I think it was a bit about the writing as well.The 3 Michonne episodes are a nice addition, but since I did not read the comics, and did not even finish the show (following the saviors part I did not watch further) I did not know all of the context.The 3rd season was nice and all, but even though Javier was a nice person I guess, I wanted to play as Clementine, not him, and most other players (based on the statistics at the end of each episode) made the Choices, that were in her favor. If I had to make a choice, between her and Javier's family, I would have chosen to stay by her side, since I basically watched her grow up during the previous seasons.The Final season was not bad by any means, but maybe due to the fact, that I do not much like kids, I think it was not as good as the first and second. I believe that Clementine as a character really gets to shine, when surrounded by adults, not kids. It is much more impressive when she is more like an adult, and makes better decisions, when she is among adults, in comparison to when she is among kids, but I guess that is up to preferences.Overall I believe that Telltale really nailed it with their game, and I do think, that the best thing to have come out of the Walking dead comics are the first two seasons of this game (even more so then the TV series in my opinion). _childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series is easily the best way to own the amazing story of Clementine that started in 2012, and put Telltale on the map. As before, each season is a banger, particularly the first and final seasons, with consistent, hard-hitting emotional beats and excellent writing.The visuals have been updated across the board, with the fantastic graphic black mode that absolutely immerses you in this world and feels like a moving comic book. I think A New Frontier benefits the most from these enhancements, as much of the glossy look from the original version is removed; and the entire season is brought back more in line with the visual tone of the rest of the series. The convenience of having all 5 games in their complete forms, all together in one place, can't be understated. It really hammers home the idea that this is one, sprawling narrative that you are getting into. The extras are a fantastic edition as well. In the menu, you can look at behind the scenes art, commentary, etc. In addition, there is a feature where you can view character models performing animations and speaking voice lines. Yes, you can view AJ riding on Lee's shoulders whilst shooting a machine gun. Did the developers have to include this? No, but I'm grateful that they did. It really makes the whole thing come together as this complete labor of love.For those who have never played Telltale's The Walking Dead, this is a perfect place to start. For those who already have, this is an excellent chance to revisit what is arguably the best story The Walking Dead has ever had, and to see it up-scaled and polished for the first time. Since playing the first season in 2012, this series has brought tears to my eyes more times than I care to admit. I highly recommend that those who haven't experienced this narrative take the time to do so, it really is one that should't be missed.Still. Not. Bitten.

_childDocuments_.review: An Unforgettable Journey through The Walking Dead: Definitive EditionRating: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️The Walking Dead: Definitive Edition by Telltale Games is an absolute masterpiece that deserves all the accolades it has received. As a fan of both the original series and the Telltale games, this definitive edition has exceeded my expectations and left a lasting impression on me.First and foremost, the visual enhancements in this edition are truly remarkable. The graphics have been remastered, giving the game a fresh and modern look while still retaining the distinctive comic book art style that fans adore. The environments are more immersive, the character models are more detailed, and the overall presentation is simply stunning.But what truly sets The Walking Dead: Definitive Edition apart is the emotional impact of its storytelling. The game takes you on an emotional rollercoaster from start to finish, forcing you to make difficult decisions that have real consequences. The writing is top-notch, with well-crafted dialogue and a compelling narrative that keeps you invested in the characters and their struggles. You'll find yourself forming deep connections with the characters, feeling their joys and sorrows as if they were your own.The voice acting in the Definitive Edition is absolutely outstanding. Melissa Hutchison's performance as Clementine is nothing short of brilliant. She brings so much depth and nuance to the character, capturing every emotion with incredible authenticity. The rest of the voice cast also delivers exceptional performances, breathing life into their respective characters and making them feel like real people.The gameplay mechanics remain faithful to the original, with a focus on decision-making and interactive storytelling. The choices you make throughout the game shape the narrative and have lasting consequences, making each playthrough a unique and personal experience. The Definitive Edition also includes all four seasons of the game, along with the additional DLC episodes, so you can experience the entire journey in one comprehensive package.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the entire game including Michonne, and in the words of the game, I was left quite . But don't get me wrong, it's not a bad game, it's overall absolutely amazing, it's an above average game with amazing artwork, storytelling and animation. You may be wondering why I'm conflicted, so let me explain.  In my playthrough, I had no issues with Season 1. It's my favorite season.   Absolutely hated the UI of this season, and especially the mouse mechanic where you have to move it when a brackety thing pops up. The game didn't catch me doing it most of the time. Michonne had a similar mechanic and for some reason it worked way better in Michonne.  I have nothing to really say other than I really question whether or not this season was really necessary to include since we don't see TNF gang again in Season 4. The only benefit I saw was us having to see Clementine linearly grow up.  It's quite weird, I ended the season with Javi asking Clem to revisit with AJ, but that never happened. Did the S4 team forget about that ending or did I just not reach a S4 ending where it happens?!?! Oh and also, in the episode 3 intro clip, you can catch Clementine wearing a wrong outfit, some purple, rainbowy jacket if I recall correctly.   I absolutely hated the given reaction times to danger in this season. It felt way shorter than previous seasons. I died so many times compared to other seasons. I'm not sure if this was intentional to resemble more accurate choice making (as in real life, you generally make choices fast) but it was quite annoying, I had to be super fast at times to make the right choices or else I'd die, I felt like a little bit more seconds to make choices would have been better. Also, I experienced an animation error at times where I'd stab a zombie but the zombie would disappear once stabbed. Also, spoiler,  I really wish this season ended with a visit to Richmond to see Javi's gang again. Also, spoiler,   So overall, this season felt a tiny bit rushed, probably because of the excitement to finish making the game.  Even though the ending wasn't exactly what I wanted, I was still very happy to see it after what went down towards the end (not spoiling).  Oh, Michonne, I really feel bad for her. I absolutely loved this separate story except for two things. One, in ep. 2 there is a lottta green outlining occasionally seen. I can't tell if it is intentional but it really irritated my eyes.  And two, the ending felt a bit incomplete if you decide to revisit your family. I wish, if you went that route, we got to see them again. Perhaps more content (a DLC or another episode) can be created for such an adventure, I'd really love to see where  Dominic and the kids are and if they're even alive.    It was really annoying to make some choices at times that essentially led to the same outcome, like I couldn't say 'No, I don't want to go / do something.' to some things. I'm guessing it was just for character/personality and relationship development and/or for the story to linearly progress. And also, there was occassional blur/glaring at times, making it harder to clearly see characters faces. If this is intentional to resemble accurate lighting / sunrays or whatever, get rid of it, it's doing you more harm than good, believe me, it irritates my eyes. This may sound like a lot of stuff to hate but the game takes days to complete and believe me, there's more positives than negatives to say about this game. Really loved it. Would love to see more of it. As mentioned, Michonne seems like a perfect story to continue, and maybe there can be more content in which Clem & AJ reunite with TNF gang again and go on a survival adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Best 10€ I've spent in a while. I had played through Season One before, but it was very much worth a replay. Not much to say about Season One, this collection is very much worth to buy on sale for that alone.Season Two is quite different, but still great. Most of the characters are very interesting and likable, and the story also works really well. Parts of the story feel a bit unconvincing for the universe, but that is just a minor nitpick. On the ending side, the amount of character deaths just for shock value gets a bit too large, and don't have the same feeling of meaningfulness to them as the ones in the first season. But overall, great stuff.Season three (A New Frontier) is much weaker than the other seasons, mainly because it never has a moment to slow down. The characters rarely get a moment to just talk without some ♥♥♥♥ immediately happening. The story of Season Three is also very out of place, and it should be thought of more as a standalone story. While it does have parts of Clem's story in the middle mainly as flashbacks, everything around that is pretty bland and uninteresting. It was still fun to play through it though.Season Four gets right back on track. There's not much to say about it without getting spoilery. This season introduces interesting new characters, and because of that, the story is also very captivating. The ending was also quite surprising, and a great way to end Clem's on-screen journey.Overall, this is one of the, if not the best story game you can find. Everyone who can appreciate the "story" as much as or more than the "game" should pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series contains all four main games, the 400 days DLC, and the Michonne spin-off. In the first game you play as Lee Everett, a man with a troubled past that finds himself having to protect and raise a little girl called Clementine, shortly after the onset of a zombie apocalypse. The sequel takes place roughly a year after the conclusion of the previous game. You now play as Clementine, as she tries to adapt and survive in the brutal world that has emerged. The remaining two games continue and conclude her story.The story told here is nothing short of phenomenal and gut-wrenching. The connection between Clementine and Lee, the struggles she faces, and the people she comes across in her journey, will not leave you indifferent by the end. Even though there is a decline in the quality of the story by the third game, the whole experience is still very much worth it. The story will change slightly depending on your choices.Despite being a point and click at its core, the characteristics you normally associate with the genre are less prevalent, having instead a more streamlined approach. The game also features many action scenes that involve quick time events.The graphics emulate a comic book style, which is fitting, as the games are based on The Walking Dead comic book series. The Definitive Series features various graphical enhancements in comparison with the original games.The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series is a classic and an achievement in storytelling. If you enjoy a good story, you must experience it!

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, to Clementine: Thank you for accompanying me to grow up. I first knew and played this game around 2013 when we were almost at the exact same age. Since then, some kind of connection has been established between us. During the first season we were both just little kids, but after that you have grown to be so much more mature than me at a heartbreaking speed. Now your story has ended in my world, still I hope you stay safe and sound in your world.Now back to the topic. I have just started replaying the game and my mood is quite different from that when I was a child. In the past, I was simply just trying to be a good person and for that I tried to please everyone cautiously, always looking for the "perfect" answer; I thought staying silent was the most useless option, now I find silence the best cure under many circumstances and there is never "perfect" option. Moreover, I finally comprehend the underlying bitterness within people that I was not so clear about before such as Kenny—He can be pretty emotional sometimes, but the reasons behind that are tragic. A wonderful thing about this game is that almost every decision you make is based on intuition because there is time limit, therefore you can easily get immersed in it. Consequently, even though I know clearly that what kind of fates these people will step into, at some certain moments I still chose like this is my first time playing this game.Lee and Clementine met each other at their darkest period—Angelic Clem has awakened his bright size of human nature while Lee has slowly healed her pain and erased her fear with great love and responsibility. Such relationship has touched my heart a lot more than many combinations of real father and daughter. I would not say that this is my favorite game because it is something isolated from being a game to me—It has become a really special existence in my life. Also, If you want to understand this game a little more, just listen to "Clementine Suite" from beginning to end—It is all told in this 7 minutes long pure music.

_childDocuments_.review: "Little girl, little girl, don't lie to me.Tell me where did you sleep last night?"I never read all of the Walking Dead comics or seen any of the live-action series. On that basis alone I declare this to be the best Walking Dead media. It is also superior to The Last of Us' narrative(yes really).I remember playing the original Walking Dead Season 1 and 2 and being astonished at the quality of the characters and story. I was so invested in Lee caring for Clementine and was a little outraged at the situation Clementine found herself in Season 2.Alas I could never get into the remaining seasons due to real life reasons. I was also saddened at the situations Telltale found themselves in. Its a miracle this collected package came at a decent price. Kudos to Skybound for providing the sendoff this series needed.Let me get the negatives out of the way. Quick time events in games see an interesting evolution.  There are time when they are annoying, but sometimes are just enough to engage the user. Over time, the games cede more control to you rather than making you a participant in "Press X to not die". There is some horror movie trope logic in play, such as zombies being ninja-like and invincible like when the plot demands it, and some instances of medical/surgical operations that would actually kill than help. Some characters even act contrary to their social context. But in the context of the story it is OK to digest it (the same way you accept some incredulous logic in superhero movies). There are times when even times where you have to take control of the characters feels arbitrary but that gets better as the seasons go on. Also the Michonne and 400 Days are clearly the weakest sets of the lot. They're not bad but it is clear that they were placeholder games between seasons. So I recommend you play the seasons in their order of release to get a better experience! Now it is time to lavish praise.This game made me nearly cry. The Last of Us could not do it. Avengers Endgame could not do it. I can only recall Mass Effect 3 and the Bioshock series doing that to me. It definitely stays in the upper rank of gaming for me purely for that. The entire series has had so many writers that there is a justifiable fear too many cooks spoiling the kitchen broth, but miraculously all the characters (good, bad, and ugly) still feel authentic, especially those who appear across multiple seasons. This is the major strength of the series. Now as far as the choices go, there is clearly a limitation in the variety that you can make across seasons, but this is an understandable issue. But Telltale at least invests you into the universe and makes the impacts memorable if not long lasting. The story telling helps cover over the limitations of choice in a great way especially if you binged it (Does binging apply to games? Let me know in the comments). I don't want to really spoil anything but the journey of Clementine as her role evolves is clearly the standout point of the entire series. Its a strange but enlightening experience though, as I did have a struggle when I  made choices for her. Did I make this choice because as I was moonlighting as a pseudo father figure? Or did I make this choice because that's what I'd do in her shoes? Or was I trying to be a good person? The choices may not be cleverly complex, but they do make you think of who are you as a person making the choices.Season 3 is a weird outlier though. It is a distraction of a story with limited impact on Season 4. But the characters are pretty strong. Don't be discouraged by its presence though, it is still a rewarding story.One thing the Walking Dead series is probably known for is its endless tragedy porn. Luckily, for the most part the writing is handled deftly in varying amounts with the right kind of impact. Very rarely did I regret the decision I made and restarted the episode. It doesn't beat you over the head with it harshly(Looking at you, The Last Of Us Part 2). Of course I did have this criticism with Season 2's potential multiple deaths but that was when it was released individually back then. When you binge on a whole it is just the right amount of tragedy. LOL, never thought I'd have to write that sentence.The graphics have also been better remastered and look better in this collected edition. As a binger it might feel a bit awkward see the evolution from a near cartoony to a 3D-ish cartoony graphics from season to season, but gamers who are used to replaying series will not find the evolution to be a distraction. Well, for me anyway.Controls are also pretty good, keyboard gamers and gamepad controls are solid enough. I played this mainly using the gamepad, and there were times I kept forgetting which analog stick I had to use for the quick time events but that's a minor issue.To sum up, go and get this collected edition for a unforgettable and compelling interactive experience with only a few dated elements here and there.

_childDocuments_.review: The series as a whole is great, with parts of the package being bad.Seasons 1, 2, and 4 are great at what they do. They are stories that really get you invested in the characters, and their choices feel somewhat influential even if they do not amount to much in the long run.A complaint I constantly see about the series is "The illusion of choice," but there are technically choices; they just affect minor parts of the game. It's how pointless choices feel that makes them frustrating to many.If the story as a whole is good, then the lack of big, impactful choices does not matter much, as that wasn't what the game was going for.What makes this package of games feel less great are seasons 3 and Michonne. Season 3 is a mediocre story with elements so bad they're laughable. The biggest instance of this is a late-game character's death after you saved them. The way both characters die is laughable, and honestly, if they were just not included, it would be better. The group you are with is not very good either; the best-handled character is Jesus, while the rest feel pointless and frustrating, even the previous main lead, Clementine.Michonne, on the other hand, was so bad that if you buy this collection, just don't play it. The game so badly wants to force you down a certain route for the story, even if it makes no logical sense. Characters just feel downright stupid, and there was not a single one I liked.I also wanted to bring up technical issues. Season 1 has a bit of jank to it, but it runs fine enough. Big choices usually lead to a bit of a lag spike. Season 2 ran smooth as butter; it is the second-best season on a technical level. Season 2 being so great makes Season 3's technical problems unacceptable. There is a ton of jank to the game on a visual and technical level. Characters eyes will become like glass for whatever reason; shadows will be so dark that characters completely disappear in the dark, ruining many scenes; and the walkers have this jittery lag to them when showing off multiple of them. It really is pathetic considering season 2 had similar large hoard scenes and looked good. Season 4 ran great for the most part, and I have no complaints with it; it's probably the best on a technical level. Michonne isn't worth discussing.Overall, I recommend the series heavily. I would just recommend that if you get this game, skip both Michonne and season 3. They are just not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very decent game. Doesn't really have any gameplay (except "maybe" in the last season).The story is obviously the main focus here, it has it's very good moments but also moments where you might get bored. i'd say it's mostly the good moments however. it worths your time , but remember, this is mostly a movie rather than a game so watch some spoiler-free gameplay before you jump into it so you know you can tolerate it as a movie. If you watched AMC's The Walking Dead series , you will see a lot of similarities between these two even though this is considered a game but that one is a serial. I can't talk about the story more without getting into spoilers. i'll just say that it has a lot of "i might cry" moments.The music is also very decent, better than what i expected and it fits the narrative well.The Graphics are...well you can see them online, but just know it gets better in later season.The Gameplay might be a little outdated for today's standards (especially the earlier season) but the focus of the game is not gameplay, rather the story and choices with their consequences.There was 2 non game breaking bugs in the last season , also the first season's achievements didn't unlock when i first played. nothing big, but i just wanted to point them out. all ignorable.Overall a decent game, worths taking a shot if you like these kind of dialogue heavy, RPG , story driven , movie like with quick time events and enjoy them.

_childDocuments_.review: So, to start I will almost certainly update this review as time goes on and I get further through the games, normally I try to have a significant portion of a game done (if not finished completely) before reviewing. However I felt the need to make a review after a few hours in the game because of one major thing:All comparisons of graphics between this version and the originals I could find online do not do this game justice at all. From what I saw before buying and downloading the game I really thought most changes where more stylistic than anything with only some small touch ups. Some of the comparisons I saw the only difference I could tell was things looked darker or lighter.However very quickly into the game (at least playing at the graphics settings I am) I realized none of that was true. None of what I saw beforehand did justice to the new lighting system in this version, which blows away any of the past (well I had played seasons 1-3 at least) versions. Sometimes in certain scenes it REALLY shines and the lighting looks downright gorgeous.Textures, textures are a huge step up in quality now too, at least a lot of them are. Some more so than others for sure, but a lot of the time you can can really tell the difference.AA, seems much better to meAlso, they greatly boosted Lee's walking speed! And not like TWDs2+ slightly faster walk button speed, like he's pretty speedy now. This is a hugely welcome edition that goes a looong way in making the game feel less dated.FPS, oh my! The FPS is so much higher and there are way less frame dips that cause stutter.Important to note: I am playing this version on my high end gaming laptop while all my past playthroughs of these games have been on console My most recent was Season 1 on a Series X/4k TV while the first time ever was a PS3.

_childDocuments_.review: I've known the series since it came out, I was a kid back in the day and saw the game and the choices in a certain way, always believed that the choice I would make was always the right one. But the truth is, finally playing the game for the first time really at 18 makes a different effect. Despite bugs, various glitches and all, the game still manages to convey something to you, distrust, insecurity, anxiety, sadness. Just like the old The Walking Dead. It made me reconsider what I thought years ago. It makes me think, reason, ponder what to do and doubt my own morals. An undoubtedly beautiful game with different stories to shape. It is also able to make you realize what kind of person you are. Recommended in every aspect. After finishing all the seasons, I feel sad and empty. A feeling I haven't felt in a long time, a good 6 years. I platonically fell in love with Clementine from seasons 3 and 4, and her facial expressions and features make her almost real. I have this feeling like I don't want to let go of her character anymore. Maybe I'm going to sound weird but I feel that way.The graphics are truly spectacular, each season gets better and more immersive, the direction is monstrous in the good sense of the word, they have created characters with real thoughts and features.We certainly have to thank Telltale for that, and not Skybound. Although they helped them in the making of the fourth season, and for that I am very grateful, as far as the future of clementine is concerned, today on June 10 2022, they are doing a bad job, releasing comics that throw **poop** on what Telltale has created, but this is not the place to talk about that, if you want to read my thoughts about it: Other than that there is little to say, a gem that must be played because it can change your life and move you like few things in the world, so much love to the friends of Telltale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's weird to review this collection with one piece as there are four seasons, but I'll do it anyway. To start, I love The Walking Dead. The show (minus seasons 7 and 8), the comics, and the games. It's a series about hope, love, and mercy all colliding with hate. It's a series about what is right and what is wrong. And they all end with cooperation and a commonality between all people overcoming what can only be described as the end of the world. That is powerful.These games fit perfectly with the comic universe. Season 1 expertly tells a tale of humanity struggling with new moral quandries. Season 2 pulls no punches when telling the story of jaded survivors who don't even stick their necks out for children anymore. Season 3 is a brotherly love story... or something. Season 4 is about the next generation that will eventually survive The Trials and build the new world back up. They're all incredibly interesting.I think each of the four seasons are great or at least really good. From best to worst, I would put Season 2 first, Season 1 second, Season 4 third, and Season 3 last. I won't comment on each of them as that would make this review much too long. All you have to know is that each of them have few flaws and, at worst, decent writing. Season 4 is the only game that holds up to modern gaming standards in regards to polish, but that doesn't mean that any of the other games have less value. Play this collection. Just finishing Season 4 left me heartsick and longing for the characters. It was the end of a beautiful saga that ended in such a perfect way. Sit back with a snack, listen to that bittersweet music, and have a great time. Seriously.9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead is a fantastic story-driven narrative game, with one of the primary selling points being that your choices matter, and they do, occasionally.Unfortunately, and due to understandable limitations (the near impossibility of writing dozens of vastly different stories dependant on choices), many of the player's choices are merely superficial, at least as far the the meta/macro story is concerned.Oftentimes a choice, that appears to be genuinely impactful, will lead to the same result regardless of your actions, with the only difference being slight variations in how the characters respond to your choice in that situation (alongside their overall view of you in some cases).Whilst this still certainly constitutes a game in which your choices "matter" in the sense that they impact, to varying degrees, the responses and interactions you have with those around you, there are very few meta story changes that the player can make.For example, where you are forced to decide who to save between two survivors, a choice that appears weighty and substantive in a meta sense, will actually have little impact in the long-run, with such characters generally going on the back burner (story wise) before being killed off by the plot within a few episodes (oftentimes sooner) regardless of who you chose to save. Given they could very well not exist in another's play-through. Once you look for these patterns your choices do begin to feel slightly shallow.That is not to say they bear no impact on the story, they do. It is just to say that such choices will almost never majorly contribute, in any form, to the narrative you follow, as you might expect when making them. At best they will affect - to a degree - the response you get from certain other characters, alongside changing a couple of interactions for a few episodes. You will still feel some real impacts based on your choices, particularly with how surrounding characters respond shortly following the events. It is, however, unfortunate that as time progresses - usually over the course of that episode alone - the choice means increasingly little and eventually fades into obscurity, constituting no major change in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with The Walking Dead. Though the five seasons vary in quality, they are overall great adventure games, albeit a bit light on actual gameplay at times. A short review of each season:- Season One: It's emotional and filled with tough decisions that really had me questioning what the moral thing to do was at times. The writing is great and the characters memorable; It's easy to see why this game was so popular when it released in 2012. Lee, Kenny, Omid and Christa, and of course Clementine: this season is filled with characters that feel so real. I haven't played that many pre-TWD Telltale games, but this one feels the most like a classic adventure game to me.- Season Two: A great followup to the first season. It's not as strong as the original, but excellent character writing makes this story memorable. They clash and disagree and it's not always clear who's right and who's wrong, which can lead to animosity among the group with Clementine (now protagonist) caught in the middle of it.- Michonne: Michonne is a fine character, but this season is otherwise unmemorable, especially since it's entirely self contained. There's not a lot of interesting decisions to be made here, and the gameplay shifts from some puzzle solving to almost none, with a lot of QTEs. There's very little "game" here and it relies on the narrative being interesting to stay engaging... which it sort of does. I'd probably like this season more if I was more familiar with the character (I have not seen the show or read the comics).- A New Frontier (Season 3): This suffers from the same gameplay issues I had with Michonne: there's not a lot of game here. The story also switches focus from Clementine to new protagonist Javi and his family. I like Javi, but I wasn't a fan of the other characters who seemed to change their relationships with each other at random. It felt very inconsistent, and though Clementine is present in the story (and I like seeing her from an outsider's perspective) this season feels inconsequential to her overall journey: you could reasonably skip from S2 to S4 with not much confusion.- The Final Season: This might be my favorite season: most seasons I played one episode per day, but this season I played all four in two days, I found it that engaging. This season's cast is almost as good as the original's, and the gameplay is better than ever. Clementine's relationship with AJ is a great parallel of Lee's relationship with Clem in season one, and he asks her a lot of difficult questions that had myself wondering how my morality would change if I lived in the zombie apocalypse. Have a box of tissues ready for the ending.If I had to rank them: The Final Season > Season One > Season Two > Michonne > A New Frontier.Some overall thoughts on the series as a whole: I liked the performances a lot. Telltale games can be kind of stiff at times and the voice acting helps to alleviate this problem. I also love the black comic art style from The Final Season that they applied to the earlier seasons, it really makes those games look a lot more visually interesting. I like the decision making a lot and there were more than a few times when I had to pause and really think about what choice I wanted to make. Seeing the decisions other players made at the end of each chapter is a nice touch. What an adventure these games were: would definitely recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series : By Triple F“The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series” is an extensive collection that brings together all four seasons of Telltale’s acclaimed episodic game series, plus the Michonne miniseries and various bonus features. Released as a tribute to the iconic saga, it allows both new players and longtime fans to experience the entirety of Clementine’s journey in one cohesive package. With updated visuals, enhanced mechanics, and a wealth of behind-the-scenes content, this collection presents “The Walking Dead” series in its most polished form, allowing the emotional story, tough decisions, and unforgettable characters to shine like never before.A standout feature of “The Telltale Definitive Series” is its graphical overhaul, known as the “Graphic Black” art style, which enhances the series’ distinctive, comic-book-inspired visuals. This style, modeled after the original “Walking Dead” graphic novels, adds bolder outlines, richer shadows, and a sharper contrast, giving the game a more dramatic and stylized appearance. Though not a complete reimagining, this visual update adds a new level of depth and consistency across all four seasons, creating a unified look that makes the series feel more cohesive. The art style is particularly effective in amplifying the tension and emotional weight in key moments, lending a heightened intensity to scenes that fans know well.Mechanically, “The Telltale Definitive Series” smooths out some of the clunkiness found in earlier seasons. The first two seasons, in particular, benefit from improvements to character movement and interaction responsiveness, making them feel less dated and more fluid to play. Small tweaks like faster loading times and refined control schemes help modernize the overall experience without sacrificing the core design of the original games. Though it’s not a complete rework, these enhancements make gameplay smoother and more accessible, bridging the gap between early Telltale mechanics and the improvements introduced in later seasons.The storytelling across the series remains as powerful as ever. Following Clementine’s transformation from a vulnerable child into a strong, resilient leader, “The Walking Dead” delivers a narrative rich with tough choices, complex relationships, and moments of heart-wrenching loss. Each season explores different facets of survival in a post-apocalyptic world, from the bonds of found family to the trauma and responsibility of raising a child in hostile circumstances. The series is deeply character-driven, and the Definitive Edition respects this legacy by preserving every critical choice and consequence, allowing players to shape their unique path through the narrative while confronting the harsh moral ambiguities of the world.“The Telltale Definitive Series” also includes the Michonne miniseries, a side story that focuses on the iconic character from the “Walking Dead” comics. While Michonne’s story is not directly tied to Clementine’s, it adds depth to the universe, highlighting how survivors from different backgrounds cope with loss and trauma. The Michonne episodes bring a fresh perspective and offer players an opportunity to explore new themes while taking a break from Clementine’s journey. This miniseries isn’t the main draw, but it adds value to the collection, especially for fans of the broader “Walking Dead” universe.One of the most enjoyable aspects for longtime fans is the series' trove of bonus content, which includes developer commentary, concept art, and a “making-of” documentary. The commentary provides valuable insights into Telltale’s creative process, shedding light on the challenges and decisions that went into crafting such a narratively complex series. Concept art showcases the evolution of characters and environments, and it’s fascinating to see how Clementine’s design changed from season to season. These extras make the Definitive Edition feel like both a game and a commemorative piece, celebrating the impact of “The Walking Dead” on interactive storytelling.In the end, “The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series” serves as a fitting tribute to one of gaming’s most beloved stories. It allows fans to relive or experience for the first time, the emotional rollercoaster of Clementine’s journey in its most refined form. Though it may not add new story content, the improvements in visual fidelity, mechanical polish, and supplementary material make this collection a worthy investment for any fan of the series or narrative-driven games. This Definitive Edition preserves the essence of Telltale’s vision while enhancing it for a new generation, offering an unforgettable experience that honors Clementine, her story, and the fans who grew alongside her.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying this is not a game. It's more like an interactive movie or show. When it comes to gameplay, it's nothing more than an interactive point and click adventure. So as a game, it's not very fun. However, as an interactive story, it's amazing. The story is pure gold. At least seasons 1 and 4 are. The first season is iconic and the most famous out of all them for obvious reasons. The second season feels more like filler. as for the Michonne season, I feel like this season got a lot of hate because people didn't realize that it's canon to the comics and the comics are very different from the show. So just don't expect show version of Michonne, and if you're unfamiliar with the comics, it might be slightly jarring and it can be skipped if you're just interested in Clementine's story. Season 3 takes us on a slight detour from Clementine. Personally, I hated the UI of season 3 and it's performance was terrible, even at low settings. For perspective, season 4 ran perfectly on high settings. On top of that, the season is kind of annoying in the sense you want to see what's up with Clementine but now you're playing as this new protagonist with his family. It felt like a commercial break from the real story and I just wanted to get through it and get back to real story. The season wasn't all bad though, at the last episode, you see that golden writing finally take place. If only they did that for the entire season. The 4th season is amazing. Filled with the same great writing as the first season. Absolutley amazing transitions, and this one felt the most like a game rather than an interactive story. Both season 1 and season 4 brought me to tears and I am confident it will do the same for you.

You will always remember the first time you played it - what you were thinking and how it felt. It's special in that way. However, The Walking Dead is not without its faults. Not everything works here. For the MOST part, the choices in this choice-based game don't matter (with a few major exceptions). The gameplay and animations can feel a little clunky. Not all the dialogue is great. But where this games shines, oh boy does it shine.What keeps you engaged is the narrative and characters. Seasons 1, 2, and 4 are FANTASTIC. There's some really great writing on display. Watching Clementine grow up and become stronger and smarter is one of the most gripping, rewarding, and heartfelt character arcs in all of gaming. When this game ends, and the realization sets in that it's over, and you can never play it for the first time again, that's when it hits you. The Walking Dead is something special.Absolutely recommend, 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so The Walking Dead game by Telltale Games is like a wild ride through a post-apocalyptic soap opera. The story? Gripping. Characters? You'll feel more attached to them than your morning coffee. The graphics? They make the apocalypse look kinda pretty.What's cool is that your choices actually matter. Like, you're not just watching; you're in the driver's seat. Every decision adds up and shapes the story. It's like being the director of your own survival drama. The game's got this way of making you feel responsible for the crazy outcomes, and that's what hooks you in for more.In a nutshell, The Walking Dead game is not just a game; it's an emotional rollercoaster set in a zombie-filled world. If you're into making tough choices, bonding with characters, and navigating through a post-apocalyptic adventure, this game is your jam. Get ready for a wild ride! 🧟‍♂️🎮
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of The Walking dead, then you will love this. If you're a fan of story-driven games, then you will love this. If you're a fan of well-written characters, then you will love this. And if it so happens that you're a fan of all three of the things that I just listed, then this game might just become one of your favorite games of all time. It's that good and I couldn't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Walking Dead: The Telltale Definitive Series

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to play an already great series, but visual upgrades to earlier seasons are minimal, so if you already own all of most of the earlier seasons your mileage may vary on if this is worth buying again. Though there are hours of behind-the-scenes/documentary style material too that may make it worth buying for some returning players, plus the convenience of having them all in one install.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember buying season 1 when it first came out and played for like 10 mins and was like what the hell is this. name: Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel
detailed_description: Finally, the 'Yu-Gi-Oh!' digital card game you've been waiting for! The definitive edition of the competitive card game that has been evolving for over 25 years! Duel at the highest level against Duelists from all over the world. Get ready: it's time to Duel! ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ [About 'Yu-Gi-Oh! MASTER DUEL'] Now you can play the 'Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG,' digitally, anywhere. Fast-paced Duels with stunning HD graphics and a new, dynamic soundtrack! Get ready to challenge Duelists around the world! ◇Play Duels at Any Level! The full Yu-Gi-Oh! experience is available for anyone at any Skill Level. Don't worry if you're a new player or if you haven't Dueled in a while, the in-game tutorials will teach you the basics on how to play the Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME. You'll be given a Deck when you finish to help you start your journey! Collect new cards as you progress through the game to power up your Decks! ◇Rotating Tournament Formats Mix it up and put your Dueling skills to the test! A wide variety of events and tournaments will be available for players. Build and Duel with different Decks utilizing 10,000+ unique cards and special rules unique to Tournaments! Choose the tournament YOU want to Duel in and aim for that number one spot! ◇Uncover the Stories Behind the Cards The Solo Mode guides you through storylines of the themes from the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG. Hone your Dueling skills by completing the stories. Recommended for beginners, returning players, and those of you who are interested in learning more about the lore of the world of the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG. ◇Features Link with the mobile app 'Yu-Gi-Oh! Neuron.' View Decklists from Duelists worldwide and improve your own Deck! Try the sample draw feature to simulate what cards you could get in your first hand! [About 'Yu-Gi-Oh!'] 'Yu-Gi-Oh!' is a popular manga created by Kazuki Takahashi that was serialized in SHUEISHA Inc.'s 'WEEKLY SHONEN JUMP' since 1996. Konami Digital Entertainment Co., Ltd. provides a Trading Card Game (TCG) and console games, based on 'Yu-Gi-Oh!' created from the original manga, that has been enjoyed around the world. [Recommended for the following players] TCG players Yu-Gi-Oh! DUEL LINKS players Players who enjoy competitive gameplay ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ This game contains in-game purchases of virtual currencies used for gaining in-game items at random.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking to play yu-gi-oh! you could really enjoy yourself with this game, i havent played yu-gi-oh since GX and I felt the new summons were convoluted, so my little brain could not handle it and dropped it off. But i saw that this one was starting and i wanted to play card games because i wasn't playing any.The game right now is very F2P friendly, but i fear that this will change when the first season pass expires, still it helps to build archetypes by using "Secret Packs" where you can get many many good cards from both your archetype and from the complete pool so you can unlock more archetypes.the core mechanics are that of the same old yu-gi-oh we all grew to love, but still it needs polishment in some QoL improvements and UI.if you are planning to join i have some good tips for you to use:-first, if you are not planning to use Blue-eyes, select synchro because they have "mystical space typhoon" which is a really nice card (i would abbreviate it but i dont know if there are new players)-then, do the solo missions, they will help you and reward you with cards and crystals both. the first two missions give you monster reborn and raigeki which are almost a staple in all decks.-buy the duel pass, its very long, you can buy it with crystals and it will help you with crafting points for cards (I didn't mention, this Yugioh has a card crafting system, and i think it is really nice, if you want an Ultra Rare, you will need ultra rare crafting points, and you can get those by disenchanting UR cards that you dont need, and all cards cost 30 points of its rarity)-If you want, you can buy the three bonus packs as well, as those three cards are  some of the best cards in the game and they come with packs for the price of 250 less, its a lot of value.-the secret packs are as i said before packs which hold cards that belong to its specific archetype. they are divided by 4 cards from the complete pool and 4 from the archetype. the secret packs are unlocked by: -1. Obtaining a Super Rare/Ultra Rare card that belongs to that archetype. -2. CRAFTING a Super Rare/Ultra Rare card that belongs to that archetype. this means that if you know what archetype you are going to build and which ones are the featured cards you could craft a highlighted card and unlock that secret pack (and give you 1 free pull!)these secret packs will be available for 24 hours, but once they dissapear you can unlock them again. So Dont worry if you dont have any gems, just take note of which card was highlighted and craft it when you are ready to buy some cards!-ALWAYS buy in packs of 10. ALWAYS. NO EXCEPTIONS. -if you are coming back, dont be afraid of new summons, the only finnicky ones are pendulums. I'm on gold tier 3 and only have seen 1 pendulum deck which i finished quite easily.Truth be told i played hearthstone before, because it was nice and fast paced, i could do quick thinking and have a good time. But then Priest with 10 cleaning cards and then it became "fighting against a wall the game" so i stopped playing, it is not that here is the same thing, but here everybody has the same capabilities of building some impressive monsters. i didnt knew anything about Synchros/XYZ/Links until last week and im having a blast, yeah, turns are longer, but the fact that you know they are long makes it better at least for me.overall i have high hopes for the game, but i fear that it will become quite aggresive when it comes to pulling cards in the future, but right now is really generous, so if you want to join, the time is now.♥♥♥♥ PENDULUMS AND ♥♥♥♥ PRIEST. and have a nice day

_childDocuments_.review: So I would recommend this game very conditionally, that being that this is a pretty good YuGiOh sim and feels very nice to play as well as having a way lower barrier to entry then buying and playing the physical game. However, this game is not very good at teaching people who have never experienced high level YuGiOh how to get into it. It teaches you the basics and gives the freedom to mess around with some fun decks in 'Solo Mode' but what you learn their isn't very synonymous with you higher ranked games of you will play in this game. If you don't want to play competitively, you don't need read further its good and free download it, if not here are some surface level tips that may help with playing the game:1. Some of the most important cards in the game are ones that let you do things during both players turns without letting your opponent know that you might have them (these are commonly referred to as handtraps) and the most important ones as of posting are 3x copies of Ash Blossom and the Joyous Spring and 3x copies of Maxx "C" these are almost necessary to compete at higher levels but buying or crafting these and learning about them are gonna be very important.2. Some of the best decks (or just the better ones) have ways to play around or past such 'handtraps' and if your deck can't do that you may want to consider upgrading or switching out your deck after considering its strength.3. If a friend or someone who is experienced in this game recommend this game to you play with each other as often as possible and ask questions, as I said before this game's tutorial is very surface level and doesn't really explain the intricacies of this game.4. The internet is your partner here, if you don't have any friends the Steam Guides section or typing "X deck yugioh master duel" are some of the best ways to figure out to play your favorite decks in this game also when you download the game and look in the top right of the menu, there's a watch Duels live button which is also pretty good for seeing how decks work in the wild.Thanks for reading and if your trying to get into this game, good luck and I hope you keep dueling!
