_childDocuments_.review: This is a "would not recommend" but at the same time I want to start out by saying that the game is mostly good.  The game functions wells, bugs are minimal and many have been fixed quickly with notifications ingame of ongoing bugs, fixed bugs, etc.  In terms of raw basic function the game is actually very good.  If all you are looking for is to make ONE(1) deck and play that with your friends and maybe some rank grind with it.  Its honestly pretty good, you will get enough gems in the first week for you to craft out ONE(1) very good deck even top tier meta stuff if you care.  If you are looking at more budget decks you might even be able to get 2-3 made.  Where do the problems start and why would I not recommend this?  The economy is atrocious, past the first week gems go from lavished on you for anything you do to maybe getting 100 a day or so if you really grind and that will only get worse as the game continues.  I'm already seeing multiple days were I will not get 100 gems in that day.  For reference a single pack is 100 gems and mostly you should be opening 10packs at 1000 gems meaning prepare for a week or two of grinding after the first week for a single 10pack realistically probably quiet more as time goes on.  The prices on gems to buy are also terrible, a "special deal" of $12 USD is 1500 gems, that is one and a half pulls for $12 with the special offer (which is limited to 3 btw).  Normally without that sale is $24 USD for 1400 gems.  This is absolutely insanely high priced and you are looking at having to drop hundreds of dollars worth of gems to acquire a new deck in the future.  I'm pretty cool with spending money on F2P games, and I've played many before and put money into them more than $60 like I would for an actual normal game price.  Yet I'm almost morally opposed to the prices in this game to the point I haven't spent anything and probably will not spend anything without some real changes taking place here.  The game has card crafting/deconstruction, HOORAY!  Though cards are hard limited to rarity and SR and UR tokens are hard to come by and you have more N and R tokens than you could ever realistically spend with no way to upgrade your N or R tokens this means you are often breaking down 3 UR's for a single UR craft, which translates to around 15packs or so per UR craft with "good luck" some 10pulls literally give you ZERO UR's and instead say "your next 10pull will have a UR, sorry lol".  Every archtype/deck has some UR's in it so even once you full craft UR staples like Ash Blossom, Infinite Imperm, and similar you'll still need the UR's for your archtype.  So the crafting is nice compared to something like say MTGA, but saying something is better than MTGA's economy doesn't mean much.What truly prompted me to write this review was the season reset the first of which just happened today/last night.  Their setup for the season rewards are so incredibly stupid and greedy.  At season reset you decay one rank tier (for instance from Plat to Gold) this makes sense and is pretty normal so whats the problem?  Well you only get rewarded next season for obtaining new ranks, this means is actually better for you as a player to surrender spam before the season ends to decay as far as you possibly can this will give you more ranks to climb and as a result more gems/rewards.  They have literally created a rank structure where the most optimal/rewarded course of play is to climb to Plat2 (not Plat1 once you get there you are stuck) then decay down to Gold so you become Silver when the season resets this gives you 400 more gems compared to to climbing to Plat1 and staying there.  There are also no rewards for getting to Plat1 (besides the normal 100gems for rank up), there is no rewards at the end of the season, there is nothing.  As it stands the ranked queue and its ladder is the only game mode in the game.  You can quickly push through the limited solo mode offerings which besides the 200gems for a full story completion offers nothing of real value.  Custom tournaments, friend duels, etc?  None of that rewards anything ingame and none of that contributes to your missions/dailies.  Yeah yeah sit down shutup and drop a few hundred bucks for each new deck you want as the banlist changes, new sets come out, etc. Its a free game they need money/payment I get it but at the same time when steam asks me if I can "recommend" this game to someone the answer as it stands right now today is a hard no.  I wouldn't feel good recommending this to my nephews/family and as a result I wouldn't recommend it to other people either.  If they really wanted a yugioh game I'd point them to Legacy of the Duelist which is just a single game purchase and you just grind out whatever deck you want and while they give up the large player base this game currently has I wouldn't be recommending them a cash vampire and to me thats what matters.

_childDocuments_.review: Master Duel is the worst form of Yugioh in the entire world! Here is why, from my perspective as a Master ranked player that has been dueling since this game first launched (on playstation and mobile)CONS: 1 - 100% Pay2Win - The whole game is based around premium currency called Gems, which are used for everything. The more money people spend on gems, the more card packs they can open, the more cards they can dismantle, and then the more they can craft the exact cards they need. People that don't spend on packs are always at a severe disadvantage game-play wise and wont be able to afford cosmetics either.2 - Crafting - The crafting system heavily forces extreme amounts of money to be spent to collect enough unwanted Ultra Rare cards to dismantle them for CP (crafting points). You get only 10 CP for dismantling a card, but need 30 CP to make a new one. And the CP system is further ruined by having separate CP for each tier of card, so you end up with infinite Normal and Rare CP but cannot use it nor convert it for Super Rare or Ultra Rare CP. Worse yet, any free, promo, event, or legacy pack cards cannot ever be dismantled for CP, even if you end up with 30 copies of the same Ultra Rare.3 - Card Packs and Gem Cost Scam - Unlike real life, card packs in Master Duel have zero guarantee of getting a single Ultra Rare. You can buy 10 packs at once, for 1000 gems ($20) and only get a single Super Rare. Then you need to spend another 1000 gems or $20 to do another 10 pull, to only get 1 single Ultra Rare guaranteed as a promo bonus, but the packs themselves still can (and often will) not give any Ultra Rares. That means you need to spend $40 to 100% get a single UR. And since one UR is only 10 CP and you need 30 CP to make a card, it costs $120 to guarantee generate any UR you want, provided the rigged packs fail to provide any extra URs to dismantle. Since meta decks have an average of 20 to 30 UR cards, you will need to spend thousands or tens of thousands to make any deck you want, without grinding for months or getting extremely "lucky". 4 - Rigged Game - Since this game is best of one format, it means whoever wins coin flip and goes first auto-wins 99% of the time. A coin flip in real life has a 50% chance to be heads or tails, and the law of large numbers would show the more flips, the closer the ratio of 50/50 it becomes. But in Master Duel, you only have a 5% chance to get heads and go first, based on the thousands of games I've played on PS5 and mobile, and the few hundred on PC. To make matters worse, the game forcibly rigs the coin flip whenever you win too much and are about to rank up, and matches you with an opponent that goes first and wins before you even get a turn. Some decks can reliably kill you turn 1 (first turn kill/FTK), or skip your turn altogether, with the meta decks able to set up unbreakable boards that banish all your cards, prevent you from summoning, using any effects or cards, or interacting in any way. 5 - Worst Banlist - The banlist of Master Duel does not follow the official TCG banlist, allowing TCG banned cards such as Maxx C and Kashtira Ariseheart to be at 3. It does not follow the OCG banlist either allowing Kashtira Fenrir and Unicorn at 3 despite banning them in real life. Master Duel's banlist follows no logic or reasoning, and is not decided by the community nor a panel of experts, rather it is made by the whims of whichever Konami intern decides to mess with the game that month. You would think in a pay2win game with cards you craft with real money, there would be more order to the banlisting process, but sadly not. Perhaps it is intentionally, to force even more money to be spent to compete with the new flavor of the month meta deck, as the deck you invested in is no longer playable.6 - No Trading - Yugioh is a "trading" card game, yet Master Duel has no trading at all. You are at the mercy of rigged packs and a p2w crafting system7 - Unreliable Servers - 40% of matches will fail to connect, lose connection mid match, or simply error crash out resulting in your automatic loss. There is no mulligan and no way to appeal.8 - Hackers/Cheaters - Some PC players run programs that allow them to see all cards opponent has in deck and hand, rig draws, or outright put cards into their hands to perfectly counter your entire deck. If all else fails, they will force you to disconnect so its counted as your loss and their win, The in-game report feature is fake and does nothing to get any cheaters banned.9 - Lacks Basic Social Features - No text or voice chat in game, which is bad, but no emoticons or stickers is unacceptable. No way to interact with the people you play with in game, so you cant make any friends or groups. You will need a third party method instead.10 - Only Ranked Mode - There is no Draft mode, no Edison or Goat format modes, no story career mode, and nothing except some other "practice" modes such as unranked, team battle, and private duels but none of those modes count towards challenge/gem progress at all. There is a solo mode with random decks and some lore and some junk rewards, but its not a real or continuous story or adventure, There are zero yugioh characters that make an appearance in this game, Not even Yugi himself. Occasionally there are limited time events or "festivals" such as "Link Monsters Only" Or "Synchro Monsters Only" but they are ruined by floodgate cards that the interns forgot to ban for the event. Such as "No Fusion Summoning" continuous effect card during the "Fusion Monsters Only" festival. Braindead.PROS 1 - Appearance - The UI is pretty good despite being a cheap Unity game made for cell phones. Once you learn the nuances, its hard to use any other yugioh UI, as this game is perfectly precise with timings and phases and chaining (and chainblocking). Often times the game will do things or prevent them, that you wont ever see in real life duels and tournaments because of agreements/judges. Since Master Duel has no judges nor appeals, all actions are final, even when the game itself is wrong and takes the interns weeks to patch. However, Master Duel is superior to real life duels in that both players are playing by the exact same rules and nobody can sneak in cheats just because opponent looked away for a second. (This is assuming both players are not running any 3rd party cheat programs), And because of how precise timing and system checks are in a duel, it allows you to know when opponent has a specific handtrap, such as flashing to opponent after 5 summons means Nibiru and flashing to opponent when searching a card means Ash Blossom. If you're smart, you can turn your effects to OFF so you can hide your handtraps and save them for the biggest hits. 2 - Sound - The sound effects and the music go hard and sound good, my only complaint is lack of music variety and no ability to change what plays. For a game that sells you pixelated .jpegs of deckboxes, card backs, home screens, duel fields, and avatars for 10 or 20 real life dollars, I'm actually shocked they don't sell background music too. Missed opportunity. 3 - Crossplatform  - Once you go through the painstaking process of making a Konami ID, yugioh account, and linking your PC, Playstation, and phone, you can seamlessly play on any of them. Your account and gems will be there, saved to the Master Duel server. The downside is when the Master Duel server is dead or under maintenance, you cant even log in nor play offline, thus your thousand dollar collection of untradeable digital NFT cards will not be accessible.TLDR:Game is big pay2win, rigged, bad banlist, bad servers, no anticheat, no trading, no social, and lack of modes other than ranked. Not worth the time or money, just play real life yugioh with a deck you can always access offline, or sell/trade if you get bored with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely who actually enjoys playing the newest meta deck? All of the cards read something like "when you normal or special summon this card, take a **archetype name** card and add it to your hand" allowing you to infinitely draw cards. Of course the "limitation" on these cards is that you can then only special summon **archetype name** for the rest of the turn, because god forbid you play anything outside of the archetype. You may as well press a button and watch as your deck empties itself and you get the same board every single game, at least then you save both players time.I started enjoying the game when I started auto conceding against meta archetypes like Labyrinth or Snake Eyes. Now I at least find people who play their own decks, and it allows me to play my own as well.

_childDocuments_.review: What can i say about this game, Its Beautiful. I had no knowledge of how to play the game of Duel Monsters. i love the cards and collecting them is really enjoyable. At the time of getting into Yu-Gi-Oh! games, Master Duel wasn't even out. I was playing Duel Links with Co Workers who played the game and was really enjoying it. In a VC my friends and i stumbled about the new game Master Duel, it only released like three days prior or something like that and we we're excited to duel each other so we decided to download it and give it a try.now i can say with confidence, gripping my 43 card deck (which used to be 58) its time.... to duel.Right away its super simple to understand, it starts with simple summoning tutorials, how to use spells and traps and then it introduces Gates, Which is the solo mode of the game. The game has a wonderful way of showing you Booster Packs relevant to what archetype you want to build in game!The Scrapping mechanic of cards is fantastic when you have extra cards you dont need in any decks but the materials needed to build specific cards can be a tedious grind at times when you are short on cards. really im just stingy when it comes to scrapping. There is a grind to the game, Winning matches gives gems and there and many challenges that give you gems but i warn. DO NOT SPEND GEMS UNTIL YOU UNDERSTAND HOW TO USE THEM TO YOUR ADVANTAGE.Since My group and i started so close to launch it feels like we spent thousands of gems on pointless packs in hopes of getting a key for a pack were looking for. Not realizing that you can just craft a SR or UR and get that cards key for that correlated pack.There is a Season pass you can buy with gems that help you get materials for crafting, icons, tokens and gems, it is worth it for the materials but i with there was a little more "hype" in the pass.Online duels can drop out and everyone plays the best decks they can, that being said. Expect to lose against certain decks until you can counter the deck. from what ive seen, there is not one deck that dominates the rest. so dont expect to win them all, since everyone is playing with the best cards they can play with, it can be a challenge. The Connection is annoying, there is no regional location filters so you play against random people around the world and sometimes the connection is smooth. sometimes its super bad and it ends the match. At the moment in the game there is not severe penalty for losing and non for a disconnection, it counts as a win. so i wont complain too bad. But when you spend a while chaining cards to get disconnected. it sucks. Overall 9.5/10 Game Good

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game from a technical perspective. The developers deserved to be commended for bringing such a comprehensive Yu-Gi-Oh experience to a wide audience for the first time. (No, Duel Links does not count. The rules are fundamentally different due to the limited field size.)Unfortunately the game is marred by the fact that Konami has never been particularly great at taking care of their game. Master Duel has to live with years of particularly lackluster banlists and increasing power creep that it has been saddled with from the paper game. It leaves the online format dominated by strictly necessary hand traps, and turn-one lock out combos. The unfortunate state of the game's balance aside, Master Duel also suffers from currently limited competitive offerings. Clearly the infrastructure is being built, but at the moment the (admittedly stellar) duel room feature can accomodate community tournaments with ease. But as of this writing, there are no official tournaments, or prize support, which is essential for any serious competitive card game.The starting funds you receive are generous, but the ranked rewards per season are pretty terrible, and these are by far the largest source of gems in the game over the long term. The game's economy is "balanced" around throwing you an extensive amount of currency at the start of the game. It is easy to acquire a single meta deck rather easily and achieve a high rank if you know what you're doing.But the strengths and much of the fun of Yu-Gi-Oh can be found in decks that are perhaps less well known, and after you acquire your first deck, perhaps afteryour second, the gem acquisition rate slows to a crawl. This isn't necessarily a problem, but long time fans of the game will know that the meta can shift arbitrarily thanks to Konami's decision making, from rules changes (such as the new pendulum rules, or the infamous release of link monsters), to heavy bans. There is no stated policy about ban refunds anywhere, although since it seems Konami is planning on allowing for some form of banlist customization in the future, perhaps this won't be as necessary as it might be in other games.Still, the economy is meant to be deceptive and draw you in, tricking you into thinking you're getting more than you are. Players who do well are punished, while players who are not as experienced are at a disadvantage since they will almost invariably waste limited resources on decks that might be bad and lose frequently, encouraging them to spend. For instance, if you hit Plat 1 in the first season, you start at Gold 5. You do NOT get rewards for skipped ranks, and the reward for going from Rookie to Bronze is three times higher than ranking up in Plat, even though Plat takes more games and is much harder. I myself managed to hit Plat 1, and there was no further incentive to play. No leaderboard, nothing beyond an arbitrary point where the game goes 'alright you ran on the hamster wheel enough'. However, people enjoy competition. And when Konami inevitably starts banning things on Master Duel, as well as adding new (and power-creeped) archetypes, people will be tempted to spend great sums of money to keep up with the meta. No one is saying that Konami isn't allowed to make money, obviously. But their current business arrangement in this game is anti-competitive and anti-consumer. I enjoy Yu-Gi-Oh immensely, but changes need to be made.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another Yugioh gacha style game meant to make money and piss off the few remaining fans (which I used to be). Balance is nonexistent, most duels in gold ranked and higher are 5 minutes of the same combos from the same 3-6 decks and then they surrender/kill you in the following turn after negating your plays/destroy your board, the actual TCG is "balanced" around having side decks in competitive. Grinding is next to impossible (War Thunder levels of grinding), the strategy that Yugitubers and tryhards used was to use multiple accounts to use the free gems for making various decks.Issues:Massive turn timers - it's set at 480 seconds, except that gets delayed whenever the other player has a potential response, and that's a resetting timer set at 210 seconds, so it's _entirely_ possible to sit there for literally 5 minutes waiting for them to finish their combo, and if you want to win, you have to wait for a particular piece of their combo to activate a handtrap. Duel Links still has its ridiculously long 180 second turn timer 5 years after it came out, it should've been capped at 60 seconds within 1 month of release, and they never changed it.Typical Gacha mechanics - considering that COD Warzone makes $53 million a day, I'd guess that Master Duel is pulling in at least $1 million USD a day. Numerous antimeta cards are either Super Rare or Ultra Rare, which as any follower of the TCG's gambling and short print days knows, are exponentially harder to get and usually 4-20x as expensive IRL.Terrible banlist - It's sad when Duel Links' sameness with the same 4 decks being meta literally for years is an actual improvement over Master Duel, as at least those duels take maybe 4 minutes to play through 6 turns. Banlist refused to actually hit Drytron, and now every deck in Gold/Platinum/Diamond is Heroes, Eldlitch, Tri-Brigade, Drytron, Dogmatika, Shaddoll, Albaz, Dragonmaid, Cyber Dragon, Pendulum, Dark Magician, Blue-Eyes, Gren Maju Gizmek Orochi and Numeron Gates. There are literally hundreds of archetypes, and maybe 1% of the cards are actively played.There's no unranked mode/only way to get rewards is to tryhard. Losses count for nothing other than duel pass creditthe duel pass system is WAY too long, 70-90 days for something that you can finish in 60 winsyou get absolutely nothing for a loss (which encourages surrenders and tryhard decks), there's no sidedecking/match play (best of 3)card acquisition is a frustrating mess, good luck getting anything from the legacy packs, which is where 4000 of the 11,000 cards are, the only way to grind them is by winning ranked duels (losses give nothing), and there's no dupe protection (you can get unlimited copies, despite only needing 3, max) or way to trade in extra cards from legacy packs/solo mode rewardsLimited time monthly events are actually _more_ tryhard than normal matchmaking (this was honestly impressive when the Synchro event rolled around with de fleur/junk speeder/shooting quasar decks showed up), fusion event turned into cyber stein/starving venom/shaddoll and then once Destiny Hero Phoenix Enforcer/Albaz showed up, hoo boy.No automatic combo/strategy/scripting system built into the game - you have to manually select the same cards over and over again to do the same plays that would be actually faster IRL to play. Even Duel Links has an option to let the game automatically put cards into random/centered zones so you don't have to do the extra click on EVERY summon/playing a card (for those not familiar with the game AND somehow reading this review, the meta decks will literally play 20+ different monsters a turn, along with 7-15 spells/traps, AND have to activate another 8-25 monster effects, which may or may not trigger more card prompts to move cards from one place to another). This scripting system already exists in some form, as there is an AI opponent that is somewhat intelligent when you play solo, and Master Duel was built on Duel Links' engine (many of the same bugs were present in both), but is not open to player usage. This will likely never be implemented, if I had to guess, because it would show that the meta decks are incredibly broken with actual data, as speeding up the game would likely make players care less about the game. This has already happened with IRL play, as only a very particular detail oriented, relatively rich and obsessive kind of player plays Yugioh seriously these days.Clunky UI/QoL issues all over the place - some cards have variable numbers of cards that they can activate on (send 0-2 cards to the graveyard, etc.), others go one card at a time, play magical mallet for ex. No option for "skip this turn for responses, then set it back to auto next turn", which has caused me to lose duels because I forget to turn it back on, and if you leave it on so you don't forget next turn, you waste time. In IRL, you can just say that you won't respond to any plays during their turn. No option to always go first/second if given the option. Animations are incredibly slow, you have to wait 4 seconds for summoning animations, playing a card takes 2 seconds, shuffling the hand takes a second, shuffling the deck takes a second, etc. Taking feedback from the community in any consistent or planned manner- there, as of May 20 2022, is NO customer service/feedback option for Master Duel on the USA Konami website. They actively refused to put up surveys in the actual game that had any sort of text box for explicitly writing to them for 3 months. They must've been yelled at/seen the internal metrics after the whole account creation meta after 2 months, because they increased the daily mission gem drop rate from 4 to 40 on each mission on average.Actually providing any credit to any of the original artists - Apparently they care enough about the cards to digitize 20+ year old artwork and cut out backgrounds/provide the original computerized raws for the game engine AND have some live2D style movement of certain cards, but good luck finding out who drew what.No punishment for slow play at all. No punishment for repeatedly being AFK and surrendering due to timeout (it took them 3 months to put out a patch that actually had a 30s timer, on release it was the 480 second turn timer).There's a whole dissertation on the actual Yugioh OCG/TCG that has nothing to do with Master Duel, but basically this is worse than playing chaos draft IRL at a local tournament, it's certainly worse than playing casually with your friends (even the tryhards!), and going to an actual IRL tournament would be more entertaining. Some highlights of the Yugioh IRL cardgame iceberg meme knowledge includes Pendulum creation+nerfing into the ground, Links changing summoning and the reversal, Firewall Dragon refusal to ban for 18 months, hatred of FTKs but loving OTKs, refusal to print cards that play from the deck, impossible to play a tier 1/2/3 all spell card deck, confusing card text everywhere, confusing rules (inherent summons vs card effect summons), rules lawyering in general, not enough hand traps/diversified antimeta, the new waifu cards, negates everywhere where there basically 3 before 2012, the existence of the banlist itself as a testament to failure of card design, failed retrains, failed archetypes in general, uselessness of normal cards, literal meme cards like Attack the Moon! and Ojama Pink. And I haven't even seen all of Yugioh GX, any of 5Ds, Zexal, Arc V, etc. and only watched like 40 eps of Rush Duel but I did watch all of Duel Monsters as a kid, but those plotlines/art/scripts are whack.2/10, fun for about 4 days/you get to make 1.5 meta decks using the free gems and that's it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good online TCG game, probably one of the best I have played. (Had no experience previously with Yu Gi Oh, only the anime)As a newbie to the franchise, you can  easily build a deck as you get a lot of gems (in game currency) by just playing, but needs to grind more to get them as you progress. You can get gems by completing the life time missions, daily quests as well as the initial tutorial missions and the later the "solo campaign". Spending money is totally optional, and I haven't felt the need of doing so, contrary to most other TCG games out there, as you can easily disenchant cards and craft new ones.The solo campaign acts as a nice tutorial to give you a more broad idea of which mechanics are there, introduces you to some deck archetypes as well as introduces you to some of the more "meta" decks, which you can play with and against, in several difficulties. PVP is also pretty nice. It can get a bit overwhelming if you just decide to jump straight into it with no previous experience, so it's kind of expected for you to lose. It can also be a bit frustrating if you are new since some decks you play against can take the whole 5 minute turn to set up and you just stay there counting sheep.Only downside of the game is regarding some uncommon connection issues that can happen. There should be some sort of activity timer to give you a victory in case of connection problems with you/your opponent to avoid having to stare at an empty board. Your Synchro or Utopia decks going to do anything to him? NO. The worst part about Ranked is, it is the ONLY mode you can play to gain progress on the Pass that they offer. The only thing you CAN do is watch as they brag about how much money they spent on this POS as they run you over like a truck driver in an isekai anime. The solo play is even worse, because at least with Duel Links, I can enjoy the little bit of story that they have. I feel like bathing in boiling water, walking out with seared nerves, then dipping myself in nitroglycerin before lighting the fuse would still be a more enjoyable experience, then getting rammed up the rectum by that one guy who spent $100 so that he can summon a singular card, which, for the low, low cost of only 2000 LP, can OBLITERATE YOUR FIELD. I didn't ask to get hit by a Raigeki when I'm trying to set up a Synchro Summon with my cute ol' Tuning Warrior. Why not lock the strength of the cards you can use based on Ranked? _childDocuments_.review: With 600+ hours in this game I simply can't recommend it. If you are a player returning to the Yugioh scene after a few years or if you were a fan of Yugioh growing up, then this game is simply not for you. Why? Because this game isn't Yugioh. At least not at heart. Master Duel destroys everything you ever like about dueling. With every update Master Duel ruins any chance of bringing balance to the game. This game has lost any sense of individuality, strategy, fairness, and most of all…funness. This game is not good for your emotional or mental health. Trust me.I have made four points on why I can't recommend this game. 1. Yugioh (IRL) is a trading card game. Which means to get the most powerful cards you have to beat the duelist who has those cards to obtain them, trade your cards for theirs, buy a pack, or buy the card from someone for a (fair price). There was an economy of some sorts. With Master Duel the most powerful cards are available to players from the very beginning in unlimited quantities in exchange for cheap in-game currency (gems/rarity points). Which means to compete with these powerful cards that everyone else is using, you of course have to use them too, meaning player’s choices of decks become bottle necked. So forget about making a “custom deck” of your favorite cards. I have seen countless players with decks made of the same cards and they play them in the EXACT same manner. The Branded, Runick, Tearlaments, Blue Eyes, Dark Magician, and Floowandereeze players are notorious for this. I can sit there and simply guess what they will play next.2. The Master Duel in-game prompts are confusing. Hitting Yes or No on a prompt incorrectly could mean shooting yourself in the foot and causing you to lose the match because you aren’t sure of the result of your decision. Will my card effect work before theirs or theirs before mine? I've lost so many duels because of this. Sometimes I get multiple prompts to use one of my effects and other times I don’t get the chance to use my effect at all and I get a message “Missed Activation Timing” when I clearly shouldn’t have. Effect timing in this game is broken beyond repair. Flip effects, quick effects, trigger effects, normal effects, and “system” effects, like tributing your opponent’s cards, added over the years have caused the effect economy to become a big mess.3. There is no way to fix this game at this point but if I had to make some suggestions to have ANY hope of fixing this game the creators would have to:a. Remove the Extra Deck completely and return it to the Side Deck like it used to be or simply limit the strength of monsters and their effect that can be summoned from the Extra Deck or make it very costly to summon them. b. Limit and severely restrict the cards that can be triggered from a player’s hand. Ban Maxx C and Ash Blossom. Two of the worst cards to ever be added to Yugioh. c. Remove negation effects from the game or make using negation effects costly to the user or make the negation effects activate under more specific rules.d. Special summons have to be fixed…somehow. There are too many cards that let you special summon too easily. I believe this was started to help younger players who couldn’t formulate intricate strategies to get around the limit of normal summoning, so they made it easier to special summon, just my opinion. e. Make more game modes in Master Duel for players to build and join custom matches. Like a custom duel mode with no extra deck or a game mode based on a particular “era” of Yugioh that includes cards from older generations but not from newer ones. I would love that, because I love the older cards to build strategies around.4. This last point was the biggest betrayal I discovered in Master Duel by far. Yugioh the card game was once great because it had clear and concise rules (somewhat) and left everything to the player to formulate their own strategies. Now it's the cards that tell you how to play them. How else can you explain multiple random players using the same decks the same way? It's because each deck or archetype (i.e. Dragonmaids) was crafted by designers to behave and act in a specific way. Ultimately it is not you the duelist building and using your Branded deck it has already been decided for you. Any additions to these decks risks taking you from that precious 40 card minimum you are so proud of. I have seen players attempt to modify the archetype deck they are using and it's just like watering down your favorite drink. Gone are the days where you are presented with a limited list of random cards from which you have to build a deck from scratch. If you do this now your deck will easily be outclassed. Listen, decks are a reflection of the duelist’s ideas, playing experience, fears, hopeful outcomes, and even moral values. By introducing overpowered cards with curated effects, it disregards this concept and forces players into a bottleneck of cards to choose from and ignores the original founding spirit of the Yugioh trading card game. Such a choice could never have been made by card designers who actually loved the original card game.Thank you. God Bless.

_childDocuments_.review: Yu-Gi-Oh! Master duel itself is a pretty good card battler game that's available for free, giving ample tutorials and ability to get free cards and other items.  Unfortunately, this is extremely limited and will only get you through a limited amount of custom decks. As a player new to actually playing the card game, this game is extremely unpredictable because of the amount of cards and card effects that can manipulate the game in ways you've never expected.  This is a really cool idea but in practice it means that unless you're familiar with an extremely wide range of decks, it can be difficult to understand what is even happening at some times. This can be incredibly frustrating for a new player, especially when confronted with situations you can't even imagine building a deck against. This frustration is compounded because you can only complete quests inside of ranked duels most of the time. Friend duels don't count for anything and reward nothing, not even milestones in completion. Solo duels reward specific milestones, but similar in that most milestones are not triggered by solo. This leads you to having to participate in ranked.Ranked is huge waste of time. Making your way up to silver rewards you with significant amounts of rewards but lands you stuck in a hell hole where people summon monsters that are immune to traps/spells on their first turn, while you are stuck with whatever 1-3 decks you spent all your free currency on without any knowledge of the game.This brings up another issue. Currency for card packs is too expensive. This is a digital version of a card game with RNG. Sometimes you'll have to pull a card pack 10 times to get a card. This costs 1000 gems typically. Purchasing this much currency is in the realm of $12 USD. This is fairly obscene for digital cards that are largely going to be duplicates of cards you've already pulled from these packs, which aren't technically even yours as it's digitally tied to this game which hopefully will be supported for a large amount of time, but if it shut down tomorrow, it would be gone forever.This brings up two more points: Secret Card Packs & Card Dismantling/CreationCard Dismantling and creation is a generally good system that allows you to build cards you are missing without spending gems on packs, however due to card tiering SR and UR cards are typically cards you're missing from being able to build a deck. These cards stand for Super Rare and Ultra Rare. As their names suggest their % to pull is low. This means that you won't even be able to get material to build SR and UR cards after you build them. For some reason milestones only reward gems, and not SR or UR materials, making a large majority of your cards obtained to be fairly random.Speaking of RNG this means if you are looking for specific cards, you'll need to unlock secret card packs. This mechanic is actual ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You can unlock secret card packs in 2 ways:1. Open another card pack with a SR that appears in that other card pack2. Finish a solo mission goal for a specific deck engineThis by itself seems like it's not that bad since you'll be opening hundreds of packs. The real problem comes in that these packs are timed. For some god-forsaken reason if you build a deck from a card pack, and the card pack expired, you'll need to find that card pack through other card packs to attempt to modify your deck. You can get access card packs with less than 24 hours remaining if you don't understand the timer rollovers. WHY. WHY IS THIS TIMED.So now you're stuck with some mediocre decks and the card packs you need are not accessible. You don't have enough material after now researching what kind of cards people play in meta decks and why. What do you do? According to the loading screen, you should git gud and buy better cards.And after all this mental suffering to find all this out, i'm going to say unless you are already relatively serious Yu-Gi-Oh player or are incredibly familiar with the game, this is a digital card game i'd pass on.

_childDocuments_.review: So, in my opinion, there are two ways to look at Master Duel; one is from the eyes of someone who doesn't or hasn't played the Yu-Gi-Oh card game previously, and someone who has or does (like me). From the first perspective, it can be a fun, if grindy, digital card game with a pleasantly large player base and some nice customisation options, as well as a staggering library of cards and a surprisingly fun single-player mode. The stories for the card lore ended up being a lot more in-depth and intricate than I would've ever guessed. Loved it. From the second perspective, Master Duel is a fantastic tool for deck testing, even if the format isn't specifically OCG or TCG. The only downside is that it's not best of 3 matches, it's just 1 shots. So no sideboard, which is a huge deal. But there's something very satisfying about being able to see, in real-time, how effective your deck is. Watching it climb in ranked and seeing where each deck kinda stalls out, unable to climb any further. All in all, the game's fun and I enjoy it, I just wish they'd put in an alternate play mode for best-of-3 games.

_childDocuments_.review: Story time.Imagine you’re X-1 about to top your first regional. You’re so excited even coming off your last loss. You know you played well, and that’s just the name of the game.You hear over the loudspeaker,“Yugioh Players, pairings are being posted for round 9, our final round”You wade through the crowd of players to get up to the pairings list. One more win and you’re top 8! You could hardly contain your excitement. You find your last name. Table 4. Then, your eyes slide over to your opponent. Your heart sinks.“Kotton, Jesse”Okay, no need to panic. You’ve been up against better players than yourself before. There’s no need to be intimidated by a big name.You go and sit down at your table. It seems like the crowd starts to thin out as most people have taken their seats. You look around, no sign of your opponent. You check the clock and it hasn’t started yet.You see other players taking their decks out and getting ready to start their games. The chatter fills the room as you look around for anyone else walking up to the table. You see no one.“Players, welcome to round 9, you have 40 minutes. You may begin.”Still no Jesse.The clock ticks down, you get to the 38 minute mark as you see him stroll up swiftly, out of breath, and take a seat. He lays his mat out and effortlessly pulls his main and extra out in a single motion.You say “high roll” he says “sure.”You roll a 9 he gets a 4.“I’ll go first,” you say as you draw your starting hand. Not the best, but it’ll get the job done.“Normal Seyfert, link for Striker Dragon”Kotton says, “hold on, I have a play”He thinks for a moment, then lays a card from his hand into his S/T zone.“Shaddoll Fusion”“Wait, it’s my turn, you can’t do that,” you say.Kotton begins searching his deck. He lays out monsters one at a time, Beast, Wendi, Hedgehog, Trick Clown, Ariel. He even throws a Construct from his Extra into the graveyard.“Summon Winda. Declare chain links...” he begins counting up to 6.You repeat, “you can’t do that”He starts coughing into his sleeve. “Sorry”, he says squinting, as he begins looking through his deck to resolve backwards.“Wait, this whole play is illegal,” you raise your hand and shout “Judge!”A judge walks over. “What seems to be the problem?”“He activated Shaddoll Fusion on my turn. You can’t do that!”The judge thinks for a moment, he looks at Kotton and asks “who’s turn player?”Kotton says, “he is”.Judge says, “okay, is this the first time this has happened today?”He looks toward you and you nod. He thinks for a moment.“Alright, game loss.”Your mouth drops wide open as the judge signs your slip “GL” next to your name. You ask for an appeal.“Denied,” you hear from Kotton as he continues resolving his chain, slapping more cards around and tossing your Seyfert on the floor to banish it. Kotton begins sweating, dripping all over the table. Smells like fries. The judge walks away.You plead with the players nearby and ask them if they saw what he did but they shrug and plead ignorance. You begin crying softly as Jesse reveals Danger Nessie from his hand.He shuffles his hand into his deck, fans it out and gestures for you to choose.You reach in and pull out a single, greasy card. Yes! It’s the Nessie! You drop it in his graveyard as Kotton picks up his deck, searches through it and pulls out another Nessie. He summons it, draws a new hand, then says “draw 1”.You raise your hand again to call a judge, as you know Danger Nessie is limited to 1 and there’s no way anyone can rule that against you.“Judge!”Kotton begins coughing uncontrollably, disregarding his sleeve and beginning to cough all over the table. Other players barely seem to notice as they’re deep into their own game. He starts licking your playmat as you plead him to stop since you never even got to declare your Striker Dragon as Chain Link 1.He picks up your Extra Deck and takes a deep exhale on each individual card until he gets to the final card: Borrelsword.He licks his lips as he pulls Borrelsword out of its sleeve and starts deepthroating it, making sure that every inch is soaking wet.He drops the sopping mess that used to be Borresword into his board and says “attack, attack, effect target, attack for game?”You drop to your knees, sobbing, as you can barely squeeze out a single word through the tears. You look at Kotton with a begging look in your eye.“Why? Why are you doing this?”Kotton leans across the table as close to you as possible and whispers into your ear, his lips still coated in blue ink.“Worlds points, bro”

_childDocuments_.review: Meta decks in Yu-Gi-Oh are all about consistency and avoiding common hand-traps that brick your combo. The worst offenders of the highest ranking decks are usually not even marginally better than the second or third best decks right under them, they are almost always massively stronger. You will run into players running the top 3 decks of the game, usually determined by which deck counters which. For every other deck in the game, with some exceptions especially if you are either a very intelligent deckbuilder or netdeck user, stand practically no chance of surviving past turn 1. There are some decks that win on turn 1, so if you lost the coinflip, realize the combo you've seen before is happening and you don't have a hand-trap that answers it, you may as well concede because it is guaranteed you will lose.If you're an old fan thinking you can come in and play good old beatdown and your favorite Blue Eyes decks, you are severely out of date.In the modern game you either play the meta, around the meta, or very specifically tuned rogue decks that have enough consistency to take some games away from the people playing the meta. You're not even safe in unranked casual play, most "players" there are bots or people practicing their meta decks before ranked.Combine this with the rather pitiful income of gems to make new decks and the constant powercreep and you quickly find yourself overwhelmed if you decide to ever take a break from the game for a while. Good luck making more than a couple decks if you don't whale or play the game as your main hobby. If you're interested in playing I would HIGHLY recommend that you find a deck list online of whatever is the strongest on that particular patch, if you can make one of those top decks you will have a relatively decent time playing the ladder until the meta shifts. This will earn you decent rewards to get started on making whatever deck you next need to be a slave to.For anyone curious, I played an out of meta rogue Traptrix deck that evolved to answer whatever the current meta was. Again, it is possible to find things you enjoy that work, but some archetypes and some cards are practically useless. Even within my dedication to Traptrix, most of their iconic Hole cards are completely unplayable.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Kazuki Takahashi for all the great memories you gave me and the countless millions other people in their childhoods. I cherish the Saturdays I'd wake up to watch the next episode of the show along with collecting the toys/collectibles every chance I could. I remember bugging my mother endlessly when I was seven years old to get me the duel disk and she finally cave in one day lol. Back then, that was the greatest thing ever to happen to me. But as I got older, I quickly realized that was just one of the very many occurrences I'd be elated to have experienced in the franchise and especially the community. I am now in my mid 20's and the show/manga still touches me to my core in every way possible and I have met so many awesome people who have made my life better by their existence. I owe you my full interest in anime and card games to this day, none of this would've been possible without you and that I will give my utmost appreciation for. You have inspired me creatively and with your creativity to tell a riveting story about something as simple as duel monsters and cards. It feels like my hero just died and there's not enough words to do this justice. I wish the news was fake so much. I watched the scene of Atem leaving to rejoin his world in the final episode of the series several months ago once again not realizing how much more that scene would mean later on, each viewing on Youtube just hits harder and harder. Please Duelists, make sure this is just the beginning of this awesome universe and franchise. I know it's been over 20 years since its inception but I want Takahashi's legacy to live on. Keep playing the TCG/OCG, video games and watch/buy the merch and the shows/films no matter how old you get and where you are in life. Whatever you do, don't let his legacy die. Live your own life with the heart of the cards and believe in yourself much like the Pharaoh and Mr. Takahashi would want you to!I am devastated but very grateful it all started back in 1996 and in my life in 2002. It's been extremely difficult to hold myself together typing this. RIP, Kazuki Takahashi. I will greatly miss you.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I like playing real world Yugioh I have to leave a negative on this one. Don't get me wrong, this game is everything the electronic version of the game should be, technically. BUT there are a lot of things that are so wrong that I can't bring myself to liking this game :- Since this isn't a best of 3 duel the banlist should reflect that. But no, we leave highly problematic cards going rampant and killing the fun for everyone.- Each duel is decided almost exclusively by your opening hand and by your opponent's. If he goes first and you don't have 3 handtraps to stop him, you get rhongo'd or VFD and can't play. If you go first and he gets all the handtraps, turn 2 you're dead.- Every duel last 2-3 turns 95% of the time, there is no skill involved, just luck. If you don't get an out, just sit back, watch your opponent summon 90 monsters, bringing 10 negates and make you totally unable to play one card.- I played with the meta decks and got to Diamond 1 without too much hassle... so no I'm not complaining about trying to play with the deck I love and not winning... it's just impossible to love this game in it's current format. - Not having the latest cards is also bad, but it wouldn't matter much if the banlist was anywhere near a bit ok.- Going to Diamond 1 becomes a bit more fun because people play differents decks without worrying about being demoted, but at the same time it become the ScoopFest where everyone scoop as soon as things doesn't go their way, making daily mission and gems hard to get.This could be a really great and fun game, somewhere along the TCG and OCG, but right now it's a total mess where players rely on luck to win. If I'm going to play a game of luck, I'll go to the casino, not play Yugioh!I hope Konami sees all those reviews and start working something up!

_childDocuments_.review: With over 1000 hours of gameplay and experience in the TCG since 2016, I approached Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel with high hopes. While the game at a rogue/casual level is great and often results in duels lasting more than 3 turns (which are the best in my opinion), I can't recommend it to new players due to the meta reliance and lack of more casual and friendly modes/formats. Here’s a breakdown of my experience:Master Duel provides a refreshing opportunity to build and enjoy decks without spending real money. The game’s currency system allows dedicated players to amass resources and build competitive decks through consistent play and smart use of crafting points.For long-time fans, the game offers a deep pool of cards from various eras, enabling diverse deck-building possibilities. The strategic complexity remains intact, providing a rich, tactical experience reminiscent of the physical TCG.Card advantage has become the critical focal point of the game. With the abundance of powerful boss monsters and low-cost hand traps, the game now favors drawing and using these cards over careful resource management and strategic planning. The current format heavily relies on Maxx "C". These and other generic cards offer powerful one-card interruptions with little to no cost, often deciding games before they truly begin, undermining the skill and strategy that should define a duel.The meta is saturated with cards designed to trigger multiple actions in a single chain, making it difficult to execute your strategy even with a decent opening hand. Many duels feel the same due to the overuse of staple cards. This reduces the uniqueness of deck-building and makes the overall experience less engaging and more frustrating for new players.While the game touts itself as an opportunity to explore and enjoy various deck types, the dominance of generic cards and strategies makes it challenging to succeed with anything outside the current meta. This contradicts the game’s promise of a versatile and rewarding deck-building experience.Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel offers a blend of nostalgic enjoyment and strategic gameplay with the single mode but is marred by significant issues that impact the overall experience. The over-reliance on generic staples, lack of balance, and mainstream playstyle detract from the depth and enjoyment that long-time fans and newcomers alike seek.If Konami addresses these balance issues and fosters a more diverse and skill-based environment focusing on a setup phase, Master Duel has the potential to be a standout digital card game. Until then, it remains a mixed experience, appealing yet frustrating for dedicated players without a consistent flow state.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Yu-G-Oh! game released in a long time, in my honest opinion.However, do your research before playing. Watch a YouTube video or two about how the game is played nowadays. It's much, much faster than any old fan would think, and requires an entirely different set of knowledge and skills. The game isn't braindead or easy at all, it's simply different than the slow-paced Yu-Gi-Oh! of the past! Give it a shot. If you don't like the long, complex turns and tons of summons, then the game simply isn't for you. As for Master Duel itself, it's very generous with rewards for beginning players, and any player can make a competitive deck from the get-go with a couple hours of play. After that, gem acquisition isn't bad. You get gems and cards with every win, and daily quests keep them coming. The concept of "Secret Packs" helps make archetypal decks, but they seem to be time-limited after you unlock them - which is done by pulling certain rarity cards of certain archetypes from the Master Packs - meaning that you need to take full advantage of them while they're available. Gameplay is veeeeery smooth, and it looks absolutely fantastic. Using cards feels great, certain big cards get awesome animated summonings that don't take too long either. There are long turn timers, which can stretch out games unnecessarily, but also allow you to get a better grasp on the board state and learn what your opponent is really playing. !!READ THE CARDS. YOU WILL DO BETTER!!!So far, there's Duel Lobbies, Spectating, Ranked, and more formats to come, so those of you who don't like any modern Yu-Gi-Oh! should keep your eyes peeled for that. Cosmetics look fantastic as well. Give it a shot, you have nothing to lose! If you reeeaaally like it, try visiting your local card store and seeing what events they have. :) Happy dueling!

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings,i have to say i really liked the old Yu-Gi-Oh Games (The very old ones.) and i knew how Yu-Gi-Oh's Gameplay developed after this but i still wanted to try this Game out for fun. Very bad decision. To be fair, the solo Singel Player contend is kinda nice and was fun to play but playing against other Players is just terrible. The Problem: Power Creep. Yu-Gi-Oh developed from a kinde fun slow Game where both Players could participate, have fun and had some quality Game into a "who-could-build-the-better-one-turn-kill-Deck."Just stupid sitting there and watching your Opponent playing his Combo for like 5-10 Minutes. playing half his Deck in one turn, (At least it feels that long.) until you end up in a positon where you often can't win anymore or outright lose in the same Round. (Playing yourself these Combo and winning that way is also stupid.) There is nearly no interaction anymore between these Players as most games End in the first few turns.In my opinion it's a waste of Time playing against other Players. It just takes to much time, where you either sit and watch your opponent play or you are doing your stuff without much possible reactions from your opponent and you often know that you have won the game. Just clicking on "You Win!" or "You lose!" Button would be more fun, especially when you are losing anyway. Compared to the old Yu-Gi-Oh where each Player would just play a few Cards each round and the Game advantages switched often between the rounds, now it's gone down the route of "all-in" for a one turn kill combo. I had Games where i gone first, played my stuff and then end my turn and the opponent won on his first Turn. That is crazy. The Game ends before it even realy starts. Better don't try playing slow decks - like Exodia, Destiny Board or Deck destruction Decks - that were viable Decks in older Yu-Gi-Oh Games. You won't have fun with it.On the positive site, you get much Gems for Questing and just playing the Single Player content to buy you Packs to build a good, strong Deck for free. You don't have to invest Money into this Game. The Problem here is, you need to unlock the "Secret Packs" you want to buy first somehow - by luck - and have enough Gems lying around to invest it as the secret Packs get locked again after 24 Hours. (You can unlock them again later but it's just stupid to lock them in the first place after you have unlocked them.)I liked the old Yu-Gi-Oh but dislike what it is now. But everybody is different. maybe you may like it but my recomendation would be to just focus on the single Player contend or go for a different Trading Card Game or even maybe for older Yu-Gi-Oh Games.As this Game is for free, you can try it out without investing Money, that's probably the best Part about this Game. You won't regret "buying" it and playing to long to refund the Game afterwards.Have fun playing!

_childDocuments_.review: With close to 400 hours into gameplay, I guess I should finally review the game.Truth is, there's not a lot to say. It's single play duels of Yu-Gi-Oh, and probably one of the easiest and best ways to play the game for those of us who don't live near a game shop that hosts tournaments.So to address, the common complaints: First off, gems. I get it, a lot of people are impatient about this one, but simply playing the game a few hours will get you enough gems to buy 10 packs. I've used free and paid gems, and the card packs don't seem different to me personally on either one. So I can't call it pay to win, because any cards I won't use I deconstruct and use to craft better ones. I've spent a combined total of maybe $30 the whole time I've played and have way more cards than most would think just from free gems during events.Second off: Long turns. Ok, this is definitely a thing, some of those people do it intentionally, some do it though because they are thinking. Some just spam 25 cards into a huge combo. But that's kinda the way it would go in person. But the chains are easier to keep track of so you know what negated what and so forth when relying on Master Duel. So, still easier than trying to do it by hand. Lastly: Meta-reliance. People always hate meta in games, but one thing I always remind people is that the meta is just a concept. It's only the meta until someone finds a better way to play, which is where I find the fun and challenge in the game. I also like mixing decks up with non-meta combos in meta decks so people have no clue what I am trying to pull off. It's true in higher levels of the game you'll mostly see the same 10 or so decks a lot, but it can be just as fun building one to counter them or play around it. Casual play has more diversity as well, but you don't normally get gems there. But you'll find a lot of old school decks there and it's a fun place to go.All in all, fun game and I've enjoyed it since the beginning. I'll stick around a long time to come, probably leaving periodically as I've done and picking it up again and again.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just start by asking, for people who are comparing this game to YGOPro or Omega or other sims, what did you even expect Master Duel to be? It's obvious Konami isn't going to make a free official sim with entirely unlimited cards, like in what dimension was that an expectation on the table? I don't mean to be insulting but like, temper your expectations just a little, it was obvious from the start that this game is eSports YGO.So this game is a 1:1 digital version of YGO basically, Konami has already stated they are going to be performing official events involving this version, and that this game is the official YGO digital version from now on, and they've clearly put a lot of time into this game. Being a free to play game, naturally you need money for boosters and such, but I'm actually pleasantly surprised by how good the card economy is, compared to the utter nightmare of Duel Links.Fair warning, the banlist IS, PARTIALLY, based off the April OCG, as of April 2021, I'm assuming that was about when this game's development hit the stage where cards were being added, and BOY is it more OCG based. Can anyone else say Maxx C at 3 copies? I have no idea if Konami plans on integrating the TCG rules as a separate ladder or something, but I hope they do, however OCG is still balanced, just in a different way, burn and combo decks aren't well liked in the OCG, etc, and I have to wonder if Konami's finally thinking about a merged banlist or something, and this is phase 1 of that plan.The boosters have a different rarity structure, with Rares being more common than one a pack, when they existed, SRs being random instead of one per pack, and URs being random but also lower than real life, where a UR is one every 5 packs or so, and there's no Secret Rare equivalent in this game. You can trade 3 cards of a rarity for any card of that same rarity, and a booster is worth about $2 each of in game currency, as opposed to $4 IRL. You also start with literally $140 of in game currency at what is nearly the start and the early challenges hand it out like candy.8 Cards a booster, and there's currently 3 25% off bundles of 10 boosters with a special card, and those special cards are all actually really good staple cards, at the moment, Ash Blossom, Solemn Judgement, and Lightning Storm. There's also structure decks that are 500 gems each, 1:1 in terms of gem per card, except you get one copy each of 40 different cards, which are mostly all good.There's also a story mode, that unlocks special cards for playing it, and also ENTIRE DECKS of certain archetypes, like Gem-Knights, or the Demise/Ruin set. Some of these cards are pretty good, and it's nice to not even have to seek out Demise King of Armageddon, or many of the Gem Knight cards. It's also, and this is subjective, actually more fun to put in some amount of work to unlock all of these cards, even if it's just a bunch of AI duels.In short, I'm pleasantly surprised at how reasonable this game's economy is compared to literally every other free to play card game, and I genuinely am going to play this game seriously. This game could be a great testing ground for new format ideas, should Konami decide to actually do that, and even without that possibility being considered, a very fun beginners platform for the game, and also potentially a cheaper way to play in official matches, without spending as much of a fortune on cards.EDIT: Yeah so now there's a fan sim that works literally as well, but it's unofficial and doesn't have event formats or a good solo mode, it's called YGO Omega, my old review still stands, but if you're on a budget, well lets just say if you're dueling friends, they'll get used to Omega pretty quickly. Also Konami needs to fix the bot problem, badly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a gacha but is very free to play friendly and very generous compared to most other online card games (way better than HS or Magic Arena for example). Hard to get into competitively and most definitely has  a steep learning curve but as a returning player who last played during 2012, I was able to achieve diamond and then master when it was released. Challenging strategy game that has layers of interactions and feels very rewarding when learned.- F2P friendly- Satisfying to master, one of the most fun strategy games I've played- Fun events that give more casual players slower formats to enjoy- Difficult to learn- Tutorial does not prepare you for the modern game- Cannot do daily missions outside of ranked queue or events- This can be seen as a pro but spending money doesn't really give you anythingBuy all the of the bundles that cost 750 gems, your main currencies in the game will be gems and UR crafting points and these bundles give you the best bang for your buck. It is advised you spend your UR dust on "staples" first (such as three Maxx "C" or other hand traps) before spending it on specific cards that can only be used in maybe 1 or 2 decks.If you want to get into modern Yugioh your best bet is building a meta deck and learning the game through that.  is a good website for looking at decklists/popular archetypes. Since the game gives you a lot of gems in the beginning, you can practically make any deck off of a fresh account (though be careful, it is easy to fall into the trap of building a deck you think is cool, only to realize it's ♥♥♥♥ and lose all of your resources while also making it hard to do daily missions, I have 2 other accounts because of this process since you can't just reroll). Take your time, play around in the solo modes, and look into archetypes you might like, either through the website linked earlier or even encountering them in game. Even a pet deck with a good pilot can get to Master 1 (the highest tier) so you have more options than you think. When in doubt, just ask about something, either through the  or . If you don't really care about ranked and just want to have some fun and get your missions done, you can play the hottest of garbage in low ranks and easily find success.The main idea of the game is to set up what we call "disruption" going first, and then trying to bait out your opponent's "disruption" when going second typically. This often involves equipping your deck with cards we call "handtraps" or "boardbreakers" such that you don't auto lose going second. Here are good examples of both.Handtraps: Maxx "C", Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring, Infinite Impermenance, Effect Veiler, Nibiru the Primal Being, Droll & Lock Bird, etc.Boardbreakers: Triple Tactics Talent, Evenly Matched, Forbidden Droplet, Dark Ruler No More, Kurikara Divincarnate, Lava Golem, Gameciel, the Sea Turtle Kaiju, etc.There is a LOT more to the game but in the current modern format (Sept. 2023 as of writing this) you will 99% see a handful of these cards (and MORE). As for the rules, just know that when a card specifically says something, THATS WHAT IT MEANS, and nothing more or nothing less. For example if a card says that it cannot be destroyed by card effects, it can still be dealt with, either by being "sent to the GY", "banished", "tributed", etc. and vice-versa. The text on cards are very precise and follow a convention called PSCT or "Problem Solving Card Text", but a good TLDR is that every card follows the structure of the following:"Activation Requirements to use Effect; Cost that must be payed to Activate Effect: Effect of the Card"Also when you respond to a card with another, it creates something called a chain (its kinda like the stack in magic but not really). Chains resolve backwards and once it starts to unravel, it cannot be stopped or added to (though before a chain resolves you can add to it by just responding with more cards). There are a lot more rules but this should be a good primer for everything the tutorial doesn't teach you.

Also all of the important keywords are written in Chinese which helps when trying to speed read.Cons: This game is frustrating to play, especially if you don't know the concede meta and end up wasting 7 minutes only for them to flip a card on your turn that stops you from playing the game.  My wins were because I memorized a spread sheet and my losses were because I went second.  I genuinely got bored after getting diamond because this game actually feels playing solitaire half the time, and a snooze fest in the other half.  Opening packs sucks because half the cards aren't even what you asked for.  Seeing a UR on the left is pain, and only URs can make URs so every other card pulled doesn't matter.  Also, Maxx C is fun when I Psy Frame Gamma it and win the game.Maybe I'll come back to this game in a few months if there's a Tier 0 meta (I hate reading my opponents cards) with more turn zero "our turn" style gameplay (I like back and forth).  But until then I'm done!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real shame. The deck building is great, the recycling functionality and card searching is great and I like all the accessories too. I 100%ed achievements for Duel Links and sunk a lot of hours to do so and can count on one hand the times I surrendered. Master Duel's main issue is timer wasters. For whatever stupid reason, Konami thought it a good idea to have a few minutes per card played instead of an overall turn timer and what that effectively means is you can find yourself in a half an hour game that you've maybe played 20-30 seconds of. I don't have a problem with people taking long turns but that is just bluntly unacceptable. Mfers will straight up hold you hostage and if the only answer the sweaties have to defend this BS is "Just surrender then" I'm sorry but I shouldn't have to forfeit ranked duels to mitigate a objectively bad timer mechanic. I hope it gets patched down the line because then i'd change my review recommendation.  There is also the issue that 2-3 deck types dominate everything else but that is significantly less annoying than waiting for people to effectively play half their deck while you lose hours of your life you'll never get back. If you don't mind people taking 20 minutes to show you just how many card they can play in a row in slow motion, check it out. Otherwise stick with Legacy of the Duelist for longform and Duel Links for short form.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very free to play friendly. They give you a lot of gems really easily to use on opening packs, and all the 70+ hours I've spent in the game has been learning how different decks work using the Solo Campaign, which you get a lot of other free gems, decks, and other various cards and accessories from. I have around 15+ decks right now, mostly free decks given to me, but I've personally made two decks and haven't spent any of my own money, just gems that were earned. As far as gameplay, I haven't played Yugioh since the original series introduced in the early 2000s, so the campaign has actually been really helpful in learning all of the additional mechanics implemented since then. There are regular online events, ranked and unranked duels, and a room system where you can play friends that you mutually add via code and other players.

_childDocuments_.review: My first online duel ever was against a pubstomper running a Superheavy Samurai deck that pleasured itself for minutes on end.  I stuck it out because I wanted the daily challenges for activating some trap cards.  I was using my modified Synchro starting deck because I was expecting a new player who was dueling for the first time.  After that horrible match, I switched to my Blue Eyes White Dragon deck that I made to test out some cards I own IRL.  My second online match was against a player who set a defense monster face-down and three trap cards.  When I summoned Azure-Eyes on my first turn, they conceded.My third online match, I found spot removal in my deck (Blue-Eyes Alternative Dragon) to destroy their boss monster, after which they conceded.The game client is very well made, but the online experience is uneven.  I had more fun playing offline campaign matches than online matches, but you only get mission completion from playing online.Also, the game seems fairly friendly to 100% free players.If you like the low-level casual experience, go buy Speed Duels decks and play with your IRL friends.  If you like the high-level experience... are you sure you actually like the high-level play experience?

_childDocuments_.review: I just picked this back up because a dire fan of yugioh and i was enjoying this until one small thing that has cost me more games than anything else.TIME LOSS.No matter what you do you sacrifice time for your turn. You loose 3 seconds every time you hae to click your own prompts to close out things when your opponent does things. Everytime something happens you have to close out prompts and those prompts take multiples of seconds to click. You get 300 seconds at the start of your first turn which seems like a  lot until you realize those 300 seconds move into your ability to respond to your opponent. In a game where hand traps and light ups determined how you make your next plays you don't get any time to think. You don't get any time to read cards if you go up against a new deck. You don't get time to understand anything you better know what you are doing or you YOLO it.I haven't played yugioh in probably 3 years and wanted to get back into it. I was having a great time until finally this latest time loss was really up in the air. Both of us were going back and fourth in a pretty good grind time of salamangreat vs horus and it was a toss up who was going to win. But you know what happens? TIME LOSS. Everytime i'm reading a horus card i sacrifice precious seconds to respond to their cards with my own and eventaully i just ran out of time. I had an entire hand full of answers and a board along with him and I"m the one that ran out of time first.This is not a "get good" Scenario you do not get to play grind games here. You just auto loose. This is NOT how you get people into the game to learn the game. This game is complex as heck and in 2 days i went from nothing to diamond 1 because i used to be pretty good at the card game. But i want to rip my hair out because of the time rules that prevent me from actually learning how to play against other decks. Thank you for reading my rant. _childDocuments_.review: Combos take too long. This game took my money. Sometimes, I genuinely wonder if my opponents are going very slow to tilt me more or the game is that laggy. Seriously, why is Trade-In a UR.So, uh. Yeah. That's modern Yu-Gi-Oh for ya. I love and hate it. Probably a good reason why I quit. But it's Yu-Gi-Oh. At this point, I'd like to describe my relationship with the game as "Stockholm Syndrome". Thanks Konami.-Updated 9/10/2022.My thoughts on Master Duel haven't really changed. Heck, I hear from the community the meta just keeps getting worse from how Konami keeps changing it.I couldn't care less, honestly.Before, I used to see Yugioh as something I didn't have time for. It was so expensive to keep as a hobby, and it wasn't cool anymore when I got in high school. It was a miracle it was cool at all in middle school.I stopped playing, but I still looked every now and then about cool cards. If a card was cool enough (for me the Frightfur archetype) I would get back to collect a deck and then quit again.I took a long hiatus... until Master Duel came out. I played the game more, but out of a necessity to see if it was good enough.And a few friends joined with me.I convinced them to play Yugioh, and I was honestly pretty scared. Certain decks could dominate, and I was afraid the deck archetypes they would like wouldn't even be meta enough for casuals; that they would quit due to losing a lot.Well, they actually liked playing the game. Like a lot. Like, more than I was expecting.Playing Master Duel with them felt like I was back in Middle School without a care in the world. We even have playground rules where if someone has shard of greed on the field you can't attack them. (Swords of revealing light is forever bad now...)Ultimately, I don't know if Master Duel is great or not. I have given it my time though, as the time I spent on it with my friends is irreplaceable.Thank you for another way to play the game, and a chance for newer people to get into it.

_childDocuments_.review: You're going second. It is currently your opponent's turn. You have gone to make breakfast and check it periodically while you wait for you [insert breakfast thing here] to finish that stage of cooking. During the entire time of you cooking breakfast, your opponent is still taking their turn. You finish breakfast and sit down to eat your delicious meal. After you finish your delicious breakfast and get up to put your dishes in the sink or even wash them. Your opponent finally finishes their turn and they have a practically unbreakable board. You are so happy and thrilled that they have finished their turn but you also feel fear and begin to panic as you come to the realization that you have probably lost the duel. But have no fear you have drawn the perfect card to complete your combo. Your opponent has another idea and then activates Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring and completely destroys your immaculate combo. After your opponent presents this card you sit there for a little while contemplating your existence and why you even play Masterduel or Yu-Gi-Oh! in general. After your come to terms with this revelation you hit escape and click on surrender. You then sit in your chair for a while longer contemplating your existence and you remember the euphoric feeling of getting your combo off and getting that FTK/OTK and you celebrate. Those 300 losses are completely negated by the fact that you won. So you start the circle all over again. You lie to yourself and say you'll quit someday but deep down buried underneath the tears of your opponnets you know that you will never quit. TL:DR - If you like Yu-Gi-Oh! make sure to get this Free to Play game. Some things are annoying sure but if you can power through it you'll be just fine. Also remember that this is a game and it has no effect on you other than how you take the feeling of losing. If you react badly you're going to have some pretty bad games too. Just don't let those losses get to you or the fact that one turn takes a long time. Because if you're complaining about that you clearly haven't play since like 2006.
