Vanguard over this, you'll end up spending a lot less as well as my $600 spent on this game has left me with 2 decks as even with free gems i have to dismantle decks to make full decks when events happen or new cards release.EDIT 2: Bots are less rampant, maybe nonexistent now. Main issue comes now from everyone running the same meta deck over and over, you could queue casual duels but then you won't get any rewards, gems, etc to keep building your decks more. Even though this has nearly every card from the TCG/OCG, I can't recommend the game in the state it's in, it needs a serious rework/overhaul of the entire game and maybe rules like only 3 special summons per turn.______________________________________________________________While it's far more free-to-play friendly than Duel Links, you'll likely need to pony up some dosh if you have a 'very' specific deck idea in mind.That said, this is the best simulator online for Yu-Gi-Oh! and everything from the visuals to the music, the flow of the game and more is all great. It seems to have nearly every card in the game, aside from a few that haven't been in any of the video games for a long time such as Shuttleroid and Neo Air Hummingbird, those in particular likely due to some kind of legal issue.The sets seem to be the ones that are released in both the TCG/OCG, if it's only out in one then it's not in the game, and the banlist seems to follow OCG but an older or modified OCG banlist, Maxx "C" is at 3 and so is Chicken Game and so forth.They are very generous with early gems, the first 2 decks you want to build can almost completely be built off of F2P gems as long as your deck isn't full of exclusively Ultra Rare cards or something to that effect. I'm guessing as events come down the line we'll have more opportunities to get gems, and maybe gems with each new box release like they did with Duel Links.Ranked is hit or miss, you'll continuously get rewards as long as you win but once you get to Gold ranking and higher you'll start to face a lot more meta decks and it'll be harder to use your fun decks, though you may be able to push through if you augment your fun decks with meta support like Nibiru, Maxx "C", Ash Blossom, Ghost Mourning/Effect Veiler, Infinite Impermanence and so forth. Just be prepared to surrender a lot(you'll get no reward if you surrender, though) if you don't want to wait for your opponent to do an 8 minute turn when you have a bricked hand and don't think you can make a board on your next turn or break their board, games in modern Yu-Gi-Oh! are over in like 5 turns at most from what I've seen.I do have to wonder what the state of the game will be once the first events start rolling out though, because you're looking at about $2 per pack and each pack has 8 cards, with a 10 pull ($20~) guaranteeing you atleast a SR or UR if you got no UR in your last 10 pull of that pack. The crafting system is good, though with any 3 of one rarity card being equal to any 1 card you want of that rarity, and with foils giving you even more up to possibly getting a 1:1 exchange from "Royal" foils.For now, there's no equal, ez 10/10. Because people have to earn cards not 'everyone' is running meta and I can find plenty of ranked duels to rank up on even with a fun deck like Toons. This game could get expensive if you immediately want 3+ playable decks day 1, but I'm hopeful that there will be ample opportunities to earn gems in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay itself is smooth and feels good. Looks nice too.As you might expect, the game will give you a nice big hunk of gems up front and the rewards will peter out to a slow drizzle over time. At bare minimum, you can earn around 1 pack per day from just doing daily missions, so "it's something". The nice thing is that, if you know what you're doing, you can make a very good deck almost instantly with wise investment thanks to the fairly generous crafting system. With luck, you can get even further than that without spending a cent. The key term is "know what you're doing". If you don't know where you should be spending your gems or what you should and shouldn't craft, it's easy for a new player to waste their free currency, and then you're going to have to either spend money or grind over time. Which brings us to the major point; This game is not friendly to new players. While the single player content exists, and is, to be fair, entirely free for you to experience, the multiplayer is a relatively brutal simulation of the real competitive game, except people don't have to spend money to get their good cards, and so you'll be jumping right into the deep end of the Yugioh card game. If you are expecting to be able to slap together a deck purely of cards you like and win in multiplayer, you will be disappointed. If you are not interested in putting in the effort to learn the ins and outs of the modern game, you will struggle.If, by chance, you actually just want to play modern Yugioh, be it because you already know how to play in a modern format, or you are interested in learning, perhaps to practice or prepare for real life games, then this is a great game. You can play against strong decks, using your own decks, with a fraction of the investment required for real life cards. End of the day? If you are looking for the casual Yugioh you played as a child, the multiplayer will be a painful experience.If you are looking to play modern Yugioh, and you know what that is, then this is probably the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This version of the game is terrible when compared to Duel Links, of which I am a long time player, and is essentially almost unplayable.  I played for a couple of hours and over that time these were my worse gripes about the game.All cons, no pros.1)  Game play is horrifying slow.  The counter for turns is waaaaay too long and you can be sitting there for minutes waiting for an opponent to make a move.2) Setting a trap card or quick play can be a huge drag.  You have to over and over and over again click cancel to not activate it for every little phase.  It starts to drive you nuts after a while, making it hard to focus on what's going on on the screen.  At one point I clicked minimize instead of cancel, where the activate window hid off screen, and I thought my game had frozen or something.3) Unfriendly to newer players because you literally have to know every yugioh card in existence in order to know which ones are most OP, and if you are willing to pay some money you can start immediately with the most OP cards.4) Unlimited Ring of Destruction, Harpies feather duster, and many more OP cards that ought to be banned or not appear in the game at all.  It's in an incredibly unbalanced state.  It literally starts you with 2 Ring of Destruction if you choose the dragon deck, which is arguably one of the most OP and cheapest cards in the game.5) Game was released with all cards.  Making is very pay to win From insanely OP to weak and unplayable cards. No time to experiment with a limited set of cards and try to build anything unique or creative.  All of the cards are available and there is no reprieve from building your cards up and putting a deck together that is not the most OP deck in the game.  YUGIOH has classicly released cards that are too OP to play competitively then later banning them.  I noticed there are some restrictions on cards, but as far as I could tell there was no banning.   Maybe they ban cards, but it's not to the extent that it accomplishes any degree of balancing.6) Game does not show you what is in a pack.  Hard to know what packs you want, when you only see what UR or SR are in the pack.  What if I want to maybe build a burn deck for example?  You might even get URs or SNs not listed.  Maybe I want the commons or rares from the pack to build it?  But I don't know where they are or what I can even get?  This promotes gambling to a degree and makes using your gems a dive into the unknown.  Unlike Duel Links.7) Releasting XYZ, Syncro, Pendulum, & Links all together simultaneously.  Anyone new to the game is just going to rage quit, lets be honest.  You must know everything if you are to play and not loose every game right from the start.7) YUGIOH already has a solid and very good game, it's called Duel Links, and is much more balanced, fast paced, and enjoyable than this.NOT NEW PLAYER FRIENDLY.  PAY TO WIN. UNBALANCE. ANNOYING UI. JUST NO.In conclusion, just play Duel Links.  This game is a waste of your effort if you want to play competitively or actually want to enjoy the game of yugioh.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked playing Yu-Gi-Oh when you are young, and want to come back to it, this game is not for you. It is full of the same predatory tactics to maximize profit as most games these days use, and it ruins the strategical play and resource management parts of the game. It is now based on copying the most effective decks and combos from the internet and letting the game play itself by summoning and calling half your deck on Turn 1 while your opponent inevitably surrenders due to boredom as he/she had to wait 5-6 minutes for you to cycle through your entire deck.+Best PvP Yu-Gi-Oh Game to date in terms of availability of cards and different tactics you can apply+Decent card recrafting system to reduce randomness in deck building-Points to buy cards get less and less as you progress instead of a steady rate to get you hooked on the  game then starve you in order to force you to spend money on it-Newest cards are always the best due to power creep while one or two year old cards are already balanced comparatively via bans and limits again just to force you to buy cards-Game is in its least balanced state ever, it is completely unplayable using older cards as you have access to 5-6 cards vs your opponent who has 15-20 on first turn-The 3 negatives above make the game itself feel like a casino after a certain amount of time, forcing you to spend money on the slot machine(card shop) just to not starve as you level up.(higher levels get less resources via gameplay, older cards become useless over time)-Most competitive decks people copy from each other to do the same thing, making the game feel repetitive. Most use different cards to achieve the exact same thing: 1.Summon a bunch of monsters in a chain to get your "destroyer monsters", destroy a card each turn with each destroyer monster, starve your opponent of cards so he/she can't play anymore2.Summon your "negater monsters" or spells/traps so your opponent can't stop your destroyer3.End your defenseless opponent who is unable to playThis causes the game to have 0 climactic moments that turn the tides as everyone has a bunch of negaters to go through just to achieve a singular effect on the field.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is a great official, accessible way to play Yu-Gi-Oh! while remaining F2P friendly, although lacking in some respects like different formats, crafting token conversion and sidedecking.The game has plenty of single player scenarios that reward you with plenty of in-game currency to buy packs, and has unlockable themed packs to quickly get the archetype cards you want to build decks for. The game's crafting system then makes it fairly easy to get the staple cards you need in order to do well against other decks and get the few cards you might not get from random drops. You can create any deck in the game without spending money simply by putting in enough playtime, so it is kind to the wallet. The game does feature real money transactions for in-game currency, but it's hardly necessary to have an enjoyable experience.The gameplay experience itself is good. The UI is mostly easy to navigate and understand, the game speed is paced well, and the card art and animations are nice to look at. The deck builder is easy to navigate, although lacking an alphabetical sorting function. The main issue is the lack of customization for how to play the card game. There are several formats in the real life card game that can't really be replicated in a seamless way. Sidedecking and best-of matches are hard if not impossible to play properly, making for a pretty frustrating experience. Ranked also is played one match, making a lot of cards and decks simply the best option due their most consistent counterplay relying on sidedecking being a part of the format. Overall something I hope they look into in the future. Perhaps have two different ladders, one for the more casual one-off matches and one for best-of-3 matches with sidedecking.Another feature I hope to see is token conversion. As you dismantle cards, you will get tokens that you can trade for other cards of the same rarity. Right now, I have an issue of having a ton of N and R rarity tokens, but struggling to get SR and UR tokens, used both for the archetypal and universal staple cards needed to play a decent deck. I'm hoping in the future, you could convert lower rarity tokens (say, 100 tokens for 1 higher rarity token) in order for players not to feel like they are collecting useless materials and their time/money is being wasted, and allow players to more quickly start playing other decks and experiment.Overall, this game is a good foundation that I hope they can build into something we can enjoy for years to come. It's not quite up to date with the physical card game, but the card pool is huge and any fan of Yu-Gi-Oh! should give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is the best YuGiOh game Konami has released in terms of usability and cosmetics. However, that is a very small part of the overall experience of Master Duel.As other people have noted before me, this game is not meant for people who are fans of the anime or how the game was back in the day. This game is played by the most competitive sweat-lords from all over the world, especially in the upper ranks of the ladder. The closest experience to the "good ol' days" you can find in this game is in the Solo mode where you play against bots with different kinds of decks.To give you insight in what the current meta game is like, if you do not win the coin toss and have an opening hand that can prevent your opponent from playing. You will lose. Currently there is one dominant deck and that's Ishizu-Tearlaments. Which allows your opponent to: Negate and destroy a card that would special summon a monster (99% of decks rely on special summoning to play their deck) they also get  a bonus of sending a monster to your grave for an additional fusion summon right away,shuffle one of your opponent's cards,permanently negate one card (negates typically only last until the end of the turn), permanently negate a monster's effects and set it's level to 1 (which really messes with any deck that relies on levels of monsters on the field such as Rituals, Synchro and XYZ and to a lesser extent Links)Also is able to shuffle cards from either player's graveyards to their decks which prevents the most common methods of trying to break your opponent's board.And all this is possible despite Konami limiting how many of the cards from these archetypes you can play on release.So with at least 4 disruptions/negates per turn most decks are not able to play at all.Now this would not be an issue if this was purely limited to the higher ranks of matches, but since the deck is so prohibitively expensive a good chunk of people will create a fresh account and use the ton of gems the game front loads you with to make this deck and climb the ladder. For context, there are effectively 25 ranks in this game (which the game incentivises you to climb to get more gems so you can make decks you want.) only the bottom 10 ranks will not have you duel against this deck constantly. Now, they had recently added Casual matches duels which lets you play against others, but you don't get any progress for your battle pass (yes this game has one too) or rewards for winning. So its purely if you want to play your pet decks for fun with less chance to encounter the meta (meta decks show up to practice their combos as casual gives you more time to play your turn).Another note, at the time of writing this, about 1 week into this meta Konami has put out a special event that forces you to playing with only Earth Air Fire and Water in your deck. Which excludes a good chunk of the meta decks from participating. Allowing you to earn the rewards from the event and progress your battle pass. But the event will end before the packs for the aforementioned deck expire and leave the store page.This game is behind on the card releases in the physical card game. Which gives us insight for future meta, which frankly, sounds even less fun, being able to lock your opponent out of using all but 2 card zones, you are left with 2 monster zones to work with, one of which is reserved for extra-deck monsters, so really you only have 1 monster to work with to get your entire strategy out.If this sounds like a jolly good time for you I highly recommend you get into this game. For everyone else highly recommend finding one of the community-made simulators and playing with your friends instead.

_childDocuments_.review: As mush as I want to recommend this to anyone, I can't. Because Yu-Gi-Oh! meta now is totally different from the days of the Duel Monsters anime/manga.For someone who followed the card game from the beginning until now, I really enjoyed the game. Being able to build my whole deck that close enough to the current meta in just 24 hours without spending a single dime is a godsend. Somehow Konami is a lot more generous in terms of Yu-Gi-Oh! Video Games. But if I put a new or returning player's perspective, this is when my opinion changed.This is not the same card game that we've played back in the day. The game now has essentially a Power Creep problem, the PvP Mode shows this very problem to everyone currently playing the game. Konami has introduced multiple ways on how to play the game, like Synchro, Xyz, Pendulum, and Link monster, which some of them has various effects that can and will break the game flow for new and returning players, such as a First Turn Kill deck (FTK) that gives the owner of the deck the ability to win in their FIRST TURN by using series of combos and summoning methods. Or something like Hand Traps, which are not necessarily a Trap Card, but they can be activated from your hand to counter your opponent's moves, it can be a Monster Card like 'Ash Blossom and Joyous Spring' or a Trap Card like 'Infinite Impermanence'. These Hand Traps are a must in order to play against an FTK deck, but recommending a type of card can never fix the core problem of the game.These decks, cards, and many other tricks that I didn't mentioned here can be detrimental to your enjoyment in PvP Mode, so I will not recommending this game to new or returning players UNLESS you have friends that are in the same level as you to play with, or if you're here just to enjoy the Solo Mode.

_childDocuments_.review: Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel is a fantastic digital adaptation of the classic card game, offering a highly immersive experience for both seasoned players and newcomers. The game stays true to the original mechanics, with thousands of cards to build diverse decks. Whether you're into classic strategies or experimenting with modern archetypes, there’s something here for everyone.The graphics are sharp, with stunning 3D animations and effects that make every duel feel epic. The game is easy to navigate, and the tutorials are perfect for beginners. The soundtrack enhances the intensity, making every match more engaging.Master Duel’s free-to-play model is refreshingly generous, providing plenty of gems upfront and a card-crafting system, though microtransactions are available for those looking to accelerate their progress. Overall, it’s a well-rounded card game that captures the spirit of Yu-Gi-Oh! while being accessible to a new generation of duelists.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game isn't fully polished yet, I'm glad that Konami finally built a worthwhile modern Yu-Gi-Oh! dueling experience. While I wish it were easier to get to crafting cards to build your own decks, I wish that were accessible earlier. Some animations/overall graphics are slightly outdated/have a fuzzy resolution, but I hope that they improve on those as well. They have a great single player system to introduce new players into the game as well as give some more obscure decks a chance to shine. Overall, while it has some downsides of being quite clearly rushed, it is a great game for Yu-Gi-Oh! fans and new players alike.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a money scheme and nothing more. Konami does not care about the cards it releases and puts no care into the balancing of the game. Its a constant struggle to create the decks that are the overpowered meta decks of the time, for which almost no other decks you may come to enjoy can compete with. Then after a couple months, Konami comes out with an even more broken deck while banning and limiting the previous meta decks you worked hard to create and may have had to spend money to obtain. Then there are the few decks that Master Duel refuses to ban even at the pleas of its community. These few cards like Maxx C with their completely broken card ability ruin your deck by forcing you to have at minimum 10 cards the community calls "hand traps" in your deck. Without these hand traps, you are unable to counter the effects of broken cards like Maxx C and break boards that can be set up to be so powerful, that many are forced to surrender on turn one. Konami and Master Duel do not care about its player and fan base. It only cares about making as much money as possible while ruining the experience of others who loved the game for so long. This is not the Yugioh some may know from the shows. Its very different by which players can take up to 15 minutes just to set up their turn 1 board. Most players will be playing the meta decks, so these board will be nearly impossible to break unless you happen to draw into one of the few cards you may need within your deck by sheer luck, which at this point, I believe to be rigged. Considering how I can draw one of the most useless cards in my deck more than I would ever draw anything else even though I have 1 copy in a 50 card deck is just astounding to me.... this includes having drawn it 5 duels in a row in my starting hand on multiple different occasions. If you are willing to pay thousands of USD to keep up with the constant shift meta decks to stay remotely relevant in the game, contend with constant frustration about how terrible your card draws are even though you built what was suppose to be a very consistent deck, suffer a coin flip that makes you go second for the 6th time in a row by which each opponent take 15 minutes to finish their turn one, and work hard to get into high ranks just for the game to set up circumstances to cause you to lose all those hard earned ranks all in a row with ♥♥♥♥ luck, then this game may just be for you......

_childDocuments_.review: Every time they unnecessarily hit a deck on the banlist without any concentrated effort to make the game as a whole better take a shot. Tearlaments getting more hits on the banlist when it barely even qualifies as a rogue deck after the last banlist. The in-game card usage and win rate cut-ins plus the MasterDuelMeta website's statistics would suggest nearly a dozen different decks are more played than Tearlaments currently. It's only completely uninformed people, redditors, total Yugi-boomers, and people who enjoy playing inherently toxic stun/floodgate decks or bad decks that turned Tearlaments into the bogyman of "toxic combo solitaire" deck they think it is. Besides Tearlaments getting another hit after the deck was functionally neutered, Konami in their infinite wisdom decided to limit nimble beaver of all things, a level 2 card being abused as an engine in spright, a deck centralized around two busted and entirely generic extra deck link-2 monsters. The same thing happened to the frog engine, point is Konami is targeting symptoms and not actual problems, because the problems are big shiny UR cards which means more money for them. Konami does actually hit problem cards on the banlist, diablosis being an unbelievably toxic card that interacts with you by banishing a card from your extra deck face down and a ton of cards from the main deck. Of course Kashtira's second wave of support is coming and besides being the most consistent stun deck ever conceived their monsters also all banish cards face down, some from the deck, some from the field, and even one from the extra deck. Of course the archetype will remail largely unscathed for likely upwards of 3-4 months so Konami can milk money out of it. One of the biggest problems with Yugioh is that the power level of the game is pretty crazy, but an even more fundamental problem is Konami's blatant lack of any effort to try and revitalize their game. People complained about the "Tear 0 meta" to no end, the current meta is whatever and the coming meta is a nightmare, but at least none of these metas were drytron's infinite negates, or floodgate eldlich, or adamancipator and spyral's actual solitare combos that take an extremely long time to execute. The point is while every meta is "crazy" in some way and could potentially be worse, the root of all of these problems are: Konami putting the actual bare minimum into balancing the game, the last time they communicated with the playerbase about the logic of a banlist being almost a decade ago, and the sheer lack of direction. Konami of the OCG and TCG are essentially black boxes that spit out new cardboard give us rules and just let people play. There are probably a hundred or two different cards that could be banned and the game would become much healthier overnight while retaining a high level of power that people have come to love, but without a lot of the things that make the game frustrating that people take for granted. No one likes having to open or draw specific cards to "counter" or out something that's nigh unbeatable otherwise, and no one likes being "outed" so it'd be nice if the out didn't exist while also not having to need crazy outs to begin with. Why even discuss the philosophy of any of what I said though, when Maxx C is still legal, Konami OCG's obsession with a card that actively ruins the game and has a 93% usage rate across ALL DECKS PLAYED IN THE GAME is actually incomprehensible. Konami is of course still a black box, it'd be great if that weren't the case even if they had terrible reasons for everything they did, at least it'd be something. Konami is too busy suing some yakuza backed horse racing gacha game to though, or maybe labbing a new pachinko machine, clearly more important than the little game that is Yugioh.There are other problems unique to Master Duel that aren't present in either the TCG or the OCG, those being the best of one format and the fact that the game's cardpool lags several months behind the TCG, the TCG already lagging many many months behind the OCG itself. The TCG and OCG not being united is another core problem with Yugioh, and the delayed card releases in Master Duel are a reflection of this.I'd still recommend the game because I have 800 hours, obviously I've enjoyed and continue to get enjoyment out of the game and have gotten my money's worth a hundred times over. I think a lot of the negative reviews are totally nonsensical, and some of you need to get a grip. Fundamentally Yugioh is a pretty good game with a lot of issues. Side Note: Yugioh being "too hard to learn" is major cope from people who can only game at a 3rd grade level. Master Duel was my first time playing Yugioh, plenty of others started with Master Duel, and one of the people who went to THE WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP started playing Yugioh with Master Duel.

Simple: Yu-Gi-Oh! is not new player friendly. Too many players come to this came expecting to relive the anime, or relive their games on the playground as kids - then they experience getting handtrapped 3 times, getting FTKd, facing multiple Omni Negates on end boards, and then are turned away.As for my criticisms of the actual game, the gem prices are unreasonable, I would buy more gems if they were like 30% cheaper. The events have slowly decreased gem rewards over time. The banlist is simply not fit for a Best-of-One format. There is no Best-of-Three ladder or mode. New card releases have been overinflated by UR. They have not released secret packs for some archetypes released in limited time packs. Far more, too, but I'm tired of writing.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this card game. It's not an overstating it to say that both the anime and the game itself have been core memories to me. It's no secret however, that due to both of these things being linked to what is supposed to be in infinitely merchandisable card game; the game costs money. It's just disparaging to see how much it costs and how much the system is made down to it's core to drain every dollar from you. You'd think that with the many Yu-Gi-Oh! simulators online they'd understand the appeal of a virtual simulator being in that the cards are cheaper and more attainable. Simply put my big issue is your inability to ACTUALLY recycle the points and cards. I understand its novel to have a simulator in where you have to purchase packs just like in real life, it does a lot to make winning with the cards you were limited to use feel better. But the UR packs being so expensive (1000? was 500? to difficult?) is downright manipulative. It's unironically 23$ for the chance of an UR, cause again it's not certain. Compounding with the cards themselves being random. It's not only possible but common that you'll buy a 10 pack and get an UR for a pack that wasn't even featured in your desired booster pack. Pair this with you only being able trade in cards for a third of the card points necessary to generate new ones. Culminates in a game that objectively costs more then it's worth to play. You'll find yourself scrambling for points and CP just to run decks you actually like. A simpler fix would be allocating the Card Points system to rarity. Making it so that if you get an UR it costs 30+ points when sold, as they are the rarest and would be the hardest for the consumer to lose and burn up. 20+ for SR and then 15+ for R and 10+ etc. This way even if you get a card you can't use. Your a lot more likely to recycle it into a card you want to use. Especially if that card is some sort of rare boss monster like the hundreds that exist. This isn't even getting to the bugs, like certain cards effects not procking correctly or just not working when their requirements have objectively been met. I'm not even going to complain about the Meta of the game, in which decks are made almost always in one turn consistently negate every effect you have. Being a turn based game I think it's important to stress how boring it can be when player interactions are one sided. The problem isn't that someone is winning or even winning considerably. But that the other player isn't allowed to do anything at all. If monster effects and hand traps are allowed to be so rampant that you literally can't activate anything with a great hand then the game just becomes indistinguishable from a single player game. The meta isn't even worth mentioning as it's a direct by-product of everyone being so starved for cards their pushed to favor cards that keep them winning. If not for the dopamine cycle then for the chance of getting their money back. Of course the meta is filled with Drytron's and Elditch if you have to choose the cards you want and those cards are the fastest and most consistent way to win. It's not on the players it's systemic problem with the game forcing them to fight like wolves for scraps. All in all while the game itself is fun to play an filled with tons of combinations of cards and combos to have great plays and fun times. The bar to entry is very expensive. Despite being a free game.

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of making this review a meme, I thought I would genuinely tell you what you;re getting yourself into. Yeah I wrote a review longer than the bible, tl;dr at the bottom.Gameplay:Literally everything is fine, the animations look good, the game itself is the nicest looking yu gi oh game i've played. It feels nice to play and everything works well.The real issue:You will either sink hours into this game or you will be turned off by either the state of the game(not the game's fault) or the way to obtain cards. The game gives you enough gems to start and make a complete deck but afterwards gems are generally harder to come by. My advice is honestly just to go to Master Duel Meta and look at the current tier list of good decks and make one of those so you can get gems though doing your challenges. Don't feel inclined as the main point is to have fun but if you wanna make the decks you want then you need gems and to get gems you need to win and play a lot doing challenges.Also you can scrap cards you get from packs to craft the cards you want so that makes it easier to get all your ash blossoms and Baronne De Fleur to make your opponent cry.The Dueling Experience:I casually played yu gi oh and various yu gi oh games and thought I understood the card game very well. Nope your opponent is gonna special summon 14 monsters a turn and lock you out of using cards before you even get something on the board. I've adjusted well. As a regular plat player trying to grind to diamond, this is gonna be the experience. This game only has ranked so if you want a more casual experience you can make custom rooms with friends or try to join randoms I guess? Either way you'll see a lot of locking down and taking away your ability to play the game kind of games. If you play for a bit you'll definitely adjust and be able to play through your opponent and win, it just involves learning the key cards of the popular decks and formulating strategy. They do have solo mode that teaches you the basics and lets you verse some pretty mediocre archetypes but gives you cards and gems for doing it so I'd say it's worth running though but don't expect a fully fleshed out solo story mode or anything from this.TL;DRPros:-Good feeling dueling-Good starting amount of gems to get you going-Card Scraping system to get cards you want-A LOT of cards-Good way to introduce yourself or get back into yu gi oh if you don't mind some commitment to learningCons:-State of yu gi oh(jk jk but definitely off putting for new players)-Less gems after your initial burst(its a free game so that's fair)-No Casual mode only ranked so expect tough competition-Not mentioned but a really wack banlist that isn't updated as much as it should be tbh.-Solo mode is definitely a side feature, don't expect to play this game exclusively solo.Hope this helps. have over 300 hours across 2 platforms and this is what I've experienced since the day 1 launch. Great game, love it to death but definitely be aware of these things and give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:OST: It's fireSolo Mode: It's fun. Provides lore on some Archetypes, and provides good rewardsCons:(where do I begin)Deck Construction: A huge chunk of your deck is just UR cards (the highest rarity) that are staples that fit into any archetype. This limits creativity and creates for a very boring match.Match Length: It's either way too fast, or way too long. You either get OTK'd turn 1/2, or the opponent negates everything you do and the game goes on for as long as a League of Legends match. It's also so annoying losing control during your own turn waiting on the opponent to decide if they want to do something.Gameplay: It's not fun constantly getting negated, nor is it fun watching your opponent combo for 15 minutes setting up their massive board, just because you were unlucky to not have a negate yourself. You seriously might as well flip a coin to determine who wins the match. Here's an example of a match. (You can't mulligan btw)"Hmm..my hand is pretty weak. No monsters to start my engine. Thankfully, I have a spell here that lets me fish for a monster that can get things going"*Opponent plays Ash Blossom from hand, negating the effect*"Oh that's fun, I sure love hand traps. There is totally ways to play around CARDS THAT ARE IN THEIR HAND." GG I guess. Literally have to hope I top-deck something at this point. I'll just surrender.Monetization: Everyone is praising Konami to the high heavens that they finally have a crafting system. Except nobody seems to mention that a huuuuge portion of decks are UR, and the rate that you get UR crafting points is abysmally low so you're either going to have to spend a toooon of money finishing a single deck, or wait till you finish like 3 battlepasses (which would take a bit under a year considering each one lasts 75 days) just to finish crafting UR staples.Card Design: Yu-Gi-Oh should've implemented icons to shorten card effects YEARS ago. It'd be so much faster to have an icon of a graveyard or something to represent "When this card is sent to the graveyard" or "If this card is in the graveyard. Instead, cards have paragraph long effects. Good luck remembering what 10k cards effects are, or have fun reading what they do every. single. time. Also, so many spells/effects/traps just boil down to - destroy X or negate Y. It's BORING.TL:DR - Play Legends of Runeterra instead. Better art, better card design, the flow of battle is more fast paced. The back and forth is actually fun and engaging not just negate negate negate GG. The monetization is EXTREMELY generous in LoR too.

All of the problematic cards that have been hit in the TCG/OCG are Normal/Rare/Super Rare and all of the ones that won't get hit are Ultra Rare's making sure the deck is as expensive as possible while providing as little refunds as possible.3.) Konami intentionally balances the banlist around rarities. Sometimes their hand will be forced (Instant fusion) but with the recent banlists it's very obvious konami does NOT want to hit cards that are at UR rarity. They'll limit cards like skill drain but won't touch cards like TCBOO for example.4.) As time goes on the game has become less and less f2p friendly. When the game started there were over a hundred secret packs and we were all waiting for more secret packs to be added but as time went on instead of getting new secret packs we got selection packs. What are selection packs? Well, a secret pack will have 1-2 archetypes in them, like Mathmech and Skystrikers, so if you wanted those decks you would reasonably get everything you wanted from it pretty quick. Selection packs are like if you mixed 2-3 secret packs together. There's so much bloat and the majority of cards aren't what you want and are filler so it becomes increasingly expensive to pull what you need. The worst part is that these are TIMED. Once they're rotated out they're gone. They're not turned into secret packs. The result is that this causes FOMO and once you miss it you're looking at certain decks, even if they're bad, being REALLY expensive because you need to manually craft them. On top of all of that there's a bunch of bots in the game and there are players playing on mobile, which in of itself isn't bad but the mobile client is extremely laggy so if you're unfortunately paired with someone who's on mobile you're going to spend most of the game waiting for them to reconnect causing your 20 second combo to take minutes as every single time their connection goes bad (which is all the time) you need to wait on them.Konami has neglected this game and has lost 90% of the players that have touched this game. They don't care if they cause an unhealthy meta because there's enough whales that give them money that they don't care. They've refused to do right by it by adding in Goat and Edison, draft, more secret packs, a healthy meta, and more custom lobby options like custom banlists.Currently I'm just logging in once every 3 days to do my dailies but one day I'm going to forget and eventually move on. This game is wasted potential, another added to Konami's list of neglected IP's.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a new or returning player please read this before playing.It's a good game. The "not recommended" label goes out to all the new players and returnes frustrated after jumping into a ranked game and being completely stomped by some guy somehow just summoning a giant golden zombie straight from his deck. I'm that guy and I'm sorry.Master Duel is definitely the most visually appealing digital Yu-Gi-Oh experience we ever had. A lot of thought went into the flow of gameplay and how the UI is navigated and playing it feels great. If you know what you're doing. Konami released this game in a somewhat unfortunate state. It's most important objective should've been to pull in and retain new and returning players into a card game that is notoriously difficult to learn. Currently it fails in that regard, maybe once the ranks have settled that might be different, but as of now if you're jumping into a game against a real opponent chances are you're going to have no idea just how much your old favorite deck from 2010 has been outclassed by pretty much everything that's been released within the last few years.Ranked play being the only matchmaking option will turn away a lot of people. Over time Master Duel is going to need some game mode that puts duelists on a level playing field. Something that makes knowledge of the current meta irrelevant. Something like a draft mode to slowly introduce players to many of the cards they have missed over the last 15 years. If they want to take inspiration from the community, some sort of progression series system would be absolutely perfect here guiding new players slowly through the history of the game, perhaps even three to five sets at a time instead of just one.So if you're not someone who has actively followed the game for some time, at least wait until events, other game modes, alternative formats or more banlists are implemented. Konami has something with a lot of potential here and I'd hate seeing all the new players walk away from it in frustration.There are alternatives to this game that shall not be named here out of respect for the community and the developers of master duel, but if you want to get back into Yu-Gi-Oh you might want to start there. Look up GOAT format, that's the game you remember from back then. Make your way up from there, there are other fan formats with limited card pools. Yu-Gi-Oh back then was sometimes just as frustrating and unbalanced as it is today, even worse during some infamous formats. Give it a chance, maybe just do it somewhere else.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing Yugioh for a long time, thinking way back to potentially 2005-2006.  I dumped hundreds of hours onto World Championship 2007 on the NDS simply because I loved the game but as a youth didn’t have the friends/the money to play.  As I got older things pretty much stayed the same, I’d get into the game really hardcore for a few months and then lose interest when it felt like the monetary ceiling forced me to prematurely plateau.  We all know Yugioh is expensive, paying 90$ for dpe or 100 for a single copy of forbidden droplet is never gonna feel that great whether you’re playing casually or competitively.  I feel that part of the appeal of a duel sim like Edopro is access to this game from the comfort of your home and fair enough it’s free.  Say what you will about the premium products like Legacy of the Duelist but at least everything was accessible as long as you played.  With things the way they are now in Master duel, you’re lucky to get enough to grind out one 10 booster package a week IF you play a bunch everyday AND win.  Playing the same deck into the same 4-5 matchups everyday gets kind of boring.  Boarding into eldlich setting 4 passing, watching a drytron player combo off and end on herald with 5-6 negates is prime snooze material.  I’ve seen enough guys loop lyrilusc into udf with simorgh-> barrier statue to last a lifetime.  Point being that with enough games played, you will just reach plat 5 naturally.  The decks that try to innovate or play for fun slowly fade away and are replaced by the aforementioned.  If you play meta/ just want to play to win that’s fine but personally the game has gotten stale.  A lack of new content(the last couple core booster sets), laughable ranked rewards, and no announced schedule for solo mode/dueling events result in something I think can die out sooner rather than later if things don’t change soon.  Obviously I’ve been very negative thus far but the game is fun when it works.  Playing 1v1 lobbies with friends is amazing once you navigate the labyrinthine ui.  Watching the countless animations for boss monster summons is uniquely satisfying.  At the start watching this unique format was fairly interesting but I think it’s about time to switch it up.  With the game as it is now, I can recommend it to returning players and brave new ones, just brace yourself with some snacks when you inevitably vs any of the top 5.  Good luck and have fun. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's pretty good.-------------Starting off with the positives, the game is very generous. A new player can easily build a powerful meta contender without spending any money at all, given they're up for a little bit of grinding the story mode. The UI is also very easy to work with and quite pretty, so playing the game is enjoyable as well. I am not new to yugioh but I feel that the tutorial explains most of the basics and would definitely help out anybody who's never touched the game before.Gameplay-wise I'm really happy with Master Duel, and it's almost everything I've wanted out of an official sim. The graphics are the best yugioh has ever had, and there are little touches all over the place that make the game feel better. ------------------------------------Keyword being "almost". I still have a few complaints about the game as a while, but most of them don't significantly impact gameplay.The biggest change is the special banlist that Master Duel uses. It's really close to an early 2021 OCG list, with some TCG tweaks. As a TCG player it can be a little jarring, and I'd much prefer them to implement offical OCG and TCG banlists, but at the end of the day it's not a dealbreaker for me.Premium Currency, ie gems, are capped at 10k, which is ridiculous considering a person who just installed the game can collect well over that amount in freebies. It feels exclusively like a ploy by Konami to prevent hoarding and promote spending your currency before it expires in the giftbox, which just strikes me as greedy. I hate this even though it doesn't affect the actual gameplay, and I think they should change it.The game did not launch with the latest Yugioh sets available (Burst of Destiny, etc). Obviously this is subject to change, but the faster they catch up with set releases the better.The game feels a little "unfinished" in certain places. There aren't that many pets/icons/banners to choose from, and even some of the pets feel like placeholders. While admittedly funny, having a pair of generic roller skates doesn't feel very yugioh, if you ask me.

_childDocuments_.review: I only recommend Master Duel if you have a friend or group of friends to play with, largely due to the fact that the ever-shifting meta will make it extremely difficult to build decks you WANT to play online. With a group of friends, you can build anti-meta decks for gems and rewards in ranked play, and then spend those gems to create the decks you truly want to make and play with friends. Most important notes, especially for those who (like me) are not big Yu-Gi-Oh fans and are more familiar with other TCGs:*Learning curve is not very steep if you have played other TCGs.*Gems are, like most other posts mention, front-loaded. You will have a seemingly endless supply at first, like in most games like this. But even if you are conservative with your spending, you will eventually hit a wall and receive so few gems that you cannot purchase anything for a long time.*First-turn-kills and one-turn-kills are not only very possible, but very prevalent. You will get FTK'd or OTK'd fairly often. *The biggest pain point is the meta. Every game like this has one, but it's so prevalent here that you can play for hours straight and see the same 2-3 decks. When Sky Divers were at their peak, they would sometimes be the only deck I saw all day long. For me, this issue got so bad that I would leave matches and take the penalty rather than fight another Sky Diver or Numeron deck (where, again, you can easily be OTK'd). Even though I could sometimes beat them, it simply wasn't fun to fight the exact same strategy over and over again. You can create anti-meta decks, but as more people do this, it then shifts the meta and you'll see more anti-meta decks that then make your own deck redundant.*Most other comments mention this as well, but the length of turns is not exaggerated. I would sometimes play while on break at work, and my entire break would pass before my opponent was finished with their first turn. I started pulling up books that I could read while waiting for my turn to come and could get through a few pages before I was able to do anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Yu-Gi-Oh! is an amazing game but the state it's in now is self destructive. The meta is perpetually toxic and you won't be able to escape it unless you're playing with your friends casually. This condition renders what might be the majority of decks in the game almost completely useless. You could at least have some fun in solo mode but the AI is pretty bad. Watch as it links away it's link 4 boss monster into a random link 2, winning you the game instantly. Also you're relegated to the decks Konami implements into solo mode, none of which are anywhere near competitive.I think the bigger issue still is that you're probably fortunate to obtain a single full deck without buying gems. This is a game with like 10,000+ cards and you'll struggle to complete one deck. Imagine how fun that is. Good luck experimenting with new cards when 1/2 of the best additions to consider are UR's. UR's are ultra rare cards that are very difficult to obtain. If you want more cards after you've dried up the main avenues for gems, you need to wait for an event or fork over the cash. But the gems are extremely expensive. The best deal is about $1.8 per pack. You will receive about 0-4 UR's per 10 packs, yes, a possible 0 UR's for $18. Many decks will require 9 or more UR's within the archetype alone. Opening packs is like gambling, the more you spend the more you feel the sunk cost fallacy, the game stops giving you gems after loading you with gems in the beginning, etc. It's quite predatory. If you're new to Yu-Gi-Oh! just don't play Master Duel it's not really worth it to get in right now.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're too lazy to read the multitude of reasons not to play this pile of festering garbage, here's the tldr;This game is rarely any kind of fun, needlessly bloated and complicated, unforgiving to newcomers and returning players alike, and has almost as worse of an effect on your mental health as League of Legends.If you're a returning player, are interested in picking up YuGiOh in any way, or are a returning player, do not, I REPEAT, DO NOT even think about playing this game. It drains your self worth as punishment for failing to understand basically anything and demands that you are up to date on basically every card that has ever existed in order to know what decks are meta and how any deck matches up to literally everything else, if you're new, you'll be bombarded by a multitude of rulings that don't make sense, if you're returning, even if you've just been away for a year or two, the number of new meta decks and generic searches, GY sends, special summons, and sheer control through removal the newer decks have blows everything out of the water. I first quit a little bit before swordsoul got added to the TCG, came back a week ago and now i genuinely cannot go 3 games without running into Kashtira Fenrir, which is a Cyber Dragon that searches more of its archetype, all of which are good, and has a targeting banish in response to attack or monster activation, and none of its effects have any costs to speak of. If that sounds un-fun to play against, then don't come back. If all that flew over your head and you don't get why that's so strong, DEFINITELY don't join. If you're thinking of joining because you like any of the anime, then I repeat, DO NOT JOIN. the card game is nothing like the anime. A grand total of 3 archetypes from the anime were ever genuine meta threats. Blackwings during the synchro era, Performapals during the Pendulum era, and Rokkets during the current post link era, and that last one barely counts since it was basically just 3 cards mixed with a bunch of generic dragon support. The game isn't centered around the gripping back and forth we see in the shows, but drowning your opponent in so many negates, removal effects, resource generation, and floodgates that they can't play the game in any meaningful way.  if you made it here, one last reminder for good measure, JUST DON'T PLAY THE GAME, YOU ARE MISSING OUT ON THINGS ANY NORMAL PERSON ACTIVELY WANTS TO AVOID.

_childDocuments_.review: From someone who plays and is aware of YGOPro and YGOmega. I can tell you that this is definitely the one we Yugioh! players have been waiting for.  An official Yugioh! game coming from Konami based on the latest Master Rule and is aimed for online play.Legacy of Duelist had some problems here and there plus the fact that it is grindy to get the deck you want (well there is a shortcut...). Followed up by some obscure controls that made it so annoying to play for PC players (if you don't own a controller). Master duels is really a well crafted experience on PC.Ok the real meat of the review. in the platforms I mentioned above, you get all of the cards for free, you just need to build your deck. In here, you have to buy the cards by packs but unlike duel links. You don't need to spend money to even get the first deck that you feel like playing both in Online and Solo.Yes this is because the game offers a crafting system where by dismantling cards on a particular rarity, you can gain fragments where if you have enough of them, you can get craft the card you exactly wanted. There is no annoying hassle gacha style that is on duel links, just buy the packs, dismantle the cards that you won't be using then be on your way.Not to mention when you craft certain cards, you unlock a time-limited secret pack that you can buy instead of the regular master pack, which usually is under a specific archtype or group of archtypes. Which makes it even easier to build.Gems can easily be obtained by doing solo quests where you play the game base on a specific story scenario. The story now revolves around a card's lore instead of retelling of the anime story over and over and over again. I love it, it's unique, it's good!Definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: **REVISION AT BOTTOMMaybe you will like playing it with your friend one on one, but if you do try to play against randoms be prepared to spend a minimum of 20 minutes waiting on players doing at least 50 things on their first turn. I can absolutely assure you that if you like spending an hour in one match waiting for your turn, you will probably like this game. If you're sane, though, don't touch this game's matchmaking unless you are a masochist who want to get eviscerated by Jeff Bezos who has probably spent over a thousand hours in the shop popping 10-packs.Revision: While my original review is still true a decent amount of the time, it has occurred a lot less than my initial impression led me to expect. One thing I didn't mention in my original review is a criticism of the community. By which I mean 50% of your matches where you aren't killed in one turn, the opponent will probably just end up surrendering. It is seriously hard to play the game as it is intended because 80% of the time it is either a one-turn-K.O. or it is a near-instant surrender/disconnect. That being said, when you are able to play the game normally, whether it is with randoms or friends, you will probably have a great time. Even despite my awful first impression, I have managed to find a lot of enjoyment with my friends and with some of playable online matches. And here is advice for new players, so that you don't stumble in blind like me: You can not reset your account in any way. Be 100% sure about your starter deck, because you can't go back. (Personally I would recommend the Synchro Unity deck. Synchro summoning is really easy to learn if you aren't familiar with it, and a lot of powerful strategies are easily pulled off this way). Even if you decide you no longer want to use the deck, there are a lot of good cards in it that can be used in any deck. Also, play through AT LEAST the first "solo" mode option after the tutorial. You can get Monster Reborn (and plenty of gems) this way. Also, structure decks are available in the shop for only 500 gems, the equivalent of 5 random card pulls. The deck I have been using lately is a modified version of the Re-Contract Universe structure deck, but I am sure that all of them are completely viable with a little maintenance. Crafting specific cards is also important and fairly simple. That means if you have deck ideas in mind, or want to recreate a deck you have in real life, you can. Without trying to gacha pull a whole 40 card deck out of the 10k+ cards in the game. The devs were very kind with that feature.

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you should get into Yugioh. It's an expensive game if you want to make a lot of decks (most do) so I recommend making Steam alts if you ever end up caring that much, but you should be able to make a healthy 5-10 on your main as long as you play a decent amount. The meta can sometimes be annoying, but there will always be anti-meta, and you won't always match up against meta decks either. If you're sincerely good at the game, you can win losing matchups just by being more clever. Doomers will tell you to forfeit every going-second game, but it hardly is ever that lopsided. This is at least somewhat a game of luck at the end of the day, after all.Other than that, just try to enjoy yourself. Don't take anything too seriously. It's just a card game, but regardless of how annoying some matchups can be, it ends up fun. I prefer it over MTG now. And remember: you learn from every loss. Don't be hard on yourself for not winning much at first. You do not need to be a lawyer to understand what's going on, but that doesn't mean you're an idiot for not picking up on everything immediately. Just give yourself some time.

_childDocuments_.review: I've loved the Yu-Gi-Oh! franchise for years, ever since I was a small boy, I bought games for my PSP, got old school yugioh games for the pc, collected cards and overall was a massive fans of the series, It's a fun card game with cool artwork and all your nerd/kid neuron activation parameters were met.This game however (or should I say, the meta present in the actual card game that has *kind* of translated itself into this game) makes this a slog of a game if you purely intend to have fun. The meta of this game (so most of the decks you are going up against) rely heavily on negates. Negates are cards that are designed with the intent to negate effects of (usually) the opponent's cards. What does this entail then? It means that every battle you have is you going against an opponent who, if he has a meta deck (which are decks where your opponent plays by himself for a good 10 minutes to set up negates for when it's eventually your turn), is going to his absolute best to make sure you can't play when he's done with his turn.It's this agonising feeling akin to watching a guy tell you for 10 minutes that he's about to kick you in the nuts really hard and you can't do anything about it...                                   and then he kicks you in the nuts.It's devolved from a fun card game where you play with these gimmicky decks with cool strats and creative ways to win into an absolute slog fest with everyone just using negates and boring combos that, for me, killed one of the big reasons why I preferred this card game over the others (barring childhood bias).I'm not even going to get into the system of getting cards (you essentially get enough points for like 2-3 decks and after that it gets real hard to make any new decks without paying for packs and stuff) but I was honestly willing to ignore that as long as I had fun.Unfortunately it's a game where powercreep is very very much present and I quit playing after dumping around 190 hours on it

_childDocuments_.review: Here its important to point out several things. Master Duel is a mix of some very good things and sadly some very bad things that most likely will overlap all the good stuff this game can offer you. Im a returning old player and this is my opinion about the current state of Master Duel and Yugioh in general.Lets start with the great stuff about Master Duel.+++ Amazing Soundtrack and sounds effects, the Audio developement team definetly did an impressive work here.++ Great Animations, FX and other UI transitions, this is also one of the strongest points, visually pleacing to watch.+ Finnaly Konami decided to release a proper official Yugioh game, there is some mini games or small atempts in the past like Duel Links but I dont count those as proper full games.And now lets go the negative sides about this game that can make you quit depending you patience or aproach to them.--- Progression system, this game forces you to go into ranked or competitive events to obtain rewards as thats the main source of ingame currency income that is crucial to progress and obtain cards you need for you decks or make new decks to have some variety. Yes you can obtain currceny on the Solo campaign mode but the amount you get there is very small so barelly makes any difference.-- Current Top Meta gameplay is not fun, its focuses around preventing you oponent from playing so he dont prevents you from playing, basically all players goal is to lockdown you oponent on turn 1 with the starting hand and who ever is able to do so wins, the game used to be much better in the past whitout the current new cards. As matches used to be longer and were not decided on turn 1 and starting hand like right now. So except if you like that I count it like something negative- No ingame chat so you cant interact with other players or make friends with them easly, you need to use external apps like Discord, Twitch or other to somehow communicate with them as ingame there is no way to do so properly.And I guess those are the important points about this game that you need to have in mind. Opinions can be different depending the players and what they enjoy, I like the idea of Yugioh and Master Duel but not the current Top gameplay of Yugioh, I will still rate this as a positive review because I want to see this game improve into something better as it have many potential but as always is up to the developers and Konami to fix these key problems and improve overall the enjoyement of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the problems I have with Yu-Gi-Oh! Master Duel has to do with the actual card game of Yu-Gi-Oh and not really much with this game in particular. If you already know about Yu-Gi-Oh and play it actively, then I highly recommend Master Duel, since it gets regular updates, has the most of the recent cards and has an active community so you won't have problems finding a match. If you just want a way to play the card game, then getting this video game is a no-brainer (Especially since it's free). The visuals are beautiful, the sound design is incredible and the music goes a bit too hard for a card game to be honest. Except for the laggy menus and questionable restrictions on gamemodes I have nothing to complain about.About the video game that is, because I have a lot of problems with Yu-Gi-Oh itself. I really don't like the current meta, the game basically revolves around making your opponent do as little as possible with negates, floodgates, handtraps and the such. Turns drag on way too long, I mean we all have seen the memes. Some interesting decks are completely unplayable, because they have been powercrept even though they are not that old. Generally this game is a mess sometime. All in all, if you enjoy Yu-Gi-Oh and just want to play it with random people, just get this game. If you are new to Yu-Gi-Oh, get ready to go through hell and back just to learn how to learn the game properly, but I think either way it's worth a try.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a John Wick fight scene but not just with guns: The two fighters are doing a crazy juggling act with grenades, Molotov cocktails, dog poop-filled baggies, literally any handheld lethal item you can hold in one hand. They not only have to keep up an appearance for the crowd, but also try to kill their opponent. You see them start to do a deadly dance-off wtih each other, with landmines, claymores, and cooked grenades littering the place. All the sudden, you hear an explosion and soon every single explosive in the room sets off. You see one of the fighters struggle for one last breath before they're executed Mortal Kombat style, until they're demolished in a pile of viscera that was once human.This, my dear reader, only captures a fraction of the least chaotic match in this game.10/10 git gud

_childDocuments_.review: Master Duel is great. The music is especially top notch, and that alone is a huge plus for me. It's true to some extent that you're going to see some duels that amount to "I have about 6 negates, gone through half my deck, and have a full board" after only turn 1. I also agree with the notion that perhaps the time limit is a tad high, but I don't think it should be lowered by much if anything. But not all duels will be like that, and it's likely best if you approach the game with an open mind, especially if you're new. Solo Mode is a decent starting point to review the many types of decks you could face against.Master Duel, much like Duel Links, is meant to be more like a journey. There's going to be cards that you might think are downright bonkers. There's going to be duels where you feel like you never played at all. But I imagine this is just the beginning for the game, and perhaps future features will add more dimensions to the game.It's going to be a little difficult to make more decks past one or two (if you plan to be F2P), so you will need to be somewhat decisive with your deck choice at first. The crafting system is a good feature, and I hope it doesn't get worse later on. Generally, it's worth giving it a legitimate shot if you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who used to love Yu-Gi-Oh, I actually enjoy the newer mechanics like Link monsters and such. However, the current state of competitive Yu-Gi-Oh has left me wanting. It feels like the game has become solely focused on having the precise exact counter to your opponent's combo. If you fail to draw your out, get ready to watch your opponent spend 5 minutes or more doing their combo, setting up multiple negations and counters, watching them go through the motions can last for what feels like an eternity. Then your turn and the rest of the match just becomes more of a spectator experience than an actual chance to play the game. It's less of an actual interactive player versus player card game and more of who gets the chance to solitaire first.I'm sorry to say but I find it difficult to recommend Yu-Gi-Oh to anyone in its current state. It has transformed into one of the more frustrating time wasting modern card games out there. However, I suppose if you're willing to download and duel friends with some fun goofy decks then there's still some fun to be had somewhere in there. Otherwise it's just best to steer clear of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an avid yugioh player and have been for over 10 years in the tcg scene, so when I saw they were finally releasing an "up to date" simulator for yugioh I was gassed! When the game launched I was on it but quickly realized that the game was two sets behind (currently 3), is best of one format and to top it off, uses an older OCG banlist instead of the current TCG banlist. My initial reaction to this game was "They lied to us, what the ♥♥♥♥ is this pile of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" and to be honest could you blame me? They advertised the game in a way that made it seem like you had so many options and that we could use this yugioh simulator for ACTUAL tournaments so you can imagine why me and many others were initially upset with this game. After clocking 50 hours now I can't lie, I'm enjoying it. I'm f2p but have 5 decks (4 being meta, 1 being fun) and the availability of it being on my phone as well always helps when I'm doing nothing. They give you a lot of free gems at the start of the game which is really nice and the game does give you a lot of gems for ranking up. If you;re a casual player you will really enjoy what they give you in this game. For me personally at the moment I would say I am bored of this game but thats only because I've wizzed through a lot of the content quickly. I can imagine the average player wouldn't be bored as of yet. Another thing thats a let down at the moment is the battle pass. A lot of the TCG community completed the battle pass in less than a month and now they have to wait 2 months for a new one. I say at the moment a lot as well because I know that Konami will bring in some sort of changes to compensate for this because they have been more active in changing things in this game than any game from yugioh in the past. They actually seem invested in master duel and only wanna make sure people stay for the long haul. I would definitely recommend this game to people because its a nice insight into yugioh and the game is very F2P friendly as long as you know what you're doing and what a few youtube videos before hand. overall I would give the game 7/10 but I know that if they make the ranked experience a little more rewarding, add an optional best of 3 format and update the sets in the game to real time then we definitely have a solid competitor for 10/10 card game simulator in my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really disappointed in what Yu-Gi-Oh! became now. I have been a big fan of the first generation of Yu-Gi-Oh!, but man, things have changed a lot since that time. Few things that I don't like about what Yu-Gi-Oh! became now:* It is so luck-dependent. Your first hand will probably determine if you will be winning the match or not basically. Back in the days, the game lasts quite long, and is less luck-dependent than now in my opinion.* It is not a duel anymore. It is more "you vs you", than "you vs someone else". It is less interactive especially when you see someone spending half of their time trying to do different combinations on their own. * It is not much balanced. I know that there are much more combinations and things to do now, but I guess that you just need to make two or three strong decks from the internet, and get used to them, and that's it.* I have never encountered the abbreviation OTK in a card game before until I played this game. (OTK stands for One Turn Kill). I won't even comment on this!Anyway, back in the days, summoning an 8-star monster was the apex of the match. Now, with those new kinds of summoning, it is a normal thing to have three 8-star monsters sitting around next to each other with very strong effects. Sorry not sorry.

That includes the past month or two when I thought it was safe to resume playing Duel Links and Master Duel, after having seen no mention of NFTs in Konami's more recent investor reports. But I didn't trust Konami to actually stop attempting to make them, so I still held off on purchasing any of their products, or anything within their products.Lo and behold, their 2024 investor report says they're still attempting to get into NFTs. The first time, I held off on Konami for 6 months, hoping that would be enough time for them to get the craze our of their system. The second time, when the investor reports revealed they were still interested in NFTs, I held off for a year. Whether or not they actually produce any NFTs within the time, short of an official statement, it seems I'll have to hold off on Konami products for 2 years this time.Here's hoping they'll conclusively and officially end their ridiculous attempts to break into the troublesome (and already dying) market by then. I'm certainly not above giving them 4 more years to think about it if they're still uncertain.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be great, even for a free to play player (I have not spent a dime), but I have a few tips for those interested.  FIRST: spend gems gained as a new player on specific packs for a deck you plan on playing (I play a "swordsoul" deck so i opened mostly packs that would get me those cards). SECOND: complete solo content missions. They give 200 gems for each one you complete. THIRD: craft staple cards by breaking down cards you will not use. This will help you not get blown out in games. I played Yu-Gi-Oh as a kid and recently got into it on Master Duel. It can be great if you are able to make a functioning deck with the ample gems they give you when you start out.  Good luck and have fun, duelists!

_childDocuments_.review: I really love Master Duel. I think it is one of the best forms of YuGiOh out there. The formats tend to be diverse, the game is F2P friendly. but I don't think I could bring myself to suggest it. I've played it on all platforms, and Steam is my least played by far. I'd estimate I have closer to 1,500 hours. And I don't regret it. The game is crisp and responsive. The devs tend to be somewhat responsive to new issues that pop up, and are pretty generous from a currency standpoint. Looking at Master Duel as a gacha, it actually is pretty decent. But when you look at it from a card game point of view, it just comes up short. They constantly add in new events, but then lock it away. There needs to be a way to play multiple formats, or at least have them on a constant rotation. The events add in so much for when the ladder is failing. There is no way to craft every card in the game. They are slowly (VERY slowly) adding the forbidden cards as craftable (things like Pot of Greed), but other cards they just haven't done yet. If they allowed all cards and a custom format for Duel Rooms, this game would straight up replace nearly all other forms of digital YuGiOh. The only thing that it would be missing is some form of limited play, but I wouldn't be surprised to see that come up in the future. YuGiOh is such a weird game. I don't think I can recommend it to anyone that isn't already into the community. It has always failed to capture new players, though Master Duel helped at the start, a lot of those new players have dropped off. They have it so close to being perfect, they just need to bridge the gap.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review of not just Master Duel, but of Yu-Gi-Oh! as a card game in the modern day. I understand many look to platforms like this as the best way to get into a game that would otherwise cost hundreds of dollars on paper.Yu-Gi-Oh! is a challenging game. It will test your ability to read and comprehend large quantities of legal text, and then it will ask you to make connections between each one and form a deck that either puts massive numbers on the board to defeat your opponent instantly or to put together a team of the most oppressive legal texts on the field and lock your opponent out of using his legal texts at all. I'm serious. Half the time you're waiting to do something, the rest of the time is you discovering that you never could have done anything from the beginning. That said, I love the game. I (mostly) love this platform. Aside from the way the game makes good decks hard to obtain and forces you to grind for a pittance, the game is visually excellent and makes the game fairly easy to understand and learn. A card will glow if you can use it, which means you always know if you have a play to make. You could (theoretically) learn the entire game through trial and error, putting down different cards each time and discovering what doesn't work until you find the most optimal combos.You can discover good combos pretty easily via competitive ranked. Your opponents will be all too happy to teach their combos by grinding you to bits. That said, good luck building the decks you see without dismantling every rare card in your collection. (To explain that, any Common or Rare card can be built essentially free. All Super Rare and Ultra Rare cards must be earned through literal luck over months. If you want specific SHINY cards, that's a whole new level of 1% chance RNG.)All that to say, Konami wants to make money and nobody's allowed to stop them. Other than that, this is Yu-Gi-Oh's best OFFICIAL form, and Yu-Gi-Oh's best looking online form ever. Well done to Konami for finally making a duel sim that lets you play the modern game normally without paying money.
