_childDocuments_.review: If you want the OG Tactic Ogre experience, it's more recommended that you just play the PSX vers. Or the PSP vers. if you don't like the gender-gated classes and instant death upon KO of your characters.even FFT (PSX and PSP) is a better representation of what Tactic Ogre was than this... "Tactic Ogre lite".it used to matter where you put your character and which direction they face. While this is mentioned in the tutorial, in this game, you will pretty much get a 100% hit chance unless buff or debuff is in play, or enemy over-levels you by a lot. You also won't dodge unless via weapon's passive parry skill.while archers are no longer overbearingly frustrating to deal with, they also become a joke when you walk them down with a band of knights, laughing at their pitiful arrows dealing barely two digits of damage. This make certain map a walkover, and certain fights like Leonar frustrating as Arycelle barely deal two digits of damage.100% hit chance skill now gives guaranteed debuff chance instead, this actually make debuff weapons overpowered and in return, debuff classes less significant.it no longer matters how you equip your characters, the WT shaved is not significant nor it will boost your dodge chance, as def stat become your only defense.grenade weapons are removed from game... this also affect fights where enemies are suppose to use grenade weapon against you, making them a cakewalk.cleric's heal no longer scale with their level, making their heal overpowered in early game while underperformed in the late game. All the while you have easy access to healing items that outperformed clerics.no more random encounters is both a blessing and a curse, on one hand, you no longer get screwed by random encounters; on the other, you don't have an extra source of income and recruit until you unlock maps like Phrompa Wildwood.Shops also no longer sell different type of recruits outside of warrior, wizard, rune fencer, cleric, archer; you will no longer gain access to extra units until the story says so. This also mean you have to face certain scenario where the game expected you to have access to extra units, when in reality, you are progress-locked out of those unit.while tarot card system is interesting, but enemies seem to have no concept of which card is beneficial, they often don't even acknowledge existence of said card.assigning certain skills to auto triggering chance sound good on paper, but also make A.I. decisions confusing and certain fights frustrating. The prime example being Meditate, spellcasting classes used to spend their first turn few turn consuming magic herbs as it is the quickest and most reliable way to regenerate MP. Enemy AI never seem to realize meditate recharged their MP and still wasting time with magic herbs.then we have Rune Fencer that become overpowered as all most skills are now MP-based and they have access to auto-meditate, throwing devastating weapon skill left right and center.all in all, it seem like they stapled all the new system and streamlines on without making the game compatible to all those new changes.the only saving grace is that it's on pc, there might be mods in the future that fix all these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's why I refunded. For a game that requires a LOT of button inputs/ mouse clicks per battle, why the F**K  can't we press a key mapped to specific actions such as move, attack, end turn etc. It all has to be navigated via menus. The tediousness of making every single unit do super basic things in a game that's a remaster of a remaster is mind boggling to me. I would adore this game if the control scheme wasn't so unbelievably idiotic by today's standards. A true SHAME.Edit: This game is meant to be played with a controller. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, while I still  have lots of praise for this game in terms of quality of the overall remake, I have to rescind my positive recommendation. The final three stages of this game's main story are unforgivably badly designed. 1 - The final battle sequence is too difficult. Heck, the battle leading UP to the final battle sequence is far more difficult than any other step of the game to that point, which leads into the next point:2  Nothing in the game prior to the final battle sequence prepares you for it. It is punishing in a way that is never reflected in the game up to that point. I'm sure those who are intimately acquainted with the list of buffs and debuffs that the game never gives you an explanation for, who know how to ideally equip their characters for every role and have already worked out how the AI will respond to certain things are going to just clown me with a 'git gud', but this isn't a game at this point, it's a homework assignment that you can't get a passing grade on without bribing the teacher.3 -The save system is poorly designed for the final sequence of story-line fights. it is impossible to adjust your troop configuration and then save before entering battle. You have whatever you used for the first fight in the trio of battles which only allowed you five units. Positioning and item load-outs are critical for difficult battles in the game, with a particular unique positioning mechanic coming into play for the final battle. Fine-tuning is often required to do well in fights, but here is nothing but 100% disrespect for the player's time. If you have all the time in the world, you can simply let your party get wiped out and start over from the beginning to keep your troop adjustments, but actually save them for future play sessions as you grind your head against this poorly balanced fight? Nah, not allowed.I am really loathe to do this, as I like the overall quality and polish of the remake. I would like to see SE make FFT again along this level of quality, but I see now why other players have gotten so angry about the inability to out-level content. The designers apparently ran out of ideas for how to make the fights challenging without making grind your only weapon against them in the earlier games, then figured out that level capping you could keep the challenge consistent through the game, but forgot that they had gone haywire overpowering the last fights in the past.TLDR: I want to like this game, but the final sequence is as if you had to fight ruby weapon instead of Sephiroth to see the ending of FF7. This game sadly deserves to be a niche game that only those with infinite time for it like in its current form due to this stupid, stupid design choice.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent tactical RPG that somehow fit on the SNES many decades ago. No idea how because there's so much going on here. If you aren't ready to spend upwards of an hour between battles tinkering in menus, you might want to look elsewhere. There's a ton to figure out, and I found myself getting lost in customizing my party sometimes, but as someone who really enjoys tactics games, I had a blast the whole time.There's a branching story and you unlock the ability to go back and try different choices in the endgame, and there's a ton of endgame content to explore if you really feel the urge to keep playing.This version of this game has level caps, which are apparently a little controversial. I was initially annoyed at not being able to just simply grind past difficult sections, but I ended up appreciating how the caps inspired me to go back to my party and figure out what was wrong. I ended up with around twenty characters that I was switching between depending on my needs, and I found that spending time to scout the map and customize my items and party was actually needed. You can't simply power through everything, you need to actually use... well, tactics. Bring the right items, use the right weapons, use the right classes with the right skill loadouts... like I said at the start, there's a lot going on in this game.Definitely worth it, but be ready to get frustrated when it starts because there's so much going on, and be ready to encounter a couple of walls here and there. My tips to you - recruit new classes often, check your loadouts, and scout each map before you start to ensure you're bringing the right combination of stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: The PSP version remains the definitive experience. The new combat system is streamlined, but it leads to lackluster and slow combat, even when using fast-forward. Classes don't need to be leveled any more and there is a party level cap, yet weapon skills (finishing moves) need to be slowly grinded out. TP has been removed, but now finishing moves now use MP, which leads to ridiculous decision making between using (generally) inferior action skills vs a finishing move for the same MP cost. Battlefields now have random cards around which significantly boost stats for the fight, but many story battles have bosses with a full loadout of cards, doing ridiculous damage. The whole card thing is probably the biggest issue -- an archer with 3-4 physical cards or a wizard with 3-4 magic cards can one shot generics. The RNG doesn't stop with the cards though, as many skills like berserk and meditation are 100% randomly triggered on start of turn -- and the activation rate is modified up by, yep, an RNG card.The changes lead to boring combat with giant HP pools that can swing wildly depending on a bunch of random factors. I'm  on fast-forward with AI combat on for most fights just so it goes a little faster. There are only a handful of story battles that are tactical in any sense of the word, due to randomness and also due to the atrocious combat AI. Nearly any fight can be won with any party composition by either just forming a defensive box and waiting for the AI to trickle in or by rushing a few physical+ or magic+ cards, getting some MP, then rushing and assassinating the leader.The PSP version isn't flawless, but for Let Us Cling Together, its the most fun version. Reborn plays more like FFTA, especially with the cards.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever play Final Fantasy Tactics War of the Lions and think to yourself, "Gee, I really like this game but I want something that doesn't have dynamic class trees, the ability to grind a few levels to stay above fighting against lousy RNG, nor do I want the ability to create cross class hybrid characters, also I need an even more annoying Argath that stays around much longer (and voice acted!), not to mention I hate my ability to see what my skills I might gain/have access to through leveling up a class, and I really want annoying guest characters that get in the way and are half the time casting/attack random things every single fight that I can't control!"Well look no further!  This game is a far cry of the psp gem and is reduced to "go in and fight it the first time to see what the enemy against you has, push as far as you can to see everything that can be thrown at you, then restart and select a team built around fighting those specific things, rinse, repeat."

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, I've played the original SNES version some twenty years ago, that game already felt dated back then and filled with mindless unfun grinding. However the story and the branching paths left a great impression and I'm glad they remade this for steam.This remake has a lot of good changes (though some of these could have been from the PSP remake). For example, the dialogues are a lot better written, the voice acting is great, the music remasters are amazing.  They've added more story and side quests to the game and even some new classes. Graphics wise, the character portraits look alot better, not much change to the sprites, though, I wished they could have done something more than just a filter.What I like most of all are the changes to classes, unlike in the original version, where for the most part the only difference between classes were their level up stat growths, since everyone could equip just about everything, there really was no point in using anything other than ninjas, archers and mages. In this version, every class has their own unique skills, weaknesses and equipment choice which allow them to perform different roles on the battlefield. The limitation of 4 skill and spell slots I feel is plenty and tests your decision making ability regarding what units to bring and what skills/spells to equip based on the battle map and the enemy units. Scouting prior to battle was not in the original and this is a very welcome addition! There is a lot less grinding compare to the original game. Back then, to level up your under leveled characters safely you basically need to unequip your characters' weapons and let them punch each other for 1 damage in training mode over and over and over again for fewer and fewer experience points. It was time consuming and unfun. In this version, you just bring your under leveled guys in their normal gear and fight against AI enemies and they will all level up to your top guy's level after just one or two battles. I am very grateful for this change as it respects my time alot more.I also like the fact that the newer equipments that you unlock/find as the game progresses actually feel like upgrades instead of downgrades. In the original game, the weight of equipments played such an important factor that it was more beneficial to just equip an early game weapon and not much else because it allows you to act more frequently than all your enemies without sacrificing much damage each hit. If you instead chose to fully arm yourself using later game equipments, maybe you'll receive 30% less damage and deal a bit more damage per hit, but the equipments weighed you down so much that all your enemies basically can attack you twice before you even get to move once. The detriment of the weight increase far outweighing the benefits of the stat improvements for later game equipments was simply absurd. Thankfully, this version has corrected most of this by reducing the effect of equipment weight which allows later game equipments to actually feel like upgrades.There are alot of reviews complaining about the game being too difficult due to the level cap and enemies being 1 or 2 higher level than you and having access to magic leaves. A lot of these reviewers I feel only focus on the Advantages the enemies have over our army and not all the advantages that our team has over the enemies, I'll list a couple:1. Crafting equipments- For most of the game, the enemies do not have the +1 equipments that we can craft for our units. These weapon upgrades offer better stats, water movement and best of all, allow our units to move one square further than enemies' can. Some weapons can also cause useful status conditions when upgraded to +1.2. Healing items- we can get healing items in shops which heal our characters much more than the enemy has access to at just about every point in the game. 3. perma death- most enemy units just die after you reduce their hp to 0. In the original SNES version, your units also die permenantly when their hp gets reduced to 0. In this version, your downed units remain on the battlefield for a set period of time and can be revived using items or spells.4. Status spells- currently the enemy AI cannot cast status spells (this is a bad thing which I hope the devs will correct). Being as it is currently, it just adds to the number of things you can do that the enemies can't. Making use of the above list should help you get through most of the game quite easily.While I have alot of good things to say about the game, I also feel there are many areas that can be improved. Namely:1. Progression- there are a good chunk of missions in chapter 2 or 3 whereby your army is stuck with the same level cap, same equipments and same classes. This can give one the impression that we are not making progress during these missions.2. Lack of interesting Loot until late game- in the original game, throughout the story, every so often you would get a unique equipment like an elemental weapon that you cannot purchase in shops. In this version, the story mission Loot drops are very boring. It seems all the unique equipments are now exclusive to the Chapter 4 dungeons.3. Uninspiring Late game relic equipments and spells- The relic equipments you find in Palace of the dead are often just elemental variations of each other, with the same elemental adverse effect  and some free uses of a single target elemental spell. The shop crafted weapons are more interesting in comparison. The new Ninjutsu summoning spells are just weaker versions of the mage summoning spells. The draconic AOE spells are just shorter ranged, more costly and  more damaging spells than the common AOE spells in shops; and Apocrypha spells are just shorter ranged, more costly and more damaging spells than the draconic AOE spells. The devs should have kept the spells' original effect in the old game version and just tweaked the damage numbers for balance.4. Dodge/parry/block mechanic- 99% of the time attacks just don't miss regardless of where you and your opponent are facing. In the original game, attacking your enemies head on reduces your chance to hit, which makes sense and would encourage more tactical play. 5. Monster units- these are actually alot more viable than they were in the original game, which I am grateful for, but most of them still fall off hard after Palace of the dead as they cannot compete with human characters with palace of the dead equipments. Monster units can only wear accesories, but why not introduce some monsters only accessories to help them keep up?6. Unclear descriptions- the game does not give clear descriptions on alot of things, such as how much beast masters boost beasts' damage, how elemental resistances on equipments work (apparently works differently than how most would expect), how much instill actually increases your damage etc. etc. There doesn't appear to be anu in game tutorial describing what all the different status effects do either, such as false step, leaden, spoil spell.7. The demi human classes should have unique sprites and portraits that make them distinguishable from other units of the same race.Despite the above problems, I ultimately feel the good of the game far outweigh the bad and my play time should reflect how much I enjoy it. Hopefully the devs will update the game to address some of the negatives I pointed out, it will get a near perfect score from me then.

_childDocuments_.review: When they call Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together the "crown jewel of the tactical role-playing genre", they're not lying.   LUCT set the standard for gameplay, presentation, combat depth, and most of all storytelling.Reborn is the 3rd Re-release of LUCT, and continues the trend of rebalancing and reworking combat to provide engaging and fun gameplay for new players, and a fresh challenge for returning fans.   Also added in is a completely re-orchestrated soundtrack and full voice acting.Reborn also has added new and returning features to respect your time more.  Gone are random battles outside of specific dungeon areas.  In it's place is the return of the Training feature in camps, plus new experience charms to help you bring new characters up to speed faster without needing to simply grind.

_childDocuments_.review: One step forward, two steps back.I don’t care about the price. I think the work with the gameplay changes, orchestration, and the voice work (although in many cases dubious) justifies it.What really bothered me was the change to how classes and skills worked: there is no more mixing and matching of skills. Each class has its own set of skills it learns, and you have no idea what they are and what level they learn it unless it’s learned. This means if you need a Cleric in your team, there is zero reason to change its class.The 4 skill limit is good in theory: make skills more impactful but limit them even more. My gripe is if your class is a damage dealer (majority of them), you NEED one slot for a weapon skill. Doesn’t matter if you have the latest equipment and level capped; if your weapon skill is too low, you will deal as low as 1 damage. This limits your skill slots to 3 in practice.It gets even worse. Because a unit is incredibly hard bound to a weapon skill, if you want to change classes, you WANT to pick a class that uses the same weapon, limiting your class choices. You can attempt to remedy this by slotting other weapon skills which accumulate XP at a slower rate, but this means you have even less skill slots to play with. There is a catch-up XP mechanic involved, but that is several battles worth of your unit being useless.A One Vision type of mod with this as the base will probably be the definitive version of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tactics Ogre: Reborn

_childDocuments_.review: For now I like the changes they made, if I want to play old version I got psp emulator, or my trusty psp.Faster game speed, is a godsend especially mid and late game. Crafting ui is miles better then psp version.Changes I like are as follows, characters leveling, and not classes, for me lack of grind in that department, opened up drive to grind in others, more important one, that improve my character, and not allow me to play that character.Ai overhaul is quite nice, they removed rogues, and AI doesnt use debuffs and buffs, but while that was offputting at first, introducion of debuffs in attack abilities, made it so there is ALOT more variety in debuffs present in battles, which is very welcome. Ai still cures debuffs, so thats nice.Training ground, and removal of random encounters (story random encounters are still there, and those are the fun ones) is a positive for me, there are places where you can go and grind, kill, recruit without annoying random encounters. _childDocuments_.review: 100%'ed the LUCT version of the game and I'm slowly working my way through this version now.Over all the game itself is solid. If you're reading this, its a brilliant tactics game that helped define the genre. However most of the changes they made in reborn, while innovative, ultimately feel constraining. For example, they've limited spell slots to 4, so you can only ever take 4 different spells. One or two of which (missile + indirect) are taken by a damage spell of your choice, leaving you with even less spell customization than you'd think. And its unfortunately the same situation with skills, as one will always be taken up by your weapon skill. The cards that drop in battle, while an interesting system on paper, just end up cluttering the field most of the time, often with auto-skill activation up, which most of your units won't even really want compared to the other options. Random battles were also removed, limiting chances to recruit to a few key dungeons as well as removing some of the more amusing battle locations from the game. I've also seen some people complain about the level cap, but in my current play-though of the game, it isn't too much of a concern for me, but it may be for others. Over all, it just feels like they've taken a step back from what Tactics ogre: Let us cling together, gave us. Yes there's bloat in that version, but it also gave us a feeling of freedom when we were putting our teams together that this version lacks. I am grateful that we saw a remake of this game within my lifetime, but I wish they had improved on Luct, rather than take steps back from it. If they ever increase the amount of spells and/or skills you can take, to like 6-8, then I'd probably switch my review to a yes. But until then, with a heavy heart I have to say that this version just isn't as good as Luct so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried SO HARD to like this game.  I tried to like this game for over 42 HOURS and reached the Heart of the Gardens.  I've played Disgaea, Fire Emblem, FFT, Langrisser, and more in this genre, and STILL I CANNOT LIKE THIS GAME.- Every map begins with every enemy aggroed, INCLUDING THE BOSS who ends the mission when killed.  Not much variety to strategy when every strategy is "HANG ON, HERE THEY COME"- Your units will ALWAYS be at the absurdly-low level cap, which is at the same level as every enemy unit- A party AI that you can never turn on in normal missions because it makes your units suicidal EVEN ON ARCHER/MAGE SETTINGS- Most missions have intentionally annoying terrain to deal with, where you are fighting uphill (literally) against same-level enemies with superior positions- All of the above problems made worse by PERMADEATH on all normal missions- And MORE!I am thankful that the genre has moved past this point, and I hope those who are nostalgic for this got what they wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Whelp. Found a new "change" that surprised me. In the previous games, your characters could die up to three times before they were permanently dead. Not in this one. Doing one of the stages that specifically builds for knocking your team off the edge, and I lost a couple of characters permanently. So that's neat. * * *I can't believe I'm going to write a negative review for this game, but hear me out. This review isn't about any of the minor detail elements (that a lot of people don't realize were also on the PSP version) or like the quality of the voice acting or anything. All of that is fine and great. The game looks and sounds really good. But: The gameplay in the game has changed it from a strategy game to something else that's mostly luck based. I'm a huge T-RPG fan. I'm a huge JRPG fan. But this remake has introduced too many random elements into the game, which totally takes away from the strategy and tactical elements to the point that just replaying the same battle can get you an entirely different result. What am I referring to, for people who have only played FFT and the previous TO/OB games? The buff cards and the huge change to skills including the removal of TP. The buff cards are cards that pop up on the battlefield randomly that are powerful enough that you can't ignore them. And they're critical to being able to win some battles because the AI has better gear, stats, and spells. Honestly, this wasn't enough for the negative review, but it did really take the game down a couple of notches because it's now less about having a strategy to beat a level and more about having a strategy to get the buffs. It really changes the meta, and makes certain characters (Canopus) like... Essential. He's no longer like S-tier or whatever, you can't win later missions without him. Spoiler: due to the fact that they've gutted the skill system, and you can no longer transfer skills between classes, he's just going to stay in Vartan the entire time. Here's the real reason for the negative review: The skill system destruction and the change to having some skills be "auto-skills." Before, you had to make strategic choices about using classes like the knight, because you had to pick between using different skills, or just using phalanx to reduce damage. Now phalanx just goes off randomly, and you can increase the likelihood with one of the 4 random buff cards that spawn. Before, you could bait enemy knights into doing things so they wouldn't use phalanx (or spellward) but now? You just might get a run of bad luck and they keep using it, shutting down your ability to do damage. While they gain mana from being hit and kill you. All those choices about using those skills like meditate, phalanx, spellward, steelstance and so on are gone. Maybe they'll get used, maybe they won't. Which makes ninjas less able to use steelstance predictably, leading them to being weird mages and so on. Don't like how a battle went? Reload and try again, because all the random elements means that's the best shot towards winning an unwinnable battle. And you can't ignore those random buffs either. I'm in chapter 3, at level cap, with the best *crafted* gear I can make, and my priest got one shot by an enemy archer than was buffed with two of the physical buffs. Enemy archer at level 19 did 730 points of damage with one attack. I don't know if they'll patch things or do any balance tweaking, but right now the game will just randomly kill you towards the middle. I can't imagine how the end game is. Already casters having functionally unlimited mana causes issues (You can get a lucky 1st action meditate auto skill and cast a spell right away- Enemy warlock hit me with a 1st round Avalanche II on my flyers) so I can't imagine what the end game is like.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I love the Ogre series games. I've played them all, I jumped on this as soon as it was announced, and I'm going to KEEP playing it make no mistake.However the further I get into the game, the more I start to feel like they sorta removed our ability to customize. I don't mind them getting rid of that horrific TP system from the PSP version, or simplifying skills....but what I do mind is them making skills level-gated and non-customizable. For instance when you change classes, you lose your skills and gain the relevant ones for your new class. There's no 'building' option.Also the level cap severely diminishes our ability to grind levels, if we so desire, to make story battles as trivial as we want. Will everyone play this way? No, but why remove it entirely and gate us behind this level lock? It makes no sense and only removes more customization.The last one is not so much customization but replayability. The removal of random battles. In the original, I would often roam the map looking for random battles that had a specific enemy type. or someone with good magical gear that I could take. It was also a great way to level up classes, especially those who were under-leveled. Now we have training which is the same enemies on the same maps, there's no randomness to it. When I first read about 'training' I thought they would do it like the original on the PSX where you split your Clan into two teams and fought it out. That was a great way to level classes that were behind, but also a way to exploit if you desired and power-level certain characters. I'd imagine that's why they didn't use it, but again: why? WHO CARES how we play single-player games?It's a great game, and a vast improvement from the PSP version, but I still feel like they hobbled the gameplay unfairly and for no reason, and as a result we're given more of a 'could've been' product which IS a shame.

_childDocuments_.review: So close to being good.  Here's why I refunded:1. Level caps.  Literally who wants this?  At most, this should have been optional; that way the super hardcore "games need to be stressful" crowd would be happy, and the "games should be relaxing" crowd could grind and play how they wanted to play as well.2. Really poor user design. Why doesn't the game tell you what skills a class gets access to?  Would it have been too difficult to include more information on the classes within the game, to help you decide which class to change into? I should be able to look at Warrior and Knight side-by-side and determine which class has which abilities and stats.3. Very limited customization.  I thought that skills could be transferred between classes once you learned them, allowing for some customizability of your squad.  NOPE.  Most of the fun of Final Fantasy Tactics was mixing and matching skills from different classes, but you don't get to do that here because that would be too fun.4. FIFTY dollars?  Get outta here.Everything else was great, but these four things were really disappointing, considering how easy they would have been to implement.

_childDocuments_.review: Tactics Ogre: Reborn is the remake of the spiritual predecessor to Final Fantasy Tactics.I loved playing Tactics type games, so I had huge expectations of Tactics Ogre which brought about the Tactics genre. I was sorely disappointed.Tactics Ogre: Reborn does not have the huge class customization we know of Tactics games, where you can take skills, passives of previous classes into new classes. Plus, limiting Items, Spells, Skills to 4 slots each, greatly diminishes the customization of each character. All characters feel like rigid roles, that have defined and fixed builds, by that i mean there is no point trying to change roles, and even class changing is limited as you want to keep their roles to do their thing.Added to that, battles feel incredibly long due to the number of characters you can take into and fight. With up to 12 characters you can take into the battle, that is more than the other tactics games i am used to. Plus everyone seems to have much more hp, with hardly any true weaknesses so battles feel like they take 4x as long. Fortunately and unfortunately, there is an AI that you can set to your characters, they make reasonable decisions based on what items and skills you give them, so it can make fights faster, but at the cost of not really playing the game. Overall, Tactics Ogre: Reborn should stay as a historical piece in Tactics games, as this remake did not take some of the more popular mechanics of the genre. Even recent indie games do a better job at the Tactics genre. I would only recommend this as a game to learn where the Tactics genre to come from, and not to actually enjoy as a Tactics game.

The battles now are slow, which some would say are more strategic and balanced but in practice they just feel like a slog. So, long tedious battles and no sense of progression in your characters boils down to what feels to me like mostly unrewarding gameplay.I'm really sad I can't recommend this. I think the game looks really good. It's just I'm already going through the later stages of the game and I feel like I'm not having any fun with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very very beautiful and amazing. I never played tactics ogre so i will describe it to new players and people new to the series. Also i bought this for switch with 90 hours in switch.  bought it on steam and plan to buy the digital deluxe with the sound track. Buying it 3 times lol. Please be patient and read this with an open mind ... SO lets see ...1.Remember this is a remake of a classic, i am new to the series and maybe some others are, but this is remake so expect some negativity from diehard fans. Still it's a beautiful series and beautiful game. Don't stress over too much of the negativity comments this game is a solid gem IF you're looking for a roleplaying experience that is complex and full of game rules and interesting mechanics. Some players may find it too complicated as there are numbers and stats skills spells gear and elemental weakness and strengths. Also complex game mechanics in the battles and fights sorta.2. There is 5 basic classes that are warrior / archer / Cleric / Wizard and / Fencer which is like a jack of all trades but very tanky shaman bard.  There i like 12 or 13 additional classes but you unlock them later in story mode. You build your team (party or squad) and do the story mode to push the story, collect loot, and get levels in your classes.  It plays more like dungeons and dragons but also a little like battle brothers.3. The mechanics are amazing. Examples including - Archers shooting over buildings and cross shots/ friendly fire and not hitting teammates with bows or magic / Line of sight blocking / dealing with undead (clerics hehe) / Fighting Dragons grpyhons undead golems giants orcs faries and other strange wonderful creatures. Although i havent seen much of it, there is like a dozen buffs and debuffs you probably should worry about later in the game. Sleep charm posion petrified fear...that sorta stuff.4. AGAIN this is a unique rpg that plays very unique. It could sorta be like final fantasy tactics but plays more like dungeons and dragons. There is not a easy overpowered way to win. Archers are nerfed and everything is pretty balanced. It plays like triangle strategy but with better crating and customization.  ALSO there is a tavern and class marks so you don't have to get stuck using storyline characters, you wing your own party and good customization.5. There is 2 handed weapons, bows and cross bows, healing and offensive magic, cursing and debuff magic, later on there is summons and some strong specialize magic and you can tame and recruit beast or turn enemy people to your side with a bit of diplomacy lol (beat them low enough to capture them ala aka pokemon but its a little hard) ALSO i seen on streamers that later in the game use magic , weapons and armor gets outta control LOL like floating , flying, teleporting, massive AOE, silencing weapons, critical and truestriking weapons that sorta huge power increase. 6. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely awful remake of a remake. Tactics Ogre: Reborn was a 2010 PSP remake of the 1990s Tactics Ogre, which had good changes. It reworked the leveling system, added quality of life changes, and updated sounds and textures. This is not the same game. It is nominally the same game, which is highly deceiving because it has been reworked AGAIN to a lesser state. This time, there are no noteworthy changes to textures or sounds and what are some of the worst balancing changes I have seen in an RPG.The original title did not have a good story, and since that has not changed, it is still a bad story. The original did have engaging and entertaining gameplay, and the 2010 release expanded that gameplay to create a solid 7/10 tactics experience. After the changes, i'd give this game a 2/10. The story is still junk, but now the gameplay is junk. I wouldn't pay a single dollar for this title if I knew it was reworked this way, and anyone who thinks the changes are good is an archaic masochist.For starters, the game will not correctly resize the window if you have two monitors. It just wont. As soon as the second screen turns on, the game changes both the resolution and aspect ration to some arbitrary values. For a modern remake at this price tag, it doesn't fly. They reworked experience gain to prevent the player from being over leveled for key fights, creating artificial difficulty that wasn't present in the original title. This is not a modern solution. This isn't even a third generation solution. Square could have spent the time implementing level scaling, instead they gave no effort and built whatever this change is. Whichever good-idea-fairy suggested these changes should be permanently barred from working on balancing in any title. There are points in the game where you will hit max level (all characters at 9 for example) and do three fights (20-35 minutes) and get nothing for them, then you will get to a story mission, struggle to win, and still get nothing after the battle besides a max level increase. The player is constantly getting nothing for their efforts. Then, you get passed a max level checkpoint, enemies increase in lv by 2 or 3 instantly, and you are left expected to grind the tedious, boring, and ridiculously easy training levels for an hour just to reach the story enemies levels.The NEW (yes, not present in the first release) in-battle card system is pointless. Going out of your way to pick up a card rewards you with negligible stat improvements, and costs a turn. If you instead spend that turn closing the gap on an enemy and take a swing, or reposition to a good title, in all situations the player is rewarded 10 fold. The cards are best ignored unless they happen to be on a tile you intend on putting a character anyways. There are also dozens of them spawning in every fight, which completely clutters the battlefield and is highly annoying. Even when they are green (permanent stat increase), it's such a small improvement that it would take tens of cards to make a real difference on any one character, and they are rare enough that it's better to just ignore them.Square, why are we gatekeeping progression for a SINGLE PLAYER RPG that is 30 years old? You aren't selling this title to a new audience. Your target audience has an expectation, you marketed the game with this expectation, and you ripped the rug out from underneath them. The team responsible for this game's balancing should be barred. It's ridiculous how unenjoyable this rework is to play. I booted the original up on an emulator and am immediately having a better time. It was ruined by hubris of the development team.Don't waste your money on this trashcan rework of a remake of a game from 1995 like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: 🟢 Great strategic turn-based JRPG🟢 Good story with branching routes🟢 Tons of playable classes🟢 Classes has been rebalanced🟢 Chariot Tarriot is such an awesome feature that allows you to rewind to any of the last 20 turns in the battle. Say goodbye to making mistakes or change RNG to your favor!🟢 Weapon skills are dope🟢 Attacks almost never misses🟢 Lots of super useful QOL features such as AI battle, trajectory and speed up🟢 Easier to level up🟢 Huge amount of contents🟢 After finishing game, you can easily rewind to any point in the story and make a different choice🔴 Skill card system introduced in Reborn version in battles is such an extremely terrible design choice. It makes the battlefield look far too messy and restricts free movement as you're always forced to get those. This has pretty much broken the core vanilla gameplay of original. It boggles my mind why they added this system, all other changes are fine but this one is a deal breaker🔴 Skill card system has made a lot of boss battles very difficult and extremely unfair. They're automatically fully buffed at the start of battle and can easily 1-hit KO any of your unit in their turn🔴 Skill card system adds more RNG to battles as sometimes the cards drop near you and sometimes they don't🔴 Enemy clerics/wizards in EVERY battle always starts off with Magic Leaf which is annoying as you can't even buy it in the game🔴 Player AI hardly picks up skill cards making far less useful🔴 Player AI aggressively uses items. Items in this game needs to be equipped separately and it was a huge headache unequipping items from every characters just to use AI battles or they'll eat all your items up🔴 Auto abilities have way to much randomness🔴 Level cap sucks🔴 When hiring, female counterpart has consistently higher strength than male counterpart which is unfair🔴 Healing does not scale with INT, just why?🔴 Huge HP buff to all units in the game. Battles drag on longer and Beasts/Dragons/Golems takes forever to killAlthough the cons sounds way too harsh, I'd still highly recommend this game to any turn-based strategy fans. _childDocuments_.review: (Apologies if this shows as just a wall.  Steam's formatting is glitching out while I try to type this.  I have had to add horizontal rules to break up sections/paragraphs.)The game is ruined by 2 things, absolutely garbage "guest" (AI controlled teammate) AI and an awful card system.Basically your AI teammates no matter what bumrush into melee range and then immediately die. You can't stop them because you can't moveblock them, you can some times change their gear to ranged weapons which slightly reduces it but not enough to matter, so you end up spending multiple units actions each turn keeping them alive, which when you're fighting normal enemies that can base 2 shot you and potentially 1 shot you if they randomly stumble on a buff card is not good.The second and greater issue is the card system. Each turn a card or two appears at a random point in the battlemap. These cards give massive buffs. But because they spawn randomly you can't control them so depending on bad luck and bad card spawns you might have an enemy that does its normal 50 damage (say) or 500 damage, and you can't control it. And even worse is the fact that these cards are how you upgrade your character, a special green variant of them spawns which gives you permanent stat increases (since they completely gutted the character progression from how it was when the game was released years ago). So the entire game becomes an awful chore of rushing to get those green cards with your units that move one or two tiles a turn and if you have guests hoping to get them before the guests do, because the guests b-line their way to them. And those green cards have an extra awful level, they seem to only spawn when you kill enemies. Except that most "story" missions are geared for you killing a specific enemy and as much as possible ignoring all other enemies. So, because you have no CC, you either have to kill this target enemy and immediately end the battle, missing out on character progression, or keep the main story enemy alive so you can kill the minions to get character upgrades which means you're just letting an enemy that can 1 or 2 shot you roam around freely. It's just a garbage game. Here's hoping Final Fantasy Tactics gets released at some point.Oh and I forgot to add.  The UI is near completely broken.  It just doesn't register clicks some times, other times it does register clicks but targets a completely different thing than what you clicked.  Some times the mouse jiggles around the screen as if it is trying to stick to a UI element while you're moving your mouse cursor which is horrible.  You're unable to do things when you would like to (for example you can't manipulate the camera while enemies are moving).

_childDocuments_.review: So, a new remake of Tactics Ogre.Let me preface this by saying that I loved the PSP version. It does a lopt of good, for the maps, the world-map, the music, among othert things. But why, oh why did it have to be such a step backwards in terms of game design ? A level cap based on story progression, really ? With enemies that are 1 or 2 levels above it, or immediately at the new level cap whenever it is increased ? Limited consumables to switch classes ? What kind of game-designer thinks that adding such restrictions to a type of game where the freedom in the way you play is part of the core appeal is good ? _childDocuments_.review: The best version of the game so far. It is as close as you can get to scratch your itch for a FFT (Final Fantasy Tactics). The game came before FFT so some of the game play system have to be updated. SNES/Sega Saturn/PSX to PSP then finally this version. If you want to be precise it has a mix of Fire Emblem and FFT game play.There are a lot of new features such as graphics, Voice Acting, UI, text fonts, Icons, and game play systems. If you played this game on SNES, Sega Saturn, or PSX that is a lot of ground to cover. I will not discuss that here so i will go with the last known which is the PSP version. Graphically it was pixel but now smoother. There are people that will dislike the choice that Square Enix made but there are players like me who favor what they did. I like Smoother look than Mosaic. If you want to know more on why they did it there is an interview of Hiroaki Kato the producer of the game about the decision. The Cinematics of the game is very subtle because of how small the characters are, hence the reason why new addition of Voice Acting is a warm welcome. If i am not mistaken most of the budget probably went here.For the UI, text fonts, and Icons they have been modernize to fit high resolution monitors. I remember playing the PSP version where sometimes i have to scrunch my eyes to read a text in the party menu. They  change the font and Icons they use from the PSP version (such as spells and Skills). If you go to Warren Reports you can also see that the art of each character is now more vibrant.Now the game play system. There are no more class/job level only character level. Energy consumption to use for spells, skills, and finishing moves is now consolidated to MP only, that is right TP is now gone. Usage of items such as Mend Leaf (lowest potion) has change. It must be equip for each character with max of 4 items per character, and this is also true for spells and skills. Speaking of spells and skills some have been combine, others have been are relegated to equipment, few became innate to the classes/jobs, or they have been completely been remove because of redundancy. But there is 1 weird thing i do not understand, why are Finishing Moves has more than double the amount of slots available? There is now a level cap but it will be unlock as the story progress more so you can not brute force yourself by over leveling, at least on you first play through. I probably miss some minor stuff but as you can see they revamp more than half of the game play system to be able to put the word "Reborn" with it.This game is a Haven for Tactical RPG players. I Have played the PSX version 3 times to recruit different characters then 200+ hours for PSP. I will probably put another 100+ hours for this game so i do recommend it. But you are probably contemplating because of the price. I got the game for $40.00 because of coupon discount and it is a major reason on why i bought the game. If this is your first time picking this game then it is worth it, otherwise wait for a sale probably somewhere around $30 to $40.Last words... do not be afraid to go blind play through because you are NOT going to miss anything. When you finish the game the WORLD (It is actually a acronym "Ways Of Reordering Life's Destiny") System will be unlock. It is essentially a new game plus but instead of starting all over again you can go to each chapter of the story and choose to travel on that specific part.edit: just found out that my favorite VA Gideon Emery (AKA Balthier) is in the game doing Hobyrim voice!

_childDocuments_.review: 23 hours in and I'm just really frustrated. I never played the original versions of this game, but heard it was supposed to be similar to FFT and Fire Emblem: Awakening, two of my favorite games. There is a level cap as you progress through the story. So you can't get past level 11 on all of your party until you've reached a certain chapter, when it will be raised. You don't get crafting until Chapter 2 and then you need a ton of resources and recipes. Changing classes does absolutely nothing and some of the classes honestly seem broken (beast tamer). You don't get to keep any of the skills the character mastered, you auto level skills based on your level as well. Your weapon level can not surpass your character level. The enemy AI is simultaneously really really dumb and overpowered. So if that enemy ninja (a class you don't get access to) collects some cards, has saved up mana, and is within range of your most squishy character...they are dead. It's 2000 gil for a blessing stone so that you can revive them within 3 turns or you lose them forever.The absolute WORST in this game is the freaking "guest" party members. You can outfit them and give them spells, tactics etc BUT YOU DON'T GET TO CONTROL THEM. And they are SUPER DUMB. That healer character who you can't change class and can't outfit in anything other than super light armor...why she will just run straight into battle with no regard for anything else. Doesn't matter if you take away her attack spells and all she's got is healing. The maps are also crappy. Most of them seem to result in an uphill bottle neck or are just a big flat plain that requires no strategy. You just whack on each other until eventually you get the target enemy to end the mission. In FFT and FE:A there was a real advantage to being higher elevation, weapon advantages, or elemental advantages (fire vs water). But in TO, it didn't seem to matter.It really feels like you should just tank all of your party, get the highest attack and highest defense, and wail on the enemy until you win. What's the point of having a beast tamer that can only hit for 20 damage when you can get the Knights to hit for 300+?Other reviewers have said this game was broken after it got updated, so maybe the original game was awesome. Really disappointed in this one, especially after it had been hyped everywhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Background: I've completed everything there is to complete in every official English version of Tactics Ogre. That means PS1, PSP, and Reborn for those curious.Don't listen to the whiners who are crying over skill slots and level caps. Reborn is a blast to play and most of the changes were for the better. The quality of life improvements, remixed soundtrack, and voice acting by themselves already make Reborn the best version. I could just end the review here, but I really want to go to bat for Reborn since too many people are overrating the PSP version. I went back to play the PSP version after beating Reborn and GOOD LORD it's so clunky and slow in comparison. The original is also clunky and slow, but I consider it better than the PSP version because it has a less bloated and more charming game design. I get that we all have our preferences, but Reborn has been unfairly attacked for too long with awful takes. Now, let's talk about some common points of contention with Reborn.1. The Level Caps: In a lot of JRPGs, you can just grind your way out of trouble, but Reborn puts a stop to that. If you want to beat this game, then you'll need to use ACTUAL TACTICS AND TEAM BUILDING. I know this is a foreign concept to a lot of you grinders, but don't worry, I believe in you. Anyone can overcome their tactical shortcomings by paying close attention to the game mechanics. No version of Tactics Ogre is hard once you overcome the initially steep learning curve. Seriously, you don't even have to deal with Fire Emblem-style permadeath AND you have turn rewinds. You have so many tools at your disposal, which leads me to my next point.2. The Skill Slots: The PSP version had 10 slots per character vs. Reborn's 4, but more doesn't always equal better. A lot of the skills in the PSP version were unexciting "tax" skills that were needed just to be able to perform basic functions of your combat role. Also, the vast majority of the exciting skills weren't transferable between classes, so you couldn't even do cool class combinations like in Final Fantasy Tactics. The original Tactics Ogre was never about class customization, so it's always bothered me that the PSP version tried to shoehorn FFT elements in, and unsuccessfully at that. The customization was as shallow as a kiddie pool in practice, and only one lategame special class truly broke the mold in this regard. Reborn cuts out most of the taxes and gives you more meaningful choices to make, despite the lower # of slots. Some skills were moved to crafted equipment, so watching your equipment benefits is now more important than ever. It's a good thing that the much-improved crafting system makes these benefits much easier to manage. It's still not a particularly great customization system, but again, Tactics Ogre was never about class customization.3. Consumable Item Changes: In Reborn, you also have access to a wide variety of useful consumables, with every character being able to equip any 4 consumables to bring into battle with them. The PSP version threw boundaries to the curb by giving every humanoid character the ability to dip into the whole army's inventory, with a tax skill called Field Alchemy needed to access certain higher rank items. This universal item command trivialized battles even without Field Alchemy, though. Spell scrolls were also consumables in PSP, which was beyond stupid given the lack of limitations on them. You could buy them from stores and easily stockpile an insane magical arsenal for your whole army to abuse. I'm so glad that Reborn got rid of those scrolls, because they made the class system and MP system mostly moot. The PSP version in general had no sense of restraint in its game design, which was obviously attractive to some people, but not to me.4. The Random Card Spawns: Now, this change I'm not 100% on board with, but I think it's more good than bad. On the negative side, I don't like the visual clutter of cards spawning everywhere. The maps are nice to look at, but the cards certainly add a bit of awkwardness to the presentation. It's nothing experience breaking, though. On the positive side, I think the cards really spice up battles by giving you mini-objectives to aim for. It's also immensely satisfying to get 4-card stacks on your best units, as they become bosses in their own right. This system might sound too chaotic, but it really isn't in practice. Good team building before the battle and good decision making during the battle will always win the day. Just carefully survey the situation with every turn and make adaptations as needed.In conclusion, I hope this gives you all a more positive vibe regarding Reborn. I truly do consider it the best version of Tactics Ogre, but really, no version is perfect. There are still a few bad design choices and weak story beats that haven't been properly rectified by either remake. With that being said, the overall awesomeness of the gameplay and the story can't be denied. It's given me more than my money's worth, and that's saying something in this era of gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: In short, if you like Tactics Games this is often considered the crown jewel that started it all.--- Pros ---Streamlined the game to make it a bit easier to jump in for first timers (you no longer have to grind meditate playing a class you don't want for a character to get the skill on a class you do want, for instance). Shortening of otherwise ridiculous quests like how to get the one and only Wicce in the game is also a nice boon.Guest AI does seem improved; I remember being extremely frustrated while playing this on an emulator with save states due to units I wanted to recruit running away from my units straight into enemy swords for the PSP version - I haven't wanted to burn down my house yet due to lack of self-preservation of any units I've encountered so far in the remaster.EXP is now given to a unit versus a class - this has a lot of really cool game changes. Didn't realize early on that a certain class fits your play style better than another? That's okay, just swap! All of the skills will be right there at your disposal. Remember getting a really cool unique class like Shaman, Wicce, or Buccaneer at level three from the PSP version and that took some of the shine off this really cool character and class? No more! Characters join at fairly applicable levels for when they show up and if they are kind of low, just throw a bunch of EXP charms at them!---Cons---The sprite artwork just doesn't appeal to me like it did on the PSP - I don't know why Square Enix keeps doing this up-scale/smeared look to their older games when they obviously have the talent/time/people to do a proper redo for their remasters. The portraits for the characters are beautiful and hand-drawn, I wish the same effort had been applied to the sprites.The level cap is probably the laziest attempt to force the game to keep a certain pace/difficulty curve. I think I had a union level cap of 19 from chapter two until deep into chapter three, and then it jumped from 19 -> 22 -> 25 in the matter of maybe four battles. Enemies are frequently at least one level higher than your cap and will usually jump to one level higher than your new cap the moment it's introduced causing you to have to grind training levels - a weird back-step considering the removal of a lot of tedious mechanics the developers recognized as unnecessary and tedious.$50 price tag. If you've played Tactics Ogre before, this doesn't really add much to the experience so I'm not sure for returning players (arguably who a remaster is aimed at) that this is priced appropriately. Over-all this is a game I love and had sunk hundreds of hours into when the PSP version was released. I love being able to play the game on Steam with the modern luxuries of cloud saves and modern hardware keeping everything at a crisp and enjoyable 60 FPS. If you love Tactics games in general I feel this is worth your time, even with the flaws it has.8/10 - I hope someone mods the level cap out of this game or SE patches it to be more reasonable or remove it entirely themselves.

That's really just asking too much. Games with pixel art SHOULD NOT HAVE A FILTER PUT ON THEM. This is very simple stuff. Apparently the original sprites were redrawn, AND THEN THEY PUT A FILTER ON IT. _childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Mind that these impressions come from a person who has gone through the SNES and PSP versions multiple times and I'm only in the early game because these love projects should get the visibility they deserve.This is far more than I have expected when the game was initially announced.  They could have stamped some graphical overhauls. options, achievements and call it a day; they actually changed A LOT.Overall I think that this is the best SRPG you can get on PC right now.  Between the changes listed below, the new music, the voice acting, it isn't broken, it isn't bugged and looks REALLY nice (except for some textures they could have upscaled) and that IT IS TACTICS OGRE ON PC; it is a must-have.I'll list the first few changes I noticed that I feel add a lot to the experience for veterans of this game:- They went back to the first iteration of the leveling system.   No more class leveling, yay!- Level Cap.  No longer cheesing it in Tynemouth Hill.  You are allowed to "overlevel" for a few in case you are stuck but you'll have to fight fair.  The good thing is that your under-leveled characters will get all the XP as the capped ones just don't consume it- They reduced the difficulty of some battles such as Qadriga or saving a certain character that used to be a complete RNG nightmare- RT is gone.  All goes through MP, for better or worse.  Now Finishers work as damage abilities instead of ultimates- Except for Denam, you can now change the affinity of characters through charms- Loot actually matters now.  You can't print money anymore because training battles don't produce any kind of loot and you need to hunt down those bags in the story battles.  I assume the multi-stage locations of the late game will allow for some farming but the early game is much more interesting now- Bonus objectives.  They are sometimes loot, sometimes spells, sometimes charms; worth paying attention to those- There are loadouts now and you can filter by race or class.  They want you to have 100 actively used characters instead of the usual "main 12"... And you can keep a certain high-maintenance archer happier in some cases- They nerfed the ones who needed to be nerfed.  The Winged ninja doesn't do the early game for you anymore (well, he kinda does but it isn't so obvious anymore)- Skills are VERY streamlined.  No more 10 item lists you have to review and replace.  Skills are down to 4 with many of the old ones becoming mechanics and "auto" skills to save you the extra "Meditate" input you saw whenever you closed your eyes- Spells are equippable and up to 4 as well.  Choose your magic and live with the consequences- AI controlled characters is still there, don't freak out.  They even added a toggle for All AI on or off before starting battles- They changed how consumables work.  Read that tutorial.  BTW @Devs: Add a toggle on the AI whether if items should be used or not, PLEASE- They added a newly randomized card system that can be absolutely chaotic.  I personally like it but it can be off putting to veterans of this game- They overhauled and FIXED crafting.  It even has shortcuts now- Charm doesn't affect only the opposite gender now.  While small, it counts- There's a "kind of faster" toggle-able mode.  I'd like a x3 somewhere, eventuallyOpen for discussion! Maybe I forgot something.

It's similar to why I hated Triangle Strategy. Stop dumbing down games and selling it as "Simplified". It's trash. One last note, I almost *never* write bad reviews and grew up as a big fan of Square games. Yet, this is the second game in my favorite genre released by square that I couldn't enjoy. _childDocuments_.review: It's great but incredibly dense and unfriendly to new players.Not gonna lie, there were multiple points when I was ready to drop this game.  I almost dropped it an hour in when I saw how much micromanagement the inventory and party management systems require (I decided to ignore these until they became impossible not to).  I almost dropped it about 10 hours in when I had no idea what was happening in the story anymore and battles were becoming a chore (I started looking up story summaries and exploring new party compositions).  I was near my breaking point 20 hours in when I kept losing a battle so badly I didn't see a way to move forward (this was when I learned about items and how to grind while being AFK using AI).The story and overall battle systems are fantastic.  I'm honestly shocked there's so much here since this was originally a SNES game.  There are multiple turns in the story that are shocking and memorable.  When you're not futzing around in party composition menus, it's a pretty good tactics system. But dang, does this game make you work for everything.  It has no respect for your evening plans.  It expects you to sit there and study it like you're going to take a college final about the game mechanics tomorrow.  Just look at my play time.  75 hours is me "main lining" the game - I did almost none of the side dungeons and quests.Playing this game is like going on an 8 hour hike.  It's brutal, it's unforgiving, and at the end you really don't want to do another hike for a long, long time.  But damn, is it satisfying to see it through.

_childDocuments_.review: I will go in a different direction from most of the negative posts. And this is on top of waiting for the game to be on sale for $29.99 rather than the outrageous price it was originally listed as. I will start with the pros.Pros: The game is a nostalgic revisiting of a game that helped define tactical strategy war games on the console 30 years ago.-Voice acting for all the text (if you like sitting through lots of text and talking, which I honestly don't), but it is still definitely a plus, and I am assuming the voice acting wasn't included in the original. But there is A LOT of blah blah blah and it doesn't make me any more interested in the game.Cons: Everything else.-Super high price for a port of a 30 year old SNES 16-bit game with the type of "upgrades" that modders do in their homes for free. Aren't emulated games usually free or really cheap?-The biggest shock for me was that it still looks like a pixelated SNES game. Its like they used some Photoshop filters to increase the resolution and blur the original art assets. But if you've ever tried to do that to a tiny 1 inch 72 DPI image you might grab off the internet and make it a 600 DPI image that's 10 inches, it still doesn't look good if the image you start with is no good.-You're playing a game designed for a 16-bit console which means it is very limited in strategic / game play depth. I play a lot of strategy games, so this is probably why I dislike the game play so much, but I remember playing it when it came out and I thought it was pretty shallow. It's sort of an RPG with so-so tactical battles, and neither is fully realized. The biggest innovation of this game was the use of 3d terrain with clear distinctions between the height of your square and the height of the enemy square. But that was 30 years ago, even though there are still a lot of games that don't utilize that basic aspect of height differences.-The maps are small enough that there is not a lot of room for maneuver. If you do try to move some people around for a "flank", then your troops just die from being split apart, and for the most part, any of your troops can get hit at any time and it's just a game of how fast you can kill the other people before they kill you. Maybe that is fun for some people, but it isn't for me.-For the lack of tactical depth of the battles, they sure do take a long time with each piece taking a while to move, and then going into a drawn out and repetitive attack animation. This is one of those tricks they used back in the day to fluff out the game so you didn't finish it too quickly.Final thoughts: Most people seem to be complaining about the change in balance. My thoughts are the game is just not fun. A lot of people seem to enjoy the game, or maybe they are just paid to write positive reviews, or there are a lot of people who just like what they like, and often times it might be garbage, like most of the stuff you see on TV or on Steam. I definitely hold a minority opinion. Everyone has different opinions so I would make an educated guess, and use the Steam refund feature after playing for a little bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give a mixed review but I understand now why it has many negative reviews. No, which is why I want to give it a mixed review, but if you came here expecting to play "ogre tactics" you will be disappointed. This game was remade to restrict A LOT of the freedoms you had in the older games from the amount of spells you can use, giving a hard level cap (why?!?!?) limiting the weapons you can equip, etc. I absolutely LOATHE games that limit me like this and don't give me the choice to make my own decisions. If I want to spend hours making an overpowered character, why should I not be allowed to do that after all I spent HOURS doing it? If I wanted to give my mage an actual sword which obviously would not be as effective as other classes, why should I not be allowed to do that? There are also many, MANY other changes that were made to this game that other people discuss.As I said, is this a bad game? No. But is this ogre tactics? No it is not, it's just another turn based RPG now.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the 2010 release, the game features improved graphics and sound, as well as updated game design, bringing to life a new Tactics Ogre that remains true to its roots. Tactics Ogre veterans will experience a game that surpasses their fondest memories, while players new to Tactics Ogre will discover a game unlike any they've ever played. Reborn and deeper than ever, the game enables players to immerse themselves in the world and intrigue of Tactics Ogre like never before. The Valerian Isles, jewels of the Obero Sea. Long a center of naval commerce, the people of the isles struggled throughout history for dominion over her shores. Finally there rose a man to put an end to this conflict: Dorgalua Oberyth. But history would know him as the "Dynast-King." King Dorgalua strove to stamp out the hatred among the people of the isles, and for fully half a century, Valeria knew prosperity. Yet upon the king's death, civil war erupted anew as three factions vied for control: the Bakram, who comprised much of Valeria's nobility; the Galgastani, whose people made up the majority of the isles' population; and the Walister, who numbered but few. The isles were soon divided between the Bakram and Galgastani, and an uneasy peace settled across the land. Yet none believed the calm would last...

name: Sunlight
detailed_description: One tree planted for every download Everything is connected, and Sunlight is no different. For every copy of the game that is downloaded, a tree will be planted. Read more about the climate project on Sunlight's Ecologi page. About the Game Sunlight is a short, vibrant and thought captivating exploration game, from the creators of Among the Sleep, Mosaic and The Plan. Journey into the uncharted forest, guided by the harmonised whispers of the trees. Each tree with different voices, genders and dialects, speaking as one. Taking artistic inspiration from expressionist painters like Monet and Munch and focusing on a powerful 3D audio experience with breath-taking choir work, Sunlight will leave you feeling entranced and in wonder in this artistic approach to telling you a story. Playtime: 30 minutes. The visuals, that were hand painted using Quill, makes the experience feel like exploring a three dimensional painting. The hauntingly beautiful music, composed by Tchaikovsky, was recorded in the Archbishops palace in Trondheim, Norway, and sung by the award winning choir Kammerkoret Aurum. Along with a wide range of voice actors spanning multiple continents, the atmospheric and meditative story comes alive.

short_description: Traverse a harmonious hand painted forest in this first person hike. ☀️The trees guide you with gentle whispers, as you explore a philosophical story.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey through a forest artistically inspired by painters such as Monet and Munch. Each tree whispers the narrative in its own voice which can be male or female and ranging all different kinds of dialects. Sunlight is very short at only thirty minutes of play time.I played through it once with headphones and once without.  The whispering trees tell the story and it just doesn’t work without headphones.Whilst the different voices, harmoniously talking in different genders and different dialects, is impressive, it also becomes quite confusing. Often, I would miss chunks of dialogue because there’s too many voices saying the same thing slightly out of sync and at varying sound levels. Instead of creating an array of different voices which enhanced the narrative, it actually marred the narrative a bit for me. I ended up moving around and hugging one tree just so that I could hear only one voice telling the story. The story was open to interpretation as a lot of games in this genre are. I did find that it felt quite poetic in its approach, using imagery and advanced language to paint its story. I didn’t get much of an emotional reaction to the tale. It was about death and rebirth and a synergy with nature. The forest is beautiful. The developers have deliberately designed the landscape to look like an oil painting and it works really well. The forest is quite uniform however and there aren’t many contrasting areas. It all looks the same. The title is described as an exploration game but I would say this is misleading. Although you can walk around whilst the narrative is being told, there isn’t much to see apart from the forest. There are no animals, birds, items to read or hidden areas. It is a straight walk through a wood that looks very similar throughout. You do get the option of picking up different coloured flowers during narrative breaks but even then, there are only two or three different flowers to add to your bunch as you are walking. I would have liked to have seen water features and buildings in the mix or anything other than more trees. The sound was the highlight for me. Arranged by Tchaikovsky and sung by the award-winning choir Kammerkoret Aurum in Norway. It is stunning and incredibly relaxing. Again, it did feel slightly repetitive but beautiful nonetheless. At the end of the game, you can leave a message on a tree stump which I thought was a nice touch. You walk through a forest listening to a narrative told by the whispering trees. Each tree has a voice, acted in different genders and dialects. They speak almost simultaneously as you pass. Every so often, usually when the narrative prose ends, a flower will appear in a cacophony of light. There are about three of four different flowers to choose from. Walking over to the flower and picking it up adds it to your bunch and the narrative begins again. This is repeated until you have a bunch of five or six flowers and the story ends.  The graphics are gorgeous to look at and are reminiscent of an oil painting. The effect looks spectacular although I did find the environment to look a bit similar and there wasn’t much contrast in areas.Sometimes the forest reacts to the narrative, for example a gust of wind will blow leaves around and the story tells of the forest breathing. It’s a shame there weren’t any animals in the woods to liven things up a bit. Arranged by Tchaikovsky and beautifully sung by the award-winning choir Kammerkoret Aurum in Norway, it lifts and enhances the narrative and gameplay. Now and again, you’ll hear the wind, some insect and bird noises and even wind chimes but I don't think there was enough of them.Curator Info:
