_childDocuments_.review: Short narrative experience of about 30 minutes with an excellent soundtrack and a beautiful landscape. It should be noted that it is not a game, so if you know it's a walking simulator in the woods, no it isn't. It is a narrative in which you are required to move only at certain moments to progress the story. Excessive price, the duration is really very short. my rating 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: For those wondering exactly what this is, be aware, this is not a *game.* There isn't anything to play, or do, nor are there any challenges or lose conditions. In fact, it's barely interactive. You stroll serenely, and you listen. As you stroll, the varied voices of the narrators envelop you, one particular voice occasionally rising above the simultaneous susurration of the others, before gently melding back into the stream of others. You are exploring a forest, dappled in sunlight and shadow. There are no specific points of interest, in a game sense. But you will find lovely clearings where the rays of the sun break through the canopy, and land among the bushes swaying in the breeze, as leaves sometimes slowly flutter past you. In all, this is something to be experienced, not "played." I would describe it as a "visual audio book," as opposed to a "visual novel." Perhaps even "visual poetry."It is beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is done and dusted. I've noticed that Krillbite Studio likes to explore stream of consciousness and the collective subconscious topics in their games, and this is no different. In this one, you are presented with the question of how you would explain the world to your child if your child was born blind.From there, you will spend your time in the game walking through a forest, listening to various thoughts and experiences which serve to address the topic at hand and then expand upon it by diving more into existentialism. The voices are presented as a cacophony of voices, singular voices, two voices, and so on, and it morphs in and out of the various speech formats and patterns. I found it difficult to really hear clearly everything that was being said, but I think that was intentional, as you pick up on the things you pick up on.For me, my first assessment is that all the unique voices a blind person hears become part of their world permanently. But, as the story progressed, I think it was more about the commonality of humanity despite our unique experiences and that our experiences become part of a pool in which we all swim.From a practical gameplay standpoint, you really just wander the forest listening to the exposition while gathering flowers for a bouquet which you will eventually carry to the edge of what has already been experienced by previous player to drop your bouquet along with a closing thought. On the way there, you will pass many other bouquets and their thoughts left by previous players. Which is a really cool idea to close out a game and really drives home the stream of consciousness and collective subconscious aspect of the game.It is a very very slow paced walking simulator despite only being about a half hour in length, so be prepared for that. This is a game designed to engage your mind philosophically. The forest and end area are just vehicles to used to take you there. It's a worthwhile experience in my opinion. Something to be enjoyed once and contemplated for a bit afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little experience of a walking simulator game, with a cryptic allegorical story. The description is very misleading, as there is barely nothing to explore, since the environment and the narration is very repetitive. It's trying to be very "enlightening" game, though with the lack of actual gameplay content, you could call this more of a piece of audio literature.  It would probably hit the spot for a poetry fan, or someone who can make more sense of the story the trees are telling you.Honestly, wouldn't recommend the game, maybe if it was free, then I might.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: For every download this game gets a tree will be planted. (oops, It's not free-to-play, don't know why I read it like that, it's still a cheap experience!)No, seriously.This is the closest I've ever come to experience mindfulness.Every tree has a different voice actor; some old, some young. You can linger by a tree that has a voice you find soothing, or you can walk around and hear how the different voice actors interpret how this story is meant to be told. I met a tree that sounded like Teemo from League of Legends, I met a tree that was read by child that clearly just had learnt how to read - quite cute. Different accents, from all over the world, which made me feel less stressed out on how my own accent is.At the end of the story you get to write a message, be it a secret or something else you want other players to read.I felt connected.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Nice little experience, with a cryptic allegorical story. Turn on subtitles because parts of the game are far too quiet. The description is very misleading, this isn't an exploration game, there is nothing to explore, since the environment and the narration is very repetitive. It's also very short and without much gameplay. The voice from the tree thing doesn't work that well, honestly, but for such a short game it doesn't outstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost: Please attempt to find my bouquet. I'm out there. The quote "If you made it this far, please join me"--that's me. I have no idea if I'm the furthest one, but I know I'm alone in the whispering winds where I keep thinking I heard a small voice asking "do you hear me?" under the rustle of leaves, and what sounds like a living forest walking behind me, close enough to breathe on my back. But when you turn around, there is no greenery like there was in the beginning. That's what I experienced from traveling who knows how long thinking the bouquets led to a path to somewhere. So if/when you try to find me, fair warning it might creep you out and want you to set down your flowers and run away. Instead, think about the life and root network that could have been as you step across stumps and decay.The game is a full-immersive experience, heavily relying on audio--so if you need subtitles put them on or you will get lost in the numerous voices providing a narrative "song" as you walk through forming your bouquet. It's not for those looking for a huge reward or achievements. It has one goal in mind, which is to remind you of the unsettling aspect of what deforestation does: removes life and sound. P.S. If you desire a game with a similar ambiance that makes you reflect in a similar unsettling way when the game ends, I recommend "The Stillness of the Wind." I think these two games compliment each other splendidly.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: It's a walking simulator, and there's nothing inherently bad about that, in fact for telling a non-interactive story it's a good way to make a visualisation. But there are a couple of problems: The pace of walking is tediously slow, and the landscape is pretty but without much variety. So it doesn't feel like you're exploring anything.I don't get the story, and the overlapping voices quickly get tiring and I had to turn on the subtitles, but that didn't make it any clearer what was going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I'm normally a fan of walking sims, but in there's literally nothing except walking forward and occasionally picking up a flower while a bunch of voices chant a story at you. To me, a "first person hike" should have a sense of exploration and different environments, but this game is just holding forward and seeing variations on the same tree over and over again. The story, or as much as I heard of it, seemed to be almost psychological horror, and that didn't work for me with an otherwise relaxing environment. Your enjoyment of this game is going to hinge entirely on whether or not you enjoy the story. I found it boring and nothing else could make up for it. Your mileage may vary.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: It may be my hearing problems but all the voices talking over top of themselves made this "game" activate an anxiety in me.  I could literally feel my skin prickle and myself getting angry.  I had to quit the game due to the jumble of disembodied voices that just made this game unplayable for me.  I am sorry.  The game is gorgeous and I really want to like it.  If you don't have hearing problems, the game is probably fantastic but for me it was just horrible.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals have a unique style and result in a beautiful environment. The sound design is amazing: I had to activate the subtitles to understand well, especially through the multiple voices, but the general effect of having multiples people speaking over each other is interesting and the accompanying music is dreamy. And then the poetry is quite nice and personal. To me, the real problem appears to be the attempt at making this an interactive experience. Walking very slowly through the forest, having the poetry cut by lengthy passages forcing you to find and pluck a flower, and an overall lack of remarkable results to most actions lead to an experience that I found tough to follow through to the end. In truth, I would simply rather read the text, listen to the music, look at the images, individually. While somewhat unrelated, I was also very annoyed but the flowers constantly glitching (like randomly jittering) as I was walking.It's short, and it's not expensive, so you probably don't lose much by trying the game if you enjoy somewhat meditative types of games, but in the end, I can't recommend it myself.4/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interactive poem/narration about life and death whose voiceover was done by a choir in the form of a 30-minute walking simulator with music by Tchaikovsky. It's a genre I usually enjoy, but the game here is too repetitive, it's always about going to the same next bright spot between each piece of poem. The environment seems to be procedurally generated because it's too uniform (just a forest). The end of the game is interesting however, but nothing more.If the project was offered for free I would give it a positive recommendation, but in the context of a commercial project, it seems to me too light in terms of content.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: While Sunlight is a walking simulator, it would be more accurate to say it is a (slightly) interactive art house short film in "game" form.  For anyone reading a review, you probably like this style and are wondering if it is worth your time.   If you don't expect any game elements other than occasional flower picking, I'd say yes, given that it is pretty to look at, the story, while somewhat pretentious, carries emotional weight, and the music and voices blend together to make a nice experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I think there definitely were some interesting aspects to this and I was enraptured by the beautiful scenery, voice acting and music, but there was also stuff that really disappointed me like the 'profound story', the flower-picking, map borders, chunk loading and well... the length, but I knew about that last one going in.So... my experience began pretty normal, listening to narrator tree until he stops talking. "Stopped talking? Is the story over?" I look around and see the fires that he had mentioned in his last words or so... which is great. You directed me without telling me what to do. I see the flower, pick it up and the story continues, but now different voices start talking. At first, I think... "huh... well I kinda liked narration tree better to be honest" So I start to walk back, but... I notice that the closer I walk to trees, the louder some voices become. "How many do they have...?" So I continue to walk around and leave behind narrator tree. At this point, I was having a pretty great experience all in all. Loved listening to the small differences in emphasis or recognizing the hint of an accent or just a voice I already had heard before and the scenery and music were still... pretty amazing.My 'problems' began once the second flower clipped into the first and well.. I generally don't care about stuff like that, but you have this beautiful scenery and now these rubbery flowers that are clipping into each other are constantly on my screen. Around this point, I also started to realize that the story was pretty... slow... and the constant interrupting to walk like... a minute to the spawn point of another clipping flower was not helping. I mean... I get it, you want to have the player do something and with a story like this you want to be descriptive and all that jazz. But... those things were a miss with me.A minor disappointment was when I met the world border at around the 20 minute mark or so. And... well... I was surprised that there was one tbh, because I think it goes against the entire point of both story and game. I expected procedural generation or something, but I guess not? It's weird because there's definitely repeating trees, voices, bushes and everything is pretty much randomly placed, so... missed opportunity, maybe? Lastly... when the game was at the end, the world tries to fade and generate a different terrain as I'm turned away, but for some reason failed to do so and I saw the entirety of the forest just pop away behind me, which ruined the moment in my opinion.I'm not saying this is all in all a bad experience, because it's not... but I personally was always pulled back to the limits of the environment and it just... broke my immersion constantly. Considering the price, length and the, in my opinion, lack of emotional story, I cannot recommend it, but you honestly should just try for yourself because the price/playtime is low and steam refund is a thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: A walking sim that gives a very serene vibe. I love the sensation of walking through the forest with the voices around me narrating a story. However, the 'art' feels shallow and evokes no real emotion, at least from me anyway. I'm sure there was a message in there somewhere, and in some parts of the script it shows beautifully, but as a whole it becomes a mess that sounds deep only for the purpose of sounding deep. The pacing could also definitely be improved as it was a short experience that also felt like it stayed for longer than it was needed to. And a bug in the ending sequence where I was stuck in the text box also did not help the experience.I will give massive props to the voice actors and the artists involved in the game. They did a fantastic job to sell the experience, however the main product and direction were just generally lacklustre. An okay time if you got it from a bundle like I did, but there are plenty of other more fulfilling experiences and walking simulators out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a walking sim, and while the sounds of the the forest are beautifully made, how the game works, is unexplained.The philisophical hike tells a story, that in no way shape or form is philosphy, but just a story. The music is beautiful, but that is to be expected from a piece hat lasted that long.In short, it's a good game to make you tired and go to bed.I give it a Sleepy/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Sunlight is a glacial walk through the forest with narration that changes voices based on your proximity to different trees. The story you're listening to poorly written, with many stock phrases, contrived metaphors, and pointless digressions. The music is good but implies gravity that the game doesn't deliver. This is not a serene stroll through nature, but an overbearing slog through flat terrain. You inch your way toward nothing in particular, click on some flowers, and listen to some drivel with Tchaikovsky playing in the background.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I was not fond of this game.While I liked the sound design and the bunch of voices reading the same text, I didn't like the script. I went from "I don't understand" to "Oh, I understand this part" to "I don't get anything at all, when does it end?". Also, it kind of bothered me that the flowers clipped after being picked up.So yeah, I don't think this game is for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Marmite game: some people will love the ASMR chorus, the ethereal abstract descriptions, and the monotonous aimless forest walking, whilst others will find it infuriating. For my own part, I find the visuals rudimentary and uninspired, the voices and descriptions pretentious, akin to the worst indie theatre acting, and the flower clipping and jittering very distracting. If the flowers formed a wonderful bouquet as you collected them, and didn't phase out of existence as I walked, I could maybe get a bit more into it, but it's absolutely not for me. If you enjoy ethereal walking simulators and ASMR, then the game's probably worth the asking price; if not don't go near it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I don't mind walking sims, or experiences over gameplay. But with the visuals, the promises of exploration, beautiful classical music, and some reviews mentioning how quiet and serene this game was...it was surprisingly the opposite. I was so excited to experience something gentle and beautiful and I would have even settled for just boring. Unfortunately it was a much worse experience for me.The overlapping voices instantly made me feel anxious the entire time and the way the forest darkens between each verse of the story didn't help. There's also some harsh sounds when you pick up the flowers and sometimes during the narration. It was honestly overwhelming, and hard to hear without sticking to one tree, which felt like it defeated the purpose. I had to turn subtitles on but I still ended up not understanding or sometimes missing parts of the story because I was concerned about moving and too anxious to stay still. It turned into some kind of horror game for me.I wanted to try to really like it. I think the concept is still very cool. But everything described was not at all how it played out in the game. The visuals are pretty, nothing too detailed, but it's going for an abstract painterly style which works. The problem is that it's so repetitive I wasn't even sure if I was going around in circles by accident. The gameplay, although not necessary in this kind of game, felt obsolete. It was pretty much a longer and more tedious version of a "continue playing audio" button. This wouldn't be as bad if the visuals didn't blend in and become repetitive as you walk through the forest.The story itself lost my interest pretty quickly and felt a bit pretentious after a while because of how dragged out it felt. And of course kind of terrifying with the multiple voices and music rather than the "gentle whispers" quoted in the description. I do like poetry, but with how it was presented I think it just irritated me. I think I might have enjoyed it in a different format.I didn't get very far in the game until I had to quit for my heart's sake, so I can't say if it gets better, but it seems that the ending is the most interesting part from other reviews. Hopefully if you give it a shot, you get a much more relaxing experience than me!
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I didn't really think anything of it. This morning I woke up feeling a bit off and remembered that I had went out on a limb on bought this game yesterday. I felt unsure about how this would work since there is no way to know what is the right way and what is going to come up to a wall. Then it hit me. That's life. That's what we feel everyday. I had never played anything like this, but now I want to tell the world about it. The feelings I had felt were overwhelming and something that I needed. It felt like someone was there to hug me through all the darkness. So understanding of mental health and the struggles. 10000000000/10. Beautiful.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I won this game as part of a giveaway system a friend of mine does. Please, please, PLEASE play this. It is a very quick game, but it is so peaceful, beautiful, and the storytelling is otherworldly. I was a sobbing mess at the end because of what changed (I don't want to spoil it). Don't sleep on this at all, it is well worth it and more.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Normally, I wouldn't recommend a "video game" such as this one, which does tow the line of whether or not it can even be considered a video game. Sure, it's a video and it's a game so on some technicality, I guess it could be a video game, but for me, a video game usually has progression. It has goals and objectives, challenges and achievements. What Sunlight is, is basically just a short story in the form of a walking simulator that gives you some visuals as it has you walking through a forest while a few different voice actors recite to you the same exact script. The trees talk to you about a “cold, white room in a doctor’s office” or something after a kid licks some sap off of a tree and starts to hallucinate. To that point, with the very little gameplay that it does have, it would have actually been better suited to a VR experience as I think you could much more reliably immerse yourself into what the developers wanted to create.The artistic direction is cool what with it all being hand-painted. I'm not an art critic nor one of those pretentious people who goes to a museum to gaze in immense wonderment at the artwork while I drift off into some fantasy world and spout ad nauseam how deeply intellectual I think myself to be, but after awhile the trees and environment does start to repeat itself and from a distance, everything is rather blobby looking until it renders in as you approach it. I assume this was intentional but I didn't like that choice. It feels like I’ve taken my glasses off and can’t see very well as all the colors are just smudged.The Steam page says something about professional musicians being involved and I was expecting some nice music to listen to but honestly barely noticed anything, except at one point when there was a choir that chimed in for like five seconds. I wondered how a studio like this could have afforded an award winning choir for a game that likely didn't sell very well due to its niche, and it turns out that they didn't really record much music at all. Maybe I'm just spoiled by the likes of Mick Gordon blasting his music as I am slaying demons but this game obviously wouldn't fit that direction as you're slowly walking through a forest and picking flowers to form a bouquet. You do start to wonder what the point of the flower picking is: are you secretly on an acid trip and that’s why the trees are talking to you and why everything looks like it does? Are you a husband who is picking flowers for your wife because she likes wildflowers? It’s actually very clever and is explained once the story finally concludes. Potential spoilers:The one saving factor of this game that actually made the 30 minute story worth it, and what ultimately saved it from a 'not recommended' rating, as I honestly tuned out after awhile, was the seamless transition from forested area to deforested area. The game effortlessly brings you to the edge of the forest just as the story concludes and you come across what is basically a grave site of tree stumps, clearly having been cut down. And as you pan around, you don't see the edge of that forest you were traversing through at all, it's a huge field lacking the beauty and diversity of a forest. Those flowers that you were collecting along the way become a clever plot to the game as you come across bouquets that other players have collected and laid within this destroyed field to give it some color and life, and you too can also lay your flowers down atop a tree stump and leave a message to be stumbled upon by other players. I probably spent about five minutes just reading these messages and it was nothing but positivity and people appreciative of the experience and the messaging, sharing their own loss or giving quotes of encouragement, to which you have to give kudos to the developers for making a game that other people can genuinely enjoy even if it isn't your type of game. It's also pretty cheap, so that helps. Unlike other video games that will waste your time for dozens of hours, this game doesn't. It's just a 30 minute journey and they kept it short before it got too preachy.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Sunlight is a pretty unique experience set to a Tchaikovsky arrangement. It's considered a walking sim by others but in my mind, it's a guided meditation track. For every installation, they plant a tree - big win in my books. If you pick it up, definitely play through to the end. It has a pretty interesting twist. And buy it with the knowledge that it's not your typical game. guided meditation, walking sims, classical music, flowers thoughtful
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful artwork and the voices are all around while going walking through the woods. So headphones are a big need, at least in my opinion. This "game" isn't really a game, but a sort of experience as you listen to the trees speak/read you poetry/narrative.I don't remember how I got this "game", however it was either on sale or in a bundle or steam gave me a discount. Nonetheless I do recommend it, but only to the handful of people who like to just chill and listen to the story. To the other people who are like eehhh, two things:1. Get the game on saleor2. Wouldn't recommend to you if you aren't a huge fan of that style
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Did not like this at all. All the voices speaking at the same time was utterly and painfully irritating, I do not feel relaxed at all. There was a story being told, but I have no clue what it was about. I like the narrators voice, all the rest was bad. I had high hopes, but this was a disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game, actually the experince might fit well. You are collecting flowers while listening a story. There are different voices everywhere. You are feeling more aware and calm somehow. It is so strange that this game lasts almost an hour and can still change your perspective. It totally worths a shot. Be gentle with yourself and take a deep breath while you still can. HF.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely an experience rather than a game. You walk, you collect flowers, you listen to the music and the narration - the voices of the trees. It has a lovely aesthetic and it's rather relaxing, but I think it's a one time only thing for me,it's not something that's got any replayability factor. I did find the ending quite amusing with all the messages left by other players.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Short 30 minute walk through a beautiful painted landscape, listening to music and soothing diverse voices. I almost fell asleep; really wanted to lay down in the sun and just listen. But, I kept walking through until surprise end.  The poetry lingers with me, paraphrasing, "at the end, not that it is the end of the story, but the story keeps going on and leaves me there."
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a walking character that gathers flowers in a forest while being told a story by some unrelenting force.It's not a dramatic story by any means, but just one that will have you think twice about littering in a forest, I presume. In the end, you can leave your own message on top of some cut trees and move on to play actual games. lol
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.  I was hoping it would be a calm stroll in the woods with a nice story.. Instead I got this creepy psychological horror story that included a hospital visit where death could be involved????  It was NOT what I needed to relax and unwind as the beginning stated.  It made me anxious, uncomfortable and wanting to NOT play it again. I am glad I only paid $4 for this or I would be very upset at the wasted time and money.This game is NOT what the world needs during a Pandemic. real or otherwise....because too many people are afraid and have family that have died from a disease or worse recently.  If you like or relax to dark stories...I guess this is the relaxing, end of the day game for you.Otherwise, I would steer clear and let this game go and find another strolling RPG to enjoy that might actually relax you!
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an insomniac and this game made me sleep which broke my insomniac pattern !On a more serious note I personally didn't like this little experience, it's around 30 mins of walking in circles to pick up flowers and listen to voices. The walking pace is super slow and I usually don't mind when it's slow if there's something amazing to look at, but the forest looks the same from every corner. I get it, it's about relaxing, taking our time to listen to the voices, but personally I didn't like hearing multiple voices at the same time I don't know if this is because English isn't my first language but I had trouble to focus and understand the meaning of it. In fact I find this more stressful than relaxing.I had more fun experiencing Antipsychotic with psychedelic visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what the meaning of the story is, if it even has one I certainly didn't pay attention to it.However, the things that I did pay plenty of attention to were the soothing aesthetics, the soft subtle music, the eloquent expressions and descriptions throughout the narration, and the harmonious yet distinct voices soliloquizing its composition.Truly for better or worse it is a piece of art, and in my personal opinion it is a good work of art at that.Very nice to play for a relaxing time.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it to play while drinking wine. Turns out I spent over 30 minutes vibing while lost in a forest walking adrift not knowing what was going on, I didn't realize I had to pick the flowers(now you know you are supposed to pick the flowers) so I literally walked around aimlessly until I accidentally picked a flower. The voices in this game mixed with the ones inside my head, I have no idea what they were saying but some few words are engraved in my head. I literally cried at the end, for some reason I thought I was attending my own funeral. I would give it a 10 for the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely experience.  This games art style is absolutely amazing, the forest feels interesting and never-ending. The overall story is delivered through several voices that make it more relate-able. The story itself is interesting and does well to initialize abstract thought in the player. Overall, I enjoyed the experience. As you pick flowers the game does bug out a little bit and the flowers will randomly twitch.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: It's an experience, that's for sure. And I will admit, even for walking simulator standards it was kinda lacking. The whole experience is just walking aimlessly in the forest listing to a story being told. It doesn't matter where you go, or if you walk at all, after the segment of the story is finished glowing flowers will spawn and you have to pick them up to continue the story. That's the "game".I will admit I wasn't expecting how the story would go, it starts off being greeted by a calming voice telling you to sit back and relax, only for the story to be  at lest from my understanding of it.I will say I'm glad I went into the settings and put the subtitles on. And that's only for the fact that that many voices are reading the story at once talking over each other. As you walk every tree you see in the game has a voice coming from it all reading the story, after finding this out I just found a tree, preferably a bit away from a different tree so I could get a mostly one voice telling the story. But due to the random generation of the forest while walking it's not always something you can come across.After your 30 minute story telling journey at the end Overall, I personally don't think it's worth it. unless you're really curious about the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pure walking simulator, consisting of walking through a procedurally-generated forest while the narrator(s) tell a story.The forest is beautiful, as you can see from the screenshots, but  becomes repetitive. _childDocuments_.review: Awful.   A collection of random voices muttering gibberish in  splat water color forest, and your arms are missing.   You can't understand what they are saying, so just tune them out.  There is nothing to interact with, just painted trees and land, and sky.  It takes a full minute to boot into it, and likewise to get out of it...   Maybe if you waste 20 minutes into it,  you can  find some angle in the 'forest'  to take a few nice screenshots and use them as desktop wall paper.   But not much else in this,  some  additional random moaning  choir music,  pleasant but formless and meaningless.   Pity,  it seemed like it would have potential if they cleaned up the broken audio noise,  reverb overload and overlapping garbled voices.  In SETTINGS -  You can turn down the voices, the Music, and or turn down the nature sounds to Silent.  Try just Nature, no voices, no music.  Then, you'll enjoy a quiet walk in the woods.  It does have an ending once you pick a handful of flowers.  You can post your thoughts at the ending to share them with others.  You could also just put on the music and silence the rest, enjoy the music playing in the background while you work.  But the voices - ugh - babbling gibberish.  Graphics 7/10 - watercolor trees.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I didn't necessarily understood everything that was being told, the combination of all the parts made it feel transcendend. However, it's not just something being told while you walk around. Both the feeling and contents of the narrative are subtly weaved together with what you see and do.With the way the mood was so ambiguous and the story not very realistically inclined, i was fretting the ending a little bit. Of course there was not really an arc to be tied up, but i was afraid it would just end and leave you hanging. But it doesn´t! It has an actual ending, with what I think to be a geniusly simplistic use of an input mechanic.It didn´t even take an hour to play through, and was an encredibly absorbing way to experience poetry, so if you´re on the fence, go play it!

_childDocuments_.review: Sunlight is not really a game, as it features no gameplay.  This is instead a "walking simulator", more art than game.  You walk (slowly) through a procedurally generated forest while long form poetry is read to you.  From time to time you collect a flower which nudges onto the next verse of the poem.  That's all there is to it.  I won't go too deep into the depths of the poem, if you're really interested there's probably a Youtube walkthrough of the "game" which will give you 100% of the experience (which is problematic given this is a product with a price tag on it). I think first up the artistic design here deserves top marks.  While the trees and forest are simplistic, they had an extraordinarily talented art team, and a good artist can make the smallest and simplest of things look visually impressive.  4K support helps, too, and a few graphics tweaks, but not a lot... the visuals for this get a pass.The sound design is also excellent... each procedurally generated tree has one of dozens of voices that all read out the poem in sync.  Walking between trees causes the different voice actors to rise and fall while the poetry drums on.  Great sound design, also really clever.There's a few reasons I really can't recommend this, apart from just the non-game nature of this as a walking sim (and not a particularly deep walking sim, either, compared to the gold standard that is Dear Elise).  The controls are locked which may prevent this game being played by differently abled gamers or gamers using AZERTY or other international keyboard layouts. Somehow, the game is both far too long and far too short.  You can get through this in just over half an hour.  Having poetry read to you for half an hour is actually a bit of a grating experience, to the point I was getting bored, and was hoping there might be some way to speed it up.However, this is a game, and games should have more content than just half an hour.So, kudos to the developers here for defying everything we know about temporal physics by making 30 minutes be both too long and too short at the same time.Ultimately if there was a "maybe" option on Steam, this walking sim would qualify, but 30 minutes of non-game poetry reading for $4 is beyond the pale.  Certainly I hope the talented artists and designers here go on to make real video games, because there is so much potential.

_childDocuments_.review: "Sunlight" will throw some people off because it is not necessarily a game, but an immersive and contemplative piece of art. As others have mentioned, you simply walk through a forest and occasionally pick flowers for progression (with a beautiful rendition of "Hymn of The Cherubim" alongside harmonious storytelling occurring all the while). All of this *seems* to occur within the span of a half hour.But-- the music, the painted world, and the sirens drag you towards this strange introspection of self. I feel like there are many ways to interpret what vaguely materialized in "Sunlight", and that is the point. This experience is to be felt by the self. I was given this game, but I believe Sunlight is well worth $4. My interpretation will not be yours, so give it a try if you are curious what "Sunlight" will do for you. I think I will listen again another night.

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but soothing and meditative game. We walk through a lush forest made out of impressionistic brushstrokes (handpainted in VR), guided by a harmonious narration and the sounds of the forest, while we pick a bunch of flowers.Sunlight is not a game for everyone. Without a traditional plot-driven narrative, and unwavering in its insistence that the player can only stroll through this forest at quite a leisurely pace, coming in with wrong expectations could easily lead to disappointment. After the eerie moods of Among The Sleep, Krillbite really seems to want to put the player in a certain kind of mindset with Sunlight. Just wander around, and let the sounds and voices take you away for a bit. If that does not sound appealing, Sunlight might not be for you. With a breathtaking soundtrack of Tchaikovsky's  accompanying the narration, Sunlight really managed to transport me away there for a little bit. Headphones recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: My finger gets tired from pressing the arrow key and almost fall asleep, but it is an interesting way of expressing a message, although I think the same technique being used should be limited to 10 ~ 15 minutes, the game overall is about 30 minutes.I would probably like it more if I didn't have to press the arrow key and focus on the voices.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: This was a relaxing experience - nothing more but also nothing less. While I sadly couldn't really connect with the story and the pacing in the flower picking parts felt too slow and annoying towards the ending, the different voices of the trees and the art style in general were beautiful. The ending was what I liked most and I had fun exploring the scenery for a bit. (The forest itself felt too 'random' or even empty for it to be engaging to explore, but I do understand that the whole point of this game is to defocus/relax). I would, however, have appreciated it if the flowers didn't start clipping into each other as soon as you pick up the second one. That doesn't do the overall design, which is nicely done, justice.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Raw, evocative artistic expression set to lavish visuals, a divine choir, and an existentially ambiguous poem that's held back slightly by performance glitches and an off-putting ASMR introduction. Sunlight is a keen example of art's general goal of eliciting a specific emotion from the viewer, even if it's accomplished with limited subtlety.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: A thought provoking walk in the woods, truthfully more an experience then a game. 10/10 recommend playing at lest once and well worth the full price. Go pick this one up now. Full Review.What can I say but wow and I wish this was a longer experience or that there will be more stories like this added in the future. Playing through Sunlight was a truly moving experience that brought me close to tears on more then one occasion.  My only critique would be that it is so short to almost be bitter sweet, you will be left wanted more. From the narration, to the BEAUTIFUL hand drawn graphics and perfect choice of atmospheric music I find is difficult to find fault with this experience in a walking sim. I also want to specifically mention the unique style of narration. I have sen some other reviews that say it is a bit disjointed, and without giving spoilers. my only comment on that is you need to focus on a single tree, or the entire forest. There is no in between. I really want to say more but it would be FULL of spoilers. In short, pick this one up as soon as possible. You will not regret it at the price point.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Even though this game could not be called as highly engaging one, but the story, deep meaning and sounds makes it a unique experience. It's a short journey through amazing soundtrack. If you're looking for an action game, this is not for you. But if you want to chill for ~30 minutes, this game is the right choice
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: A solid little indie experience! This story-focused walking sim takes right around 30 minutes or so to complete, though it may warrant a 2nd playthrough to fully grasp all of the story points. It's definitely a 'game' that makes you think, with many metaphors and allusions in the storytelling. I can't say that I fully understood all of the ideas that were presented but I did leave satisfied and it did create some conversation opportunities. It's great to find and support small, focused, passion projects like this. If you think you might enjoy this short story, check it out. It's worth the half an hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: I won't pretend to understand what the narrative is telling me, at first it was a little jarring to hear about needles and intense feelings whilst roaming such a calm and beautiful environment, but now and then you are told to breathe in and breathe out. It leads me to believe these are accounts of peoples experiences, good and bad, and how they have dealt with them.That sometimes, when things become too much, remember to breathe. I may be wrong about all of that, but it's nice to think about.As for gameplay, I'll be honest, there isn't much of it. You walk around in any direction, doesn't matter which, and listen to the narration. In the quiet moments, you find a flower to pick, and a new narration starts.All in all, your playtime will be roughly 30 minutes. However short it is, the experience is one of beauty. The art was handpainted (literally in VR), and the music is a composition of Tchaikovsky and sung by award-winning choir Kammerkoret Aurum.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game. It's a visual story! A beautiful one both in the sense of the story itself and the music combined with the graphic style. Very relaxing. However this is not for everyone! There are no puzzles or actual gameplay, and the game itself takes about 30 minutes to complete. But for the prize, it is well worth a playthrough if you are in the meditative mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Sunlight

_childDocuments_.review: Traverse a harmonious hand painted forest in this first person hike. The trees guide you with gentle whispers, as you explore a philosophical story.

name: Undisputed
detailed_description: Undisputed is an authentic boxing game developed with care by dedicated fight fans, alongside the professional boxing community. Here’s what you can expect from day one of Early Access: Boxing isn’t just about throwing punches. The ring is a strategic battlefield where fighters can choose an angle of attack, set up traps, and outsmart opponents through clever tactics. That’s why we’ve added several layers of fight mechanics to Undisputed, giving more control than ever to master the Sweet Science. Play through the epic journey from amateur boxing tournaments, all the way to becoming Undisputed Champion, in the true-to-life Career Mode. Create your own fighter with Character Creator, customising everything from build, to tattoos, to shorts and gloves. Revolutionary footwork mechanics, including a Loose Movement toggle to help you get around the ring with ease, and Flat-Footed Movement when your stamina drops. More than 60 individual punches. Punch from multiple angles and directions. Feint to set up a trap and counter. All the tools needed to be a defensive wizard. Slip punches, weave, dodge, and block. Physics driven interactions, so punches can sometimes go around or even through the guard. Up close and personal inside fighting like never before. Manage stamina over the course of a fight with the Adrenaline system. 50 Attributes & Traits to differentiate styles and capabilities of fighters. Multiple AI styles and difficulty settings for everyone from amateurs to pound-for-pound masters. We’ve licensed and collaborated with real-life boxers, governing bodies, and brands to bring unprecedented authenticity to Undisputed. 70+ licensed fighters in the game so far. From legendary names like Muhammad Ali and Sugar Ray Robinson to boxing’s modern champions, including Canelo Álvarez, Terence Crawford, and Tyson Fury. An exciting Women’s Division with stars like Katie Taylor, Jessica McCaskill, Natasha Jonas and Ebanie Bridges. The WBC, British Boxing Board of Control, and other real-life boxing organizations. Boxing equipment and apparel brands such as Empire Pro Tape, Everlast, Adams Footwear and more. Punch stats and presentation featuring CompuBox. Fighter introductions by the legendary Jimmy Lennon Jr. Distinguished referee Kenny Bayless. We’ve taken great care to make sure Undisputed looks and feels like boxing should. Incredibly detailed boxer models, utilizing the latest scanning technology. Customise your professional fighters with ring attire, taunts and ringwalk music for the ultimate in authenticity. 6 unique fight locations, including a large arena, Coldwell’s Gym, & an outdoor venue. Realistic damage, progressive sweat, and facial deformation. Broadcast presentation with expert commentary by Todd Grisham and Johnny Nelson, as well as ring walks, and referee instructions.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved every single boxing game since back when KO Kings 2002 was a thing.This game plays like fight night, but also plays nothing like it at the same time. The core mechanics are there but they are way too slow. The ability to bob and weave would be great if it actually worked, i found the easiest way to dodge is to just spam up and down on the stick, because weaving and leaning is absolutely useless.I've had maybe 10-15 quick fights and never once have i been able to stagger or daze, every timed counter i land does nothing, but when the same timed counters hit me i am staggered every time (unbalanced much?)Getting to your feet after being knocked down, that mechanic is atrocious.  Unless you have exotropia you will just about get up once. It should have been something similar to fight night.Opponents never seem to lose stamina regardless of how many punches they throw or how many body shots are landed.The way the boxers look and move in the ring is absolutely spot on, no faults there.I'd love to recommend the game because i know there is a lot of passion going into this and if it's done right could top fight night, but in it's current state with laggy and unresponsive mechanics i can't recommend it yet. My review may change with future updates.Edit: Almost 1 year later, the game feels no different than it did a year ago, final thought is this game isn't worth a penny right now

_childDocuments_.review: As a single player I can't recommend this for the moment. I am not playing this for the online mode but for the career mode. I loved Fight Night round 3 and if I could play it right now on my PC or PS5 I would. This game has potential but right now it's not worth it. It's focused on online mode but that mode doesn't seem to have a proper match making system or it's swarmed with smurfs. Either way it's not fun.Loading times are insanely long and hooks seem to be the go to mechanic. Jabs and uppercuts are not relevant.Career mode is bland and repetitive. According to online feedback it doesn't seem to get any updates either. You can't change the entrance (or entrance music) of your character, your nickname isn't used by the comentators, there are no training mini games, cuts and swellings seem very random, title matches don't have any flavor to them. AI is very predictable and easy to trick. If you get a promotional or discounted code and are looking for a single player boxing game that will provide you with 10-15 hours of content, then go for it otherwise wait until it releases because as of february 2024 it's not worth 45 buck. If you are looking for online fights then maybe this is for you, but be prepared to be destroyed during your first matches as you will be matched with very experienced players.

_childDocuments_.review: NEW REVIEW as of 2 Feb, 2024OMG This game has evolved so much. It is way way better now. The new experimental camera (similar to Real Boxing and PSP games Rocky Balboa and Victorious Boxers) is something you cannot miss to experience. **********************************OUTDATED REVIEW: Posted: 25 Oct, 2023 @ 12:28pm This Early Access game is already beginning to shape up. I have no doubt it is going to be a great boxing game upon completion. There is one glaring issue though: Online.ONLINE is atrocious. AVOID THIS GAME if this is a deal breaker for you. Players are using only top tier fighters as well as mods to cheat their way to victory. Desync is also an issue as there are no online servers - though this is more of an issue with humanity's primitive internet technology which is still currently just too slow. As long as you have couch buddies around to play this with you, thus eliminating the need to play Online, this game can offer many hours of joy and satisfaction.For now, it's an okay Fight Night clone...which means it is very mediocre gamplay-wise. However, I am still in the hopes that SCI adds unique movesets for each fighter in the game (similar to Hellish Quart). As a matter of fact, it might become the ultimate boxing game if it reaches Tekken levels of depth and complexity upon full release.Still, it is fairly enjoyable and is getting good over time. My recommendation is to buy it if you are looking for:- a Fight Night fan who needs a competent boxing game on PC- looking for something basic and simple- somewhat realistic stat-based gameplayAvoid it if you are looking for:- deep and thoughtful gameplay- you are looking for an online game. It is simply NOT, and IMO never will be - balanced game where player skill determines success. To a certain degree, it can be; however, stats are very meaningful in this game. The higher tier fighters are really OP; whereas the lower tier fighters are really garbage. You can still win as the underdog...against the PC; however, against a decent player, the outcome is most likely already predeterminedIn conclusion, BUY IT...but don't expect much. No point being disappointed and complaining in the forums like a beotch. Enjoy the game for what it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Undisputed is an incomplete but much needed boxing title. We haven't seen a legit boxing game since the xbox 360 and as someone who loved fight night and wanted a newer option with current fighters, this game gets the job done. Cons- Knockouts. Knockout I feel are one of the most exciting things in any fighting games. The satisfying feeling of rocking your opponent and watching them hit the canvas. Unfortunately in the games current state, knockout animations are extremely lack luster. Every knockout consist of your opponent stumbling and slowly going to the ground. I would love to be able to feel the power of my knockouts. I want to see my opponents slam to the canvas after a viscous upper cut. It is extremely underwhelming and I hope this is improved in later updates.-Punches not registering. This may be a nitpick but I have noticed in every single match I have played I will swing at an opponent and very obviously land a direct shot and it ends up not registering and has 0 effect-Gamemodes. As of now the game lacks many modes outside of local matches and online play. They have announced that a career mode and create a character are in the works but as of this review there is very limited things to take advantage of-Commentary. The commentary in this game is extremely repetitive and a lot of the time doesn't relate to what is happening in the match. Example: I am dominating an opponent to the point of bleeding and several knock downs while I have barely been touched and the announcers will say something like "Those score cards must be close I can't imagine who they have winning this one"Pros-Gameplay. While I had a few complaints of the gameplay, I love it overall. Combos feel fluid and satisfying. Dodging, blocking, punching all feel great and are very easy to learn-Graphics. The graphics are absolutely amazing in this. The fighters look incredible and very similar to their real life counter parts. Skin ripples as punches land, cuts look gnarly and authentic everything looks absolutely awesome-Arenas. While I feel a lot more can be added, the variety of arenas are great. You can fight in a gym, an opera theater, an outdoor venue, a stadium there are lots of unique choices-Roster. While there is room for a lot more legends and fictional characters, the roster here is what I have been wanting. Being able to fight as wilder, fury, garcia is awesome and something I have been waiting for. Can't wait to see who else is addedUndisputed is a game that is lacking many components but is a game with ultimate potential to be the best boxing game of all time. It is absolutely worth the purchase even in its current state especially if you are like me and have been dying for a new boxing experience. Hats off to the developers for listening to the community and producing a game with incredible potential. Cannot wait to see the state of this game this time next year

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of boxing games, I was excited to dive into Undisputed, hoping for a worthy successor to the beloved Fight Night Champion. Unfortunately, what I found was a game that falls flat on its face in its attempt to emulate its predecessor's success.Undisputed, a game attempting to pay homage to the legendary Fight Night Champion, unfortunately falls short in more ways than one. As an avid fan of boxing games, I had high hopes for this title, but it fails to capture the essence of what made its predecessor great.Undisputed aims to replicate the magic of Fight Night Champion, but it falters where it matters most – the gameplay mechanics. The use of the joystick to throw punches feels clunky and unresponsive, a far cry from the fluidity and precision of its inspiration. This forced reliance on buttons to execute punches disrupts the immersion and enjoyment of the boxing experience.One of the most disappointing aspects of Undisputed is its abundance of bugs and glitches. From narrators repeating the same tired commentary lines to clothing items glitching out mid-fight. It's jarring to hear commentators speak as if you're fighting in a weight division you're not even close to, breaking any semblance of immersion.Undisputed sorely lacks the polish and refinement that made Fight Night Champion a classic. It's evident that the developers cut corners, resulting in a subpar gaming experience. Even basic mechanics such as clinching often fail to function correctly, leaving you frustrated and disconnected from the action.Adding insult to injury, the developer's approach to increasing difficulty is both lazy and uninspired, rather than providing a challenging and engaging experience through intelligent AI and strategic gameplay, the developers opted for a lazy solution of simply making the player weaker while boosting the opponent's strength to unrealistic levels. This results in encounters that feel more like battling an invincible sponge than engaging in a skillful boxing matchUltimately, my recommendation for boxing enthusiasts is to stick with the original Fight Night Champion, perhaps on an emulator if necessary. Undisputed has potential, but it requires significant polishing and refinement before it can even begin to rival its predecessor. For now, players would be better served revisiting the original on an emulator, as Undisputed lacks the polish and finesse necessary to deliver a truly satisfying boxing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that they've patched the game and it's playable, I actually enjoy it so much! Now, you will always have those who complain about fighting styles and different techniques. Don't listen to that stuff! This game is like any other fighting game. Once you put the time in and get good, it's enjoyable. You very well may not like it at first because it isn't like fight night. But the game is really simple and is actually a lot easier to play than fight night was during its time. Could some things be improved? Yes, like the fact that some punches cancel out when you try to hold your block immediately after punching. And also the fact that you can't hold block while sidestepping at the same time. I also don't like the fact that they tried to center this game around brawling when there are so many other elements to boxing. A few people have complained about outside fighting being too "overpowered" and supposedly the devs agree now. And I think that's bull crap! You shouldn't apply pressure if you don't want to get countered. Naturally, if you're walking your opponent down they will have to go the opposite way to create space. Some of us actually like to use our brains when we fight. But other than that, I'm glad to have a boxing game and I've gotten pretty good at it quickly with my fight night experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This games graphics are not important, in fact the graphics of any game is not important, unless the graphics is intricately linked with the games play, the big issue with early release games is the fact that the players are often focused on unimportant aspects of the game, often people will describe the feelings or the vague belief that the game has something that makes it not enjoyable to play, the game reviews with a list of pro's and con's is the typical feedback that game makers will get, it's pointless though, and distracting to the games developers, the type that are gifted with the ability to code games are not the type of people that have played games throughout their lives, even if they are that type, gamer are not generally highly experienced with games from the beginning of video games right through to the present age of games, I am experienced, people would say I've wasted my life playing games but it doesn't have to be a complete waste, this games developers could take advantage of that experience, this game and all the boxing games as well as third person combat games of all kinds, copy the combat physics of a game called Fight Night, 2 and Fight night 3 I think they were the games that had the "Haymaker" move/punch, that punch was thrown in an intuitive way, with the controller right stick, you might be able to have the mouse do this action, but it's perfectly suited to the controllers from X Box and Play Station.You use the twin right and left controller sticks,the left stick is for player movement, around the ring or buy holding down the left trigger, your boxers torso moves, you lean back, left, right or forwards with the L-Stick, that's how you dodge punches, the same left trigger makes your blocking and punches attack the body or defend from body punches. Right-Stick is used to throw left and right punches, high or low, by holding the left trigger, to throw a straight punch, you simply move the right stick forward and slightly to the left of centre, this will throw a left jab, slightly to the right of centre to throw a right straight punch, or (cross) to throw a right hook for example you move the right punching stick on the controller, side ways to the right and then move it on to the forward position and your boxer will do a right hook, if you push the right stick sideways and then back before you continue forwards you will throw a charged extra strong punch that that old game called a (haymaker) to throw a right uppercut move the controllers right stick to the back and right diagonal and roll the stick to the forward position, then your boxer will throw a uppercut, the left trigger, If memory serves would modify the punch from being a normal head punch to a low gut punch, if you want to block I think that was done by holding down right trigger, and moving the right stick in the corresponding direction, if you just held the right trigger to block but you didn't hold the (R-Stick) in any direction than you would simply block your head with your gloves and not be able to catch your opponents gloves when they attacked, or avoid all the damage witch would happen if you got the correct block for the hand punch that your opponent threw, it's difficult to explain, but if you would just go get a copy of the game and copy that fighting physics then you would have a real fun game there, I'd buy it, I can't get fight night on the PC or steam and I can't play it on the play station or the x box because I don't play games on the console anymore, I play games on the PC, sometimes I would play games with the controller from the Xbox, if there was any game.

_childDocuments_.review: Undisputed is a boxing game that attempts to recreate the thrill of stepping into the ring. Unfortunately, my experience with the game left me feeling more like I'd been sucker-punched than anything else. Undisputed bills itself as the ultimate boxing experience, but in reality, it's little more than a series of repetitive button mashing exercises. Sure, there are different fighters to choose from and a variety of venues to fight in, but at its core, the gameplay is shallow and uninspired.The graphics are decent enough, but the animations leave a lot to be desired. Punches don't feel like they have any weight behind them, and the fighters move in a way that's more robotic than human. It's hard to get invested in a fight when the action on-screen looks like it's being performed by mannequins.The sound design is equally lackluster. The crowd noise is generic and the announcer's commentary is repetitive to the point of being annoying. And while the game does offer licensed music to listen to, it's hard to enjoy when you're focused on punching your opponent in the face.But perhaps the biggest issue I had with Undisputed was the lack of strategy. In a real boxing match, there are multiple factors to consider, from your opponent's fighting style to your own stamina. But in this game, it's all about throwing as many punches as possible and hoping for the best. There's no sense of nuance or finesse, just mindless button mashing.In conclusion, while Undisputed may scratch a certain kind of itch for boxing fans, it's not a game that I would recommend. The gameplay is shallow, the animations are lackluster, and the sound design is forgettable. If you're looking for a truly knockout boxing game, you're better off looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I´ve been a avid gamer and enjoyed countless of genres but if there is one genre that I am passionate about, it´s combat sport games. Being full aware that boxing is difficult to translate into game mechanics, another aspect should not be as complicated imo and that is the fun-factor within the gameplay loop. Now don´t get me wrong, I want to be optimistic and I do not regret time nor money spent because there are a few things to appreciate but I have to be honest.Pros: - The Footwork + Loose movement system - Take a knee which is a nice touch and implements a layer of strategy - Surprisingly enough they´ve made huge improvements to the AI though it becomes quite predictable even on the hardest difficulty.- Replays (only offline currently)- Audio design (specifically the impact of landing punches)Cons: Everything elsewe have a quite impressive roster stacked with familiar boxers that are known for their distinctive fighting styles yet everyone fundamentally throws basic techniques in similar fashion--except for Canelo and Jones Jr. There are a few other stand outs who have something unique about them but the fact remains. Let me try to explain. Boxers are divided into four categories.Boxer puncher: The all around puncher who receives no modifications to the baseline stats.Out Boxer: The boxer who relies on footwork, ringwork and receives the following- Punch stamina cost reduction by 15%- Punch damage reduction by 5%- Stamina drains 7.5% slower Slugger: Represents the hard-hitting in the pocket type of boxer and receives the following- Increase in their health pools and a 15% increase to punch damage- Stamina drains 5% slower while punch stamina cost is increased by 20% ? Swarmer: Is the pressure style fighter and receives the following- Punch stamina cost reduced by 10%- Punch damage increased by 5%- Stamina drains 5% slower while starting health is reduced by 10%These styles share 20 different punch sets and 11 of them are unique to said boxer (I believe Loma is exclusive but I could be wrong) and they actually look good & quite distinctive when showcasing them inside the creation screen but unfortunately, this does not translate well inside of the ring except for the animations while moving about. Not only do the boxing feel similar among the boxers, they all seem to use the same coach for head movement. You can only weave with your feet planted and you cannot pivot out nor combine head movement with any kind of footwork, only with the block and strikes. The slip mechanic works in similar fashion. It´s a dedicated movement and you can slip in four directions but cannot combine a slip with any kind of footwork. Your only option is to slip & punch to counter or just slip to show that you´re a dare devil, and then move.Then we have a hit and miss block system in place, where shots will bleed through even when block staminais full due to bad net coding / desync, traits? I don´t know but let me be fair here because the block system do have a layer of depth to it but currently when playing online, where hackers roam free & body uppercuts remains meta, it won´t help much to get into it atm. Just unnaturally move in & out while holding the block, pray & play.Stats & traits are present and and they do present more problems rather than uniqueness among the boxers. Not only are some traits broken but this has been done before so where´s the "innovation" here, by over doing it? What I am trying to say is that combat games are generally about outwitting your opponent but here we are facing the same issues we´ve faced in the past as we yet again rely on stats & traits. Let me further attempt to explain.VIT represents Health, Health Regeneration, Health Recovery, Head Health and Body HealthSTM represents Stamina, Stamina Regeneration, Stamina Recovery, Conditioning and EnduranceSPD represents Agility, Movement Speed, Punch Speed and AccuracySTR represents Left Hand Power, Right Hand Power, Jabs, Hooks, Uppercuts, Straights, Power Punching and Counter PunchingDEF represents Guarding, Swelling Resistance, Cut Resistance, Chin Resistance and Body ResistanceHRT represents Courage, Block Health, Block RegenerationThese main categories are set with an overall number based on the numbers the sub categories have, and in turn gives the boxer his / her overall stat number. Slapped on top of this, 1 of the 4 boxing styles which comes with set bonuses (excluding the BP) and on top of that, 1 up to 4 out of the 42 traits that have 3 additional tiers. This is convoluted. Now do I as a competitive player chose my favorite boxer and purely rely on my boxing IQ or do I simply pick the boxer with the highest stats & best perks to increase my chances of winning? There has to be a better approach to this because it quickly becomes redundant facing the same top roster fighters online but again, I digress and I could be wrong, this is just a matter of opinion, like the stats of some of these boxers.Credit where credit is due because there is one fundamental aspect of the game that sticks out, the footwork / movement. Here is where UB truly shines but also where it stops because it is limited and very much flawed. It just doesn't blend well with the boxing, the weaving and slip animations, it all feels disconnected.Conclusion, UB is far from ready and I cannot recommend it due to the many fundamental issues at play here. I do get what SCI is trying to achieve though and I can honestly respect it but the vision needs to be clear & transparency is key here. You can’t claim to be innovative while building of a decade-old formula (Fight Night) and not being able to show out where it actually matters—the gameplay loop.

_childDocuments_.review: **Title: A Knockout Experience – Undisputed****Rating: ★★★★☆ (4.5/5)**Undisputed is a standout title in the world of boxing games, delivering an authentic and immersive experience for both boxing fans and gamers alike. With its stunning graphics, realistic gameplay, and extensive roster, it captures the essence of the sport while offering a satisfying and competitive environment.**Gameplay Mechanics:**The combat mechanics in Undisputed are fluid and intuitive, striking a perfect balance between accessibility and depth. The controls allow players to execute a wide range of punches, defensive maneuvers, and combinations, making each fight feel dynamic and engaging. The stamina system adds strategic depth, requiring players to manage their energy throughout each round.**Graphics and Presentation:**Visually, Undisputed is impressive. The character models are highly detailed, and the animations are smooth, capturing the intensity and rhythm of boxing. The arenas are well-designed, complete with cheering crowds and an immersive atmosphere that enhances the overall experience. The presentation, including the commentary and fight introductions, adds to the authenticity of the sport.**Roster and Customization:**The game boasts an extensive roster of real-life boxing legends and current stars, allowing players to create dream matchups. The ability to customize fighters, including appearance and attributes, adds a personal touch that fans will appreciate. Whether you want to take control of a historic champion or create your own fighter, the options are plentiful.**Career Mode:**The career mode is robust, offering players the chance to progress from an amateur to a world champion. The journey includes training, managing your fighter’s stats, and making critical decisions that impact your career trajectory. While engaging, some players might find certain aspects of the mode could benefit from more depth, such as a richer narrative.**Online Play:**Undisputed also features competitive online play, allowing players to test their skills against others around the world. While the online experience is generally smooth, occasional matchmaking issues can arise, but the overall competitive atmosphere keeps the experience thrilling.**Final Thoughts:**Undisputed is a fantastic addition to the boxing genre, offering a blend of realistic mechanics, stunning visuals, and an extensive roster that will please both casual gamers and boxing aficionados. While there are minor areas for improvement in the career mode and online matchmaking, the overall package delivers a knockout experience. If you’re a fan of boxing or looking for an engaging sports game, Undisputed is definitely worth stepping into the ring for!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love that there is a new boxing game to finally play and I love the new mechanics compared to Fight Night Champions. My only HUGE ISSUE I have is with people leaving the multiplayer ranked games and then having  it count as a loss on my record. I should be 5-0-1 but now my record is 3-2-1 because of people leaving since I was up big on the scorecards. I don't want to play the ranked mode anymore if it's just going to be counted as a loss whenever my opponent leaves. I hope there will soon be a fix for this and until then I will just be playing quick match. The little problems I have are things like the camera is sometimes too far away. I checked in the settings for different camera angles and there are only 2 options and there isn't much of a difference in them. I love that for different venues there are individual settings to have the camera set. But back to the movement of the game. Thank you for putting in a way to block lower half and block upper half into the game. I always wished I could do that in Fight Night. The free movement when pressing up on the d-pad is also a beautiful addition to the game and is essential to really feeling like you're playing as those loose hands-down style boxers like Ali and Roy Jones Jr. The ability to also do a quick slip was also one of the genius ideas by this team. You don't have to hold a button to go into one set weaving mode and then release to come back up. Just press down on the left analog stick and pick a direction and it's just a quick little slip of the punch. The choice to have a fighter take a knee in the middle of the fight can be strategic and to my knowledge it's never been done before in any boxing game and I love the addition. I also hope that in the future the punches will seem to have more of an impact. If there are any people who are worried that it won't live up to be like Fight Night you should know that this game is different. Sure it doesn't have all the fighters you would hope to be here like Tyson, Jack Dempsy, Thomas Hearns, and others. But mechanically I would say it's even better than Fight Night. For the price of $30 instead of a full $60/$70 game I would say this game is worth giving a try. Especially since Steam is pretty relaxed with the refund policy. So go through the tutorial, fight a couple fight and see if you like it. I know this game is still under development since there are still modes missing like career mode. So I can't wait to see what this amazing team will do in the future patches and updates coming to this innovative boxing game.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in early access because I love Fight Night, and it's been a while since there's been a decent boxing game that has come out. The game was in rough shape during early access but had potential, so after putting some time in, I decided to wait for the 1.0 release in hopes the main issues with the game would be fixed. I have to say, not only were most of the issues not fixed, many are somehow worse, to the point that this game is essentially unplayable in online mode. Here are a handful of the main issues that occur during online play:-The movement is glitchy and at time just locks up, freezing your fighter in place-The camera often jerks around to the point that one of the fighters is nearly off camera or their head is partially off the top of the screen-The punching is unresponsive with long delays between pressing the stick and the punch being thrown -Often punches just won't throw at all when you press the stick-Dodging punches and countering is ineffective and often doesn't work-Power punching is broken/overpowered so currently the best strategy is just to walk straight at your opponent throwing power punches over and over until the opponent goes down-Ghost punching still exist so sometimes the opponent will throw a punch from across the screen and it will still landI really wanted to like this game, and hopefully, they patch it and fix some of these issues, but as the game stands, it's a huge waste of money. I imagine most people who pick it up, especially those looking to play online, will be extremely disappointed and feel ripped off.

_childDocuments_.review: Undisputed, a boxing game for PC, boasts some impressive features, but ultimately falls short in several key areas.One of the game's major strengths is its graphics, which are stunningly lifelike. The detail in the fighters' faces and bodies, as well as the attention to detail in the arenas, make for a visually immersive experience.However, there are several cons to this game that cannot be overlooked. The first is that the game feels incomplete - there are few options beyond a standard fight, and the pool of playable boxers is disappointingly small. Additionally, the lack of recognizable boxing legends is a missed opportunity to hype the game and add more depth to the roster.The controls are another issue with Undisputed. They are merely adequate, and not particularly intuitive or satisfying to use. The techniques available to the player are also very limited, with little variation between different boxers. It would have been much better if each fighter had their own unique moveset, which is a feature that previous boxing games have done well.Overall, while the graphics in Undisputed are impressive, they cannot make up for the game's shortcomings. With limited options and an unsatisfying control scheme, this game falls short of what could have been a great boxing game.Recommendation: Not for now. Wait for the complete game.
