_childDocuments_.review: The Good- The Visuals are stunning. The Models look incredible and some of the boxers have incredibly lifelike animations.- Hit reactions are quite nice with heads being popped back and body shots actually moving the opponents body, with flesh rippling from the impact.- Punch impacts sound really good, much better than in Fight Night Champion.- The presentation that IS there is really good, quite accurate to real life.- Although not all present at the moment, the game has a huge roster with a lot of big names past and present represented.- Generally speaking the feeling, look and sound of punching someone in the head/body is decent enough, unfortunately this is where the good points for this game (and most other boxing games to date) come to and end.The Bad- The commentary, it's bad. A small number of poorly written oft repeated lines read by two overly excited guys who sound like they're reading canned lines from a script rather than having a natural free flowing conversation. Hardly any boxer specific lines. There are even lines that sound as though the commentators are talking to you as the player, which is very strange and immersion breaking.- The music. Unless you're a fan of UK rap, have an ice pick on hand as you will want to drive it through your brain.- The presentation although good, is still lacking in some areas. There are no robes during entrances, and the entrances themselves are just a snippet rather than the full entrance. In between rounds goes on far too long with nothing interesting happening. Victory scenes are especially bad, with no entourage in the ring at all and only very basic presentation.- There's too big a difference in speed and responsiveness between the big name fighters and the lesser known ones. Hell, even some of the big names feel pretty sluggish. Especially at heavyweight. I understand the devs wanting there to be a difference but I would argue it's actually counter productive at this point. A lot of people will only want to use the best fighters because of this, rendering that huge roster wasted potential. In real life the difference in speed between weight classes and between world level and domestic level is not this pronounced. If anything it's actually stamina that is more affected.- The Knockouts. There are a few issues with the knockouts. The canned animations the opponent goes into when knocked out are incredibly obvious, immersion breaking and look pretty bad. The "Get Up" minigame itself isn't bad, but the way it cuts away and places you in the centre of the ring is extremely jarring. The random 1 Punch KO's are a bad idea, always have been. There are just some aspects of the sport that can't be simulated in a videogame.- The stunned states are a little over the top, and basically render you completely incapable of fighting back. They either need to be toned down, or introduce a second minor stunned state.- The damage system. It's tied far too closely to the stamina system. Playing against the computer I quickly realised it was far more effective to let the CPU tee off on me and deplete his stamina and then simply unload my combination on him as it would almost always send him into a stunned state due to his stamina already being low. This also makes body punching (especially uppercuts for some reason) far more effective than head shots. Essentially you're punished for going to the head and rewarded for going to the body, punished for initiating an exchange rewarded for ending it.- The perfect block. Catching and countering is quite rare in boxing and when performed it often ends in a knockdown/knockout. In this game (especially against the CPU) it happens almost every exchange. It also punishes you for using the jab, against the CPU at least. Either implement it in a way that makes it difficult to pull off and a rare occurrence or remove it entirely.- Upper body/head movement. A mechanic that has been poorly implemented in every boxing game to date, made worse in Undisputed. Like all other boxing games there's no proper bob and weave and you can't slip or weave while moving, rendering head movement useful only to defensive fighters who stand still waiting for you to come to them. Undisputed however somehow manages to make this even worse by making their "Weave" mechanic utterly useless and placing the actually useful "Slip" mechanic on Left Analogue Click which is extremely uncomfortable and unreliable in frantic exchanges.- The footwork, although beautifully animated is actually fairly shallow with some serious flaws. Footwork was one of the things the devs talked up from the early stages of development, yet this is another boxing game where you cannot shift or pivot. On top of this you move too far too fast. Boxing is often a game of inches, an inch too close you get knocked out, a couple of inches back the punch misses completely. You simply don't have tight enough control over your footwork to control distance effectively the way boxers do in real life. Ever wondered why you often see people online exchange and then both back off completely to the other side of the ring, very unrealistically? This, I think is why. I also think it's why the camera seems to have trouble keeping up at times and causes performance issues. It simply can't keep up with the frantic movement, especially with all the flashing and shaking going on from the constant "perfect block" counters.- The range on some of the punches just seems odd. I've seen a few people in the reviews point this out and I agree with it. It seems to be just as easy, if not easier to land an uppercut to the body from range than a jab to the head. And generally speaking it sometimes feels like you almost have to be standing on your opponents toes in order to hit them.- The "Haymakers" or power punches, whatever you want to call them. Again same issue as with all the other Fight Night games, the wind up/charge is just ridiculous and something you would never see in a high level professional bout. Control wise it can also be an issue as some punches feel quite uncomfortable and difficult to pull off. There are other issues I could point to as well such as the clinch, but I'll leave it here for the bad points as some of these mechanics are obviously not properly implemented yet, and this "review" will never end if I do.Suggestions- Have power shots performed by holding down the button instead of using another button as a modifier and get rid of the wind up/charge. For example hold X to perform a "power" or "stiff" jab. This would improve the controls and would be a more realistic implementation of power punching with the downside being that you can't chain power punches together as quickly as normal punches as you have to hold the button down instead of just tapping it.- Move punching off of the Right Analogue Stick to just the face buttons, and use the Right Analogue to control upper body/head movement. Perform slips by flicking the analogue in a direction, and the ability to weave by pressing the analogue in a direction and then rotating it towards another direction. This way, you could actually perform a proper bob and weave and could even chain weaves together. You could also utilise head movement while moving which would make head movement effective for come forward pressure fighters for the first time in a boxing game, and stop the game from turning into a counter punchers paradise.- Introduce a "Footwork Modifier" button (preferably Right Bumper) to allow for advanced footwork such as pivoting and shifting. This would enable you to perform a proper check left hook, and even things like adding a pivot to the end of your bob and weave.- Place "Switch Stance" on Left Bumper and move the "Body Modifier" to Left Trigger, and give the player the ability to punch while shifting by holding down the switch stance button and throwing a punch off the back hand.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave reviews but I feel as though I need to with this game. I’m pretty fanatical about the sport of boxing, I’ve been a life long fan and even use to run my own weekly boxing news website. Alongside this I’m a hardcore gamer, I probably average around 4-6 hours a day. I’ve been waiting for this game to be released for so long and praying for a true next gen boxing game to replace fight night champion, I’ve played every boxing game available since 4D boxing back  in the late 80s.Disregarding the intermittent motion blur, as impressive as this game is visually, it fulls down on nearly every other aspect. The commentary is limited, has no reflection to what’s actually happening in the ring and constantly reuses the same clips over and over. I’m not sure what Johny Nelson was thinking, but incase you haven’t actually heard him talk in real life, he sounds nothing like he does on the game, it’s voice acting at it’s worse. I’ve not played online but the 4 hours I have played against computer controlled opponents really has left a bad taste in my mouth. The CPU seems to have an unbelievable ability to counter a high percentage of your shots, usually with a perfectly timed body shot. The level of accuracy is so high that there stamina hardly even drops. Most of the characters don’t fight anything like the real life fighter they are based on. The CPU doesn’t seem to care if you land  4,5,6 clean head shots, they will just keep walking you down. There needs to be some realism, if a real fighter was to take 4 clean punches, 1 of which was a power punch and 2 or 3 hooks, they would back off and reset, even if they weren’t badly hurt, they would back away and compose themself. It seems you are constantly forced into a toe to toe battle which you rarely win as the CPU is so accurate especially with their counter body shots. Body shots are not a highly used shot in boxing as you are far more likely to be countered with a head shot, unfortunately the AI seems to hit any point that is not guarded instead of resembling a real boxing match., don’t get me wrong, I understand a boxer will try and look for openings, just not repeatedly throwing the same shots at the same spot with no fear on what may be thrown back.Unless you are a rangy fast fighter like Ali or Fury, you tend to get drawn into unrealistic fights that doesn’t resemble anything close to real life. One of my highlights was constantly being backed up by Kell Brook whilst I was controlling Canelo Alvarez, a fighter who has gone as high as light heavyweight and still knocked people out, amazingly Kell Brook, a fighter who ventured into middleweight, only to be savagely destroyed by GGG, a beating so bad he actually needed part of his face reconstructed. After landing 3 of Canelo’s trade mark body shots and 2 uppercuts, Kell Brook, unfazed just kept walking me down winging in his impressive body shots that he pretty much never used in his professional career.I think this was only topped by an interesting outcome on the score cards, I lost as Wilder, losing by 10 rounds to Rocky Marciano. I landed 460 punches to his 170, 186 of my shots were clean right hands, 88 of these were power punches, I dropped him once and out-landed him in every single round. The only thing that Marciano did during this fight that was better than me was his punch accuracy percentage, mine was 42% compared to his unbelievably impressive 61% so I’m presuming the computer judges a fight on a fighters punches thrown to landed accuracy instead of the bigger picture. All of this alongside the terrible generic repetitive knock down sequence, put boxer down, boxers gets to knees, boxer beats count, 3 repetitive knockdowns later, the fighter doesn’t beat the count and flops to there back in the same manner over and over again, no flash knockouts, no ability to push in close, no dirty boxing in the clinch.After playing this I’m left deflated and let down, hopefully this can all be resolved and they can actually focus on the sport and art and realism of boxing for the purist out there.

_childDocuments_.review: This game kinda blows. I get wanting to make a realistic boxing game but this is still a video game and there should be some sort of focus towards entertainment, inside fighting, mid range fighting and getting the finish within 3-5 rounds in most fights. Not making it extremely easy for literally anyone to run around for 12 rounds or until you've bored your opponent straight to sleep. Anytime a fight goes past 7-8 rounds I don't even care if I'm winning or not, I'm ready to play something else. Also you don't even have to run around for a fight to go that long. You can fight in spurts at close range and you'll still more than likely last at least 7 rounds. Body shots feel like they do nothing to slow fighters down except let them recover less stamina between rounds which basically has no effect when punches are being thrown. Don't get me started on the button layout either. It's terrible. It feels like there isn't enough buttons on the control to fully utilize your fighter to their maximum potential. It takes 3 buttons, that you pretty much have to have your fingers on the whole game, just to block. While also controlling movement, slips, throwing your own punches and the power modifier. Im a huge boxing fan. I remember when they first announced the game on twitter a few years ago I couldn't wait to play it. It was even the first game I bought on my pc. But after playing it the first time I returned it after not really liking it. Then I came back and bought it again just because I thought maybe I didnt give it enough time but no it really is that bad. I wish I could get another refund at this point. I'll take any UFC game over this garbage. It's the worse and most boring game ive played on my pc so far.Edit: I take it all back. This game is fun there was just a learning curve.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 Update is honestly a giant step in the right direction. The punch mechanics are excellent. They gave us an overhand right, combos are fluid, and punches have more impact. Throwing and comboing regular punches is a massive drain on stamina, but against an opponent that legitimately throws 300+ power shots, over the course of 8 rounds, he has 86% stamina  by the end of the Fight. Online rounds for quick play and ranked have been brought down from 12 to 8 which I am not a fan of and the judging is even more ludicrous. The lag and desync is in the absolute worst state it's ever been in. The punch registry is abysmal. We still have peer to peer connection. Honestly dedicated servers would fix ALOT of problems. I honestly love  this game and plan to keep playing it. However, the launch really feels like a cash grab because it's obviously catering to the noobs. It feels like Steel City could give a rats rear end about the early access players who have been playing and supporting their game for 2 years. I cannot recommend this game in its current state. Steel City needs to fix this fast before we go back to playing the same 20 people again because everyone else quit.

_childDocuments_.review: The AI and stun mechanics need to be balanced before I can recommend this game.Not only does the AI not lose stamina like the player, but it feels like a ridiculous amount of punches are needed to stun or potentially knockdown an opponent. The only way to play this game is with modifiers turned up for stamina or lower the overall difficulty, perhaps both. I know this sounds funny, but the problem is very apparent when you play a heavyweight match and see fighters take serious punches without even being rattled or stunned, and it can happen for 12 rounds. I'd rather have a stun meter like older games that simply builds up with the more powerful punches you receive over all, encouraging you to not take punches at all and really watch your blocking.Instead, this game wants you to use sparing with light punches to wear down health meters for the left or right side of the face or body to achieve a stun that leads to a knockdown, but you're required to continue hitting that side/spot to achieve it. The main issue with this, is how many power punches it requires to achieve a stun when in reality, punches to either side of your head should be counting towards an overall stun. You don't become less rattled just because your opponent switches what side he's punching your head, especially power punches. And when Cuts and serious bruising should be slowing or helping to rattle the AI, it just seems to cause the AI to block even more while still firing accurate counter punches with max stamina... its annoying. The AI/player should honestly receive handicaps to their stamina or something when receiving cuts because aside from the doctor stopping the fight for a progressed cut, its like there is no pain mechanic or other side effect. i.e. If an opponent is cut or a cut is worsened, their should be some kind of reaction to this, but there isn't. A cut is technically just a second health bar that can be used to potentially end a fight early if you continue to repeatedly worsen the cut.Scorecard counting btw feels extremely imbalanced in favor of the AI, (i.e. punches thrown, punches missed, ect). Many people including myself feel these mechanics are not right, especially hit detection. (i.e. a majority of punches thrown that should be counted as 'landed' are counted as missed). Honestly, if you don't lose to being knocked down, you'll lose to the scorecard. As someone in another review said and is echoed in the discussions, "its like the Judges are watching a completely different fight". Potential new buyers should be completely aware that the campaign does not currently exist in game and is under development, the only option for fights is to setup skirmishes by the player with cheating AI, fight a 'daily fight', or play online.Playing an online match with your friend currently requires you to exit to the main menu after each game and re-setup another lobby, kicking your friend in the process. To make this even more tedious, the game does not use steam to join, it uses a code system provided to the host to share with the joining player. This has been an extreme nuisance to the experience. Ending a private match should return both the host and the guest to a private lobby, but it doesn't. And then, depending on the connection of each fighter, an obnoxious "High Ping" warning can display at the top of the window while fighting that is very distracting and takes up an unnecessary amount of screen space. A small icon would have sufficed. The main problem I'm experiencing with online atm, is when players experience high enough ping, (what ever that may be) the game exits to the main menu with a box that reads "connection error". This happened to a bulk of the private matches my friend and I tried to play.I understand this game is early alpha and it is pretty good (at least its kinda scratching my fight game itch atm), but it needs some real polishing to be recommendable. I'll update this review if future updates change my mind.Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I played it for 49 minutes so far, and that is enough time to tell you what you feel about the game. First off, I was underwhelmed by the roster selection. But I understand that it's easier said that done in that regards. As for the game's overall presentation from menu to the actual game, it's lacking a lot. They could've done a lot better like adding a great background songs and more choices for game modes. And for a game that claims that they prioritize simulation, I am quite disappointed. For example, Dmitry Bivol doesn't move like how he does in real life. The wide foot work, volume jabs, and great defense are not present at all. It's like they just created his lookalike but didn't bother making it box like him. I bet other fighters are also like that.The knock outs could've been better, as the fighters always get teleported in the middle of the ring after the knock down to start the countdown animation of the ref. Why can't they just stay on the exact same spot where the got knock down and for the animation to start there as well if they mean to still get up?Overall, I regret buying it. I wish I could've just waited for a lot of patches before buying. I will see if there will be more improvements in the future which I hope very much.

_childDocuments_.review: Undisputed: A Solid Start, But Room for ImprovementUndisputed has made a noteworthy impact on the boxing gaming scene, offering a much-needed simulation-focused experience. While the core gameplay is commendable, the game's longevity hinges on significant additions and improvements.Key Strengths: * Deep Gameplay: The game's boxing mechanics are well-crafted, providing a realistic and strategic experience. * Graphics: Arenas, crowds, and cuts look impressive, contributing to a visually appealing presentation.Areas for Improvement: * Lack of Content: The game's features and career mode options feel limited, especially for those who played the early access version. * Limited Customization: The ability to customize your boxer and the overall experience is somewhat restricted. * Online Features: The absence of an online career mode and weight class flexibility is a significant omission.Recommendations for the Future: * Expanded Career Mode: Introduce more features, customization options, and story elements to keep players engaged. * Online Features: Implement an online career mode and allow for weight class movement to enhance the competitive aspect. * More Customization: Offer a wider range of items, equipment, and training options. * Refined Gameplay: Address any remaining gameplay quirks and improve the overall balance.Conclusion:Undisputed is a promising start, but its long-term success depends on the developers' willingness to listen to player feedback and implement substantial updates. By addressing the current shortcomings and adding more depth and features, the game can solidify its position as a must-have for boxing fans.

_childDocuments_.review: A few days into Early Access, it's hard to recommend Undisputed. I'm hopeful that it'll find its way to a more presentable state eventually, but at the moment, it's highly competitively and mechanically unsatisfying.I won't fault it for its expected Early Access jank, but I'm slightly worried about its long-term appeal (to me, as an online-only player) after seeing that it's already suffering from the usual UFC video game problem of having 1 meta character per weight class. The unique traits are nearly meaningless when there's such a stat gap between the bottom 95% of characters and the unstoppable 5% on top. There's practically no reason to not pick a Robinson or a Fury -- picking just about anyone else puts you at a ridiculous disadvantage if you're matched against someone not feeling quite as adventurous. Unfortunately, where the UFC games at least give the occasional non-meta character some interesting tools to try to make up the difference (in terms of kicks and clinches and submissions) and help you pull off a hail Mary when you're outmatched, Undisputed can really only be 'properly' played in a couple of ways, and at this point of the game's development, you never really feel like you're in control of your destiny once you're behind (conversely, you feel boringly on top of things if you're the one leading the dance). In my last ranked fight, my Wilder was predictably getting out-combo'd by my opponent's Ali, but I figured I had a shot at turning things around eventually since I was landing double digit power straights (a nearly 100 rated punch, as well as Wilder's 'trait' that makes it more likely to score knockdowns) every round. But nope. Never even wobbled the guy! If your one-dimensional giant whose one dimension is supposed to be extreme knockdown ability when he does land is doing no damage, why would anyone pick him over Ali, let alone the other, faster, slicker, more durable, nearly-as-heavy-handed (as per the stats) giant in Tyson Fury? Trying to make Hatton's liver shot trait pay dividends against Crawfords and Robinsons also felt like a fool's errand, despite landing a ridiculous amount of 'em.Even if the balancing remains poor, the game does look very good, and, for better or worse, it scratches an itch that no other game out on PC currently comes close to. I'll be coming back to it a bunch, even if it continues to frustrate me--if nothing else, surely matches will stop disconnecting half the time a month or two from now, right? Crossing my fingers (sans thumb) that future updates will come to include a 180 degree turn of my Steam thumb!

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time boxing fan and boxing gamer I can safely say that it's a work in progress. Very good mechanics overall. Can definitely tell Fight Night heavily inspired the punching system. One could honestly step right out of Fight Night and know the basic fundamentals of gameplay. I know this is beta which is why I feel this has great potential. The character models look fantastic, and much improved over Fight Night Champion, BUT some of the hair textures look rough. Tommy Morrison's hair looks like it was taken off an action figure. Improved hair textures and flow would be a major improvement. Another thing is the punches feel weak. Kind of like punching in a dream, slamming fist against a pillow. I hate to keep referring to Fight Night but its really the only thing to compare to. In this aspect it is highly superior in feel to Undisputed. The roster I know is being added to with each update, but I can't express enough how much this game needs Mike Tyson to feel like a true boxing game. Everyone who's a boxing gamer loves putting Tyson vs Ali. The only thing comparable to this on Undisputed is Marciano vs Ali. To end my criticism, the last improvement i'd suggest is everything overall just feels too stiff. I have an extreme amount of faith that this can be one of the best boxing games ever made with enough love and tweaking. I doubt any of this will be read by developers, but great job guys, keep up the good work. It's already a fun game, and I'm looking forward to seeing what improvements the future holds.

_childDocuments_.review: While it's not perfect, it's still a lot of fun and easily the best boxing game out there right now. I even compared it to Fight Night 4 and 3 and found that it surpassed them in terms of gameplay.The game has a solid offline mode with quick fights, training, and local 2-player options. You can also play online in quick and ranked matches. The slip and weave mechanics are very satisfying and add depth to the gameplay. The animations are next level and it's very satisfying to land a liver shot and see the ripples on your opponent's torso.The graphics are very impressive and remind me of the first time I played Fight Night 3 on the Xbox 360. The ripples on the face after a slow-mo knockout are even better in this game. The range of arenas and licensed music are also impressive.There are some areas that need improvement, such as the lack of replay after a knockout and too many cutscenes before fights that need to be skipped. There are also some slight glitches in the animations, and after a knockdown, the lack of ragdoll physics means that you can hover on your knees at times. Creating a lobby can also be a hassle since you have to share a code every time.Overall, this is a fantastic game for the price and I can see it becoming the new Fight Night. I'm excited to see the upcoming career mode and create-a-boxer features that will be added in the future. If you're a fan of boxing games, this one is definitely worth checking out.

Unrelated to the game-play, The fact that immediately upon releasing the game they lock fighters behind a paywall to attempt and milk more money from those who supported them from the beginning, shows where their focus truly lies. All in all, While I hope that they cam fix all of these issues and make a playable BOXING game, but as it stands now this can only be described as a waste of $30 for me. Not only do the CPU boxer still have a force-field , Steel Series Interactive think that it is impossible to throw a short punch while moving forward and rather chooses to throw a wild lunge punch that always bounce off of the, still present, force-field.With this update The CPU has gained a new ability to interrupt my punches and combos with almost robotic accuracy. BUT, it could be an incredibly good spiritual successor with a bit more polish and a few additional features in the career mode. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to share my feedback regarding the "Undisputed" boxing game, and unfortunately, my experience has left me with some concerns about the game's representation and diversity.While the concept of featuring boxers from 70% UK, 20% USA, and 10% other countries initially intrigued me, I couldn't help but notice the absence of true global representation. In the world of boxing, where talent and champions hail from various corners of the globe, the roster of "Undisputed" seems disproportionately skewed towards the UK and the USA.One glaring omission is the absence of the 8 world division champion, a hallmark of boxing greatness. This exclusion significantly diminishes the authenticity of the game, as these champions represent the pinnacle of the sport. The absence of these iconic figures from different weight classes is a notable oversight that impacts the overall credibility of the game.Furthermore, the underrepresentation of pound-for-pound champions from powerhouse boxing nations like Japan, the Philippines, and Mexico is disappointing. While I appreciate the inclusion of Canelo Alvarez, limiting the representation to just one boxer from Mexico falls short of capturing the diverse talent and achievements of Mexican fighters in the sport. The omission of legendary boxers from Japan and the Philippines is equally concerning, given their rich contributions to boxing history.I believe that enhancing the game's roster to include a more extensive and globally diverse selection of boxers, especially champions from different weight classes and regions, would significantly improve the gaming experience. A more comprehensive representation would not only appeal to a broader audience but also reflect the true spirit of international boxing.I hope you take this feedback into consideration for future updates to ensure "Undisputed" becomes a more accurate and inclusive representation of the dynamic world of boxing.Sincerely,Me

_childDocuments_.review: Well done Dev team. For early access this plays really well. The analogue controls are a joy, graphically really good (need to work on the motion blur though as it's overkill). Looking forward to seeing this progress and new modes/fighters and venues becoming available.  After playing for a couple of hours there are issues, listed here in order of significance:* Stamina - CPU stamina way too high, e.g Scenario 1: after 11 rounds and its still at 80% whereas players is at 15%. Scenario 2: Its round 4 and I've knocked CPU down twice within this timeframe, I've been knocked down zero times. CPU's remaining stamina is higher than mine.* Judges scoring - Totally weighted in favour of CPU, e.g: After 12 rounds I've landed 194 punches and not been down, CPU has landed 86 and has been down, yet two of the judges have scored the rounds 8-4 in favour of CPU, makes no sense* Motion blur when boxers are moving is making boxers look like a blurry mess.* Knockouts - can happen to you at random despite not having been down previously in the fight, and having dominated/knocked your CPU opponent down multiple times. Also KO's are very uninspiring, blink and you'll miss them and no replays.* Boxer Chantelle Camero has an age of 0, and doesn't resemble Chantelle Cameron at all.Overall, I'm glad that we have a boxing game with people from the Boxing community represented, and am looking forward to seeing the improvements to come. The stamina issues vs CPU however will need to be addressed quickly though as they make the game frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my personal opinion on the early access. I've been a huge boxing game enthusiast since the Knockout Kings and Fight Night eras. I have played all Fight Night games since 2004, Rd. 2, Rd.3 and Champions.  TLDR: Graphics are stunning. Current Gameplay is stiff, slow and heavy, physics is bad which make the game boring and just not fun. No career mode as of this time.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------GRAPHICS: This game has top-notch graphics. Stunning and realistic. No complaints as to that area.GAMEPLAY: The current gameplay feels stiff and is kinda frustrating since this is the most important aspect of a boxing game. But as of now, its just not fun to play. The movement of the fighters are excellent, but the bobbing and weaving feel kinda weak and are non-factor if you are avoiding punches, or on the defensive. You cant move while bobbing or weaving. Punches feel telegraphed, stiff, slow and heaving, but doesn't have much impact, and its difficult or just not fun to pull combinations. I feel like they could tweak the head physics a little bit when hitting your opponent or when your'e getting hit by them. Its unrealistic to throw power punches and see the fighter merely affected.Its very difficult to bruise or cut your opponent or character even after battering or getting battered for several rounds. Visual damages are almost non-existent as to my experience which add to the game being less interesting.Stamina management is bad and feels intrusive to the core gameplay. AUDIO: No complaints.ROSTER: Good selection of fighters so far. Considering that its still in early access.ONLINE: No comment. Since I'm not having fun with Quick Fights, I rarely play online.Hard to recommend the game at this point, but I would love for it to succeed.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're here to scratch an itch, I'll keep it short and say that it's close enough to a Fight Night game that you'll feel satisfied enough as long as you don't mind that the game is still incomplete. As of right now, we're not getting another one and almost nobody wants to play a ps3 game. The fighter's are well made. Good gait and movement simulation. Decent enough CPU AI on higher difficulties. They will fight and throw a volume and bag similar to the fighters themselves. You guys are doing a good job with this. A lot of your animations are great. Better than Fight Night. Like your punches when the fighter L-Steps or stops moving to throw. Well done. The movement is less game-like than Fight Night. Momentum exists and bigger guys with notably worse movement will behave that way. It's a simulation game in this regard. Slipping punches is much harder. Too hard imo. You pretty much need a fighter with the correct traits and stats to slip punches - which is unrealistic. Most fighters don't move like a grandpa regardless of weight. There's a balance you need to find between making guys move like prime Roy and your uncle Dave. The offence is close to fight night. One of the later ones like Champion with less complex joystick movement. I'd say it feels even better. Good job with this as well. The fighters react to punches coming in realistically, which means that keep someone at bay with a jab feels really good. Except if you fight an ai of a guy that fights at distance, you can't weave in. Fix your slipping or add a weave command where the guy steps forward weaving liek Tyson did. The Roster is filled with British fighters most people don't care about - the 50+ fighters are misleading. There are a handful of very notable fighters though. If they are struggling with licensing, I'd suggest a very complex fighter creator and a download system so that people can make the missing fighters for the time being. The graphics are good. Realistically, it's hard to care when you're playing a timing game. I don't play online. Can't comment. This is a good game and I hope they make enough money to develop it further and add more fighters. We needed a good boxing game and this is it. Support them if you want it to come out great. 8/10 for now. Easily worth the price for anyone who loved Fight Night imo.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the 1.0 version of Undisputed is probably the worst version of this game for singleplayer.As someone who played comfortably on undisputed difficulty all throughout early access I do not understand the changes they've made.When the opponent is stunned, they constantly step backwards and block. Your fighter gets "stuck" and instead of becoming aggressive the punches seem to slow down and you stop moving. The only way to KO a fighter is a combo they get stunned halfway through or by just spamming punches and hoping your character feels like moving forwards. This is incredibly frustrating as in a tough fight, stunning your opponent and then your character standing completely still throwing slow punches and then walking forward slowly is probably the least effective way to win and the game forces you to do this. It feels horrible.Punch animations are different based on whether or not the opponent has blocked. If you want to do a simple straight, L hook R hook and any of these are blocked, the subsequent punch is thrown from "standing" and not part of the combo meaning they take way way longer and the player cannot predict this.I don't know if damage has been adjusted in some way but every single fighter, career mode or quick play, results in me beating the hell out of the AI's face over and over and them stunning me with a few power punches, which the AI seem to spam.The game massively favours counter punching over everything else, which would be fine if the AI couldn't read your inputs. There was a version of EA like this and it was horrible and the devs changed it shortly after so I don't know why we've gone back to this.Career mode is poor, you start with minimal basic stats, do 1 amateur tournament and then need to fight your way up the roster. The problem with this is that you're constantly against the power curve. You can't level your character up well until much much later in the career - this is fine but it isn't fun. Needing to be 40 years old before you can meaningfully up your more important stats doesn't make for a fun time. There's no form of NG+ where you can bring your stats to a new fighter and be a young star or anything like that. In summary, the game feels bare bones and unfinished. The punching feels incredibly week, power punch spam is the obvious winning tactic and I have no idea how this is the gameplay we've received after a much much better early access. I cannot recommend Undisputed in its current state - nor can I say you can rely on updates to improve things as they clearly haven't.

_childDocuments_.review: It has potential, but I am leaving this has negative for the time-being, as there are far too many glitches for this to be a full release game, given the amount of development time they have had and poor online infrastructure.I want to address the online side of things first: again, they have had more than enough time to make improvements here. If, by luck, both yours and your opponents connections are perfect, you might not notice any issues. However, if there is even a remote hitch, then you WILL see desync (getting hit with punches that weren't even remotely near you from your perspective). This is due to their poorly designed online infrastructure (and using p2p). If Tekken can do it, and EA can do it with UFC 5 - say what you will about that game, but at least the online side if reliable. This should have been corrected by now. You will experience rocks happening when people are no-where near you, in its current state. There is also no penalty for people quitting out, so you don't get the win.As far as striking goes: it is more fun, it has been improved. There is a feeling that a fight can end at any time. That is the right way to go about this. You feel (and hear) the punches more. Before the full release update, it favoured more of the passive jab and retreat type fighters, which might be great for the minority boxing elitists - but they are not the people that buy the game. If they want it to sell, it needs to be fun. Nobody wants 8-12 rounds against someone that is approaching the fight like it's life or death, or like there is something real on the line. Stamina could do with a little bit of adjustment, as in its current state, you can spam power shots none stop and be left with little penalty to your stamina. SCI, don't cave to the vocal minority of boxing purists who want 12 rounds worth of jab and retreat.Striking is of course no-where near perfect. I find myself getting stuck in the pocket at times. This needs to be improved. As well as glitches such as being in a rocked state for no reason (after getting back up).They have implemented cuts and swelling, which adds another element of effecting fight outcomes.SCI: please work on your online infrastructure, make it cross-play, and address the cheaters - if you can get that perfect, then you stand a chance of making this game successful. Without it, the game will be dead within the month (again, look at UFC, Tekken, Mortal Kombat). Online is currently sub-par.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget what you've seen and forget what you heard. Especially the negative reviews here. This game is a boxing breath of fresh air. If not only for the fact of not having had a new boxing game for 10+ years. I keep seeing comparisons between this and Fight Night Champion. Undisputed has mechanics that make the two incomparable. It flows more freely than the almost predictable motions of FNC. It's more random. More a simulation. It's not perfect by any means. It definitely has it's mechanical flaws and lacks polish in certain areas(for me mainly the transition between inside and outside fighting. On the outside it's good but it gets slightly messy/whiffy when moving into the pocket/on the inside), but what's here is very positive. The dev team may be small but you can tell that they are very dedicated to their game, which is promising for it's future.  The potential is immense. Releasing it in early access is actually a plus here too bc you get it into the hands of players and you get to use the feedback from that to move forward. That's a positive. I'm happy with the purchase. Half the price of a triple a title. If nothing I implore you to give it the 2 hour return window chance. I don't think you'll regret trying it  in the slightest.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a boxing game! But how does it hold up? So I've played an hour so far and experienced fairly good performance for an early access. In game high settings I was hitting 144 FPS (Ryzen 5 5600X and 3060). I noticed occasional frame stutters in the character selection screen. In this early access we have a basic quick play mode, online multiplayer and local multiplayer which all in all I think is great to see at this stage in development. There's quite a lot of settings you can tweak. Let's talk about gameplay the footwork is great but the punching definitely needs some work nothing quite feels like it has any impact other than the simple flash on the screen when you get a good counter shot in. However I will say the controls feel smooth. The important thing is the core mechanics are there and they really just require some balancing and polish. The audio seems to be very weak and often cuts out and the corner men seem to just stare into oblivion which really takes away from the overall immersion. Other than that so far so good. Is it worth your money at this point? I would say so anyone who is into boxing games should 100% give this a try. For me this is going to be a lot of fun to play locally or online with friends. _childDocuments_.review: WOULD I RECOMMEND THIS GAME?to this i would answer, no not right now.i was an original beta tester and avid fight fan. i love fighting, spanning from fight night to UFC all though i would say this is on its way to being the best fighting game it is so under developed in every area. this means if your looking for a flushed out online/ranking mode you want to be playing UFC. (yes i know they have issues as well) and if your looking for in depth career mode then either fight night (any of them) or UFC is your bet.Saying this i do think eventually Undisputed will be better.The issues with Undisputed are but not limited too:• The Online Systemcurrently there is no anti cheat, like none. to prove this to myself i just loaded up WEMOD and went into prize fights and got ranked number 1, yes WEMOD.this will obviously be fixed with an implementation of anti cheat but currently online is virtually unplayable because either every fight or every other fight there are cheaters. This is why i have not played ranked since a month after early access.as well as the cheaters there is not much to do. I don't know if they will implement anything other than just fighting in either quick play or ranked but there is no special modes like tournament or maybe even switch rules up per fight in ranked so you would have to adjust the game plan per fight. something else does not to come there.• Career ModeFirst off i love career mode, i have probably played every EA title including a career mode as well as 2K.Its my favourite game mode as you get to take a custom made person through out there career.SCI did get the core elements of a career mode but you can tell that is under developed.This is the first time we have ever got "making weight" and through all the dev talks leading up to early access this was the thing i was most excited for.Needless to say it was lack luster. You just have to make sure your you don't go over during training, not with in game exercise but with a click of a button.Also no in game weigh ins/ press conference so say goodbye to immersion.Even if you wanted to spar in game before a fight you cant do that even tho it was clipped back in the ESBC days. The AI is way to easy to beat but more on that later. For some reason earlier in your career its harder to beat the AI because they have like 99 speed or power while you are supposed to pad your record with journey men but i guess not.Another thing is if you play for a while you will watch your opponents record and it will be 33-1-1 with 9KOso your telling me Deontay Wilder the hardest hitter in the game only got 9KO. OKAY.one last thing make an amateur career!I do hope everything i mentioned does get added or fixed as Career mode is a massive focus for a lot of players.there is more wrong and needing fixing but i don't want to drone on.• Quick PlayI wont go on for too much of this because its pretty obvious im not like the best boxer in the world but i understand the fundamentals of fighting, saying this i should not have a stroll in the park with any fighter against the best in the division on Undisputed difficulty.I have many ways in my mind to fix this but im not going to list them here.Also what happened to open weight classes? hope that's still on the way.•  GameplayI have already mention the AI needs fixingthe only other thing is the animations at this moment of posting they are broken. feels like im slapping someone with a wet sock, actually i think that would look cooler.I wont go on about the animations because it looks like with full release its mostly getting fixed.The movement is actually pretty good, and it should be because it was there main focus from start of development. although because of the loose movement feature it is currently possible to just bounce around the ring and never get hit (only tried against AI) and win rounds, there needs to be a feature to cut of the ring kinda like the lean in step forward movement but with that if the enemy is in corner of the ring the will have a movement penalty being stuck for like 3-5 seconds before attempting to get out. this would give an incentive to be aggressive with inside fighters. Current everyone will bounce on the outside and point fight. The stamina needs a rework from the ground up. currently i have never got the gassed animation.you can beat someones ribs for 12 hole rounds and you would probably have less stamina for trying, punches need to cost something. On both sides of the coin. I have to think about every punch i throw and everyone he lands especially to the body. Like if you wanna play Canelo and carefully land 4-5 good power punches to the body to take your opponent out in like round 7-11 like he does in real life. that aint happening.• Damage VFXso far you can only cut the left and right of your opponent. (you can get a cut on the nose but takes no real effect to the fight)my suggestions are that you are able to get real injury in mid fight (this would help career mode and also gameplay)for example • Broken/fracture orbital bone     (Cause blurriness to the screen)• Broken/sprained hand                 (Turn down Damage buy the hand/ pain to the fighter if used)• Broken/cut nose                          (Stamina goes down/ more prone to knockout because mouths open)• Broken/sprained ribs                   (Stamina drop and also drain faster and causing gassed animation)• Sprained ankle                            (Slow movement/ gassed animation)• Cuts on different areas of the face       ( would cause blurriness if leaking into the eye/ Stamina drop if leaking into the mouth)This doesn't have to be in Quick play or ranked because it would be RNG in a sense but would amplify the immersion and help career.• GraphicsThey are amazing...• Extra StuffThe cinematic all need workjust to list a fewbelts while walking out, same animation for every fighter walking out, no robes, no belt holding up when winning a title, announcers just sound stupid through most fights, saying good left hook to the body when you gave a straight to the face,theirs no event creator, no tournament creator, no special modes like bear knuckle or armature modes. All body punches feel slow and dangerous to do.jab cant be done like how it was in fight night, so you cant dance around the right jabbing your opponent.also cant knock out with a jab (i don't know if i agree with this or not) just think you should be able to but your opponent has to be caught seriously clean with a power jab or seriously low health.cross has zero turn, so feels like someone brand new is throwing that thing.  ( get some boxers don't turn a lot into there cross )just doesn't feel right.Left hook feels pretty good, especially the check hookRight hook feels clunky and no power (looks fixed in full release)Uppercuts look better in full release.Character creator looks completely rushed to reach a deadline of release for investors.No robes, barely any hair on facial hair options. tattoos is the worst system since the old fight nights., shorts and gloves is 3 templates with an rgb slider. not good!This is pretty much everything i can remember without spending days on this review.So yes dont buy right now, its rushed out as i assume to meet the investors deadlines. this is not what we expected when SCI promised us the world.I do still have high hopes for SCI to fix this because during beta they listened to our feedback and fixed a lot of things.just seems after early access its not been for the people. I completely understand that from business standpoint.I just hope they over time with every update Fix more and more.Im still hopefull and still will be. _childDocuments_.review: So this game is thus far a VERY mixed bag. It has some things it did well, some things it didn't, and some things that are really missing entirely. I paid for the early access, and have been following this game throughout its development.The good: The gameplay mechanics are great! The punching, footwork, blocking, weaving, and slipping have all been improved upon since early access, and over previous boxing games. I haven't bothered with multiplayer so I can't really review that piece, but other reviews are praising it, so it seems to be good. Career mode is okay enough, but still limited. Seems like a rehash of Fight Night Champion.The bad: Local play features are bare bones or missing entirely. The CAB is overall one of the weakest I've ever seen. It's not all bad of course, as the facial and body morphing are well done. However, that's where the good ends. Everything else about it is trash. Very limited hair styles, limited range of height and weight across weight classes. (Specifically limits to heavyweight). A pitiful allocation of available points means you won't be able to make a halfway decent rated CAB for local play. I'm guessing this is partly because Steel City wants to charge people for more boxers in the future who could be made locally, and partly to keep people from having an unfair advantage online, but why not just disable CABs for online play? There is also currently no option for cross-weight class or catchweight fights. Want to do some fun David vs Goliath lightweight vs heavyweight matches? Forget about it. You can't do that, even though that was a feature available in previous Fight Night Titles. Want to make a squat 5'6" heavyweight fighter? Want to make a lanky 6'7" featherweight? Nope. Sorry.Also, there is no option to make your own local fight cards or tournaments. Want to make a tournament bracket? Not unless you just do individual fights and fill in your own head canon. Want to make a fight card event? Same thing. All in all, it really feels like a step forward in 2 or 3 areas, and 2 steps back in all others. There are features that were available in boxing games from over a decade ago that this one doesn't have. In the year 2024, and the amount of time they had to develop this, I was expecting a lot more. If more features get added and improved on with subsequent updates, I'll change my opinion. However, at this stage on initial release, don't waste your time unless you just really love limited and straightforward PVP boxing. Steel City; you can do A LOT better!

_childDocuments_.review: Nobody is playing this game because of the persistent problems in the mechanics of the game, everything has been overhyped because this is the first boxing game in years. I had to fight the AI rather than an online player simply because online connectivity is horrible.- Spammers - Hook and jab spammers have been a problem since the game first came out and to combat this, they decided to make hooks stronger instead of providing stamina drain and arm fatigue. Those features were in UFC 1 and 2, preventing players from using the same move over and over again.- Health depletion - When a fighter's head or body health is reduced, they are still able to withstand even further damage before they are even ko'ed. Rocked moments are absolutely useless since blocking is op even in those moments.- Blocking - Blocking is a fundamental problem with the game coinciding with the punching mechanics. During rocked moments, punches have little to no effect as you play. And players wonder why most matches go on too long when YOU'RE the one winning.- No arm fatigue - Like I said previously, there is no arm fatigue preventing these players that just hold block from being susceptible to punches. Again, a feature that was in a game almost a decade old.The last thing I will say about this game, and I hope it reaches the developers is this, You have pretty much copied EA's Fight Night here but have not branched off or did anything to make this game enjoyable or fun. You continue to implement these random updates that either do noting, or harm the core gameplay. If you want this to be the next big boxing compared to it, fix the core problems of the game instead adding miscellaneous things like new boxers and venus, don't nobody care about that. The issue is no one is playing your game right now. You have something competent here, improve upon it smartly.

_childDocuments_.review: One year later and the game is worse..UNDISPUTEDLY THE WORST GAME EVER!!RAN OUT OF SPACE TO SAY HOW BAD THIS GAME ISTHIS GAME IS COMPLETE TRASH. DON'T BUY, LET IT DIE, SO ANOTHER STUDIO CAN MAKE A BETTER BOXING GAME. THESE UNTALENTED DEV'S DON'T CARE, THEY JUST WANT TO MAKE SOME MONEY BEFORE THEY ABANDON THE GAME. SO MANY THINGS ARE WRONG IN THIS GAME, UTTER DISAPPOINTMENT. FEEL LIKE I GOT SCAMMED. GIVE ME MY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MONEY BACK!!! NOT ENJOYABLE, JUST FRUSTRATION. DEV'S SHOULD RE-THINK THEIR CAREER CHOICE. I TRIED LIKING THE GAME, BUT IT IS SO HARD TO IGNORE HOW BAD IT IS. DEV'S PROMISED A CHAMP AND GAVE US A CHUMP! And we shall continue to wait for a good boxing game...Played for 4 hrs and I can report that this game reminds me of a bad cell phone game from 2015. Game needs so much work that I can only hope the dev's don't abandon it, and start hyping up undisputed 2 by June 2023.Graphics are ok. Interested in game play, would trade better graphics for game play any day. Game play is frustrating, human fighters feel they are in the 15th round when starting the 3rd round. PC fighter NEVER loses stamina. Human fighter get slow and weak to fast, throwing a 2-3 punch combo becomes almost impossible. It drains your fighter and can only throw slow motion punches. Fights become painfully boring, slow and unreal. Human fighters do almost no damage compared to the PC fighter. I have hit opponents with 2-3 consecutive good shots without effect. Opponent takes a step back, recovers fully in seconds, and rushes back at me while I'm still gassed out. PC countering is unrealistic and extremely accurate. PC counters hit you before your hand finishes the punch you threw. Stamina drain is ridiculously fast for human players and the game gets quite boring in a hurry since you can't generate enough momentum to re-create the excitement of a boxing match. Human fighters feel stiff, but PC can still be lightning fast with no stamina. Game is terrible, but what takes the cake is the mini game to get up after being knockdown. You have to have lizard eyes to be able to pull that one off. It needs to go. Defense side of the game is good animation wise, but useless. PC punches through any defense you put up. They generate damage even if you block punches. Their reach is exaggerated. Undisputed level fighter is stupid fast even without stamina. Game feels like it was shelved for a year and a half, then released because the studio ran out of money. I REGRET buying it. Really hope they keep working on it, it could become a good game. Haven't played online and would not dare to for fear of the cheaters that I'm sure by now are using the no stamina drain, ultra damage, speed cheats that will make you feel as if you are fighting Mike Tyson in god mode, versus you with hands tied behind your back.Comments might point out that this is an early access version, and I get that, but dev's had a lot of time to work on this game before releasing it in this disastrous state. Should have made it a free demo so they could get feedback, fix it and then charge for it.   Dev's should add sliders to increase/decrease pc/human fighter abilities like accuracy, punch speed and power. Adjust the disadvantages of PC stamina drain versus human stamina drain, redesign the mini game to get a fighter back up after a knockdown. Give us replays, round by round scoring. Please look at speeding up the punches for human player fighter when tired. Avoid this game until they patch it up. Thanks! * UPDATE 1* after playing for 20 hours*. Dev's you want to make a realistic boxing game??? ADD A DAMN REF!!!  Even Mike Tyson's punch out had a ref. The last boxing game I remember without a ref was Intellivision's boxing from 1978. And please be real, fights should not end up with a fighter throwing over 1000 punches. Much less with a fighter absorbing 600 head punches and somehow still manage to win...Or stay alive.Human Fighter's attributes do not seem to matter, punches do not do damage, I found that to have success against the PC is to become a counter puncher. If you go on the attack the PC unrealistically counter punches and blocks you every time. The result and downside is that you engage in a very boring fight. Compubox scoring here is completely broken and unrealistic, the score per round seems to be assigned at random. I have finished rounds or full fights with a much higher accuracy in all punch types and still lose many rounds. Fix the uneven stamina drain, I've had fights where my fighter stamina is at 60% by the 4th round and the PC player is still at 100%. A good way to describe how bad the punching is when boxers get tired...it feels like they are fighting UNDER WATER. It's an underwater tap and slap match. A boxer will slow down and have decreased power when tired, but not at the rate you see in this game. A real fighter will never get gassed out in the first 3 rounds of a fight, that's what they train for. Fighters in this game get so tired after throwing a couple of combos, they fight like they can't lift their arms anymore. Plus, a fighter if successful at blocking or avoiding a flurry of punches could regain stamina via the adrenaline rush he gets. Include that.  Dev's focus on the human vs PC game play, not just on online play. Human vs PC is completely unrealistic and frustrating. I have encountered game play bugs like PC fighter just standing next to me getting hit and doing nothing to defend himself. There are many times where the PC boxer moves weirdly and I end up facing his back. PC fighter stuck in "HUG MODE" and won't stop wanting to clinch (or make out). One time I was protecting my body and my boxers hand was twisted outwards. Fix the ridiculous clinches. There is no one to break up the clinch, human player can't do anything to break it and once over you have no stamina. Why would the fighter who clinches get his stamina back? but not he one who gets clinched. If anything the one who gets clinched should get it back faster than the clincher, as the clincher will be using more stamina to sustain the clinch. At least make it even. Also encountered punches that seem to go through my opponent, punches that just stop before landing, unnatural arm angles when punching, ghost punches, and punches that don't register at all. I have also seen the PC start a punch, then stop midway and start another punch. Issues regarding controller response as well, pressing buttons at times doesn't do anything, or they are late in activating.   Bottom line is that the game is terribly unrealistic and boring. Not worth buying at this time. Wait until it's fixed.*UPDATE 2* After 20+ hours...Uninstalled this garbage game. Maybe I'll try again after a couple of months if they fix the game. Steer clear of this trash. Not worth $30, not even worth free.  *UPDATE 3* Gave it another chance. DO NOT BELIEVE positive reviews, they are FAKE, computer generated, or done by people who got the game free. Had two fights in which the PC fighter did not lose stamina, they lost a little more of the red bar, but how can a PC boxer's white bar be at 100% in the 15th round?? While mine was at 48%? The PC fighters DO NOT receive damage, unless you spam one single punch. This game reduces boxing to a joke. This game will die in a couple of months. I highly doubt it will make it to a full release. Crappy selection of boxers, the good ones probably felt embarrassed to be on such a bad game. The ones included probably didn't play it or they just cared about the pay they got.*UPDATE 4* Heard they released a patch for the game, so I tried it out. The game is still TRASH and I honestly do not believe it will get better. Did the Sugar Ray Robinson vs Sugar Ray Leonard challenge, and Leonard had 100% stamina in the 15th round. Refund policy should be more forgiving as it's an early access disaster. Do not see a full release in this game's future, unless studio brings in more experienced talent to work on the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Playable in it's current state but needs improvement. Needs more boxers and would benefit from showcasing more styles such as for fighters of the mexican style, make footwork quicker on the inside and make angling easier. For Soviet style fighters, increase the ability to move in and out of range, etc. I understand the effect of the directional punches and footwork, but punching can sometimes still feel clunky even when those two things are implemented. Some animations need work as many punches just appear to miss for no reason. For instance many punches that would land on the shoulder just drift off to the side of your opponent. The learning curve is certainly greater than fight night as the mechanics are most definitely more advanced. A decent early access game but looking forward to the full release hopefully this September.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently purchased Undisputed, a boxing game that had been promising a career mode update for this fall. Based on the developers' assurances and my own enthusiasm for boxing games, I decided to take a chance on the game. Unfortunately, my experience with Undisputed has been far from satisfactory, and I have ultimately decided to request a refund.The most significant reason for my dissatisfaction is the delay of the career mode update. The promise of a career mode was a major selling point for me, as I enjoy the depth and progression that career modes offer. However, the developers have pushed the update back to next year, leaving me with a game that feels incomplete and lacking in substance.Apart from the missing career mode, I have also encountered several issues with the game's multiplayer mode. The multiplayer experience is marred by a rampant hacking problem, with cheaters disrupting matches and ruining the competitive spirit of the game. It has become increasingly difficult to find fair and enjoyable matches online, further diminishing the game's appeal.In addition to these major issues, I have also found the game's overall gameplay to be unpolished and lacking in depth. The combat mechanics feel repetitive, and the lack of variety in game modes makes the experience feel stale.Overall, my experience with Undisputed has been disappointing. The delayed career mode update, the rampant cheating in multiplayer, and the overall lack of polish have made the game unplayable for me. I have requested a refund and would not recommend this game to others until significant improvements are made.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he let me borrow his logitech wheel. Me and my son then played in turns and I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. _childDocuments_.review: Just bad. I've had the game since the beginning of Early Access. It was better at the start of the game. They've slowly destroyed the game with pointless updates and "balance patches". Then they dropped Career mode and it seemed like things might get better... Nope, more patches that broke the game and controls that evolved to be even clunkier than before. So there is hope for the 1.0 release right? Nope again.. 1.0 is trash. To release a game in this state and call it a 1.0 is a slap in the face to everyone who purchased this game. Whether you bought it early or after 1.0 you'll be disappointed. The game feels worse than before, fighters are oiled up and shiny as hell, the physics don't make sense and overall it feels like a rushed game with little character to it. Immersion: non-existent. In career mode, the AI and your character look just awful with no attention to detail. If EA were the ones to make this game, I'd believe it, but this is an indy dev that has lost their way. They've built paywalls and there are countless desync issues. Additionally, they don't even have a ref in the ring except for the 3 options of knockdown animations they've included in the game. Everything feels half-assed and then some in this game when it comes to the immersion side. For multiplayer, characters are locked behind money, desync happens often, and the boxing mechanics are abused, not to mention cheaters already wreaking havoc on the game. 1/10 - just go buy Fight Night: Champions on Xbox or emulate it on your PC and you'll have a much better experience and quality of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Wicked.This is not Tekken. More like Bushido Blade, but with less death. Twitch skills won't get you much here. Look where the opponent is open, hit them there. Back off. Think. Move in and toss a couple jabs to bring their guard up and then launch a few body shots to run their stamina down. Block. Duck. Back off. Think. Target the cut. Jab to bring the guard up, hook to the body to bring it back down, and then BAM, big straight right to the cheekbone and they're staggering and dripping blood. Big finish. Solid right hook to the jaw, there goes the mouthguard and they're down. Will they get back up?Gonna have to just play and find out.This is a really good boxing sim, and the fact you can create your own boxers and work them through a career and training camps to improve their skills is all just icing on the cake. 100% recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, congrats on getting this far. The game looks great. I played the tutorial and the opening match and started using loose movement after the first round of the opening match that I won but decision. I used Roy Jones vs Canelo in my next match, then Brook vs Crawford , and noticed that I was falling behind in the cards but throwing and landing at almost twice the rate of the other guy just at a slightly lower percentage. I won all 4 of my first fights by KO but then came the Wilder vs Fury fight and what I noticed about the scoring come into play. I used Wilder using loose movement ( which is supposed to give you a higher chance of getting a KO or being KO'd) and throw over 1,200 punches in the fight and landed over 500. Fury threw about 500 punches and landed about 250. I landed 61% of my power shots to his 41% and I still lose every round of the fight on all three judges score cards. I even switched to using the power modifier in the last few round after seeing how the fight was being scored. I had Fury rocked during the last round and still could not drop him ( witch is okay) but I lost that round on the cards as well. The bottom line is the balancing has to be better. NO ONE alive can take almost 300 power shots from Wilder or go the distance with him landing 61% of his power shots. Plus, to still lose on the cards after throwing 1,200 punches and landing at over 40% and 61% of my power shots and having the guy rocked in the last round. I landed as many punches as Fury threw. This just can't happen. I already see guy give horrible tutorials on how to cheese this game and take advantage of how scoring is being done on YouTube. The damage has to be balance and judging damage done vs percentage of punches landed has to be changed. I love the game and how it moves and plays, but I will never play online like this ( which I don't play online anyway) and it will kill my enjoyment of the game offline as well. It was so sad because I really loved the gameplay.  Pleeaaasssse, fix this. I understand you're trying to make the game technical but at the cost of realism. I can't have a game where I throw 1,000 punches and land 400 and the other guy throws 400 but lands 180 but I lose the fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a better game than the mixed feedback gives it credit for. Career mode is very bare bones on initial release, but a great addition that makes the game more playable in the long term and more worth buying. Experimenting with different builds, traits, etc. provides hours of gameplay, and was sorely needed. Still needs LOTS of fine tuning in fight mechanics. The long and short is the game absolutely favors outboxers and counterpunchers too much. Play as an outboxer with superior reach and punch speed, counter the enemy for a couple rounds while avoiding trading punches, and then pressure for KO whenever opponent is dazed, and you will have virtually 100% KOs against AI at any difficulty and against many human players as well.The game does not really do justice to sluggers currently, and especially penalizes infighting to the point that it is hard to do well at max difficulty, while outboxing the AI is just too easy. Power punching definitely needs to be majorly buffed (it costs too much stamina and does not do enough damage currently), and counterpunches might need to be somewhat nerfed. This would at least help balance out the fighting styles and make sluggers and infighters more dangerous.Multiplayer is not the best part of the game in my opinion. Some punchsets are still a bit too good, and prone to exploits/cheese. Better than a while ago, when everyone was playing Ali and spamming hooks, but still needs lots of work for balance. Contrary to some, I do think things are at least improving here.All in all its better than much feedback suggests for a game still in early access, and which seems to be gradually improving. Definitely better than if it was made by EA

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: The game is really bad and has made very little improvements. I wouldn't waste your time. Unless you like to run away the whole match and call it "boxing". There's no way to close distance or cut off the ring effectively. The animations lock you into place so if someone just circles and runs constantly you will never catch them. Even if you jab straight or try to explode forward to cover distance you will not be able to get into a comfortable fighting distance.I would wait on the game for future improvements. There are cool things you can do in the game. Directional punches are nice and once you master some things and learn the animations you can control distance and unleash combos on your opponents. There are other things to master like movement and sidesteps that feel nice at times.Despite some positives, the game doesn't feel rewarding whatsoever. I consistently can out strike my opponents and hit them 500 times with little to no effect. 100+ power shots seemingly do nothing. The game rewards plodding forward and eating shots while spamming hooks or other quick punches/combos and trying to land a lucky power shot. Counter shots do no damage, sidesteps into a combo, nothing, sitting down on a combo and picking my opponent apart does nothing. Perfectly timed movement and check hook while dodging a short right hook, you guessed it, it does nothing. Timing my opponent and reading them should feel rewarding and do something. Damage and stamina were addressed at points in the beta, but are extremely bad in the game right now. Like most, I was extremely excited for a new and realistic boxing game. After around 200 rounds played, I can't see myself playing the game all that much. I might login and play a game here and there, but it's not something I am dying to play. I would like to hope major balancing changes happen, but with the game as it is after seemingly being corrected throughout the second beta with changes to damage and stamina, I don't know if there will be. Certain animations in the game are completely useless because they feel clunky and inconsistent. The forward moving and standing straight (cross) is pretty much useless in the game because it's clunky, awkward and slow combined with doing very little damage and only stuns my opponent for a millisecond after connecting. This rewards hook and other spam punches even more. Other than that, the game does feel a bit robotic. I think it's because of most of the animations being the same or very very similar and not all that fluid. Some of them are really nice, but most are not. There was a ton of talk about true to form fighting and animations, but outside a few fighters stances and certain fighters like Roy Jones most of the punches are the same from fighter to fighter. Every fighter has the same useless cross and most of them have the same animations for hooks, power hooks, and hooks to the body as well. If you were excited about fighters feeling very different and there being fluidity and differences between all their punches, I would temper your expectations. I don't think the devs can do that much about this, but it was marketed early on about being true to fighters with how they motion capture punches and stuff. Everyone having similar animations also contributes to the game feeling more robotic.The game has potential, but it's a long way from what has been marketed and a long way from a full product.DO NOT buy a cpu just for the game it is not worth it. Once the hype for a new boxing game dies down, the true worth of the game to most will come out so people should wait for right now. For me, after the hype of wanting to play, people should wait for improvements before buying.Do not get tricked by positive reviews at least 1/4 of the positive reviews are actually negative and from people who did not know to change the thumbs up to thumbs down. Do more research before buying, streams videos, etc. Do that and make a decision for yourself.At the moment this game is unbearable. It's easy to win, but it's pretty much impossible to have a fun game. Every game is against whatever boxer has the silliest most spammy punches. The damage system in this game is completely flawed and broken. There is hard health for your boxer as a whole and temporary health for areas such as the right side of your head, right side of body, etc,etc. What ends up happening at the end of every round is that the temporary bars are completely recovered according to overall health. Overall health is the only thing that can decrease the amount of temporary health specific areas have. If you hit someone in the head 600 times, which I have without any effect, his body health will basically heal his brain damage. There are core problems with this game. Ping, damage system, animations, etc, etc. Even if this is early access I would recommend others to wait to purchase this for at least a month or two.
